1 chronicles_1.t: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah; Shem, Ham and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one on the earth.
Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim and the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came out, and the Caphtorim.
Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusites, the Amorites and the Girgashites,
and the Hivites, the Arkites and the Sinites,
and the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram; and Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshech.
Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
To Eber two sons were born: one was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; and his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth and Jerah,
and Hadoram, Uzal and Diklah,
and Ebal, Abimael and Sheba,
and Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram — that is, Abraham.
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These were their generations: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal: Alyan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon. And the sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran and Keran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan and Jaakan. The sons of Dishon: Uz and Aran.
These were the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the people of Israel: Bela son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad reigned in his place — the one who struck down Midian in the region of Moab; and the name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth-on-the-River reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal-hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place; the name of his city was Pai, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
And Hadad died. And the chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

1 chronicles_2.t: These were the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan and Shelah — three were born to him from Bath-shua the Canaanite woman. And Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, so he put him to death.
And Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.
The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Kalkol and Dara — five of them in all.
The sons of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who acted unfaithfully with what was devoted to destruction.
The sons of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons of Hezron who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.
Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, leader of the people of Judah.
Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz,
and Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse,
and Jesse fathered his firstborn Eliab, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.
And their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah: Abshai, Joab and Asahel — three of them.
And Abigail bore Amasa; and Amasa's father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
And Caleb son of Hezron had children by Azubah his wife, and by Jerioth; and these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrath for himself, and she bore him Hur.
And Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
And later Hezron went in to the daughter of Makir the father of Gilead — he'd taken her when he was sixty years old — and she bore him Segub.
And Segub fathered Jair, and he had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
And Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair from them, with Kenath and its daughter-villages — sixty cities. All these were the descendants of Makir the father of Gilead.
And after the death of Hezron in Caleb-ephrathah — and Hezron's wife was Abijah — she bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
And the sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were the firstborn Ram, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.
And Jerahmeel had another wife whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin and Eker.
And the sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada; and the sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
And the name of Abishur's wife was Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
And the sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. And Seled died without sons.
And the sons of Appaim: Ishi. And the sons of Ishi: Sheshan. And the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.
And the sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan. And Jether died without sons.
And the sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
And Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. And Sheshan had an Egyptian slave whose name was Jarha.
And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his slave as a wife, and she bore him Attai.
And Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad,
and Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed,
and Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah,
and Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah,
and Eleasah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum,
and Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.
And the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
And the sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.
And Shema fathered Raham the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem fathered Shammai.
And the son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
And Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza and Gazez; and Haran fathered Gazez.
And the sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
And she bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and of Gibea. And Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma the father of Bethlehem, Hareph the father of Beth-gader.
And Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had sons: Haroeh, and half the Menuhoth.
And the clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites and the Mishraites; from these came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma: Bethlehem and the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half the Manahathites, the Zorites.
And the clans of the scribes who lived at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

1 chronicles_3.t: And these were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel; the second Daniel, by Abigail of Carmel;
the third, Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah his wife.
Six were born to him in Hebron. He reigned there seven years and six months, and for thirty-three years he reigned in Jerusalem.
And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon — four, by Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel.
And Ibhar, Elishama and Eliphelet,
and Nogah, Nepheg and Japhia,
and Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet — nine.
All these were the sons of David, besides the sons of concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
And the son of Solomon: Rehoboam; Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.
And the sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.
And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
And the sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son,
and Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.
And the sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. And the sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah; and Shelomith was their sister.
and Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-hesed — five.
And the sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
And the sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. And the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat — six.
And the sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam — three.
And the sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani — seven.

1 chronicles_4.t: The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal.
And Reaiah son of Shobal fathered Jahath, and Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.
And these were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma and Idbash; and their sister's name was Hazzelelponi;
and Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrath, the father of Bethlehem.
And Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
And Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
And the sons of Helah: Zereth, Zohar and Ethnan.
And Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.
And Jabez was more honoured than his brothers; and his mother had called him Jabez, saying, "Because I gave birth in pain."

And Jabez called on the God of Israel: "If only you would bless me and enlarge my territory, and your hand be with me, and you keep me from harm so that it doesn't hurt me!" And God brought him what he'd asked for.
And Kelub the brother of Shuhah fathered Mehir; he was the father of Eshton.
And Eshton fathered Beth-rapha, Paseah and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah.
And the sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. And the sons of Othniel: Hathath.
And Meonothai fathered Ophrah; and Seraiah fathered Joab the father of Ge-harashim, for they were craftsmen.
And the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah and Naam. And the sons of Elah: and Kenaz.
And the sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria and Asarel.

And the sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon. These are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered took as his wife: she conceived Miriam, Shammai and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
And his Judahite wife bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Socoh, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah.
And the sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham: the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
And the sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
The sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the linen-workers' guild, of the house of Ashbea,
and Jokim, the men of Cozeba, and Joash and Saraph who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem. And these records are ancient.
They were the potters and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah; they lived there with the king, in his service.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah and Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
And the descendants of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers did not have many sons, and their whole clan did not increase as much as the people of Judah.
And they lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
and in Bilhah, Ezem and Tolad,
and in Bethuel, Hormah and Ziklag,
and in Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri and Shaaraim. These were their cities until David reigned.
And their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen and Ashan — five cities,
and all their villages that were around these cities as far as Baal. These were their dwelling places, and they had their own genealogical record.
And Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
and Joel, and Jehu son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel,
and Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel and Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah.
These, listed by name, were leaders in their clans, and their ancestral houses increased greatly.
They went to the entrance of Gedor, east of the valley, looking for pasture for their flocks.
And they found rich, good pasture, and the land was broad on both sides, quiet and at ease; the people who had lived there before were from Ham.

And these, listed by name, came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and struck down their tents and the Meunites who were found there, and they devoted them to destruction to this day, and settled in their place; because there was pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them, of the Simeonites, went to Mount Seir — five hundred men — with Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, at their head.
And they struck down the remaining survivors of Amalek, and they've lived there to this day.

1 chronicles_5.t: And the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel — he was the firstborn, but when he profaned his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so he isn't enrolled as the firstborn;
for Judah prevailed among his brothers, and a leader came from him; but the birthright belonged to Joseph —
the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
The descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
Beerah his son, whom Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took into exile; he was a leader of the Reubenites.
And his relatives by their clans, when the genealogical record of their generations was made: the chief Jeiel, and Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. He lived in Aroer, and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.
And to the east he settled as far as the edge of the wilderness, from the river Euphrates; for their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul they made war on the Hagrites, and the Hagrites fell by their hand; and they lived in their tents throughout all the east of Gilead.
And the Gadites lived opposite them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah:
Joel the chief, Shapham the second, and Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.
And their relatives by their ancestral houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber — seven.
These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was chief of their ancestral house.
And they lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its daughter-villages, and in all the pasture lands of Sharon to their limits.
All of them were enrolled by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh — fighting men who bore shield and sword and bent the bow, and were trained for war — numbered forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty who went out to the army.
And they made war on the Hagrites, and on Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

And they were helped against them, and the Hagrites were given into their hand, and everyone with them; because they cried out to God in the battle, and he was entreated by them, since they trusted in him.
And they captured their livestock: fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys — and a hundred thousand human beings.
Many fell slain, because the battle was from God. And they lived in their place until the exile.
And the people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land, from Bashan to Baal-hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon; they multiplied.
And these were the chiefs of their ancestral houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel — mighty men of valour, men of renown, chiefs of their ancestral houses.
But they acted unfaithfully against the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land, the ones God had destroyed before them.

And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he took them into exile — the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh — and he brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river of Gozan, to this day.

1 chronicles_6.t: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
And the children of Amram: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. And the sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas; Phinehas fathered Abishua;
and Abishua fathered Bukki; and Bukki fathered Uzzi;
and Uzzi fathered Zerahiah; and Zerahiah fathered Meraioth;
Meraioth fathered Amariah; and Amariah fathered Ahitub;
and Ahitub fathered Zadok; and Zadok fathered Ahimaaz;
and Ahimaaz fathered Azariah; and Azariah fathered Johanan;
and Johanan fathered Azariah — he is the one who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem;
and Azariah fathered Amariah; and Amariah fathered Ahitub;
and Ahitub fathered Zadok; and Zadok fathered Shallum;
and Shallum fathered Hilkiah; and Hilkiah fathered Azariah;
and Azariah fathered Seraiah; and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.
And Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. And these are the clans of the Levites, by their fathers.
Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.
The descendants of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, Shaul his son.
And the sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah. The descendants of Elkanah: Zophai his son, Nahath his son,
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.
And the sons of Samuel: the firstborn, Joel, and the second, Abijah.
The descendants of Merari: Mahli; Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
And these are the ones David put over the service of song in the house of the LORD, after the ark came to rest.
And they ministered with song in front of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem; and they stood at their service according to their ordinance.
And these are the ones who served, and their sons: of the Kohathites, Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
And his relative Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph son of Berekiah, son of Shimea,
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malkijah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.
And the Merarites, their relatives, were at the left hand: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
And their relatives the Levites were assigned to all the service of the tabernacle of the house of God.

And Aaron and his sons burned offerings as smoke on the altar of the burnt offering and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
And these are the descendants of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
And these were their dwelling places, by their settlements within their territory: to the descendants of Aaron, of the Kohathite clan — for the lot fell to them —
and they gave them Hebron in the land of Judah, with its pasture lands around it.
But the field of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
And to the descendants of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron, and Libnah with its pasture lands, and Jattir, and Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
and Hilez with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
and Ashan with its pasture lands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Geba with its pasture lands, Alemeth with its pasture lands, and Anathoth with its pasture lands. All their cities were thirteen cities by their clans.
And to the remaining descendants of Kohath, from the clan of the tribe, from the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, by lot, ten cities.
And to the descendants of Gershom by their clans: from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
To the descendants of Merari by their clans: from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and the tribe of Zebulun, by lot, twelve cities.
And the people of Israel gave the Levites the cities and their pasture lands.
And they gave by lot, from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon and the tribe of Benjamin, these cities which are called by name.
And as for some of the clans of the descendants of Kohath, the cities of their territory were from the tribe of Ephraim.
And they gave them the cities of refuge: Shechem with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer with its pasture lands,
and Jokmeam with its pasture lands, and Beth-horon with its pasture lands,
and Aijalon with its pasture lands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner with its pasture lands, and Bileam with its pasture lands — for the clan of the remaining descendants of Kohath.
To the descendants of Gershom: from the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its pasture lands, and Ashtaroth with its pasture lands;
and from the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
and Ramoth with its pasture lands, and Anem with its pasture lands;
and from the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasture lands, and Abdon with its pasture lands,
and Hukok with its pasture lands, and Rehob with its pasture lands;
and from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, Hammon with its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim with its pasture lands.
To the remaining descendants of Merari: from the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono with its pasture lands, Tabor with its pasture lands;
and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, east of the Jordan: from the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with its pasture lands, Jahzah with its pasture lands,
and Kedemoth with its pasture lands, and Mephaath with its pasture lands;
and from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
and Heshbon with its pasture lands, and Jazer with its pasture lands.

1 chronicles_7.t: And the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron — four.

And the sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam and Samuel, chiefs of their ancestral house, of Tola, mighty men of valour in their generations; their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
And the sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah — five, all of them chiefs.
And with them, by their generations and their ancestral houses, were troops of the army of war, thirty-six thousand; for they had many wives and sons.
And their relatives, of all the clans of Issachar, were mighty men of valour: eighty-seven thousand in their genealogical record, all told.
Benjamin: Bela, Beker and Jediael — three.
And the sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri — five, chiefs of an ancestral house, mighty men of valour; and their genealogical record was twenty-two thousand and thirty-four.
And the sons of Beker: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Beker.
And their genealogical record, by their generations, chiefs of their ancestral houses, mighty men of valour: twenty thousand two hundred.
And the sons of Jediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.
All these were the sons of Jediael, listed by the chiefs of their ancestral houses, mighty men of valour: seventeen thousand two hundred going out to the army for battle.
And Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir; Hushim, the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shallum — the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom she bore; his Aramean concubine bore Makir the father of Gilead.
And Makir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim; and his sister's name was Maacah; and the name of the second was Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters.
And Maacah the wife of Makir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh; and his brother's name was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.
And the sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Makir, son of Manasseh.
And his sister Hammoleketh bore Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.
And the sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.
And the descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead. And the men of Gath who were born in the land killed them, because they'd gone down to take their livestock.
And Ephraim their father mourned for many days, and his relatives came to comfort him.
And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son; and he called him Beriah, because his house had been in distress.
And his daughter was Sheerah, and she was the one who built Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.
And Rephah his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, Joshua his son.

And their possession and their dwelling places were Bethel and its daughter-villages, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer with its daughter-villages, and Shechem with its daughter-villages, as far as Ayyah with its daughter-villages.

And along the borders of the Manassites: Beth-shan with its daughter-villages, Taanach with its daughter-villages, Megiddo with its daughter-villages, Dor with its daughter-villages. In these lived the descendants of Joseph son of Israel.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah; and Serah was their sister.
And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel; he was the father of Birzaith.
And Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer and Hotham, and Shua their sister.
And the sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.
And the sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah and Aram.
And the sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran and Beera.
And the sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispah and Ara.
And the sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel and Rizia.

All these were the descendants of Asher, chiefs of the ancestral houses, choice mighty men of valour, chiefs of the leaders. And their genealogical record for army service in battle: their number was twenty-six thousand men.

1 chronicles_8.t: And Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Ahrah the third,
Nohah the fourth and Rapha the fifth.
And Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
and Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
and Gera, Shephuphan and Huram.
And these were the sons of Ehud — these were the chiefs of the ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Geba, and they were taken into exile to Manahath —
and Naaman, Ahijah and Gera — he was the one who took them into exile — and he fathered Uzzah and Ahihud.
And Shaharaim fathered children in the region of Moab, after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives.
And by Hodesh his wife he fathered Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malkam,
and Jeuz, Sakia and Mirmah. These were his sons, chiefs of ancestral houses.
And by Hushim he fathered Abitub and Elpaal.
And the sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham and Shemed — he built Ono and Lod with its daughter-villages —
and Beriah and Shema — they were the chiefs of the ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon; they were the ones who put the inhabitants of Gath to flight —
and Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
and Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
and Michael, Ishpah and Joha — the sons of Beriah.
And Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
and Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab — the sons of Elpaal.
And Jakim, Zikri, Zabdi,
and Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
and Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath — the sons of Shimei.
And Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
and Abdon, Zikri, Hanan,
and Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
and Iphdeiah and Penuel — the sons of Shashak.
And Shamsherai, Shechariah, Athaliah,
and Jaareshiah, Elijah and Zikri — the sons of Jeroham.
These were chiefs of ancestral houses, by their generations, chiefs. These lived in Jerusalem.
And in Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon; and his wife's name was Maacah.
And his firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
and Gedor, Ahio and Zeker.
And Mikloth fathered Shimeah. And they too lived opposite their relatives in Jerusalem, with their relatives.
And Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malki-shua, Abinadab and Eshbaal.
And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal fathered Micah.
And the sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea and Ahaz.
And Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah, and Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.
And Moza fathered Binea; Raphah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.
And the sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second and Eliphelet the third.
And the sons of Ulam were mighty men of valour, who bent the bow, and had many sons and grandsons — a hundred and fifty. All these were of the Benjaminites.

1 chronicles_9.t: And all Israel was enrolled by genealogy, and there they are, written in the book of the kings of Israel. And Judah was taken into exile to Babylon for their unfaithfulness.
And the first inhabitants back in their own possessions, in their cities, were Israel, the priests, the Levites and the temple servants.
And in Jerusalem lived some of the people of Judah, some of the people of Benjamin, and some of the people of Ephraim and Manasseh:
Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, of the descendants of Perez son of Judah;
and of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons;
and of the descendants of Zerah: Jeuel; and their relatives, six hundred and ninety.
And of the Benjaminites: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah;
and Ibneiah son of Jeroham; and Elah son of Uzzi, son of Mikri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah;
and their relatives, by their generations, nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were chiefs of ancestral houses, by their ancestral house.
And of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib and Jakin;
and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, leader of the house of God;
and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malkijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer;
and their relatives, chiefs of their ancestral houses — one thousand seven hundred and sixty, mighty in ability for the work of the service of the house of God.
And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the descendants of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh and Galal; and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zikri, son of Asaph;
and Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berekiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
And the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon and Ahiman; and their relative Shallum was the chief.
And until now they were the gatekeepers at the king's gate on the east, for the camps of the Levites.

And Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his relatives of his ancestral house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent; and their fathers had been over the camp of the LORD, keepers of the entrance.
And Phinehas son of Eleazar had been leader over them in earlier times; the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

All those chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds were two hundred and twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in their villages; David and Samuel the seer were the ones who had put them in their trusted office.
And they and their sons were over the gates of the house of the LORD, the house of the tent, for guard duties.
The gatekeepers were on four sides: east, west, north and south.
And their relatives in their villages were to come in for seven days at a time, taking their turn with these.
For the four chief gatekeepers held a trusted office; they were Levites, and they were over the store-rooms and over the treasuries of the house of God.
And they spent the night around the house of God, because the duty was theirs; and they were in charge of the key, morning by morning.
And some of them were over the articles used in the service — they brought them in by count and took them out by count.
And some of them were appointed over the articles and over all the articles of the holy place, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense and the spices.
And some of the priests' sons mixed the blending of the spices.
And Mattithiah, one of the Levites — he was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite — held the trusted office over the making of the flat cakes.
And some of the Kohathites, of their relatives, were over the bread of the row, to prepare it sabbath by sabbath.
And these were the singers, chiefs of the ancestral houses of the Levites, in the rooms, free of other duty; because the work was on them by day and by night.
These were chiefs of the ancestral houses of the Levites, by their generations, chiefs. These lived in Jerusalem.
And in Gibeon lived Jeiel the father of Gibeon; and his wife's name was Maacah;
and his firstborn son Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
and Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah and Mikloth.
And Mikloth fathered Shimeam. And they too lived opposite their relatives in Jerusalem, with their relatives.
And Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malki-shua, Abinadab and Eshbaal.
And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Meri-baal fathered Micah.
And the sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech and Tahrea.
And Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.
And Moza fathered Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

1 chronicles_10.t: The Philistines fought against Israel. The men of Israel ran from the Philistines, and they fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they struck down Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-shua, Saul's sons.
The fighting bore down hard on Saul. The archers with the bow found him, and they wounded him badly.

Saul said to his weapon-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised will come and deal wantonly with me." But his weapon-bearer wouldn't do it, because he was very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.
When his weapon-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell on the sword too and died.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his whole household died together.
When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they left their cities and ran; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
The next day the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him and took his head and his weapons, and they sent them all around the land of the Philistines, to carry the news to their idols and to the people.
They put his weapons in the house of their gods, and they fastened his skull in the house of Dagon.
All of Jabesh-gilead heard everything the Philistines had done to Saul.
So all the mighty men set out, and they took Saul's body and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
So Saul died for his unfaithfulness — he acted unfaithfully against the LORD, over the word of the LORD that he didn't keep, and he consulted a medium as well, to seek guidance;
and he didn't seek guidance of the LORD. So he put him to death and turned the kingship over to David son of Jesse.

1 chronicles_11.t: All Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "Here we are — we're your own bone and flesh."

In the past, even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them in; and the LORD your God said to you, "You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be leader over my people Israel."

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them there before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel, just as the LORD had said by the hand of Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem — that is, Jebus — and the Jebusites, the people living in the land, were there.
The people of Jebus said to David, "You're not coming in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion — that is, the city of David.
David had said, "Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first will become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.
David lived in the fortress, so they called it the city of David.
He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the rest of the city.
And David kept growing greater and greater, and the LORD of hosts was with him.
These were the chiefs of David's mighty men, the ones who gave him strong support in his kingdom, along with all Israel, to make him king, just as the LORD had said concerning Israel.
This is the number of David's mighty men. Jashobeam a Hacmonite, chief of the officers — he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time.
After him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he was one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. The plot of field was full of barley, and the people ran from the Philistines.
They took their stand in the middle of the plot and defended it, and they struck the Philistines down; and the LORD brought about a great deliverance.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock, to David, to the cave of Adullam; and the Philistine camp was pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
David was in the stronghold then, and the Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem then.
David had a craving, and he said, "Who'll give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, the one at the gate?"

So the three broke through the Philistine camp and drew water from the well of Bethlehem at the gate, and they carried it back and brought it to David. But David wouldn't drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.

He said, "Far be it from me before my God to do this! Am I to drink the blood of these men at the cost of their lives? They brought it at the cost of their lives." And he wouldn't drink it. That is what the three mighty men did.
Abshai the brother of Joab — he was chief of the three. He wielded his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the three.
Of the three he was doubly honoured, and he became their commander; but he didn't reach the three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, great in deeds, from Kabzeel — he struck down the two Ariel of Moab. And he went down and struck the lion down inside the pit on a snowy day.

And he struck down the Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits tall. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand like a weaver's beam, and he went down to him with a club, tore the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
That is what Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
Of the thirty he was honoured, but he didn't reach the three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
And the mighty men of the forces: Asahel the brother of Joab; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira son of Ikkesh of Tekoa; Abiezer of Anathoth;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai of Netophah; Heled son of Baanah of Netophah;
Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites; Benaiah of Pirathon;
Hurai from the wadis of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite;
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shageh the Hararite;
Ahiam son of Sakar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mekerathite; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro of Carmel; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel the brother of Nathan; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai of Beeroth, the weapon-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him;
Hanan son of Maacah; and Joshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia of Ashtaroth; Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham of Aroer;
Jediael son of Shimri, and Joha his brother the Tizite;
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel, Obed and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

1 chronicles_12.t: These were the ones who came to David at Ziklag while he was still shut off from Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty men, helpers in the war.
equipped with the bow, able with right hand and left alike, with stones and with arrows on the bow; kinsmen of Saul, from Benjamin.
The chief was Ahiezer, and Joash, the sons of Hasshemaah of Gibeah; and Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; and Berachah and Jehu of Anathoth;
and Ishmaiah of Gibeon, a mighty man among the thirty and over the thirty; and Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan and Jozabad of Gederah;
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah and Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

From the Gadites, men went over to David at the fortress in the wilderness — mighty men of valour, men of the army for battle, handling shield and spear. Their faces were the faces of a lion, and they were as swift as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These were the Gadites, chiefs of the army: the least was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.
These were the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put to flight everyone in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Some of the Benjaminites and of Judah came to the fortress, to David.

David went out to meet them, and he answered and said to them, "If you've come to me in peace, to help me, my heart will be joined to you; but if to betray me to my adversaries, when there's no violence in my hands, may the God of our fathers see and judge."

And a spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the officers: "We're yours, David, and with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to the one who helps you, for your God has helped you." So David received them and put them among the chiefs of the band.

Some of Manasseh went over to David when he came with the Philistines against Saul for battle — but they didn't help them, because the rulers of the Philistines took counsel and sent him away, saying, "He'll go over to his lord Saul at the cost of our heads."
As he went to Ziklag, these of Manasseh went over to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu and Zillethai, chiefs of the thousands of Manasseh.
They helped David against the raiding band, because they were all mighty men of valour; and they became commanders in the army.
Day after day they kept coming to David to help him, until it was a great camp, like the camp of God.
These are the numbers of the chiefs of those equipped for the army, who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul's kingdom over to him, just as the LORD had said.
The men of Judah, bearing shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred, equipped for the army.
Of the Simeonites, mighty men of valour for the army: seven thousand one hundred.
Of the Levites: four thousand six hundred.
And Jehoiada was the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred;
and Zadok, a young man mighty in valour, and his ancestral house — twenty-two commanders.
And of the Benjaminites, the kinsmen of Saul: three thousand — and until then most of them had kept their duty to the house of Saul.
And of the Ephraimites: twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valour, men of renown in their ancestral houses.
And of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who had been designated by name to come and make David king.
And of the Issacharites, men who understood the times, to know what Israel should do: their chiefs were two hundred, and all their kinsmen were under their command.
Of Zebulun, those going out to the army, drawn up for battle with every weapon of war: fifty thousand, and to help with an undivided heart.
And of Naphtali: a thousand commanders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.
And of the Danites, drawn up for battle: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
And of Asher, those going out to the army, to draw up for battle: forty thousand.
And from beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, with every weapon of the army of war: one hundred and twenty thousand.
All these were men of war, drawn up in the battle line. They came to Hebron with a whole heart to make David king over all Israel, and all the rest of Israel too were of one heart to make David king.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, because their kinsmen had made provision for them.

And those near them too, as far as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali, were bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen — provisions of flour, fig cakes and clusters of raisins, wine and oil, and oxen and sheep in abundance. There was joy in Israel.

1 chronicles_13.t: David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

And David said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you, and it's from the LORD our God, let's send far and wide to our kinsmen who are left in all the lands of Israel, and with them to the priests and Levites in the cities with their pasture lands, so they can gather to us."
"And let's bring the ark of our God back to us, because we didn't seek it in the days of Saul."
And the whole assembly agreed to do it, because it seemed right to all the people.
So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt as far as Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
And David and all Israel went up to Baalah, to Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD who sits enthroned on the cherubim, where his name is invoked.
They carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, with Uzzah and Ahio leading the cart.
And David and all Israel were celebrating before God with everything they had, with songs, lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets.
They came as far as the threshing floor of Kidon, and Uzzah reached out his hand to take hold of the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.
And the LORD's anger burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had stretched out his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.
David was angry that the LORD had broken out in anger against Uzzah, and he called that place Perez-uzzah, to this day.
And David feared God that day, and he said, "How can I bring the ark of God to me?"
So David didn't bring the ark to himself, to the city of David; he turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of God stayed with Obed-edom's household, in his house, three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-edom's household and everything he had.

1 chronicles_14.t: Huram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar wood and masons and carpenters, to build him a house.
So David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, because his kingdom was raised high for the sake of his people Israel.
And David took more wives in Jerusalem, and he fathered more sons and daughters.
And these are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon,
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to look for David; and David heard of it and went out to face them.
The Philistines had come and raided in the valley of Rephaim.
And David enquired of God: "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?" And the LORD said to him, "Go up, and I'll give them into your hand."

So they went up at Baal-perazim, and David struck them down there. And David said, "God has burst out against my enemies by my hand, like water bursting through." That is why they called that place Baal-perazim.
They abandoned their gods there; and David gave the word, and they were burned with fire.
The Philistines did it again, and raided in the valley.
So David enquired of God again, and God said to him, "Don't go up after them; circle round away from them and come at them opposite the balsam trees."
"And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, because God has gone out ahead of you to strike down the camp of the Philistines."
And David did what God had commanded him, and they struck down the camp of the Philistines from Gibeon as far as Gezer.
And David's fame went out into all the lands, and the LORD put the dread of him on all the nations.

1 chronicles_15.t: He made houses for himself in the city of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one is to carry the ark of God but the Levites, because the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him for ever."
And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.
And David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
of the descendants of Kohath, Uriel the leader and his kinsmen — one hundred and twenty;
of the descendants of Merari, Asaiah the leader and his kinsmen — two hundred and twenty;
of the descendants of Gershom, Joel the leader and his kinsmen — one hundred and thirty;
of the descendants of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the leader and his kinsmen — two hundred;
of the descendants of Hebron, Eliel the leader and his kinsmen — eighty;
of the descendants of Uzziel, Amminadab the leader and his kinsmen — one hundred and twelve.
And David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites: Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel and Amminadab.

And he said to them, "You are the chiefs of the ancestral houses of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your kinsmen, and bring up the ark of the LORD the God of Israel to the place I've prepared for it."
"Because you weren't there the first time, the LORD our God burst out against us; we didn't seek him according to the ordinance."
So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD the God of Israel.
And the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles on them, just as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD.
And David told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their kinsmen the singers, with instruments of song — harps, lyres and cymbals — sounding aloud, raising the voice for joy.
And the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; and of his kinsmen, Asaph son of Berekiah; and of the Merarites, their kinsmen, Ethan son of Kushaiah.

And with them their kinsmen of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and Obed-edom and Jeiel the gatekeepers.
And the singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan were to sound aloud with bronze cymbals;
and Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah and Benaiah, with harps set to alamoth;
and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel and Azaziah, with lyres set to the sheminith, to lead.
And Kenaniah, leader of the Levites in music, was in charge of the music, because he was skilled at it.
And Berekiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
And Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah and Eliezer, the priests, were blowing trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers for the ark.
So David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands were the ones who went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom with joy.
And because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
And David was wrapped in a robe of fine linen, and so were all the Levites who carried the ark, and the singers, and Kenaniah the leader of the music of the singers; and David wore a linen ephod.
So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with a shout and with the sound of a horn, with trumpets and cymbals, sounding aloud with harps and lyres.

And as the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David dancing and celebrating; and she despised him in her heart.

1 chronicles_16.t: So they brought the ark of God in and set it inside the tent David had pitched for it, and they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David had finished offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
And he gave to every person of Israel, men and women alike, a round loaf of bread, a portion of meat and a raisin-cake.
And he appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to bring to remembrance, to give thanks and to praise the LORD the God of Israel:

Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah; then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom and Jeiel, with instruments — harps and lyres; and Asaph sounded aloud with the cymbals;
and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests, with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
On that day David first put the giving of thanks to the LORD into the hands of Asaph and his kinsmen:
Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name, let the peoples know what he has done.
Sing to him, make music to him, talk of all his wonders.
Boast in his holy name; let the heart of those who seek the LORD be glad.
Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face continually.
Remember the wonders he has done, his portents and the judgements he has spoken,
offspring of Israel his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the LORD our God; his judgements are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant for ever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
which he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac,
and he made it stand for Jacob as a statute, for Israel as a covenant for ever,
saying, "To you I'll give the land of Canaan, the portion that is your inheritance;"
when you were few in number, very few, and sojourners in it.
They wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one oppress them, and he rebuked kings because of them:
"Don't touch my anointed ones, and don't harm my prophets."
Sing to the LORD, all the earth; announce his salvation day after day.
Tell of his glory among the nations, of his wonders among all the peoples.
For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised, and he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendour and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his place.
Give to the LORD, clans of the peoples, give to the LORD glory and strength.
Give to the LORD the glory of his name; bring an offering and come before him; bow down to the LORD in holy adornment.
Tremble before him, all the earth; yes, the world stands firm, it will not be shaken.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad, and let them say among the nations, "The LORD is king!"
Let the sea thunder and all that fills it; let the field be full of joy, and everything in it.
Then the trees of the forest will sing out for joy before the LORD, because he is coming to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his steadfast love is for ever.
And say, "Save us, God of our salvation; gather us and rescue us from the nations, so we can give thanks to your holy name and boast in your praise."
Blessed be the LORD the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. And all the people said, "Amen!" And they praised the LORD.
And he left Asaph and his kinsmen there, before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to minister before the ark continually, as each day's duty required;
and Obed-edom and their kinsmen, sixty-eight; and Obed-edom son of Jedithun, and Hosah, as gatekeepers;
and Zadok the priest and his kinsmen the priests, before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place that was in Gibeon,
to offer up burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, and according to everything written in the law of the LORD, which he commanded Israel.
And with them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen, who were named one by one, to give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love is for ever;
and with them Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for those who sound aloud, and the instruments for the song of God; and the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.
Then all the people went off, each to his own house; and David turned back to bless his household.

1 chronicles_17.t: When David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Here I am living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under tent curtains."
And Nathan said to David, "Do whatever is in your heart, because God is with you."
That night the word of God came to Nathan:
"Go and say to David my servant: This is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build me the house to dwell in."
"I haven't lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until today. I've gone from tent to tent, from one tabernacle to another."
"Wherever I went about among all Israel, did I ever say a word to one of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, 'Why haven't you built me a house of cedar?'"
"And now, this is what you shall say to my servant David: This is what the LORD of hosts says: I myself took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be leader over my people Israel."
"And I was with you wherever you went, and I cut off all your enemies in front of you; and I'll make your name like the name of the great ones of the earth."

"And I'll establish a place for my people Israel, and I'll plant them, and they'll live in their own place and be disturbed no more; and the sons of injustice will not wear them down again, as they did at the first,"
"and from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I'll subdue all your enemies. And I tell you: the LORD will build you a house."
"And when your days are over and you go to be with your fathers, I'll raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I'll establish his kingdom."
"He'll build me a house, and I'll establish his throne for ever."
"I'll be a father to him, and he'll be a son to me; and I won't take my steadfast love away from him, the way I took it from the one who was before you."
"And I'll set him over my house and my kingdom for ever, and his throne will be established for ever."
So Nathan told David all these words and all this vision.
Then King David came and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you've brought me this far?"
"And this was a small thing in your eyes, God, and you've spoken concerning the house of your servant for a time far off; and you've looked on me as on a man of high rank, LORD God."
"What more can David say to you for the honour of your servant? You yourself know your servant."
"LORD, for the sake of your servant, and following your own heart, you've done all this greatness, making all these great things known."
"LORD, there's none like you, and there's no God besides you, in all that we've heard with our ears."

"And who is like your people Israel, one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, to make yourself a name of great and awesome deeds, by driving out nations from before your people whom you redeemed from Egypt?"
"You made your people Israel your own people for ever, and you, LORD, became their God."
"And now, LORD, let the word you've spoken concerning your servant and his house stand for ever, and do as you've spoken."

"And let it stand, and let your name be great for ever, so that it is said, 'The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, God to Israel'; and let the house of David your servant be established before you."
"For you, my God, have let your servant know that you'll build him a house; that is why your servant has found the courage to pray before you."
"And now, LORD, you are God, and you've spoken this good thing concerning your servant."
"And now you've been pleased to bless the house of your servant, so that it may continue for ever before you; for you, LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed for ever."

1 chronicles_18.t: After this David struck the Philistines down and subdued them, and he took Gath and its daughter-villages out of the hand of the Philistines.
He struck Moab down, and the Moabites became David's subjects, bearers of tribute.
And David struck down Hadadezer king of Zobah, towards Hamath, when he went to set up his monument at the river Euphrates.
David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but he left a hundred chariots' worth.
When Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men of Aram.
Then David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became David's subjects, bearers of tribute. And the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
And David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's servants carried, and brought them to Jerusalem.
And from Tibhath and from Kun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze; Solomon used it to make the bronze sea, the pillars and the bronze articles.
When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck down the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

he sent Hadoram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and beaten him — Hadadezer had been at war with Tou — and he sent all kinds of articles of gold, silver and bronze.
King David consecrated these to the LORD as well, along with the silver and the gold he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the people of Ammon, the Philistines and Amalek.
Abshai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's subjects; and the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
So David reigned over all Israel, and he did justice and righteousness for all his people.
And Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
and Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; and Shavsha was scribe;
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were the chief officials at the king's side.

1 chronicles_19.t: After this Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.

And David said, "I'll show loyalty to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed loyalty to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And David's servants came into the land of the Ammonites, to Hanun, to comfort him.

And the officials of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honouring your father, sending you comforters? Haven't his servants come to you to explore and overthrow and spy out the land?"
So Hanun took David's servants and shaved them, and he cut their robes off at the middle, up to the buttocks, and sent them away.
And they went and told David about the men, and he sent to meet them, because the men were deeply humiliated. And the king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards grow back, and then come back."
When the Ammonites saw that they'd made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariotry and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah and Zobah.

They hired thirty-two thousand chariots for themselves, and the king of Maacah with his people; and they came and camped in front of Medeba. And the Ammonites gathered from their cities and came for battle.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and the whole army, the mighty men.
The Ammonites went out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the city, and the kings who had come were by themselves out in the open country.
When Joab saw that the battle faced him front and rear, he chose from all the choice men in Israel and drew up to meet Aram.
And the rest of the people he put under the command of his brother Abshai, and they drew up to meet the Ammonites.
And he said, "If Aram is too strong for me, then you'll come to my rescue; and if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I'll rescue you."
"Be strong! Let's show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and the LORD will do what is good in his eyes."
So Joab and the people who were with him drew near for battle in front of Aram, and the Arameans ran from him.
And when the Ammonites saw that Aram had fled, they too ran from Abshai his brother and went into the city. And Joab came to Jerusalem.
When Aram saw that they'd been defeated before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.
David was told, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan; he came to them and drew up against them. And David drew up for battle to meet Aram, and they fought with him.
And Aram ran from Israel, and David killed seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers of Aram; and he put Shophach the commander of the army to death.
And when the servants of Hadadezer saw that they'd been defeated before Israel, they made peace with David and served him; and Aram was no longer willing to help the Ammonites.

1 chronicles_20.t: At the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out to war, Joab led the army out and devastated the land of the Ammonites. He came and besieged Rabbah, while David stayed in Jerusalem. And Joab struck Rabbah and overthrew it.

And David took the crown of their king off his head and found that it weighed a talent of gold, with a precious stone in it; and it was placed on David's head. And he brought a great quantity of plunder out of the city.

And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to work with the saw and with iron picks and with axes; and that is what David did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the people went back to Jerusalem.
After this a battle broke out at Gezer with the Philistines; that was when Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaites, and they were subdued.
There was another battle with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
And there was another battle at Gath; and there was a man of great stature, whose fingers and toes were six and six, twenty-four in all; and he too was descended from the Rapha.
He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down.
These were descended from the Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hand of David and at the hand of his servants.

1 chronicles_21.t: Satan stood up against Israel, and he stirred David up to count Israel.
And David said to Joab and to the leaders of the people, "Go and count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me the number, so I can know it."

And Joab said, "May the LORD add to his people a hundred times as many as they are! Aren't they all my lord's subjects, my lord the king? Why does my lord want this? Why should it bring guilt on Israel?"
But the king's word won out over Joab, so Joab went out and travelled through all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the number of the muster of the people: all Israel was one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
But he didn't enrol Levi and Benjamin among them, because the king's word was abhorrent to Joab.
And God was displeased with this thing, and he struck Israel.
And David said to God, "I've sinned greatly in doing this thing. Now take away the guilt of your servant, because I've acted very foolishly."
Then the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer:
"Go and speak to David: This is what the LORD says: Three things I hold out over you; choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you."
And Gad came to David and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Take your choice —"

"either three years of famine; or three months of being swept away before your foes, with your enemies' sword overtaking you; or three days of the sword of the LORD, with pestilence in the land and the angel of the LORD destroying throughout all the territory of Israel. Now decide what word I should take back to the one who sent me."
And David said to Gad, "I'm in great distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, because his compassion is very great; but don't let me fall into human hands."
So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it; and as he was destroying, the LORD saw and relented over the calamity, and he said to the destroying angel, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." And the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

And David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with his drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem; and David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, fell on their faces.

And David said to God, "Wasn't it I who ordered the people to be counted? I'm the one who has sinned and done great evil; but these, the sheep — what have they done? LORD my God, let your hand be against me and against my father's house, but not against your people, for a plague."
And the angel of the LORD told Gad to say to David that David should go up and set up an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up at the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
And Ornan turned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid; and Ornan was threshing wheat.
And David came to Ornan, and Ornan looked up and saw David, and he went out from the threshing floor and bowed down to David with his face to the ground.

And David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of the threshing floor, so I can build an altar to the LORD on it — give it to me for the full price in silver — so the plague may be held back from the people."

And Ornan said to David, "Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good in his eyes. Look, I'm giving the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering — I'm giving it all."
And King David said to Ornan, "No — I'll certainly buy it for the full price in silver. I won't take what is yours for the LORD, or offer up a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.

And David built an altar to the LORD there, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings; and he called out to the LORD, and he answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
Then the LORD spoke to the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
That was when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, and he sacrificed there.
Now the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
But David couldn't go before it to seek God, because he was terrified of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

1 chronicles_22.t: So David said, "This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."
And David gave orders to gather the sojourners who were in the land of Israel, and he put stonecutters to work cutting dressed stones to build the house of God.
And David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and bronze in abundance, more than could be weighed;
and cedar wood beyond counting — because the Sidonians and the Tyrians had brought cedar wood in abundance to David.

And David said, "Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD is to be made exceedingly great, for a name and for splendour throughout all the lands. Let me prepare for it." So David prepared in abundance before he died.
Then he called for Solomon his son and commanded him to build a house for the LORD the God of Israel.
And David said to Solomon, "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God."
"But the word of the LORD came to me: 'You've shed blood in abundance and made great wars. You will not build a house for my name, because you've shed much blood on the ground before me.'"

"'Look, a son will be born to you. He'll be a man of rest, and I'll give him rest from all his enemies round about; Solomon will be his name, and I'll give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.'"
"'He'll build a house for my name, and he'll be a son to me and I a father to him; and I'll establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.'"
"Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, and may you succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he said concerning you."
"Only may the LORD give you insight and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel, so that you keep the law of the LORD your God."

"Then you'll succeed, if you take care to carry out the statutes and the judgements that the LORD commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and be courageous; don't be afraid, and don't be dismayed."

"And look — with great effort I've prepared for the house of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, because there is so much of it; and I've prepared wood and stone, and you'll add to them."
"And you have workers with you in abundance: stonecutters, craftsmen in stone and wood, and every kind of skilled man for every kind of work."
"Of gold, silver, bronze and iron there's no counting. Get up and act, and may the LORD be with you."
And David ordered all the officials of Israel to help Solomon his son:

"Isn't the LORD your God with you? Hasn't he given you rest on every side? For he has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and before his people."

"Now set your heart and your being to seek the LORD your God; and get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the house that will be built for the name of the LORD."

1 chronicles_23.t: David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
He gathered all the officials of Israel and the priests and the Levites.
The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward, and their number, head by head, of grown men, was thirty-eight thousand.
Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD; six thousand were officers and judges;
four thousand were gatekeepers; and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments that I made for praising.
And David split them into divisions, following the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, and Zetham and Joel — three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomith and Haziel and Haran — three. These were the heads of the ancestral houses of Ladan.
And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, and Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei — four.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; and Jeush and Beriah didn't have many sons, so they were counted as one ancestral house, one muster.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel — four.
