The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart, to be consecrated as most holy, he and his sons for ever — to burn incense as smoke before the LORD, to serve him and to bless in his name for ever.
And as for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted with the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
And the sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's sons were exceedingly numerous.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their kinsmen, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jeremoth — three.

These were the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses, the heads of the ancestral houses as they were enrolled, listed by name, head by head, doing the work of the service of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
For David had said, "The LORD the God of Israel has given rest to his people, and he's taken up his dwelling in Jerusalem for ever."
And so the Levites don't need to carry the tabernacle any more, or any of the articles for its service.
For by the last words of David, these were the number of the sons of Levi from twenty years old and upward.

For their duty was to be at the side of the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house of the LORD, over the courts and over the store-rooms and over the cleansing of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God;

and for the bread of the row, and for the fine flour for a grain offering, and for the wafers of unleavened bread, and for what is baked on the griddle, and for the well-mixed dough, and for every measure of volume and length.
And to stand every morning to give thanks and praise the LORD, and the same in the evening;

and for every offering up of burnt offerings to the LORD on the sabbaths, at the new moons and at the appointed times, in the required number, according to the ordinance laid on them, continually before the LORD.
And they kept the charge of the tent of meeting and the charge of the holy place and the charge of the sons of Aaron their kinsmen, for the service of the house of the LORD.

1 chronicles_24.t: And for the sons of Aaron, their divisions. The sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
And David divided them up, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, according to their appointed order of service.

And the sons of Eleazar turned out to have more chief men than the sons of Ithamar, so this is how they divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen heads of ancestral houses; and for the sons of Ithamar, eight by their ancestral houses.
And they divided them by lot, one group alongside the other, because there were officials of the holy place and officials of God among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.

And Shemaiah son of Nethanel the scribe, one of the Levites, wrote them down in front of the king and the officials and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and of the Levites — one ancestral house drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.
And the first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malkijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jakin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

These were their appointed orders of service, to come into the house of the LORD according to the ordinance given them, by the hand of Aaron their ancestor, just as the LORD the God of Israel had commanded him.
And for the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites: Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
And the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno; and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, and he had no sons.
Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
And the sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites by their ancestral houses.

And they too cast lots, just as their kinsmen the sons of Aaron did, in front of David the king and Zadok and Ahimelech and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and of the Levites — the chief ancestral house treated no differently from the youngest brother's.

1 chronicles_25.t: And David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals. And this is how many men did this work in their service:
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.

Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun — Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, in giving thanks and praising the LORD.
Of Heman: the sons of Heman — Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman the king's seer, in the words of God, to lift up a horn. And God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the direction of their father in the song of the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps and lyres, for the service of the house of God — under the direction of the king: Asaph and Jeduthun and Heman.
And their number, along with their kinsmen trained in song to the LORD, all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
And they cast lots for their duties, one alongside another, the small as well as the great, the trained alongside the pupil.
And the first lot fell for Asaph, to Joseph; the second, Gedaliah: he and his brothers and sons, twelve;
The third, Zaccur: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fourth, to Izri: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The fifth, Nethaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The sixth, Bukkiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The seventh, Jesharelah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eighth, Jeshaiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The ninth, Mattaniah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The tenth, Shimei: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The eleventh, Azarel: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
The twelfth, to Hashabiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the thirteenth, Shubael: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fourteenth, Mattithiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the fifteenth, to Jeremoth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the sixteenth, to Hananiah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the seventeenth, to Joshbekashah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the eighteenth, to Hanani: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the nineteenth, to Mallothi: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twentieth, to Eliathah: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-first, to Hothir: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-second, to Giddalti: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-third, to Mahazioth: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.
For the twenty-fourth, to Romamti-ezer: his sons and his kinsmen, twelve.

1 chronicles_26.t: For the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
And Obed-edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third and Sakar the fourth, and Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth — for God had blessed him.
And sons were born to Shemaiah his son, and they ruled over their ancestral house, because they were mighty men of ability.
The sons of Shemaiah: Othni and Rephael and Obed, Elzabad; his kinsmen were men of ability, Elihu and Semakiah.
All these were of the sons of Obed-edom — they and their sons and their kinsmen, men of ability with the strength for the service — sixty-two of them belonging to Obed-edom.
And Meshelemiah had sons and kinsmen, men of ability — eighteen.
And Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief — he wasn't the firstborn, but his father made him chief —
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and kinsmen of Hosah were thirteen.
These had the divisions of the gatekeepers, under their chief men, with duties matching those of their kinsmen, to serve in the house of the LORD.
And they cast lots, the small as well as the great, by their ancestral houses, gate by gate.
And the lot for the east fell to Shelemiah; and for Zechariah his son, a counsellor with insight, they cast lots, and his lot came out for the north.
To Obed-edom, the south; and to his sons, the storehouse.
To Shuppim and to Hosah, the west, beside the gate of Shalleketh on the ascending highway — guard post alongside guard post.
On the east, six Levites; on the north, four each day; on the south, four each day; and at the storehouse, two at a time.
At the Parbar on the west: four at the highway, two at the Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers, of the sons of the Korahites and of the sons of Merari.
And of the Levites: Ahijah was over the storehouses of the house of God and over the storehouses of the holy things.
The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the ancestral houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brother, who were over the storehouses of the house of the LORD.
Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
And Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was leader over the storehouses.
And his kinsmen, through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zikri his son, and Shelomith his son.

That Shelomoth and his kinsmen were over all the storehouses of the holy things that King David had consecrated, and that the heads of the ancestral houses, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army had consecrated.
They had consecrated it from the wars and from the plunder, to keep the house of the LORD in repair.

And everything that Samuel the seer had consecrated, and Saul son of Kish, and Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah — everything anyone consecrated was under the hand of Shelomith and his kinsmen.
Of the Izharites: Kenaniah and his sons were assigned to the work outside, over Israel, as officers and as judges.

Of the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his kinsmen, men of ability, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel on the western side of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

Of the Hebronites: Jeriah was the chief of the Hebronites, by his generations, by ancestral houses. In the fortieth year of David's reign they were searched out, and mighty men of ability were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.

And his kinsmen, men of ability, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of ancestral houses; and King David put them over the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter of God and every matter of the king.

1 chronicles_27.t: And the people of Israel by their number: the heads of the ancestral houses and the commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers who served the king, in every matter of the divisions that came on duty and went off month by month, through all the months of the year — each division numbering twenty-four thousand.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
He was of the sons of Perez, the chief of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.
And over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, with his division; and Mikloth was the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The commander of the third army, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
This was the Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty; and in his division was Ammizabad his son.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the leader Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the house of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
And over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer son of Zikri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
for the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
for the half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the commanders of the tribes of Israel.
And David didn't take the number of those twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would make Israel as many as the stars of the heavens.
Joab son of Zeruiah started to count and didn't finish, and because of this wrath came on Israel; and the number was never entered in the account of the days of King David.
And over the king's storehouses was Azmaveth son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the open country, in the cities and in the villages and in the towers, was Jonathan son of Uzziah.
And over those doing the work of the field, for the labour of the ground, was Ezri son of Kelub.
And over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over the produce of the vineyards for the wine stores was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
And over the olive trees and the sycamore figs that were in the Shephelah was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the stores of oil was Joash.
And over the cattle grazing in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the valleys was Shaphat son of Adlai.
And over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the she-asses was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
And over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials over the property that belonged to King David.
And Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counsellor; he was a man of understanding and a scribe. And Jehiel son of Hacmoni attended the king's sons.
And Ahithophel was a counsellor to the king; and Hushai the Arkite was the king's friend.
And after Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. And the commander of the king's army was Joab.

1 chronicles_28.t: And David gathered all the officials of Israel at Jerusalem: the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions who served the king, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the officials over all the property and livestock of the king and of his sons, along with the court officials and the mighty men and every mighty man of ability.

And King David got to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and for the footstool of our God's feet, and I got ready to build."
"But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for my name, because you're a man of war and you've shed blood.'"

"And the LORD the God of Israel chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel for ever. He chose Judah as leader, and within the house of Judah, my father's house; and among my father's sons he took pleasure in me, to make me king over all Israel."
"And out of all my sons — the LORD has given me many sons — he chose Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel."
"And he said to me, 'Solomon your son — he's the one who will build my house and my courts, because I've chosen him to be a son to me, and I'll be a father to him.'"
"'And I'll establish his kingdom for ever, if he holds firm to carry out my commandments and my judgements, as he does today.'"

"And now, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you can possess the good land and leave it to your sons after you as an inheritance for ever."

"And you, Solomon my son — know the God of your father, and serve him with a whole heart and a willing being; because the LORD searches every heart and understands every inclination of the thoughts. If you seek him, he'll let himself be found by you; and if you forsake him, he'll reject you for ever."
"See now — the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and act."
Then David gave Solomon his son the plan of the porch and of its buildings and its treasuries and its upper rooms and its inner rooms, and the house of the mercy seat;

and the plan of all that he had in mind by the spirit, for the courts of the house of the LORD and for all the surrounding rooms, for the storehouses of the house of God and for the storehouses of the holy things;
and for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of the service of the house of the LORD;
for the gold, by weight of gold, for the articles of each and every service; for all the silver articles, by weight, for the articles of each and every service;

and the weight for the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, by the weight of each and every lampstand and its lamps; and for the silver lampstands, by weight for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the service of each and every lampstand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of the row, for each and every table; and silver for the silver tables;
and the forks and the basins and the jugs, of pure gold; and for the gold bowls, by weight for each and every bowl; and for the silver bowls, by weight for each and every bowl;
and for the altar of incense, purged gold by weight; and for the plan of the chariot, the gold cherubim, spreading their wings and covering the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
"All this," David said, "is in writing from the hand of the LORD upon me; he gave me understanding of all the works of the plan."

And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and be courageous, and act. Don't be afraid and don't be dismayed, because the LORD God, my God, is with you. He won't abandon you and he won't forsake you, until all the work of the service of the house of the LORD is finished."

"And here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the service of the house of God. And with you in every task is every willing man skilled in every kind of service; and the officials and all the people are at your command."

1 chronicles_29.t: And King David said to the whole assembly, "Solomon my son, the one God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great; because the citadel is not for a man but for the LORD God."

"And with all my strength I've prepared for the house of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron and wood for the wood; onyx stones and stones for setting, stones of antimony and of variegated work, and every precious stone, and alabaster in abundance."

"And what's more, because I take pleasure in the house of my God, I have a treasure of gold and silver of my own; I'm giving it to the house of my God, on top of everything I've prepared for the holy house:"
"three thousand talents of gold, gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of purged silver, to overlay the walls of the buildings;"
"gold for the gold work and silver for the silver, and for all the work done by the hand of craftsmen. So who's willing to consecrate himself today to the LORD?"
Then the leaders of the ancestral houses and the leaders of the tribes of Israel and the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the officials over the king's work, gave willingly;

and for the service of the house of God they gave five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand darics, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
And anyone who had stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
And the people were glad at their willing giving, because with a whole heart they had given willingly to the LORD; and King David rejoiced too, with great joy.
And David blessed the LORD before the eyes of all the assembly, and he said, "Blessed are you, LORD, God of Israel our father, from everlasting to everlasting."

"Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the might and the splendour and the endurance and the majesty; everything in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and you are the one who lifts himself as head above all."
"And wealth and honour come from before you, and you rule over all; and strength and might are in your hand, and it lies in your hand to make great and to give strength to all."
"And now, our God, we thank you and praise your splendid name."
"And who am I, and who are my people, that we should have the strength to give willingly like this? For everything comes from you, and out of your own hand we've given to you."
"We're sojourners before you, and resident aliens, as all our ancestors were; our days on the earth are like a shadow, and there's no hope."
"LORD our God, all this abundance we've prepared to build you a house for your holy name — it's from your hand, and all of it is yours."

"And I know, my God, that you test the heart and take pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I've given all these things willingly; and now I've seen with joy that your people who are here give willingly to you."
"LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our ancestors, keep this for ever as the inclination of the thoughts of your people's heart, and turn their heart towards you."
"And give Solomon my son a whole heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies and your statutes, and to carry it all out, and to build the citadel I have made preparation for."
And David said to the whole assembly, "Bless the LORD your God." And the whole assembly blessed the LORD the God of their ancestors; and they bowed low and bowed down to the LORD and to the king.

And the next day they sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD and offered up burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
And they ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. And they made Solomon son of David king a second time, and they anointed him to the LORD as leader, and Zadok as priest.
So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father, and he succeeded; and all Israel listened to him.
And all the officials and the mighty men, and King David's sons as well, pledged themselves under Solomon the king.
And the LORD made Solomon exceedingly great before the eyes of all Israel, and he put on him a royal majesty such as no king before him over Israel had had.
So David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
And the days he reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, wealth and honour; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
And the matters of King David, the former and the latter, are written in the words of Samuel the seer and in the words of Nathan the prophet and in the words of Gad the seer,
together with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him and over Israel and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

1 kings_1.t: King David was old now, well on in years. They covered him with clothes, but he couldn't get warm.

So his servants said to him, 'Have them look for a young woman for my lord the king, a virgin. Let her wait on the king and be his nurse, and let her lie in your bosom, so my lord the king can get warm.'
So they searched all over the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
The young woman was extremely beautiful. She became the king's nurse and waited on him, but the king didn't know her.
Now Adonijah son of Haggith was putting himself forward. 'I'm going to be king,' he said. And he got himself a chariot and horsemen, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
His father had never rebuked him in all his life, never said, 'Why have you done this?' He was very good-looking too, and he was born after Absalom.
He talked it over with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they backed Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei and Rei, and David's mighty men — they weren't with Adonijah.
Adonijah sacrificed sheep and cattle and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth, next to En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother — he didn't invite them.
Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, 'Haven't you heard? Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David doesn't know it.'
'So come now, let me give you some advice. Save your own life, and the life of your son Solomon.'

'Go in to King David and say to him, "My lord the king, didn't you swear to your maidservant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me and he will sit on my throne? So why has Adonijah become king?"'
'And while you're still in there talking with the king, I'll come in right behind you and back up what you say.'
So Bathsheba went in to the king, into the inner room. The king was very old by now, and Abishag the Shunammite was waiting on him.
Bathsheba bowed low and bowed down to the king. 'What do you want?' the king said.
'My lord,' she said, 'you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God, "Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne."'
'And now look — Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, don't know it.'
'He's sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and invited all the king's sons, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army — but Solomon your servant he hasn't invited.'
'And you, my lord the king — the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.'
'Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted sinners.'
She was still speaking with the king when Nathan the prophet came in.
They told the king, 'Nathan the prophet is here.' He came in before the king and bowed down with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, 'My lord the king, did you say, "Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne"?'

'Because today he's gone down and sacrificed oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and invited all the king's sons, and the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And there they are, eating and drinking in front of him and saying, "Long live King Adonijah!"'
'But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant — he hasn't invited.'
'If this has come from my lord the king, then you haven't let your servant know who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.'
King David answered, 'Call Bathsheba in for me.' And she came in before the king and stood before him.
The king swore an oath. 'As the LORD lives, who has ransomed my life from every trouble —'
'just as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, "Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place" — that is exactly what I'll do today.'
Bathsheba bowed low with her face to the ground and bowed down to the king. 'May my lord King David live for ever!' she said.
King David said, 'Call in Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.' And they came in before the king.
The king said to them, 'Take your lord's servants with you, put Solomon my son on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.'
'There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Then blow the ram's horn and say, "Long live King Solomon!"'
'Then come up after him, and he is to come in and sit on my throne. He'll reign in my place — I've appointed him ruler over Israel and over Judah.'
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, 'Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.'
'As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.'
So Zadok the priest went down, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites. They set Solomon on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the ram's horn, and all the people said, 'Long live King Solomon!'
And all the people came up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy, till the ground was split open by the noise of them.
Adonijah heard it, and so did all his guests — they'd just finished eating. And when Joab heard the sound of the ram's horn he said, 'Why is the town in an uproar?'
He was still speaking when Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came in. Adonijah said, 'Come in — you're a man of worth, and you bring good news.'
Jonathan answered Adonijah. 'Indeed — our lord King David has made Solomon king.'
'The king sent Zadok the priest with him, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and they've set him on the king's mule.'
'Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they've come up from there rejoicing, and the town's in an uproar. That's the noise you heard.'
'Solomon has taken his seat on the throne of the kingship as well.'

'And the king's servants have come in to bless our lord King David. They said, "May God make Solomon's name better than your name, and his throne greater than your throne." And the king bowed down on his bed.'
'And this is what the king said: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has given someone to sit on my throne this day, with my own eyes seeing it."'
Then all of Adonijah's guests trembled. They got up and went, each his own way.
And Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

Solomon was told, 'Look, Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He's taken hold of the horns of the altar and he's saying, "Let King Solomon swear to me today that he won't put his servant to death by the sword."'
Solomon said, 'If he shows himself a man of worth, not a hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he dies.'
So King Solomon sent and they brought him down from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, 'Go home.'

1 kings_2.t: David's time to die was coming near, and he gave Solomon his son his orders:
'I'm going the way of all the earth. Be strong. Be a man.'

'Keep the charge of the LORD your God: walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commandments, his judgements and his testimonies, as it's written in the law of Moses, so that you'll do well in all you do and wherever you turn;'

'and so that the LORD may make good the word he spoke about me: "If your sons keep to their way, walking before me in faithfulness with all their heart and all their soul, you'll never lack a man on the throne of Israel."'

'And you know yourself what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them. He shed the blood of war in a time of peace, and he put the blood of war on the belt at his waist and the sandals on his feet.'
'Act with the wisdom you have, and don't let his grey head go down to Sheol in peace.'
'But show loyalty to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite — let them be among those who eat at your table, because that's how they came to me when I fled from Absalom your brother.'

'And there with you is Shimei son of Gera the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a grievous curse the day I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, "I won't put you to death by the sword."'
'So now, don't leave him unpunished. You're a wise man — you'll know what to do to him. Bring his grey head down to Sheol in blood.'
Then David lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David.
David reigned over Israel for forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his reign was firmly established.
Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. 'Do you come in peace?' she said. 'In peace,' he said.
Then he said, 'I have something to say to you.' 'Go ahead,' she said.
'You know the kingship was mine,' he said, 'and that all Israel had their faces set on me to be king. But the kingship turned round and went to my brother, because it was his from the LORD.'
'And now I'm asking one petition of you — don't turn me down.' And she said to him, 'Go ahead.'
And he said, 'Ask King Solomon — he won't turn you down — to give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.'
'Good,' said Bathsheba. 'I'll speak to the king myself for you.'

So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him about Adonijah. The king got up to meet her and bowed down to her, and then sat down on his throne. He had a throne put there for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
'I'm asking one small petition of you,' she said. 'Don't turn me down.' And the king said to her, 'Ask, my mother — I won't turn you down.'
And she said, 'Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife.'

And King Solomon answered his mother, 'And why are you asking Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingship for him too — he's my brother, older than I am — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!'
And King Solomon swore by the LORD: 'May God do so to me, and more, if Adonijah hasn't spoken this word at the cost of his own life.'
'And now, as the LORD lives, who established me and set me on the throne of David my father and who made me a house just as he promised — Adonijah will be put to death today.'
So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he fell on him, and he died.

And to Abiathar the priest the king said, 'Go to Anathoth, to your own fields. You deserve to die, but I won't put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before David my father, and because you were afflicted in everything my father was afflicted in.'
So Solomon drove Abiathar out from being a priest to the LORD — fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken about the house of Eli at Shiloh.
The news reached Joab — for Joab had gone over to Adonijah, though he hadn't gone over to Absalom — and Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was there beside the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada: 'Go, fall on him.'

Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, 'This is what the king says: come out.' 'No,' he said. 'I'll die here.' So Benaiah brought word back to the king: 'This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.'
And the king said to him, 'Do just as he says. Fall on him and bury him, and clear away from me and from my father's house the blood Joab shed for no reason.'

'And the LORD will bring his blood back on his own head, because he fell on two men more righteous and better than he was and killed them with the sword — and my father David knew nothing about it: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army.'
'Their blood will come back on Joab's head and on the head of his offspring for ever. But for David and his offspring, for his house and his throne, there will be peace for ever from the LORD.'
So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and fell on him and put him to death, and they buried him at his own house in the wilderness.
And the king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and put Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.
Then the king sent for Shimei and said to him, 'Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Don't go out of it anywhere at all.'
'On the day you do go out and cross the wadi of Kidron, know for certain that you will certainly die. Your blood will be on your own head.'
And Shimei said to the king, 'The word is good. Whatever my lord the king has said, that's what your servant will do.' And Shimei lived in Jerusalem a long time.
But at the end of three years, two of Shimei's servants ran off to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, 'Look, your servants are in Gath.'
So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to look for his servants. He went and brought his servants back from Gath.
And Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and come back.

So the king sent for Shimei and said, 'Didn't I make you swear by the LORD and warn you: "On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, know for certain that you will certainly die"? And you said to me, "The word is good. I have heard."'
'So why haven't you kept the oath of the LORD and the command I gave you?'
And the king said to Shimei, 'You know all the evil your own heart knows, all you did to David my father. The LORD will bring your evil back on your own head.'
'But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will be established before the LORD for ever.'
Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and fell on him, and he died. And the kingdom was firmly in Solomon's hand.

1 kings_3.t: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the city of David, until he'd finished building his own house, the house of the LORD, and the wall round Jerusalem.
Only, the people were sacrificing at the high places, because up to that time no house had been built for the name of the LORD.
And Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father — only, he kept sacrificing and making offerings smoke at the high places.
The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, because that was the great high place. Solomon offered up a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night, and God said, 'Ask what I should give you.'

And Solomon said, 'You showed great steadfast love to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness and righteousness and uprightness of heart with you. And you've kept this great steadfast love for him — you've given him a son sitting on his throne, as he is today.'
'And now, LORD my God, you've made your servant king in place of David my father, and I'm a young lad. I don't know how to go out or come in.'
'And your servant is here in the middle of your people, the people you chose — a numerous people, too many to be numbered or counted.'
'So give your servant a listening heart, to judge your people, to tell good from evil. Who is able to judge this massive people of yours?'
It was good in the Lord's eyes that Solomon had asked this.
And God said to him, 'Because you asked for this — you didn't ask for a long life for yourself, or for wealth, or for the life of your enemies, but you asked for understanding to hear a case —'
'look, I'm doing what you said. I'm giving you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and after you no one like you will arise.'
'And what you didn't ask for I'm giving you as well — both wealth and honour — so that there'll be no one like you among the kings, all your days.'
'And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, the way David your father walked, then I'll lengthen your days.'

Then Solomon woke up — and it had been a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, offered up burnt offerings and made peace offerings, and gave a feast for all his servants.
Then two women, prostitutes, came to the king and stood in front of him.
And the one woman said, 'Pardon me, my lord. This woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was there in the house.'
'Then on the third day after I gave birth, this woman gave birth too. We were together. There was no stranger with us in the house — just the two of us.'
'And in the night this woman's son died, because she'd lain on him.'
'So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant was asleep, and laid him in her bosom — and laid her dead son in my bosom.'
'When I got up in the morning to suckle my son, there he was, dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, he wasn't my son, the one I'd borne.'

And the other woman said, 'No — my son is the living one and your son is the dead one.' And this one kept saying, 'No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one.' That's how they talked in front of the king.
And the king said, 'This one says, "This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one," and that one says, "No — your son is the dead one and my son is the living one."'
And the king said, 'Bring me a sword.' So they brought the sword in before the king.
And the king said, 'Cut the living child in two, and give half to the one and half to the other.'

Then the woman whose son was the living one said to the king — because her compassion grew warm over her son — 'Pardon me, my lord. Give her the living child. Don't kill him, whatever you do.' But the other kept saying, 'He'll be neither mine nor yours — cut!'
And the king answered, 'Give her the living child. Don't kill him, whatever you do. She's his mother.'
And all Israel heard the judgement the king had judged, and they were in awe of him, because they saw the wisdom of God was inside him to do justice.

1 kings_4.t: And King Solomon was king over all Israel.
And these were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the recorder;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
Azariah son of Nathan over the overseers; Zabud son of Nathan, a priest, the king's friend;
Ahishar over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda over the forced labour.
Solomon had twelve overseers over all Israel, and they kept the king and his household supplied; each one had one month in the year to supply.
And these are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher;
Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor; Taphath the daughter of Solomon became his wife;
Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan, below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him belonged the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead, and the region of Argob in Bashan — sixty large cities with wall and bronze bar;
Ahinadab son of Iddo, at Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he too took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as a wife;
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and there was one overseer in the land.
Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea — eating and drinking and rejoicing.
Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, right up to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all his life.
Solomon's provision for a single day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of flour,
ten fat cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelle, roe-deer and fattened birds.
For he ruled over the whole region beyond the River, from Tiphsah all the way to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River — and he had peace on every side.
And Judah and Israel lived in security, everyone under his own vine and his own fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all Solomon's days.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariotry, and twelve thousand horsemen.
And those overseers kept King Solomon supplied, and everyone who came to King Solomon's table, each in his own month. They let nothing run short.
They also brought the barley and the straw for the horses and the steeds to wherever it was needed, each according to his measure.
And God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.
Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the east, and greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
He was wiser than anyone alive — than Ethan the Ezrahite, than Heman and Kalkol and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His name was known among all the nations round about.
He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five.
He talked about the trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop that comes out of the wall; and he talked about the animals and the birds and the creeping things and the fish.
And people came from every nation to hear Solomon's wisdom — sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard about his wisdom.

1 kings_5.t: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he'd heard they had anointed him king in place of his father; Hiram had always been a friend to David.
And Solomon sent word to Hiram:
'You know about David my father — that he couldn't build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars all round him, until the LORD put them under the soles of my feet.'
'And now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There's no opponent, and nothing bad happening.'

'So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD said to David my father: "Your son, whom I'll put on your throne in your place — he's the one who will build the house for my name."'

'So now, give the order for cedars to be cut for me from Lebanon. My servants will work alongside yours, and I'll pay you your servants' wages, whatever you say — because you know there's no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.'
When Hiram heard what Solomon said he was overjoyed, and he said, 'Blessed be the LORD this day, who has given David a wise son over this great people.'
And Hiram sent word to Solomon: 'I've heard what you sent me. I'll do everything you want about the cedar timber and the cypress timber.'

'My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I'll make them into rafts on the sea and float them to wherever you tell me. I'll break them up there, and you can carry them away. And you'll do what I want by supplying food for my household.'
So Hiram gave Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all he wanted.
And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pressed oil. That's what Solomon gave Hiram year by year.
And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he'd promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
And King Solomon raised forced labour out of all Israel; the forced labour was thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays: one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was over the forced labour.
Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stone-cutters in the hill country,
besides the chiefs of Solomon's overseers who were over the work — three thousand three hundred of them — who ruled over the people doing the work.
And the king gave the order, and they quarried large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.
And Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the Gebalites cut them to shape, and got the timber and the stones ready to build the house.

1 kings_6.t: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the coming out of the Israelites from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv — that is the second month — he built the house for the LORD.
The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty broad and thirty cubits high.
And the porch in front of the temple of the house was twenty cubits across, matching the breadth of the house, and ten cubits deep, in front of the house.
And he made windows for the house with recessed frames.
And he built an extension against the wall of the house all around — against the walls of the house, for the temple and for the innermost room; and he made side-chambers all around.

The lowest storey of the extension was five cubits broad, the middle six, and the third seven; for he made ledges around the outside of the house, so that the beams would not take hold in the walls of the house.
And the house, when it was built, was built of whole stone from the quarry; no hammer or axe or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
The entrance to the middle side-chamber was on the south side of the house; a stairway went up to the middle storey, and from the middle to the third.
So he built the house and finished it, and roofed it with beams and planks of cedar.
And he built the extension against the whole house, five cubits high, and fastened it to the house with cedar timber.
And the word of the LORD came to Solomon:

'As for this house you're building: if you walk in my statutes and observe my judgements and keep all my commandments, walking in them, then I'll make good with you the word I spoke to David your father;'
'and I'll dwell among the Israelites, and I won't abandon my people Israel.'
So Solomon built the house and finished it.

He lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling he overlaid them with wood on the inside, and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
And he built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor to the walls, and made it on the inside an innermost room, the holy of holies.
And the house — that is, the temple in front — was forty cubits.
The inside of the house was cedar — carved gourds and open flowers. The whole was cedar; no stone was visible.
And he prepared an innermost room inside the house, to put there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
The innermost room was twenty cubits long, twenty broad and twenty high; he overlaid it with refined gold, and overlaid the altar with cedar.
Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with refined gold, drew chains of gold across in front of the innermost room, and overlaid it with gold.
He overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished; and the whole altar belonging to the innermost room he overlaid with gold.
And in the innermost room he made two cherubim of olive wood, ten cubits high.
One wing of the cherub was five cubits and the other five cubits — ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
And the second cherub was ten cubits; the two cherubim had one measurement and one shape.
The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the second.

He put the cherubim in the middle of the inner house with their wings spread out: the wing of the one touched one wall, the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and their wings towards the middle of the house touched wing to wing.
And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
And on all the walls of the house round about he carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, both within and without.
And he overlaid the floor of the house with gold, both within and without.
And for the entrance of the innermost room he made doors of olive wood; the pillar and the doorposts were five-sided.
The two doors were of olive wood; on them he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, overlaid them with gold, and hammered the gold out over the cherubim and the palm trees.
And so also for the entrance of the temple he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.
And two doors of cypress wood: each door had two leaves that folded.
And he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, fitted smoothly over the carved work.
And he built the inner court with three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams.
In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — that is the eighth month — the house was complete in all its parts and according to all its specifications. He built it in seven years.

1 kings_7.t: And Solomon built his own house over thirteen years, and completed all of it.
He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: a hundred cubits long, fifty broad and thirty high, on four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
And it was panelled with cedar above, over the side-chambers that were on the pillars — forty-five of them, fifteen to a row.
And there were window frames in three rows, window opposite window, three times.
And all the openings and doorposts were square in their framework; and at the front, window opposite window, three times.
He made the Porch of the Pillars, fifty cubits long and thirty broad, with a porch in front of them, and pillars and a threshold in front of them.
And he made the Porch of the Throne, where he would give judgement — the Porch of Judgement — panelled with cedar from floor to floor.
His own house where he would live, in the other court, inward from the porch, was of the same workmanship. And he made a house like this porch for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon had taken.
All these were costly stones, cut to the measurements of dressed stone, sawn with the saw within and without — from the foundation to the coping, and from the outside as far as the great court.
The foundation was of costly stones, large stones — stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
And above were costly stones, cut to the measurements of dressed stone, and cedar.
The great court all around had three rows of dressed stone and a row of cedar beams — and so also the inner court of the house of the LORD, and the porch of the house.
And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, skill and knowledge to do any work in bronze; and he came to King Solomon and did all his work.
He cast the two pillars of bronze: the one pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits went round the second pillar.
And he made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars: the one capital was five cubits high, and the second capital five cubits.
There were networks, the work of a network, and festoons, the work of chains, for the capitals on the top of the pillars: seven for the one capital and seven for the second capital.
And he made the pillars, and two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates; and so he did for the second capital.
And the capitals on the top of the pillars were a work of lilies, in the porch: four cubits.
The capitals were on the two pillars, also above, close to the bulge beside the network; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around, on the second capital.
He set up the pillars at the porch of the temple: he set up the right-hand pillar and called its name Jakin, and he set up the left-hand pillar and called its name Boaz.
And on the top of the pillars was a work of lilies. So the work of the pillars was complete.
And he made the sea of cast metal: ten cubits from lip to lip, circular all around, five cubits high; and a measuring line of thirty cubits went round it.
And gourds were beneath its lip all around, encircling it — ten to a cubit — surrounding the sea; the gourds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was on top of them, and all their hindquarters were inward.
Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its lip was shaped like the lip of a cup, a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
And he made the ten stands of bronze: each stand was four cubits long, four cubits broad and three cubits high.
And this was the workmanship of the stand: they had rims, and there were rims between the crossbars.
On the rims between the crossbars were lions, oxen and cherubim; on the crossbars there was a base above; and beneath the lions and the oxen were garlands of hanging work.
Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles, and its four feet had supports. Beneath the washbasin were the cast supports, with garlands beside each one.
Its opening, from inside the capital and upward, was a cubit; the opening was round, the work of a base, a cubit and a half. On its opening also were carvings, and their rims were square, not round.
The four wheels were beneath the rims, and the axle-supports of the wheels were in the stand; each wheel was a cubit and a half high.
The wheels were made like a chariot wheel: their axle-supports, rims, spokes and hubs — all of it cast.
Four supports were at the four corners of each stand; the supports were of one piece with the stand.
At the top of the stand there was a half-cubit in height, round all about; and on the top of the stand its axle-supports and its rims were of one piece with it.
And on the plates of its axle-supports and on its rims he engraved cherubim, lions and palm trees, according to the clear space of each, with garlands all around.
In this way he made the ten stands: one casting, one measurement, one shape for all of them.
And he made ten washbasins of bronze: each held forty baths, each was four cubits across, and there was one washbasin on each of the ten stands.
He set the stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left; and the sea he set on the right side of the house, towards the east, opposite the south.
And Hiram made the washbasins, the shovels and the basins. So Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:
two pillars; the two bowls of the capitals on the top of the pillars; the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the top of the pillars;
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network — to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the face of the pillars;
and the ten stands, and the ten washbasins on the stands;
and the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it;
and the pots, the shovels and the basins. All these articles that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of polished bronze.
In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
Solomon left all the articles unweighed, because there were so very many; the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
And Solomon made all the articles for the house of the LORD: the altar of gold; the table of gold on which was the bread of the presence;
and the lampstands of refined gold, five on the right and five on the left before the innermost room; and the blossoms, the lamps and the tongs, of gold;

and the bowls, the snuffers, the basins, the pans and the firepans, of refined gold; and the sockets for the doors of the inner house — for the holy of holies — and for the doors of the house of the temple, of gold.

So all the work King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was complete. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father — the silver, the gold and the articles — and put them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

1 kings_8.t: Then Solomon called together the elders of Israel — all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites — to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, that is, Zion.
So every man of Israel gathered to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival — that's the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted the ark.
They brought up the ark of the LORD, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy articles that were in the tent — the priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had gathered to him were there with him in front of the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle — too many to be counted or numbered.
Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the innermost room of the house, the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim were spreading their wings out over the place of the ark, and they covered the ark and its poles from above.
The poles were long, and you could see the ends of them from the holy place in front of the innermost room, but you couldn't see them from outside. And they're still there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark but the two tablets of stone that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt.
And when the priests came out of the holy place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD.
The priests couldn't stand and serve because of the cloud, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
Then Solomon said: 'The LORD has said he would dwell in thick darkness.'
'And I — I have built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in for ever.'
Then the king turned round and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood there.
And he said: 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his own mouth to David my father and with his own hand has carried it out. He said:'

'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I never chose a city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house in for my name to be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
'And it was on the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.'
'But the LORD said to David my father, "It was on your heart to build a house for my name — you did well to have that on your heart."'
'"Only, you are not the one to build the house. Your son, the one who comes out from your loins — he's the one who will build the house for my name."'

'And the LORD has made good the word he spoke. I have arisen in place of David my father and taken my seat on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD said, and I've built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.'
'And I've made a place there for the ark, where the covenant of the LORD is — the covenant he made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.'
Then Solomon stood in front of the altar of the LORD, before the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms towards the heavens.

And he said: 'LORD, God of Israel, there's no God like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath — you keep the covenant and the steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.'
'You have kept for your servant David my father what you promised him. You spoke it with your mouth, and with your hand you have carried it out, as it is today.'

'And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him: "You shall never lack a man before me sitting on the throne of Israel" — only if your sons keep to their way, walking before me just as you have walked before me.'
'And now, God of Israel, let the word you spoke to your servant David my father be made good.'
'But will God really dwell on the earth? The heavens, and the heaven of heavens, can't contain you — how much less this house I've built!'
'Yet turn to your servant's prayer and his supplication, LORD my God; listen to the cry and the prayer your servant is praying before you today,'
'so that your eyes may be open towards this house night and day, towards the place you said, "My name shall be there" — to listen to the prayer your servant prays towards this place.'

'And listen to the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray towards this place. You yourself will hear in the place where you dwell, in the heavens — you will hear, and you will forgive.'
'When someone sins against his neighbour and is put under oath, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house —'

'then hear in the heavens and act. Judge your servants: condemn the guilty one, bringing his conduct back on his own head, and declare the righteous one righteous, giving him according to his righteousness.'
'When your people Israel are beaten by an enemy because they've sinned against you, and then they turn back to you and give thanks to your name and pray and seek favour before you in this house —'
'then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the ground you gave their fathers.'

'When the heavens are shut up and there's no rain because they've sinned against you, and then they pray towards this place and give thanks to your name and turn back from their sin because you're afflicting them —'

'then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, when you teach them the good way they should walk in; and give rain on your land, the land you gave your people as an inheritance.'
'When there's famine in the land, or pestilence, blight, mildew, locust or grasshopper; when an enemy besieges them in the land of their towns — any plague, any sickness —'
'whatever prayer, whatever supplication comes from any human being, from all your people Israel, each one knowing the plague of his own heart and spreading out his palms towards this house —'

'then hear in the heavens, the place where you dwell, and forgive and act. Give each one according to all his ways, since you know his heart — you alone know the heart of all the children of humankind —'
'so that they may fear you all the days they live on the face of the ground you gave to our fathers.'
'And the foreigner too — who isn't one of your people Israel but comes from a distant land for the sake of your name —'
'for they'll hear of your great name, your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — and he comes and prays towards this house —'

'then hear in the heavens, the place where you dwell, and do everything the foreigner calls to you for — so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you the way your people Israel do, and may know that your name has been called over this house I've built.'
'When your people go out to battle against their enemy by the way you send them, and they pray to the LORD towards the city you have chosen and the house I've built for your name —'
'then hear their prayer and their supplication in the heavens, and maintain their cause.'

'When they sin against you — and there's no human being who doesn't sin — and you're angry with them and give them up to an enemy, and their captors carry them off to the enemy's land, far away or near by,'

'and then they take it to heart in the land where they've been carried off, and turn back and seek favour before you in the land of their captors, saying, "We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly" —'

'and they come back to you with all their heart and all their soul, there in the land of the enemies who carried them off, and they pray to you towards their land, the land you gave their fathers, the city you have chosen and the house I've built for your name —'
'then hear their prayer and their supplication in the heavens, the place where you dwell, and maintain their cause;'

'and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all the transgressions they committed against you; and make them objects of compassion before their captors, so that their captors will have compassion on them.'
'because they're your people, your own inheritance, the ones you brought out of Egypt, out of the middle of the iron furnace.'
'so that your eyes may be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they call to you.'

'For you yourself separated them out for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as you spoke through Moses your servant when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, Lord GOD.'

And when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to the LORD, he got up from in front of the altar of the LORD, from kneeling on his knees with his palms spread out towards the heavens.
And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice:
'Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all his good promise, spoken through Moses his servant.'
'May the LORD our God be with us, just as he was with our fathers. May he never leave us or abandon us,'
'but incline our heart to him, so that we walk in all his ways and keep his commandments, his statutes and his judgements, which he commanded our fathers.'

'And may these words of mine, the words I've used to seek favour before the LORD, stay near to the LORD our God day and night, so that he maintains the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel as each day requires;'
'so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God — there is no other.'
'And let your heart be complete with the LORD our God, to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, as it is today.'
And the king, and all Israel with him, were offering sacrifice before the LORD.

And Solomon offered as the sacrifice of the peace offerings that he sacrificed to the LORD twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. That's how the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.

That day the king consecrated the middle of the court in front of the house of the LORD, because that's where he offered the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings — the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat of the peace offerings.
And Solomon kept the festival at that time, and all Israel with him — a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the wadi of Egypt — before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days: fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king; and they went home to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the good the LORD had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

1 kings_9.t: When Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the king's house, and everything else Solomon wanted and was pleased to do,
the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, the way he'd appeared to him at Gibeon.

And the LORD said to him: 'I've heard your prayer and your supplication, the one you made before me. I've consecrated this house you built, to put my name there for ever; and my eyes and my heart will be there always.'
'And as for you — if you walk before me the way David your father walked, with integrity of heart and with uprightness, doing everything I've commanded you and keeping my statutes and my judgements,'
'then I'll establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel for ever, just as I promised about David your father: "You shall never lack a man on the throne of Israel."'
'But if you and your sons do turn away from following me and don't keep my commandments and my statutes that I've set before you, and you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,'

'then I'll cut Israel off from the face of the ground I gave them, and the house I've consecrated for my name I'll throw out of my sight; and Israel will become a byword and a taunt among all the peoples.'
'And this house will be most high. Everyone who passes by will be appalled, and will hiss, and say, "Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?"'

'And they'll say, "Because they forsook the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them — that's why the LORD has brought all this calamity on them."'
At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built the two houses — the house of the LORD and the king's house —
— Hiram king of Tyre having supported Solomon with cedar timber, cypress timber and gold, everything he wanted — King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
But when Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities Solomon had given him, they didn't please him.
'What are these cities you've given me, my brother?' he said. And they've been called the land of Cabul to this day.
And Hiram had sent the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.
This is the account of the forced labour King Solomon raised, to build the house of the LORD, his own house, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and killed the Canaanites living in the city. He'd given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, and lower Beth-horon,
and Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land,

and all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, and the cities for the chariotry and the cities for the horsemen — whatever Solomon wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and anywhere in the land he ruled.
All the people left over from the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who weren't Israelites —
their descendants who were left after them in the land, the ones the Israelites hadn't been able to devote to destruction — these Solomon raised as a forced labour force, to this day.
But Solomon didn't make a slave of any Israelite. They were the men of war, his servants, his officials and his officers, and the commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
These were the chiefs of the overseers over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty of them, ruling over the people doing the work.
Only, Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her own house, the one he'd built for her. Then he built the Millo.
And three times a year Solomon offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he'd built for the LORD, and made offerings smoke on it, before the LORD. So he finished the house.
And King Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, beside Elath on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.
And Hiram sent his own servants in the fleet — sailors who knew the sea — along with Solomon's servants.
They went to Ophir and took gold from there — four hundred and twenty talents — and brought it to King Solomon.

1 kings_10.t: Now the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon, in connection with the name of the LORD, and she came to test him with hard questions.
She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue — camels carrying spices, and a great deal of gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and told him everything that was on her heart.
And Solomon answered all her questions. There was nothing hidden from the king that he didn't tell her.
And when the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon's wisdom, and the house he'd built,

and the food on his table, and the seating of his servants, and the attendance of his attendants and what they wore, and his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he offered up at the house of the LORD — there was no breath left in her.
She said to the king, 'It was true, the report I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.'
'I didn't believe the reports till I came and saw it with my own eyes — and I hadn't been told the half of it. You've added wisdom and good beyond the report I heard.'
'How blessed your people are! How blessed these servants of yours are, standing in front of you all the time and hearing your wisdom!'
'Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! It's because the LORD loves Israel for ever that he has made you king, to do justice and righteousness.'
And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a great deal of spice, and precious stones. Never again has spice come in such abundance as the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
And Hiram's fleet, which carried gold from Ophir, also brought from Ophir a great deal of almug wood and precious stones.

The king made the almug wood into supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and into lyres and harps for the singers. No almug wood like it has ever come in, or been seen, to this day.

And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted and asked for, besides what he gave her out of King Solomon's own bounty. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her servants.
The weight of the gold that came in to Solomon in a single year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
besides the revenue of the merchants and the merchandise of the traders, and from all the kings of the Arabs and the governors of the land.
