King Solomon made two hundred body shields of beaten gold — six hundred shekels of gold went into each body shield.
And three hundred shields of beaten gold — three minas of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with refined gold.
The throne had six steps, and a round top behind it, and arms on either side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the arms.
And twelve lions stood there on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made for any kingdom.
All King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the articles of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were refined gold. There was no silver — it counted for nothing in the days of Solomon.
For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea along with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish would come in, carrying gold and silver, ivory, monkeys and apes.
And King Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
And the whole earth was seeking Solomon's face, to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
And each of them brought his gift — articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weaponry, spices, horses and mules — year after year.
Solomon gathered chariotry and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the cities of the chariotry and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as common as the sycamores of the Shephelah, for abundance.
Solomon's horses came in from Egypt and from Que; the king's traders would buy them from Que at a price.

A chariot came up from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. And that's how, through them, they were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

1 kings_11.t: Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides Pharaoh's daughter — Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite women —

from the nations the LORD had spoken about to the Israelites: 'Don't go among them, and they must not come among you; they'll turn your heart aside after their gods, for certain.' These are the ones Solomon clung to and loved.
He had seven hundred wives who were noblewomen, and three hundred concubines — and his wives turned his heart aside.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart aside after other gods, and his heart wasn't complete with the LORD his God the way the heart of David his father had been.
Solomon followed Astarte the god of the Sidonians, and Milcom the detestable thing of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he didn't fully follow the LORD the way David his father had.
That was when Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable thing of Moab, on the mountain facing Jerusalem, and one for Molech, the detestable thing of the sons of Ammon.
And he did the same for all his foreign wives, who made offerings smoke and sacrificed to their gods.
And the LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned aside from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had given him a command about this very thing — not to go after other gods. But he didn't keep what the LORD commanded.

So the LORD said to Solomon, 'Since this is how it's been with you, and you haven't kept my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.'
'Only, I won't do it in your own days, for the sake of David your father. I'll tear it out of your son's hand.'
'And I won't tear away the whole kingdom. I'll give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I've chosen.'
And the LORD raised up an opponent against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, who was of the royal offspring in Edom.
For when David was with Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, he struck down every male in Edom —
Joab stayed there six months with all Israel, until he'd cut off every male in Edom.
But Hadad fled — he and some Edomite men from among his father's servants with him — to go to Egypt. Hadad was a young lad at the time.
They set out from Midian and came to Paran, and took men with them from Paran, and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, assigned him food and gave him land.
And Hadad found great favour with Pharaoh, who gave him his own wife's sister as a wife — the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
Tahpenes's sister bore him Genubath his son, and Tahpenes weaned him inside Pharaoh's house; and Genubath lived in Pharaoh's house among Pharaoh's sons.
And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, 'Let me go, so I can go to my own land.'
And Pharaoh said to him, 'But what are you short of here with me, that now you want to go to your own land?' And he said, 'Nothing — only let me go.'
And God raised up another opponent against him: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
He gathered men round him and became the leader of a marauding band, at the time David killed them. They went to Damascus, settled there, and reigned in Damascus.
He was an opponent to Israel all the days of Solomon — on top of the harm Hadad did. He loathed Israel, and he reigned over Aram.
Jeroboam son of Nebat as well — an Ephrathite from Zeredah, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow, a servant of Solomon — he too raised his hand against the king.
And this is why he raised his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach in the city of David his father.
Now the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of strength, and when Solomon saw that the young man was a capable worker, he put him over all the forced labour of the house of Joseph.

And at that time, when Jeroboam had gone out of Jerusalem, Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, met him on the road. He was wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone out in the open country.
And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.

And he said to Jeroboam, 'Take ten pieces for yourself. Because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "I'm about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand, and I'll give you the ten tribes."'
'"And the one tribe will be his, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I've chosen out of all the tribes of Israel."'

'"Because they've forsaken me and bowed down to Astarte the god of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab and to Milcom the god of the sons of Ammon, and they haven't walked in my ways, doing what's right in my eyes, keeping my statutes and my judgements, the way David his father did."'
'"But I won't take the whole kingdom out of his hand. I'll make him a ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes."'
'"And I'll take the kingship out of his son's hand and give it to you — the ten tribes."'
'"And to his son I'll give one tribe, so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I chose for myself, to put my name there."'
'"And you — I'll take you, and you'll reign over everything your being desires, and you'll be king over Israel."'

'"And if you listen to everything I command you and walk in my ways and do what's right in my eyes, keeping my statutes and my commandments the way David my servant did, then I'll be with you, and I'll build you an enduring house the way I built one for David, and I'll give Israel to you."'
'"And I'll afflict the offspring of David because of this — but not for all time."'
So Solomon tried to put Jeroboam to death; but Jeroboam got up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he stayed in Egypt until Solomon died.
The rest of the acts of Solomon, and everything he did, and his wisdom — aren't they written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
The days Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.
And Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

1 kings_12.t: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
And when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it — he was still in Egypt, where he'd fled from King Solomon — Jeroboam stayed on in Egypt.
So they sent and called for him. And Jeroboam came, and the whole assembly of Israel, and they said to Rehoboam:
'Your father made our yoke hard. Now you — lighten your father's hard service and that heavy yoke he put on us, and we'll serve you.'
And he said to them, 'Go away for three more days, then come back to me.' So the people went.
And King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive: 'What do you advise me to answer this people?'
And they said to him, 'If today you'll be a servant to this people and serve them, and answer them and speak kind words to them, then they'll be your servants for ever.'
But he put aside the counsel the elders had given him and consulted the young men who'd grown up with him and were standing before him.
And he said to them, 'What do you advise? How should we answer this people who've said to me, "Lighten the yoke your father put on us"?'

And the young men who'd grown up with him said, 'Here's what you should say to these people who said to you, "Your father made our yoke heavy; you lighten it for us" — say this to them: "My little finger is thicker than my father's loins."'
'"So then: my father loaded a heavy yoke on you — I'll add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips — I'll discipline you with scorpions."'
And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had said: 'Come back to me on the third day.'
And the king answered the people harshly. He put aside the counsel the elders had given him
and spoke to them the way the young men had advised: 'My father made your yoke heavy, and I'll add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I'll discipline you with scorpions.'
So the king didn't listen to the people — for it was a turn of events from the LORD, to make good the word the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And all Israel saw that the king hadn't listened to them, and the people answered the king: What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David! And Israel went off to its tents.
But as for the Israelites living in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was over the forced labour, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. King Rehoboam scrambled into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

And when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back, they sent and called him to the congregation and made him king over all Israel. Nobody followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.

And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and called together the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, warriors — to fight the house of Israel and bring the kingship back to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
'Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to the whole house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:'

'This is what the LORD says: Don't go up, and don't fight your countrymen, the Israelites. Go home, every one of you, because this thing has come about from me.' And they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back and went, according to the word of the LORD.
And Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. Then he went out from there and built Penuel.
And Jeroboam said to himself, 'Now the kingdom will go back to the house of David.'

'If these people go up to make sacrifices in the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, then their heart will go back to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah. They'll kill me and go back to Rehoboam king of Judah.'
So the king took counsel and made two calves of gold, and he said to them, 'It's too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
And he set the one up in Bethel and the other in Dan.
And this thing became a sin, and the people went before the one, as far as Dan.
He also made a house of high places, and appointed priests from among the common people, who weren't of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam appointed a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival in Judah, and he offered up on the altar. That's what he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he'd made; and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places he'd made.

And he offered up on the altar he'd made in Bethel, on the fifteenth day in the eighth month — the month he'd devised out of his own heart — and he appointed a festival for the Israelites, and went up on the altar to make offerings smoke.

1 kings_13.t: And a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD, just as Jeroboam was standing at the altar to make offerings smoke.

And he called out against the altar by the word of the LORD: 'Altar, altar! This is what the LORD says: A son is going to be born to the house of David — Josiah will be his name — and he'll sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who make offerings smoke on you, and human bones will be burned on you.'
And he gave a sign that day: 'This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: the altar is about to be torn apart, and the fatty ash on it will spill out.'

When the king heard what the man of God called out against the altar at Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar and said, 'Seize him!' And the hand he stretched out against him dried up, and he couldn't pull it back.
And the altar was torn apart, and the fatty ash spilled out from the altar, just as the sign the man of God had given by the word of the LORD had said.

And the king said to the man of God, 'Entreat the face of the LORD your God, and pray for me, so my hand comes back to me.' And the man of God entreated the face of the LORD, and the king's hand came back to him and was as it had been before.
And the king said to the man of God, 'Come home with me and take some refreshment, and let me give you a gift.'
And the man of God said to the king, 'If you gave me half your house, I wouldn't go with you. And I won't eat bread or drink water in this place.'
'Because this is what he commanded me by the word of the LORD: "You shall not eat bread or drink water, and you shall not go back by the way you came."'
So he went by another way, and didn't go back by the way he'd come to Bethel.
Now an old prophet was living in Bethel, and his son came and told him everything the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he'd spoken to the king. They told it all to their father.
And their father said to them, 'Which way did he go?' His sons had seen the way the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
And he said to his sons, 'Saddle the donkey for me.' So they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode off on it.
He went after the man of God and found him sitting under the oak. 'Are you the man of God who came from Judah?' he said. 'I am,' he said.
And he said to him, 'Come home with me and eat bread.'
And he said, 'I can't turn back with you or go with you. And I won't eat bread or drink water with you in this place.'
'Because a word came to me by the word of the LORD: "You shall not eat bread or drink water there; you shall not go back by the way you came."'

And he said to him, 'I'm a prophet too, just like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD: "Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water."' He was lying to him.
So he went back with him, and ate bread in his house, and drank water.
And while they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.
And he called out to the man of God who had come from Judah, 'This is what the LORD says: Because you disobeyed the mouth of the LORD and didn't keep the command the LORD your God gave you,'
'and you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place he told you, "Don't eat bread and don't drink water" — your corpse won't come to the grave of your fathers.'
And after he'd eaten bread and after he'd drunk, he saddled the donkey for him — for the prophet he had brought back.
And off he went, and a lion met him on the road and killed him. His corpse lay thrown down in the road, with the donkey standing beside it and the lion standing beside the corpse.
And men passing by saw the corpse thrown down in the road and the lion standing beside the corpse, and they came and talked about it in the city where the old prophet was living.

When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard it, he said, 'It's the man of God, who disobeyed the mouth of the LORD. The LORD has given him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, just as the word of the LORD that he spoke to him said.'
And he said to his sons, 'Saddle the donkey for me.' And they saddled it.
And he went and found the corpse thrown down in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion hadn't eaten the corpse and hadn't mauled the donkey.
So the prophet picked up the corpse of the man of God, laid him on the donkey and brought him back; and he came to the city of the old prophet, to mourn for him and bury him.
And he laid the corpse in his own grave, and they mourned over him: 'Alas, my brother!'
And after he'd buried him he said to his sons, 'When I die, bury me in the grave where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.'
'Because the word he called out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, is certainly going to come to pass.'

Even after this, Jeroboam didn't turn back from his evil way. He went right on appointing priests of the high places from among the common people. Anyone who wanted it, he ordained, and he became one of the priests of the high places.
And by this thing it became the sin of the house of Jeroboam, to annihilate it and wipe it off the face of the ground.

1 kings_14.t: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam fell sick.

And Jeroboam said to his wife, 'Get up and disguise yourself, so they won't know you're Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there — the one who spoke about me, that I'd be king over this people.'
'And take ten loaves with you, and cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He'll tell you what's going to happen to the boy.'
And Jeroboam's wife did just that. She got up and went to Shiloh and came to Ahijah's house. Ahijah couldn't see — his eyes were fixed with old age.
But the LORD had said to Ahijah, 'Jeroboam's wife is coming to consult you for a word about her son — he's sick. Say such and such to her. And when she comes she'll be pretending to be someone else.'
And when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet coming in at the door, he said, 'Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you pretending to be someone else? I've been sent to you with a hard message.'
'Go and say to Jeroboam: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel,"'

'"and I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you — and still you haven't been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and walked after me with all his heart, doing only what is right in my eyes;"'
'"and you've done more evil than everyone before you: you've gone and made yourself other gods and cast images, to provoke me to anger, and me you've thrown behind your back."'

'"So I'm bringing calamity on the house of Jeroboam. I'll cut off from Jeroboam every one who urinates against a wall, bond and free in Israel, and I'll sweep out after the house of Jeroboam the way you sweep out dung, till it's all gone."'
'"Anyone of Jeroboam's who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone who dies out in the open country, the birds of the heavens will eat — because the LORD has spoken."'
'And as for you — get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.'

'And all Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He's the only one of Jeroboam's who will come to a grave, because in him something good towards the LORD, the God of Israel, was found in the house of Jeroboam.'
'And the LORD will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam — this day; and what? — even now.'

'And the LORD will strike Israel the way a reed sways in the water, and he'll pull Israel up out of this good ground he gave their fathers and scatter them beyond the River — because they've made their Asherim, provoking the LORD to anger.'
'And he'll give Israel up, because of the sins Jeroboam sinned and by which he made Israel sin.'
So Jeroboam's wife got up and went and came to Tirzah; and as she reached the threshold of the house, the lad died.
And all Israel buried him and mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned — there they are, written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
The days Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. Then he lay down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

And Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
And Judah did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they provoked him to jealousy more than all their fathers had done, by the sins they sinned.
They too built themselves high places and pillars and Asherim, on every high hill and under every green tree.
And there were cult prostitutes in the land as well. They did all the same abominations as the nations the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
He took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house — he took the lot — and he took all the gold shields Solomon had made.
So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them, and handed them over to the commanders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house.
And whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the runners would carry them, and then bring them back to the runners' guardroom.
And the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and everything he did — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
And Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. And Abijam his son reigned in his place.

1 kings_15.t: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
And he walked in all the sins his father had done before him. His heart wasn't complete with the LORD his God the way the heart of David his father had been.
For it was for David's sake that the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him and establishing Jerusalem —
because David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and hadn't turned aside from anything he commanded him, all the days of his life — except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
And the rest of the acts of Abijam, and everything he did — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
And Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah.
And he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, like David his father.
He swept the male cult prostitutes out of the land, and he got rid of all the idols his fathers had made.
He even removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she'd made an abominable image for the Asherah. Asa cut her abominable image down and burned it in the wadi of Kidron.
But the high places weren't removed. Still, Asa's heart was complete with the LORD all his days.
And he brought into the house of the LORD the holy things of his father and his own holy things: silver, gold and articles.
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah, so that nobody could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

So Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the treasuries of the king's house, and put it into the hands of his servants; and King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

'There's a covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I've sent you a bribe of silver and gold. Go and break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he'll pull back from me.'
And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa. He sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Kinnereth, with all the land of Naphtali.
And when Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.

Then King Asa made a proclamation to all Judah — nobody was exempt — and they carried off the stones and timber of Ramah that Baasha had been building with; and with them King Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

And the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and everything he did, and the cities he built — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah? Only, in his old age he was diseased in his feet.
And Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
And Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father and in the sin by which he made Israel sin.
And Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him, and struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
So Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

And as soon as he was king he struck down the whole house of Jeroboam. He didn't leave Jeroboam anything that breathed, until he'd destroyed it — according to the word of the LORD spoken through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
because of the sins Jeroboam sinned and by which he made Israel sin, and because of the provocation with which he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
And the rest of the acts of Nadab, and everything he did — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and reigned twenty-four years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel sin.

1 kings_16.t: And the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha:
'I raised you up out of the dust and made you a ruler over my people Israel, and you've walked in the way of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, provoking me to anger with their sins —'
'so I'm sweeping away after Baasha and after his house, and I'll make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.'
'Anyone of Baasha's who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone of his who dies out in the open country, the birds of the heavens will eat.'
And the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his place.

And the word of the LORD had also come through Jehu son of Hanani the prophet against Baasha and against his house — both for all the evil he did in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, so as to be like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah, and reigned two years.
And his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariotry, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
Zimri came in, struck him down and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.

And as soon as he was king, the moment he sat on his throne, he struck down the whole house of Baasha. He didn't leave him one who urinates against a wall — not one of his kinsmen-redeemers, not one friend.
So Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that he'd spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,
because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and by which they made Israel sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities.
And the rest of the acts of Elah, and everything he did — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. The people were camped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
And the people in the camp heard it said, 'Zimri has conspired, and he's struck the king down too.' So that same day, in the camp, all Israel made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel.
And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they laid siege to Tirzah.
And when Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the fortress of the king's house and burned the king's house down over himself with fire, and he died —
because of the sins he sinned, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he did, to make Israel sin.
And the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy he made — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel split in half: half the people were behind Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half were behind Omri.
But the people behind Omri were stronger than the people behind Tibni son of Ginath. And Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel and reigned twelve years; six of them in Tirzah.
And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and named the city he built after Shemer, the owner of the hill: Samaria.
And Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD — he did more evil than everyone before him.
He walked in every way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in the sin by which he made Israel sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities.
And the rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might he showed — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his place.
And Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah; and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
And Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than everyone before him.

And as if it were a small thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians as a wife, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
And he set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.
And Ahab made the Asherah. Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.

In his days Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. It cost him Abiram his firstborn to lay its foundation, and Segub his youngest to set up its gates — according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through Joshua son of Nun.

1 kings_17.t: And Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, 'As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand — there won't be dew or rain these years, except by my word.'
And the word of the LORD came to him:
'Leave here and turn east, and hide yourself at the wadi of Kerith, opposite the Jordan.'
'You can drink from the wadi, and I've commanded the ravens to supply you there.'
So he went and did what the LORD had said: he went and lived at the wadi of Kerith, opposite the Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
But after a while the wadi dried up, because there'd been no rain in the land.
And the word of the LORD came to him:
'Get up and go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and live there. I've commanded a widow there to supply you.'
So he got up and went to Zarephath, and when he came to the entrance of the city, there was a widow gathering wood. He called to her, 'Fetch me a little water in a vessel, so I can drink.'
And as she went to get it, he called after her, 'Bring me a piece of bread in your hand.'

And she said, 'As the LORD your God lives, I've nothing baked — only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug. Here I am gathering two sticks, and I'm going in to make it for myself and my son, and we'll eat it and die.'
And Elijah said to her, 'Don't be afraid. Go and do as you said. Only make me a small cake from it first and bring it out to me, and afterwards make some for yourself and your son.'
'Because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: The jar of flour won't run out and the jug of oil won't fail, till the day the LORD gives rain on the face of the ground.'
And she went and did what Elijah said; and she ate, she and he and her household, for many days.
The jar of flour didn't run out and the jug of oil didn't fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke through Elijah.
And after this the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick. His sickness was very severe, till there was no breath left in him.
And she said to Elijah, 'What have I to do with you, man of God? You've come to me to call my iniquity to mind and put my son to death.'
And he said to her, 'Give me your son.' He took him out of her bosom, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
And he called out to the LORD, 'LORD my God, have you brought harm even on the widow I'm staying with as a sojourner, by putting her son to death?'
And he stretched himself out over the lad three times and called out to the LORD, 'LORD my God, let the life of this lad come back into his inward parts.'
And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the life of the lad came back into his inward parts, and he lived.
And Elijah took the lad and brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother. 'Look,' Elijah said, 'your son is alive.'
And the woman said to Elijah, 'Now I know it — you're a man of God, and the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth.'

1 kings_18.t: And after many days, in the third year, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: 'Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I'll give rain on the face of the ground.'
So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria.
And Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the household. Now Obadiah feared the LORD very much.
When Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men to a cave, and supplied them with bread and water.
And Ahab said to Obadiah, 'Go through the land, to all the springs of water and all the wadis. Maybe we'll find grass and keep horse and mule alive, and not lose any of the livestock.'
So they divided the land between them to go through it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
And Obadiah was on his way when Elijah met him. He recognised him and fell on his face and said, 'Is that you, my lord Elijah?'
'It is,' he said. 'Go and tell your lord, "Elijah is here."'
And he said, 'What have I done wrong, that you're handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?'

'As the LORD your God lives, there isn't a nation or a kingdom my lord hasn't sent to look for you in. And when they said, "He isn't here," he made that kingdom and nation swear they hadn't found you.'
'And now you're saying, "Go and tell your lord, Elijah is here."'

'And here's what will happen: I'll go from you, and the spirit of the LORD will carry you off to somewhere I don't know, and I'll come to tell Ahab, and he won't find you, and he'll kill me. And your servant has feared the LORD since I was young.'

'Hasn't my lord been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD — how I hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets, fifty and fifty, in the caves, and supplied them with bread and water?'
'And now you're saying, "Go and tell your lord, Elijah is here" — and he'll kill me!'
And Elijah said, 'As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I'll show myself to him today.'
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
And when Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to him, 'Is that you, you troubler of Israel?'
And he said, 'I haven't troubled Israel — you have, you and your father's house, by forsaking the commandments of the LORD and going after the Baals.'
'Now then, send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the Asherah, the ones who eat at Jezebel's table.'
So Ahab sent word among all the Israelites and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.

And Elijah came up to all the people and said, 'How long are you going to go limping on two crutches? If the LORD is God, go after him; and if Baal is, go after him.' And the people didn't answer him a word.
And Elijah said to the people, 'I'm the only prophet of the LORD left, and the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men.'

'Let them give us two young bulls. Let them pick one bull for themselves and cut it in pieces and lay it on the wood, but set no fire. And I'll prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood, but set no fire.'
'Then you call on the name of your god, and I'll call on the name of the LORD; and whichever god answers by fire — he is God.' And all the people answered, 'The word is good.'
And Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, 'Pick one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, since there are more of you; and call on the name of your god — but set no fire.'

So they took the bull they were given and prepared it, and they called on the name of Baal from morning till noon: 'Baal, answer us!' But there was no voice and nobody answering. And they went limping around the altar that had been made.

And at noon Elijah started mocking them. 'Shout louder!' he said. 'He's a god, after all. Maybe he's deep in thought, or he's stepped aside to relieve himself, or he's off on a journey. Perhaps he's asleep and he'll wake up.'
So they shouted louder, and they cut themselves, as their custom was, with swords and lances, till the blood poured out over them.
And when noon had gone by, they went on prophesying until the time of the going up of the offering. But there was no voice, nobody answering, and no attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, 'Come over here to me.' And all the people came over to him. And he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, the one the word of the LORD had come to: 'Israel shall be your name.'
And he built the stones into an altar in the name of the LORD, and he made a trench round the altar big enough to hold two seahs of seed.
He arranged the wood, cut the bull in pieces and laid it on the wood. Then he said, 'Fill four jars with water and pour it over the burnt offering and over the wood.'
'Do it again,' he said. And they did it again. 'Do it a third time,' he said. And they did it a third time.
And the water ran all round the altar; he even filled the trench with water.

And at the time of the going up of the offering, Elijah the prophet came forward and said, 'LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, and that I'm your servant, and that I've done all these things at your word.'
'Answer me, LORD, answer me — so this people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you have turned their heart back.'
Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the dust; and it licked up the water that was in the trench.
And all the people saw it, and they fell on their faces and said, 'The LORD, he is God! The LORD, he is God!'
And Elijah said to them, 'Seize the prophets of Baal. Don't let one of them get away.' So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi of Kishon and slaughtered them there.
And Elijah said to Ahab, 'Go on up, eat and drink — there's the sound of the roar of rain.'
So Ahab went up to eat and drink; and Elijah went up to the top of Carmel, crouched down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
And he said to his servant, 'Go up and look towards the sea.' He went up and looked. 'There's nothing,' he said. And he said, 'Go back seven times.'
And the seventh time he said, 'A small cloud like a man's hand is coming up out of the sea.' And he said, 'Go up and say to Ahab, "Harness up and get down, so the rain doesn't stop you."'
And meanwhile the heavens went black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode off to Jezreel.
And the hand of the LORD was on Elijah. He girded up his loins and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.

1 kings_19.t: And Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, and how he'd killed all the prophets with the sword.
So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: 'May the gods do so to me, and more, if by this time tomorrow I haven't made your life like the life of one of them.'
And he saw, and he got up and ran for his life. He came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
And he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness. He came and sat under a broom bush and asked to die. 'Enough!' he said. 'Now, LORD, take my life — I'm no better than my fathers.'
Then he lay down and slept under the broom bush. And an angel touched him and said, 'Get up. Eat.'
He looked, and there at his head was a cake baked on hot stones, and a jug of water. So he ate and drank and lay down again.
And the angel of the LORD came back a second time and touched him. 'Get up and eat,' he said, 'because the journey is too much for you.'
So he got up and ate and drank; and on the strength of that food he went forty days and forty nights, to Horeb, the mountain of God.
He came there, to the cave, and spent the night in it. And the word of the LORD came to him: 'What are you doing here, Elijah?'

And he said, 'I've been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have forsaken your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I'm the only one left, and they're after my life, to take it.'

And he said, 'Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.' And there was the LORD passing by, and a great strong wind tearing mountains apart and breaking rocks before the LORD — but the LORD wasn't in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake — but the LORD wasn't in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake, a fire — but the LORD wasn't in the fire. And after the fire, the faint sound of a hush.
And when Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And a voice came to him: 'What are you doing here, Elijah?'

And he said, 'I've been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have forsaken your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I'm the only one left, and they're after my life, to take it.'
And the LORD said to him, 'Go back the way you came, to the wilderness of Damascus. And when you get there, anoint Hazael as king over Aram.'
'And Jehu son of Nimshi you're to anoint as king over Israel; and Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, you're to anoint as prophet in your place.'
'And whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death; and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.'
'And I'll leave seven thousand in Israel — every knee that hasn't bowed to Baal, and every mouth that hasn't kissed him.'
So he went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was ploughing, with twelve pairs of oxen ahead of him, and he was with the twelfth. And Elijah went past him and threw his cloak over him.
So he left the oxen and ran after Elijah. 'Let me kiss my father and my mother,' he said, 'and then I'll go after you.' And he said to him, 'Go on back — what have I done to you?'

So he turned back from following him, and took the pair of oxen and sacrificed them; and with the oxen's equipment he cooked the flesh and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up and went after Elijah and served him.

1 kings_20.t: And Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army — thirty-two kings were with him, with horses and chariotry — and he went up and laid siege to Samaria and fought against it.
And he sent messengers into the city, to Ahab king of Israel, and said to him, 'This is what Ben-hadad says:'
'Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children, the best of them, are mine.'
And the king of Israel answered, 'It's as you say, my lord the king: I'm yours, and so is everything I have.'
And the messengers came back and said, 'This is what Ben-hadad says: I sent you word, Your silver and your gold and your wives and your children you shall give to me —'
'— but about this time tomorrow I'll send my servants to you, and they'll search your house and the houses of your servants; and everything your eyes delight in they'll lay hands on and carry off.'

And the king of Israel called in all the elders of the land and said, 'Know and see that this man is out for harm. He sent to me for my wives and my children and my silver and my gold, and I didn't refuse him.'
And all the elders and all the people said to him, 'Don't listen, and don't agree.'
So he said to Ben-hadad's messengers, 'Say to my lord the king: Everything you first sent to your servant for, I'll do — but this thing I can't do.' And the messengers went and brought word back.
And Ben-hadad sent to him: 'May the gods do so to me, and more, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for a handful each for all the people at my feet.'
And the king of Israel answered, 'Tell him this: The one buckling on his armour shouldn't boast like the one taking it off.'
And when he heard this word — he was drinking, he and the kings, in the booths — he said to his servants, 'Take your positions.' And they took their positions against the city.

And a certain prophet came up to Ahab king of Israel and said, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you seen all this great multitude? I'm giving it into your hand today, and you'll know that I am the LORD.'
And Ahab said, 'By whom?' And he said, 'This is what the LORD says: By the young men of the officials of the provinces.' And he said, 'Who's to start the battle?' And he said, 'You.'
So he mustered the young men of the officials of the provinces: two hundred and thirty-two. And after them he mustered all the people, all the Israelites: seven thousand.
They went out at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the booths — he and the kings, the thirty-two kings who were helping him.
The young men of the officials of the provinces went out first. And Ben-hadad sent out scouts, and they told him, 'Men have come out of Samaria.'
And he said, 'If they've come out for peace, take them alive; and if they've come out for battle, take them alive.'
So these came out of the city — the young men of the officials of the provinces, and the army behind them.
And they struck down, each his man; and Aram fled, and Israel went after them. And Ben-hadad king of Aram got away on a horse, with horsemen.
And the king of Israel went out and struck down the horses and the chariotry, and struck Aram with a great slaughter.
Then the prophet came up to the king of Israel and said, 'Go and make yourself strong, and know and see what you're to do — because at the turn of the year the king of Aram is coming up against you.'

And the servants of the king of Aram said to him, 'Their God is a god of the mountains — that's why they were stronger than we were. But let's fight them on level ground, and we're sure to be stronger than they are.'
'And do this: get rid of the kings, each from his place, and appoint governors instead of them.'

'And you — muster yourself an army like the army you lost, horse for horse and chariotry for chariotry; and let's fight them on level ground, and we're sure to be stronger than they are.' And he listened to them and did it.
And at the turn of the year Ben-hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek for battle with Israel.
And the Israelites were mustered and supplied, and they went out to meet them. The Israelites camped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.

And the man of God came up and spoke to the king of Israel: 'This is what the LORD says: Because Aram have said, The LORD is a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys — I'm going to give all this great multitude into your hand, and you'll know that I am the LORD.'
And they camped opposite each other for seven days. On the seventh day the battle was joined, and the Israelites struck down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
The rest fled to Aphek, into the city — and the wall fell on the twenty-seven thousand men who were left. And Ben-hadad fled into the city, into an inner room.

And his servants said to him, 'We've heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of loyalty. Let's put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel — maybe he'll spare your life.'

So they girded sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said, 'Your servant Ben-hadad says, Let me live.' And he said, 'Is he still alive? He's my brother.'

Now the men were watching for an omen, and they seized on it quickly. 'Your brother Ben-hadad,' they said. And he said, 'Go and fetch him.' And Ben-hadad came out to him, and he brought him up onto the chariot.

And Ben-hadad said to him, 'The cities my father took from your father I'll give back, and you can set up streets for yourself in Damascus, the way my father did in Samaria.' Ahab said, 'And I — I'll let you go with a covenant.' So he cut a covenant with him and let him go.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, by the word of the LORD, 'Strike me.' But the man refused to strike him.

So he said to him, 'Because you didn't listen to the voice of the LORD, when you go from me the lion will strike you down.' And he went off from beside him, and the lion found him and struck him down.
And he found another man and said, 'Strike me.' And the man struck him — struck him and wounded him.
Then the prophet went and stood waiting for the king beside the road, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.

And as the king was going past, he cried out to the king, 'Your servant went out into the thick of the battle, and a man turned aside and brought a man over to me and said, Guard this man; if he goes missing, your life will be in place of his life, or you'll weigh out a talent of silver.'
'And while your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.' And the king of Israel said to him, 'That's your sentence — you decided it yourself.'
Then he quickly pulled the bandage off his eyes, and the king of Israel recognised him as one of the prophets.

And he said to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Because you let go out of your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, your life will be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people.'
And the king of Israel went home sullen and furious, and came to Samaria.

1 kings_21.t: Now after this: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, right beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab said to Naboth, 'Let me have your vineyard for a vegetable garden — it's right next to my house — and I'll give you a better vineyard in its place. Or if you'd rather, I'll give you silver, the price of it.'
And Naboth said to Ahab, 'The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.'
So Ahab came home sullen and furious over what Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him — 'I won't give you the inheritance of my fathers.' He lay down on his bed, turned his face away and wouldn't eat.
And Jezebel his wife came to him and said, 'Why is this? Your spirit's so sullen, and you're not eating.'

And he said to her, 'Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said, Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you'd rather, I'll give you a vineyard in its place. And he said, I won't give you my vineyard.'
And Jezebel his wife said to him, 'You — are you the one exercising kingship over Israel now? Get up, eat, and cheer up. I'll get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite myself.'
So she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and nobles in his city, the ones who lived with Naboth.
And in the letters she wrote, 'Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.'
'And seat two men in front of him, worthless men, and have them testify against him: You have cursed God and the king. Then take him out and stone him, and let him die.'
And the men of his city — the elders and the nobles who lived in his city — did what Jezebel had sent word to do, just as it was written in the letters she'd sent them.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

And the two worthless men came and sat in front of him and testified against Naboth in front of the people: 'Naboth has cursed God and the king.' So they took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
Then they sent word to Jezebel: 'Naboth has been stoned. He's dead.'

And as soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, 'Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, the one he wouldn't give you for silver. Naboth isn't alive — he's dead.'
And as soon as Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
'Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who's in Samaria. He's there in Naboth's vineyard — he's gone down to take possession of it.'

'And say to him, This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered, and taken possession too? And say to him, This is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, the dogs will lick up your blood — yours too.'
And Ahab said to Elijah, 'Have you found me, my enemy?' And he said, 'I have found you — because you've sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.'
'I'm bringing harm on you. I'll sweep away after you, and I'll cut off from Ahab every male, bond and free in Israel.'

'And I'll make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you've provoked me to anger, and because you've made Israel sin.'
And of Jezebel too the LORD has spoken: 'The dogs will devour Jezebel at the rampart of Jezreel.'
'Anyone of Ahab's who dies in the city, the dogs will devour; and anyone who dies out in the open country, the birds of the heavens will devour.'
There was certainly no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, with Jezebel his wife inciting him.
And he acted exceedingly abominably by going after the idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD dispossessed before the Israelites.
And when Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his body and fasted; and he lay in the sackcloth and went about dejectedly.
And the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
'Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I won't bring the harm in his own days. I'll bring the harm on his house in the days of his son.'

1 kings_22.t: And they went three years with no war between Aram and Israel.
But in the third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said to his servants, 'Do you realise Ramoth-gilead is ours, and here we sit doing nothing about taking it from the hand of the king of Aram?'
And he said to Jehoshaphat, 'Will you come with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?' And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, 'I'm as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.'
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, 'Consult the word of the LORD today.'

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, 'Shall I go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?' And they said, 'Go up, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.'
But Jehoshaphat said, 'Isn't there still a prophet of the LORD here, so we can consult him?'

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, 'There's still one man to consult the LORD through — but I hate him, because he never prophesies good about me, only evil: Micaiah son of Imlah.' And Jehoshaphat said, 'Don't let the king say that.'
So the king of Israel called a court official and said, 'Bring Micaiah son of Imlah, quickly.'

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying in front of them.
And Zedekiah son of Kenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, 'This is what the LORD says: With these you'll gore Aram till you've finished them off.'
And all the prophets were prophesying the same: 'Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, and the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.'

And the messenger who'd gone to fetch Micaiah said to him, 'Look — the prophets are all saying the same thing, and it's favourable to the king. Let your word be like the word of one of them; speak favourably.'
And Micaiah said, 'As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, that's what I'll speak.'

And he came to the king, and the king said to him, 'Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we hold back?' And he said, 'Go up and succeed, and the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.'
And the king said to him, 'How many times do I have to make you swear to tell me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?'
And he said, 'I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like a flock with no shepherd. And the LORD said, These have no masters; let them go home, each to his house, in peace.'
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, 'Didn't I tell you? He never prophesies good about me, only evil.'
And he said, 'Then hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing beside him, on his right and on his left.'
And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab, so he'll go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said one thing, and another said another.
And the spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I'll entice him.'
And the LORD said to him, 'How?' And he said, 'I'll go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he said, 'You'll entice him, and you'll prevail too. Go out and do it.'
'So now the LORD has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these prophets of yours — and the LORD has spoken evil about you.'
Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, 'Which way did the spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak with you?'
And Micaiah said, 'You'll see, on the day you go into an inner room to hide yourself.'
And the king of Israel said, 'Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son.'
'And say, This is what the king says: Put this man in the prison house and feed him bread of oppression and water of oppression, until I come back in peace.'
And Micaiah said, 'If you ever come back in peace, the LORD hasn't spoken by me.' And he said, 'Listen, peoples, all of you.'
So the king of Israel went up, with Jehoshaphat king of Judah, to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, 'I'll disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your own robes.' So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.
Now the king of Aram had ordered the thirty-two commanders of his chariotry, 'Don't fight with small or great — only with the king of Israel.'
And when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat, they said, 'That must be the king of Israel,' and they turned aside to fight him. And Jehoshaphat cried out.
And when the commanders of the chariotry saw that he wasn't the king of Israel, they turned back from following him.
But a man drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the joints of his armour. And he said to his charioteer, 'Turn about and get me out of the camp — I'm wounded.'
And the battle grew fierce that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing Aram. He died in the evening, and the blood from the wound ran down into the bottom of the chariot.
And the cry went through the camp as the sun was going down: 'Each to his city! Each to his land!'
So the king died, and he was brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.
And they washed the chariot off at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood; and the prostitutes washed there — according to the word of the LORD that he had spoken.
And the rest of the acts of Ahab, and everything he did, and the ivory house he built, and all the cities he built — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Ahab lay down with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
And Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

And he walked in all the way of Asa his father and didn't turn aside from it, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD. Only, the high places weren't removed — the people were still sacrificing and burning offerings at the high places.
And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and the might he showed, and how he waged war — aren't they written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And the rest of the cult prostitutes who were left from the days of Asa his father, he swept out of the land.
There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they never went — the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, 'Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.' But Jehoshaphat wasn't willing.
And Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father and the way of his mother and the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
He served Baal and bowed down to him, and provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.

1 samuel_1.t: There was a man from Ramathaim-zophim, in the hill country of Ephraim. His name was Elkanah son of Jeroham son of Elihu son of Tohu son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
He had two wives. The name of one was Hannah and the name of the second was Peninnah. Peninnah had children; Hannah had none.
That man would go up from his town year after year to bow down and sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh. And there the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
When the day came, Elkanah sacrificed, and he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.
And to Hannah he would give one portion, a double one — because he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.
And her rival provoked her bitterly, to upset her, because the LORD had closed her womb.
And so it went year after year. Whenever she went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah would provoke her, and she wept and wouldn't eat.
And Elkanah her husband said to her, 'Hannah, why are you weeping? Why aren't you eating? Why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?'
Then Hannah got up, after they had eaten at Shiloh and after they had drunk. Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
She was bitter in herself, and she prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

And she vowed a vow: 'LORD of hosts, if you will only look on the affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant, and will give your maidservant a male child, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor will go on his head.'
And as she went on praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth.
Now Hannah was speaking in her heart. Only her lips moved; her voice wasn't heard. And Eli took her for a drunken woman.
And Eli said to her, 'How long are you going to be drunk? Put your wine away from you.'
And Hannah answered, 'No, my lord. I'm a woman hard-pressed in spirit. I haven't drunk wine or strong drink. I've poured out my being before the LORD.'
Don't take your maidservant for a daughter of worthlessness. It's out of the greatness of my complaint and my provocation that I've been speaking all this time.
And Eli answered, 'Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant the petition you've asked of him.'
And she said, 'May your maidservant find favour in your eyes.' Then the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer as it had been.
They rose early in the morning and bowed down before the LORD, then returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.
And in the course of time Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, saying, 'From the LORD I asked him.'
And the man Elkanah went up with all his household to sacrifice to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and to pay his vow.
But Hannah didn't go up. She said to her husband, 'Once the boy is weaned, I'll bring him, and he'll appear before the LORD and stay there for ever.'
And Elkanah her husband said to her, 'Do what seems good to you. Stay until you've weaned him — only may the LORD carry out his word.' So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
When she had weaned him she took him up with her, with three bulls, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the boy was still young.
They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
And she said, 'Pardon me, my lord — as you live, my lord — I am the woman who stood here with you, praying to the LORD.'
It was for this boy that I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I asked of him.
And I in turn have lent him to the LORD: as long as he lives, he is lent to the LORD.' And he bowed down there to the LORD.

1 samuel_2.t: And Hannah prayed and said: My heart rejoices in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, because I rejoice in your deliverance.
There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you; and there is no Rock like our God.
Don't go on speaking so haughtily, so haughtily; let no arrogance come out of your mouth. For the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him deeds are weighed.
The bow of warriors is shattered, and those who stumbled gird on strength.
Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, and those who were hungry go hungry no more. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who had many sons languishes.
The LORD kills and gives life; he brings down to Sheol and brings up.
The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, and he exalts.

He raises the poor from the dust; from the ash heap he lifts the needy, to seat them with nobles, and a throne of glory he gives them as an inheritance. For the pillars of the earth belong to the LORD, and he has set the world upon them.
The feet of his loyal ones he guards, and the wicked are silenced in the darkness; for no one prevails by strength.

The LORD — those who contend with him are shattered; against them he thunders in the heavens. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.
Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, and the boy served the LORD in the presence of Eli the priest.
Now the sons of Eli were sons of worthlessness. They did not know the LORD.
This was the custom of the priests with the people: whenever anyone sacrificed a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,

and thrust it into the pan or the kettle or the cauldron or the cooking pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. That is what they did to all Israel who came there, at Shiloh.
And before they burned the fat, the priest's servant would come and say to the man sacrificing, 'Give meat to roast for the priest. He won't take boiled meat from you — only raw.'
And the man would say, 'Let them burn the fat first, and then take whatever you want.' And he'd say, 'No — you'll give it now. And if you won't, I'll take it by force.'
The sin of the young men was very great in the presence of the LORD, because the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.
And Samuel was serving in the presence of the LORD — a boy, wearing a linen ephod.
And his mother would make him a small robe and bring it up to him year after year, when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the yearly sacrifice.
And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, 'May the LORD appoint you offspring from this woman in place of the petition that was asked for the LORD.' And they would go home.
For the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up with the LORD.
Eli was very old, and he heard everything his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they were lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
And he said to them, 'Why do you do such things? I hear of your evil doings from all these people.'
No, my sons. The report I hear is not good — you're making the people of the LORD transgress.

If a man sins against a man, God will mediate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?' And they did not listen to their father's voice, because the LORD desired to put them to death.
And the boy Samuel went on growing, and he was good both with the LORD and with people.
And a man of God came to Eli and said to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Did I not reveal myself to the house of your ancestor when they were in Egypt, to the house of Pharaoh?

I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel for myself as a priest, to go up on my altar, to burn incense, to bear an ephod in my presence. And I gave to the house of your ancestor all the food offerings of the people of Israel.
Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I commanded for my dwelling, and honour your sons above me, fattening yourselves on the choicest of every offering of Israel, my people?

Therefore, declares the LORD, the God of Israel: I did say that your house and the house of your ancestor would walk before me for ever. But now, declares the LORD, far be it from me! Those who honour me I will honour, and those who despise me will be made light of.
Look, days are coming when I'll cut off your arm and the arm of your ancestor's house, so that there won't be an old man in your house.
And you will look on the distress of my dwelling, in all the good he does to Israel; and there will never be an old man in your house.
And I will not cut off every man of yours from my altar — one will be left, to make your eyes fail and to grieve your being; and all the increase of your house will die as men.
And this will be the sign for you, which will come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: on a single day the two of them will die.
And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest. He will do what is in my heart and in my being, and I will build him a sure house, and he will walk before my anointed all the days.
And everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a payment of silver and a loaf of bread, and say, 'Attach me, please, to one of the priestly offices, so I can eat a piece of bread.'

1 samuel_3.t: The boy Samuel was serving the LORD before Eli. The word of the LORD was rare in those days; vision was not widespread.
And on that day, when Eli was lying in his place — his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he couldn't see —
and the lamp of God hadn't yet gone out, and Samuel was lying in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was —
the LORD called to Samuel, and he said, 'Here I am.'
He ran to Eli and said, 'Here I am — you called me.' And Eli said, 'I didn't call. Go back and lie down.' So he went and lay down.
And the LORD called again: 'Samuel!' And Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am — you called me.' And he said, 'I didn't call, my son. Go back and lie down.'
Now Samuel didn't yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD hadn't yet been revealed to him.
And the LORD called Samuel again, a third time. He got up and went to Eli and said, 'Here I am — you called me.' And Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.
And Eli said to Samuel, 'Go and lie down; and if he calls you, say, "Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening."' So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
And the LORD came and stood, and called as before: 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak, for your servant is listening.'
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Look, I am about to do a thing in Israel that will make both ears of everyone who hears it tingle.'
On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.
And I have told him that I am about to judge his house for ever, for the iniquity he knew about: that his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he didn't rebuke them.
And so I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of the house of Eli will never be atoned for by sacrifice or by offering.
Samuel lay there until morning, and then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. And Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
And Eli called Samuel and said, 'Samuel, my son.' And he said, 'Here I am.'
And he said, 'What is the word he spoke to you? Don't hide it from me. May God do so to you, and more also, if you hide from me a single word of all he spoke to you.'
So Samuel told him all the words and hid nothing from him. And he said, 'He is the LORD. Let him do what is good in his eyes.'
And Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was established as a prophet to the LORD.
And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, because the LORD revealed himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

1 samuel_4.t: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle and encamped at Ebenezer, while the Philistines encamped at Aphek.
The Philistines deployed to meet Israel, the battle spread, and Israel was defeated before the Philistines. They struck down about four thousand men in the battle line, in the field.

When the people came into the camp, the elders of Israel said, 'Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let's bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so it may come among us and deliver us from the hand of our enemies.'

So the people sent to Shiloh and carried from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli were there with the ark of the covenant of God — Hophni and Phinehas.
And when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel gave a great shout, and the ground shook.
The Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said, 'What is this great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?' And they knew that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, 'A god has come into the camp.' And they said, 'Woe to us! Nothing like this has ever happened before.'
Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness.
Be strong, be men, Philistines — or you'll serve the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men, and fight!
So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tents. The slaughter was very great: thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
And the ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli died — Hophni and Phinehas.
A man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that day, his garments torn and earth on his head.
When he came, Eli was sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, because his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And the man came to tell it in the city, and the whole city cried out.
Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, 'What is this sound of uproar?' And the man hurried and came and told Eli.
Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed, so that he could not see.
And the man said to Eli, 'I'm the one who has come from the battle line — I fled from the battle line today.' And he said, 'What has happened, my son?'

And the bearer of news answered, 'Israel has fled before the Philistines. There's been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons have died — Hophni and Phinehas. And the ark of God has been taken.'
