And when he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backwards off his seat, beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died — for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.

His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the report that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she crouched down and gave birth, for her pangs had come upon her.
And about the time of her death, the women standing over her said, 'Don't be afraid — you've borne a son.' But she didn't answer, and she paid no attention.
And she called the boy Ichabod, saying, 'Glory has gone into exile from Israel' — because the ark of God had been taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
And she said, 'Glory has gone into exile from Israel, because the ark of God has been taken.'

1 samuel_5.t: The Philistines took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
The Philistines took the ark of God, brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.
The Ashdodites rose early the next day, and there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and put him back in his place.

They rose early the next morning, and there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD — and the head of Dagon and the two palms of his hands were cut off, on the threshold. Only Dagon was left of him.
That is why the priests of Dagon and all who enter the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, to this day.
And the hand of the LORD was heavy against the Ashdodites. He devastated them and struck them with tumours — Ashdod and its territories.
When the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, 'The ark of the God of Israel is not to remain with us, for his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.'

So they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, 'What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?' And they said, 'Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought round to Gath.' And they brought the ark of the God of Israel round.
And after they had brought it round, the hand of the LORD was against the city — a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumours broke out on them.
So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And when the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, 'They have brought round to me the ark of the God of Israel, to kill me and my people!'

So they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, 'Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it return to its own place, so it won't kill me and my people.' For there was a panic of death in all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
And the men who didn't die were struck with tumours, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

1 samuel_6.t: The ark of the LORD was in the region of the Philistines seven months.
The Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, 'What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back to its place.'

And they said, 'If you're sending away the ark of the God of Israel, don't send it away empty — send back a guilt offering with it. Then you'll be healed, and you'll know why his hand doesn't turn aside from you.'

And they said, 'What guilt offering shall we send back to him?' And they said, 'By the number of the rulers of the Philistines — five gold tumours and five gold mice. For one plague was on all of them and on your rulers.'
Make images of your tumours and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he'll lighten his hand from you, from your gods and from your land.
Why harden your heart, as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Wasn't it when he had dealt wantonly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
Now take and make a new cart and two nursing cows that have never had a yoke on them. Harness the cows to the cart and take their calves back home, away from them.
Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart, and put the articles of gold that you're sending back to him as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send it away, and let it go.

Then watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory, to Beth-shemesh, then he has done us this great harm. And if not, then we'll know it wasn't his hand that touched us — it was chance that happened to us.
The men did so. They took two nursing cows, harnessed them to the cart, and shut their calves up at home.
And they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, with the box, the gold mice and the images of their tumours.

The cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh. They kept to one highway, going and lowing, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the rulers of the Philistines went after them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
The people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

The cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there, where there was a large stone. They split up the wood of the cart and offered the cows up as a burnt offering to the LORD.

And the Levites brought down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and put them on the large stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.
The five rulers of the Philistines saw it and returned to Ekron that day.
These are the gold tumours that the Philistines sent back as a guilt offering to the LORD: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

And the gold mice were the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to open village — and as far as Abel the great, on which they set down the ark of the LORD, to this day, in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

And he struck down among the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the LORD; and he struck down among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, because the LORD had struck the people with a great blow.
And the men of Beth-shemesh said, 'Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall he go up, away from us?'
So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim: 'The Philistines have brought back the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to yourselves.'

1 samuel_7.t: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
From the day the ark came to rest at Kiriath-jearim, the days grew many — twenty years — and all the house of Israel mourned after the LORD.

And Samuel said to all the house of Israel, 'If you are turning back to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods from among you, and the Ashtaroth. Direct your heart to the LORD and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.'
So the people of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD alone.
And Samuel said, 'Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I'll pray for you to the LORD.'
So they gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted that day, and said there, 'We have sinned against the LORD.' And Samuel judged the people of Israel at Mizpah.

When the Philistines heard that the people of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the people of Israel heard, they were afraid of the Philistines.
And the people of Israel said to Samuel, 'Don't keep silent toward us — cry out to the LORD our God, so he may deliver us from the hand of the Philistines.'
So Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it up as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. And Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

While Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great sound that day against the Philistines and routed them, and they were defeated before Israel.
And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah, pursued the Philistines and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
And Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, 'Until now the LORD has helped us.'
So the Philistines were brought low, and they did not come again into the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

The cities the Philistines had taken from Israel were returned to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath, and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
Year after year he would go on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.
And his return was to Ramah, because his house was there, and there he judged Israel. And he built an altar to the LORD there.

1 samuel_8.t: When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
But his sons did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after unjust gain, took bribes, and turned justice aside.
So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
And they said to him, 'Look, you've grown old, and your sons have not walked in your ways. Now appoint a king for us to judge us, like all the nations.'
The matter was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel when they said, 'Give us a king to judge us.' And Samuel prayed to the LORD.
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to the voice of the people in all they say to you. It is not you they have rejected — they have rejected me from reigning over them.'
Just as they have done in all their deeds from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day — forsaking me and serving other gods — so they are doing to you as well.
So now, listen to their voice — only warn them solemnly, and tell them the right of the king who will reign over them.
And Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
And he said, 'This will be the right of the king who will reign over you. He will take your sons and put them in his chariotry and among his horsemen, and they'll run before his chariot;

he'll appoint commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties for himself, and set men to plough his ploughing and reap his reaping, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariotry.
He'll take your daughters as perfumers, cooks and bakers.
He'll take your fields, your vineyards and your best olive groves, and give them to his servants.
He'll take a tenth of your grain and your vineyards, and give it to his officials and his servants.
He'll take your male and female servants, your best young men and your donkeys, and put them to his work.
He'll take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his servants.
And on that day you'll cry out because of the king you have chosen for yourselves — and the LORD will not answer you on that day.
But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel. They said, 'No! We will have a king over us,
so that we too will be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.'
And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.
And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Listen to their voice, and make a king reign over them.' And Samuel said to the men of Israel, 'Go, each to his own city.'

1 samuel_9.t: There was a man from Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel son of Zeror son of Becorath son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a man of substance.
He had a son whose name was Saul, a young man and handsome. There was no one among the people of Israel better than he — from his shoulders up he was taller than all the people.
The donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost, and Kish said to Saul his son, 'Take one of the servants with you, get up and go and look for the donkeys.'

He passed through the hill country of Ephraim and the land of Shalishah, and they didn't find them. They passed through the land of Shaalim — nothing. He passed through the land of the Benjaminites, and they didn't find them.
They came into the land of Zuph, and Saul said to his servant, 'Come, let's turn back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.'
And he said to him, 'Look, there's a man of God in this city, and the man is honoured. Everything he says certainly comes to pass. Let's go there — perhaps he'll tell us the way we should go.'
And Saul said to his servant, 'But if we go, what shall we bring the man? The bread is used up from our bags, and there's no gift to bring to the man of God. What have we got?'
And the servant answered Saul again, 'Look, I have a quarter of a shekel of silver in my hand. I'll give it to the man of God, and he'll tell us our way.'
(Formerly in Israel, this is what a man would say when he went to consult God: 'Come, let's go to the seer' — because the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)
And Saul said to his servant, 'Your word is good. Come, let's go.' So they went to the city where the man of God was.
As they were going up the ascent to the city, they met young women coming out to draw water, and they said to them, 'Is the seer here?'
And they answered, 'He is — he's just ahead of you. Hurry now, because today he has come to the city, since there's a sacrifice today for the people at the high place.'

As soon as you come into the city you'll find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat — because the people won't eat until he comes, since he blesses the sacrifice, and after that those who are invited eat. Go up now, and you'll find him right away.
So they went up to the city. As they were coming into the middle of the city, there was Samuel coming out to meet them, on his way up to the high place.
Now the LORD had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came, saying:

'About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him as leader over my people Israel. He will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have seen my people; their cry has come to me.'
And Samuel saw Saul, and the LORD answered him: 'Here is the man I spoke to you about. This one is to rule over my people.'
And Saul went up to Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, 'Tell me, please — where is the house of the seer?'
And Samuel answered Saul, 'I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the high place, and you'll eat with me today. In the morning I'll send you away, and I'll tell you all that is in your heart.'
As for the donkeys lost to you three days ago, don't set your heart on them — they've been found. And to whom does all the desire of Israel belong? Isn't it to you and to all your father's house?
And Saul answered, 'Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And isn't my clan the least of all the clans of the tribes of Benjamin? Why have you spoken to me like this?'
And Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the room, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited — about thirty men.
And Samuel said to the cook, 'Bring the portion I gave you, the one I told you to put aside.'

And the cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it and set it before Saul. And he said, 'Here is what was kept back — set it before you and eat; it's been kept for you for this appointed time, as I said, "I have invited the people."' And Saul ate with Samuel that day.
Then they went down from the high place into the city, and he spoke with Saul on the roof.
They rose early, and as the dawn came up Samuel called to Saul on the roof, 'Get up, and I'll send you on your way.' So Saul got up, and the two of them went outside, he and Samuel.
As they were going down at the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, 'Tell the servant to go on ahead of us' — and he went on — 'and you stand still just now, and I'll let you hear the word of God.'

1 samuel_10.t: And Samuel took the flask of oil, poured it on his head and kissed him, and said, 'Has not the LORD anointed you over his inheritance as leader?'

When you leave me today, you'll find two men near Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin, at Zelzah, and they'll say to you, 'The donkeys you went to look for have been found. And now your father has left off the matter of the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'

You'll pass on from there and beyond and come to the great tree of Tabor, and three men will find you there, going up to God at Bethel — one carrying three kids, one carrying three round loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.
They'll greet you and give you two loaves of bread, and you'll take them from their hand.

After that you'll come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistine garrisons are. And as you come to the city you'll meet a company of prophets coming down from the high place, with a harp, a tambourine, a flute and a lyre before them, and they'll be prophesying.
And the spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you'll prophesy with them, and you'll be turned into another man.
And when these signs come to you, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.

And you are to go down ahead of me to Gilgal, and I'll come down to you to offer up burnt offerings and sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you, and I'll make known to you what you are to do.
And when he turned to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart; and all these signs came that day.
They came to Gibeah, and there was a company of prophets to meet him. And the spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
And when all who knew him from before saw him prophesying with prophets, the people said to one another, 'What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?'
And a man from there answered, 'And who is their father?' That is why it became a proverb: 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'
And he finished prophesying and came to the high place.
And Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, 'Where did you go?' And he said, 'To look for the donkeys. And when we saw they weren't there, we went to Samuel.'
And Saul's uncle said, 'Tell me, please — what did Samuel say to you?'
And Saul said to his uncle, 'He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found.' But the matter of the kingship, which Samuel had spoken of, he did not tell him.
And Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.

And he said to the people of Israel, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought Israel up from Egypt and delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.

And today you have rejected your God, who is your deliverer from all your calamities and troubles, and you have said to him, "Set a king over us." So now, present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands.'
So Samuel brought near all the tribes of Israel, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
He brought near the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of the Matrite was taken; and Saul son of Kish was taken. But when they looked for him, he wasn't found.
So they enquired again of the LORD, 'Has the man come here yet?' And the LORD said, 'He's hiding among the baggage.'
So they ran and took him from there, and he presented himself among the people — and he was taller than all the people from his shoulders up.
And Samuel said to all the people, 'Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is none like him among all the people.' And all the people shouted, 'Long live the king!'
And Samuel spoke to the people the right of the kingship, wrote it in the book and set it before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each to his house.
And Saul too went to his house at Gibeah, and the force whose heart God had touched went with him.
But sons of worthlessness said, 'How is this one going to deliver us?' And they despised him and brought him no gift. And he acted as though he had not heard.

1 samuel_11.t: Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead, and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, 'Make a covenant with us, and we'll serve you.'
And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, 'On this condition I'll make it with you: that I gouge out every right eye of yours — and I'll make it a reproach on all Israel.'
And the elders of Jabesh said to him, 'Give us seven days, and let us send messengers through all the territory of Israel. If there's no one to deliver us, we'll come out to you.'
The messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the hearing of the people, and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
And there was Saul, coming in after the cattle from the field. And Saul said, 'What's the matter with the people, that they're weeping?' And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
And the spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned fiercely.

So he took a pair of oxen, cut them in pieces and sent them through all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, 'Whoever doesn't come out after Saul and after Samuel — this is what will be done to his oxen.' And the dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
He mustered them at Bezek: the people of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

And they said to the messengers who had come, 'This is what you are to say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: Tomorrow deliverance will be yours, when the sun is hot.' And the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.
And the men of Jabesh said, 'Tomorrow we'll come out to you, and you can do to us whatever seems good to you.'

The next day Saul set the people in three companies. They came into the middle of the camp in the morning watch and struck down Ammon until the heat of the day. Those who were left were scattered, and no two of them were left together.
And the people said to Samuel, 'Who was it who said, "Shall Saul reign over us?" Hand the men over, and we'll put them to death.'
And Saul said, 'No one is to be put to death on this day, because today the LORD has done deliverance in Israel.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'Come, let's go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.'

So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD at Gilgal. They sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings there before the LORD, and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

1 samuel_12.t: And Samuel said to all Israel, 'Look, I have listened to your voice in all you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
And now the king walks before you, and I am old and grey-haired, and my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed: Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I oppressed? Whom have I crushed? From whose hand have I taken a ransom, to blind my eyes with it? And I'll restore it to you.'
And they said, 'You haven't oppressed us, you haven't crushed us, and you haven't taken anything from anyone's hand.'
And he said to them, 'The LORD is a witness against you, and his anointed is a witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.' And he said, 'He is a witness.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'It is the LORD, who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors up from the land of Egypt.
So now, present yourselves, and let me enter into judgement with you before the LORD, concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did with you and with your ancestors.
When Jacob came to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the LORD, and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your ancestors out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

But they forgot the LORD their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab — and they fought against them.
And they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. Now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we'll serve you.'
And the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you from the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelt in security.
And you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was coming against you, and you said to me, 'No — a king shall reign over us' — while the LORD your God was your king.
And now, here is the king you have chosen, the one you asked for — and the LORD has set a king over you.
If you fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice, and don't rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be after the LORD your God —
And if you don't listen to the voice of the LORD, and you rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your ancestors.
Now stand and see this great thing that the LORD is about to do before your eyes.

Isn't it the wheat harvest today? I'll call to the LORD, and he'll give thunder and rain. Know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of the LORD by asking for yourselves a king.
So Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD gave thunder and rain that day; and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
And all the people said to Samuel, 'Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, so that we won't die — because we have added to all our sins an evil, by asking for ourselves a king.'
And Samuel said to the people, 'Don't be afraid. You have done all this evil — but don't turn aside from following the LORD; serve the LORD with all your heart.
Don't turn aside — that would be after emptiness, which can't benefit and can't rescue, because they are emptiness.
For the LORD will not abandon his people, for the sake of his great name; the LORD was pleased to make you a people for himself.
As for me, far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will teach you the good and upright way.
Only fear the LORD and serve him in faithfulness with all your heart — consider what great things he has done with you.
But if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.

1 samuel_13.t: Saul was a year old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel.

Saul chose three thousand men from Israel for himself. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, each to his tents.
Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the ram's horn throughout all the land, saying, 'Let the Hebrews hear!'
And all Israel heard it said, 'Saul has struck the Philistine garrison, and Israel has made itself odious among the Philistines.' And the people were summoned after Saul to Gilgal.

The Philistines gathered to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and a people like the sand on the seashore for multitude. They came up and encamped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
The men of Israel saw that they were in distress, for the people were hard pressed, and they hid themselves in caves, thickets, rocks, underground chambers and cisterns.
And Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
He waited seven days, to the appointed time Samuel had set; but Samuel didn't come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
And Saul said, 'Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.' And he offered up the burnt offering.
And just as he finished offering up the burnt offering, Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him, to bless him.

And Samuel said, 'What have you done?' And Saul said, 'I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you hadn't come at the appointed time of the days, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
so I said, "Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I haven't entreated the face of the LORD." So I forced myself, and I offered up the burnt offering.'

And Samuel said to Saul, 'You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which he commanded you — for now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for ever.

And now your kingdom will not stand. The LORD has sought out for himself a man according to his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him as leader over his people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.'
And Samuel got up and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul mustered the people who were found with him — about six hundred men.
Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines encamped at Michmash.
And the raiding party went out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
one company turned toward the road to Beth-horon; and one company turned toward the road of the border that looks down over the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
No craftsman was to be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines said, 'The Hebrews might make a sword or a spear.'
So all Israel would go down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his ploughshare, his mattock, his axe and his ploughshare.
And the charge was a pim for the ploughshares, the mattocks, the three-pronged fork and the axes, and for setting the goad straight.
And so on the day of battle, no sword or spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan — but Saul and Jonathan his son had them.
And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

1 samuel_14.t: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armour, 'Come, let's cross over to the garrison of the Philistines on the other side.' But he didn't tell his father.
Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree at Migron, and the people with him were about six hundred men.
Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was bearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

Between the passes by which Jonathan meant to cross over to the Philistine garrison there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other. The name of the one was Bozez and the name of the other Seneh.
The one crag stood as a pillar on the north, opposite Michmash, and the other on the south, opposite Geba.

And Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armour, 'Come, let's cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us — there's no restraint on the LORD, to deliver by many or by few.'
And his armour-bearer said to him, 'Do everything that is in your heart. Turn wherever you will — here I am with you, whatever your heart says.'
And Jonathan said, 'Look, we're crossing over to the men, and we'll reveal ourselves to them.
If they say to us, "Stand still until we reach you," then we'll stand where we are and won't go up to them.
And if they say, "Come up to us," then we'll go up, because the LORD has given them into our hand. That will be the sign for us.'
So the two of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines, and the Philistines said, 'Look — Hebrews coming out of the holes where they've hidden themselves.'

And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armour-bearer, 'Come up to us, and we'll tell you something.' And Jonathan said to his armour-bearer, 'Come up after me — the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel.'
So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armour-bearer after him. And they fell before Jonathan, and his armour-bearer was killing after him.
The first slaughter that Jonathan and his armour-bearer struck was about twenty men, within about half a furrow of an acre of field.
And there was trembling in the camp, in the field and among all the people. The garrison and the raiding party trembled too. And the earth quaked, and it became a trembling of God.
And Saul's watchmen at Gibeah of Benjamin saw the multitude melting away, going this way and that.
And Saul said to the people with him, 'Muster now and see who has gone from us.' So they mustered, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer were not there.
And Saul said to Ahijah, 'Bring near the ark of God' — for on that day the ark of God was with the people of Israel.
And while Saul was speaking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Philistines kept growing and growing. And Saul said to the priest, 'Withdraw your hand.'
So Saul and all the people with him were called together, and they came to the battle. And each man's sword was against his neighbour — a very great panic.
And the Hebrews who had belonged to the Philistines as before, who had gone up with them into the camp round about — they too turned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.
And every man of Israel who had hidden in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they too joined the pursuit in the battle.
So the LORD delivered Israel that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

And the men of Israel were hard pressed that day, because Saul had put the people under an oath: 'Cursed be the man who eats food before evening, until I have avenged myself on my enemies.' And none of the people tasted food.
And all the land came into the forest, and there was honey on the surface of the field.
And the people came into the forest, and there was honey flowing — but no one put his hand to his mouth, because the people feared the oath.

But Jonathan hadn't heard when his father put the people under the oath. He stretched out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb, brought his hand back to his mouth — and his eyes brightened.
And a man from the people said, 'Your father solemnly put the people under an oath: "Cursed be the man who eats food today."' And the people were weary.
And Jonathan said, 'My father has troubled the land. Look how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
How much more, if the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of their enemies that they found! As it is, the defeat among the Philistines hasn't been great.'
They struck down the Philistines that day, from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very weary.
And the people rushed on the plunder, took sheep, cattle and calves, slaughtered them on the ground, and ate with the blood.
And they told Saul, 'Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood.' And he said, 'You have acted treacherously. Roll a large stone to me today.'

And Saul said, 'Scatter among the people and tell them, "Each of you bring me his ox and his sheep, and slaughter here and eat — and don't sin against the LORD by eating with the blood."' And all the people brought near, each his ox in his hand, that night, and slaughtered there.
And Saul built an altar to the LORD. This was the first altar he began to build to the LORD.

And Saul said, 'Let's go down after the Philistines by night and plunder among them until the light of morning, and not leave a man of them.' And they said, 'Do whatever is good in your eyes.' And the priest said, 'Let us draw near here to God.'
And Saul enquired of God, 'Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?' But he didn't answer him that day.
And Saul said, 'Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see how this sin has come about today.
For as the LORD lives, who delivers Israel — even if it's in Jonathan my son, he will surely die.' And not one of all the people answered him.
And he said to all Israel, 'You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son on the other.' And the people said to Saul, 'Do what is good in your eyes.'
And Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, 'Give Thummim.' And Jonathan and Saul were taken, and the people went free.
And Saul said, 'Cast between me and Jonathan my son.' And Jonathan was taken.
And Saul said to Jonathan, 'Tell me what you have done.' And Jonathan told him, 'I did taste a little honey with the end of the staff in my hand. Here I am. I will die.'
And Saul said, 'May God do so to me, and more also — you shall surely die, Jonathan.'

And the people said to Saul, 'Shall Jonathan die — the man who has done this great deliverance in Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground, for he has acted with God this day.' And the people redeemed Jonathan, and he did not die.
So Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.
And Saul took the kingship over Israel and waged war round about against all his enemies — Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah and the Philistines. And wherever he turned, he routed them.
He did valiantly and struck Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered it.
The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi and Malchi-shua; and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab and the name of the younger Michal.
The name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz, and the name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
Kish was Saul's father, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
The war was severe against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and whenever Saul saw a mighty man or a man of strength, he gathered him to himself.

1 samuel_15.t: And Samuel said to Saul, 'It was I whom the LORD sent to anoint you as king over his people, over Israel. Now listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.'
This is what the LORD of hosts says: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how it set itself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that it has. Do not spare it, but put to death man and woman, child and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'
So Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.
And Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the wadi.

And Saul said to the Kenites, 'Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, or I'll sweep you away with them — for you showed loyalty to all the people of Israel when they came up from Egypt.' And the Kenites departed from among Amalek.
And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is opposite Egypt.
And he took Agag king of Amalek alive, and devoted all the people to destruction with the edge of the sword.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle, the fatlings and the lambs, and everything that was good. They weren't willing to devote them to destruction — but all the property that was despised and worthless, that they devoted to destruction.
And the word of the LORD came to Samuel:
'I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not carried out my words.' And Samuel was angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.

And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, and it was told to Samuel, 'Saul came to Carmel, and there he was setting up a monument for himself; then he turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.'
And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, 'Blessed are you to the LORD! I have carried out the word of the LORD.'
And Samuel said, 'And what is this sound of sheep in my ears, and the sound of cattle that I hear?'
And Saul said, 'They brought them from the Amalekites — the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle in order to sacrifice to the LORD your God. And the rest we devoted to destruction.'
And Samuel said to Saul, 'Stop — and let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.' And he said, 'Speak.'
And Samuel said, 'Wasn't it when you were small in your own eyes that you became the head of the tribes of Israel? And the LORD anointed you as king over Israel.
And the LORD sent you on a journey and said, "Go and devote to destruction the sinners, Amalek, and wage war against them until they are finished."
So why didn't you listen to the voice of the LORD? Why did you rush on the plunder and do the evil in the eyes of the LORD?'
And Saul said to Samuel, 'I did listen to the voice of the LORD. I went on the journey the LORD sent me on; I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.
But the people took from the plunder sheep and cattle, the choicest of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.'
And Samuel said: Has the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? See, to listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you from being king.
And Saul said to Samuel, 'I have sinned. I transgressed the mouth of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
Now please forgive my sin, and return with me, so I can bow down to the LORD.'
And Samuel said to Saul, 'I will not return with you. You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.'
And Samuel turned round to go, and Saul caught hold of the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
And Samuel said to him, 'The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and given it to your neighbour, who is better than you.
And the Glory of Israel does not deal falsely and does not regret — for he is not a man, that he should regret.'
And he said, 'I have sinned. Now honour me, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel; and return with me, and I'll bow down to the LORD your God.'
So Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.
And Samuel said, 'Bring me Agag king of Amalek.' And Agag came to him cheerfully. And Agag said, 'Truly the bitterness of death has departed.'
And Samuel said, 'As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women.' And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
And Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

1 samuel_16.t: And the LORD said to Samuel, 'How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I'm sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite — I have seen among his sons a king for myself.'
And Samuel said, 'How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me.' And the LORD said, 'Take a heifer of the herd with you and say, "I have come to sacrifice to the LORD."'
Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I'll make known to you what you are to do; and you are to anoint for me the one I tell you.
So Samuel did what the LORD had said and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, 'Do you come in peace?'
And he said, 'In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.' And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
And when they came, he saw Eliab and said, 'Surely the LORD's anointed is before him.'

And the LORD said to Samuel, 'Don't look at his appearance or at the height of his stature — I have rejected him. It is not what a human sees: a human sees by the eyes, but the LORD sees by the heart.'
And Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel, and he said, 'Neither has the LORD chosen this one.'
And Jesse made Shammah pass by, and he said, 'Neither has the LORD chosen this one.'
And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, 'The LORD has not chosen these.'

And Samuel said to Jesse, 'Are these all your young men?' And he said, 'The youngest still remains — he's out shepherding the flock.' And Samuel said to Jesse, 'Send and bring him. We won't sit down until he comes here.'
So he sent and brought him. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and good to look at. And the LORD said, 'Get up and anoint him — this is he.'
And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and the spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day onwards. And Samuel got up and went to Ramah.
And the spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him.
And Saul's servants said to him, 'Look, an evil spirit of God is terrifying you.

Let our lord say the word — your servants are here before you — and let them look for a man who knows how to play the lyre; and when an evil spirit of God is upon you, he'll play, and it will be good for you.'
And Saul said to his servants, 'Find me a man who plays well, and bring him to me.'

And one of the young men answered, 'Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play — a mighty man of valour, a man of war, discerning in speech, a man of form; and the LORD is with him.'
And Saul sent messengers to Jesse: 'Send me David your son, who is with the flock.'
And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.
And David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armour-bearer.
And Saul sent to Jesse: 'Let David stand before me, for he has found favour in my eyes.'
And whenever a spirit of God was upon Saul, David would take the lyre and play, and there would be relief for Saul; it was good for him, and the evil spirit departed from him.

1 samuel_17.t: The Philistines gathered their armies for battle. They gathered at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes-dammim.
And Saul and the men of Israel gathered and encamped in the Valley of Elah, and deployed for battle to meet the Philistines.
The Philistines stood on the mountain on one side and Israel on the mountain on the other, with the valley between them.
And a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines. His name was Goliath, from Gath. His height was six cubits and a span.
A bronze helmet was on his head, and he was clothed in scale body armour; and the weight of the body armour was five thousand shekels of bronze.
Bronze leg armour was on his legs, and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.
The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the blade of his spear was six hundred shekels of iron; and the bearer of his body shield walked before him.

And he stood and called out to the battle lines of Israel, 'Why do you come out to deploy for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
If he's able to fight with me and strike me down, then we'll become your slaves; and if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you'll become our slaves and serve us.'
And the Philistine said, 'I defy the battle lines of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let's fight together.'
And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
Now David was the son of that Ephrathite man from Bethlehem of Judah, whose name was Jesse, and he had eight sons. In the days of Saul the man was old, well on in years.
The three eldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who had gone into the battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab his second, and Shammah the third.
And David was the youngest, and the three eldest had gone after Saul.
And David went back and forth from Saul to shepherd his father's flock at Bethlehem.
And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and took his stand for forty days.
And Jesse said to David his son, 'Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers, and hurry them to the camp.
And take these ten portions of cheese to the commander of the thousand. Enquire after your brothers' welfare, and bring back some token from them.'
Now Saul and they and every man of Israel were in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines.

David rose early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, took up the load and went, just as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the camp as the army was going out to the battle line, and they shouted the war cry for the battle.
And Israel and the Philistines deployed, battle line facing battle line.
David left the baggage with the keeper of the baggage and ran to the battle line, and came and greeted his brothers.
And while he was speaking with them, the champion was coming up — Goliath the Philistine was his name, from Gath — from the battle lines of the Philistines. He spoke the same words, and David heard.
And every man of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

And the men of Israel said, 'Have you seen this man who comes up? He comes up to defy Israel. And the man who strikes him down — the king will make him rich with great riches, give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel.'

And David said to the men standing with him, 'What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has defied the battle lines of the living God?'
And the people answered him in the same way: 'So it will be done for the man who strikes him down.'

And Eliab his eldest brother heard him speaking to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said, 'Why have you come down? And who did you leave those few sheep with in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness of your heart — you came down to see the battle.'
And David said, 'What have I done now? Was it not just a word?'
And he turned away from him toward another and said the same thing, and the people answered him as before.
And the words David spoke were heard and reported before Saul, and he sent for him.
And David said to Saul, 'Let no one's heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight this Philistine.'
And Saul said to David, 'You're not able to go against this Philistine and fight him — you're a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth.'
And David said to Saul, 'Your servant was shepherding his father's flock, and a lion came — and a bear — and carried off a sheep from the flock.
And I went out after it, struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth; and when it rose up against me, I took hold of its beard, struck it and killed it.
Your servant has struck down both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has defied the battle lines of the living God.'

And David said, 'The LORD, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine.' And Saul said to David, 'Go, and may the LORD be with you.'
And Saul clothed David in his own garments, put a bronze helmet on his head and clothed him in body armour.
And David girded his sword over the garments and tried to walk, because he hadn't tested them. And David said to Saul, 'I can't walk in these — I haven't tested them.' And David took them off.
And he took his stick in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the wadi and put them in the shepherds' bag he had — in the pouch — with his sling in his hand; and he drew near to the Philistine.
And the Philistine came on, drawing near to David, with the man who bore the body shield before him.
And the Philistine looked and saw David, and despised him — he was a youth, ruddy, with a handsome appearance.
And the Philistine said to David, 'Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?' And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
And the Philistine said to David, 'Come to me, and I'll give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and the animals of the field.'

And David said to the Philistine, 'You come against me with sword and spear and javelin; and I come against you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the battle lines of Israel, whom you have defied.

This day the LORD will deliver you up into my hand, and I'll strike you down and take your head from you. And I'll give the corpses of the Philistine camp this day to the birds of the heavens and the animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that Israel has a God.
And all this assembly will know that the LORD does not save by sword or spear — for the battle is the LORD's, and he will give you into our hand.'
And when the Philistine got up and came and drew near to meet David, David hurried and ran to the battle line to meet the Philistine.
And David put his hand into the bag, took out a stone, slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
So David was stronger than the Philistine with the sling and the stone; he struck the Philistine down and killed him — and there was no sword in David's hand.
And David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, killed him and cut off his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, they fled.

And the men of Israel and Judah arose, shouted the war cry and pursued the Philistines as far as the entrance to Gath and the gates of Ekron. The slain of the Philistines fell on the road to Shaaraim, and as far as Gath and Ekron.
And the people of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camps.
And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and put his weapons in his own tent.
And when Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, 'Whose son is this youth, Abner?' And Abner said, 'As you live, O king, I do not know.'
And the king said, 'You find out whose son the young man is.'
And when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
And Saul said to him, 'Whose son are you, young man?' And David said, 'The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.'

1 samuel_18.t: And when he had finished speaking to Saul, the being of Jonathan was bound to the being of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own being.
And Saul took him that day and would not let him return to his father's house.
And Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own being.
And Jonathan stripped off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, with his garments, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.
And David went out wherever Saul sent him and prospered, and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people, and of Saul's servants too.

And as they were coming, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, the women came out from all the cities of Israel with singing and dancing, to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy and with three-stringed instruments.
And the women who played sang out: Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
And Saul burned with anger, and this matter was displeasing in his eyes. He said, 'They have ascribed ten thousands to David, and to me the thousands. What more is there for him but the kingship?'
And Saul kept his eye on David from that day onwards.
The next day an evil spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house. David was playing with his hand as he did day by day, and the spear was in Saul's hand.
And Saul hurled the spear, saying, 'I'll pin David to the wall!' And David turned aside from before him twice.
And Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him and had turned aside from Saul.
So Saul removed him from his presence and made him a commander of a thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.
And David prospered in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.
And Saul saw that he was prospering greatly, and he was in dread of him.
And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.

And Saul said to David, 'Here is my elder daughter Merab. I'll give her to you as a wife. Only be a man of valour for me and fight the battles of the LORD.' For Saul thought, 'Let my hand not be against him — let the hand of the Philistines be against him.'
And David said to Saul, 'Who am I, and who are my kinsfolk, my father's clan in Israel, that I should be the king's son-in-law?'
And at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.
And Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David; and they told Saul, and the matter was right in his eyes.

And Saul thought, 'I'll give her to him, and she'll become a snare for him, and the hand of the Philistines will be against him.' And Saul said to David, 'By the second one you shall be my son-in-law today.'
And Saul commanded his servants, 'Speak to David in secret: "Look, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you. Now be the king's son-in-law."'
And Saul's servants spoke these words in David's hearing, and David said, 'Is it a small thing in your eyes to be the king's son-in-law, when I'm a poor man and lightly esteemed?'
And Saul's servants reported to him, 'This is what David said.'

And Saul said, 'This is what you are to say to David: The king has no delight in a bride-price — only in a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to avenge himself on the king's enemies.' And Saul planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
And his servants told David these words, and the matter was right in David's eyes, to be the king's son-in-law. And before the days were completed,

David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred of the Philistines. And David brought their foreskins and they gave them in full to the king, to be the king's son-in-law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.
And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.
And Saul was still more afraid of David, and Saul was David's enemy all his days.
And the commanders of the Philistines went out; and as often as they went out, David was more successful than all Saul's servants, and his name was greatly esteemed.

1 samuel_19.t: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David — but Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted in David exceedingly.
And Jonathan told David, 'Saul my father is seeking to kill you. Take care in the morning — stay in a hiding place and hide yourself.'
And I'll go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I'll speak about you to my father. And whatever I see, I'll tell you.
And Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father: 'Let the king not sin against his servant David — he hasn't sinned against you, and his deeds have been very good for you.

He put his life in his palm and struck down the Philistine, and the LORD made a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. So why will you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?'
And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, 'As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.'
And Jonathan called David and told him all these words. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.
And the war continued. David went out and fought the Philistines and struck them with a great defeat, and they fled from him.
And an evil spirit of the LORD was upon Saul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing with his hand.
And Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from Saul, and the spear struck the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
And Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and kill him in the morning. And Michal his wife told David, 'If you don't save your life tonight, tomorrow you'll be put to death.'
And Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.
And Michal took the teraphim, put it on the bed, put the quilt of goats' hair at its head and covered it with the garment.
And Saul sent messengers to fetch David, and she said, 'He is sick.'
And Saul sent the messengers to see David: 'Bring him up to me on the bed, so I can kill him.'
And the messengers came, and there was the teraphim on the bed, with the quilt of goats' hair at its head.
And Saul said to Michal, 'Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he escaped?' And Michal said to Saul, 'He said to me, "Let me go — why should I kill you?"'
And David fled and escaped and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.
And Saul was told, 'David is at Naioth in Ramah.'

And Saul sent messengers to fetch David; and they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing as chief over them. And the spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.
And they told Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers a third time, and they also prophesied.
And he went himself to Ramah, and came as far as the great cistern at Secu, and asked, 'Where are Samuel and David?' And someone said, 'At Naioth in Ramah.'
And he went there, to Naioth in Ramah, and the spirit of God came upon him too, and he went on, prophesying as he went, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay naked all that day and all night. That is why they say, 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'

1 samuel_20.t: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said before Jonathan, 'What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he's seeking my life?'
And he said to him, 'Far be it! You will not die. Look, my father does nothing great or small without uncovering my ear — so why should my father hide this from me? It isn't so.'

And David swore again, 'Your father knows well that I have found favour in your eyes, and he has said, "Don't let Jonathan know this, or he'll be grieved." But as the LORD lives and as you live, there's only a step between me and death.'
And Jonathan said to David, 'Whatever you say, I'll do for you.'
And David said to Jonathan, 'Look, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should be sitting with the king to eat. But let me go, and I'll hide myself in the field until the third evening.
If your father misses me at all, say, "David asked my leave urgently to run to Bethlehem his town, because the yearly sacrifice is there for all the clan."
If he says, "Good," then your servant is safe. But if he burns with anger, know that the harm has been determined by him.
And do loyalty to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. And if there's iniquity in me, kill me yourself — but why bring me to your father?'
And Jonathan said, 'Far be it from you! If I ever know that the harm has been determined by my father to come upon you, wouldn't I tell you?'
And David said to Jonathan, 'Who will tell me? Or what if your father answers you harshly?'
And Jonathan said to David, 'Come, let's go out to the field.' And the two of them went out to the field.

And Jonathan said to David, 'The LORD, God of Israel — when I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and there is good toward David, shall I not then send to you and uncover your ear?

May the LORD do so to Jonathan, and more also, if it seems good to my father to bring the harm upon you and I don't uncover your ear and send you away, so you go in peace. And may the LORD be with you, as he has been with my father.
And while I am still alive, may you not fail to do the loyalty of the LORD with me, so that I do not die;
and may you not cut off your loyalty from my house for ever — not even when the LORD cuts off the enemies of David, every one, from the face of the ground.
And Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David: 'And may the LORD require it at the hand of David's enemies.'
And Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him with the love of his own being.
And Jonathan said to him, 'Tomorrow is the new moon, and you'll be missed, because your seat will be empty.
And on the third day go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself when the business was in hand, and stay beside the stone Ezel.
And I'll shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though shooting at a target.

And I'll send the lad: "Go, find the arrows." If I say plainly to the lad, "Look, the arrows are on this side of you" — then fetch it and come, because you're safe and there's nothing wrong, as the LORD lives.
But if I say to the young man, "Look, the arrows are beyond you" — go, for the LORD has sent you away.
And as for what we have spoken, you and I — the LORD is between me and you for ever.
So David hid himself in the field. And when the new moon came, the king sat down to eat.
And the king sat on his seat as usual, on the seat by the wall. Jonathan arose, and Abner sat at Saul's side, and David's place was empty.
And Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, 'It's an accident. He isn't clean — surely he isn't clean.'
And on the next day, the second of the new moon, David's place was empty, and Saul said to Jonathan his son, 'Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?'
And Jonathan answered Saul, 'David asked my leave urgently for Bethlehem,

and he said, "Let me go, because we have a clan sacrifice in the town, and my brother himself has ordered me to come. Now, if I have found favour in your eyes, let me slip away and see my brothers." That is why he hasn't come to the king's table.'

And Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, 'Son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Don't I know that you're choosing the son of Jesse — to your own shame and to the shame of your mother's nakedness?'
For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, you will not be established, you and your kingdom. Now send and fetch him to me — he is a son of death.'
And Jonathan answered Saul his father, 'Why should he be put to death? What has he done?'
And Saul hurled the spear at him to strike him; and Jonathan knew that it had been determined by his father to kill David.
And Jonathan got up from the table in the heat of anger, and he ate no food on the second day of the new moon, because he was grieved concerning David, and because his father had put him to shame.
In the morning Jonathan went out to the field at the time appointed with David, with a small lad with him.
And he said to his lad, 'Run, find the arrows I'm shooting.' The lad ran, and he shot the arrow to make it pass beyond him.
And the lad came to the place of the arrow Jonathan had shot, and Jonathan called after the lad, 'Isn't the arrow beyond you?'
And Jonathan called after the lad, 'Quick, hurry, don't stand still!' And Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows and came to his master.
And the lad knew nothing. Only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
And Jonathan gave his weapons to the lad who was with him and said, 'Go, take them to the city.'
The lad went, and David got up from beside the south side, fell on his face to the ground and bowed down three times. And they kissed one another and wept with one another, until David wept the more.

And Jonathan said to David, 'Go in peace, since we have both sworn, the two of us, by the name of the LORD: "The LORD will be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, for ever."' And he got up and went, and Jonathan came to the city.

1 samuel_21.t: And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech trembled at meeting David and said to him, 'Why are you alone, with no man with you?'

And David said to Ahimelech the priest, 'The king has given me an order, and he said to me, "Let no one know anything about the matter I am sending you on, or what I have commanded you." And I have directed the young men to such and such a place.
So now, what have you got? Give me five loaves, or whatever can be found.'
And the priest answered David, 'I have no common bread to hand, but there is holy bread — if only the young men have kept themselves from a woman.'

And David answered the priest, 'Indeed, woman has been withheld from us as before, when I came out; and the vessels of the young men were holy — and this is a common journey; how much more will it be holy today in the vessel.'

And the priest gave him what was holy, because there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD, to put hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away.
And a man of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's shepherds.
And David said to Ahimelech, 'Isn't there a spear or a sword here under your hand? I brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent.'

And the priest said, 'The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the valley of Elah — it's wrapped in a cloak behind the ephod. If you'll take it for yourself, take it; there's no other here but that one.' And David said, 'There's none like it. Give it to me.'
And David got up and fled that day from Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath.
And the servants of Achish said to him, 'Isn't this David, the king of the land? Isn't he the one they sing about in the dances — "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands"?'
And David took these words to heart, and he was very afraid of Achish king of Gath.
And he changed his behaviour in front of them and acted like a madman in their hands, scratching marks on the doors of the gate and letting his spittle run down onto his beard.
And Achish said to his servants, 'Look, you can see the man is behaving like a madman. Why bring him to me?
Am I short of madmen, that you have brought this one to act like a madman at me? Is this one to come into my house?'

1 samuel_22.t: And David went from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. His brothers and all his father's house heard of it and went down to him there.
And every man in distress, every man who had a creditor, and every man bitter of being gathered to him. He became their commander, and there were about four hundred men with him.
And David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab and said to the king of Moab, 'Let my father and my mother come out and stay with you, until I know what God will do for me.'
And he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the time David was in the stronghold.
And Gad the prophet said to David, 'Don't stay in the stronghold. Go into the land of Judah.' So David went and came to the forest of Hereth.
And Saul heard that David had been discovered, and the men with him. Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk on the height, his spear in his hand, and all his servants standing about him.

And Saul said to his servants who were standing about him, 'Listen, Benjaminites. Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards too? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

For all of you have conspired against me, and no one uncovers my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you is grieved for me or uncovers my ear that my son has raised up my servant against me to lie in ambush, as at this day.'
And Doeg the Edomite answered — he was standing with Saul's servants — 'I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
And he enquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.'
And the king sent to summon Ahimelech son of Ahitub the priest, and all his father's house, the priests at Nob; and all of them came to the king.
And Saul said, 'Listen, son of Ahitub.' And he said, 'Here I am, my lord.'

And Saul said to him, 'Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse — giving him bread and a sword and enquiring of God for him, so that he rises up against me to lie in ambush, as at this day?'
And Ahimelech answered the king, 'And who among all your servants is like David — faithful, the king's son-in-law, captain of your bodyguard, honoured in your house?

Was this day the first time I enquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king lay nothing against his servant, against all my father's house — your servant knew nothing of any of this, small or great.'
And the king said, 'You shall surely die, Ahimelech — you and all your father's house.'

And the king said to the runners standing about him, 'Turn and put the priests of the LORD to death, because their hand is with David too, and because they knew he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear.' But the king's servants were not willing to stretch out their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.

And the king said to Doeg, 'You turn and fall upon the priests.' And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he himself fell upon the priests, and that day he put to death eighty-five men who carried an ephod of linen.
And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword — man and woman, child and suckling, and ox and donkey and sheep — with the edge of the sword.
And one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled after David.
And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
And David said to Abiathar, 'I knew that day, because Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I myself am responsible for every being of your father's house.
Stay with me; don't be afraid. The one who seeks my life seeks your life — you are in safekeeping with me.'

1 samuel_23.t: And they told David, 'The Philistines are fighting against Keilah and plundering the threshing floors.'
And David enquired of the LORD, 'Shall I go and strike these Philistines?' And the LORD said to David, 'Go, strike the Philistines, and deliver Keilah.'
And David's men said to him, 'We're afraid here in Judah — how much more if we go to Keilah, against the battle lines of the Philistines!'
And David enquired of the LORD again, and the LORD answered him, 'Get up, go down to Keilah — I am giving the Philistines into your hand.'
So David and his men went to Keilah, fought the Philistines, drove away their livestock and struck them with a great defeat; and David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
And when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.
And it was told to Saul that David had come to Keilah, and Saul said, 'God has handed him over to me — he has shut himself in by going into a city with gates and a bar.'
And Saul summoned all the people to battle, to go down to Keilah and lay siege against David and his men.
And David knew that Saul was devising harm against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, 'Bring the ephod near.'
And David said, 'LORD, God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on my account.
Will the citizens of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant.' And the LORD said, 'He will come down.'
And David said, 'Will the citizens of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?' And the LORD said, 'They will hand you over.'

So David and his men arose, about six hundred of them, and went out from Keilah and moved about wherever they could. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, so he gave up going out.
And David lived in the wilderness, in the strongholds, and he lived in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him all that time, but God did not give him into his hand.
And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph, at Horesh.
And Jonathan son of Saul arose and went to David at Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.
And he said to him, 'Don't be afraid — the hand of Saul my father will not find you. You will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you. And Saul my father knows it too.'
And the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went to his house.
And Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah: 'Isn't David hiding with us, in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?
And now, whenever it is your desire to come down, O king, come down; and it will be ours to hand him over into the king's hand.'
And Saul said, 'May you be blessed by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.'
Go, make further preparation, and know and see the place where his foot is — who has seen him there — because someone has told me he is very crafty.
See and know all the hiding places where he hides, and come back to me with something certain, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.'
And they arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah, south of Jeshimon.
And Saul and his men went to seek him. They told David, and he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And Saul heard of it and pursued David into the wilderness of Maon.

Saul went along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side; and David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were closing round David and his men to seize them.
And a messenger came to Saul, 'Hurry and come — the Philistines have made a raid on the land.'
So Saul turned back from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why they called that place Sela Hammahlekoth.
And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.

1 samuel_24.t: And when Saul came back from following the Philistines, they told him, 'David is in the wilderness of En Gedi.'
And Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men on the face of the rocks of the mountain goats.
And he came to the sheepfolds by the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet. David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave.

And David's men said to him, 'This is the day the LORD spoke of to you: "I am giving your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as seems good to you."' And David arose and secretly cut off the skirt of the robe that was Saul's.
And afterwards David's heart struck him, because he had cut off the skirt that was Saul's.

And he said to his men, 'Far be it from me, before the LORD, that I should do this thing to my lord, to the anointed of the LORD, and stretch out my hand against him — for he is the anointed of the LORD.'
