And David reprimanded his men sharply, and did not permit them to rise against Saul. And Saul got up from the cave and went on his way.
And David got up afterwards and went out from the cave and called after Saul, 'My lord the king!' And Saul looked behind him, and David bowed his face to the ground and bowed down.
And David said to Saul, 'Why do you listen to a man's words, saying, "David is seeking your harm"?

This day your own eyes have seen that the LORD gave you into my hand in the cave; and someone said to kill you, but my eye had compassion on you. And I said, "I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the anointed of the LORD."

And my father, look — look at the skirt of your robe in my hand! When I cut off the skirt of your robe I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you; yet you are lying in wait for my life, to take it.
May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; but my hand will not be against you.
As the proverb of the ancients says, 'From the wicked comes wickedness.' But my hand will not be against you.
After whom has the king of Israel come out? Who are you pursuing? A dead dog! A single flea!
And the LORD will be judge, and he will judge between me and you; may he see and conduct my case, and vindicate me from your hand.
And when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, 'Is this your voice, my son David?' And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
And he said to David, 'You are more righteous than I am, for you have dealt out good to me, and I have dealt out evil to you.
And you have told this day the good you have done me — that the LORD delivered me up into your hand and you did not kill me.
If a man finds his enemy, does he send him away on a good journey? So may the LORD reward you with good in place of this day, for what you have done to me.
And now I know that you will surely reign, and the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me, and that you will not destroy my name from my father's house.'
And David swore to Saul. And Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold.

1 samuel_25.t: And Samuel died. All Israel gathered and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. And David got up and went down to the wilderness of Paran.
There was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. The man was very great: he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
The man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. The woman was good of insight and beautiful of form, but the man was hard and evil in his deeds — and he was a Calebite.
And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
And David sent ten young men, and said to them, 'Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
Say this: "Long life to you! Peace to you, and peace to your house, and peace to everything that is yours.
Now I hear that you have shearers. Your shepherds were with us; we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were in Carmel.
Ask your own young men and they will tell you. Let the young men find favour in your eyes, for we've come on a good day. Give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son David."'
And David's young men came and spoke all these words to Nabal in David's name, and then they waited.
And Nabal answered David's servants, 'Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? These days there are plenty of servants breaking away from their masters.
And am I to take my bread and my water and the meat I've slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men I don't know where they come from?'
And David's young men turned back the way they came, and returned and told him all these words.

And David said to his men, 'Every man gird on his sword.' And every man girded on his sword, and David girded on his too. About four hundred men went up after David, and two hundred stayed with the baggage.
And one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, 'David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he screamed at them.
But the men were very good to us. We were not humiliated, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we went about with them in the field.
They were a wall about us, night and day, the whole time we were with them shepherding the flock.
So now, know and see what you will do, because harm has been determined against our master and against all his house — and he is a son of worthlessness, past speaking to.'

And Abigail made haste and took two hundred loaves, two skins of wine, five sheep prepared, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred bunches of raisins and two hundred fig cakes, and loaded them on the donkeys.
And she said to her young men, 'Go on ahead of me; I'm coming behind you.' But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
And as she was riding on the donkey, going down under the cover of the mountain, David and his men were coming down towards her; and she met them.
David had been saying, 'It was for nothing that I guarded all this man has in the wilderness, and nothing of his went missing — and he has returned me evil in place of good.
So may God do to David's enemies, and more also, if I leave until morning, of all that is his, one who urinates against a wall.'
And when Abigail saw David she made haste, got down from the donkey, fell before David on her face and bowed down to the ground.
And she fell at his feet and said, 'On me, my lord, on me be the iniquity! Let your slave woman speak in your ears, and hear the words of your slave woman.

Let my lord not set his heart on this man of worthlessness, on Nabal; for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and disgraceful folly is with him. But I, your slave woman, did not see my lord's young men whom you sent.

And now, my lord, as the LORD lives and as you live, since the LORD has restrained you from coming into bloodguilt and from delivering yourself by your own hand — may your enemies, and those who seek harm against my lord, be like Nabal.
And now let this blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow at my lord's feet.

Forgive the transgression of your slave woman, for the LORD will surely make my lord an enduring house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD; and evil will not be found in you all your days.

And though a man has arisen to pursue you and seek your life, the being of my lord will be bound up in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God; but the being of your enemies he will sling out from the hollow of the sling.
And when the LORD does for my lord all the good he has spoken concerning you, and appoints you as leader over Israel,

then this will not be a staggering or a stumbling of heart for my lord — the pouring out of blood without cause, and my lord delivering himself. And when the LORD does good to my lord, remember your slave woman.'
And David said to Abigail, 'Blessed be the LORD, God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.
And blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from delivering myself by my own hand.

But as the LORD, God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from doing you harm — if you had not made haste and come to meet me, there would not have been left to Nabal by morning light one who urinates against a wall.'
And David took from her hand what she had brought him and said to her, 'Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and have granted your request.'

And Abigail came to Nabal, and he had a feast in his house like a king's feast. Nabal's heart was good within him, and he was very drunk; so she told him nothing at all, small or great, until the light of the morning.
And in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things; and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
And about ten days later the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.

And David heard that Nabal was dead and said, 'Blessed be the LORD, who has conducted the case of my disgrace from the hand of Nabal and has kept his servant back from evil; and the LORD has returned Nabal's evil on his own head.' And David sent and spoke with Abigail, to take her to himself as a wife.
And David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, 'David has sent us to you, to take you to him as a wife.'
And she arose and bowed down with her face to the ground and said, 'Here is your slave woman, a maidservant to wash the feet of my lord's servants.'
And Abigail made haste and got up and rode on the donkey, with five of her young women walking at her feet; and she went after David's messengers and became his wife.
And David had taken Ahinoam from Jezreel, and the two of them became his wives.
And Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

1 samuel_26.t: And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah: 'Isn't David hiding on the hill of Hakilah, facing Jeshimon?'
And Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
And Saul encamped on the hill of Hakilah, facing Jeshimon, by the way. David was living in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
And David sent spies, and he knew for certain that Saul had come.

And David got up and came to the place where Saul had encamped, and he saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. Saul was lying in the encampment, with the people encamped around him.
And David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, 'Who will go down with me to Saul, to the camp?' And Abishai said, 'I will go down with you.'
And David and Abishai came to the people by night. Saul was lying asleep in the encampment, his spear thrust into the ground at his head, and Abner and the people lying around him.
And Abishai said to David, 'God has delivered your enemy into your hand this day. Let me strike him with the spear into the ground once — I won't need a second blow.'
And David said to Abishai, 'Don't destroy him. Who has stretched out his hand against the anointed of the LORD and been free of guilt?'
And David said, 'As the LORD lives, the LORD himself will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or he will go down into battle and be swept away.
Far be it from me, before the LORD, to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD. Now take the spear that is at his head, and the jug of water, and let's go.'

And David took the spear and the jug of water from beside Saul's head, and they went. No one saw, no one knew, no one awoke — they were all sleeping, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
And David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the hill, far off, with a great space between them.
And David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, 'Will you not answer, Abner?' And Abner answered, 'Who are you, calling to the king?'
And David said to Abner, 'Aren't you a man? Who is like you in Israel? Then why haven't you kept watch over your lord the king? One of the people came to destroy the king your lord.

This thing you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, you are sons of death, because you have not kept watch over your lord, over the anointed of the LORD. Now see where the king's spear is, and the jug of water that was at his head!'
And Saul recognised David's voice and said, 'Is this your voice, my son David?' And David said, 'It is my voice, my lord the king.'
And he said, 'Why is this, that my lord is pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?

And now let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, may he accept an offering; but if it is the sons of man, cursed are they before the LORD, for they have driven me out this day from having a share in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, "Go, serve other gods."
And now, don't let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as a man hunts a partridge in the mountains.'
And Saul said, 'I have sinned. Come back, my son David — I will not do you harm again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. I have acted foolishly and have gone very greatly astray.'
And David answered, 'Here is the king's spear. Let one of the young men come over and take it.
And the LORD will return to each man his righteousness and his faithfulness, for the LORD gave you today into my hand, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the LORD.
And as your life was great in my eyes this day, so may my life be great in the eyes of the LORD, and may he deliver me from every trouble.
And Saul said to David, 'Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do, and you will surely prevail.' And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

1 samuel_27.t: And David said in his heart, 'One day now I'll be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing good for me but to escape to the land of the Philistines; then Saul will give up seeking me anywhere in the territory of Israel, and I'll be delivered from his hand.'
And David arose and crossed over, he and the six hundred men with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
And David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each with his household — David and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the Carmelite, Nabal's wife.
And it was told to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he did not seek him again.
And David said to Achish, 'If I have found favour in your eyes, let me be given a place in one of the country towns to live in. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?'
And Achish gave him Ziklag that day. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
And the length of time David lived in the region of the Philistines was a year and four months.

And David and his men went up and made raids against the Geshurites, the Girzites and the Amalekites; for they were the inhabitants of the land from of old, from the approach to Shur as far as the land of Egypt.
And David struck the land and let neither man nor woman live; and he took sheep and cattle, donkeys, camels and clothing, and returned and came to Achish.
And Achish said, 'Against whom did you raid today?' And David said, 'Against the Negev of Judah, and the Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and the Negev of the Kenites.'

And David would not let a man or a woman live to be brought to Gath, saying, 'They might tell about us, "This is what David has done."' And that was his practice the whole time he lived in the region of the Philistines.
And Achish trusted David, saying, 'He has surely made himself odious among his own people, among Israel — he will be my servant for ever.'

1 samuel_28.t: And in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, 'You know you are to go out with me in the camp, you and your men.'
And David said to Achish, 'Then you will know what your servant will do.' And Achish said to David, 'Then I will make you keeper of my head for good.'
Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, in his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land.
And the Philistines gathered and came and encamped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel and they encamped at Gilboa.
And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
And Saul enquired of the LORD, and the LORD did not answer him — not by dreams, not by the Urim, not by the prophets.
And Saul said to his servants, 'Find me a woman who is a medium, and I will go to her and enquire of her.' And his servants said to him, 'There is a woman who is a medium at En Dor.'

And Saul disguised himself and put on other clothes, and he went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. And he said, 'Divine for me by the ghost, and bring up for me the one I name to you.'
And the woman said to him, 'You know what Saul has done — that he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why are you setting a trap for my life, to put me to death?'
And Saul swore to her by the LORD, 'As the LORD lives, no punishment will come to you in this matter.'
And the woman said, 'Whom shall I bring up for you?' And he said, 'Bring up Samuel for me.'
And the woman saw Samuel, and she cried out with a loud voice; and the woman said to Saul, 'Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!'
And the king said to her, 'Don't be afraid. What have you seen?' And the woman said to Saul, 'I have seen a divine being coming up from the earth.'
And he said to her, 'What is his form?' And she said, 'An old man is coming up, wrapped in a robe.' And Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed his face to the ground and bowed down.

And Samuel said to Saul, 'Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?' And Saul said, 'I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned aside from me and no longer answers me, either by the hand of the prophets or by dreams. So I have called you, to make known to me what I should do.'
And Samuel said, 'Why then do you ask me, when the LORD has turned aside from you and has become your enemy?
And the LORD has done to him as he spoke by my hand: the LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbour, to David.
Since you did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and did not execute the burning of his anger upon Amalek, the LORD has done this thing to you this day.
And the LORD will give Israel with you into the hand of the Philistines. And tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also give the camp of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
And Saul hastened and fell full length to the ground, exceedingly afraid because of Samuel's words. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten no food all that day and all that night.

And the woman came to Saul and saw that he was greatly terrified, and she said to him, 'Your maidservant has listened to your voice; I have taken my life in my hand and listened to the words you spoke to me.
And now you also listen to the voice of your maidservant. Let me set a piece of bread before you, and eat, so that there may be strength in you, for you will go on your way.'
And he refused and said, 'I will not eat.' But his servants urged him, and the woman too; and he listened to their voice, and rose from the ground and sat on the bed.
And the woman had a stall-fed calf in the house, and she hastened and slaughtered it; and she took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.
And she set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they arose and went away that night.

1 samuel_29.t: And the Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, while Israel were encamped at the spring in Jezreel.
And the rulers of the Philistines were passing along by hundreds and by thousands, and David and his men were passing along at the rear with Achish.

And the commanders of the Philistines said, 'What are these Hebrews?' And Achish said to them, 'Isn't this David, the servant of Saul king of Israel, who has been with me these days — these years? And I have found nothing in him from the day he fell away until this day.'

And the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him and said to him, 'Send the man back — let him return to the place where you assigned him. He is not to go down with us into the battle, or he may become an opponent to us in the battle. How would this fellow make himself acceptable to his master? Would it not be with the heads of these men?'
Isn't this David, the one they sing about in the dances — 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?

And Achish called David and said to him, 'As the LORD lives, you are upright, and your going out and coming in with me in the camp is good in my eyes; I have found no evil in you from the day you came to me until this day. But in the eyes of the rulers you are not good.
So now return and go in peace, and do nothing evil in the eyes of the rulers of the Philistines.'

And David said to Achish, 'But what have I done? What have you found in your servant, from the day I came before you until this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?'
And Achish answered David, 'I know that you are good in my eyes, like an angel of God; but the commanders of the Philistines have said, "He shall not go up with us into the battle."
So rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your master who came with you; rise early in the morning, and when it is light, go.'
And David rose early, he and his men, to go in the morning and return to the land of the Philistines; and the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

1 samuel_30.t: And when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag; they had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
And they had taken captive the women who were in it, from small to great; they had killed no one, but had driven them away and gone on their way.
And David and his men came to the city, and it was burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
And David and the people with him lifted up their voice and wept, until there was no strength in them to weep.
And David's two wives had been taken captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

And David was in great distress, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the being of all the people was bitter, each for his sons and for his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, 'Bring the ephod near to me.' And Abiathar brought the ephod near to David.
And David enquired of the LORD, 'Shall I pursue this band? Will I overtake it?' And he said to him, 'Pursue, for you will surely overtake and will surely rescue.'
And David went, he and the six hundred men with him, and they came to the wadi Besor; and those who were left behind stayed there.
And David pursued, he and four hundred men; two hundred men remained, too exhausted to cross the wadi Besor.
And they found an Egyptian man in the open country and brought him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink.
And they gave him a slice of fig cake and two bunches of raisins; and he ate, and his spirit returned to him, for he had eaten no food and drunk no water for three days and three nights.
And David said to him, 'To whom do you belong? Where are you from?' And he said, 'I am an Egyptian lad, a slave to an Amalekite man; and my master abandoned me because I fell sick three days ago.'
'We had raided the Negev of the Kerethites, and what belongs to Judah, and the Negev of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.'

And David said to him, 'Will you take me down to this band?' And he said, 'Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hand of my master, and I will take you down to this band.'

And he took him down, and there they were, spread out over the face of the whole land, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode camels and fled.
And David rescued all that Amalek had taken, and his two wives David rescued.
And nothing of theirs was missing — from small to great, sons and daughters, plunder, everything they had taken for themselves. David brought back the whole of it.
And David took all the sheep and the cattle. They drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, 'This is David's plunder.'

And David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to go after him and had been left behind at the wadi Besor. They went out to meet David and the people with him, and David approached them and greeted them.

And every evil and worthless man among those who had gone with David said, 'Because they did not go with me, we will not give them any of the plunder we have recovered — except each man his wife and his children. Let them take them and go.'
And David said, 'You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us, and has given the band that came against us into our hand.
And who will listen to you in this matter? The share of the one who goes down into the battle and the share of the one who stays with the baggage are the same; they shall share alike.
And so it was from that day onward: he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel, to this day.
And David came to Ziklag and sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, to his neighbours: 'Here is a blessing for you, from the plunder of the enemies of the LORD.'
to those in Bethel, and to those in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those in Jattir,
and to those in Aroer, and to those in Siphmoth, and to those in Eshtemoa,
and to those in Racal, and to those in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those in the cities of the Kenites,
and to those in Hormah, and to those in Bor Ashan, and to those in Athach,
and to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David had gone about, he and his men.

1 samuel_31.t: Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines pursued closely after Saul and his sons, and they struck down Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
And the battle grew heavy against Saul, and the archers, men with the bow, found him; and he was in severe pain from the archers.

And Saul said to his armour-bearer, 'Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised will come and run me through and deal wantonly with me.' But his armour-bearer was not willing, for he was very afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.
And his armour-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he too fell on his sword and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons and his armour-bearer, and all his men too, on that day together.

And the men of Israel on the other side of the valley, and those on the other side of the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead; and they abandoned the cities and fled. And the Philistines came and lived in them.
And on the next day the Philistines came to strip the slain, and they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
And they cut off his head and stripped off his armour, and they sent word through the land of the Philistines all around, to bear the news to the house of their idols and to the people.
And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth, and they fixed his body to the wall of Beth Shan.
And the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead heard concerning him what the Philistines had done to Saul.
And every man of valour arose and went all night, and they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth Shan; and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.
And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

2 chronicles_1.t: Solomon son of David strengthened his hold on his kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel — to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the ancestral houses —
and Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, because the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness, was there.
But the ark of God — David had brought that up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he'd prepared for it, because he'd pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
And the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur had made was standing there in front of the tabernacle of the LORD; and Solomon and the assembly sought it out.
And Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, the one that belonged to the tent of meeting, and he offered up a thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I should give you."
And Solomon said to God, "You've shown great steadfast love to David my father, and you've made me king in his place.
"Now, LORD God, let your word to David my father stand; because you've made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
"So give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I can go out before this people and come in. Who could judge this great people of yours?"

And God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart — you didn't ask for wealth, riches and honour, or for the life of those who hate you, and you didn't even ask for long life, but you asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge my people, over whom I've made you king —
"the wisdom and the knowledge are given to you. And I'll give you wealth and riches and honour such as no kings before you have had, and none after you will have."
Then Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as common as the sycamores of the Shephelah — that is how plentiful they were.
Solomon's horses were exported from Egypt and from Que; the king's traders bought them from Que at a price.
They imported chariots from Egypt at six hundred shekels of silver each and horses at a hundred and fifty; and through them the same was done for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

2 chronicles_2.t: And Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the LORD and a house for his kingship.
Solomon counted out seventy thousand men as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers over them.
And Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre: "As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in —

"I'm building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to set it apart as holy to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, and for the continual row of bread, and burnt offerings morning and evening, for the sabbaths and the new moons and the appointed times of the LORD our God — this is laid on Israel for ever.
"And the house I'm building will be great, because our God is greater than all gods.
"And who has the strength to build him a house, when the heavens and the highest heavens can't contain him? And who am I to build him a house — except to burn incense before him?

"So now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, scarlet and violet, who knows how to engrave engravings, to work with the skilled men I have here in Judah and Jerusalem, the ones David my father appointed.
"And send me cedar, fir and algum timber from Lebanon; I know your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon. And my servants will work with your servants,
"to get me timber in plenty; because the house I'm building is to be great and wonderful.

"And to the woodcutters, the men who fell the timber, I'm giving crushed wheat for your servants: twenty thousand cors, and twenty thousand cors of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
And Huram king of Tyre replied in a letter, which he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he's made you king over them."

And Huram said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who's going to build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingship.
"And now I've sent you a skilled man, endowed with understanding — Huram-abi,

"the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father a man of Tyre — skilled to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in stone and wood, in purple, violet, fine linen and scarlet, and to engrave any engraving and work out any design he's given, together with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
"So now let my lord send his servants the wheat and the barley, the oil and the wine he's spoken of.
"And we'll cut timber from Lebanon, as much as you need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa; and you can take it up to Jerusalem."
And Solomon counted all the resident aliens in the land of Israel, following the census by which David his father had counted them; and they came to a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
And he made seventy thousand of them burden-bearers, eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred overseers to keep the people at work.

2 chronicles_3.t: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where he had appeared to David his father, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits by the former measure, sixty cubits; the breadth, twenty cubits.
The porch in front, running the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height a hundred and twenty. He overlaid it inside with pure gold.
The great house he panelled with fir wood and overlaid with fine gold, and set palms and chains on it.
He adorned the house with precious stone for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
He overlaid the house — beams, thresholds, walls and doors — with gold, and engraved cherubim on the walls.
He made the house of the holy of holies: its length, running the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its breadth twenty cubits. He overlaid it with fine gold, six hundred talents' worth.
The nails weighed fifty shekels of gold, and the upper rooms he overlaid with gold.
In the house of the holy of holies he made two cherubim of cast work, and they overlaid them with gold.
The wings of the cherubim spanned twenty cubits: one wing of the first, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.
One wing of the second cherub, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, clung to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubim spread twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing toward the house.
He made the veil of violet, purple, scarlet and fine linen, and worked cherubim on it.
He made two pillars in front of the house, thirty-five cubits long, with a capital of five cubits on the top of each.
He made chains in the inner sanctuary and set them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and set them on the chains.
He set up the pillars in front of the main hall, one on the right and one on the left, and named the right-hand one Jakin and the left-hand one Boaz.

2 chronicles_4.t: He made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty wide and ten high.
He made the sea, cast in metal: ten cubits from rim to rim, perfectly round, five cubits high, with a line of thirty cubits going round it.
Beneath it, all around, was the likeness of oxen encircling it — ten to the cubit, running right round the sea — the oxen in two rows, cast in one piece with it.
It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three west, three south, three east. The sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters turned inward.
It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.
He made ten washbasins and set five on the right and five on the left, for washing; what belonged to the burnt offering they rinsed in them. The sea was for the priests to wash in.
He made the ten gold lampstands to their specification and set them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left.
He made ten tables and placed them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left, and he made a hundred gold basins.
He made the court of the priests and the great precinct, with doors for the precinct, and overlaid the doors with bronze.
He put the sea on the right side, toward the east, facing south.
Huram made the pots, the shovels and the basins, and finished the work he did for King Solomon in the house of God:
two pillars; the bowls and the capitals on the tops of the two pillars; the two networks covering the two bowls of the capitals on the tops of the pillars;
and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network — covering the two bowls of the capitals in front of the pillars.
He made the stands, and the washbasins on the stands;
the one sea, with the twelve oxen under it;
and the pots, the shovels, the forks and all their articles Huram-abi made for King Solomon, for the house of the LORD, of polished bronze.
The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made all these articles in great abundance — the weight of the bronze was never determined.
Solomon made all the articles for the house of God: the gold altar, and the tables with the bread of the Presence on them;
and the lampstands with their lamps, to burn as prescribed before the inner sanctuary, of refined gold;
and the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold — the purest gold;
and the snuffers, the basins, the pans and the firepans, of refined gold. As for the entrance of the house: its inner doors to the holy of holies, and the doors of the main hall, were gold.

2 chronicles_5.t: So all the work Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father — the silver, the gold and all the articles — and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the chiefs of the tribes and the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, that is, Zion.
Every man of Israel assembled to the king at the festival, in the seventh month.
All the elders of Israel came, and the Levites took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark and the tent of meeting and all the holy articles that were in the tent — the priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who'd gathered to him before the ark were sacrificing sheep and cattle — more than could be counted or numbered.
The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, to the inner sanctuary of the house, the holy of holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, covering the ark and its poles from above.
And the poles were long, and the ends of the poles could be seen from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, though they couldn't be seen from outside; and it's been there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark but the two tablets that Moses put there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
And when the priests came out of the holy place — all the priests who were there had set themselves apart as holy, without keeping to their divisions —

and the Levites, the singers — all of them: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, with their sons and their brothers — dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps and lyres, stood east of the altar, and a hundred and twenty priests with them blowing trumpets —

and the trumpeters and the singers were as one, making one voice heard in praise and thanks to the LORD; and as they lifted up their voice with trumpets and cymbals and instruments of song, praising the LORD — "For he is good, for his steadfast love is for ever" — the house was filled with a cloud, the house of the LORD,
and the priests couldn't stand and serve because of the cloud, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.

2 chronicles_6.t: Then Solomon said: "The LORD has said he would dwell in thick darkness.
"And I've built you a lofty house, a place for you to dwell in for ever."
Then the king turned round and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and has fulfilled it with his hands. He said,

"'From the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I haven't chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house in for my name to be there, and I haven't chosen a man to be ruler over my people Israel;
"'but I've chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I've chosen David to be over my people Israel.'
"Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
"And the LORD said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well to have it in your heart;
"'only you're not the one to build the house. Your son, the one who comes from your loins — he's the one who will build the house for my name.'

"And the LORD has kept the word he spoke: I've risen in place of David my father and sat on the throne of Israel, as the LORD said, and I've built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
"And I've put the ark there, where the covenant of the LORD is, the covenant he made with the Israelites."
And he stood in front of the altar of the LORD, before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.

For Solomon had made a bronze platform and set it in the middle of the precinct, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high. And he stood on it, then knelt down in front of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands towards the heavens.
And he said, "LORD, God of Israel, there's no God like you in the heavens or on the earth, keeping covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart;
"you've kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him — you spoke it with your mouth and you've fulfilled it with your hand, as it is this day.

"And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him when you said, 'You'll never lack a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel — if only your sons keep their way, walking in my law as you have walked before me.'
"And now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word stand, the word you spoke to your servant David.
"But will God really dwell with humankind on the earth? Look — the heavens and the highest heavens can't contain you; how much less this house that I've built!
"Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his supplication, LORD my God, and listen to the cry and to the prayer your servant is praying before you,
"so that your eyes may be open towards this house day and night, towards the place you said you'd put your name — and listen to the prayer your servant prays towards this place.
"And listen to the supplications of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray towards this place. Hear from the place where you dwell, from the heavens — hear and forgive.
"If anyone sins against his neighbour and an oath is laid on him to put him under oath, and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this house,

"then hear from the heavens and act: judge your servants, repaying the guilty by bringing his conduct down on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by giving him what his righteousness deserves.
"And if your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they've sinned against you, and they turn back and give thanks to your name and pray and make supplication before you in this house,
"then hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the ground you gave to them and to their ancestors.

"When the heavens are shut up and there's no rain because they've sinned against you, and they pray towards this place and give thanks to your name and turn from their sin because you're afflicting them,

"then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel — you'll direct them to the good way they should walk in; and give rain on your land, the land you gave your people as an inheritance.
"If there's famine in the land, if there's pestilence, blight or mildew, locust or grasshopper; if their enemies besiege them in the land of their own towns — any plague, any sickness —
"whatever prayer, whatever supplication comes from anyone, or from all your people Israel, each one knowing his own plague and his own pain, and he spreads out his hands towards this house,
"then hear from the heavens, the place where you dwell, and forgive; and give to each one according to all his ways, since you know his heart — you alone know the heart of the children of humankind —
"so that they'll fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live on the face of the ground you gave our ancestors.

"And the foreigner too, who isn't of your people Israel, who comes from a distant land for the sake of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray towards this house —

"then hear from the heavens, from the place where you dwell, and do everything the foreigner calls to you for; so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and know that your name is called over this house that I've built.
"If your people go out to battle against their enemies by the way you send them, and they pray to you towards this city you've chosen and the house I've built for your name,
"then hear their prayer and their supplication from the heavens, and maintain their cause.
"If they sin against you — and there's no one who doesn't sin — and you're angry with them and give them up to an enemy, and their captors carry them off to a land far away or near,

"and they take it to heart in the land where they've been taken captive, and they turn back and make supplication to you in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We've sinned, we've done wrong, we've acted wickedly';

"and they come back to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray towards their land that you gave their ancestors, and the city you've chosen, and towards the house that I've built for your name;
"then hear their prayer and their supplications from the heavens, from the place where you dwell, and maintain their cause; and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
"Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
"And now arise, LORD God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let your loyal ones rejoice in the good.
"LORD God, don't turn away the face of your anointed one; remember your steadfast love for David your servant."

2 chronicles_7.t: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
And the priests couldn't go into the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

And all the Israelites were watching as the fire came down and the glory of the LORD was over the house; and they bowed with their faces to the ground on the pavement and prostrated themselves, giving thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his steadfast love is for ever."
The king and all the people were offering sacrifices before the LORD.
King Solomon sacrificed twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep, and the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

The priests stood at their duties, and the Levites with the instruments of the song of the LORD that King David had made, to give thanks to the LORD — "for his steadfast love is for ever" — when David praised by their hand. The priests blew trumpets facing them, and all Israel stood.

And Solomon set apart as holy the middle of the court in front of the house of the LORD; that's where he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made couldn't hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat.
And Solomon kept the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him — a very great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the wadi of Egypt.
And on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly; they'd kept the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.
And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart over the good the LORD had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel his people.
So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king's house; and everything he'd set his heart on doing in the house of the LORD and in his own house he carried through successfully.
And the LORD appeared to Solomon in the night and said to him, "I've heard your prayer, and I've chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
"If I shut up the heavens so that there's no rain, or command the grasshopper to devour the land, or send pestilence among my people,
"and my people, over whom my name is called, humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I'll hear from the heavens and forgive their sin and heal their land.
"From now on my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
"And now I've chosen and set apart as holy this house, for my name to be there for ever; and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.
"And as for you — if you walk before me as David your father walked, and do everything I've commanded you, and keep my statutes and my judgements,
"then I'll establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father when I said, 'You'll never lack a man to rule in Israel.'
"But if you turn away and forsake my statutes and my commandments that I've set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

"then I'll pluck them up from my ground that I've given them; and this house that I've set apart as holy for my name I'll cast away from before my face, and make it a byword and a taunt among all the peoples.
"And this house, which was so exalted — everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

"And they'll say, 'Because they forsook the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them — that's why he's brought all this calamity on them.'"

2 chronicles_8.t: At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,
the cities Huram had given to Solomon — Solomon rebuilt them and settled the Israelites there.
Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and prevailed over it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities he built in Hamath.
He built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, doors and bars;

and Baalath, all the storage cities Solomon had, all the chariot cities and the cities of the horsemen, and everything he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and throughout the land of his dominion.
All the people left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, who were not of Israel —
their descendants who remained after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed — Solomon brought them up as forced labour, and so it is to this day.
But Solomon didn't make slaves of any of the Israelites for his work; they were the men of war, the commanders of his officers, and the commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
These were the commanders of the overseers under King Solomon: two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.

And Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to the house he'd built for her; because he said, "No wife of mine is going to live in the house of David king of Israel — the places the ark of the LORD has come to are holy."
Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the porch,

and according to the requirement of each day, offering up as Moses commanded: for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed times, three times a year — at the festival of unleavened bread, the festival of weeks and the festival of booths.

He appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests over their service and the Levites over their duties, to praise and to serve before the priests as each day required; and the gatekeepers by their divisions for each gate — for such was the commandment of David the man of God.
And they didn't turn aside from the king's commandment about the priests and the Levites in anything, or about the treasuries.
So all Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the house of the LORD was founded until it was completed; the house of the LORD was finished.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth, on the seashore in the land of Edom.

And Huram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, and crews who knew the sea; and they went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and brought back four hundred and fifty talents of gold from there to King Solomon.

2 chronicles_9.t: And the queen of Sheba heard the report about Solomon, and she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions, with a very great retinue, and camels carrying spices and gold in abundance and precious stone. She came to Solomon and talked with him about everything that was on her mind.
And Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from Solomon that he didn't tell her.
And the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom, and the house he'd built,

and the food on his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his attendants and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD — and there was no breath left in her.
And she said to the king, "It was true, the report I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
"I didn't believe what they said until I came and saw with my own eyes — and I wasn't told half the greatness of your wisdom. You've surpassed the report I heard.
"How blessed your men are, and how blessed these servants of yours who stand before you all the time and hear your wisdom!

"Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for the LORD your God. Because your God loves Israel and would establish it for ever, he's made you king over them, to do judgement and righteousness."
And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in very great abundance, and precious stone; there's never been spice like the spice the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum timber and precious stone.

And the king made the algum timber into walkways for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and into lyres and harps for the singers; nothing like them had ever been seen before in the land of Judah.
And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted and asked for, besides what she'd brought the king. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her servants.
The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents,
apart from what the travelling merchants and traders brought in; and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold, six hundred shekels of beaten gold on each shield.
And three hundred shields of beaten gold, three hundred shekels of gold on each. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps and a gold footstool attached to it, with armrests on either side of the seat and two lions standing beside the armrests;
and twelve lions standing there on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.
And all King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were refined gold; silver counted for nothing in the days of Solomon.
For the king had ships going to Tarshish with the servants of Huram; once every three years the ships of Tarshish would come in, carrying gold and silver, ivory, monkeys and apes.
King Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
And all the kings of the earth sought the face of Solomon, to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
And each of them brought his gift — articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weaponry, spices, horses and mules — year after year.
Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as common as the sycamores of the Shephelah — that is how plentiful they were.
Horses were brought out for Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.

And the rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last — isn't it written in the words of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
Solomon lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_10.t: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
And when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it — he was in Egypt, where he'd fled from King Solomon — Jeroboam came back from Egypt.
So they sent and called him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
"Your father made our yoke hard. Lighten your father's hard labour now, and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we'll serve you."
And he said to them, "Come back to me in three days." And the people went away.
And King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive: "How do you advise me to answer these people?"
And they said to him, "If you'll be good to these people and show them favour and speak kindly to them, they'll be your servants always."
But he abandoned the counsel the elders had given him and consulted the young men who'd grown up with him and stood before him.
And he said to them, "What's your advice? How do we answer these people who've said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"

And the young men who'd grown up with him said to him, "Here's what you should say to the people who told you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; now lighten it for us' — this is what you should say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
"'My father loaded a heavy yoke on you; I'm going to add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I'll use scorpions.'"
Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said: "Come back to me on the third day."
And the king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders,
and spoke to them by the counsel of the young men: "I'll make your yoke heavy, and I'll add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I'll use scorpions."
And the king didn't listen to the people; it was a turn of events from God, so that the LORD might establish the word he'd spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

And when all Israel saw that the king hadn't listened to them, the people answered the king: "What share do we have in David? We've no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel — every one of you! Now look to your own house, David!" And all Israel went off to their tents.
But Rehoboam reigned over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
And King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the forced labour; and the Israelites stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam scrambled into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

2 chronicles_11.t: Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin — a hundred and eighty thousand chosen fighting men — to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
The word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin:

"This is what the LORD says: 'You're not to go up and fight against your brothers. Go back, every one of you, to his own house — this thing has come about from me.'" And they obeyed the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built fortified cities in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam and Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Socoh and Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah and Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish and Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, which are in Judah and Benjamin — fortified cities.
He strengthened the fortifications and put commanders in them, with stores of food, oil and wine.
And in every single city he put large shields and spears, and made them exceedingly strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
The priests and Levites throughout all Israel took their stand with him from all their territory,
The Levites left their pasture lands and holdings and went to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD.
He appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-demons and for the calves he had made.
And after them, people from all the tribes of Israel who'd set their heart on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam son of Solomon strong for three years, because for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam took as his wife Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse,
and she bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
After her he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
And Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines; he'd taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, as leader among his brothers, because he meant to make him king.

And he acted with understanding: he spread some of all his sons through all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities; and he gave them provisions in abundance, and sought a multitude of wives for them.

2 chronicles_12.t: And once Rehoboam's kingdom was established and he'd grown strong, he forsook the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem — because they'd acted unfaithfully against the LORD —
with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and people beyond counting who came with him from Egypt — Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.
He captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who'd gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "This is what the LORD says: 'You've abandoned me, so I've abandoned you too, into the hand of Shishak.'"
The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

And when the LORD saw that they'd humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They've humbled themselves. I won't destroy them; I'll give them a measure of deliverance, and my rage won't be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
"But they'll become his servants, so that they'll know what it is to serve me and what it is to serve the kingdoms of the lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house — he took the lot; and he took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
And King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them, and put them in the charge of the commanders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house.
And whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the runners would come and carry them, and then take them back to the guardroom of the runners.
And because he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned back from him, so as not to destroy him utterly; and in Judah too there were good things.

So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
And he did evil, because he didn't set his heart on seeking the LORD.

And the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last — aren't they written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, arranged by genealogy? And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the time.
Rehoboam lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David, and Abijah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_13.t: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
And Abijah joined battle with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam drew up in battle against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty in strength.
And Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
"Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave kingship over Israel to David for ever — to him and to his sons, by a covenant of salt?
"But Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
"And empty men, worthless fellows, gathered round him and made themselves strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon; and Rehoboam was young and weak of heart, and he didn't stand up to them.

"And now you say you're going to stand up to the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hand of the sons of David. You're a great multitude, and you've got the golden calves with you that Jeroboam made you as gods.

"Haven't you driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made yourselves priests like the peoples of the lands? Anyone who comes to fill his hand with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest to what are not gods.
"But as for us — the LORD is our God, and we haven't forsaken him. The priests who serve the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites are at their work.

"And they burn burnt offerings to the LORD morning by morning and evening by evening, and fragrant incense, and they set the row of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps to burn every evening. We keep the duty of the LORD our God — and you have forsaken him.

"And look — God is with us, at our head, and his priests with the trumpets of alarm, ready to sound the alarm against you. Israelites, don't fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors — you won't succeed."
But Jeroboam had sent the ambush round to come at them from behind; so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.
And Judah turned round — and there was the battle in front of them and behind. And they cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
The men of Judah sounded the alarm, and when they did, God defeated Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The Israelites fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.
Abijah and his people struck them a great blow, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.
And the Israelites were humbled at that time, and the people of Judah prevailed, because they leaned on the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephrain with its villages.
And Jeroboam never recovered his strength again in the days of Abijah; and the LORD struck him, and he died.
Abijah grew strong. He took fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his words, are written in the record of the prophet Iddo.

2 chronicles_14.t: Abijah lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David, and Asa his son became king in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He removed the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim.
He told Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to keep the law and the commandment.
He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was quiet under him.
And he built fortified cities in Judah, because the land was quiet; there was no war against him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.

And he said to Judah, "Let's build these cities and put walls round them, with towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we've sought the LORD our God; we sought him, and he's given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

Asa had an army bearing large shield and spear — three hundred thousand from Judah — and from Benjamin, bearing shield and drawing the bow, two hundred and eighty thousand. All these were mighty men of valour.
Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a million and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up for battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa called out to the LORD his God: "LORD, there's no one like you to help — whether it's the mighty or the one with no strength at all. Help us, LORD our God; we're leaning on you, and in your name we've come against this multitude. LORD, you are our God; don't let any man hold out against you."
The LORD defeated the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

And Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and the Cushites fell until there was none of them left alive, because they were broken before the LORD and before his army. And they carried off a great deal of booty.
And they struck all the cities around Gerar, because the dread of the LORD was on them; and they plundered all the cities, because there was a great deal of plunder in them.
They also struck the herdsmen's tents and carried off sheep in abundance and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.

2 chronicles_15.t: The spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.

And he went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you while you're with him; and if you seek him, he'll let himself be found by you; but if you forsake him, he'll forsake you.
"For a long time Israel was without a true God, without a teaching priest and without law;
"but in its distress it turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel, and they sought him, and he let himself be found by them.
"And in those times there was no peace for anyone going out or coming in, because great disturbances lay on everyone living in the lands.
"And they were crushed, nation against nation and city against city, because God troubled them with every kind of trouble.
"But you — be strong, and don't let your hands drop; there's a reward for your work."

When Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and got rid of the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities he'd captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of the LORD that stood before the porch of the LORD.

And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the people from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon living among them — they'd deserted to him from Israel in great numbers when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
On that day they sacrificed to the LORD from the booty they had brought: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
They entered into the covenant, to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and all their soul;
and anyone who wouldn't seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, small or great, man or woman.
They swore to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets and with ram's horns.

And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, because they'd sworn it with all their heart and had sought him with all their will; and he let himself be found by them, and the LORD gave them rest on every side.

And Maacah, King Asa's mother, he removed from being queen mother as well, because she'd made an abominable image for an Asherah; and Asa cut her abominable image down, crushed it and burned it in the wadi Kidron.
But the high places weren't removed from Israel; even so, Asa's heart was undivided all his days.
He brought into the house of God the holy things of his father and his own: silver, gold and articles.
And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

2 chronicles_16.t: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and fortified Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
And Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king's house, and sent word to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus:

"Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Here — I've sent you silver and gold. Go and break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he'll withdraw from me."
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And when Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and let the work drop.
And King Asa took all Judah, and they carried off the stones of Ramah and the timber Baasha had been building with; and he used them to build Geba and Mizpah.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you leaned on the king of Aram and didn't lean on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
"Weren't the Cushites and the Libyans a great army, with chariots and horsemen in exceedingly great abundance? And yet because you leaned on the LORD, he gave them into your hand.
"The eyes of the LORD rove through all the earth, to show himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is undivided towards him. You've acted foolishly in this; from now on you'll have wars."
And Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the house of the stocks, because he was in a rage with him over this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa's feet became diseased; his disease was exceedingly severe. And even then he didn't seek the LORD, but the physicians.
Asa lay down with his ancestors and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

And they buried him in his own tomb, which he'd cut for himself in the city of David, and laid him on the bier he'd filled with spices and various kinds blended by the perfumer's art; and they made an exceedingly great fire for him.

2 chronicles_17.t: Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
He stationed an army in all the fortified cities of Judah, and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
And the LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of David his ancestor and didn't seek the Baals;
he sought the God of his father and walked in his commandments, and not by what Israel did.
The LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had wealth and honour in abundance.
And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD; and he removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah again.
In the third year of his reign he sent his officials — Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah — to teach in the cities of Judah;
and with them the Levites — Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah — and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
And they taught in Judah, and they had the scroll of the law of the LORD with them; they went round all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
And the dread of the LORD was on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, and they didn't make war on Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat tribute and silver as a load; the Arabs too brought him flocks — seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
And Jehoshaphat went on growing greater and greater; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah.
He had much property in the cities of Judah, and men of war, mighty men of valour, were in Jerusalem.
These were their musters by ancestral house. Of Judah, commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
next to him, Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred and eighty thousand;
next to him, Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered himself to the LORD, with two hundred thousand mighty men of valour;
and of Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valour, with two hundred thousand equipped with bow and shield;
next to him, Jehozabad, with a hundred and eighty thousand equipped for war.
These were the men who served the king, besides the ones the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

2 chronicles_18.t: Jehoshaphat had wealth and honour in abundance, and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
And some years later he went down to Ahab at Samaria; and Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people with him, and talked him into going up against Ramoth-gilead.

And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you come with me to Ramoth-gilead?" And he said to him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we'll be with you in the battle."
And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Consult the word of the LORD today."
