So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I hold back?" And they said, "Go up, and God will give it into the king's hand."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Isn't there still a prophet of the LORD here, so that we can enquire of him?"

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There's still one man we could consult the LORD through — but I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil, all his days. Micaiah son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said, "The king shouldn't talk like that."
And the king of Israel called one court official and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah, quickly."

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting there, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you'll gore Aram until they're finished.'"
And all the prophets were prophesying the same: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed; the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
And the messenger who'd gone to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the prophets are speaking with one voice in the king's favour. Let your word be like one of theirs — speak favourably."
And Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that's what I'll speak."
And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or shall I hold back?" And he said, "Go up and succeed; they'll be given into your hand."
And the king said to him, "How many times do I have to make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
And he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These men have no masters; let them go back home, each to his own house, in peace.'"
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil?"
And he said, "So hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on his right hand and on his left.
"And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he goes up and falls at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said one thing and another said another.
"Then the spirit came out and stood before the LORD and said, 'I'll entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'How?'
"And it said, 'I'll go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And he said, 'You'll entice him, and you'll succeed too. Go out and do it.'
"And now look — the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours; and the LORD has spoken calamity about you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the spirit of the LORD go when it passed from me to speak to you?"
And Micaiah said, "You'll find out on the day you go into an inner room to hide yourself."
And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and hand him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king's son,
"and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in the prison house and feed him meagre bread and meagre water, until I come back in peace.'"
And Micaiah said, "If you really do come back in peace, the LORD hasn't spoken by me." And he said, "Hear it, you peoples, all of you!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up against Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I'll disguise myself and go into the battle; but you wear your own robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
Now the king of Aram had ordered the commanders of his chariotry, "Don't fight with small or great — only with the king of Israel."

And when the commanders of the chariotry saw Jehoshaphat they said, "That's the king of Israel," and they surrounded him to fight. And Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him, and God lured them away from him.
And when the commanders of the chariotry saw that he wasn't the king of Israel, they turned back from chasing him.
And a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armour; and he said to the charioteer, "Turn round and get me out of the camp — I'm wounded."
And the battle grew fierce that day; and the king of Israel was propped up in his chariot facing Aram until the evening, and he died about sunset.

2 chronicles_19.t: Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.

And Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you be helping the wicked and loving those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath is upon you from before the LORD.
"All the same, good things have been found in you: you've burned the Asherahs out of the land, and you've set your heart to seek God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and turned them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city;
and he said to the judges, "Think what you're doing. You aren't judging for humankind but for the LORD, and he's with you when you give judgement.
"So now, let the dread of the LORD be upon you. Be careful how you act, because with the LORD our God there's no injustice, no partiality and no taking of a bribe."

In Jerusalem too Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and priests and some of the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel, for the judgement of the LORD and for disputes; and they returned to Jerusalem.
And he gave them their orders: "This is how you're to act — in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness and with an undivided heart.

"And whatever dispute comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities — between one kind of bloodshed and another, between law and commandment, statutes and judgements — you're to warn them, so that they don't become guilty before the LORD and wrath come upon you and your brothers. Do that, and you won't become guilty.

"And Amariah the chief priest is over you for every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, for every matter of the king; and the Levites are officials before you. Be strong and act — and may the LORD be with the good."

2 chronicles_20.t: After this the Moabites and the Ammonites, and with them some of the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.
And they came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram; and they're already at Hazazon-tamar" — that is, En-gedi.
Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set his face to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
And Judah gathered to seek from the LORD; they came from all the cities of Judah too, to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,
and said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, aren't you God in the heavens? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; power and might are in your hand, and no one can stand against you.
"Didn't you, our God, dispossess the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend for ever?
"And they lived in it and built you a sanctuary in it for your name, and they said,

"'If calamity comes upon us — sword, judgement, pestilence or famine — we'll stand before this house and before you, because your name is in this house; and we'll cry out to you out of our distress, and you'll hear and save.'
"And now look — the Ammonites and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you wouldn't let Israel invade when they came from the land of Egypt, so that they turned aside from them and didn't destroy them —
"and here they are paying us back, coming to drive us out of your possession that you gave us to possess.
"Our God, won't you judge them? We've no strength against this great multitude that's coming against us, and we don't know what to do — but our eyes are on you."
And all Judah was standing there before the LORD — their little ones too, and their wives and their children.
And the spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the descendants of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, "Listen, all Judah, and you who live in Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD says to you: 'Don't be afraid and don't be dismayed by this great multitude, because the battle isn't yours but God's.
"'Go down against them tomorrow. They'll be coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you'll find them at the end of the wadi, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

"'You won't have to fight this one. Take your stand, stand still and see the salvation of the LORD with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Don't be afraid and don't be dismayed. Go out to meet them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you.'"
And Jehoshaphat bowed low, face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, to prostrate themselves to the LORD.
The Levites, of the Kohathites and the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with an exceedingly loud voice.

And they got up early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were going out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah, and you who live in Jerusalem! Trust in the LORD your God and you'll be established; trust in his prophets and you'll succeed."

And he consulted with the people, and appointed singers to the LORD, and men to praise in holy adornment, to go out ahead of the armed men, singing: "Give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love is for ever."
And the moment they began the shout and the praise, the LORD set ambushers against the Ammonites, Moab and Mount Seir who'd come against Judah, and they were defeated.

And the Ammonites and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, to devote them to destruction and to annihilate them; and when they'd finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped destroy one another.
And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness and looked out towards the multitude — and there they were, corpses fallen to the ground; not one had escaped.

And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their booty, and they found among them goods in abundance, and corpses, and precious articles; and they stripped off so much for themselves that they couldn't carry any more. They were three days plundering the booty, there was so much of it.
And on the fourth day they gathered in the valley of Berachah, because that's where they blessed the LORD; that's why the name of that place has been called the valley of Berachah, to this day.
And every man of Judah and Jerusalem turned back, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to go back to Jerusalem with joy; because the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
And the dread of God was on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
The kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, and his God gave him rest on every side.
So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king and reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of Asa his father and didn't turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Only the high places weren't removed, and the people still hadn't set their heart on the God of their ancestors.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which was taken up into the scroll of the kings of Israel.
After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly in what he did.
He allied himself with him to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.

And Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you've allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works." And the ships were broken, and they couldn't go to Tarshish.

2 chronicles_21.t: Jehoshaphat lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David, and Jehoram his son became king in his place.
He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
And their father gave them many gifts — silver, gold and precious things — along with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
And Jehoram rose over his father's kingdom and made himself strong; and he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the leaders of Israel too.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he followed the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done — a daughter of Ahab was his wife — and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD wasn't willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he'd made with David, and because he'd said he would give him a lamp, and his sons, for all time.
In his days Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah, and they set up a king of their own.
And Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariotry; and he got up in the night and struck Edom, which had surrounded him, and the chariot commanders.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah to this day. And Libnah rebelled against his hand at the same time, because he'd forsaken the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He made high places in the mountains of Judah as well, and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves, and led Judah astray.

And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet: "This is what the LORD, the God of David your ancestor, says: 'You haven't walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

"'but you've walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem prostitute themselves as the house of Ahab did, and you've killed your brothers too, your father's house, who were better than you —
"'so the LORD is about to strike a great blow on your people, on your sons and your wives and all your property;
"'and you yourself will suffer great sicknesses, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day.'"
The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who were beside the Cushites,

and they came up against Judah and broke into it, and carried off all the property found in the king's house, and his sons and his wives as well; and he was left with no son but Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
After all this, the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.

And in the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his disease, and he died in agonising diseases. And his people made no fire for him like the fires for his ancestors.

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he went with no one sorry to see him go; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the graves of the kings.

2 chronicles_22.t: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the raiding band that had come with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the older ones. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor, to act wickedly.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab; they were his counsellors after his father died, and it was his destruction.
He also followed their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And he went back to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds they'd given him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.
And Ahaziah's downfall came from God, in his going to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And while Jehu was executing judgement on the house of Ahab, he came across the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who served Ahaziah, and he killed them.

And he searched for Ahaziah, and they caught him while he was hiding in Samaria; and they brought him to Jehu and put him to death. And they buried him — they said, "He's the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." And the house of Ahaziah had no one left able to hold the kingship.
And when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she went and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath the king's daughter took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest — she was Ahaziah's sister — hid him from Athaliah, and she didn't kill him.
And he stayed with them, hidden in the house of God, for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

2 chronicles_23.t: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and brought the commanders of hundreds — Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri — into a covenant with him.
They went round through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said to them, "Look — the king's son is going to reign, just as the LORD has spoken concerning the sons of David.
"This is what you're to do. A third of you who come on duty on the sabbath, of the priests and the Levites, are to be gatekeepers at the thresholds;
"a third at the king's house, and a third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people in the courts of the house of the LORD.
"And no one is to come into the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who serve — they may go in, because they're holy; and all the people are to keep the duty of the LORD.

"And the Levites are to surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand; and anyone who comes into the house is to be put to death. Stay with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."

And the Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each of them took his men — those coming on duty on the sabbath together with those going off duty — because Jehoiada the priest hadn't dismissed the divisions.
Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, shields and bucklers that had belonged to King David and were in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each with his weapon in hand, from the right side of the house to the left, by the altar and by the house, around the king.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown and the testimony on him and made him king; and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they shouted, "Long live the king!"
And Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, and she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

And she looked — and there was the king, standing at his pillar at the entrance, with the officials and the trumpets beside him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers leading the praise with instruments of song. And Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, "Treason! Treason!"

And Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her is to be put to death with the sword" — because the priest had said, "You're not to put her to death in the house of the LORD."
And they laid hands on her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's house; and there they put her to death.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they'd be a people belonging to the LORD.
And all the people went to the house of Baal and pulled it down; they smashed its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.

Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hands of the priests, the Levites, whom David had apportioned over the house of the LORD, to offer up the burnt offerings of the LORD as it is written in the law of Moses, with joy and song, according to the directions of David.
And he stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any way could get in.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers among the people and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They came through the Upper Gate to the king's house and seated the king on the royal throne.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they'd put Athaliah to death with the sword.

2 chronicles_24.t: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And after this Joash set his heart on renewing the house of the LORD.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and collect silver from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year; and be quick about it." But the Levites weren't quick.

And the king summoned Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why haven't you required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy of Moses the servant of the LORD, and of the assembly of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?"
For Athaliah, that wicked woman — her sons had broken into the house of God, and they'd even used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
So the king gave orders, and they made a chest and set it at the gate of the house of the LORD, outside.
They made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy of Moses the servant of God, laid on Israel in the wilderness.
And all the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought it in and threw it into the chest until it was full.

And whenever the chest was brought to the king's officers by the hand of the Levites, and they saw there was a lot of silver in it, the king's scribe and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, and then take it back to its place. That's what they did day by day, and they gathered silver in abundance.

And the king and Jehoiada gave it to the men who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and craftsmen to renew the house of the LORD, and craftsmen in iron and bronze as well, to repair the house of the LORD.
And the men doing the work worked, and the repair went forward under their hand; and they restored the house of God to its proper condition and made it strong.

And when they'd finished, they brought the rest of the silver to the king and Jehoiada, and it was made into articles for the house of the LORD — articles of service and for offering up, pans, and articles of gold and silver. And they offered up burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually, all the days of Jehoiada.
And Jehoiada grew old and was full of days, and he died; he was a hundred and thirty years old when he died.
And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he'd done good in Israel, and towards God and his house.
And after Jehoiada died, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king; and now the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherim and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
And he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD; and they warned them, but they wouldn't listen.

And the spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood up above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: 'Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD? You can't prosper that way. Because you've forsaken the LORD, he's forsaken you.'"
They conspired against him and stoned him to death at the king's command, in the court of the house of the LORD.
And King Joash didn't remember the loyalty that Jehoiada his father had shown him — he killed his son. And as he was dying he said, "May the LORD see this and require it."
At the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against him. They came to Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the leaders of the people, and sent all their booty to the king of Damascus.

For the army of Aram came with only a small number of men, and the LORD gave into their hand an army of exceedingly great size, because they'd forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors; and on Joash they executed judgements.

And when they'd gone from him — they left him severely wounded — his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in the city of David, but they didn't bury him in the graves of the kings.
These are the men who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
And as for his sons, and the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God — they're written in the record of the scroll of the kings. And Amaziah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_25.t: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD — only not with an undivided heart.
And once the kingdom was firmly his, he killed the servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he didn't put their children to death; it's as written in the law, in the scroll of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers are not to die for children, and children are not to die for fathers; each is to die for his own sin."

Amaziah assembled Judah and organised them by ancestral houses, under commanders of thousands and of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered them from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand chosen men, fit for war, holding spear and large shield.
He hired from Israel a hundred thousand mighty men of valour for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "King, don't let the army of Israel go with you. The LORD isn't with Israel — not with any of the Ephraimites.
"But if you go anyway — act, be strong for the battle — God will make you stumble before the enemy; there's strength in God to help and to make stumble."
And Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what about the hundred talents I paid to the troop of Israel?" And the man of God said, "The LORD has more than that to give you."
So Amaziah dismissed the troop that had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home; and they were furious with Judah, and they went home in fierce anger.
Amaziah took courage and led out his people, went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the people of Seir.
And the people of Judah took ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of the rock and threw them down from the top of the rock; and every one of them was split open.

And the men of the troop that Amaziah had turned back from going with him to the battle raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria as far as Beth-horon; and they struck down three thousand of them and took a great deal of plunder.
And after Amaziah came back from defeating the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
And the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent him a prophet, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of a people who didn't deliver their own people from your hand?"

And while he was still speaking to him, the king said, "Have we made you a counsellor to the king? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" And the prophet stopped, but he said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you've done this and haven't listened to my counsel."
And Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come on — let's face each other."

And Joash king of Israel sent back to Amaziah king of Judah: "The thistle in Lebanon sent word to the cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And a wild animal of Lebanon came by and trampled the thistle.
"You've said, 'Look, I've struck down Edom' — and it's gone to your head and made you boast. Now stay at home. Why stir up disaster and fall — you, and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah wouldn't listen; it was from God, so as to give them into the enemy's hand, because they'd sought the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel went up, and they faced one another, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
And Judah was beaten by Israel, and they fled, every man to his tent.

Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh, brought him to Jerusalem, and broke down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem, from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate.
He took all the gold and silver, all the articles found in the house of God in Obed-edom's charge, the treasures of the king's house, and hostages — and returned to Samaria.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last — isn't it written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel?
And from the time Amaziah turned aside from following the LORD, they conspired against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
They carried him on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.

2 chronicles_26.t: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as Amaziah his father had done.
And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the seeing of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
He went out and fought against the Philistines, broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
And the Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the entrance of Egypt, because he'd grown exceedingly strong.
Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the Buttress, and fortified them.

And he built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, because he had a lot of livestock both in the Shephelah and on the plain; and he had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in the fertile land, because he loved the soil.

Uzziah had an army fit for war, going out to battle by divisions, according to the muster taken by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The whole number of the heads of the ancestral houses, mighty men of valour, was two thousand six hundred.
Under their command was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, making war with powerful strength, to help the king against the enemy.
Uzziah provided for them, for the whole army, shields, spears, helmets, body armour, bows and sling stones.

And in Jerusalem he made engines, devised by inventors, to stand on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. And his fame spread far, because he was wonderfully helped until he was strong.

But once he was strong, his heart grew haughty — and it was his own destruction. He acted unfaithfully against the LORD his God: he went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of valour.

And they stood up to King Uzziah and said to him, "It isn't for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD — that's for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are set apart as holy to burn incense. Get out of the sanctuary; you've acted unfaithfully, and it'll bring you no honour from the LORD God."

And Uzziah was enraged, with a censer in his hand to burn incense; and while he was raging at the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead, right in front of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.

And Azariah the chief priest turned to him, and all the priests did — and there he was, with leprosy on his forehead. They hurried him out of there, and he rushed to get out himself, because the LORD had struck him.

And King Uzziah had leprosy until the day he died, and he lived in a separate house, having leprosy, because he was cut off from the house of the LORD; and Jotham his son was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet wrote.

And Uzziah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings — they said, "He has leprosy." And Jotham his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_27.t: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as Uzziah his father had done — only he didn't go into the temple of the LORD. And the people still acted corruptly.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and built extensively on the wall of the Ophel.
He built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded areas he built fortresses and towers.

And he fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them; and that year the Ammonites gave him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. That's what the Ammonites brought him in the second year and the third as well.
And Jotham grew strong, because he'd ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the city of David, and Ahaz his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_28.t: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he didn't do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his ancestor had.
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and he also made molten images for the Baals.
And he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and burned his sons in the fire, following the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.

And the LORD his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram, and they struck him and took a great many captives from him and brought them to Damascus. He was given into the hand of the king of Israel too, who struck him a great blow.
And Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, all of them men of valour, because they'd forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Zichri, a warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer over the house, and Elkanah, second to the king.
And the Israelites took two hundred thousand of their brothers captive — women, sons and daughters — and they took a great deal of booty from them as well, and brought the booty to Samaria.

And there was a prophet of the LORD there — Oded was his name — and he went out to meet the army coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look — the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, so he gave them into your hand; and you've killed among them in a rage that has reached to the heavens.
"And now you say you're going to subdue the people of Judah and Jerusalem as your own male and female slaves. But haven't you got guilty acts of your own against the LORD your God?
"So listen to me: send back the captives you've taken from your brothers, because the burning of the LORD's anger is upon you."

And men from among the heads of the Ephraimites stood up — Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai — against the men coming from the war,

and said to them, "You're not bringing the captives in here. You mean to bring guilt on us before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt — and our guilt is great enough already, and burning anger is upon Israel."
So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the commanders and the whole assembly.

And the men designated by name got up and took charge of the captives; and all who were naked among them they clothed from the plunder. They clothed them, gave them sandals, fed them, gave them drink and anointed them, and they put everyone who was stumbling on donkeys and brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, to their brothers; and then they went back to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
And the Edomites had come again and struck Judah and carried off captives.
The Philistines had raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah and had captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, and Socoh, Timnah and Gimzo with their villages, and settled there.
For the LORD had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, because he'd let Judah run wild and had acted very unfaithfully against the LORD.
Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and harassed him, and gave him no strength.
For Ahaz had stripped the house of the LORD and the house of the king and the officials, and given it to the king of Assyria — and it was no help to him.
And at the very time he was harassed, he acted still more unfaithfully against the LORD — this same King Ahaz.

And he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, the ones who'd struck him, and said, "The gods of the kings of Aram are helping them, so I'll sacrifice to them and they'll help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.
And Ahaz gathered up the articles of the house of God and cut them up, and shut the doors of the house of the LORD; and he made himself altars on every corner in Jerusalem.
In every single city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Ahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem — they didn't bring him to the graves of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_29.t: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as David his ancestor had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east,
and said to them, "Listen to me, Levites! Set yourselves apart as holy now, and set apart as holy the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and bring the impurity out of the holy place.

"Our ancestors acted unfaithfully and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God, and they forsook him; they turned their faces away from the tabernacle of the LORD and turned their backs on it.
"They shut the doors of the porch too, and put out the lamps, and they didn't burn incense or offer up burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
"And the wrath of the LORD was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, of horror and of hissing — you can see it with your own eyes.
"And look — our ancestors have fallen by the sword, and our sons and daughters and wives are in captivity because of it.
"So now it's in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that the burning of his anger may turn back from us.
"My sons, don't be negligent now; the LORD has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and to be his ministers and those who burn incense."

The Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the Kohathites; of the Merarites, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
of the descendants of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
And they gathered their brothers and set themselves apart as holy, and they came, as the king had commanded by the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.

And the priests went inside the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and they brought out into the court of the house of the LORD all the uncleanness they found in the temple of the LORD; and the Levites took it from there to carry it out to the wadi Kidron, outside.

And they began setting apart as holy on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the porch of the LORD; they set apart as holy the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
And they went in to Hezekiah the king and said, "We've cleansed the whole house of the LORD — the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, and the table of the row of bread and all its articles.
"And all the articles that King Ahaz rejected in his reign, in his unfaithfulness, we've prepared and set apart as holy; and there they are, in front of the altar of the LORD."
And Hezekiah the king got up early and gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah, and he told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them up on the altar of the LORD.

They slaughtered the cattle, and the priests received the blood and dashed it against the altar; they slaughtered the rams and dashed the blood against the altar; they slaughtered the lambs and dashed the blood against the altar.
They brought the goats of the sin offering near, before the king and the assembly, and laid their hands on them.

And the priests slaughtered them and purified from sin with their blood against the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; because the king had said the burnt offering and the sin offering were for all Israel.

He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps and lyres, by the commandment of David and of Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet — for the commandment was by the hand of the LORD, through his prophets.
The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with trumpets.
Hezekiah gave the order to offer up the burnt offering on the altar; and as the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began, with the trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.
The whole assembly prostrated themselves, the singers sang and the trumpets sounded — all of it until the burnt offering was finished.
And when they'd finished offering up, the king and everyone who was present with him bowed and prostrated themselves.
And Hezekiah the king and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer; and they praised him with joy, and bowed low and prostrated themselves.

And Hezekiah spoke up: "You've consecrated yourselves to the LORD now. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." And the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and everyone who was willing of heart brought burnt offerings.
The number of the burnt offerings the assembly brought was seventy cattle, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs — all these as a burnt offering to the LORD.
The holy offerings were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.

Only the priests were too few — they couldn't skin all the burnt offerings; so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had set themselves apart as holy. For the Levites were more upright of heart in setting themselves apart as holy than the priests.
There were also burnt offerings in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offering. So the service of the house of the LORD was set in order.
And Hezekiah rejoiced, and all the people with him, over what God had prepared for the people; because the thing had come about suddenly.

2 chronicles_30.t: And Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and he wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh as well, to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep a passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king, his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel to keep the passover in the second month.
They hadn't been able to keep it at that time, because the priests hadn't set themselves apart as holy in sufficient numbers, and the people hadn't gathered at Jerusalem.
The plan was right in the eyes of the king and of the whole assembly.

And they established a decree to send a proclamation through all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, to come and keep a passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem; because they hadn't kept it in great numbers as it is written.

And the couriers went with the letters from the hand of the king and his officials through all Israel and Judah, as the king had ordered: "Israelites, come back to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, so that he may come back to those of you who are left, who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
"And don't be like your ancestors and your brothers, who acted unfaithfully against the LORD, the God of their ancestors, so that he made them an object of horror, as you can see.

"Don't stiffen your neck now, as your ancestors did. Give a hand to the LORD, and come to his sanctuary, which he's set apart as holy for ever, and serve the LORD your God, so that the burning of his anger may turn back from you.

"For if you come back to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion before their captors and will come back to this land. The LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and he won't turn his face away from you if you come back to him."
And the couriers went from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh and as far as Zebulun; but the people laughed at them and mocked them.
All the same, men from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah too the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to do what the king and the officials had commanded by the word of the LORD.
A great many people gathered at Jerusalem to keep the festival of unleavened bread in the second month — an exceedingly great assembly.
And they got up and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem; and all the incense altars they removed and threw into the wadi Kidron.
They slaughtered the passover on the fourteenth of the second month. The priests and the Levites were ashamed, set themselves apart as holy, and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
They stood at their posts, according to their ordinance, according to the law of Moses the man of God; the priests dashed the blood, taking it from the hand of the Levites.

For there were many in the assembly who hadn't set themselves apart as holy; so the Levites had charge of slaughtering the passover lambs for everyone who wasn't clean, to set them apart as holy to the LORD.

For most of the people — many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun — hadn't cleansed themselves, and they ate the passover otherwise than as it is written. For Hezekiah prayed for them: "May the LORD, who is good, make atonement for
"everyone who's set his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his ancestors, even though not according to the cleansing required for the holy place."
And the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
The Israelites present in Jerusalem kept the festival of unleavened bread for seven days with great joy, and the Levites and priests praised the LORD day by day, with loud instruments to the LORD.

And Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding towards the LORD. And they ate the appointed feast for seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
And the whole assembly agreed to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days with joy.

Hezekiah king of Judah contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and priests set themselves apart as holy in great numbers.
All the assembly of Judah rejoiced, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, and the resident aliens who came from the land of Israel and those living in Judah.
And there was great joy in Jerusalem; there'd been nothing like it in Jerusalem since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel.
And the priests and the Levites got up and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling, to the heavens.

2 chronicles_31.t: And when all this was finished, all the Israelites who were there went out to the cities of Judah and broke the pillars, cut down the Asherim and pulled down the high places and the altars, out of all Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they'd finished. Then all the Israelites went back, each to his holding, to their cities.

Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to serve, give thanks and praise in the gates of the camps of the LORD.

The king's portion from his own property went for the burnt offerings — the morning and evening burnt offerings, and those for the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed times — as it is written in the law of the LORD.
And he told the people, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, so that they could hold firmly to the law of the LORD.
As the word spread, the Israelites brought in abundance the firstfruits of grain, new wine, fresh oil and honey, and all the produce of the field, and the tithe of everything.

And the Israelites and Judahites who lived in the cities of Judah — they brought a tithe of herd and flock too, and a tithe of the holy things set apart as holy to the LORD their God; and they piled them up heap on heap.
In the third month they began the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.
Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, and blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
And Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, said to him, "Ever since the contribution began to be brought to the house of the LORD, we've eaten and been satisfied and had plenty left over. The LORD has blessed his people — and what's left over is all this."
Hezekiah gave orders to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.
They brought in the contribution, the tithe and the holy things in faithfulness. Conaniah the Levite was officer over them, with Shimei his brother second in command.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were officers under Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the officer of the house of God.
Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper on the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the contribution of the LORD and the most holy things.
Under his direction were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, faithfully distributing to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike,

besides the enrolment by genealogy of males from three years old and upward — everyone who entered the house of the LORD for the daily requirement, for their service in their duties by their divisions;
and the enrolment by genealogy of the priests by their ancestral houses, and of the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their duties by their divisions;
and to enrol by genealogy all their little children, their wives, their sons and their daughters, for the whole assembly — for in their faithfulness they set themselves apart as holy.

For the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pasture lands of their cities, in every single city, there were men designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled by genealogy among the Levites.
And Hezekiah did this throughout Judah; and he did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.
And in every work he began, in the service of the house of God and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God — he did it with all his heart, and he prospered.

2 chronicles_32.t: After all this, and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah; he encamped against the fortified cities, meaning to break into them for himself.
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was set on war against Jerusalem.
He took counsel with his officials and his warriors to stop up the waters of the springs outside the city, and they helped him.
And a great many people gathered and stopped up all the springs and the wadi that flowed through the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?" they said.

And he took courage and rebuilt all the broken-down wall, raised towers on it and built another wall outside it; and he strengthened the Millo of the city of David, and made weapons in abundance, and shields.
He appointed commanders of war over the people, gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and spoke encouragingly to them:
"Be strong and be courageous. Don't be afraid and don't be dismayed by the king of Assyria or by all the multitude with him; because there's one with us who is greater than the one with him.
"With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people leaned on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem — he was at Lachish with all his imperial might — to Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah in Jerusalem:
"This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: 'What are you relying on, that you're staying under siege in Jerusalem?
"'Isn't Hezekiah misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, "The LORD our God will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria"?
"'Isn't this the same Hezekiah who removed his high places and his altars and told Judah and Jerusalem, "You're to bow down before one altar, and burn incense on it"?
"'Don't you know what I and my ancestors have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands ever able to deliver their land from my hand?
"'Which of all the gods of those nations that my ancestors devoted to destruction was able to deliver his people from my hand — that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand?

"'So don't let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and don't believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has ever been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my ancestors — how much less will your gods deliver you from my hand!'"
And his servants spoke still more against the LORD God, and against Hezekiah his servant.

And he wrote letters to taunt the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him: "Just as the gods of the nations of the lands didn't deliver their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah won't deliver his people from my hand."
And they called out at the top of their voices in Judean to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten them and terrify them, so that they could capture the city.
They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
Hezekiah the king and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet prayed about this and cried out to the heavens.

And the LORD sent an angel, who annihilated every mighty man of valour and every officer and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. And he went back to his own land with shame of face; and when he went into the house of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
The LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of everyone, and gave them rest on every side.
And many brought an offering to the LORD at Jerusalem, and precious gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah; and from then on he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations.
In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death, and he prayed to the LORD; and the LORD spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah didn't repay according to the benefit done to him — his heart grew haughty; and wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
But Hezekiah humbled himself for the haughtiness of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and so the wrath of the LORD didn't come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and honour. He made himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stone, spices, shields and all kinds of desirable articles,
and storehouses for the yield of grain, new wine and fresh oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and pens for the flocks.
And he acquired cities for himself, and flocks and herds in abundance; because God had given him a great deal of property.
And it was Hezekiah who stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them down to the west of the city of David. And Hezekiah prospered in everything he did.

And so it was too in the matter of the envoys of the officials of Babylon, who were sent to him to enquire about the sign that had happened in the land — God left him, to test him, to know everything that was in his heart.
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his acts of loyalty, are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet, in the scroll of the kings of Judah and Israel.

And Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the graves of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did him honour when he died. And Manasseh his son became king in his place.

2 chronicles_33.t: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the abominations of the nations the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had pulled down, set up altars to the Baals, made Asherahs, bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the LORD, the house the LORD had said this about: "My name will be in Jerusalem for ever."
He built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courts of the house of the LORD.

And he made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and practised soothsaying, divination and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did a great deal of evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him.

And he set the carved image of the idol he'd made in the house of God — the house God had spoken about to David and to Solomon his son: "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I've chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I'll put my name for ever.

"And I won't remove the foot of Israel again from the ground I appointed for your ancestors — only if they're careful to do everything I've commanded them, all the law and the statutes and the judgements given by the hand of Moses."
And Manasseh misled Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had annihilated before the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
So the LORD brought the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria against them, and they captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze fetters and took him to Babylon.
And when he was in distress, he begged the LORD his God for favour, and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors.
He prayed to him, and he was entreated by him and heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. And Manasseh knew that the LORD — he is God.

And after this he built an outer wall for the city of David, west of Gihon in the wadi, running to the entrance at the Fish Gate; and he carried it round the Ophel and raised it very high. And he stationed commanders of the army in all the fortified cities in Judah.
And he removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, and all the altars he'd built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.
And he rebuilt the altar of the LORD and sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving on it; and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
But the people still sacrificed at the high places — though only to the LORD their God.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are in the acts of the kings of Israel.

And his prayer, and how God was entreated by him, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up the Asherim and the carved images before he humbled himself — they're written in the words of Hozai.
Manasseh lay down with his ancestors and was buried in his own house, and Amon his son became king in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done; and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made, and served them.
And he didn't humble himself before the LORD as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; instead Amon piled up more guilt.
His servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house.
And the people of the land struck down everyone who'd conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

2 chronicles_34.t: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the ways of David his ancestor, and didn't turn aside to the right or the left.

And in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of David his ancestor; and in the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images.

And they pulled down the altars of the Baals in front of him, and he cut down the incense stands that stood above them; and the Asherim, the carved images and the cast images he broke in pieces and ground to dust, and scattered it on the graves of the men who'd sacrificed to them.
He burned the bones of priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, among their ruins all around —
— he pulled down the altars, crushed the Asherim and carved images to dust, and cut down all the incense stands throughout the land of Israel; then he returned to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

They went to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought to the house of God, which the Levites who kept the threshold had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they went back to Jerusalem.

And they put it into the hands of the men doing the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD; and the men doing the work in the house of the LORD spent it on mending and repairing the house.
And they gave it to the craftsmen and the builders, to buy hewn stone and timber for the couplings, and to make beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

The men did the work faithfully. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the Kohathites, as overseers — and the Levites, every one of them skilled with instruments of song.
They were over the burden-bearers and directed all the workmen, service by service; and some of the Levites were scribes, officials and gatekeepers.
As they were bringing out the money that had been brought to the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the scroll of the law of the LORD given through Moses.
And Hilkiah said to Shaphan the scribe, "I've found the scroll of the law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.
And Shaphan brought the scroll to the king, and he brought the king a further report: "Everything that was entrusted to your servants — they're doing it.
"They've emptied out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and put it into the hands of the men appointed and the men doing the work."
And Shaphan the scribe told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll." And Shaphan read aloud from it before the king.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
And the king gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go and seek the LORD for me and for what's left in Israel and in Judah, about the words of the scroll that's been found. The wrath of the LORD that's been poured out on us is great, because our ancestors didn't keep the word of the LORD and didn't do everything written in this scroll."

And Hilkiah, with the men the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe — she was living in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter — and they spoke to her to that effect.
And she said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says. Tell the man who sent you to me:
"This is what the LORD says: I'm bringing harm on this place and on the people who live here — all the curses written in the scroll they read before the king of Judah.
"Because they've forsaken me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger with everything their hands have made, my wrath will pour out on this place and won't be quenched."
"And to the king of Judah, who sent you to seek the LORD — this is what you're to tell him: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the words you've heard:

"Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and against the people who live here — you humbled yourself before me and tore your clothes and wept before me — I have heard you too, declares the LORD.

"I'll gather you to your ancestors, and you'll be gathered to your graves in peace; and your eyes won't see all the distress I'm bringing on this place and on the people who live here." And they brought word back to the king.
Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up to the house of the LORD, with every man of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people from the greatest to the least; and he read out in their hearing all the words of the scroll of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

And the king stood at his place and made the covenant before the LORD — to follow the LORD and to keep his commandments, his testimonies and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, and to carry out the words of the covenant written in this scroll.
He made everyone present in Jerusalem and Benjamin take their stand in it, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

And Josiah removed all the abominations from all the territories that belonged to the Israelites, and he made everyone in Israel serve — serve the LORD their God. All his days they didn't turn aside from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

2 chronicles_35.t: Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them for the service of the house of the LORD.

And he said to the Levites who instructed all Israel, the ones who were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David king of Israel built. It isn't a burden on your shoulders any more. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel,
"and get yourselves ready by your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, following the writing of David king of Israel and the document of Solomon his son.
"And stand in the holy place, grouped by the ancestral houses of your kinsmen, the lay people, with a division of a Levite ancestral house for each.
"Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and make preparation for your kinsmen, to do what the LORD said by the hand of Moses."

Josiah contributed to the people flocks — lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings, for everyone present — thirty thousand in number, plus three thousand cattle, all from the king's own property.

His officials made a freewill contribution for the people, the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the officers of the house of God, gave the priests two thousand six hundred for the Passover offerings, and three hundred cattle.
Conaniah, Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, contributed five thousand for the Levites' Passover offerings, and five hundred cattle.
The service was arranged: the priests took their places and the Levites their divisions, at the king's command.
And they slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests sprinkled the blood from their hand while the Levites did the skinning.

And they set aside the burnt offerings, to give them to the groupings of the ancestral houses of the lay people, to present to the LORD as it's written in the scroll of Moses; and they did the same with the cattle.
They cooked the Passover lamb over the fire, according to the rule, and boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons and pans, then brought them quickly to all the people.

And afterwards they got things ready for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were offering up the burnt offerings and the fat pieces until nightfall; so the Levites got things ready for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their post, as David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer had commanded; and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They didn't have to leave their service, because their kinsmen the Levites made preparation for them.
So all the service of the LORD was arranged that day, to keep the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, at King Josiah's command.
The Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

And no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
After all this, when Josiah had put the house in order, Necho king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

But he sent messengers to him: "What's between me and you, king of Judah? It isn't you I'm against today, but the house I'm at war with; and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing the God who's with me, for your own sake, or he'll destroy you."

But Josiah wouldn't turn away from him; instead he disguised himself to fight him, and he didn't listen to the words of Necho, which came from the mouth of God; and he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
And the archers shot King Josiah; and the king said to his servants, "Take me away — I'm badly wounded."

And his servants took him out of the chariot and put him in his second chariot and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died, and was buried in the graves of his ancestors. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josiah.

And Jeremiah lamented over Josiah; and all the singers, men and women, have spoken of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them a fixed practice in Israel, and they're written in the Laments.
The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his acts of loyalty, in accordance with what is written in the law of the LORD,
and his acts, earlier and later, are written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah.

2 chronicles_36.t: The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and fined the land a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
The king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and Necho took Jehoahaz his brother away to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against him, bound him with bronze fetters and set out to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar took some of the articles of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his palace there.

And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and the abominations he committed, and what was found against him — they're written in the scroll of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

At the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and had him brought to Babylon, along with the precious articles of the house of the LORD, and made Zedekiah his kinsman king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He didn't humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
He rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar as well, who'd made him swear an oath by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning back to the LORD, the God of Israel.

The leaders of the priests and the people multiplied acts of unfaithfulness too, following all the abominations of the nations; and they made unclean the house of the LORD that he'd consecrated in Jerusalem.
And the LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them again and again by the hand of his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
But they kept deriding the messengers of God, despising his words and mocking his prophets, until the wrath of the LORD rose against his people and there was no healing.

So he brought the king of the Chaldeans up against them, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and he had no compassion on young man or virgin, the old or the infirm — he gave them all into his hand.
And all the articles of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and his officials — he brought the lot to Babylon.
They burned the house of God, pulled down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all its citadels with fire, and destroyed all its precious articles.
And he took into exile to Babylon those who'd survived the sword, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the rise of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfil the word of the LORD spoken by Jeremiah — until the land had accepted its sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, until seventy years were complete.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah would be completed, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent out a proclamation through his whole kingdom — and put it in writing too. It said:

"This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: 'The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Any of you from all his people — the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.'"

2 kings_1.t: After Ahab died, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and became ill. So he sent messengers and told them, "Go and consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron about whether I'll recover from this illness."

But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up and go to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is there no God in Israel, that you're on your way to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?'
"So this is what the LORD says: 'That bed you've gone up on — you won't be coming down from it. You're certainly going to die.'" And Elijah went.
