The messengers came back to him, and he said, "Why are you back?"

They told him, "A man came up to meet us and said, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him: This is what the LORD says: Is there no God in Israel, that you're sending to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? So that bed you've gone up on — you won't be coming down from it. You're certainly going to die.'"
He asked them, "What did the man look like, the one who came up to meet you and said this to you?"
They said, "A hairy man, with a leather belt round his waist." And he said, "That's Elijah the Tishbite."
Then he sent a commander of fifty to him with his fifty men. He went up to him, and there he was, sitting on top of the hill. And he said to him, "Man of God, the king says: Come down!"
Elijah answered the commander of fifty, "If I'm a man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.
Then he sent another commander of fifty to him with his fifty men, and he said to him, "Man of God, this is what the king says: Come down quickly!"
Elijah answered them, "If I'm the man of God, let fire come down from the heavens and consume you and your fifty." And the fire of God came down from the heavens and consumed him and his fifty.

Then he sent a third commander of fifty with his fifty men. And the third commander of fifty went up, and he came and knelt down in front of Elijah and pleaded with him: "Man of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.
"Look, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the first two commanders of fifty and their fifties. Now let my life be precious in your eyes."
Then the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Don't be afraid of him." So he got up and went down with him to the king.

And he said to him, "This is what the LORD says: You sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub the god of Ekron — is there no God in Israel whose word you could consult? — so that bed you've gone up on, you won't be coming down from it. You're certainly going to die."
So he died, just as the LORD had said through Elijah. And Jehoram became king in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because Ahaziah had no son.
The rest of what Ahaziah did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?

2 kings_2.t: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to the heavens in a whirlwind, Elijah set out from Gilgal with Elisha.
And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here. The LORD has sent me on to Beth-el." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I'm not leaving you." So they went down to Beth-el.
The sons of the prophets at Beth-el came out to Elisha and said, "Do you know that the LORD is taking your master from over your head today?" "I know that too," he said. "Be quiet."
And Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here. The LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I'm not leaving you." So they came to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and said, "Do you know that the LORD is taking your master from over your head today?" "I know that too," he said. "Be quiet."
And Elijah said to him, "Stay here. The LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I'm not leaving you." So the two of them went on.
Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them, a good way off, while the two of them stood at the Jordan.
Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the waters, and they parted to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed on dry ground.
Once they were across, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I should do for you before I'm taken from you." And Elisha said, "Let me have a double share of your spirit."
"You've asked a hard thing," he said. "If you see me taken from you, it'll be so for you; if not, it won't be."
And as they went on, walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in the whirlwind to the heavens.
Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!" And he didn't see him again. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
He picked up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and he went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters and said, "Where's the LORD, the God of Elijah?" And when he too struck the waters they parted to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.
The sons of the prophets at Jericho saw him from across the way and said, "The spirit of Elijah has rested on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed to the ground in front of him.

And they said to him, "Look, your servants have fifty able men here. Let them go and search for your master — maybe the spirit of the LORD has carried him off and set him down on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys." But he said, "Don't send them."
But they kept pressing him until he was embarrassed, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days and didn't find him.
They came back to him while he was still at Jericho, and he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, the city is well placed, as my lord can see — but the water's bad, and the land is barren."
And he said, "Bring me a new jar and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
He went out to the spring of the waters and threw the salt in and said, "This is what the LORD says: I've healed these waters. No more death or barrenness will come from them."
And the waters have been healed to this day, just as Elisha said they would be.
From there he went up to Beth-el, and as he was going up the road, small boys came out of the city and jeered at him: "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
He turned round and looked at them and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And two she-bears came out of the forest and tore forty-two of the boys to pieces.
From there he went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he went back to Samaria.

2 kings_3.t: Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father and mother; he got rid of the pillar of the Baal that his father had made.
But he held on to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he didn't turn away from them.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So King Jehoram marched out from Samaria that day and mustered all Israel.

He sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you come with me to fight Moab?" And he said, "I'll go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
"Which way shall we go up?" he asked. "By way of the wilderness of Edom," he said.
So the king of Israel set out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. They went round by a seven days' march, and there was no water for the army or for the animals following them.
And the king of Israel said, "Oh no! The LORD has called these three kings out only to hand them over to Moab."

But Jehoshaphat said, "Isn't there a prophet of the LORD here, so we can consult the LORD through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here — the one who poured water on Elijah's hands."
And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel went down to him, and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went too.

And Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets." But the king of Israel said to him, "No — the LORD has called these three kings out only to hand them over to Moab."
And Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, the one I stand before — if I didn't have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I wouldn't look at you or even see you.
"But now bring me a musician." And while the musician played, the hand of the LORD came on him.
And he said, "This is what the LORD says: Make this wadi full of ditches.
"For this is what the LORD says: You won't see wind and you won't see rain, yet that wadi is going to fill with water, and you'll drink — you and your livestock and your animals.
"And this is a small thing in the eyes of the LORD. He'll give Moab into your hand as well.
"You'll strike down every fortified city and every choice city, cut down every good tree, stop up all the springs of water and ruin every good plot of land with stones."
And in the morning, at the time of the grain offering, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land filled with water.
Now all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight them, so every man old enough to buckle on a belt was called out, and they took their stand at the border.
They got up early in the morning, and the sun was shining on the water; and Moab saw the water opposite them, red as blood.
And they said, "That's blood! The kings have fought each other and struck each other down. Now — to the plunder, Moab!"
But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck them, and the Moabites fled before them; and Israel pushed on into the land, striking Moab down.

They tore down the cities; every man threw his stone on every good plot of land until it was covered; they stopped up every spring of water and cut down every good tree — until only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left. And the slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but they couldn't.

Then he took his firstborn son, the one who was to reign in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great wrath against Israel, so they pulled back from him and went home to their own land.

2 kings_4.t: A woman, one of the wives of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know yourself that your servant feared the LORD; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
And Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what have you got in the house?" "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house," she said, "except a jar of oil."
And he said, "Go and ask your neighbours for vessels — empty vessels, and don't collect just a few.
"Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these vessels; and as each one fills up, set it aside."
So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They kept bringing her the vessels, and she kept pouring.
And when the vessels were full she said to her son, "Bring me another one." And he said, "There aren't any more." And the oil stopped.
She came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay off your debt, and you and your sons can live on what's left."
One day Elisha went over to Shunem, where there was a woman of standing, and she pressed him to stay and eat. After that, whenever he passed by, he'd turn in there to eat.
And she said to her husband, "I know that this man who keeps coming by us is a holy man of God.
"Let's make him a small walled upper room, and put a bed, a table, a chair and a lampstand in it for him; then when he comes to us he can turn in there."
One day he came there, and he turned into the upper room and lay down.
And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and she stood in front of him.

And he said to him, "Tell her this: You've gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Is there a word to be spoken for you to the king, or to the commander of the army?" And she said, "I live among my own people."
And he said, "Then what can be done for her?" And Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
And he said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
And he said, "At this same time next year, you'll be holding a son in your arms." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God — don't lie to your maidservant."
And the woman conceived and bore a son at that same time the next year, just as Elisha had told her.
The child grew up; and one day he went out to his father, to the harvesters.
And he said to his father, "My head! My head!" And his father said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
He picked him up and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees till noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door on him and went out.
Then she called her husband and said, "Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, and let me run to the man of God and come back."
And he said, "Why go to him today? It's not new moon or sabbath." And she said, "It's all right."
Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Lead on, and keep going. Don't slow down for me in the riding unless I tell you."
So she set off and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And when the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "There's that Shunammite!
"Run and meet her now, and ask her: Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?" And she said, "It is well."

She came to the man of God at the mountain and took hold of his feet. Gehazi came up to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone — she's bitter in herself, and the LORD has hidden it from me and hasn't told me."
And she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Didn't I say, 'Don't mislead me'?"
And he said to Gehazi, "Gird your loins, take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, don't greet him; and if anyone greets you, don't answer him. And lay my staff on the boy's face."
And the boy's mother said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I'm not leaving you." So he got up and followed her.
Gehazi had gone on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound and no response. So he went back to meet him and told him, "The boy hasn't woken up."
And Elisha came to the house, and there was the boy, dead, laid on his bed.
So he went in and shut the door on the two of them, and he prayed to the LORD.
Then he went up and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, his palms on his palms; and as he crouched over him, the child's flesh grew warm.
Then he turned away and walked up and down in the house, once one way and once the other; and he went up and crouched over him again. And the boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
And he called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." So he called her, and she came to him. And he said, "Pick up your son."
She came and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground; then she picked up her son and went out.

Elisha went back to Gilgal while the famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting in front of him. And he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on and boil some stew for the sons of the prophets."

One of them went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a wild vine and gathered wild gourds from it, as much as his garment would hold; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew — they didn't know what they were.
They poured it out for the men to eat; and as they were eating the stew they cried out, "There's death in the pot, man of God!" And they couldn't eat it.
And he said, "Then bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing bad in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalisha and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits — twenty barley loaves — and fresh grain in his sack. And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat."
And his attendant said, "How am I to set this in front of a hundred men?" And he said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat. For this is what the LORD says: They'll eat and have some left over."
So he set it in front of them, and they ate and had some left over, just as the LORD had said.

2 kings_5.t: Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and highly regarded, because through him the LORD had given victory to Aram; and the man was a mighty man of valour — and he was afflicted with leprosy.
Now the Arameans had gone out in raiding bands, and they'd taken a young girl captive from the land of Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.
And she said to her mistress, "If only my lord were before the prophet who is in Samaria! He'd deliver him from his leprosy."
And he went in and told his master, "The girl from the land of Israel said such and such."
And the king of Aram said, "Go ahead — and let me send a letter to the king of Israel." So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold and ten changes of clothes.
And he brought the letter to the king of Israel. It said, "Now when this letter reaches you — look, I've sent you my servant Naaman, and you're to deliver him from his leprosy."

And when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends me a man to deliver from his leprosy? Just look and see how he's picking a quarrel with me."

And when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent word to the king: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he'll know that there's a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and his chariot and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
And Elisha sent a messenger out to him: "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored to you, and you'll be clean."

But Naaman was angry and walked away. "Look," he said, "I told myself, 'He'll surely come out to me, and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place, and deliver the one afflicted with leprosy.'
"Aren't Amanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn't I wash in them and be clean?" And he turned and went off in a rage.

But his servants came up and spoke to him. "My father," they said, "if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, wouldn't you have done it? How much more when all he said to you was, 'Wash and be clean'?"
So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, just as the man of God had said; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

Then he went back to the man of God, he and all his company, and he came and stood in front of him and said, "Now I know that there's no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please, accept a gift from your servant."
But he said, "As the LORD lives, the one I stand before, I won't accept it." And he urged him to accept, but he refused.
And Naaman said, "If not, then let your servant be given two mule-loads of earth; because your servant won't be offering a burnt offering or a sacrifice to other gods any more, but to the LORD.

"And may the LORD forgive your servant for this one thing: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he's leaning on my hand and I bow down in the house of Rimmon — when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant for it."
And he said to him, "Go in peace." And he had gone some distance from him

But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "Look, my master has let this Naaman the Aramean off by not accepting what he brought. As the LORD lives, I'll run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi went after Naaman. And when Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is everything all right?"

And he said, "Everything's all right. My master sent me to say, 'Two young men have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

And Naaman said, "Please — take two talents." And he pressed him, and he tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them ahead of Gehazi.
And when he came to the hill, he took them from their hands and put them away in the house; then he sent the men off, and they went.
And he went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant hasn't been anywhere at all."

And he said to him, "Didn't my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is this a time to be taking silver — and to be taking clothes and olive groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male and female servants?
"So Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and to your offspring for ever." And he went out from his presence, afflicted with leprosy, white as snow.

2 kings_6.t: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, this place where we live before you is too cramped for us.
"Let's go to the Jordan and each of us get a beam from there, and make ourselves a place to live." And he said, "Go."
And one of them said, "Please, come with your servants." And he said, "I'll go."
So he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
And as one of them was felling a beam, the iron fell into the water; and he cried out, "Oh no, my lord — and it was borrowed!"
And the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place; and he cut off a piece of wood and threw it in, and made the iron float.
And he said, "Lift it out." So he reached out his hand and took it.
Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel, and he talked it over with his servants and said, "My camp will be at such and such a place."
And the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Watch out — don't go past this place, because the Arameans are coming down there."
And the king of Israel sent to the place the man of God had told him about and warned him; and he was on his guard there, more than once or twice.
The heart of the king of Aram was enraged over this, and he called his servants and said to them, "Won't you tell me which of us is for the king of Israel?"
And one of his servants said, "No, my lord the king. It's Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel — he tells the king of Israel the words you speak in your own bedchamber."
And he said, "Go and find out where he is, so I can send and seize him." And he was told, "He's in Dothan."
So he sent horses and chariots there, and a massive force; and they came by night and surrounded the city.

The attendant of the man of God got up early and went out — and there was a force surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. And his servant said to him, "Oh no, my lord! What are we going to do?"
And he said, "Don't be afraid. There are more with us than there are with them."
And Elisha prayed, "LORD, open his eyes so he can see." And the LORD opened the eyes of the servant, and he saw — and there was the hill, full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Strike this nation with dazzlement." And he struck them with dazzlement, just as Elisha had said.
And Elisha said to them, "This isn't the way, and this isn't the city. Follow me, and I'll take you to the man you're looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
And when they came into Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open these men's eyes so they can see." And the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw — and there they were, in the middle of Samaria.
And when the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "Shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down, my father?"

And he said, "You're not to strike them down. Would you strike down men you'd taken captive with your own sword and bow? Set bread and water in front of them; let them eat and drink and go back to their master."
So he laid on a great feast for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them off, and they went back to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram didn't come into the land of Israel again.
Some time after this, Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army and marched up and laid siege to Samaria.
And there was a great famine in Samaria — they kept up the siege until a donkey's head sold for eighty pieces of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
And as the king of Israel was going along the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Deliver, my lord the king!"
And he said, "If the LORD doesn't deliver you, where am I to get deliver for you? From the threshing floor? From the wine-press?"
And the king said to her, "What's the matter?" And she said, "This woman said to me, 'Give me your son and we'll eat him today, and we'll eat my son tomorrow.'
"So we boiled my son and ate him. And the next day I said to her, 'Give me your son and we'll eat him' — but she'd hidden her son."
And when the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes — he was going along the wall — and the people could see he had sackcloth on his flesh underneath.
And he said, "May God do this to me and more, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat is still on him at the end of today!"

Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And the king sent a man on ahead; but before the messenger got to him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent someone to take my head off? Look — when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it against him. Isn't that the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
He was still speaking to them when the messenger came down to him. And he said, "Look, this trouble is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

2 kings_7.t: And Elisha said, "Listen to the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will go for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

And the officer the king leaned on answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were making windows in the heavens, could a thing like that happen?" And he said, "You're going to see it with your own eyes, but you won't eat any of it."
Now there were four men afflicted with leprosy at the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here till we die?

"If we say, 'We'll go into the city' — the famine's in the city, and we'll die there; and if we sit here, we'll die. So come on, let's go over to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we live; and if they put us to death, we die."
So they got up at twilight to go to the camp of Aram; and they came to the edge of the camp of Aram, and there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the camp of Aram hear a sound of chariots, a sound of horses, the sound of a great army; and they'd said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us!"
So they got up and fled at twilight and left their tents, their horses and their donkeys — the camp just as it was — and they ran for their lives.

And these men afflicted with leprosy came to the edge of the camp and went into one tent, and they ate and drank and carried off silver and gold and clothes from it, and went and hid them. Then they came back and went into another tent and carried things off from there, and went and hid them.

Then they said to one another, "We're not doing right. This is a day of good news, and we're keeping it to ourselves. If we wait till morning light, punishment will catch up with us. Come on, let's go and tell the king's household."

So they came and called out to the gatekeeper of the city and told them, "We went into the camp of Aram, and there was no one there — not a sound of anyone, only the horses tied up and the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
And the gatekeepers called out, and word was passed to the king's household inside.

And the king got up in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we're hungry, so they've gone out of the camp to hide in the open country. They're saying, 'When they come out of the city we'll take them alive, and we'll get into the city.'"

And one of his servants answered, "Let them take five of the horses that are left in the city — they'll fare like the whole multitude of Israel that is left in it, they'll fare like the whole multitude of Israel that has perished — and let's send them out and see."
So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the camp of Aram: "Go and see."
They followed them as far as the Jordan, and the whole road was full of clothes and equipment the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. And the messengers came back and told the king.
Then the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram. And a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel and two seahs of barley for a shekel, just as the LORD had said.
Now the king had put the officer he leaned on in charge of the gate; and the people trampled him in the gate and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
It happened just as the man of God had told the king: "Two seahs of barley will go for a shekel and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria" —

and the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were making windows in the heavens, could a thing like that happen?" And he'd said, "You're going to see it with your own eyes, but you won't eat any of it."
And that's exactly what happened to him: the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

2 kings_8.t: Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he'd brought back to life, "Get up and go, you and your household, and stay wherever you can; because the LORD has called for a famine, and it's coming on the land for seven years."
So the woman got up and did what the man of God had said; she went with her household and lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
And at the end of seven years the woman came back from the land of the Philistines, and she went out to cry out to the king for her house and her field.
Now the king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and he said, "Tell me about all the great things Elisha has done."

And just as he was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead back to life, the woman whose son he'd brought back to life came in, crying out to the king for her house and her field. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman — and this is her son, the one Elisha brought back to life."

And the king asked the woman about it, and she told him. So the king assigned her a court official and said, "Give her back everything that's hers, and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now."
And Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram was ill, and he was told, "The man of God has come here."
And the king said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go and meet the man of God, and consult the LORD through him. Ask, 'Am I going to recover from this illness?'"

So Hazael went to meet him, taking a gift with him — every good thing of Damascus, forty camel-loads. And he came and stood in front of him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you to ask, 'Am I going to recover from this illness?'"
And Elisha said to him, "Go and tell him, 'You'll surely recover.' But the LORD has shown me that he'll surely die."
And he set his face and held it fixed until he was ashamed; and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" And he said, "Because I know the harm you're going to do to the Israelites: you'll set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their children to pieces and rip open their pregnant women."
And Hazael said, "But what is your servant — a dog — that he should do such a great thing?" And Elisha said, "The LORD has shown me you as king over Aram."
And he left Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he said, "He told me you'd surely recover."
And the next day he took the coverlet, dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died; and Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He followed the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done — Ahab's daughter was his wife — and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD wasn't willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, because he had promised him a lamp for his sons for all time.
In his days Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah, and they set up a king of their own.
So Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots; and he got up in the night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, and the chariot commanders — and the army fled to their tents.
So Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah to this day. And Libnah rebelled at the same time.
And the rest of the acts of Joram, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Joram lay down with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
And he went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

And King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.

2 kings_9.t: Now Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your loins, take this flask of oil with you and go to Ramoth-gilead.
"When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, get him up from among his brothers and take him into an inner room.
"Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I've anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run — don't wait."
So the young man went — the young man the prophet — to Ramoth-gilead.
He came in, and there were the commanders of the army, sitting there. And he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which one of us?" And he said, "For you, commander."

So he got up and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I've anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
"And you're to strike down the house of Ahab your master, and I'll avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.
"The whole house of Ahab will perish, and I'll cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, bond and free alike.
"And I'll make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah."
"And the dogs will devour Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and there'll be no one to bury her." And he opened the door and ran.
And Jehu went out to his master's servants, and one of them said to him, "Is everything all right? What did this madman want with you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and the way he talks."
And they said, "That's not true! Tell us." And he said, "This is what he said to me: 'This is what the LORD says: I've anointed you king over Israel.'"
And they hurried, and each of them took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps; and they blew the ram's horn and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been holding Ramoth-gilead with all Israel against Hazael king of Aram;

but King Jehoram had gone back to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had given him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Jehu said, "If this is what you want, don't let anyone slip out of the city to go and tell it in Jezreel."
So Jehu got into his chariot and went to Jezreel, because Joram was lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see Joram.

Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw Jehu's throng as he came, and he said, "I see a throng." And Jehoram said, "Get a horseman and send him to meet them, and have him ask, 'Is it peace?'"

So the horseman went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: Is it peace?" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Get round behind me." And the watchman reported, "The messenger reached them, but he isn't coming back."
So he sent out a second horseman, and he came to them and said, "This is what the king says: Peace?" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Get round behind me."
And the watchman reported, "He reached them, and he isn't coming back either. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi — he drives like a madman."

And Jehoram said, "Harness up!" And they harnessed his chariot. And Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his own chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu and found him at the plot of land of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And when Jehoram saw Jehu he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he said, "What peace, while the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and all her sorceries go on?"
And Jehoram wheeled round and fled, and he called to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
And Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and struck Jehoram between the shoulders; the arrow came out at his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

And he said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him into the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember — you and I were riding side by side behind Ahab his father when the LORD lifted up this oracle against him:

"'Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday — declares the LORD — and I'll repay you on this plot of land — declares the LORD.' So now, pick him up and throw him onto the plot of land, just as the LORD said."

And when Ahaziah king of Judah saw it, he fled by way of Beth-haggan; and Jehu went after him and said, "Strike him down too, there in the chariot!" — at the ascent of Gur, which is near Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
And his servants carried him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his grave with his ancestors in the city of David.
Now it was in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab that Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
And Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard about it, she painted her eyes and did her hair, and she looked down through the window.
And as Jehu came in at the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
And he looked up at the window and said, "Who's with me? Who?" And two or three court officials looked down at him.
And he said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
Then he went in and ate and drank, and he said, "See to this accursed woman and bury her — she's a king's daughter."
But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her but the skull, the feet and the palms of her hands.

So they came back and told him, and he said, "This is the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'In the territory of Jezreel the dogs will devour the flesh of Jezebel;
"'and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field, in the territory of Jezreel, so that no one will say, "This is Jezebel."'"

2 kings_10.t: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders and the guardians of Ahab's sons. They said:
"Now when this letter reaches you — you have your master's sons with you, and you have the chariots and the horses and a fortified city and the weaponry —
"pick the best and most upright of your master's sons, put him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
But they were terrified, and they said, "Look, the two kings couldn't stand before him — how are we going to stand?"

So the man over the palace, and the man over the city, and the elders and the guardians sent word to Jehu: "We're your servants. We'll do whatever you tell us. We won't make anyone king. Do what seems good to you."

Then he wrote them a second letter: "If you're for me, and you're listening to my voice, take the heads of the men, your master's sons, and come to me at Jezreel about this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
And when the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered them — seventy men — and they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
And the messenger came and told him, "They've brought the heads of the king's sons." And he said, "Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
And in the morning he went out and stood there and said to all the people, "You're innocent. Look — I conspired against my master and killed him. But who struck down all these?
"So know this: not one word of the LORD will fall to the ground, the word the LORD spoke about the house of Ahab. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah."
And Jehu struck down everyone left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel — all his great men, his close friends and his priests — until he left him no survivor.
Then he set out and went to Samaria. On the way he was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

and Jehu came across the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We're the brothers of Ahaziah, and we've come down to greet the king's sons and the sons of the queen mother."
And he said, "Take them alive." And they took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked — forty-two men — and he didn't spare one of them.

And he went on from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is, it is." "Then give me your hand." And he gave him his hand, and Jehu pulled him up into the chariot with him.
And he said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So they had him ride in his chariot.
And he came to Samaria and struck down everyone left of Ahab in Samaria, until he had destroyed him, just as the LORD had said to Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served the Baal a little. Jehu will serve him a great deal.

"So now, summon me all the prophets of the Baal, all who serve him and all his priests. Don't let anyone be missing, because I have a great sacrifice for the Baal. Anyone who's missing won't live." But Jehu was acting with guile, to destroy those who serve the Baal.
And Jehu said, "Set apart an assembly for the Baal." And they proclaimed it.
And Jehu sent word throughout all Israel, and all who serve the Baal came; not one stayed away. They came into the house of the Baal, and the house of the Baal was full from end to end.
And he said to the man over the wardrobe, "Bring out clothing for all who serve the Baal." So he brought the clothing out for them.

And Jehu went into the house of the Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab, and he said to those who serve the Baal, "Look around and make sure there's no servant of the LORD here with you — only those who serve the Baal, and no one else."

And they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside, and he'd said, "Whoever lets one of the men I'm putting into your hands escape — his life for his life."

And as soon as he'd finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the runners and the officers, "Go in and strike them down. Don't let anyone out." And they struck them with the edge of the sword; and the runners and the officers threw them out and went on into the city of the house of the Baal.
And they brought out the pillars of the house of the Baal and burned them.
And they pulled down the pillar of the Baal, and they pulled down the house of the Baal and made it into latrines — and that's what it is to this day.
So Jehu wiped out the Baal from Israel.
But Jehu didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin — the calves of gold that were at Beth-el and at Dan.

And the LORD said to Jehu, "Because you've done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab everything that was in my heart, your sons will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation."
But Jehu wasn't careful to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
In those days the LORD began to cut parts off Israel, and Hazael struck them down throughout the territory of Israel,
from the Jordan eastward: all the land of Gilead — the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites — from Aroer by the wadi Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.
And the rest of the acts of Jehu, and everything he did, and all his might — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehu lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
And the days Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years, in Samaria.

2 kings_11.t: Now when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she went and destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death — him and his nurse — into the bedchamber. So they hid him from Athaliah, and he wasn't put to death.
And he stayed with her in the house of the LORD, hidden, for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

But in the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the runners and brought them to him in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and he showed them the king's son.
And he gave them their orders: "This is what you're to do. A third of you, those coming on duty on the sabbath, are to keep watch over the king's house;
"a third at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the runners; and you're to keep watch over the house by turns.
"And the two divisions of you who go off duty on the sabbath are to keep watch over the house of the LORD for the king.

"You're to surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand; and anyone who comes into the ranks is to be put to death. Stay with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

And the commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each of them took his men — those coming on duty on the sabbath along with those going off duty — and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
And the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spear and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
And the runners took their places, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and by the house, all around the king.
Then he brought out the king's son and put the crown on him, and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"
And when Athaliah heard the noise of the runners and the people, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

And she looked — and there was the king, standing by the pillar as the custom was, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. And Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"

And Jehoiada the priest gave orders to the commanders of hundreds, the officers of the force: "Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her, put to death with the sword" — because the priest had said, "She's not to be put to death in the house of the LORD."
So they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.
And Jehoiada made the covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they'd be a people for the LORD — and between the king and the people.

And all the people of the land went to the house of the Baal and pulled it down; they smashed his altars and his images to pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of the Baal in front of the altars. And the priest appointed overseers over the house of the LORD.

And he took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the runners and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD; they came by way of the gate of the runners to the king's house, and he sat on the throne of the kings.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet — and they'd put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king's house.
Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.

2 kings_12.t: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.
And Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Only the high places weren't removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.

And Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money from the holy gifts that's brought into the house of the LORD — the census money, the money assessed for persons at his valuation, and all the money a man takes it into his heart to bring into the house of the LORD —
"let the priests take it, each from the people he knows; and they're to repair the damage to the house, wherever damage is found."
But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash the priests still hadn't repaired the damage to the house.

So King Jehoash called in Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why aren't you repairing the damage to the house? From now on, don't take any more money from the people you know — hand it over for the damage to the house."
And the priests agreed that they wouldn't take money from the people and wouldn't repair the damage to the house.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid, and he set it beside the altar, on the right as you come into the house of the LORD; and the priests who kept the threshold put in it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
And whenever they saw there was a lot of money in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest would come up and bag it and count the money found in the house of the LORD.

Then they'd hand the money they'd weighed out to the men doing the work, who were appointed over the house of the LORD; and they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders working on the house of the LORD,
and to the masons and the stonecutters, and for buying timber and hewn stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD — and for everything else that was laid out on the house to repair it.
But no silver bowls, snuffers, basins, trumpets or any articles of gold or silver were made for the house of the LORD out of the money brought into the house of the LORD;
it went to the men doing the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
And they didn't settle accounts with the men they handed the money to for paying the workers, because they were dealing in good faith.
Money from a guilt offering and money from sin offerings wasn't brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
Then Hazael king of Aram went up, fought against Gath and captured it; and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

So Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy things that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and he sent them to Hazael king of Aram; and he withdrew from Jerusalem.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And his servants rose up and formed a conspiracy, and they struck Joash down at Beth-millo, on the road going down to Silla.

It was Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down, and he died; and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David. And Amaziah his son became king in his place.

2 kings_13.t: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned seventeen years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin; he didn't turn away from them.
And the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, all their days.
But Jehoahaz begged the LORD for favour, and the LORD listened to him, because he saw Israel's oppression, how the king of Aram was oppressing them.
And the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they got out from under the hand of Aram; and the Israelites lived in their tents as they had before.
All the same, they didn't turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; they kept on in them. And the Asherah stayed standing in Samaria too.
For he'd left Jehoahaz no army but fifty horsemen, ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers; the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust to be trampled.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and everything he did, and his might — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he didn't turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin — he kept on in them.
And the rest of the acts of Joash, and everything he did, and his might, with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Joash lay down with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now Elisha had fallen ill with the illness he was going to die of; and Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over him and said, "My father, my father! The chariotry of Israel and its horsemen!"
And Elisha said to him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So he got himself a bow and arrows.
And he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So he put his hand on it, and Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands.

And he said, "Open the window towards the east." And he opened it. And Elisha said, "Shoot." And he shot. And he said, "An arrow of victory for the LORD, and an arrow of victory over Aram! You'll strike Aram at Aphek until you've finished them off."
And he said, "Take the arrows." And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." And he struck three times and stopped.
And the man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times! Then you'd have struck Aram until you'd finished them off. But now you'll strike Aram three times."
And Elisha died, and they buried him. Now marauding bands of Moab used to come into the land at the turn of the year.

And once, while they were burying a man, they suddenly caught sight of a raiding band, so they threw the man into Elisha's grave; and when the man touched Elisha's bones, he came to life and stood up on his feet.
Now Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the LORD showed them favour and had compassion on them and turned to them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; he wasn't willing to destroy them, and he hasn't cast them out from his presence to this day.
And Hazael king of Aram died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.

And Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in battle. Three times Joash struck him down, and he took back the cities of Israel.

2 kings_14.t: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, though not like David his ancestor. He did just as Joash his father had done.
Only the high places weren't removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.
And once the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he struck down the servants who had struck down the king his father.

But he didn't put the sons of those who struck him down to death, in keeping with what's written in the book of the law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers are not to be put to death for sons, and sons are not to be put to death for fathers; each is to be put to death for his own sin."
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and took Sela in the battle, and he named it Joktheel — that's what it's called to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu king of Israel: "Come on — let's look each other in the face."

And Jehoash king of Israel sent back to Amaziah king of Judah: "The thornbush in the Lebanon sent word to the cedar in the Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' But a wild animal in the Lebanon came by and trampled the thornbush.
"You've certainly struck Edom, and it's gone to your head. Take the honour and stay at home! Why stir up trouble and fall — you, and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah wouldn't listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and they looked each other in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
And Judah was beaten by Israel, and they fled, every man to his tents.

And Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh; and he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate — four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and hostages as well; and he went back to Samaria.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoash, what he did, and his might, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoash lay down with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
And the rest of the acts of Amaziah — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent men after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
And they carried him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his ancestors.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and reigned forty-one years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he didn't turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the sea of the Arabah, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had said through his servant Jonah son of Amittai the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher.
For the LORD had seen how bitter Israel's affliction was, with none left, bond or free, and no one to help Israel.
And the LORD hadn't said he would wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens; so he delivered them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and everything he did, and his might, how he fought and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, for Israel — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam lay down with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_15.t: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as Amaziah his father had done.
Only the high places weren't removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places.

And the LORD struck the king, and he was afflicted with leprosy until the day he died; and he lived in a house of separateness. And Jotham the king's son was over the palace, judging the people of the land.
And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Azariah lay down with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned six months.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done; he didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down before the people and killed him, and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Zechariah — look, they're written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
That was the word of the LORD that he had spoken to Jehu: "Your sons will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation." And that's how it turned out.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, came to Samaria, struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he formed — look, they're written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah and everyone in it and its territories, starting from Tirzah — because it wouldn't open to him, he attacked it; and he ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, all his days.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that his hands would be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the wealthy men, to give to the king of Assyria — fifty shekels of silver from each man. So the king of Assyria turned back and didn't stay there in the land.
And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem lay down with his ancestors, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

And Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the fortress of the king's house, along with Argob and Arieh; and fifty Gileadites were with him. And he killed him and reigned in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and everything he did — look, they're written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twenty years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he didn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead and Galilee — all the land of Naphtali — and took them into exile to Assyria.
And Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down and killed him, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
And the rest of the acts of Pekah, and everything he did — look, they're written in the chronicle of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD; he did just as Uzziah his father had done.
Only the high places weren't removed; the people still sacrificed and made offerings of smoke at the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.
And the rest of the acts of Jotham, what he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
And Jotham lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David his ancestor; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_16.t: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah became king.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he didn't do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as David his ancestor had done.
He followed the way of the kings of Israel, and he even made his son pass through the fire, following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.
And he sacrificed and burned offerings at the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up to Jerusalem to fight, and they besieged Ahaz, but they weren't able to fight against him.
At that time Rezin king of Aram took Elath back for Aram and cleared the Judeans out of Elath; and Edomites came to Elath, and they've lived there to this day.

And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria: "I'm your servant and your son. Come up and deliver me from the grip of the king of Aram and from the grip of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
And Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and he sent it to the king of Assyria as a bribe.
And the king of Assyria listened to him: he went up to Damascus, took it, carried its people off into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.

And King Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria at Damascus, and he saw the altar there in Damascus. And King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a likeness of the altar and its pattern, with all its workmanship.
And Uriah the priest built the altar; he did it exactly as King Ahaz had sent word from Damascus, before King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
And when the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar; and the king went up to the altar and made an offering on it.
And he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
And the bronze altar that stood before the LORD he moved from the front of the house, from between the new altar and the house of the LORD, and he put it on the north side of the altar.

And King Ahaz gave Uriah the priest his orders: "On the great altar make the morning burnt offering smoke, and the evening grain offering, and the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice. The bronze altar will be mine, to consult."
And Uriah the priest did everything King Ahaz had ordered.
And King Ahaz cut off the rims of the stands and took the washbasin off them; and he took the sea down from the bronze oxen that were under it and set it on a stone pavement.
And the covered structure for the sabbath that had been built in the house, and the king's outer entrance, he moved away from the house of the LORD, because of the king of Assyria.
And the rest of the acts of Ahaz, what he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Ahaz lay down with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_17.t: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel, and reigned nine years.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like the kings of Israel before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his subject and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria found treason in Hoshea: he'd sent messengers to So king of Egypt and hadn't brought up tribute to the king of Assyria as he had year by year. So the king of Assyria arrested him and shut him up in a prison house.
And the king of Assyria came up throughout the land; he came up to Samaria and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria captured Samaria, took Israel into exile to Assyria, and settled them in Halah, on the Habor (the river of Gozan), and in the cities of Media.

And all this happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and they had feared other gods,
and they'd followed the customs of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites, and the customs the kings of Israel had brought in.
And the Israelites did things secretly that weren't right, against the LORD their God, and they built themselves high places in all their cities, from a watchman's tower to a fortified city.
And they set up for themselves pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every green tree,
and they made offerings of smoke there at all the high places, like the nations the LORD had taken into exile before them; and they did evil things that provoked the LORD to anger.
And they served the idols, the very thing the LORD had told them, "You are not to do this."

And the LORD warned Israel and Judah through every prophet, every seer: "Turn back from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law I commanded your ancestors and sent to you through my servants the prophets."
But they wouldn't listen; they stiffened their neck like the neck of their ancestors, who hadn't trusted in the LORD their God.

And they rejected his statutes and his covenant that he'd made with their ancestors, and the testimonies he'd warned them with; and they followed emptiness and became empty, and followed the nations around them, the ones the LORD had commanded them not to imitate.

And they abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God; they made themselves a cast image, two calves, and they made an Asherah and bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served the Baal.

And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and they practised divination and read omens; and they sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
So the LORD was furious with Israel, and he removed them from his presence; no one was left but the tribe of Judah alone.
Judah didn't keep the commandments of the LORD their God either; they followed the customs Israel had brought in.
And the LORD rejected all the offspring of Israel and afflicted them and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until he had cast them out from before him.
For he tore Israel away from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and made them commit a great sin.
And the Israelites followed all the sins Jeroboam had committed; they didn't turn away from them,
until the LORD removed Israel from his presence, just as he'd said through all his servants the prophets. And Israel went into exile from its land to Assyria, and there they've been to this day.

And the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the Israelites; and they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
And when they first settled there, they didn't fear the LORD; so the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

And they said to the king of Assyria, "The nations you took into exile and settled in the cities of Samaria don't know the custom of the god of the land. So he's sent lions among them, and the lions are killing them, because they don't know the custom of the god of the land."
And the king of Assyria gave the order: "Send back one of the priests you took into exile from there. Let him go and live there, and let him teach them the custom of the god of the land."
So one of the priests they'd taken into exile from Samaria came and lived in Beth-el, and he taught them how they should fear the LORD.
But every nation went on making its own gods, and they put them in the house of the high places the Samaritans had made — each nation in the cities where they were living.
The people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the people of Cuthah made Nergal, the people of Hamath made Ashima,
the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
And they feared the LORD, and they appointed their own men as priests of the high places, who offered for them in the house of the high places.
They feared the LORD and served their own gods, following the custom of the nations they'd been taken into exile from.

To this day they go on with the old customs. They don't fear the LORD, and they don't act according to their statutes and their judgement, or according to the law and the commandment that the LORD commanded the descendants of Jacob, whose name he made Israel.
And the LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them: "You are not to fear other gods, or bow down to them, or serve them, or sacrifice to them.
"But the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm — he's the one you're to fear, the one you're to bow down to, the one you're to sacrifice to.
"And the statutes and the judgements and the law and the commandment that he wrote for you — you're to be careful to do them all your days; and you're not to fear other gods.
"And the covenant I made with you — don't forget it; and don't fear other gods.
"It's the LORD your God you're to fear, and he'll deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
But they wouldn't listen; they went on with their old custom.
So these nations feared the LORD and served their images; and their children and their children's children do just what their ancestors did, to this day.

2 kings_18.t: In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as David his ancestor had done.

He removed the high places, broke the pillars and cut down the Asherah; and he smashed the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because up to that time the Israelites had been making offerings of smoke to it — it was called Nehushtan.
He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel; and there was no one like him among all the kings of Judah after him, or among those before him.
And he clung to the LORD; he didn't turn away from following him, and he kept his commandments that the LORD had commanded Moses.
And the LORD was with him; wherever he went out, he did well. And he rebelled against the king of Assyria and wouldn't serve him.
He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territories, from a watchman's tower to a fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah — the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel — Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
And they captured it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hezekiah — the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel — Samaria was captured.
And the king of Assyria took Israel into exile to Assyria and settled them in Halah, on the Habor (the river of Gozan), and in the cities of Media,
because they hadn't listened to the voice of the LORD their God; they'd broken his covenant — everything Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded. They wouldn't listen, and they wouldn't do it.
And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.

And Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have sinned. Withdraw from me, and whatever you impose on me I'll bear." And the king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
And Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house.
At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doorposts that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and he gave them to the king of Assyria.
