And the king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rab-saris and the Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a massive force, to Jerusalem. They went up and came to Jerusalem, and they came and took their stand at the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the launderer's field.
And they called for the king; and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace, went out to them, with Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
And the Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah this. This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What's this trust of yours that you're trusting in?
"You say you have counsel and strength for war — but that's just talk. Now who are you relying on, that you've rebelled against me?

"Look at you — you're relying on that crushed reed of a staff, on Egypt. If a man leans on it, it goes into his hand and pierces it. That's what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to everyone who relies on him.

"And if you say to me, 'We trust in the LORD our God' — isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah took away, telling Judah and Jerusalem, 'You're to bow down in front of this altar in Jerusalem'?
"Come on then, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I'll give you two thousand horses, if you can find riders for them.
"How could you turn back even one governor, the least of my master's servants? And yet you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
"And now — is it without the LORD that I've come up against this place to destroy it? The LORD himself said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, and Shebna and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic — we understand it. Don't speak to us in Judean, with the people on the wall listening."

But the Rabshakeh said to them, "Is it to your master and to you that my master sent me to say this? Isn't it to the men sitting on the wall — who are going to eat their own excrement and drink the water of their own feet, along with you?"
Then the Rabshakeh stood up and called out at the top of his voice in Judean: "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
"This is what the king says: Don't let Hezekiah fool you — he won't be able to deliver you from his hand.
"And don't let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, 'The LORD will surely deliver us, and this city won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'

"Don't listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me, and every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree and drink the water of his own cistern,

"until I come and take you to a land like your own land — a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees, of fresh oil and of honey. Live — don't die! And don't listen to Hezekiah; he's misleading you when he says, 'The LORD will deliver us.'
"Has any god of the nations ever delivered his own land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
"Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
"Which of all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand — that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
But the people kept quiet and didn't answer him a word, because the king's order was, "Don't answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the palace, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they told him what the Rabshakeh had said.

2 kings_19.t: And when King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.
And he sent Eliakim, who was over the palace, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz.
And they said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress and rebuke and disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, and there's no strength to bring them out.

"Maybe the LORD your God will hear all the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that's left."
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
And Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master this. This is what the LORD says: Don't be afraid of the words you've heard, the ones the servants of the king of Assyria blasphemed me with.
"Look, I'm putting a spirit in him: he'll hear a report and go back to his own land, and I'll make him fall by the sword in his own land."
And the Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah — he'd heard that he'd left Lachish.
And he heard about Tirhakah king of Cush, "He's come out to fight against you." So he sent messengers to Hezekiah again:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah this: Don't let your God, the one you're trusting in, fool you by saying, 'Jerusalem won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'
"Look, you've heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction — and you're going to be delivered?
"Did the gods of the nations deliver them — the nations my ancestors destroyed: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
"Where is he — the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivvah?"
And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you are the God — you alone — of all the kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth.
"Turn your ear, LORD, and hear; open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words Sennacherib has sent to taunt the living God.
"It's true, LORD — the kings of Assyria have laid the nations and their lands waste,
"and they've thrown their gods into the fire; because they weren't gods but the work of human hands, wood and stone — and so they destroyed them.
"And now, LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, LORD, are God — you alone."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I've heard what you prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria."
This is the word the LORD has spoken about him: "She despises you, she laughs at you, the virgin daughter of Zion; she shakes her head behind your back, the daughter of Jerusalem.
"Who is it you've taunted and blasphemed? Who have you raised your voice against, and lifted your eyes so high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

"By the hand of your messengers you've taunted the Lord, and you've said: 'With my many chariots I've gone up the heights of the mountains, to the remotest parts of Lebanon; and I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest pines; and I came to its farthest lodging place, its densest forest.
"'I've dug and drunk foreign waters, and with the soles of my feet I dry up all the canals of Egypt.'
"Haven't you heard? I did it long ago, I formed it from days of antiquity; now I've brought it about, and you're to make fortified cities crash into ruined heaps.
"And the people living in them, powerless, were dismayed and put to shame; they were the vegetation of the field, the greenery of grass, grass of the housetops, blighted before it stands up.
"I know when you sit down and when you go out and when you come in, and how you rage against me.
"Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, I'll put my hook in your nose and my bridle on your lips, and I'll turn you back the way you came."

"And this will be the sign for you: this year you'll eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs up from that; and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
"And the escaped remnant of the house of Judah that's left will take root downward again and bear fruit upward.
"For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and an escaped remnant from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this."

So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: "He won't come into this city, and he won't shoot an arrow there; he won't confront it with a shield, and he won't throw up a siege mound against it.
"He'll go back the way he came; and into this city he won't come — declares the LORD.
"And I'll defend this city and deliver it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
And that night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria; and when they got up early in the morning, there they all were, dead corpses.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and went back, and he stayed in Nineveh.

And as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword and got away to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.

2 kings_20.t: In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death; and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: Put your house in order, because you're dying — you won't live."
And he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD:
"Please, LORD, remember how I've walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and how I've done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
And before Isaiah had got out of the middle court, the word of the LORD came to him:

"Go back and tell Hezekiah the ruler of my people: This is what the LORD, the God of David your ancestor, says: I've heard your prayer, I've seen your tears. Look, I'm healing you; on the third day you'll go up to the house of the LORD.
"And I'll add fifteen years to your days. And I'll deliver you and this city from the grip of the king of Assyria, and I'll defend this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
And Isaiah said, "Take a cake of figs." So they took it and put it on the boil, and he recovered.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What's the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I'll go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
And Isaiah said, "This is the sign for you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he's spoken: Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it go back ten steps?"
And Hezekiah said, "It's a small thing for the shadow to lengthen ten steps. No — let the shadow go back ten steps."
And Isaiah the prophet called out to the LORD, and he brought the shadow back on the steps it had gone down on the steps of Ahaz — back ten steps.
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he'd heard that Hezekiah had been ill.

And Hezekiah listened to them, and he showed them his whole treasure house — the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil — and his armoury, and everything in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah didn't show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and where did they come to you from?" And Hezekiah said, "They came from a distant land — from Babylon."
And he said, "What did they see in your house?" And Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my house. There's nothing in my storehouses I didn't show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD.
"Look, days are coming when everything in your house, and what your ancestors have stored up to this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
"And some of your own sons, the ones who come from you, whom you'll father, will be taken away; and they'll be court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon."
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD you've spoken is good." And he said, "Why not — if there'll be peace and stability in my days?"
And the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Hezekiah lay down with his ancestors, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_21.t: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the Israelites.

And he rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed; he set up altars to the Baal and made an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel had done; and he bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
And he built altars in the house of the LORD, the house the LORD had said this about: "In Jerusalem I'll put my name."
And he built altars to all the host of the heavens in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD.

And he made his son pass through the fire; he practised soothsaying and divination, and dealt with mediums and with spiritists. He did a great deal that was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.

And he put the carved image of the Asherah he'd made in the house — the house the LORD had spoken about to David and to Solomon his son: "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I've chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I'll put my name for ever.

"And I won't make the foot of Israel wander again from the ground I gave their ancestors — only if they're careful to do everything I've commanded them, and all the law my servant Moses commanded them."
But they wouldn't listen; and Manasseh misled them into doing more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
And the LORD spoke through his servants the prophets:
"Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations — he's done more evil than all the Amorites before him did — and has made Judah sin with his idols as well,
"this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Look, I'm bringing such a calamity on Jerusalem and Judah that both ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.
"And I'll stretch the measuring line of Samaria over Jerusalem, and the plummet of the house of Ahab; and I'll wipe Jerusalem the way you wipe a bowl — wiping it and turning it upside down.
"And I'll abandon the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies; and they'll become spoil and plunder for all their enemies,
"because they've done what is evil in my eyes and have been provoking me to anger from the day their ancestors came out of Egypt to this day."
And Manasseh shed a great deal of innocent blood as well, until he'd filled Jerusalem from end to end — besides his sin, by which he made Judah sin and do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
And the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and everything he did, and the sin he committed — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Manasseh lay down with his ancestors and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as Manasseh his father had done.
And he followed every way his father had followed; he served the idols his father had served and bowed down to them.
And he abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors, and didn't walk in the way of the LORD.
And Amon's servants conspired against him, and they killed the king in his own house.
But the people of the land struck down everyone who had conspired against King Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
And the rest of the acts of Amon, what he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And he was buried in his grave in the garden of Uzza; and Josiah his son reigned in his place.

2 kings_22.t: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.
And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD; he walked in every way of David his ancestor and didn't turn aside to the right or to the left.
And in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of the LORD with these orders:
"Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and have him total up the silver that's been brought into the house of the LORD, which the keepers of the threshold have collected from the people;

"and have them put it into the hands of the men doing the work, who are appointed over the house of the LORD; and let them give it to the men working on the house of the LORD, to repair the damage to the house —
"to the craftsmen and the builders and the masons, and for buying timber and hewn stones to repair the house."
Only, no account was taken of the silver put into their hands, because they were working in good faith.
And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I've found the book of the law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

And Shaphan the scribe came to the king and brought him word back: "Your servants have poured out the silver that was found in the house, and they've put it into the hands of the men doing the work, who are appointed over the house of the LORD."
And Shaphan the scribe told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud to the king.
And when the king heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his clothes.
And the king gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go and consult the LORD for me and for the people and for all Judah about the words of this book that's been found. The rage of the LORD that's been kindled against us is great, because our ancestors didn't listen to the words of this book and didn't do everything written there about us."

So Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments — she was living in Jerusalem in the Second District — and they spoke to her.
And she said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says. Tell the man who sent you to me:
"This is what the LORD says: Look, I'm bringing calamity on this place and on the people who live here — everything in the book the king of Judah has read.
"Because they've abandoned me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger with everything their hands have made, my rage will be kindled against this place and won't be quenched.
"And to the king of Judah, who sent you to consult the LORD — this is what you're to tell him: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the words you've heard:

"Because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I'd spoken against this place and against the people who live here — that they'd become a horror and a curse — and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I have heard you too — declares the LORD.
"So I'm gathering you to your ancestors, and you'll be gathered to your grave in peace, and your eyes won't look on all the calamity I'm bringing on this place." And they brought the king word back.

2 kings_23.t: And the king sent word, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem gathered to him.

And the king went up to the house of the LORD, with every man of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from the least to the greatest; and he read out in their hearing everything in the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.

And the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD — to follow the LORD and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and with all their soul, and to carry out the words of this covenant written on this book. And all the people took their stand in the covenant.

And the king ordered Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and the keepers of the threshold to bring out of the temple of the LORD all the articles made for the Baal and for the Asherah and for all the host of the heavens; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried their dust to Bethel.

And he put down the idolatrous priests the kings of Judah had appointed, who had burned offerings at the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem — and those who burned offerings to the Baal, to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations and to all the host of the heavens.

And he brought the Asherah out of the house of the LORD, outside Jerusalem to the wadi Kidron, and burned it there at the wadi Kidron and crushed it to dust, and threw its dust on the burial place of the common people.
And he broke down the houses of the cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women were weaving hangings for the Asherah.

And he brought all the priests in from the cities of Judah, and he made unclean the high places where the priests had burned offerings, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down the high places of the gates at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, on the left as you come in at the city gate.
All the same, the priests of the high places didn't go up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem, though they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
And he made the Topheth in the valley of Ben-hinnom unclean, so that no one could make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to the Molech.

And he got rid of the horses the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance of the house of the LORD, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the court official, which was in the precincts; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.

And the altars that were on the roof, the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD — the king pulled them down; and he smashed them there and threw their dust into the wadi Kidron.

And the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of the Destroyer, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte the detestable thing of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites — the king made them unclean.
And he broke the pillars, cut down the Asherim, and filled their places with human bones.

And the altar at Bethel too, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made — that altar and the high place he tore down as well; and he burned the high place, crushed it to dust, and burned the Asherah.

And Josiah turned and saw the graves there on the mountain, and he sent and took the bones out of the graves and burned them on the altar and made it unclean, just as the LORD had said through the man of God who proclaimed these words.

And he said, "What's that monument I can see?" And the men of the city told him, "That's the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed the very things you've done to the altar of Bethel."
And he said, "Leave him alone — no one is to disturb his bones." So they left his bones undisturbed, along with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
And all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria too, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke to anger — Josiah got rid of them; and he did to them everything he'd done at Bethel.
And he slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there, on the altars, and burned human bones on them; and then he went back to Jerusalem.
And the king gave all the people this order: "Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it's written in this book of the covenant."
For no Passover like it had been kept since the days of the judges who judged Israel, or in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah;
but in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.

And the mediums too, and the spiritists and the teraphim and the idols and all the detestable things that could be seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem — Josiah burned them away, to carry out the words of the law written on the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.

And there'd never been a king like him before, who turned back to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses; and after him no one like him arose.
Even so, the LORD didn't turn back from the burning of his great anger, which burned against Judah because of all the provocations Manasseh had provoked him with.
And the LORD said, "I'll remove Judah from before my face too, as I removed Israel; and I'll reject this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house I said my name would be in."
And the rest of the acts of Josiah, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria, to the river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Neco killed him at Megiddo as soon as he saw him.

And his servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own grave. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his ancestors had done.
And Pharaoh Neco shut him up at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he couldn't reign in Jerusalem; and he laid a fine on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father and changed his name to Jehoiakim; and he took Jehoahaz away, and he came to Egypt and died there.

And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he had to assess the land to raise the silver at Pharaoh's command — he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, from each man according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebidah, daughter of Pedaiah, from Rumah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his ancestors had done.

2 kings_24.t: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his vassal for three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.

And the LORD sent against him the raiding bands of the Chaldeans and the raiding bands of Aram and the raiding bands of Moab and the raiding bands of the Ammonites; he sent them against Judah to destroy it, just as the LORD had said through his servants the prophets.
Surely it was at the command of the LORD that this came on Judah, to remove them from before his face, because of the sins of Manasseh, everything he'd done,
and because of the innocent blood he'd shed, filling Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the LORD wasn't willing to forgive.
And the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and everything he did — isn't it written in the chronicle of the kings of Judah?
And Jehoiakim lay down with his ancestors, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
And the king of Egypt didn't come out of his land again, because the king of Babylon had taken everything that had belonged to the king of Egypt, from the wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father had done.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.
And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, with his mother, his servants, his officials and his court officials; and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; and he cut up all the gold articles that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of the LORD, just as the LORD had said.

And he took all Jerusalem into exile — all the officials and all the mighty men of valour, ten thousand exiles, and every craftsman and smith; no one was left but the poorest of the people of the land.
And he took Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon, and the king's mother, the king's wives, his court officials and the leading men of the land he led away into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And all the men of valour, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand — all of them warriors, trained for war — the king of Babylon brought into exile to Babylon.
And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
For it was because of the anger of the LORD that all this happened in Jerusalem and in Judah, until he cast them out from before his face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

2 kings_25.t: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem. He encamped against it, and they built a siege wall around it.
And the city stayed under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
By the ninth of the month the famine in the city was severe, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

Then the city was broken into. All the men of war fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city; and he went by way of the Arabah.
And the army of the Chaldeans went after the king and caught up with him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they passed sentence on him.
And they slaughtered Zedekiah's sons in front of his eyes; then he blinded Zedekiah's eyes and bound him with bronze fetters and brought him to Babylon.

In the fifth month, on the seventh of the month — the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard, the servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of the LORD and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.
And the whole army of the Chaldeans with the chief of the guard broke down the walls of Jerusalem all around.
And the rest of the people left in the city, and the deserters who'd gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude — Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took them into exile.
But the chief of the guard left some of the poorest of the land behind, to be vinedressers and ploughmen.
And the bronze pillars in the house of the LORD, the stands, and the bronze sea in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried the bronze to Babylon.
And the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the pans and all the bronze articles used in the service — they took them.
And the fire-pans and the basins — the gold as gold and the silver as silver — the chief of the guard took.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD — there was no weighing the bronze of all these articles.

One pillar was eighteen cubits high, with a bronze capital on it three cubits high, and a network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with its network.
And the chief of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold,

and from the city he took one court official who was officer of the men of war, five of those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
And over the people left behind in the land of Judah, the ones Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

And all the commanders of the armies, with their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, with their men.
And Gedaliah swore an oath to them and to their men, and he said, "Don't be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Settle in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it'll go well for you."

But in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal line, came with ten men; and they struck Gedaliah down, and he died — and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, and the commanders of the armies, got up and went to Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of the prison house.
And he spoke kindly with him and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he put off his prison clothes, and he ate bread before him regularly, all the days of his life.
And his allowance, a regular allowance, was given him by the king, a daily portion for each day, all the days of his life.

2 samuel_1.t: After Saul died, David came back from defeating the Amalekites and stayed two days in Ziklag.
On the third day a man came in from the camp, from Saul, his clothes torn and earth on his head. When he reached David he fell to the ground and bowed down.
David said to him, "Where have you come from?" He said, "I've escaped from the camp of Israel."
David said, "What happened? Tell me." He said, "The army fled the battle. Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan died too."
David said to the young man bringing the news, "How do you know Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
The young man bringing the news said, "I just happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the horsemen right on him."
He turned round, saw me, and called out to me, and I said, "Here I am."
He said to me, "Who are you?" I said, "I'm an Amalekite."
He said to me, "Stand over me and kill me. The convulsion has hold of me, and I'm still alive."
So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew he wouldn't live after he'd fallen. Then I took the crown off his head and the armlet off his arm, and I've brought them here to my lord.
David grabbed his clothes and tore them, and so did every man with him.
They mourned and wept and fasted until evening over Saul and over his son Jonathan, over the people of the LORD and over the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
David said to the young man who had brought the news, "Where are you from?" He said, "I'm the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite."
David said to him, "How is it you weren't afraid to lift your hand and destroy the LORD's anointed?"
David called one of his young men over and said, "Come here — strike him down." He struck him down and he died.
David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head. Your own mouth testified against you: 'I killed the LORD's anointed.'"
And David sang this lament over Saul and over his son Jonathan,
and he gave word that the people of Judah should be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the scroll of Jashar:
The beauty, Israel, lies slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
Don't tell it in Gath, don't bear the news in the streets of Ashkelon, or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice, or the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew and no rain on you, nor fields of contributions; for there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
Saul and Jonathan, beloved and lovely, in their lives and in their death they were not parted. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxuries, who put ornaments of gold on your clothing.
How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan lies slain on your high places.
I'm in distress over you, my brother Jonathan. You were very pleasant to me. Your love to me was more wonderful than the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!

2 samuel_2.t: After this David asked the LORD, "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" The LORD said, "Go up." David said, "Where shall I go up?" He said, "To Hebron."
So David went up there, and his two wives with him, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
David brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns around Hebron.
Then the men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over the house of Judah. And they told David, "It was the men of Jabesh Gilead who buried Saul."
David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh Gilead to say to them, "May the LORD bless you for showing this loyalty to your lord Saul, and burying him."
"And now may the LORD show you steadfast love and faithfulness. And I too will do you good, because you did this."
"So take heart and be brave, for your lord Saul is dead — and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."
But Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Saul's son Ish-bosheth over to Mahanaim,
and made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin and all Israel.
Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.
David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months.
Abner son of Ner went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon with the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul.
Joab son of Zeruiah and David's servants went out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. One group sat on one side of the pool, the other on the other side.
Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men get up and make sport in front of us." Joab said, "Let them get up."
So they got up and crossed over, counted out: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from David's servants.
Each seized the head of the man opposite him, with his sword in the man's side, and they fell together. That place was called Helkath Hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
The battle that day was very hard, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by David's servants.
The three sons of Zeruiah were there — Joab, Abishai and Asahel — and Asahel was swift of foot, like one of the gazelles of the open country.
Asahel went after Abner and did not turn aside to right or left from following him.
Abner looked behind him and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" He said, "It is."
Abner said to him, "Turn off to your right or your left. Take one of the young men and take his gear for yourself." But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
Abner said to Asahel again, "Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I face Joab your brother?"

He refused to turn aside, and Abner struck him in the belly with the butt of his spear. The spear came out behind him, and he fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.
Joab and Abishai kept after Abner, and the sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which faces Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
The Benjaminites gathered behind Abner into a single band and took their stand on top of one hill.
Abner called out to Joab, "Is the sword going to devour for ever? Don't you know the end will be bitter? How long before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?"
Joab said, "As God lives — if you hadn't spoken, the people would've kept after their brothers till morning."
So Joab blew the horn, and all the people halted. They stopped pursuing Israel and did not fight any more.
Abner and his men marched through the Arabah all that night, crossed the Jordan, went on through the whole Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
Joab came back from pursuing Abner and gathered all the people. Nineteen of David's servants were missing — and Asahel.
But David's servants had struck down three hundred and sixty of Benjamin and of Abner's men, and they died.
They carried Asahel up and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Joab and his men marched all night, and day broke on them at Hebron.

2 samuel_3.t: The war between the house of Saul and the house of David went on a long time. David kept growing stronger and the house of Saul kept growing weaker.
Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;
his second, Kileab, by Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
While the war between the house of Saul and the house of David went on, Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.
Now Saul had a concubine named Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

Abner was furious at what Ish-bosheth said. "Am I a dog's head, one of Judah's? To this day I've shown loyalty to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and his friends, and I haven't handed you over to David. And now you charge me with guilt over this woman!"
"So may God do to Abner, and more, if I don't do for David just what the LORD swore to him:
"to take the kingdom away from the house of Saul and set up David's throne over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
He could not say another word to Abner, because he was afraid of him.
Abner sent messengers to David on his own account, saying, "Whose is the land?" — and, "Make your covenant with me, and I will be at your side to bring all Israel round to you."
He said, "Good. I'll make a covenant with you. Just one thing I ask: you won't see my face unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see me."
David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul: "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.
Her husband went with her, walking and weeping behind her, as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back." And he went back.
Abner had a word with the elders of Israel: "For some time now you have been wanting David as king over you.
"So act now. For the LORD has said to David, 'By the hand of David my servant I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
Abner also spoke to Benjamin, and then went to tell David at Hebron everything that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, and David made a feast for Abner and the men with him.

Abner said to David, "Let me go and gather all Israel to my lord the king. Let them make a covenant with you, and you'll reign over all you could wish for." And David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
Just then David's servants and Joab came in from a raid, bringing a great deal of plunder with them. Abner was no longer with David at Hebron — David had sent him away and he had gone in peace.
When Joab and all the army with him arrived, they told Joab, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and the king sent him away, and he went in peace."
Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you! Why did you send him away, so that he's gone clean off?"
"You know Abner son of Ner. He came to deceive you, to learn your comings and goings, and to learn everything you're doing."
Joab went out from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. And David didn't know.
When Abner came back to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the gateway to speak with him privately, and struck him there in the belly. He died for the blood of Asahel his brother.
David heard of it afterwards and said, "I and my kingdom are innocent before the LORD for ever of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

"Let it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father's house. Let the house of Joab never be without a man with a discharge, a man with leprosy, a man who holds the spindle, a man who falls by the sword, a man who has no bread."
So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner because he had put their brother Asahel to death at Gibeon in the battle.
David said to Joab and to all the people with him, "Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth and mourn for Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.
They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept at Abner's grave, and all the people wept.
And the king sang a lament over Abner: "Should Abner die as a fool dies?
Your hands weren't bound, your feet weren't put in bronze fetters. You fell as one falls before wicked men." And all the people wept over him again.
All the people came to get David to eat bread while it was still day, but David swore, "So may God do to me, and more, if I taste bread or anything at all before the sun goes down."
All the people took note, and it seemed good to them — as everything the king did seemed good to all the people.
And all the people and all Israel knew that day that the killing of Abner son of Ner had not come from the king.
And the king said to his servants, "Don't you know that a leader and a great man has fallen today in Israel?
"And today I'm weak, though I'm the anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May the LORD repay the one who does evil according to his evil."

2 samuel_4.t: When Saul's son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands went slack, and all Israel was dismayed.
Saul's son had two men who commanded raiding bands: one was named Baanah, the second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the Benjaminites — for Beeroth too is reckoned to Benjamin,
and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as resident aliens to this day.

Now Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was crippled in both feet. He was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, and in her haste he fell and was lamed. His name was Mephibosheth.
The sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.
They came into the middle of the house as though fetching wheat, and struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
They had come into the house while he was lying on his bed in his bedchamber, struck him and killed him and took off his head. Then they took his head and travelled by way of the Arabah all night.

They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here's the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his offspring."
David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, "As the LORD lives, who has ransomed my life from every trouble —
"when the man who told me 'Saul is dead' — and thought he was bringing good news — I seized him and killed him in Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news.
"How much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house, on his own bed! Shouldn't I now require his blood from your hand and rid the earth of you?"

David gave the order to the young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them by the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner's tomb at Hebron.

2 samuel_5.t: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "Here we are — your own bone and flesh.

"For some time now, while Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"
So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.
David was thirty when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, who lived in the land. And they said to David, "You won't get in here — the blind and the lame will turn you back," meaning, "David won't get in here."
But David captured the stronghold of Zion — that is, the City of David.

And David said that day, "Anyone who strikes a Jebusite, let him get at the lame and the blind by the water shaft — they are hated by David." That is why they say, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."
David settled in the stronghold and called it the City of David, and he built all round, from the Millo inward.
And David grew steadily greater, and the LORD, God of hosts, was with him.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar timber and craftsmen in wood and stone, and they built a house for David.
And David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to look for David. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
The Philistines came and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
David asked the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you give them into my hand?" And the LORD said to David, "Go up. I'll certainly give the Philistines into your hand."
David came to Baal Perazim and struck them down there. He said, "The LORD has burst through my enemies before me like a bursting of waters." That is why the place was called Baal Perazim.
They abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.
The Philistines came up once more and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
David asked the LORD, and he said, "Do not go up. Go round behind them and come at them opposite the balsam trees.
"When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, act at once — for then the LORD's gone out ahead of you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
David did so, just as the LORD had commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines from Geba as far as Gezer.

2 samuel_6.t: David again gathered all the chosen men in Israel, thirty thousand of them.
David and all the people with him set out from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of hosts, who sits enthroned on the cherubim.
They set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart,
and they carried it from the house of Abinadab on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio walked ahead of the ark.
David and all the house of Israel were making music before the LORD with every kind of fir wood — lyres and harps, tambourines, rattles and cymbals.
They came to the threshing floor of Nacon, and Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen had let it slip.
The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
David was angry because the LORD had burst out against Uzzah, and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.
David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"
David was not willing to bring the ark of the LORD round to himself in the City of David, so he turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
The ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.
When those carrying the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
And David danced with all his strength before the LORD, wearing a linen ephod.
David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sound of the horn.

As the ark of the LORD was coming into the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
They brought the ark of the LORD and set it in its place, inside the tent David had pitched for it, and David offered up burnt offerings before the LORD, and peace offerings.
When David had finished offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
He gave out to all the people, to the whole multitude of Israel, men and women alike, one loaf of bread each, one date-cake and one raisin-cake. And all the people went home, each to his house.

David went back to bless his household, and Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet him. "How the king of Israel has honoured himself today," she said, "uncovering himself before the eyes of his servants' maidservants, as one of the worthless men shamelessly uncovers himself!"

David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me rather than your father and all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel — and I'll make music before the LORD!
"And I'll make myself lighter still than this, and be lowly in my own eyes. But with the maidservants you spoke of — with them I'll be honoured."
And Michal daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

2 samuel_7.t: When the king was settled in his house and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I'm living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God is under a tent curtain."
Nathan said to the king, "Whatever is in your heart, go and do it — the LORD's with you."
But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan:
"Go and say to my servant David: Thus says the LORD: Are you the one to build me a house to dwell in?
"I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt until this day. I have been moving about, in a tent and a tabernacle.
"In all my moving about among all the Israelites, did I ever say a word to one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel — Why haven't you built me a house of cedar?"
"And now say this to my servant David: Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
"I have been with you wherever you went, and I have cut off all your enemies before you, and I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth.
"I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them there. They will dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more, and wicked men will not afflict them again as they did at the first,
"from the day I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. And the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make you a house.
"When your days are done and you lie down with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
"He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
"I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. When he does wrong I will reprove him with the rod of men, with the blows human beings give.
"But my steadfast love will not depart from him, as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
"Your house and your kingdom will be made sure for ever before you. Your throne will be established for ever."
Just so, in all these words and all this vision, Nathan spoke to David.
Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
"And even this was a small thing in your eyes, Lord GOD, and you have spoken also about the house of your servant for a long time to come. And this is the instruction of humankind, Lord GOD.
"And what more can David say to you? You know your servant, Lord GOD.
"For the sake of your word and according to your own heart you have done all this great thing, to let your servant know it.
"Therefore you are great, Lord GOD. There's none like you, and there's no God besides you, in all we have heard with our own ears.

"And who is like your people, like Israel — one nation in the earth, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, and to make himself a name, and to do for you the great things and awesome deeds for your land, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and their gods?
"And you established your people Israel as your own people for ever, and you, LORD, became their God.
"And now, LORD God, the word you have spoken about your servant and about his house — establish it for ever, and do as you have said.
"Let your name be great for ever, so that it is said, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel' — and let the house of your servant David be established before you.
"For you, LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house.' That's why your servant has found the courage to pray this prayer to you.
"And now, Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are faithfulness, and you have spoken this good to your servant.
"And now, be pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may be before you for ever. For you, Lord GOD, have spoken, and from your blessing may the house of your servant be blessed for ever."

2 samuel_8.t: After this David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

He struck Moab and measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground: two lines to be put to death and one full line to be kept alive. And Moab became David's servants, bearers of tribute.
David struck Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to restore his control at the River Euphrates.
David captured from him a thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all the chariot horses but kept a hundred chariots' worth.
The Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.
David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became his servants, bearers of tribute. And the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.
When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck down all of Hadadezer's army,

Toi sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and bless him, because he had made war on Hadadezer and struck him down — Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. And with him he brought vessels of silver, gold and bronze.
These too King David consecrated to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had consecrated from all the nations he subdued —
from Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
And David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down Aram in the Valley of Salt — eighteen thousand of them.
He put garrisons in Edom — in all Edom he put garrisons — and all Edom became David's servants. And the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David reigned over all Israel, and he administered justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;
and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.

2 samuel_9.t: David said, "Is there anyone still left of the house of Saul, that I may show loyalty to him for Jonathan's sake?"
Now the house of Saul had a servant named Ziba, and he was summoned to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" He said, "Your servant."
The king said, "Is there really no one left of the house of Saul, that I may show him the loyalty of God?" Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, crippled in both feet."
The king said to him, "Where is he?" Ziba said, "He's in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
So King David sent and had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, at Lo-debar.
Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came to David, fell on his face and bowed down. David said, "Mephibosheth." He said, "Here is your servant."

David said to him, "Don't be afraid. I'll certainly show you loyalty for the sake of Jonathan your father. I'll restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you'll always eat bread at my table."
He bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should turn to a dead dog like me?"
Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.

"You shall work the ground for him — you and your sons and your servants — and bring in the produce, so that your master's son has food to eat. But Mephibosheth your master's son will always eat bread at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
Ziba said to the king, "Your servant will do everything my lord the king commands his servant." And Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.
Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and everyone living in Ziba's household were servants to Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he ate continually at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet.

2 samuel_10.t: After this the king of the Ammonites died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

David said, "I will show loyalty to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed loyalty to me." So David sent his servants to comfort him for his father, and David's servants came to the land of the Ammonites.

But the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honouring your father, that he has sent you comforters? Hasn't David sent his servants to you to explore the city and spy on it and overthrow it?"
So Hanun took David's servants, shaved off half their beards, cut their robes off at the middle as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
When they told David, he sent to meet them, because the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards grow back, then come home."

When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, they sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.
When David heard of it, he sent Joab and the whole army, the mighty men.
The Ammonites came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were on their own in the open country.
When Joab saw that the battle front was against him both before and behind, he picked from all the choice men of Israel and drew them up to meet the Arameans.
The rest of the people he put under his brother Abishai, and drew them up to meet the Ammonites.
He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, you shall be my deliverance; and if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and deliver you.
"Be strong, and let's show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do what is good in his eyes."
So Joab advanced, with the people who were with him, to the battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they fled before Abishai and went into the city. And Joab turned back from the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they gathered together.
Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.
When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. The Arameans drew up to meet David, and they fought with him.
The Arameans fled before Israel. David killed seven hundred of their charioteers and forty thousand horsemen, and struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.
When all the kings who served Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. And the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites again.

2 samuel_11.t: At the turn of the year, at the time when the messengers go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel. They ravaged the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
At evening David got up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing. The woman was very beautiful.
David sent and enquired about the woman, and someone said, "Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
David sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he lay with her — she had been consecrating herself from her uncleanness — and she returned to her house.
The woman conceived, and she sent and told David, "I'm pregnant."
David sent word to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
Uriah came to him, and David asked after the welfare of Joab, the welfare of the people and the welfare of the war.
David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." Uriah went out from the king's house, and a gift from the king went out after him.
But Uriah lay down at the entrance of the king's house with all his lord's servants, and did not go down to his house.
They told David, "Uriah did not go down to his house." So David said to Uriah, "Haven't you come from a journey? Why haven't you gone down to your house?"

Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in booths, and my lord Joab and my lord's servants are camping in the open field. And am I to go to my house to eat and drink and lie with my wife? By your life and by the life of your being, I won't do this thing."
David said to Uriah, "Stay here today too, and tomorrow I'll send you off." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.
David summoned him, and he ate and drank before him, and David made him drunk. In the evening he went out to lie down on his bed with his lord's servants, and he did not go down to his house.
In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
He wrote in the letter, "Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest fighting, then draw back from behind him, so that he is struck down and dies."
While Joab was besieging the city, he put Uriah at the place where he knew there were valiant men.
The men of the city came out and fought with Joab, and some of the people, some of David's servants, fell. And Uriah the Hittite also died.
Joab sent and told David everything about the battle.
He instructed the messenger, "When you have finished telling the king everything about the battle,
"then, if the king's anger rises and he says to you, 'Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot from the wall?

"'Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Didn't a woman throw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' — then you say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.'"
The messenger went and came and told David everything Joab had sent him with.
The messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out at us into the open field, and we drove them back as far as the entrance of the gate.
"And the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's servants died. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead."

David said to the messenger, "Say this to Joab: 'Don't let this thing seem evil to you — the sword devours now one and now another. Press your battle against the city and tear it down.' And encourage him."
The wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, and she mourned over her husband.
When the mourning was over, David sent and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

2 samuel_12.t: The LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said, "There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.
"The rich man had very many flocks and herds.

"But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb he'd bought. He kept it alive, and it grew up with him and his children. It would eat from his morsel, drink from his cup, lie in his bosom — it was like a daughter to him.

"A traveller came to the rich man, and he wouldn't take from his own flock or his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him. He took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
David's anger burned hot against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
"And he shall pay back the ewe lamb four times over, because he did this thing and because he had no pity."
Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the LORD, God of Israel: I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
"I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if that were too little, I would have added this much and this much again.

"Why have you despised the word of the LORD, to do what is evil in my eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck down with the sword; his wife you took for yourself as a wife; and him you killed with the sword of the Ammonites.
"And now the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.

"Thus says the LORD: I am raising up evil against you out of your own house. I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
"You acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun."
David said to Nathan, "I've sinned against the LORD." Nathan said to David, "The LORD also has taken away your sin. You won't die.
"Nevertheless, because by this you have utterly scorned the enemies of the LORD, the son born to you shall also surely die."
Then Nathan went home. And the LORD struck the child that the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and the child became sick.
David sought God for the boy. He fasted, and he went in and spent the night lying on the ground.
The elders of his house stood over him to raise him from the ground, but he would not, and he would not eat food with them.

On the seventh day the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him the child was dead, for they said, "While the child was alive we spoke to him and he wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him the child is dead? He may do himself harm."
But David saw his servants whispering to one another, and he understood that the child was dead. David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" They said, "He's dead."

Then David got up from the ground, washed, anointed himself and changed his clothes. He went into the house of the LORD and bowed down. Then he went to his own house and asked, and they set food before him and he ate.
His servants said to him, "What is this you have done? While the child was alive you fasted and wept for him, and when the child died you got up and ate."
He said, "While the child was still alive I fasted and wept, because I said, 'Who knows? The LORD may show me favour and the child may live.'
"But now he's dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back? I am going to him, but he will not return to me."
David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and he went in to her and lay with her. She bore a son, and she called his name Solomon. And the LORD loved him,
and he sent word by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, for the LORD's sake.
Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal city.
Joab sent messengers to David: "I've fought against Rabbah, and I've captured the city of waters.
"So gather the rest of the people, encamp against the city and capture it — or I'll capture the city myself, and my name will be called over it."
So David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, fought against it and captured it.

He took the crown of their king from his head — it weighed a talent of gold and had a precious stone in it — and it was set on David's head. And he brought out the plunder of the city, a very great quantity.

And the people who were in it he brought out and set to labour with the saws, the iron picks and the iron axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. And so he did to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

2 samuel_13.t: After this: Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
Amnon was so distressed over Tamar his sister that he made himself ill, because she was a virgin. It seemed impossible in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
He said to him, "Why are you so wasted, son of the king, morning after morning? Won't you tell me?" Amnon said, "Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother — I love her."

Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and make yourself ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Let Tamar my sister come and give me food to eat. Let her prepare the food before my eyes, so that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"
So Amnon lay down and made himself ill. The king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, "Let Tamar my sister come and make two cakes before my eyes, so that I may eat from her hand."
David sent word to Tamar at the house: "Go to the house of Amnon your brother and make the food for him."
Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. She took the dough, kneaded it, made the cakes before his eyes and cooked them.
She took the pan and turned them out in front of him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me." And everyone went out from him.
Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner room, so that I may eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother, into the inner room.
She brought them near for him to eat, and he took hold of her and said, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
She said to him, "No, my brother! Don't violate me. Such a thing isn't done in Israel. Don't do this outrage.
"And I — where could I carry my shame? And you'd be like one of the fools in Israel. Speak to the king now; he won't withhold me from you."
But he would not listen to her, and he was stronger than she was, and he violated her and lay with her.
Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred — the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up. Go."
She said to him, "No! This great evil of sending me away is worse than the other you did to me." But he would not listen to her.
He summoned the young man who served him and said, "Send this one away from me, outside, and bolt the door after her."
She was wearing a long tunic, for that is how the virgin daughters of the king wore robes. And his servant brought her outside and bolted the door after her.
Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the long tunic she was wearing, put her hand on her head and went away, crying out as she went.

Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now, my sister, keep quiet. He's your brother. Don't take this to heart." And Tamar remained, desolate, in the house of Absalom her brother.
King David heard all this, and he was very angry.
And Absalom did not speak with Amnon, bad or good, because Absalom hated Amnon for having violated Tamar his sister.
Two full years later, Absalom had shearers at Baal-hazor, near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
Absalom came to the king and said, "Your servant has shearers. Let the king and his servants come with your servant."
The king said to Absalom, "No, my son. Let's not all go, or we'll be a burden on you." Absalom pressed him, but he would not go, and he blessed him.
Absalom said, "If not, then let Amnon my brother go with us." The king said, "Why should he go with you?"
But Absalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon with him, and all the king's sons.

Absalom commanded his young men, "Watch — when Amnon's heart is merry with wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' put him to death. Don't be afraid. Haven't I myself commanded you? Be strong and be valiant."
Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons got up, each mounted his mule, and they fled.
While they were still on the road, the report came to David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left."
