The king got up, tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn.

But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "Don't let my lord say they have put to death all the young men, the king's sons. Amnon alone is dead. It has been determined by Absalom's own word from the day he violated Tamar his sister.
"So don't let my lord the king take to heart the report that all the king's sons are dead. Amnon alone is dead."
And Absalom fled. The young man on watch lifted his eyes and looked, and there were many people coming along the road behind him, from the side of the mountain.
Jonadab said to the king, "The king's sons have come. It has happened just as your servant said."
And as he finished speaking, the king's sons came in, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king too, and all his servants, wept very bitterly.
Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.
Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
And King David gave up going out against Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, now that he was dead.

2 samuel_14.t: Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was toward Absalom.

Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, "Play the mourner. Put on mourning garments, don't anoint yourself with oil, and be like a woman who has been mourning many days for a dead man.
"Then go to the king and speak to him in this way." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
The woman of Tekoa came before the king, fell on her face to the ground and bowed down, and said, "Help, O king!"
The king said to her, "What is your trouble?" She said, "I'm a widow, truly, and my husband is dead.
"Your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them struggled together in the field, and there was no one to part them. One struck the other and killed him.

"And now the whole clan has risen against your maidservant, and they say, 'Give up the one who struck down his brother. We'll put him to death for the life of the brother he killed, and destroy the heir as well' — and so they would quench my coal that is left, leaving my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the ground."
The king said to the woman, "Go home, and I'll give orders about you."
The woman of Tekoa said to the king, "Let the iniquity be on me, my lord the king, and on my father's house, and let the king and his throne be innocent."
The king said, "Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he won't touch you again."

She said, "Let the king remember the LORD your God, so that the avenger of blood doesn't multiply destruction and they don't destroy my son." He said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
The woman said, "Let your maidservant speak one word to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."
The woman said, "Then why have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in giving this ruling the king convicts himself, because he doesn't bring back his own banished one.

"We shall surely die, and we are like water spilt on the ground, which can't be gathered up. And God doesn't take away a life; he devises plans so that the banished one may not remain banished from him.
"And that I have come to speak this word to the king my lord is because the people made me afraid. Your maidservant said, 'Let me speak to the king. Perhaps the king will do what his servant asks.
"'For the king will hear, and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'
"And your maidservant said, 'Let the word of my lord the king bring rest — for my lord the king is like the angel of God, to discern good and bad.' And may the LORD your God be with you."
The king answered the woman, "Don't hide from me the thing I'm about to ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As your being lives, my lord the king, there's no turning to right or left from anything my lord the king has said. It was your servant Joab who commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
"It was to change the face of the matter that your servant Joab did this. And my lord is wise, with the wisdom of the angel of God, to know all that is in the land."
The king said to Joab, "See, I've done this thing. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."

Joab fell on his face to the ground, bowed down and blessed the king, and said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my lord the king, in that the king has done what his servant asked."
So Joab got up, went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
But the king said, "Let him go to his own house; he shall not see my face." So Absalom went to his own house, and he did not see the face of the king.
In all Israel there was no man so handsome as Absalom, so greatly to be praised: from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
And when he shaved his head — he did it at the end of every year, because it grew heavy on him — he would weigh the hair of his head: two hundred shekels by the king's weight.
Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter named Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.
Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years without seeing the face of the king.
Absalom sent to Joab, to have him sent to the king, but Joab would not come to him. He sent a second time, and he would not come.
So he said to his servants, "Look — Joab's field is next to mine, and he's got barley there. Go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
Then Joab got up and came to Absalom at his house and said, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

Absalom said to Joab, "I sent to you and said, 'Come here, so that I may send you to the king to say: Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be still there.' Now let me see the face of the king; and if there's iniquity in me, let him put me to death."
So Joab came to the king and told him. He summoned Absalom, and he came to the king and bowed down before him with his face to the ground; and the king kissed Absalom.

2 samuel_15.t: After this Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.

Absalom would get up early and stand beside the road to the gate, and whenever anyone had a dispute to bring before the king for judgement, Absalom would call him over and say, "What city are you from?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
And Absalom would say to him, "Look, your case is good and right, but there's no one appointed by the king to hear you."
And Absalom would say, "If only I were made a judge in the land! Then anyone with a case or a claim could come to me, and I'd give him justice."
And whenever anyone came near to bow down to him, he would put out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.
Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgement, and he stole the heart of the men of Israel.
At the end of forty years Absalom said to the king, "Let me go and pay my vow that I vowed to the LORD in Hebron.
"For your servant vowed a vow while I was living at Geshur in Aram: 'If the LORD will surely bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.'"
The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he got up and went to Hebron.
But Absalom sent scouts through all the tribes of Israel: "When you hear the sound of the horn, say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron.'"
Two hundred men went with Absalom from Jerusalem. They had been invited and went in all innocence, knowing nothing at all.
Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counsellor, from his city of Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
A messenger came to David and said, "The heart of the men of Israel has gone after Absalom."

David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Get up, let's flee — there'll be no escape for us from Absalom. Hurry and go, or he'll move quickly, overtake us, bring disaster down on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
The king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king chooses — your servants are here."
The king went out, with all his household following on foot, and he left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
The king went out, with all the people following on foot, and they halted at the last house.

All his servants were passing by at his side, and all the Kerethites and all the Pelethites; and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come in his train from Gath, were passing on before the king.
The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you go with us too? Go back and stay with the king — you're a foreigner, and an exile from your own place besides.
"You came only yesterday; should I make you wander about with us today, when I'm going wherever I go? Go back, and take your brothers with you. Loyalty and faithfulness be with you."
Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king is — for death or for life — there your servant will be."
David said to Ittai, "Go on, then." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones with him.
All the land wept aloud as the people passed by. The king crossed the Wadi Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the way of the wilderness.
And there was Zadok too, with all the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
The king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back to the city. If I find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he'll bring me back and let me see it and its dwelling place.
"And if he says, 'I take no delight in you' — here I am. Let him do to me whatever seems good in his eyes."
The king said to Zadok the priest, "Aren't you a seer? Go back to the city in peace, with Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons.
"See, I will wait at the desert plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to tell me."
So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and remained there.
David went up the ascent of the olive trees, weeping as he went, his head covered, walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
David was told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "Turn Ahithophel's counsel to foolishness, LORD."
When David came to the summit, where he would bow down to God, Hushai the Arkite came to meet him, his tunic torn and earth on his head.
David said to him, "If you come over with me, you'll be a burden to me.
"But if you go back to the city and say to Absalom, 'I am your servant, O king; I was your father's servant before, and now I am your servant' — then you'll frustrate Ahithophel's counsel for me.
"And aren't Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Every word you hear from the king's house you are to tell to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
"Their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz for Zadok and Jonathan for Abiathar. By their hand send me every word you hear."
So Hushai, David's friend, came to the city as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.

2 samuel_16.t: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, there was Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth to meet him, with a pair of saddled donkeys carrying two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits and a skin of wine.

The king said to Ziba, "What are these for?" Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride, the bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for anyone weary in the wilderness to drink."
The king said, "And where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "He's staying in Jerusalem. He said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me my father's kingdom.'"
The king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is yours." Ziba said, "I bow down. May I find favour in your eyes, my lord the king."
King David came as far as Bahurim, and out came a man from the clan of the house of Saul, named Shimei son of Gera, cursing as he came.
And he threw stones at David and at all King David's servants, though all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.
And this is what Shimei said as he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!

"The LORD has brought back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you reigned, and the LORD has given the kingship into the hand of Absalom your son. And here you are, caught in your own calamity — you're a man of blood!"
Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."
The king said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse. The LORD has said to him, 'Curse David.' And who's to say, 'Why have you done so?'"

David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "My own son, who came from my own body, is seeking my life — how much more now this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has spoken to him.
"Perhaps the LORD will look upon my eye, and the LORD will repay me with good in place of his cursing today."
David and his men went on along the road, while Shimei went along the side of the mountain opposite him, cursing as he went, throwing stones opposite him and flinging dust.
The king came, and all the people with him, exhausted, and he refreshed himself there.
Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
And when Hushai the Arkite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?"
Hushai said to Absalom, "No — the one whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will remain.
"And another thing: whom should I serve? Shouldn't it be his son? As I served in your father's presence, so I will be in yours."
Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel. What shall we do?"

Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."
So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
Now the counsel Ahithophel gave in those days was like enquiring of the word of God: so was all Ahithophel's counsel, both to David and to Absalom.

2 samuel_17.t: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men, and let me set out and pursue David tonight.
"I'll come on him while he's weary and his hands are slack, and I'll terrify him. All the people with him will flee, and I'll strike down the king alone.
"And I'll bring all the people back to you. When all return — it is only the one man you are seeking — all the people will be at peace."
The word seemed right to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.
But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Arkite too, and let's hear what he has to say as well."
Hushai came to Absalom, and Absalom said to him, "This is what Ahithophel has said. Shall we do as he says? If not, you speak."
Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel Ahithophel has given isn't good this time."

And Hushai said, "You know your father and his men — they're mighty men, and they're enraged, like a bear robbed of her cubs in open country. Your father is a man of war, and he won't spend the night with the people.

"By now he's hidden in one of the ravines or in some other place; and when some of them fall at the first onset, whoever hears of it will say, 'There's been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'
"And even the valiant man, whose heart is like a lion's, will utterly melt — for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and that those with him are valiant men.
"But my counsel is that all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand by the sea, and that you yourself go into the battle.
"We'll come on him wherever he's found, and settle on him as the dew falls on the ground; and not one of him or of all the men with him will be left.
"And if he withdraws into a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we'll drag it down to the wadi until not even a pebble is found there."

And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Arkite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained to frustrate the good counsel of Ahithophel, so that the LORD might bring disaster upon Absalom.
Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "This and this is what Ahithophel counselled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this and this is what I counselled.
"So send quickly and tell David, 'Don't spend the night at the desert plains of the wilderness. Be sure to cross over, or the king will be swallowed up, and all the people with him.'"
Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, and a maidservant would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David — they could not risk being seen entering the city.
But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
The woman took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, and spread out grain on it, and nothing was known.

Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said, "They've crossed the brook of water." They searched and did not find them, and they returned to Jerusalem.
After they had gone, the two came up out of the well, went and told King David. They said to David, "Get up and cross the water quickly — this is what Ahithophel has counselled against you."
So David rose, with all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By first light not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

When Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been carried out, he saddled his donkey and set off for his house, to his city. He gave orders concerning his household and hanged himself. He died and was buried in the tomb of his father.
David had come to Mahanaim, while Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Jether the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
brought bedding, basins and earthenware vessels, and wheat, barley, flour and roasted grain, beans, lentils and roasted grain,
and honey, curds, sheep and cheese from the herd. They brought these to David and to the people with him, to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

2 samuel_18.t: David mustered the people who were with him and set over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

David sent out the people: a third under Joab, a third under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I'll certainly go out with you myself."

But the people said, "You mustn't go out. If we flee, they won't care about us; if half of us die, they won't care about us. But you're worth ten thousand of us. So it's better that you be ready to help us from the city."
The king said to them, "Whatever seems good to you I'll do." The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man, with Absalom." And all the people heard the king give all the commanders this command concerning Absalom.
The people went out into the open country to meet Israel, and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.
The people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter that day was great: twenty thousand.
The battle there spread over the face of the whole country, and the forest consumed more of the people that day than the sword consumed.

Absalom happened to meet David's servants. He was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great oak, and his head caught fast in the oak, and he was left hanging between the heavens and the earth, while the mule that was under him passed on.
One man saw it and told Joab, "I saw Absalom hanging in the oak."
Joab said to the man who told him, "You saw him! Why didn't you strike him to the ground there? I'd have been bound to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt."

The man said to Joab, "Even if I had a thousand pieces of silver weighed out in my hands, I wouldn't put out my hand against the king's son. For in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Whoever you are, protect the young man Absalom.'
"Or if I had acted falsely at the cost of my own life — and nothing is hidden from the king — you'd have stood aloof."
Joab said, "I won't waste time with you like this." He took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom, while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
And ten young men, Joab's armour-bearers, surrounded him and struck Absalom and killed him.
Joab blew the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab restrained the people.
They took Absalom and threw him into the great pit in the forest and raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his tents.

Now Absalom, in his lifetime, had taken and set up for himself the pillar in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.
Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and carry the news to the king — that the LORD has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
Joab said to him, "You're not the man to carry news today. Carry news another day, but not today, because the king's son is dead."
Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed down to Joab and ran.
Ahimaaz son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, let me run after the Cushite too." Joab said, "Why would you run, my son, when you have no news that will bring you a reward?"
"Come what may, I will run." He said to him, "Run." So Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
David was sitting between the two gates, and the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway, on the wall, lifted his eyes and looked, and there was a man running alone.
The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, "If he's alone, there's news in his mouth." And he came on, drawing steadily nearer.
The watchman saw another man running, and called to the gatekeeper, "There's another man running alone." The king said, "This one also is bearing news."
The watchman said, "The first runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." The king said, "He's a good man, and he comes with good news."

Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down to the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted their hand against my lord the king."
The king said, "Is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" Ahimaaz said, "I saw a great commotion when the king's servant Joab sent your servant, but I don't know what it was."
The king said, "Turn aside and stand here." He turned aside and stood.
Then the Cushite came and said, "Let my lord the king receive the news: the LORD has vindicated you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you."

The king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" The Cushite said, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen against you for harm, be like the young man."

The king was shaken. He went up to the upper room over the gate and wept, and this is what he said as he went: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died — I, instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!"

2 samuel_19.t: Joab was told, "The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom."
And the victory that day was turned to mourning for all the people, for the people heard that day that the king was grieved over his son.
The people stole into the city that day, the way people steal in when they are ashamed after fleeing in battle.
The king covered his face and cried out with a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

Joab came to the king in the house and said, "Today you've put to shame the faces of all your servants, who this day saved your life, and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives and of your concubines,

"by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. Today you've made plain that commanders and servants mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, it would be right in your eyes.

"So get up, go out and speak to the heart of your servants. For I swear by the LORD that if you don't go out, not a man will stay with you tonight — and that'll be worse for you than all the harm that has come on you from your youth until now."
So the king got up and sat in the gate. They told all the people, "The king is sitting in the gate," and all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, each to his tents.

All the people were quarrelling throughout all the tribes of Israel: "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies and rescued us from the hand of the Philistines — and now he's fled the land because of Absalom.
"And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in the battle. So why are you saying nothing about bringing back the king?"

King David sent to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Speak to the elders of Judah — 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house?' " — and the word of all Israel had come to the king, to his house.
"You're my brothers, my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?"
"And say to Amasa, 'Aren't you my bone and my flesh? So may God do to me, and more, if you are not commander of the army in my presence from now on, in place of Joab.'"
He turned the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent word to the king, "Return, you and all your servants."
So the king returned and came to the Jordan, and Judah came to Gilgal to go and meet the king and bring him over the Jordan.
Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
A thousand men of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan ahead of the king.
And the ferry went across to bring over the king's household and to do whatever seemed good to him. And Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,

and said to the king, "Don't hold guilt against me, my lord, and don't remember what your servant did perversely on the day my lord the king went out from Jerusalem. Don't let the king take it to heart.
"For your servant knows that I've sinned, and I've come today, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down and meet my lord the king."
But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?"
David said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become an opponent to me today? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don't I know that today I am king over Israel?"
And the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore it to him.
Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, trimmed his moustache or washed his clothes, from the day the king left until the day he came back in peace.
And when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, "Why didn't you go with me, Mephibosheth?"
He said, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. Your servant said, 'Let me saddle the donkey for myself, so that I may ride on it and go with the king' — for your servant is lame.
"And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.

"All my father's house were nothing but men doomed to death before my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What claim have I still, to cry out further to the king?"
The king said to him, "Why speak of your affairs any more? I've said it: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come home in peace."
Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king, to see him off at the Jordan.
Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age, and he had supplied the king while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I'll provide for you at my side in Jerusalem."
Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

"I'm eighty years old today. Can I tell good from bad? Can your servant taste what he eats or what he drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
"Your servant would go only a little way over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king reward me with such a reward?

"Let your servant go back and die in his own city, near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Kimham — let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him whatever is good in your eyes."
The king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I'll do for him what is good in your eyes. And whatever you ask of me I'll do for you."
All the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned to his own place.
The king crossed over to Gilgal, and Kimham crossed with him. All the people of Judah brought the king over, and half the people of Israel as well.
Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"

All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is a near relative of ours. Why should that anger you? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense, or has anything been taken for us?"

The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, and in David we have more than you. Why then have you treated us with contempt? Wasn't our word first, to bring back our king?" And the word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.

2 samuel_20.t: Now a worthless man happened to be there, named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew the horn and said, "We have no portion in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each to his tents, O Israel!"
So all the men of Israel left off following David and followed Sheba son of Bichri, but the men of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

David came to his house at Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house of confinement. He provided for them but did not go in to them. They were shut up until the day of their death, in living widowhood.
The king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to me within three days, and you yourself be here."
Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time set for him.
David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bichri will now do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your master's servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities for himself and escape us."
So Joab's men went out after him, with the Kerethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men, and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

They were by the great stone in Gibeon when Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his robe, and over it a belt with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath; and as he stepped forward, it fell out.
Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" And Joab's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.

Amasa did not take heed of the sword in Joab's hand, and Joab struck him with it in the belly and poured out his bowels on the ground. He did not strike twice, and Amasa died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
A man stood over him, one of Joab's young men, and called, "Whoever favours Joab, and whoever is for David — follow Joab!"

Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the highway. When the man saw that all the people were stopping, he moved Amasa off the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, since he saw that everyone who came upon him stopped.
Once he had been removed from the highway, every man passed on after Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-maacah and all the Berites, and they assembled and followed him too.
They came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, threw up a siege mound against the city so that it stood against the rampart, and all the people with Joab were battering the wall to bring it down.
Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Say to Joab, 'Come near, so that I may speak with you.'"
He came near, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" He said, "I am." She said, "Listen to the words of your maidservant." He said, "I'm listening."
She said, "In former times they used to say, 'Let them ask at Abel', and so the matter was settled.
"I'm one of the peaceable and faithful of Israel. You're seeking to put to death a city that is a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?"
Joab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy!

"That's not the matter. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, named Sheba son of Bichri, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give him up alone, and I'll withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you over the wall."

The woman went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He blew the horn, and they dispersed from the city, each to his tents, and Joab returned to Jerusalem, to the king.
Now Joab was over all the army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites;
Adoram was over the forced labour; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
and Ira the Jairite also was priest to David.

2 samuel_21.t: There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, "It is because of Saul and because of the house of blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

The king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them — now the Gibeonites were not Israelites but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the Israelites had sworn an oath to them, and Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the Israelites and Judah —
and David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? With what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?"

The Gibeonites said to him, "It's not a matter of silver and gold between us and Saul and his house, and it's not for us to put any man to death in Israel." He said, "Whatever you say I'll do for you."
They said to the king, "The man who made an end of us and planned against us that we should be destroyed from standing anywhere in the territory of Israel —
"let seven of his sons be given to us, and we will impale them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the LORD's chosen." The king said, "I'll give them."
But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul, because of the oath of the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

The king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul — Armoni and Mephibosheth — and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite,

and he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they impaled them on the mountain before the LORD. The seven of them fell together. They were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured out on them from the heavens. She did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done.

David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the open square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them up on the day they struck down Saul at Gilboa.
He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of those who had been impaled.

They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father, and they did all that the king commanded. And after that God was entreated for the land.
There was war again between the Philistines and Israel, and David went down with his servants and they fought the Philistines. And David grew weary.
And Ishbi-benob, who was among the descendants of the giant — the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with a new sword — said he would strike David down.

But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his help, struck the Philistine down and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, "You shall not go out to battle with us any more. You shall not quench the lamp of Israel."
After this there was war again at Gob with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was among those born of the Raphah.
There was war again at Gob with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
There was war again at Gath, and there was a man of great stature, whose fingers and toes were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to the Raphah.
He taunted Israel, and Jonathan son of Shimei, David's brother, struck him down.
These four were born to the Raphah in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

2 samuel_22.t: David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
And he said: The LORD is my rock and my stronghold, and my deliverer, mine;
My God, my rock, the one I take refuge in, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my fastness and my place of escape, my saviour — you save me from violence.
The one to be praised — I call on the LORD, and I'm saved from my enemies.
For the breakers of death surrounded me, the torrents of worthlessness overwhelmed me;
the cords of Sheol surrounded me, the snares of death came at me.
In my distress I called on the LORD, and cried out to my God; he heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help was in his ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because he was angry.
Smoke went up from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth consumed; coals burned out of him.
He stretched out the heavens and came down, with thick darkness under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew; he appeared on the wings of the wind.
He set darkness around him for shelters, a sieve of waters, dark clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before him coals of fire blazed.
The LORD thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.
He sent out arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed them.
The channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were uncovered, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He reached down from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.
He rescued me from my strong enemy, from those who hate me, for they were too strong for me.
They came at me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was a support to me.
He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me, for he delighted in me.
The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the purity of my hands he repaid me.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and I haven't acted wickedly away from my God.
For all his judgements are before me, and I don't turn aside from his statutes.
I was blameless toward him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
The LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my purity before his eyes.
With the loyal you show yourself loyal, with the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless;
with the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself twisted.
An afflicted people you save, but your eyes are on the haughty — you bring them low.
For you're my lamp, LORD, and the LORD lightens my darkness.
For by you I can charge a raiding band, by my God I can leap a wall.
As for God — his way is blameless, the speech of the LORD is refined; he's a shield to all who take refuge in him.
For who's God apart from the LORD, and who's a Rock apart from our God?
God is my strong refuge, and he set my way free, blameless.
making my feet like the does', and on my high places he makes me stand.
training my hands for battle, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
You gave me the shield of your salvation, and your answering makes me great.
You enlarge my step beneath me, and my ankles don't slip.
I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I didn't turn back until they were finished.
I finished them and shattered them, and they didn't rise; they fell under my feet.
You girded me with strength for battle; you made those who rose against me bow down beneath me.
My enemies — you gave me their neck; those who hate me — I destroyed them.
They looked, and there was no deliverer; to the LORD — and he didn't answer them.
I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; like the mud of the streets I crushed them and stamped them out.
You rescued me from the strifes of my people; you kept me as head of nations — a people I didn't know serves me.
Foreigners cringe before me; at the hearing of the ear they obey me.
Foreigners wither, and they come girded out of their strongholds.
The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock, and exalted be the God of the Rock of my salvation —
the God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples down beneath me,
and who brings me out from my enemies. And from those who rise against me you lift me up; from the man of violence you rescue me.
Therefore I'll give you thanks, LORD, among the nations, and I'll make music to your name —
a tower of salvation for his king, and showing steadfast love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring for ever.

2 samuel_23.t: And these are the last words of David: The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the pleasant one of the songs of Israel.
The spirit of the LORD has spoken by me; his word is on my tongue.
The God of Israel said, to me the Rock of Israel spoke: One who rules over humankind, righteous, ruling in the fear of God —
and like the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds; through brightness after rain grass springs from the earth.
Isn't my house so with God? For he has made with me a perpetual covenant, ordered in every part and kept. All my salvation and every desire — won't he make it grow?
But the worthless — all of them like thorns chased away, because they can't be taken by hand;
and the man who touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear; and they're utterly burned with fire where they lie.
These are the names of the mighty men who belonged to David: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the three; he was Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.
After him was Eleazar son of Dodo son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel had withdrawn.

He rose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary and stuck to the sword. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance that day, and the people came back after him only to strip the slain.
After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines gathered into a band, and there was a plot of field full of lentils, and the people fled before the Philistines.
But he took his stand in the middle of the plot, defended it, and struck the Philistines. And the LORD brought about a great deliverance.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down and came at harvest time to David, at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.
David craved and said, "Who'll give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, at the gate?"

The three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem at the gate, carried it and brought it to David. But he would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.
And he said, "Far be it from me, LORD, that I should do this! Isn't it the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" And he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
Abishai the brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three. He wielded his spear against three hundred slain, and he had a name among the three.
Wasn't he the most honoured of the three? He became their commander, but he did not attain to the three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a valiant man, great in deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two ariels of Moab, and he went down and struck down a lion inside a pit on a snowy day.
He struck down an Egyptian, an imposing man. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, seized the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
He was honoured above the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. And David set him over his bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem;
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite;
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite;
Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite;
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite;
Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjaminites;
Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Gaash;
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite;
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Ararite;
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai son of the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite;
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite;
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armour-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite — thirty-seven in all.

2 samuel_24.t: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel again, and he incited David against them: "Go, count Israel and Judah."
The king said to Joab the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and enrol the people, so that I may know the number of the people."
Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want this?"
But the king's word prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the army, and Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the king's presence to enrol the people, Israel.
They crossed the Jordan and encamped at Aroer, south of the city in the middle of the wadi of Gad, and went on to Jazer.
They came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and round to Sidon.
They came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they went out to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
They went about through the whole land, and at the end of nine months and twenty days they came to Jerusalem.
Joab gave the number of the muster of the people to the king: Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand.

But David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to the LORD, "I've sinned greatly in what I've done. Now, LORD, take away the iniquity of your servant — I've acted very foolishly."
David rose in the morning, and the word of the LORD came to Gad the prophet, David's seer:
"Go and speak to David: Thus says the LORD: Three things I am laying on you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you."

Gad came to David and told him, "Shall seven years of famine come on you in your land? Or three months of fleeing before your foes while they pursue you? Or three days of pestilence in your land? Now think it over and see what answer I'm to bring back to the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I'm in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of the LORD — his compassions are many. But don't let me fall into human hands."
The LORD sent a pestilence on Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and of the people from Dan to Beersheba seventy thousand men died.

The angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, but the LORD relented concerning the harm and said to the angel who was destroying among the people, "Enough! Now let your hand drop." And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

And David said to the LORD when he saw the angel striking the people, "I've sinned and I've done wrong; but these sheep — what have they done? Let your hand be against me and against my father's house."
Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
David went up according to the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, and he went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague may be held back from the people."
Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up whatever seems good to him. Here are the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the oxen's gear for the wood."
"All this Araunah gives to the king, O king." And Araunah said to the king, "May the LORD your God accept you favourably."

But the king said to Araunah, "No — I'll certainly buy it from you for a price. I won't offer up to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." And David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
David built an altar to the LORD there and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings. And the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was held back from Israel.

amos_1.t: The words of Amos, one of the sheep-breeders from Tekoa. This is what he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
And he said: The LORD roars from Zion; from Jerusalem he raises his voice. The shepherds' pastures dry up, and the top of Carmel withers.
This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.
And I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben Hadad.

And I will break the bar of Damascus. I will cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the sceptre from Beth Eden, and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried a whole people into exile, to hand them over to Edom.
And I will send fire into the wall of Gaza, and it will consume her fortresses.
And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the one who holds the sceptre from Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says Lord GOD.
This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they handed a whole people over to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
And I will send fire into the wall of Tyre, and it will consume her fortresses.

This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he chased his brother with the sword and ruined all compassion, and his anger tore away for ever, and he held on to his fury without end.
And I will send fire into Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.

This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of the people of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their own territory.
And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will consume her fortresses, with a shout of alarm on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
And their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.

amos_2.t: This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
And I will send fire into Moab, and it will consume the fortresses of Kerioth, and Moab will die in an uproar, with a shout of alarm, with the sound of a horn.
And I will cut off the judge from her midst, and kill all her officials along with him, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray — the same lies their fathers walked after.
And I will send fire into Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.
This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sold the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth and push the humble off their way. A man and his father go to the same young woman, and so they profane my holy name.
They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and they drink the wine of the fined in the house of their gods.
And I myself destroyed the Amorite in front of them — as tall as the cedars, as strong as the oaks — and I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.
And I myself brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you through the wilderness for forty years, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
And I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as nazirites. Isn't that so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.
But you made the nazirites drink wine, and you gave the prophets an order: "Do not prophesy."
Look, I am about to press you in your place, the way a cart presses when it is loaded with cut grain.
The swift will have nowhere to run, the strong will not keep his power, and the mighty will not save his own being.
The one who handles the bow will not stand, the swift-footed will not get away, and the horseman will not save his own being.
And the bravest of the warriors will run away naked on that day, declares the LORD.

amos_3.t: Hear this word the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel — against the whole clan I brought up from the land of Egypt:
You alone have I known out of all the clans of the earth; so I will call you to account for all your iniquities.
Do two people walk together unless they've arranged to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has caught nothing? Does a young lion growl from his den unless he's taken something?
Does a bird drop into a trap on the ground when there's no snare set for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground and catch nothing at all?
If a horn is blown in a city, don't the people tremble? If calamity comes on a city, hasn't the LORD done it?
For Lord GOD doesn't do anything without revealing his secret counsel to his servants the prophets.
A lion has roared — who is not afraid? Lord GOD has spoken — who can help prophesying?

Proclaim it to the fortresses in Ashdod and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: "Gather on the mountains of Samaria. Look at the great disturbances inside her, at the acts of oppression in her midst."
"They do not know how to do what is straight," declares the LORD — these people who pile up violence and devastation in their fortresses.
So this is what Lord GOD says: An adversary — all around the land! He will bring your strength down from you, and your fortresses will be plundered.

This is what the LORD says: Just as a shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two shin-bones or a scrap of an ear, that is how the people of Israel will be rescued — the ones sitting in Samaria with the corner of a bed and the silk of a couch.
Hear, and give warning to the house of Jacob, declares Lord GOD, the God of hosts.
For on the day I call Israel to account for his transgressions, I will also call the altars of Bethel to account; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
And I will strike the winter house along with the summer house. The houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.

amos_4.t: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan up on the mountain of Samaria, you who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to their masters, "Bring us a drink!"
Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Look, days are coming upon you when you will be carried off on hooks, your posterity on fish-hooks.
And you will go out through the breaches, each one straight ahead, and you will be flung out to Harmon, declares the LORD.
Come to Bethel — and transgress! Go to Gilgal — and transgress all the more! Bring your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes on the third day.
Burn as smoke a thanksgiving offering from what is leavened, and announce your freewill offerings — make sure they are heard! For this is what you love, people of Israel, declares Lord GOD.
And I myself gave you clean teeth in all your cities and no bread in any of your places, and still you didn't return to me, declares the LORD.

And I myself withheld the rain from you when there were still three months to the harvest. I sent rain on one city and on another city I sent none. One plot of ground got rain, and the plot that got none dried up.
Two or three cities staggered to one city for water and were not satisfied, and still you didn't return to me, declares the LORD.
I struck you with blight and mildew. The locust ate up the many gardens and vineyards, the fig trees and the olive trees you had, and still you didn't return to me, declares the LORD.

I sent pestilence among you the way I did in Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were taken, and I made the stench of your camp rise into your nostrils, and still you didn't return to me, declares the LORD.
I overthrew among you the way God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand pulled out of the fire, and still you didn't return to me, declares the LORD.
So this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I am going to do this to you, get ready to meet your God, Israel!

For here is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and tells humankind what he is thinking, who turns the dawn to darkness and treads on the high places of the earth — the LORD, God of hosts, is his name.

amos_5.t: Hear this word I am raising over you — a lamentation, house of Israel:
She has fallen, and she will not rise again — the virgin Israel. She lies abandoned on her own ground, and there's no one to raise her up.
For this is what Lord GOD says: The city that marches out a thousand will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live.
But do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, do not cross over to Beersheba — for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the LORD and live, or he will break out like fire on the house of Joseph and consume it, with no one to put it out for Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and throw righteousness down to the ground!

The maker of Kimah and Kesil, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens the day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth — the LORD is his name;
who flashes devastation on the strong, and devastation comes down on the fortress.
They hate the one who calls them to account in the gate, and they can't stand the one who speaks blamelessly.

So, because you trample on the poor and take a portion of grain from him, you have built houses of dressed stone but you won't live in them; you have planted fine vineyards but you won't drink their wine.
For I know how many your transgressions are and how numerous your sins — you who oppose the righteous, who take a bribe, who push the needy aside in the gate.
So the prudent keep quiet at a time like that, because it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and then it may be that the LORD, God of hosts, is with you just as you have been saying.
Hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, God of hosts, will show favour to the remnant of Joseph.

So this is what the LORD, God of hosts, the Lord says: In all the open squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!" They will call the farmer to mourning, and summon to wailing those who know how to lament.
And in all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
Woe to those who long for the day of the LORD! What do you want with it — the day of the LORD? It's darkness and not light.
It is like a man running from a lion and a bear meets him; or he goes into the house, leans his hand on the wall, and a serpent bites him.
Isn't the day of the LORD darkness and not light — gloom with no brightness in it at all?
I hate them, I reject them — your festivals; I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even if you offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I won't accept them, and I won't so much as look at the peace offering from your fatlings.
Take the noise of your songs away from me; I won't listen to the music of your harps.
Let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.
Was it sacrifices and grain offering that you brought me in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
And you will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods, the ones you made for yourselves.
And I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD — God of hosts is his name.

amos_6.t: Woe to those living at ease in Zion and those who feel safe on the mountain of Samaria — the notables of the foremost of the nations, the ones the house of Israel comes to!
Cross over to Calneh and look; go on from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory bigger than yours?
You who push the day of evil away and bring a seat of violence near,
who lie on beds of ivory and sprawl across their couches, who eat lambs from the flock and calves straight out of the stall;
who improvise to the sound of the harp and, like David, have made up instruments of song for themselves;
who drink wine out of bowls and rub themselves with the finest oils, and are not sickened by the ruin of Joseph.
So now they will go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of the sprawlers will be over.
Lord GOD has sworn by his own being — declares the LORD, God of hosts: I loathe the pride of Jacob and I hate his fortresses, and I will hand over the city and everything in it.
And if ten men are left in one house, they will die.

A man's kinsman will lift him up — and the one who burns him — to carry the bones out of the house. He will call to whoever is in the back of the house, "Is anyone still with you?" And he will say, "No one." And he will say, "Hush! The name of the LORD is not to be brought to remembrance."
For look, the LORD is giving the command, and the great house will be smashed to fragments and the small house to rubble.
Do horses run on the rock? Does anyone plough there with oxen? And yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who rejoice over Lo Debar, who say, "Didn't we take Karnaim by our own strength?"
For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel — declares the LORD, God of hosts — and they will oppress you from Lebo Hamath to the wadi of the Arabah.

amos_7.t: This is what Lord GOD showed me: he was forming locusts just as the late growth was starting to come up — and this was the late growth that comes after the king's mowings.
And when it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said: "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How will Jacob stand? He's so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "It will not be," said the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD showed me: Lord GOD was calling for a contention by fire, and it consumed the great deep, and it consumed the portion of land.
And I said: "Lord GOD, stop, please! How will Jacob stand? He's so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "This also will not be," said Lord GOD.
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing on a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." And the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I won't pass them by again."
And the high places of Isaac will be made desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos has conspired against you right in the middle of the house of Israel. The land can't endure all his words."
"For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile from its ground.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer — go on, get away to the land of Judah. Earn your bread there, and prophesy there."
"And don't prophesy at Bethel again — it's a king's sanctuary, a royal house."
And Amos answered Amaziah: "I'm no prophet, and I'm no prophet's son. I'm a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
"And the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
"And now hear the word of the LORD: You say, 'Don't prophesy against Israel; don't preach against the house of Isaac.'"

So this is what the LORD says: Your wife will be a prostitute in the city; your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword; your ground will be divided by the measuring-line; you yourself will die on unclean ground; and Israel will surely go into exile from its ground.

amos_8.t: This is what Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
And he said, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." And the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon my people Israel. I won't pass them by again."
And the songs of the temple will turn to wailing on that day, declares Lord GOD. So many corpses! Thrown out everywhere. Hush!
Hear this, you who trample on the needy and put an end to the afflicted of the land,
saying, "When will the new moon be over, so we can sell grain, and the sabbath, so we can open the wheat?" — making the ephah small and the shekel great, falsifying the scales,
to buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and to sell the sweepings of the wheat.
The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "I will never forget a single one of their deeds."
Won't the land tremble over this, and everyone living in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile, and be tossed and sink like the River of Egypt.
And on that day, declares Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

And I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will bring sackcloth up on every waist and baldness on every head, and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
Look, days are coming, declares Lord GOD, when I will send a famine in the land — not a famine for bread, not a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the LORD.
And they will stagger from sea to sea, from the north to the east, roving about to seek the word of the LORD — and they won't find it.
On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, "As your god lives, Dan!" and, "As the way of Beersheba lives!" — they will fall and never rise again.

amos_9.t: I saw the Lord standing on the altar, and he said: "Strike the capital until the thresholds shake, and break them off on the heads of them all. Their posterity I will kill with the sword. No one who flees among them will get away; no escapee among them will escape."
If they dig down into Sheol, my hand will take them from there; and if they go up to the heavens, I will bring them down from there.

And if they hide on the top of Carmel, I will search them out and take them from there; and if they hide from my eyes at the bottom of the sea, I will command the serpent from there, and it will bite them.
And if they go into captivity in front of their enemies, I will command the sword from there, and it will kill them. And I will set my eye on them for harm and not for good.
And Lord GOD of hosts, who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live in it mourn, and all of it rises like the Nile and sinks like the River of Egypt;
who builds his stairs in the heavens and has founded his vault upon the earth, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth — the LORD is his name.
Aren't you like the Cushites to me, people of Israel? declares the LORD. Didn't I bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
Look, the eyes of Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the ground — except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, declares the LORD.
For look, I am giving the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations the way grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble will fall to the ground.
By the sword all the sinners of my people will die — the ones who say, "The calamity won't come near us or reach us."
On that day I will raise up the falling booth of David. I will wall up their breaches, raise up his ruins, and rebuild her as in the days of old,
so that they may take possession of the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom my name is called, declares the LORD, who does this.

Look, days are coming, declares the LORD, when the ploughman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes the sower of seed. The mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.
And I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, make gardens and eat their fruit.
And I will plant them on their own ground, and they will never again be plucked up from the ground I have given them, says the LORD your God.

daniel_1.t: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the articles of the house of God. He took them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and put the articles into his god's treasury.
And the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his officials, to bring in some of the sons of Israel — some of the royal offspring and some of the nobles —

young men with no blemish on them, good-looking, with insight into all wisdom, knowledgeable and quick to understand, fit to stand in the king's palace — and to teach them the writing and the tongue of the Chaldeans.
And the king assigned them a daily portion of the king's delicacies and of the wine he drank. They were to be brought up for three years, and at the end of that they were to stand before the king.
Among them, from the sons of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
And the chief of the officials gave them names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abed-nego.
But Daniel made up his mind that he wouldn't defile himself with the king's delicacies or with the wine he drank, and he asked the chief of the officials for leave not to defile himself.
And God gave Daniel favour and compassion in the sight of the chief of the officials.

But the chief of the officials said to Daniel, 'I'm afraid of my lord the king. He's the one who assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the young men your own age? You'd be making my head forfeit to the king.'
So Daniel said to the guardian the chief of the officials had put over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,
'Give your servants a ten-day test. Let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.'
'Then have a look at us, and at the young men who are eating the king's delicacies, and deal with your servants according to what you see.'
And he listened to them about this and tested them for ten days.
And at the end of ten days they looked better and were fatter of flesh than all the young men who were eating the king's delicacies.
So the guardian kept taking away their delicacies and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.
And to these four young men God gave knowledge and insight into all writing and wisdom; and Daniel understood every vision and dream.
And at the end of the time the king had set for bringing them in, the chief of the officials brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king talked with them, and out of them all not one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. So they stood before the king.
And in every matter of wisdom and understanding the king put to them, he found them ten times better than all the soothsayer-priests and conjurers in his whole kingdom.
And Daniel stayed on until the first year of Cyrus the king.

daniel_2.t: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and his sleep left him.
So the king gave orders to call in the soothsayer-priests, the conjurers, the sorcerers and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. And they came and stood in front of the king.
And the king said to them, 'I've had a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.'
And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: 'King, live for ever! Tell your servants the dream, and we'll declare the interpretation.'
The king answered the Chaldeans, 'My word on it is firm: if you don't make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you'll be cut into limbs and your houses made a refuse heap.'
'But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you'll get gifts from me, and a reward, and great honour. So declare the dream and its interpretation to me.'
They answered a second time, 'Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we'll declare the interpretation.'
The king answered, 'I know for certain that you're buying time, because you've seen that my word on it is firm —'

'that if you don't make the dream known to me, there's one law for you. You've agreed together to speak a lying and corrupt word in front of me until the time changes. So tell me the dream, and then I'll know you can declare its interpretation to me.'
The Chaldeans answered the king, 'There's no one on earth who can declare the king's matter. No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician or conjurer or Chaldean.'
'What the king is asking is hard, and there's no one else who can declare it in front of the king except the gods, and their dwelling is not with flesh.'
At this the king was angry — exceedingly furious — and he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
So the law went out, and the wise men were about to be killed; and they went looking for Daniel and his companions, to kill them.
Then Daniel answered with counsel and discretion to Arioch, the chief of the king's executioners, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He said to Arioch the king's captain, 'Why is the law from the king so harsh?' Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, and he would declare the interpretation to the king.
Then Daniel went home and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions,
and told them to ask compassion from before the God of the heavens about this secret, so that Daniel and his companions wouldn't be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of the heavens.
Daniel said: 'Let the name of God be blessed from age to age — wisdom and power are his.'
'He changes the times and the appointed times; he removes kings and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and understanding to those who know discernment.'
'He reveals what's deep and what's hidden; he knows what's in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.'
'To you, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because you've given me wisdom and power. And now you've made known to me what we asked of you — you've made known to us the king's matter.'

So Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, 'Don't destroy the wise men of Babylon. Take me in before the king, and I'll declare the interpretation to the king.'
Then Arioch rushed Daniel in before the king and said, 'I've found a man among the exiles of Judah who'll make the interpretation known to the king.'
The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, 'Are you able to make known to me the dream I saw, and its interpretation?'
