Daniel answered the king, 'The secret the king is asking about — no wise men, no conjurers, no magicians, no astrologers can declare it to the king.'

'But there is a God in the heavens who reveals secrets, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be at the end of the days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:'
'As for you, King — your thoughts came up on your bed about what will be after this, and the revealer of secrets has made known to you what will be.'

'And as for me — this secret wasn't revealed to me because I have more wisdom than anyone alive, but so that the interpretation should be made known to the king, and so that you should know the thoughts of your heart.'
'You, King, were looking, and there it was: one great image. That image was great, its splendour extraordinary. It stood in front of you, and its appearance was terrible.'
'That image: its head was of fine gold, its breast and arms of silver, its belly and loins of bronze,'
'its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.'
'You went on looking until a stone was cut out — not by hands — and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.'

'Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were shattered together, and became like chaff off the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.'
'That's the dream. And we'll tell its interpretation in front of the king.'
'You, King, are the king of kings. The God of the heavens has given you the kingdom, the power, the strength and the honour,'
'and wherever the sons of humankind live, he's given the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens into your hand and made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.'
'And after you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you; and then a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.'
'And a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. Iron shatters and crushes everything, and like iron that breaks things in pieces, it'll shatter and crush all these.'

'And that you saw the feet and toes partly of a potter's clay and partly of iron — it'll be a divided kingdom, with some of the firmness of iron in it, because you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud.'
'And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly breakable.'
'And that you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud — they'll mix with the offspring of humankind, but they won't cling to one another, just as iron doesn't mix with clay.'

'And in the days of those kings the God of the heavens will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and the kingdom won't be left to another people. It'll shatter and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it'll stand for ever.'

'Because you saw a stone cut out of the mountain — not by hands — and it shattered the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold: the great God has made known to the king what will be after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation trustworthy.'
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and gave orders to offer him an offering and soothing offerings.
The king answered Daniel, 'In truth your God is the God of gods and the lord of kings and a revealer of secrets, since you've been able to reveal this secret.'
Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief of the prefects over all the wise men of Babylon.
And Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego over the administration of the province of Babylon; and Daniel himself was in the king's gate.

daniel_3.t: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

And King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to gather the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

So the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counsellors, the ministers, the judges, the magistrates and all the authorities of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the image King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood in front of the image Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
And the herald called out at full power: 'You are commanded, peoples, nations and languages:'

'The moment you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and every kind of music, you're to fall down and pay homage to the image of gold King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.'
'And anyone who doesn't fall down and pay homage will be thrown, then and there, into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.'

So at that time, the moment all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations and languages fell down and paid homage to the image of gold King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
So at that time certain Chaldean men came forward and denounced the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, 'King, live for ever!'

'You, King, made a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and every kind of music is to fall down and pay homage to the image of gold;'
'and anyone who doesn't fall down and pay homage is to be thrown into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.'

'Well, there are Jewish men you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon — Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. These men have paid no attention to you, King. They don't serve your god, and they don't pay homage to the image of gold you set up.'
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in a rage and fury, ordered Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego brought in. So these men were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar said to them, 'Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, that you don't serve my gods and don't pay homage to the image of gold I set up?'

'Now, if you're ready — the moment you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the trigon, the harp, the pipe and every kind of music, fall down and pay homage to the image I've made. But if you don't pay homage, you'll be thrown, then and there, into the middle of the burning fiery furnace. And who is the god who'll deliver you out of my hands?'
Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego answered the king, 'Nebuchadnezzar, we don't need to send you back a word about this matter.'
'If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace and from your hand, King, he'll deliver.'
'But if not, you should know, King, that we don't serve your god, and we won't pay homage to the image of gold you set up.'
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with anger, and the image of his face changed towards Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. He ordered the furnace heated seven times more than it was proper to heat it.
And he ordered mighty men of power in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego and throw them into the burning fiery furnace.
So these men were bound in their mantles, their trousers, their caps and their other clothes, and thrown into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
Because the king's word was harsh and the furnace so fiercely heated, the flame of the fire killed the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego up.
And those three men — Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego — fell bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was alarmed and jumped up. He said to his counsellors, 'Didn't we throw three men into the middle of the fire, bound?' They answered, 'It's certain, King.'
He said, 'Look — I see four men, loose, walking about in the middle of the fire, and there's no hurt on them. And the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'

Then Nebuchadnezzar went up to the door of the burning fiery furnace and called, 'Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!' So Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego came out of the middle of the fire.

And the satraps, the prefects, the governors and the king's counsellors gathered round and saw these men: the fire had had no power over their bodies, the hair of their heads wasn't singed, their mantles weren't changed, and the smell of fire hadn't touched them.

Nebuchadnezzar said, 'Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, who sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him. They violated the king's word and gave up their bodies rather than serve or pay homage to any god except their own God.'

'And I make this decree: any people, nation or language that says anything amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego will be cut into limbs and his house made a refuse heap — because there's no other god who can rescue like this.'
Then the king made Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego prosper in the province of Babylon.

daniel_4.t: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all the peoples, nations and languages living in all the earth: may your peace increase.
It's seemed good to me to declare the signs and the wonders that the Most High God has done with me.
How great his signs are, and how strong his wonders! His kingdom is a perpetual kingdom, and his dominion goes from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house, flourishing in my palace.
I saw a dream, and it frightened me. Imaginings on my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.
So I made a decree to bring all the wise men of Babylon in before me, to make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the magicians, the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers came in, and I told them the dream — but they couldn't make its interpretation known to me.
And at last Daniel came in before me — the one named Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, the one in whom is a spirit of holy gods — and I told him the dream:
'Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians — I know a spirit of holy gods is in you, and no secret is too hard for you. Tell me the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation.'
'The visions of my head on my bed were these: I was looking, and there was a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.'
'The tree grew great and strong. Its height reached to the heavens, and it could be seen to the end of all the earth.'

'Its foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and there was food in it for all. The animals of the field found shade under it, the birds of the heavens nested in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.'
'I was looking, in the visions of my head on my bed, and there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens.'
'He called out at full power: Cut the tree down, cut off its branches, strip off its foliage and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.'

'But leave the stump of its roots in the ground, with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let it be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.'
'Let his heart be changed from a human's, and let the heart of an animal be given him. And let seven times pass over him.'

'The command is by the decree of the watchers, the affair by the word of the holy ones — so that the living may know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind, and gives it to whomever he pleases, and sets the lowliest of humankind over it.'

'That's the dream I saw, I, King Nebuchadnezzar. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation — all the wise men of my kingdom can't make the interpretation known to me, but you can, because a spirit of holy gods is in you.'

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king said, 'Belteshazzar, don't let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.' Belteshazzar answered, 'My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your adversaries.'
'The tree you saw, which grew great and strong, whose height reached to the heavens and which could be seen over all the earth,'
'whose foliage was beautiful and its fruit plentiful, with food in it for all, under which the animals of the field lived and in whose branches the birds of the heavens lived —'
'that's you, King. You've grown great and strong; your greatness has grown and reached to the heavens, and your dominion to the end of the earth.'

'And that the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying: Cut the tree down and destroy it — but leave the stump of its roots in the ground, with a fetter of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; let it be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let its portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over it —'
'this is the interpretation, King. It's the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:'

'You'll be chased away from humankind. Your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; you'll be fed grass like oxen and made wet with the dew of the heavens. Seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he pleases.'
'And that they said to leave the stump of the roots of the tree: your kingdom will stay yours, from the time you know that the heavens have mastery.'
'So, King, let my advice be acceptable to you: break off your sin by doing righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps your prosperity may be prolonged.'
It all came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he was walking about on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.
The king said, 'Isn't this Babylon the great, which I built myself as a royal house, by the strength of my power and for the honour of my majesty?'
The word was still in the king's mouth when a voice fell from the heavens: 'To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has passed away from you,'

'and you're about to be chased away from humankind. Your dwelling will be with the animals of the field; you'll be fed grass like oxen, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he pleases.'

That very moment the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was chased away from humankind and ate grass like oxen; his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until his hair grew long like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

And at the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my understanding came back to me. I blessed the Most High. I praised and glorified the one who lives for ever, whose dominion is a perpetual dominion and whose kingdom goes from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth count for nothing. He does as he pleases with the army of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth, and there's no one who can strike his hand or say to him, 'What have you done?'

At that time my understanding came back to me, and for the honour of my kingdom my majesty and my splendour came back to me. My counsellors and my nobles sought me out, I was established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of the heavens. All his deeds are truth and his ways are justice, and those who walk in pride he's able to bring low.

daniel_5.t: King Belshazzar put on a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and in front of the thousand he was drinking wine.

Belshazzar, under the influence of the wine, gave orders to bring in the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem, so the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines could drink from them.
So they brought in the gold vessels that had been taken out of the temple, the house of God, in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.
That very moment the fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace — and the king watched the palm of the hand as it wrote.
Then the king's colour changed, his thoughts alarmed him, the joints of his loins gave way and his knees knocked together.

The king called out at full power to bring in the conjurers, the Chaldeans and the astrologers, and he said to the wise men of Babylon, 'Anyone who reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me will be clothed in purple, with a necklace of gold on his neck, and he'll rule as third in the kingdom.'
Then all the king's wise men came in, but they couldn't read the writing or make its interpretation known to the king.
Then King Belshazzar was exceedingly alarmed; his colour kept changing, and his nobles were dumbfounded.
The queen, because of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the banqueting house and said, 'King, live for ever! Don't let your thoughts alarm you, and don't let your colour change.'

'There's a man in your kingdom who has a spirit of holy gods in him. In the days of your father, illumination and insight and wisdom like the wisdom of gods were found in him, and King Nebuchadnezzar your father made him chief of the magicians, conjurers, Chaldeans and astrologers — your father the king —'

'because an extraordinary spirit, and understanding and insight — interpreting dreams, declaring riddles, loosening knots — were found in him, in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. So send for Daniel, and he'll declare the interpretation.'
So Daniel was brought in before the king. The king said to him, 'Are you that Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah whom the king my father brought from Judah?'
'I've heard about you — that a spirit of gods is in you, and that illumination and insight and extraordinary wisdom have been found in you.'
'And now the wise men and the conjurers have been brought in before me to read this writing and make its interpretation known to me — but they couldn't declare the interpretation of the matter.'

'And I've heard about you that you can interpret interpretations and loosen knots. So if you can read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you'll be clothed in purple, with a necklace of gold on your neck, and you'll rule as third in the kingdom.'
Then Daniel answered the king, 'Keep your gifts for yourself, and give your rewards to somebody else. Even so, I'll read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.'
'You, King — the Most High God gave the kingdom and the greatness and the honour and the majesty to Nebuchadnezzar your father.'

'And because of the greatness he gave him, all the peoples, nations and languages trembled and feared before him. Whoever he pleased he killed, and whoever he pleased he let live; whoever he pleased he lifted up, and whoever he pleased he brought low.'
'But when his heart rose up and his spirit grew strong to act presumptuously, he was deposed from the throne of his kingdom, and the honour was taken from him.'

'He was chased away from the sons of humankind; his heart was made like an animal's, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. They fed him grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until he knew that the Most High God has mastery over the kingdom of humankind and appoints over it whoever he pleases.'
'And you, his son Belshazzar, haven't brought your heart low — and you knew all this.'

'You've lifted yourself up against the lord of the heavens. They brought the vessels of his house in front of you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them; and you praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which don't see or hear or know. But the God who holds your breath in his hand, and to whom all your ways belong — him you haven't glorified.'
'So from before him the palm of the hand was sent out, and this writing was inscribed.'
'And this is the writing that was inscribed: MENE MENE TEQEL AND PHARSIN.'
'This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE — God has numbered your kingdom and finished it.'
'TEQEL — you've been weighed in the scales and found lacking.'
'PERES — your kingdom has been broken in two and given to the Medes and the Persians.'
Then Belshazzar gave orders, and they clothed Daniel in purple and put a necklace of gold on his neck, and made proclamation about him that he was to rule as third in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.

daniel_6.t: It seemed good to Darius to appoint a hundred and twenty satraps over the kingdom, to be throughout the whole kingdom;
and over them three overseers, one of whom was Daniel, whom these satraps were to report to, so the king shouldn't suffer any injury.
Then this Daniel stood out above the overseers and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king planned to put him over the whole kingdom.

So the overseers and the satraps looked for an occasion against Daniel in the affairs of the kingdom, but they couldn't find any occasion or corruption, because he was trustworthy — no negligence and no corruption was found in him.
Then these men said, 'We'll never find an occasion against this Daniel unless we find it against him in the law of his God.'
So these overseers and satraps came in a crowd to the king and said, 'Darius the king, live for ever!'

'All the overseers of the kingdom — the prefects, the satraps, the counsellors and the governors — have taken counsel together to establish a royal statute and to enforce a prohibition: that anyone who asks a petition of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, is to be thrown into the den of lions.'
'So now, King, establish the prohibition and sign the writing — which can't be changed, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.'
So King Darius signed the writing and the prohibition.

And Daniel, when he knew the writing had been signed, went into his house — where windows were open for him in his upper room facing Jerusalem — and three times a day he knelt on his knees and prayed and gave praise before his God, just as he'd been doing all along.
Then these men came in a crowd and found Daniel asking and imploring favour before his God.

So they went to the king and put the king's prohibition to him: 'Didn't you sign a prohibition that anyone who asks of any god or person for thirty days, except of you, King, is to be thrown into the den of lions?' The king answered, 'The word is certain, according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which does not pass away.'
Then they answered the king, 'Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah, has paid no attention to you, King, or to the prohibition you signed. Three times a day he asks his petition.'
When the king heard the word, he was exceedingly displeased. He set his mind on Daniel, to deliver him, and till sunset he was struggling to rescue him.
Then these men came in a crowd to the king and said, 'Know, King, that the law of the Medes and the Persians is that no prohibition or statute the king establishes can be changed.'
Then the king gave orders, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel, 'Your God, whom you serve continually — may he deliver you.'

And a stone was brought and set over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing should be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No diversions were brought in before him, and his sleep fled from him.
Then the king got up at dawn, at first light, and hurried to the den of lions.

And as he came near the den, to Daniel, he cried out in a pained voice. The king said to Daniel, 'Daniel, servant of the living God — your God, whom you serve continually: has he been able to deliver you from the lions?'
Then Daniel spoke with the king: 'King, live for ever!'
'My God sent his angel and shut the mouth of the lions, and they didn't harm me, because innocence was found in me before him. And before you too, King, I've done no hurtful act.'
Then the king was exceedingly glad, and gave orders to take Daniel up out of the den. And Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no hurt was found on him, because he'd trusted in his God.

And the king gave orders, and they brought those men who had denounced Daniel and threw them into the den of lions — them, their sons and their wives. They hadn't reached the bottom of the den before the lions had power over them and shattered all their bones.
Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages living in all the earth: may your peace increase.

'From me a decree is made: in all the dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel. For he's the living God, and he endures for ever; his kingdom won't be destroyed, and his dominion goes to the end.'
'He delivers and rescues, and he does signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth — he's the one who delivered Daniel from the hand of the lions.'
And this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

daniel_7.t: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head on his bed. Then he wrote the dream down and told the sum of the matters.
Daniel said: 'I was looking in my vision in the night, and there were the four winds of the heavens stirring up the great sea.'
'And four great beasts were coming up out of the sea, each one different from the others.'

'The first was like a lion, and it had eagle's wings. I went on looking until its wings were plucked off; it was lifted up off the earth and made to stand on two feet like a human being, and a human heart was given it.'
'And there was another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, with three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and they said to it, Get up, devour much flesh.'
'After this I was looking, and there was another one, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird on its back. The beast had four heads, and dominion was given it.'

'After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and there was a fourth beast — fearful, terrible, exceedingly strong. It had great teeth of iron; it was devouring and shattering and trampling the rest with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.'

'I was studying the horns, and there was another horn, a small one, coming up among them, and three of the earlier horns were uprooted from in front of it. And there in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a human being, and a mouth speaking great things.'

'I went on looking until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white like snow, the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was flames of fire, its wheels burning fire.'
'A river of fire was flowing out from in front of him. A thousand thousands were ministering to him, and a myriad of myriads were standing in front of him. The court sat, and books were opened.'
'I kept looking then, because of the sound of the great words the horn was speaking. I kept looking until the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given over to the burning of fire.'
'And as for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away — but a prolonging of life was given them until a time and a season.'
'I was looking in the visions of the night, and there with the clouds of the heavens was one like a son of man, coming. He came to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him.'

'And to him were given dominion and honour and a kingdom, and all the peoples, nations and languages will serve him. His dominion is a perpetual dominion that won't pass away, and his kingdom one that won't be destroyed.'
'As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed inside its sheath, and the visions of my head alarmed me.'
'I went up to one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. And he told me — he made known to me the interpretation of the matters:'
'These great beasts, four of them, are four kings who will arise out of the earth.'
'But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and they'll take possession of the kingdom for ever, for ever and ever.'

'Then I wanted to make certain about the fourth beast, the one that was different from all the others — exceedingly terrible, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, devouring, shattering, and trampling the rest with its feet —'

'and about the ten horns on its head, and the other one that came up, the one three fell before — that horn with eyes, and a mouth speaking great things, whose appearance was greater than its companions'.'
'I was looking, and that horn was making war on the saints and prevailing against them,'
'until the Ancient of Days came, and judgement was given in favour of the saints of the Most High; and the appointed time arrived, and the saints took possession of the kingdom.'
'He said: The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will be on the earth, different from all the kingdoms. It'll devour all the earth, tread it down and shatter it.'
'And the ten horns: out of that kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He'll be different from the ones before, and he'll bring low three kings.'

'He'll speak words against the Most High; he'll wear out the saints of the Most High, and he'll think to change appointed times and law; and they'll be given into his hand for a time and times and half a time.'
'Then the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to be annihilated and destroyed until the end.'

'And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens were given to a people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is a perpetual kingdom, and all the empires will serve him and obey him.'
'Here's the end of the matter.' As for me, Daniel, my thoughts alarmed me greatly and my colour changed; but I kept the matter in my heart.

daniel_8.t: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me earlier.
And I saw in the vision — and as I saw, I was in Susa the citadel, in the province of Elam — and I saw in the vision, and I was by the canal of Ulai.
I looked up, and there was a single ram standing in front of the canal, and it had two horns. Both horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.

I saw the ram thrusting westward, northward and southward, and no living creatures could stand in front of it; there was no one who could deliver from its hand. It did as it pleased and magnified itself.
And I was watching, and there was a he-goat coming from the west over the face of the whole earth, without touching the earth; and the he-goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
It came to the ram with the two horns, the one I'd seen standing in front of the canal, and it ran at it in the rage of its strength.

I saw it reach the ram, enraged at it. It struck the ram and broke both its horns, and there was no strength in the ram to stand in front of it. It threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one who could deliver the ram from its hand.
And the he-goat magnified itself exceedingly; but when it grew mighty, the great horn was broken, and four conspicuous horns came up in its place, towards the four winds of the heavens.
And out of one of them came a single horn, small at first, and it became exceedingly great towards the south and towards the east and towards the beautiful land.
It grew great as far as the host of the heavens, and it made some of the host and some of the stars fall to the ground, and it trampled them.
It magnified itself as far as the Prince of the host; from him the perpetual offering was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
And an army will be set over the perpetual offering in transgression, and it'll throw truth to the ground; and it'll act and succeed.

And I heard one holy one speaking, and one holy one said to the certain one who was speaking, 'How long does the vision hold — the perpetual offering, and the transgression that desolates, the giving over of both the sanctuary and the host to trampling?'
And he said to me, 'Until evening and morning — two thousand three hundred. Then the sanctuary will be restored.'
And it happened, when I, Daniel, had seen the vision and was seeking to understand it, that there stood in front of me one who looked like a man.
And I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, calling out, 'Gabriel, explain the vision to this one.'
So he came and stood beside me; and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. And he said to me, 'Understand, son of humankind, that the vision is for the time of the end.'
And while he was speaking with me I was dazed, face down on the ground. He touched me and set me on my feet where I'd been standing.
And he said, 'I'm going to make known to you what will be at the end of the indignation — because it's for the appointed time of the end.'
'The ram you saw, the one with the two horns, is the kings of Media and Persia.'
'And the hairy he-goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.'
'And as for the broken horn and the four that arose in its place: four kingdoms will arise out of that nation, but not with its power.'
'And at the end of their reign, when the rebels have reached their full measure, a king will arise, strong of face and understanding intrigues.'
'His power will be mighty — but not by his own power. He'll destroy wonderfully; he'll succeed and act, and he'll destroy the mighty and a people of holy ones.'

'Through his insight deceit will succeed in his hand; in his heart he'll magnify himself, and in prosperity he'll destroy many. He'll stand against a prince of princes, and by no hand he'll be broken.'
'And the vision of the evening and the morning that has been told is truth. But you — keep the vision secret; it's for many days.'
And I, Daniel, was overcome, and I lay sick for days. Then I got up and did the king's work. But I was appalled at what I'd seen, and there was no one who could give understanding.

daniel_9.t: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of Media, who'd been made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, saw in the books the number of the years that the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet — seventy years to be completed for the ruins of Jerusalem.
And I set my face to the Lord God, to seek him in prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.
And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed: 'I beg you, Lord — the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments —'
'we've sinned and committed iniquity, we've acted wickedly and rebelled, and we've turned aside from your commandments and from your judgements.'
'And we haven't listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.'

'To you, Lord, belongs the righteousness, and to us the shame of faces, as it is today — to the people of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far, in all the lands where you've banished them, in the unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against you.'
'LORD, to us belongs the shame of faces — to our kings, our leaders and our ancestors — because we've sinned against you.'
'To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness — and we have rebelled against him,'
'and we haven't listened to the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in his laws, which he set in front of us through his servants the prophets.'

'And all Israel have transgressed your law and turned aside, not listening to your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we've sinned against him.'

'And he's carried out his word, the word he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing on us a great calamity — nothing has been done under all the heavens like what has been done in Jerusalem.'

'Just as it's written in the law of Moses, all this calamity has come on us; and we haven't entreated the face of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquity and giving attention to your faithfulness.'
'And the LORD kept watch over the calamity and brought it on us; for the LORD our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done — and we haven't listened to his voice.'
'And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for yourself, as it is today: we've sinned, we've acted wickedly.'

'Lord, according to all your righteousnesses, let your anger and your rage turn back from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to everyone around us.'
'And now listen, our God, to the prayer of your servant and to his supplications, and make your face shine on your desolate sanctuary, for the Lord's sake.'

'Incline your ear, my God, and listen. Open your eyes and look at our desolations and at the city your name has been called over. It isn't on our righteousnesses that we lay our supplications in front of you, but on your great compassion.'
'Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, be attentive and act — don't delay — for your own sake, my God; because your name has been called over your city and over your people.'
And while I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my supplication before the LORD my God about the holy mountain of my God —
while I was still speaking in the prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I'd seen in the vision at the beginning, came to me when I was worn out and spent, about the time of the evening offering.
And he gave understanding, and he spoke with me: 'Daniel, I've come out now to give you insight and understanding.'
'At the beginning of your supplications a word went out, and I've come to declare it, because you are precious. So understand the word, and understand the vision.'

'Seventy weeks have been decreed on your people and on your holy city: to put an end to the transgression, to complete sin, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy place of holy places.'

'So know this and understand it: from the going out of a word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, is seven weeks; and for sixty-two weeks it'll be restored and rebuilt, with open place and moat, and in the distress of the times.'

'And after the sixty-two weeks an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing. And the people of the prince who's coming will destroy the city and the sanctuary; its end will come in the flood, and until the end there's war — desolations are determined.'

'And he'll make a covenant strong for the many for one week; and in the middle of the week he'll cause sacrifice and offering to cease. And on a wing of detestable things will come one who desolates — and until a complete destruction, what's determined will be poured out on the desolator.'

daniel_10.t: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The word was truth, and a great war. He understood the word, and understanding came to him in the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three sevens of days.
I ate no desirable food; no meat or wine came into my mouth, and I didn't anoint myself at all, until three sevens of days were completed.
And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month I was on the bank of the great river — that is, the Tigris.
I looked up, and there was a single man clothed in linen, his loins girded with the gold of Uphaz.

His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like torches of fire; his arms and his feet like the appearance of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
And I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision; the men who were with me didn't see it. But a great terror fell on them, and they ran off and hid.
So I was left on my own, and I saw this great vision. No strength was left in me; my vigour turned to ruin in me, and I kept no strength at all.
And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I fell dazed, face down, my face to the ground.
And then a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.

And he said to me, 'Daniel, greatly precious man, understand the words I'm speaking to you, and stand where you're standing — because I've been sent to you now.' And when he spoke this word with me, I stood up, trembling.
And he said to me, 'Don't be afraid, Daniel. From the first day you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard — and I've come because of your words.'
'But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me for twenty-one days; and then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there beside the kings of Persia.'
'And I've come to make you understand what will happen to your people at the end of the days — because the vision is still for those days.'
And while he was speaking with me in these words, I set my face to the ground and was struck dumb.

And then one like the likeness of the sons of humankind touched my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and said to the one standing in front of me, 'My lord, because of the vision my pangs have turned on me, and I've kept no strength.'
'And how can this servant of my lord speak with this my lord? As for me, from now on no strength is left in me, and there's no breath left in me.'
And again he touched me — one like the appearance of a human being — and he strengthened me.
And he said, 'Don't be afraid, greatly precious man; peace to you. Be strong. Be strong.' And as he spoke with me I was strengthened, and I said, 'Let my lord speak, because you've strengthened me.'
And he said, 'Do you know why I've come to you? Now I'll go back to fight with the prince of Persia; and as I go out, here comes the prince of Greece.'
'But I'll tell you what's inscribed in a writing of truth. There's no one who stands strong with me against these except Michael your prince.'

daniel_11.t: 'And as for me — in the first year of Darius the Mede, I took my stand to strengthen and protect him.'

'And now I'll tell you the truth. Three more kings are about to arise for Persia, and the fourth will gain great wealth, more than all of them; and by his strength, through his wealth, he'll stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.'
'And a mighty king will arise. He'll rule with great dominion and do as he pleases.'

'And as soon as he's arisen, his kingdom will be broken up and divided to the four winds of the heavens — not to his posterity, and not according to the dominion he ruled with. His kingdom will be plucked up and given to others besides these.'
'And the king of the south will grow strong, and one of his commanders too; but that one will grow stronger than he is, and he'll exercise dominion — his dominion will be a great dominion.'

'And at the end of years they'll make an alliance: the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she won't hold on to the power of the arm, and he won't stand, nor his arm; and she'll be given up — she and those who brought her, and the one who fathered her, and the one who strengthened her in those times.'
'And one from the shoot of her roots will arise in his place. He'll come against the army and get into the stronghold of the king of the north, and he'll act against them and prevail.'
'And their gods too, with their molten images and their precious vessels of silver and gold, he'll carry off into captivity to Egypt; and for years he'll keep clear of the king of the north.'
'And he'll come into the kingdom of the king of the south, and then go back to his own land.'
'And his sons will wage war and gather a multitude of great armies; and one will surely come, and overflow and pass over, and then come back and wage war as far as his stronghold.'
'And the king of the south will be enraged. He'll go out and fight with him, with the king of the north. And that one will raise up a great multitude — but the multitude will be given into his hand.'
'The multitude will be carried off, and his heart will be lifted up. He'll make tens of thousands fall — but he won't prevail.'
'And the king of the north will come back and raise up a multitude greater than the first; and at the end of the times, after years, he'll surely come with a large army and much equipment.'
'And in those times many will rise against the king of the south; and the sons of the violent ones among your own people will exalt themselves to fulfil the vision — but they'll stumble.'
'And the king of the north will come and throw up a siege mound and capture a fortified city; and the forces of the south won't stand, nor his chosen troops — there'll be no strength to stand.'
'And the one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand in front of him. He'll stand in the land of beauty, with complete destruction in his hand.'

'And he'll set his face to come with the power of his whole kingdom, and terms of agreement with him; and he'll act. And he'll give him the daughter of women, to destroy her — but she won't stand, and she won't be his.'
'And he'll set his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to the scorn he offers; without his scorn, he'll turn it back on him.'
'And he'll turn his face to the strongholds of his own land; and he'll stumble and fall, and not be found.'
'And there'll arise in his place one who sends an oppressor through the splendour of a kingdom; and in a few days he'll be broken — not in anger and not in battle.'
'And there'll arise in his place a despicable one, on whom the honour of royalty hasn't been conferred. He'll come in a time of quiet and take hold of royalty by intrigues.'
'And the forces of the flood will be swept away from in front of him and broken — and a prince of a covenant too.'
'And from the time an alliance is made with him he'll act deceitfully; he'll rise and grow mighty with a small nation.'

'In a time of quiet he'll come into the fertile places of the province, and do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers never did: scatter plunder and booty and property among them, and lay his plans against strongholds — but only for a time.'

'And he'll stir up his strength and his heart against the king of the south with a large army; and the king of the south will make ready for battle with an exceedingly large and mighty army. But he won't stand, because plans will be laid against him.'
'And those who eat his delicacies will break him; his army will be swept away, and many slain will fall.'
'And as for the two kings — their heart is bent on evil, and at one table they'll speak falsehood. But it won't succeed, because the end is still for the appointed time.'
'And he'll go back to his own land with great property, and his heart will be against the covenant of holiness. He'll act, and go back to his own land.'
'At the appointed time he'll come back and come into the south, but it won't be like the former time or like the latter.'

'And ships of Kittim will come against him, and he'll be disheartened. He'll turn back and direct his indignation against the covenant of holiness, and he'll act; and he'll turn back and give attention to those who forsake the covenant of holiness.'
'And forces from him will arise. They'll profane the sanctuary, the stronghold, abolish the perpetual offering, and set up the detestable thing that desolates.'
'And those who act wickedly against the covenant he'll pollute with flattering words; but a people who know their God will show strength and act.'
'And those who have insight among the people will give understanding to the many; but they'll stumble by sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, for days.'
'And when they stumble they'll be helped with a little help; and many will join themselves to them with intrigues.'
'And some of those who have insight will stumble, so as to refine among them and to purge and to make white, until the time of the end — because it's still for the appointed time.'

'And the king will do as he pleases. He'll exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and he'll speak extraordinary things against the God of gods. And he'll succeed until the indignation is completed, because what's decreed will be done.'
'And he'll pay no attention to the gods of his fathers, or to the one desired by women, or to any god; because above all he'll magnify himself.'
'But to a god of strongholds, in its place, he'll give honour; and to a god his fathers didn't know he'll give honour with gold and silver and costly stone and precious things.'
'And he'll act against the fortresses of strongholds with a foreign god. Whoever acknowledges him he'll increase in honour, and he'll make them rule over the many, and he'll divide land for a price.'

'And at the time of the end the king of the south will wage war with him; and the king of the north will storm against him with chariotry and horsemen and many ships, and he'll come into lands, and overflow, and pass through.'
'And he'll come into the land of beauty, and many will stumble; but these will escape out of his hand: Edom, and Moab, and the first of the people of Ammon.'
'And he'll stretch out his hand against lands, and the land of Egypt won't escape.'
'And he'll rule over the treasures of gold and silver and over all the precious things of Egypt; and Libyans and Cushites will be in his train.'
'But reports from the east and from the north will dismay him, and he'll go out in great rage to destroy and to devote many to destruction.'
'And he'll pitch the tents of his palace between the seas and the mountain of the beauty of holiness; and he'll come to his end, with no one to help him.'

daniel_12.t: 'And at that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people. And there'll be a time of distress such as has not happened since a nation came to be, until that time. And at that time your people will escape — everyone who's found written in the scroll.'
'And many of those who sleep in the ground of dust will wake up — these to everlasting life, and these to reproaches, to everlasting abhorrence.'
'And those who have insight will shine like the shining of the vault, and those who turn the many to righteousness like the stars, for ever and ever.'
'And you, Daniel — keep the words secret and seal up the scroll until the time of the end. Many will rove about, and knowledge will increase.'
And I, Daniel, looked, and there were two others standing, one on this bank of the River and one on that bank of the River.
And one said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the River, 'How long until the end of the wonders?'

And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the River. He raised his right hand and his left to the heavens and swore by the one who lives for ever: that it's for a time, times and a half; and when the shattering of the hand of the people of holiness is finished, all these things will be finished.
And I heard, but I didn't understand. And I said, 'My lord, what will be the latter part of these things?'
And he said, 'Go, Daniel. The things are kept secret and sealed up until the time of the end.'
'Many will purge themselves and make themselves white and be refined; and the wicked will act wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand — but those who have insight will understand.'
'And from the time the perpetual offering is abolished, and the setting up of the detestable thing that desolates, there'll be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.'
'How blessed is the one who waits and reaches a thousand three hundred and thirty-five days!'
'And you — go to the end. You'll rest, and you'll arise to your allotted portion at the end of the days.'

deuteronomy_1.t: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan — in the wilderness, in the desert plain opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di Zahab.
It's eleven days from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, Moses spoke to the Israelites, exactly as the LORD had commanded him for them.
This was after he'd struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Across the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses set out to make this law plain. He said:
The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb: "You've stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn around and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbours — in the desert plain, the hill country, the Shephelah, the Negev, along the seacoast — the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.

Look, I've set the land in front of you. Go in and take possession of the land the LORD swore to your ancestors — to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob — to give to them and to their offspring after them."
At that time I told you, "I can't carry you on my own.
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today there are as many of you as the stars in the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you just as he promised.
How can I carry your load, your burden and your disputes all by myself?
Choose men who are wise and understanding and experienced, from your tribes, and I'll put them at your head.
And you answered me, "What you've said is a good thing to do."
So I took the heads of your tribes — wise men, experienced men — and put them at your head: leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, of tens, and officials for your tribes.
At that time I gave your judges their orders: "Hear what's between your brothers, and judge rightly between a man and his brother, and between a man and the sojourner living with him.

Don't show partiality when you judge. Hear the small and the great alike. Don't be afraid of anyone, because the judgement belongs to God. And any case too hard for you, bring to me, and I'll hear it."
And at that time I gave you all your instructions.

Then we set out from Horeb and went through that whole great and awesome wilderness you saw, by way of the hill country of the Amorites, just as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
And I said to you, "You've reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
Look, the LORD your God has set the land in front of you. Go up and take it, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, told you. Don't be afraid, and don't lose heart."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let's send men ahead to search out the land and bring back word about which way we should go up and which cities we'll come to."
It seemed like a good idea to me, so I took twelve men from among you, one for each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country, came to the Wadi Eshcol, and spied it out.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and brought back word: "The land the LORD our God is giving us is good."
But you weren't willing to go up. You rebelled against what the LORD your God had said.
And you grumbled in your tents: "The LORD hated us — that's why he brought us out of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites and wipe us out.

Where are we going? Our brothers have made our hearts melt. They said, 'The people are bigger and taller than we are, the cities are huge and fortified right up to the sky, and we even saw the sons of the Anakim there.'"
And I said to you, "Don't be terrified. Don't be afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who goes ahead of you, will fight for you himself, just as he did for you in Egypt, right in front of you,
and in the wilderness, where you saw the LORD your God carry you the way a man carries his son, the whole way you went until you came to this place."
And still, in this, you didn't trust the LORD your God —
the one who went ahead of you on the road to find you a place to camp — in the fire at night, to show you the way to go, and in the cloud by day.
And the LORD heard the sound of your words. He was angry, and he swore:
"Not one of these men, this evil generation, will see the good land I swore to give your ancestors —
"except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He'll see it, and I'll give the land he walked on to him and his sons, because he followed the LORD fully.
The LORD was angry with me too, on your account. He said, 'You're not going in there either.'
Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you — he's the one going in. Strengthen him, because he's the one who will give Israel possession of it.

And your little ones, the ones you said would be carried off as plunder, and your children, who today don't know good from evil — they're the ones going in. I'll give it to them, and they'll take possession of it.
But you — turn around and set out for the wilderness, by way of the Sea of Reeds."

Then you answered me, "We've sinned against the LORD. We'll go up and fight ourselves, just as the LORD our God commanded us." And every one of you strapped on his weapons of war, and you thought going up into the hill country would be easy.
But the LORD said to me, "Tell them: Don't go up and don't fight, because I'm not among you. You'll be struck down in front of your enemies."
So I spoke to you, and you didn't listen. You rebelled against what the LORD had said, you acted presumptuously, and you went up into the hill country.
And the Amorites living in that hill country came out to meet you, chased you the way bees do, and beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
And you came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD didn't listen to you and didn't give ear to you.
And you stayed at Kadesh a long time — as long as you stayed.

deuteronomy_2.t: Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by way of the Sea of Reeds, just as the LORD had told me, and we went round the hill country of Seir for a long time.
And the LORD said to me:
"You've gone round this hill country long enough. Turn north.
And give the people this order: 'You're about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They'll be afraid of you. So be very careful.
Don't provoke them. I'm not giving you any of their land, not so much as a footstep's worth, because I've given the hill country of Seir to Esau as a possession.
Buy your food from them with silver and eat it; buy your water from them with silver and drink it.
The LORD your God has blessed you in everything you've done. He's known your going through this great wilderness. For forty years now the LORD your God has been with you, and you've lacked nothing.'

So we passed on, away from our brothers the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, away from the desert-plain road, from Elath and Ezion Geber. Then we turned and went along the way of the wilderness of Moab.
And the LORD said to me, "Don't harass Moab and don't provoke them to battle. I'm not giving you any of their land as a possession, because I've given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession.
The Emim used to live there — a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim.
They too were counted as Rephaim, like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.

And in Seir the Horites used to live, and the descendants of Esau dispossessed them, destroyed them, and settled in their place — just as Israel did with the land of its possession, which the LORD gave them.
'Now get up and cross the Wadi Zered.' So we crossed the Wadi Zered.

The time we travelled from Kadesh Barnea until we crossed the Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years — until the whole generation, the fighting men, had died out of the camp, just as the LORD had sworn to them.
And the hand of the LORD was against them too, driving them out of the camp until they were finished.
And when all the fighting men had finished dying out from among the people,
the LORD spoke to me:
"Today you're passing through Moab's territory, through Ar.

And you'll come up opposite the Ammonites. Don't harass them and don't provoke them. I'm not giving you any of the Ammonites' land as a possession, because I've given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.
That was counted a land of Rephaim too. Rephaim used to live there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
a people great and numerous and tall, like the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place —
just as he did for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, and they dispossessed them and have lived in their place to this day.
And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza — the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.
'Get up, set out, cross the Wadi Arnon. Look, I've given Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, into your hand, along with his land. Begin taking possession, and provoke him to battle.
Today I begin putting the dread and fear of you on the peoples under all the heavens. They'll hear the report of you, and they'll tremble and be in anguish because of you.'
Then I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace:
'Let me pass through your land. I'll keep to the road — I won't turn off to the right or the left.
Sell me food for silver and I'll eat; give me water for silver and I'll drink. Just let me pass through on foot —
just as the descendants of Esau in Seir did for me, and the Moabites in Ar — until I cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us.'

But Sihon king of Heshbon wasn't willing to let us pass through his land, because the LORD your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, so as to give him into your hand, as he has today.
And the LORD said to me, "Look, I've begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin taking possession, so you may possess his land."
Then Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.
And the LORD our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down — him, his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities and devoted to destruction every one of them — the men, the women and the little ones. We left no survivor.
Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the cities we'd captured.
From Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city in the wadi, as far as Gilead — there was no town too high for us. The LORD our God handed it all over to us.
The one place you didn't go near was the land of the Ammonites — all along the side of the Wadi Jabbok, the cities of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had commanded.

deuteronomy_3.t: Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, to fight at Edrei.

And the LORD said to me, "Don't be afraid of him. I've given him into your hand, along with all his people and his land, and you'll do to him just what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So the LORD our God gave Og king of Bashan into our hand too, along with all his people, and we struck him down until he had no survivor left.
At that time we captured all his cities. There wasn't a town we didn't take from them — sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.
All these were fortified cities with a high wall, double gates and a bar — besides a great many unwalled towns.
And we devoted them to destruction, just as we'd done to Sihon king of Heshbon — devoting to destruction every city: the men, the women and the little ones.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon —
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir)
— all the cities of the plateau, all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan.
Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron — isn't it in Rabbah of the Ammonites? Nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the ordinary cubit.
This land we took possession of at that time. From Aroer, by the Wadi Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, Og's kingdom, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh — the whole region of Argob, all that part of Bashan. It's called the land of Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and named them after himself — Bashan, that is: Havvoth Jair, to this day.
And to Makir I gave Gilead.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the land from Gilead as far as the Wadi Arnon — the middle of the wadi being the boundary — and as far as the Jabbok, the wadi that forms the Ammonite border;
and the Arabah, with the Jordan as its boundary, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah — the Salt Sea — under the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I gave you this order: "The LORD your God has given you this land to take possession of. You'll cross over armed, ahead of your brothers the Israelites — all of you who are fighting men.
Only your wives, your little ones and your livestock — I know you have a lot of livestock — will stay in the cities I've given you,

until the LORD gives your brothers rest as he has you, and they too take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you can go back to the possession I've given you."
At that time I told Joshua: "Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God did to these two kings. That's what the LORD will do to all the kingdoms you're crossing over into.
Don't be afraid of them. The LORD your God is the one fighting for you."
And at that time I pleaded with the LORD:
"Lord GOD, you've begun to show your servant your greatness and your strong hand. What god in the heavens or on the earth can do what you do, or match your mighty deeds?
Please let me cross over and see the good land across the Jordan — this good hill country, and Lebanon."
But the LORD was furious with me on your account and wouldn't listen to me. He said, "That's enough from you. Don't speak to me about this again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west and north and south and east. See it with your own eyes — because you're not crossing this Jordan.
But commission Joshua. Encourage him and strengthen him, because he's the one who'll cross over ahead of this people, and he's the one who'll give them possession of the land you'll see."
And we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.

deuteronomy_4.t: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and ordinances I'm teaching you to keep, so that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Don't add anything to the word I'm commanding you, and don't take anything away from it. Keep the commandments of the LORD your God, which I'm commanding you.
Your own eyes saw what the LORD did at Baal Peor. Every man who followed Baal Peor — the LORD your God destroyed him from among you.
But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all alive today.
Look, I've taught you statutes and ordinances, just as the LORD my God commanded me, so you'd keep them in the land you're going into to take possession of.

Keep them and do them, because that's your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples. They'll hear all these statutes and say, "This great nation really is a wise and understanding people."
What great nation has a god as near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has statutes and ordinances as righteous as all this law I'm setting before you today?

Only take care, and guard yourself closely, so you don't forget the things your eyes have seen, and so they don't slip from your heart as long as you live. Make them known to your children, and to your children's children —

the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people to me and I'll let them hear my words, so they'll learn to fear me as long as they live on the ground, and teach their children too."
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire right up to the heart of the heavens — darkness, cloud and thick darkness.
And the LORD spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words but saw no form — only a voice.
And he declared his covenant to you, which he commanded you to do — the ten words — and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
And me — the LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, for you to keep in the land you're crossing over into to take possession of.
So watch yourselves carefully. You saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb out of the fire.
or you'll act corruptly and make yourselves a carved image, a form of any figure — a likeness of male or female,
a likeness of any animal on the earth, of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
of anything that creeps on the ground, of any fish in the waters beneath the earth.

and don't lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them — things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under all the heavens.
But you — the LORD took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his own people of inheritance, as you are today.
And the LORD was angry with me on account of your words. He swore that I wouldn't cross the Jordan or enter the good land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
I'm going to die in this land. I'm not crossing the Jordan. But you are crossing over, and you'll take possession of this good land.
Watch yourselves. Don't forget the covenant of the LORD your God that he made with you, and don't make yourselves a carved image, a form of anything, which the LORD your God has forbidden you.
The LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you've had children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, a form of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking him to anger —

I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you today: you'll quickly and utterly perish from the land you're crossing the Jordan to take possession of. You won't prolong your days there — you'll be utterly destroyed.
And the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you'll be left few in number among the nations the LORD drives you to.
And there you'll serve gods that are the work of human hands — wood and stone — which don't see, don't hear, don't eat and don't smell.
But from there you'll seek the LORD your God, and you'll find him — if you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you're in distress, when all these things have come on you, in the days to come, you'll return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
The LORD your God is a compassionate God. He won't abandon you or destroy you, and he won't forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.

Ask about the days that came before you, from the day God created humankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything like this great thing ever happened? Has anything like it ever been heard?
Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire, the way you have, and lived?

Or has any god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from the middle of another nation — by trials, by signs and wonders, by battle, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm and great terrors — like everything the LORD your God did for you in Egypt, right in front of you?
You yourself were shown all this, so you'd know that the LORD is God, and there is no other besides him.
From the heavens he made you hear his voice, to discipline you; and on the earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words out of the fire.
And because he loved your ancestors, he chose their offspring after them, and brought you out by his own presence, by his great power, from Egypt,
to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you as you advanced, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as he has today.
So know today, and take it to heart: the LORD is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath. There is no other.

So keep his statutes and his commandments, which I'm commanding you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may live long on the ground the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three cities across the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
so that a killer could flee there — one who kills his neighbour without meaning to, and hadn't hated him beforehand. He can flee to one of these cities and live —
Bezer in the wilderness, on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the law Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, the statutes and the ordinances Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon — the one Moses and the Israelites struck down when they came out of Egypt.
And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan — the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, toward the sunrise —
from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Siyon (that is, Hermon),
and the whole Arabah across the Jordan on the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

deuteronomy_5.t: Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: "Listen, Israel, to the statutes and ordinances I'm speaking in your hearing today. Learn them, keep them, and do them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It wasn't with our ancestors that the LORD made this covenant, but with us — us, the ones here today, all of us alive.
Face to face the LORD spoke with you at the mountain, out of the fire.
I was standing between the LORD and you at that time, to declare the word of the LORD to you — because you were afraid of the fire and didn't go up the mountain. He said:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
"You shall have no other gods before my face.
"You shall not make yourself a carved image of any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.
"You shall not bow down to them or serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers on sons, on the third generation and the fourth, of those who hate me,
"and showing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
"You shall not take up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who takes up his name for emptiness.
"Keep the sabbath day, to set it apart as holy, just as the LORD your God commanded you.
"Six days you shall labour and do all your work,

"but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work — not you, or your son or your daughter, or your male servant or your female servant, or your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, or the sojourner within your gates — so that your male servant and your female servant may rest, just as you do.

"Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That's why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the sabbath day.
"Honour your father and your mother, just as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and it may go well with you on the ground the LORD your God is giving you.
"You shall not murder.
"You shall not commit adultery.
"You shall not steal.
"You shall not give empty testimony against your neighbour.

"You shall not covet your neighbour's wife. And you shall not desire your neighbour's house, or his field, his male servant or female servant, his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbour."

These words the LORD spoke to your whole assembly at the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, with a great voice — and he added no more. Then he wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
And when you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came to me — all the heads of your tribes, and your elders —

and you said, "Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we've heard his voice out of the fire. Today we've seen that God can speak with a human being and that person still lives.
So now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we keep on hearing the voice of the LORD our God, we'll die.
Who, of all flesh, has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, the way we have, and lived?
You go near and hear everything the LORD our God says. Then you tell us everything the LORD our God tells you, and we'll listen and do it."

And the LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me. The LORD said to me, "I've heard the sound of the words of this people, which they spoke to you. They've done well in everything they said.
If only this heart of theirs would stay theirs, to fear me and keep all my commandments always, so that it would go well with them and with their children forever!
Go and tell them: 'Go back to your tents.'

But you — stand here with me, and I'll speak to you the whole commandment and the statutes and the ordinances you're to teach them, and they'll do them in the land I'm giving them to take possession of."
So be careful to do just what the LORD your God has commanded you. Don't turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in the whole way the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may live long in the land you're going to take possession of.

deuteronomy_6.t: And this is the commandment — the statutes and the ordinances — that the LORD your God commanded to be taught to you, for you to do in the land you're crossing over into to take possession of,
