so that you may fear the LORD your God by keeping all his statutes and his commandments that I'm commanding you — you, your son and your son's son — as long as you live, and so that your days may be long.

So listen, Israel, and be careful to do them, so that it may go well with you and you may increase greatly, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you — a land flowing with milk and honey.
Listen, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.
And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
And these words I'm commanding you today are to be on your heart.
Repeat them to your children. Speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they'll be as marks between your eyes.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you — great and good cities you didn't build,
and houses full of every good thing you didn't fill, and hewn cisterns you didn't hew, vineyards and olive trees you didn't plant — and you eat and are satisfied:
then watch yourself, so you don't forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
Fear the LORD your God. Serve him. Swear by his name.
Don't go after other gods, the gods of the peoples around you —
because the LORD your God among you is a jealous God — or the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and he'll destroy you from the face of the ground.
Don't put the LORD your God to the test, the way you tested him at Massah.
Keep the commandments of the LORD your God diligently, along with his testimonies and his statutes that he has commanded you.
Do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you, and you'll go in and take possession of the good land the LORD swore to your ancestors,
driving out all your enemies before you, just as the LORD said.
When your son asks you in time to come, "What are these testimonies and statutes and ordinances that the LORD our God commanded you?" —
then you'll tell your son, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
The LORD gave signs and wonders, great and terrible, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his household, right in front of us.
And us — he brought us out of there, so as to bring us in and give us the land he swore to our ancestors.
And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, to keep us alive, as he has today.
And it will be righteousness for us if we're careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, just as he commanded us.

deuteronomy_7.t: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you're entering to take possession of, and clears away many nations before you — the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you —
and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you strike them down — then you're to devote them utterly to destruction. Don't make a covenant with them, and don't show them favour.
And don't intermarry with them. Don't give your daughter to his son, and don't take his daughter for your son,
because he'd turn your son away from following me, and they'd serve other gods, and the anger of the LORD would burn against you, and he'd destroy you quickly.
Instead, this is what you're to do to them: break down their altars, shatter their pillars, cut down their Asherim, and burn their images with fire.
You're a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God chose you to be his own treasured people, out of all the peoples on the face of the ground.
It wasn't because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD set his love on you and chose you. You were the fewest of all the peoples.

It was because the LORD loved you, and because he kept the oath he swore to your ancestors, that the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from a house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
So know that the LORD your God is God — the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations,
and repaying to his face the one who hates him, to destroy him. He won't delay with the one who hates him — he repays him to his face.
So keep the commandment, the statutes and the ordinances I'm commanding you today, and do them.
And in return for your listening to these ordinances and keeping and doing them, the LORD your God will keep for you the covenant and the steadfast love that he swore to your ancestors.

He'll love you and bless you and multiply you. He'll bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground — your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock — on the ground he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You'll be blessed above all the peoples. There won't be a sterile male or a barren female among you, or among your livestock.
The LORD will take every sickness away from you. None of the terrible diseases of Egypt you knew will he put on you — he'll put them on all who hate you.
You'll consume all the peoples the LORD your God hands over to you. Your eye is not to look on them with pity, and you're not to serve their gods — that would be a snare to you.
If you say to yourself, "These nations are greater than I am — how can I dispossess them?" —
don't be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt —

the great trials your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. That's what the LORD your God will do to all the peoples you're afraid of.
And the LORD your God will send the hornet among them too, until those who are left and those hiding from you perish.
Don't be terrified of them. The LORD your God is among you, a great and awesome God.
And the LORD your God will clear these nations away before you little by little. You won't be able to finish them off quickly, or the wild animals would grow too many for you.
And the LORD your God will hand them over to you and throw them into great confusion, until they're destroyed.
He'll give their kings into your hand, and you'll destroy their name from under the heavens. No one will stand before you until you've destroyed them.
Burn the images of their gods with fire. Don't covet the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself, or you'll be ensnared by it — it's an abomination to the LORD your God.
Don't bring an abomination into your house, or you'll become devoted to destruction like it. Utterly detest it, utterly abhor it — it's devoted to destruction.

deuteronomy_8.t: Be careful to do the whole commandment I'm commanding you today, so that you may live and increase, and go in and take possession of the land the LORD swore to your ancestors.
Remember the whole way the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart — whether you'd keep his commandments or not.

He humbled you and let you go hungry, and he fed you the manna, which you didn't know and your ancestors didn't know, to make you know that a human being doesn't live on bread alone — a human being lives on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Your clothing didn't wear out on you, and your foot didn't swell, these forty years.
Know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
So keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
The LORD your God is bringing you into a good land — a land of streams of water, of springs and deeps flowing out in the valley and in the hill country,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines and figs and pomegranates, a land of the oil-olive and of honey,
a land where you'll eat bread without scarcity, where you'll lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and from whose hills you'll dig copper.
You'll eat and be satisfied, and you'll bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
Watch yourself, so you don't forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commandments, his ordinances and his statutes, which I'm commanding you today —
or you'll eat and be satisfied, and build good houses and live in them,
and your herd and your flock increase, and silver and gold increase for you, and everything you have increases,
and your heart is lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves,
who led you through the great and awesome wilderness — fiery serpent and scorpion, thirsty ground with no water — who brought water out for you from the flinty rock,
who fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors didn't know, to humble you and to test you, to do you good in the end —
and you say to yourself, "My own strength and the might of my hand made this wealth for me."
But remember the LORD your God — he's the one who gives you strength to make wealth, so as to confirm his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as he has today.
And if you utterly forget the LORD your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them — I testify against you today that you'll utterly perish.
Like the nations the LORD is destroying before you, that's how you'll perish — because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

deuteronomy_9.t: Listen, Israel: today you're crossing the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you — cities great and fortified right up to the sky,
a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anakim, whom you know and have heard about: "Who can stand before the descendants of Anak?"

So know today that the LORD your God is the one crossing over ahead of you, a consuming fire. He'll destroy them and subdue them before you, and you'll dispossess them and destroy them quickly, just as the LORD said to you.

Don't say to yourself, when the LORD your God drives them out before you, "It's because of my righteousness that the LORD brought me in to take possession of this land." It's because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is dispossessing them before you.

It isn't because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you're going in to take possession of their land. It's because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you — and to confirm the word the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
Know this: it isn't because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to take possession of. You're a stiff-necked people.

Remember — don't forget — how you provoked the LORD your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you've been rebelling against the LORD.
At Horeb you provoked the LORD to anger, and the LORD was angry enough with you to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone — the tablets of the covenant the LORD made with you — I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
And the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God. On them was everything the LORD spoke with you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
And at the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

And the LORD said to me, "Get up, go down quickly from here. Your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They've turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them; they've made themselves a molten image."
And the LORD said to me: "I've seen this people, and they are a stiff-necked people.
Leave me alone, and I'll destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I'll make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are."
So I turned and went down from the mountain, with the mountain burning with fire and the two tablets of the covenant on my two hands.
And I looked, and there it was: you had sinned against the LORD your God. You'd made yourselves a calf of cast metal. You'd turned aside quickly from the way the LORD had commanded you.
So I seized the two tablets, threw them out of my two hands, and broke them in front of you.

And I fell down before the LORD as I had before, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water — because of all the sin you had sinned, in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
I was afraid of the anger and the rage the LORD was angry with against you, enough to destroy you. And the LORD listened to me that time too.
The LORD was very angry with Aaron too, enough to destroy him — and I prayed for Aaron as well at that time.

And your sin, the thing you'd made — the calf — I took and burned with fire, and I crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the wadi that comes down from the mountain.
And at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth Hattaavah you provoked the LORD to anger.

And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh Barnea, saying, "Go up and take possession of the land I've given you," you rebelled against what the LORD your God had said. You didn't trust him and didn't listen to his voice.
You've been rebelling against the LORD from the day I knew you.
So I fell down before the LORD the forty days and forty nights that I fell down, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
And I prayed to the LORD: "Lord GOD, don't destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Don't turn toward this people's stubbornness, or its wickedness, or its sin,

or the land you brought us out of will say, 'The LORD wasn't able to bring them into the land he spoke of to them, and because he hated them he brought them out to put them to death in the wilderness.'
And they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great strength and your outstretched arm."

deuteronomy_10.t: At that time the LORD said to me, "Cut yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain, and make yourself an ark of wood.
And I'll write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you broke, and you'll put them in the ark."
So I made an ark of acacia wood, cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
And he wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the ten words the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly — and the LORD gave them to me.
So I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I'd made, and there they've been, just as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD and serve him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
That's why Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God said to him.)
And I stayed on the mountain as I had before, forty days and forty nights, and the LORD listened to me that time too. The LORD wasn't willing to destroy you.
And the LORD said to me, "Get up, set out ahead of the people, so they can go in and take possession of the land I swore to their ancestors to give them."
And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the LORD and his statutes, which I'm commanding you today, for your good?
Look — the heavens and the heavens of the heavens belong to the LORD your God, and the earth and everything in it.
And yet it was on your ancestors that the LORD set his love, to love them; and he chose their offspring after them — you — out of all the peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and don't stiffen your neck again.
The LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords — the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe,
who does justice for the fatherless and the widow, and who loves the sojourner, giving him bread and clothing.
So love the sojourner — you were sojourners in the land of Egypt yourselves.
Fear the LORD your God. Serve him. Cling to him. Swear by his name.
He is your praise and he is your God, who has done these great and awesome things for you, the things your eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt seventy persons strong, and now the LORD your God has made you as many as the stars in the sky.

deuteronomy_11.t: So love the LORD your God, and keep his charge, his statutes, his ordinances and his commandments, always.
And know today — I'm not speaking with your children, who haven't known and haven't seen the discipline of the LORD your God, his greatness, his strong hand and his outstretched arm,
and his signs and his deeds that he did in the middle of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,
and what he did to the army of Egypt, its horses and its chariotry, when he made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them as they pursued you — and the LORD destroyed them, to this day;
and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place;

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing at their feet, in the middle of all Israel —
Your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD, everything he did.
So keep the whole commandment I'm commanding you today, so that you may be strong, and go in and take possession of the land you're crossing over into to take possession of,
and so that you may live long on the ground the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their offspring — a land flowing with milk and honey.
The land you're going into to take possession of isn't like the land of Egypt you came out of, where you'd sow your seed and water it by hand, like a vegetable garden.
But the land you're crossing over into to take possession of is a land of mountains and valleys, drinking water from the rain of the heavens —
a land the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are on it continually, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
And if you listen carefully to my commandments that I'm commanding you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I'll give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, and you'll gather your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil.
And I'll give grass in your field for your livestock, and you'll eat and be satisfied.
Watch yourselves, or your heart will be enticed, and you'll turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them,
and the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and he'll shut up the heavens so there's no rain and the ground gives no produce, and you'll perish quickly from the good land the LORD is giving you.
Put these words of mine on your heart and on your soul. Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they'll be as marks between your eyes.
Teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit at home and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and your children's days may be many on the ground the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them — like the days of the heavens above the earth.
If you diligently keep this whole commandment I'm commanding you to do — loving the LORD your God, walking in all his ways and clinging to him —
then the LORD will dispossess all these nations before you, and you'll dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
Every place the sole of your foot treads on will be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River — the river Euphrates — to the western sea will be your territory.
No one will stand before you. The LORD your God will put the dread and fear of you over the whole land you tread on, just as he said he would.
Look — I'm setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I'm commanding you today;
and the curse, if you don't listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way I'm commanding you today, to go after other gods you haven't known.
And when the LORD your God brings you into the land you're going into to take possession of, you're to set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Aren't they across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
You're crossing the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you, and you'll take possession of it and live in it.
So be careful to do all the statutes and ordinances I'm setting before you today.

deuteronomy_12.t: These are the statutes and ordinances you're to be careful to do in the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to take possession of, for as long as you live on the ground.
Utterly destroy all the places where the nations you're dispossessing served their gods — on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Break down their altars, shatter their pillars, burn their Asherim with fire, cut down the images of their gods, and destroy their name from that place.
That is not how you're to do for the LORD your God.
Instead, to the place the LORD your God will choose out of all your tribes, to put his name there — to his dwelling you'll resort, and there you'll come.
Bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vows and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.
And you'll eat there before the LORD your God, and rejoice in everything you put your hand to, you and your households, in which the LORD your God has blessed you.
You're not to do as we're all doing here today, each of us doing whatever is right in his own eyes.
You haven't yet come to the resting place and the inheritance the LORD your God is giving you.
You'll cross the Jordan and live in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and he'll give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you'll live in security.

And the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell there — that's where you'll bring all that I'm commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and the choicest of the vows you vow to the LORD.
And you'll rejoice before the LORD your God — you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite in your towns, since he has no portion or inheritance with you.
Watch yourself — don't offer up your burnt offerings in just any place you see.
It's in the place the LORD chooses in one of your tribes that you'll offer up your burnt offerings, and there you'll do everything I'm commanding you.

But you may slaughter and eat meat wherever you like, as much as you want, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you, in any of your towns. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it, just as they eat the gazelle and the deer.
Only the blood you must not eat — pour it out on the ground like water.

You may not eat in your own towns the tithe of your grain, your new wine or your fresh oil, or the firstborn of your herd or flock, or any of the vows you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand.

It's before the LORD your God that you'll eat it, in the place the LORD your God chooses — you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite in your towns — and you'll rejoice before the LORD your God in everything you put your hand to.
Watch yourself — don't neglect the Levite as long as you live on your ground.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he promised you, and you say, "I want to eat meat," because you have an appetite for it — then eat meat, as much as you want.

If the place the LORD your God chooses to put his name there is too far from you, then slaughter from your herd and your flock that the LORD has given you, just as I've commanded you, and eat in your own towns, as much as you want.
Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, that's how you'll eat it. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
Only be firm about not eating the blood — the blood is the life, and you're not to eat the life with the meat.
You're not to eat it — pour it out on the ground like water.
Don't eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
Only your holy things and your vows — those you'll take and go to the place the LORD chooses.
Offer your burnt offerings — the flesh and the blood — on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices is to be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and the flesh you'll eat.
Be careful to hear all these words I'm commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations you're going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,
watch yourself. Don't be ensnared into following them after they've been destroyed before you, and don't enquire after their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? I'll do the same."

You're not to do that for the LORD your God, because every abomination of the LORD, everything he hates, they have done for their gods — they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire for their gods.
Everything I'm commanding you — that's what you're to be careful to do. Don't add to it, and don't take anything away from it.

deuteronomy_13.t: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or wonder does come to pass, the one he spoke to you about, saying, "Let's go after other gods, whom you haven't known, and serve them,"
you're not to listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams. The LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
Walk after the LORD your God. Fear him. Keep his commandments. Listen to his voice. Serve him. Cling to him.

And that prophet or that dreamer of dreams is to be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from a house of slaves — to thrust you aside from the way the LORD your God commanded you to walk in. So you'll burn out the evil from among you.

If your brother, your own mother's son, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own self, entices you in secret, saying, "Let's go and serve other gods" — gods you haven't known, neither you nor your ancestors,
gods of the peoples around you, near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other —
don't yield to him and don't listen to him. Your eye is not to look on him with pity, and you're not to spare him or cover for him.
You're to kill him. Your hand is to be against him first, to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.
Stone him with stones so that he dies, because he sought to thrust you aside from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
And all Israel will hear and fear, and they won't do such an evil thing as this among you again.
If you hear it said of one of your cities that the LORD your God is giving you to live in —
"Worthless men have gone out from among you and have thrust aside the inhabitants of their city, saying, 'Let's go and serve other gods,' gods you haven't known,"
then investigate, search and enquire thoroughly. And if it's true, if the thing is established that this abomination has been done among you,
you're to strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, devoting it to destruction — it and everything in it and its livestock — with the edge of the sword.
Gather all its plunder into the middle of its open square, and burn the city and all its plunder with fire, as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It's to be a mound forever, never rebuilt.

Nothing of what is devoted to destruction is to cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from the burning of his anger and give you compassion — have compassion on you and multiply you, just as he swore to your ancestors —
when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments that I'm commanding you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

deuteronomy_14.t: You are children of the LORD your God. Don't cut yourselves, and don't make yourselves bald between your eyes for the dead.
You are a people holy to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be his own treasured people, out of all the peoples on the face of the ground.
You're not to eat anything that is an abomination.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat,
the deer, the gazelle and the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.
Every animal with a divided hoof, cleft right through into two hooves, that chews the cud — that you may eat.

But of those that chew the cud and those with a divided, cloven hoof, you're not to eat these: the camel, the hare and the rock hyrax. They chew the cud but don't have a divided hoof — they're unclean for you.
And the pig — it has a divided hoof but doesn't chew the cud, so it's unclean for you. Don't eat their meat, and don't touch their carcasses.
These you may eat, of everything in the water: anything with fins and scales you may eat.
And anything without fins and scales you're not to eat — it's unclean for you.
Every clean bird you may eat.
And these are the ones you're not to eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the falcon, the kite of every kind,
every raven of every kind,
the ostrich, the owl, the gull, the hawk of every kind,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the desert owl, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, the heron of every kind, the hoopoe and the bat.
And every winged swarming creature is unclean for you — they're not to be eaten.
Every clean winged creature you may eat.

Don't eat any carcass. You may give it to the sojourner in your towns, and he may eat it, or sell it to a foreigner — you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Don't boil a kid in its mother's milk.
Be sure to tithe all the produce of your seed that comes out of the field, year by year.

And you'll eat before the LORD your God, in the place he chooses to make his name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, and the firstborn of your herd and flock — so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
And if the way is too long for you to carry it, because the place the LORD your God chooses to put his name there is too far from you — since the LORD your God will bless you —
then exchange it for silver, bind up the silver in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses.

Spend the silver on whatever you have an appetite for — cattle, flock, wine, strong drink, whatever your appetite asks of you — and eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.
And the Levite in your towns — don't neglect him. He has no portion or inheritance with you.
At the end of three years, bring out all the tithe of your produce for that year and deposit it in your towns.

Then the Levite will come — he has no portion or inheritance with you — and the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow in your towns, and they'll eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

deuteronomy_15.t: At the end of seven years you're to make a release.

And this is how the release works: every creditor is to release the loan he has made to his neighbour. He's not to press his neighbour or his brother, because a release has been proclaimed for the LORD.
You may press the foreigner, but whatever of yours is held by your brother, your hand is to release.
All the same, there'll be no needy person among you, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to take possession of —
but only if you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do this whole commandment I'm commanding you today.
The LORD your God has blessed you, as he promised, and you'll lend to many nations but won't borrow; you'll rule over many nations, but they won't rule over you.

If there's a needy person among you, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in the land the LORD your God is giving you, don't harden your heart and don't shut your hand against your needy brother.
Open your hand wide to him, and lend him enough for his need — whatever he lacks.

Watch yourself. Don't let there be a worthless thought in your heart — "The seventh year, the year of release, is near" — so that your eye is evil toward your needy brother and you give him nothing, and he cries out against you to the LORD, and it becomes sin on you.
Give to him freely, and don't let your heart be grieved when you give to him — because on account of this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and everything you put your hand to.
The needy will never cease from the land. That's why I'm commanding you: open your hand wide to your brother, to your poor and to your needy in your land.
If your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he'll serve you six years, and in the seventh year you're to send him out free.
And when you send him out free, don't send him out empty-handed.
Furnish him generously from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress. As the LORD your God has blessed you, so give to him.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you. That's why I'm commanding you this thing today.
And if he says to you, "I won't leave you," because he loves you and your household, because he's well off with you,
then take the awl and put it through his ear into the door, and he'll be your slave forever. Do the same for your maidservant.
Don't find it hard when you send him out free, because he has served you six years at double the wage of a hired worker — and the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
Every firstborn male born in your herd and flock you're to set apart as holy to the LORD your God. Don't work with the firstborn of your ox, and don't shear the firstborn of your flock.
You'll eat it before the LORD your God, year by year, in the place the LORD chooses, you and your household.
And if it has a blemish — lame or blind, any serious blemish — don't sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
Eat it in your own towns, the unclean and the clean alike, just as they eat the gazelle and the deer.
Only its blood you must not eat — pour it out on the ground like water.

deuteronomy_16.t: Keep the month of Abib and make the passover to the LORD your God, because it was in the month of Abib that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt, at night.
Sacrifice the passover to the LORD your God from the flock and the herd, in the place the LORD chooses to make his name dwell there.

Don't eat leavened bread with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction — because you came out of the land of Egypt in haste — so that you'll remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt as long as you live.
No leaven is to be seen with you anywhere in your territory for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice in the evening on the first day is to be left overnight until morning.
You may not sacrifice the passover in any of your own towns that the LORD your God is giving you,

but at the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell there — that's where you'll sacrifice the passover, in the evening, as the sun goes down, at the appointed time of your coming out of Egypt.
Cook it and eat it in the place the LORD your God chooses, and in the morning turn and go to your tents.
Six days you'll eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there's to be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God. Do no work.
Count seven weeks for yourself. From the time the sickle first goes into the standing grain, begin counting seven weeks.
Keep a festival of weeks to the LORD your God, with the tribute of a freewill offering from your hand, as the LORD your God has blessed you.

And you'll rejoice before the LORD your God — you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite in your towns, and the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow among you — in the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell there.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to do these statutes.
Keep the festival of booths for seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice in your festival — you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow in your towns.

For seven days keep the festival to the LORD your God in the place the LORD chooses, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands — and you'll be nothing but joyful.

Three times a year every male of yours is to appear before the face of the LORD your God in the place he chooses: at the festival of unleavened bread, the festival of weeks, and the festival of booths. And he's not to appear before the face of the LORD empty-handed.
Each one according to what his hand can give, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that he has given you.
Appoint judges and officials for yourself in all your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they'll judge the people with righteous judgement.
Don't pervert judgement. Don't show partiality. Don't take a bribe — a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
Righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue — so that you may live, and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Don't plant for yourself an Asherah of any wood beside the altar of the LORD your God that you make for yourself.
And don't set up a pillar for yourself — the LORD your God hates it.

deuteronomy_17.t: Don't sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep with a blemish in it, any serious defect — that's an abomination to the LORD your God.
If there's found among you, in any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, transgressing his covenant —
and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them — the sun or the moon or all the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded —
and it's told to you and you hear it, then investigate thoroughly. And if it's true, if the thing is established that this abomination has been done in Israel,
then bring out to your gates that man or that woman who has done this evil thing — the man or the woman — and stone them with stones, and they'll die.
It's on the testimony of two or three witnesses that the one who is to die is to be put to death. He's not to be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
The hand of the witnesses is to be against him first, to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you'll burn out the evil from among you.

If a matter is too difficult for you to judge — between blood and blood, case and case, wound and wound, matters of dispute in your towns — then arise and go up to the place the LORD your God chooses.
Come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge in office at the time, and enquire, and they'll declare to you the word of the verdict.
Act according to the word they declare to you from that place the LORD chooses, and be careful to do everything they instruct you.
Act according to the law they give you and the verdict they pronounce. Don't turn aside from the word they declare to you, to the right or the left.

And the man who acts presumptuously, refusing to listen to the priest who stands to serve there before the LORD your God, or to the judge — that man is to die. So you'll burn out the evil from Israel.
And all the people will hear and fear, and they won't act presumptuously again.
When you come into the land the LORD your God is giving you, and take possession of it and live in it, and you say, "Let me set a king over me, like all the nations around me,"
then you're to set over yourself a king whom the LORD your God chooses. Set a king over yourself from among your brothers. You may not put a foreign man over yourself, one who is not your brother.

Only he's not to multiply horses for himself, and he's not to make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses — because the LORD has said to you, "You are never to go back that way again."
He's not to multiply wives for himself, so that his heart doesn't turn aside; and silver and gold he's not to multiply for himself excessively.
And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he's to write out for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, from the one kept before the priests, the Levites.
It's to stay with him, and he's to read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, and do them —

so that his heart isn't lifted up above his brothers, and he doesn't turn aside from the commandment to the right or the left, and so that he may reign long over his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

deuteronomy_18.t: The priests, the Levites—the whole tribe of Levi—get no share and no inheritance alongside Israel. What they eat is the LORD's food offerings and his inheritance.
He gets no inheritance among his kinsmen. The LORD himself is his inheritance—just as he said to him.
Here is what the priests are owed from the people, from anyone offering a sacrifice, ox or sheep: give the priest the foreleg, the two cheeks and the stomach.
Give him the first of your grain, your new wine and your fresh oil, and the first fleece off your flock.
The LORD your God chose him out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the LORD's name—him and his sons, always.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns, anywhere in Israel, where he has been living as a sojourner, and he comes with all his desire to the place the LORD chooses,
then he can serve in the name of the LORD his God just like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They eat share for share—besides what comes from the sale of his patrimony.
When you get to the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to do what those nations do—their abominations.
No one is to be found among you who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or who practises divination, or is a soothsayer, an augurer, a sorcerer,
or casts spells, or consults a medium or a spiritist, or questions the dead.
Anyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD, and it is because of these abominations that the LORD your God is driving them out ahead of you.
Be blameless with the LORD your God.
These nations you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and diviners. But as for you—the LORD your God has not allowed you that.
The LORD your God will raise up a prophet like me for you, from among you, from your own kinsmen. Listen to him.

This is just what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb, on the day of the assembly, when you said, 'Do not let me hear the voice of the LORD my God again, and do not let me see this great fire any more, so I do not die.'
And the LORD said to me, 'They are right in what they said.'
'I will raise up a prophet like you for them, from among their own kinsmen. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.'
'And anyone who will not listen to my words that he speaks in my name—I myself will require it of him.'
'But a prophet who dares to speak a word in my name that I never commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet is to die.'
'And if you are thinking, "How will we know a word the LORD has not spoken?"'
'When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen, does not come about—that is a word the LORD did not speak. The prophet said it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.'

deuteronomy_19.t: When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you dispossess them and settle in their cities and their houses,
set apart three cities for yourself in the middle of the land the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it.
Prepare the road, and divide the territory of the land the LORD your God is giving you to inherit into three parts, so that any killer can flee there.
Here is the case of the killer who can flee there and live: someone who strikes his neighbour without intending it, and had not hated him beforehand.

Or say a man goes into the forest with his neighbour to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to fell the tree, and the iron head flies off the handle and hits his neighbour, and he dies—he flees to one of these cities and lives.

Otherwise the avenger of blood might chase the killer down while his blood is up, and catch him because the road is long, and strike him dead—when there is no sentence of death against him, since he had not hated him beforehand.
That is why I am commanding you: set apart three cities for yourself.
And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you the whole land he said he would give them—
if you keep this whole commandment and do it, as I command you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always—then add three more cities for yourself to these three.
so that innocent blood is not shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt fall on you.
But if a man hates his neighbour, lies in wait for him, comes at him and strikes him dead, and then runs to one of these cities,
then the elders of his city send and take him from there and hand him over to the avenger of blood, and he dies.
Do not let your eye pity him. Purge the blood of the innocent from Israel, and it will go well with you.
Do not move back your neighbour's boundary marker, set by those who came before you, in the inheritance you receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it.
One witness alone is not enough to stand against a man for any iniquity or any sin, whatever the sin he commits. A matter stands on the testimony of two witnesses or three.
If a malicious witness stands against a man, testifying against him falsely,
then the two men in the dispute stand before the LORD—before the priests and the judges who are in office at the time.
The judges investigate thoroughly, and if the witness turns out to be a false witness, having testified falsely against his brother,
then do to him exactly what he schemed to do to his brother. That is how you purge the evil from among you.
The rest will hear and be afraid, and they will not do such an evil thing among you again.
Do not let your eye pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

deuteronomy_20.t: When you go out to war against your enemies and you see horses and chariots, an army bigger than yours, do not be afraid of them. The LORD your God is with you—the one who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
As you draw near to the battle, the priest comes forward and speaks to the people.
He says to them: 'Hear, Israel! Today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart go faint. Do not be afraid, do not panic, do not be in dread of them.
The LORD your God goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to give you victory.'
Then the officers speak to the people: 'Is there a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go home. Otherwise he may die in the battle and another man will dedicate it.
Is there a man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet begun to use its fruit? Let him go home. Otherwise he may die in the battle and another man will have the use of it.
Is there a man who has betrothed a woman and has not yet taken her? Let him go home. Otherwise he may die in the battle and another man will take her.
The officers speak to the people again: 'Is there a man who is afraid, soft of heart? Let him go home, so he does not melt his brothers' hearts the way his own is melted.'
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, commanders of the forces are appointed at the head of the people.
When you approach a city to fight against it, call out to it an offer of peace.
If it answers you with peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it become forced labour for you and serve you.
But if it will not make peace with you and makes war against you, then you besiege it.
And the LORD your God will give it into your hand, and you are to put every male in it to the sword.

Only the women, the little ones, the livestock and everything else in the city—all its spoil—you plunder for yourself, and you consume the spoil of your enemies, which the LORD your God has given you.
This is what you do to all the cities far away from you, the ones that do not belong to these nations.
But in the cities of these peoples, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you are not to let anything that breathes remain alive.
You are to devote them completely to destruction—the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite—as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they do not teach you to do all the abominations they have done for their gods, and so make you sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by taking an axe to them. You may eat from them, but do not cut them down—is the tree of the field a man, that it should come under siege from you?
Only a tree you know is not a food tree may you destroy and cut down, and use to build siege works against the city that is making war against you, until it falls.

deuteronomy_21.t: If someone is found slain in the land the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of it, lying out in the open country, and no one knows who struck him,
then your elders and your judges go out and measure the distance to the cities around the slain one.
And the city nearest to the slain one—its elders take a heifer from the herd that has never been worked and never pulled in a yoke,
and the elders of that city bring the heifer down to an ever-flowing wadi that is not tilled or sown, and there in the wadi they break the heifer's neck.
Then the priests, the sons of Levi, come forward—the LORD your God chose them to serve him and to bless in his name, and every dispute and every case of affliction is settled by their word.
And all the elders of that city, the ones nearest to the slain one, wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi,
and they declare: 'Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you ransomed, LORD, and do not lay innocent blood on your people Israel.' And the blood will be atoned for them.
That is how you purge the innocent blood from among you—by doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God gives them into your hand and you take captives,
and among the captives you see a woman beautiful in form, and you desire her, and you take her for yourself as a wife,
then you bring her into your house, and she shaves her head and trims her nails,

and she takes off the clothing of her captivity, lives in your house, and weeps for her father and her mother for a full month. After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she becomes your wife.
And if you take no delight in her, let her go where she wishes. You must not sell her for money, and you must not treat her as a slave, because you have violated her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both bear him sons—the loved one and the hated one—and the firstborn son is the hated wife's,
then on the day he divides his inheritance among his sons, he may not treat the loved wife's son as firstborn ahead of the hated wife's son, who is the firstborn.
Instead he acknowledges the firstborn, the hated wife's son, by giving him a double portion of everything he owns. He is the first of his strength, and the right of the birthright is his.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not listen to his father's voice or his mother's voice, and they discipline him and he still will not listen,
then his father and his mother seize him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his town,
and they say to the elders of his city: 'This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not listen to us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.'
Then all the men of his city stone him with stones, and he dies. That is how you purge the evil from among you—and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
And if a man has committed a sin that carries a sentence of death, and he is put to death and you hang him on a tree,
his corpse must not stay overnight on the tree. Bury him that same day, for a hanged man is a curse of God—and do not defile your land, which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

deuteronomy_22.t: If you see your brother's ox or his sheep straying, do not look the other way. Take them back to your brother.
And if your brother does not live nearby, or you do not know who he is, bring it into your house and keep it with you until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him.
Do the same for his donkey, the same for his garment, the same for anything your brother loses and you find. You may not ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or his ox collapsed on the road, do not look the other way. Help him get it up.
A woman is not to wear a man's gear, and a man is not to put on a woman's garment. Everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God.
If you come upon a bird's nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs in it and the mother sitting on them, do not take the mother along with the young.
Let the mother go; the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you live long.
When you build a new house, put a parapet round the roof, so you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if anyone falls from it.
Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield becomes forfeit as holy—both what you sow and what the vineyard produces.
Do not plough with an ox and a donkey together.
Do not wear mixed fabric—wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels for yourself on the four corners of the covering you wrap yourself in.
If a man takes a wife, goes in to her, and then hates her,
and brings charges against her and spreads a bad name about her, saying, 'I took this woman, and when I came near to her I did not find the tokens of virginity in her,'
then the young woman's father and her mother take the tokens of the young woman's virginity and bring them out to the elders of the city at the gate.
And the young woman's father says to the elders: 'I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, and he hated her.

And now he has brought charges, saying, "I did not find the tokens of virginity in your daughter." But here are the tokens of my daughter's virginity.' And they spread the garment out before the elders of the city.
And the elders of that city take the man and punish him.

They fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give it to the young woman's father, because he spread a bad name about a virgin of Israel. She stays his wife, and he may not send her away as long as he lives.
But if the charge was true, and the tokens of virginity were not found for the young woman,

then they bring the young woman out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her city stone her with stones, and she dies—because she has done an outrage in Israel by acting the prostitute in her father's house. That is how you purge the evil from among you.
If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, both of them die—the man who lay with her, and the woman. That is how you purge the evil from Israel.
If there is a young woman, a virgin betrothed to a man, and another man finds her in the city and lies with her,

then you bring both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them with stones, and they die—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbour's wife. That is how you purge the evil from among you.
But if the man finds the betrothed young woman out in the open country, and he seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her dies.
To the young woman you do nothing; she has committed no sin deserving death. This case is like a man rising against his neighbour and murdering him.
He found her out in the open country. The betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
then the man who lay with her gives the young woman's father fifty pieces of silver, and she becomes his wife, because he violated her. He may not send her away as long as he lives.
A man is not to take his father's wife, and he is not to uncover his father's skirt.

deuteronomy_23.t: No man whose testicles are crushed or whose penis is cut off is to enter the assembly of the LORD.
One of illegitimate birth is not to enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation, none of his descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite is to enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, ever.
because they did not come out to meet you with food and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because he hired Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Aram-naharaim, to curse you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. The LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.
Do not seek their welfare or their good, all your days, ever.
Do not abhor an Edomite—he is your brother. Do not abhor an Egyptian—you were a sojourner in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you go out as a camp against your enemies, keep yourself from every evil thing.
If there is a man among you who is not clean because of a nocturnal emission, he goes outside the camp and does not come inside it.
Toward evening he washes with water, and when the sun goes down he comes back inside the camp.
You are to have a place outside the camp, and you go out there.
Keep a peg with your equipment, and when you sit down outside, dig with it, then turn back and cover your excrement.

The LORD your God walks about in the middle of your camp, to deliver you and to hand your enemies over to you. So your camp is to be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from following you.
Do not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped to you from his master.
He lives with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses in one of your towns, wherever suits him. Do not maltreat him.
There is to be no cult prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and none among the sons of Israel.
Do not bring the fee of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow. Both of them are an abomination to the LORD your God.
Do not charge your brother interest—interest on money, interest on food, interest on anything lent at interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother—so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you set your hand to, in the land you are entering to take possession of it.
When you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not delay in paying it. The LORD your God will certainly require it of you, and you will incur sin.
But if you refrain from vowing, you incur no sin.
Keep and do what your lips have said, just as you vowed to the LORD your God as a freewill offering, which you spoke with your own mouth.
When you go into your neighbour's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, until you have had your fill—but do not put any into your basket.
When you go into your neighbour's standing grain, you may pluck the ears with your hand—but do not put a sickle to your neighbour's standing grain.

deuteronomy_24.t: When a man takes a wife and marries her, and then she does not find favour in his eyes because he has found something indecent in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her away from his house,
and she leaves his house, goes, and becomes another man's wife,
and the second man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her away from his house; or if the second man who took her as his wife dies—

then her first husband, the one who sent her away, may not take her back as his wife after she has been made unclean. That is an abomination before the LORD, and you must not bring sin upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he does not go out with the army, and no obligation is laid on him for anything. He is free at home for one year, to gladden the wife he has taken.
No one is to take a hand-mill or an upper millstone in pledge—that is taking a life in pledge.
If a man is found stealing a person from among his brothers, the people of Israel, and treats him as a slave and sells him, that thief dies. That is how you purge the evil from among you.
Take care in a case of the skin disease leprosy: be very careful, and do everything the priests, the Levites, instruct you. Be careful to do just as I commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.
When you make your neighbour a loan of any kind, do not go into his house to take his pledge.
Stand outside, and the man you are lending to brings the pledge out to you.
And if he is a poor man, do not sleep in his pledge.
Give the pledge back to him at sunset, so that he can sleep in his garment and bless you. It will count as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
Do not oppress a hired labourer who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the sojourners in your land, in your towns.
Pay him his wages the same day, before the sun goes down on them. He is poor, and he sets his life on them. Otherwise he will call out against you to the LORD, and you will incur sin.
Fathers are not to be put to death for their sons, and sons are not to be put to death for their fathers. Each is put to death for his own sin.
Do not pervert the justice due to a sojourner or a fatherless one, and do not take a widow's garment in pledge.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I am commanding you to do this.

When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf out there, do not go back for it. It belongs to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive tree, do not go back over the boughs. What is left belongs to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not go back over it for what is left. What remains belongs to the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I am commanding you to do this.

deuteronomy_25.t: If there is a dispute between men and they come to court and are tried, the judges acquit the one in the right and condemn the one in the wrong.
And if the guilty one deserves a beating, the judge has him lie down and be beaten in his presence, the number of strokes matching his offence.
Forty strokes he may give him, no more. If he goes further and gives him a heavy beating on top of that, your brother is degraded before your eyes.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

If brothers live together and one of them dies leaving no son, the dead man's wife is not to marry outside the family, to a stranger. Her husband's brother goes in to her, takes her as his wife, and does the duty of a husband's brother for her.
And the firstborn she bears carries on the name of the dead brother, so that his name is not wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to take his brother's widow, she goes up to the gate, to the elders, and says: 'My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel. He is not willing to do the duty of a husband's brother for me.'
Then the elders of his city summon him and speak to him. And if he stands his ground and says, 'I do not want to take her,'

then his brother's widow comes up to him in front of the elders, pulls his sandal off his foot and spits in his face, and declares: 'This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's house.'
And his household is called in Israel 'The house of the one whose sandal was pulled off.'
If men are fighting, a man and his brother, and one man's wife comes near to rescue her husband from the man striking him, and reaches out her hand and seizes his genitals,
then you cut off her hand. Your eye is not to pity her.
Do not keep two kinds of weight in your bag, a heavy one and a light one.
Do not keep two kinds of measure in your house, a large one and a small one.
Keep a full and honest weight and a full and honest measure, so that your days may be long on the land the LORD your God is giving you.
Everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God—everyone who acts unjustly.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way and cut off your rear—all the stragglers behind you—when you were exhausted and weary. He did not fear God.

And when the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land he is giving you as an inheritance to take possession of it, you are to wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens. Do not forget.

deuteronomy_26.t: When you come into the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and settle in it,

then take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land, which the LORD your God is giving you, put it in a basket, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses to make his name dwell there.
Come to the priest who is in office at the time and say to him: 'I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.'
The priest takes the basket from your hand and sets it down before the altar of the LORD your God.
And you declare before the LORD your God: 'A wandering Aramean was my father. He went down to Egypt and sojourned there, few in number, and there he became a nation great, mighty and numerous.
The Egyptians did us harm, afflicted us and laid hard labour on us.
We cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil and our oppression.
And the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you have given me, LORD.' Then set it down before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.
And you rejoice in all the good the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite and the sojourner among you.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, give it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, and they will eat in your towns and be satisfied.

And you say before the LORD your God: 'I have cleared the holy portion out of my house and given it to the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, according to everything you commanded me. I have not transgressed any of your commandments and I have not forgotten them.

I have not eaten any of it while in mourning, I have not cleared any of it out while unclean, and I have not given any of it to the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God; I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.'
Today the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and ordinances. Keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared the LORD to be your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commandments and his ordinances, and listen to his voice.
And today the LORD has declared you to be his own treasured people, as he said to you, and that you will keep all his commandments,
and to set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise and fame and honour, and that you should be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he has spoken.

deuteronomy_27.t: Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: 'Keep the whole commandment I am commanding you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up large stones for yourself and coat them with lime.

Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over, so that you may come into the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD the God of your fathers has spoken to you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones, as I am commanding you today, on Mount Ebal, and coat them with lime.
And build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use an iron tool on them.
Build the altar of the LORD your God of whole stones, and offer up burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
Sacrifice peace offerings, eat there, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
And write all the words of this law on the stones, making them very plain.
Then Moses and the priests, the Levites, spoke to all Israel: 'Be silent and hear, Israel! Today you have become a people belonging to the LORD your God.
Obey the voice of the LORD your God and do his commandments and his statutes, which I am commanding you today.'
And that day Moses commanded the people:
'These stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.
And these stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
And the Levites declare to every man of Israel in a loud voice:
'Cursed be the man who makes a carved image or a cast image, an abomination to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' And all the people answer, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who dishonours his father and his mother.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who moves back his neighbour's boundary marker.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who leads a blind man astray on the road.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who perverts the justice due to a sojourner, a fatherless one or a widow.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with any animal.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his sister, whether his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who lies with his mother-in-law.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who strikes down his neighbour in secret.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who takes a bribe to strike down a person, shedding innocent blood.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed be the one who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people say, 'Amen.'

deuteronomy_28.t: And if you truly obey the voice of the LORD your God, taking care to do all his commandments that I am commanding you today, then the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of the LORD your God.
Blessed you will be in the city, and blessed you will be in the open country.
Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Blessed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
Blessed you will be when you come in, and blessed you will be when you go out.
The LORD will make your enemies who rise against you be defeated before you. By one road they will come out against you, and by seven roads they will flee before you.
The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in everything you set your hand to, and he will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will establish you for himself as a holy people, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
And all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.
And the LORD will make you abound in good things—the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground—on the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.

The LORD will open his good storehouse for you, the heavens, to give your land its rain at the right time and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, and you will not borrow.

And the LORD will make you the head and not the tail. You will be only on top and never underneath, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you today, keeping them and doing them.
and if you do not turn aside from any of the words I am commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.

But if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, taking care to do all his commandments and his statutes that I am commanding you today, then all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
Cursed you will be in the city, and cursed you will be in the open country.
Cursed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
Cursed will be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Cursed you will be when you come in, and cursed you will be when you go out.
The LORD will send upon you the curse, the panic and the rebuke, in everything you set your hand to, until you are destroyed and perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, in forsaking me.
The LORD will make the pestilence cling to you until he has made an end of you, off the land you are entering to take possession of it.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation and burning heat, and with the sword, with blight and with mildew. They will pursue you until you perish.
The heavens over your head will be bronze, and the ground under you iron.
The LORD will turn your land's rain into dust and powder. It will come down on you from the heavens until you are destroyed.

The LORD will make you be defeated before your enemies. By one road you will go out against them, and by seven roads you will flee before them. You will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpse will become food for every bird of the heavens and for the animals of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them off.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumours, with scab and with itch, and you will not be able to be healed.
The LORD will strike you with madness, with blindness and with bewilderment of heart.
You will grope about at noon the way a blind man gropes in the dark, and nothing you do will succeed. You will be nothing but oppressed and robbed, all your days, with no one to save you.
You will betroth a woman, and another man will lie with her. You will build a house and not live in it. You will plant a vineyard and never begin to use its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be seized in front of you and never returned. Your flock will be given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all day long, and there will be nothing your hand can do.
A people you have never known will eat the fruit of your ground and everything you have worked for, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed, all your days.
And you will be driven mad by the sight of what your eyes see.
The LORD will strike you with malignant boils on the knees and the legs, and you will not be able to be healed—from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
The LORD will lead you, and the king you set over yourself, to a nation you have not known, neither you nor your fathers, and there you will serve other gods—wood and stone.
And you will become an object of horror, a byword and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
You will carry much seed out to the field and gather little in, for the locust will consume it.
You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will not drink the wine or gather it in, for the worm will eat it.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
All your trees and the fruit of your ground the whirring locust will take possession of.
The sojourner among you will rise above you higher and higher, and you will go down lower and lower.
He will lend to you, and you will not lend to him. He will become the head, and you will become the tail.
