If you lend silver to my people — to the poor among you — do not act as a creditor toward him. Do not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's cloak as a pledge, give it back before the sun goes down,
It is his only covering, the cloak against his skin. What else would he sleep in? And when he cries out to me, I will hear — I am gracious.
Do not revile God, and do not curse a leader among your people.
Do not hold back the fullness of your harvest or the outflow of your press. Give me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your oxen and your sheep. Seven days it stays with its mother; on the eighth day you give it to me.
You are to be people set apart as holy to me. Do not eat flesh torn in the field — throw it to the dogs.

exodus_23.t: Do not spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a malicious witness.
Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing. Do not testify in a lawsuit just to side with the many and pervert justice.
Do not show partiality to a poor man in his lawsuit.
When you come across your enemy's ox or his donkey wandering off, take it back to him.
When you see the donkey of someone who hates you down under its load, and you would rather not help — you are to help him with it.
Do not deny justice to your needy in his lawsuit.
Keep well clear of a false charge. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous — I will not acquit the guilty.
Do not take a bribe. A bribe blinds those who see clearly and twists the words of the righteous.
Do not oppress a sojourner. You know a sojourner's life yourselves — you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
For six years, sow your land and gather in its produce.
In the seventh year, let it rest and leave it fallow, so the needy of your people can eat, and whatever they leave, the wild animals eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
Six days do your work. On the seventh, stop — so your ox and your donkey can rest, and your female slave's son and the sojourner can catch their breath.
Be watchful in everything I have said to you. Do not invoke the name of other gods; do not let it be heard from your mouth.
Three times a year, hold a festival to me.

Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread: for seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib — that is when you came out of Egypt. And no one is to appear before me empty-handed.
And the Festival of Harvest, the firstfruits of the work you sow in the field. And the Festival of Ingathering at the close of the year, when you gather your work in from the field.
Three times a year every male among you is to appear before the Lord GOD.
Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice along with anything leavened, and do not let the fat of my festival offering sit overnight until morning.
Bring the choicest of the firstfruits of your ground to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you to the place I have prepared.
Be watchful before him and listen to his voice. Do not defy him — he will not pardon your transgression, because my name is within him.
But if you really listen to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to those who oppose you.
My angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites — and I will annihilate them.
Do not bow down to their gods or be drawn into serving them, and do not do what they do. Tear them down completely and shatter their pillars.
Serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from among you.
No one in your land will miscarry or be barren. I will fill out the number of your days.
I will send my terror ahead of you, throw every people you come among into confusion, and make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
I will send hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from before you.
I will not drive them out in a single year, or the land would go to waste and the wild animals would multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have become fruitful and taken possession of the land.

I will fix your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River. I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you will drive them out from before you.
Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They are not to live in your land, or they will make you sin against me. You would serve their gods, and it would become a snare to you.

exodus_24.t: To Moses he said, "Come up to the LORD — you, Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel — and bow down at a distance."
Moses alone is to draw near to the LORD. The others are not to draw near, and the people are not to come up with him.
Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the rulings. All the people answered with one voice: "Everything the LORD has spoken, we will do."
Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early in the morning he got up and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent the young men of the sons of Israel, and they offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half the blood and put it in bowls, and dashed the other half against the altar.
He took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, "Everything the LORD has spoken, we will do — and we will obey."
Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, "This is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words."
Then Moses went up, with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
And they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.
He did not stretch out his hand against the nobles of the sons of Israel. They beheld God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the stone tablets, with the law and the commandment I have written, to teach them."
So Moses got up, with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
To the elders he said, "Stay here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you — whoever has a dispute can go to them."
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day he called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the sons of Israel watching, the glory of the LORD looked like a consuming fire on the mountaintop.
Moses went into the cloud and up the mountain. He was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

exodus_25.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Tell the sons of Israel to take up a contribution for me. Take my contribution from everyone whose heart moves him.
This is the contribution you are to take from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
violet, purple, and scarlet; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and the breastpiece.
They are to make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.
Make it according to all that I show you: the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its articles.
They are to make an ark of acacia wood: two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold moulding around it.
Cast four gold rings for it and put them on its four feet — two rings on one side and two on the other.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.
The poles are to stay in the rings of the ark; they are not to be removed.
Put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
Make a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Make two cherubim of gold, of hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat.
Make one cherub at one end and one at the other; make the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim are to spread their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with them, their faces toward one another — the faces of the cherubim turned toward the mercy seat.
Put the mercy seat on top of the ark, and put the testimony that I will give you into the ark.
There I will meet with you and speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim over the ark of the testimony — everything I command you for the sons of Israel.
Make a table of acacia wood: two cubits long, a cubit wide, a cubit and a half high.
Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold moulding around it.
Make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a gold moulding for the rim all around.
Make four gold rings for it and put them at the four corners, at its four legs.
The rings are to sit close to the rim, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and the table is carried by them.
Make its dishes and pans, and its jars and bowls for pouring out; make them all of pure gold.
Keep the bread of the Presence on the table before me continually.
Make a lampstand of pure gold, of hammered work — its base and shaft, its cups, bulbs, and blossoms all of one piece with it.
Six branches are to go out from its sides — three from one side and three from the other.
Three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the one branch, with bulb and blossom; three on the next branch, with bulb and blossom — so for all six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its bulbs and blossoms.
A bulb under the first pair of branches, a bulb under the second pair, and a bulb under the third — for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
Their bulbs and branches are to be of one piece with it — the whole thing one hammered work of pure gold.
Make its seven lamps and set them up so they light the space in front of it.
Its tongs and firepans are to be of pure gold.
It is to be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these articles.
See that you make them by the pattern you are being shown on the mountain.

exodus_26.t: Make the tabernacle of ten curtains of fine twisted linen with violet, purple, and scarlet, and have a designer work cherubim into them.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide, all of one measure.
Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another.
Make loops of violet on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and the same on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty at the end of the curtain in the second set, the loops opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with them, so the tabernacle becomes one whole.
Make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle — eleven of them.
Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide, the eleven of them all one measure.
Join five of the curtains together by themselves and six by themselves, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the one set, and fifty on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps, put them into the loops, and join the tent so it becomes one whole.
As for the surplus overhanging in the tent curtains, the half curtain left over is to hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The extra cubit on each side, left over in the length of the tent curtains, is to hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather over that.
Make the frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame is to have two tenons, joined to one another; the same for all the frames of the tabernacle.
Make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side.
Make forty silver bases under the twenty frames — two bases under each frame, for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases — two under each frame.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, make six frames.
Make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They are to be paired at the bottom and joined complete at the top into a single ring — the same for both, at the two corners.
So there are to be eight frames with their silver bases — sixteen bases, two under each frame.
Make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the frames of the second side, and five for the frames at the rear, on the west.
The middle bar, halfway up the frames, is to run through from end to end.
Overlay the frames with gold, make their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlay the bars with gold.
Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you have been shown on the mountain.
Make a veil of violet, purple, and scarlet, and of fine twisted linen — the work of a designer, with cherubim.
Hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold, with gold hooks, on four silver bases.
Hang the veil under the clasps and bring the ark of the testimony inside it. The veil separates the holy place from the holy of holies.
Put the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.
Set the table outside the veil, with the lampstand opposite it on the south side of the tabernacle, and the table on the north side.
Make a screen for the entrance of the tent, of violet, purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen — the work of an embroiderer.
Make five pillars of acacia for the screen, overlay them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.

exodus_27.t: Make the altar of acacia wood: five cubits long, five wide — the altar is to be square — and three cubits high.
Make its horns on its four corners, of one piece with it, and overlay it with bronze.
Make its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, basins, forks, and firepans — all its articles of bronze.
Make a grating for it, a bronze network, with four bronze rings at its four ends.
Put it under the ledge of the altar, below, so the network reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
Its poles are put into the rings, and the poles are on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make it hollow, of boards. As he showed you on the mountain, so they are to do.
Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side, hangings for the courtyard of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long.
Its pillars are twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze, with the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
The same along the north side: hangings a hundred cubits long, twenty pillars and twenty bronze bases, with the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
Across the width of the courtyard on the west side, hangings of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
Across the width of the courtyard on the east side, fifty cubits.
Fifteen cubits of hangings on the one side, with three pillars and three bases.
And on the second side, fifteen cubits of hangings, with three pillars and three bases.
For the gate of the courtyard, a screen of twenty cubits, of violet, purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen — the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars around the courtyard are to be banded with silver, their hooks of silver and their bases of bronze.
The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long, fifty wide, and five cubits high, of fine twisted linen, with bronze bases.
All the articles of the tabernacle for all its service, and all its tent pegs and the courtyard's tent pegs, are to be of bronze.
You yourself are to command the sons of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that stands before the testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend it from evening until morning before the LORD. This is a perpetual statute for their generations, on behalf of the sons of Israel.

exodus_28.t: Bring your brother Aaron to you, and his sons with him, out of the Israelites, to serve me as priest — Aaron, and Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and for beauty.
Speak to everyone who's skilled, the ones I've filled with a spirit of skill, and they'll make Aaron's garments to consecrate him, so he can serve me as priest.

Here are the garments they're to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a checkered tunic, a turban and a sash. They're to make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so he can serve me as priest.
They're to take the gold, the violet, the purple, the scarlet and the fine linen.
They're to make the ephod of gold, violet, purple, scarlet and fine twisted linen — the work of a designer.
It's to have two shoulder-pieces joined to it at its two ends, so it's held together.
The band of the ephod, the one on it, is to be made the same way and of one piece with it: gold, violet, purple, scarlet and fine twisted linen.
Take two onyx stones and engrave the names of Israel's sons on them:
six of the names on one stone and the other six on the second stone, in the order they were born.
Engrave the two stones with the names of Israel's sons the way a craftsman in stone does it, like the engraving on a seal, and set them in gold settings.
Put the two stones on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the Israelites. Aaron will carry their names before the LORD on his two shoulders, for remembrance.
Make gold settings,
and two chains of pure gold made like cords, braided work, and attach the braided chains to the settings.
Make a breastpiece of judgement, the work of a designer — make it like the ephod: gold, violet, purple, scarlet and fine twisted linen.
It's to be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide.
Set stones in it, four rows of them. First row: ruby, topaz, emerald.
Second row: turquoise, sapphire, diamond.
Third row: jacinth, agate, amethyst.
Fourth row: beryl, onyx, jasper. They're to be set in gold in their settings.
The stones are to match the names of Israel's sons, twelve of them, each engraved like a seal with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
Make braided chains of twisted work on the breastpiece, out of pure gold.
Make two gold rings for the breastpiece and put them on its two ends.
Put the two gold braids through the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
Attach the two ends of the two braids to the two settings, and attach those to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod at the front.
Make two more gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on the inner edge facing the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and put them low on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, at the front, close to the seam, just above the band.
They're to tie the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a violet cord, so it sits on the band of the ephod and doesn't come loose from it.
Aaron will carry the names of Israel's sons on the breastpiece of judgement over his heart whenever he goes into the holy place — a continual remembrance before the LORD.

Put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgement, and they'll be over Aaron's heart when he comes before the LORD. So Aaron will carry the judgement of the Israelites over his heart before the LORD, continually.
Make the robe of the ephod entirely of violet.
The head opening goes in the middle, with a woven edge all around it, like the opening of a corselet, so it won't tear.
On its hem make pomegranates of violet, purple and scarlet, all the way around, with gold bells between them:
a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all the way around the hem of the robe.
Aaron is to wear it when he serves, and the sound of it will be heard when he goes into the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out — so he won't die.
Make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like a seal: Holy to the LORD.
Fasten it with a violet cord so it sits on the turban, on the front of it.

It's to be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron will carry the iniquity attaching to the holy things the Israelites consecrate, for all their holy gifts. It's to stay on his forehead, so they'll be accepted before the LORD.
Weave the tunic of fine linen in checker-work, make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash — the work of an embroiderer.
For Aaron's sons make tunics, and make them sashes, and make them headdresses, for glory and for beauty.
Dress your brother Aaron and his sons in them, anoint them, ordain them, consecrate them, and they'll serve me as priests.
Make them linen undergarments to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the hips to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons are to wear them when they go into the tent of meeting or come near the altar to serve in the holy place, so they don't incur iniquity and die. This is a perpetual statute for him and his descendants after him.

exodus_29.t: Here's what you're to do to consecrate them so they can serve me as priests: take one young bull and two rams without blemish;
and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil — make them out of fine wheat flour.
Put them in one basket and bring them near in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Take the garments and put them on Aaron — the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod and the breastpiece — and gird him with the band of the ephod.
Put the turban on his head, and the holy crown on the turban.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head and anoint him.
Bring his sons near and put tunics on them.
Gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, tie headdresses on them, and the priesthood will be theirs as a perpetual statute. So you'll ordain Aaron and his sons.
Bring the bull near, in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the bull before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, then pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and burn them as smoke on the altar.
But the bull's flesh, its hide and its offal you're to burn with fire outside the camp. It's a sin offering.
Take the first ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
Slaughter the ram, take its blood and throw it against the altar all around.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and put them with the pieces and the head.
Burn the whole ram as smoke on the altar. It's a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing smell, a food offering to the LORD.
Take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.

Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's ear, on the lobes of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet; then throw the blood against the altar all around.

Take some of the blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil and spatter it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments with him. Then he'll be holy — he and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.
From the ram take the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh — because it's a ram of ordination.
And one round loaf, one oil-bread cake and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that's before the LORD.
Put all of it on Aaron's palms and on his sons' palms, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then take them from their hands and burn them as smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering, as a soothing smell before the LORD. It's a food offering to the LORD.
Take the breast of Aaron's ordination ram and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD, and it will be your portion.
Consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution — the parts that were waved and raised — from the ordination ram, from what belongs to Aaron and to his sons.

It's to belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites, because it's a contribution — a contribution from the Israelites out of their peace offerings, their contribution to the LORD.
Aaron's holy garments will pass to his sons after him, for them to be anointed in and ordained in.
The priest who takes his place from among his sons is to wear them seven days when he comes into the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place.
Take the ordination ram and boil its flesh in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram's flesh and the bread in the basket at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They're to eat the things by which atonement was made, to ordain them and consecrate them. No outsider is to eat them, because they're holy.
If any of the ordination meat or the bread is left until morning, burn what's left with fire. It's not to be eaten, because it's holy.
Do all this for Aaron and his sons, exactly as I've commanded you. Seven days you're to ordain them.
Each day offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement, purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it, and the altar will be most holy. Whatever touches the altar becomes holy.
Here's what you're to offer on the altar: two year-old lambs every day, continually.
Offer the one lamb in the morning and the second at twilight.
With the one lamb, a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning — a soothing smell, a food offering to the LORD.
This is to be a continual burnt offering down your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I'll meet with you and speak to you.
There I'll meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.
I'll consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar, and I'll consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I'll live among the Israelites, and I'll be their God.
And they'll know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so I could live among them. I am the LORD their God.

exodus_30.t: Make an altar for burning incense — make it out of acacia wood.
It's to be a cubit long, a cubit wide — square — and two cubits high, with its horns of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold — the top, the sides all around and the horns — and make a gold moulding around it.
Make two gold rings for it below the moulding, on its two sides — on its two flanks — as holders for the poles it's carried by.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put it in front of the veil that's over the ark of the testimony, in front of the mercy seat that's over the testimony, where I'll meet with you.
Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it as smoke every morning when he tends the lamps.
And when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight he's to burn it — a continual incense before the LORD, down your generations.
Don't offer any strange incense on it, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering, and don't pour out a drink offering on it.
Once a year Aaron is to make atonement on its horns, using the blood of the sin offering of atonement — once a year, down your generations. It's most holy to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
When you take a census of the Israelites, each of them is to give a ransom for his life to the LORD as he's enrolled, so no plague breaks out among them when they're counted.
This is what everyone who crosses over to be enrolled is to give: half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel — a shekel is twenty gerahs — half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
Everyone who crosses over to be enrolled, from twenty years old and up, is to give the LORD's contribution.
The rich aren't to give more and the poor aren't to give less than half a shekel, when you give the LORD's contribution to make atonement for your lives.
Take the atonement money from the Israelites and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a remembrance for the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.
The LORD said to Moses:
Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand for washing, put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet from it.
When they come into the tent of meeting they're to wash with water, so they won't die; the same when they come near the altar to serve, to burn a food offering to the LORD as smoke —
they're to wash their hands and feet so they won't die. This is a perpetual decree for them, for him and his descendants down their generations.
The LORD said to Moses:
Take the finest spices: five hundred of flowing myrrh, half that of fragrant cinnamon — two hundred and fifty — and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane;
and five hundred of cassia by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
Make it into a holy anointing oil, a compounded perfume, the work of a perfumer. It's to be a holy anointing oil.
With it anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its articles, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, and the washbasin with its stand.
Consecrate them, and they'll be most holy. Whatever touches them becomes holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them, to serve me as priests.
Tell the Israelites: This is to be a holy anointing oil to me, down your generations.
It's not to be poured on anyone's body, and you're not to make anything like it in the same proportions. It's holy, and it's to be holy to you.
Anyone who mixes anything like it, or puts any of it on an outsider, is to be cut off from his kin.
The LORD said to Moses: Take spices — stacte, onycha and galbanum — spices with pure frankincense, an equal part of each.
Make it into an incense, a compound, the work of a perfumer — salted, pure, holy.
Grind some of it very fine and put some of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I'll meet with you. It's to be most holy to you.
As for the incense you make, don't make any for yourselves in the same proportions. It's to be holy to you, belonging to the LORD.
Anyone who makes anything like it to smell it is to be cut off from his kin.

exodus_31.t: Look — I've called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
And I've filled him with the Spirit of God — with skill, understanding and knowledge in every kind of work,
to devise designs, to work in gold, silver and bronze,
in cutting stones for setting and carving wood — every kind of work.
And I've appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, to work with him; and I've put skill in the heart of everyone who's skilled, so they can make everything I've commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark for the testimony, the mercy seat on it, all the articles of the tent,
the table and its articles, the pure lampstand and all its articles, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its articles, the washbasin and its stand,
the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons' garments for serving as priests,
the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the holy place. They're to do everything just as I've commanded you.
Tell the Israelites: Above all, keep my sabbaths. It's a sign between me and you down your generations, so you'll know that I am the LORD who consecrates you.
Keep the sabbath, because it's holy to you. Anyone who profanes it is to be put to death; anyone who does work on it is to be cut off from his kin.
Six days work is to be done, but the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who does work on the sabbath day is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to keep the sabbath, observing it down their generations as a perpetual covenant.
It's a sign forever between me and the Israelites, because in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he stopped and took a breath.
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony — stone tablets, written by the finger of God.

exodus_32.t: When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered against Aaron and said, "Get up and make us gods to go ahead of us. This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt — we don't know what's become of him."
Aaron said to them, "Tear off the gold rings in your wives' ears, and your sons' and your daughters', and bring them to me."
So all the people tore the gold rings out of their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took it from their hands, worked it with a graving tool and made it into a cast-metal calf. And they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this he built an altar in front of it, and he called out, "Tomorrow there's a festival to the LORD."
The next day they got up early, offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings, and the people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to play.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go on down. Your people, the ones you brought up from the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.

They've turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them. They've made themselves a cast-metal calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
The LORD said to Moses, "I've seen this people, and they're a stiff-necked people.
Now leave me alone, so my anger can burn against them and I can make an end of them — and I'll make you into a great nation."
But Moses entreated the face of the LORD his God: "Why, LORD, does your anger burn against your people, the ones you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?

Why should the Egyptians be able to say, 'He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn from your burning anger and relent about the harm to your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants — the ones you swore to by yourself when you said, 'I'll multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land I've spoken of I'll give to your offspring, and they'll possess it forever.'"
And the LORD relented about the harm he'd said he would do to his people.
Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand — tablets written on both sides, on the one side and on the other.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the people shouting, he said to Moses, "That's the sound of war in the camp."
But Moses said, "It's not the sound of singing for victory, and it's not the sound of singing for defeat. What I hear is the sound of singing."
As he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger burned. He threw the tablets out of his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they'd made, burned it with fire, ground it down to powder, scattered it on the water and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you brought such a great sin on them?"
Aaron said, "Don't let my lord's anger burn. You know this people yourself — they're set on evil.
"They said to me, 'Make us gods to go ahead of us. This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt — we don't know what's become of him.'
"So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, tear it off.' They gave it to me, I threw it in the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were running wild — Aaron had let them run wild, so that their enemies could jeer at them.
Then Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Who's for the LORD? To me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Each of you put your sword on your thigh. Go back and forth from gate to gate through the camp, and kill — your brother, your companion, your kin."
The sons of Levi did what Moses said, and about three thousand of the people fell that day.
And Moses said, "Today you've filled your hand for the LORD — each of you against his own son and his own brother — and so to bring a blessing on yourselves today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin. Now I'm going up to the LORD — maybe I can make atonement for your sin."
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Ah, this people has sinned a great sin — they've made themselves gods of gold.
"And now — if you'll forgive their sin—; and if not, then wipe me out of your book, the one you've written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me — that's who I'll wipe out of my book.
"Now go — lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go ahead of you. But on the day I visit, I'll visit their sin on them."
And the LORD struck the people because they had made the calf — the one Aaron made.

exodus_33.t: The LORD said to Moses, "Go up from here, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob when I said, 'I'll give it to your offspring.'
I'll send an angel ahead of you, and I'll drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites,
a land flowing with milk and honey. But I won't go up among you, because you're a stiff-necked people — I might make an end of you on the way."
When the people heard this bad news they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

The LORD had said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites: You're a stiff-necked people. If I went up among you for one moment I'd make an end of you. Now take your ornaments off, and I'll decide what to do with you."
So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.

Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, well away from it, and he called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who was seeking the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would get up and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watch him until he'd gone inside.
Whenever Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance, and he would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they'd all get up and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
And the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, the way a man speaks to his companion. Then Moses would go back to the camp, but his servant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, wouldn't leave the tent.

Moses said to the LORD, "Look, you tell me, 'Bring up this people,' and you haven't let me know who you'll send with me. And yet you've said, 'I know you by name, and you've also found favour in my eyes.'
Now, if I've found favour in your eyes, please show me your ways, so I can know you and find favour in your eyes. And consider: this nation is your people."
And he said, "My presence will go, and I'll give you rest."
And Moses said to him, "If your presence isn't going, don't bring us up from here.
How else will anyone know that I've found favour in your eyes, I and your people, unless you go with us? That's what will set us apart, I and your people, from every people on the face of the earth."
The LORD said to Moses, "I'll do this thing you've asked too, because you've found favour in my eyes and I know you by name."
And Moses said, "Please — show me your glory."

And he said, "I'll make all my goodness pass in front of you, and I'll proclaim the name of the LORD before you. I'll be gracious to whom I'll be gracious, and I'll have compassion on whom I'll have compassion.
And he said, "You can't see my face, because no human being can see me and live."
And the LORD said, "There's a place beside me — you're to stand on the rock.
And when my glory passes by, I'll put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with my palm until I've gone past.
Then I'll take my palm away and you'll see my back; but my face won't be seen.

exodus_34.t: The LORD said to Moses, "Cut yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and I'll write on them the words that were on the first tablets, the ones you shattered.
Be ready by morning. In the morning come up Mount Sinai and station yourself for me there on the top of the mountain.
No one is to come up with you, and no one is to be seen anywhere on the mountain — and the flocks and herds aren't to graze in front of it either.
So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones, got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hand.
The LORD came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
The LORD passed by in front of him and proclaimed: "The LORD, the LORD — a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,

keeping steadfast love for thousands, bearing iniquity and transgression and sin — and yet by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of fathers on sons and on sons' sons, to the third and fourth generation."
Moses quickly bowed low to the ground and bowed down.
And he said, "If I've found favour in your eyes, my Lord, then let my Lord go with us — yes, they're a stiff-necked people — and forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as your possession."

And he said, "I'm making a covenant. In front of all your people I'll do wonders that have never been created in all the earth or among any of the nations, and all the people you live among will see the work of the LORD — because what I'm about to do with you is fearful.
Keep what I'm commanding you today. I'm about to drive out ahead of you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you're going into, or it will become a snare among you.
Instead, pull down their altars, break their pillars and cut down their Asherahs.
You're not to bow down to any other god, because the LORD — Jealous is his name — is a jealous God.

Don't make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land — because when they prostitute themselves after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, one of them will invite you and you'll eat from his sacrifice;
and you'll take some of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters will prostitute themselves after their gods and make your sons do the same.
Don't make yourself cast-metal gods.

Keep the festival of unleavened bread: seven days you're to eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib — because it was in the month of Abib that you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn of a womb is mine, and all your livestock that bears a male — the firstborn of ox and sheep.
The firstborn of a donkey you're to redeem with a sheep; if you don't redeem it, break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you're to redeem, and no one is to appear before me empty-handed.
Six days you're to work, but on the seventh day you're to stop — at ploughing time and at harvest you're to stop.
Keep the festival of weeks — the firstfruits of the wheat harvest — and the festival of ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
I'll dispossess nations ahead of you and enlarge your border, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times a year.
Don't slaughter the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and don't leave the passover festival sacrifice over until morning.
Bring the first of the firstfruits of your ground to the house of the LORD your God. Don't boil a kid in its mother's milk.
The LORD said to Moses, "Write these words down, because it's according to these words that I've made a covenant with you and with Israel."
He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, he didn't know that the skin of his face shone because he'd been speaking with him.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation came back to him, and Moses spoke to them.
Afterward all the Israelites came near, and he commanded them everything the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a face covering over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he'd take the face covering off until he came out; then he'd come out and tell the Israelites what he'd been commanded.
And the Israelites would see Moses' face, that the skin of it shone; and Moses would put the face covering back over his face until he went in to speak with him.

exodus_35.t: Moses called the whole congregation of the Israelites together and said to them, "These are the words the LORD has commanded, to do them.
Work is to be done six days. But the seventh day is a holy thing for you, a sabbath of solemn rest to the LORD. Anyone who does work on it is to be put to death.
Don't light a fire in any of your dwellings on the sabbath day.
Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take a contribution for the LORD from among yourselves. Everyone whose heart is willing should bring it — the LORD's contribution: gold, silver, and bronze;
violet, purple, and scarlet; fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense;
and onyx stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
And let everyone among you who is skilled come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its bars, its pillars and its bases;
the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the screening veil;
the table and its poles and all its articles, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light and its articles and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense and its poles; the anointing oil and the fragrant incense; and the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of the burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its articles; the washbasin and its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the tent pegs of the courtyard, and their cords;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for serving as priests."
Then the whole congregation of the Israelites went out from Moses' presence.

And they came — everyone whose heart moved him, everyone whose spirit made him willing — and brought the LORD's contribution for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.

The men came with the women. Everyone whose heart was willing brought brooches, rings, signet rings and ornaments — every kind of gold article, every man who waved a wave-offering of gold to the LORD.
And everyone who had violet, purple or scarlet, fine linen or goat hair, ram skins dyed red or fine leather brought them.
Everyone offering a contribution of silver or bronze brought the LORD's contribution, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought that.
Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun — the violet and the purple, the scarlet and the fine linen.
And all the women whose heart moved them, and who had the skill, spun the goat hair.
The leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
and the spice and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring something for all the work the LORD had commanded to be done through Moses — the Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
Then Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God — with skill, understanding and knowledge in every kind of work —
to devise designs, to work in gold, silver and bronze,
in cutting stones for setting and carving wood — every kind of designed craft.
And he has put it in his heart to teach — both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill of heart to do all the work of a craftsman, a designer, an embroiderer in violet and purple and scarlet and fine linen, and a weaver — workers in every craft, devisers of designs.

exodus_36.t: So Bezalel and Oholiab are to work, and every skilled man in whom the LORD has put the skill and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the holy place — everything the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled man in whose heart the LORD had put skill — everyone whose heart moved him to come near the work and do it.

They received from Moses all the contribution the Israelites had brought for the work of the service of the holy place, to do it. And the people still kept bringing him freewill offerings morning after morning.
So all the skilled men doing the work of the holy place came, each from the work he was doing,
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing far more than enough for the service of the work the LORD commanded to be done."
So Moses gave an order, and they sent a proclamation through the camp: "No man or woman is to do any more work for the contribution of the holy place." And the people were held back from bringing.
What they had was enough for all the work — enough, and more than enough.
All the skilled men among those doing the work made the tabernacle: ten curtains of fine twisted linen and violet and purple and scarlet, with cherubim, the work of a designer. He made them.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were the same size.
He joined five of the curtains to each other, and the other five to each other.
He made violet loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and did the same on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty on the end of the curtain in the second set, the loops facing one another.
He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to each other with the clasps, and the tabernacle became one.
He made curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle — eleven of them.
Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; all eleven were the same size.
He joined five of the curtains together, and six of them together.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain of the one set, and fifty on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together so it would be one.
He made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather over that.
He made the frames for the tabernacle out of acacia wood, standing upright.
Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
Each frame had two tenons joined to one another. He did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
He made the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side.
He made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames — two bases under each frame, for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames,
and their forty silver bases, two under each frame.
And for the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, he made six frames.
And he made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were doubled from below and joined together at the top into the one ring. He did this for both of them, at the two corners.
So there were eight frames with sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
He made bars of acacia wood — five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the frames of the second side, and five for the frames at the rear, on the west.
He made the middle bar to run through the middle of the frames from end to end.
He overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold to hold the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold too.
He made the veil of violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen — the work of a designer, with cherubim.
He made four acacia pillars for it and overlaid them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast four silver bases for them.
And he made a screen for the entrance of the tent of violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
and its five pillars with their hooks. He overlaid their tops and bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.

exodus_37.t: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood — two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and out, and made a gold moulding around it.
He cast four gold rings for it, on its four feet — two rings on one side, two on the other.
He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.
He made a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
He made two cherubim of gold, of hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat.
One cherub at one end and one cherub at the other. He made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim spread their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, facing one another; the faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia wood — two cubits long, a cubit wide, a cubit and a half high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold moulding around it.
He made a rim a handbreadth wide around it, and a gold moulding for the rim.
He cast four gold rings for it and put them on the four corners at its four legs.
The rings were close to the rim, holding the poles for carrying the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.
He made the articles for the table — its dishes and pans and bowls, and the jars used for pouring — all of pure gold.
He made the lampstand of pure gold, of hammered work — its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms were all of one piece with it.
Six branches went out from its sides — three from one side and three from the other.
Three cups shaped like almond blossoms on one branch, with a bulb and a blossom, and three on the next, with a bulb and a blossom — the same for all six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their bulbs and blossoms.
There was a bulb under the first pair of branches, a bulb under the second pair, and a bulb under the third — for the six branches going out from it.
Their bulbs and branches were of one piece with it; the whole thing was one piece of hammered work in pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its tongs and firepans, of pure gold.
He made it and all its articles out of a talent of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide — square — and two cubits high. Its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold — its top, its sides all around, and its horns — and made a gold moulding around it.
He made two gold rings for it below the moulding, on its two sides, on both flanks, to hold the poles for carrying it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.

exodus_38.t: He made the altar of the burnt offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide — square — and three cubits high.
He made its horns on its four corners, of one piece with it, and overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the articles of the altar — the pots, shovels, basins, forks and firepans. He made all of them of bronze.
He made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, under its ledge below, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings at the four ends of the bronze grating, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with. He made it hollow, out of boards.
He made the washbasin of bronze and its stand of bronze, out of the mirrors of the serving women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. On the south side, the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long;
their twenty pillars and twenty bases were bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
On the north side, a hundred cubits; their twenty pillars and twenty bases were bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
On the west side, hangings of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
And on the east side, fifty cubits.
There were hangings of fifteen cubits on the one side, with three pillars and three bases,
and for the second side, on either side of the gate of the courtyard, hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the pillars were bronze; the hooks and bands were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver. All the pillars of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer — violet, purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long, and its height, measured across the fabric, was five cubits, matching the hangings of the courtyard.
Their four pillars and four bases were bronze; their hooks were silver, and their tops and bands were overlaid with silver.
And all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and the courtyard all around were bronze.
These are the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, drawn up at Moses' command — the service of the Levites, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD had commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan — a craftsman, a designer, and an embroiderer in violet, purple and scarlet and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the holy place — the gold of the wave-offering — came to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from those of the congregation who were enrolled came to a hundred talents and 1,775 shekels by the sanctuary shekel:
a beka a head — half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel — for everyone who passed over to those enrolled, from twenty years old and up: 603,550 men.
The hundred talents of silver went to cast the bases of the holy place and the bases of the veil — a hundred bases for a hundred talents, a talent to a base.
And from the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their tops, and banded them.
The bronze of the wave-offering was seventy talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating, and all the articles of the altar,
the bases around the courtyard and the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs around the courtyard.

exodus_39.t: From the violet and the purple and the scarlet they made woven garments for serving in the holy place, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
They hammered gold into thin sheets and he cut it into threads, to work in among the violet and the purple and the scarlet and the fine linen — the work of a designer.
They made joined shoulder-pieces for it, joined at its two ends.
The band of its ephod, the one on it, was of one piece with it and made the same way: gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They prepared the onyx stones, set in gold settings and engraved like a seal, with the names of the sons of Israel.
He put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece, the work of a designer, like the work of the ephod: gold, violet, purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
It was square. They made the breastpiece doubled over — a span long and a span wide, doubled over.
They set four rows of stones in it. The first row was ruby, topaz and emerald;
the second row was turquoise, sapphire and diamond;
the third row was jacinth, agate and amethyst;
and the fourth row was beryl, onyx and jasper, enclosed in gold settings in their mountings.
The stones matched the names of the sons of Israel — twelve of them, engraved like a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
They made braided chains of twisted work on the breastpiece, of pure gold.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
They put the two gold braids on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
The two ends of the two braids they attached to the two settings, and put those on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on the edge facing the ephod, on the inside.
They made two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, low down at the front, close to its seam, above the band of the ephod.
They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a violet cord, so it would sit on the band of the ephod and not come loose from it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, entirely of violet.
The opening of the robe was in the middle, like the opening of a corselet, with a binding around it so it wouldn't tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of violet, purple and scarlet, twisted.
They made bells of pure gold and put them among the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around, among the pomegranates —
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe, for serving — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons,
the turban of fine linen, the head-wraps of the headdresses of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen and violet and purple and scarlet, the work of an embroiderer — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and inscribed on it, like the engraving of a seal: Holy to the LORD.
They fastened a violet cord to it, to set it on the turban above, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the labour of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished. The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses — exactly that is what they did.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its articles — its clasps, its frames, its bars, its pillars and its bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the screening veil;
the ark of the testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat;
the table with all its articles, and the bread of the Presence;
the pure lampstand with its lamps set in their row, and all its articles, and the oil for the light;
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its articles; the washbasin and its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and bases, the screen for the courtyard gate, its cords and tent pegs, and all the articles for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests.
Everything the LORD had commanded Moses — that is how the Israelites did all the labour.
And Moses saw all the work, and there it was — they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So they had done. And Moses blessed them.

exodus_40.t: And the LORD said to Moses:
"On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
Put the ark of the testimony there, and screen the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out its arrangement; bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Put the golden altar for incense in front of the ark of the testimony, and set up the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle.
Put the altar of the burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
Put the washbasin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and put up the screen for the gate of the courtyard.
Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it, with all its articles, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of the burnt offering and all its articles. Consecrate the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
Anoint the washbasin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him and consecrate him, and he will serve me as priest.
Bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, and they will serve me as priests. Their anointing will be a perpetual priesthood for them throughout their generations."
And Moses did everything the LORD commanded him. That is what he did.
In the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle: he laid its bases, set up its frames, put in its bars and raised its pillars.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent over it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and put it into the ark, set the poles on the ark, and put the mercy seat on top of the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle, set up the screening veil, and screened the ark of the testimony, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He set out an arrangement of bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the tent of meeting in front of the veil,
and he sent up fragrant incense on it in smoke, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put up the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle.
He set the altar of the burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered the burnt offering and the grain offering on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the washbasin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing.
Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet at it.
Whenever they went into the tent of meeting or drew near to the altar, they washed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and put up the screen for the gate of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
And Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, they wouldn't set out until the day it was.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

ezekiel_1.t: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the exiles by the river Kebar, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth of the month — it was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's exile —
the word of the LORD came — it really came — to Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Kebar; and the hand of the LORD was on him there.

And I looked, and there it was — a storm wind coming out of the north, a great cloud and flashing fire, with brightness all around it; and from the middle of it, something like glowing metal, out of the middle of the fire.
And out of the middle of it came a likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had a likeness of a human.
Each one had four faces, and each of them had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot, and they gleamed like the gleam of burnished bronze.
And human hands were under their wings on all four sides; and all four of them had their faces and their wings.
Their wings touched one another. They didn't turn as they moved; each moved straight in the direction its face was turned.

And this was the likeness of their faces: the face of a human; the face of a lion on the right, for all four of them; the face of an ox on the left, for all four of them; and the face of an eagle, for all four of them.
And their faces and their wings were spread apart above; each had two wings touching another's, and two covering its body.
And each moved in the direction its face was turned. Wherever the spirit was to go, they went; they didn't turn as they moved.

And as for the likeness of the living creatures: their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. It kept moving about among the living creatures; the fire had brightness, and lightning came out of the fire.
And the living creatures darted back and forth, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
And I looked at the living creatures, and there was one wheel on the ground beside them, for each of its four faces.
The appearance of the wheels and the way they were made was like the gleam of beryl, and all four had one likeness; and their appearance and their making was as though a wheel were inside a wheel.
They moved on all four of their sides as they moved; they didn't turn as they moved.
And their rims — they were tall, and they were fearsome; and their rims were full of eyes all around, all four of them.
When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up off the ground, the wheels were lifted up too.
Wherever the spirit was to go, they went — there the spirit was to go — and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, because the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

When they moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they were lifted up off the ground, the wheels were lifted up alongside them, because the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
And over the heads of the living creature was a likeness of a vault, like the gleam of awesome ice, spread out over their heads above.
And under the vault their wings were straight out toward one another; each had two covering it, and each had two covering it — covering their bodies.

And I heard the sound of their wings — like the sound of many waters, like the sound of the Almighty, as they moved; a sound of tumult, like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.
And a sound came from above the vault that was over their heads. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.

And above the vault that was over their heads was something like the appearance of a sapphire stone, a likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the appearance of a human upon it, above.

And I saw something like glowing metal, like the appearance of fire enclosing it all around, from the appearance of his loins upward; and from the appearance of his loins downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and he had brightness all around.

Like the appearance of the bow that's in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. That was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And I saw it, and I fell on my face, and I heard a voice speaking.

ezekiel_2.t: And he said to me, "Mortal, stand on your feet, and I'll speak with you."
And a spirit came into me as he spoke to me, and it set me on my feet; and I heard the one speaking to me.
And he said to me, "Mortal, I'm sending you to the people of Israel, to rebellious nations who have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have transgressed against me to this very day.
And the children are stern-faced and hard-hearted. I'm sending you to them, and you'll say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says.'
And they — whether they listen or whether they refrain, because they're a house of rebellion — will know that a prophet has been among them.

And you, mortal — don't be afraid of them, and don't be afraid of their words, though nettles and thorns are with you and you're living among scorpions. Don't be afraid of their words, and don't be dismayed at the sight of them, for they are a house of rebellion.
And you'll speak my words to them, whether they listen or whether they refrain, because they are rebellion.
And you, mortal, hear what I'm speaking to you. Don't be rebellion like the house of rebellion. Open your mouth and eat what I'm giving you."
And I looked, and there was a hand stretched out to me, and in it a scroll of a document.
And he spread it out in front of me, and it was written on the front and on the back; and written on it were lamentations and moaning and wailing.

ezekiel_3.t: And he said to me, "Mortal, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go and speak to the house of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and he made me eat this scroll.
And he said to me, "Mortal, feed your belly and fill your insides with this scroll that I'm giving you." And I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
And he said to me, "Mortal, go — go to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them.
You're not being sent to a people whose speech is obscure and whose language is hard — you're being sent to the house of Israel —
not to many peoples whose speech is obscure and whose language is hard, whose words you wouldn't understand. Surely if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel won't be willing to listen to you, because they aren't willing to listen to me; the whole house of Israel is hard of forehead and stern of heart.
Look — I've made your face hard to match theirs, and your forehead hard to match their forehead.
Like shamir, harder than flint, I've made your forehead. Don't be afraid of them and don't be dismayed at the sight of them, for they are a house of rebellion."
And he said to me, "Mortal, all my words that I'll speak to you — take them into your heart, and hear them with your ears.
And go — go to the exiles, to the children of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says' — whether they listen or whether they refrain."
And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place!"
And the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels alongside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
And a spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went bitter, in the rage of my spirit; and the hand of the LORD was strong on me.
And I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were living by the river Kebar, and I sat where they were living; and I sat there seven days, appalled among them.
And at the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, I've made you a watchman for the house of Israel. You'll hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.

When I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and you haven't warned him, haven't spoken to warn the wicked off his wicked way so he can live — that wicked one will die in his iniquity, and I'll require his blood from your hand.
But if you have warned the wicked and he hasn't turned from his wickedness and from his wicked way — he'll die in his iniquity, and you have delivered your own life.

And when a righteous one turns from his righteousness and does injustice, and I put an obstacle in front of him — he will die. Because you didn't warn him, he'll die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did won't be remembered; and I'll require his blood from your hand.
But if you have warned him, the righteous one, so that the righteous one doesn't sin, and he hasn't sinned — he will surely live, because he was warned; and you have delivered your own life."
And the hand of the LORD was on me there, and he said to me, "Get up, go out to the plain, and there I'll speak with you."
So I got up and went out to the plain, and there the glory of the LORD was standing, like the glory I had seen by the river Kebar; and I fell on my face.
And a spirit came into me and set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself up inside your house.
And you, mortal — look, they'll put ropes on you and bind you with them, and you won't go out among them.
And I'll make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you'll be mute, and you won't be a man who reproves them, for they are a house of rebellion.

And when I speak with you I'll open your mouth, and you'll say to them, 'This is what Lord GOD says.' Let the one who hears, hear; and let the one who refrains, refrain — for they are a house of rebellion."

ezekiel_4.t: "And you, mortal, take a brick and set it in front of you, and carve a city on it — Jerusalem.
