Lay a siege against it, build a siege-wall against it, throw up a ramp against it, set camps against it, and place battering-rams around it.

And you, take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city; set your face against it — it will be under siege, and you will besiege it. It is a sign for the house of Israel.
And you, lie down on your left side and put the iniquity of the house of Israel on it. For as many days as you lie on it, you'll bear their iniquity.
And I myself have assigned you the years of their iniquity as a number of days: three hundred and ninety days. And you'll bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

And when you've completed these, lie down a second time, on your right side, and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah: forty days. A day for a year, a day for a year — that's what I've assigned you.
And you'll set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
And look — I'll put ropes on you, and you won't turn from one side to the other until you've completed the days of your siege.

And you, take wheat and barley and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, put them in one vessel, and make them into bread for yourself. For as many days as you're lying on your side — three hundred and ninety days — you'll eat it.
And the food you eat will be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from time to time you'll eat it.
And water by measure you'll drink, a sixth of a hin; from time to time you'll drink.
And you'll eat it as a barley cake, and you'll bake it over balls of human excrement, in front of them."
And the LORD said, "That's how the people of Israel will eat their bread — unclean — among the nations where I'll banish them."

And I said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Look — I have never been made unclean. From my youth until now I haven't eaten an animal that died of itself or one torn by beasts, and no foul flesh has come into my mouth."
And he said to me, "See — I'm giving you cattle dung instead of human dung, and you'll prepare your bread over it."
And he said to me, "Mortal, look — I'm about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem, and they'll eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,
so that they'll go short of bread and water, and be appalled, each with his brother, and waste away in their iniquity."

ezekiel_5.t: "And you, mortal, take a sharp sword — take it as a barber's razor — and pass it over your head and over your beard. Then take a set of scales and divide the hair.

A third you'll burn in the fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are over. And you'll take a third and strike it with the sword all around the city; and a third you'll scatter to the wind, and I'll draw a sword after them.
And you'll take a few of them, just a small number, and tie them into the skirts of your robe.
And from these you'll take some again, and throw them into the middle of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it a fire will go out to all the house of Israel."
This is what Lord GOD says: "This is Jerusalem. I set her in the middle of the nations, with lands around her.

And she has rebelled against my judgements more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the lands around her; they have rejected my judgements, and as for my statutes — they haven't walked in them.

So this is what Lord GOD says: "Because your tumult is greater than that of the nations around you — you haven't walked in my statutes, you haven't done my judgements, and you haven't even acted by the judgements of the nations around you —
therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against you — I myself — and I'll perform acts of judgement in the middle of you, before the eyes of the nations.
And I'll do in you what I have never done, and the like of which I'll never do again, because of all your abominations.
So fathers will eat sons in the middle of you, and sons will eat their fathers; and I'll perform acts of judgement in you, and scatter all your remnant to every wind.

So, as I live — declares Lord GOD — because you have made my sanctuary unclean with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I too will cut you back; my eye will not spare, and I will show no pity.

A third of you will die by pestilence and come to an end by famine in the middle of you; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I'll scatter to every wind, and I'll draw a sword after them.
And my anger will be spent, and I'll give my rage rest on them, and I'll be relieved; and they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my jealousy, when I have completed my rage on them.
And I'll make you a ruin and a reproach among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.

And it will be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I perform acts of judgement on you in anger and in rage and with rebukes of rage. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I shoot the evil arrows of famine at them — arrows that are for destruction, that I'll shoot to destroy you — and when I increase famine on you and break your staff of bread —
and I'll send famine and wild beasts on you, and they'll leave you childless; and pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I'll bring a sword on you. I, the LORD, have spoken."

ezekiel_6.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,

and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of Lord GOD. This is what Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: Look — I myself am bringing a sword on you, and I'll destroy your high places.
Your altars will be made desolate and your incense altars shattered; and I'll make your slain fall in front of your idols.
And I'll lay the corpses of the people of Israel in front of their idols, and scatter your bones around your altars.

In all your dwelling places the cities will be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars are laid waste and held guilty, your idols shattered and brought to an end, your incense altars cut down, and your works wiped out.
And the slain will fall in the middle of you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
But I'll leave some over: some of you will escape the sword among the nations, when you're scattered among the lands.

And your escapees will remember me among the nations where they've been taken captive — how I was broken by their whoring heart that turned away from me, and by their eyes that whored after their idols — and they'll loathe themselves to their own faces for the evils they did, for all their abominations.
And they will know that I am the LORD: it wasn't for nothing that I said I would do this evil to them."

This is what Lord GOD says: Strike with your hand, stamp with your foot, and say, "Alas!" — over all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, who will fall by the sword, by famine and by pestilence.
The one far off will die by pestilence, the one near will fall by the sword, and the one left over and kept alive will die by famine; and I'll complete my rage on them.

And you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountain tops, under every green tree and under every leafy terebinth — the place where they gave a soothing odour to all their idols.
And I'll stretch out my hand over them and make the land a desolation and a waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_7.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"And you, mortal — this is what Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come on the four corners of the land.
Now the end is on you, and I'll send my anger against you, and I'll judge you according to your ways, and requite on you all your abominations.
And my eye won't spare you, and I won't show pity; I'll requite your ways on you, and your abominations will be in the middle of you. And you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: An evil! One single evil! Look — it's coming.
An end has come! The end has come! It has woken up against you. Look — it's coming.
Doom has come on you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come, the day is near — confusion, and not a shout on the mountains.
Now, soon, I'll pour out my rage on you and complete my anger against you; I'll judge you according to your ways and requite on you all your abominations.
And my eye won't spare, and I won't show pity. According to your ways I'll requite on you, and your abominations will be in the middle of you. And you will know that I, the LORD, am the one striking.
Look — the day! Look, it's coming. Doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.
Violence has risen into a rod of wickedness. Nothing of them, nothing of their multitude, nothing of their tumult; and there is no distinction among them.
The time has come, the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for burning anger is against her whole multitude.

For the seller won't return to what was sold, even while they're still alive; the vision concerning her whole multitude won't turn back, and no one will strengthen himself in his iniquity, in his life.
They've blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one is going to the battle, because my burning anger is against her whole multitude.
The sword is outside, pestilence and famine inside. Whoever is out in the open country will die by the sword; whoever is in the city — famine and pestilence will consume him.
And their escapees will escape and be on the mountains, like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each in his iniquity.
Every hand will drop, and every knee will run with water.
And they'll gird on sackcloth, and shuddering will cover them; on every face, shame; on every head, baldness.

They'll throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will become an impurity. Their silver and their gold won't be able to deliver them on the day of the LORD's fury; they won't satisfy their appetite or fill their insides, because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.
And the beauty of its ornament — he turned it into pride, and in it they made the images of their abominations, their detestable things. So I've made it an impurity to them.
And I'll give it into the hand of strangers as spoil, and to the wicked of the earth as plunder, and they'll profane it.
And I'll turn my face away from them, and they'll profane my treasured place; robbers will come into it and profane it.
Make the chain! For the land is full of the judgement of blood, and the city is full of violence.
And I'll bring the worst of the nations, and they'll take possession of their houses; I'll put an end to the pride of the strong, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
Anguish has come. They'll look for peace, and there's none.
Disaster on disaster will come, report on report. And they'll seek a vision from a prophet, and law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will clothe himself in desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will be terrified. I'll deal with them according to their way, and by their own judgements I'll judge them; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_8.t: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting in front of me, and there the hand of Lord GOD fell on me.

And I looked, and there was a likeness like the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins downward, fire; and from his loins upward, something like the appearance of brightness, like glowing metal.

And he stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my hair; and a spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of God, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the idol of jealousy stood — the one that provokes to jealousy.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the appearance I had seen on the plain.
And he said to me, "Mortal, look up now toward the north." So I looked up toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, was this idol of jealousy, at the entrance.
And he said to me, "Mortal, do you see what they're doing — the great abominations the house of Israel are doing here, driving me far from my sanctuary? And you'll see still greater abominations."
And he brought me to the entrance of the court; and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
And he said to me, "Mortal, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was an opening.
And he said to me, "Go in and see the wicked abominations they're doing here."
So I went in and looked, and there it was — every form of creeping thing and detestable animal, and all the idols of the house of Israel, carved on the wall all around, all around.

And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, were standing in front of them, each with his censer in his hand; and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was going up.

And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in the rooms of his carved image? Because they're saying, 'The LORD doesn't see us; the LORD has abandoned the land.'"
And he said to me, "You'll see still more great abominations that they're doing."
And he brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of the LORD that faces north; and there the women were sitting, weeping for the Tammuz.
And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal? You'll see abominations greater than these."

And he brought me to the inner court of the house of the LORD; and there, at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces eastward, bowing down eastward to the sun.

And he said to me, "Have you seen, mortal? Is it too slight a thing for the house of Judah to do the abominations they've done here, that they've filled the land with violence and turned back to provoke me to anger? And look — they're putting the branch to their nose.
And I too will act in rage. My eye won't spare, and I won't show pity; and though they call out in my ears with a great voice, I won't hear them."

ezekiel_9.t: And he called out in my ears with a great voice: "The punishments of the city have drawn near — each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

And there were six men coming from the direction of the upper gate that faces north, each with his weapon of shattering in his hand; and one man among them was clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing case at his waist. They came and stood beside the bronze altar.

And the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from over the cherub where it had been, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the scribe's writing case at his waist;

and the LORD said to him, "Pass through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and put a taw on the foreheads of the people who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are done in it."
And to the others he said, in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike. Let your eye not spare, and don't show pity.

Old man, young man and virgin, little ones and women — kill them to destruction. But don't go near any man who has the taw on him. And begin at my sanctuary." And they began with the old men who were in front of the house.
And he said to them, "Make the house unclean, and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!" And they went out and struck in the city.
And while they were striking, and I was left, I fell on my face and cried out: "Alas, Lord GOD! Are you destroying all the remnant of Israel, pouring out your rage on Jerusalem?"

And he said to me, "The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is very, very great; the land is filled with blood and the city is full of perversity. Because they've said, 'The LORD has abandoned the land, and the LORD doesn't see.'
And I too — my eye won't spare, and I won't show pity. I've requited their conduct on their own head."
And there was the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his waist, bringing back a word: "I've done everything you commanded me."

ezekiel_10.t: And I looked, and there, toward the vault that was over the head of the cherubim, was something like a sapphire stone; like the appearance of the likeness of a throne, it appeared above them.

And he said to the man clothed in linen, "Go in between the whirling wheels, under the cherub, and fill your cupped hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." And he went in as I watched.
And the cherubim were standing on the south side of the house when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court.
And the glory of the LORD rose from over the cherub to the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the glory of the LORD.
And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the sound of God Almighty when he speaks.
And when he commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim," he went in and stood beside the wheel.
And the cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim to the fire that was among them, lifted some, and put it into the cupped hands of the one clothed in linen; and he took it and went out.
And there appeared on the cherubim the form of a human hand under their wings.
And I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim — one wheel beside one cherub, and one wheel beside one cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of beryl.
And as for their appearance: all four had one likeness, as though a wheel were inside a wheel.
When they moved, they moved toward all four of their sides; they didn't turn as they moved. Wherever the head turned, they went after it; they didn't turn as they moved.
And their whole body and their backs and their hands and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around — all four of them, their wheels.
As for the wheels — in my hearing they were called "the whirling wheel".
And each one had four faces: the first face was the face of the cherub, the second the face of a human, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
And the cherubim rose. That was the living creature I had seen by the river Kebar.
And when the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels didn't turn away from beside them either.
When they stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose, the wheels rose with them; because the spirit of the living creature was in them.
And the glory of the LORD went out from the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.

And the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground as I watched, going out, with the wheels alongside them. And it stood at the entrance of the eastern gate of the house of the LORD, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
That was the living creature I had seen under the God of Israel by the river Kebar; and I knew they were cherubim.
Each had four faces — four — and each four wings; and the likeness of human hands was under their wings.
And as for the likeness of their faces: they were the faces I had seen by the river Kebar — their appearance, and themselves. Each moved in the direction its face was turned.

ezekiel_11.t: And a spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of the house of the LORD, which faces east; and there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men, and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
And he said to me, "Mortal, these are the men who plan wickedness and give evil counsel in this city,
who say, 'It's not near — building houses! This city is the pot and we are the meat.'
So prophesy against them. Prophesy, mortal."
And the spirit of the LORD fell on me and said to me, "Say: This is what the LORD says: So you have said, house of Israel — and the risings of your spirit, I know them myself.
You've multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the slain."
So this is what Lord GOD says: Your slain, whom you've put in the middle of it — they are the meat, and it is the pot; but you he will bring out from the middle of it.
A sword you have feared, and a sword I'll bring on you — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll bring you out from the middle of it and give you into the hand of strangers, and I'll perform acts of judgement on you.
By the sword you'll fall. At the border of Israel I'll judge you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
It won't be a pot for you, and you won't be the meat in the middle of it. At the border of Israel I'll judge you,
and you will know that I am the LORD — you who haven't walked in my statutes, haven't done my judgements, but have acted by the judgements of the nations around you."
And while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. And I fell on my face and cried out with a great voice: "Alas, Lord GOD! Are you making a complete end of the remnant of Israel?"
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, your brothers, your brothers — the men who hold your right of redemption — and the whole house of Israel, all of it, the ones the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said this to: 'Keep far from the LORD; this land has been given to us as a possession' —

therefore say: This is what Lord GOD says: Though I've removed them far off among the nations, and though I've scattered them among the lands, yet I have become for them a sanctuary for a little while in the lands where they've gone.
So say: This is what Lord GOD says: I'll gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the lands where you've been scattered, and I'll give you the land of Israel.
And they'll come there and remove all its detestable things and all its abominations from it.
And I'll give them one heart, and a new spirit I'll put within you; and I'll remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they can walk in my statutes and keep my judgements and do them. And they'll be my people, and I'll be their God.
But as for those whose heart goes after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I've requited their conduct on their own head — declares Lord GOD."
And the cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels alongside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
And the glory of the LORD went up from over the middle of the city and stood on the mountain east of the city.
And a spirit lifted me up and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision, by the spirit of God; and the vision I had seen went up from me.
And I told the exiles all the words of the LORD that he had shown me.

ezekiel_12.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, you're living in the middle of the house of rebellion — people who have eyes to see and don't see, ears to hear and don't hear; because they are a house of rebellion.

And you, mortal, get an exile's baggage ready for yourself, and go into exile by day where they can see you; go into exile from your place to another place where they can see you. Perhaps they'll see — because they are a house of rebellion.
And you'll bring out your baggage like an exile's baggage, by day, where they can see; and you yourself will go out in the evening where they can see, like people going out into exile.
Where they can see, dig through the wall for yourself, and bring your baggage out through it.
Where they can see, lift it on your shoulder; in the dark bring it out. Cover your face and don't look at the land, because I've made you a sign for the house of Israel."

And I did it, just as I was commanded. My baggage I brought out like an exile's baggage, by day; and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand; in the dark I brought it out and lifted it on my shoulder, where they could see.
And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, hasn't the house of Israel — the house of rebellion — said to you, 'What are you doing?'
Say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: The prince — this oracle — in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel who are among them.
Say: I am your sign. As I have done, so it will be done to them: into exile, into captivity they will go.

And the prince who is among them will lift his baggage onto his shoulder in the dark and go out; they'll dig through the wall to bring it out. He'll cover his face because he himself won't see the land with his eye.
And I'll spread my net over him, and he'll be caught in my hunting net; and I'll bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans — and he won't see it, and there he'll die.
And all who are around him — his help and all his troops — I'll scatter to every wind, and I'll draw a sword after them.
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the lands.

But I'll leave a few of them over — from the sword, from famine and from pestilence — so that they can recount all their abominations among the nations where they've gone; and they will know that I am the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with anxiety.

And say to the people of the land: This is what Lord GOD says about the inhabitants of Jerusalem, about the land of Israel: They'll eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water with horror, so that her land is stripped of its fullness, because of the violence of everyone living in it.
And the inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will become a desolation; and you will know that I am the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, what is this proverb you have about the land of Israel: 'The days drag on, and every vision comes to nothing'?

So say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: I'll put an end to this proverb, and they won't use it as a proverb in Israel any more. Say this to them instead: The days have drawn near — and the matter of every vision.
For there'll be no more worthless vision or flattering divination in the middle of the house of Israel.
For I, the LORD, will speak. What I speak as a word will be done; it won't be postponed any more. In your days, house of rebellion, I'll speak a word and do it — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, look — the house of Israel are saying, 'The vision he's seeing is for many days off; he's prophesying about distant times.'
So say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: None of my words will be postponed any more. What I speak as a word will be done — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_13.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy out of their own heart: Hear the word of the LORD!
This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets, who walk after their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Your prophets have been like foxes among ruins, Israel.
You haven't gone up into the breaches, or built a wall around the house of Israel, to stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.
They have seen worthlessness and lying divination — the ones who say, 'Declares the LORD,' when the LORD hasn't sent them; and they have waited for a word to be fulfilled.
Haven't you seen a worthless vision and spoken a lying divination, saying, 'Declares the LORD,' when I have not spoken?
So this is what Lord GOD says: Because you have spoken worthlessness and seen falsehood, therefore look — I am against you, declares Lord GOD.

And my hand will be against the prophets who see worthlessness and divine falsehood. They won't be in the council of my people, they won't be written in the register of the house of Israel, and they won't come into the land of Israel; and you will know that I am Lord GOD.
Because — yes, because — they've led my people astray, saying 'Peace!' when there is no peace; and one builds a flimsy partition, and look, they plaster it with whitewash —
say to the ones plastering with whitewash that it will fall. There'll be an overflowing rain; and you, hailstones, will fall; and a tempest wind will break through.
And look — the wall has fallen. Won't it be said to you, "Where is the plastering that you plastered?"
So this is what Lord GOD says: I'll make a tempest wind break out in my rage, and an overflowing rain will come in my anger, and hailstones in rage, for a complete end.

And I'll tear down the wall you plastered with whitewash and bring it down to the ground, and its foundation will be laid bare; it will fall, and you'll come to an end in the middle of it; and you will know that I am the LORD.
And I'll complete my rage on the wall and on the ones who plastered it with whitewash; and I'll say to you: The wall is gone, and the ones who plastered it are gone —
— the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw a vision of peace for her, when there was no peace. Declares Lord GOD.
And you, mortal, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own heart, and prophesy against them.

And say: This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew magic bands onto all the joints of the hands and make veils for the head of every stature, to hunt lives! Will you hunt the lives of my people and keep your own lives alive?

And you've profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and fragments of bread, putting to death lives that shouldn't die and keeping alive lives that shouldn't live — by your lying to my people, who listen to falsehood.

So this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I am against your bands, the ones you hunt lives with, like birds — and I'll tear them off your arms; and I'll set free the lives, the lives you're hunting like birds.
And I'll tear off your veils and deliver my people from your hand, and they'll no longer be prey in your hand; and you will know that I am the LORD.

Because you've disheartened the righteous with falsehood, when I myself hadn't caused him pain, and strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he doesn't turn back from his evil way and stay alive —
therefore you won't see worthlessness or practise divination any more; and I'll deliver my people from your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_14.t: And men from the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, these men have brought their idols up into their heart and set the stumbling block of their iniquity in front of their faces. Am I really to let myself be consulted by them?

So speak with them and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Anyone at all of the house of Israel who brings his idols up into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity in front of his face, and then comes to the prophet — I, the LORD, will let myself answer him, as he comes, according to the multitude of his idols,
so as to seize the house of Israel by their heart, because all of them have become estranged from me through their idols.
So say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Turn back, and turn away from your idols; turn your faces away from all your abominations.

For anyone at all of the house of Israel, or of the sojourner living in Israel, who separates himself from following me and brings his idols up into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity in front of his face, and then comes to the prophet to consult me through him — I, the LORD, will let myself answer him myself.
And I'll set my face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I'll cut him off from the middle of my people; and you will know that I am the LORD.
And the prophet, if he is deceived and speaks a word — I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet; and I'll stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from the middle of my people Israel.
And they'll bear their iniquity: as the iniquity of the one who enquires, so will be the iniquity of the prophet,
so that the house of Israel will no longer wander from following me or make themselves unclean with all their transgressions. And they'll be my people, and I'll be their God — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its staff of bread and send famine on it and cut off humankind and animals from it —
and these three men were in the middle of it — Noah, Danel and Job — they would deliver their own lives by their righteousness, declares Lord GOD.
If I send wild beasts through the land and they leave it bereaved, and it becomes a desolation with no one passing through because of the beasts —
these three men in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters. They alone would be delivered, and the land would be a desolation.
Or if I bring a sword on that land and say, 'Sword, pass through the land,' and I cut off humankind and animals from it —
and these three men in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they wouldn't deliver sons or daughters; they alone would be delivered.
Or if I send pestilence against that land and pour out my rage on it in blood, to cut off humankind and animals from it —
and Noah, Danel and Job were in the middle of it — as I live, declares Lord GOD, they would deliver neither son nor daughter. They would deliver their own lives by their righteousness.
For this is what Lord GOD says: How much more when I send my four evil judgements — sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence — against Jerusalem, to cut off humankind and animals from it!

And look — there'll be left in it an escaped remnant, those being brought out: sons and daughters. Look, they're coming out to you, and you'll see their conduct and their practices; and you'll be comforted about the evil I have brought on Jerusalem, all that I have brought on it.
And they'll comfort you when you see their conduct and their practices; and you will know that it wasn't without cause that I did all that I did in it — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_15.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, what is the wood of the vine more than any other wood — the vine branch that's among the trees of the forest?
Is wood taken from it to make anything at all? Do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on?
Look — it's given to the fire for fuel; the fire consumes its two ends and its middle is charred. Is it fit for anything?
Look — when it was whole it couldn't be made into anything. How much less, now that fire has consumed it and it's charred, can it be made into anything!
So this is what Lord GOD says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I have given the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And I'll set my face against them. They have come out from the fire, and the fire will consume them; and you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
And I'll make the land a desolation, because they've acted unfaithfully — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_16.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, make Jerusalem know her abominations,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origins and your birth were from the land of the Canaanite; your father was the Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
And as for your birth: on the day you were born your umbilical cord wasn't cut, you weren't washed with water to clean you, you weren't rubbed with salt at all, and you weren't wrapped at all.
No eye looked on you with compassion, to do any one of these things for you, to pity you; and you were thrown out onto the open field, in loathing of your life, on the day you were born.
And I passed by you and saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you in your blood, "Live!" — and I said to you in your blood, "Live!"
A myriad, like the growth of the field, I made you; and you grew and became great and came to the finest of ornaments. Your breasts were firm and your hair had grown, and you were naked and bare.

And I passed by you and saw you, and there — your time was the time of love. And I spread the skirt of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; and I swore to you and entered a covenant with you — declares Lord GOD — and you became mine.
And I washed you with water and rinsed your blood off you, and I anointed you with oil.
And I clothed you with embroidered cloth and shod you with fine leather, and I wrapped your head with fine linen and covered you with silk.
And I adorned you with ornaments, and put bracelets on your hands and a chain on your neck.
And I put a ring in your nose and earrings on your ears, and a crown of beauty on your head.

And you adorned yourself with gold and silver; your clothing was fine linen and silk and embroidered cloth. Fine flour and honey and oil you ate, and you became beautiful — very, very — and you prospered into kingship.
And a name went out for you among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through my splendour that I had put on you — declares Lord GOD.
But you trusted in your beauty and whored on the strength of your name, and you poured out your whorings on every passer-by — let it be his!
And you took some of your clothes and made yourself high places of many colours, and you whored on them — such as should not come and should not be.
And you took your articles of beauty — from my gold and my silver that I'd given you — and made yourself male images, and whored with them.
And you took your embroidered clothes and covered them, and set my oil and my incense in front of them.
And my bread that I gave you — fine flour and oil and honey I fed you — you set in front of them for a soothing odour; and so it was, declares Lord GOD.
And you took your sons and your daughters, whom you'd borne to me, and sacrificed them to be devoured by them. Was your whoring too little?
And you slaughtered my children and gave them up, making them pass over to them.
And in all your abominations and your whorings you didn't remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.
And after all your evil — woe, woe to you! declares Lord GOD —
you built yourself a mound and made yourself a high place in every open square.
At the head of every road you built your high place, and you made your beauty an abomination, and you spread your legs open to every passer-by, and you multiplied your whorings.
And you whored with the Egyptians, your neighbours, big of flesh; and you multiplied your whoring to provoke me to anger.

And look — I stretched out my hand against you and cut back your allotted portion, and gave you over to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your licentious conduct.
And you whored with the Assyrians, because you weren't satisfied; you whored with them, and even so you weren't satisfied.
And you multiplied your whoring toward a land of merchants, toward Chaldea; and even by this you weren't satisfied.
How sick your heart is — declares Lord GOD — that you do all these things, the deeds of a woman, a whore, and a domineering one!
When you built your mound at the head of every road and made your high place in every open square — and you weren't like the whore: you scorned the whore's fee.
The adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
Men give a gift to all whores; but you gave your gifts to all your lovers and bribed them to come to you from all around for your whorings.
And in you it was the opposite of other women in your whorings: no one whored after you; you gave a fee when no fee was given to you. You became the opposite.
So, whore, hear the word of the LORD!

This is what Lord GOD says: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your whorings with your lovers, and because of all the idols of your abominations, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them —

therefore look — I'm gathering all your lovers, the ones you pleased, and all you loved along with all you hated; and I'll gather them against you from all around, and I'll uncover your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.
And I'll judge you with the judgements of adulteresses and of women who shed blood, and I'll bring on you the blood of rage and jealousy.
And I'll give you into their hand, and they'll tear down your mound and break down your high places; they'll strip your clothes off you and take your articles of beauty, and leave you naked and bare.
And they'll bring up a company against you and stone you with stones and cut you to pieces with their swords.
And they'll burn your houses with fire and perform acts of judgement on you before the eyes of many women; and I'll make you stop being a whore, and you'll give a fee no more.
And I'll give my rage rest on you, and my jealousy will turn aside from you; and I'll be quiet and won't be angry any more.

Because you didn't remember the days of your youth and enraged me with all these things — look, I too have requited your conduct on your head, declares Lord GOD. And have you not committed licentiousness on top of all your abominations?
Look, everyone who quotes a proverb will quote one about you: "Like mother, like daughter."

You are your mother's daughter, who loathed her husband and her children; and you're the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
And your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters, living to your north; and your sister who is younger than you, living to your south, is Sodom and her daughters.
And you didn't walk in their ways or act according to their abominations — as if that were a little thing — and you acted more corruptly than they did in all your ways.
As I live — declares Lord GOD — Sodom your sister, she and her daughters, did not do what you have done, you and your daughters.
Look, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, surfeit of food and untroubled ease belonged to her and her daughters; and she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and the needy.
And they were haughty and did abomination before me; and I removed them when I saw it.
And Samaria didn't sin as much as half your sins; you multiplied your abominations more than they did, and you made your sisters look righteous by all the abominations you've done.

You too, bear your disgrace — you who interceded for your sister. By your sins, in which you acted more abominably than they did, they are more righteous than you. And you too, be ashamed and bear your disgrace, because you made your sisters look righteous.
And I'll turn back their captivity — the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, the captivity of Samaria and her daughters — and the captivity of your captives among them,
so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you've done, in comforting them.
And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state; Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state; and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
And wasn't Sodom your sister a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride —
before your own evil was uncovered — like the time of the reproach of the daughters of Aram and all those around her, the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you on every side?
Your licentiousness and your abominations — you have borne them, declares the LORD.
For this is what Lord GOD says: I'll deal with you as you have done, you who despised an oath by breaking a covenant.
But I myself will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I'll establish for you a perpetual covenant.
And you'll remember your ways and be ashamed, when you receive your sisters, both older and younger than you; and I'll give them to you as daughters — though not by your covenant.
And I myself will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,
so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never open your mouth again because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all you have done — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_17.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, put a riddle and speak a proverb to the house of Israel,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says: The great eagle — great of wing, long of pinion, full of plumage, with variegated feathers — came to Lebanon and took the treetop of the cedar.
It plucked off the top of its shoots and brought it to a land of merchants; in a city of traders it set it.
And it took some of the seed of the land and put it in a seed-field; it took it by many waters and set it like a willow.
And it sprouted and became a spreading vine, low of stature, its branches turning toward it and its roots under it; and it became a vine, and produced shoots and sent out boughs.

And there was another great eagle, great of wing and abundant of plumage; and look — this vine bent its roots toward it and sent out its branches to it, for it to water the vine, away from the beds where it was planted.
It was planted in a good field, by many waters, to produce branches and bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.

Say: This is what Lord GOD says: Will it prosper? Won't he pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers — all its fresh growth will wither — and not by a great arm or by many people, to lift it from its roots?
And look, it's planted — will it prosper? When the east wind touches it, won't it utterly wither? On the beds where it grew it will wither."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Say now to the house of rebellion: Don't you know what these things are? Say: Look, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its princes and brought them to himself, to Babylon.
And he took one of the royal offspring and made a covenant with him and put him under an oath; and he took away the leading men of the land,
so that the kingdom would be lowly and not exalt itself, but keep his covenant so that it might stand.
But he rebelled against him by sending his messengers to Egypt, to give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will the one who does these things escape? Will he break a covenant and escape?
As I live — declares Lord GOD — in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, with him, in the middle of Babylon, he will die.
And Pharaoh won't act for him in the battle with a large army or a great company, when a ramp is thrown up and a siege-wall built to cut off many lives.
He despised an oath by breaking a covenant; and look — he had given his hand, and he did all these things. He will not escape.
So this is what Lord GOD says: As I live — my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke — I'll requite it on his own head.

And I'll spread my net over him, and he'll be caught in my hunting net; and I'll bring him to Babylon and enter into judgement with him there for the unfaithfulness by which he acted unfaithfully against me.
And all his fugitives, among all his troops, will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.

This is what Lord GOD says: And I myself will take from the treetop of the high cedar and set it out; from the top of its shoots I'll pluck a tender one, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

On the mountain height of Israel I'll plant it, and it will bear branches and produce fruit and become a majestic cedar; and under it will dwell every bird of every wing — in the shade of its branches they'll dwell.

And all the trees of the field will know that I, the LORD, bring low the tall tree and raise up the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree sprout. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it."

ezekiel_18.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"What do you mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: 'Fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?
As I live — declares Lord GOD — you'll no longer have occasion to quote this proverb in Israel.
Look, all lives are mine: the life of the father as much as the life of the son — they are mine. The person who sins, that one will die.
And if a man is righteous and does justice and righteousness —
he hasn't eaten on the mountains or lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; he hasn't made his neighbour's wife unclean or drawn near to a woman in her menstrual impurity;
and he hasn't oppressed anyone; he's returned the debtor's pledge, robbed no one, given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing;
he hasn't lent at interest or taken increase; he's turned his hand back from injustice and done true justice between one person and another;
he walks in my statutes and has kept my judgements, acting faithfully — he is righteous. He will surely live, declares Lord GOD.
And he fathers a violent son, a shedder of blood, who does any one of these things —
though the father himself did none of these things — the son has even eaten on the mountains and made his neighbour's wife unclean,
has oppressed the poor and the needy, robbed and robbed, not returned a pledge; and he has lifted his eyes to the idols, done abomination,
has lent at interest and taken increase — and shall he live? He shall not live. He has done all these abominations; he will surely be put to death. His blood will be on him.
And look, he fathers a son who has seen all the sins his father did — and he saw, and didn't do the same:
he hasn't eaten on the mountains or lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; he hasn't made his neighbour's wife unclean;
and he hasn't oppressed anyone or taken a pledge; he's robbed no one, given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing;
he has turned his hand back from the poor, hasn't taken interest or increase, has done my judgements and walked in my statutes — he won't die for his father's iniquity. He will surely live.
His father, because he extorted and extorted, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people — look, he'll die for his own iniquity.
And you say, "Why hasn't the son borne the iniquity of the father?" But the son has done justice and righteousness, has kept all my statutes and done them; he will surely live.

The person who sins, that one will die. A son won't bear the iniquity of the father, and a father won't bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be on him.
And if the wicked turns back from all the sins he has done and keeps all my statutes and does justice and righteousness, he will surely live; he won't die.
None of the transgressions he has done will be remembered against him. For the righteousness he has done, he will live.
Do I really take pleasure in the death of the wicked — declares Lord GOD — and not rather that he should turn back from his ways and live?

And when a righteous one turns from his righteousness and does injustice, doing all the abominations the wicked does — shall he live? None of the righteous acts he has done will be remembered. For the unfaithfulness by which he acted unfaithfully and the sin by which he sinned — for those he will die.
And you say, "The way of the Lord isn't right." Listen now, house of Israel: Is my way not right? Isn't it your ways that aren't right?
When a righteous one turns from his righteousness and does injustice and dies for them — for the injustice he has done he dies.
And when a wicked one turns from the wickedness he has done and does justice and righteousness, he'll keep his own life alive.
And he saw and turned back from all the transgressions he had done; he will surely live, he won't die.
And the house of Israel say, "The way of the Lord isn't right." Are my ways not right, house of Israel? Isn't it your ways that aren't right?
So I'll judge you, each according to his ways, house of Israel — declares Lord GOD. Turn back and turn away from all your transgressions, and iniquity won't be a stumbling block to you.
Throw away from yourselves all the transgressions by which you have transgressed, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. And why will you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of the one who dies — declares Lord GOD. So turn back and live!"

ezekiel_19.t: "And you, take up a lamentation over the princes of Israel,
and say: What a lioness your mother was among lions! She lay down among young lions; she reared her cubs.
And she brought up one of her cubs; he became a young lion. He learned to tear prey; he devoured humans.
And nations heard of him; he was caught in their pit, and they brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt.
And she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost; and she took one of her cubs and made him a young lion.
And he went about among lions; he became a young lion. He learned to tear prey; he devoured humans.
And he knew their widows, and he laid waste their cities; and the land and all that fills it were desolate at the sound of his roaring.
And nations set on him from the provinces all around; they spread their net over him — he was caught in their pit.
And they put him in a cage with hooks and brought him to the king of Babylon; they brought him into strongholds, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted by water; she was fruitful and full of branches from the abundant waters.
And she had strong branches fit for the sceptres of rulers; its stature towered above the thick boughs, and it stood out in its height, in the abundance of its branches.
But she was plucked up in rage, thrown down to the ground; and the east wind dried up her fruit. They were torn off and withered — her strong branch; fire consumed it.
And now she's planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
And fire went out from the branch of her shoots; it consumed her fruit. And there was in her no strong branch, no sceptre for ruling. This is a lamentation, and it has become a lamentation.

ezekiel_20.t: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, men from the elders of Israel came to consult the LORD, and they sat down in front of me.
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, speak with the elders of Israel and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Is it to consult me that you are coming? As I live, I won't let myself be consulted by you — declares Lord GOD.
Will you judge them? Will you judge, mortal? Make known to them the abominations of their fathers,

and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand in an oath to the offspring of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt; and I raised my hand in an oath to them, saying, 'I am the LORD your God.'
On that day I raised my hand in an oath to them, to bring them out of the land of Egypt to a land I had searched out for them, flowing with milk and honey — the beauty of all lands.
And I said to them: Each of you, throw away the detestable things your eyes are set on, and don't make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

But they rebelled against me and weren't willing to listen to me. Not one of them threw away the detestable things his eyes were set on; they didn't forsake the idols of Egypt. And I said I would pour out my rage on them, to complete my anger against them in the middle of the land of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it wouldn't be profaned before the eyes of the nations among whom they were — before whose eyes I had made myself known to them, bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
And I brought them out of the land of Egypt and brought them into the wilderness.
And I gave them my statutes and made known to them my judgements, which a person will live by if he does them.
And I also gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sets them apart as holy.

But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They didn't walk in my statutes; they rejected my judgements, which a person will live by if he does them; and they profaned my sabbaths exceedingly. And I said I would pour out my rage on them in the wilderness, to make an end of them.
But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it wouldn't be profaned before the eyes of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
And I also raised my hand in an oath to them in the wilderness, not to bring them into the land I had given, flowing with milk and honey — the beauty of all lands —
because they had rejected my judgements, hadn't walked in my statutes and had profaned my sabbaths; their heart was walking after their idols.
But my eye spared them, so as not to destroy them, and I didn't make an end of them in the wilderness.
And I said to their children in the wilderness: Don't walk in the statutes of your fathers, don't keep their judgements, and don't make yourselves unclean with their idols.
I am the LORD your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my judgements and do them,
and set my sabbaths apart as holy; and they'll be a sign between me and you, so that you will know that I am the LORD your God.

But the children rebelled against me. They didn't walk in my statutes and didn't keep my judgements, to do them — which a person will live by if he does them; my sabbaths they profaned. And I said I would pour out my rage on them, to complete my anger against them in the wilderness.
But I turned back my hand and acted for the sake of my name, so that it wouldn't be profaned before the eyes of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
I also raised my hand in an oath to them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the lands,
because they hadn't done my judgements, had rejected my statutes and profaned my sabbaths, and their eyes were after their fathers' idols.
And I also gave them statutes that were not good, and judgements by which they could not live;
and I made them unclean by their own gifts, making every firstborn of the womb pass over — so that I might make them appalled, so that they would know that I am the LORD.
So speak to the house of Israel, mortal, and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: In this also your fathers blasphemed me, by acting unfaithfully against me.

And I brought them into the land I had raised my hand in an oath to give them; and they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they sacrificed their sacrifices, there they presented their provoking offering, there they set their soothing odours, there they poured out their drink offerings.
And I said to them: What is this high place that you keep going to? And its name has been called Bamah to this day.
So say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Are you making yourselves unclean in the way of your fathers, whoring after their detestable things?

And in lifting up your gifts, in making your children pass through the fire, you're making yourselves unclean with all your idols to this day. And shall I let myself be consulted by you, house of Israel? As I live — declares Lord GOD — I will not let myself be consulted by you.
And what comes up in your spirit will certainly not happen — what you're saying: 'We'll be like the nations, like the clans of the lands, serving wood and stone.'
As I live — declares Lord GOD — with a strong hand and an outstretched arm and rage poured out, I will reign over you.
And I'll bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you've been scattered, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm and rage poured out.
And I'll bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I'll enter into judgement with you, face to face.
Just as I entered into judgement with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I'll enter into judgement with you — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll make you pass under the rod, and I'll bring you into the bond of the covenant.

And I'll purge out from among you those who rebel and those who transgress against me. From the land where they have lived as sojourners I'll bring them out, but into the land of Israel they won't come; and you will know that I am the LORD.

And you, house of Israel — this is what Lord GOD says: Go, serve each of you his idols; and afterwards, if you won't listen to me — but my holy name you shall no longer profane with your gifts and with your idols.

For on my holy mountain, on the mountain height of Israel — declares Lord GOD — there the whole house of Israel, all of it, will serve me in the land. There I will accept them, and there I'll seek your contributions and the choicest of your gifts, with all your holy things.

As a soothing odour I'll accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you've been scattered; and I'll show myself holy among you before the eyes of the nations.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land I raised my hand in an oath to give to your fathers.
And there you'll remember your ways and all your practices by which you made yourselves unclean; and you'll loathe yourselves to your own faces for all the evils you have done.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I deal with you for the sake of my name — not according to your evil ways or your corrupt practices, house of Israel — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward the south, and prophesy against the south, and prophesy against the forest land of the Negev.

And say to the forest of the Negev: Hear the word of the LORD. This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm kindling a fire in you, and it will consume in you every green tree and every dry tree. The blazing flame won't be extinguished, and every face from the south to the north will be scorched by it.
And all flesh will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it won't be extinguished."
And I said, "Alas, Lord GOD! They're saying about me, 'Isn't he just a maker of parables?'"

ezekiel_21.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward Jerusalem and prophesy against the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
And say to the land of Israel: This is what the LORD says: Look, I am against you, and I'll bring my sword out of its sheath and cut off from you the righteous and the wicked.
Because I am cutting off from you the righteous and the wicked, my sword will go out of its sheath against all flesh, from south to north.
And all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have brought my sword out of its sheath; it won't go back again."
"And you, mortal, groan; with breaking loins and with bitterness, groan where they can see.

And when they say to you, 'Why are you groaning?' you'll say: Because of a report — it's coming, and every heart will melt and all hands hang limp, every spirit grow faint and all knees run with water. Look, it's coming, and it will happen — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord says: Say: A sword, a sword — sharpened, and also polished!
Sharpened for slaughtering a slaughter, polished so as to flash like lightning — or shall we rejoice? The rod of my son rejects every tree.
And he gave it to be polished, to be gripped in the hand. It has been sharpened, a sword, it has been polished, to be put into the hand of the slayer.
Cry out and wail, mortal, for it has come on my people; it is on all the princes of Israel. Thrown to the sword they have been, along with my people. So slap your thigh.
For it has been tested — and what if even the rejecting rod does not come? declares Lord GOD."
"And you, mortal, prophesy and strike palm against palm. And let the sword be doubled a third time — the sword of the slain; it is the sword of the great slain one that closes in on them,
so that the heart may melt and the stumblings be many. At all their gates I have set the slaughter of a sword. Alas! It's made to flash like lightning, wrapped for slaughtering.
Be sharp! Go right! Set yourself! Go left! Wherever your face is appointed.
And I too will strike my palm against my palm and give my rage rest. I, the LORD, have spoken."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"And you, mortal, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to come by. Both of them will go out from one land; and make a signpost — make it at the head of the road to a city.
Mark out a road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and to Judah, in fortified Jerusalem.
For the king of Babylon has stopped at the fork of the road, at the head of the two roads, to practise divination. He has shaken the arrows, enquired of the teraphim, looked at the liver.

Into his right hand came the divination — Jerusalem: to set up battering-rams, to open the mouth with a killing shout, to lift the voice with a war cry, to set up battering-rams against the gates, to throw up a ramp, to build a siege-wall.
And it will seem to them like a false divination — they who have sworn oaths! But he brings iniquity to remembrance, so that they may be seized.

So this is what Lord GOD says: Because you have brought your iniquity to remembrance, in that your transgressions are uncovered so that your sins are seen in all your practices — because you have been brought to remembrance, you'll be seized by the hand.
And you, profaned and wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has come at the time of final punishment —
this is what Lord GOD says: Remove the turban and lift off the crown! This shall not be this. Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted.
A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! And this too will not be, until he comes to whom the judgement belongs; and I'll give it to him.

"And you, mortal, prophesy and say: This is what Lord GOD says concerning the Ammonites and concerning their reproach; and say: A sword, a sword — drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, so as to flash like lightning!
while they see worthlessness for you, while they divine falsehood for you — to lay you on the necks of the profaned wicked, whose day has come at the time of final punishment.
Put it back into its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origins, I will judge you.
And I'll pour out my indignation on you; with the fire of my wrath I'll blow on you, and I'll give you into the hand of brutish men, craftsmen of destruction.
You'll become fuel for the fire; your blood will be in the middle of the land; you won't be remembered. For I, the LORD, have spoken."

ezekiel_22.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"And you, mortal — will you judge? will you judge the city of blood? Then make known to her all her abominations,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says: A city that sheds blood in her midst, so that her time comes; and that has made idols for herself, to become unclean!

By the blood you've shed you've become guilty, and by the idols you've made you've become unclean; you've brought your days near and come to your years. So I've made you a reproach to the nations and a derision to all the lands.
Those near and those far from you will deride you — you of unclean name, great in turmoil!
Look, the princes of Israel — each according to his own strength — have been in you, so as to shed blood.
Father and mother they've treated with contempt in you; the sojourner they've oppressed in your midst; the fatherless and the widow they've maltreated in you.
My holy things you've despised, and my sabbaths you've profaned.
Men of slander have been in you, so as to shed blood; they've eaten on the mountains in you; licentiousness they've done in your midst.
A father's nakedness has been uncovered in you; the woman unclean in her menstrual impurity has been violated in you.
One has done abomination with his neighbour's wife; one has made his daughter-in-law unclean with licentiousness; one has violated his sister, his father's daughter, in you.
A bribe they've taken in you, so as to shed blood. Interest and increase you've taken; you've made unjust gain from your neighbours by oppression; and me you've forgotten — declares Lord GOD.
And look — I've struck my palm at the unjust gain you've made, and at the blood that has been in your midst.
Will your heart endure, or will your hands be strong, in the days when I deal with you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
And I'll scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the lands, and I'll make an end of your uncleanness from you.
And you will be profaned by your own doing before the eyes of the nations; and you will know that I am the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are copper and tin and iron and lead in the middle of a furnace; they've become the dross of silver.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Because all of you have become dross, therefore look — I'm gathering you into the middle of Jerusalem.
As silver and copper and iron and lead and tin are gathered into the middle of a furnace, to blow fire on it to melt it, so I'll gather you in my anger and in my rage; I'll set you down and melt you.
And I'll gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you'll be melted in the middle of it.
As silver is melted in the middle of a furnace, so you'll be melted in the middle of it; and you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my rage on you."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, say to her: You are a land that hasn't been cleansed, not rained on in a day of indignation.
A conspiracy of her prophets is in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing prey. They've devoured lives; they take treasure and precious things; they've made many widows in her midst.

Her priests have done violence to my law and have profaned my holy things. Between the holy and the common they have not separated, and between the unclean and the clean they've taught no difference; from my sabbaths they've hidden their eyes, and I have been profaned among them.
Her princes in her midst are like wolves tearing prey, to shed blood, to destroy lives, so as to make unjust gain.
And her prophets have plastered whitewash for them, seeing worthlessness and divining falsehood for them, saying, 'This is what Lord GOD says,' when the LORD had not spoken.
The people of the land have oppressed and oppressed, robbed and robbed; they've maltreated the poor and the needy, and oppressed the sojourner without justice.
And I looked among them for someone to build up a wall and stand in the breach before me for the land, so that I wouldn't destroy it; but I found no one.
And I've poured out my indignation on them; with the fire of my wrath I've made an end of them. Their conduct I've requited on their own head — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_23.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, there were two women, daughters of one mother.
And they whored in Egypt; in their youth they whored. There their breasts were handled, and there their virgin nipples were squeezed.
And their names were Oholah the elder and Oholibah her sister; and they became mine and bore sons and daughters. And their names: Samaria is Oholah, Jerusalem is Oholibah.
And Oholah whored while she was mine, and lusted after her lovers, after Assyria — warriors,
clothed in violet, governors and officials, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding horses.
And she gave her whorings to them — all of them the choicest of the Assyrians — and by all whom she lusted after, by all their idols, she made herself unclean.
And she didn't forsake her whorings from Egypt: they had lain with her in her youth, squeezed her virgin nipples and poured out their whoring on her.
So I gave her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, after whom she lusted.
They uncovered her nakedness; they took her sons and her daughters, and killed her with the sword. And she became a byword among women, and they carried out acts of judgement on her.
And her sister Oholibah saw — and she was more corrupt in her lusting than her sister, and her whorings were more than her sister's whorings.
She lusted after the Assyrians — governors and officials, warriors magnificently clothed, horsemen riding horses, all of them desirable young men.
And I saw that she had made herself unclean; both of them had one way.
And she added to her whorings. She saw men carved on the wall, images of Chaldeans inscribed in vermilion,
girded with a waistband at their hips, with flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, the likeness of the Babylonians — Chaldea was the land of their birth.
And she lusted after them at the sight of her eyes, and sent messengers to them, to Chaldea.
And the Babylonians came to her, to the bed of love, and made her unclean with their whoring; and she became unclean by them, and she turned away from them in disgust.
And she uncovered her whorings and uncovered her nakedness; and I turned away from her in disgust, as I had turned away from her sister.
And she multiplied her whorings, remembering the days of her youth, when she whored in the land of Egypt.
And she lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys and whose emission is the emission of horses.
And you sought out the licentiousness of your youth, when the Egyptians squeezed your nipples, on account of the breasts of your youth.
So, Oholibah, this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm rousing your lovers against you — the ones you turned away from in disgust — and I'll bring them against you from all around —

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, all the Assyrians with them — desirable young men, governors and officials, all of them, officers and men of renown, all of them riding horses.

And they'll come against you with weapons, chariots and wheels, and with a company of peoples. Body shield and shield and helmet they'll set against you all around; and I'll set judgement before them, and they'll judge you by their own judgements.

And I'll set my jealousy against you, and they'll deal with you in rage. Your nose and your ears they'll cut off, and what's left of you will fall by the sword. They'll take your sons and your daughters, and what's left of you will be consumed by fire.
And they'll strip you of your clothes and take away your articles of beauty.
And I'll put an end to your licentiousness and to your whoring from the land of Egypt; you won't lift your eyes to them, and you won't remember Egypt any more.
For this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm giving you into the hand of those you hate, into the hand of those you turned away from in disgust.
And they'll deal with you in hatred and take all your property and leave you naked and bare; and the nakedness of your whorings will be uncovered — your licentiousness and your whorings.
These things have been done to you because you whored after the nations, because you made yourself unclean with their idols.
In the way of your sister you have walked; and I'll put her cup into your hand.
This is what Lord GOD says: You will drink your sister's cup, the deep and the wide one; you will become laughter and mockery — it holds much.
With drunkenness and sorrow you will be filled — the cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
And you will drink it and drain it, and you'll gnaw its shards and tear out your own breasts. For I have spoken — declares Lord GOD.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Because you have forgotten me and thrown me behind your back, you too must bear your licentiousness and your whorings.
And the LORD said to me: "Mortal, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations,
for they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. With their idols they have committed adultery, and even their children, whom they bore to me, they have made pass over to them, as food.
This too they have done to me: they made my sanctuary unclean on that same day, and profaned my sabbaths.
And when they had slaughtered their children for their idols, they came into my sanctuary that same day to profane it. And look — this is what they did inside my house.
And more than that: they sent for men coming from far off, to whom a messenger was sent — and look, they came. For them you bathed, painted your eyes and put on ornaments.
And you sat on a glorious couch, with a table laid out in front of it; and you set my incense and my oil on it.

And the sound of a carefree multitude was in her; and to the men, out of the crowds of people, Sabeans were brought in from the wilderness. And they put bracelets on their hands and a crown of beauty on their heads.
And I said of the worn-out one, "Adulteries! Now they'll whore her whorings, and she with them."
And they went in to her as one goes in to a whore. So they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, the licentious women.
And righteous men — they will judge them with the judgement of adulteresses and the judgement of women who shed blood; for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.
For this is what Lord GOD says: Bring up a company against them and give them over to terror and to spoil.
And the company will stone them with stones and cut them down with their swords; they'll kill their sons and their daughters, and burn their houses with fire.
And I'll put an end to licentiousness in the land, and all the women will take warning, and they won't act according to your licentiousness.
And they'll requite your licentiousness on you, and you'll bear the sins of your idols; and you will know that I am Lord GOD."

ezekiel_24.t: And the word of the LORD came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month:
"Mortal, write down for yourself the name of the day — this very day. The king of Babylon has thrown himself against Jerusalem this very day.
And speak a parable to the house of rebellion, and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Set on the pot, set it on, and pour water into it.
Gather its pieces into it, every good piece — thigh and shoulder; fill it with the choicest bones.
Take the choicest of the flock, pile the bones under it; make it boil hard; its bones too have been cooked inside it.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Woe, city of blood — a pot whose rust is in it, whose rust has not gone out of it! Piece by piece take it out; no lot has fallen on it.
For her blood is in her midst; she set it on the bare rock. She didn't pour it out on the ground, to cover it with dust.
To stir up rage, to take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, so that it wouldn't be covered.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Woe, city of blood! I too will make the fire-pile great.
Heap on the wood, kindle the fire, finish off the meat, mix in the seasoning; and let the bones be charred.
And set it empty on its coals, so that it grows hot and its bronze burns, and its uncleanness is melted inside it and its rust consumed.
It has worn itself out with toil, and its great rust hasn't gone out of it — its rust, into the fire!
