In your uncleanness is licentiousness. Because I cleansed you and you weren't clean, you won't be clean from your uncleanness again, until I have given my rage rest on you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. It's coming, and I will do it. I won't refrain, I won't have compassion, I won't relent. According to your ways and your practices they have judged you — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, look — I'm about to take from you the desire of your eyes with a blow; and you shall not lament, you shall not weep, and your tears shall not come.
Groan — but in silence. Don't perform mourning for the dead. Bind your turban on your head and put your sandals on your feet; don't cover your upper lip, and don't eat the bread of mourners.
And I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening; and in the morning I did as I had been commanded.
And the people said to me, "Won't you tell us what these things mean for us — what you're doing?"
And I said to them: The word of the LORD came to me:

Say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm about to profane my sanctuary — the pride of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and what your very self spares. And your sons and your daughters whom you've left behind will fall by the sword.
And you'll do as I have done: you won't cover your upper lip and won't eat the bread of mourners;
and your turbans will be on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You won't lament and won't weep, but you'll waste away in your iniquities and groan, each to his brother.
And Ezekiel will be a sign for you: everything he has done, you will do. When it comes, you will know that I am Lord GOD."

"And you, mortal — will it not be on the day I take from them their stronghold, the joy of their splendour, the desire of their eyes and the uplifting of their being — their sons and their daughters —
on that day an escapee will come to you, to bring the news to your ears?
On that day your mouth will be opened with the escapee, and you'll speak and no longer be mute. And you'll be a sign for them; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_25.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them,

and say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of Lord GOD. This is what Lord GOD says: Because you said 'Aha!' over my sanctuary when it was profaned, and over the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and over the house of Judah when they went into exile —
therefore look — I'm giving you to the people of the east as a possession. They'll set up their encampments among you and put their dwellings among you; they'll eat your fruit and drink your milk.
And I'll make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks; and you will know that I am the LORD.
For this is what Lord GOD says: Because you clapped your hand and stamped your foot and rejoiced with all the scorn of your being against the land of Israel —

therefore look — I've stretched out my hand against you and will give you as spoil to the nations; I'll cut you off from the peoples and destroy you from the lands. I'll annihilate you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because Moab and Seir said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the nations' —
therefore look — I'm about to lay open the flank of Moab, from the cities — from his cities, from his frontier — the beauty of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and Kiriathaim,
to the people of the east, along with the Ammonites; and I'll give it as a possession, so that the Ammonites won't be remembered among the nations.
And on Moab I'll perform acts of judgement; and they will know that I am the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because Edom acted by taking vengeance on the house of Judah, and became utterly guilty in avenging themselves on them —
therefore this is what Lord GOD says: I'll stretch out my hand against Edom and cut off from it humankind and animals, and I'll make it a ruin. From Teman as far as Dedan, they'll fall by the sword.
And I'll put my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they'll deal with Edom according to my anger and according to my rage; and they will know my vengeance — declares Lord GOD.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and avenged themselves with scorn in the self, to destroy in perpetual enmity —
therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm stretching out my hand against the Philistines; I'll cut off the Kerethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast.
And I'll perform great acts of vengeance on them, with rebukes of rage; and they will know that I am the LORD, when I put my vengeance on them."

ezekiel_26.t: In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, because Tyre said over Jerusalem, 'Aha! The doors of the peoples are broken; trade has turned to me; I'll be filled, now that she's laid waste' —
therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Tyre, and I'll bring up many nations against you, the way the sea brings up its waves.
And they'll destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers; and I'll scrape her soil off her and make her a bare rock.
She'll be a place for spreading nets in the middle of the sea, for I have spoken — declares Lord GOD. And she will become spoil for the nations.
And her daughters on the mainland will be killed by the sword; and they will know that I am the LORD.

For this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm bringing against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north — king of kings — with horses and chariotry and horsemen, a company and a numerous people.
Your daughters on the mainland he'll kill with the sword; he'll set a siege-wall against you, throw up a ramp against you and raise a body shield against you.
And the blow of his battering-ram he'll set against your walls, and your towers he'll break down with his weapons.
From the mass of his horses their dust will cover you; at the sound of horseman and wheel and chariot your walls will shake, when he enters your gates the way men enter a city broken into.
With the hooves of his horses he'll trample all your streets; your people he'll kill with the sword, and the pillars of your strength will come down to the ground.

And they'll plunder your wealth and take your merchandise as spoil, tear down your walls and pull down your fine houses; and your stones, your timber and your soil they'll throw into the middle of the water.
And I'll put an end to the noise of your songs, and the sound of your lyres won't be heard again.
And I'll make you a bare rock; you'll be a place for spreading nets. You won't be built again, for I, the LORD, have spoken — declares Lord GOD.
This is what Lord GOD says to Tyre: Won't the islands quake at the sound of your downfall, when the fatally wounded groan, when slaughter is done in your midst?

And all the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones, remove their robes and strip off their embroidered clothes. They'll clothe themselves in trembling; they'll sit on the ground and tremble every moment and be appalled at you.

And they'll take up a lamentation over you and say to you: How you have perished, you who were peopled from the seas, the praised city that was mighty on the sea — she and her inhabitants, who put their terror on all who dwell there!
Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your downfall, and the islands in the sea are terrified at your passing.
For this is what Lord GOD says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the many waters cover you,

then I'll bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago, and make you dwell in the world below, among ruins from of old, with those who go down to the pit, so that you won't be inhabited; and I'll set splendour in the land of the living.
I'll make you a horror, and you will be no more; you'll be sought and not found again, for ever — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_27.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"And you, mortal, take up a lamentation over Tyre,
and say to Tyre, who sits at the entrances of the sea, the trader of the peoples to many islands: This is what Lord GOD says: Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."
In the heart of the seas were your borders; your builders perfected your beauty.
Of fir trees from Senir they built all your planking; a cedar from Lebanon they took, to make a mast for you.
Oaks from Bashan they made into your oars; your deck they made of ivory inlaid in pine from the islands of Kittim.
Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was your sail, to serve as your banner; violet and purple from the islands of Elishah was your awning.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your own skilled men, Tyre, were in you — they were your sailors.
The elders of Gebal and her skilled men were in you, repairing your leaks. All the ships of the sea and their mariners were in you, to trade your merchandise.
Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war. Shield and helmet they hung in you; they gave you your splendour.
The people of Arvad and Helech were on your walls all around, and the Gammadites were in your towers. Their shields they hung on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
Tarshish was your trading partner because of your abundance of every kind of wealth; for silver, iron, tin and lead they exchanged your wares.
Javan, Tubal and Meshech — they were your traders. For human lives and vessels of bronze they exchanged your merchandise.
From Beth-togarmah they exchanged your wares for horses, warhorses and mules.
The people of Dedan were your traders; many islands were the market at your command. Horns of ivory and ebony they brought back to you as payment.
Aram was your trading partner because of your abundance of products. For emeralds, purple, embroidered cloth, fine linen, corals and ruby, they traded for your wares.
Judah and the land of Israel — they were your traders. For wheat of Minnith and pannag and honey and oil and balm they exchanged your merchandise.
Damascus was your trading partner in the abundance of your products, because of your abundance of every kind of wealth — with the wine of Helbon and white wool.
And Vedan and Javan from Uzal exchanged for your wares: wrought iron, cassia and calamus were among your merchandise.
Dedan was your trader in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar — they were the traders at your command, in lambs and rams and goats; in these they were your traders.
The traders of Sheba and Raamah — they were your traders. For the best of every spice and every precious stone and gold they exchanged your wares.
Haran and Canneh and Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad were your traders.
They were your traders in fine garments, in wrappings of violet and embroidered cloth, in chests of variegated cloth, bound with cords and made firm — in your market.
The ships of Tarshish were the caravans that carried your merchandise; and you were filled and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
Into many waters your rowers brought you; the east wind broke you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners and your sailors, those who repaired your leaks and those who traded your merchandise, and all your men of war who were in you, and all your company that was in your midst — they will fall into the heart of the seas on the day of your downfall.
At the sound of the outcry of your sailors the pasturelands will quake.
And all who wield an oar will come down from their ships; the mariners, all the sailors of the sea, will stand on the land.
And they'll make their voice heard over you and cry out bitterly; they'll throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
And they'll shave themselves bald for you and gird on sackcloth, and weep for you in bitterness of heart, with bitter wailing.
And in their wailing they'll take up a lamentation over you and lament over you: Who was like Tyre, like one silenced in the middle of the sea?
When your wares went out from the seas you satisfied many peoples; with the abundance of your wealth and your merchandise you made the kings of the earth rich.
Now you are broken, gone from the seas, in the depths of the water; your merchandise and all your company have fallen in your midst.
All the inhabitants of the islands are appalled at you, and their kings shudder with horror; their faces are troubled.
The traders among the peoples hiss at you; you have become a horror, and you will be no more, for ever."

ezekiel_28.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, say to the ruler of Tyre: This is what Lord GOD says: Because your heart has been haughty and you've said, 'I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods, in the heart of the seas' — yet you are a human and not a god, and you've made your heart like the heart of a god —
look, you're wiser than Danel; no secret is too dark for you!
By your wisdom and your understanding you've acquired wealth for yourself, and acquired gold and silver in your treasuries.
By the greatness of your wisdom, by your trading, you've increased your wealth; and your heart has been haughty in your wealth.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Because you have made your heart like the heart of a god,
therefore look — I'm bringing against you strangers, the most ruthless of nations; and they'll draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendour.
They'll bring you down to the pit, and you'll die the deaths of the slain in the heart of the seas.
Will you really say, 'I am a god,' in front of the one who kills you? You're a human and not a god, in the hand of those who pierce you.
You'll die the deaths of the uncircumcised, by the hand of strangers; for I have spoken — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and say to him: This is what Lord GOD says: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

You were in Eden, the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: ruby, topaz and diamond, beryl, onyx and jasper, sapphire, turquoise and emerald — and gold. The workmanship of your settings and your mountings was in you; on the day you were created they were prepared.
You were an anointed cherub who covers, and I appointed you; you were on the holy mountain of God, you walked about among stones of fire.
You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, until unrighteousness was found in you.
In the abundance of your trading your midst was filled with violence, and you sinned; and I profaned you from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, covering cherub, from among the stones of fire.
Your heart was haughty in your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom because of your splendour. I threw you to the ground; before kings I set you, for them to gaze at you.

From the greatness of your iniquities, by the unrighteousness of your trading, you profaned your sanctuaries. And I brought fire out of your midst; it consumed you, and I made you ashes on the ground before the eyes of all who saw you.
All who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you. You have become a horror, and you'll be no more, for ever."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her,

and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Sidon, and I'll gain glory in your midst; and they will know that I am the LORD when I perform acts of judgement on her and show myself holy in her.
And I'll send pestilence into her, and blood into her streets; and the slain will fall in her midst, by the sword against her from all around; and they will know that I am the LORD.
And there will no longer be for the house of Israel a pricking brier or a painful thorn from any around them who despise them; and they will know that I am Lord GOD.

This is what Lord GOD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they've been scattered, and show myself holy among them before the eyes of the nations, then they'll dwell on their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

And they'll dwell on it in safety, build houses and plant vineyards, and dwell in safety, when I perform acts of judgement on all who despise them from around them; and they will know that I am the LORD their God."

ezekiel_29.t: In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.
Speak and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great sea monster lying among his canals, who has said, 'My Nile is my own, and I made it for myself.'
And I'll put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your canals cling to your scales; and I'll bring you up out of your canals, with all the fish of your canals clinging to your scales.

And I'll abandon you in the wilderness, you and all the fish of your canals. You'll fall on the open field; you won't be gathered up or collected. To the beasts of the earth and the birds of the heavens I've given you for food.
And all the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they were a staff of reed for the house of Israel.
When they grasped you by the hand you splintered, and tore open every shoulder of theirs; and when they leaned on you, you broke, and made all their hips give way.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm bringing a sword on you, and I'll cut off from you humankind and animals.
And the land of Egypt will become a desolation and a ruin; and they will know that I am the LORD — because he said, 'The Nile is mine, and I made it.'
So look — I'm against you and against your canals, and I'll make the land of Egypt utterly desolate ruins, a waste, from Migdol to Syene and as far as the border of Cush.
No human foot will pass through it, and no animal's foot will pass through it; and it won't be inhabited for forty years.

And I'll make the land of Egypt a desolation in the midst of desolated lands, and her cities a desolation among laid-waste cities for forty years; and I'll scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands.
For this is what Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I'll gather Egypt from the peoples where they were scattered.
And I'll turn back the captivity of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, to the land of their origin; and there they'll be a lowly kingdom.
It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and won't exalt itself over the nations again; and I'll make them few, so that they won't rule over the nations.
And it will no longer be a confidence for the house of Israel, bringing iniquity to remembrance when they turned after them; and they will know that I am Lord GOD."
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labour a great labour against Tyre: every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder rubbed bare. But neither he nor his army got wages out of Tyre for the labour he had laboured against it.

So this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and he'll carry off her wealth, plunder her plunder and take her spoil as spoil; and it will be wages for his army.
As his recompense, for which he laboured, I've given him the land of Egypt, because they acted for me — declares Lord GOD.
On that day I'll make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and I'll give you an opening of the mouth in their midst; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_30.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, prophesy and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Wail — Alas for the day!
For a day is near, and a day for the LORD is near — a day of cloud; it will be the time of the nations.
And a sword will come on Egypt, and there'll be anguish in Cush when the slain fall in Egypt; and they'll take away her wealth, and her foundations will be torn down.
Cush and Put and Lud, and all the mixed people, and Kub, and the people of the land of the covenant — with them they'll fall by the sword.
This is what the LORD says: The supporters of Egypt will fall, and the pride of her strength will come down. From Migdol to Syene they'll fall in her by the sword — declares Lord GOD.
And they'll be desolate in the midst of desolated lands, and her cities will be among laid-waste cities.
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are broken.
On that day messengers will go out from before me in ships, to make Cush tremble in her security; and there'll be anguish among them on the day of Egypt — for look, it's coming.
This is what Lord GOD says: I'll put an end to the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought to destroy the land; and they'll draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
And I'll make the canals dry land and sell the land into the hand of the wicked, and I'll devastate the land and all that fills it by the hand of strangers. I, the LORD, have spoken.
This is what Lord GOD says: I'll destroy idols and put an end to worthless idols from Memphis; there'll no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt, and I'll put fear in the land of Egypt.
And I'll devastate Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and perform acts of judgement on Thebes.
And I'll pour out my rage on Sin, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of Thebes.
And I'll set fire to Egypt. Sin will writhe in anguish; Thebes is about to be broken into; and Memphis — distress in broad daylight.
The young men of On and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.

And in Tahpanhes the day will grow dark, when I break the yoke-bars of Egypt there, and the pride of her strength will cease in her. As for her — a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
And I'll perform acts of judgement on Egypt; and they will know that I am the LORD."
In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and look, it hasn't been bound up to give it healing — no bandage put on to bind it and make it strong enough to wield the sword.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I'll break his arms — the strong one and the one already broken — and I'll make the sword fall from his hand.
And I'll scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands.
And I'll make strong the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand; and I'll break the arms of Pharaoh, and he'll groan the groans of a fatally wounded man before him.

And I'll strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and the arms of Pharaoh will fall; and they will know that I am the LORD, when I put my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.
And I'll scatter Egypt among the nations and disperse them among the lands; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_31.t: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?
Look, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon — beautiful in its branches, a shading thicket, tall; and its treetop was among the thick boughs.
Waters made it grow; the deep raised it up, sending its rivers around the place where it was planted, and sending out its channels to all the trees of the field.
So its height was taller than all the trees of the field; its boughs became many and its branches long, from the abundant waters, as it sent them out.
In its boughs all the birds of the heavens made their nests; under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth; and in its shade all the great nations dwelt.
And it was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its root reached abundant waters.
Cedars didn't eclipse it in the garden of God; fir trees weren't like its boughs, and plane trees weren't like its branches. No tree in the garden of God was like it in its beauty.
Beautiful I made it, in the abundance of its branches; and all the trees of Eden that were in the garden of God envied it.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Because you were tall in height, and it set its treetop among the thick boughs, and its heart was lifted up in its height,
I gave it into the hand of a leader of nations; he will surely deal with it. According to its wickedness I drove it out.

And strangers cut it down, the most ruthless of nations, and abandoned it. On the mountains and in all the valleys its boughs fell, and its branches were broken in all the ravines of the land; and all the peoples of the earth went down out of its shade and abandoned it.
On its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens settled, and to its branches came all the beasts of the field —

so that no trees by water may be lifted up in their height or set their treetops among the thick boughs, and no drinkers of water may stand up to them in their height. For all of them have been given over to death, to the world below, among the children of humankind, with those who go down to the pit.

This is what Lord GOD says: On the day it went down to Sheol I caused mourning; I covered the deep over it and restrained its rivers, and the abundant waters were held back. And I made Lebanon mourn over it, and all the trees of the field wilted over it.

At the sound of its downfall I made nations tremble, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit; and all the trees of Eden — the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the drinkers of water — were comforted in the world below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword — and its arm, those who had dwelt in its shade among the nations.

Whom are you like in this, in splendour and in greatness, among the trees of Eden? And you'll be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below; among the uncircumcised you'll lie, with those slain by the sword. That is Pharaoh and all his multitude — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_32.t: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: You likened yourself to a young lion of the nations, but you were like the sea monster in the seas; you burst out in your rivers, made the waters turbid with your feet and fouled their rivers.
This is what Lord GOD says: I'll spread my net over you with a company of many peoples, and they'll haul you up in my dragnet.
And I'll abandon you on the land; on the open field I'll fling you, and I'll settle on you every bird of the heavens and satisfy the beasts of all the earth from you.
And I'll put your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your carcass.
And I'll make the land drink your outflow, from your blood, as far as the mountains; and the ravines will be filled from you.
And when I snuff you out I will cover the heavens and darken their stars; the sun I'll cover with a cloud, and the moon won't give its light.
All the shining lights in the heavens I'll darken over you, and I'll put darkness over your land — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll disturb the heart of many peoples when I bring news of your breaking among the nations, to lands you have not known.

And I'll make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder with horror over you when I brandish my sword before their faces; and they'll tremble every moment, each for his own life, on the day of your downfall.
For this is what Lord GOD says: The sword of the king of Babylon will come on you.
By the swords of warriors I'll make your multitude fall — all of them the most ruthless of nations. They'll devastate the pride of Egypt, and all her multitude will be destroyed.
And I'll destroy all her livestock from beside the abundant waters; and no human foot will muddy them again, nor will the hooves of livestock muddy them.
Then I'll let their waters settle and make their rivers run like oil — declares Lord GOD.
When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, and the land is emptied of its fullness, when I strike down all who dwell in it — then they will know that I am the LORD.
It is a lamentation, and they will chant it; the daughters of the nations will chant it. Over Egypt and over all her multitude they will chant it — declares Lord GOD.
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, wail over the multitude of Egypt, and bring her down — her and the daughters of majestic nations — to the world below, with those who go down to the pit.
Whom do you surpass in loveliness? Go down and be laid with the uncircumcised!
Among those slain by the sword they will fall. The sword has been appointed; drag her down, and all her multitudes.
The leaders of the mighty will speak to him from the midst of Sheol, along with his helpers: They have gone down, they lie still — the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.
Assyria is there, and all her company; her graves are all around her. All of them are slain, fallen by the sword —
whose graves are set in the remotest parts of the pit, and her company is around her grave; all of them slain, fallen by the sword — those who put terror in the land of the living.

Elam is there, and all her multitude around her grave; all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the world below — those who put their terror in the land of the living. And they have borne their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

Among the slain they have made a bed for her, with all her multitude; her graves are all around her. All of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because their terror was put in the land of the living; and they have borne their disgrace with those who go down to the pit. Among the slain she was laid.
Meshech, Tubal and all their multitude are there; their graves are all around them. All of them uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, because they put their terror in the land of the living.

And they do not lie with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were laid under their heads and whose shields were on their bones — for the terror of these warriors was in the land of the living.
And you'll be broken among the uncircumcised and will lie with those slain by the sword.
Edom is there, her kings and all her princes, who for all their strength were placed with those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised and with those who go down to the pit.

The princes of the north are there, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain — ashamed, for all the terror their strength inspired; and they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and they have borne their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude — Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword — declares Lord GOD.
For I put my terror in the land of the living; and he'll be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword — Pharaoh and all his multitude — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_33.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, speak to the children of your people and say to them: When I bring a sword on a land, and the people of the land take one man from among them and make him their watchman,
and he sees the sword coming on the land and blows the trumpet and warns the people —
then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and doesn't take warning, and the sword comes and takes him — his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the sound of the trumpet and didn't take warning; his blood will be on him. But the one who took warning has delivered his life.

But the watchman, if he sees the sword coming and doesn't blow the trumpet, and the people aren't warned, and the sword comes and takes a life from among them — that one is taken in his own iniquity, but his blood I'll require from the hand of the watchman.
And you, mortal, I've appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel; you'll hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.

When I say to the wicked, 'Wicked one, you will surely die,' and you haven't spoken to warn the wicked off his way — that wicked one will die in his iniquity, and I'll require his blood from your hand.
But if you have warned the wicked off his way, to turn back from it, and he hasn't turned back from his way — he'll die in his iniquity, and you have delivered your life.
"And you, mortal, say to the house of Israel: This is what you've said: 'Our transgressions and our sins are on us, and in them we're wasting away — how then shall we live?'

Say to them: As I live — declares Lord GOD — I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn back from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?

"And you, mortal, say to the children of your people: The righteousness of the righteous won't deliver him on the day of his transgression; and as for the wickedness of the wicked, he won't stumble by it on the day he turns back from his wickedness; and a righteous one won't be able to live by his righteousness on the day he sins.

When I say to the righteous, 'You will surely live,' and he relies on his righteousness and does unrighteousness — none of the righteous acts he has done will be remembered, and in the unrighteousness he has done, in that he will die.
And when I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and he turns back from his sin and does justice and righteousness —
if the wicked returns a pledge, repays what he has robbed, and walks in the statutes of life, doing no unrighteousness — he will surely live; he won't die.
None of the sins he has sinned will be remembered against him. He has done justice and righteousness; he will surely live.
And the children of your people say, 'The way of the Lord isn't right' — but it's their own way that isn't right.
When a righteous one turns back from his righteousness and does unrighteousness, he'll die by them.
And when a wicked one turns back from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, by them he'll live.
And you say, 'The way of the Lord isn't right.' I'll judge each of you according to his ways, house of Israel."
In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, the escapee came to me from Jerusalem and said, "The city has been struck."

And the hand of the LORD had been on me in the evening, before the escapee came, and he had opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, the inhabitants of these waste places in the land of Israel are saying: 'Abraham was one, and he took possession of the land; and we are many — the land has been given to us as a possession.'
So say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: You eat with the blood, you lift your eyes to your idols, and you shed blood — and shall you possess the land?
You've relied on your sword; you've done abomination; and each of you has made his neighbour's wife unclean — and shall you possess the land?

This is what you'll say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: As I live, surely those in the waste places will fall by the sword; the one out in the open field I'll give to the beasts to be devoured; and those in the strongholds and in the caves will die of pestilence.
And I'll make the land a desolation and a waste, and the pride of her strength will cease; and the mountains of Israel will be desolate, with no one passing through.
And they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolation and a waste, because of all the abominations they have done.

"And you, mortal — the children of your people who talk about you beside the walls and in the doorways of the houses, one speaking to another, each with his brother: 'Come now and hear what the word is that comes out from the LORD!' —

and they come to you the way a crowd comes, and my people sit in front of you and hear your words — but they don't do them. With their mouths they make a show of desire, but their heart goes after their unjust gain.
And look — to them you're like a love-song, a beautiful voice, well played; and they hear your words but don't do them.
And when it comes — and look, it's coming — then they will know that a prophet has been among them."

ezekiel_34.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:

"Mortal, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy, and say to them, to the shepherds: This is what Lord GOD says: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been shepherding themselves! Shouldn't the shepherds shepherd the flock?
You eat the fat and clothe yourselves with the wool; you slaughter the fattened sheep; you don't shepherd the flock.

The weak you haven't strengthened, the sick you haven't healed, the broken you haven't bound up, the strayed you haven't brought back, the lost you haven't sought; and with force you've ruled them, and with harshness.
And they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and became food for every beast of the field; and they were scattered.
My flock wander on all the mountains and on every high hill; over all the face of the earth my flock have been scattered, with no one searching and no one seeking.
So, shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

As I live — declares Lord GOD — because my flock has become prey and my flock has become food for every beast of the field, for lack of a shepherd, and my shepherds didn't search for my flock, and the shepherds shepherded themselves and didn't shepherd my flock —
therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:

This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against the shepherds; I'll require my flock from their hand and make them stop shepherding a flock, and the shepherds will no longer shepherd themselves. And I'll deliver my flock from their mouth, and they won't be food for them.
For this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I myself will search for my flock and seek them out.

As a shepherd seeks out his flock on the day he's among his scattered sheep, so I'll seek out my flock; and I'll deliver them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

And I'll bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the lands and bring them to their own land; and I'll shepherd them on the mountains of Israel, in the ravines and in all the habitable places of the land.

In good pasture I'll shepherd them, and on the mountain heights of Israel will be their pastureland. There they'll lie down in good pastureland, and on rich pasture they'll graze, on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will shepherd my flock, and I myself will make them lie down — declares Lord GOD.
The lost I'll seek, the strayed I'll bring back, the broken I'll bind up, the sick I'll make strong; and the fat and the strong I'll destroy. I'll shepherd them with justice.
And as for you, my flock — this is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm judging between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats.
Is it too little for you that you graze the good pasture — must you trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? And that you drink the clear water — must you foul the rest with your feet?
And my flock — must they graze what your feet have trampled and drink what your feet have fouled?
So this is what Lord GOD says to them: Look, I myself will judge between a fat sheep and a lean sheep.
Because you push with side and shoulder and thrust at all the weak with your horns, until you've scattered them abroad —
I'll save my flock, and they'll no longer be prey; and I'll judge between one sheep and another.
And I'll raise up over them one shepherd, and he will shepherd them — my servant David. He will shepherd them, and he will be their shepherd.
And I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David a prince among them. I, the LORD, have spoken.
And I'll make with them a covenant of peace and put an end to wild beasts in the land; and they'll dwell in the wilderness in safety and sleep in the forests.
And I'll make them and the places around my hill a blessing, and I'll send down the rain in its season; they'll be rains of blessing.

And the tree of the field will give its fruit, and the land will give its produce; and they'll be on their own land in safety. And they will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and deliver them from the hand of those who made them labour.
And they'll no longer be spoil for the nations, and the beasts of the land won't devour them; and they'll dwell in safety, with no one making them afraid.
And I'll establish for them a planting of renown; and they'll no longer be swept away by famine in the land, and they won't bear the insult of the nations any more.
And they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they are my people, the house of Israel — declares Lord GOD.
And you are my flock, the flock of my pasture. You are human beings; I am your God — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_35.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it,
and say to it: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Mount Seir; I'll stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolation and a waste.
Your cities I'll make a ruin, and you will be a desolation; and you will know that I am the LORD.
Because you had a perpetual enmity and delivered the people of Israel over to the sword at the time of their disaster, at the time of final punishment —
therefore, as I live — declares Lord GOD — I'll appoint you to blood, and blood will pursue you. Surely you have not hated blood, and blood will pursue you.
And I'll make Mount Seir an utter desolation, and I'll cut off from it anyone who comes or goes.
And I'll fill its mountains with its slain; your hills, your valleys and all your ravines — those slain by the sword will fall in them.
I'll make you perpetual desolations, and your cities won't be inhabited again; and you will know that I am the LORD.
Because you said, 'The two nations and the two lands will be mine, and we will take possession of them' — and the LORD was there —
therefore, as I live — declares Lord GOD — I'll act according to your anger and your jealousy, which you showed out of your hatred of them; and I'll make myself known among them when I judge you.
And you will know that I, the LORD, have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel: 'They are desolate; they've been given to us to devour.'
And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth and multiplied your words against me. I have heard.
This is what Lord GOD says: When all the earth rejoices, I'll make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I'll do to you. You will be a desolation, Mount Seir, and all Edom, all of it; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_36.t: "And you, mortal, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because the enemy has said over you, 'Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession' —

therefore prophesy and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Because, yes because, they've made you desolate and crushed you from every side, so that you became a possession for the rest of the nations, and you were taken up on people's lips and in their gossip —

therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of Lord GOD. This is what Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys, and to the desolate waste places and to the forsaken cities that have become spoil and mockery to the rest of the nations all around —

therefore this is what Lord GOD says: Surely in the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who made my land their own possession with whole-hearted joy and with scorn of self, so that its pastureland might be plundered.

So prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, in my jealousy and in my rage I have spoken, because you have borne the insult of the nations.
So this is what Lord GOD says: I raise my hand in an oath: surely the nations around you — they will bear their own insult.
And you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they are soon to come.
For look — I am for you, and I'll turn toward you; and you'll be tilled and sown.
And I'll multiply humankind on you — the whole house of Israel, all of it; and the cities will be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt.

And I'll multiply on you humankind and animals, and they'll increase and be fruitful; and I'll make you inhabited as you were before, and do better for you than at your beginnings. And you will know that I am the LORD.
And I'll make humankind walk on you — my people Israel; and they'll take possession of you, and you'll be their inheritance; and you'll no longer bereave them of children.
This is what Lord GOD says: Because they say to you, 'You devour people, and you've bereaved your nations of children' —
therefore you'll no longer devour people or bereave your nations of children — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll no longer make you hear the insult of the nations, and you'll no longer bear the reproach of the peoples; and you'll no longer cause your nations to stumble — declares Lord GOD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, the house of Israel were dwelling on their own land, and they made it unclean by their conduct and by their practices. Like the uncleanness of menstrual impurity was their conduct before me.
And I poured out my rage on them for the blood they had poured out on the land, and because they had made it unclean with their idols.
And I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed among the lands; according to their conduct and their practices I judged them.
And they came to the nations where they went, and they profaned my holy name, when it was said of them, 'These are the people of the LORD, and they've come out of his land.'
But I had pity on my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they had gone.

So say to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: It is not for your sake that I'm acting, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you have gone.

And I'll set apart as holy my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you profaned in their midst; and the nations will know that I am the LORD — declares Lord GOD — when I show myself holy among you before their eyes.
And I'll take you from the nations, gather you from all the lands and bring you to your own land.
And I'll sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; from all your uncleannesses and from all your idols I'll cleanse you.
And I'll give you a new heart, and a new spirit I'll put within you; and I'll remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
And my spirit I'll put within you, and I'll bring it about that you walk in my statutes, keep my judgements and do them.
And you'll dwell in the land I gave to your fathers; and you'll be my people, and I myself will be your God.
And I'll save you from all your uncleannesses; and I'll summon the grain and multiply it, and I won't bring famine on you.
And I'll multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you'll no longer receive the reproach of famine among the nations.
And you'll remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you'll loathe yourselves to your own faces because of your iniquities and your abominations.
It is not for your sake that I'm acting — declares Lord GOD — let that be known to you. Be ashamed and humiliated because of your ways, house of Israel!"
This is what Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I'll cause the cities to be inhabited, and the waste places will be rebuilt.
And the desolated land will be tilled, instead of lying a desolation before the eyes of everyone who passes by.
And they'll say, 'This land that was desolated has become like the garden of Eden; and the cities that were wasted and desolated and broken down are fortified and inhabited.'
And the nations that are left around you will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was broken down and planted what was desolated. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
This is what Lord GOD says: This also I'll let myself be sought for by the house of Israel, to do for them: I'll multiply their people like a flock.
Like a flock of holy offerings, like the flock of Jerusalem at her appointed feasts, so the wasted cities will be full of flocks of people; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_37.t: The hand of the LORD was on me, and he brought me out by the spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; and it was full of bones.
And he made me pass among them, all around, all around; and there they were — very many on the surface of the valley, and very dry.
And he said to me, "Mortal, will these bones live?" And I said, "Lord GOD, you know."
And he said to me, "Prophesy to these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
This is what Lord GOD says to these bones: Look, I'm bringing breath into you, and you will live.
And I'll put sinews on you, bring up flesh over you and cover you with skin, and I'll put breath in you, and you will live; and you will know that I am the LORD."
So I prophesied as I was commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and a rattling; and the bones drew near, bone to its bone.
And I looked, and there were sinews on them, and flesh came up, and skin covered them over from above; but there was no breath in them.

And he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, mortal, and say to the breath: This is what Lord GOD says: From the four winds come, breath, and blow on these killed ones, so that they may live."
So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived and stood on their feet — a very, very great army.
And he said to me, "Mortal, these bones are all the house of Israel. Look, they're saying, 'Our bones have dried up and our hope has perished; we're cut off completely.'
So prophesy and say to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm about to open your graves and bring you up from your graves, my people; and I'll bring you to the land of Israel.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from your graves, my people.
And I'll put my spirit in you, and you will live; and I'll set you down on your own land. And you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it — declares the LORD."
And the word of the LORD came to me:

"And you, mortal, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and for the people of Israel, his associates'; and take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and all the house of Israel, his associates.'
And bring them together, one to the other, into a single stick; and they'll become one in your hand.
And when the children of your people say to you, 'Won't you tell us what these mean for you?' —

speak to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm about to take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his associates, and I'll put them with it — with the stick of Judah — and make them a single stick; and they'll be one in my hand.
And the sticks you write on will be in your hand where they can see.

And speak to them: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm about to take the people of Israel from among the nations where they've gone; I'll gather them from all around and bring them to their own land.
And I'll make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king will be king over all of them. They'll no longer be two nations, and won't be divided into two kingdoms any more.

And they'll no longer make themselves unclean with their idols and their detestable things and all their transgressions; and I'll save them from all their dwelling places in which they have sinned, and I'll cleanse them. And they'll be my people, and I myself will be their God.
And my servant David will be king over them, and they'll all have one shepherd; and they'll walk in my judgements, keep my statutes and do them.

And they'll dwell on the land I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt. And they'll dwell on it — they and their children and their children's children — for ever; and David my servant will be their prince for ever.
And I'll make with them a covenant of peace; it will be a perpetual covenant with them. I'll establish them and multiply them, and I'll put my sanctuary in their midst for ever.
And my dwelling place will be over them; and I'll be their God, and they'll be my people.
And the nations will know that I, the LORD, am the one who sets Israel apart as holy, when my sanctuary is in their midst for ever."

ezekiel_38.t: And the word of the LORD came to me:
"Mortal, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

And I'll turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out — you and all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them magnificently clothed, a great company with body shield and shield, all of them wielding swords —
Persia, Cush and Put with them, all of them with shield and helmet;
Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah from the remotest parts of the north, and all its troops — many peoples with you.
Be prepared and prepare yourself, you and all your company that have assembled to you; and you'll be their guard.

After many days you'll be mustered; at the end of the years you'll come into a land restored from the sword, gathered from many peoples, on the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual desolation. Its people have been brought out from the peoples, and they're all dwelling in safety.
And you'll go up; like a storm you'll come; like a cloud covering the land you'll be — you and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
This is what Lord GOD says: And on that day thoughts will come up in your heart, and you'll plan an evil plan.
And you'll say: I'll go up against a land of unwalled villages; I'll come against those at peace, dwelling in safety — all of them living with no wall, no bars and no gates —

to plunder plunder and take spoil as spoil; to turn your hand against inhabited waste places and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions, who dwell at the centre of the earth.

Sheba and Dedan and the traders of Tarshish and all its young lions will say to you: Have you come to plunder plunder? Have you assembled your company to take spoil as spoil — to carry away silver and gold, to take livestock and possessions, to plunder great plunder?
So prophesy, mortal, and say to Gog: This is what Lord GOD says: On that day, when my people Israel are dwelling in safety, won't you know it?
And you'll come from your place, from the remotest parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding horses — a great company and a mighty army.

And you'll go up against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. At the end of the days it will happen, and I'll bring you against my land, so that the nations may know me, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes, Gog.
This is what Lord GOD says: Are you the one I spoke of in former days through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days, for years, that I would bring you against them?
And on that day, the day Gog comes against the land of Israel — declares Lord GOD — my rage will rise in my anger.
And in my jealousy, in the fire of my wrath, I have spoken: surely on that day there will be a great earthquake on the land of Israel.

And the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the beasts of the field, every creeping thing that creeps on the ground and every human being on the face of the ground will shake before me. And the mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.
And I'll summon a sword against him on all my mountains — declares Lord GOD; each man's sword will be against his brother.
And I'll enter into judgement with him by pestilence and by blood; and an overflowing rain and hailstones, fire and sulphur, I'll rain down on him and on his troops and on the many peoples with him.
And I'll show myself great and show myself holy and make myself known before the eyes of many nations; and they will know that I am the LORD."

ezekiel_39.t: "And you, mortal, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what Lord GOD says: Look, I'm against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
And I'll turn you around and lead you on, and bring you up from the remotest parts of the north, and bring you against the mountains of Israel.
And I'll strike your bow out of your left hand and make your arrows fall from your right hand.
On the mountains of Israel you'll fall — you and all your troops and the peoples with you. To birds of prey of every kind and to the beasts of the field I'll give you for food.
On the open field you'll fall, for I have spoken — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll send fire on Magog and on those who dwell in safety in the coastlands; and they will know that I am the LORD.
And my holy name I'll make known in the midst of my people Israel, and I won't let my holy name be profaned any more; and the nations will know that I am the LORD, holy in Israel.
Look, it's coming, and it will happen — declares Lord GOD. That is the day I have spoken of.
And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out and kindle and burn weapons — shield and body shield, bow and arrows, hand-staff and spear; and they'll make fire with them for seven years.

And they won't carry wood from the field or cut it from the forests, because they'll make fire with the weapons; and they'll plunder those who plundered them and take spoil from those who took spoil from them — declares Lord GOD.

And on that day I'll give Gog a place there, a burial site in Israel: the Valley of the Travellers, east of the sea. It will block the way of those who travel; and they'll bury Gog and all his multitude there, and they'll call it the Valley of Hamon-gog.
And the house of Israel will bury them for seven months, to cleanse the land.
And all the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown, on the day I show myself glorious — declares Lord GOD.

And they'll set apart men on continual duty, passing through the land, burying those who travel — the ones left on the face of the land — to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they'll make a search.
And those who pass through will pass through the land; and when one sees a human bone, he'll build a marker beside it, until the buriers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
And the name of a city there is also Hamonah. And they'll cleanse the land.

"And you, mortal — this is what Lord GOD says: Say to the birds of every wing and to every beast of the field: Assemble and come; gather from all around to my sacrifice, which I'm sacrificing for you — a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel — and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
The flesh of warriors you'll eat, and the blood of the princes of the earth you'll drink — rams, lambs and goats, bulls, all of them fatlings of Bashan.
And you'll eat fat to satiety and drink blood to drunkenness, from my sacrifice that I've sacrificed for you.
And you'll be satisfied at my table with horse and charioteer, warrior and every man of war — declares Lord GOD.
And I'll set my glory among the nations; and all the nations will see the judgement I have executed and the hand I have laid on them.
And the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God, from that day onwards.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they acted unfaithfully against me; and I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword.
According to their uncleanness and their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them.
So this is what Lord GOD says: Now I'll turn back the captivity of Jacob and have compassion on all the house of Israel; and I'll be jealous for my holy name.
And they'll bear their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness by which they acted unfaithfully against me, when they dwell on their own land in safety with no one disturbing them.
when I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, and show myself holy through them before the eyes of many nations.
And they will know that I am the LORD their God, in that I sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them to their own land; and I'll leave none of them there any more.
And I won't hide my face from them any more, because I've poured out my spirit on the house of Israel — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_40.t: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck — on that very day the hand of the LORD was on me, and he brought me there.
In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain; and on it, to the south, was something like the structure of a city.
And he brought me there, and there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a linen cord in his hand and a measuring reed; and he was standing in the gate.

And the man spoke to me: "Mortal, see with your eyes and hear with your ears and set your heart on all that I'm about to show you — you've been brought here in order to be shown it. Tell everything you see to the house of Israel."

And there was a wall on the outside of the house, all around, all around. In the man's hand was the measuring reed, six cubits — by the long cubit, a cubit and a handbreadth. And he measured the breadth of the structure: one reed; and the height: one reed.
And he went to the gate that faces east and went up its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate: one reed deep; and the other threshold: one reed deep.
And each guard chamber: one reed long and one reed wide; and between the guard chambers, five cubits. And the threshold of the gate, beside the porch of the gate on the inside: one reed.
And he measured the porch of the gate on the inside: one reed.
And he measured the porch of the gate: eight cubits; and its jambs: two cubits. And the porch of the gate was on the inside.
And the guard chambers of the east gate: three on one side and three on the other — one measurement for all three; and one measurement for the jambs on either side.
And he measured the width of the gate's entrance: ten cubits; the width of the gateway: thirteen cubits.
And a barrier in front of the guard chambers: one cubit; and one cubit a barrier on the other side. And each guard chamber: six cubits on one side and six on the other.
And he measured the gate from the roof of one guard chamber to the roof of the other: a width of twenty-five cubits, entrance opposite entrance.
And he made the jambs sixty cubits; and to the jamb was the court, the gate all around, all around.
And from the front of the outer gate's entrance to the front of the porch of the inner gate: fifty cubits.

And recessed windows opened onto the guard chambers and their jambs, inward to the gate, all around, all around; and so also onto the porches. There were windows all around, all around, inward; and on the jambs, palm trees.
And he brought me into the outer court; and there were rooms, and a pavement made for the court all around, all around — thirty rooms on the pavement.
And the pavement was at the side of the gates, matching the length of the gates — the lower pavement.
And he measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court, on the outside: a hundred cubits — on the east and on the north.
And the gate of the outer court that faces north — he measured its length and its width.
And its guard chambers: three on one side and three on the other; its jambs and porches were the same measurement as the first gate — fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
And its windows, porches and palm trees were the same measurement as the gate that faces east; one goes up to it by seven steps, and its porches were in front of them.
And a gate to the inner court was opposite the gate on the north and on the east; and he measured from gate to gate: a hundred cubits.
And he led me toward the south, and there was a gate facing south; and he measured its jambs and porches according to these measurements.
And it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around, like these windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
And its stairway was seven steps, and its porches were in front of them; and it had palm trees, one on each side, on its jambs.
And the inner court had a gate facing south; and he measured from gate to gate on the south: a hundred cubits.
And he brought me into the inner court by the south gate; and he measured the south gate according to these measurements.
And its guard chambers, jambs and porches were according to these measurements; it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
And porches all around, all around: twenty-five cubits long and five wide.
And its porches faced the outer court, and palm trees were on its jambs; and its ascent was eight steps.
And he brought me into the inner court toward the east; and he measured the gate according to these measurements.
And its guard chambers, jambs and porches were according to these measurements; it had windows, and its porches had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
And its porches faced the outer court, with palm trees on its jambs on either side; and its ascent was eight steps.
And he brought me to the north gate, and he measured according to these measurements —
its guard chambers, its jambs and porches; and it had windows all around, all around — fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide.
And its jambs faced the outer court, with palm trees on its jambs on either side; and its ascent was eight steps.
And there was a room, with its entrance at the jambs of the gateways; there they rinse the burnt offering.
And in the porch of the gate: two tables on one side and two on the other, on which to slaughter the burnt offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering.
And at the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate: two tables; and at the other side, belonging to the porch of the gate: two tables.
Four tables on one side and four on the other, at the side of the gate — eight tables, on which they slaughter.

And four tables for the burnt offering, of hewn stone: a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide and one cubit high; on them they set down the equipment with which they slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
And hooks, one handbreadth long, were fixed inside, all around, all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering.
And outside the inner gate were rooms for the singers, in the inner court, at the side of the north gate, facing south; one was at the side of the east gate, facing north.
And he spoke to me: "This room facing south is for the priests who keep the charge of the house;
and the room facing north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. They are the sons of Zadok, who among the sons of Levi draw near to the LORD to serve him."
And he measured the court: a hundred cubits long and a hundred wide, a square; and the altar was in front of the house.

And he brought me to the porch of the house, and he measured the jambs of the porch: five cubits on one side and five on the other; and the width of the doorway: three cubits on one side and three on the other.
The porch was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide; one goes up to it by steps. And there were columns at the jambs, one on each side.

ezekiel_41.t: And he brought me to the great hall, and he measured the jambs: six cubits wide on one side and six on the other — the width of the tent.
And the width of the entrance: ten cubits; the sides of the entrance: five cubits on each side. And he measured its length: forty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits.
And he went inside and measured the jamb of the entrance: two cubits; the entrance itself: six cubits; and the width of the entrance: seven cubits.
And he measured its length: twenty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits, at the front of the great hall. And he said to me, "This is the holy of holies."
And he measured the wall of the house: six cubits; and the width of each side chamber: four cubits, all around, all around the house, all around.

And the side chambers, side chamber upon side chamber: three and thirty times. They went into the wall belonging to the house, for the side chambers, all around, all around, so as to be held fast — and they were not held fast in the wall of the house itself.

And it broadened and wound upward, upward, to the side chambers, because the house's surrounding structure went upward, upward, all around, all around the house; so the house grew wider as it rose. And so one goes up from the lowest storey to the highest by way of the middle one.
And I saw that the house had a raised base all around, all around; the foundations of the side chambers were a full reed — six long cubits.
The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers: five cubits. What was left free was the open space of the side chambers belonging to the house.
And between the rooms: a width of twenty cubits around the house, all around, all around.
And the entrance of the side chambers opened onto the open space: one entrance on the north and one on the south. And the width of the open place: five cubits all around, all around.
And the structure at the front of the separate place, on the western side: seventy cubits wide; the wall of the structure five cubits thick all around, all around; and its length ninety cubits.
And he measured the house: a hundred cubits long; and the separate place and the building and its walls: a hundred cubits long.
And the width of the front of the house and of the separate place, on the east: a hundred cubits.
And he measured the length of the structure at the front of the separate place behind it, and its galleries on either side: a hundred cubits. And the inner great hall, and the porches of the court,

the thresholds and the recessed windows and the galleries all around, for all three of them — opposite the threshold, wood panelling all around, all around; the floor up to the windows; and the windows were covered over.
over the entrance and as far as the inner house, and outside, and on the whole wall all around, all around, inside and outside: measured spaces.
And it was made with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between one cherub and the next; and each cherub had two faces:
a human face toward the palm tree on one side, and a young lion's face toward the palm tree on the other. It was made so for the whole house all around, all around.
From the floor up to above the entrance the cherubim and the palm trees were made; and the wall of the great hall.
The great hall: a squared doorpost; and the front of the holy place — the appearance of one was like the appearance of the other.
The altar was of wood, three cubits high and two cubits long; and it had its corners; its length and its sides were of wood. And he spoke to me: "This is the table that is before the LORD."
And the great hall and the holy place each had two doors.
And the doors had two leaves apiece, two turning leaves — two for the one door and two for the other.
And on them, on the doors of the great hall, cherubim and palm trees were made, just as they were made for the walls; and there was a wooden canopy at the front of the porch, outside.
And recessed windows and palm trees on either side, on the sides of the porch; and the side chambers of the house, and the canopies.

ezekiel_42.t: And he brought me out to the outer court by the way toward the north, and brought me to the room that faced the separate place and the structure, toward the north.
At the front of the hundred-cubit length was the north entrance; and the width was fifty cubits.
Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court, and opposite the pavement belonging to the outer court, was gallery facing gallery, in three storeys.
And in front of the rooms was a walk ten cubits wide toward the inner part, a way of one cubit; and their entrances faced north.
And the upper rooms were shortened, because the galleries took space from them, more than from the lower and the middle ones of the structure.
For they were in three storeys, and they had no columns like the columns of the courts; so the upper storey was set back, more than the lower and the middle ones, from the ground up.
And the wall outside, alongside the rooms, on the side of the outer court in front of the rooms — its length was fifty cubits.
For the length of the rooms belonging to the outer court was fifty cubits; and at the front of the great hall, a hundred cubits.
And below these rooms was the entry from the east, as one comes to them from the outer court.
In the thickness of the court's wall, on the east, facing the separate place and facing the structure: rooms.
And a way ran in front of them, like the appearance of the rooms on the north — as their length, so their width; and all their exits, and according to their plans and their entrances.
And like the entrances of the rooms on the south: an entrance at the head of a way, a way in front of the matching wall, on the east as one comes to them.

And he said to me, "The rooms on the north and the rooms on the south that face the separate place — they are the holy rooms, where the priests who draw near to the LORD eat the holiest of the holy things. There they set down the holiest of the holy things: the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering — because the place is holy.

When the priests go in, they are not to go out from the holy place into the outer court; there they set down the garments they serve in, because they are holy. And they put on other garments, and draw near to what belongs to the people."
And he finished the measurements of the inner house, and brought me out by the gate that faces east, and measured it all around, all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
The south side he measured: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He turned to the west side and measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He measured it on its four sides. It had a wall all around, all around: five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate between the holy and the common.

ezekiel_43.t: And he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east; and his voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his glory.

And it was like the appearance of the vision that I saw, like the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Kebar. And I fell on my face.
And the glory of the LORD came into the house by way of the gate that faces east.
And a spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and there, the glory of the LORD filled the house.
And I heard someone speaking to me from the house; and a man was standing beside me.

And he said to me: "Mortal, the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the people of Israel for ever. And the house of Israel will not make my holy name unclean again — they and their kings — by their whoring and by the corpses of their kings at their high places,

when they put their threshold against my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only the wall between me and them; and they made my holy name unclean by the abominations they committed. And I made an end of them in my anger.
Now let them put their whoring and the corpses of their kings far away from me, and I will dwell among them for ever.
You, mortal, describe the house to the house of Israel, and let them be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.

And if they are ashamed of all that they have done, make known to them the design of the house and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, and all its designs, and all its statutes, and all its designs, and all its laws; and write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep all its design and all its statutes and do them.
This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, all its territory all around, all around, is a holy of holies. This is the law of the house.

And these are the measurements of the altar in cubits — the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: the gutter, a cubit deep; a cubit wide; and its rim on its edge all around, one span. And this is the base of the altar.
And from the gutter at the ground to the lower ledge: two cubits, with a setback of one cubit. And from the small ledge to the great ledge: four cubits, with a setback of one cubit.
And the altar hearth: four cubits; and from the hearth upward, the four horns.
And the altar hearth: twelve cubits long by twelve wide, square, on all four sides.
And the ledge: fourteen cubits long by fourteen wide, on all four sides; the rim around it, half a cubit; and its gutter, a cubit all around. And its steps face east.
And he said to me: "Mortal, this is what Lord GOD says: These are the statutes of the altar on the day it is made, to offer up a burnt offering on it and to dash blood on it.
And you shall give to the priests, the Levites who are of the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to me — declares Lord GOD — to serve me, a bull, a young one of the herd, for a sin offering.
And you shall take some of its blood and put it on its four horns, on the four corners of the ledge and on the rim all around; and so purify it from sin and make atonement for it.
And you shall take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burnt in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
And on the second day you shall bring near a male goat of the goats, unblemished, for a sin offering; and they shall purify the altar from sin as they purified it from sin with the bull.
When you finish purifying it from sin, you shall bring near a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished, and a ram from the flock, unblemished.
And you shall bring them near before the LORD; and the priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
