Seven days you shall offer a male goat as a sin offering each day; and a bull, a young one of the herd, and a ram from the flock, unblemished, they shall offer.
Seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; and so they shall install it.
And they shall complete the days. And from the eighth day onwards the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your peace sacrifices; and I will accept you — declares Lord GOD."

ezekiel_44.t: And he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east; and it was shut.
And the LORD said to me: "This gate is to be shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall go in by it, because the LORD the God of Israel has gone in by it; and it shall be shut.
As for the prince — a prince, he may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He is to come in by way of the porch of the gate, and go out the same way."
And he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house; and I looked, and there — the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD. And I fell on my face.

And the LORD said to me: "Mortal, set your heart and see with your eyes and hear with your ears everything I am speaking to you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its laws. And set your heart to the entrance of the house, with all the exits of the sanctuary.
And you shall say to rebellion, to the house of Israel: This is what Lord GOD says: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel!

when you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it — my house — while you brought near my food, the fat and the blood; and they broke my covenant, on top of all your abominations.
And you did not keep the charge of my holy things; instead you appointed keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.
This is what Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised of heart and uncircumcised of flesh, shall come into my sanctuary — none of the foreigners who are among the people of Israel.
But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who strayed from me after their idols — they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall be servants in my sanctuary, overseers at the gates of the house and serving the house. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became for the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity — therefore I have raised my hand in an oath against them, declares Lord GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall not draw near to me to serve me as priests, nor draw near to any of my holy things, to the holiest of the holy things; and they shall bear their disgrace and the abominations they have done.
And I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is done in it.

But the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me — they shall draw near to me to serve me, and they shall stand before me to bring near to me fat and blood, declares Lord GOD.
They shall come into my sanctuary, and they shall draw near to my table to serve me; and they shall keep my charge.
And when they come into the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen garments; no wool is to come on them when they serve at the gates of the inner court and inside.
Linen head-dresses on their heads, and linen undergarments on their loins. They are not to gird themselves with anything that makes them sweat.

And when they go out to the outer court — to the outer court, to the people — they are to take off the garments they serve in and set them down in the holy rooms; and they put on other garments, so as not to consecrate the people with their garments.
And they are not to shave their heads, and not to let their hair go loose; they are to keep their hair trimmed.
And no priest is to drink wine when they come into the inner court.
And they are not to take a widow or a divorced woman as a wife, but virgins from the offspring of the house of Israel; and a widow who is the widow of a priest they may take.
And they are to instruct my people in the difference between the holy and the common, and make known to them the difference between the unclean and the clean.
And in a dispute they are to stand to give judgement; they are to judge it by my judgements. And they are to keep my laws and my statutes at all my appointed times, and keep my sabbaths holy.
And he is not to go near a dead person, and so become unclean; only for a father or a mother, a son or a daughter, a brother or an unmarried sister may they make themselves unclean.
And after his cleansing they shall count seven days for him.
And on the day he goes into the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he is to bring near his sin offering — declares Lord GOD.
And this shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. And you are to give them no holding in Israel: I am their holding.
The grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering — they eat them; and every devoted thing in Israel is theirs.

And the best of all the first fruits of everything, and every contribution of everything, from all your contributions, belongs to the priests. And the best of your dough you are to give to the priest, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
The priests are not to eat any carcass or torn animal, whether bird or beast.

ezekiel_45.t: And when you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to offer up a contribution to the LORD, a holy portion out of the land: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. It is holy in all its territory all around.
Of this there shall be for the holy place five hundred by five hundred, square all around; and fifty cubits of pasture land for it all around.
And from this measured area you are to measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand; and in it shall be the sanctuary, a holy of holies.
It is a holy portion out of the land; it belongs to the priests who serve the sanctuary, who draw near to serve the LORD; and it shall be a place for their houses, and a holy place for the sanctuary.
And twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide shall belong to the Levites who serve the house, as their holding: twenty rooms.
And as the holding of the city you are to give five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the holy contribution. It belongs to all the house of Israel.

And to the prince: on either side of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, in front of the holy contribution and in front of the holding of the city, from the west side westward and from the east side eastward; its length corresponding to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
As for the land, it will be his as a holding in Israel; and my princes will no longer oppress my people, and they will give the land to the house of Israel by their tribes.
This is what Lord GOD says: Enough of you, princes of Israel! Put away violence and destruction, and do justice and righteousness. Lift your evictions off my people — declares Lord GOD.
You are to have balances of righteousness, an ephah of righteousness and a bath of righteousness.
The ephah and the bath are to be of one measure, so that the bath holds a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer is the standard for both.
And the shekel shall be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
This is the contribution you are to offer up: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
And the prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath: a tenth of a bath from each cor — ten baths make a homer, since ten baths make a homer.

And one sheep from the flock, one from every two hundred, from the well-watered land of Israel — for a grain offering, a burnt offering and peace sacrifices, to make atonement for them, declares Lord GOD.
All the people of the land shall be bound to this contribution to the prince in Israel.

And it falls to the prince to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offering and the drink offering at the festivals, at the new moons and on the sabbaths, at all the appointed times of the house of Israel. He is to provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering and the peace sacrifices, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
This is what Lord GOD says: In the first month, on the first of the month, you are to take a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished, and purify the sanctuary from sin.

And the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorpost of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorpost of the gate of the inner court.
And you are to do the same on the seventh of the month, for anyone who errs and for the simple; and so make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you are to have the Passover, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread is to be eaten.
And on that day the prince is to provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.
And for the seven days of the festival he is to provide a burnt offering to the LORD: seven bulls and seven rams, unblemished, each day for the seven days; and a sin offering, a male goat, each day.
And a grain offering: an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he is to provide the same for the seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering and oil.

ezekiel_46.t: This is what Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to be shut the six working days; on the sabbath day it is to be opened, and on the day of the new moon it is to be opened.

And the prince is to come by way of the porch of the gate from outside and stand at the doorpost of the gate; and the priests offer his burnt offering and his peace sacrifices. He bows down at the threshold of the gate and goes out; and the gate is not shut until the evening.
And the people of the land bow down at the entrance of that gate on the sabbaths and on the new moons, before the LORD.
And the burnt offering the prince brings near to the LORD on the sabbath day: six lambs, unblemished, and a ram, unblemished.
And a grain offering: an ephah for the ram; and for the lambs, a grain offering as much as he chooses to give; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
And on the day of the new moon: a bull, a young one of the herd, unblemished; and six lambs and a ram — all unblemished.
And an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram he provides as a grain offering; and for the lambs, as much as his hand can afford; and oil, a hin to the ephah.
And when the prince comes in, he comes by way of the porch of the gate, and goes out the same way.

And when the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed times: whoever comes in by the north gate to bow down goes out by the south gate, and whoever comes in by the south gate goes out by the north gate. No one returns by the gate he came in by; he goes out opposite it.
And the prince is among them: when they come in, he comes in; and when they go out, they go out together.
And at the festivals and at the appointed times the grain offering is an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he chooses to give; and oil, a hin to the ephah.

And when the prince provides a freewill offering — a burnt offering or peace sacrifices, a freewill offering to the LORD — the gate that faces east is opened for him, and he offers his burnt offering and his peace sacrifices as he does on the sabbath day; then he goes out, and the gate is shut after he has gone out.
And a lamb, a year old, unblemished, you are to provide as a burnt offering each day to the LORD; morning by morning you are to provide it.

And a grain offering you are to provide with it, morning by morning: a sixth of an ephah, and a third of a hin of oil, to moisten the fine flour — a grain offering to the LORD, a perpetual statute, continually.
They are to provide the lamb, the grain offering and the oil, morning by morning: a continual burnt offering.
This is what Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance; it belongs to his sons — it is their holding by inheritance.
And if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it is his until the year of liberty, and then it returns to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons; it shall be theirs.

And the prince is not to take from the inheritance of the people, oppressing them out of their holding. From his own holding he is to give his sons an inheritance, so that my people are not scattered, each from his holding.
And he brought me by the entrance at the side of the gate, to the holy rooms for the priests, which face north; and there was a place there, in the far corners to the west.

And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they bake the grain offering, so as not to carry them out into the outer court and consecrate the people."
And he brought me out to the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court; and there was a court in each corner of the court, a court in each corner of the court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty wide: one measurement for all four, set in the corners.
And a row of masonry ran around inside them, around all four; and cooking hearths were made under the rows all around.
And he said to me, "These are the kitchens, where those who serve the house boil the people's sacrifice."

ezekiel_47.t: And he brought me back to the entrance of the house; and there were waters going out from under the threshold of the house eastward, because the front of the house faces east. And the waters were going down from under the south side of the house, south of the altar.
And he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me round the outside to the outer gate, by the way that faces east; and there were waters trickling from the south side.
When the man went out eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and made me pass through the waters: ankle-deep.
And he measured off a thousand and made me pass through the waters: knee-deep. And he measured off a thousand and made me pass through: waist-deep.
And he measured off a thousand — a river I could not pass through, because the waters had risen: deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
And he said to me, "Do you see, mortal?" And he led me and brought me back to the bank of the river.
When I returned, there at the bank of the river were very many trees, on both sides.
And he said to me: "These waters are going out to the eastern region and will go down to the Arabah and come to the sea; when they are brought out into the sea, the waters will be healed.

And every living creature that swarms, wherever the two rivers go, will live; and there will be very many fish, because these waters have come there and they will be healed. And everything will live wherever the river goes.
And fishermen will stand beside it; from En-gedi to En-eglaim there will be a place for spreading nets. Their fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.
Its swamps and its marshes will not be healed; they are given over to salt.

And by the river, on its bank on either side, every tree for food will grow. Its foliage will not wither and its fruit will not fail; month by month it will bear early fruit, because its waters come out from the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its foliage for healing.
This is what Lord GOD says: This is the boundary by which you are to give the land as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph, two portions.
And you are to divide it as an inheritance, each alike with his brother, the land I raised my hand in an oath to give to your fathers; and this land will fall to you as an inheritance.
And this is the boundary of the land. On the north side: from the Great Sea by the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the territory of Damascus and the territory of Hamath; Hazer-hattikon, which is on the border of Hauran.
And the boundary runs from the sea: Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus, and north northward, and the territory of Hamath. This is the north side.
And the east side: between Hauran and Damascus and Gilead and the land of Israel — the Jordan; from the border to the eastern sea you are to measure. This is the east side.
And the south side, southward: from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea. This is the south side, southward.
And the west side: the Great Sea, from the border across from Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
And you are to divide this land among yourselves, according to the tribes of Israel.

And you are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the sojourners who sojourn among you, who have fathered children among you. They are to be to you as the native-born among the people of Israel; with you they are to have an inheritance allotted among the tribes of Israel.
And in whatever tribe the sojourner sojourns, there you are to give him his inheritance — declares Lord GOD.

ezekiel_48.t: And these are the names of the tribes. From the northern end, beside the road of Hethlon, to Lebo-hamath, Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus northward, beside Hamath — and the east side and the west side shall be his: Dan, one portion.
And beside the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side: Asher, one portion.
And beside the border of Asher, from the east side and to the west side: Naphtali, one portion.
And beside the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side: Manasseh, one portion.
And beside the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side: Ephraim, one portion.
And beside the border of Ephraim, from the east side and to the west side: Reuben, one portion.
And beside the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side: Judah, one portion.

And beside the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, is the contribution you are to offer up: twenty-five thousand wide, and in length like one of the tribal portions, from the east side to the west side; and the sanctuary is in the midst of it.
The contribution you are to offer up to the LORD: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.

And the holy contribution belongs to these, to the priests: on the north, twenty-five thousand; on the west, ten thousand wide; on the east, ten thousand wide; and on the south, twenty-five thousand long. And the sanctuary of the LORD is in the midst of it.
It is for the priests, the consecrated ones from the sons of Zadok, who kept my charge, who did not go astray when the people of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.
And it is for them a contribution out of the contribution of the land, a holy of holies, beside the border of the Levites.
And the Levites, alongside the border of the priests: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. The whole length, twenty-five thousand; the width, ten thousand.
And they are not to sell any of it, and none may exchange it, nor may the choicest of the land be transferred; for it is holy to the LORD.
And the five thousand that remain in the width, alongside the twenty-five thousand, is common land for the city, for dwelling and for pasture land; and the city is in the midst of it.

And these are its measurements: the north side, four thousand five hundred; the south side, four thousand five hundred; the east side, four thousand five hundred; and the west side, four thousand five hundred.
And the city has pasture land: two hundred and fifty on the north, two hundred and fifty on the south, two hundred and fifty on the east, and two hundred and fifty on the west.

And what remains in the length, alongside the holy contribution — ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the west; it lies alongside the holy contribution, and its produce is food for those who work the city.
And those who work the city work it, drawn from all the tribes of Israel.
The whole contribution: twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand, a square. You are to offer up the holy contribution together with the holding of the city.

And what remains is for the prince, on either side of the holy contribution and of the holding of the city, in front of the twenty-five thousand of the contribution as far as the eastern border; and westward, in front of the twenty-five thousand as far as the western border, alongside the tribal portions — for the prince. And the holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house are in the midst of it.
And the holding of the Levites and the holding of the city lie in the midst of what belongs to the prince: between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, it is the prince's.
And the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.
And beside the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side: Simeon, one portion.
And beside the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side: Issachar, one portion.
And beside the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side: Zebulun, one portion.
And beside the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side: Gad, one portion.
And beside the border of Gad, on the south side southward: the border runs from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, the Wadi, to the Great Sea.
This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel; and these are their portions — declares Lord GOD.
And these are the exits of the city. On the north side, four thousand five hundred by measure —
and the gates of the city are named for the tribes of Israel: three gates on the north — the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one.
And on the east side, four thousand five hundred, and three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one.
And the south side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; the gate of Zebulun, one.
The west side, four thousand five hundred; their gates, three: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; the gate of Naphtali, one.
The circuit: eighteen thousand. And the name of the city from that day: The LORD Is There.

ezra_1.t: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD from the mouth of Jeremiah would be completed, the LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent out a proclamation through his whole kingdom — and put it in writing too. It said:

"This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: 'The LORD, the God of the heavens, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he himself has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
"'Any of you from all his people — may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel. He's the God who is in Jerusalem.

"'And everyone still left, wherever he's living as a foreigner — let the people of his place support him with silver and gold, with property and cattle, along with the freewill offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.'"

Then the heads of the ancestral houses of Judah and Benjamin got up, and the priests and the Levites — everyone whose spirit God had stirred — to go up and build the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem.
And all their neighbours strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with property and cattle and precious things, besides everything that was freely offered.
And King Cyrus brought out the articles of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods.
Cyrus king of Persia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
This was the count: thirty gold dishes, a thousand silver dishes, twenty-nine knives,
thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of a second sort, and a thousand other articles.
That was five thousand four hundred articles of gold and silver in all. Sheshbazzar brought all of it up when the exiles were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

ezra_2.t: These are the people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exile — the ones Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile to Babylon — and who came back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own city —
those who came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the descendants of Parosh — two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Shephatiah — three hundred and seventy-two;
the descendants of Arah — seven hundred and seventy-five;
the descendants of Pahath-moab, of the line of Jeshua and Joab — two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the descendants of Elam — one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Zattu — nine hundred and forty-five;
the descendants of Zaccai — seven hundred and sixty;
the descendants of Bani — six hundred and forty-two;
the descendants of Bebai — six hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Azgad — one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
the descendants of Adonikam — six hundred and sixty-six;
the descendants of Bigvai — two thousand and fifty-six;
the descendants of Adin — four hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Ater, of the line of Hezekiah — ninety-eight;
the descendants of Bezai — three hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Jorah — a hundred and twelve;
the descendants of Hashum — two hundred and twenty-three;
the descendants of Gibbar — ninety-five;
the people of Bethlehem — a hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Netophah — fifty-six;
the men of Anathoth — a hundred and twenty-eight;
the people of Azmaveth — forty-two;
the people of Kiriath-arim, Kephirah and Beeroth — seven hundred and forty-three;
the people of Ramah and Geba — six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas — a hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai — two hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Nebo — fifty-two;
the people of Magbish — a hundred and fifty-six;
the descendants of the other Elam — one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the descendants of Harim — three hundred and twenty;
the people of Lod, Hadid and Ono — seven hundred and twenty-five;
the people of Jericho — three hundred and forty-five;
the people of Senaah — three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua — nine hundred and seventy-three;
the descendants of Immer — one thousand and fifty-two;
the descendants of Pashhur — one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the descendants of Harim — one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the line of Hodaviah — seventy-four.
The singers: the descendants of Asaph — a hundred and twenty-eight.
The gatekeepers' descendants: those of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita and Shobai — a hundred and thirty-nine in all.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Siaha, Padon,
Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub,
Hagab, Shalmai, Hanan,
Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah,
Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam,
Uzza, Paseah, Besai,
Asnah, Meunim, Nephussim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants: Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda,
Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim and Ami.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants — three hundred and ninety-two.
And these are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan and Immer, but couldn't declare their ancestral house or their descent, whether they were from Israel:
the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah and Nekoda — six hundred and fifty-two.
And from the descendants of the priests: the descendants of Habaiah, of Hakkoz, and of Barzillai — who'd taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These men searched for their register among those enrolled by genealogy, and it wasn't found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
And the Tirshatha told them they weren't to eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand with Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together — forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants — seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven of them — and they had two hundred male and female singers.
Their horses numbered seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules, two hundred and forty-five;
their camels, four hundred and thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And some of the heads of the ancestral houses, when they came to the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem, made freewill offerings for the house of God, to erect it on its site.
According to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand darics of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and a hundred priestly tunics.
The priests and the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants settled in their cities — and all Israel in their cities.

ezra_3.t: When the seventh month came, and the Israelites were in their cities, the people gathered as one man in Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak got up, with his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel to offer up burnt offerings on it, as it's written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
And they set the altar on its foundations, because they were in terror of the peoples of the lands; and they offered up burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening.
And they kept the festival of booths, as it's written, and the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance for each day, on its own day;

and after that the continual burnt offering, and the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed times of the LORD that are set apart as holy, and for everyone who made a freewill offering to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began offering burnt offerings to the LORD — but the temple of the LORD hadn't been founded yet.

And they gave silver to the masons and the craftsmen, and food and drink and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, under the permission Cyrus king of Persia had granted them.

In the second year after they came to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak made a start, with the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites and everyone who'd come back from the captivity to Jerusalem; and they appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work on the house of the LORD.

And Jeshua took his place with his sons and his brothers, and Kadmiel with his sons, the sons of Judah, together, to oversee the men doing the work on the house of God — and the sons of Henadad too, with their sons and their brothers, the Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, they appointed the priests, robed, with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the directions of David king of Israel.

And they sang back and forth, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "For he is good, for his steadfast love is upon Israel for ever." And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

And many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the ancestral houses, the old men who'd seen the first house, wept out loud when this house was founded in front of their eyes; and many others lifted up their voices with a shout of joy and gladness.
And nobody could tell the sound of the shout of gladness from the sound of the people's weeping; because the people were shouting a great shout, and the sound was heard far off.

ezra_4.t: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel.

So they came to Zerubbabel and the heads of the ancestral houses and said to them, "Let us build with you. We seek your God just as you do, and we've been sacrificing to him ever since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here."

But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel said to them, "It's not for you and us to build a house for our God. We ourselves, together, will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us."
Then the people of the land set about making the hands of the people of Judah slack, and they frightened them out of building,
and they hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia and on into the reign of Darius king of Persia.
And in the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote out an accusation against the people living in Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of his colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; the letter was written in Aramaic script and translated into Aramaic.
Rehum the commissioner and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter concerning Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, as follows —
then Rehum the commissioner and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates — the judges and officials, the Tarpelites, Apharsites, Erechites, Babylonians, Susanchites, Dehavites, Elamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and honourable Osnappar carried into exile and settled in the city of Samaria and the rest of Beyond the River — and now:
This is the copy of the letter they sent him: "To King Artaxerxes: your servants, the men of Beyond the River. And now:

"The king should know that the Jews who came up from you have come to us, to Jerusalem. They're rebuilding that rebellious and evil city; they've finished the walls and they're repairing the foundations.
"Now the king should know this: if this city is rebuilt and the walls are finished, they won't pay tribute, tax or toll, and the royal revenue will certainly suffer.
"Now, because we eat the salt of the palace, and it isn't right for us to look on while the king is dishonoured, we've sent and made this known to the king,

"so that a search can be made in the book of records of your fathers. You'll find in the book of records, and you'll know, that this city is a rebellious city, injurious to kings and provinces, and that revolt has been made inside it from ancient days. That's why this city was laid waste.
"We're telling the king: if this city is rebuilt and the walls are finished, you'll have no possession in Beyond the River."
The king sent this reply to Rehum the commissioner and Shimshai the scribe and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and the rest of Beyond the River: "Peace. And now:
"the letter you sent us has been read out plainly in front of me.
"And I issued a decree, and they searched and found that this city has risen up against kings from ancient days, and that rebellion and revolt have been made in it.
"And mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem, with mastery over all Beyond the River, and tribute, tax and toll were paid to them.
"So now issue a decree to make these men stop; and this city isn't to be rebuilt until a decree is issued by me.
"And be careful not to be slack about this. Why should the damage grow, to the injury of kings?"

Then, as soon as the copy of King Artaxerxes' letter was read out in front of Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates, they hurried off to Jerusalem, to the Jews, and made them stop by force and power.
So the work on the house of God in Jerusalem stopped; and it stayed at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

ezra_5.t: Then Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak got up and started building the house of God in Jerusalem; and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.
At that point Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their associates, came to them and said, "Who issued you a decree to build this house and finish this structure?"
Then we said to them, "What are the names of the men putting up this building?"
But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they didn't make them stop until a report could go to Darius and a letter be sent back about it.
This is the copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates the officials in Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
They sent him a report, and this is what was written in it: "To King Darius: all peace.

"The king should know that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It's being built with dressed stone, and timber is being set in the walls; this work is being done diligently and it's prospering in their hands.
"So we asked those elders, 'Who issued you a decree to build this house and finish this structure?'
"And we asked their names too, so that we could let you know — so that we could write down the names of the men at their head.

"And this is the report they gave us back: 'We're the servants of the God of the heavens and the earth, and we're rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

'But because our ancestors enraged the God of the heavens, he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and he destroyed this house and carried the people into exile to Babylon.
'Even so, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree to build this house of God.

'And the articles of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar had brought out of the temple in Jerusalem and carried to the temple of Babylon — King Cyrus brought them out of the temple of Babylon, and they were handed over to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he'd made governor.
'And he said to him, "Take these articles, go and deposit them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site."
'So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem; and from then till now it's been under construction, and it isn't finished.'

"And now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the king's treasure house there in Babylon, to see whether a decree really was issued by King Cyrus to build this house of God in Jerusalem. And let the king send us word of his will in the matter."

ezra_6.t: Then King Darius issued a decree, and a search was made in the house of the books, where the treasures were deposited in Babylon.
And at Ecbatana, in the citadel in the province of Media, a single scroll was found, and this is what was written in it — a memorandum:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decree: 'The house of God in Jerusalem — let the house be rebuilt as a place where sacrifices are offered, and let its foundations be kept; its height sixty cubits, its width sixty cubits,
'three courses of dressed stone and one course of new timber, with the cost paid from the king's house.

'And the articles of the house of God, of gold and silver, that Nebuchadnezzar brought out of the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon — let them be sent back, and let each one go to the temple in Jerusalem, to its place; and you're to deposit them in the house of God.'"
"Now then, Tattenai governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and your associates, the officials in Beyond the River — keep well away from there.
"Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.

"And I issue a decree about what you're to do for these elders of the Jews in the building of this house of God: out of the king's property, from the tribute of Beyond the River, the cost is to be paid to these men diligently, so that they aren't made to stop.

"And whatever they need — young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of the heavens, wheat, salt, wine and oil, according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem — is to be given them day by day without fail,
"so that they can offer soothing offerings to the God of the heavens and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
"And I issue a decree: anyone who violates this command — let a beam be pulled out of his house, and let him be lifted up and impaled on it; and let his house be made a refuse heap for it.

"And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out a hand to violate this decree and destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decree. Let it be done diligently."
Then Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their associates did just that, diligently, in accordance with what King Darius had sent.

And the elders of the Jews went on building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. And they built and finished it according to the decree of the God of Israel and according to the decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
And the Israelites — the priests, the Levites and the rest of the returned exiles — kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.

For the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, one for each of the tribes of Israel.
And they appointed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their classes, over the service of God in Jerusalem, as it's written in the book of Moses.
The returned exiles kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

For the priests and the Levites had cleansed themselves as one — every one of them was clean. And they slaughtered the passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.

And the Israelites who'd come back from the exile ate it, along with everyone who'd separated himself from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them, to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

And they kept the festival of unleavened bread for seven days with joy; because the LORD had made them rejoice and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria towards them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.

ezra_7.t: After these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia — Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest —

that Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses that the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and the king granted him everything he asked, according to the hand of the LORD his God upon him.
Some of the Israelites, and of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers and the temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king.
For the going up from Babylon began on the first day of the first month, and he came to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had set his heart on studying the law of the LORD and doing it, and on teaching statute and ordinance in Israel.
And this is the copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave Ezra the priest and scribe — a scribe of the words of the commandments of the LORD and his statutes for Israel:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens: perfect peace. And now:
"I issue a decree that anyone in my kingdom of the people of Israel, or of its priests and the Levites, who volunteers to go to Jerusalem with you may go.
"You're sent from the king and his seven counsellors to enquire about Judah and Jerusalem by the law of your God, which is in your hand,
"and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose abode is in Jerusalem,
"and all the silver and gold that you find in the whole province of Babylon, with the freewill offering of the people and the priests who offer freely for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
"So with this silver you're to buy bulls, rams and lambs diligently, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
"And whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do it according to the will of your God.
"And the articles that are given you for the service of the house of your God — hand them over in full before the God of Jerusalem.
"And the rest of what's needed for the house of your God, whatever falls to you to supply, you're to supply from the king's treasury.
"And I, King Artaxerxes, issue a decree to all the treasurers in Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of the heavens, asks of you, it's to be done diligently,
"up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil — and salt without limit.
"Whatever is by the decree of the God of the heavens, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of the heavens. Why should there be wrath against the kingdom of the king and his sons?
"And we're telling you: it isn't permitted to impose tribute, tax or toll on any of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the Nethinim, or the servants of this house of God.

"And you, Ezra, by the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in Beyond the River — all who know the laws of your God; and anyone who doesn't know, you're to instruct.
"And anyone who doesn't do the law of your God and the law of the king — let judgement be executed on him diligently: death, or banishment, or confiscation of property, or imprisonment."
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who has put a thing like this in the heart of the king, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem,

and who has extended steadfast love to me before the king and his counsellors and all the king's mighty officials. And I took strength, because the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, and I gathered leading men from Israel to go up with me.

ezra_8.t: These are the heads of their ancestral houses, with their genealogical enrolment, who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes:
Of the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; of Ithamar, Daniel; of David, Hattush;
of Shecaniah; of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty males enrolled by genealogy;
of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males;
of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males;
and of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
and of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males;
and of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
and of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty males;
and of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight males;
and of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten males;
and of Adonikam, the last ones — their names are Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah — and with them sixty males;
and of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy males.
And I gathered them at the river that runs to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. And I looked closely at the people and at the priests, and I found none of the sons of Levi there.
So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah and Meshullam — leading men — and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were teachers.

And I gave them orders for Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia, and I put the words in their mouth to say to Iddo and his brothers the temple servants at the place Casiphia, to bring us servants for the house of our God.

And because the good hand of our God was upon us, they brought us a man of insight from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi son of Israel — Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen of them;
and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the descendants of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty;
and of the temple servants whom David and the officials had appointed for the service of the Levites — two hundred and twenty temple servants, all of them designated by name.
And there, at the river Ahava, I proclaimed a fast, so that we could humble ourselves before our God and seek from him a straight way for us, for our little children and for all our property.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for an escort and horsemen to help us against an enemy on the way; we'd told the king, "The hand of our God is upon everyone who seeks him, for good; and his strength and his anger are against everyone who forsakes him."
So we fasted and sought this from our God, and he was entreated by us.
Then I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers with them.

And I weighed out to them the silver, the gold and the articles — the contribution for the house of our God that the king and his counsellors and his officials and all Israel who were there had offered.
I weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver articles worth a hundred talents, a hundred talents of gold,
twenty gold bowls worth a thousand darics, and two articles of fine gleaming bronze, as precious as gold.
And I said to them, "You're holy to the LORD, and the articles are holy, and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.

"Watch over them and keep them until you weigh them out in front of the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the ancestral houses of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD."
So the priests and the Levites took charge of the weighed silver, gold and articles, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

And we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from ambush on the way.
And we came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.

On the fourth day the silver, the gold and the articles were weighed out in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, with Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui, the Levites —
everything by number and by weight; and the whole weight was written down then and there.

Those who had come from the captivity, the returned exiles, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering — all of it a burnt offering to the LORD.
They delivered the king's laws to the king's satraps and to the governors of Beyond the River, and these supported the people and the house of God.

ezra_9.t: When all this was finished, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, and the priests and the Levites, haven't separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, with their abominations — from the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians and the Amorites.

"They've taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy offspring have mixed themselves with the peoples of the lands; and the hand of the leaders and the officials has been foremost in this unfaithfulness."
When I heard it, I tore my garment and my robe, pulled out some of the hair of my head and my beard, and sat there appalled.
And everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered round me, over the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles; and I sat there appalled until the evening offering.
And at the evening offering I got up from my humiliation, and with my garment and my robe torn I fell on my knees and spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
And I said, "My God, I'm ashamed — too humiliated to lift my face to you, my God. Our iniquities have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown as great as the heavens.

"From the days of our ancestors we've been in great guilt, right up to this day; and for our iniquities we — we, our kings and our priests — have been given into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder and to shame of face, as we are today.

"And now, for a brief moment, there's been favour from the LORD our God, to leave us some who escape and to give us a tent peg in his holy place, so that our God might light up our eyes and give us a little reviving in our servitude.

"We're slaves; and yet in our servitude our God hasn't forsaken us. He's extended steadfast love to us before the kings of Persia, giving us a reviving to raise up the house of our God and to set up its ruins, and giving us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.
"And now, our God, what can we say after this? We've forsaken your commandments,

"the ones you commanded by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying, 'The land you're entering to take possession of is a land of impurity, through the impurity of the peoples of the lands, through their abominations, which they've filled it with from end to end in their uncleanness.

'And now, don't give your daughters to their sons, and don't take their daughters for your sons; and never seek their peace or their good — so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it to your children as an inheritance for ever.'
"And after everything that's come on us for our evil deeds and our great guilt — and you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquity deserved, and have given us an escaped remnant like this —

"are we to turn back and break your commandments and intermarry with the peoples of these abominations? Wouldn't you be angry with us to the point of making an end, so that there'd be no remnant and no one who escapes?
"LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous; and here we are, left as an escaped remnant, as we are today. Here we are before you in our guilt — because no one can stand before you on account of this."

ezra_10.t: While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a very great assembly gathered round him from Israel — men, women and children — because the people were weeping bitterly.

And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Elam, spoke up and said to Ezra, "We've acted unfaithfully against our God: we've married foreign women from the peoples of the land. And even so, there's hope for Israel in this.

"So now let's make a covenant with our God to send away all the wives and those born of them, by the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.
"Get up — this matter rests on you, and we're with you. Be strong and act."
So Ezra got up and made the leaders of the priests, the Levites and all Israel swear to act according to this word; and they swore.

Then Ezra rose from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; and he went in there. He ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles.
They sent a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to all the returned exiles, to assemble at Jerusalem;

and that anyone who didn't come within three days, by the counsel of the leaders and the elders, would have all his property forfeited, and would himself be separated from the assembly of the returned exiles.

So all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within three days — it was the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month — and all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, trembling over the matter, and because of the rains.
And Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You've acted unfaithfully: you've married foreign women, and you've added to the guilt of Israel.
"So now give praise to the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and do his will; and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women."
And all the assembly answered in a loud voice, "That's right. It's on us to do as you say.
"But there are a great many of us, and it's the rainy season, and there's no standing about outside; and this business isn't for a day or two, because we've transgressed badly in this matter.

"Let our leaders stand for the whole assembly; and let everyone in our cities who's married foreign women come at appointed times, and the elders of each city and its judges with them — until the burning of our God's anger is turned back from us in this matter."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah stood against this, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supporting them.

And the returned exiles did it. Ezra the priest, and men who were heads of the ancestral houses, by their ancestral house and all of them by name, set themselves apart; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to look into the matter.
And by the first day of the first month they'd finished with all the men who had married foreign women.
And among the descendants of the priests there were men who'd married foreign women: of the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers — Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib and Gedaliah.
And they gave their hand to send their wives away; and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt.
Of the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Of the descendants of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel and Uzziah.
Of the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad and Eleasah.
And of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah and Eliezer.
And of the singers: Eliashib. Of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem and Uri.
And of Israel: of the descendants of Parosh — Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah and Benaiah.
Of the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth and Elijah.
Of the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad and Aziza.
Of the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai and Athlai.
Of the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal and Ramoth.
Of the descendants of Pahath-moab: Adna, Kelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui and Manasseh.
And the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Isshiah, Malkijah, Shemaiah, Simeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, Shemariah.
Of the descendants of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh and Shimei.
Of the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Keluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasai,
Bani, Binnui, Shimei,
Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, Joseph.
Of the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel and Benaiah.
All these had taken foreign women; and some of these women had borne children.

genesis_1.t: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was formless and empty. Darkness lay over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God hovered over the waters.
Then God said, "Let there be light." And there was light.
God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light "day" and the darkness "night". There was evening, there was morning — the first day.
Then God said, "Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate water from water."
So God made the expanse, separating the water under it from the water above it. And it was so.
God called the expanse "sky". There was evening, there was morning — a second day.
Then God said, "Let the water under the sky gather in one place, so dry ground appears." And it was so.
God called the dry ground "earth" and the gathered waters "seas". And God saw that it was good.
Then God said, "Let the earth grow things — plants with seed, and fruit trees whose fruit carries its own seed, each of its own kind." And it was so.
The earth brought it forth — seed-bearing plants of every kind, and trees with seed-bearing fruit of every kind. And God saw that it was good.
There was evening, there was morning — a third day.
Then God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to separate day from night, and to mark out seasons, days and years —
and let them be lights in the expanse of the sky to shine on the earth." And it was so.
God made the two great lights — the greater one to govern the day, the lesser to govern the night — and the stars.
God set them in the expanse of the sky to shine on the earth,
to govern day and night, and to separate light from darkness. And God saw that it was good.
There was evening, there was morning — a fourth day.
Then God said, "Let the water teem with swarms of living things, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse."
So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves and teems in the water, each of its kind, and every winged bird of its kind. And God saw that it was good.
God blessed them: "Be fruitful, multiply, fill the waters of the seas — and let the birds multiply on the earth."
There was evening, there was morning — a fifth day.
Then God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures of every kind — livestock, things that creep, wild animals." And it was so.
God made the wild animals of every kind, the livestock of every kind, and everything that creeps on the ground of every kind. And God saw that it was good.

Then God said, "Let us make humankind in our image, after our likeness — and let them rule the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the livestock, the whole earth, and everything that creeps on it."
So God created humankind in his own image. In the image of God he created it. Male and female he created them.
God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth and subdue it. Rule the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, and every animal that moves on the earth."
Then God said, "Look — I've given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the earth, and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. That's your food.
And to every wild animal, every bird of the sky, and everything that creeps on the earth — everything with the breath of life in it — I've given every green plant for food." And it was so.
God saw everything he had made, and look — it was very good. There was evening, there was morning — the sixth day.

genesis_2.t: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and everything in them.
By the seventh day God had finished the work he'd been doing, and on the seventh day he rested from all of it.
God blessed the seventh day and set it apart, because on it he rested from all the work of creating he had done.
This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day the LORD God made earth and heaven.
No shrub of the field was on the earth yet, no plant had sprouted, because the LORD God hadn't sent rain and there was no human to work the ground.
But water would rise up from the earth and water the whole surface of the ground.
Then the LORD God shaped the man from the dust of the ground, breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
The LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and put the man he had formed there.
Out of the ground the LORD God grew every tree that's good to look at and good for food — with the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it split into four branches.
The first is called the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there's gold.
The gold of that land is good; there's bdellium and onyx there too.
The second river is called the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.
The third river is called the Tigris; it flows east of Assyria. And the fourth is the Euphrates.
The LORD God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and look after it.
And the LORD God commanded the man, "You're free to eat from any tree in the garden —
but not from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. The day you eat from it, you will certainly die."
Then the LORD God said, "It's not good for the man to be alone. I'll make him a helper who matches him."

The LORD God formed out of the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and he brought them to the man to see what he'd call them. Whatever the man called each living creature — that was its name.
So the man named all the livestock, the birds of the sky and every wild animal — but for Adam, no helper matching him was found.
So the LORD God put the man into a deep sleep, and while he slept he took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
And the LORD God built the rib he'd taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to him.
Then the man said, "This one, at last — bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh. She'll be called woman, because she was taken out of man."
That's why a man leaves his father and mother and holds fast to his wife, and they become one flesh.
The two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they felt no shame.

genesis_3.t: Now the serpent was shrewder than any wild animal the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, "Did God really say you can't eat from any tree in the garden?"
The woman said to the serpent, "We can eat fruit from the trees in the garden.
But about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, 'Don't eat from it, don't even touch it, or you'll die.'"
But the serpent said to the woman, "You certainly won't die.
God knows that the day you eat from it your eyes will open, and you'll be like God, knowing good and evil."

So the woman saw the tree was good for food, a delight to look at, and desirable for making you wise. She took some of the fruit and ate it, and she gave some to her husband, who was right there with her, and he ate.
Then both their eyes were opened, and they knew they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves coverings.
Then they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
But the LORD God called to the man, "Where are you?"
He said, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid."
And he said, "Who told you you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree I told you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman you put here with me — she gave me the fruit, and I ate."
Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you've done?" The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."

So the LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you did this, you're cursed above all the livestock and above every animal of the field. You'll go on your belly, and you'll eat dust, all the days of your life."
And I'll put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. He'll strike you at the head, and you'll strike him at the heel.
To the woman he said, "I'm going to greatly increase your pain and your conceiving. You'll bear children in pain. Your desire is for your husband, and he'll rule over you."

And to Adam he said, "Because you listened to your wife's voice and ate from the tree I commanded you not to eat from — the ground is cursed on your account. You'll eat from it in pain all the days of your life."
It'll bring up thorns and thistles for you, and you'll eat the vegetation of the field.
You'll eat your bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, since that's where you were taken from. You're dust, and you'll return to dust.
The man named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all the living.
The LORD God made tunics of skin for Adam and his wife, and he dressed them.
And the LORD God said, "Look, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now — what if he reaches out his hand and takes from the tree of life too, and eats, and lives forever—"
So the LORD God sent him out of the garden of Eden, to till the ground he was taken from.
He drove the man out. And east of the garden of Eden he stationed the cherubim and the flame of the whirling sword, to keep the way to the tree of life.

genesis_4.t: The man slept with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. And she said, "I've gotten a man with the help of the LORD."
Then she gave birth again, to his brother Abel. Abel herded flocks, and Cain tilled the ground.
After some time, Cain brought the LORD an offering from the fruit of the ground.
And Abel brought one too — from the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. And the LORD regarded Abel and his offering,
but he didn't regard Cain and his offering. And Cain burned with anger, and his face fell.
The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why has your face fallen?"
If you do well, won't you be accepted? And if you don't do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, and you must rule over it.
And Cain said to his brother Abel […]. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
The LORD said to Cain, "Where is Abel your brother?" He said, "I don't know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
He said, "What have you done? Your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground."
And now you're cursed from the ground — the ground that opened its mouth to take your brother's blood from your hand.
When you till the ground, it won't give you its strength again. You'll be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth.
Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than can be borne."
"Look, you've driven me out today from the face of the ground, and I'll be hidden from your face. I'll be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth, and everyone who finds me will kill me."
The LORD said to him, "So then, whoever kills Cain will be avenged sevenfold." And the LORD set a sign for Cain, so that everyone who found him wouldn't strike him.
So Cain went out from before the LORD, and he settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain slept with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. And he was building a city, and he named the city after his son, Enoch.
Enoch had Irad, and Irad had Mehujael, and Mehujael had Methushael, and Methushael had Lamech.
Lamech took two wives for himself. One was named Adah, and the second Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who live in tents, and of livestock.
His brother was named Jubal. He was the father of everyone who handles the lyre and the pipe.
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-cain, a sharpener of every worker of bronze and iron. And Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.
And Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, give ear to what I say. I have killed a man for wounding me, and a boy for striking me."
"Cain is avenged sevenfold — and Lamech seventy-seven."
Adam slept with his wife again, and she gave birth to a son, and she named him Seth, for she said, "God has set for me another offspring in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
And Seth had a son too, and he named him Enosh. That was when people began to call on the name of the LORD.

genesis_5.t: This is the book of Adam's account. On the day God created Adam, he made him in God's likeness.
He created them male and female, blessed them, and named them Adam on the day they were created.
Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and then he had a son in his own likeness, after his image, and he named him Seth.
After Seth was born, Adam lived another eight hundred years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years in all, and then he died.
Seth lived a hundred and five years, and then he had Enosh.
After Enosh was born, Seth lived another eight hundred and seven years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Seth lived nine hundred and twelve years in all, and then he died.
Enosh lived ninety years, and then he had Kenan.
After Kenan was born, Enosh lived another eight hundred and fifteen years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Enosh lived nine hundred and five years in all, and then he died.
Kenan lived seventy years, and then he had Mahalalel.
After Mahalalel was born, Kenan lived another eight hundred and forty years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Kenan lived nine hundred and ten years in all, and then he died.
Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, and then he had Jared.
After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived another eight hundred and thirty years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived eight hundred and ninety-five years in all, and then he died.
Jared lived a hundred and sixty-two years, and then he had Enoch.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived another eight hundred years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Jared lived nine hundred and sixty-two years in all, and then he died.
Enoch lived sixty-five years, and then he had Methuselah.
After Methuselah was born, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Enoch's days came to three hundred and sixty-five years in all.
Enoch walked with God, and he was not, because God took him.
Methuselah lived a hundred and eighty-seven years, and then he had Lamech.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived another seven hundred and eighty-two years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Methuselah lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years in all, and then he died.
Lamech lived a hundred and eighty-two years, and then he had a son.
He named him Noah, saying, 'This one will bring us comfort from our work and from the pain of our hands, from the ground the LORD has cursed.'
After Noah was born, Lamech lived another five hundred and ninety-five years, and he had more sons and daughters.
Lamech lived seven hundred and seventy-seven years in all, and then he died.
Noah was five hundred years old, and he had Shem, Ham and Japheth.

genesis_6.t: When people began to grow numerous across the ground, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of people were good, and they took wives for themselves from any they chose.
The LORD said, 'My spirit won't stay in people forever — they're flesh too. Their days will be a hundred and twenty years.'

The Nephilim were on the earth in those days — and afterward too — when the sons of God went in to the daughters of people and they bore them children. These were the mighty ones of long ago, the men of renown.
The LORD saw how great human evil was on the earth — that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was nothing but evil, all day long.
The LORD was sorry he had made people on the earth, and it hurt him in his heart.
The LORD said, 'I'm going to wipe out the people I created from the face of the ground — people and livestock, crawling things and the birds of the sky. I'm sorry I made them.'
But Noah found favour in the LORD's eyes.
This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time; Noah walked with God.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
The earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was full of violence.
God looked at the earth, and there it was — corrupt, because all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
God said to Noah, 'The end of all flesh has come before me. The earth is full of violence because of them. So here I am — I'm going to destroy them, and the earth with them.'
Make yourself an ark out of gopher wood. Build it with compartments, and cover it inside and out with pitch.
Here's how you are to make it: the ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Make a roof for the ark, and finish it to within a cubit of the top. Put the ark's door in its side, and give it lower, second and third decks.
As for me, I'm about to bring the flood — water — on the earth, to destroy all flesh that has the breath of life in it, from under the heavens. Everything on the earth will die.
But I'll establish my covenant with you, and you'll go into the ark — you and your sons, your wife and your sons' wives with you.
Of every living thing, of all flesh, bring two of each into the ark to keep them alive with you. They are to be male and female.
Birds of every kind, livestock of every kind, every crawling thing of the ground of every kind — two of each will come to you, to be kept alive.
And you — take some of every food that gets eaten, and store it up for yourself. It will be food for you and for them.
Noah did everything just as God commanded him. That is what he did.

genesis_7.t: The LORD said to Noah, 'Come into the ark, you and your whole household. You are the one I have seen to be righteous before me in this generation.'
Take seven of each clean animal with you, the male and its mate; and of the animals that aren't clean, two, the male and its mate.
And of the birds of the sky, seven of each, male and female, so that offspring stay alive over the face of all the earth.
In seven more days I'm going to send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I'll wipe everything I have made off the face of the ground.
Noah did everything just as the LORD commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came — water over the earth.
Noah went into the ark, and his sons, his wife and his sons' wives with him, because of the waters of the flood.
Of the clean livestock, of the livestock that isn't clean, of the birds, and of everything that crawls on the ground —
they came to Noah two by two into the ark, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
After the seven days, the waters of the flood were on the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month — that very day, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the sky were opened.
The rain was on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah went into the ark, and Shem, Ham and Japheth his sons, and his wife, and his sons' three wives with them.
