they went in, and every animal of its kind, all the livestock of their kinds, every crawling thing that crawls on the earth of its kind, and every bird of its kind — every bird, everything with wings.
They came to Noah into the ark, two of each, of all flesh with the breath of life in it.
Those that came, male and female of all flesh, came just as God had commanded him. And the LORD shut him in.
The flood was on the earth for forty days, and the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose up off the earth.
The waters prevailed and increased greatly over the earth, and the ark moved along on the face of the waters.
The waters prevailed over the earth more and more, and every high mountain under the whole sky was covered.
The waters prevailed fifteen cubits above, and the mountains were covered.
All flesh that moves on the earth died — birds, livestock, animals, every swarming thing that swarms on the earth — and every human being.
Everything with the breath of the breath of life in its nostrils, everything that was on the dry land, died.

He wiped out everything that was on the face of the ground — people and livestock, crawling things and the birds of the sky — and they were wiped off the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.
The waters prevailed over the earth a hundred and fifty days.

genesis_8.t: Then God remembered Noah — and every animal and all the livestock with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the water went down.
The springs of the deep were shut, and the floodgates of the heavens, and the rain from the heavens was held back.
The water pulled back off the earth, little by little. After a hundred and fifty days it had gone down.
The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day, on the mountains of Ararat.
The water kept dropping until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the mountain tops came into view.
Forty days later Noah opened the window he'd made in the ark.
He sent the raven out, and it kept going and coming back until the water had dried off the earth.
Then he sent the dove out to see if the water had gone down off the ground.

The dove couldn't find anywhere to set the sole of her foot, so she came back to him at the ark — there was water over the surface of the whole earth. He reached out his hand, took her, and brought her in to himself, into the ark.
He waited another seven days and sent the dove out from the ark again.
The dove came back to him toward evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her mouth. That's how Noah knew the water had gone down off the earth.
He waited another seven days and sent the dove out, and she didn't come back to him again.
In the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the water was dried up off the earth. Noah took off the covering of the ark and looked — the surface of the ground was dry.
And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
Then God said to Noah,
Go out of the ark — you, your wife, your sons and your sons' wives.
Bring out with you every animal that's with you, of all flesh — the birds, the livestock, everything that creeps on the earth — and let them swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on it.
So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
Every animal, every creeping thing, every bird — everything that creeps on the earth — came out of the ark, family by family.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every clean animal and every clean bird, and offered up burnt offerings on it.

The LORD smelled the soothing aroma, and the LORD said to himself, "I won't curse the ground again on account of humankind. The inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. And I won't strike down every living thing again, the way I have done."
For as long as the earth has days: sowing and reaping, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night — they won't stop.

genesis_9.t: Then God blessed Noah and his sons. He said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth."
Every animal of the earth and every bird of the heavens, everything the ground creeps with, and all the fish of the sea will fear you and dread you. They are given into your hand.
Anything alive that moves is food for you. Like the green plants, I've given you all of it.
But don't eat flesh with its life in it — its blood.
And your blood, for your lives, I will require. I'll require it from the hand of every animal, and from the hand of a human being — from the hand of each, his brother — I'll require a human life.
Whoever sheds a human being's blood, by a human being will his own blood be shed — because God made humankind in his own image.
As for you — be fruitful and multiply. Swarm on the earth and multiply in it.
Then God said to Noah and his sons who were with him,
"As for me — I'm establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
and with every living creature with you — the birds, the livestock, every animal of the earth that's with you, everything that came out of the ark, every animal of the earth.
I'll establish my covenant with you: never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth."
And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I'm making between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come.
I've set my bow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
Whenever I bring a cloud over the earth, the bow will be seen in the cloud,
and I'll remember my covenant — between me and you and every living creature among all flesh — and the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The bow will be in the cloud, and I'll see it and remember the lasting covenant between God and every living creature — all flesh that is on the earth."
And God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I've established between me and all flesh that is on the earth."
Noah's sons who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah's sons, and from these the whole earth was scattered abroad.
Noah — a man of the ground — made a start, and planted a vineyard.
He drank some of the wine, got drunk, and uncovered himself inside his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and he told his two brothers outside.

Shem and Japheth took the garment, laid it across the shoulders of the two of them, walked backwards and covered their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned backwards, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
Noah woke up from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
And he said, "Cursed be Canaan. The lowest of slaves he'll be to his brothers."
And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem. And let Canaan be a slave to them.
May God give Japheth room, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem. And let Canaan be a slave to them."
Noah lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood.
All the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

genesis_10.t: This is the account of Noah's sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
Japheth's sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
Gomer's sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.
Javan's sons: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
From these the coastland peoples spread out into their lands, each with its own language, by families, in their nations.
Ham's sons: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
Cush's sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. Raamah's sons: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod. He was the one who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the LORD. That's why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."
His kingdom began with Babel, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went out to Asshur and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-ir and Calah,
and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah — that is the great city.
Mizraim fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim and the Naphtuhim,
and the Pathrusim and the Casluhim — the Philistines came out from there — and the Caphtorim.
Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
and the Jebusites, the Amorites and the Girgashites,
and the Hivites, the Arkites and the Sinites,
and the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites. Afterwards the Canaanite families were scattered.
The Canaanite border ran from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim as far as Lasha.
These are Ham's sons, by families, by languages, in their lands, in their nations.
Shem too had children born to him. He was the father of all the sons of Eber, the older brother of Japheth.
Shem's sons: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram.
Aram's sons: Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.
Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth and Jerah,
and Hadoram, Uzal and Diklah,
and Obal, Abimael and Sheba,
and Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were Joktan's sons.
Their dwelling place ran from Mesha toward Sephar, the hill country of the east.
These are Shem's sons, by families, by languages, in their lands, by nations.
These are the families of Noah's sons, by their generations, in their nations. From these the nations separated out across the earth after the flood.

genesis_11.t: The whole earth had one language and the same words.
As they travelled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
They said to each other, "Come, let's make bricks and fire them hard." They used brick for stone and bitumen for mortar.
And they said, "Come, let's build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and make a name for ourselves — otherwise we'll be scattered over the face of the whole earth."
And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the children of humankind had built.
And the LORD said, "Here they are — one people, one language for all of them, and this is only the beginning of what they'll do. Now nothing they plan to do will be withheld from them."
"Come, let's go down and confuse their language there, so they can't understand each other's language."
So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
That is why its name is Babel — because there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth, and from there the LORD scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
This is the account of Shem. Shem was a hundred years old when he fathered Arphaxad, two years after the flood.
After he fathered Arphaxad, Shem lived five hundred years and had sons and daughters.
Arphaxad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah.
After he fathered Shelah, Arphaxad lived four hundred and three years and had sons and daughters.
Shelah lived thirty years and fathered Eber.
After he fathered Eber, Shelah lived four hundred and three years and had sons and daughters.
Eber lived thirty-four years and fathered Peleg.
After he fathered Peleg, Eber lived four hundred and thirty years and had sons and daughters.
Peleg lived thirty years and fathered Reu.
After he fathered Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years and had sons and daughters.
Reu lived thirty-two years and fathered Serug.
After he fathered Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years and had sons and daughters.
Serug lived thirty years and fathered Nahor.
After he fathered Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years and had sons and daughters.
Nahor lived twenty-nine years and fathered Terah.
After he fathered Terah, Nahor lived a hundred and nineteen years and had sons and daughters.
Terah lived seventy years and fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran.
This is the account of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.
Haran died in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran — Haran was the father of Milcah and of Iscah.
Sarai was barren. She had no child.

Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran — his son's son — and Sarai his daughter-in-law, Abram's wife, and they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They got as far as Haran and settled there.
Terah's days were two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran.

genesis_12.t: The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives, your father's house. Go to the land I'll show you."
"I'll make you into a great nation. I'll bless you and make your name great. And you'll be a blessing."
"I'll bless the ones who bless you, and whoever treats you with contempt I'll curse. And in you all the clans of the ground will be blessed."
So Abram went, just as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran.
Abram took Sarai his wife and his nephew Lot, everything they'd accumulated, and the people they'd acquired in Haran. They set out for the land of Canaan, and they came to the land of Canaan.
Abram passed through the land as far as Shechem, to the great tree of Moreh. The Canaanites were in the land at that time.
The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "I'll give this land to your offspring." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
From there he moved into the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. He built an altar there to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
Abram kept moving, stage by stage, down toward the Negev.
There was a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to stay there a while, because the famine was severe.
Just before they reached Egypt he said to Sarai his wife, "Listen, I know you're a beautiful woman."
"When the Egyptians see you they'll say, 'That's his wife.' They'll kill me and keep you alive."
"Please say you're my sister, so that things go well for me because of you, and I stay alive because of you."
When Abram got to Egypt, the Egyptians saw how beautiful the woman was.
Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
He treated Abram well because of her, and Abram came to have sheep and cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his household with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Pharaoh sent for Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?"
"Why did you say, 'She's my sister,' so that I took her as a wife? Well — here's your wife. Take her and go."
Pharaoh gave his men orders about him, and they sent him off with his wife and everything he had.

genesis_13.t: Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev — he, his wife, everything he had, and Lot with him.
Abram was very rich — livestock, silver, gold.
He travelled in stages from the Negev up to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the start, between Bethel and Ai —
to the place of the altar he'd made there before. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
Lot, who was travelling with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents of his own.
The land couldn't support the two of them living together. They had too much, and they couldn't stay together.
Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen started quarrelling. The Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land at the time.
Abram said to Lot, "Please, let's not have strife between me and you, or between my herdsmen and yours. We're brothers."
"Isn't the whole land in front of you? Please, separate from me. You go left, I'll go right. You go right, I'll go left."

Lot looked up and saw the whole Jordan plain, well watered everywhere — this was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah — like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, all the way to Zoar.
So Lot picked the whole Jordan plain for himself and moved east, and the two of them separated.
Abram settled in the land of Canaan. Lot settled among the cities of the plain and pitched his tent as far over as Sodom.
The men of Sodom were wicked. They sinned against the LORD, badly.
After Lot separated from him, the LORD said to Abram, "Look up. From right where you are, look north and south, east and west."
"All this land you're looking at — I'll give it to you and your offspring, for all time."
"I'll make your offspring like the dust of the earth. If anyone could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted too."
"Get up. Walk the land, its length and its breadth. I'll give it to you."
So Abram moved his tent, came to the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, and settled there. And he built an altar there to the LORD.

genesis_14.t: In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim —
these kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela — that is, Zoar.
All of these joined forces in the valley of Siddim — that is, the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they'd served Kedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer came with the kings who were with him, and they defeated the Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim,
and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El-paran on the edge of the wilderness.
Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat — that is, Kadesh — and they defeated the whole territory of the Amalekites, and the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar as well.
Then the king of Sodom went out, along with the kings of Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela — that is, Zoar — and they drew up for battle against them in the valley of Siddim —
against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goyim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar — four kings against the five.
The valley of Siddim was pit after pit of bitumen. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell there, and the ones who were left escaped to the hill country.
They took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and left.
They also took Lot and his goods — Abram's nephew — and left. He was living in Sodom.
A survivor came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living at the great trees of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner, and these men were in a covenant with Abram.
When Abram heard his kinsman had been taken, he called out his trained men — three hundred and eighteen of them, all born in his household — and gave chase as far as Dan.
He split his forces against them by night — he and his servants — struck them, and chased them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
He brought back all the goods, and Lot his kinsman and his goods too, and the women and the people.
The king of Sodom came out to meet him after he got back from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings with him, at the valley of Shaveh — the King's Valley.
And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
And he blessed him: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth —
and blessed be God Most High, who handed your adversaries over to you." And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people. Keep the goods for yourself."
But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I raise my hand to the LORD, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth —
"Not a thread, not a sandal strap — I won't take anything of yours. You are never going to say, 'I made Abram rich.'"
"Nothing for me. Only what the young men have already eaten, and the share belonging to the men who went with me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."

genesis_15.t: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Don't be afraid, Abram. I'm a shield for you. Your reward will be very great."
But Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will you give me? I'm going on childless, and the one who inherits my house is Eliezer of Damascus."
And Abram said, "Look, you haven't given me any offspring, so someone born in my house is going to inherit from me."
Then the word of the LORD came to him: "He won't be your heir. One who comes from your own body — he'll be your heir."
Then he brought him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars — if you can count them." And he said to him, "So will your offspring be."
And he believed the LORD. And he counted it to him as righteousness.
And he said to him, "I am the LORD. I brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."
But he said, "Lord GOD, by what am I to know that I'll possess it?"
He said to him, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
He brought him all these, cut them in half down the middle, and laid each piece opposite its match. The birds he didn't cut.
Birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them off.
As the sun was going down, a deep sleep came over Abram, and a dread — a great darkness — was falling on him.
And he said to Abram, "Know this for certain: your offspring will be foreigners in a land that isn't theirs. They'll serve those people, and those people will afflict them, for four hundred years."
"But I'll bring judgement on the nation they serve, and after that they'll come out with great possessions."
"As for you, you'll go to your fathers in peace. You'll be buried at a good old age."
"In the fourth generation they'll come back here, because the iniquity of the Amorite isn't yet complete."
When the sun had gone down and it was thick darkness, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.
That day the LORD made a covenant with Abram: "To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates —
the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."

genesis_16.t: Sarai, Abram's wife, hadn't borne him any children. She had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram, "Look, the LORD has kept me from having children. Go to my maidservant. Maybe I'll be built up through her." And Abram listened to Sarai.
So Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant — this was after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan — and gave her to her husband Abram as a wife.
He went to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw she had conceived, she began to despise her mistress.
Sarai said to Abram, "The wrong done to me is on you. I put my maidservant in your arms myself, and when she saw she had conceived, she despised me. Let the LORD judge between me and you."
Abram said to Sarai, "Your maidservant is in your hands. Do to her whatever seems good to you." So Sarai afflicted her, and she ran away from her.
The angel of the LORD found her at a spring of water in the wilderness — the spring on the road to Shur.
He said, "Hagar, maidservant of Sarai — where have you come from, and where are you going?" She said, "I'm running away from Sarai my mistress."
The angel of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress. Submit to her."
The angel of the LORD said to her, "I'll multiply your offspring so greatly that they can't be counted."
The angel of the LORD said to her, "You're pregnant, and you'll bear a son, and you'll name him Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your affliction."
"He'll be a wild donkey of a man — his hand against everyone, everyone's hand against him. And he'll live over against all his brothers."
So she named the LORD who spoke to her: "You are a God who sees me." For she said, "Have I really seen here, after the one who sees me?"
That's why the well is called Beer-lahai-roi. It's between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named the son Hagar bore him Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

genesis_17.t: When Abram was ninety-nine, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Walk before me. Be blameless."
"I'll set my covenant between me and you, and I'll multiply you greatly."
Abram fell face down, and God spoke with him:
"As for me — here is my covenant with you: you'll become the father of a multitude of nations."
"Your name won't be Abram any longer. Your name will be Abraham — because I've made you the father of a multitude of nations."
"I'll make you exceedingly fruitful. I'll make you into nations, and kings will come from you."
"I'll establish my covenant between me and you, and your offspring after you through their generations, as a perpetual covenant — to be God to you and to your offspring after you."
"And I'll give you and your offspring after you the land where you've lived as a foreigner — all the land of Canaan — as a perpetual possession. And I'll be God to them."
And God said to Abraham, "As for you — you're to keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you through their generations."
"This is my covenant, the one you're to keep, between me and you and your offspring after you: every male among you is to be circumcised."
"You're to be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and that will be a sign of the covenant between me and you."

"Every male among you is to be circumcised at eight days old, through all your generations — the one born in your household and the one bought with silver from any foreigner who isn't of your offspring."
"He must certainly be circumcised — the one born in your household and the one bought with your silver — and my covenant will be in your flesh as a perpetual covenant."
"Any uncircumcised male who isn't circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin — that person is to be cut off from his kin. He has broken my covenant."
And God said to Abraham, "Sarai your wife — you're not to call her Sarai. Her name is Sarah."
"I'll bless her, and I'll also give you a son by her. I'll bless her, and she'll become nations — kings of peoples will come from her."
Abraham fell face down and laughed, and he said to himself, "Can a child be born to a man of a hundred? Can Sarah bear a child at ninety?"
And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live before you."
But God said, "No — Sarah your wife is going to bear you a son, and you're to name him Isaac. And I'll establish my covenant with him as a perpetual covenant, for his offspring after him."
"And as for Ishmael — I've heard you. I'll bless him, make him fruitful, and multiply him exceedingly. He'll father twelve princes, and I'll make him into a great nation."
"But my covenant I'll establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear you at this appointed time next year."
When he had finished speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

Then Abraham took Ishmael his son, everyone born in his household, and everyone bought with his silver — every male among the men of his household — and on that very day he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin, just as God had spoken with him.
Abraham was ninety-nine when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
On that very day Abraham was circumcised, and so was Ishmael his son.
And all the men of his household — those born in the household and those bought with silver from a foreigner — were circumcised with him.

genesis_18.t: The LORD appeared to him at the great trees of Mamre. He was sitting in the tent doorway in the heat of the day.
He looked up, and there were three men standing there. When he saw them he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed to the ground.
He said, "My Lord, if I've found favour with you, please don't pass your servant by."
Let a little water be brought — wash your feet, and rest under the tree.
"Let me bring a bit of bread so you can keep your strength up, and then go on — after all, you've come by your servant." They said, "Do just as you've said."
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said, "three seahs of flour, the fine kind. Knead it and make cakes."
Abraham ran to the herd, took a good tender calf, and handed it to the servant, who hurried to prepare it.
Then he brought curds and milk and the calf he'd prepared and set it in front of them, and he stood there by them under the tree while they ate.
They asked him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" "There, in the tent," he said.
He said, "I will come back to you at this same time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent door, just behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were old, well on in years, and Sarah was past the way of women.
So Sarah laughed to herself. "Worn out as I am, am I to have pleasure? And my husband is old."
And the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Am I really going to have a child, old as I am?'"
Is anything too wonderful for the LORD? I will come back to you at the appointed time, this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.
Sarah denied it. "I didn't laugh," she said — she was afraid. And he said, "No. You laughed."
Then the men got up and looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way.
And the LORD said, "Am I going to hide from Abraham what I am about to do?"
Abraham is going to become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him.

For I have known him, so that he will direct his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just — so that the LORD may bring about for Abraham what he promised him.
And the LORD said, "The outcry over Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is very heavy.
I will go down and see whether what they have done matches the outcry that has reached me. And if not, I will know."
The men turned and went on toward Sodom, but Abraham was still standing there before the LORD.
Then Abraham came closer and said, "Are you really going to sweep away the righteous along with the wicked?
Suppose there are fifty righteous people in the city. Will you really sweep it away instead of sparing the place for the sake of the fifty righteous in it?

Far be it from you to do such a thing — to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked come out the same. Far be it from you! Shall the judge of all the earth not do justice?"
And the LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous in Sodom, in the city itself, I will spare the whole place for their sake."
Abraham answered, "I have taken it on myself to speak to my Lord, and I am dust and ashes.
Suppose the fifty righteous are five short — will you destroy the whole city over five?" And he said, "I will not destroy it, if I find forty-five there."
He spoke to him again: "Suppose forty are found there." And he said, "I will not do it, for the sake of the forty."
And he said, "Please don't be angry, my Lord, and let me speak. Suppose thirty are found there." And he said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."
And he said, "I have taken it on myself to speak to my Lord. Suppose twenty are found there." And he said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty."
And he said, "Please don't be angry, my Lord, and let me speak just this once more. Suppose ten are found there." And he said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten."
And the LORD went on his way when he had finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham went back to his place.

genesis_19.t: The two angels came to Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom, and when he saw them he got up to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.
He said, "Please, my lords, turn aside to your servant's house. Spend the night, wash your feet, and get up early and go on your way." But they said, "No. We'll spend the night in the square."
But he pressed them hard, so they turned aside and came into his house. He made them a feast and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they had lain down, the men of the city — the men of Sodom — surrounded the house, young and old, all the people, to the last man.
They called to Lot, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so we can know them."
Lot went out to them at the entrance and shut the door behind him.
"Please, my brothers," he said, "don't do this evil."

"Look, I have two daughters who have not known a man. Let me bring them out to you, and do to them whatever seems good to you. Only do nothing to these men — they have come under the shelter of my roof."

But they said, "Out of the way!" And they said, "This man came here as a foreigner, and now he sets himself up as judge. We'll do worse to you than to them." They pressed hard against the man, against Lot, and moved in to break down the door.
But the men reached out, pulled Lot in to them in the house, and shut the door.
And they struck the men at the entrance of the house with blindness, small and great alike, so that they wore themselves out looking for the entrance.
Then the men said to Lot, "Who else do you have here? A son-in-law, sons, daughters, anyone of yours in the city — get them out of this place.
"We are about to destroy this place. The outcry against them has become great before the LORD, and the LORD has sent us to destroy it."

So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, the ones who were to marry his daughters. "Get up, get out of this place," he said. "The LORD is about to destroy the city." But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.
As dawn came up, the angels pressed Lot: "Get up. Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away when the city is punished."
But he hesitated. So the men took him by the hand, and his wife, and his two daughters — the LORD was compassionate toward him — and they brought them out and set them outside the city.
When they had brought them outside, he said, "Run for your life. Don't look behind you, and don't stop anywhere in the plain. Get to the hill country, or you'll be swept away."
And Lot said to them, "No — please, my Lord."
"Your servant has found favour with you, and you have shown me great loyalty in keeping me alive. But I can't escape to the hill country — the disaster will catch me and I'll die.
"Look, that city is close enough to run to, and it's a small place. Let me escape there — it's only a small place, isn't it? — and my life will be spared."
And he said to him, "Very well — I grant you this too. I will not overthrow the city you spoke of.
"Hurry — escape there. I can do nothing until you get there." That is why the city is called Zoar.
The sun had risen over the earth as Lot came to Zoar.
Then the LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, from the LORD, out of the heavens.
He overthrew those cities and the whole plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and everything growing on the ground.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham got up early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and over the whole land of the plain, and he saw the smoke of the land going up like smoke from a kiln.
So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of the middle of the overthrow — out of the cities where Lot had lived, when he overthrew them.
Lot went up from Zoar and settled in the hill country with his two daughters, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. So he lived in the cave, he and his two daughters.
The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to come in to us, as is the way of all the earth.
"Come, let's have our father drink wine, and lie with him, so we can keep our father's line alive."
So they made their father drink wine that night, and the older daughter went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day the older daughter said to the younger, "I lay with my father last night. Let's have him drink wine again tonight, and you go in and lie with him, so we can keep our father's line alive."
So they made their father drink wine that night too, and the younger daughter got up and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
Both of Lot's daughters conceived by their father.
The older daughter bore a son and named him Moab. He is the father of Moab to this day.
The younger also bore a son and named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.

genesis_20.t: Abraham moved on from there toward the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he stayed as a foreigner in Gerar.
Abraham said of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream at night and said, "You are about to die because of the woman you have taken. She is a married woman."
Now Abimelech had not gone near her. And he said, "My Lord, will you kill even a nation that has done no wrong?
"Didn't he tell me himself, 'She is my sister'? And she said it too — 'He is my brother.' I did this with an honest heart and clean hands."
And God said to him in the dream, "I know you did this with an honest heart, and I was the one who kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
"Now give the man's wife back. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you don't give her back, know this: you will surely die, you and everyone who is yours."
So Abimelech got up early in the morning, called all his servants, and told them everything that had been said, and the men were very afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham and said, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you, that you should bring such a great sin on me and on my kingdom? You have done to me things that are simply not done."
And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you have in mind, doing a thing like this?"
And Abraham said, "Because I thought, 'There is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me over my wife.'"
"And in fact she is my sister — my father's daughter, though not my mother's — and she became my wife."
"And when God set me wandering from my father's house, I said to her, 'This is the loyalty you owe me: everywhere we go, say of me, He is my brother.'"
Then Abimelech took sheep and cattle and male and female servants and gave them to Abraham, and he gave Sarah his wife back to him.
And Abimelech said, "My land is in front of you. Settle wherever you like."
And to Sarah he said, "See, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is a covering of the eyes for you, before everyone with you — you are cleared in the sight of all."
Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his slave women, and they bore children.
For the LORD had closed up every womb in Abimelech's household because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

genesis_21.t: And the LORD attended to Sarah just as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah just as he had spoken.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time God had spoken of.
Abraham named his son, the one born to him, whom Sarah bore him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
And Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me. Everyone who hears will laugh with me."
And she said, "Who would ever have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age."
The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, the one she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
So she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son. The son of this slave woman is not going to inherit along with my son, with Isaac."
The matter troubled Abraham greatly, because of his son.

But God said to Abraham, "Don't be troubled about the boy and about your slave woman. Listen to Sarah's voice in everything she says to you, for it is through Isaac that offspring will be named for you.
"And I will make the son of the slave woman into a nation too, because he is your offspring."

So Abraham got up early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar, putting them on her shoulder, and the child with them, and sent her away. She went off and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin ran out, she put the child down under one of the bushes.

Then she went and sat down by herself across from him, a good way off — about a bowshot — because she said, "Let me not watch the child die." So she sat across from him, and she lifted up her voice and wept.
And God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from the heavens: "What is troubling you, Hagar? Don't be afraid. God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
"Get up, lift the boy up and take him firmly by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy. He grew up and lived in the wilderness, and he became an archer.
He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother got him a wife from the land of Egypt.
About that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.

"So swear to me here by God that you won't deal falsely with me, or with my children, or with my children's children. Deal with me as loyally as I have dealt with you — and with the land where you have lived as a foreigner."
And Abraham said, "I swear it."
But Abraham took Abimelech to task over the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
And Abimelech said, "I don't know who did this. You never told me, and I hadn't heard of it until today."
So Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
Then Abraham set seven ewe-lambs of the flock apart from the rest.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What are these seven ewe-lambs you have set apart?"
And he said, "You are to take the seven ewe-lambs from my hand, so that it will be a witness for me that I dug this well."
That is why the place is called Beersheba — because the two of them swore an oath there.
So they made a covenant at Beersheba, and Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
And he planted a tamarisk at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
And Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines a long time.

genesis_22.t: Some time after this, God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
And he said, "Take your son, your only one, the one you love, Isaac — go to the land of Moriah and offer him up there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will tell you about."
So Abraham got up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, took two of his servants with him and Isaac his son, split the wood for a burnt offering, and set out for the place God had told him about.
On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place from a distance.
And Abraham said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there, and we will bow down, and we will come back to you."
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son, and carried the fire and the knife in his own hand. And the two of them walked on together.
Then Isaac said to Abraham his father, "Father." And he said, "Here I am, my son." And he said, "Here are the fire and the wood — but where is the sheep for a burnt offering?"
And Abraham said, "God will see to the sheep for a burnt offering for himself, my son." And the two of them walked on together.
They came to the place God had told him about, and Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. Then he bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
And Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
But the angel of the LORD called to him from the heavens: "Abraham! Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
And he said, "Don't stretch out your hand against the boy. Don't do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me."
Abraham looked up and saw a ram behind him, caught in the thicket by its horns. So Abraham went and took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.
And Abraham called that place "The LORD will see", and that is why it is said today, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen."
And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time from the heavens.
And he said, "By myself I have sworn — this is the LORD's declaration — that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only one,
"I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and the sand on the seashore. Your offspring will take possession of the gate of their enemies.
"And all the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you listened to my voice."
Then Abraham went back to his servants, and they set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.
Some time after this, Abraham was told, "Milcah too has borne sons to Nahor your brother:
"Uz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
"and Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

genesis_23.t: Sarah lived a hundred and twenty-seven years — the years of Sarah's life.
Sarah died at Kiriath-arba — that is, Hebron — in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
Then Abraham rose from beside his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth:
"I am a foreigner living among you. Give me a burial holding among you, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight."
And the sons of Heth answered Abraham:
"Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our burial places. Not one of us will refuse you his burial place for burying your dead."
Then Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
And he spoke with them: "If you are willing for me to bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and speak for me to Ephron son of Zohar,
"so that he may give me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him, at the end of his field. Let him give it to me for the full price, here in your presence, as a burial holding."
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, before all who came in at the gate of his city:
"No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and the cave that is in it — I give it to you. In the sight of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
Then Abraham bowed before the people of the land.
And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land: "If only you would hear me — I give the price of the field. Take it from me, and let me bury my dead there."
And Ephron answered Abraham:
"My lord, hear me. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver — what is that between me and you? Go and bury your dead."
Abraham listened to Ephron and weighed out to him the silver he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth: four hundred shekels of silver, at the merchants' standard.
So Ephron's field in Machpelah, facing Mamre, passed over — the field, the cave in it, and every tree in the field, within all its boundaries —
— to Abraham as a purchase, in the sight of the sons of Heth, before all who came in at the gate of his city.
After this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre — that is, Hebron — in the land of Canaan.
So the field and the cave in it passed to Abraham as a burial holding, from the sons of Heth.

genesis_24.t: Now Abraham was old, well on in years, and the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything.
And Abraham said to his servant, the senior man of his household, who had charge of everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh,
"and I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live,
"but you are to go to my land and my kindred and take a wife for my son, for Isaac."
And the servant said to him, "Suppose the woman isn't willing to come back with me to this land. Should I then take your son back to the land you came from?"
And Abraham said to him, "Be careful not to take my son back there.

"The LORD, the God of the heavens, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my kindred, who spoke to me and swore to me, 'To your offspring I will give this land' — he will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
"But if the woman isn't willing to come with you, then you are free from this oath of mine. Only you must not take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him about this matter.
Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and set out, with the best of his master's goods in his hand, and went to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water, toward evening, at the time when the women who draw water come out.
And he said, "O LORD, God of my master Abraham, let it happen for me today, and show loyalty to my master Abraham.
"Here I am, standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

"Let it be that the young woman I say to, 'Please lower your jar so I can drink,' and who answers, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too' — let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown loyalty to my master."
Before he had finished speaking, there was Rebekah coming out — born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother — with her jar on her shoulder.
The young woman was very good to look at, a virgin, and no man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.
The servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me have a sip of water from your jar."
And she said, "Drink, my lord." She hurried, lowered her jar onto her hand, and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "I'll draw for your camels too, until they have finished drinking."
So she hurried, emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
And the man watched her in silence, to know whether the LORD had made his journey successful or not.
When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing a beka and two gold bracelets for her hands weighing ten shekels,
and he said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."
And she said to him, "We have plenty of straw and fodder, and room to spend the night."
And the man bowed his head and bowed down to the LORD.

And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loyalty and his faithfulness toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the way, to the house of my master's kin."
And the young woman ran and told her mother's household about all this.
Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and Laban ran out to the man at the spring.

When he saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's hands, and heard Rebekah his sister say, "This is what the man said to me," he went out to the man — and there he was, standing with the camels at the spring.
And he said, "Come in, blessed of the LORD. Why are you standing outside? I've cleared the house, and a place for the camels."
So the man came into the house. The camels were unharnessed and given straw and fodder, and water was brought to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him.
Food was set before him, but he said, "I won't eat until I have said what I have to say." And he said, "Speak."
And he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
"The LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
"And Sarah, my master's wife, bore my master a son in her old age, and he has given him everything he has.
"And my master made me swear, 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
'but you are to go to my father's house and my family and take a wife for my son.'
"And I said to my master, 'Suppose the woman won't come with me.'
"And he said to me, 'The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and make your journey successful, and you will take a wife for my son from my family and my father's house.
'Then you will be free from my oath, once you have come to my family; and if they won't give her to you, you'll be free from my oath.'
"And today I came to the spring and said, 'O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if you are indeed making the journey I am on successful —
'here I am standing by the spring of water. Let it be that the young woman who comes out to draw, and to whom I say, "Please give me a little water from your jar,"
'and who says to me, "You drink, and I'll draw for your camels too" — let her be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master's son.'
"Before I had finished speaking in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
"She hurried and lowered her jar and said, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels as well.
"Then I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him.' So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
"And I bowed my head and bowed down to the LORD, and I blessed the LORD, God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way, to take the daughter of my master's kinsman for his son.
"So now, if you will show loyalty and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."
Then Laban and Bethuel answered, "This has come from the LORD. We cannot say anything to you, bad or good.
"Here is Rebekah, right in front of you. Take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken."
And when Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.
The servant brought out silver and gold articles and garments and gave them to Rebekah, and he gave costly gifts to her brother and her mother.
Then they ate and drank, he and the men with him, and spent the night. In the morning they rose, and he said, "Send me on my way to my master."
But her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us a while — ten days or so — and after that she can go."
But he said to them, "Don't delay me — the LORD has made my journey successful. Send me on my way, so I can go to my master."
And they said, "Let's call the young woman and ask her."
So they called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" And she said, "I will go."
So they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, along with Abraham's servant and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become thousands upon thousands, and may your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate them."
Then Rebekah and her young women rose, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and went.
Now Isaac had come from the direction of Beer-lahai-roi; he was living in the land of the Negev.
Isaac went out to walk in the field toward evening. He looked up, and there were camels coming.
And Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, and she got down from the camel.
And she said to the servant, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" And the servant said, "He is my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

genesis_25.t: Abraham married again. Her name was Keturah.
She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's sons were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim.
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All of these were Keturah's sons.
Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac.
To the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away from his son Isaac, east, to the land of the east.
These are the days of the years of Abraham's life: a hundred and seventy-five years.
Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and content, and he was gathered to his kin.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him at the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre —
the field Abraham bought from the sons of Heth. That is where Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, and Isaac settled by Beer-lahai-roi.
This is the account of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
These are the names of Ishmael's sons, name by name, in birth order: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are Ishmael's sons, and these are their names, by their villages and their camps: twelve chiefs, one for each of their peoples.
These are the years of Ishmael's life: a hundred and thirty-seven. He breathed his last and died, and he was gathered to his kin.
They settled from Havilah as far as Shur, which faces Egypt, on the way to Asshur. Over against all his brothers, he fell.
This is the account of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham fathered Isaac.
Isaac was forty when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she couldn't have children. The LORD answered him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
The sons struggled with each other inside her, and she said, "If it's like this, then why am I?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.
The LORD said to her, "There are two nations in your womb. Two peoples will come apart from inside you. One will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
When her time came to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
The first one came out ruddy, all of him like a hairy cloak, and they named him Esau.
After that his brother came out, his hand gripping Esau's heel, and he named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty when they were born.
The boys grew up. Esau knew how to hunt and lived in the open country; Jacob was a quiet man who lived among the tents.
Isaac loved Esau, because he had a taste for game; and Rebekah loved Jacob.
Jacob was cooking a stew when Esau came in from the open country, worn out.
Esau said to Jacob, "Let me gulp down some of that red stuff, that red there — I'm worn out." That's why he was named Edom.
Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright, right now."
Esau said, "Look, I'm going to die. So what good is a birthright to me?"
Jacob said, "Swear it to me right now." So he swore to him, and he sold his birthright to Jacob.
Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate, he drank, he got up, he left. That is how Esau despised the birthright.

genesis_26.t: There was a famine in the land, on top of the earlier famine back in Abraham's day. So Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
The LORD appeared to him and said, "Don't go down to Egypt. Settle in the land I tell you."
"Live here as an outsider, and I'll be with you and bless you. To you and your offspring I'll give all these lands, and I'll keep the oath I swore to Abraham your father."
"I'll multiply your offspring like the stars in the sky, and I'll give your offspring all these lands, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring —"
"— because Abraham listened to me and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws."
So Isaac settled in Gerar.
The men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, "She's my sister." He was afraid to say "my wife" — the men of the place might kill me over Rebekah, he thought, because she was beautiful.
After he'd been there a long while, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through the window, and there was Isaac, playing with Rebekah his wife.
Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "Look, she is obviously your wife. How could you say, 'She's my sister'?" Isaac said, "Because I thought I'd die over her."
Abimelech said, "What have you done to us? One of the people could easily have slept with your wife, and you'd have brought guilt down on us."
So Abimelech gave orders to all his people: "Anyone who touches this man or his wife will be put to death — no question."
Isaac sowed in that land, and that year he reaped a hundred times over; and the LORD blessed him.
The man grew rich, and he kept growing richer and richer, until he was very rich indeed.
He came to have flocks and herds and a large household of servants, and the Philistines were jealous of him.
As for all the wells his father's servants had dug back in Abraham's day, the Philistines stopped them up and filled them with earth.
Abimelech said to Isaac, "Leave us. You've become far too strong for us."
So Isaac moved on, camped in the Wadi of Gerar, and settled there.
Isaac dug out again the wells that had been dug in Abraham his father's day and that the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died, and he gave them the same names his father had given them.
Isaac's servants dug in the wadi and found a well of living water there.
The herdsmen of Gerar quarrelled with Isaac's herdsmen: "The water is ours." So he named the well Esek, because they had contended with him.
They dug another well, and they quarrelled over that one too, so he named it Sitnah.
He moved on from there and dug another well, and nobody quarrelled over that one. So he named it Rehoboth, and said, "Now the LORD has made room for us, and we'll be fruitful in the land."
From there he went up to Beer-sheba.
The LORD appeared to him that night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Don't be afraid — I am with you. I'll bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant."
So he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. He pitched his tent there, and Isaac's servants dug a well there.
Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me? You hate me, and you sent me away."
They said, "We've seen plainly that the LORD has been with you, so we said: let there be an oath between us — between us and you — and let's cut a covenant with you,"
"that you'll do us no harm, just as we never laid a hand on you and did nothing but good to you and sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD."
So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
They got up early in the morning and swore the oath to each other. Isaac sent them off, and they left him in peace.
That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they'd dug. "We've found water," they said.
So he named it Shibah. That's why the city is called Beer-sheba to this day.
When Esau was forty, he married Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
They were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and Rebekah.

genesis_27.t: When Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see, he called Esau his elder son. "My son," he said. "Here I am," he answered.
He said, "Look, I'm old. I don't know the day of my death."
"So now, take your gear, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the open country and hunt game for me,"
"and make me the savoury food I love, and bring it to me, and let me eat, so that I myself may bless you before I die."
Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau went out to the open country to hunt game and bring it back.
Rebekah said to Jacob her son, "Listen — I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother. He said,"
"'Bring me game and make me savoury food, let me eat, and let me bless you before the LORD before I die.'"
"Now then, my son, listen to me — to what I'm telling you to do."
"Go to the flock and fetch me two good young goats, and I'll make them into the savoury food your father loves,"
"and you'll bring it to your father, and he'll eat, so that he can bless you before he dies."
Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, and I'm smooth-skinned."
"What if my father feels me? I'll look to him like a mocker, and I'll bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing."
His mother said to him, "Let your curse fall on me, my son. Just listen to me — go and fetch them."
So he went and fetched them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made the savoury food his father loved.
Then Rebekah took her elder son Esau's garments — the choice ones she had in the house — and dressed her younger son Jacob in them.
And she put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
Then she put the savoury food and the bread she'd made into the hand of Jacob her son.
He came to his father and said, "My father." "Here I am," he said. "Which of my sons are you?"
Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau your firstborn. I've done what you told me. Please get up, sit, and eat some of my game, so that you yourself can bless me."
Isaac said to his son, "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" He said, "Because the LORD your God brought it my way."
Isaac said to Jacob, "Come here and let me feel you, my son — to see whether you really are my son Esau, or not."
Jacob came near to Isaac his father, and he felt him, and he said, "The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are Esau's hands."
He didn't recognise him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau's hands. So he blessed him.
And he said, "Are you really my son Esau?" He said, "I am."
He said, "Bring it here, and let me eat some of my son's game, so that I myself can bless you." So he brought it to him and he ate, and he brought him wine and he drank.
Then Isaac his father said to him, "Come here and kiss me, my son."
So he came near and kissed him, and he smelled the smell of his garments, and he blessed him. He said: "See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field the LORD has blessed."
"And may God give you the dew of the heavens and the rich places of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine."
"May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Those who curse you, be they cursed; those who bless you, be they blessed."
Just as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob — Jacob had barely gone out from his father Isaac's presence — Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
He too made savoury food and brought it to his father, and he said to his father, "Let my father get up and eat some of his son's game, so that you yourself can bless me."
Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" He said, "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."
Isaac trembled a great trembling, violently, and said, "Then who was it who hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it all before you came, and I blessed him. And indeed, he will stay blessed."
When Esau heard his father's words, he cried out — a great and bitter cry — and said to his father, "Bless me too, my father!"
He said, "Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing."
He said, "Is that why he's called Jacob? He has supplanted me twice now. He took my birthright, and now he's taken my blessing." And he said, "Haven't you kept back a blessing for me?"

Isaac answered Esau, "Look, I have made him lord over you, and I've given him all his brothers as servants, and I've sustained him with grain and new wine. So what is there left for me to do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father, "Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!" And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
Isaac his father answered him: "Look — your dwelling will be away from the rich places of the earth, away from the dew of the heavens above."
"You'll live by your sword, and you'll serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you'll tear his yoke off your neck."
Esau held a grudge against Jacob over the blessing his father had given him, and Esau said to himself, "The days of mourning for my father are coming close. Then I'll kill Jacob my brother."

Esau's words — her elder son's words — were reported to Rebekah, so she sent and called for Jacob her younger son and said to him, "Look, Esau your brother is consoling himself about you by planning to kill you."
"Now then, my son, listen to me: get up and run to Laban my brother in Haran,"
"and stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury dies down,"
"until your brother's anger turns away from you and he forgets what you did to him. Then I'll send for you and bring you back. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"
Rebekah said to Isaac, "I'm sick of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth like these, from the women of this land, what is life worth to me?"

genesis_28.t: So Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and he gave him this command: "You are not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan."
"Get up, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother."
"May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful, and multiply you, and may you become a company of peoples."
"And may he give you the blessing of Abraham — to you and to your offspring with you — so that you may take possession of the land where you have lived as an outsider, the land God gave to Abraham."
So Isaac sent Jacob off, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him off to Paddan-aram to find a wife there, and that when he blessed him he had ordered him, "You are not to take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"
and that Jacob had listened to his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan-aram.
So Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing to Isaac his father.
So Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, Nebaioth's sister, as a wife, on top of the wives he already had.
Jacob left Beer-sheba and set out for Haran.
He came upon the place and stopped there for the night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, put it at his head, and lay down there.
And he dreamed: there was a ladder set on the earth, its top reaching the heavens, and angels of God were going up and coming down on it.
And there was the LORD, standing over it, and he said, "I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land you are lying on — I will give it to you and to your offspring."
"Your offspring will be like the dust of the earth, and you'll spread out west and east, north and south; and all the families of the earth will be blessed in you and in your offspring."
"And look, I am with you. I'll keep you wherever you go, and I'll bring you back to this ground. I won't abandon you until I've done what I've promised you."
Jacob woke from his sleep and said, "The LORD really is in this place, and I didn't know it."
And he was afraid, and he said, "How fearsome this place is! This is nothing but the house of God — this is the gate of the heavens."
Jacob got up early in the morning, took the stone he'd put at his head, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
And he named that place Beth-el, though the city had earlier been called Luz.
Then Jacob vowed a vow: "If God will be with me and keep me on this journey I'm making, and give me bread to eat and clothes to wear,"
"and I come back safe to my father's house — then the LORD will be my God,"
"and this stone, which I've set up as a pillar, will be the house of God; and of everything you give me, I will certainly give a tenth back to you."

genesis_29.t: Then Jacob lifted his feet and went on to the land of the people of the east.
He looked, and there was a well in the open country with three flocks of sheep lying beside it — that was where the flocks were watered — and the stone over the mouth of the well was large.
All the flocks would be gathered there, and they'd roll the stone off the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and then put the stone back over the mouth of the well, in its place.
Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" They said, "We're from Haran."
He said to them, "Do you know Laban son of Nahor?" They said, "We know him."
He said to them, "Is he well?" They said, "He is. And look — Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep."
He said, "Look, the day is still long. It's not time for the livestock to be gathered in. Water the sheep and go, put them out to pasture."
They said, "We can't, not until all the flocks are gathered and the stone is rolled off the mouth of the well. Then we water the sheep."
While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, because she was a shepherd.

When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob came forward, rolled the stone off the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.
Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he lifted up his voice and wept.
Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's kinsman and Rebekah's son, and she ran and told her father.
When Laban heard the news of Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban the whole story.
Laban said to him, "You really are my bone and my flesh." And he stayed with him a full month.
Then Laban said to Jacob, "Just because you're my kinsman, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me — what should your wages be?"
Now Laban had two daughters. The elder was named Leah, the younger Rachel.
Leah's eyes were soft, but Rachel was beautiful in form and beautiful to look at.
Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I'll serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter."
Laban said, "Better that I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me."
So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him like a few days, because of his love for her.
Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife — my days are completed — so that I may go in to her."
So Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.
In the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.
And Laban gave Zilpah his maidservant to her — to Leah his daughter — as a maidservant.
In the morning — there she was: Leah. And he said to Laban, "What is this you've done to me? Wasn't it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?"
Laban said, "That's not how it's done in our place — giving the younger before the firstborn."
"Finish this one's bridal week, and we'll give you the other one too, in return for another seven years of service with me."
So Jacob did that and completed Leah's bridal week, and Laban gave him Rachel his daughter as a wife.
And Laban gave Bilhah his maidservant to Rachel his daughter, to be her maidservant.
So he went in to Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served him another seven years.
The LORD saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb; and Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived and bore a son, and she named him Reuben, because she said, "The LORD has looked on my affliction — surely now my husband will love me."
She conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has given me this one too." And she named him Simeon.
She conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me — I've borne him three sons." So he named him Levi.
She conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "This time I will praise the LORD." So she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing children.

genesis_30.t: When Rachel saw that she'd borne Jacob no children, she was jealous of her sister, and she said to Jacob, "Give me children! And if not, I'm dead."
Jacob's anger burned against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in God's place? He is the one who has withheld the fruit of the womb from you."
She said, "Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Go in to her, and let her give birth on my knees, and I too will be built up through her."
So she gave him Bilhah her maidservant as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.
Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said, "God has judged me, and he has also listened to my voice and given me a son." So she named him Dan.
Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob.
And Rachel said, "With mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed." And she named him Naphtali.
When Leah saw that she'd stopped bearing children, she took Zilpah her maidservant and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore Jacob a son.
And Leah said, "Fortune has come!" And she named him Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, bore a second son to Jacob.
And Leah said, "How happy I am! Daughters will call me happy." And she named him Asher.
In the days of the wheat harvest Reuben went out and found mandrakes in the open country, and he brought them to Leah his mother. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."

She said to her, "Is it a small thing that you took my husband? Now you'd take my son's mandrakes as well?" And Rachel said, "All right — let him lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."

When Jacob came in from the open country that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, "You're to come in to me — I have hired you, and paid with my son's mandrakes." And he lay with her that night.
And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
And Leah said, "God has given me my wages, because I gave my maidservant to my husband." And she named him Issachar.
Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
And Leah said, "God has endowed me with a good endowment. This time my husband will exalt me — I've borne him six sons." And she named him Zebulun.
And afterward she bore a daughter, and she named her Dinah.
Then God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb.
She conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has taken away my reproach."
And she named him Joseph, saying, "May the LORD add another son to me."
When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me off, so I can go to my place and my land."
