Then his brothers themselves came and fell down before him and said, "Here we are — your slaves."
But Joseph said to them, "Don't be afraid. Am I in the place of God?"
"You devised evil against me; God devised it for good — to bring about what we see today, to keep a great many people alive.
"So don't be afraid. I will provide for you and your children myself." And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.
So Joseph stayed in Egypt, he and his father's household, and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
Joseph saw Ephraim's descendants to the third generation, and the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were also born on Joseph's knees.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will surely attend to you and bring you up out of this land to the land he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath: "God will surely attend to you, and you must carry my bones up from here."
So Joseph died at a hundred and ten years old. They embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

habakkuk_1.t: The oracle Habakkuk the prophet saw.
How long, LORD, have I cried for help and you don't hear? I cry out to you, "Violence!" and you don't save.
Why do you make me see wickedness, and look on mischief? Devastation and violence are right in front of me; there's strife, and contention keeps rising.
So law goes numb, and justice never comes out. The wicked hem in the righteous; so when justice comes out, it comes out twisted.
Look among the nations — look hard — and be astounded, astonished! Because there's a work being done in your days that you wouldn't believe if you were told it.
Look — I'm raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter, headlong nation, marching across the wide places of the earth to take possession of homes that aren't theirs.
It is terrifying, dreadful; its justice and its standing come from nowhere but itself.
Its horses are swifter than leopards, keener than wolves at evening; its warhorses paw the ground. Its horsemen come from a long way off; they fly in like an eagle rushing to devour.
All of it comes for violence; their faces are all set one way, eastward; it gathers captives like sand.
It makes fun of kings; rulers are a joke to it. It laughs at every fortress — heaps up a ramp of earth and takes it.
Then it sweeps on like a wind and passes over — and he is guilty, this one whose strength is his god.
Aren't you from of old, LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, you appointed it for judgement; and Rock, you established it to reprove.
Your eyes are too pure to look at evil; you can't look at mischief. So why do you look at the treacherous, and keep silent while the wicked swallows someone more righteous than he is?
And you make humankind like fish in the sea, like creeping things with no one ruling over them.
He hauls all of it up on a hook; he drags it off in his net and gathers it into his dragnet. So he rejoices, he is glad.
So he sacrifices to his net and sends up smoke to his dragnet, because thanks to them his portion is fat and his food is rich.
Is he to keep emptying his net, killing nations on and on and never sparing them?

habakkuk_2.t: I'll stand at my post, I'll station myself on the rampart, and I'll watch to see what he'll say to me — and what I'm to answer about my complaint.
And the LORD answered me: Write the vision down, make it plain on the tablets, so that whoever reads it can run.
The vision is still waiting for its appointed time; it pants toward the end, and it does not lie. If it's slow, wait for it — it will surely come; it won't be late.
Look — his being is puffed up; there is nothing upright in it. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

And more than that — wine is treacherous. An arrogant man, and he never rests; he has made his throat as wide as Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself, he assembles all the peoples to himself.
Won't all of them take up a saying against him, a mocking song full of riddles, and say: "Woe to the one who piles up what isn't his — how long? — and loads himself down with pledges!"
Won't your creditors suddenly get up, and the ones who make you tremble wake? And you'll become plunder for them.
Because you plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you — because of human blood and violence done to the land, to the town and everyone living in it.
Woe to the one who makes an evil profit for his house, setting his nest up high to get himself out of harm's reach!
You've planned shame for your house — cutting off many peoples, and sinning against your own being.
A stone will cry out from the wall, and a rafter from the woodwork will answer it.
Woe to the one who builds a city with blood, and founds a town on injustice!
Isn't it from the LORD of hosts that peoples labour only for fire, and nations wear themselves out for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, the way the waters cover the sea.
Woe to the one who makes his neighbour drink — you, pouring out your rage, getting them drunk too — so you can stare at their nakedness!
You've had your fill of shame instead of glory. Drink, you too — and be uncircumcised! The cup in the LORD's right hand will come round to you, and disgrace on top of your glory.
For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the devastation of the animals will terrify them — because of human blood and violence done to the land, to the town and everyone living in it.
What good is a carved image, that its maker went and carved it — a cast image, a teacher of lies — so that the one who shaped it trusts in his own shaping, making worthless idols that can't speak?
Woe to the one who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" — "Awake!" to a stone that says nothing. Can it teach? Look at it: overlaid with gold and silver, and not a breath inside it.
But the LORD is in his holy temple. Hush before him, all the earth.

habakkuk_3.t: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, on shigionoth.
LORD, I've heard the report of you, and I was afraid. LORD, your work — in the middle of the years, revive it; in the middle of the years, make it known. In wrath, remember to have compassion.
God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendour has covered the heavens; his praise has filled the earth.
And the brightness is like daylight; rays come from his hand; and there is the hiding place of his strength.
Pestilence goes ahead of him, and a flame goes out at his feet.
He stood, and the earth shook; he looked, and the nations jumped. The ancient mountains were shattered; the everlasting hills bowed down. The everlasting ways are his.
I saw the tents of Cushan in trouble; the curtains of the land of Midian are trembling.
Was the LORD angry at the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, or your fury against the sea, that you ride on your horses, your chariots of salvation?
Your bow is stripped bare; oaths of arrows — a word. Selah. With rivers you split the earth.
The mountains saw you and writhed. A downpour of water swept past. The deep gave its voice; it lifted its hands high.
Sun, moon — it stood still in its lofty abode at the light of your arrows going out, at the brightness of your flashing spear.
In indignation you marched through the earth; in anger you trampled the nations down.
You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You shattered the head off the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
You pierced the head of his warriors with his own arrows — they storm out to scatter me, exulting as if to devour the afflicted in secret.
You trod on the sea with your horses, the heaping up of many waters.

I heard, and my belly trembled; at the sound my lips quivered. Rottenness came into my bones; I trembled where I stood — knowing I must wait quietly for the day of distress, for the coming up against the people who attack us.

Though the fig tree doesn't blossom, and there's no produce on the vines; though the olive crop fails, and the fields produce no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there's no cattle in the stalls —
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
GOD the Lord is my strength. He makes my feet like a doe's, and he makes me tread on my high places. To the choirmaster, with my stringed instruments.

haggai_1.t: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: These people say, 'The time hasn't come — the time for the LORD's house to be built.'
Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet.
Is it time for you — you yourselves — to live in your panelled houses while this house lies desolate?
So now, this is what the LORD of hosts says: Set your heart on your ways.

You've sown a lot and brought in a little. You eat, and you're not satisfied. You drink, and you're never filled. You put on clothes, and nobody's warm. And whoever earns wages earns them into a bag full of holes.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Set your heart on your ways.
Go up into the hill country, bring wood, and build the house. Then I'll take pleasure in it, and I'll be honoured, says the LORD.

You looked for a lot, and it came to little. And when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of hosts. Because my house lies desolate while every one of you runs off to his own house.
That's why the heavens above you have withheld their dew, and the land has withheld its produce.
And I called down a drought on the land and the mountains — on the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, on what the ground brings forth, on people and livestock, and on all the toil of your hands.

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the LORD their God and to the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people were afraid before the LORD.
Then Haggai, the LORD's messenger, gave the people the LORD's message: I am with you, declares the LORD.

And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. They came and set to work on the house of the LORD of hosts their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.

haggai_2.t: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet.
Say to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and to the remnant of the people:
Who's left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how does it look to you now? Isn't it as nothing in your eyes?

So now, be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD — and get to work. Because I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts.
The word that I cut with you when you came out of Egypt — and my spirit stands among you. Don't be afraid.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Once more — it's only a little while — and I'm going to shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I'll shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come in, and I'll fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.
The silver is mine and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of hosts.
The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts. And in this place I'll give peace, declares the LORD of hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Ask the priests about the law.
Suppose a man is carrying holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with that skirt he touches bread, or cooked food, or wine, or oil, or any food. Does it become holy? The priests answered, No.
Then Haggai said: If someone made unclean by a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean? The priests answered, It becomes unclean.
Then Haggai answered: So it is with this people, so it is with this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so it is with every work of their hands. And what they offer there is unclean.
So now, set your heart on this, from this day on: before stone was laid on stone in the temple of the LORD —
from how things were then: you'd come to a heap of twenty measures and find ten; you'd come to the vat to draw off fifty and find twenty.
I struck you with blight and mildew and hail — all the work of your hands — and still you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
Set your heart on this, from this day on — from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid. Set your heart on it.
Is the seed still in the granary? Even the vine, the fig, the pomegranate and the olive tree haven't borne. From this day on, I will bless.
And the word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time, on the twenty-fourth day of the month.
Say to Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah: I'm going to shake the heavens and the earth,

and I'll overthrow the throne of kingdoms and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I'll overthrow chariotry and its riders, and horses and their riders will go down, each by his brother's sword.

On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I'll take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declares the LORD. I'll make you like a signet ring, because I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts.

hosea_1.t: The word of the LORD came to Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

This is where the LORD began speaking through Hosea. The LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, because the land is prostituting itself away from the LORD."
So he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
And the LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel, because in a little while I'll visit the bloodshed of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and I'll put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
On that day I'll break Israel's bow in the valley of Jezreel."
She conceived again and bore a daughter. And he said to him, "Name her Lo-ruhamah, because I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel — I won't forgive them at all.
But on the house of Judah I'll have compassion. I'll save them by the LORD their God — not by bow or sword or battle, not by horses or horsemen."
When she'd weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
And he said, "Name him Lo-ammi, because you are not my people, and I will not be your God."

Yet the number of the people of Israel will be like the sand of the sea — it can't be measured, it can't be counted. And in the very place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."
The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together. They'll appoint one head for themselves and go up from the land — great will be the day of Jezreel.

hosea_2.t: Say to your brothers, "Ammi," and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."
Bring a case against your mother, bring a case — she is not my wife and I am not her husband. Let her put away her prostitutions from her face, her adulteries from between her breasts,
or I will strip her naked and set her out as on the day she was born, make her like the wilderness, set her like a parched land, and kill her with thirst.
And on her children I will have no compassion, for they are children of prostitution.

Their mother has prostituted herself; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. She said, "Let me go after my lovers — they give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
So I am about to hedge up your way with thorns, and wall up her wall, so she can't find her paths.
She'll chase her lovers and not catch them; she'll look for them and not find them. And she'll say, "Let me go back to my first husband — it was better for me then than now."
She didn't know that it was I who gave her the grain and the new wine and the fresh oil, that I lavished silver on her, and gold — which they made into the Baal.
So I'll take back my grain when its time comes and my new wine at its appointed time, and snatch away my wool and my flax, the things meant to cover her nakedness.
And now I'll uncover her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
And I'll put an end to all her rejoicing — her festival, her new moon, her sabbath, all her appointed feasts.
I'll lay waste her vine and her fig tree, the ones she said were her fee, the gift of her lovers. I'll turn them into a thicket, and the wild animals of the field will devour them.
I'll visit on her the days of the Baals, when she burned offerings to them, decked herself with her ring and her jewellery, and went after her lovers — and forgot me. Declaration of the LORD.
So I am about to allure her. I'll lead her into the wilderness and speak to her heart.
From there I'll give her back her vineyards, and the valley of Achor as a door of hope. She'll answer there as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up from the land of Egypt.
On that day — declaration of the LORD — you will call me "My husband," and you'll no longer call me "My baal."
I'll remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they'll no longer be invoked by name.

On that day I'll cut a covenant for them with the wild animals of the field, the birds of the sky, and the creeping things of the ground. Bow and sword and battle I'll break from the land, and I'll make them lie down in safety.
I will betroth you to myself for ever. I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in steadfast love and compassion.
I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
On that day I will answer — declaration of the LORD — I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth,
and the earth will answer the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
I'll sow her for myself in the land. I'll have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I'll say to Lo-ammi, "You are my people," and he will say, "My God."

hosea_3.t: And the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another and commits adultery — the way the LORD loves the people of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins."
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, a homer of barley and a lethech of barley.
And I said to her, "For a long time you're to stay for me. You're not to prostitute yourself, not to belong to a man — and I likewise will be toward you."
For a long time the people of Israel will remain without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or teraphim.
Afterwards the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king, and they'll come in dread to the LORD and to his goodness at the end of the days.

hosea_4.t: Hear the word of the LORD, people of Israel. The LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land: there is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, no knowledge of God in the land.
Cursing, deceiving, murder, theft, adultery — they've broken out, and bloodshed touches bloodshed.
So the land mourns, and everyone living in it withers — with the wild animals of the field and the birds of the sky; even the fish of the sea are swept away.
Yet let no one bring a case; let no one reprove — your people are like those who contend with a priest.
You will stumble by day, and a prophet will stumble with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you've rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving me as a priest; and because you've forgotten the law of your God, I in turn will forget your children.
The more they increased, the more they sinned against me. I will exchange their glory for shame.
They feed on the sin offering of my people, and set their appetite on their iniquity.
And it will be: as the people, so the priest. I'll visit his ways on him and repay him his deeds.
They'll eat and not be satisfied; they'll prostitute themselves and not increase, for they have abandoned the LORD, to keep —
Prostitution and wine and new wine take away the heart.
My people ask a piece of wood, and their stick tells them, because a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they've prostituted themselves out from under their God.

On the mountaintops they sacrifice, on the hills they burn offerings, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because the shade is good. So your daughters prostitute themselves and your brides commit adultery.

I won't visit judgement on your daughters when they prostitute themselves, or on your brides when they commit adultery — the men themselves go apart with the prostitutes and sacrifice with the shrine prostitutes. And a people with no understanding comes to ruin.
Though you prostitute yourself, Israel, don't let Judah become guilty. Don't go to Gilgal, don't go up to Beth-aven, and don't swear, "As the LORD lives."
Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. Will the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in an open meadow?
Ephraim is joined to idols. Let him alone.
Their drink is gone; they have utterly prostituted themselves. Her shields dearly love shame.
A wind has wrapped her up in its wings, and they'll be ashamed of their sacrifices.

hosea_5.t: Hear this, priests; pay attention, house of Israel; give ear, house of the king — the sentence falls on you. You've been a trap at Mizpah, a net spread over Tabor.
And in slaughtering, rebels have gone deep; and I am a discipline to all of them.
I know Ephraim, and Israel isn't hidden from me. Now you've prostituted yourself, Ephraim; Israel has made itself unclean.
Their deeds won't let them return to their God, because a spirit of prostitution is inside them, and they don't know the LORD.
Israel's pride testifies against him; Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their iniquity, and Judah has stumbled with them.
With their flocks and their herds they'll go to seek the LORD, and they won't find him. He has withdrawn from them.
They've dealt treacherously against the LORD; they've borne strange children. Now a new moon will devour them along with their fields.
Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Raise the alarm at Beth-aven — behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will become a waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I make known what is certain.
Judah's leaders have become like those who move a boundary marker. On them I'll pour out my fury like water.
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in his right, because he was set on going after a command.
I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to king Jareb. But he can't heal you, or cure your wound.
I am like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I, I myself will tear and go; I'll carry off, and there is no one to deliver.
I will go and return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they'll seek me earnestly.

hosea_6.t: Come, let us return to the LORD. He has torn, and he will heal us; he has struck, and he will bind us up.
He'll revive us after two days; on the third day he'll raise us up, and we'll live before him.
Let us know — let us pursue the knowledge of the LORD. His going forth is as sure as the dawn. He'll come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your steadfast love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that's gone early.
So I have hewn them by the prophets, killed them by the sayings of my mouth; and my judgement on you goes forth like light.
It is steadfast love I desire, not sacrifice — the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they dealt treacherously with me.
Gilead is a town of evildoers, tracked with blood.
Like marauders lying in wait for a man, so is a company of priests — they murder on the road to Shechem. They have committed depravity.
In the house of Israel I've seen a horrible thing: Ephraim's prostitution is there; Israel has made itself unclean.
For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I turn back the fortunes of my people.

hosea_7.t: When I would heal Israel, Ephraim's iniquity is uncovered and the evils of Samaria — they practise falsehood. A thief breaks in; a marauding band strips outside.
And they never say in their heart that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds have surrounded them; they are right before my face.
With their evil they make the king glad, with their lies, the princes.
They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker who stops stirring the fire from the kneading of the dough until it rises.
On the day of our king the princes made themselves sick with the fever of wine; he stretched out his hand with scorners.
They bring their heart near like an oven in their ambush. All night their baker sleeps; in the morning it burns like a flaming fire.
They all grow hot like the oven and devour their rulers. All their kings have fallen; not one of them calls to me.
Ephraim mixes himself in among the peoples. Ephraim has become a flat cake that was never turned over.
Strangers have devoured his strength, and he doesn't know it; grey hair is sprinkled on him too, and he doesn't know it.
Israel's pride testifies against him, yet they haven't returned to the LORD their God or sought him, for all this.
Ephraim has become like a silly dove with no sense: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
As they go, I'll spread my net over them; I'll bring them down like a bird of the sky. I'll chastise them according to the report to their assembly.
Woe to them — they have strayed from me! Devastation to them — they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they have spoken lies against me.
They haven't cried out to me from their heart; they wail on their beds, assemble themselves over grain and new wine, and turn away from me.
I disciplined them, I strengthened their arms, and against me they plot evil.
They turn — but not upward. They've become like a slack bow. Their princes will fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongue. This will be their derision in the land of Egypt.

hosea_8.t: Put the horn to your lips! One comes like an eagle over the house of the LORD — because they have transgressed my covenant and rebelled against my law.
To me they cry out, "My God, we know you — Israel!"
Israel has rejected good; an enemy will pursue him.
They made kings for themselves, but not from me; they made princes, and I didn't know it. Out of their silver and gold they made idols for themselves — so that it will be cut off.
He has rejected your calf, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
It is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. The calf of Samaria will be broken to pieces.
They sow wind, and they'll reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; the shoot will yield no flour; and if it did, strangers would swallow it.
Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a vessel no one wants.
They've gone up to Assyria — a wild donkey off on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
Even though they hire among the nations, now I'll gather them in; and they have begun to dwindle under the burden of a king of princes.
Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, and they have become to him altars for sinning.
I wrote out for him the multitude of my law, and it was regarded as something foreign.
As for the sacrifices of my gifts — they sacrifice flesh and eat it; the LORD is not pleased with them. Now he'll remember their iniquity and visit their sins: they will return to Egypt.
Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied fortified cities. But I'll send fire on his cities, and it will consume her fortresses.

hosea_9.t: Don't rejoice, Israel, don't exult like the peoples — you have prostituted yourself away from your God. You've loved a prostitute's fee on every threshing floor of grain.
Threshing floor and winepress won't feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
They won't remain in the land of the LORD. Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they'll eat what is unclean.

They won't pour out wine to the LORD, and their sacrifices won't please him. Their bread will be like the bread of mourners: everyone who eats it makes himself unclean. Their bread is for their own hunger; it will not come into the house of the LORD.
What will you do on the day of the appointed feast, on the day of the festival of the LORD?
Look — they have gone away from devastation; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them. Nettles will take over the treasure of their silver; thorns will fill their tents.

The days of punishment have come; the days of recompense have come. Let Israel know it! "The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad" — because your iniquity is great, and great is the animosity.
The prophet is Ephraim's watchman with my God; yet a fowler's trap lies on all his ways, and animosity is in the house of his God.
They've gone deep in corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. He'll remember their iniquity; he'll visit their sins.

Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like an early fig on a fig tree in its first season I saw your fathers. But they came to Baal-peor and devoted themselves to the shameful thing, and they became as detestable as the thing they loved.
Ephraim — their glory will fly away like a bird: no birth, no womb, no conception.
Even if they raise their children, I'll bereave them of every one. Woe to them when I turn away from them!
Ephraim, as I have seen it, is planted in a meadow like Tyre; yet Ephraim must bring out his children to the slayer.
Give them, LORD — what will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
All their evil is at Gilgal — there I came to hate them. Because of the evil of their deeds I'll drive them out of my house. I'll not love them again; all their princes are rebels.
Ephraim is struck down; their root is dried up; they'll bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I'll put to death the precious fruit of their womb.
My God will reject them, because they haven't listened to him; and they'll be wanderers among the nations.

hosea_10.t: Israel is a spreading vine that makes fruit for itself. The more his fruit, the more altars he built; the better his land, the better the pillars they made.
Their heart is divided; now they'll bear their guilt. He'll break down their altars; he'll destroy their pillars.
Now they'll say, "We have no king, because we didn't fear the LORD — and what could a king do for us anyway?"
They speak words, swear false oaths, cut covenants; and justice springs up like a poison-weed in the furrows of a field.
For the calves of Beth-aven the inhabitants of Samaria will be in dread. Its people will mourn over it, its idol-priests will writhe over it — over its glory, because it has gone into exile.
It too will be carried off to Assyria as tribute to king Jareb. Ephraim will take shame; Israel will be ashamed of its own counsel.
Samaria is destroyed; her king is like a twig on the face of the water.
The high places of Aven — the sin of Israel — will be destroyed. Thorn and thistle will come up over their altars. And they'll say to the mountains, "Cover us," and to the hills, "Fall on us."
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel; there they have stood. Will war not overtake them in Gibeah, against the sons of injustice?
At my desire I'll discipline them, and peoples will be gathered against them when they're harnessed to their double iniquity.
Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, and I passed over the goodness of her neck. I'll put Ephraim to the yoke; Judah will plough; Jacob will harrow for himself.
Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap according to steadfast love. Break up for yourselves untilled ground. It is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
You've ploughed wickedness, reaped injustice, eaten the fruit of lying, because you trusted in your own way, in the multitude of your warriors.
An uproar will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel on the day of battle — mothers dashed to pieces on their children.
This is what will be done to you, Bethel, because of your great evil. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly destroyed.

hosea_11.t: When Israel was a boy, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
They called to them, and so they went away from them. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned offerings to the carved images.
I myself taught Ephraim to walk, taking them in my arms — and they didn't know it was I who healed them.
With human cords I drew them, with ropes of love. I was to them like one who lifts the yoke from their jaws, and I bent down to him and fed him.
He won't return to the land of Egypt — Assyria will be his king, because they've refused to return.
A sword will whirl through his cities, put an end to his gate-bars and devour them, because of their counsels.
My people are bent on turning away from me. Though they call him upward, not one of them exalts him.

How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart is overturned within me; my compassions have grown warm together.
I won't carry out the burning of my anger; I won't turn back to destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not a human, the Holy One in your midst — and I will not come in rage.
They will walk after the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, children will come trembling from the west.
They'll come trembling like a bird from Egypt, like a dove from the land of Assyria; and I'll settle them in their homes. Declaration of the LORD.
Ephraim has surrounded me with lying, the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still walks with God, and with the Holy One he is faithful.

hosea_12.t: Ephraim feeds on wind and chases the east wind all day long; he multiplies lying and violence. They cut a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried off to Egypt.
The LORD has a case against Judah, to visit judgement on Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he'll repay him.
In the womb he grabbed his brother's heel, and in his vigour he struggled with God.
He struggled against an angel and prevailed; he wept and sought his favour. At Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us —
and the LORD, the God of hosts — the LORD is his memorial name.
And you — return to your God! Keep steadfast love and justice, and wait for your God continually.
A merchant! In his hand are crooked scales; he loves to defraud.
And Ephraim said, "I've grown rich; I've made a fortune for myself. In all my gains they'll find no iniquity in me, nothing that is sin."
I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will make you dwell in tents again, as in the days of the appointed feast.
I spoke to the prophets; I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I gave likenesses.
If Gilead is iniquity, they've certainly become worthless. In Gilgal they have sacrificed bulls, and their altars are like heaps of stones in the furrows of a field.
Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept flocks.
And by a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was kept.
Ephraim has given bitter provocation; so his Lord will leave his bloodshed on him and turn his reproach back on him.

hosea_13.t: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty through the Baal, and he died.

And now they go on sinning: they've made themselves a molten image out of their silver, idols of their own devising, all of it the work of craftsmen. Of them they say, "Let the men who sacrifice kiss calves."
So they'll be like a morning cloud, like dew that's gone early, like chaff driven off a threshing floor by a storm, like smoke from a lattice.
I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. You shall know no god but me; there is no saviour besides me.
I knew you in the wilderness, in a land of drought.
When they had their pasture they were satisfied; they were satisfied, and their heart grew proud. So they forgot me.
So I became to them like a lion; like a leopard I'll watch beside the road.
I'll meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs and tear open the enclosure of their heart. I'll devour them there like a lion; the wild animals of the field will rip them open.
It has destroyed you, Israel, that you were against me, against your help.
Where now is your king, to save you in all your cities? Where are your rulers, the ones you asked for when you said, "Give me a king and princes"?
I gave you a king in my anger, and I take him away in my fury.
Ephraim's iniquity is bound up; his sin is stored away.
The pains of a woman in labour will come on him. He is a son with no wisdom: when the time comes he doesn't present himself at the mouth of the womb.
I will ransom them from the hand of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death. Where are your plagues, Death? Where is your destruction, Sheol? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.

Though he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come — the wind of the LORD, coming up from the wilderness. His spring will dry up, his fountain will be parched. It will plunder the treasury of every precious thing.
Samaria will bear her guilt, for she has rebelled against her God. By the sword they will fall; their infants will be dashed to pieces, her pregnant women ripped open.

hosea_14.t: Return, Israel, to the LORD your God — you have stumbled in your iniquity.
Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him, "Forgive all iniquity, receive what is good, and let us pay the bulls of our lips."
Assyria won't save us; we won't ride on horses; we'll no longer say "Our God" to the work of our hands — for in you the fatherless finds compassion.
I'll heal their turning away; I'll love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.
I'll be like the dew to Israel. He'll blossom like the lily and strike his roots like Lebanon.
His young shoots will spread out; his splendour will be like the olive tree, his fragrance like Lebanon.
Those who dwell in his shade will return; they'll revive the grain and blossom like the vine. His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim — what have I to do with idols any more? I have answered and I will watch over him. I am like a green cypress; from me your fruit is found.
Who is wise? Let him understand these things. Who is discerning? Let him know them. The ways of the LORD are upright; the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.

isaiah_1.t: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Listen, heavens; give ear, earth — the LORD has spoken: I brought children up, I raised them high, and they have transgressed against me.
An ox knows who owns it, a donkey knows its master's trough; Israel doesn't know, my people doesn't understand.

Woe — a sinning nation, a people weighed down with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They've forsaken the LORD, they've spurned the Holy One of Israel, they've turned their backs.
Where do you want to be struck next? You keep on turning away. The whole head is sick, the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the head there's no sound place in it — bruise and welt and open wound, not pressed out, not bound up, not softened with oil.
Your land is a desolation, your cities are burned with fire; your ground — right in front of you strangers are devouring it, a desolation, like an overthrow by strangers.
And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, like a shelter in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
If the LORD of hosts hadn't left us a few survivors, we'd have been like Sodom, we'd have been just like Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the LORD, rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the law of our God, people of Gomorrah!
'What are all your sacrifices to me?' says the LORD. 'I've had my fill of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts. The blood of bulls and lambs and he-goats — I take no pleasure in it.
When you come to appear before me, who asked this of you — this trampling of my courts?
Stop bringing worthless offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moon and sabbath, the calling of an assembly — I can't endure wrongdoing alongside solemn assembly.
Your new moons and your appointed times — I hate them with my whole being. They've become a burden to me. I'm tired of carrying them.
When you spread out your hands, I'll hide my eyes from you. Even if you pray and pray, I'm not listening. Your hands are full of blood.
Wash. Make yourselves clean. Get the evil of your deeds out of my sight. Stop doing evil.
learn to do good. Seek justice. Set the oppressor right. Vindicate the fatherless. Take up the widow's case.
'Come now, let's argue it out together,' says the LORD. 'Though your sins are like scarlet, they'll turn white as snow; though they're red like the worm, they'll be like wool.
If you're willing and you listen, you'll eat the good of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, you'll be eaten by the sword. The mouth of the LORD has spoken.
How she's become a prostitute — the faithful town! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her — and now, murderers.
Your silver has turned to dross; your drink is watered down.
Your officials are stubborn, friends of thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases after payments. They don't vindicate the fatherless, and the widow's case never gets to them.
Therefore — declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: 'Ah, I'll get relief from my foes and take my revenge on my enemies.
And I'll turn my hand against you, refine your dross away as with lye, and remove all your alloy.
And I'll restore your judges as they were at first, your counsellors as at the beginning. After that you'll be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful Town.
Zion will be ransomed by justice, and those in her who turn back, by righteousness.
But transgressors and sinners will be crushed together, and those who forsake the LORD will come to an end.
For they'll be ashamed of the great trees you wanted, and humiliated by the gardens you chose.
For you'll be like a terebinth with its leaves withering, and like a garden with no water.
And the strong one will become tow, and his work a spark; the two of them will burn together, and no one will put them out.

isaiah_2.t: The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
And it will be, at the end of the days, that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established at the head of the mountains, lifted above the hills; and all the nations will stream to it.

And many peoples will come and say: 'Come, let's go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so he can teach us his ways and we can walk in his paths.' For law goes out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

And he'll judge between the nations and hand down decisions for many peoples; and they'll beat their swords into ploughshares and their spears into pruning knives. Nation won't lift up sword against nation, and they won't learn war any more.
House of Jacob — come, let's walk in the light of the LORD.
For you've abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because they're full of what comes from the east, and of soothsayers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with foreigners' children.
His land is filled with silver and gold, and there's no end to his treasures; his land is filled with horses, and there's no end to his chariots.
His land is filled with idols; they bow down to the work of his hands, to what his fingers made.
And humankind is brought low, each man made low; and don't forgive them.
Get into the rock, hide in the dust, from the dread of the LORD and the magnificence of his majesty.
The haughty eyes of humankind will be brought low, the pride of men humbled; and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
For the LORD of hosts has a day against everything proud and lofty, against everything lifted up — and it will be brought low;
and against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
and against all the lofty mountains, and all the hills that are lifted up;
and against every high tower, and every fortified wall;
and against all the ships of Tarshish, and against all the desirable craft.
And the haughtiness of humankind will be humbled, the pride of men brought low; and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
And the idols will pass away completely.
And people will go into the caves of the rocks and the holes in the ground, from the dread of the LORD and the magnificence of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
In that day humankind will throw away its idols of silver and its idols of gold, which they made for themselves to bow down to — throw them to the burrowing moles and the bats;
to go into the crevices of the rocks and the clefts of the rocks, from the dread of the LORD and the magnificence of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
Stop relying on humankind, whose breath is in his nostrils. What is he worth?

isaiah_3.t: For look — the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah support and support, every support of bread and every support of water;
warrior and man of war, judge and prophet, diviner and elder,
commander of fifty and man of rank, counsellor, skilled magician, expert charmer.
And I'll make boys their officials, and caprice will rule over them.
And the people will oppress each other, each man against a man, each against his neighbour; the boy will act insolently against the old man, the lightly esteemed against the honoured.
A man will grab hold of his brother in his father's house: 'You've got a cloak — you be our ruler, and let this heap of ruins be under your hand.'
In that day he'll speak up: 'I won't be a binder of wounds. In my house there's no bread and no cloak. Don't make me a ruler of the people.'
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongue and their deeds are against the LORD, rebelling against the eyes of his glory.
The look on their faces testifies against them. They declare their sin like Sodom — they don't hide it. Alas for them: they've dealt out evil to themselves.
Say of the righteous that it will go well — they'll eat the fruit of their deeds.
Alas for the wicked — it will go badly for him: what his hands have dealt out will be done to him.
My people — their oppressors act like children, and women rule over them. O my people, your guides mislead you; they've swallowed up the way of your paths.
The LORD is taking his stand to conduct a case, standing to judge the peoples.
The LORD will come into judgement with the elders of his people and its officials: 'You are the ones who have consumed the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
What do you mean, crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor?' The declaration of the Lord GOD of hosts.
And the LORD said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, walking with necks stretched out, making eyes as they go, walking and mincing along, tinkling with their feet —
therefore the Lord will make the scalp of the daughters of Zion scabby, and the LORD will lay their foreheads bare.
In that day the Lord will remove the splendour of the anklets, the headbands and the crescents,
the pendants, the bracelets and the veils,
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume boxes and the amulets,
the signet rings and the nose rings,
the festal robes, the over-tunics, the cloaks and the purses,
the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans and the shawls.
And it will be: instead of perfume, rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of set hair, baldness; instead of a rich robe, sackcloth tied on; a brand instead of beauty.
Your men will fall by the sword, your might in battle.
And her gates will lament and mourn, and emptied out, she'll sit on the ground.

isaiah_4.t: And seven women will take hold of one man in that day and say: 'We'll eat our own bread and wear our own clothing — just let your name be called over us. Take away our reproach.'
In that day the Branch of the LORD will be beauty and glory, and the fruit of the land exaltation and splendour, for those of Israel who have escaped.
And whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy — everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem;
when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed away the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgement and a spirit of burning.

And the LORD will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the brightness of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
And there will be a booth for shade by day from the heat, and a refuge and a shelter from the storm and the rain.

isaiah_5.t: Let me sing for my beloved my love's song about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.

He dug it and cleared it of stones, planted it with choice vines, built a tower in the middle of it, and hewed out a winepress in it. He waited for it to produce grapes, and it produced rotten grapes.
And now, people of Jerusalem, people of Judah — judge between me and my vineyard.
What more was there to do for my vineyard that I didn't do in it? Why, when I waited for grapes, did it produce rotten grapes?
And now let me tell you what I'm about to do to my vineyard: I'll remove its hedge, and it will become grazing land; I'll break down its wall, and it will become a trampling ground.
And I'll make it a waste. It won't be pruned, it won't be hoed, and thorns and briars will come up; and I'll command the clouds not to rain rain on it.

For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the planting of his delight. He waited for justice — and there was bloodshed; for righteousness — and there was an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house, who bring field up against field, until there's no room left, and you're left to dwell alone in the middle of the land.
In my ears the LORD of hosts has sworn: Many houses will become a waste, great and good ones, with nobody living in them.
For ten acres of vineyard will produce one bath, and a homer of seed will produce an ephah.
Woe to those who get up early in the morning to chase strong drink, who stay on into the twilight while wine inflames them.
Lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine — that's their feasting; but the deed of the LORD they don't regard, and the work of his hands they haven't seen.
So my people has gone into exile for lack of knowledge; its nobility are starving, and its multitude parched with thirst.
So Sheol has widened its being and opened its mouth beyond measure; her magnificence and her multitude and her uproar go down, and whoever exults in her.
And humankind is brought low, each man made low, and the eyes of the proud brought low.
And the LORD of hosts is exalted in judgement, and the holy God shows himself holy in righteousness.
And lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and sojourners will eat among the waste places of the fat ones.
Woe to those who drag iniquity along with cords of falsehood, and sin as with a cart rope;
who say: 'Let him hurry, let him hasten his work, so we can see it; let the plan of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, so we can know it.'
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and discerning in their own sight.
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and men of valour at mixing strong drink,
who acquit the wicked for a bribe, and strip the righteous of their righteousness.

So, as a tongue of fire consumes stubble and dry grass sinks down in the flame, their root will be like rottenness and their blossom will go up like dust; because they've rejected the law of the LORD of hosts and spurned the speech of the Holy One of Israel.

So the anger of the LORD has burned against his people. He stretched out his hand against it and struck it, and the mountains quaked, and their corpses were like refuse in the middle of the streets. In all this his anger hasn't turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
And he'll lift up a standard for the nations from afar, and whistle for one from the end of the earth; and there it is — swiftly, quickly, it comes.
None of them is weary, none stumbles; nobody slumbers, nobody sleeps; the waistcloth at their waist isn't loosed, and the thong of their sandals isn't torn.
Their arrows are sharpened, all their bows bent; their horses' hooves are reckoned like flint, and their wheels like the storm wind.
Their roaring is like a lion's; they roar like young lions, growl, seize the prey and carry it off, and there's no one to rescue.
And they'll growl over it in that day like the growling of the sea; and you look to the land, and there's darkness and distress, and the light has gone dark in its clouds.

isaiah_6.t: In the year King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hem of his robe filled the temple.
Seraphim were standing above him. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one who called, and the house filled with smoke.
And I said: Alas for me, I'm destroyed! I'm a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips — and my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.
And one of the seraphim flew to me with a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with tongs from the altar.
And he touched it to my mouth and said: Look — this has touched your lips. Your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.
And I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send? Who will go for us? And I said: Here I am — send me.
And he said: Go, and say to this people: Keep on hearing, but don't understand; keep on seeing, but don't perceive.
Make the heart of this people fat, make its ears heavy, seal its eyes shut — so it won't see with its eyes, or hear with its ears, or understand with its heart, and turn back and be healed.
And I said: How long, Lord? And he said: Until cities lie waste with no inhabitant, houses with no one in them, and the ground devastated, a desolation;
and the LORD has sent humankind far away, and the abandoned places are many in the middle of the land.
and though a tenth is still in it, it will again be for burning — like a terebinth or an oak, which when it's felled still has its stump. A holy seed is its stump.

isaiah_7.t: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up to Jerusalem to make war on it, but they couldn't fight against it.
And word came to the house of David: Aram has settled on Ephraim. And his heart shook, and the heart of his people, the way the trees of the forest shake before a wind.
And the LORD said to Isaiah: Go out to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, to the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field,

and say to him: Take care and keep quiet. Don't be afraid, and don't let your heart go weak, because of these two smoking stubs of firebrands — the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
Because Aram has planned evil against you — Ephraim and the son of Remaliah — saying,
Let's go up against Judah, tear it apart and break it open for ourselves, and set up a king in it — the son of Tabeel.
This is what the Lord GOD says: It will not stand, and it will not happen.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. And within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered and be a people no longer.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you won't hold firm, you won't be held firm.
And the LORD spoke to Ahaz again:
Ask a sign for yourself from the LORD your God — make it deep as Sheol, or high as the heights.
And Ahaz said: I won't ask, and I won't put the LORD to the test.
And he said: Listen, house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God as well?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look — the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and she'll call his name Immanuel.
Curds and honey he'll eat, by the time he knows to refuse the evil and choose the good.
For before the boy knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be abandoned.
The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on your father's house days such as haven't come since the day Ephraim turned aside from Judah — the king of Assyria.
And in that day the LORD will whistle for the fly at the end of the canals of Egypt, and for the bee in the land of Assyria.
And they'll all come and settle in the wadis of the cliffs and the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and at all the watering places.
In that day the Lord will shave, with a razor hired from beyond the River — with the king of Assyria — the head and the hair of the legs; and it will sweep away the beard as well.
And in that day a man will keep alive one heifer and two sheep,
And from all the milk they give he'll eat curds; for curds and honey will be the food of everyone left in the land.
And in that day every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand pieces of silver will become thorns and briars.
You'll go there with arrows and a bow, for the whole land will be thorns and briars.
And all the hills that were hoed with the hoe — you won't go there for fear of thorns and briars; they'll become a place for turning out oxen and for sheep to trample.

isaiah_8.t: And the LORD said to me: Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
And I called reliable witnesses for myself: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.
And I went in to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the LORD said to me: Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
For before the boy knows how to say 'my father' and 'my mother', the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria.
And the LORD spoke to me again:
Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah that go gently, and rejoices over Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
therefore, look — the Lord is bringing up over them the waters of the River, mighty and many: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will rise over all its channels and go over all its banks.
And it will sweep on into Judah, overflowing and passing over; it will reach up to the neck. And the spread of its wings will fill the breadth of your land, Immanuel.
Be broken, you peoples, and be shattered! Give ear, all you distant places of the earth! Gird yourselves and be shattered! Gird yourselves and be shattered!
Plan a plan — and it will be frustrated; speak a word — and it will not stand; for God is with us.
For this is what the LORD said to me, with the strength of his hand on me, warning me not to walk in the way of this people:
Don't call conspiracy everything this people calls conspiracy; don't fear what it fears, and don't hold it in awe.
The LORD of hosts — him you shall regard as holy. He is your fear, he is the one you hold in awe.
And he will become a sanctuary — and a stone to strike against and a rock to stumble over for the two houses of Israel, a trap and a snare for the people of Jerusalem.
And many of them will stumble and fall and be broken, be ensnared and captured.
Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.
And I'll wait for the LORD, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob, and I'll hope for him.
Look — I and the children the LORD has given me are signs and portents in Israel, from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
And when they say to you, 'Consult the ghosts and the knowing spirits, the ones who chirp and mutter' — shouldn't a people consult its God? On behalf of the living, the dead?
To the law and to the testimony! If they don't speak according to this word, there's no dawn for them.
And he'll pass through the land, hard pressed and hungry; and when he's hungry he'll be enraged and curse his king and his God, and turn his face upward.
And he'll look to the earth, and there — distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish; and he's thrust into thick darkness.

isaiah_9.t: But there'll be no gloom for her that was in distress. In the former time he treated the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali with contempt, but in the latter he'll make it honoured — the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light; on those who dwell in a land of deep darkness light has shone.
You have multiplied the nation; you have made its joy great. They rejoice before you as with the joy of harvest, the way people are glad when they divide plunder.
For the yoke of his burden, the staff on his shoulder, the rod of the one who oppresses him — you have shattered them as on the day of Midian.
For every boot that marches with a shaking, and every cloak rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for fire.
For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us, and the dominion is on his shoulder; and his name is called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Father Everlasting, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of the dominion and of peace there will be no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and sustain it in justice and in righteousness, from now and for ever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
And all the people will know it — Ephraim and the people of Samaria — who say in pride and greatness of heart:
Bricks have fallen — we'll build with hewn stone; sycamores have been cut down — we'll put cedars in their place.
And the LORD has raised the adversaries of Rezin against him, and stirred up his enemies —
Aram from the east and the Philistines from behind, and they've devoured Israel with open mouth. In all this his anger hasn't turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
And the people hasn't turned back to the one who struck it, and they haven't sought the LORD of hosts.
And the LORD has cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.
The elder and the man of rank — he's the head; the prophet who teaches falsehood — he's the tail.
And the guides of this people have been misleading them, and those they guided have been swallowed up.

So the Lord doesn't rejoice over its young men, and has no compassion on its fatherless and its widows; for all of it is godless and doing evil, and every mouth speaks disgraceful folly. In all this his anger hasn't turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
For wickedness burns like fire. It consumes thorns and briars, kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they swirl upward in a rising of smoke.
By the wrath of the LORD of hosts the land is scorched, and the people has become like fuel for fire. No one spares his brother.
One devours on the right and is still hungry, eats on the left and they're not satisfied; each devours the flesh of his own arm.
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they're against Judah. In all this his anger hasn't turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

isaiah_10.t: Woe to those who decree decrees of wrongdoing, and to the writers who write out trouble,
to turn the weak aside from judgement, to rob the poor of my people of justice, so widows become their prey and they can plunder the fatherless.
And what will you do on the day of reckoning, at the devastation that comes from afar? Who will you flee to for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
There's nothing left but to crouch among the prisoners, and among the slain they will fall. In all this his anger hasn't turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
Woe, Assyria — the rod of my anger! The staff in their hand is my indignation.
Against a godless nation I send him, against the people of my wrath I command him, to plunder plunder and spoil spoil, and make it a trampling ground like the mud of the streets.
But he doesn't intend it that way, and his heart doesn't plan it that way; what's in his heart is to destroy and cut off nations, not a few.
For he says: Aren't my commanders all of them kings?
Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?
Just as my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idol — and their images were more than those of Jerusalem and Samaria —
shall I not do to Jerusalem and its figures what I've done to Samaria and its idols?
And when the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will attend to the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria, and to the splendour of his haughty eyes.

For he has said: By the strength of my hand I did it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I removed the boundaries of peoples, plundered their stores, and like a mighty one I brought down those who sat enthroned.

And my hand has found the wealth of the peoples as you find a nest; and as you gather abandoned eggs, I myself gathered all the earth; and there wasn't one that fluttered a wing or opened a mouth or chirped.

Does the axe glorify itself over the one who hews with it? Does the saw magnify itself over the one who wields it? As if a rod should wield the one who lifts it, as if a staff should lift what isn't wood.
So the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will send leanness among his fat ones; and under his glory a burning will burn like the burning of fire.
And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame; it will burn and consume his briars and his thorns in one day.
And the glory of his forest and his orchard he will bring to an end, from being to flesh; and it will be like a sick man wasting away.
And the remnant of the trees of his forest will be so few a boy could write them down.
And in that day the remnant of Israel and the escaped of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in faithfulness.
A remnant will return — the remnant of Jacob — to the Mighty God.
For though your people Israel were as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of it will return. Annihilation is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
For a complete destruction, and one decreed, the Lord GOD of hosts is about to make in the midst of all the land.
So this is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: Don't be afraid of Assyria, my people who dwell in Zion — he strikes you with the rod and lifts up his staff against you as Egypt did.
For in a very little while indignation will be finished, and my anger will turn to their destruction.
And the LORD of hosts will wield a whip against him, like the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb; his staff will be over the sea, and he'll lift it up as he did in Egypt.
And in that day his burden will be removed from your shoulder and his yoke from your neck; and the yoke will be broken because of fatness.
He has come to Aiath, passed through Migron; at Michmash he stores his baggage.
They've crossed the pass: 'Geba is our lodging place.' Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah has fled; the people of Gebim have taken refuge.
This very day he'll halt at Nob; he shakes his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Look — the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is lopping off the boughs with a crash; the lofty in height are cut down, the tall are brought low.
And he'll cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by a mighty one.

isaiah_11.t: And a shoot will come out from the stock of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
And the spirit of the LORD will rest on him: a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and might, a spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
And his delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He won't judge by what his eyes see, or decide by what his ears hear;

but he'll judge the weak with righteousness, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth; he'll strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips put the wicked to death.
And righteousness will be the waistcloth around his hips, and trustworthiness the waistcloth around his loins.
And a wolf will live with a lamb, and a leopard will lie down with a kid; a calf and a young lion and a fatling together, with a small boy leading them.
And a cow and a bear will graze; their young will lie down together; and a lion will eat straw like the ox.
And a nursing child will play over the hole of a cobra, and a weaned child will put his hand over the viper's den.
They won't do harm and they won't destroy in all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
And in that day the root of Jesse, who stands as a standard for the peoples — the nations will resort to him, and his resting place will be glory.

And in that day the Lord will put out his hand a second time to acquire the remnant of his people that remains from Assyria and Egypt, from Pathros and Cush, from Elam and Shinar and Hamath and the coastlands of the sea.
And he'll lift up a standard for the nations, and gather the banished of Israel; and the scattered of Judah he'll assemble from the four corners of the earth.
And the jealousy of Ephraim will come to an end, and the opponents of Judah will be cut off; Ephraim won't be jealous of Judah, and Judah won't oppose Ephraim.
And they'll swoop on the shoulder of the Philistines to the west; together they'll plunder the people of the east. Edom and Moab will be the reach of their hand, and the Ammonites their subjects.

And the LORD will utterly destroy the tongue of the sea of Egypt, and wave his hand over the River with the scorching of his wind; he'll strike it into seven wadis and let people walk across in sandals.
And there'll be a highway for the remnant of his people that remains from Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day it came up from the land of Egypt.

isaiah_12.t: And you will say in that day: I'll give you thanks, LORD, for you were angry with me; your anger has turned back, and you've comforted me.
Look — God is my deliverance. I'll trust and not be afraid. For the LORD, the LORD, is my power and my might, and he has become my deliverance.
And you'll draw water with rejoicing from the springs of deliverance.
And you will say in that day: Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known his deeds among the peoples, proclaim that his name is exalted.
Make music to the LORD, for he has done majestically; let this be made known in all the earth.
Cry aloud and shout, you who dwell in Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.

isaiah_13.t: The oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
On a bare mountain lift up a standard; raise your voice to them, wave a hand, and let them enter the gates of the nobles.
I myself have commanded my consecrated ones; I've summoned my warriors to serve my anger, my proudly exulting ones.
The sound of a tumult on the mountains, like a numerous people! The sound of an uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering! The LORD of hosts is mustering an army for battle.
They come from a distant land, from the end of the heavens — the LORD and the weapons of his indignation — to destroy all the earth.
Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
So all hands will go slack, and every human heart will melt.
And they'll be terrified; pangs and pains will seize them; they'll writhe like a woman in labour. Each will stare at his neighbour; their faces will be faces of flame.
Look — the day of the LORD comes, cruel, with wrath and burning anger, to make the land a waste, and destroy its sinners from it.
For the stars of the heavens and their constellations won't flash their light; the sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon won't shed its light.
And I'll visit evil on the world, and their iniquity on the wicked; I'll put an end to the pride of the arrogant, and bring low the haughtiness of the ruthless.
I'll make a human being more precious than pure gold, and humankind than the gold of Ophir.
So I'll make the heavens tremble, and the earth will shake from its place, in the wrath of the LORD of hosts and in the day of his burning anger.
And it will be like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no one to gather them: each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
Everyone found will be run through, and everyone swept up will fall by the sword.
And their children will be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered and their wives lain with.
Look — I'm rousing the Medes against them, who don't value silver and take no delight in gold.
And their bows will dash young men in pieces; they'll have no compassion on the fruit of the womb; their eye won't look with pity on children.
And Babylon, the beauty of kingdoms, the splendour of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be like God's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.
She'll never be inhabited, never settled from generation to generation; no Arab will pitch a tent there, and shepherds won't make their flocks lie down there.
But desert creatures will lie down there, and their houses will be full of howling things; ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about there.
And hyenas will cry in its citadels, and jackals in the palaces of delight. Her time is near to come, and her days won't be prolonged.

isaiah_14.t: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will choose Israel again, and give them rest on their own ground; and the sojourner will join himself to them, and they'll attach themselves to the house of Jacob.

And peoples will take them and bring them to their place; and the house of Israel will take them as an inheritance on the land of the LORD, as male and female servants. They'll take their captors captive and rule over their oppressors.
And on the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and your turmoil and the hard labour that was forced on you,
you'll take up this taunt against the king of Babylon and say: How the oppressor has ceased! How the raging has ceased!
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of rulers,
that struck peoples in wrath with unceasing blows, that ruled nations in anger with a persecution nobody restrained.
All the earth is at rest and at peace; people have broken out in a shout of joy.
Even the fir trees rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon: 'Since you lay down, no woodcutter has come up against us.'
Sheol beneath is stirred for you, to meet you as you come; it rouses the shades for you, all the leaders of the earth; it has raised from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
All of them will answer and say to you: 'You too have been made weak, like us. You've become like us.'
Your pride has been brought down to Sheol, and the sound of your harps; beneath you maggots are spread as a bed, and worms are your covering.
How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of dawn! You've been cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low!
And you said in your heart: 'I will ascend to the heavens; above the stars of God I'll raise my throne; and I'll sit on the mountain of assembly, in the remotest parts of the north.
I'll ascend above the heights of the clouds; I'll make myself like the Most High.'
Nevertheless, you're brought down to Sheol, to the remotest parts of the pit.
Those who see you will stare at you; they'll look you over closely: 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who made kingdoms shake,
who made the world like the wilderness and tore down its cities, who wouldn't let his prisoners go home?'
All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie down in glory, each in his own house.
But you've been thrown out of your tomb like an abhorred branch, covered with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit — like a trampled corpse.
You won't be joined with them in burial, for you've ruined your land and slain your people. May the offspring of evildoers never be named.
Prepare a place of slaughter for his sons because of the iniquity of their fathers, so they don't rise and take possession of the earth and fill the face of the world with cities.
And I'll rise up against them — declares the LORD of hosts — and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and posterity — declares the LORD.
And I'll make it a possession of the hedgehog, and pools of water; and I'll sweep it away with the broom of destruction — declares the LORD of hosts.
The LORD of hosts has sworn: Surely as I intended, so it has come to be; and as I planned, it will stand.
to break Assyria in my land, and on my mountains I'll trample him; and his yoke will be removed from them, and his burden from their shoulder.
This is the plan that is planned against all the earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of hosts has planned — who will frustrate it? His hand is stretched out — who will turn it back?
In the year King Ahaz died this oracle came.
Don't rejoice, all Philistia, that the rod of the one who struck you is broken; for from the root of a serpent a viper will come out, and its fruit will be a flying serpent.
And the firstborn of the weak will graze, and the needy will lie down in safety; but I'll put your root to death with famine, and it will kill your remnant.
Wail, gate! Cry out, city! Melt away, all Philistia! For from the north smoke is coming, and there's no straggler in his ranks.
And what will one answer the messengers of a nation? That the LORD has founded Zion, and in her the poor of his people will take refuge.

isaiah_15.t: The oracle concerning Moab. Because in a night Ar of Moab was devastated and destroyed; because in a night Kir of Moab was devastated and destroyed —
The temple and Dibon have gone up to the high places to weep. Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. On every head is baldness; every beard is cut off.
In its streets they've put on sackcloth; on its roofs and in its squares all of it wails, going down in weeping.
