And Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; as far as Jahaz their voice is heard. So the armed men of Moab cry aloud; its whole being trembles within it.
My heart cries out for Moab; its fugitives are as far as Zoar, Eglath-shelishiyah. For the ascent of Luhith — with weeping they go up it; and on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of shattering.
For the waters of Nimrim are desolate; the grass has dried up, the vegetation has wasted away, there's no greenery.
So the surplus they've made, and their store, they carry over the Wadi of the Poplars.
For the cry has gone round the territory of Moab; its wailing reaches Eglaim, its wailing Beer-elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I'll bring yet more on Dimon — a lion for those of Moab who escape, and for the remainder of the ground.

isaiah_16.t: Send a lamb to the ruler of the land, from Sela toward the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
And it will be: like a fluttering bird, a nest driven out, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
'Bring counsel, make a decision; make your shade like night at high noon; hide the outcasts, don't expose the fugitive.
Let my outcasts sojourn among you, Moab; be a shelter for them from the destroyer.' For the oppressor will come to an end, devastation will cease, those who trample will be finished from the land.
And a throne will be established in steadfast love, and one will sit on it in faithfulness, in the tent of David, judging and seeking justice and swift to do righteousness.
We've heard of the pride of Moab — exceedingly proud — its haughtiness and its pride and its fury; its empty boasts are not right.
So Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail. For the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth you'll groan, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon have withered, the vine of Sibmah; the rulers of nations have struck down its choice branches, which reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; its shoots spread out, they crossed the sea.
So I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh; for over your summer fruit and your harvest the shout has fallen.
And joy and gladness are taken away from the orchard; in the vineyards there's no singing, no shouting; no treader treads out wine in the winepresses. I have made the shout to cease.
So my inward parts moan like a lyre for Moab, and my inner being for Kir-heres.
And when Moab presents itself, when it wearies itself on the high place and comes to its sanctuary to pray, it will not prevail.
This is the word the LORD spoke concerning Moab in time past.

And now the LORD has spoken: Within three years, like the years of a hired labourer, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all its great multitude; and the remnant will be very few and not mighty.

isaiah_17.t: The oracle concerning Damascus. Look — Damascus is being removed from being a city, and it will be a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer are abandoned; they'll be for flocks, and they'll lie down with no one to terrify them.
And the fortress will cease from Ephraim, and kingship from Damascus and the remnant of Aram; they'll be like the glory of the Israelites — declares the LORD of hosts.
And in that day the glory of Jacob will be brought low, and the fatness of his flesh will be made lean.
And it will be like the gathering of a harvest of standing grain, with the arm reaping the ears; like one gleaning ears in the Valley of Rephaim.
And gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the top of the topmost bough; four or five on its fruiting branches — declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
In that day a person will look to his Maker, and his eyes will see the Holy One of Israel;
and he won't look to the altars, the work of his hands, and he won't see what his fingers made — the asherahs and the incense altars.
In that day his fortified cities will be like the forsaken places of the wood and the topmost bough, which they abandoned because of the Israelites; and it will be a desolation.
For you've forgotten the God of your deliverance, and the Rock of your refuge you haven't remembered. So you plant pleasant plantings and sow them with a stranger's vine-shoot.
On the day of your planting you make it grow, and in the morning you make your seed sprout; but the harvest flees away in a day of sickness and incurable pain.
Woe — the tumult of many peoples! Like the roaring of seas they roar. And the uproar of nations! Like the uproar of mighty waters they are in uproar.
Nations are in uproar like the uproar of many waters — but he rebukes them, and they flee far away, chased like chaff of the mountains before a wind, like whirling dust before a storm.
At evening time — sudden terror! Before morning, it's gone. This is the portion of those who plunder us, the lot of those who despoil us.

isaiah_18.t: Woe — land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,

which sends envoys by the sea, in vessels of papyrus on the face of the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared from that place and beyond, a nation of strength upon strength and of trampling, whose land the rivers divide.
All you inhabitants of the world, all who dwell on the earth: when a standard is lifted on the mountains, you'll see it; and when a ram's horn is sounded, you'll hear it.
For this is what the LORD said to me: I'll be quiet and look on from my place, like dazzling heat in the sunlight, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
For before the harvest, when the bud is finished and the ripening grape becomes a blossom, he'll cut off the shoots with pruning knives and remove the tendrils, cutting them away.
They'll be abandoned together to the birds of prey of the mountains and to the animals of the earth; and the birds of prey will pass the summer on them, and every animal of the earth the winter.

At that time a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared from that place and beyond, a nation of strength upon strength and of trampling, whose land the rivers divide — to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, Mount Zion.

isaiah_19.t: The oracle concerning Egypt. Look — the LORD is riding on a swift cloud, coming to Egypt; and the idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
And I'll provoke Egypt against Egypt, and they'll fight, each against his brother, each against his neighbour, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
And the spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and its plan I'll confuse; and they'll consult the idols and the mutterers, the ghosts and the knowing spirits.
And I'll hand Egypt over into the hand of a cruel master, and a strong king will rule over them — declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
And the waters will be dried up from the sea, and the river will run dry and be dry.
And the rivers will stink; the canals of Egypt will run low and dry up; reed and rush will wither.
The bare places by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and everything sown by the Nile, will dry up, be driven away, and be no more.
And the fishermen will lament, and all who cast a hook in the Nile will mourn; and those who spread a net on the waters will languish.
And those who work combed flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of white cloth.
And her foundations will be crushed; all who work for wages will be grieved in their being.
The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools; the wise counsellors of Pharaoh — their counsel is stupid. How can you say to Pharaoh, 'I'm a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings'?
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now — let them know what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
The officials of Zoan have become fools; the officials of Memphis are deceived; they've led Egypt astray — the cornerstone of its tribes.
The LORD has mixed within her a spirit of confusion, and they've made Egypt stagger in all its work, like a drunkard staggering in his vomit.
And there'll be no work for Egypt that head or tail, palm branch or reed can do.
In that day Egypt will be like women, and will tremble and be in dread before the brandishing of the hand of the LORD of hosts, which he is brandishing over it.
And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone it's mentioned to will be in dread, because of the plan of the LORD of hosts, which he is planning against it.
In that day there'll be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there'll be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD beside its border.

And it will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt; for they'll cry out to the LORD because of oppressors, and he'll send them a deliverer and a defender, and he'll rescue them.
And the LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and Egypt will know the LORD in that day; and they'll serve with sacrifice and offering, and they'll vow a vow to the LORD and pay it.
And the LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; and they'll turn back to the LORD, and he'll be entreated by them and will heal them.
In that day there'll be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will come into Egypt and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will serve with Assyria.
In that day Israel will be a third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
which the LORD of hosts will bless, saying: Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.

isaiah_20.t: In the year the commander-in-chief came to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and captured it —
at that time the LORD spoke by the hand of Isaiah son of Amoz: Go and loosen the sackcloth from your hips, and take your sandals off your feet. And he did so, going naked and barefoot.
And the LORD said: Just as my servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot for three years, a sign and a portent against Egypt and against Cush,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered — the nakedness of Egypt.
And they'll be dismayed and ashamed of Cush their hope and of Egypt their splendour.
And the people of this coastland will say in that day: Look at our hope — the place we fled to for help, to be rescued from the king of Assyria! And how are we ourselves going to escape?

isaiah_21.t: The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea. Like storms sweeping through the Negeb, it comes from the wilderness, from a land to be feared.
A severe vision has been told to me: the traitor betrays, the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I've put an end to all her groaning.
So my loins are filled with anguish; pangs have seized me like the pangs of a woman in labour. I'm too bent over to hear; I'm too terrified to see.
My heart reels; shuddering has overwhelmed me. The twilight I longed for he has turned into trembling for me.
They arrange the table, they spread the rug — eating, drinking. Get up, officials! Oil the shield!
For this is what the Lord said to me: Go, station the watchman; let him tell what he sees.
And he'll see riders, a pair of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels; and he'll listen closely, with great attentiveness.
And the lookout called out: On a watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day, and at my post I'm stationed all through the nights.
And look — here it comes: riders, a man, a pair of horsemen! And he answered and said: Fallen, fallen is Babylon, and all the images of her gods are shattered to the ground.
My threshed one, son of my threshing floor: what I've heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I've told you.
The oracle concerning Dumah. Someone is calling to me from Seir: Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?
The watchman says: Morning comes, and also night. If you would enquire, enquire. Come back again.
The oracle concerning Arabia. In the thickets in Arabia you'll spend the night, caravans of Dedanites.
Bring water to meet the thirsty! People of the land of Tema, meet the fugitive with bread.
For they've fled from swords, from a drawn sword, from a bent bow, from the weight of battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: Within a year, like the years of a hired labourer, all the glory of Kedar will be finished.
And the remnant of the number of the bowmen, the warriors of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.

isaiah_22.t: The oracle concerning the Valley of Vision. What's the matter with you, then, that all of you have gone up to the roofs?
You that are full of noise, turbulent city, jubilant town! Your slain are not slain by the sword, not dead in battle.
All your rulers have fled together; they were captured without a bow. All of you who were found were captured together; they had fled from far off.
So I said: Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Don't insist on comforting me over the devastation of the daughter of my people.
For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day of consternation and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision — a breaking down of walls, a crying out to the mountain.
And Elam took up the quiver, with chariotry and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.
And your choicest valleys were full of chariotry, and the horsemen took a firm stand at the gate.
And he stripped away the covering of Judah. And in that day you looked to the weaponry of the House of the Forest,
and you saw that the breaches in the City of David were many; and you gathered the waters of the lower pool.
And you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and pulled the houses down to fortify the city wall.
And you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool; but you didn't look to the one who made it, and you didn't consider the one who formed it long ago.
And in that day the Lord GOD of hosts called for weeping and for wailing, for baldness and for girding on sackcloth;
and instead — rejoicing and joy, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: 'Let's eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!'
And the LORD of hosts revealed himself in my ears: Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die, says the Lord GOD of hosts.
This is what the Lord GOD of hosts says: Go, come to this steward, to Shebna who is over the house,
What have you here, and whom have you here, that you've dug out a tomb for yourself here — you who dig your tomb on a height, cutting a dwelling for yourself in the rock?
Look — the LORD is about to hurl you away with a hurling, O man, and grasp you firmly.
He'll wind you round and round like a ball, into a land broad on both hands. There you'll die, and there the chariots of your splendour will be the disgrace of your master's house.
And I'll push you from your office, and from your post he will tear you down.
And in that day I'll summon my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah,
and I'll clothe him with your tunic and fasten your sash on him, and put your authority into his hand; and he'll become a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
And I'll put the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open.
And I'll drive him in like a tent peg in a firm place; and he'll become a seat of honour for his father's house.
And they'll hang on him all the honour of his father's house — the descendants and the offshoots, all the small vessels, from the bowls to all the jars.
In that day — declares the LORD of hosts — the tent peg driven in a firm place will be removed; it will be cut down and fall, and the burden that was on it will be cut off; for the LORD has spoken.

isaiah_23.t: The oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it is devastated — no house, no way in! From the land of Cyprus it was revealed to them.
Be silent, people of the coastland! The traders of Sidon, crossing the sea, have filled you.
And on many waters the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue; and she became the traffic of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea: I have not been in labour and I have not given birth; I haven't brought up young men or raised virgins.
When the report reaches Egypt, they'll be in anguish at the report of Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, people of the coastland!
Is this your jubilant city, whose beginning is from days of antiquity, whose feet carried her far off to settle?
Who has planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders were princes, whose merchants were the honoured of the earth?
The LORD of hosts has planned it, to profane the pride of all beauty, to bring into contempt all the honoured of the earth.
Cross over your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there's no restraint any more.
He has stretched out his hand over the sea; he has made kingdoms tremble. The LORD has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds.
And he said: You won't exult again, oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Get up, cross over to Cyprus; even there you'll have no rest.
Look — the land of the Chaldeans: this is the people that was not; Assyria allotted it to desert creatures. They raised up their siege towers, stripped bare her palaces, made her a ruin.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is devastated.
And in that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
Take a lyre, go about the city, forgotten prostitute! Play well, sing many songs, so you'll be remembered.
And at the end of seventy years the LORD will visit Tyre, and she'll return to her hire and prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.

And her profit and her hire will be holy to the LORD. It won't be stored up and it won't be hoarded; her profit will belong to those who dwell before the LORD, to eat their fill and for fine clothing.

isaiah_24.t: Look — the LORD is laying the earth waste and devastating it; he'll twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.

And it will be: as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maidservant, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the creditor, so with the one who owes him.
The earth will be utterly laid waste; it will be utterly plundered. For the LORD has spoken this word.
The earth dries up and withers; the world languishes and withers; the exalted of the people of the earth languish.
And the earth has been polluted under its inhabitants, for they've transgressed laws, overstepped the statute, broken the everlasting covenant.
So a curse has consumed the earth, and those who dwell in it are held guilty. So the inhabitants of the earth have dwindled, and few humans are left.
The new wine dries up, the vine languishes; all the joyful of heart groan.
The gaiety of tambourines has ceased; the uproar of the jubilant has stopped; the gaiety of the lyre has ceased.
They won't drink wine with song; strong drink will be bitter to those who drink it.
The town of emptiness is broken; every house is shut, with no way in.
There's an outcry over wine in the streets; all joy has darkened to evening; the gaiety of the earth has departed.
Desolation is left in the city, and the gate is battered to ruin.
For so it will be in the midst of the earth, among the peoples: like the beating of an olive tree, like gleanings when the grape harvest is over.
They lift up their voice, they shout for joy; over the majesty of the LORD they cry aloud from the west.
Therefore in the east give glory to the LORD, in the coastlands of the sea the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

From the edge of the earth we've heard songs: 'Glory to the righteous one!' And I said: I waste away, I waste away! Alas for me! The treacherous act treacherously; with treachery the treacherous act treacherously.
Dread and pit and snare are upon you, inhabitant of the earth!

And whoever flees from the sound of the dread will fall into the pit, and whoever comes up out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is utterly broken; the earth is torn apart; the earth is violently shaken.
The earth staggers wildly like a drunkard; it sways like a shelter; its transgression is heavy on it, and it falls and will not rise again.
And in that day the LORD will visit the host of the height on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
And they'll be gathered together, prisoners gathered into a pit, and shut up in a prison; and after many days they'll be punished.
And the moon will be abashed and the sun ashamed; for the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders — glory.

isaiah_25.t: LORD, you are my God; I'll exalt you, I'll give thanks to your name, for you have done a wonder — plans from long ago, in perfect faithfulness.
For you've made a city into a heap, a fortified town into a ruin; the fortress of strangers is no longer a city; it will never be rebuilt.
So a strong people will honour you; the town of ruthless nations will fear you.
For you've been a refuge for the weak, a refuge for the needy in his distress, a shelter from the rainstorm, a shade from the heat; for the breath of the ruthless is like a rainstorm against a wall.
Like heat in a dry land you subdue the uproar of strangers; as heat is subdued by the shade of a cloud, so the song of the ruthless is quietened.
And on this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all the peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of old wines, rich food full of marrow, old wines distilled.
And on this mountain he will swallow up the covering that covers all the peoples, and the veil that is woven over all the nations.
He will swallow up death for ever; and the Lord GOD will wipe the tears from every face, and he'll remove the reproach of his people from all the earth — for the LORD has spoken.
And it will be said in that day: Look — this is our God; we waited for him, and he delivered us. This is the LORD; we waited for him. Let's be glad and rejoice in his deliverance.
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain; and Moab will be trampled down where it stands, as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
And he will spread out his hands in the midst of it as a swimmer spreads them out to swim; and the LORD will bring low his haughtiness together with the trickery of his hands.
And the high fortification of your walls he will lay low; he'll bring it low, bring it down to the ground, to the dust.

isaiah_26.t: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; he sets deliverance as walls and rampart.
Open the gates, so a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faith.
The firm of mind you keep in peace, perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
Trust in the LORD for ever, for in the LORD, the LORD, is an everlasting Rock.
For he has laid low those who dwell on high, the town set on high; he brings it low, he brings it low to the ground, he brings it down to the dust.
A foot will trample it — the feet of the poor, the footsteps of the weak.
The path of the righteous is level; upright one, you make level the track of the righteous.
Also in the path of your judgements, LORD, we have waited for you; your name and your remembrance are what the whole being desires.
My whole being has desired you in the night; yes, my spirit within me seeks you at dawn. For when your judgements are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
If the wicked is shown favour, he doesn't learn righteousness; in a land of uprightness he acts unjustly, and doesn't see the majesty of the LORD.
LORD, your hand is raised, and they don't see it. Let them see and be ashamed of your zeal for your people; let the fire meant for your adversaries consume them.
LORD, you will establish peace for us; for even all our works you have done for us.
LORD our God, lords other than you have ruled over us; by you alone do we make mention of your name.
The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. So you have visited and destroyed them, and made all remembrance of them perish.
You have added to the nation, LORD; you have added to the nation, you have gained glory; you have extended all the boundaries of the land.
LORD, in distress they sought you; they poured out a whispered prayer when your chastening was on them.
As a pregnant woman drawing near to give birth writhes and cries out in her labour pains, so were we before you, LORD.
We were pregnant, we writhed — it was as if we gave birth to wind. We've accomplished no deliverance in the earth, and the inhabitants of the world haven't fallen.
Your dead will live; my corpses will rise. Awake and shout for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will give birth to the departed spirits.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your door behind you; hide for a little moment until the indignation passes by.

For look — the LORD is going out from his place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitants of the earth upon them; and the earth will disclose the blood shed on her and will no longer cover over her slain.

isaiah_27.t: In that day the LORD will visit, with his fierce and great and mighty sword, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, and Leviathan the twisting serpent; and he'll slay the sea monster that is in the sea.
In that day: A delightful vineyard — sing of it!
I, the LORD, am its keeper; every moment I water it. So that no one may injure it, night and day I guard it.
I have no rage. If only there were thorns and briars against me in battle! I'd march against them and burn them altogether.
Or else let him take hold of my protection; let him make peace with me; let him make peace with me.
In the days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and bud, and they'll fill the face of the world with fruit.
Has he struck him as he struck the one who struck him? Or has he been slain as those he slew were slain?
By banishing, by sending her away, you contended with her; he drove her out with his fierce wind on the day of the east wind.

So by this the iniquity of Jacob will be atoned for, and this is the whole fruit of the removing of his sin: when he makes all the stones of the altar like pulverised chalkstones, no asherahs or incense altars will stand.
For the fortified city stands alone, a habitation deserted and forsaken like the wilderness. There a calf will graze, and there it will lie down and strip its branches bare.

When its branches dry up they're broken off; women come and set light to them. For it isn't a people of understanding; so the one who made it will not have compassion on it, and the one who formed it will not show it favour.
And in that day the LORD will beat out the grain from the flowing stream of the River to the Wadi of Egypt; and you'll be gathered one by one, Israelites.

And in that day a great ram's horn will be blown; and those lost in the land of Assyria will come, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt; and they'll bow down to the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

isaiah_28.t: Woe — the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, and the withering flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of the fertile valley, of those struck down with wine!
Look — the Lord has one mighty and strong; like a storm of hail, a tempest of destruction, like a storm of mighty overflowing waters, he'll thrust it down to the ground with his hand.
It will be trampled underfoot — the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim.

And the withering flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, will be like an early fig before summer: whoever sees it, the moment he sees it, swallows it while it's still in his hand.
In that day the LORD of hosts will become a crown of beauty and a diadem of splendour for the remnant of his people,
and a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgement, and might for those who turn back the battle at the gate.

And these too reel with wine and stagger with strong drink: priest and prophet reel with strong drink, they're confused by wine, they stagger from strong drink; they reel in vision, they totter in giving judgement.
For all the tables are full of vomit and filth, with no room left.
Who's he going to teach knowledge to? Who's he going to explain the message to? Children just weaned from milk, just taken from the breast?
For it's 'command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there.'
For with stammering lips and a foreign tongue he will speak to this people —
he who said to them: This is the resting place — give rest to the weary; and this is the place of repose. But they weren't willing to listen.

And the word of the LORD will be to them 'command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there' — so that they may go and stumble backward and be broken, and be ensnared and captured.
So hear the word of the LORD, you mockers, rulers of this people who are in Jerusalem.

Because you've said: We've cut a covenant with death, and with Sheol we've made an agreement. The overflowing scourge, when it passes through, won't reach us, for we've made falsehood our refuge and hidden ourselves in deception.
So this is what the Lord GOD says: Look — I'm laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. The one who trusts will not be in haste.
And I'll make justice the measuring-line and righteousness the plummet; and hail will sweep away the refuge of falsehood, and waters will overflow the hiding place.
And your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol won't stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, you'll become a trampling ground for it.
As often as it passes through it will take you; morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night. And it will be sheer terror to understand the message.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap yourself in.
For the LORD will rise as at Mount Perazim; he'll rage as in the valley at Gibeon, to do his deed — strange is his deed — and to work his work — alien is his work.
And now, don't mock, or your fetters will be made strong; for I've heard of a complete destruction, one decreed, from the Lord GOD of hosts against all the land.
Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my speech.
Does the ploughman plough all day to sow? Does he keep loosening and harrowing his ground?
Doesn't he, when he's levelled its surface, scatter black cumin and sprinkle cumin, set wheat in rows and barley in its place and spelt at its border?
And he instructs him in the right way; his God teaches him.
For black cumin isn't threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a cart wheel rolled over cumin; black cumin is beaten out with a staff, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread is crushed; but he doesn't go on threshing it for ever. He drives the wheel of his cart and his horses over it, but he doesn't crush it to powder.
This too comes from the LORD of hosts: he has made his counsel wonderful, he has made sound wisdom great.

isaiah_29.t: Woe — Ariel, Ariel, the town where David encamped! Add year to year; let the festivals go round.
And I'll bring distress on Ariel, and there'll be mourning and lamentation; and she'll be to me like an Ariel.
And I'll encamp against you all round, lay siege against you with siege-works, and raise fortifications against you.

And you'll be brought low; from the ground you'll speak, and from the dust your speech will be humbled. And your voice will be like a ghost's from the ground, and from the dust your speech will whisper.
And the multitude of your strangers will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless like passing chaff; and it will happen in an instant, suddenly.
From the LORD of hosts she will be visited, with thunder and earthquake and a great noise, storm and tempest and the flame of a devouring fire.
And the multitude of all the nations who wage war against Ariel will be like a dream, a vision of the night — all who wage war against her and her stronghold, and those who bring distress on her.

And it will be like a hungry man dreaming that he's eating, and he wakes and his being is empty; or a thirsty man dreaming that he's drinking, and he wakes and there he is, faint, his throat still longing: so will be the multitude of all the nations who wage war against Mount Zion.
Linger and be astounded! Blind yourselves and be blind! They're drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep; he has shut your eyes — the prophets — and covered your heads — the seers.
And the whole vision has become for you like the words of a sealed scroll, which people hand to someone who can read, saying: Read this, please. And he says: I can't — it's sealed.
And the scroll is handed to someone who can't read, saying: Read this, please. And he says: I can't read.
And the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth and honours me with its lips, while its heart is far from me, and their fear of me has become a commandment of men, learned by rote —
therefore, look — I'll again deal wonderfully with this people, wonder upon wonder; and the wisdom of its wise men will perish, and the understanding of its discerning men will hide itself.
Woe to those who go deep to hide a plan from the LORD, whose deeds are in a dark place, and who say: Who sees us? Who knows us?

How you turn things upside down! Shall the potter be reckoned as the clay, so that a thing made says of its maker: He didn't make me, and a thing formed says of the one who formed it: He has no understanding?
Isn't it yet a very little while until Lebanon turns into an orchard, and the orchard is reckoned as a forest?
And in that day the deaf will hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and out of darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
And the humble will have joy upon joy in the LORD, and the neediest of humankind will be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless will come to an end and the mocker be finished, and all who lie in wait to do wrong will be cut off —
those who make a person out to be guilty with a word, lay a trap for the one who arbitrates in the gate, and turn the righteous aside with an empty case.
So this is what the LORD says to the house of Jacob, he who ransomed Abraham: Jacob won't now be ashamed, and his face won't now grow pale.
For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they'll regard my name as holy; they'll regard as holy the Holy One of Jacob, and hold the God of Israel in awe.
And those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding, and murmurers will learn instruction.

isaiah_30.t: Woe to stubborn children — declares the LORD — who carry out a plan, but not from me, and pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, heaping sin on sin;
who set out to go down to Egypt but haven't consulted my mouth, to take refuge in the refuge of Pharaoh and seek shelter in the shadow of Egypt.
And the refuge of Pharaoh will become your shame, and the shelter in the shadow of Egypt your ignominy.
For his officials have been in Zoan, and his messengers have reached Hanes.
All are put to shame over a people who bring them no profit, no help and no profit, only shame and reproach.

The oracle concerning the animals of the Negeb. Through a land of trouble and distress, of lioness and lion, viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the shoulders of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people who bring no profit.
And Egypt — its help is futility and emptiness. So I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
Now go, write it on a tablet before them, and inscribe it on a scroll, so it may be for a later day, for ever, to eternity.
For they're a people of rebellion, lying children, children who haven't been willing to hear the law of the LORD;
who say to the seers: Don't see; and to the visionaries: Don't give us visions of what's right. Speak smooth things to us; give us visions of illusion.
Turn aside from the way; turn away from the path; make the Holy One of Israel cease from before us!
So this is what the Holy One of Israel says: Because you've rejected this word and trusted in oppression and crookedness and leaned on them,
therefore this iniquity will be to you like a breach about to fall, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
And it will be broken like a potter's jar, smashed without pity, so that among its fragments not a sherd will be found to carry fire from a hearth or scoop water from a cistern.
For this is what the Lord GOD says, the Holy One of Israel: In returning and rest you will be delivered; in quietness and in trust will be your might. But you weren't willing.
And you said: No — we'll flee on horses! So you will flee. And: We'll ride on swift ones! So your pursuers will be swift.
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you'll flee, until you're left like a flagstaff on a mountain top and like a standard on a hill.
And therefore the LORD waits to show you favour, and therefore he rises up to have compassion on you; for the LORD is a God of justice. How blessed are all who wait for him!
For a people will dwell in Zion, in Jerusalem. You'll weep no more. He will surely show you favour at the sound of your crying out; when he hears it, he'll answer you.
And the Lord will give you the bread of distress and the water of oppression; but your Teacher will no longer hide himself, and your eyes will see your Teacher.
And your ears will hear a word behind you, saying: This is the way; walk in it — whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
And you'll make unclean the plating of your silver images and the sheathing of your molten image of gold. You'll throw them away like a menstrual rag; you'll say to it: Filth!
And he'll give rain for the seed with which you sow the ground, and bread, the produce of the ground, will be rich and fat; in that day your livestock will graze in a broad pasture.
And the cattle and the donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
And on every high mountain and on every lifted hill there'll be streams, watercourses of water, on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the fracture of his people and heals the wound of his blow.
Look — the name of the LORD comes from afar, his anger burning, and in thick rising smoke; his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.
And his breath is like an overflowing torrent that reaches up to the neck, to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction, and a bridle that leads astray is on the jaws of the peoples.
You'll have a song as on a night when a festival is consecrated, and gladness of heart as when one walks to the flute to go to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
And the LORD will make the grandeur of his voice heard, and show his arm descending in raging anger and the flame of a devouring fire, in driving storm and rainstorm and hailstones.
For at the voice of the LORD Assyria will be shattered; he will strike with the rod.
And every stroke of the appointed staff that the LORD lays on it will be to the sound of tambourines and lyres; and with brandishing battles he'll fight against them.

For a place of burning has long been arranged; it too has been prepared for the king. He has made it deep and wide; its pyre is fire and much wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of sulphur, sets it ablaze.

isaiah_31.t: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and lean on horses, and trust in chariotry because there's so much of it and in horsemen because there are so many; but they don't look to the Holy One of Israel and don't seek the LORD.
But he too is wise, and he has brought disaster; and he hasn't turned aside his words. He'll rise against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who do wrong.

And Egypt is human and not God, and their horses are flesh and not spirit. And the LORD will stretch out his hand, and the helper will stumble and the helped will fall, and together all of them will come to an end.

For this is what the LORD said to me: As a lion growls, a young lion over its prey, when a whole band of shepherds is called out against it — at their voice it isn't dismayed, at their tumult it doesn't cringe — so the LORD of hosts will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.
Like birds hovering, so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem; shielding and rescuing, passing over and bringing to safety.
Return to him from whom you've turned away so deeply, Israelites!
For in that day everyone will reject his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made for you as sin.
And Assyria will fall by a sword that isn't a man's, and a sword that isn't humankind's will devour it; and it will flee before the sword, and its young men will be put to forced labour.
And its rock will pass away in terror, and its commanders will be dismayed at a standard — declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

isaiah_32.t: Look — a king will reign for righteousness, and officials will rule for justice.
And each will be like a hiding place from the wind and a shelter from the rainstorm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
And the eyes of those who see won't be closed, and the ears of those who hear will pay attention.
And the heart of the rash will come to understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will speak readily and clearly.
A fool will no longer be called noble, and a scoundrel won't be called eminent.
For a fool speaks folly, and his heart does wrong: practising godlessness, speaking error about the LORD, leaving the being of the hungry empty, depriving the thirsty of drink.
And a scoundrel — his weapons are evil; he plans wicked schemes, ruining the poor with sayings of falsehood even when the needy speaks what is just.
But a noble plans noble things, and on noble things he stands.
Carefree women, get up, hear my voice! Confident daughters, give ear to my speech!
In little more than a year you'll be agitated, you confident ones; for the grape harvest will fail, the gathering won't come.
Tremble, you carefree ones! Be agitated, you confident ones! Strip off and make yourselves bare, and tie sackcloth on your waists!
Beating your breasts for the fields of delight, for the fruitful vine —
on the ground of my people, where briars and thorns come up; yes, on all the houses of gaiety in the jubilant town.
For the palace will be forsaken, the tumult of the city abandoned; the hill and the watchtower will become bare places for ever, a delight of wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks —
until a spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes an orchard, and the orchard is reckoned a forest.
And justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will remain in the orchard.
And the work of righteousness will be peace, and the labour of righteousness, quietness and security for ever.
And my people will dwell in a habitation of peace, in dwelling places of security, in undisturbed resting places.
And it will hail when the forest comes down, and the city will be brought utterly low.
How blessed are you who sow beside every water, who let the ox and the donkey range free!

isaiah_33.t: Woe, destroyer, and you yourself not destroyed; traitor, and no one has dealt treacherously with you! When you've finished destroying, you'll be destroyed; when you've done with dealing treacherously, they'll deal treacherously with you.
LORD, show us favour; we've waited for you. Be their arm every morning, and our deliverance in a time of distress.
At the sound of tumult peoples flee; at your rising, nations scatter.
And your plunder will be gathered the way the locust gathers; as locusts rush, so they'll rush upon it.
The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he fills Zion with justice and righteousness.
And he will be the trustworthiness of your times, a wealth of deliverance, wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the LORD — that is his treasure.
Look — their valiant ones cry out in the streets; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are desolate; the traveller on the road has stopped. A covenant has been broken, cities rejected; no human being has been valued.
The land dries up and languishes; Lebanon is shamed and withers; Sharon has become like the desert plain, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
Now I will arise, says the LORD; now I will exalt myself; now I will lift myself up.
You conceive dry grass; you give birth to stubble. Your own breath is a fire that will consume you.
And peoples will be burnings of lime, thorns cut down and kindled in the fire.
Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and know, you who are near, my might.
Sinners in Zion are in dread; trembling has seized the godless: Who among us can live with a devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting hearths?

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks uprightly, who rejects the gain of extortion, who shakes his hands free from taking a bribe, who stops his ear against hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes against looking on evil —
he will dwell on the heights; the strongholds of the rocks will be his refuge; his bread will be given him, his water sure.
Your eyes will behold a king in his beauty; they'll see a land stretching far away.
Your heart will muse on the terror: Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed? Where is the one who counted the towers?
You won't see the barbarous people, a people whose speech is too obscure to make out, stammering of tongue, without understanding.

Look on Zion, the town of our appointed times! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, an undisturbed habitation, a tent that will not be struck, whose tent pegs will never be pulled out, and none of whose ropes will be torn apart.
But there the majestic LORD will be for us a place of rivers, of broad canals, where no rowing ship will go and no majestic vessel will pass.
For the LORD is our judge; the LORD is our lawgiver; the LORD is our king — he will deliver us.
Your ropes hang loose; they don't hold the base of the mast firm; they haven't spread out the sail. Then abundant booty of plunder will be divided; the lame will take spoil.
And no inhabitant will say: I'm sick. The people who dwell in her will be forgiven their iniquity.

isaiah_34.t: Draw near, nations, to hear; peoples, pay attention! Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that comes from it.
For the LORD has wrath against all the nations and rage against all their host; he has devoted them to destruction, given them over to slaughter.
And their slain will be thrown out, the stench of their corpses will go up, and the mountains will melt with their blood.
And all the host of the heavens will rot away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll; and all their host will wither as the leaves wither from a vine, like withered fruit from a fig tree.
For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens. Look — it will come down on Edom, and on the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgement.

The LORD has a sword; it's full of blood, gorged with fat — with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
And wild oxen will go down with them, and young bulls with the mighty bulls; their land will drink its fill of blood, and their dust will be gorged with fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of retribution for the cause of Zion.
And her torrents will be turned into pitch, her dust into sulphur; and her land will become burning pitch.
Night and day it won't be quenched; its smoke will go up for ever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; for ever and ever no one will pass through it.
And the desert owl and the hedgehog will possess it, the great owl and the raven will dwell in it. And he'll stretch over it a measuring-line of emptiness and the plumb-stones of emptiness.
As for her nobles, there's no kingship there to proclaim, and all her princes will be nothing.
And thorns will grow up in her fortresses, nettles and thornbushes in her fortifications; and she'll become a habitation of jackals, grass for the daughters of the ostrich.
And desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and the goat-demon will call to its companion. Surely there Lilith will settle and find herself a resting place.
There the owl will nest and lay, hatch and gather her brood in her shadow. Surely there the kites will be gathered, each with her companion.
Seek from the scroll of the LORD and read: not one of these will be missing; none will lack her companion. For his mouth has commanded, and his spirit has gathered them.
And he himself has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it out to them by the measuring-line. For ever they'll possess it; from generation to generation they'll dwell in it.

isaiah_35.t: The wilderness and the dry region will rejoice, and the desert plain will be glad and bud like a crocus.

It will bud abundantly and be glad — yes, with gladness and shouting for joy! The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the magnificence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendour of our God.
Strengthen the slack hands, and make firm the stumbling knees.
Say to those who are hasty of heart: Be strong, don't be afraid! Look — your God: vengeance will come, the requital of God; he himself will come and deliver you.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy; for waters will burst forth in the wilderness, and torrents in the desert plain.
And the parched ground will become a pool, the thirsty ground springs of water; in the habitation of jackals, where they lay down, there'll be grass for reeds and papyrus.
And there'll be a highway there, and a way, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean won't pass along it; it's for them alone — whoever walks the way, even fools, won't go astray.
No lion will be there, and no ravening beast will go up on it; none will be found there. And the redeemed will walk there.
And the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting joy will be on their head. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

isaiah_36.t: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.

And the king of Assyria sent the chief commander from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a massive army; and he took his stand at the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field.
And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, went out to him, with Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
And the chief commander said to them: Tell Hezekiah — this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this trust of yours that you trust in?
You say you have a plan and the strength for war — but that's only talk! Now, who are you trusting in, that you've rebelled against me?
Look — you're trusting in the staff of this crushed reed, Egypt, which will go into a man's hand and pierce it if he leans on it. That's what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to everyone who trusts in him.
And if you say to me: We trust in the LORD our God — isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem: You'll bow down before this altar?
And now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I'll give you two thousand horses, if you can put riders on them!
And how are you going to turn back a single governor among the least of my master's servants, when you've been relying on Egypt for chariotry and horsemen?
And now — have I come up against this land to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me: Go up against this land and destroy it.
And Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the chief commander: Please speak to your servants in Aramaic — we understand it. Don't speak to us in Judean where the people on the city wall can hear.

And the chief commander said: Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you — and not to the men sitting on the city wall, who are going to eat their own excrement and drink the water of their own feet along with you?
And the chief commander stood and called out in a loud voice in Judean: Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: Don't let Hezekiah deceive you — he won't be able to rescue you.
And don't let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying: The LORD will surely rescue us; this city won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

Don't listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink the water of his own cistern,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land — a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Don't let Hezekiah mislead you, saying: The LORD will deliver us. Have the gods of the nations rescued, any one of them, their own land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
Which of all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?
And they kept silent and didn't answer him a word, for the king's order was: Don't answer him.

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and told him the words of the chief commander.

isaiah_37.t: And when King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
And he sent Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.
And they said to him: This is what Hezekiah says: This day is a day of distress and rebuke and insult. Children have come to the birth, and there's no strength to bring them out.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the chief commander, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.
And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

And Isaiah said to them: This is what you're to say to your master: This is what the LORD says: Don't be afraid because of the words you've heard, with which the attendants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
Look — I'm putting a spirit in him, and he'll hear a report and return to his own land; and I'll make him fall by the sword in his own land.
And the chief commander returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah — he had heard that he'd left Lachish.
And he heard about Tirhakah king of Cush: He's come out to do battle with you. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah:
This is what you're to say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Don't let your God, the one you're trusting in, deceive you, saying: Jerusalem won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Look — you've heard yourself what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations rescue them — the nations my fathers destroyed: Gozan and Haran and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?
And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them. He went up to the house of the LORD and spread them out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
LORD of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim: you alone are the God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Incline your ear, LORD, and hear! Open your eyes, LORD, and see! Hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.
It's true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,
and have put their gods into the fire — for they weren't gods but the work of human hands, wood and stone — and so they destroyed them.
And now, LORD our God, deliver us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD.
And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria —
this is the word the LORD has spoken concerning him: She despises you, she mocks you — the virgin daughter of Zion; behind your back she shakes her head — the daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By the hand of your servants you have taunted the Lord, and said: With the abundance of my chariotry I've gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the remotest parts of Lebanon; and I'll cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest pines, and come to its farthest height, its densest forest.
I myself have dug wells and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I'll dry up all the canals of Egypt.
Haven't you heard? Long ago I did it; from days of antiquity I planned it; now I've brought it to pass, so that you should turn fortified cities into ruined heaps.
And their inhabitants were powerless; they were dismayed and ashamed. They were the vegetation of the field, the green of growing things, grass on the roofs, blasted before it is grown.
And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against me.
Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, I'll put my hook in your nose and my bridle on your lips, and turn you back by the way you came.
And this will be the sign for you: this year you'll eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
And those of the house of Judah who escape and remain will again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and the escaped from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

So this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: He won't come into this city, he won't shoot an arrow there; he won't confront it with a shield, and he won't throw up a siege mound against it.
By the way he came he will return, and into this city he will not come — declares the LORD.
And I'll shield this city, to deliver it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
And the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria; and when they rose early in the morning, there they all were — dead corpses.
And Sennacherib king of Assyria set out, went back, and stayed in Nineveh.

And while he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

isaiah_38.t: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. And Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said: This is what the LORD says: Put your household in order — you're about to die and won't live.
And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
And he said: Please, LORD, remember how I've walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and done what is good in your eyes. And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
Go and say to Hezekiah: This is what the LORD, the God of David your father, says: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look — I'm adding fifteen years to your days.
And I'll rescue you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I'll shield this city.
And this will be the sign for you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing he has spoken:
Look — I'm turning back the shadow of the steps, which has gone down on the steps of Ahaz with the sun, backward ten steps. And the sun went back ten steps on the steps by which it had gone down.
A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness.
I said: In the noontide of my days I must go into the gates of Sheol; I'm deprived of the remainder of my years.
I said: I won't see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living; I won't look on humankind any more with the inhabitants of the world that ceases.
My dwelling is pulled up and carried off from me like a shepherd's tent. I've rolled up my life like a weaver; he cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you make an end of me.
I've quieted myself until morning; like a lion, so he breaks all my bones. From day to night you make an end of me.
Like a swift or a crane, so I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes are worn out looking to the heights. Lord, I'm oppressed — stand surety for me!
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I'll walk slowly all my years because of the bitterness of my whole being.
Lord, by these things people live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit. So restore me to health and keep me alive.
Look — it was for my welfare that I was bitterly embittered; but you've held my life back from the pit of destruction, for you've thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol does not give you thanks; death does not praise you; those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness.
The living, the living — he gives you thanks, as I do this day. A father makes your faithfulness known to his children.
The LORD is at hand to deliver me; and we'll play my songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives, at the house of the LORD.
And Isaiah had said: Let them take a cake of figs and rub it on the boil, and he'll live.
And Hezekiah had said: What is the sign that I'll go up to the house of the LORD?

isaiah_39.t: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he'd heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

And Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them his treasure house — the silver and the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his whole armoury, and everything in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah didn't show them.
And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said: What did these men say, and where have they come to you from? And Hezekiah said: They've come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.
And he said: What did they see in your house? And Hezekiah said: They saw everything in my house. There was nothing in my storehouses I didn't show them.
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah: Hear the word of the LORD of hosts!
Look — days are coming when everything in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will remain, says the LORD.
And some of your own sons who come from you, whom you'll father, will be taken; and they'll be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: The word of the LORD that you've spoken is good. For, he said, there'll be peace and security in my days.

isaiah_40.t: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call out to her that her hard service is over, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she's received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.
A voice calling: In the wilderness, clear the way of the LORD; out in the desert plain, make a highway straight for our God.
Every valley will be lifted up, every mountain and hill brought low; the steep place will become level ground, and the rough places a plain.
And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all flesh together will see it; the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
A voice saying: Proclaim! And he said: What am I to proclaim? All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field.
The grass dries up, the flower withers when the wind of the LORD blows on it. Truly, the people is grass.
The grass dries up, the flower withers, but the word of our God will stand for ever.
Go up on a high mountain, bearer of good news to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, bearer of good news to Jerusalem! Lift it up, don't be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah: Look — your God!
Look — the Lord GOD is coming with strength, and his arm rules for him. Look — his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
Like a shepherd he will shepherd his flock; in his arm he'll gather the lambs and carry them in his bosom; he'll gently lead the nursing ewes.
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, marked off the heavens with a span, held the dust of the earth in a measure, weighed the mountains in a balance and the hills in scales?
Who has directed the spirit of the LORD? Who has been his counsellor and instructed him?
With whom did he take counsel? Who gave him understanding, taught him the path of justice, taught him knowledge, and made known to him the way of understanding?
Look — the nations are like a drop from a bucket, reckoned like the dust on the scales. Look — he lifts the coastlands like fine dust.
And Lebanon isn't enough for the fire, and its animals not enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before him; he reckons them as less than nothingness and emptiness.
So who will you liken God to? And what likeness will you set beside him?
The image — a craftsman casts it, a refiner overlays it with gold and casts silver chains for it.
The one too poor for such an offering chooses wood that won't rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an image that won't topple.
Do you not know? Do you not hear? Hasn't it been told you from the beginning? Haven't you understood since the earth was founded?
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; he stretches out the heavens like a thin curtain and spreads them like a tent to live in;
He brings rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stock taken root in the ground, when he blows on them and they dry up, and a tempest carries them off like stubble.
So who will you liken me to, that I should be his equal? says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes on high and look: who created these? He brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; by the greatness of his might and the strength of his power, not one of them is missing.
Why do you say, Jacob, and declare, Israel: My way is hidden from the LORD, and my cause passes away from my God?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the creator of the ends of the earth. He doesn't grow faint and doesn't grow weary; his understanding can't be searched out.
He gives strength to the faint, and to those with no vigour he increases might.
Youths grow faint and weary, and young men stumble and fall;
but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength; they'll rise on wings like eagles; they'll run and not grow weary; they'll walk and not grow faint.

isaiah_41.t: Be silent before me, coastlands; let the peoples renew their strength. Let them draw near, and then let them speak; let's come near together for judgement.
Who stirred up one from the east — whom he calls in righteousness to his foot? He gives up nations before him and subdues kings; he makes them like dust by his sword, like driven stubble by his bow.
He pursues them; he passes on unharmed, by a path his feet have never travelled.
Who has done it and accomplished it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, am first, and with the last ones — I am he.
The coastlands have seen it and they're afraid; the ends of the earth tremble; they've drawn near and come.
Each one helps his neighbour, and to his brother he says: Be strong!
And the craftsman encouraged the refiner, the one who smooths with the hammer him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering: It is good. And he fastened it with nails so it wouldn't topple.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend —
you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth and called from its farthest parts, and I said to you: You are my servant; I have chosen you and haven't rejected you.
Don't be afraid, for I am with you; don't be dismayed, for I am your God. I have strengthened you, I have helped you, I have upheld you with the right hand of my righteousness.
See, all who are angry with you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be as nothing and will perish.
You will look for them and not find them, those who strive with you. Those who make war on you will be as nothing, as nothingness.
For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand, who says to you: Don't be afraid; I myself will help you.
Don't be afraid, worm Jacob, men of Israel! I myself will help you, declares the LORD, and your redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
See, I have made you a threshing-sledge, sharp, new, and full of teeth. You'll thresh mountains and crush them, and make hills like chaff.
You'll winnow them, and a wind will carry them away, and a tempest will scatter them. And you'll be glad in the LORD; in the Holy One of Israel you'll boast.
The poor and the needy are looking for water, and there is none; their tongue is parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I'll make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry region springs of water.
I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle and the olive tree. I'll set in the desert plain the juniper, the plane and the cypress together.
so that they may see and know, take it to heart and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Bring near your case, says the LORD; bring forward your arguments, says the King of Jacob.

Let them bring them near and tell us what will happen. The former things — what were they? Tell us, and let us take it to heart and know how they turned out; or make us hear the things that are coming.
Tell us the things that are coming afterwards, and we'll know that you are gods. Go on — do good or do harm, so we may be dismayed and see it together.
See, you are nothing, and your work is worthless. Whoever chooses you is an abomination.
I have stirred up one from the north, and he has come; from the rising of the sun he'll call on my name. And he'll trample officials like mud, the way a potter tramples clay.
Who told it from the beginning, so that we might know, and beforehand, so that we might say: He is right? No — there was none who told; none who proclaimed; none who heard a saying from you.
I was first to say to Zion: See, here they are! and to Jerusalem I gave a bearer of good news.
And I look, and there is no one; among these there is no counsellor, that I might ask them and get an answer.
See, all of them — deception; their deeds are nothingness; their cast images are wind and emptiness.

isaiah_42.t: See, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom my being delights. I've put my spirit on him; he will bring forth judgement to the nations.
He will not cry out or raise his voice, or make it heard in the street.
A crushed reed he won't break, and a dim wick he won't snuff out; in faithfulness he will bring forth judgement.
He will not grow dim and will not be crushed until he establishes judgement on the earth; and the coastlands hope for his law.

Thus says the God, the LORD, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and what it brings forth, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness, and I'll take hold of your hand; and I'll watch over you and make you a covenant for the people, a light of the nations,
to open blind eyes, to bring the prisoner out of the prison, and out of the house of imprisonment those who dwell in darkness.
I am the LORD — that is my name; and I won't give my glory to another, or my praise to images.
The former things — see, they've come; and new things I'm telling now. Before they spring up I make you hear them.
Sing the LORD a new song, his praise from the end of the earth — you who go down to the sea and all that fills it, the coastlands and those who live in them.
Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voice, and the villages where Kedar dwells. Let the inhabitants of Sela shout for joy; let them cry aloud from the mountain tops.
Let them give glory to the LORD and declare his praise in the coastlands.
The LORD will go forth like a warrior; like a man of war he'll stir up his zeal. He'll raise a war-cry, yes, a battle shout; against his enemies he'll prevail.
I have kept quiet a long time; I have held still, I have restrained myself. Like a woman in labour I groan; I gasp and pant all at once.
I'll lay waste mountains and hills and dry up all their vegetation. I'll turn rivers into dry ground and dry up the pools.

And I will lead the blind by a way they have not known; in paths they've never known I will guide them. I'll turn the darkness before them into light, and the rough places into level ground. These are the things I will do, and I will not abandon them.
They're turned back and utterly disgraced, those who trust in the image, those who say to a molten image: You are our gods.
You deaf, listen! And you blind, look — and see!
Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like my dedicated one, and blind like the servant of the LORD?
You've seen many things but don't keep them; your ears are open, but he doesn't listen.
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of his righteousness, to make his law great and glorious.

But this is a people despoiled and plundered; all of them trapped in holes and hidden away in houses of imprisonment. They've become spoil, and there's no rescuer; plunder, and no one says: Bring it back.
Who among you will give ear to this, will pay attention and listen for the time to come?
Who gave Jacob up to plunder, and Israel to despoilers? Wasn't it the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They were not willing to walk in his ways, and they did not listen to his law.
So he poured out on him the heat of his anger and the fierceness of battle. It set him ablaze all round, and he didn't know it; it burned in him, and he didn't take it to heart.

isaiah_43.t: And now, thus says the LORD, who created you, Jacob, and who formed you, Israel: Don't be afraid, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name — you are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I am with you; and through the rivers, they won't overwhelm you. When you walk through fire you won't be scorched, and the flame won't burn you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your deliverer. I've given Egypt as your ransom price, Cush and Seba in place of you.
Because you're precious in my eyes, you are honoured, and I myself love you; and I give humankind in place of you, peoples in place of your being.
Don't be afraid, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north: Give them up! and to the south: Don't hold them back! Bring my sons from far off, and my daughters from the end of the earth —
everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed, whom I also made.
Bring out a people that's blind, though it has eyes, and deaf, though they have ears.

All the nations have assembled together, and the peoples have gathered. Who among them declares this, and makes us hear the former things? Let them bring their witnesses and be shown right; and let them hear and say: It is true.
You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and my servant whom I've chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me there'll be none.
I, I am the LORD, and apart from me there is no deliverer.
I declared and delivered and proclaimed, and there was no strange god among you; and you are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and I am God.
Also, from this day on, I am he, and there's no one who rescues from my hand. I act — and who can reverse it?
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I've sent to Babylon and brought them all down as fugitives, and the Chaldeans in the ships of their shout of joy.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.
Thus says the LORD, who makes a way in the sea and a path through mighty waters;
who brings out chariot and horse, army and mighty one together. They lie down and do not rise; they are snuffed out, quenched like a wick.
Don't remember the former things, and don't dwell on the ancient things.
See, I am doing a new thing; now it springs up — do you not see it? I will make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland.
The animals of the field will honour me, jackals and daughters of the ostrich, because I've put water in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland, to give my people a drink, my chosen one.
The people I formed for myself will recount my praise.
But you haven't called on me, Jacob, for you have grown weary of me, Israel.
You haven't brought me the sheep of your burnt offerings, and with your sacrifices you haven't honoured me. I haven't burdened you with offerings, and I haven't made you weary with frankincense.
You haven't bought me sweet cane with money, and with the fat of your sacrifices you haven't satisfied me. Instead you have burdened me with your sins; you have made me weary with your iniquities.
I, I am he who wipes out your transgressions for my own sake, and I won't remember your sins.
Remind me; let us go to judgement together. Make your own case, so that you may be shown right.
Your first ancestor sinned, and your spokesmen transgressed against me.
So I profaned the officials of the sanctuary, and gave Jacob over to be devoted to destruction, and Israel to reviling.

isaiah_44.t: And now listen, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the LORD, who made you and formed you from the belly, who will help you: Don't be afraid, Jacob my servant, and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
