For I will pour water on the thirsty ground and streams on the dry ground. I'll pour my spirit on your offspring and my blessing on your descendants.
And they will spring up among the grass, like poplars by streams of water.
One will say: I belong to the LORD; another will call himself by the name of Jacob; another will write on his hand: Belonging to the LORD, and will take the name of Israel.
Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel, and its redeemer, the LORD of hosts: I am first and I am last, and apart from me there's no god.

And who is like me? Let him proclaim it, let him declare it and set it out before me, since I established an ancient people; and the things coming, and the things that will come — let them declare them.
Do not dread and do not be afraid. Didn't I make you hear it long ago and declare it? And you are my witnesses. Is there a god apart from me? There is no Rock — I know none.
Those who form an image are all of them emptiness, and the things they treasure are no use; and their own witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so that they may be ashamed.
Who has formed a god or cast an image that is no use?
See, all his companions will be ashamed, and the craftsmen — they're only human. Let them all gather together and stand; let them dread, let them be ashamed together.
The ironsmith takes a tool, works it on the coals and forms it with hammers, and works it with the arm of his strength. He grows hungry and has no strength; he has drunk no water, and he grows weary.

The woodworker stretches out a measuring-line; he outlines it with a marker; he works it with scraping tools and outlines it with a compass. And he makes it like the form of a man, like the splendour of humankind, to dwell in a house.
cutting down cedars for himself — he took a cypress and an oak and let it grow strong for himself among the trees of the forest. He plants a cedar, and the rain makes it grow.

And it becomes something for a person to burn: he takes some of it and warms himself; he also kindles a fire and bakes bread; he also makes a god and bows down; he makes it an image and prostrates himself before it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over half of it he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied. He warms himself and says: Aha! I'm warm; I've seen the fire.
And the rest of it he makes into a god, into his image; he prostrates himself to it and bows down and prays to it and says: Rescue me, for you are my god.
They do not know and do not understand, for their eyes are smeared shut so they cannot see, their hearts so they cannot understand.

And no one takes it back to heart, and there is no knowledge and no understanding, to say: Half of it I burned in the fire, and I baked bread on its coals; I roast meat and eat. And shall I make the rest of it into an abomination? Shall I prostrate myself to a block of wood?
He feeds on ashes; a deceived heart has turned him aside, and he will not rescue his own being, or say: Is there not a lie in my right hand?
Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you're my servant. I formed you; you're a servant of mine. Israel, I won't forget you.
I've wiped out your transgressions like a dark cloud, and your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I've redeemed you.

Shout for joy, heavens, for the LORD has acted! Shout in triumph, depths of the earth! Break forth in a shout of joy, mountains, forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and in Israel he will get glory for himself.
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, and the one who formed you from the belly: I am the LORD, who makes everything, who stretches out the heavens alone, who spreads out the earth — by myself.
He frustrates the signs of empty talkers and makes diviners look foolish; he turns the wise back and makes their knowledge foolish;

who establishes the word of his servant and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem: It will be inhabited, and of the cities of Judah: They will be rebuilt, and I will raise up its waste places;
He says to the deep: Be dried up — and I will make your rivers dry;
who says of Cyrus: My shepherd, and he will carry out all my desire; and who says of Jerusalem: Let it be rebuilt, and of the temple: Let its foundation be laid.

isaiah_45.t: Thus says the LORD to his anointed one, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have taken hold of, to subdue nations before him and to loosen the belts of kings, to open doors before him and gates that will not be shut:
I myself will go before you and make the rough places smooth. I'll break doors of bronze and cut through bars of iron.
And I'll give you treasures of darkness and hidden hoards of secret places, so that you may know that I am the LORD, who calls you by your name — the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, I called you by your name; I gave you a title, though you don't know me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides me there is no god. I arm you, though you don't know me,
so that they may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is nothing apart from me. I am the LORD, and there is no other;
who forms light and creates darkness, who makes well-being and creates calamity. I am the LORD, who does all these things.
Drip down, heavens, from above, and let the clouds flow with righteousness. Let the earth open, and let deliverance bear fruit, and let righteousness sprout with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
Woe to the one who contends with the one who formed him — a potsherd among the potsherds of the ground! Does the clay say to the one who forms it: What are you making? Or: Your work has no hands?
Woe to the one who says to a father: What are you fathering? and to a woman: What are you in labour with?
Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel and the one who formed it: Ask me about the things that are coming! As for my children and the work of my hands — would you command me?
I myself made the earth and created humankind on it. I — my own hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
I myself have stirred him up in righteousness, and I'll make all his ways smooth. He'll build my city and let my exiles go, not for a price and not for a bribe, says the LORD of hosts.

Thus says the LORD: The produce of Egypt and the traffic of Cush and the Sabeans, men of stature — they will pass over to you and will be yours; they will walk behind you; in fetters they will pass over; and to you they will bow down, to you they will pray: Only among you is God, and there is no other; there are no gods.
Truly you are a God who hides himself, God of Israel, deliverer.
They're ashamed and disgraced, all of them; they walk in ignominy together — the makers of effigies.
Israel has been delivered by the LORD with an everlasting deliverance. You will not be ashamed or disgraced for ever and ever.

For thus says the LORD, the creator of the heavens — he is God — the one who formed the earth and made it; he established it; he didn't create it an emptiness; he formed it to be lived in: I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I didn't speak in secret, in a place of a land of darkness. I didn't say to the offspring of Jacob: Seek me in emptiness. I, the LORD, speak righteousness, declaring what is upright.
Gather together and come; draw near together, you fugitives of the nations! They know nothing — those who carry the wood of their image and pray to a god that cannot deliver.

Declare it and bring it near; yes, let them take counsel together. Who made this heard from of old, who declared it long ago? Was it not I, the LORD? And there is no god apart from me — a righteous God and a deliverer; there is none besides me.
Turn to me and be delivered, all you ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other.
By myself I've sworn; righteousness has gone out from my mouth, a word that won't return: that to me every knee will bend, and every tongue will swear.
Only in the LORD, it will be said of me, are righteousness and power. To him they will come, and all who are angry with him will be ashamed.
In the LORD all the offspring of Israel will be justified and will boast.

isaiah_46.t: Bel has bent down; Nebo is stooping low. Their figures are loaded on the animals, on the cattle. The things you carried in procession are loaded up, a load for a weary beast.
They have stooped low and bent down together; they could not bring the load to safety, and they themselves have gone into captivity.
Listen to me, house of Jacob and all the remnant of the house of Israel, you who've been carried since the belly, borne since the womb.
And to your old age I am he, and to your grey hair I will carry you. I made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and bring you to safety.
Who will you liken me to and make me equal with? Who will you compare me to, that we should be alike?
Those who pour out gold from a bag and weigh silver on the scales — they hire a refiner, and he makes it a god; they prostrate themselves; they bow down too.

They lift it on a shoulder and carry it and set it down in its place, and there it stands; from its place it does not move. Even if you cry out to it, it does not answer; it does not deliver you from your distress.
Remember this and take courage; bring it back to heart, you transgressors.
Remember the former things from of old: that I am God and there's no other, God, and there's nothing like me;
declaring the end from the beginning, and from long ago the things not yet done; saying: My plan will stand, and all my desire I will do —
calling a bird of prey from the east, from a distant land the man of my plan. I've spoken; I'll also bring it about. I've formed it; I'll also do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn of heart, far from righteousness:
I've brought my righteousness near; it isn't far off, and my deliverance won't delay. I'll give deliverance in Zion, to Israel my splendour.

isaiah_47.t: Go down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground — there is no throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you'll no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take a hand-mill and grind flour. Uncover your veil; strip off your skirt; bare your leg; wade through rivers.
Let your nakedness be uncovered; let your reproach be seen too. I will take vengeance, and I'll spare no one.
Our redeemer — the LORD of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit silently and go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; for you'll no longer be called queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and gave them into your hand. You showed them no compassion; on the old you laid your yoke very heavily.
And you said: I will be a queen for ever — so you never took these things to heart; you did not think how it would end.
And now hear this, voluptuous one, sitting there in security, saying in her heart: I, and besides me there is no other. I will not sit as a widow or know childlessness.

And both of these will come to you in a moment, in one day: childlessness and widowhood. In their full measure they'll come upon you, for all the abundance of your sorceries, for all the great might of your spells.
And you trusted in your wickedness. You said: No one sees me. Your wisdom and your knowledge have led you astray; and you said in your heart: I, and besides me there is no other.
And calamity will come upon you that you won't know how to charm away, and disaster will fall on you that you won't be able to avert; and ruin will come upon you suddenly, before you know it.
Stand up, then, with your spells and all the abundance of your sorceries, which you have laboured at from your youth. Perhaps you'll manage to profit; perhaps you'll inspire awe.
You have worn yourself out with all your counsels. Let them stand up and deliver you — those who divide the heavens, who gaze at the stars, who at the new moons make known what will come upon you.
See, they have become like stubble; fire has burned them. They cannot rescue themselves from the hand of the flame. There will be no coal to warm them, no fire to sit before.
So they have become for you — those you laboured for, your traders from your youth. Each has wandered off his own way; there is no one to deliver you.

isaiah_48.t: Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and who came out from the waters of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD and invoke the God of Israel — but not in truth and not in righteousness.
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel — the LORD of hosts is his name.
The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came about.
Because I knew that you are stubborn, your neck a sinew of iron and your forehead bronze,
so I declared it to you long ago; before it happened I proclaimed it to you, so you could not say: My figure did them, my image and my cast image commanded them.
You have heard it; look at all of it! And you — will you not declare it? From now on I make you hear new things, hidden things you have never known.
They are created now, not long ago, and before this day you had not heard of them, so you could not say: See, I knew them.
You had neither heard nor known, nor was your ear opened long ago; for I knew you would deal treacherously indeed, and that you were called a transgressor from the belly.
For the sake of my name I'll hold back my anger, and for my praise I'll restrain myself towards you, so as not to cut you off.
See, I've refined you, but not as silver; I've tested you in the furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake I'll act — for how should my name be profaned? And I won't give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, my called one: I am he; I am first, yes, I am last.
My own hand founded the earth, and my right hand spanned the heavens. I call to them; they stand together.
Gather together, all of you, and listen! Who among them declared these things? The LORD loves him; he will do his desire on Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I, I have spoken; yes, I've summoned him. I've brought him, and he'll make his way succeed.
Draw near to me; hear this! From the beginning I haven't spoken in secret; from the time it came about, I was there. And now the Lord GOD has sent me — and his spirit.
Thus says the LORD, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you in the way you should go.
If only you'd paid attention to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like the river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
And your offspring would have been like the sand, and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off or destroyed from before me.
Go out from Babylon; flee from the Chaldeans! With a sound of joyful shouting declare this; proclaim it; send it out to the end of the earth. Say: The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob.
And they weren't thirsty when he led them through the waste places; he made water flow for them from a rock; he split a rock, and the waters gushed out.
There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked.

isaiah_49.t: Listen to me, coastlands, and pay attention, you peoples far off! The LORD called me from the belly; from the inward parts of my mother he named my name.
And he made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. And he made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he concealed me.
And he said to me: You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will get glory for myself.
And I myself said: I have laboured for nothing; I have spent my strength for emptiness and futility. Yet my cause is with the LORD, and my recompense with my God.

And now the LORD says — who formed me from the belly to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, and that Israel might be gathered to him; and I'm honoured in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has been my power —

and he said: It's too slight a thing for you to be my servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel. I'll make you a light of the nations, to be my deliverance to the end of the earth.

Thus says the LORD, the redeemer of Israel, its Holy One, to the one deeply despised, to the one abhorred by a nation, to a servant of rulers: Kings will see and stand up, princes — and they will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, and he has chosen you.

Thus says the LORD: In a time of favour I answered you, and on a day of deliverance I helped you. I'll watch over you and make you a covenant for the people, to raise up the land, to apportion the desolate inheritances,
saying to the prisoners: Come out! to those in darkness: Show yourselves! Along the roads they will graze, and on all the bare heights will be their pasture.
They will not hunger or thirst, and burning heat and sun will not strike them; for the one who has compassion on them will guide them, and by springs of water he will gently lead them.
And I'll make all my mountains a road, and my highways will be raised up.
See, these come from far off, and see, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.
Shout for joy, heavens, and be glad, earth! Break forth in a shout of joy, mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people and has compassion on his poor.
And Zion said: The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.
Does a woman forget her nursing child, or stop having compassion on the child of her womb? Even these may forget, but I will not forget you.
See, on the palms of my hands I've inscribed you; your walls are before me continually.
Your children have hurried back; those who tore you down and made you desolate go out from you.
Lift up your eyes all around and look: all of them have gathered together; they've come to you. As I live, declares the LORD, you'll put them all on like an ornament and tie them on like a bride.
For your waste places and your desolate places and the land of your destruction — now you'll be too cramped for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far off.
The children of your bereavement will yet say in your ears: This place is too cramped for me; make room for me, so I can live here.
And you'll say in your heart: Who fathered these for me? I was bereaved and barren, gone into exile and thrust away — and these, who brought them up? See, I was left alone; these — where were they?

Thus says the Lord GOD: See, I'll lift up my hand to the nations and raise my standard to the peoples; and they'll bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

And kings will be your foster-fathers, and their princesses your nursing-mothers. With faces to the ground they'll bow down to you and lick up the dust of your feet. And you'll know that I am the LORD, and those who wait for me won't be ashamed.
Can booty be taken from a warrior, or the captives of a righteous one escape?

For thus says the LORD: Even the captives of a warrior will be taken, and the booty of a ruthless one will escape; and I myself will contend with the one who contends with you, and I myself will deliver your children.

And I'll make those who maltreat you eat their own flesh, and they'll be drunk on their own blood as on sweet wine. And all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your deliverer and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

isaiah_50.t: Thus says the LORD: Where is this document of your mother's divorce, by which I sent her away? Or which of my creditors is it I sold you to? See, for your iniquities you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.

Why did I come and there was no one? I called, and no one answered. Is my hand really too short to ransom? Or is there no strength in me to rescue? See, by my rebuke I dry up the sea; I make rivers a wilderness. Their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst.
I clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
The Lord GOD has given me a tongue of disciples, to know how to sustain the weary with a word. He wakes me morning by morning; he wakens my ear to hear like disciples.
The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not turn back.
I gave my back to those who struck it, and my cheeks to those who pulled out the beard. I didn't hide my face from insults and spitting.
And the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been humiliated. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know I will not be put to shame.
The one who justifies me is near. Who will contend with me? Let's stand together. Who has a case against me? Let him draw near to me.
See, the Lord GOD helps me. Who is he who'll condemn me? See, all of them will wear out like a garment; a moth will eat them.
Who among you fears the LORD, listening to the voice of his servant, who has walked in darkness and has no brightness? Let him trust in the name of the LORD and lean on his God.
See, all of you who kindle a fire, who gird on firebrands: walk by the light of your fire and by the firebrands you've kindled. This has come to you from my hand: you'll lie down in pain.

isaiah_51.t: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock you were hewn from, and to the quarry of the pit you were dug out of.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave birth to you; for he was only one when I called him, and I blessed him and multiplied him.

For the LORD has comforted Zion; he's comforted all her waste places and made her wilderness like Eden and her desert plain like the garden of the LORD. Rejoicing and joy will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of music.
Pay attention to me, my people, and give ear to me, my nation; for law will go out from me, and I'll set my judgement as a light of peoples.
My righteousness is near; my deliverance has gone out, and my arms will judge peoples. The coastlands will wait for me, and for my arm they'll hope.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens and look at the earth beneath; for the heavens will be dispersed like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die like gnats. But my deliverance will be for ever, and my righteousness won't be broken.
Listen to me, you who know righteousness, a people with my law in their heart: don't fear the reproach of humankind, and don't be dismayed by their reviling.
For a moth will eat them like a garment, and a clothes-moth will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will be for ever, and my deliverance to generation after generation.
Awake, awake, put on power, arm of the LORD! Awake as in the days of old, the generations of long ago. Wasn't it you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the sea monster?
Wasn't it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
And the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with a shout of joy, and everlasting joy will be on their head. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
I, I am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you're afraid of a mortal who dies, and of a child of humankind who's made grass?

And you've forgotten the LORD your maker, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth, and you dread continually, all day long, before the rage of the oppressor, when he's made ready to destroy. And where is the rage of the oppressor?
The one bowed down hastens to be set free; he won't die and go down to the pit, and his bread won't run out.
And I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar — the LORD of hosts is his name.
And I've put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens and to found the earth, and to say to Zion: You are my people.
Rouse yourself, rouse yourself, arise, Jerusalem, you who've drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of his rage; the bowl, the cup of staggering, you've drunk and drained.
There's no one to lead her of all the children she's borne, and no one to take hold of her hand of all the children she's brought up.
These two things have happened to you — who'll show sympathy to you? — the devastation and the destruction, the famine and the sword. How shall I comfort you?
Your children have become faint; they've lain down at the head of every street like an antelope in a net, full of the rage of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear this, poor one, drunken, but not with wine:
Thus says your Lord, the LORD, your God, who contends for his people: See, I've taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the bowl, the cup of my rage — you won't drink it again.
And I will put it into the hand of those who torment you, who said to your being: Lie down, so we can walk over you. And you made your back like the ground, like the street for those who pass over.

isaiah_52.t: Awake, awake, put on your power, Zion! Put on the garments of your splendour, Jerusalem, holy city; for the uncircumcised and the unclean will never come into you again.
Shake yourself free from the dust! Arise, be seated, Jerusalem! Loosen the fetters from your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For thus says the LORD: You were sold for nothing, and you won't be redeemed with money.
For thus says the Lord GOD: To Egypt my people went down at the first, to sojourn there; and Assyria oppressed it for nothing.
And now, what is there for me here — declares the LORD — for my people has been taken for nothing? Its rulers wail — declares the LORD — and continually, all day long, my name is reviled.
Therefore my people will know my name; therefore, in that day — that I am he who speaks: here I am.
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who bears news, who proclaims peace, who bears good news, who proclaims deliverance, who says to Zion: Your God reigns!
The voice of your watchmen — they lift up their voice; together they shout for joy; for eye to eye they'll see when the LORD returns to Zion.
Break forth, shout for joy together, waste places of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth will see the deliverance of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing unclean! Go out from her midst; purify yourselves, you who carry the articles of the LORD!
For you won't go out in haste, and you won't go in flight; for the LORD is going before you, and the God of Israel is your rearguard.
See, my servant will prosper; he will be high and lifted up and greatly exalted.
Just as many were appalled at you — so disfigured was his appearance, beyond that of a man, and his form beyond that of the children of humankind —
so he'll sprinkle many nations; kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what hadn't been recounted to them they'll see, and what they hadn't heard they'll understand.

isaiah_53.t: Who has believed our report, and the arm of the LORD — who has it been revealed to?
And he grew up before him like a shoot, like a root out of dry ground. He had no form and no magnificence, that we should look at him; no appearance, that we should desire him.
He was despised and rejected by others, a man of pains and acquainted with sickness; and like one from whom people hide their face he was despised, and we did not value him.
Truly he bore our sicknesses and carried our pains; and we ourselves considered him stricken, struck by God and afflicted.
And he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The chastening that brought us peace was on him, and by his wound we were healed.
All of us like sheep have gone astray; each has turned to his own way. And the LORD made the iniquity of us all fall upon him.
He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, and he did not open his mouth. Like a sheep brought to the slaughter, like a ewe silent before her shearers, he did not open his mouth.

By oppression and judgement he was taken away; and as for his generation — who gives it a thought? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of the transgression of my people he was stricken.
And they assigned his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, though he'd done no violence and there was no deceit in his mouth.
And the LORD desired to crush him; he made him sick. If his being makes a guilt offering, he will see offspring, he will prolong days; and the desire of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
From the labour of his being he'll see; he'll be satisfied. By his knowledge the righteous one, my servant, will justify the many, and he himself will carry their iniquities.

Therefore I'll allot him a portion among the many, and with the mighty he'll apportion plunder, because he poured out his being to death and was numbered with transgressors; and he himself bore the sin of many and makes intercession for the transgressors.

isaiah_54.t: Shout for joy, barren one who has not given birth! Break forth in a shout of joy and cry aloud, you who have never been in labour! For the children of the desolate one are more than the children of the married one, says the LORD.
Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; don't hold back. Lengthen your tent cords and drive your tent pegs firm.
For you'll spread out to the right and to the left, and your offspring will take possession of nations and will resettle desolated cities.

Don't be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; don't be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated. For you will forget the shame of your youth, and the reproach of your widowhood you will not remember again.
For your husband is your maker — the LORD of hosts is his name — and your redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; he's called the God of all the earth.
For like a wife abandoned and grieved in spirit the LORD has called you, and like a wife of one's youth when she's rejected, says your God.
For a small moment I abandoned you, and with great compassion I'll gather you.
In a flood of wrath I hid my face for a moment from you; but with everlasting steadfast love I'll have compassion on you, says your redeemer, the LORD.
For this is like the waters of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn not to be angry with you or to rebuke you.
For the mountains may be removed and the hills may shake, but my steadfast love won't be removed from you, and my covenant of peace won't shake, says the one who has compassion on you, the LORD.
Poor one, storm-tossed, not comforted: see, I'm setting your stones in antimony and will lay your foundations with sapphires.
And I'll make your battlements of ruby, and your gates of stones of beryl, and all your border of precious stones.
And all your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be the peace of your children.
In righteousness you'll be established. Be far from oppression, for you won't be afraid, and from terror, for it won't come near you.
See, if anyone quarrels, it is not from me; whoever quarrels with you will fall because of you.
See, I myself created the craftsman who blows on a fire of charcoal and brings out a weapon for its work; and I myself created the destroyer to ruin.

No weapon formed against you will succeed, and every tongue that rises against you in judgement you'll condemn. This is the inheritance of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is from me, declares the LORD.

isaiah_55.t: Ah, every thirsty one, come to the waters! And whoever has no money — come, buy grain and eat! Come, buy grain without money and without price — wine and milk!
Why do you weigh out money for what isn't bread, and your toil for what doesn't satisfy? Listen, listen to me and eat what is good, and let your being take delight in rich food.
Incline your ear and come to me; listen, and let your being live. And I'll make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful steadfast loves of David.
See, I made him a witness to peoples, a leader and a commander of peoples.
See, a nation you don't know you'll call, and a nation that hasn't known you will run to you, because of the LORD your God and for the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the LORD while he lets himself be found; call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the man of wrongdoing his thoughts; and let him return to the LORD, and he'll have compassion on him, and to our God, for he will abundantly forgive.
For my thoughts aren't your thoughts, and your ways aren't my ways, declares the LORD.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and don't return there until they've watered the earth and made it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater —
so will my word be that goes out from my mouth: it won't return to me empty, but will do what I've desired and prosper in what I sent it for.
For in joy you'll go out, and in peace you'll be led. The mountains and the hills will break forth before you in a shout of joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
In place of the thornbush a cypress will grow up, and in place of the nettle a myrtle will grow up. And it will be a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.

isaiah_56.t: Thus says the LORD: Keep justice and do righteousness; for my deliverance is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
How blessed is the mortal who does this, and the child of humankind who takes hold of it: keeping the sabbath and not profaning it, keeping his hand from doing any evil.
And don't let the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say: The LORD will surely separate me from his people. And don't let the eunuch say: See, I'm a dry tree.
For thus says the LORD to the eunuchs who keep my sabbaths and choose what I desire and take hold of my covenant:
I'll give them in my house and within my walls a monument and a name, better than sons and daughters. I'll give him an everlasting name that won't be cut off.

And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him and to love the name of the LORD, to become his servants — every one who keeps the sabbath from profaning it and who takes hold of my covenant —

I'll bring them to my holy mountain and make them rejoice in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all the peoples.
Declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the banished of Israel: I will gather still more to him, besides those already gathered.
All you animals of the field, come and devour — all you animals in the forest!
Its watchmen are blind, all of them; they know nothing. All of them are dumb dogs; they can't bark — dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber.
And the dogs are greedy; they never know satiety. And they are shepherds who do not know how to understand. All of them have turned to their own way, each to his own unjust gain, to the last of them.
Come, let me fetch wine, and let us drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be like today — great, and far more so.

isaiah_57.t: The righteous one has perished, and no one takes it to heart; and men of loyalty are taken away, with no one understanding that the righteous one is taken away from before the evil.
Peace will come; they'll rest on their beds — each one who walks in his uprightness.
And you, draw near here, children of a soothsayer, offspring of an adulterer and of a prostitute!
Who are you making fun of? Who do you open your mouth wide at and stick out your tongue at? Aren't you children of transgression, offspring of deception?
you who inflame yourselves among the great trees, under every luxuriant tree, you who slaughter the children in the wadis, under the clefts of the rocks.

Among the smooth stones of the wadi is your portion; they, they are your allotted portion. Even to them you've poured out a drink offering, you've offered up a grain offering. Shall I relent over these?
On a high and lofty mountain you've set your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.

And behind the door and the doorpost you've set up your memorial. For away from me you've uncovered yourself and gone up; you've made your bed wide and made a bargain for yourself with them. You've loved their bed; you've gazed on nakedness.
And you journeyed to the king with oil and increased your perfumes. You sent your envoys far off and brought yourself low as far as Sheol.
With the length of your journey you became weary; you didn't say: It's hopeless. You found renewal of strength; so you didn't become weak.
And who were you in dread of and afraid of, that you should lie and not remember me, not take it to heart? Isn't it that I've been silent, even from long ago, and so you don't fear me?
I myself will declare your righteousness — and your deeds; and they won't benefit you.

When you cry out, let your collection of idols rescue you! But a wind will carry them all away; a vapour will take them. But the one who takes refuge in me will inherit the land and will possess my holy mountain.
And it will be said: Build up, build up! Clear the way! Lift the obstacle out of the way of my people!

For thus says the high and lofty one, who dwells for ever, and whose name is holy: I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the contrite and lowly of spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and to restore the heart of the contrite.
For I won't contend for ever and won't be angry for all time; for the spirit would grow faint before me, and the breaths that I myself have made.
For the iniquity of his unjust gain I was angry, and I struck him, hiding myself, and was angry; and he went on, turning away, in the way of his own heart.
I've seen his ways, and I'll heal him; and I'll lead him and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
creating the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to the far off and to the near, says the LORD, and I'll heal him.
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, for it can't be quiet, and its waters toss up mire and mud.
There's no peace, says my God, for the wicked.

isaiah_58.t: Call out full-throated; don't hold back! Like the trumpet raise your voice, and declare to my people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

And me they seek day after day, and they desire the knowledge of my ways, like a nation that has done righteousness and has not forsaken the judgement of its God. They ask me for righteous judgements; they desire the approach of God.
Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? We have humbled our being, and you take no notice. See, on the day of your fasting you pursue your own desire, and you drive hard all your labourers.
See, you fast for strife and contention and to strike with a wicked fist. You aren't fasting as you do this day if you want your voice heard on high.

Is a fast like this the one I choose, a day for a person to humble his being? Is it to bow his head like a bulrush and spread sackcloth and ashes as a bed? Is this what you call a fast and a day of acceptance to the LORD?
Is not this the fast I choose: to loosen the bonds of wickedness, to unfasten the bindings of the yoke-bar, to let the crushed go free, and to tear apart every yoke-bar?
Isn't it to break your bread for the hungry, and to bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover him, and not to hide yourself from your own flesh?
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly; your righteousness will go before you; the glory of the LORD will be your rearguard.
Then you'll call and the LORD will answer; you'll cry for help and he'll say: Here I am. If you remove the yoke-bar from among you, the pointing finger and the speaking of wrongdoing,
and you offer your very being to the hungry and satisfy the being of the afflicted, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like noon.
And the LORD will lead you continually and satisfy your being in arid regions and strengthen your bones. And you will be like a watered garden and like a spring of waters whose waters never fail.
And some of you will rebuild the ancient waste places; you will raise up the foundations laid generations ago. And you will be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.

If you turn back your foot from the sabbath, from doing your own desires on my holy day, and call the sabbath a delight, the holy day of the LORD honourable, and honour it by not going your own ways, not pursuing your desire or speaking idle words —
then you'll take delight in the LORD, and I'll make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.

isaiah_59.t: See, the hand of the LORD isn't too short to deliver, and his ear isn't too dull to hear.
But your iniquities have been separating between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he doesn't hear.
For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken deception; your tongue mutters injustice.
There's no one who calls in righteousness, and no one who goes to judgement in trustworthiness. They trust in emptiness and speak worthlessness; they conceive mischief and bring forth wrongdoing.
They've hatched viper's eggs and they weave spider's webs. Whoever eats any of their eggs will die, and the crushed egg hatches a snake.
Their webs won't become clothing, and no one will cover himself with what they make. What they make is the product of wrongdoing, and a deed of violence is in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wrongdoing; devastation and destruction are on their highways.
They don't know a way of peace, and there's no justice on their tracks. They've made their paths crooked for themselves; no one who treads on them knows peace.
So justice is far from us, and righteousness doesn't reach us. We wait for the light, and see — darkness; for brightness, and we walk in gloom.
We grope for the wall like the blind, and like those with no eyes we grope. We stumble at noon as in the twilight; among the vigorous we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears, and like doves we moan and moan. We wait for justice, and there's none; for deliverance — it's far from us.
For our transgressions are many before you, and our sins have testified against us; our transgressions are with us, and our iniquities — we know them.
Transgressing and denying the LORD, turning back from following our God; speaking oppression and rebellion, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of deception.
And justice has been driven back, and righteousness stands far off; for truth has stumbled in the public square, and uprightness can't enter.
And truth has become lacking, and whoever turns aside from evil is plundered. And the LORD saw, and it was evil in his eyes that there was no justice.
And he saw that there was no one, and he was appalled that there was no one to intervene. And his own arm brought him deliverance, and his own righteousness — it sustained him.
And he put on righteousness like body armour, and a helmet of deliverance on his head. He put on garments of vengeance as clothing and wrapped himself in zeal like a robe.
According to their deeds, that's how he'll repay: rage to his adversaries, requital to his enemies; to the coastlands he'll repay requital.
And they'll fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he'll come like a rushing stream that the wind of the LORD drives.
And a redeemer will come to Zion, and to those in Jacob who turn from transgression, declares the LORD.

And I — this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: my spirit that is on you, and my words that I've put in your mouth, won't depart from your mouth or from the mouth of your offspring or from the mouth of your offspring's offspring, says the LORD, from now and for ever.

isaiah_60.t: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has dawned on you.
For see, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but upon you the LORD will dawn, and his glory will appear over you.
And nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
Lift up your eyes all around and look: all of them have gathered together; they've come to you. Your sons will come from far off, and your daughters will be carried on the hip.
Then you'll see and be radiant, and your heart will throb and swell; for the abundance of the sea will be turned over to you, the wealth of nations will come to you.
A multitude of camels will cover you, the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all of them will come from Sheba. They'll carry gold and frankincense and will bear news of the praises of the LORD.
Every flock of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They'll go up on my altar and be accepted, and I'll beautify my splendid house.
Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their cotes?

For the coastlands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first of all, to bring your children from far off, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God and for the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
And foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you; for in my wrath I struck you, and in my favour I've had compassion on you.
And your gates will stand open continually; day and night they won't be shut, to bring to you the wealth of nations, with their kings led in.
For the nation and the kingdom that won't serve you will perish, and those nations will be utterly desolate.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you — the juniper, the plane and the cypress together — to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I'll glorify the place of my feet.

And the children of those who afflicted you will come to you bowing down, and all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet. And they'll call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
In place of your being forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting majesty, a joy from generation to generation.
And you'll suck the milk of nations and suck the breast of kings; and you'll know that I, the LORD, am your deliverer, and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

In place of the bronze I'll bring gold, and in place of the iron I'll bring silver, and in place of the wood, bronze, and in place of the stones, iron. And I'll make peace your overseer and righteousness your taskmaster.
Violence won't be heard in your land any more, nor devastation and destruction within your territories; and you'll call your walls Deliverance and your gates Praise.
The sun won't be your light by day any more, and the moon won't shine on you for brightness; but the LORD will be for you an everlasting light, and your God your splendour.
Your sun won't go down any more, and your moon won't withdraw; for the LORD will be for you an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be complete.
And your people — all of them righteous — will possess the land for ever: the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, so that I may glorify myself.
The small one will become a thousand, and the little one a mighty nation. I am the LORD; in its time I'll hasten it.

isaiah_61.t: The spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to bear good news to the humble. He's sent me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to captives and release to prisoners,
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favour and the day of our God's vengeance, to comfort all mourners,

to appoint for the mourners of Zion, to give them a turban in place of ashes, oil of rejoicing in place of mourning, a mantle of praise in place of a faint spirit; and they'll be called the great trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may glorify himself.
And they'll rebuild the ancient waste places; they'll raise up the former desolate places and renew the ruined cities, desolate for generation after generation.
And strangers will stand and shepherd your flocks, and foreigners will be your farmers and your vinedressers.
And you'll be called the priests of the LORD; ministers of our God will be said of you. You'll consume the wealth of nations, and in their glory you'll boast.
In place of your shame — a double portion; and instead of ignominy they'll shout for joy over their share. So in their land they'll possess double; everlasting joy will be theirs.
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery with injustice. And I'll give their recompense in faithfulness and make an everlasting covenant with them.
And their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognise them, that they're the offspring the LORD has blessed.

I'll greatly rejoice in the LORD; my being will be glad in my God; for he's clothed me with garments of deliverance, has covered me with a robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom who wears his turban as a priest does, and like a bride who adorns herself with her ornaments.
For as the ground brings forth its growth, and as a garden makes what's sown in it grow, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise grow before all the nations.

isaiah_62.t: For Zion's sake I won't be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I won't remain quiet, until her righteousness goes forth like brightness and her deliverance burns like a torch.
And nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you'll be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will designate.
And you'll be a crown of splendour in the hand of the LORD, and a royal headdress in the palm of your God.

They won't say of you any more: Forsaken, and of your land they won't say any more: Desolation. For you'll be called My-Delight-Is-In-Her, and your land Married; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a virgin, your sons will marry you; and with the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I've appointed guards; all day and all night, continually, they won't be silent. You who bring the LORD to remembrance, take no rest!
And give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her a praise in the earth.
The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his power: I'll never again give your grain as food to your enemies, and foreigners won't drink your new wine that you've laboured for.
For those who gather it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who collect it will drink it in my holy courts.
Pass through, pass through the gates! Clear the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway; clear away the stones! Raise a standard over the peoples!
See, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion: See, your deliverance is coming! See, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
And they'll be called the holy people, the redeemed of the LORD; and you'll be called Sought-Out, a city not forsaken.

isaiah_63.t: Who is this coming from Edom, in garments stained red, from Bozrah? This one, magnificent in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to deliver.
Why is your clothing red, and your garments like someone treading in a winepress?

I have trodden the winepress alone, and from the peoples there was no one with me. I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my rage, and their lifeblood spattered on my garments, and all my clothes I have stained.
For a day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.
And I looked, and there was no helper, and I was appalled that there was no one to sustain me. And my own arm brought me deliverance, and my rage — it sustained me.
And I trod down peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my rage, and I brought their lifeblood down to the ground.

I'll bring to remembrance the steadfast loves of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has dealt out to us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel that he's dealt out to them according to his compassion and the greatness of his steadfast loves.
And he said: Surely they're my people, children who won't deal falsely. And he became their deliverer.
In all their distress he was distressed, and the angel of his presence delivered them. In his love and in his mercy he redeemed them, and he lifted them and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his holy spirit; and he turned himself into an enemy to them; he himself fought against them.
And he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people: Where's the one who brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where's the one who put his holy spirit in their midst,
who made the arm of his splendour go at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name,
who made them walk through the deeps — like a horse in the wilderness, they didn't stumble.
Like livestock going down into the valley, the spirit of the LORD gave them rest. That's how you led your people, to make yourself a name of splendour.
Look down from the heavens and see, from your holy and splendid abode! Where are your zeal and your mighty deeds, the stirring of your inward parts and your compassion? They're held back from me.
For you are our father, though Abraham doesn't know us and Israel doesn't acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our father; our redeemer from of old is your name.
Why, LORD, do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart so that we don't fear you? Return, for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance!
For a little while your holy people possessed it; our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary.
We've become like those you've never ruled over, like those your name has never been called on.

isaiah_64.t: If only you would tear open the heavens and come down — the mountains would shake before you!
As fire kindles brushwood, as fire makes water boil, to make your name known to your adversaries, so that nations would quake before you!
When you did awesome deeds we weren't looking for, you came down; the mountains shook before you.
And from of old no one's heard, no one's given ear; no eye has seen a God besides you who acts for the one who waits for him.
You meet the one who rejoices and does righteousness, who remembers you in your ways. See, you were angry, and we sinned — in our sins for a long time — and shall we be delivered?
And we've all become like the unclean, and all our righteous acts like a menstrual garment. And we've all withered like a leaf, and our iniquities carry us off like the wind.
And there is no one who calls on your name, no one who rouses himself to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us and melted us away by the hand of our iniquity.
And now, LORD, you're our father. We are the clay, and you are the one who formed us, and all of us are the work of your hand.
Don't be angry, LORD, beyond measure, and don't remember iniquity for ever. See, look now — all of us are your people!
Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and splendid house, where our fathers praised you, has been burned with fire; and all our pleasant things have become a ruin.
Over these will you restrain yourself, LORD? Will you keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?

isaiah_65.t: I let myself be sought by those who didn't ask; I let myself be found by those who didn't seek me. I said: Here I am, here I am! to a nation not called by my name.
I spread out my hands all day long to a rebellious people who walk in the way that isn't good, after their own thoughts —
the people who provoke me to anger to my face continually, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on the bricks,
who sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places, who eat the flesh of the pig, with broth of unclean meat in their vessels —
who say: Keep to yourself; don't come near me, for I am holier than you! These are smoke in my nose, a fire burning all day long.
See, it's written before me: I won't be silent, but I'll repay; and I'll repay into their bosom —
your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the LORD, who burned incense on the mountains and taunted me on the hills. And I'll measure their former work into their bosom.
Thus says the LORD: As the new wine is found in the cluster and one says: Don't destroy it, for a blessing is in it — so I'll act for the sake of my servants, so as not to destroy them all.
And I'll bring out offspring from Jacob, and from Judah a possessor of my mountains; and my chosen ones will take possession of it, and my servants will dwell there.
And Sharon will become a pasture for sheep, and the valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who've sought me.
But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who spread a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny —

I'll appoint you for the sword, and all of you will bow down to the slaughter; because I called and you didn't answer, I spoke and you didn't listen, and you did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I didn't desire.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: See, my servants will eat, but you'll be hungry; see, my servants will drink, but you'll be thirsty; see, my servants will rejoice, but you'll be ashamed;
see, my servants will shout for joy from gladness of heart, but you'll cry out from pain of heart and wail from brokenness of spirit.
and you'll leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones. And the Lord GOD will put you to death, and he'll call his servants by another name,

so that the one who blesses himself in the land will bless himself by the God of Amen, and the one who swears in the land will swear by the God of Amen; for the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
For see, I'm creating new heavens and a new earth; and the former things won't be remembered or come to mind.
But rejoice and be glad for ever in what I'm creating; for see, I'm creating Jerusalem a joy and her people a gladness.
And I'll be glad in Jerusalem and rejoice in my people; and the sound of weeping won't be heard in her any more, nor the sound of a cry of distress.

There won't be there any more an infant of days, or an old one who doesn't complete his days; for the young man will die a hundred years old, and the one who fails to reach a hundred years will be cursed.
And they'll build houses and live in them, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They won't build and another dwell; they won't plant and another eat. For like the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen ones will enjoy to the full the work of their hands.
They won't labour for emptiness and won't bring forth children for sudden terror; for they're the offspring of those blessed by the LORD, and their descendants with them.
And it will be that before they call, I'll answer; while they're still speaking, I'll hear.
Wolf and lamb will graze as one, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, and as for the snake — dust will be its food. They'll do no harm and won't destroy in all my holy mountain, says the LORD.

isaiah_66.t: Thus says the LORD: The heavens are my throne, and the earth my footstool. Where is this house that you'd build for me, and where is this place of my rest?
And all these my hand made, and all these came to be, declares the LORD. And this is the one I'll look to: the poor and stricken in spirit and the one who trembles at my word.

The one who slaughters the ox is like one who strikes down a person; the one who sacrifices the lamb is like one who breaks a dog's neck; the one who offers up a grain offering is like one who offers the blood of a pig; the one who offers frankincense as a memorial is like one who blesses wrongdoing. They too have chosen their own ways, and their being has delighted in their detestable things.

I too will choose their punishments and bring their fears upon them; because I called and no one answered, I spoke and they didn't listen, and they did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I didn't desire.

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: Your brothers who hate you, who exclude you for my name's sake, have said: Let the LORD be honoured, so we can look on your joy! But they'll be ashamed.
A sound of uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! The sound of the LORD repaying requital to his enemies!
Before she was in labour she gave birth; before the pain came to her she'd delivered a male child.

Who has heard the like of this? Who has seen the like of these? Can a land be brought forth in one day? Or can a nation be born in a single moment? For Zion was in labour and also gave birth to her children.
Shall I bring to the birth and not deliver? says the LORD. Or am I the one who delivers, and shall I close the womb? says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad in her, all who love her! Rejoice with her a rejoicing, all who mourn over her!
so that you may suck and be satisfied from the breast of her consolations, so that you may drain and take delight from the breast of her glory.
For thus says the LORD: See, I'm extending peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like an overflowing torrent; and you'll suck, be carried on the hip and be dandled on the knees.
Like someone whose mother comforts him, that's how I'll comfort you; and in Jerusalem you'll be comforted.
And you'll see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will sprout like grass; and the hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, and his indignation against his enemies.
For see, the LORD will come in fire, and his chariots like the storm-wind, to render his anger in rage and his rebuke in flames of fire.
For by fire the LORD will enter into judgement, and by his sword, with all flesh; and those slain by the LORD will be many.

Those who consecrate themselves and cleanse themselves for the gardens, following one in the middle, eating the flesh of the pig and the detestable thing and the mouse — they will come to an end together, declares the LORD.
And I know their deeds and their thoughts; the time's coming to gather all the nations and tongues; and they'll come and see my glory.

And I'll perform a sign among them and send survivors from them to the nations — Tarshish, Pul and Lud, who draw the bow, Tubal and Javan, the distant coastlands that haven't heard my report and haven't seen my glory — and they'll declare my glory among the nations.

And they'll bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD — on horses and in chariots and in wagons and on mules and on camels — to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring the grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
And I'll also take some of them for the priests, for the Levites, says the LORD.
For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I'm making endure before me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will endure.
And it will be that from new moon to new moon and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh will come to bow down before me, says the LORD.
And they'll go out and look on the corpses of the people who transgressed against me; for their worm won't die and their fire won't be extinguished, and they'll be an abhorrence to all flesh.

judges_1.t: After Joshua died, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Which of us goes up against the Canaanites first, to fight them?"
The LORD said, "Judah goes up. Look — I've given the land into his hand."
Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into my share of the land and let's fight the Canaanites, and I'll go with you into yours." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD handed the Canaanites and Perizzites over to them, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought him, and struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek ran, but they chased him down and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. What I did, God has done back to me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
Judah fought against Jerusalem and took it. They struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
After that, Judah went down to fight the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Negev and the Shephelah.
Judah went against the Canaanites living in Hebron — Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba — and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.
From there he went against the people of Debir — Debir used to be called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and takes it — I'll give him my daughter Achsah as a wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
When she came to him, she pressed him to ask her father for a field. Then she got down off her donkey, and Caleb said, "What is it?"
She said, "Give me a blessing. You've given me land in the Negev — give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The Kenites, the descendants of Moses' father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the men of Judah into the wilderness of Judah in the Negev of Arad, and settled there among the people.
Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they struck the Canaanites living in Zephath and devoted it to destruction, and they named the city Hormah.
Judah captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and he took the hill country; but he could not drive out the people of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
They gave Hebron to Caleb, just as Moses had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
The Benjaminites did not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem, and the Jebusites have lived alongside them in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph went up too, against Beth-el, and the LORD was with them.
The house of Joseph sent men to scout Beth-el — the city used to be called Luz.
The scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us the way in, and we'll deal loyally with you."
He showed them the way in, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man and his whole family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city and called it Luz, and that is its name to this day.
Manasseh did not drive out Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the people of Dor, Ibleam and Megiddo and their villages; the Canaanites were set on staying in that land.
When Israel grew strong, it put the Canaanites to forced labour — but it never did drive them out.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, and the Canaanites went on living among them there.
Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or Nahalol, and the Canaanites lived among them and became forced labour.
Asher did not drive out the people of Acco or Sidon, or Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik or Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land, because they had not driven them out.

Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath, and lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land; but the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labour for them.
The Amorites pushed the Danites back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the valley.
The Amorites were set on staying in Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim; but the hand of the house of Joseph pressed hard on them, and they became forced labour.
The Amorite border ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela on up.

judges_2.t: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you up out of Egypt and into the land I swore to your ancestors, and I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you.
"'And you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land; you are to pull down their altars.' But you have not listened to me. What is this you have done?"
"So now I say this: I will not drive them out ahead of you. They will be there at your side, and their gods will be a snare to you."
When the angel of the LORD had said all this to the Israelites, the people lifted up their voice and wept.
So they named that place Bokim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
When Joshua dismissed the people, the Israelites went, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
The people served the LORD as long as Joshua lived, and as long as the elders who outlived him lived — those who had seen the whole great work the LORD had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at a hundred and ten.
They buried him in his own territory, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
That whole generation was gathered to their ancestors, and another generation grew up after them who did not know the LORD or the work he had done for Israel.
The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they served the Baals.

They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of Egypt. They went after other gods — the gods of the peoples around them — and bowed down to them, and they provoked the LORD to anger.
They abandoned the LORD and served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.

The anger of the LORD burned against Israel. He gave them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them, and sold them into the hand of the enemies all around them, and they could no longer stand against their enemies.
Wherever they marched out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, exactly as the LORD had said and sworn to them, and they were in terrible distress.
Then the LORD raised up judges, and they delivered them from the hand of those plundering them.

But they would not listen to their judges either. They prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way their ancestors had walked, obeying the LORD's commandments; they did not do as they had.

Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and delivered them from their enemies as long as that judge lived, because their groaning under those who oppressed and crushed them moved him to compassion.

But when the judge died, they would go back and behave worse than their ancestors — going after other gods, serving them, bowing down to them. They gave up none of their practices, none of their stubbornness.
So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has broken my covenant, which I commanded their ancestors, and has not listened to me,
"then I too will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died."
This was to test Israel by them: would they keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did, or not?
So the LORD left these nations where they were, not driving them out quickly; he had not given them into Joshua's hand.

judges_3.t: These are the nations the LORD left in order to test Israel by them — all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan;
only so that the generations of Israelites might learn war — to teach those who had not known it before.
the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains, from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
They were there to test Israel — to find out whether they would obey the commandments the LORD had given their ancestors through Moses.
The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
They married their daughters, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him for eight years.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them who delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war. The LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over him.
And the land had rest for forty years; then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
He gathered the Ammonites and Amalek to himself, went and struck Israel, and they took the city of palms.
The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.

Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a man impeded in his right hand. The Israelites sent tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a two-edged sword, a gomed long, and strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was a very fat man.
When he had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, king." The king said, "Quiet!" — and everyone standing by him left.
Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a word from God for you." And Eglon rose from his seat.
Ehud reached across with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into his belly.
The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because he did not pull the sword out of his belly; and the dung came out.
Then Ehud went out onto the porch, shut the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them.
After he had gone, the king's servants came and looked, and there were the doors of the upper room, locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool room."
They waited until they were embarrassed, and still he did not open the doors. So they took the key and opened them — and there was their lord, fallen to the ground, dead.
Ehud got away while they were delaying. He passed the images and escaped to Seirah.
When he arrived he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came down with him from the hill country, with him leading them.
He said, "Follow me — the LORD has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." So they went down after him, captured the fords of the Jordan toward Moab, and let no one cross.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites — every stout one, every able man — and not one escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath. He struck down six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, and he too delivered Israel.

judges_4.t: The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, now that Ehud was dead.
So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. His army commander was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, because he had nine hundred chariots of iron and had oppressed them harshly for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophetess, Lappidoth's wife, was judging Israel at that time.
She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah, between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came up to her for judgement.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali and said to him, "Hasn't the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you — go, march to Mount Tabor and take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you?"
"And I will draw Sisera, Jabin's army commander, with his chariots and his troops, to you at the wadi Kishon, and I will give him into your hand."
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I'll go. If you don't go with me, I won't go."

She said, "I will certainly go with you — but the honour on this road will not be yours, because the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." Then Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called up Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up behind him, and Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the rest of the Kenites — the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law — and had pitched his tent as far off as the great tree in Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called out all his chariots — nine hundred chariots of iron — and all his troops, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the wadi Kishon.

Deborah said to Barak, "Get up — this is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Hasn't the LORD gone out ahead of you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.
And the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak chased the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the edge of the sword. Not one was left.
Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said, "Turn aside, my lord, turn in to me. Don't be afraid." So he turned in to her, into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.
He said, "Please give me a little water — I'm thirsty." So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
He said, "Stand at the tent door, and if anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' — say no."
But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and picked up the hammer, came to him quietly, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground. He was fast asleep and exhausted, and he died.

Just then Barak came by, chasing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said, "Come — I'll show you the man you're looking for." He came in, and there was Sisera, fallen dead, the peg in his temple.
So that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
The hand of the Israelites bore down harder and harder on Jabin king of Canaan, until they cut off Jabin king of Canaan.

judges_5.t: That day Deborah sang, and Barak son of Abinoam with her:
When the leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people came forward freely — bless the LORD!
Hear, you kings! Listen, you rulers! I — to the LORD, I — I will sing; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the country of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens dripped, the clouds dripped water.
The mountains flowed down before the LORD — this Sinai — before the LORD, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the caravans stopped, and those who travelled the paths went by roundabout roads.
