The villagers ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I arose, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
New gods were chosen; then — war at the gates. Was a shield to be seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, who came forward freely among the people — bless the LORD!
You who ride tawny she-asses, you who sit on rich carpets, you who walk the road — tell it!

From the sound of those who parcel out the flocks among the watering places, there they tell of the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake — sing! Get up, Barak, and take your captives captive, son of Abinoam!
Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the LORD's people came down to me as warriors.
From Ephraim, their root in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; from Machir the commanders came down, and from Zebulun those who carry the muster-officer's staff.
My princes in Issachar were with Deborah; and as Issachar, so Barak — sent into the valley at his heels. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great resolves of heart.
Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, listening to the whistling for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan; and Dan — why did he linger by the ships? Asher stayed on the coast and settled by his landings.
Zebulun is a people that held its own life cheap, even to death — and Naphtali too, on the heights of the open country.
Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. They took no plunder of silver.
From heaven they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
The wadi Kishon swept them away — that ancient wadi, the wadi Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
Then the horses' hooves hammered from the galloping, the galloping of his stallions.
"Curse Meroz," says the angel of the LORD. "Curse her inhabitants bitterly, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD among the mighty."
Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; of women in the tent, most blessed.
He asked for water; she gave milk. In a lordly bowl she brought him curds.
She reached her hand to the tent peg, her right hand to the workmen's hammer; she struck Sisera, shattered his head, smashed and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell — destroyed.
Through the window she looked out and wailed, Sisera's mother, through the lattice: "Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots delay?"
Her wisest ladies answer her — and indeed she says the same sayings back to herself:

"Aren't they finding and dividing the spoil? — a womb, two wombs for each man; spoil of dyed cloths for Sisera, spoil of dyed cloths, embroidered, a dyed cloth, two embroidered ones, for the necks of the spoil."
So may all your enemies perish, LORD; and may those who love him be like the sun rising in its strength. And the land had rest for forty years.

judges_6.t: The Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed over Israel, and because of Midian the Israelites made themselves the dens in the mountains, and the caves and the strongholds.
Whenever Israel sowed, Midian would come up — Amalek and the people of the east with them — and come up against them.
They would camp against them and destroy the produce of the land as far as Gaza, leaving no food in Israel, and no sheep, ox or donkey.
They and their livestock and their tents would come up, coming in like locusts for sheer number — they and their camels beyond counting — and they came into the land to destroy it.
So Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,
the LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of a house of slaves.
"I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you. I drove them out ahead of you and gave you their land.
"And I said to you, 'I am the LORD your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you are living.' But you have not listened to me."
The angel of the LORD came and sat under the oak at Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from Midian.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said, "The LORD is with you, mighty man of valour."

Gideon said, "Pardon me, my lord — but if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about, saying, 'Didn't the LORD bring us up out of Egypt?' Now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the grip of Midian."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you will deliver Israel from the grip of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
He said, "Pardon me, my Lord — with what am I to deliver Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The LORD said to him, "I will be with you, and you will strike down Midian as if they were one man."
He said, "If I have found favour in your eyes, give me a sign that it's really you speaking with me.
"Please don't leave until I come back and bring out my gift and set it before you." And he said, "I'll stay until you return."
Gideon went and prepared a young goat, and an ephah of flour as unleavened bread. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brought them out to him under the oak, and set them before him.
The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, set them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

The angel of the LORD reached out the end of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread, and fire went up from the rock and consumed them. And the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
Then Gideon realised it was the angel of the LORD, and he said, "Alas, Lord GOD — I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!"
But the LORD said to him, "Peace to you. Don't be afraid; you will not die."
So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it 'The LORD is peace'. It is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.
That night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull — the second bull, seven years old — tear down the altar of the Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah beside it.
"Then build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold, laid out in order, and take the second bull and offer it up as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah you cut down."
So Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But he was too afraid of his father's household and the men of the city to do it by day, so he did it at night.
When the men of the city got up in the morning, there was the altar of the Baal torn down, the Asherah beside it cut down, and the second bull offered up on the altar that had been built.
They said to one another, "Who did this?" And when they investigated and searched, they said, "Gideon son of Joash did this."
The men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son so he can die — he has torn down the altar of the Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it."

But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Are you going to contend for the Baal? Are you going to deliver him? Whoever contends for him will be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself — someone has torn down his altar."
So that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, "Let the Baal contend against him — he has torn down his altar."
Now all Midian and Amalek and the people of the east gathered together, crossed over, and camped in the valley of Jezreel.
And the spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon. He blew the ram's horn, and Abiezer was called out to follow him.
He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too were called out to follow him; and he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
Then Gideon said to God, "If you are going to deliver Israel by my hand, as you said —
"look, I'm putting the fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there's dew on the fleece alone and the ground is all dry, then I'll know you will deliver Israel by my hand, as you said."
And it was so. He got up early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and wrung dew out of it — a bowlful of water.

Then Gideon said to God, "Don't let your anger burn against me; let me speak just this once. Let me test just once more with the fleece — let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground."
And God did so that night: the fleece alone was dry, and there was dew all over the ground.

judges_7.t: Jerubbaal — that is, Gideon — got up early with all the people who were with him and camped at En-harod. The camp of Midian was north of him, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
The LORD said to Gideon, "There are too many people with you for me to give Midian into their hand. Israel might glorify itself over me and say, 'My own hand delivered me.'
"Now announce to the people: anyone who is afraid and trembling should turn back and leave Mount Gilead." Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

The LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many. Bring them down to the water and I will refine them for you there. Whoever I tell you is to go with you will go with you; and anyone I tell you is not to go with you will not go."

So he brought the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Set apart by himself everyone who laps the water with his tongue, the way a dog laps — and everyone who kneels down to drink."
The number of those who lapped, hand to mouth, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
The LORD said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will deliver you, and I will give Midian into your hand. Let all the rest go, each to his own place."
So they took the people's provisions and their ram's horns; and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tents, keeping only the three hundred. The camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
That night the LORD said to him, "Get up, go down into the camp — I have given it into your hand.
"But if you are afraid to go down, go down with Purah your servant to the camp,
"and you will hear what they say; after that your hands will be strengthened and you can go down into the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the edge of the armed men in the camp.
Midian and Amalek and all the people of the east lay in the valley like locusts for sheer number; their camels were beyond counting, like the sand on the seashore.

Gideon arrived just as a man was telling a dream to his neighbour. He said, "I've had a dream: a round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian, hit the tent so that it fell, turned it upside down, and the tent collapsed."
His neighbour answered, "That is nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
When Gideon heard the dream told and interpreted, he bowed down. Then he went back to the camp of Israel and said, "Get up — the LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put a ram's horn into every man's hand, and empty jars with torches inside them.
He said to them, "Watch me and do the same. When I get to the edge of the camp, do exactly what I do.
"When I blow the ram's horn, I and everyone with me, you blow yours too, all around the camp, and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

Gideon came to the edge of the camp with the hundred men who were with him at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the watch had been posted. They blew the ram's horns and smashed the jars in their hands.

The three companies blew the ram's horns and broke the jars. They held the torches in their left hand and the ram's horns in their right to blow, and they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
They stood, each in his place, all around the camp; and the whole camp ran, crying out, and fled.

The three hundred blew the ram's horns, and the LORD turned every man's sword against his neighbour throughout the camp. The camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
The men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim: "Come down to meet Midian and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." So every man of Ephraim was called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

They captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb; then they pursued Midian and brought the head of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from across the Jordan.

judges_8.t: The men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this you have done to us — not calling us when you went to fight Midian?" And they quarrelled with him bitterly.
He said to them, "What have I done compared with you? Isn't Ephraim's gleaning better than Abiezer's whole vintage?
"God gave the commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into your hand. What have I been able to do compared with you?" At that their anger toward him relaxed.
Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over with the three hundred men who were with him — exhausted, and still pursuing.
He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people following me — they're exhausted, and I'm pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
But the officials of Succoth said, "Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your grasp, that we should give bread to your army?"
Gideon said, "Very well — when the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers."
He went up from there to Penuel and said the same to them, and the men of Penuel answered just as the men of Succoth had.
So he said to the men of Penuel too, "When I come back in peace, I will tear down this tower."

Now Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with their armies, about fifteen thousand — all that remained of the whole army of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand sword-bearing men had fallen.
Gideon went up by the route of the tent-dwellers, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the camp while it was off its guard.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and routed the whole army.
Gideon son of Joash came back from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
He captured a young man from Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the names of Succoth's officials and elders — seventy-seven men.

Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna — the ones you taunted me about: 'Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your grasp, that we should give bread to your weary men?'"
So he took the elders of the city and the thorns of the wilderness and the briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.
He tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "They were like you — each one like a king's son to look at."
He said, "They were my brothers, my own mother's sons. As the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not be killing you."
Then he said to Jether his firstborn, "Get up and kill them." But the boy did not draw his sword. He was afraid, because he was still only a boy.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Do it yourself — as the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescents from their camels' necks.
Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us — you, your son, and your son's son — because you delivered us from the hand of Midian."
But Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
Then Gideon said to them, "Let me ask one thing of you: each of you give me the earring from his plunder." (They had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
They said, "We'll gladly give them." So they spread out a garment, and each man threw in the earring from his plunder.

The weight of the gold earrings he asked for was seventeen hundred in gold, apart from the crescents, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and the necklaces on their camels' necks.
Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, Ophrah; and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
So Midian was subdued before the Israelites and never lifted its head again, and the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons of his own fathering, for he had many wives.
His concubine in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and made Baal-berith their god.
The Israelites did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies all around.
And they did not deal loyally with the house of Jerubbaal — Gideon — in return for all the good he had done for Israel.

judges_9.t: Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and spoke to them and to all his mother's father's clan:
"Ask all the lords of Shechem: 'Which is better for you — that seventy men, all Jerubbaal's sons, rule over you, or that one man rule over you?' And remember, I am your own bone and flesh."
His mother's brothers repeated all this about him to all the lords of Shechem, and their heart turned to Abimelech, because they said, "He is our brother."
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith, and with it Abimelech hired worthless, reckless men, and they followed him.
He came to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal — seventy men, on one stone. Only Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, because he had hidden.
Then all the lords of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered and went and made Abimelech king, by the great tree of the pillar at Shechem.
When Jotham was told, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim, lifted up his voice and called out: "Listen to me, lords of Shechem, and may God listen to you."
"Once the trees went out to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
"But the olive tree said, 'Shall I give up my fatness, by which gods and men are honoured, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'You come and reign over us.'
"But the fig tree said, 'Shall I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then the trees said to the vine, 'You come and reign over us.'
"But the vine said, 'Shall I give up my new wine, which gladdens gods and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
"Then all the trees said to the bramble, 'You come and reign over us.'
"And the bramble said to the trees, 'If you are truly anointing me king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'
"Now then — if you acted in faithfulness and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and treated him as his own hands deserved —
"— for my father fought for you and threw his own life away out in front, and delivered you from the hand of Midian;

"and today you have risen up against my father's house and killed his sons — seventy men, on one stone — and made Abimelech, the son of his female slave, king over the lords of Shechem, because he is your brother —
"— if you have acted in faithfulness and integrity toward Jerubbaal and his house today, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him rejoice in you too.
"But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire come out from the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech."
Then Jotham fled and ran away and went to Beer, and he stayed there because of Abimelech his brother.
Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with him,

so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come home, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
The lords of Shechem set ambushes against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by on the road; and Abimelech was told of it.
Then Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers, and they moved into Shechem, and the lords of Shechem put their trust in him.
They went out into the fields, gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them, and held a festival. Then they went into the house of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn't he Jerubbaal's son, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?"
"If only this people were under my hand — I would get rid of Abimelech!" And he said of Abimelech, "Build up your army and come out!"
When Zebul, the official of the city, heard what Gaal son of Ebed said, his anger burned.
He sent messengers to Abimelech secretly: "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are turning the city against you.
"So get up in the night, you and the people with you, and lie in wait in the field.
"In the morning, when the sun rises, get up early and raid the city; and when he and his people come out against you, do to him whatever your hand finds to do."
So Abimelech and all his people got up in the night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate, and Abimelech and his people rose from the ambush.
When Gaal saw them he said to Zebul, "Look — people are coming down from the mountaintops." But Zebul said, "That's the shadow of the mountains you're seeing, that looks like men."
Gaal spoke again: "Look — people coming down from the navel of the land, and one company from the direction of the Soothsayers' Tree."
Then Zebul said to him, "Where's your big mouth now — you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Isn't this the people you despised? Go out now and fight him."
So Gaal went out at the head of the lords of Shechem and fought Abimelech.
Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many fell fatally wounded right up to the entrance of the gate.
Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out so they could not stay in Shechem.
The next day the people went out into the fields, and Abimelech was told.
So he took his people, divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field; and when he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose against them and struck them down.
Abimelech and the companies with him raided forward and took position at the entrance of the city gate, while the other two companies raided everyone in the field and struck them down.
Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured it, killed the people in it, pulled the city down and sowed it with salt.
When all the lords of the tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.
Abimelech was told that all the lords of the tower of Shechem had gathered together.

So Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon with all the people who were with him. He took an axe, cut a branch from the trees, lifted it onto his shoulder, and said to his people, "What you have seen me do — hurry, do the same."

So all the people cut branches too, each his own, followed Abimelech, piled them against the stronghold and set it on fire over them; and all the people of the tower of Shechem died too — about a thousand men and women.
Then Abimelech went to Thebez, camped against it, and captured it.
But there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and women and all the lords of the city fled there. They shut the door behind them and went up onto the roof.
Abimelech came up to the tower and fought against it, and drew near the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
But one woman threw an upper millstone down on Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.
He called quickly to his armour-bearer and said, "Draw your sword and kill me, so they won't say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man ran him through, and he died.
When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they went home, each to his own place.
So God repaid the evil Abimelech had done to his father, in killing his seventy brothers;
and all the evil of the men of Shechem God repaid on their heads; and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

judges_10.t: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to deliver Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years; then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns; they are called Havvoth-jair to this day, in the land of Gilead.
Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram, of Sidon, of Moab, of the Ammonites and of the Philistines. They forsook the LORD and did not serve him.
The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites.
They shattered and crushed the Israelites that year — for eighteen years — all the Israelites beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, in Gilead.
The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in terrible distress.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD: "We have sinned against you — we have forsaken our God and served the Baals."
The LORD said to the Israelites, "Was it not from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the Ammonites, from the Philistines,
"and when the Sidonians, Amalek and Maon oppressed you, and you cried out to me — did I not deliver you from their hand?
"But you have forsaken me and served other gods. So I will not deliver you again.
"Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them deliver you in the time of your distress."
The Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good to you — only deliver us today."
So they got rid of the foreign gods among them and served the LORD; and he could no longer bear Israel's trouble.
The Ammonites were called out and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites gathered and camped at Mizpah.
And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, "Who is the man who will start the fight against the Ammonites? He will be chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

judges_11.t: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour. He was the son of a prostitute, and Gilead fathered Jephthah.
Gilead's wife bore him sons, and when her sons grew up they drove Jephthah out and told him, "You will not inherit in our father's house — you are another woman's son."
So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, and worthless men gathered around him and went out with him.
Some time later the Ammonites went to war against Israel.
When the Ammonites went to war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah from the land of Tob.
They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, and let's fight the Ammonites."
But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Wasn't it you who hated me and drove me out of my father's house? Why come to me now, when you're in distress?"
The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That is exactly why we have come back to you now: come with us and fight the Ammonites, and you will be our chief over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over to me, then I will be your chief."
The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The LORD is the one who hears between us — if we do not do exactly as you say."
So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their chief and commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites: "What is there between you and me, that you have come to fight in my land?"
The king of the Ammonites said to Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt — from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now give it back peaceably."
Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites,
and said to him, "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
"When they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

"Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom: 'Please let us pass through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. It sent to the king of Moab too, and he was not willing; so Israel stayed at Kadesh.

"Then it went through the wilderness, around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east of Moab. They camped beyond the Arnon and did not enter Moab's territory, because the Arnon was Moab's border.
"Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon: 'Please let us pass through your land to our place.'
"But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz and fought against Israel.
"And the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into Israel's hand, and they struck them down; and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived in that land.
"They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
"So now the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites before his people Israel — and you would take possession of it?
"Isn't it so: whatever Chemosh your god gives you to possess, you possess; and whatever the LORD our God has dispossessed before us, we possess."
"And now — are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel? Did he ever go to war with them?
"Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for three hundred years. Why didn't you recover them in all that time?
"I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by making war on me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge today between the Israelites and the Ammonites."
But the king of the Ammonites did not listen to the message Jephthah sent him.
Then the spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead went on against the Ammonites.
And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: "If you will indeed give the Ammonites into my hand,
"then whatever comes out — whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Ammonites — will be the LORD's, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering."
So Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
He struck them from Aroer as far as Minnith — twenty cities — and as far as Abel-keramim, a very great defeat; and the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
Then Jephthah came home to Mizpah — and there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was an only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.

When he saw her he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low; you are among those who bring me trouble. I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I cannot take it back."
She said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me what has come out of your mouth, now that the LORD has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, the Ammonites."
And she said to her father, "Let this be done for me: leave me alone for two months, and let me go down on the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
He said, "Go." He sent her away for two months, and she went with her companions and wept over her virginity on the mountains.
At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he did to her according to the vow he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became a custom in Israel,
that year after year the daughters of Israel go to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in the year.

judges_12.t: The men of Ephraim were called out and crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house down over you!"
Jephthah said to them, "I was in a bitter quarrel, I and my people, with the Ammonites. I summoned you, and you did not deliver me from their hand.

"When I saw that you would not deliver me, I took my life in my hands and crossed over against the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into my hand. So why have you come up against me today to fight me?"

So Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim down, because they had said, "You Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim, living in the middle of Ephraim and Manasseh."

Gilead captured the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim; and whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would ask him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" and he would say, "No."

they would say, "Say shibboleth" — and he would say "sibboleth," because he could not get it right; and they would seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell at that time.
Jephthah judged Israel six years; then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
He had thirty sons; he sent thirty daughters away to marry outside and brought in thirty daughters from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.
Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
After him Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys, and he judged Israel eight years.
Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

judges_13.t: The Israelites again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
There was a man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren and had borne no children.
The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and have borne no children — but you will conceive and bear a son.
"So take care: don't drink wine or strong drink, and don't eat anything unclean.
"You will conceive and bear a son, and no razor is to touch his head, because the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb. And he will begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
The woman came and told her husband, "A man of God came to me, and he looked like the angel of God — very fearsome. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

"And he said to me, 'You will conceive and bear a son. Now don't drink wine or strong drink, and don't eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day he dies.'"
Then Manoah prayed to the LORD: "Pardon me, my Lord — let the man of God you sent come to us again, and teach us what we are to do for the boy who is to be born."
God listened to Manoah's voice, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field — and Manoah her husband was not with her.
The woman hurried and ran and told her husband, "The man has appeared to me — the one who came to me the other day."
Manoah got up and followed his wife. He came to the man and said, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."
Manoah said, "When your words come true, what is the rule for the boy, and what is he to do?"
The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Let her be careful about everything I told the woman.
"She is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, she is not to drink wine or strong drink, and she is not to eat anything unclean. Everything I commanded her she is to keep."
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Let us keep you here, and prepare a young goat for you."

The angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "If you keep me here, I will not eat your food; and if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.
Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that when your word comes true we can honour you?"
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding."
So Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them up on the rock to the LORD; and he did an extraordinary thing while Manoah and his wife looked on.
When the flame went up from the altar toward the heavens, the angel of the LORD went up in the flame of the altar, while Manoah and his wife looked on; and they fell face down on the ground.
The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah or to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.
And Manoah said to his wife, "We are going to die — we have seen God."
But his wife said to him, "If the LORD had wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, or shown us all this, or let us hear such things now."
The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
And the spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

judges_14.t: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman there, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
He went up and told his father and mother, "I've seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. Now get her for me as a wife."

But his father and mother said, "Is there no woman among your own kin, or among all my people, that you have to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson said to his father, "Get her for me — she is right in my eyes."
His father and mother did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. They came as far as the vineyards of Timnah — and there was a young lion, roaring at him.
And the spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and he tore the lion apart as one tears apart a young goat — with nothing in his hand. And he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
Then he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
After some days he came back to take her, and turned aside to look at the lion's carcass — and there was a swarm of bees in the lion's body, and honey.

He scraped it out into his hands and went on eating as he walked; and he came to his father and mother and gave them some, and they ate. But he did not tell them he had scraped the honey out of the lion's body.
His father went down to the woman, and Samson held a feast there, because that was what young men did.
When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.
Samson said to them, "Let me put a riddle to you. If you can tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast and work it out, I'll give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.
"But if you can't tell me, then you give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." And they said, "Ask your riddle; let's hear it."
And he said to them: "Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet." For three days they could not tell the riddle.
On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into telling us the riddle, or we'll burn you and your father's house down. Did you invite us here to strip us bare?"

Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me — you don't love me. You've put a riddle to my own people and you haven't told me the answer." He said, "I haven't told my own father or mother. Why should I tell you?"
She wept over him for the seven days their feast lasted; and on the seventh day he told her, because she kept pressing him. And she told the riddle to her own people.

And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before sunset: "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them: "If you hadn't ploughed with my heifer, you wouldn't have found out my riddle."

And the spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and he went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty men there, took what they had, and gave the changes of clothes to those who had told the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
And Samson's wife was given to his companion, the one who had been his best man.

judges_15.t: After some days, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson went to visit his wife, bringing a young goat, and said, "Let me go in to my wife, into her room." But her father would not let him in.
Her father said, "I was sure you had come to hate her, so I gave her to your companion. Isn't her younger sister better than she is? Take her instead."
Samson said to them, "This time I'll be in the clear with the Philistines when I do them harm."
So Samson went and caught three hundred foxes. He took torches, turned the foxes tail to tail, and put a torch between each pair of tails.
He set fire to the torches and let them loose in the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the stacked sheaves, the standing grain and the olive groves.

The Philistines said, "Who did this?" And they said, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite — because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
Samson said to them, "If this is how you act, I will take my revenge on you — and after that I will stop."
And he struck them down, leg and thigh, a great slaughter; then he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out at Lehi.
The men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" They said, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he did to us."

Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Don't you know the Philistines are ruling over us? What is this you have done to us?" He said, "As they did to me, so I have done to them."
They said, "We've come down to bind you and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said, "Swear to me that you won't fall on me yourselves."
They said, "No — we will only bind you and hand you over; we certainly won't kill you." So they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

As he came to Lehi, the Philistines came shouting to meet him; and the spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and the ropes on his arms became like flax burned with fire, and his bonds dropped off his hands.
He found a fresh donkey's jawbone, reached out and took it, and with it struck down a thousand men.
And Samson said: "With the jawbone of the donkey, a heap, two heaps — with the jawbone of the donkey I struck down a thousand men."
When he had finished speaking he threw the jawbone away, and he called that place Ramath-lehi.

He was very thirsty, and he called out to the LORD: "You yourself have given this great victory by the hand of your servant. And now am I to die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"
So God split open the hollow at Lehi, and water came out of it and he drank. His spirit returned and he revived. That is why he called it En-hakkore, which is at Lehi to this day.
And he judged Israel twenty years, in the days of the Philistines.

judges_16.t: Samson went to Gaza, saw a prostitute there, and went in to her.
Word reached the Gazites: "Samson has come here." So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They kept quiet all night, saying, "At first light we'll kill him."

But Samson lay down only until midnight. At midnight he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two doorposts, pulled them up bar and all, put them on his shoulders and carried them to the top of the mountain facing Hebron.
After this he fell in love with a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

The lords of the Philistines went up to her and said, "Coax him, and find out where his great strength lies and how we can overpower him, so we can bind him and bring him low. Each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."
So Delilah said to Samson, "Tell me where your great strength lies, and what you could be tied up with, to bring you low."
Samson said to her, "If they tie me with seven fresh cords that haven't been dried, I'll become weak and be like anyone else."
So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh cords that had not been dried, and she tied him with them.

Now the ambusher was waiting in the inner room for her. She said to him, "The Philistines are on you, Samson!" But he snapped the cords like a thread of tow when it touches fire; and the secret of his strength was not found out.
Then Delilah said to Samson, "You've deceived me and told me lies. Now tell me what you could be tied up with."
He said, "If they tie me with new ropes that have never been used, I'll become weak and be like anyone else."
So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them and said, "The Philistines are on you, Samson!" — and the ambusher was waiting in the inner room. But he tore them off his arms like a thread.
Then Delilah said to Samson, "Up to now you've deceived me and told me lies. Tell me what you could be tied up with." And he said, "If you weave the seven plaits of my head into the web."
And she drove in the pin and said, "The Philistines are on you, Samson!" But he woke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom, and the web with it.
She said to him, "How can you say 'I love you' when your heart isn't with me? Three times now you've deceived me, and you still haven't told me where your great strength lies."
And because she pressed him with her words day after day and kept urging him, he was worn out to the point of death.

So he told her everything in his heart: "No razor has come on my head, because I have been a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I'd become weak and be like anyone else."

When Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart, she sent for the lords of the Philistines: "Come up this time — he has told me everything." So the lords of the Philistines came up to her, bringing the silver with them.
She made him sleep on her knees, summoned the man, and shaved off the seven plaits of his head. Then she began to bring him low, and his strength left him.
And she said, "The Philistines are on you, Samson!" He woke from his sleep and said, "I'll go out as I did before and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza, bound him with bronze fetters, and he ground grain in the prison house.
But the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
Now the lords of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to celebrate, and they said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
And when the people saw him they praised their god, saying, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy — the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain."

And when their heart was merry, they said, "Bring Samson out, and let him make sport for us." So they brought Samson from the prison house, and he made sport before them; and they set him between the pillars.
And Samson said to the young man holding his hand, "Let go of me and let me feel the pillars the house rests on, so I can lean on them."
Now the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson make sport.
Then Samson called out to the LORD: "Lord GOD, remember me and strengthen me, only this once, O God, so that I may take one act of vengeance on the Philistines for my two eyes."
Then Samson took hold of the two middle pillars the house rested on and braced himself against them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

And Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." Then he pushed with all his strength, and the house fell on the lords and on all the people in it. And the dead he killed in his death were more than those he had killed in his life.
Then his brothers and all his father's household went down and carried him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. He had judged Israel twenty years.

judges_17.t: There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micayehu.

He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you — the ones you cursed over, and said so in my hearing — the silver is with me. I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the LORD."

So he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, and she said, "I do consecrate the silver to the LORD from my own hand, for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. Now I'll give it back to you."

So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to the silversmith, who made it into a carved image and a cast image; and it stood in the house of Micayehu.
Now the man Micah had a house of God. He made an ephod and teraphim, ordained one of his sons, and the son became his priest.
In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
Now there was a young man from Bethlehem of Judah, of the clan of Judah. He was a Levite, and he was living there as a sojourner.
The man left the city of Bethlehem in Judah to settle wherever he could find a place, and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he went on his way.
Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I'm going to settle wherever I can find a place."
Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I'll give you ten pieces of silver a year, an outfit of clothes and your keep." So the Levite went in.
The Levite was willing to stay with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in Micah's house.
Then Micah said, "Now I know the LORD will do good to me, because the Levite has become my priest."

judges_18.t: In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was looking for an inheritance to settle in, because until then nothing had fallen to them as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

So the Danites sent five men from their whole number — men of valour, from Zorah and Eshtaol — to spy out the land and explore it, saying, "Go, explore the land." They came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.

While they were near the house of Micah they recognised the voice of the young man, the Levite. So they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What have you got here?"
He said to them, "Micah has done such and such for me. He hired me, and I became his priest."
And they said to him, "Enquire of God for us, so we may know whether the journey we're on will succeed."
And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. The way you are going is before the LORD."

So the five men went on and came to Laish, and saw the people there living in security, after the manner of the Sidonians — quiet and secure. No ruler in the land put anyone to shame in anything; they were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
They came back to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said, "Well?"
And they said, "Get up — let's go up against them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. And here you are, doing nothing! Don't hesitate to go in and take possession of the land.
"When you go you will come to a people who are secure, and the land is broad on every side, for God has given it into your hand — a place where nothing on earth is lacking."
So six hundred men of the clan of the Danites, armed with weapons of war, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why that place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it lies west of Kiriath-jearim.
From there they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod, teraphim, a carved image and a cast image? Now think what you will do."
So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite — the house of Micah — and greeted him.
Meanwhile the six hundred Danites, armed with their weapons of war, stood at the entrance of the gate.

And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, went in, and took the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim and the cast image — while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred armed men.
These men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim and the cast image; and the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

And they said, "Be quiet. Put your hand over your mouth and come with us, and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be priest to one man's household, or priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
The priest's heart was glad. He took the ephod, the teraphim and the carved image and went along in the midst of the people.
So they turned and went on, putting the little ones, the livestock and the goods ahead of them.
When they had gone some distance from the house of Micah, the men in the houses near his were called out, and they caught up with the Danites.
They called out to the Danites, who turned round and said to Micah, "What's the matter with you, that you've been called out?"
And he said, "You have taken my gods that I made, and the priest, and off you go. What is left to me? How can you say to me, 'What's the matter with you?'"
And the Danites said to him, "Don't let us hear your voice, or bitter-tempered men will fall on you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."
So the Danites went on their way; and when Micah saw they were too strong for him, he turned and went back home.
And they took what Micah had made and the priest who was his, and came upon Laish — a people quiet and secure — struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.
And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone; it lay in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and lived in it.
They named the city Dan, after Dan their ancestor, who was born to Israel; but the city's name was formerly Laish.
And the Danites set up the carved image for themselves; and Jonathan son of Gershom son of Manasseh, he and his sons, were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day the land went into exile.
So they set up for themselves the carved image Micah had made, all the days that the house of God was at Shiloh.

judges_19.t: In those days, when there was no king in Israel, there was a Levite sojourning in the remotest parts of the hill country of Ephraim, and he took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem of Judah.
And his concubine prostituted herself against him and left him for her father's house at Bethlehem of Judah, and she was there some days — four months.

Then her husband got up and went after her, to speak to her heart and bring her back, with his servant and a pair of donkeys. She brought him into her father's house, and the young woman's father saw him and was glad to meet him.
His father-in-law, the young woman's father, kept hold of him, and he stayed with him three days. They ate and drank and spent the night there.
On the fourth day they got up early, and he rose to go; and the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Have a morsel of bread to sustain your heart, and then you can go."
So the two of them sat and ate and drank together, and the young woman's father said to the man, "Please, stay the night and let your heart be glad."
The man got up to go, but his father-in-law pressed him, and he turned back and spent the night there.
He got up early on the fifth day to go, and the young woman's father said, "Please have something to sustain your heart, and wait until the day is far gone." And the two of them ate.

The man got up to go, he and his concubine and his servant; and his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said, "Look, the day is sinking toward evening. Please stay the night. Look, the day is nearly done. Stay here and let your heart be glad, and tomorrow you can start early on your journey and go home."
But the man was not willing to stay the night. He got up and set out and came opposite Jebus — that is, Jerusalem — with a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine with him.
When they were near Jebus and the day was nearly gone, the servant said to his master, "Come, let's turn aside to this Jebusite city and spend the night there."
But his master said, "We will not turn aside to a foreign city that is not Israelite. We'll go on as far as Gibeah."
And he said to his servant, "Come on, let's get to one of these places and spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah."
So they went on, and the sun set on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
They turned aside there to spend the night in Gibeah. He went in and sat down in the open square of the city, and no one took them into a house for the night.
Then an old man came in from his work in the field in the evening. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was sojourning in Gibeah, and the men of the place were Benjaminites.
He looked up and saw the traveller in the open square of the city, and the old man said, "Where are you going? Where do you come from?"

And he said, "We are passing from Bethlehem of Judah to the remotest parts of the hill country of Ephraim. I'm from there. I went to Bethlehem of Judah, and I'm going to the house of the LORD. And no one takes me into a house.
"We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me, for your maidservant and for the young man with your servants. We lack nothing."
And the old man said, "Peace to you. Whatever you need is on me — only do not spend the night in the open square."
So he brought him into his house and fed the donkeys, and they washed their feet, ate and drank.

While they were making their hearts glad, the men of the city — worthless men — surrounded the house, beating violently on the door, and said to the man, the master of the house, the old man, "Bring out the man who came into your house, so we may know him."
The master of the house went out to them and said, "No, my brothers, do not do this evil. Since this man has come into my house, do not do this outrage."
"Here are my daughter, a virgin, and his concubine. Let me bring them out. Afflict them, do to them whatever is good in your eyes — but to this man do not do this outrageous thing."
But the men would not listen to him. So the man took hold of his concubine and put her outside to them; and they knew her and abused her all night until morning, and let her go as the dawn came up.
And the woman came at daybreak and fell at the entrance of the house where her master was, and lay there until it was light.

Her master got up in the morning, opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way — and there was the woman, his concubine, fallen at the entrance of the house, her hands on the threshold.
And he said to her, "Get up, let's go." But there was no answer. So he put her on the donkey, and the man got up and went to his place.
And he came to his house, took the knife, took hold of his concubine and cut her in pieces, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.
And everyone who saw it said, "Nothing like this has happened or been seen from the day the Israelites came up out of Egypt to this day. Consider it, take counsel, and speak."

judges_20.t: Then all the Israelites went out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan to Beer-sheba and the land of Gilead, to the LORD at Mizpah.
And the chiefs of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God — four hundred thousand men on foot, drawing the sword.
The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. And the Israelites said, "Tell us — how did this evil happen?"
And the man, the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered, "I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.
"And the lords of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house by night. They meant to kill me; and they abused my concubine, and she died.
"So I took hold of my concubine, cut her in pieces and sent her through all the land of Israel's inheritance, because they had done depravity and outrage in Israel.
"Here you all are, Israelites. Give your word and counsel here."
And all the people rose as one man: "Not one of us will go to his tent, not one of us will turn aside to his house."
"Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: go up against it by lot.

"We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, a thousand out of every ten thousand, to fetch provisions for the people — so that when they come to Geba of Benjamin they may deal with it for all the outrage it has done in Israel."
So every man of Israel gathered against the city as one man, united.
And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the tribes of Benjamin: "What is this evil that has happened among you?

"Now hand over the men — the worthless men who are in Gibeah — so we may put them to death and burn evil out of Israel." But the Benjaminites would not listen to the voice of their brothers the Israelites.
And the Benjaminites gathered from their cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle against the Israelites.
The Benjaminites were mustered that day from the cities — twenty-six thousand men drawing the sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were mustered at seven hundred chosen men.
Out of all these people were seven hundred chosen men impeded in the right hand; every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
And the men of Israel were mustered, apart from Benjamin — four hundred thousand men drawing the sword, every one of them a man of war.
They rose and went up to Beth-el and enquired of God, and the Israelites said, "Who shall go up for us first to the battle against the Benjaminites?" And the LORD said, "Judah first."
The Israelites rose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.
The men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin and deployed for battle against them at Gibeah.
The Benjaminites came out from Gibeah, and that day they struck down twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground.
But the people, the men of Israel, took courage and again deployed for battle in the same place where they had deployed on the first day.

And the Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they enquired of the LORD: "Shall I again draw near to battle against the Benjaminites, my brother?" And the LORD said, "Go up against him."
So the Israelites drew near to the Benjaminites on the second day.
And Benjamin came out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and again struck down eighteen thousand men of the Israelites to the ground; all of them drawers of the sword.

Then all the Israelites and all the people went up and came to Beth-el, and they wept and sat there before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening, and they offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
And the Israelites enquired of the LORD — for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,

and Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron was ministering before it in those days — saying, "Shall I go out again to battle against the Benjaminites, my brother, or shall I stop?" And the LORD said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."
So Israel set ambushes around Gibeah.
And the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites on the third day and deployed against Gibeah as they had before.

The Benjaminites came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city, and they began to strike down some of the people, fatally wounded, as before, on the highways — one going up to Beth-el and one to Gibeah — and in the open country: about thirty men of Israel.
And the Benjaminites said, "They are being beaten before us just as before." But the Israelites said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city onto the highways."
And every man of Israel rose from his place and deployed at Baal-tamar, while the ambush of Israel burst out of its place, from the open ground of Geba.
And ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came against Gibeah, and the fighting was heavy; and they did not know that calamity was upon them.
And the LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and that day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin; all of them drawing the sword.
And the Benjaminites saw that they were defeated; for the men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, trusting in the ambush they had set against Gibeah.
And the men in ambush hurried and raided Gibeah; the ambush deployed and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the men in ambush was that they should send a great column of smoke up from the city.

And the men of Israel turned in the battle. Benjamin had begun to strike down about thirty of the men of Israel, fatally wounded, because they said, "He is being utterly beaten before us, just as in the first battle."
But the column began to rise from the city, a pillar of smoke; and Benjamin turned round — and there was the whole city going up toward the heavens.
And the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, because they saw that calamity had come upon them.
They turned away from the men of Israel toward the wilderness road, but the battle overtook them, and those coming out of the cities destroyed them in their midst.
They surrounded Benjamin, pursued him and trod him down at his resting place, as far as opposite Gibeah toward the east.
And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell — all of them men of valour.
They turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon; and on the highways they gleaned five thousand of them, pursued them closely as far as Gidom, and struck down two thousand more.
So all who fell of Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men drawing the sword, all of them men of valour.
But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and stayed there four months.

And the men of Israel turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them with the edge of the sword — from the city, everything sound, to the animals, to all that was found; and all the cities they found they set on fire.

judges_21.t: Now the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, "Not one of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."
And the people came to Beth-el and sat there before God until evening, and they lifted up their voice and wept bitterly.
And they said, "Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel — that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"
The next day the people rose early, built an altar there, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.

And the Israelites said, "Who among all the tribes of Israel did not go up in the assembly to the LORD?" — for a great oath had been sworn about anyone who did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah: "He shall surely be put to death."
And the Israelites were moved to compassion for Benjamin their brother, and said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
"What shall we do about wives for those who are left? We have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters as wives."
And they said, "Which of the tribes of Israel did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And it turned out that no one from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp, to the assembly.
For when the people were mustered, no one was there from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.
So the congregation sent twelve thousand men of valour there and commanded them, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword — the women and the little ones as well.
"And this is what you are to do: every male, and every woman who has known lying with a male, you are to devote to destruction."

And among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young women, virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
Then the whole congregation sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon and proclaimed peace to them.
And Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women they had kept alive from the women of Jabesh-gilead — but there were not enough for them.
And the people were moved to compassion for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do about wives for those who are left? The women have been wiped out of Benjamin."
And they said, "There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe is not wiped out from Israel."
"But we ourselves cannot give them wives from our own daughters, because the Israelites have sworn, "Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin."
And they said, "There is a yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh — north of Beth-el, east of the highway that goes up from Beth-el to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
And they instructed the Benjaminites, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

"and watch; and when the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves, each man his wife, from the daughters of Shiloh; and go to the land of Benjamin.

"And when their fathers or brothers come to complain to us, we will say to them, 'Show us favour concerning them. We did not take each man his wife in the battle, and you did not give them — otherwise you would now be guilty.'"
And the Benjaminites did so. They carried off wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized, and went back to their inheritance, rebuilt the cities and lived in them.
And the Israelites dispersed from there at that time, each to his tribe and to his clan, and went out from there, each to his own inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

jeremiah_1.t: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah — one of the priests at Anathoth, in Benjamin's territory.
The LORD's word came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign,

and it kept on coming in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, right up to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah — up to the month Jerusalem went into exile, the fifth month.
The LORD's word came to me:
Before I formed you in the belly, I knew you. Before you came out of the womb, I set you apart as holy. I made you a prophet to the nations.
And I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! I don't know how to speak — I'm a boy."
But the LORD said to me, "Don't say, 'I'm a boy.' You'll go to everyone I send you to, and you'll say everything I command you."
"Don't be afraid of them — I'm with you to rescue you," declares the LORD.
Then the LORD reached out his hand and touched my mouth, and he said to me, "There — I've put my words in your mouth."
"Look — today I'm setting you over the nations and over the kingdoms: to uproot and to pull down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."
The LORD's word came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see an almond branch."
And the LORD said to me, "You've seen rightly. I'm watching over my word, to carry it out."
The LORD's word came to me a second time: "What do you see?" I said, "I see a pot boiling over, and it's tipping away from the north."
And the LORD said to me, "Out of the north, disaster will break loose on everyone living in the land."

"I'm about to summon all the clans of the northern kingdoms," declares the LORD, "and they'll come, and each one will set up his throne at the entrance to the gates of Jerusalem, against all her walls round about, and against all the cities of Judah."
"And I'll pass sentence on them for all the evil they've done — they abandoned me, burned offerings to other gods, and bowed down to what their own hands had made."
"As for you — get yourself ready, stand up, and tell them everything I command you. Don't lose your nerve in front of them, or I'll break your nerve in front of them."
"And I — look — today I've made you a fortified city, an iron pillar, bronze walls, standing against the whole land: against Judah's kings, her officials, her priests, and the people of the land."
"They'll fight against you, but they won't overcome you, because I'm with you," declares the LORD, "to rescue you."

jeremiah_2.t: The LORD's word came to me:

Go and call out in Jerusalem's hearing: Here's what the LORD says: I remember it to your credit — the loyalty of your youth, the love of your betrothal, how you followed me through the wilderness, through a land nobody had sown.
Israel was holy to the LORD, the first of his harvest. Everyone who ate her was held guilty; disaster came on them, declares the LORD.
Listen to the word of the LORD, house of Jacob — all you clans of the house of Israel.
Here's what the LORD says: What did your ancestors find wrong in me, that they went so far from me, chasing after worthless things and turning worthless themselves?

They never said, "Where is the LORD, who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness — through a land of desert plain and pit, through a land of drought and deep darkness, through a land no one travels and nobody lives in?"
I brought you into a land of orchards, to eat its fruit and everything good in it — and you came and made my land unclean, you turned my inheritance into something detestable.
The priests never asked, "Where is the LORD?" The ones who handle the law didn't know me. The shepherds rebelled against me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and went after things that do no good.
So I will bring my case against you again, declares the LORD — and against your children's children I will bring it.
Cross over to the coasts of Kittim and look; send to Kedar and watch closely; see whether anything like this has ever happened.
Has any nation ever swapped its gods — and they aren't even gods? But my people have swapped their glory for what does no good.
Be appalled at this, you heavens — shudder, be laid utterly waste, declares the LORD.
My people have done two evil things: they've abandoned me, the spring of living water, and dug out cisterns for themselves — cracked cisterns that can't hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Was he born into slavery in the house? Then why has he become plunder?
Young lions have roared over him; they've let out their voice. They've turned his land into a waste; his cities are burned, with nobody left in them.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes, too, have cropped your scalp bare.
Haven't you brought this on yourself, by abandoning the LORD your God while he was leading you on the way?
So what's the road to Egypt to you now, to drink the water of the Shihor? And what's the road to Assyria to you, to drink the water of the River?

Your own evil will discipline you; your turnings away will rebuke you. Know it, then — see how evil and bitter it is that you abandoned the LORD your God, and that no dread of me is on you, declares Lord GOD of hosts.
Long ago I broke your yoke; I tore off your bonds. And you said, "I won't transgress." But on every high hill and under every green tree you were sprawling there, a prostitute.
I planted you myself, a choice vine, wholly a faithful seed. So how have you turned on me, turned into the degenerate shoots of a foreign vine?
Even if you wash yourself with natron and use soap by the handful, your iniquity is a stain in front of me, declares Lord GOD.
How can you say, "I haven't made myself unclean; I haven't gone after the Baals"? Look at your way in the valley; know what you've done — a young camel running loose, criss-crossing her tracks,

a wild donkey at home in the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the craving of her appetite — when she's in heat, who can turn her back? Nobody who wants her has to tire himself out; in her month they'll find her.
Keep your feet from going bare, your throat from going dry. But you said, "It's hopeless. No — I've loved strangers, and I'm going after them."
The way a thief is shamed when he's caught, that's how the house of Israel has been shamed — they and their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets,
who say to a tree, "You're my father," and to a stone, "You gave birth to us." They've turned their backs to me, not their faces — and then, when disaster comes, they say, "Get up and save us!"
So where are the gods you made for yourself? Let them get up, if they can save you when your disaster comes — because you have as many gods as you have cities, Judah.
Why bring a case against me? Every one of you has rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
I struck your children for nothing; they took no correction. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a lion on the kill.
