You of this generation — look at the word of the LORD! Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? So why have my people said, "We roam free. We won't come back to you again"?
Does a virgin forget her jewellery, or a bride her sashes? But my people have forgotten me, days beyond counting.
How well you set your course when you're after love! So you've even taught your ways to wicked women.
And on your skirts is the blood of the lives of the innocent poor. You didn't catch them breaking in — and still, it's for all of this.
And you said, "I'm innocent — his anger has turned away from me." Well, I'm about to bring you to judgement because you say, "I haven't sinned."
Why do you go around so cheaply, changing your way? Egypt will shame you too, just as Assyria shamed you.
You'll come away from this one too with your hands on your head, because the LORD has rejected the ones you trust, and you'll get nowhere with them.

jeremiah_3.t: If a man sends his wife away and she leaves him and becomes another man's, does he go back to her again? Wouldn't that land be utterly polluted? And you've played the whore with lover after lover — and you'd come back to me? declares the LORD.

Lift your eyes to the bare heights and look — where have you not been lain with? You sat by the roads waiting for them like an Arab in the wilderness. You polluted the land with your whoring and your evil.
So the showers were held back and the spring rain never came — and still you had a whore's brazen face. You refused to be ashamed.
Haven't you only just called out to me, "My father — you're the companion of my youth"?
"Will he stay angry for ever? Will he hold on to it to the end?" That's how you talk — and then you do evil things, and you get your way.
The LORD said to me back in the days of King Josiah: Have you seen what Turning-away Israel did? She went up on every high hill and under every green tree, and played the whore there.
And I thought, after she'd done all that, "She'll come back to me" — but she didn't. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

And I saw that for everything Turning-away Israel had committed adultery over, I sent her away and handed her a certificate of divorce — and still her treacherous sister Judah wasn't afraid. She went and played the whore herself.
And so, taking her whoring so lightly, she polluted the land — committing adultery with stone and with wood.
And even after all that, her treacherous sister Judah did not come back to me with her whole heart — only in falsehood, declares the LORD.
And the LORD said to me: Turning-away Israel has come out more in the right than treacherous Judah.

Go and call these words out toward the north, and say: Turn back, Turning-away Israel, declares the LORD. I won't look on you in anger, because I am loyal, declares the LORD. I won't stay angry for ever.
Only acknowledge your iniquity — that you rebelled against the LORD your God, scattered your ways among strangers under every green tree, and didn't listen to my voice, declares the LORD.
Turn back, turning-away sons, declares the LORD — I am master over you. And I'll take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
And I'll give you shepherds after my own heart, and they'll shepherd you with knowledge and insight.

And in those days, when you've multiplied and become fruitful in the land, declares the LORD, people will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD." It won't come to mind. They won't remember it, they won't miss it, and it won't be made again.

At that time they'll call Jerusalem "The Throne of the LORD," and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD, at Jerusalem — and they'll no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will walk alongside the house of Israel, and together they'll come from the land of the north to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

And I said to myself: How I would set you among the sons and give you a land to be desired, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations! And I thought: You'll call me "My father," and you won't turn away from following me.
But just as a wife betrays her husband, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel, declares the LORD.
A sound is heard on the bare heights — the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel, because they've twisted their way and forgotten the LORD their God.
Turn back, turning-away sons; I'll heal your turnings away. "Here we are, we've come to you — you are the LORD our God."
The hills really are a falsehood — all that tumult on the mountains. It really is in the LORD our God that Israel's salvation lies.
And the Shame has eaten up what our ancestors worked for, ever since we were young — their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us, because we have sinned against the LORD our God — we and our ancestors, from our youth right up to this day — and we haven't listened to the voice of the LORD our God.

jeremiah_4.t: If you're going to turn back, Israel, declares the LORD, turn back to me. And if you'll take your detestable things out of my sight, then you won't have to wander.
and you'll swear, "As the LORD lives," in faithfulness, in justice and in righteousness — and the nations will bless themselves by him, and boast in him.
Here's what the LORD says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up your unbroken ground. Don't sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the LORD; cut away the foreskins of your heart, people of Judah, you who live in Jerusalem — or my wrath will break out like fire and burn with nobody to put it out, because of the evil of your deeds.
Announce it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say: Blow the ram's horn through the land! Shout it out at the top of your voice: Gather together — let's get into the fortified cities!
Raise a standard toward Zion! Take cover — don't stand still! Because I'm bringing disaster from the north, and a great shattering.
A lion has come up out of his thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. He's left his own place to turn your land into a waste. Your cities will fall in ruins, with nobody living in them.
So put on sackcloth; mourn and wail, because the burning of the LORD's anger hasn't turned away from us.
And on that day, declares the LORD, the king's heart will fail, and the officials' hearts too. The priests will be appalled, the prophets astounded.
And I said: Oh, Lord GOD! You have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, telling them, "You'll have peace" — and now a sword is at their throat.
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind off the bare heights in the wilderness is blowing toward the daughter of my people — not to winnow, not to cleanse.
A wind stronger than any of that will come at my bidding. Now I too will pass sentence on them.
Look — he's coming up like storm clouds, his chariots like a whirlwind, his horses swifter than eagles. Woe to us — we're devastated!
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so you can be saved. How long are your wicked thoughts going to stay lodged inside you?
A voice is announcing it from Dan, proclaiming trouble from the hill country of Ephraim.
Make it known to the nations — look — proclaim it against Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from a far country, raising their voice against the cities of Judah.
They ring her round like men guarding a field, because she has rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
Your own way and your own deeds have brought this on you. This is your evil — and it's bitter, and it has reached your very heart.

My insides, my insides! I have to wait it out! The walls of my heart! My heart is in turmoil inside me; I can't keep quiet, because you've heard the sound of the ram's horn, my very self — the shout of battle.
Shattering on shattering is announced, because the whole land is devastated. In an instant my tents are devastated, in a moment, my curtains.
How long must I look at the standard and listen to the sound of the ram's horn?
My people are fools; they don't know me. They're senseless children with no understanding. They're expert at doing evil, and they don't know how to do good.
I looked at the earth — and there it was, formless and empty; and at the heavens, and their light was gone.
I looked at the mountains — they were quaking, and all the hills were reeling.
I looked — and there was no one at all, and every bird of the sky had fled.
I looked — and the orchard land was wilderness, and all its cities were pulled down before the LORD, before the burning of his anger.
Here's what the LORD says: The whole land will be a desolation — but I won't make a full end of it.
For this the land will mourn and the heavens above will go dark, because I have spoken and I have purposed, and I haven't relented, and I won't turn back from it.
At the sound of horseman and archer every city takes flight. They've gone into the thickets; they've climbed up among the rocks. Every city stands abandoned, with nobody living in them.

And you, devastated one — what are you doing, dressing in scarlet, decking yourself out in gold, opening your eyes wide with paint? You beautify yourself for nothing. Your lovers have rejected you; they're after your life.

I've heard a sound like a woman in labour, anguish like a woman bearing her first child — the sound of the daughter of Zion, gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: "Woe to me now — my life is fainting away before murderers!"

jeremiah_5.t: Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem; look now, and see, and search her open squares: if you can find one man, if there's anyone doing justice and seeking faithfulness — then I'll forgive her.
And even when they say, "As the LORD lives," they're swearing to a falsehood.

LORD, aren't your eyes on faithfulness? You struck them, and they didn't even flinch; you finished them off, and they refused to take correction. They set their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.
And I thought: These are only the poor; they've acted foolishly because they don't know the way of the LORD, what their God requires.
Let me go to the great, then, and speak with them, because they know the way of the LORD, what their God requires. But they had broken the yoke just the same; they had torn off the bonds.

So a lion from the forest will strike them, a wolf from the desert plains will devastate them, a leopard is watching their cities. Anyone who goes out from them will be torn to pieces, because their rebellions are many, their turnings away are past counting.
Why should I forgive you for this? Your children have abandoned me and sworn by what aren't gods at all. I fed them full, and they committed adultery, trooping off to a whore's house.
They were like well-fed stallions in heat, each one neighing after his neighbour's wife.
Shall I not call them to account for this, declares the LORD? On a nation like this, shall I not take my own revenge?
Go up among her vine rows and destroy — but don't make a full end of her. Strip away her tendrils, because they aren't the LORD's.
The house of Israel and the house of Judah have betrayed me utterly, declares the LORD.
They've denied the LORD and said, "He's nothing! No disaster is coming on us; we'll never see sword or famine."
The prophets will turn out to be nothing but wind; the word isn't in them. Let it be done to them just like that.
So here's what the LORD, the God of hosts, says: Because you have said this, I'm about to make my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood — and it will consume them.

I'm about to bring a nation on you from far away, house of Israel, declares the LORD — an enduring nation, a nation from long ago, a nation whose language you don't know; you won't understand a word it says.
Their quiver is like an open grave; every one of them is a warrior.

It will devour your harvest and your food; they will devour your sons and your daughters; it will devour your flocks and your herds; it will devour your vines and your fig trees. With the sword it will shatter the fortified cities you're trusting in.
Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I won't make a full end of you.

And when you ask, "What did the LORD our God do all this to us for?", tell them: Just as you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you'll serve strangers in a land that isn't yours.
Announce this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah:
Listen to this now, you foolish people, with no heart in you: eyes they have, and they don't see; ears they have, and they don't hear.

Do you not fear me, declares the LORD? Do you not tremble before me — the one who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, a perpetual statute it can't cross? The waters heave, but they can't prevail; its waves roar, but they can't cross it.
But this people has a stubborn, rebellious heart. They've turned aside and gone.
They haven't said in their heart, "Let's fear the LORD our God, who gives the rain — autumn rain and spring rain — in its season, who keeps the appointed weeks of harvest for us."
Your iniquities have turned all this aside; your sins have kept the good from you.
There are wicked men found among my people. He lies in wait the way fowlers crouch; they've set something to destroy with — and it's men they catch.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit. That's how they've become great and grown rich.

They've grown fat, they've grown sleek; they overflow with deeds of evil. They won't plead a cause — the cause of the fatherless — so that it might come out right; and they haven't judged the case of the needy.
Shall I not call them to account for this, declares the LORD? On a nation like this, shall I not take my own revenge?
Something appalling, something horrifying, has happened in the land:
The prophets prophesy falsehood, the priests rule by their own authority, and my people love it that way. But what will you do when the end comes?

jeremiah_6.t: Take cover, people of Benjamin — get out of Jerusalem! Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa; raise a signal over Beth-hakkerem! Disaster is looking down from the north, and a great shattering.
The comely one, the delicate one — I destroy the daughter of Zion.
Shepherds will come to her with their flocks; they'll pitch their tents against her all around; each will graze his own portion.
Consecrate war against her! Up — let's attack at noon! Woe to us, the day has turned; the evening shadows are stretching out.
Up — let's attack by night and destroy her fortresses!
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Cut down timber; throw up a siege mound against Jerusalem. She's the city that must be called to account — nothing in her but oppression.
The way a well keeps its water fresh, she keeps her evil fresh. Violence and havoc are heard in her; sickness and wounds are before me all the time.
Take correction, Jerusalem, or I'll be torn away from you — or I'll make you a desolation, a land where nobody lives.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: They'll glean the remnant of Israel clean, like a vine. Pass your hand back over it again, the way a grape gatherer goes over the branches.

Who can I speak to? Who can I warn, so that they'll hear? Look — their ear is uncircumcised; they can't pay attention. Look — the word of the LORD has become a reproach to them; they take no delight in it.

I'm full of the wrath of the LORD; I'm worn out holding it in. Pour it out on the child in the street and on the gathering of young men; for husband and wife alike will be taken, the old with the one full of days.
Their houses will be handed over to others, their fields and wives with them, because I'm going to stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD.
From the least of them to the greatest, every one of them is out for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, every one of them practises falsehood.
They've healed the shattering of my people as if it were nothing, saying, "Peace, peace" — and there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they did something detestable? Not in the least ashamed; they didn't even know how to blush. So they'll fall among the fallen; when I call them to account they'll stumble, says the LORD.
Here's what the LORD says: Stand at the roads and look; ask for the ancient paths — where the good way is — and walk in it, and you'll find rest for yourselves. But they said, "We won't walk in it."
I raised up watchmen over you: "Pay attention to the sound of the ram's horn!" But they said, "We won't pay attention."
So hear it, you nations; and know, you congregation, what will happen to them.
Hear it, earth! I'm about to bring disaster on this people — the fruit of their own schemes — because they haven't paid attention to my words, and my law, they've rejected.
What is this to me — frankincense brought in from Sheba, the good cane from a far country? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices don't please me.
So here's what the LORD says: I'm about to put stumbling blocks in front of this people, and they'll stumble over them — fathers and sons together, neighbour and friend — and they'll perish.
Here's what the LORD says: Look — a people is coming from the land of the north, and a great nation is being roused from the far ends of the earth.
They take up bow and javelin; they are cruel, and they show no mercy. Their noise roars like the sea. They ride on horses, drawn up like one man for battle against you, daughter of Zion.
We've heard the report of it, and our hands hang limp. Distress has seized us, anguish like a woman in labour.
Don't go out into the field; don't walk on the road — the enemy has a sword. Terror all around.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only child; wail bitterly — because the destroyer will come on us suddenly.
I've made you an assayer among my people, a fortification, so you can know and test their way.
Every one of them is a stubborn rebel, going about slandering. They are bronze and iron; every one of them is a destroyer.
The bellows puff; the lead is burned away by the fire. The refiner has refined for nothing — the evil ones haven't been separated out.
"Rejected silver" is what they're called, because the LORD has rejected them.

jeremiah_7.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Stand in the gate of the house of the LORD and proclaim this word there. Say: Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah — all of you who come in at these gates to bow down to the LORD.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Make your ways and your deeds good, and I'll let you live in this place.
Don't put your trust in the words of falsehood, saying: "The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD — that's what these are!"
Because if you really do make your ways and your deeds good — if you really do justice between one person and another —
if you don't oppress the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, don't shed innocent blood in this place, and don't go after other gods to your own harm —
then I'll let you live in this place, in the land I gave your ancestors, from of old and for ever.
Look — you're trusting in the words of falsehood, which do no good at all.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn offerings to Baal, and go after other gods you've never known —
and then come and stand in front of me in this house that bears my name and say, "We're safe!" — so that you can go on doing all these detestable things?
Has this house that bears my name become a den of robbers in your eyes? I've seen it too, declares the LORD.
Go now to my place that was at Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the evil of my people Israel.
And now, because you've done all these things, declares the LORD — and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, and you didn't listen; I called you, and you didn't answer —
so I'll do to the house that bears my name — the one you're trusting in — and to the place I gave you and your ancestors, exactly what I did to Shiloh.
And I'll throw you out of my presence, just as I threw out all your brothers, the whole offspring of Ephraim.
And you — don't pray for this people. Don't lift up a cry or a prayer for them. Don't press me, because I won't be listening to you.
Don't you see what they're doing in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?

The children gather the wood, the fathers light the fire, the women knead the dough — to make cakes for the queen of the heavens. And they pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke me to anger.
Is it me they're provoking? declares the LORD. Isn't it themselves — to the shame of their own faces?

So here's what Lord GOD says: My anger and my wrath are about to be poured out on this place — on humankind and on the animals, on the trees of the field and on the fruit of the ground. It will burn, and it won't be put out.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Pile your burnt offerings onto your sacrifices, and eat the meat yourselves.
Because on the day I brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt, I didn't speak to them or command them about burnt offering and sacrifice.
This is what I commanded them: Listen to my voice, and I'll be God to you and you'll be a people to me. Walk in every way I command you, and it will go well for you.
But they didn't listen; they didn't incline their ear. They walked in their own counsels, in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and they went backward and not forward.
From the day your ancestors came out of the land of Egypt right up to this day, I sent you all my servants the prophets, day after day, rising early and sending them.
But they didn't listen to me; they didn't incline their ear. They stiffened their neck. They did worse than their ancestors.
You'll speak all these words to them, and they won't listen to you. You'll call to them, and they won't answer you.
Say to them: This is the nation that didn't listen to the voice of the LORD its God and wouldn't take correction. Faithfulness has perished; it's been cut off from their mouth.
Cut off your consecrated hair and throw it away; take up a lamentation on the bare heights, because the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his fury.
The people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They've put their detestable things in the house that bears my name, and made it unclean.
And they've built the high places of the Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire — something I never commanded, something that never came into my mind.

So days are coming, declares the LORD, when it won't be called "the Topheth" or "the Valley of Ben-hinnom" any more, but "the Valley of Slaughter" — and they'll bury in Topheth because there's no room anywhere else.
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, with no one to scare them off.

And I'll put an end, in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, to the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride — because the land will become a desolation.

jeremiah_8.t: At that time, declares the LORD, they'll bring out of their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the people who lived in Jerusalem.

And they'll spread them out to the sun and the moon and all the host of the heavens — the ones they loved and served and followed and consulted and bowed down to. They won't be gathered up; they won't be buried. They'll be dung on the face of the ground.
And death will be preferred to life by everyone left of this evil clan, in all the places left, wherever I've banished them, declares the LORD of hosts.
Say to them: Here's what the LORD says: When people fall, don't they get up? When someone turns away, doesn't he turn back?
Why has this people, Jerusalem, turned away and gone on turning away? They've kept their grip on deceit; they've refused to turn back.
I've paid attention; I've listened. They don't speak rightly. Not one of them relents over his evil, saying, "What have I done?" Every one turns to his own course, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork up in the sky knows her appointed times; the turtle-dove, the swift and the crane keep to the time of their coming. But my people don't know what the LORD requires.
How can you say, "We're wise, and the law of the LORD is with us"? The truth is, it's been turned into falsehood by the scribes' false stylus.
The wise will be put to shame; they'll be dismayed and captured. Look — they've rejected the word of the LORD. So what wisdom do they have?

So I'll give their wives to others, their fields to those who take them over; because from the small to the great, every one of them is out for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, every one of them practises falsehood.
They've healed the shattering of the daughter of my people as if it were nothing, saying, "Peace, peace" — and there is no peace.

Were they ashamed when they did something detestable? Not in the least ashamed; they didn't know how to be shamed. So they'll fall among the fallen; at the time of their punishment they'll stumble, says the LORD.
I will make a complete end of them, declares the LORD. There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree; the leaf has withered, and what I gave them slips away from them.

Why are we sitting here? Gather together — let's get into the fortified cities and perish there. For the LORD our God has silenced us and given us poisoned water to drink, because we've sinned against the LORD.
We waited for peace, and no good came; for a time of healing, and instead — terror.
From Dan you can hear the snorting of his horses; at the sound of his stallions neighing the whole land quakes. They come and devour the land and everything in it, the city and everyone living in it.
I'm about to send serpents among you — vipers that no charm can handle — and they'll bite you, declares the LORD.
Whatever cheer I had is gone in sorrow; my heart inside me is faint.

Listen — the sound of the cry of the daughter of my people from a far country: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her king not in her?" Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, with foreign worthlessness?
The harvest is past, the summer is over, and we are not saved.
For the shattering of the daughter of my people I am shattered. I'm in mourning. Desolation has taken hold of me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Then why hasn't new flesh grown over the daughter of my people?

jeremiah_9.t: If only my head were water and my eye a fountain of tears, so I could weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
If only I had a travellers' lodge out in the wilderness, so I could leave my people and get away from them! Every one of them is an adulterer, a whole assembly of traitors.
They bend their tongue like a bow of falsehood; it isn't for faithfulness that they grow strong in the land. They go from evil to evil, and they don't know me, declares the LORD.
Be on guard, each of you, against your neighbour; don't rely on any brother. Every brother is out to supplant; every neighbour goes about slandering.
Every one of them deceives his neighbour; faithfulness is not what they speak. They've trained their tongue to speak falsehood; they wear themselves out being perverse.
You live surrounded by deceit; in their deceit they've refused to know me, declares the LORD.
So here's what the LORD of hosts says: I'm about to refine them and test them. What else can I do, faced with the daughter of my people?
Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbour, but inside him he's laying his ambush.
Shall I not call them to account for this, declares the LORD? On a nation like this, shall I not take my own revenge?

Over the mountains I'll take up weeping and wailing, and over the wilderness pastures a lamentation, because they're burned up, with no one passing through and not a sound of livestock to be heard. From the birds of the sky to the animals, they've fled; they're gone.
I'll turn Jerusalem into heaps of stones, a lair of jackals, and the cities of Judah into a waste, with nobody living there.
Who is wise enough to understand this? Who has had the mouth of the LORD speak to him, so he can explain it — why the land has perished, burned up like the wilderness, with nobody passing through?
And the LORD said: Because they abandoned my law that I set in front of them, and didn't listen to my voice or walk in it,
and instead followed the stubbornness of their own heart, and the Baals their ancestors taught them —
so here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
And I'll scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, and I'll send the sword after them until I've made an end of them.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Think about it — summon the wailing women; let them come. Send for the skilled women; let them come.
Let them come quickly and take up a wailing over us, so our eyes run down with tears and our eyelids flow with water.
A sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are devastated! We are utterly shamed, because we've left the land, because they've torn down our dwellings."
Hear the word of the LORD, you women; let your ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters a wailing, and each woman teach her neighbour a lamentation.
Death has climbed in at our windows; it's got into our fortresses, cutting off the children from the street, the young men from the open squares.
Say this — this is the LORD's own declaration: The corpses of humankind will fall like dung on the open field, like cut grain behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.
Here's what the LORD says: Let the wise not boast in his wisdom, let the mighty not boast in his might, let the rich not boast in his riches.

If anyone is going to boast, let him boast in this: that he has insight and knows me — that I am the LORD, who does steadfast love, justice and righteousness in the earth. These are what I delight in, declares the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll call to account everyone circumcised in the foreskin —

against Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites and Moab, and against all who have their temples clipped, who live in the wilderness — because all the nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised of heart.

jeremiah_10.t: Hear the word the LORD has spoken to you, house of Israel.
Here's what the LORD says: Don't learn the way of the nations; don't be dismayed at the signs of the heavens, even though the nations are dismayed at them.
The customs of the peoples are worthless: it's a tree from the forest that someone cut down, shaped by a craftsman's hands with a tool.
He decorates it with silver and gold; they fasten it with nails and hammers so it won't topple over.
They're like a scarecrow in a cucumber field; they don't speak. They have to be carried, because they can't walk. Don't be afraid of them — they can do no harm, and doing good isn't in them either.
There is no one like you, LORD. You are great, and your name is great in strength.
Who would not fear you, King of the nations? It is your due — because among all the wise of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is no one like you.
All of them together are stupid and foolish: what these worthless things teach is wood.
Beaten silver is brought in from Tarshish, gold from Uphaz — the work of a craftsman, of a metalsmith's hands. Violet and purple are what they wear; every one of them is the work of skilled men.
But the LORD is a God of faithfulness; he is the living God, the everlasting King. At his rage the earth quakes, and the nations can't endure his indignation.
This is what you're to say to them: The gods that did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from under these heavens.
He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.
At the sound of his voice there's a tumult of waters in the heavens; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
Every human being is stupid, without knowledge; every metalsmith is shamed by his idol, because his molten image is falsehood and there's no breath in them.
They are worthless, a thing to be mocked; at the time of their punishment they'll perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these, because he is the one who formed all things — and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of hosts is his name.
Gather up your bundle off the ground, you who are living under siege.
Here's what the LORD says: This time I'm slinging out the inhabitants of the land, and I'll bring distress on them, so that they'll feel it.
Woe to me for my shattering! My wound is severe. But I said: This is only a sickness; I can bear it.
My tent is devastated; all my tent cords are snapped. My children have gone from me; they're no more. There's no one left to pitch my tent again or raise up my curtains.
The shepherds have behaved stupidly; they haven't sought the LORD. So they haven't prospered, and their whole flock is scattered.
The sound of a report — it's coming! A great din from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a lair of jackals.
I know, LORD, that a person's way is not his own — that the one who walks doesn't direct his own step.
Correct me, LORD, but only in justice — not in your anger, or you'll leave me next to nothing.

Pour out your wrath on the nations that don't know you, and on the clans that haven't called on your name; because they've devoured Jacob — devoured him and made an end of him, and devastated his habitation.

jeremiah_11.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the people living in Jerusalem.
And say to them: Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is anyone who does not hear the words of this covenant,

the covenant I commanded your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying: Listen to my voice and do them, everything I command you — and you'll be a people to me, and I'll be God to you —
so I could keep the oath I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today. And I answered, "Amen, LORD."
And the LORD said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
I solemnly warned your ancestors on the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and right up to this day — rising early and warning them: Listen to my voice.

But they didn't listen; they didn't incline their ear. Each one walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do and they didn't do.
And the LORD said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem.

They've turned back to the iniquities of their forebears, who refused to hear my words. They've gone after other gods and served them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant, the one I cut with their ancestors.
So here's what the LORD says: I'm about to bring a disaster on them that they can't escape. They'll cry out to me, and I won't listen to them.
And the cities of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn offerings to — and those gods will certainly not deliver them when their disaster comes.
You have as many gods as you have cities, Judah; and as many altars to the Shame as Jerusalem has streets — altars for burning offerings to Baal.
And you — don't pray for this people. Don't lift up a cry or a prayer for them. I won't be listening when they call to me about their disaster.
What is my beloved doing in my house, carrying out her schemes with the crowd? And will holy flesh pass away from you? When your evil comes — then you exult.
"A luxuriant olive tree, beautiful with shapely fruit" — that was the name the LORD called you. At the sound of a great roar he has set fire to it, and its branches are broken.

And the LORD of hosts, who planted you, has spoken disaster against you — because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done to themselves, provoking me to anger by burning offerings to Baal.
The LORD made it known to me, and I knew. Then you showed me what they were doing.

And I was like a docile lamb led to the slaughter; I didn't know they had laid plans against me: "Let's destroy the tree with its fruit; let's cut him off from the land of the living, and his name won't be remembered any more."
But LORD of hosts, judging righteously, testing kidneys and heart — let me see your vengeance on them, because I've laid my case before you.
So here's what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth, who are after your life, saying: "You are not to prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you'll die at our hands" —
so here's what the LORD of hosts says: I'm about to call them to account. The young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die by famine.
There'll be no remnant left of them, because I'm bringing disaster on the men of Anathoth — the year of their punishment.

jeremiah_12.t: You are in the right, LORD, whenever I bring a case to you — and still I'll argue my judgements with you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are all who deal treachery at ease?
You planted them, and they took root; they go on, and they've borne fruit. You are near in their mouth and far from their kidneys.
But you, LORD, know me; you see me; you've tested my heart toward you. Drag them off like sheep for slaughter; set them apart for a day of killing.

How long will the land mourn and the vegetation of every field wither, because of the evil of the people living in it? Beasts and birds have been swept away, because they said, "He won't see how we end up."
If you've run with men on foot and they wore you out, how will you keep up with horses? And if you feel safe in a land of peace, how will you manage in the thicket of the Jordan?
Even your brothers and your own father's house — even they have betrayed you; even they have shouted after you at full voice. Don't trust them, however well they speak to you.
I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance. I have given the one I love into the hand of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has raised her voice against me. That is why I hate her.
Is my inheritance a hyena to me, with birds of prey ringed all around her? Go, gather all the animals of the field; bring them in to eat.
Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they've trampled my portion; they've turned the portion I delighted in into a desolate wilderness.
He has made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns before me. The whole land is made desolate, because not one person takes it to heart.
Over all the bare heights in the wilderness the destroyers have come. A sword of the LORD is devouring from one end of the land to the other. There is no peace for any flesh.
They've sown wheat and reaped thorns; they've worn themselves out for nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests, because of the burning of the LORD's anger.

Here's what the LORD says about all my evil neighbours who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel: I'm about to uproot them from their own soil, and I'll uproot the house of Judah from among them.
And after I've uprooted them, I'll turn back and have compassion on them, and bring them back, each to his own inheritance and each to his own land.
And if they really will learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, "As the LORD lives," just as they taught my people to swear by Baal — then they'll be built up among my people.
But if they won't listen, then I'll uproot that nation completely and destroy it, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_13.t: This is what the LORD said to me: Go and buy yourself a linen loincloth and put it on your loins, but don't put it in water.
So I bought the loincloth as the LORD said, and I put it on my loins.
And the LORD's word came to me a second time:
Take the loincloth you bought, the one on your loins, and get up, go to Perath, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock.
So I went and hid it at Perath, just as the LORD had commanded me.
And after many days the LORD said to me: Get up, go to Perath, and take the loincloth from there — the one I commanded you to hide there.
So I went to Perath and dug, and took the loincloth from the place where I'd hidden it — and there it was, ruined. Good for nothing.
And the LORD's word came to me:
Here's what the LORD says: This is how I'll ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart and have gone after other gods to serve and bow down to them — let them be like this loincloth, good for nothing.

Just as the loincloth clings to a man's loins, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, declares the LORD — to be a people to me, and a name, a praise and a splendour. But they didn't listen.

And speak this word to them: Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every wineskin will be filled with wine. And they'll say to you: Don't we know perfectly well that every wineskin gets filled with wine?

And say to them: Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to fill all the inhabitants of this land — the kings who sit for David on his throne, the priests, the prophets, and everyone living in Jerusalem — with drunkenness.
And I'll smash them one against another, fathers and sons together, declares the LORD. I won't show pity, I won't spare, I won't have compassion — nothing will stop me destroying them.
Hear, and give ear; don't be haughty — the LORD has spoken.

Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings the darkness, before your feet stumble on the mountains of twilight — and you wait for light, and he turns it to deep darkness, makes it thick darkness.
But if you won't listen to it, I'll weep in secret because of your pride; my eye will weep bitterly and run down with tears, because the flock of the LORD has been taken captive.
Say to the king and the queen mother: Humble yourselves; sit down — because it has come down off your heads, your crown of splendour.
The cities of the Negev are shut up, with no one to open them. Judah is carried into exile, all of it — carried off completely.
Lift up your eyes and look at those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, the sheep you took such pride in?
What will you say when he sets over you the very ones you taught to be over you — close companions, as your head? Won't pangs seize you like a woman in labour?
And if you say to yourself, "Why has all this happened to me?" — it's for the greatness of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped up and your heels have suffered violence.
Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Then you could do good too — you who are trained to do evil.
And I'll scatter them like chaff blown away on the wilderness wind.
This is your lot, the portion measured out to you from me, declares the LORD, because you forgot me and trusted in falsehood.
And I myself have stripped your skirts up over your face, and your shame is seen.
Your adulteries and your neighings, the wickedness of your whoring — on the hills, in the open field, I've seen your detestable things. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You will not be clean. How much longer?

jeremiah_14.t: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah about the droughts:
Judah mourns; her gates languish. They mourn down to the ground, and the outcry of Jerusalem goes up.
Their nobles send their servants for water. They come to the cisterns and find no water; they go back with their vessels empty. They're ashamed and humiliated, and they cover their heads.
Because the ground is cracked, because no rain has come on the land, the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
Even the doe out in the field gives birth and then abandons her fawn, because there's no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights, panting for breath like jackals. Their eyes fail, because there's no vegetation.
Even though our iniquities testify against us, LORD, act for the sake of your name. Our turnings away are many; we've sinned against you.
Hope of Israel, its deliverer in time of distress — why are you like a sojourner in the land, like a traveller who turns in for one night?
Why are you like a man taken by surprise, like a warrior who can't save? And yet you are in our midst, LORD, and your name is called over us. Don't leave us!

Here's what the LORD says about this people: So — they have loved to wander; they haven't restrained their feet. And the LORD has not accepted them. Now he'll remember their iniquity and call their sins to account.
And the LORD said to me: Don't pray for this people, for their good.
When they fast, I won't listen to their cry. When they offer up a burnt offering and a grain offering, I won't accept them. By sword and famine and pestilence I'm bringing them to an end.
And I said: Oh, Lord GOD! Look — the prophets are telling them: You won't see the sword; famine won't come on you; I'll give you a peace that holds, in this place.

And the LORD said to me: The prophets are prophesying falsehood in my name. I didn't send them; I didn't command them; I didn't speak to them. A vision of falsehood, divination, a worthless thing, the deceit of their own heart — that's what they're prophesying to you.

So here's what the LORD says about the prophets who prophesy in my name — and I never sent them — and who say, "Sword and famine won't touch this land": By sword and by famine those prophets will meet their end.

And the people they prophesy to will be thrown out in the streets of Jerusalem, because of the famine and the sword, with no one to bury them — them, their wives, their sons and their daughters. And I'll pour out their own evil on them.

And speak this word to them: Let my eyes run down with tears, night and day; let them not cease — because the virgin daughter of my people is shattered with a great shattering, with a wound made very grievous.
If I go out into the field — there they are, the sword's dead. If I go into the city — there they are, the diseases of famine. Both prophet and priest go about in a land they do not know.
Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your very self loathe Zion? Why have you struck us, with no healing for us? We waited for peace, and no good came; for a time of healing, and instead — terror.
We know our wickedness, LORD, the iniquity of our ancestors. We have sinned against you.
Don't spurn us, for the sake of your name; don't treat the throne of your glory with contempt. Remember — don't break your covenant with us.

Is there anything among the worthless things of the nations that can send rain? Do the heavens give showers on their own? Isn't it you, LORD our God? So we wait for you — you are the one who made all this.

jeremiah_15.t: And the LORD said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, I would not turn toward this people. Send them out of my sight — let them go.

And when they ask you, "Where are we to go?", say to them: Here's what the LORD says: Those for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity.
And I'll appoint four kinds over them, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth to devour and destroy.
And I'll make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will show you sympathy? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You abandoned me, declares the LORD; you keep going backward. So I've stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you. I'm weary of relenting.
I've winnowed them with a winnowing fork in the gates of the land. I've bereaved them; I've destroyed my people. They didn't turn back from their ways.

Their widows have become more numerous to me than the sand of the seas. I've brought against them — against the mother of a young man — a destroyer at noon. I've made anguish and sudden terror fall on her all at once.

She who bore seven has grown feeble; she has breathed out her life. Her sun set while it was still day; she is ashamed and disgraced. And what is left of them I'll give to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD.
Woe to me, my mother, that you bore me — a man of strife and a man of contention to the whole land! I've lent nothing, and nobody has lent to me, and still every one of them curses me.
The LORD said: Surely I've set you free for good; surely I've made the enemy plead with you in a time of evil, in a time of distress.
Can iron be broken — iron from the north — or bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I'll give away as plunder, for nothing — and that for all your sins, throughout all your territories.
And I'll make your enemies pass over into a land you don't know, because a fire is kindled in my anger, and it will burn against you.
You know, LORD. Remember me; attend to me; avenge me on those who harass me. Don't let your patience carry me off — know that it's for your sake I bear reproach.
Your words were found, and I ate them, and your word became a joy to me, the delight of my heart, because your name is called over me, LORD, God of hosts.
I never sat in the company of merrymakers, enjoying myself; because of your hand I sat alone, because you filled me with indignation.
Why has my pain become perpetual, my wound incurable, refusing to heal? Will you really be to me like a deceitful stream, waters that can't be relied on?

So here's what the LORD says: If you turn back, I'll bring you back; you'll stand before me. And if you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you'll be as my mouth. They will turn back to you; you are not to turn back to them.
And I'll make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze. They'll fight against you, but they won't overcome you, because I'm with you to save you and to deliver you, declares the LORD.
And I'll deliver you from the hand of the wicked and ransom you from the grip of the ruthless.

jeremiah_16.t: The LORD's word came to me:
You are not to take a wife, and you are not to have sons or daughters in this place.
Here's what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born in this place, and about the mothers who bore them and the fathers who fathered them in this land:

They'll die of deadly diseases. They won't be mourned; they won't be buried. They'll be dung on the face of the ground. By sword and famine they'll come to an end, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

Here's what the LORD says: Don't enter a house of mourning; don't go to lament; don't show sympathy for them. I have withdrawn my peace from this people, declares the LORD — the steadfast love and the compassion.
Great and small alike will die in this land. They won't be buried; nobody will lament for them; nobody will gash himself or shave his head bald for them.
Nobody will break bread for them in mourning, to comfort anyone for the dead; nobody will give them the cup of consolations to drink, for his father or his mother.
And you're not to enter a house of feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Before your eyes and in your days, I'm about to put an end in this place to the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride.

And when you tell this people all these words, and they ask you, "Why has the LORD spoken all this great disaster against us? What is our iniquity? What is our sin, that we've sinned against the LORD our God?" —
then say to them: Because your ancestors abandoned me, declares the LORD, and went after other gods and served them and bowed down to them — they abandoned me and didn't keep my law;
and you yourselves have done worse than your ancestors — look at you, each one walking after the stubbornness of his own evil heart, so as not to listen to me.
So I'll hurl you off this land into a land you have not known, you or your ancestors; and there you'll serve other gods day and night, because I'll grant you no favour.
So days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,"

but, "As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where he had banished them." And I'll bring them back to their own soil, the soil I gave their ancestors.

I'm about to send for many fishermen, declares the LORD, and they'll fish them out; and after that I'll send for many hunters, and they'll hunt them from every mountain and every hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.
My eyes are on all their ways. They aren't hidden from me, and their iniquity isn't concealed from before my eyes.
And first I'll repay double for their iniquity and their sin, because they profaned my land with the corpses of their detestable things and filled my inheritance with their abominations.

LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in a day of distress — to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth and say: Our ancestors inherited nothing but falsehood, worthlessness, with nothing in it that does any good.
Can a human being make gods for himself? And they aren't gods at all!
So this time I'm going to make them know — I'll make them know my hand and my might; and they'll know that my name is the LORD.

jeremiah_17.t: The sin of Judah is written with an iron stylus, engraved with a point of flint on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars.
the way their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside every green tree, on the high hills.
My mountain in the open country — your wealth, all your treasures I'll give away as plunder, your high places too, for sin throughout all your territories.

And you'll let go — by your own doing — of the inheritance I gave you; and I'll make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, because you have kindled a fire in my anger, and it will burn for ever.
Here's what the LORD says: Cursed is the man who trusts in humankind and makes flesh his arm, whose heart turns aside from the LORD.
He'll be like a bush in the desert plain, and he won't see it when good comes. He'll live in parched places in the wilderness, a land of salt where nobody lives.
Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD.

He'll be like a tree planted by water, sending its roots out by a stream. It won't see it when the heat comes; its leaf will stay green. In a year of drought it won't be anxious; it won't stop producing fruit.
The heart is more crooked than anything else, and it is incurable. Who can know it?
I, the LORD, search the heart and test the kidneys, to give to each according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.
A partridge that gathers a brood it never laid — that's the man who makes wealth, and not by justice. Halfway through his days it will leave him, and at his end he'll be a fool.
A throne of glory, exalted from the first — that is the place of our sanctuary.
Hope of Israel, LORD! All who forsake you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from me will be written in the earth, because they have forsaken the spring of living water — the LORD.
Heal me, LORD, and I'll be healed; save me, and I'll be saved — you are my praise.
Look — they're saying to me: "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come, then!"
But I haven't run from being a shepherd after you, and I haven't wanted the day of ruin. You know it — what came out of my lips was right there before your face.
Don't become a terror to me — you are my refuge in a day of disaster.
Let my pursuers be put to shame — not me; let them be dismayed — not me. Bring a day of disaster on them, and shatter them with a double shattering.
This is what the LORD said to me: Go and stand in the People's Gate, where the kings of Judah come in and go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem.
And say to them: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah, all Judah, and everyone who lives in Jerusalem and comes in at these gates.
Here's what the LORD says: Take heed for your lives — don't carry a burden on the sabbath day, and don't bring one in at the gates of Jerusalem.
Don't bring a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, and do no work. Set the sabbath day apart as holy, just as I commanded your ancestors.
But they didn't listen; they didn't incline their ear. They stiffened their neck so as not to listen or accept correction.
And if you really will listen to me, declares the LORD, and not bring a burden in at the gates of this city on the sabbath day, and set the sabbath day apart as holy by doing no work on it,

then kings and officials will come in at the gates of this city, sitting on the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses — they and their officials, the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem — and this city will remain for ever.

And they'll come from the cities of Judah and from around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, the Shephelah, the hill country and the Negev, bringing burnt offering and sacrifice, grain offering and frankincense, and bringing a thank offering to the house of the LORD.

But if you won't listen to me, and won't set the sabbath day apart as holy, and go on carrying a burden and coming in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day, then I'll kindle a fire in her gates, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem, and it won't be put out.

jeremiah_18.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I'll let you hear my words.
So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
And the vessel he was making with the clay was spoiled in the potter's hand — so he would start over and make it into another vessel, whatever seemed right in the potter's eyes to make.
Then the LORD's word came to me:
Can I not do with you as this potter does, house of Israel? declares the LORD. Look — as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
At one moment I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, to uproot and pull down and destroy;
and if that nation turns back from its evil, the evil I spoke about, then I'll relent over the disaster I had planned to do to it.
And at another moment I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, to build and to plant;
and if it does what is evil in my eyes, and won't listen to my voice, then I'll relent over the good I said I'd do to it.

Now say to the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem: Here's what the LORD says: I'm shaping disaster against you, planning a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil way; make your ways and your deeds good.
But they say: It's hopeless. We'll walk after our own plans; each of us will act on the stubbornness of his evil heart.
So here's what the LORD says: Ask among the nations — who has ever heard anything like this? A most horrible thing the virgin of Israel has done.
Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave the rock of the field? Are those cool waters, flowing from far off, ever plucked up?
But my people have forgotten me; they burn offerings to a delusion. And they've made them stumble in their ways, the paths of old, to walk in bypaths, on a road no one has built,
making their land a waste, a perpetual hissing. Everyone who passes by will be appalled and shake his head.
Like an east wind I'll scatter them before the enemy. I'll show them my back and not my face on the day of their doom.

And they said: Come on, let's plan plans against Jeremiah. Law won't be lost from the priest, or counsel from the wise, or the word from the prophet. Come on — let's strike him with the tongue, and pay no attention to anything he says.
Be attentive to me, LORD; listen to the voice of those bringing a case against me.
Is evil what you get back for good? But they've dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your wrath back from them.

So give their children to famine; pour them out onto the hands of the sword. Let their wives be left childless and widowed; let their men be slain by death, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when you bring a raiding band on them suddenly — because they've dug a pit to capture me and hidden snares for my feet.

And you, LORD, know their whole plan against me — for my death. Don't make atonement for their iniquity; don't wipe out their sin from before you. Let them be overthrown before you; in the time of your anger, deal with them.

jeremiah_19.t: This is what the LORD said: Go and buy a potter's earthenware flask, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests;
and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words I speak to you.

And say: Hear the word of the LORD, kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem. Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to bring disaster on this place — the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.

Because they've abandoned me and made this place foreign, and burned offerings in it to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and filled this place with the blood of the innocent —
and they've built the high places of Baal, to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal — something I never commanded, never spoke of, that never came into my mind.
So days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called the Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

And I'll make void the plan of Judah and Jerusalem in this place. I'll make them fall by the sword before their enemies, by the hand of those who seek their life, and I'll give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
And I'll make this city a waste and a hissing; everyone who passes by will be appalled and hiss over all its wounds.

And I'll make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters; each will eat the flesh of his neighbour, in the siege and the distress their enemies press on them — those who seek their life.
Then break the flask in front of the men who go with you,

and say to them: Here's what the LORD of hosts says: This is how I'll shatter this people and this city — the way someone shatters a potter's vessel that can never be repaired. And they'll bury in Topheth, for lack of room to bury.
That's what I'll do to this place, declares the LORD, and to the people living in it — making this city like Topheth.

And the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be like the place of the Topheth — the unclean ones — all the houses on whose roofs they burned offerings to all the host of the heavens and poured out drink offerings to other gods.
Then Jeremiah came back from the Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the house of the LORD and said to all the people:

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to bring on this city and all its towns all the disaster I have spoken against it, because they've stiffened their neck so as not to hear my words.

jeremiah_20.t: Now Pashhur son of Immer the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
And Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, in the house of the LORD.
The next day Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks, and Jeremiah said to him: The LORD has not called your name Pashhur, but Terror All Around.

Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to make you a terror to yourself and to all who love you. They'll fall by the sword of their enemies while your own eyes watch. And all Judah I'll give into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he'll carry them into exile to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.

And I'll give all the wealth of this city, all its produce and all its precious things, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah I'll give into the hand of their enemies. They'll plunder them, take them, and carry them off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, and everyone living in your house will go into captivity. You'll come to Babylon, and there you'll die, and there you'll be buried — you and all who love you, the ones you prophesied falsehood to.
You deceived me, LORD, and I was deceived; you overpowered me, and you won. I've become a laughing-stock all day long; every one of them mocks me.
Every time I speak I have to cry out; "Violence and havoc!" is what I proclaim. The word of the LORD has become for me a reproach and derision all day long.
And if I say, "I won't remember him; I won't speak in his name any more," then it becomes a burning fire in my heart, shut up in my bones. I'm worn out holding it in, and I can't.

I hear the whispering of many — Terror All Around! — "Denounce him! Let's denounce him!" Every friend of mine watches for me to stumble: "Maybe he'll be deceived, and we'll prevail over him and take our vengeance on him."

But the LORD is with me like a ruthless warrior, so my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They'll be utterly shamed, because they won't succeed — a perpetual ignominy that will not be forgotten.
LORD of hosts, testing the righteous, seeing kidneys and heart — let me see your vengeance on them, because I've laid my case before you.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! He has delivered the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
Cursed be the day I was born! The day my mother bore me — let it never be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, saying, "A son is born to you — a boy!" — and made him so glad.
Let that man be like the cities the LORD overturned without relenting; let him hear a cry in the morning and an alarm at noon,
because he didn't kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and her womb pregnant for ever.
Why did I come out of the womb to see trouble and sorrow, and have my days end in shame?

jeremiah_21.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to him, saying:
Seek the LORD on our behalf, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is waging war against us. Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all his wonders, and he'll withdraw from us.
And Jeremiah said to them: This is what you're to say to Zedekiah:

Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to turn back the weapons of war in your hand, the ones you're fighting the king of Babylon with, and the Chaldeans besieging you outside the wall — and I'll gather them into the middle of this city.
And I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm — in anger, in wrath, in great rage.
And I'll strike down the inhabitants of this city, humankind and animals alike; they'll die of a great pestilence.

And after that, declares the LORD, I'll give Zedekiah king of Judah and his servants and the people — everyone left in this city after the pestilence, the sword and the famine — into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their life. He'll strike them down by the edge of the sword. He won't spare them; he won't show pity; he won't have compassion.
And say to this people: Here's what the LORD says: I'm setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine and pestilence; and whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans besieging you will live, and his life will be his as plunder.
I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he'll burn it with fire.
And to the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD.

House of David, here's what the LORD says: Administer justice every morning; deliver the robbed from the hand of the oppressor — or my wrath will break out like fire and burn with nobody to put it out, because of the evil of your deeds.
Look — I am against you, you who sit above the valley, rock of the plain, declares the LORD — you who say, "Who will come down on us? Who will get into our lairs?"
And I'll call you to account according to the fruit of your deeds, declares the LORD. I'll kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume everything around her.

jeremiah_22.t: This is what the LORD said: Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there,
and say: Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, sitting on the throne of David — you and your servants and your people who come in at these gates.

Here's what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness. Deliver the robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Don't maltreat the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow; don't treat them violently; don't shed innocent blood in this place.
If you really will do this, then kings will come in at the gates of this house, sitting for David on his throne, riding in chariots and on horses — he and his servants and his people.
But if you won't listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a ruin.
Here's what the LORD says about the house of the king of Judah: You are Gilead to me, the summit of Lebanon — and yet I will surely make you a wilderness, cities where no one lives.
And I'll set apart destroyers against you, each with his weapons; they'll cut down the choicest of your cedars and throw them on the fire.
And many nations will pass by this city, and each will say to his neighbour: Why did the LORD do this to this great city?
And they'll say: Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them.
Don't weep for the dead; don't show sympathy for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away — he will never come back to see the land of his birth.
Here's what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of Josiah his father, and who has gone out from this place: He'll never come back here;
because in the place where they've taken him into exile, that's where he'll die — and he won't see this land again.
Woe to the one who builds his house with no righteousness and his upper rooms with no justice, who makes his neighbour work for nothing and doesn't give him his wages;
who says, "I'll build myself a great house with spacious upper rooms," and cuts out windows for himself, panels it with cedar and paints it with vermilion.
Do you reign because you outdo everyone in cedar? Your father — didn't he eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? And then it went well with him.
He defended the cause of the poor and the needy, and then it went well. Isn't that what it is to know me? declares the LORD.
But your eyes and your heart are on nothing except your unjust gain, on shedding the blood of the innocent, on oppression and extortion — on doing it.

So here's what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They won't lament for him: "Alas, my brother!" "Alas, sister!" They won't lament for him: "Alas, lord!" "Alas, his splendour!"
He'll be buried with a donkey's burial — dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out; in Bashan raise your voice; cry out from Abarim — all your lovers are shattered.
I spoke to you when things were going well; you said, "I won't listen." This has been your way since you were young: you haven't listened to my voice.
The wind will shepherd all your shepherds; your lovers will go into captivity. Then you'll be ashamed and humiliated because of all your evil.
You who live in Lebanon, nested among the cedars — how you'll groan when the pangs come on you, anguish like a woman in labour!
As I live, declares the LORD — even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would pull you off.
And I'll give you into the hand of those who seek your life, into the hand of the ones you're afraid of, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
And I'll hurl you and your mother who bore you into another land, where you weren't born — and there you'll die.
And the land they long to return to — they will never return there.
Is this man Coniah a despised, smashed pot, a vessel nobody wants? Why have they been hurled out, he and his offspring, thrown into a land they don't know?
Land, land, land — hear the word of the LORD!
Here's what the LORD says: Record this man as childless, a man who won't prosper in his days — because none of his offspring will prosper, sitting on the throne of David and ruling over Judah again.

jeremiah_23.t: Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the flock of my pasture, declares the LORD.

So here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who shepherd my people: You've scattered my flock and driven them away, and you haven't attended to them. So I'm about to call you to account for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.
And I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I've banished them, and bring them back to their pasture; and they'll be fruitful and increase.
And I'll raise up shepherds over them who will shepherd them; they'll no longer be afraid or dismayed, and none will be missing, declares the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll raise up for David a righteous Branch. A king will reign and act prudently, and will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell in security. And this is the name he'll be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
So days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As the LORD lives, who brought up the people of Israel from the land of Egypt,"

but, "As the LORD lives, who brought up and who brought the offspring of the house of Israel from a land to the north and from all the lands where I banished them." And they'll dwell on their own soil.
Concerning the prophets: My heart is shattered inside me; all my bones tremble. I've become like a drunken man, like someone wine has overcome, because of the LORD and because of his holy words.
The land is full of adulterers; because of a curse the land mourns, and the wilderness pastures are dried up. Their course has turned evil, and their strength is not right.
Both prophet and priest are polluted; even in my house I've found their evil, declares the LORD.
So their way will become for them like slippery ground in the dark; they'll be driven on and fall in it. I'll bring disaster on them, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something offensive: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I've seen something horrible: committing adultery and walking in falsehood; they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns back from his evil. All of them have become to me like Sodom, her inhabitants like Gomorrah.

So here's what the LORD of hosts says about the prophets: I'm about to feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, because from the prophets of Jerusalem pollution has gone out to the whole land.

Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Don't listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They're filling you with worthless hopes. They speak the vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the LORD.
They keep telling those who despise me: "The LORD has spoken: You'll have peace." And to everyone walking in the stubbornness of his heart they say: "No disaster will come on you."
Who has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear his word? Who has paid attention to his word and listened?
Look — the storm of the LORD! Wrath has gone out, a whirling storm; it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.
The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and carried out the purposes of his heart. At the end of the days you'll understand it fully.
I didn't send the prophets, and they ran; I didn't speak to them, and they prophesied.
If they had stood in my council, they would have made my people hear my words, and turned them back from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
Am I a God who is near, declares the LORD, and not a God far off?
Can anyone hide himself away where I won't see him? declares the LORD. Do I not fill the heavens and the earth? declares the LORD.
I've heard what the prophets have said — the ones who prophesy falsehood in my name, saying: I've had a dream! I've had a dream!
How long? Is there anything in the heart of these prophets who prophesy falsehood, prophets of the deceit of their own heart —
who plan to make my people forget my name by the dreams they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot my name for Baal?
The prophet who has a dream, let him tell the dream; and the one who has my word, let him speak my word in faithfulness. What has straw to do with grain? declares the LORD.
Isn't my word like fire? declares the LORD — like a hammer that smashes rock?
So I'm against the prophets, declares the LORD — the ones who steal my words from one another.
I'm against the prophets, declares the LORD — the ones who take their own tongue and utter a declaration.

I'm against those who prophesy dreams of falsehood, declares the LORD, and tell them, and lead my people astray with their falsehoods and their recklessness. I didn't send them; I didn't command them; and they do this people no good at all, declares the LORD.
And when this people, or the prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the LORD?", say to them: "What burden?" And I will abandon you, declares the LORD.
And the prophet, the priest and the people who say, "The burden of the LORD" — I'll call that man and his house to account.
This is what you're to say to one another, each to his brother: What has the LORD answered? What has the LORD spoken?
And you're not to mention the burden of the LORD again — the burden is each man's own word; and you have overturned the words of the living God, the LORD of hosts, our God.
This is what you're to say to the prophet: What has the LORD answered you? What has the LORD spoken?

But if you do say, "The burden of the LORD" — then here's what the LORD says: Because you have spoken this word, "The burden of the LORD," when I sent to you saying, You are not to say, "The burden of the LORD" —
