therefore I will surely forget you and lift you up, and cast you away — you and the city I gave to you and your ancestors — from before my face.
And I'll put on you a perpetual reproach and a perpetual shame that will never be forgotten.

jeremiah_24.t: The LORD showed me: two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile, along with the officials of Judah and the craftsmen and the smiths, from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like first-ripe figs; the other had very bad figs, too bad to be eaten.
And the LORD said to me: What do you see, Jeremiah? I said: Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad — too bad to be eaten.
Then the LORD's word came to me:
Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, that's how I'll regard the exiles of Judah for good — the ones I sent from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I'll set my eye on them for good, and bring them back to this land. I'll build them and not tear them down; I'll plant them and not uproot them.
And I'll give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They'll be a people to me, and I'll be God to them, because they'll return to me with their whole heart.

And like the bad figs, too bad to be eaten — here's what the LORD says — that's what I'll make of Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials and the remnant of Jerusalem, those left in this land and those living in the land of Egypt.
And I'll make them a horror, an evil thing, to all the kingdoms of the earth — a reproach, a byword, a taunt and a curse in all the places where I banish them.
And I'll send sword, famine and pestilence against them, until they're finished off the soil I gave to them and their ancestors.

jeremiah_25.t: The word that came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah — the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon —
which Jeremiah the prophet spoke about all the people of Judah and to everyone living in Jerusalem:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, right up to today — twenty-three years now — the word of the LORD has come to me, and I've spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you haven't listened.
And the LORD sent you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them — and you didn't listen; you didn't incline your ear to listen.
saying: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from the evil of your deeds, and live on the soil the LORD gave you and your ancestors, from of old and for ever.
Don't go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them; don't provoke me to anger with the work of your hands — and I won't do you harm.
But you didn't listen to me, declares the LORD — provoking me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.
So here's what the LORD of hosts says: Because you haven't listened to my words,

I'm about to send for all the clans of the north, declares the LORD, and for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant; and I'll bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all these nations round about. I'll devote them to destruction and make them a waste, a hissing, perpetual ruins.
And I'll destroy among them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride, the sound of the hand-mill and the light of the lamp.
And this whole land will become a desolation and a waste, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

And when seventy years are completed, I'll call the king of Babylon and that nation to account, declares the LORD, for their iniquity — and the land of the Chaldeans too; and I'll make it perpetual desolations.
And I'll bring on that land all my words that I've spoken against it — everything written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
Many nations and great kings will make slaves of them too; and I'll repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands.
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand, and make all the nations I send you to drink it.
And they'll drink and stagger and behave like madmen, because of the sword I'm sending among them.
So I took the cup from the hand of the LORD and made all the nations he sent me to drink:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, her kings and her officials — to make them a ruin, a waste, a hissing and a curse, as they are today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people;
and all the mixed people, all the kings of the land of Uz, all the kings of the land of the Philistines — Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab and the Ammonites;
and all the kings of Tyre and Sidon, and the kings of the coastland beyond the sea;
Dedan, Tema and Buz, and all who have their temples clipped;
and all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mixed people living in the wilderness;
and all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media;
and all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground. And the king of Sheshach will drink after them.
And say to them: Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk and vomit; fall and don't get up — because of the sword I'm sending among you.
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them: Here's what the LORD of hosts says: You shall surely drink!

Look — in the city that bears my name I'm beginning to do harm; and are you to go completely unpunished? You will not go unpunished. I'm calling a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth, declares the LORD of hosts.

And you, prophesy all these words to them. Say to them: The LORD roars from on high; from his holy dwelling he gives forth his voice. He roars mightily over his habitation; he raises a shout like those who tread the winepress, against all the inhabitants of the earth.
An uproar has reached the end of the earth, because the LORD has a case against the nations; he is bringing all flesh to judgement. The wicked he has given to the sword, declares the LORD.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Disaster is going out from nation to nation, and a great storm is being roused from the far ends of the earth.
And the slain of the LORD on that day will lie from one end of the earth to the other. They won't be mourned or gathered or buried. They'll be dung on the face of the ground.
Wail, shepherds, and cry out; roll in ashes, you nobles of the flock! Your days for slaughter are complete, and your dispersions; and you'll fall like a precious vessel.
There'll be no place of escape for the shepherds, no escape for the nobles of the flock.
The sound of the shepherds crying out, the wailing of the nobles of the flock! The LORD is destroying their pasture,
and the peaceful pastures are devastated because of the burning of the LORD's anger.
He has left his lair like a young lion, because their land has become a waste because of the anger of the oppressor and because of the burning of his anger.

jeremiah_26.t: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:

This is what the LORD said: Stand in the court of the house of the LORD and speak to all the cities of Judah who come to bow down at the house of the LORD — all the words I've commanded you to speak to them. Don't hold back a word.
Perhaps they'll listen and turn back, each from his evil way — and then I'll relent over the disaster I'm planning to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.
And say to them: Here's what the LORD says: If you won't listen to me, and walk in my law that I've set before you,
and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I keep sending to you — rising early and sending them, and you haven't listened —
then I'll make this house like Shiloh, and I'll make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.
And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
And when Jeremiah had finished speaking everything the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him, saying: You shall surely die!

Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying: This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate, with nobody living in it? And all the people crowded round Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
And the officials of Judah heard about it, and they came up from the house of the king to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD.
And the priests and the prophets said to the officials and all the people: A sentence of death for this man! He has prophesied against this city, as you've heard with your own ears.
And Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people: The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words you've heard.
So now, make your ways and your deeds good, and listen to the voice of the LORD your God — and the LORD will relent over the disaster he has spoken against you.
As for me, here I am in your hand. Do to me whatever seems good and right to you.

Just know for certain that if you put me to death, you're bringing innocent blood on yourselves and on this city and on the people living in it — because in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing.
And the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets: There's no sentence of death for this man. He has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.
And some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of the people:

Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah: Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Zion will be ploughed like a field; Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins; and the mountain of the house a wooded high place.

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah actually put him to death? Didn't he fear the LORD and entreat the face of the LORD, so that the LORD relented over the disaster he had spoken against them? And here we are, about to do a great evil against our own lives.
There was another man prophesying in the name of the LORD — Uriah son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and against this land, in the same words as Jeremiah.
And King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, and the king sought to put him to death. Uriah heard about it, and he was afraid and fled to Egypt.
And King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt — Elnathan son of Achbor and men with him — to Egypt.
And they brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, and he struck him down with the sword and threw his corpse into the graves of the common people.
But the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.

jeremiah_27.t: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD said to me: Make yourself bonds and yoke-bars, and put them on your neck.

And send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre and the king of Sidon, by the hand of the messengers who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
And command them to say to their masters: Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says. This is what you're to say to your masters:
I myself made the earth, humankind and the animals on the face of the earth, by my great power and my outstretched arm — and I give it to whoever seems right in my eyes.
And now I myself have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I've given him the animals of the field as well, to serve him.
And all the nations will serve him, and his son and his son's son, until the time of his own land comes — and then many nations and great kings will make him serve.

And any nation or kingdom that won't serve him — Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — and won't put its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon: with sword and famine and pestilence I'll call that nation to account, declares the LORD, until I've finished them by his hand.
And as for you — don't listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreams, your soothsayers or your sorcerers, who tell you: You won't serve the king of Babylon.
They're prophesying falsehood to you, so as to remove you far from your own soil — and I'll drive you out, and you'll perish.
But the nation that brings its neck into the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I'll let stay on its own soil, declares the LORD, and it will work it and live on it.
And to Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke all these same words: Bring your necks into the yoke of the king of Babylon; serve him and his people, and live.
Why should you die, you and your people, by sword and famine and pestilence, as the LORD has spoken about the nation that won't serve the king of Babylon?
Don't listen to the words of the prophets who tell you: You won't serve the king of Babylon. They're prophesying falsehood to you.
I didn't send them, declares the LORD, and they're prophesying in my name to falsehood — so that I drive you out and you perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.

And to the priests and to all this people I said: Here's what the LORD says: Don't listen to the words of your prophets, who prophesy to you: The articles of the house of the LORD are about to be brought back from Babylon now, any day — they're prophesying falsehood to you.
Don't listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

If they really are prophets, and if the word of the LORD is with them, then let them entreat the LORD of hosts, so that the articles left in the house of the LORD and the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem don't go to Babylon.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says about the pillars, the sea, the stands, and the rest of the articles left in this city —
the ones Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says about the articles left in the house of the LORD and the house of the king of Judah and Jerusalem:
They'll be taken to Babylon, and there they'll stay until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD, and bring them up and bring them back to this place.

jeremiah_28.t: That year — at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month — Hananiah son of Azzur the prophet, who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD, in front of the priests and all the people:
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I'm bringing back to this place all the articles of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon.

And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon I'm bringing back to this place, declares the LORD — because I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, in front of the priests and in front of all the people standing in the house of the LORD —

and Jeremiah the prophet said: Amen! May the LORD do it. May the LORD carry out the words you've prophesied, and bring back the articles of the house of the LORD and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But listen now to this word that I'm about to speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets who came before me and before you, from of old, prophesied against many lands and great kingdoms — of war and disaster and pestilence.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace — when that prophet's word comes true, then the prophet will be known, the one the LORD has truly sent.
And Hananiah the prophet took the yoke-bar off the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

And Hananiah said in front of all the people: Here's what the LORD says: This is how I'll break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two years, from off the neck of all the nations. And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
Then the LORD's word came to Jeremiah, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke-bar off the neck of Jeremiah the prophet:
Go and say to Hananiah: Here's what the LORD says: You've broken yoke-bars of wood — and you'll make yoke-bars of iron in their place.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I've put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations, to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — and they will serve him. And I've given him the animals of the field as well.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet: Listen, Hananiah — the LORD did not send you, and you've made this people rely on falsehood.
So here's what the LORD says: I'm about to cast you off the face of the ground. This year you're to die, because you have spoken rebellion against the LORD.
And Hananiah the prophet died that year, in the seventh month.

jeremiah_29.t: These are the words of the letter Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders of the exile, and to the priests and the prophets and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon,
after Jeconiah the king and the queen mother and the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and the smiths had gone out from Jerusalem —
by the hand of Eleasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It said:
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I sent into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat their produce.
Take wives and father sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so they can bear sons and daughters. Multiply there; don't dwindle.
And seek the welfare of the city where I sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD for it — because in its welfare you'll have welfare.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Don't let your prophets among you, or your diviners, deceive you; and don't listen to the dreams you're dreaming.
They're prophesying falsehood to you in my name. I didn't send them, declares the LORD.
Here's what the LORD says: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I'll attend to you and carry out my good word for you, and bring you back to this place.
I myself know the plans I'm planning for you, declares the LORD — plans of well-being and not of harm, to give you a future and a hope.
And you'll call on me and come and pray to me, and I'll listen to you.
And you'll seek me and find me, when you seek me with your whole heart.

And I'll let myself be found by you, declares the LORD, and I'll restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and all the places where I've banished you, declares the LORD — and I'll bring you back to the place I sent you into exile from.
But you've said: The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.
Here's what the LORD says about the king who sits on the throne of David and about all the people living in this city — your brothers who didn't go into exile with you —
here's what the LORD of hosts says: I'm about to send sword, famine and pestilence against them, and make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

And I'll pursue them with sword, famine and pestilence, and make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth — a curse, a waste, a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I've banished them,
because they didn't listen to my words, declares the LORD, which I sent them by my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them — and you didn't listen either, declares the LORD.
So you, hear the word of the LORD — all you exiles I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying falsehood to you in my name: I'm about to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he'll strike them down before your eyes.
And from them a curse will be taken up by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon: May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire —

because they did folly in Israel and committed adultery with their neighbours' wives, and spoke a word in my name — falsehood — which I never commanded them. And I am the one who knows; I am a witness, declares the LORD.
And to Shemaiah the Nehelamite you're to say:

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest and to all the priests, saying:

The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be officers in the house of the LORD over every man who is mad and prophesies — and you're to put him in the stocks and the iron collar.
So now — why haven't you rebuked Jeremiah the Anathothite, who's prophesying to you?
That's why he has sent word to us in Babylon: It will be a long time. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their produce.
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter out in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the LORD's word came to Jeremiah:
Send word to all the exiles: Here's what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, and I didn't send him, and he has made you rely on falsehood —

so here's what the LORD says: I'm about to call Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring to account. He'll have no one left living among this people, and he won't see the good I'm doing for my people, declares the LORD — because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.

jeremiah_30.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Write down for yourself in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the LORD — and I'll bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they'll take possession of it.
And these are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
Here's what the LORD says: We've heard a sound of trembling — dread, and there is no peace.
Ask, and see: does a male give birth? Then why have I seen every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labour, and every face gone pale?
Woe! That day is great; there's none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob — and out of it he will be saved.
And on that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I'll break his yoke off your neck and tear apart your bonds, and strangers will no longer make him serve.
And they'll serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I'll raise up for them.

And you, don't be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD; don't be dismayed, Israel. I'm about to save you from far off, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and be undisturbed and at ease, with no one to frighten him.

I am with you, declares the LORD, to save you. I'll make a full end of all the nations among whom I scattered you — but of you I won't make a full end. I'll discipline you in due measure, and I certainly won't leave you unpunished.
Here's what the LORD says: Your shattering is incurable; your wound is severe.
There's no one to plead your cause, no remedy for the sore; there are no medicines of healing for you.
All your lovers have forgotten you; they don't care about you. I've struck you with an enemy's blow, the correction of a cruel one, because of the greatness of your iniquity; your sins are many.
Why do you cry out over your shattering? Your pain is incurable. Because of the greatness of your iniquity, because your sins are many, I have done these things to you.
So all who devour you will be devoured, and all your foes, every one, will go into captivity. Those who plunder you will become plunder; all who despoil you I'll make into spoil.
I'll make new flesh grow over you, and heal you of your wounds, declares the LORD, because they've called you an outcast: "That's Zion — nobody cares about her."

Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob; I'll have compassion on his dwellings. A city will be rebuilt on its mound, and a fortress will stand in its proper place.
Out of them will come thanksgiving and the sound of merrymakers. I'll multiply them and they won't dwindle; I'll make them honoured and they won't be counted as nothing.
His children will be as they were long ago; his congregation will be established before me; and I'll call to account all who oppress him.

His noble one will be one of his own; his ruler will come out from among him. I'll bring him near, and he'll draw near to me — for who else would pledge his heart to draw near to me? declares the LORD.
And you will be a people to me, and I will be God to you.
Look — the storm of the LORD! Wrath has gone out, a storm sweeping on; it will whirl down on the head of the wicked.
The burning of the LORD's anger won't turn back until he has done and carried out the purposes of his heart. At the end of the days you'll understand it.

jeremiah_31.t: At that time, declares the LORD, I'll be God to all the clans of Israel, and they'll be a people to me.
Here's what the LORD says: A people, the survivors of the sword, found favour in the wilderness when Israel went to find rest.
From far off the LORD appeared to me: I have loved you with an everlasting love; so I have prolonged steadfast love toward you.
Again I'll build you, and you'll be rebuilt, virgin of Israel. Again you'll deck yourself with your tambourines and go out in the dance of the merrymakers.
Again you'll plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; planters will plant, and enjoy the fruit themselves.
There will be a day when watchmen call out in the hill country of Ephraim: Up — let's go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!
Here's what the LORD says: Cry out with gladness for Jacob; shout for joy at the head of the nations! Proclaim it, praise, and say: Save your people, LORD — the remnant of Israel!

I'm about to bring them from the land of the north, and gather them from the far ends of the earth — among them the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labour together. A great company will return here.

They'll come with weeping; with pleas for mercy I'll bring them. I'll lead them to torrents of water, on a straight way where they won't stumble. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the LORD, you nations; declare it in the coastlands far off. Say: The one who scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock.
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

They'll come and cry out for joy on the height of Zion, radiant over the goodness of the LORD — over grain and new wine and fresh oil, over the young of the flock and the herd. Their life will be like a watered garden; they'll never languish again.
Then a virgin will rejoice in the dance, and young men and old together; and I'll turn their mourning into joy, and comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.
I'll satisfy the appetite of the priests with fatness, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness, declares the LORD.
Here's what the LORD says: A voice is heard in Ramah, a wailing, bitter weeping — Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because he is no more.
Here's what the LORD says: Hold back your voice from weeping, your eyes from tears — there is a reward for your work, declares the LORD, and they'll return from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and children will return to their own territory.
I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself: You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Turn me back, and I'll turn back — you are the LORD my God.
After I turned away, I was sorry; after I was made to know, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed, and humiliated too, because I bore the reproach of my youth.

Is Ephraim a dear son to me, a child of delight? As often as I speak against him, I still remember him. So my inward parts are in tumult for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares the LORD.
Set up signposts for yourself; place guideposts. Set your heart on the highway, the road you travelled. Return, virgin of Israel; return to these cities of yours!
How long will you waver, turning-away daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing in the land: a female will encompass a man.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Again they'll say this in the land of Judah and its cities, when I restore their fortunes: May the LORD bless you, abode of righteousness, holy mountain!
And Judah and all its cities will dwell there together — farmers and those who move about with the flock.
I'll give water to the weary throat, and fill every faint person.
At this I woke and looked around, and my sleep had been pleasant to me.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of humankind and the seed of animals.
And just as I watched over them to uproot and pull down, to overthrow and destroy and do harm, so I'll watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
In those days people will no longer say: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
Instead, each will die for his own iniquity. Every human being who eats the sour grapes will have his own teeth set on edge.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll cut a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah —

not like the covenant I cut with their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt — my covenant that they themselves broke, though I was a husband to them, declares the LORD.

This is the covenant I'll cut with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I'll put my law within them and write it on their heart; and I'll be God to them, and they'll be a people to me.

And they'll no longer teach one another, each his neighbour and each his brother, saying: Know the LORD! Because all of them will know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD — for I'll forgive their iniquity, and their sin I'll remember no more.

Here's what the LORD says — the one who gives the sun for light by day, the fixed orders of the moon and stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; the LORD of hosts is his name:
If these fixed orders ever depart from before me, declares the LORD, then the offspring of Israel too will cease from being a nation before me, for all time.

Here's what the LORD says: If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below explored, then I too will reject all the offspring of Israel for everything they've done, declares the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
And the measuring line will go out farther, straight ahead, to the hill of Gareb, then turn toward Goah.

And the whole valley of the corpses and the fatty ash, and all the terraced fields as far as the Wadi Kidron, as far as the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never be uprooted or overthrown again.

jeremiah_32.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah — the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, in the house of the king of Judah,

where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying: Why are you prophesying this? — This is what the LORD says: I'm about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he'll capture it;
and Zedekiah king of Judah won't escape from the hand of the Chaldeans; he'll surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he'll speak with him mouth to mouth and see him eye to eye;
and he'll take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he'll stay until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight the Chaldeans, you won't succeed.
And Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me:
Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you to say: Buy my field at Anathoth for yourself — the right of redemption is yours, so buy it.

And Hanamel my cousin came to me, just as the LORD had said, to the courtyard of the guard, and said: Buy my field at Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin — the right of possession is yours, and the redemption is yours. Buy it for yourself. And I knew this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field from Hanamel my cousin, the one at Anathoth, and weighed out the silver for him — seventeen shekels of silver.
I wrote in the document, sealed it, had witnesses attest it, and weighed the silver on scales.
And I took the document of purchase — the sealed one, with the terms and conditions, and the open one —

and I gave the document of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, in front of Hanamel my cousin, in front of the witnesses who had signed the document of purchase, and in front of all the Judeans sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
And in front of them all I commanded Baruch:

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these documents — this document of purchase, the sealed one and the open one — and put them in an earthenware jar, so they'll last a long time.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses and fields and vineyards will be bought again in this land.
And after I had given the document of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
Oh, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your outstretched arm. Nothing is too difficult for you —
who shows steadfast love to thousands and repays the iniquity of the ancestors into the bosom of their children after them — the great and mighty God; the LORD of hosts is his name,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, with your eyes open to all the ways of the children of humankind, to give to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds;
who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt — and to this day, in Israel and among humankind — and made a name for yourself, as it is today;
and you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm and great terror;
and you gave them this land, which you had sworn to their ancestors to give them — a land flowing with milk and honey;

and they came and took possession of it — but they didn't listen to your voice or walk in your law. Everything you commanded them to do, they didn't do. And you have made all this disaster happen to them.

Look — the siege mounds have reached the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans fighting against it, because of sword and famine and pestilence. What you spoke has happened, and you are seeing it.
And you yourself said to me, Lord GOD: Buy the field with silver and have witnesses attest it — and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans!
Then the LORD's word came to Jeremiah:
Look — I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too difficult for me?
So here's what the LORD says: I'm about to give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he'll capture it.

And the Chaldeans fighting against this city will come and set it on fire and burn it, along with the houses on whose roofs they burned offerings to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger.

The people of Israel and the people of Judah have done nothing but evil in my eyes from their youth; the people of Israel have done nothing but provoke me to anger with the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
This city has been a provocation of my anger and my wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I should remove it from before my face,

because of all the evil the people of Israel and the people of Judah did to provoke me to anger — they, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets, the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me, not their faces; and though I taught them, rising early and teaching them, they wouldn't listen or accept correction.
And they put their detestable things in the house that bears my name, making it unclean.

And they built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to make their sons and daughters pass over to Molech — something I never commanded them, that never came into my mind, to do this detestable thing and make Judah sin.
And now, therefore, here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about this city that you're saying has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword and famine and pestilence:
I'm about to gather them from all the lands where I've banished them in my anger and my wrath and great rage — and I'll bring them back to this place and let them live in security.
And they will be a people to me, and I will be God to them.
I'll give them one heart and one way, to fear me all their days — for their own good and their children's after them.
And I'll cut a perpetual covenant with them: that I won't turn back from following them, to do them good; and I'll put the fear of me in their heart, so they won't turn aside from me.
And I'll rejoice over them, to do them good; and I'll plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and with all my being.
Here's what the LORD says: Just as I brought all this great disaster on this people, so I'm bringing on them all the good I'm speaking about them.
And fields will be bought in this land — the land you say is a desolation, with no human being or animal in it, given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Fields will be bought with silver, and documents written and sealed and witnessed, in the land of Benjamin and around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, the cities of the hill country, the cities of the Shephelah and the cities of the Negev — because I'll restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_33.t: And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still shut up in the courtyard of the guard:
Here's what the LORD says — the one who made it, the LORD who formed it to establish it; the LORD is his name:
Call to me and I'll answer you, and I'll tell you great and inaccessible things you don't know.
Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, pulled down to make a defence against the siege mounds and the sword:

they are coming to fight the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of humankind, whom I struck down in my anger and my wrath — and I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil:
I'm about to make new flesh and healing grow over it, and I'll heal them; and I'll reveal to them an abundance of well-being and faithfulness.
And I'll restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and rebuild them as they were at first.
And I'll cleanse them from all the iniquity they sinned against me with, and forgive all their iniquities — the sinning and the rebelling against me.

And it will be to me a name of joy, a praise and a splendour, to all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good I'm doing for them. They'll be in awe and tremble at all the good and all the well-being I'm doing for it.

Here's what the LORD says: Again there will be heard in this place — the one you say is desolate, with no human being or animal — in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, made desolate, with no human being, no inhabitant, no animal —

the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride, the sound of people saying: Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good, for his steadfast love is for ever! — bringing a thank offering to the house of the LORD. Because I'll restore the fortunes of the land as they were at first, says the LORD.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Again in this place — desolate, without human being or even animal — and in all its cities, there will be a pasture of shepherds making their flocks lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah, the flocks will pass again under the hands of one who counts them, says the LORD.
Days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll carry out the good word I've spoken to the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I'll make a Branch of righteousness sprout for David, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will dwell in security. And this is what she will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
Here's what the LORD says: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel;
and the priests, the Levites, will never lack a man before me, offering up a burnt offering, burning a grain offering as smoke, and making a sacrifice, all the days.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah:
Here's what the LORD says: If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer came at their appointed time,
then my covenant with David my servant could also be broken, so that he had no son reigning on his throne — and my covenant with the Levites, the priests, my ministers.
As the host of the heavens can't be counted and the sand of the sea can't be measured, so I'll increase the offspring of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah:
Haven't you seen what this people are saying? — The two clans the LORD chose, he has rejected them. And so they spurn my people, as though they were no longer a nation in their sight.
Here's what the LORD says: If I have not established my covenant with day and night, the fixed orders of heaven and earth,

then I'll reject the offspring of Jacob and David my servant too, and not take rulers from his offspring for the offspring of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I'll restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.

jeremiah_34.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his whole army, and all the kingdoms of the earth under the rule of his hand, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities:

Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to Zedekiah king of Judah — say to him: Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he'll burn it with fire.

And you won't escape from his hand. You'll surely be captured and given into his hand. Your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon; his mouth will speak with your mouth; and you'll go to Babylon.
But hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah: Here's what the LORD says about you: You will not die by the sword.

You'll die in peace; and as with the burnings for your ancestors, the former kings before you, so they'll burn spices for you, and they'll lament for you: Alas, lord! For I myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.
And Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left — against Lachish and Azekah; these were the fortified cities still remaining among the cities of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had cut a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty to them:
that each should let his male slave and his female slave go free, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman — so that no one would make a slave of a Judean, his own brother.

And all the officials and all the people who had entered the covenant obeyed — that each should let his male slave and his female slave go free, and not make slaves of them again. And they obeyed, and let them go.
But afterwards they turned back and took back the male slaves and the female slaves they had let go free, and forced them back into slavery.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I myself cut a covenant with your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slaves:

At the end of seven years each of you is to let go his brother, the Hebrew who sells himself to you and serves you six years; you're to let him go free. But your ancestors didn't listen to me; they didn't incline their ear.
And you yourselves turned back today and did what is right in my eyes, proclaiming liberty each to his neighbour; and you cut a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.

But you turned back and profaned my name, and each took back his male slave and his female slave, the ones you'd let go free as they wished, and forced them back to be male slaves and female slaves for you.

So here's what the LORD says: You haven't listened to me, to proclaim liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbour. So I'm proclaiming liberty for you, declares the LORD — liberty to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I'll make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And the men who transgressed my covenant, who didn't carry out the words of the covenant they cut before me — the calf they cut in two and walked between its pieces — I'll make them
the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the court officials and the priests and all the people of the land, who walked between the pieces of the calf —
I'll give them into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their life; and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I'll give into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their life, into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon that has withdrawn from you.

I'm about to give the command, declares the LORD, and I'll bring them back to this city. They'll fight against it, capture it and burn it with fire. And the cities of Judah I'll make a waste, with nobody living there.

jeremiah_35.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them; bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink.
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites,

and brought them to the house of the LORD, to the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, beside the room of the officials and above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
And I set bowls full of wine, and cups, in front of the sons of the house of the Rechabites, and said to them: Drink wine.
And they said: We don't drink wine. Jonadab son of Rechab our ancestor commanded us: You are not to drink wine, you or your children, ever.
And don't build a house, don't sow seed, don't plant a vineyard or own one; live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the soil where you're sojourning.
And we've listened to the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab our ancestor, in everything he commanded us — not to drink wine all our days: we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,
and not to build houses to live in; and we have no vineyard, no field, no seed.
We've lived in tents, and we've obeyed and done everything Jonadab our ancestor commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said: Come, let's go to Jerusalem, because of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram. And that's why we're living in Jerusalem.
Then the LORD's word came to Jeremiah:
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the people of Judah and the people living in Jerusalem: Will you not accept correction and listen to my words? declares the LORD.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, who commanded his sons not to drink wine, have been carried out. They haven't drunk to this day, because they obeyed their father's commandment. But I myself have spoken to you, rising early and speaking — and you haven't listened to me.

And I sent you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way; make your deeds good; don't go after other gods to serve them — and live on the soil I gave you and your ancestors. But you didn't incline your ear; you didn't listen to me.
The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have carried out their father's commandment, the one he commanded them — but this people has not listened to me.

So here's what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to bring on Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster I've spoken against them — because I spoke to them and they didn't listen, and I called to them and they didn't answer.

And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said: Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have listened to the commandment of Jonadab your ancestor and kept all his commandments and done everything he commanded you,
therefore here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man standing before me, all the days.

jeremiah_36.t: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Take a scroll for yourself and write on it all the words I've spoken to you about Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, until today.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the harm I'm planning to do to them, and turn back, each from his evil way — and I'll forgive their iniquity and their sin.
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll, from Jeremiah's mouth, all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.
And Jeremiah commanded Baruch: I'm shut up. I can't go to the house of the LORD.

So you go and read from the scroll you've written from my mouth — the words of the LORD — in the hearing of the people, in the house of the LORD on a fast day; and read them in the hearing of all Judah, who come in from their cities.
Perhaps their supplication will fall before the LORD, and they'll turn back, each from his evil way — because the anger and the wrath the LORD has spoken against this people are great.
And Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading the words of the LORD from the scroll in the house of the LORD.

And in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, they proclaimed a fast before the LORD — all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came in from the cities of Judah.

And Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the scroll, in the house of the LORD, in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
And Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll.

And he went down to the house of the king, to the room of the scribe; and there all the officials were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah — all the officials.
And Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

And all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch: The scroll you read from in the hearing of the people — take it in your hand and come. And Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him: Sit down and read it in our hearing. And Baruch read it in their hearing.
And when they heard all the words, they were in dread, looking at one another, and they said to Baruch: We'll have to tell the king all these words.
And they asked Baruch: Tell us — how did you write all these words from his mouth?
And Baruch said to them: He proclaimed all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them on the scroll with ink.
And the officials said to Baruch: Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are.
And they went in to the king, into the court, having left the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe; and they told all the words in the king's hearing.
And the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll, and he fetched it from the room of Elishama the scribe; and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials standing beside the king.
And the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, with the fire-pot burning in front of him.

And each time Jehudi read three or four columns, he would cut them off with the scribe's knife and throw them into the fire in the fire-pot — until the whole scroll was consumed on the fire in the fire-pot.
And they weren't afraid, and they didn't tear their clothes — the king and all his servants who heard all these words.
And even Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had entreated the king not to burn the scroll — but he wouldn't listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD hid them.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned the scroll and the words Baruch had written from Jeremiah's mouth:
Take another scroll for yourself and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, the one Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah, say: Here's what the LORD says: You yourself burned this scroll, saying: Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and make human being and animal cease from it?
So here's what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He'll have no one to sit on the throne of David; and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and the frost by night.

And I'll call him and his offspring and his servants to account for their iniquity; and I'll bring on them and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the people of Judah all the disaster I've spoken against them — and they didn't listen.

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the document Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire — and many more words like them were added.

jeremiah_37.t: And Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim; Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made him king in the land of Judah.
But he didn't listen — he or his servants or the people of the land — to the words of the LORD that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet: Pray for us now to the LORD our God.
Now Jeremiah was coming and going among the people; they hadn't put him in the prison house.
Now Pharaoh's army had come out of Egypt, and the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the report of it and withdrew from Jerusalem.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah the prophet:

Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: This is what you're to say to the king of Judah, who is sending you to me to consult me: Pharaoh's army that came out to help you is about to go back to its own land, Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will come back and fight against this city, capture it and burn it with fire.
Here's what the LORD says: Don't deceive yourselves, saying: The Chaldeans will surely leave us. They won't go.
Even if you struck down the whole Chaldean army fighting against you, and only wounded men were left, each in his tent, they would get up and burn this city with fire.
And when the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to take possession of a portion there among the people.
And he was at the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a captain of the guard named Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah. He arrested Jeremiah the prophet, saying: You're deserting to the Chaldeans!
And Jeremiah said: That's a falsehood! I'm not deserting to the Chaldeans. But he wouldn't listen. Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
And the officials were angry at Jeremiah and beat him, and they put him in the house of fetters — the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had made into the prison house.
So Jeremiah went into the house of the cistern, into the cells, and stayed there many days.

And King Zedekiah sent and had him brought, and questioned him in his house, in secret: Is there a word from the LORD? And Jeremiah said: There is. And he said: You'll be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah: How have I sinned against you, or your servants, or this people, that you've put me in the prison house?
And where are your prophets, the ones who prophesied to you: The king of Babylon won't come against you or against this land?
And now hear me, my lord the king: let my supplication fall before you. Don't send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, or I'll die there.

And King Zedekiah gave the order, and they placed Jeremiah in the courtyard of the guard; and a round loaf of bread was given him every day from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

jeremiah_38.t: And Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:
Here's what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by sword, famine and pestilence; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live — his life will be his as plunder, and he will live.
Here's what the LORD says: This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he'll capture it.

And the officials said to the king: Let this man be put to death. He's weakening the hands of the fighting men left in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking words like these to them. This man isn't seeking this people's welfare, but their harm.
And King Zedekiah said: Look — he's in your hand. The king can do nothing against you.

And they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, in the courtyard of the guard, letting him down with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud — and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin.
And Ebed-melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king:

My lord the king, these men have done evil in everything they've done to Jeremiah the prophet, throwing him into the cistern. He'll die where he is, because of the famine — there's no more bread in the city.
And the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite: Take thirty men from here with you, and bring Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies.

And Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the house of the king, to a place under the storehouse, and took worn-out clothes and worn-out rags from there, and let them down to Jeremiah in the cistern with ropes.
And Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah: Put the worn-out clothes and rags under your armpits, under the ropes. And Jeremiah did so.
And they drew Jeremiah out with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern; and Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

And King Zedekiah sent and had Jeremiah the prophet brought to him, to the third entrance in the house of the LORD. And the king said to Jeremiah: I'm asking you something. Don't hide anything from me.
And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: If I tell you, won't you have me put to death? And if I give you counsel, you won't listen to me.
And King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret: As the LORD lives, who made this life for us — I won't put you to death, and I won't give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life.

And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: Here's what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you'll go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then your life will be spared, this city won't be burned with fire, and you'll live, you and your household.
But if you don't go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they'll burn it with fire — and you won't escape from their hand.
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: I'm afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans — they might hand me over to them, and they'd deal wantonly with me.
And Jeremiah said: They won't hand you over. Listen to the voice of the LORD, to what I'm telling you, and it will go well for you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what the LORD has shown me:

And look — all the women left in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, and they're saying: They misled you and prevailed over you, those you trusted; your feet are sunk in the mire, and they've turned back.

And all your wives and your children they'll bring out to the Chaldeans; and you won't escape from their hand — you'll be captured by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire.
And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: Let no one know about these words, and you won't die.

And if the officials hear that I've spoken with you, and they come and say: Tell us what you said to the king; don't hide it from us, and we won't put you to death — and what did the king say to you? —
then say to them: I was laying my supplication before the king, asking him not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.
And all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he told them exactly what the king had commanded; and they said nothing more to him, because the conversation had not been overheard.
And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. And when Jerusalem was captured —

jeremiah_39.t: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his whole army came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the city was breached.

And all the officials of the king of Babylon came and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebu, Sarsekim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

And when Zedekiah king of Judah and all the fighting men saw them, they fled — they went out of the city by night, by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls; and he went out toward the Arabah.

And the Chaldean army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah at Riblah before his eyes; and all the nobles of Judah the king of Babylon slaughtered.
And he blinded Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze fetters to take him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the house of the king and the house of the people with fire, and pulled down the walls of Jerusalem.

And the rest of the people left in the city, and the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the people who were left, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards carried into exile to Babylon.
But some of the poor people, who had nothing, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields that day.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon gave orders concerning Jeremiah, by the hand of Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards:
Take him and keep your eye on him. Do him no harm at all — do with him exactly as he tells you.
So Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards sent — he and Nebushazban the Rab-saris and Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag and all the chiefs of the king of Babylon;
and they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him home. And he stayed among the people.
Now the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah while he was shut up in the courtyard of the guard:

Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to bring my words against this city for harm and not for good, and they'll happen before your eyes on that day.
But I'll deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you won't be given into the hand of the men you're afraid of.
I will surely rescue you; you won't fall by the sword. Your life will be yours as plunder, because you trusted in me, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_40.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards set him free from Ramah — when he took him, bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah being carried off to Babylon.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Jeremiah and said to him: The LORD your God spoke this harm against this place,
and the LORD has brought it and done exactly what he said. You sinned against the LORD and didn't listen to his voice — and this is what has happened to you.

And now, look — I've set you free today from the chains on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I'll keep my eye on you; and if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, then don't. Look, the whole land is before you. Go wherever it seems good and right to you to go.

And while he still hadn't turned back — Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever seems right to you. And the chief of the bodyguards gave him a food allowance and a present, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

And all the commanders of the armies out in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and had put in his charge men and women and little ones, and some of the poor of the land — those who hadn't been carried off to Babylon.

And they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite — they and their men.
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men: Don't be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.
As for me, I'm staying at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans when they come to us. You gather wine and summer fruit and oil, put them in your vessels, and live in the cities you've taken hold of.

And all the Judeans in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom and in all the lands heard that the king of Babylon had given a remnant to Judah, and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over them.
And all the Judeans came back from all the places where they'd been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah; and they gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies out in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
and said to him: Do you know for certain that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you down and take your life? But Gedaliah son of Ahikam didn't believe them.

And Johanan son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah: Let me go and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah — no one will know. Why should he take your life, and all the Judeans who have gathered to you be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish?
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah: Don't do this. You're speaking falsehood about Ishmael.

jeremiah_41.t: And in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama — of the royal offspring, one of the chiefs of the king — came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. And they were eating bread there together at Mizpah.

And Ishmael son of Nethaniah got up, and the ten men with him, and they struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword — and he killed the man the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there — the fighting men — Ishmael struck down.
And on the second day after the killing of Gedaliah, before anyone knew,

men came from Shechem, from Shiloh and from Samaria — eighty men, their beards shaven, their clothes torn, and having gashed themselves — with a grain offering and frankincense in their hand, to bring to the house of the LORD.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went; and when he met them he said: Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
And when they came into the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them into the middle of the cistern — he and the men with him.
But ten men among them said to Ishmael: Don't kill us — we have hidden stores in the field: wheat and barley and oil and honey. And he held back and didn't kill them along with their brothers.

And the cistern where Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had struck down alongside Gedaliah — it was the one King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people at Mizpah — the daughters of the king and all the people left at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him heard all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
And they took all the men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him at the great waters in Gibeon.
And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him, they were glad.
And all the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned round; they turned back and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men from Johanan and went to the Ammonites.

And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him took all the rest of the people he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah — after Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam — men, the fighting men, and women and little ones and court officials, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they went and stayed at Geruth Kimham, beside Bethlehem, intending to go on into Egypt,
because of the Chaldeans — they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

jeremiah_42.t: And all the commanders of the armies came forward, with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to Jeremiah the prophet: Let our supplication fall before you. Pray for us to the LORD your God, for all this remnant — because we are left a few out of many, as your own eyes can see.
And let the LORD your God tell us the way we should go and what we should do.
And Jeremiah the prophet said to them: I've heard you. I'm going to pray to the LORD your God as you ask; and every word the LORD answers you, I'll tell you. I won't withhold a word from you.
And they said to Jeremiah: May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we don't act on every word the LORD your God sends you to us with.
Whether it's good or bad, we'll listen to the voice of the LORD our God, the one we're sending you to — so that it may go well for us, because we'll listen to the voice of the LORD our God.
And at the end of ten days the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
And he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says — the one you sent me to, to lay your supplication before him:
If you will stay in this land, then I'll build you and not tear you down, plant you and not uproot you — for I relent over the harm I've done to you.
Don't be afraid of the king of Babylon, the one you're afraid of. Don't be afraid of him, declares the LORD — I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
And I'll grant you compassion, and he'll have compassion on you and restore you to your own soil.
But if you say: We won't stay in this land — refusing to listen to the voice of the LORD your God —
saying: No — we'll go to the land of Egypt, where we won't see warfare or hear the sound of the ram's horn or go hungry for bread; and we'll live there —
then hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you do set your faces to go to Egypt, and go to sojourn there,
then the sword you're afraid of will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you're anxious about will follow hard after you there in Egypt — and there you'll die.
And all the men who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by sword, famine and pestilence. They'll have no survivor, no escapee, from the disaster I'm bringing on them.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You'll become an execration and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and you won't see this place again.
The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Don't go to Egypt. Know for certain that I have warned you today.
You have gone astray at the cost of your lives. You yourselves sent me to the LORD your God, saying: Pray for us to the LORD our God, and whatever the LORD our God says, tell us, and we'll do it.
And I've told you today — and you haven't listened to the voice of the LORD your God, or to anything he sent me to you with.
So now, know for certain: you'll die by sword, famine and pestilence in the place you want to go and sojourn.

jeremiah_43.t: And when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God, which the LORD their God had sent him to them with — all these words —

Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah: You're speaking falsehood! The LORD our God did not send you to say: You are not to go to Egypt to sojourn there.
It's Baruch son of Neriah inciting you against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans, to put us to death and carry us into exile to Babylon.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies and all the people didn't listen to the voice of the LORD, to stay in the land of Judah.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took all the remnant of Judah — those who had come back from all the nations where they'd been driven, to sojourn in the land of Judah —

the men, the women, the little ones and the daughters of the king, and every person Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan — and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
And they went to the land of Egypt, because they didn't listen to the voice of the LORD; and they came to Tahpanhes.
And the LORD's word came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the mortar, in the brick terrace at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in front of Judean men,

and say to them: Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to send and fetch Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I'll set his throne above these stones I have hidden; and he'll spread his canopy over them.
And he'll come and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; those for the sword, to the sword.

And I'll kindle fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; he'll burn them and carry them off. He'll pick the land of Egypt clean the way a shepherd picks his garment clean, and he'll go out from there in peace.
And he'll shatter the pillars of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and burn the houses of the gods of Egypt with fire.

jeremiah_44.t: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt — at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Memphis and in the land of Pathros:
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You yourselves have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah. Today they're a ruin, with nobody living in them,
because of the evil they did, provoking me to anger by going to burn offerings and serve other gods they had never known — they, and you, and your ancestors.
And I sent you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them: Don't do this abominable thing, which I hate.
But they didn't listen; they didn't incline their ear, or turn back from their evil and stop burning offerings to other gods.
And my wrath and my anger poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as they are today.

And now, here's what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great harm to your own lives, cutting off from among you man and woman, child and infant, out of the midst of Judah, and leaving yourselves no remnant —

provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, burning offerings to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you've come to sojourn — cutting yourselves off, and making yourselves a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
