Have you forgotten the evils of your ancestors, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of his wives, and your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they haven't been humbled; they haven't feared; they haven't walked in my law and my statutes that I set before you and your ancestors.
So here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm setting my face against you for harm, to cut off all Judah.

And I'll take away the remnant of Judah, who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to sojourn there. They'll all meet their end in the land of Egypt. They'll fall by the sword; by famine they'll meet their end, from the least to the greatest; by sword and famine they'll die, and they'll become an execration, a horror, a curse and a reproach.
And I'll call to account those living in the land of Egypt, just as I called Jerusalem to account — by sword, famine and pestilence.

And there'll be no escapee, no survivor, for the remnant of Judah who went to sojourn in the land of Egypt — none to return to the land of Judah, which they long to go back to and live in. They won't return, except as fugitives.

And all the men who knew that their wives were burning offerings to other gods, and all the women standing by — a great company — and all the people living in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
As for the word you've spoken to us in the name of the LORD — we're not going to listen to you.

We're going to do everything that has come out of our own mouth: burn offerings to the queen of the heavens and pour out drink offerings to her, as we did — we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials — in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. We had plenty of bread; we were well off; we saw no disaster.
But since we stopped burning offerings to the queen of the heavens and pouring out drink offerings to her, we've lacked everything, and by sword and famine we've met our end.

And when we were burning offerings to the queen of the heavens and pouring out drink offerings to her — was it without our husbands that we made cakes for her, shaped in her image, and poured out drink offerings to her?
And Jeremiah said to all the people — the men and the women and all the people who had answered him:

Wasn't it the offerings of smoke you burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem — you and your ancestors, your kings and your officials and the people of the land — that the LORD remembered, that came into his mind?

And the LORD could no longer endure it, because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations you did; and your land has become a ruin, a waste and a curse, with nobody living in it, as it is today.

Because you burned offerings, and because you sinned against the LORD and didn't listen to the voice of the LORD, and didn't walk in his law and his statutes and his testimonies — that's why this disaster has come on you, as it is today.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women: Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives — you spoke with your mouths and fulfilled it with your hands, saying: We'll surely perform the vows we vowed, to burn offerings to the queen of the heavens and pour out drink offerings to her. Then go ahead — carry out your vows! Perform your vows!

So hear the word of the LORD, all Judah living in the land of Egypt: I have sworn by my great name, says the LORD: My name will never again be named in the mouth of any man of Judah, saying: As Lord GOD lives! — anywhere in the land of Egypt.
I'm watching over them for harm and not for good; and every man of Judah in the land of Egypt will meet his end by sword and famine, until they're finished.

And a few escapees of the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah who went to the land of Egypt to sojourn there will know whose word stands — mine or theirs.
And this will be the sign for you, declares the LORD, that I'm about to call you to account in this place — so that you'll know my words will surely stand against you for harm:

Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, into the hand of those who seek his life — just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.

jeremiah_45.t: The word Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll from Jeremiah's mouth, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Here's what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
You said: Woe to me — the LORD has added sorrow to my pain! I'm worn out with my groaning, and I've found no rest.
This is what you're to say to him: Here's what the LORD says: What I have built I'm tearing down; what I have planted I'm uprooting — and that means the whole land.
And you — are you seeking great things for yourself? Don't seek them. I'm about to bring disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD — but I'll give you your life as plunder, wherever you go.

jeremiah_46.t: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Get buckler and shield ready; draw near for battle!
Harness the horses; mount up, horsemen! Take your stand in your helmets; polish the spears; put on the armour!
Why do I see it? They're terrified, turning back; their warriors are crushed. They've fled in headlong flight and haven't turned round — terror all around! declares the LORD.
Let the swift not flee; let the warrior not escape! Northward, beside the river Euphrates, they've stumbled and fallen.
Who is this that rises like the Nile, whose waters surge like the rivers?
Egypt rises like the Nile; its waters surge like the rivers. And it said: I will rise, I will cover the earth; I'll destroy the city and everyone living in it.
Go up, horses; drive madly, chariots! Let the warriors go out — Cush and Put, who wield the shield, and the Ludites, who wield and bend the bow.

And that day belongs to Lord GOD of hosts — a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword will devour and be satisfied, and drink its fill of their blood; because Lord GOD of hosts has a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter of Egypt! You've multiplied remedies for nothing; there's no healing for you.
The nations have heard your shame; your outcry has filled the earth. Warrior has stumbled against warrior; both of them have fallen together.
The word the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Announce it in Egypt; proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes! Say: Take your stand and get ready — the sword has devoured all around you.
Why have your mighty ones been swept away? They didn't stand — the LORD pushed them down.
He has made many stumble; each one has fallen against his neighbour. And they said: Up — let's go back to our own people, to the land of our birth, because of the sword of the oppressor.
They have called out there: Pharaoh king of Egypt is nothing but noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.
As I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts — surely, like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel by the sea, he will come.
Pack your baggage for exile, you who live there, daughter of Egypt! Memphis will become a waste, laid desolate, with nobody living in it.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer — and a gadfly from the north is coming, coming.

Her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves — they too have turned and fled together; they haven't stood their ground. The day of their doom has come on them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound goes like a serpent's; for they come with an army, and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.
They've cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it can't be searched out — because they're more numerous than locusts, beyond number.
The daughter of Egypt is put to shame, given into the hand of the people of the north.
The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to call to account Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods and her kings — Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

And I'll give them into the hand of those who seek their life, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. But afterwards it will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.

And you, don't be afraid, my servant Jacob; don't be dismayed, Israel. I'm about to save you from far off, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and be undisturbed and at ease, with no one to frighten him.

You, don't be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD — I am with you. I'll make a full end of all the nations where I've driven you; but of you I won't make a full end. I'll discipline you in due measure, and I certainly won't leave you unpunished.

jeremiah_47.t: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Here's what the LORD says: Waters are rising from the north, and they'll become an overflowing torrent; they'll overflow the land and everything in it, the city and everyone living in it. The people will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail
at the sound of the stamping hooves of his stallions, at the rattling of his chariotry, the din of his wheels. Fathers haven't turned back for their children — their hands hang slack —

because of the day that's coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every surviving helper. The LORD is devastating the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
Baldness has come on Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. Remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?
Oh, sword of the LORD! How long until you're quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest, and be still.
How can it be quiet, when the LORD has given it its orders? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast — that is where he has sent it.

jeremiah_48.t: Concerning Moab. Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo — it's devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.
Moab's praise is gone. In Heshbon they've planned calamity against her: Come, let's cut her off from being a nation! You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will come after you.
A sound of crying from Horonaim: devastation and great ruin!
Moab is broken; her little ones have made their crying heard.
On the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping as they climb; and on the descent of Horonaim they've heard the anguish of the cry of ruin.
Flee! Save your lives! Be like a bush in the wilderness!
Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too will be captured; and Chemosh will go into exile, with his priests and his officials together.
A devastator will come to every city, and no city will escape; the valley will perish and the plain be destroyed, just as the LORD has said.
Give a ṣiṣ to Moab, for she will surely go out in flight; her cities will become a waste, with no one living in them.
Cursed is the one who does the LORD's work slackly, and cursed is the one who holds back his sword from blood!
Moab has been at ease since he was young, left to settle on his lees; he has never been poured from jar to jar, never gone into exile. So his taste has stayed in him, and his aroma hasn't changed.
So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll send him men who tip, and they will tip him; they'll empty his vessels and smash their jars.
And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, the way the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, the thing they trusted.
How can you say: We're warriors, fighting men, ready for battle?
Moab is devastated; her cities have been stormed, and his finest young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
Moab's doom is close, and his calamity is coming fast.
Grieve for him, all of you around him, all of you who know his name! Say: How the staff of strength is broken, the rod of splendour!
Come down from your honour and sit in the dust of thirst, you who live there, daughter of Dibon! The devastator of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer! Ask the man fleeing and the woman escaping; say: What has happened?
Moab is put to shame — shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce at the Arnon that Moab is devastated.
And judgement has come to the land of the plain — to Holon, to Jahzah, against Mephaath,
against Dibon, against Nebo, against Beth-diblathaim,
against Kiriathaim, against Beth-gamul, against Beth-meon,
against Kerioth, against Bozrah, and against every city in the land of Moab, far and near.
Moab's horn is cut off; his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
Make him drunk, because he made himself great against the LORD; and Moab will sprawl in his own vomit, and he too will become a laughing-stock.
Wasn't Israel a laughing-stock to you? Was he caught among thieves, that every time you spoke of him you shook your head?
Leave the cities and live in the rock, you who live in Moab! Be like a dove nesting on the sides of a ravine's mouth.
We've heard about Moab's pride — how very proud he is — his haughtiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the loftiness of his heart.
I myself know his insolence, declares the LORD — it is not right; his empty boasts have accomplished nothing right.
So I'll wail over Moab; I'll cry out for all Moab; for the people of Kir-heres there is groaning.
I'll weep for you more than Jazer weeps, vine of Sibmah! Your tendrils crossed the sea; they reached the sea of Jazer. On your summer fruit and your vintage a devastator has fallen.
Joy and gladness are taken away from the garden-land and from the land of Moab; I've made the wine stop flowing from the winepresses. No one will tread with the shout; the shout will be no shout.
From the cry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have raised their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim, Eglath-shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim will become wastes.
And I'll put an end for Moab, declares the LORD, to anyone who offers up at a high place and anyone who burns offerings to his gods.
So my heart groans for Moab like flutes; my heart groans like flutes for the people of Kir-heres; and so the wealth he gathered has perished.
Every head is shaved bald, every beard clipped; there are gashes on every hand, and sackcloth round the waist.
On every roof in Moab and in her open squares there's wailing everywhere; for I've shattered Moab like a vessel no one delights in, declares the LORD.
How shattered it is! They wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughing-stock and a thing of terror to everyone around him.
For here's what the LORD says: Someone will swoop like the eagle and spread his wings against Moab.
Kerioth is captured; the strongholds are seized; and on that day the heart of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
And Moab will be destroyed as a people, because he made himself great against the LORD.
Terror and pit and snare are on you, you who live in Moab, declares the LORD.

Whoever runs from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare; because I'll bring on her, on Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.

In the shadow of Heshbon those who flee have stopped, with no strength left; for a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the midst of Sihon, and it has devoured the forehead of Moab and the crown of the head of the sons of uproar.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh has perished; your sons have been taken captive, and your daughters taken captive.
But I'll restore the fortunes of Moab in the days to come, declares the LORD. That is as far as the judgement of Moab goes.

jeremiah_49.t: Concerning the sons of Ammon. Here's what the LORD says: Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Then why has Milcom dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?

So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll sound the shout of battle against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon; and it will become a mound of desolation, and her daughter-towns will be set on fire. And Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the LORD.
Wail, Heshbon — Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, mourn, run to and fro among the walls; for Milcom will go into exile, with his priests and his officials together.
Why do you boast about your valleys — your valley flowing away, you turning-away daughter, trusting in your treasures and saying: Who will come against me?
I'm about to bring terror on you, declares Lord GOD of hosts, from everyone around you; and you'll be driven out, each one straight ahead, with no one to gather the fugitive.
But afterwards I'll restore the fortunes of the sons of Ammon, declares the LORD.
Concerning Edom. Here's what the LORD of hosts says: Is there no wisdom left in Teman? Has counsel perished from those who understand? Has their wisdom gone rotten?
Flee, turn back, go deep down to hide, you who live in Dedan! For I've brought Esau's doom on him, the time when I called him to account.
If grape-pickers came to you, wouldn't they leave some gleanings? If thieves came at night, they'd only take as much as they wanted.
I myself have stripped Esau bare; I've uncovered his hiding-places, and he can't hide. His offspring is devastated, and his brothers and his neighbours, and he is gone.
Leave your fatherless children — I'll keep them alive myself. And let your widows trust in me.
Here's what the LORD says: Those whose sentence was not to drink the cup will certainly drink it — and are you the one who gets off entirely? You won't get off. You will certainly drink.
By myself I swear, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a waste, a reproach, a desolation and a curse; and all her cities will become everlasting ruins.
I've heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: Gather yourselves and come against her; rise up for battle!
I've made you small among the nations, despised among people.

The horror you inspire has deceived you, the presumption of your heart — you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I'll bring you down, declares the LORD.
And Edom will become a horror. Everyone who passes by will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.
Like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbours, says the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will settle in her.

Like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; in a moment I'll drive him away from her, and I'll appoint over her whoever is chosen. For who is like me? Who will summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

So hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counselled against Edom, and the purposes he has purposed against the people of Teman: the little ones of the flock will surely be dragged away; their pasture will surely be made desolate over them.
At the sound of their fall the earth quakes; the outcry — its sound is heard as far as the Sea of Reeds.
Like the eagle he will go up and swoop, spreading his wings over Bozrah; and on that day the heart of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labour.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame — they've heard a bad report; they melt away. In the sea there is anxiety; it cannot be quiet.
Damascus has gone limp; she's turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pains have gripped her, like a woman giving birth.
How is the city of praise not abandoned, the town of my joy?
So her young men will fall in her open squares, and all her fighting men will be silenced that day, declares the LORD of hosts.
And I'll kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will devour the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Here's what the LORD says: Arise, go up against Kedar, devastate the sons of the east!
Their tents and their flocks will be taken; their tent-curtains, all their equipment and their camels will be carried off; and they'll call out over them: Terror all around!
Flee, get far away, go deep down to hide, you who live in Hazor, declares the LORD! For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counselled counsel against you and purposed a purpose against you.
Arise, go up against a nation at ease, living in security, declares the LORD, with no gates and no bars; they live alone.
Their camels will become spoil, and all their livestock plunder; and I'll scatter to every wind those who have their temples clipped, and from every side I'll bring their doom, declares the LORD.
And Hazor will become a lair of jackals, desolate for ever; no one will live there; no human being will settle in her.
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: I'm about to break the bow of Elam, the chief of their strength.
And I'll bring against Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I'll scatter them to all these winds; there will be no nation the outcasts of Elam don't reach.

And I'll shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life; and I'll bring calamity on them, the burning of my anger, declares the LORD. And I'll send the sword after them until I've made an end of them.
And I'll set my throne in Elam, and destroy king and officials from there, declares the LORD.
And in the days to come, I'll restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.

jeremiah_50.t: The word the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet.

Announce it among the nations and proclaim it; lift up a standard; proclaim it, don't hide it! Say: Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame, Marduk is shattered; her images are put to shame, her idols are shattered.
For a nation has come up against her from the north; it will make her land a waste, and no one will live in her. From human being to animal, they've fled; they've gone.
In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Judah together; they will go along weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.
They'll ask the way to Zion, their faces set that way: Come, let's join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.
My people have become lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray; on the mountains they've turned them away. From mountain to hill they've gone; they've forgotten their resting-place.
Everyone who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said: We're not guilty — because they sinned against the LORD, the habitation of righteousness, the hope of their fathers, the LORD.
Take flight out of Babylon; go out from the land of the Chaldeans; be like he-goats leading the flock.

I'm about to rouse and bring up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north; they'll draw up against her — from there she'll be captured. His arrows are like a skilled warrior's; he doesn't come back empty.
And Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will have their fill, declares the LORD.
Because you rejoice, because you gloat, you plunderers of my inheritance; because you skip about like a threshing heifer and neigh like stallions —
your mother is utterly put to shame; she who bore you is disgraced. Look — the last of the nations: a wilderness, a parched land, a desert plain.
Because of the rage of the LORD she won't be inhabited; she'll be wholly desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and will hiss over all her wounds.
Draw up against Babylon on every side, all you who bend the bow! Shoot at her; spare no arrow — she has sinned against the LORD.

Shout against her on every side! She has given her hand in surrender; her towers have fallen, her walls are torn down. This is the vengeance of the LORD: take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the oppressor, each will turn back to his own people; each will flee to his own land.
Israel is a scattered sheep that lions have driven off. The first devoured him — the king of Assyria; and this last one has gnawed his bones — Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
So here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I'm about to call the king of Babylon and his land to account, just as I called the king of Assyria to account.
And I'll bring Israel back to his own pasture, and he'll graze on Carmel and Bashan; and in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead he'll eat his fill.

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the iniquity of Israel will be looked for and there will be none, and the sins of Judah, and they won't be found; for I'll forgive those I leave as a remnant.
Against the land of Merathaim — go up against her, and against the people of Pekod! Slay and utterly destroy them, declares the LORD, and do everything I've commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land — and great ruin.
How the hammer of all the earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
I set a snare for you, Babylon, and you were caught, and you didn't know it. You were found and seized, because you took on the LORD.
The LORD has opened his armoury and brought out the weapons of his indignation; for Lord GOD of hosts has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come at her from the farthest end; open her granaries; pile her up in heaps and destroy her utterly; leave her no remnant.
Slay all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them — their day has come, the time of their punishment.
A sound of fugitives and escapees from the land of Babylon, coming to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for his temple!

Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow! Encamp against her on every side; let no one escape from her. Repay her for what she did; according to all she has done, do to her. Because she has been presumptuous against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her open squares, and all her fighting men will be silenced that day, declares the LORD.
I am against you, Arrogance, declares Lord GOD of hosts — your day has come, the time when I call you to account.
And Arrogance will stumble and fall, with no one to raise him up; and I'll kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour everything around him.
Here's what the LORD of hosts says: The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah with them; all their captors have kept hold of them and refused to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name. He will certainly take up their case, to give rest to the earth and to disquiet the people of Babylon.
A sword against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD, and against the people of Babylon, and against her officials and her wise men!
A sword against the empty talkers, and they'll become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they'll be shattered!
A sword against his horses and his chariotry, and against all the mixed people among them, and they'll become women! A sword against her treasuries, and they'll be plundered!
A drought against her waters, and they'll dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and over their dread things they act like madmen.
So desert creatures will live there with hyenas, and ostriches will live in her. She'll never be inhabited again, never settled, from generation to generation.
Like the overthrow by God of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbours, declares the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will settle in her.
A people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will be roused from the remotest parts of the earth.
Bow and javelin they take hold of; they are cruel, and show no mercy. Their sound roars like the sea; they ride on horses, drawn up as one man for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Distress has gripped him, anguish like a woman giving birth.

Like a lion he will come up from the thicket of the Jordan to the ever-flowing pasture; in a moment I'll drive them away from her, and I'll appoint over her whoever is chosen. For who is like me? Who will summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

So hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counselled against Babylon, and the purposes he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: the little ones of the flock will surely be dragged away; their pasture will surely be made desolate over them.
At the sound of the cry Babylon is captured! — the earth quakes, and an outcry is heard among the nations.

jeremiah_51.t: Here's what the LORD says: I'm about to rouse against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-qamai a destroying wind.
And I'll send winnowers to Babylon, and they'll winnow her and empty out her land; for they'll be against her from every side on the day of calamity.
Let no archer bend his bow; let no one rise up in his armour! Don't spare her young men; utterly destroy all her army.
The slain will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, those run through, in her streets.
Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God, the LORD of hosts — though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
Flee out of Babylon; each of you save your own life! Don't be destroyed for her iniquity — this is a time of vengeance for the LORD; he is repaying her what she deserves.
Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; that's why the nations act like madmen.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen, broken. Wail over her! Fetch balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she wasn't healed. Leave her; let each of us go to his own land. Her judgement has reached to the heavens; it has been lifted up to the clouds.
The LORD has brought out our vindication. Come, let's tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done!

Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers! The LORD has roused the spirit of the kings of Media, because his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her; this is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for his temple.
Against the walls of Babylon lift up a standard! Strengthen the watch; post watchmen; set the ambushes! For the LORD has both purposed and done what he spoke concerning the people of Babylon.
You who live by many waters, rich in treasures: your end has come, the measure of your cutting off.
The LORD of hosts has sworn by himself: I will surely fill you with men like locusts, and they'll raise the shout over you.
He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.

At the sound of his giving forth, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens; he makes clouds rise from the end of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every human is stupid, without knowledge; every metalsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his molten image is a fraud, and there is no breath in them.
They are vapour, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment they will perish.
Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed everything; and the tribe of his inheritance — the LORD of hosts is his name.
You are my war-club, my weapons of war; with you I smash nations, with you I destroy kingdoms.
with you I smash horse and rider, with you I smash chariot and driver;
with you I smash man and woman, with you I smash old and young, with you I smash young man and virgin;
with you I smash shepherd and flock, with you I smash farmer and team, with you I smash governors and officials.
And I'll repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion before your eyes, declares the LORD.
I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD — you who destroy all the earth! I'll stretch out my hand against you and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain.
And no one will take a stone from you for a corner or a stone for foundations, for you'll be everlasting wastes, declares the LORD.

Lift up a standard in the land; blow a horn among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. Appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like a bristling swarm of locusts.
Consecrate nations against her: the kings of Media, their governors and all their officials, and every land under their rule.
The land quakes and writhes, because the LORD's purposes against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a waste, with no one living in it.
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they sit in the strongholds. Their strength has dried up; they've become women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
Runner runs to meet runner, messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is captured from end to end,
that the fords are seized, the reed-marshes burned, and the fighting men are terrified.
Here's what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it's trodden. A little while longer, and her harvest time will come.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has thrown me into confusion; he has set me down an empty jar. He has swallowed me like the sea-monster; he has filled his belly with my delicacies; he has rinsed me out.
The violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babylon — she who lives in Zion will say. And my blood be on the inhabitants of Chaldea — Jerusalem will say.
So here's what the LORD says: I'm about to take up your case, and I will take vengeance for you; I'll dry up her sea and make her spring dry.
And Babylon will become heaps of stones, a lair of jackals, a horror and a hissing, with no one living there.
Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.
When they're heated I'll set out their drinking-feast, and I'll make them drunk, so that they exult; and they'll sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake, declares the LORD.
I'll bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he-goats.
How Sheshach is captured, the praise of all the earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has gone up over Babylon; she is covered by the tumult of its waves.
Her cities have become a waste, a parched land and a desert plain, a land where no one lives and no human being passes through.
And I'll call Bel to account in Babylon, and I'll bring out of his mouth what he swallowed; and the nations will no longer stream to him. The wall of Babylon has fallen too.
Come out of her, my people; each of you save your own life from the burning of the LORD's anger!

Don't let your heart grow faint, and don't be afraid at the report that's heard in the land; for the report will come in one year, and after it the report in the next year, and violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.
So the days are coming when I'll call to account the carved images of Babylon; all her land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
And heaven and earth and everything in them will shout for joy over Babylon; for from the north the destroyers will come against her, declares the LORD.
Babylon too must fall for the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen for Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go — don't stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind.
We are put to shame — we have heard the reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, because strangers have come into the holy places of the house of the LORD.
So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I'll call to account her carved images; and throughout her land the fatally wounded will groan.
Even if Babylon climbed to the heavens, even if she fortified her stronghold on high, destroyers would come against her from me, declares the LORD.
A sound of crying from Babylon, great ruin from the land of the Chaldeans!
For the LORD is devastating Babylon, silencing in her the great voice; and their waves roar like many waters; the uproar of their voice goes out.
A devastator has come against her, against Babylon; her warriors are captured; their bows are broken. For the LORD is a God of recompense — he will certainly repay.

And I'll make her officials and her wise men, her governors and her officers and her warriors drunk; and they'll sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.

Here's what the LORD of hosts says: The broad walls of Babylon will be utterly demolished, and her high gates burned with fire; peoples labour for nothing, nations for fire — and they wear themselves out.
The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was quartermaster.
And Jeremiah wrote all the calamity that would come on Babylon in a single scroll — all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you get to Babylon, see that you read aloud all these words,
and say: LORD, you yourself have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off, so that no one will live in it, from human being to animal — it will be everlasting desolations.
And when you've finished reading this scroll aloud, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
and say: So Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the calamity that I'm bringing on her — and they will grow weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

jeremiah_52.t: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
It came about because of the anger of the LORD against Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his whole army against Jerusalem; they encamped against it and built a siege-wall around it.
And the city stayed under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine in the city was severe, and there was no food for the people of the land.

The city was broken into; and all the fighting men fled and went out of the city by night, through the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden — the Chaldeans were all around the city — and they went by way of the Arabah.
And the Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and his whole army scattered from him.
They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.
And the king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, and slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah too.
He blinded Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze fetters; and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and kept him in the prison-house until the day he died.

In the fifth month, on the tenth of the month — the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the house of the LORD and the house of the king and all the houses of Jerusalem; he burned every great house.
And the whole Chaldean army that was with the chief of the bodyguards broke down all the walls around Jerusalem.

And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile some of the poorest of the people, the rest of the people left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the artisans.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards left behind some of the poorest of the land, to be vinedressers and ploughmen.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the LORD, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the LORD; and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
And they took away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the basins and the pans, and all the bronze vessels used in the service.
And the chief of the bodyguards took away the bowls, the fire-pans, the basins, the pots, the lampstands, the pans and the libation-bowls — what was gold as gold, and what was silver as silver.
The two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD — the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.
As for the pillars: one pillar stood eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits went round it; it was four fingers thick, and hollow.
A bronze capital was on it; the one capital was five cubits high, with a network and pomegranates around it, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with pomegranates.
There were ninety-six pomegranates to a side; the pomegranates on the network all around came to one hundred.
And the chief of the bodyguards took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.

From the city he took one court official who was an officer over the fighting men, seven men from those who saw the king's face, who were found in the city, the scribe of the army commander, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found inside the city.
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
These are the people Nebuchadnezzar took into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Judeans;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, from Jerusalem, eight hundred and thirty-two persons;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the chief of the bodyguards took into exile seven hundred and forty-five Judean persons. In all, four thousand six hundred persons.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of the prison-house.
And he spoke kindly to him and set his seat above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed out of his prison clothes, and he ate at his table continually, all the days of his life.
And his allowance — a continual allowance — was given him by the king of Babylon, a day's portion each day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

job_1.t: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright; he feared God and turned aside from evil.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

His livestock was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and a very large household of servants. That man was greater than all the people of the east.
His sons used to hold a feast, each in his own house on his own day, and they'd send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

And when the round of feast days was over, Job would send and set them apart as holy, rising early in the morning and offering up burnt offerings for the whole number of them; for Job said, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and cursed God in their heart." This is what Job did continually.
Now the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came among them too.
The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" And Satan answered the LORD, "From roving about on the earth, from walking up and down on it."
And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There's none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns aside from evil."
And Satan answered the LORD, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
Haven't you yourself put a hedge around him and his house and everything he has, on every side? You've blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out over the land.
But stretch out your hand now and touch everything he has — see if he doesn't curse you to your face!"
And the LORD said to Satan, "Everything he has is in your hand; only don't stretch out your hand against him." So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
Now the day came when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house.
And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were ploughing and the female donkeys grazing beside them,
and Sabeans fell on them and carried them off, and put the servants to the sword. I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
He was still speaking when another came and said, "The fire of God fell from the heavens, burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them. I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."

He was still speaking when another came and said, "Chaldeans formed three companies, raided the camels and carried them off, and put the servants to the sword. I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house,
and a great wind came in off the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house. It fell on the young people and they died. I alone have escaped, only I, to tell you."
Then Job got up, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground and bowed down.
And he said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I shall return there. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken. May the name of the LORD be blessed."
In all this Job did not sin, and he did not charge God with anything unseemly.

job_2.t: Now the day came when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came among them too, to present himself before the LORD.
And the LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" And Satan answered the LORD, "From roving about on the earth, from walking up and down on it."

And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There's none like him on the earth — a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns aside from evil. And still he holds fast to his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without cause."
And Satan answered the LORD, "Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has for his life.
But stretch out your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh — see if he doesn't curse you to your face!"
And the LORD said to Satan, "He is in your hand; only preserve his life."
So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with malignant boils, from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
He took a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
And his wife said to him, "Are you still holding fast to your integrity? Curse God and die."
But he said to her, "You're speaking as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we accept the good from God and not accept the evil?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

Now Job's three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, and each came from his own place — Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite. They met together by appointment to come and show him sympathy and comfort him.
When they lifted their eyes from a distance they did not recognise him, and they lifted up their voice and wept. Each tore his robe, and they sprinkled dust on their heads toward the heavens.
And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

job_3.t: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
And Job answered and said:
Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, "A man has been conceived."
That day — let it be darkness. Let God above not seek it out; let no daylight shine on it.
Let darkness and deep darkness reclaim it; let a cloud settle over it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
That night — let gloom seize it; let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not enter the number of the months.
That night — let it be barren; let no cry of joy come into it.
Let those who curse the day damn it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.
Let the stars of its twilight go dark; let it hope for light and find none; let it never see the eyelids of dawn —
because it did not shut the doors of the womb I came from or hide trouble from my eyes.
Why did I not die at birth, come out from the belly and expire?
Why did knees receive me? Why were there breasts for me to suck?
For now I'd be lying down at peace; I'd have slept, and there would be rest for me,
with kings and counsellors of the earth who rebuilt ruins for themselves,
or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
Or I would not have been at all, like a hidden miscarriage, like infants who never saw light.
There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary of strength are at rest.
Together the prisoners are at ease; they do not hear the taskmaster's voice.
Small and great are there, and a slave is free from his master.
Why is light given to a sufferer, and life to the bitter in spirit —
who long for death and it does not come, who dig for it more than for hidden treasure;
those who rejoice, who exult, who are glad when they find the grave.
to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in.
My groaning comes before my bread; my roarings pour out like water.
The fear I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has come to me.
I am not at ease, not at peace, not at rest — and turmoil has come.

job_4.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
If someone ventures a word to you, will you be impatient? But who can hold back from speaking?
See — you have instructed many; you have strengthened slack hands.
Your words have raised up those who stumble; you have made firm the buckling knees.
But now it comes to you and you're impatient; it touches you and you're dismayed.
Isn't your fear of God your confidence, your hope the integrity of your ways?
Remember: who that was innocent ever perished? Where were the upright destroyed?
As I've seen it: those who plough iniquity and sow trouble reap the same.
By the breath of God they perish; by the blast of his anger they come to an end.
The roaring of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions — broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the lioness's whelps are scattered.
Now a word was brought to me by stealth, and my ear caught a whisper of it.
In disquieting thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
fear came over me, and trembling, and it set all my bones shaking.
And a spirit passed over my face; it made the hair of my flesh stand up.
It stood still, but I couldn't recognise its appearance; a form was before my eyes. There was silence, and I heard a voice:
"Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be clean before his Maker?"
See — he doesn't trust his servants; he charges his angels with error;
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth!
Between morning and evening they're shattered; with no one giving it a thought, they perish for ever.
Is their tent-cord not pulled up within them? They die, and not in wisdom.

job_5.t: Call now — is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy slays the simple.
I myself have seen a fool taking root, and suddenly I pronounced his dwelling cursed.
His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, with no one to deliver them.
Whose harvest the hungry eat, taking it even out of the thorns, while a snare pants after their wealth.
For hardship does not come out of the dust, and trouble does not spring up from the ground;
for a human is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
But as for me, I would seek God, and lay my case before God.
who does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond number;
who gives rain on the face of the earth and sends water over the open fields;
to set the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
who frustrates the plans of the shrewd, so that their hands achieve nothing.
who catches the wise in their own shrewdness, and the counsel of the twisted is swept away.
By day they meet darkness; at noon they grope as if it were night.
But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth, and from the hand of the strong.
So there is hope for the poor, and injustice shuts its mouth.
See how blessed is the mortal whom God reproves — so do not reject the discipline of the Almighty,
for he wounds and he binds up; he shatters, and his own hands heal.
In six troubles he'll deliver you; in seven, no harm will touch you.
In famine he'll ransom you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
You'll be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and you won't fear destruction when it comes.
At destruction and hunger you'll laugh, and you need not fear the wild animals of the earth.
For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the wild animals of the field will be at peace with you.
And you'll know that your tent is at peace; you'll inspect your fold and find nothing missing.
And you'll know that your offspring are many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
You'll come to the grave in full vigour, like a shock of grain brought in at its season.
See — this we have searched out, and so it is. Hear it, and know it for yourself.

job_6.t: And Job answered and said:
If only my vexation were truly weighed, my calamity laid with it in the balances!
It would outweigh the sand of the seas — that's why my words have been rash.
The arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison; the terrors of God are drawn up against me.
Does a wild donkey bray over grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg?
I refuse to touch them; they are like sickness in my food.
Who will grant that my petition come, that God give me what I hope for?
That God would be willing to crush me, that he would loose his hand and cut me off!
And this would still be my comfort — I'd exult in unsparing anguish — that I have not concealed the sayings of the Holy One.
What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should prolong my life?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
Is there no help within me? Has sound wisdom been driven from me?
The despairing is owed kindness from his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have been as treacherous as a wadi, like the bed of wadis that pass away —
dark with ice, the snow hiding itself in them;
The moment they grow warm, they fall silent; in the heat they vanish from their place.
The paths of their course wind about; they go up into the waste and perish.
The caravans of Tema looked for them; the travelling companies of Sheba hoped.
They were ashamed because they'd been confident; they came there and were disappointed.
For now you've become just that to me; you see something terrifying and you're afraid.
Is it because I said, "Give me something"? Or "Out of your wealth pay a bribe for me"?
Or "Rescue me from an adversary's hand, ransom me from the hand of the ruthless"?
Teach me, and I'll be silent; make me understand where I've erred.
How painful honest sayings are! But what does your reproof prove?
Do you plan to reprove mere words, and treat a despairing man's sayings as wind?
You'd even cast lots over an orphan, and bargain over your own friend.
And now be willing — turn and look at me. I would not lie to your faces.
Turn back, please; let there be no injustice. Turn back again — my righteousness still stands in this.
Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not tell what is ruinous?

job_7.t: Isn't there hard service for a mortal on earth? Aren't his days like a hired labourer's days?
like a slave panting for shade, like a hired labourer waiting for his wages —
so I've been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of trouble apportioned to me.
When I lie down I say, "When will I get up?" But the evening drags on, and I have my fill of tossing until twilight.
My flesh is clothed with maggots and caked with dirt; my skin closes up and then breaks out afresh.
My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
Remember that my life is a breath; my eye will not return to see good.
The eye that sees me will not behold me; your eyes will be on me, and I'll be gone.
A cloud is spent and gone; so the one who goes down to Sheol does not come up.
He never returns again to his house, and his place no longer recognises him.
So I won't restrain my mouth. I'll speak in the distress of my spirit; I'll complain in the bitterness of my being.
Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a watch over me?
When I say, "My couch will comfort me, my bed will carry away my complaint,"
then you dismay me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
so that I would choose strangling, death rather than this frame of mine.
I've had enough — I won't live for ever. Let me alone; my days are a breath.
What is a mortal, that you make so much of him, that you set your heart on him,
and visit him every morning, test him every moment?
How long will you not look away from me, or let me alone long enough to swallow my spittle?
If I have sinned, what do I do to you, watcher of humankind? Why have you made me your target, so that I've become a burden to myself?
And why do you not lift away my transgression and make my iniquity pass? For soon I'll lie down in the dust, and you'll seek me, and I'll be gone.

job_8.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long will you say such things, and let the sayings of your mouth be a mighty wind?
Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert righteousness?
If your children sinned against him, he gave them over into the hand of their transgression.
If you yourself will seek God and plead for favour from the Almighty,
if you are pure and upright, surely he will rouse himself for you now and restore your righteous abode.
And though your beginning was small, your latter end will grow very great.
Ask the former generation; give attention to what their fathers searched out.
For we are of yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are a shadow.
Won't they teach you and tell you, and bring forth words out of their heart?
Does papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Does reed-grass grow without water?
While it's still green and uncut, it withers before any other plant.
Such are the paths of all who forget God; the hope of the godless perishes,
whose confidence is fragile, whose trust is a spider's house.
He leans on his house, and it doesn't stand; he takes hold of it, and it doesn't endure.
He is a well-watered plant in the sun, his shoot spreading over his garden.
His roots are interwoven over a heap of rocks; he finds a place among the stones.
If he's swallowed up from his place, then it denies him: "I never saw you."
See — that is the joy of his way, and from the dust others spring up.
See — God does not reject a blameless man, and does not take the hand of evildoers.
until he fills your mouth with laughter, your lips with a shout of joy.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.

job_9.t: And Job answered and said:
Truly I know that it is so — but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
If anyone wanted to contend with him, he couldn't answer him once in a thousand times.
Wise of heart and mighty in strength — who has hardened himself against him and come out unharmed?
who moves mountains and they don't know it, who overturns them in his anger;
who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars shudder;
who speaks to the sun and it doesn't rise, who seals up the stars;
who alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the high places of the Sea;
who makes the Bear, Orion and the Pleiades, and the chambers of the south;
who does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond number.
See — he passes by me and I don't see him; he moves on and I don't perceive him.
See — he snatches away; who can turn him back? Who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
God does not turn back his anger; beneath him the helpers of Rahab lay prostrate.
How much less can I answer him, or pick my words to argue with him!
Though I were in the right, I couldn't answer him; I'd have to plead for favour with my judge.
If I called and he answered me, I wouldn't believe he was listening to my voice —
he who crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He won't let me get my breath back; he fills me to surfeit with bitterness.
If it's a matter of strength — he is the mighty one! And if of justice — who will summon him?
Though I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; blameless as I am, it would declare me perverse.
I am blameless — I don't care about myself. I reject my life.
It's all one — therefore I say: he brings the blameless and the wicked alike to an end.
When a scourge kills suddenly, he mocks at the despair of the innocent.
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it isn't he, then who is it?
My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away and have seen no good.
They've passed on like ships of reed, like an eagle swooping on its food.
If I say, "I'll forget my complaint, I'll change my expression and cheer up,"
then I dread all my pains; I know you won't hold me innocent.
I'll be counted guilty — so why should I labour in vain?
If I washed myself in snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
then you'd plunge me into the pit, and my own clothes would abhor me.
For he is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could come to trial together.
There is no arbiter between us who might lay his hand on us both.
Let him take his rod off me, and let his terror not dismay me.
Then I'd speak and not fear him — for that is not how I am in myself.

job_10.t: I loathe my life. I'll give free rein to my complaint; I'll speak in the bitterness of my being.
I will say to God: Do not condemn me. Make known to me why you contend with me.
Does it do you good to oppress, to reject the labour of your own hands and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
Are your days like a mortal's days, or your years like a man's days,
that you seek out my iniquity and search for my sin,
though you know that I am not guilty, and there's no one to deliver out of your hand?
Your hands shaped me and made me, every part of me — and now you swallow me up.
Remember that you made me like clay — and will you return me to dust?
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh, knitted me together with bones and sinews.
Life and steadfast love you have shown me, and your care has kept my spirit.
Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was your purpose all along.
If I sinned, you'd be watching me, and you would not acquit me of my iniquity.
If I'm guilty — woe to me! And if I'm in the right, I still can't lift my head, sated with shame, looking on my affliction.
And if it rises up, you hunt me like a lion, and you turn again and show yourself marvellous against me.
You bring fresh witnesses against me and increase your vexation with me; relief troops and an army come at me.
So why did you bring me out from the womb? I'd have expired, and no eye would have seen me.
I'd have been as though I had never been, carried from the womb to the grave.
Aren't my days few? Then stop. Turn away from me, so I can be cheerful a little,
before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deep darkness,
a land of gloom like darkness, of deep darkness with no order, where the light itself is like darkness.

job_11.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
Shall a flood of words go unanswered? Shall a man of mere talk be acquitted?
Shall your empty talk silence men? Shall you mock with no one to shame you?
For you've said, "My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes."
But if only God would speak and open his lips against you!
and tell you the secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom has two sides — and know this: God is overlooking part of your iniquity.
Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you reach the limit of the Almighty?
Higher than the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than Sheol — what can you know?
Its measure is longer than the earth, broader than the sea.
If he passes by, shuts a man up and calls an assembly, who can turn him back?
For he knows men of falsehood; when he sees iniquity, will he not take note?
A hollow man will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born a human.
If you set your heart right and spread out your hands to him,
if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away; don't let injustice dwell in your tents,
then you'll lift up your face without blemish; you'll be firmly established and unafraid.
You'll forget your trouble; you'll remember it like waters gone by.
Your life will rise brighter than noon; though it grow dark, it will be like morning.
You'll be secure, because there is hope; you'll look about you and lie down in safety.
You'll lie down with no one to frighten you, and many will seek your favour.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail; all escape will perish from them, and their hope is the last gasp of life.

job_12.t: And Job answered and said:
No doubt you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
I have a mind like yours; I don't fall short of you. Who doesn't know such things as these?
I am a laughingstock to my friend — I called on God and he answered me — a laughingstock: the righteous, the blameless man.
Contempt for misfortune, in the mind of one at ease; a shove for those whose foot is slipping.
The tents of destroyers are at peace; those who provoke God are secure — whoever carries his god in his hand.
But ask the animals, and let them teach you; ask the birds of the heavens, and let them tell you;
or speak to the earth, and let it teach you; let the fish of the sea recount it to you.
Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all human flesh.
Doesn't the ear test words, as the palate tastes its food?
With the aged is wisdom; in length of days, understanding.
With him are wisdom and might; counsel and understanding are his.
See — he tears down, and it is not rebuilt; he shuts a man in, and there is no opening.
See — he holds back the waters and they dry up; he lets them go and they overturn the earth.
With him are strength and sound wisdom; both the deceived and the deceiver are his.
He leads counsellors away stripped, and makes fools of judges.
He loosens the bond of kings and ties a loincloth on their loins.
He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the long-established.
He takes the speech from the trusted, and the discernment from the elders.
He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the mighty.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep darkness out into the light.
He makes nations great and destroys them; he spreads nations out and leads them away.
He takes the understanding from the leaders of the people of the earth, and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
They grope in darkness with no light, and he makes them stagger like a drunkard.

job_13.t: See — my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard it and understood.
What you know, I know too; I don't fall short of you.
But I would speak to the Almighty; I want to argue my case with God.
But you are plasterers of lies; you are all worthless physicians.
If only you'd be completely silent — that would be wisdom in you.
Hear my argument now, and attend to the contentions of my lips.
Will you speak unrighteousness for God, and deceit on his behalf?
Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?
Would it go well if he examined you? Or will you deceive him as you would deceive a mortal?
He will surely rebuke you if you secretly show partiality.
Won't his majesty terrify you, and his dread fall on you?
Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defences are defences of clay.
Be silent, leave me alone, and let me speak — and let come on me what may.
Why do I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my own hand?
See, he will kill me; in him I will hope — yet I will argue my ways to his face.
This too will be my deliverance: that no godless man can come before him.
Listen carefully to my speech; let my declaration be in your ears.
See now — I've set out my case. I know that I am in the right.
Who is there who will contend with me? If there is, I'll be silent and die.
Only two things — don't do them to me, and then I won't hide from your face.
Take your hand far away from me, and let your dread not terrify me.
Then call, and I'll answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make known to me my transgression and my sin.
Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
Will you terrify a driven leaf and chase dry chaff?
For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you score a mark around the soles of my feet.
And a man wears out like something rotten, like a garment eaten by a moth.

job_14.t: A human, born of a woman, is short of days and full of turmoil.
Like a flower he comes up and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not last.
Yet on such a one you open your eye, and you bring me to trial with you.
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one.
Since his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you've set limits he cannot pass —
look away from him and let him rest, until like a hired labourer he can enjoy his day.
For there is hope for a tree: if it's cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoot won't fail.
Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the dust,
at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a new plant.
But a man dies and is laid low; a human breathes his last — and where is he?
Waters vanish from the sea, and a river dries up and is parched;
so a man lies down and doesn't rise; till the heavens are no more they won't awake, or be roused out of their sleep.
If only you'd hide me in Sheol, conceal me until your anger turns back, set me a term and remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait, until my relief came.
You would call and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
For then you'd count my steps, but you wouldn't keep watch over my sin.
My transgression would be sealed up in a bag, and you'd plaster over my iniquity.
But a falling mountain crumbles away, and a rock is moved from its place;
waters wear away stones; their torrents wash away the dust of the earth — and so you destroy a mortal's hope.
You overpower him for ever and he goes; you change his face and send him away.
His sons are honoured, and he doesn't know it; they are brought low, and he doesn't perceive it.
Only his own flesh feels pain for him, and his own being mourns for him.

job_15.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Does a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill his belly with the east wind?
arguing with talk that does no good, with words nobody profits by?
You yourself annul the fear of God and diminish devotion before God.
Your iniquity instructs your mouth; you choose the tongue of the crafty.
Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.
Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you listen in on God's council and keep wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we don't know? What do you understand that isn't with us?
Both the grey-haired and the aged are among us, older in days than your father.
Are God's consolations too little for you, and a word spoken gently to you?
Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
that you turn your spirit against God and let such words out of your mouth?
What is a mortal, that he should be pure — one born of a woman, that he should be in the right?
See — he doesn't trust his holy ones, and the heavens aren't pure in his eyes;
how much less one abhorrent and corrupt, a man who drinks unrighteousness like water!
I'll declare it to you — listen to me — and what I have seen I'll recount:
what wise men have told and not hidden — received from their fathers,
to whom alone the land was given, and among whom no stranger passed:
All his days the wicked man writhes in pain — the number of years stored up for the ruthless.
The sound of terrors is in his ears; in time of peace the destroyer comes on him.
He doesn't believe he'll return from darkness; he is marked out for the sword.
He wanders about for bread — where is it? He knows a day of darkness is ready at hand.
Anxiety and distress terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle.
For he stretched out his hand against God and acted proudly against the Almighty;
he charges at him with a stiff neck, behind the thick bosses of his shields.
For he has covered his face with his fat and made rolls of fat on his loins.
He settled in ruined cities, in houses where no one lives, houses destined to become heaps of stones.
He won't be rich; his wealth won't endure; his possessions won't spread over the earth.
He won't escape from darkness; a flame will wither his shoot, and he'll depart by the breath of God's mouth.
Let him not trust in emptiness — he's deceived; for emptiness will be his recompense.
It will be paid in full before his day, and his palm branch will not stay green.
He'll shake off his unripe grapes like a vine, cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
They conceive trouble and give birth to iniquity; their belly prepares deceit.

job_16.t: And Job answered and said:
I've heard plenty like this before; miserable comforters, all of you.
Is there no end to windy words? What provokes you to keep answering?
I could speak as you do if you were in my place; I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the condolence of my lips would hold back your pain.
If I speak, my pain isn't held back; and if I stop, what leaves me?
But now he has worn me out; you have devastated all my company.
You have shrivelled me up — and it has become a witness; my leanness has risen up against me and testifies to my face.
His anger has torn me and assailed me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes against me.
They've opened their mouths wide at me; in scorn they've struck my cheeks; together they mass themselves against me.
God delivers me up to the unjust and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces; he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me; he splits my kidneys open without pity; he pours out my gall on the ground.
He breaks through me, breach upon breach; he charges at me like a warrior.
I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust.
My face is red from weeping, and deep darkness is on my eyelids,
though there's no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover my blood; let my outcry have no resting place!
Even now — see, my witness is in the heavens, and the one who vouches for me is on high.
My friends scorn me; my eye weeps to God.
that he might argue a man's case with God, as a man argues for his companion.
For a few numbered years will come, and then I'll go the way from which there's no return.

job_17.t: My spirit is broken, my days snuffed out; the graves are ready for me.
Surely mockers are around me, and my eye must dwell on their provocation.
Lay down a pledge for me with yourself — who else will strike hands with me?
For you have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you won't let them triumph.
One who denounces his friends for plunder — the eyes of his children will fail.
He has made me a byword among peoples; I am one spat in the face.
My eye has grown dim from vexation; all my limbs are like a shadow.
Upright men are appalled at this, and the innocent rouses himself against the godless.
The righteous holds to his way, and the clean of hands grows stronger.
But all of you — turn back, come again! I won't find a wise man among you.
My days have passed; my plans are torn apart — the desires of my heart.
They turn night into day: 'Light is near,' they say, in the face of darkness.
If I hope for Sheol as my house, if I've spread my bed in the darkness,
to the pit I have said, "You are my father," and to the maggot, "My mother, my sister" —
where then is my hope? My hope — who will see it?
Will it go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we descend together into the dust?

job_18.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long until you put an end to words? Understand, and then we'll speak.
Why are we counted as cattle, reckoned stupid in your eyes?
You who tear yourself in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, and a rock be moved from its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked is put out, and the flame of his fire doesn't shine.
The light grows dark in his tent; the lamp above him is put out.
The steps of his vigour are hemmed in, and his own counsel throws him down.
For his own feet send him into a net; he walks about on a mesh.
A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare closes on him.
A rope is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him on the path.
On every side sudden terrors terrify him and chase him at his heels.
His strength is hunger-worn, and disaster is ready for his stumbling.
It consumes the parts of his skin; death's firstborn consumes his limbs.
His trust is torn from his tent, and he's marched off to the king of terrors.
In his tent dwells what is not his; sulphur is scattered over his home.
Below, his roots dry up; above, his branch withers.
His memory perishes from the earth; he has no name in the open street.
They drive him from light into darkness and chase him out of the world.
He has no offspring, no posterity among his people, no survivor where he lived.
