At his day those in the west are appalled, and those in the east are seized with horror.
Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, and this is the place of one who does not know God.

job_19.t: And Job answered and said:
How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
Ten times now you have insulted me; you're not ashamed to wrong me.
And even if it's true that I've erred, my error stays with me.
If you really do magnify yourselves against me and use my disgrace to argue against me,
know this: God has wronged me and closed his net around me.
See — I cry out "Violence!" and get no answer; I cry for help, and there is no justice.
He has walled up my way so I can't pass; he puts darkness on my paths.
He has stripped my honour from me and taken the crown from my head.
He tears me down on every side, and I'm gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
He has kindled his anger against me and counted me among his foes.
His troops come together; they throw up a siege-road against me and encamp around my tent.
He has put my brothers far from me; my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.
My kindred have failed me; those who knew me have forgotten me.
The guests of my house and my slave women count me a stranger; I've become a foreigner in their eyes.
I call my servant and he doesn't answer; I have to beg him with my own mouth.
My breath is loathsome to my wife; I am repulsive to my own brothers.
Even young boys despise me; when I get up, they speak against me.
All the men of my circle abhor me; those I loved have turned against me.
My bone clings to my skin and my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Have pity on me, have pity on me, my friends — the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you pursue me as God does? Are you never satisfied with my flesh?
If only my words were written down! If only they were inscribed in a scroll!
with an iron stylus and lead, engraved in the rock for ever!
And I myself know that my redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.
And after my skin has been destroyed like this, yet from my flesh I shall see God,
whom I myself shall see for myself — my own eyes shall see him, and not another's. My inmost self is consumed within me.
If you say, "How shall we pursue him, since the root of the matter is found in him" —
be afraid for yourselves of the sword, for wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgement.

job_20.t: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
So my disquieting thoughts make me answer, because of the agitation within me.
I hear a correction that insults me, and a spirit out of my understanding answers me.
Do you know this, from of old, from when humankind was set upon the earth,
that the exulting of the wicked is brief, the gladness of the godless a moment long?
Though his loftiness rises to the heavens and his head reaches the clouds,
like his own dung he perishes for ever; those who saw him will say, "Where is he?"
Like a dream he flies away and is not found; he's chased away like a vision of the night.
The eye that glimpsed him does so no more; his place beholds him no longer.
His children will beg favour from the poor, and his own hands will give back his wealth.
His bones were full of youthful vigour, but it will lie down with him in the dust.
Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
though he spares it and won't let it go, holding it back in his palate,
his food is turned in his inward parts — the venom of cobras within him.
He swallows wealth and vomits it up; God drives it out of his belly.
He sucks the poison of cobras; the viper's tongue kills him.
He will not look on the streams, the rivers and wadis of honey and curds.
He gives back his gain and doesn't swallow it; for all the wealth of his trading he will not rejoice.
For he crushed and abandoned the poor; he seized a house he did not build.
He knew no quiet within him; he won't escape with what he coveted.
Nothing was left over from his devouring; so his prosperity will not endure.
At the height of his plenty he'll be in distress; every hand of the wretched will come against him.
Let it come, to fill his belly: God will send against him the burning of his anger and rain it down on him as his food.
He'll flee from an iron weapon; a bow of bronze will pierce him through.
He draws it out and it comes from his back, the glittering point from his gall. Terrors come upon him.
Total darkness is laid up for his treasures; a fire no one fanned will consume him; it will go badly for any survivor in his tent.
The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
The produce of his house will be carried off, poured away on the day of his anger.
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the inheritance decreed for him by God.

job_21.t: And Job answered and said:
Listen carefully to my speech — let that be your consolation to me.
Bear with me while I speak; and after I've spoken, mock on.
Is my complaint against a human? And if it were, why shouldn't I be impatient?
Turn to me and be appalled; lay your hand over your mouth.
When I remember, I'm dismayed, and shuddering seizes my flesh.
Why do the wicked live on, grow old, and grow mighty in strength?
Their offspring is established before them, with them, their descendants before their eyes.
Their houses are at peace, without fear; the rod of God is not on them.
His bull breeds and doesn't fail; his cow calves and doesn't miscarry.
They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children skip about.
They raise the tambourine and lyre and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
They finish their days in prosperity, and in a moment they go down to Sheol.
And they say to God, "Depart from us — we don't want the knowledge of your ways."
"What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What do we gain by entreating him?"
See — their prosperity is not in their own hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does calamity come on them, and God apportion pains in his anger?
Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff a whirlwind has carried off?
"God stores up a man's iniquity for his children" — let him repay the man himself, and let him know it!
Let his own eyes see his own destruction; let him drink of the rage of the Almighty.
For what pleasure has he in his household after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
Shall anyone teach God knowledge, seeing that he judges those on high?
One man dies in the full strength of his prime, wholly at ease and quiet.
His body is well nourished, and the marrow of his bones is moist.
And another dies with a bitter spirit, never having tasted anything good.
Together they lie down in the dust, and the maggot covers them both.
See — I know your thoughts, and the schemes by which you wrong me.
For you say, "Where is the house of the noble? Where is the tent, the dwelling of the wicked?"
Haven't you asked those who travel the roads? Don't you recognise their evidence —
that the evil man is spared on the day of calamity, rescued on the day of wrath?
Who declares his way to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
And he is carried to the graves, and a watch is kept over his tomb.
The clods of the wadi are sweet to him; all humanity follows after him, and before him there were countless others.
How then will you comfort me with emptiness? Of your answers, only treachery is left.

job_22.t: And Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Can a man be of use to God? Surely a wise man is of use only to himself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you're in the right? Is it any gain to him that you make your ways blameless?
Is it for your reverence that he reproves you and brings you to trial?
Is your evil not great? Is there no end to your iniquities?
You've taken pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the clothes off the naked.
You've given the weary no water to drink, and withheld bread from the hungry.
But the man with a strong arm owned the land, and the favoured man lived in it.
You've sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of the fatherless were crushed.
That's why snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
or darkness, so that you can't see, and a flood of waters covers you.
Is God not in the height of the heavens? Look at the topmost stars — how high they are!
And you say, "What does God know? Can he judge through thick darkness?"
"Clouds are his hiding place and he cannot see; he walks about on the vault of the heavens."
Will you keep to the ancient path that men of iniquity have trodden,
who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation a river washed away?
who said to God, "Depart from us!" and, "What can the Almighty do to us?"
Yet he filled their houses with good things — and the counsel of the wicked is far from me!
The righteous see it and rejoice; the innocent mocks them:
"Surely our adversary is destroyed, and fire has consumed what was left of them."
Come to terms with him now and be at peace; by this good will come to you.
Accept law from his mouth, and set his sayings in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty you'll be restored; you'll put injustice far from your tent.
and lay your gold in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the wadi rocks,
and the Almighty will be your gold, your precious silver.
For then you'll take delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
You'll pray to him and he'll hear you, and you'll pay your vows.
You'll pronounce a decision and it will stand, and light will shine on your ways.
When men are brought low, you'll say, "Lift them up!" and he saves the downcast.
He will deliver even the one who is not innocent, and he'll be delivered by the purity of your hands.

job_23.t: Even today my complaint is bitter rebellion; his hand lies heavy on my groaning.
If only I knew where to find him, that I might come to where he dwells!
I'd set out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I'd know the words he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.
Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No — surely he would give heed to me.
There an upright man could reason with him, and I'd be acquitted for ever by my judge.
I go east and he is not there; I go west and I don't perceive him;
in the north when he works, I don't see him; he turns to the south, and I don't see him.
For he knows the way I take; when he has tested me, I'll come out like gold.
My foot has held to his step; I've kept his way and not turned aside.
I haven't departed from the commandment of his lips; I've treasured the sayings of his mouth more than my daily bread.
But he is unchanging — who can turn him back? What he desires, he does.
For he carries out what is decreed for me, and many such things are with him.
That's why I'm terrified before him; when I consider, I dread him.
God has made my heart faint; The Almighty has terrified me.
for I was not silenced by the darkness, nor because thick gloom covers my face.

job_24.t: Why does the Almighty not lay up set times? Why do those who know him not see his days?
Men move boundary markers; they seize a flock and pasture it.
They drive off the orphan's donkey; they take the widow's ox in pledge.
They push the needy off the road; the poor of the earth all go into hiding.
Like wild donkeys in the wilderness they go out to their work, scavenging for food; the desert plain yields food for their children.
In the field they reap what isn't theirs; they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
Naked they spend the night, without clothing, with no covering in the cold.
They're drenched by the mountain rains, and for lack of shelter they hug the rock.
They tear the fatherless child from the breast and take a pledge from the poor.
Naked they go about, without clothing; hungry, they carry the sheaves.
Among the olive rows they press out oil; they tread the winepresses and go thirsty.
From the city men groan; the throat of the wounded cries for help — and God charges no one with wrong.
They are among those who rebel against the light; they don't recognise its ways or dwell in its paths.
At daybreak the murderer rises; he kills the poor and needy, and at night he's like a thief.
The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight, saying, "No eye will see me," and he covers his face.
In the darkness he digs through houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
For morning is deep darkness to them all; each is acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.
Swift is he on the face of the waters; their portion in the land is cursed; no one turns toward their vineyards.
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so Sheol takes those who have sinned.
The womb forgets him; the maggot feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
He preys on the barren woman who bears no child, and does no good to the widow.
Yet God drags off the mighty by his power; he rises up, and no one is sure of his life.
God gives him security, and he leans on it — yet his eyes are on their ways.
They're exalted a little, then gone; they're brought low and gathered in like everyone else, and like a head of grain they wither.
And if it isn't so, who will prove me a liar and reduce my speech to nothing?

job_25.t: And Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
Dominion and dread are with him; he makes peace in his heights.
Is there any counting his troops? On whom does his light not rise?
How then can a mortal be in the right before God? How can one born of a woman be pure?
See — even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
how much less a mortal, a maggot — a son of humankind, a worm!

job_26.t: What a help you've been to the powerless! What a rescue for the arm with no strength!
What counsel you've given to one with no wisdom! What abundance of sound wisdom you've made known!
To whom have you uttered words? Whose breath came out of you?
The shades writhe beneath the waters, with those who dwell there.
Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the north over emptiness; he hangs the earth on nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud doesn't split under their weight.
He covers the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it.
He has drawn a circle as a boundary on the face of the waters, at the frontier of light and darkness.
The pillars of the heavens shake, astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he stilled the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his wind the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
See — these are only the outskirts of his ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear of him! But the thunder of his might — who can understand?

job_27.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
As God lives, who has taken away my right, and the Almighty, who has made me bitter —
as long as my breath is in me and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak injustice, my tongue will not utter deceit.
Far be it from me to declare you in the right! Until I die I will not put away my integrity.
I've kept hold of my righteousness and won't let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unrighteous.
For what hope has the godless when he's cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
I'll teach you about the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I won't conceal.
You've all seen it yourselves — so why do you talk such empty nonsense?
This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the inheritance the ruthless receive from the Almighty:
If his children increase, it's for the sword; his descendants will not have bread enough.
His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
he prepares it, and the righteous will wear it; the innocent will divide the silver.
He has built his house like a moth's, like the shelter a watchman makes.
He lies down rich, but will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and it's all gone.
Terrors overtake him like a flood; by night a storm-wind carries him off.
The east wind lifts him up and he's gone; it whirls him away from his place.
It hurls itself at him without pity; he flees headlong from its power.
Men clap their hands at him and hiss him out of his place.

job_28.t: Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for the gold they purge.
Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted out of stone.
Man puts an end to darkness, searching out to the farthest limit the ore in gloom and deep darkness.
He breaks open a shaft far from where anyone lives — places the foot has forgotten; they dangle far from human beings and swing.
The earth — from it comes food, yet underneath it is turned over as by fire.
Its stones are the place of lapis lazuli; it holds dust of gold.
It's a path no bird of prey knows, that the falcon's eye has never glimpsed.
The proud beasts have not trodden it; no lion has passed over it.
He puts his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains at their roots.
In the rocks he cuts out channels, and his eye sees every precious thing.
He dams the streams from trickling, and brings what is hidden out to light.
But wisdom — where shall it be found? Where is the place of understanding?
No human knows its price, and it is not found in the land of the living.
The deep says, "It's not in me"; the sea says, "It's not with me."
Fine gold cannot be given for it, nor silver weighed out as its price.
It cannot be paid for with the gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or lapis lazuli.
Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor a vessel of fine gold be traded for it.
Coral and crystal aren't worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is beyond pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be paid for with pure gold.
And wisdom — where does it come from? Where is the place of understanding?
It is concealed from the eyes of every living thing, hidden from the birds of the sky.
Abaddon and Death say, "With our ears we've heard a rumour of it."
God understands the way to it; he knows its place.
For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens,
when he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters by measure;
when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
then he saw it and declared it; he established it and searched it out.
And he said to humankind: "See — the fear of the Lord is wisdom, and to turn from evil is understanding."

job_29.t: And Job again took up his discourse and said:
If only I were as in months long past, in the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was over my tent,
when the Almighty was still with me and my young men were around me;
when my steps were washed in curds, and the rock poured out streams of oil beside me;
when I went out to the town gate and took my seat in the public square;
the young men saw me and withdrew; the aged rose and stood;
princes held back their words and laid a hand over their mouth;
the voice of nobles was hushed; their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth;
for the ear that heard called me blessed, and the eye that saw bore witness for me;
For I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no helper.
The blessing of the perishing came on me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
I put on righteousness and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy, and I looked into the case of a stranger.
I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and made him drop the prey from his teeth.
And I said, "I'll die in my own nest, and multiply my days like the sand."
My root reaches open to the water, and dew lies all night on my branch.
My honour stays fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.
Men listened to me and waited, silent, for my counsel.
After my word no one spoke again; my speech fell on them like dew.
They waited for me as for the rain, opening their mouths wide as for the spring rain.
I smiled on them when they had lost confidence, and they did not let the light of my face fall.
I chose their way and sat as chief; I dwelt like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.

job_30.t: But now they laugh at me — men younger than I, whose fathers I'd have refused to put with my sheepdogs.
What use to me was the strength of their hands? All vigour had perished from them.
Gaunt with want and hunger, they gnaw the dry ground — by night, waste and desolation;
who pluck saltwort among the bushes, whose food is the root of the broom plant.
They're driven out from among men; people shout after them as after a thief.
They live in the gullies of the wadis, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
Sons of fools, sons of no name, they were whipped out of the land.
And now I've become their taunt-song; I'm a byword to them.
They abhor me and keep their distance; they don't hold back from spitting in my face.
Because God has loosened my bowstring and afflicted me, they've cast off all restraint before me.
On my right a rabble rises; they drive my feet from under me and throw up their siege-roads of disaster against me.
They've broken up my path; they profit from my ruin, with no one to hold them back.
They come on as through a wide breach; amid the crash they come rolling in.
Terrors are turned on me; my dignity is driven off like the wind, my prosperity gone like a cloud.
And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
At night my bones are pierced through, and the pains that gnaw me never rest.
With great force my clothing is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I've become like dust and ashes.
I cry to you for help, and you don't answer; I stand, and you only stare at me.
You have turned cruel toward me; with the might of your hand you assail me.
You lift me up to the wind and make me ride it, and you toss me about in the storm.
For I know you'll bring me back to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Surely no one strikes at a ruined man — or is there no cry for help in his disaster?
Didn't I weep for the one whose day was hard? Wasn't I grieved for the needy?
Yet when I waited for good, evil came; when I hoped for light, darkness came.
My inward parts boil and are never still; days of affliction have come to meet me.
I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I've become a brother to jackals, a companion to ostriches.
My skin has turned black on me; my bones burn with fever.
My lyre has turned to mourning, my flute to the sound of weeping.

job_31.t: I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I gaze at a virgin?
And what is the portion from God above, the inheritance from the Almighty on high?
Isn't it calamity for the unrighteous, disaster for those who do iniquity?
Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
If I have walked with falsehood, if my foot has hurried after deceit —
let him weigh me in honest balances, and let God acknowledge my integrity!
If my step has turned aside from the way, if my heart has gone after my eyes, if any stain has stuck to my hands —
let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be torn up by the roots!
If my heart has been enticed by a woman, if I've lain in wait at my neighbour's door —
let my wife grind for another, and let others kneel over her!
For that would be depravity, an iniquity for the judges to punish;
for it is a fire that devours down to Abaddon and would root up all my increase.
If I've rejected the cause of my manservant or my slave woman when they brought a complaint against me —
then what will I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what will I answer?
Did not the one who made me in the belly make him? Did not the same one form us in the womb?
If I've withheld from the poor what they wanted, or made a widow's eyes fail with waiting,
or eaten my morsel alone while the fatherless got none of it —
for from my youth I reared him as a father would, and from my birth I guided her —
if I've seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or a needy man with no covering,
if his loins have not blessed me, warmed by the fleece of my lambs —
if I've raised my hand against the fatherless because I knew I had support in the gate —
let my shoulder fall from its socket, my arm be broken off at the joint!
For the calamity of God was a terror to me; before his majesty I could do nothing.
If I've made gold my confidence and called fine gold my security —
if I rejoiced that my wealth was great, that my hand had found so much —
if I looked at the sun when it shone, or the moon moving in splendour,
and my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand kissed my mouth in homage —
that too would be an iniquity for the judges, for I would have denied God above.
If I rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me, or exulted when calamity found him —
and I never let my mouth sin by asking for his life with a curse —
if the men of my household have not said, "Who is there that his meat hasn't filled?" —
no sojourner spent the night in the street; I opened my doors to the traveller —
If I've covered my transgressions the way people do, hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
because I feared the crowd and the contempt of the clans dismayed me, so that I kept silent and stayed indoors —
If only I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature — let the Almighty answer me! — and let my accuser write out his indictment.
Surely I'd carry it on my shoulder; I'd bind it on me like a crown.
I would give him an account of my every step; like a prince I would approach him.
If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
if I've eaten its produce without paying, and snuffed out the life of its owners —
let thorns come up instead of wheat, and foul weeds instead of barley! The words of Job are finished.

job_32.t: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, grew angry. His anger burned against Job because he justified himself rather than God.
And his anger burned against his three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he was.
When Elihu saw that the three men had no answer, his anger burned.
And Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite answered and said: I am young in days and you are aged; so I held back, afraid to tell you what I know.
I said, "Let days speak; let many years make wisdom known."
But there is a spirit in a mortal, and the breath of the Almighty gives understanding.
It's not the many who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.
So I say, listen to me; I too will tell what I know.
See — I waited for your words; I listened to your reasonings while you searched out what to say.
I gave you my full attention — and see, there was no one to refute Job, not one of you answering his sayings.
Don't say, "We have found wisdom — let God rout him, not a man" —
He hasn't marshalled his words against me, and I won't answer him with your sayings.
They're dismayed; they answer no more; words have failed them.
And shall I wait, because they don't speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
I'll answer, for my part; I too will tell what I know.
For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.
See — my belly is like wine with no vent, like new wineskins ready to burst.
Let me speak and find relief; let me open my lips and answer.
Let me show partiality to no one, and flatter no one;
for I don't know how to flatter; my Maker would soon carry me off.

job_33.t: But now, Job, hear my speech; give ear to all my words.
See now — I've opened my mouth; my tongue is speaking.
My sayings come from an upright heart; my lips speak knowledge sincerely.
The spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can; set out your case before me and take your stand.
See — before God I am just as you are; I too was pinched off from clay.
See — no dread of me will terrify you; no pressure of mine will weigh on you.
Surely you've spoken in my hearing, and I've heard the sound of your words:
"I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there's no iniquity in me.
See, he finds pretexts against me; he counts me his enemy."
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths."
In this you are not in the right — I'll answer you — for God is greater than a mortal.
Why have you contended against him, saying he answers none of a man's words?
For God speaks in one way, and in a second, though no one perceives it.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people, in slumber on the bed,
then he opens people's ears and seals a warning on them,
to turn a person aside from what he is doing and to keep pride from a man;
he keeps him back from the pit, and his life from crossing over by the weapon.
Or he is chastened with pain on his bed, with unceasing strife in his bones;
so that his life loathes bread, and he loathes the food he once craved.
His flesh wastes out of sight; his bones, once unseen, stick out.
His life draws near to the pit, and to those who bring death.
If there is at his side an angel, a mediator, one out of a thousand, to declare to a man what is right for him,
then he shows him favour and says, "Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom" —
his flesh grows fresher than a boy's; he returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and God restores his righteousness to him.
He sings out before others and says, "I have sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not repaid to me as I deserved."
He has ransomed my life from going down to the pit, and my life shall look on the light.
See — God does all these things twice, three times, with a man,
to bring his life back from the pit, to be lit with the light of the living.
Pay attention, Job; listen to me; be silent, and I'll speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak — I'd gladly declare you in the right.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I'll teach you wisdom.

job_34.t: And Elihu answered and said:
Hear my words, you wise men; give ear to me, you who know;
for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
Let us choose what is just for ourselves; let us learn among ourselves what is good.
For Job has said, "I am in the right, and God has taken away my right."
"Am I to lie about my own case? My wound is incurable, though I've done no wrong."
What man is like Job, who drinks up mockery like water,
who keeps company with doers of iniquity and walks with wicked men?
For he has said, "It profits a man nothing to take delight in God."
So, men of understanding, hear me: far be it from God to do wickedness, from the Almighty to do wrong!
He repays a person according to his work, and makes each man's way find him out.
Truly, God does not act wickedly; The Almighty does not pervert justice.
Who gave him charge of the earth? Who appointed him over the whole world?
If he set his heart on a man and gathered back his spirit and his breath,
all flesh would expire together, and humankind would return to dust.
If you have understanding, hear this; give ear to the sound of my words.
Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the Righteous and Mighty One?
Does anyone say to a king, "You worthless one," or to nobles, "You wicked ones"?
who shows no partiality to princes and does not favour the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
In a moment they die, at midnight; a people is shaken and passes away, and the mighty are removed by no human hand.
For his eyes are on a man's ways; he sees all his steps.
There is no darkness, no deep darkness, where the doers of iniquity can hide.
For he need set no time for a man to come before God for judgement.
He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets others in their place.
So he takes note of their deeds; he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
He strikes them down as wicked men where people can see,
because they turned aside from following him and paid no regard to any of his ways,
so that they brought the outcry of the poor before him, and he heard the outcry of the afflicted.
When he is quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can behold him? — over a nation and over one man alike,
so that no godless man should reign, or be a snare to the people.
For has anyone said to God, "I have borne my punishment; I'll offend no more;
teach me what I cannot see; if I've done wrong, I won't do it again"?
Should he repay on your terms, because you refuse them? You must choose, not I — so say what you know.
Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me:
"Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight."
Would that Job were tested to the utmost, for answering like men of iniquity!
For he adds transgression to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his sayings against God.

job_35.t: Do you call this justice? You have said, "My righteousness is greater than God's."
For you say, "What use is it to you? What do I gain more than if I'd sinned?"
I will answer you in words, and your friends along with you.
Look at the heavens and see; look at the clouds, higher than you.
If you have sinned, what does it do to him? If your transgressions are many, what does it do to him?
If you're in the right, what do you give him? What does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself; your righteousness, only a fellow human.
Under a weight of oppressions people cry out; they cry for help against the arm of the great.
But no one says, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?"
There they cry out and he doesn't answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God does not hear an empty cry; The Almighty does not regard it.
How much less when you say you can't see him — the case is before him; you must wait for him!
And now, because his anger has not punished, and he has taken little notice of transgression,
Job opens his mouth to no purpose; without knowledge he multiplies words.

job_36.t: And Elihu went on and said:
Bear with me a little and I'll show you — there is still something to say on God's behalf.
I'll fetch my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
Truly my words are no falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
See — God is mighty and despises no one; he is mighty in strength of understanding.
He does not keep the wicked alive, but gives justice to the afflicted.
He does not take his eyes off the righteous; with kings on the throne he seats them for ever, and they are exalted.
And if they are bound in fetters, caught in cords of affliction,
then he shows them what they've done, and their transgressions — that they behaved proudly.
He opens their ear to correction and tells them to turn back from iniquity.
If they listen and serve him, they'll finish their days in prosperity, their years in pleasantness.
But if they don't listen, they pass away by the weapon and die without knowledge.
The godless in heart cherish anger; they don't cry for help when he binds them.
They die young, their life spent among the shrine prostitutes.
He rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ear through oppression.
He also lured you out of distress into a broad place with no constraint, and your table set with rich food.
But you are full of the wicked man's case; judgement and justice have taken hold of you.
Beware lest wrath entice you into scoffing; let no great ransom turn you aside.
Will your wealth keep you out of distress, or all your efforts of strength?
Do not long for the night, when peoples are cut off where they stand.
Take heed; don't turn to iniquity — you've chosen this rather than affliction.
See — God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
Who has prescribed his way for him? Who has said, "You have done wrong"?
Remember to magnify his work, the work people have sung of.
All humankind has looked on it; a mortal beholds it from far off.
See — God is exalted beyond our knowing; the number of his years is past searching out.
For he draws up the drops of water; they distil as rain from his mist,
which the clouds pour down; they drip abundantly on humankind.
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thunder of his pavilion?
See — he spreads his lightning about him and covers the depths of the sea.
For by these he judges peoples and gives food in abundance.
He covers his hands with lightning and commands it to strike the mark.
His thunder tells of him; even the cattle sense what is coming.

job_37.t: At this too my heart trembles and leaps from its place.
Listen carefully to the raging of his voice, the rumbling that goes out from his mouth.
Under all the heavens he lets it loose, his lightning to the ends of the earth.
After it a voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he holds nothing back when his voice is heard.
God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things beyond our knowing.
For to the snow he says, "Fall on the earth" — and so to the shower of rain, and the showers of his mighty rain.
He seals up every human hand, so that all whom he has made may know his work.
The wild animals go into their lairs and stay in their dens.
From its chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds.
By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen fast.
He loads the thick cloud with moisture and scatters his lightning-cloud abroad.
It turns round and round by his guidance, to do all that he commands over the face of the inhabited world.
Whether for correction, or for his earth, or for steadfast love, he makes it strike its mark.
Give ear to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
Do you know how God lays his charge on them and makes the lightning of his cloud flash out?
Do you know how the clouds are balanced — the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
you whose clothes are hot when the earth lies still under the south wind?
Can you beat out the skies with him, hard as a mirror of cast metal?
Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot marshal a case because of darkness.
Shall he be told that I want to speak? Did anyone ever ask to be swallowed up?
And now people cannot look at the light when it is brilliant in the skies, after a wind has passed and swept them clear.
Out of the north comes golden splendour; about God is awesome majesty.
The Almighty — we cannot find him out; he is exalted in power, and he does not violate justice and abundant righteousness.
Therefore people fear him; he regards none who think themselves wise.

job_38.t: Then the LORD answered Job out of the tempest:
Who is this that darkens counsel with words without knowledge?
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform me.
Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you have understanding.
Who fixed its measurements — surely you know! — or who stretched the measuring line over it?
On what were its bases sunk? Who laid its cornerstone,
when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
And who shut in the sea with doors when it burst out from the womb,
when I made the cloud its clothing and thick darkness its swaddling band,
and I fixed my limit for it and set bars and doors,
and said, "This far you shall come and no further; here your proud waves shall be stayed"?
Have you ever in your life commanded the morning, or caused the dawn to know its place,
to take hold of the earth by its corners and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its features stand out like a garment.
The wicked are deprived of their light, and the uplifted arm is broken.
Have you gone to the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know it all.
Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And where is the place of darkness,
that you could take it to its own territory and know the paths to its house?
You know, of course — you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
Have you entered the storehouses of snow, or seen the storehouses of hail,
which I've kept back for the time of distress, for the day of battle and war?
Where is the way by which light is distributed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the torrent and a path for the thunderbolt,
to bring rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness with no one in it,
to satisfy waste and desolate ground and make the fresh grass sprout?
Has the rain a father? Who fathered the drops of dew?
From whose womb did the ice come? The frost of heaven — who gave it birth?
The waters become hard as stone, and the surface of the deep freezes solid.
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you bring out the constellations in their season, or guide the Bear with her young?
Do you know the statutes of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, so that a flood of water covers you?
Can you send out lightnings, and they go and say to you, "Here we are"?
Who put wisdom in the hidden parts, or gave understanding to the mind?
Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Who can tip the waterskins of heaven,
when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods stick fast together?
Can you hunt prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides food for the raven when its young cry to God for help and wander about for lack of food?

job_39.t: Do you know when the mountain goats of the rock give birth? Do you watch over the labour of the does?
Can you count the months they carry, and do you know the time when they give birth,
when they crouch and deliver their young, and their labour pains are done?
Their young grow strong out in the open; they go out and never return.
Who let the wild donkey go free? Who loosed the bonds of the wild ass?
whose home I made the desert plain, its dwellings the salt flats?
It laughs at the tumult of the town; it never hears a driver's shouts.
It ranges the mountains for pasture, searching after every green thing.
Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Will it spend the night by your feeding trough?
Can you rope the wild ox to a furrow? Will it harrow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust it because its strength is great, and leave your labour to it?
Will you trust it to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
The ostrich's wing flaps joyously — but is it the pinion and plumage of a stork?
For it leaves its eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the dust,
and it forgets that a foot may crush them, that a wild animal may trample them.
It treats its young harshly, as if they weren't its own; its labour is in vain, and it feels no fear,
for God has made it forget wisdom and given it no share of understanding.
Yet when it rouses itself to run, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse his strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?
Do you make him leap like a locust? The majesty of his snorting is terrifying.
He paws in the valley and exults in his strength; he goes out to meet the weapons.
He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and javelin.
Quivering with rage, he swallows the ground; he won't stand still at the sound of the horn.
At every blast of the horn he says, "Aha!" He smells the battle from afar — the thunder of the commanders and the war-cry.
Is it by your understanding that the falcon soars, spreading its wings toward the south?
Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up and builds its nest on high?
It dwells on the rock and lodges there, on the rock's tooth, a stronghold.
From there it spies out its food; its eyes look far off.
Its young lap up blood; and where the slain are, there it is.

job_40.t: And the LORD answered Job:
Shall a faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who accuses God answer for it.
And Job answered the LORD:
See — I am of small account. What can I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
Once I have spoken, and I won't answer; twice, and I'll say no more.
Then the LORD answered Job out of the tempest:
Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform me.
Will you even annul my justice? Will you condemn me so that you can be in the right?
Have you an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
Deck yourself now with majesty and dignity; clothe yourself with glory and honour.
Pour out the overflowings of your anger; look on every proud one and bring him low.
Look on every proud one and humble him; tread down the wicked where they stand.
Hide them in the dust together; shut their faces away in the hidden place.
Then I too will acknowledge you, that your own right hand can save you.
Look now at Behemoth, which I made along with you; he eats grass like an ox.
See — his strength is in his loins, his power in the muscles of his belly.
He stiffens his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are tubes of bronze, his limbs like bars of iron.
He is the first of God's works; only his Maker can bring a sword near him.
The mountains bring him their produce, and all the wild animals play there.
Under the lotus plants he lies down, in the cover of the reeds and marsh.
The lotus plants cover him with their shade; the poplars of the wadi surround him.
If the river rages, he is not alarmed; he is confident even when the Jordan bursts against his mouth.
Can anyone capture him while he watches, or pierce his nose with a snare?

job_41.t: Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish-hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?
Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Will he plead with you at length? Will he speak soft words to you?
Will he cut a covenant with you, that you should take him as a slave for life?
Will you play with him like a bird, or put him on a leash for your girls?
Will trading partners bargain over him? Will they parcel him out among merchants?
Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fish-spears?
Lay a hand on him — remember the battle; you'll not do it again!
See — any hope of him proves false; is a man not cast down at the mere sight of him?
No one is fierce enough to rouse him. Who then can stand before me?
Who has ever confronted me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.
I will not keep silent about his limbs, his mighty strength, his graceful frame.
Who has stripped off his outer covering? Who can get inside his double coat of mail?
Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.
His back is rows of shields, sealed shut and tight.
One is so near another that no air can pass between them.
Each clings to the next; they grip one another and cannot be parted.
His snorting flashes out light; his eyes are like the eyelids of dawn.
From his mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap out.
Smoke goes out from his nostrils, as from a pot boiling over burning rushes.
His breath kindles coals; a flame goes out from his mouth.
Strength lodges in his neck; dismay dances before him.
The folds of his flesh cling together, firmly cast on him and immovable.
His heart is hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
At his rising the mighty are afraid; at the crashing they lose their senses.
The sword that reaches him does not hold — nor spear, nor dart, nor javelin.
He counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood.
The arrow doesn't make him flee; sling-stones turn to chaff against him.
A club is counted as chaff; he laughs at the rattling of a javelin.
Beneath him are sharp potsherds; he spreads a threshing sledge across the mud.
He makes the deep boil like a pot; he stirs the sea like an ointment-pot.
Behind him he leaves a shining wake; you would think the deep had turned white-haired.
There is nothing on earth like him, a creature made without fear.
He looks down on everything that is high; he is king over all the sons of pride.

job_42.t: I know you can do anything, and no plan of yours can be blocked.
'Who is this, hiding counsel without knowledge?' So I spoke of what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
'Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you tell me.'
I had heard of you by report, but now my own eye has seen you.
Therefore I reject, and I am consoled, upon dust and ashes.
After the LORD had said all this to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: I am angry with you and your two friends, because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job will pray for you; I will accept his prayer and not deal with you as your folly deserves — because you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job.
And the LORD restored Job's fortunes when he prayed for his friends, and gave him twice as much as he had before.

All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house; they shook their heads over him and comforted him for all the trouble the LORD had brought on him. Each gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.
And the LORD blessed the latter end of Job's life more than his beginning: fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.
And he had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
Job lived a hundred and forty years after this, and saw his children and his grandchildren — four generations.
And Job died, old and full of days.

joel_1.t: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Listen to this, elders. Pay attention, everyone living in the land. Has this happened in your day, or in your ancestors' day?
Tell your children about it, and let them tell theirs, and theirs tell another generation.
Whatever the shearing locust left, the swarming locust ate. Whatever the swarming locust left, the licking locust ate. Whatever the licking locust left, the consuming locust ate.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep. Wail, all of you who drink wine, over the sweet wine — it's cut off from your mouth.
A nation has come up against my land, mighty, beyond counting. Its teeth are a lion's teeth; it has a lioness's fangs.
It's laid my vine waste and splintered my fig tree. It stripped it bare, right down, and threw it away; its branches have gone white.
Wail like a virgin in sackcloth mourning the husband of her youth.
The grain offering and the drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests are mourning, the ones who serve the LORD.
The field is ruined, the ground is in mourning — the grain is ruined, the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil withers.
Be ashamed, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and the barley — the field's harvest is gone.
The vine has dried up, the fig tree withers, pomegranate, palm and apple with them — every tree in the field has dried up. Joy itself has dried up from the human race.

Put on sackcloth and lament, you priests; wail, you who serve at the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God — grain offering and drink offering are being withheld from the house of your God.
Set a fast apart as holy, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and everyone living in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
What a day! The day of the LORD is near — it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
Hasn't food been cut off right before our eyes, and joy and gladness from the house of our God?
The seeds have shrivelled under their clods; the storehouses are empty, the granaries pulled down — the grain has dried up.
Listen to the livestock groan. The cattle herds mill about with nowhere to go; there's no pasture for them. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
I'm calling to you, LORD — fire has eaten up the wilderness pastures, and a flame has set every tree in the field alight.
Even the wild animals pant for you — the stream channels have dried up, and fire has eaten up the wilderness pastures.

joel_2.t: Blow a ram's horn in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let everyone living in the land tremble — the day of the LORD is coming. It's near.

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness. Like dawn spreading over the mountains — a people, numerous and mighty. There has never been anything like it, and after it there won't be again, not for generations upon generations.
Fire consumes ahead of it, a flame blazes behind it. Ahead of it the land is like the garden of Eden; behind it, desolate wilderness. Nothing escapes it.
It looks like horses; like cavalry, that's how they run.
They leap over the mountain tops with a sound like chariots, like a flame of fire crackling through stubble, like a mighty army drawn up for battle.
Peoples writhe in anguish before it; every face gathers a glow.
They run like warriors, they scale a wall like soldiers. Each one holds its own line; they never swerve from their paths.
They don't jostle each other; each keeps to its own track. They come through the weapons and nothing stops them.
They rush the city, they run along the wall, they climb into the houses, they come in through the windows like a thief.
The earth trembles before it, the heavens shake. Sun and moon go dark; the stars pull back their light.
The LORD has raised his voice at the head of his army. His camp is enormous; mighty is the one who carries out his word. The day of the LORD is great and terrible. Who can endure it?
"Even now," says the LORD, "come back to me with all your heart — with fasting, with weeping, with mourning."
"Tear your heart, not your clothes. Come back to the LORD your God. He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, and he relents over harm."
Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him — a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
Blow a ram's horn in Zion. Set a fast apart as holy. Call a solemn assembly.
Gather the people. Set the assembly apart as holy. Bring in the elders. Gather the children, even the babies at the breast. Let the bridegroom come out of his room, and the bride out of her chamber.

Between the porch and the altar let the priests weep — those who serve the LORD — and let them say: "Spare your people, LORD. Don't hand your inheritance over to reproach, with nations ruling over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
Then the LORD became jealous for his land, and he had compassion on his people.
The LORD answered his people: "I'm sending you the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, and you'll have your fill of it. I won't make you a reproach among the nations any more.

I'll drive the northerner far away from you, into a dry and desolate land, its face toward the eastern sea, its rear toward the western sea. The stench of it will go up, the reek of it will go up — because it has done great things.
Don't be afraid, ground. Be glad and rejoice — the LORD has done great things.
Don't be afraid, animals of the field — the wilderness pastures have turned green. The trees are bearing fruit; fig tree and vine are giving their best.

People of Zion, be glad, rejoice in the LORD your God — he has given you the early rain for your vindication, he has sent the rains down for you, the early rain and the spring rain, in the first month.
The threshing floors will be full of grain; the vats will overflow with new wine and fresh oil.
"I'll make up to you the years the swarming locust ate — the licking locust, the consuming locust, the shearing locust, my great army that I sent among you.
"You'll eat your fill and be satisfied, and you'll praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt with you wondrously. My people will never be ashamed.
"You'll know that I am in the midst of Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other. My people will never be ashamed."
"Afterwards, this is what will happen: I'll pour out my spirit on all flesh. Your sons and daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
"And on the male servants and the female servants too — in those days I'll pour out my spirit.
"I'll set wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
"The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the day of the LORD comes, the great and terrible day.
"Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape. On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, just as the LORD said — among the survivors the LORD is calling."

joel_3.t: "Look — in those days, at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I'll gather all the nations and bring them down to the valley of Jehoshaphat, and there I'll enter into judgement with them over my people, my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations — and they carved up my land.
They cast lots for my people. They traded a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine, and drank it.
"And what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon, and all the regions of Philistia? Are you paying me back for something? If you are paying me back, I'll return your payment on your own head, and fast —
you who took my silver and my gold and carried my finest treasures off into your temples;
and you sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to put them far away from their own territory.
"I'm rousing them out of the place where you sold them, and I'll return your payment on your own head.
I'll sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they'll sell them on to the Sabeans, to a nation far away" — the LORD has spoken.
Announce this among the nations: Set a war apart as holy! Rouse the warriors! Let all the fighting men come near and come up!
Beat your plowshares into swords, your pruning knives into spears. Let the weak one say, "I'm a warrior."
Hurry, come, all you nations round about; gather yourselves there. Bring your warriors down, LORD!
"Let the nations be roused and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat. There I'll take my seat to judge all the nations round about.
Put in the sickle — the harvest is ripe. Come and tread — the winepress is full, the vats are overflowing. Their evil is great."
Crowds upon crowds in the valley of decision. The day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
Sun and moon have gone dark; the stars have pulled back their light.
The LORD will roar from Zion; from Jerusalem he'll raise his voice, and the heavens and the earth will shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the Israelites.
"You'll know that I am the LORD your God, living in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy place, and strangers will never pass through it again."

"On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will run with milk, every ravine in Judah will run with water. A spring will flow out of the house of the LORD and water the Wadi of the Acacias.
Egypt will become a desolation, Edom a desolate wilderness, because of the violence done to the people of Judah — they shed innocent blood in their land.
But Judah will remain for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
"I'll clear their bloodguilt — the guilt I did not clear." And the LORD is dwelling in Zion.

jonah_1.t: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
'Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out against it. Their evil has come up in front of me.'

But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish, out of the LORD's presence. He went down to Joppa, found a ship bound for Tarshish, paid the fare, and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, out of the LORD's presence.
But the LORD hurled a great wind at the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought it was going to break up.

The sailors were terrified. Each of them cried out to his own god, and they hurled the ship's gear into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost part of the vessel, lain down, and fallen fast asleep.
The captain came to him and said, 'What are you doing, sleeper? Get up and call on your god! Maybe the god will give us a thought and we won't die.'
They said to each other, 'Come on, let's cast lots and find out who's behind this evil that's on us.' They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
They said to him, 'Tell us — who's behind this evil that's on us? What do you do? Where do you come from? What's your country? What people are you from?'
He said, 'I'm a Hebrew. I fear the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry ground.'
Then the men were terrified, and they said to him, 'What have you done?' They knew he was running from the LORD's presence, because he had told them.
They said to him, 'What should we do with you, so the sea will settle down for us?' The sea was getting rougher and rougher.
He said, 'Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will settle down for you. I know this great storm is on you because of me.'
But the men rowed hard to get back to dry ground, and they couldn't — the sea was getting rougher and rougher against them.
So they called out to the LORD: 'Please, LORD, don't let us die for this man's life, and don't hold innocent blood against us. You, LORD, have done what you wanted.'
Then they picked Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
Then the men feared the LORD with a great fear. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
And the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish three days and three nights.

jonah_2.t: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from inside the fish.
He said: I called from my distress to the LORD, and he answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried for help, you heard my voice.
You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current closed around me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.
And I said, 'I've been driven out of your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters closed over me, right to my throat; the deep surrounded me; reeds were wound around my head.
I went down to the roots of the mountains; the earth's bars were shut behind me for ever; but you brought my life up from the pit, LORD my God.
When my life was ebbing away in me, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
People who hold on to worthless nothings let go of the steadfast love that could be theirs.
But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving; what I have vowed I will pay. Deliverance belongs to the LORD.
Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry ground.

jonah_3.t: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
'Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out to it the proclamation I'm speaking to you.'
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the LORD had said. Nineveh was an exceedingly great city — three days' journey across.
Jonah started into the city, a day's journey in, and he proclaimed: 'Forty days more, and Nineveh is overthrown!'
And the people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their smallest.
The word reached the king of Nineveh. He got up from his throne, took off his robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat down in the ashes.

And he had it proclaimed in Nineveh: 'By order of the king and his great ones: no people, no livestock, no cattle, no flocks are to taste anything. They're not to graze, and they're not to drink water.

Let them cover themselves with sackcloth — people and livestock — and let them call out to God with everything they have, and let each one turn back from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.
Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn back from his burning anger, and we won't die.'
And God saw what they did — that they had turned back from their evil way — and God relented over the evil he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

jonah_4.t: But to Jonah this was a terrible thing, and he was furious.

And he prayed to the LORD: 'Please, LORD — isn't this exactly what I said while I was still back home? That's why I ran off to Tarshish in the first place. I knew you were a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, and one who relents over evil.'
'So now, LORD, please take my life from me. My death is better than my life.'
And the LORD said, 'Are you right to be angry?'
Then Jonah went out of the city and sat down to the east of it. He made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, waiting to see what would happen in the city.
And the LORD God appointed a plant, and it came up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to get him out of his misery. And Jonah was overjoyed about the plant — a great joy.
But God appointed a worm at daybreak the next day. It attacked the plant, and the plant withered.
And when the sun came up, God appointed a hot east wind. The sun beat on Jonah's head and he became faint. He asked to die, and he said, 'My death is better than my life.'
And God said to Jonah, 'Are you right to be angry about the plant?' And he said, 'I am right to be angry — angry enough to die.'
And the LORD said, 'You had pity on the plant, which you didn't work for and didn't grow — it came in a night and it perished in a night.
And should I not have pity on Nineveh, the great city, where there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who don't know their right hand from their left — and all those animals?'

joshua_1.t: After Moses the servant of the LORD died, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant,
"Moses my servant is dead. So get up now and cross this Jordan, you and all these people, into the land I am giving them, the Israelites.
"Everywhere the sole of your foot treads I have given to you, just as I told Moses.

"Your territory will run from the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates — all the land of the Hittites — and as far as the Great Sea, toward the setting of the sun.
"No one will stand before you as long as you live. I will be with you just as I was with Moses. I won't abandon you, I won't forsake you.
"Be strong, be bold — you are the one who will give this people the land as their inheritance, the land I swore to their ancestors I would give them.

"Only be strong and very bold. Take care to act according to all the law that Moses my servant commanded you. Don't turn aside from it to the right or the left, so that you'll act wisely wherever you go.

"This book of the law is not to leave your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you take care to act according to everything written in it. Then you'll make your ways succeed, and then you'll act wisely.
"Haven't I commanded you? Be strong, be bold. Don't be terrified, don't be dismayed — the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
So Joshua gave the officers of the people this command:

"Go right through the camp and tell the people, 'Get provisions ready. In three days you are to cross this Jordan, to go in and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
Then Joshua said to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
"Remember what Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest, and he'll give you this land.'

"Your wives, your little ones and your livestock are to stay in the land Moses gave you beyond the Jordan. But you yourselves cross over armed for battle ahead of your brothers — all the mighty men of valour — and help them,

"until the LORD gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them. Then you can go back to the land that is yours and take possession of it, the land Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun."
They answered Joshua, "Everything you've commanded us we'll do, and wherever you send us we'll go.
"We listened to Moses in everything, and we'll listen to you the same way. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as he was with Moses.
"Anyone who rebels against your command and doesn't listen to your words, to everything you command him, is to be put to death. Only be strong and bold."

joshua_2.t: Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men out from Shittim as spies. "Go and look the land over," he said, "and Jericho." So off they went, and they came to the house of a prostitute called Rahab, and they lay down there.
The king of Jericho was told, "Some men have come here tonight, Israelites, to spy out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you, the ones who came into your house — they've come to spy out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. "Yes, the men did come to me," she said, "but I didn't know where they were from.
"And when it was dark, just as the gate was about to be shut, the men left. I don't know where they went. Go after them quickly — you'll catch them."
But she'd taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax she'd laid out there.
The men went after them on the Jordan road, as far as the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers were out.
Before the men lay down for the night, she came up to them on the roof
and said to them, "I know the LORD has given you the land. Dread of you has fallen on us, and everyone living in the land has melted away before you.

"We've heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds in front of you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
"We heard it, and our heart melted, and no courage was left in anyone because of you. The LORD your God — he is God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
"So now swear to me by the LORD: I've shown you loyalty, so you'll show loyalty to my father's house too. And give me a sign of faithfulness —
"let my father and mother live, and my brothers and sisters and everyone who belongs to them; save our lives from death."
The men said to her, "Our life for yours, to the death — as long as you don't tell this business of ours! And when the LORD gives us the land, we'll show you loyalty and faithfulness."
So she let them down by a rope through the window — her house was in the outer wall, and she lived in the city wall itself.
She told them, "Head for the hill country, or the pursuers will run into you. Hide there three days until they've gone back, and then go on your way."
The men said to her, "We'll be free of this oath of yours that you've made us swear —

"when we come into the land, tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window you let us down by, and gather your father and mother, your brothers and your whole father's household to yourself in the house.

"Anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street — his blood is on his own head, and we're free of it. And anyone who's with you in the house — his blood is on our head, if a hand is laid on him.
"And if you tell this business of ours, we're free of the oath you've made us swear."
"Let it be as you say," she answered. Then she sent them off and they went, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went off to the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers had gone back. The pursuers searched the whole way and didn't find them.
Then the two men turned back. They came down from the hill country, crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.
"The LORD has given the whole land into our hand," they told Joshua. "Everyone living in the land has melted away before us."

joshua_3.t: Joshua was up early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites, and they stayed there before crossing over.
At the end of three days the officers went right through the camp,
and gave the people this command: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, with the priests, the Levites, carrying it, leave your place and follow it.
"Only keep your distance from it — about two thousand cubits by measure. Don't come near it, so that you can see the way you're to go; you've not passed this way before."
Joshua told the people, "Consecrate yourselves — tomorrow the LORD is going to do wonders among you."
And Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I am going to begin making you great in the eyes of all Israel, so they'll know that I will be with you just as I was with Moses.
"And you are to command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, 'When you reach the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand still there in the Jordan.'"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come over here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."

And Joshua said, "This is how you'll know that a living God is among you, and that he will surely dispossess the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites and the Jebusites before you:
"the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to go ahead of you into the Jordan.
"So now pick out twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.

"And when the soles of the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off — the waters coming down from above — and they'll stand in one heap."
When the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of them,
and as the ark-bearers reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying it were dipped in the edge of the waters — the Jordan runs over all its banks the whole of harvest time —

the waters coming down from above stood still. They rose up in one heap a long way off, at Adam, the city beside Zarethan, and the waters going down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry land in the middle of the Jordan while all Israel crossed over on dry land, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.

joshua_4.t: Once the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Pick out twelve men from the people, one from each tribe,

"and tell them, 'Take up twelve stones from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm. Carry them over with you and put them down at the lodging place where you stay tonight.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men he'd appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe.
He said to them, "Go over ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you lift one stone onto his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites,
"so that this will be a sign among you. When your children ask you one day, 'What do these stones mean to you?'

"you'll tell them, 'Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off.' And these stones are to be a memorial to the Israelites for ever."

The Israelites did just as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, just as the LORD had said to Joshua, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites; they carried them over with them to the lodging place and put them down there.
And Joshua set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the spot where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood; and they're there to this day.

The priests carrying the ark stood there in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that the LORD had commanded Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried across.
When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD crossed over, with the priests, in front of the people.
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed for battle ahead of the Israelites, just as Moses had told them —
about forty thousand of them, armed for war, crossed over before the LORD for battle, onto the plains of Jericho.
That day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him just as they'd feared Moses all his life.
The LORD said to Joshua,
"Tell the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

And as soon as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of their feet were drawn up onto dry ground, the waters of the Jordan went back where they'd been and ran over all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.
And Joshua set up at Gilgal those twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, "When your children ask their fathers one day, 'What are these stones?'
"you are to let your children know: 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground,'

"because the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan in front of you until you'd crossed over, just as the LORD your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which he dried up in front of us until we'd crossed over —
"so that all the peoples of the earth will know the hand of the LORD, how mighty it is, and so that you will fear the LORD your God all your days."

joshua_5.t: When all the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan to the west, and all the kings of the Canaanites by the sea, heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan in front of the Israelites until they'd crossed over, their heart melted and there was no courage left in them because of the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make yourself some flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at the Hill of the Foreskins.
