This is why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt.
All the people who came out had been circumcised, but the people born in the wilderness on the way, after they came out of Egypt, hadn't been.

For forty years the Israelites walked in the wilderness, until the whole nation was gone — the men of war who came out of Egypt, the ones who hadn't listened to the voice of the LORD. The LORD had sworn to them that he wouldn't let them see the land he had sworn to their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
It was their children he raised up in their place, and these are the ones Joshua circumcised; they were uncircumcised, because they hadn't been circumcised on the way.
When the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they'd healed.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled the reproach of Egypt off you." And the name of that place was called Gilgal, and it still is.
The Israelites camped at Gilgal, and they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
The day after the passover they ate some of the produce of the land — unleavened bread and roasted grain — that very day.
The manna stopped the day after, once they'd eaten some of the produce of the land. The Israelites had no more manna; they ate what the land of Canaan yielded that year.
When Joshua was at Jericho, he looked up, and there was a man standing opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went over to him and said, "Are you for us, or for our foes?"
"No," he said. "I am the commander of the army of the LORD. Now I have come." Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and said to him, "What is my lord saying to his servant?"
The commander of the army of the LORD said to Joshua, "Take the sandal off your foot — the place where you're standing is holy." And Joshua did.

joshua_6.t: Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the Israelites. Nobody went out and nobody came in.
And the LORD said to Joshua, "Look, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and the mighty men of valour.
"Go around the city, all you men of war, circling it once. Do that for six days.
"Seven priests are to carry seven trumpets of rams' horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day, go around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.

"And when they blow a long blast on the ram's horn, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people are to give a great shout. Then the wall of the city will fall down where it stands, and the people will go up, each straight ahead."
So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and told them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and have seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns in front of the ark of the LORD."
And he told the people, "Move out and go around the city, and have the armed men go on ahead of the ark of the LORD."

As soon as Joshua had said this to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the LORD moved out, blowing the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went after them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rearguard came behind the ark, with the trumpets blowing all the way.
And Joshua commanded the people: "Don't shout, don't let your voice be heard, don't let a word out of your mouth, until the day I tell you, 'Shout!' Then shout."
So he had the ark of the LORD go around the city, circling it once. Then they came into the camp and spent the night there.
Joshua was up early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns in front of the ark of the LORD went on and on, blowing the trumpets; the armed men went ahead of them, and the rearguard came behind the ark of the LORD, with the trumpets blowing all the way.
On the second day they went around the city once and came back to the camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they were up at first light and went around the city the same way — seven times. That was the only day they went around the city seven times.
On the seventh time round, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! The LORD has given you the city.
"The city is to be devoted to destruction, it and everything in it, to the LORD. Only Rahab the prostitute is to live, she and everyone with her in the house, because she hid the messengers we sent.

"But you — keep away from what is devoted to destruction, or you'll devote yourselves to destruction by taking any of it, and make the camp of Israel itself devoted to destruction and bring trouble on it.
"All the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD. They go into the treasury of the LORD."

So the people shouted, and they blew the trumpets. And when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, they gave a great shout, and the wall fell down where it stood. The people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and took it.
They devoted to destruction everything in the city — men and women, young and old, ox and sheep and donkey — with the edge of the sword.
And Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring out the woman and everyone who belongs to her, just as you swore to her."

So the young men who had spied went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers and everyone who belonged to her — they brought out all her clans — and put them outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city with fire, and everything in it. Only the silver, the gold and the articles of bronze and iron went into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

But Rahab the prostitute, and her father's household and everyone who belonged to her, Joshua let live; and she has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua put them under oath: "Cursed before the LORD be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. It will cost him his firstborn to lay its foundation, and his youngest to set up its gates."
And the LORD was with Joshua, and word of him went through the whole land.

joshua_7.t: But the Israelites broke faith over what was devoted to destruction: Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted to destruction. And the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.

They came back to Joshua and said, "Don't let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Don't make all the people wear themselves out up there — there aren't many of them."
So about three thousand of the people went up there — and they fled before the men of Ai.

The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them. They chased them from in front of the gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the way down. And the heart of the people melted and turned to water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.
And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD! Why did you bring this people right across the Jordan — to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we'd been content to stay beyond the Jordan!
"Pardon me, Lord! What am I to say, now that Israel has turned tail before its enemies?
"The Canaanites and everyone living in the land will hear of it, and they'll surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! What are you doing on your face?

"Israel has sinned. They've transgressed my covenant that I commanded them. They've taken some of what is devoted to destruction, they've stolen, they've deceived, and they've put it in among their own belongings.

"The Israelites can't stand before their enemies; they turn tail before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I won't be with you any more unless you destroy what is devoted to destruction from among you.

"Get up, consecrate the people, and say, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow. For thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: There is something devoted to destruction among you, Israel. You won't be able to stand before your enemies until you get rid of what is devoted to destruction from among you.'

"In the morning you are to come forward by your tribes. The tribe the LORD takes comes forward by families, the family the LORD takes comes forward by households, and the household the LORD takes comes forward man by man.

"And whoever is taken with what is devoted to destruction is to be burned with fire, he and everything that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD and done an outrage in Israel."
Joshua was up early in the morning and brought Israel forward by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
He brought the family of Judah forward and took the family of the Zerahites; he brought the family of the Zerahites forward man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
He brought his household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD the God of Israel and make confession to him. Tell me what you've done — don't hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It's true, I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

"I saw among the spoil one fine cloak of Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels; and I coveted them and took them. They're there now, hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent — and there it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and poured them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver, the cloak and the wedge of gold, and his sons and his daughters, his ox, his donkey, his flock, his tent and everything that belonged to him — and all Israel went with him — and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
And Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? Today the LORD brings trouble on you." And all Israel stoned him with stones; they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

They raised a great heap of stones over him, and it's there to this day. And the LORD turned from the burning of his anger. That is why the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor, and it still is.

joshua_8.t: The LORD said to Joshua, "Don't be afraid, don't be dismayed. Take all the people of war with you, and get up and go up to Ai. Look, I have given the king of Ai into your hand, with his people, his city and his land.
"Do to Ai and its king just what you did to Jericho and its king. Only its spoil and its livestock you may take as plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city, behind it."
So Joshua set out with all the people of war to go up to Ai. He picked thirty thousand men, mighty men of valour, and sent them out by night.
He gave them their orders: "Look — you're to lie in ambush for the city, behind it. Don't go far from the city, and all of you stay ready.
"I and all the people with me will come up close to the city, and when they come out to meet us as they did the first time, we'll flee before them.
"They'll come out after us until we've drawn them away from the city, because they'll say, 'They're running from us like the first time.' So we'll flee before them.
"Then you rise up out of the ambush and take possession of the city, and the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
"And once you've captured the city, set it on fire. Do it according to the word of the LORD. Look — I've commanded you."
So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and waited between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. And Joshua spent that night among the people.
Joshua was up early in the morning and mustered the people, and he went up to Ai ahead of them, he and the elders of Israel.
All the people of war with him went up, came in close and arrived in front of the city, and camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So the people set the whole camp north of the city, with its rear guard west of the city. And that night Joshua went into the middle of the valley.

When the king of Ai saw it, the men of the city hurried and were up early, and out they went to meet Israel for battle — he and all his people — at the appointed place before the Arabah. He didn't know there was an ambush waiting for him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten in front of them and fled by the wilderness road.
All the people in Ai were called out to chase them, and they chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
Not a man was left in Ai and Bethel who didn't go out after Israel. They left the city wide open and went after Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the javelin in your hand toward Ai, for I am giving it into your hand." And Joshua held out the javelin in his hand toward the city.
The moment he held out his hand, the men in ambush were up out of their place and running. They got into the city, captured it, and quickly set it on fire.

The men of Ai turned round and looked, and there was the smoke of the city going up to the heavens — and they had no strength to flee this way or that. And the people who'd been fleeing toward the wilderness turned back on their pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city was going up, they turned back and struck the men of Ai.

And the others came out of the city to meet them, so that they were caught by Israel in the middle, some on one side and some on the other. They struck them down until not one of them was left alive or got away.
The king of Ai they took alive and brought to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai out in the open country, in the wilderness where they'd chased them, and every one of them had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were gone, all Israel went back to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
In all, twelve thousand fell that day, men and women — all the people of Ai.
Joshua didn't draw back the hand he'd held out with the javelin until he had devoted to destruction everyone living in Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it a mound for ever, a desolation, and so it is to this day.

And the king of Ai he hanged on the tree until evening. At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took his corpse down from the tree, threw it at the entrance of the city gate and raised a great heap of stones over it, which is there to this very day.
Then Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,

just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites, and as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones that no one has taken an iron tool to. On it they offered up burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings.
And there, on the stones, he wrote a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written in front of the Israelites.

All Israel — its elders, officers and judges — stood on either side of the ark, before the priests, the Levites, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the resident alien with the native-born; half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded, to bless the people Israel first of all.
After that he read out all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, exactly as it is written in the book of the law.
There wasn't a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua didn't read out before the whole assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones and the resident aliens who walked among them.

joshua_9.t: When all the kings beyond the Jordan heard of it — in the hill country, in the Shephelah and along the whole coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites —
they all banded together to fight against Joshua and Israel, with one voice.
But the people of Gibeon had heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
and they worked a trick of their own. They went and got themselves provisions, and took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and worn-out wineskins, split and patched up,
and worn-out patched sandals on their feet and worn-out clothes on their backs; and all the bread in their provisions was dry and crumbling.
They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We've come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us."
The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "For all we know you live right among us. How could we make a covenant with you?"
"We're your servants," they said to Joshua. And Joshua said to them, "Who are you? Where do you come from?"
They said to him, "Your servants have come from a very distant land, because of the name of the LORD your God. We've heard the report of him and everything he did in Egypt,
"and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
"So our elders and everyone living in our land said to us, 'Take provisions in hand for the journey and go and meet them, and say to them: We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.'
"This bread of ours — we took it warm from our homes for provisions on the day we set out to come to you, and now it's dry and crumbling.
"And these wineskins we filled were new, and now they've split. And these clothes of ours and our sandals have worn out from the sheer length of the journey."
The men took some of their provisions, but they didn't enquire of the mouth of the LORD.
So Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them, to let them live; and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
Three days after they'd made the covenant with them, they heard that these people were near neighbours, living right among them.
So the Israelites set out and came to their cities on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.
The Israelites didn't strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled at the leaders.
But all the leaders said to the whole congregation, "We've sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we can't touch them.
"Here's what we'll do with them: let them live, so that no wrath comes on us because of the oath we swore to them."
And the leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became cutters of wood and drawers of water for the whole congregation, just as the leaders had said.
Joshua summoned them and said, "Why did you deceive us? You said, 'We are very far from you,' and here you are, living among us.
"So now you're cursed, and none of you will ever stop being slaves — cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "Your servants were plainly told that the LORD your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you all the land and to destroy everyone living in the land before you. So we were in great fear for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this.
"And now we're in your hand. Do to us whatever seems good and right in your eyes."
And that is what he did: he delivered them from the hand of the Israelites, and they didn't kill them.
That day Joshua made them cutters of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD — as they are to this day — at the place he would choose.

joshua_10.t: When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction — doing to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king — and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
they were terrified, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and bigger than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up and help me, and let's strike Gibeon — it has made peace with Joshua and with the Israelites."

So the five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon — joined forces and went up, they and all their armies, and camped against Gibeon and fought it.

The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal: "Don't let your hands drop from your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, help us — all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, all the mighty men of valour.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Don't be afraid of them. I have given them into your hand; not a man of them will stand before you."
Joshua came on them suddenly; he had marched up from Gilgal all night.
And the LORD routed them before Israel. He struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon, chased them up the road to Beth-horon and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

And as they fled before Israel, on the way down from Beth-horon, the LORD threw great stones down on them from the heavens all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over before the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD, and in the sight of Israel he said: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the Valley of Aijalon."

And the sun was still and the moon stood there, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Isn't this written in the Scroll of Jashar? The sun stood in the middle of the heavens and was in no hurry to set for about a whole day.
There's been no day like it, before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man — because the LORD was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua went back to the camp at Gilgal, and all Israel with him.
Meanwhile those five kings had fled and hidden themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found — hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
And Joshua said, "Roll great stones up against the mouth of the cave, and post men over it to guard them.
"But the rest of you — don't stand still. Go after your enemies and cut off their rear. Don't let them get into their cities; the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
When Joshua and the Israelites had finished striking them with a very great defeat, until they were finished, and the survivors who did survive had got into the fortified cities,
all the people came back safely to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah. No one sharpened his tongue against any of the Israelites.
Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring me those five kings out of it."
They did so, and brought him those five kings out of the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

And when they had brought those kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel together and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came and put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, "Don't be afraid, don't be dismayed. Be strong and bold — this is what the LORD will do to all your enemies, the ones you're fighting."
After that Joshua struck them and put them to death and hanged them on five trees, and they hung there on the trees until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they'd hidden themselves, and put great stones over the mouth of the cave — they're there to this very day.

That day Joshua captured Makkedah and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king with it. He devoted them to destruction, and every person in it — he left no survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah just what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua moved on from Makkedah to Libnah, and all Israel with him, and fought against Libnah.

The LORD gave that city too into the hand of Israel, with its king. He struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it — he left no survivor in it. And he did to its king just what he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua moved on from Libnah to Lachish, and all Israel with him, and camped against it and fought it.
The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people down until he had left him no survivor.
Joshua moved on from Lachish to Eglon, and all Israel with him, and they camped against it and fought it.
They captured it that same day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it he devoted to destruction that day, just as he had done to Lachish.
Joshua went up from Eglon to Hebron, and all Israel with him, and they fought against it.

They captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its cities and every person in it — he left no survivor, just as he had done to Eglon. He devoted it to destruction, and every person in it.
Then Joshua turned back to Debir, and all Israel with him, and fought against it.

He captured it and its king and all its cities; they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it — he left no survivor. What he had done to Hebron he did to Debir and its king, and what he had done to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua struck the whole land — the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah and the slopes — and all their kings. He left no survivor; every breathing thing he devoted to destruction, just as the LORD the God of Israel had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea all the way to Gaza, and the whole land of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land all at one time, because the LORD the God of Israel was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua went back to the camp at Gilgal, and all Israel with him.

joshua_11.t: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron and to the king of Acshaph,
and to the kings up in the north — in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Kinnereth, in the Shephelah and on the heights of Dor to the west,
to the Canaanites in the east and the west, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites under Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
Out they came, they and all their armies with them, a people as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
All these kings met up, and they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

The LORD said to Joshua, "Don't be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I am giving every one of them over, slain, before Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."
So Joshua came on them suddenly at the waters of Merom, he and all the people of war with him, and they fell on them.

The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and chased them as far as Greater Sidon, as far as Misrephoth-maim and as far as the Valley of Mizpeh eastward; they struck them until he had left them no survivor.
Joshua did to them just what the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor, and struck its king down with the sword — Hazor had once been the head of all these kingdoms.
They struck every person in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction; not a breathing thing was left. And Hazor he burned with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, and struck them with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
But Israel didn't burn any of the cities standing on their mounds — except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

All the spoil of these cities, and the livestock, the Israelites took as plunder for themselves; but every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them — they left not a breathing thing.
What the LORD had commanded Moses his servant, Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua did it. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took the whole of this land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the Shephelah, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its Shephelah,
from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. And all their kings he captured, struck down and put to death.
Joshua made war on all these kings for a long time.
Not one city made peace with the Israelites, except the Hivites, the people of Gibeon. They took all the rest in battle.

For it came from the LORD, this hardening of their heart to go and meet Israel in battle, so that they would be devoted to destruction and receive no favour, but be destroyed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country — from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, from all the hill country of Judah and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction, with their cities.
No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites. Only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod did any remain.
So Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses, and gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions, by their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_12.t: These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites struck, and whose land they took possession of beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the middle of the wadi, and half of Gilead, as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites;
and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth eastward, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, on the way to Beth-jeshimoth; and from the south, under the slopes of Pisgah;
and the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
and ruling over Mount Hermon, Salecah and all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the LORD and the Israelites struck them, and Moses the servant of the LORD gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

And these are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites struck beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession, according to their divisions:
in the hill country, in the Shephelah, in the Arabah, on the slopes, in the wilderness and in the Negev: the Hittites, the Amorites and the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Acshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor, of the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goyim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. In all, thirty-one kings.

joshua_13.t: Now Joshua was old, well on in years, and the LORD said to him, "You're old, well on in years, and there's a great deal of the land still to be taken possession of.
"Here is the land that's left: all the regions of the Philistines and all the Geshurites,

"from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north — reckoned as Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron; and the Avvim,
"from the south: all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, as far as the border of the Amorites;
"and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal-gad under Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.

"Everyone living in the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians — I myself will dispossess them before the Israelites. You just allot it to Israel as an inheritance, as I commanded you.
"So now apportion this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With it the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, just as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:
from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Moses struck them and dispossessed them.
But the Israelites did not dispossess the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath have dwelt among Israel to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance: the food offerings of the LORD, the God of Israel — that is its inheritance, just as he spoke to it.
And Moses gave to the tribe of the Reubenites, by their clans;
and their territory was from Aroer on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and the city in the middle of the wadi, and all the plain by Medeba;
Heshbon and all its cities in the plain: Dibon, Bamoth-baal and Beth-baal-meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth and Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah and Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah and Beth-jeshimoth,

and all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck, with the leaders of Midian — Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who dwelt in the land.
And Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the Israelites killed with the sword among their slain.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan and its territory. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites, by their clans;
and their territory was Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer which faces Rabbah;
and from Heshbon as far as Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim as far as the territory of Lo-debar;

and in the valley: Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and its territory, as far as the end of the Sea of Kinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites by their clans, the cities and their villages.
And Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh; and it belonged to the half-tribe of the Manassites by their clans.
Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities;
and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, belonged to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the descendants of Machir by their clans.
These are the inheritances that Moses apportioned in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward.
To the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: the LORD, the God of Israel — he is their inheritance, just as he told them.

joshua_14.t: These are the inheritances the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites apportioned to them,
by the lot of their inheritance, just as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

The descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, so they gave the Levites no portion in the land — only cities to live in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and their property.
The Israelites did just what the LORD had commanded Moses, and they apportioned the land.
The Judahites came up to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God about me and about you at Kadesh-barnea.
"I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me out from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back word just as it was in my heart.
"My brothers who went up with me melted the heart of the people, but I followed the LORD my God fully.
"And that day Moses swore, 'The land your foot has trodden on will surely be an inheritance for you and for your children for ever, because you have followed the LORD my God fully.'
"And here I am — the LORD has kept me alive, just as he said, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old.
"And I'm as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me. My strength then is my strength now, for war and for going out and coming in.

"So give me this hill country the LORD spoke about that day. You heard yourself, that day, that the Anakim were there, with great fortified cities. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I'll dispossess them, just as the LORD said."
So Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
That is how Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and it still is, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, fully.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba — Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

joshua_15.t: The lot for the tribe of the Judahites, by their clans, ran toward the border of Edom, the Wilderness of Zin, southward, from the far end of the south.
Their southern border was from the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward;
and it goes out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, passes on to Zin, goes up south of Kadesh-barnea, passes on to Hezron, goes up to Addar and turns to Karka,
passes on to Azmon and goes out at the Wadi of Egypt, and the border ends at the sea. This shall be your southern border.
The eastern border is the Salt Sea as far as the end of the Jordan. The northern border runs from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan;
the border goes up to Beth-hoglah, passes north of Beth-arabah, and goes up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben;

the border goes up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and northward turns toward Gilgal, opposite the Ascent of Adummim, south of the wadi; then it passes on to the waters of En-shemesh and ends at En-rogel;

the border goes up the Valley of Ben-hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusites — that is Jerusalem — and up to the top of the mountain facing the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim;
the border bends from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, goes out to the cities of Mount Ephron, and bends to Baalah — that is Kiriath-jearim;
the border turns from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, passes on to the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is Kesalon — goes down to Beth-shemesh and passes on to Timnah;
the border goes out to the northern slope of Ekron, bends to Shikkeron, passes on to Mount Baalah, goes out at Jabneel, and ends at the sea.
The western border is the Great Sea and its coast. This is the border of the Judahites round about, by their clans.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the Judahites, according to the mouth of the LORD to Joshua: Kiriath-arba — Arba was the father of Anak — that is, Hebron.
Caleb dispossessed the three sons of Anak from there — Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, those born of Anak.
From there he went up against the people of Debir; Debir used to be called Kiriath-sepher.
And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it — I'll give him my daughter Achsah as a wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, and he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
And when she came, she incited him to ask her father for a field. Then she got down off the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What's the matter?"
She said, "Give me a blessing. You've given me the land of the Negev — give me springs of water as well." And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Judahites by their clans.
The cities at the far end of the tribe of the Judahites, toward the border of Edom in the south, were Kabzeel, Eder and Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah and Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor and Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem and Bealoth,
Hazor-hadattah and Kerioth-hezron — that is Hazor —
Amam, Shema and Moladah,
Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon and Beth-pelet,
Hazar-shual, Beersheba and Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim and Ezem,
Eltolad, Kesil and Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah and Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon: twenty-nine cities in all, with their villages.
In the Shephelah: Eshtaol, Zorah and Ashnah,
Zanoah and En-gannim, Tappuah and Enam,
Jarmuth and Adullam, Socoh and Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen cities, with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah and Migdal-gad,
Dilean, Mizpeh and Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath and Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmas and Kitlish,
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen cities, with their villages.
Libnah, Ether and Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah and Nezib,
Keilah, Aczib and Mareshah: nine cities, with their villages.
Ekron, with its daughter-towns and its villages;
from Ekron westward, all that lies beside Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod, its daughter-towns and its villages; Gaza, its daughter-towns and its villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt, and the Great Sea and its coast.
And in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir and Socoh,
Dannah and Kiriath-sannah — that is Debir —
Anab, Eshtemoh and Anim,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh: eleven cities, with their villages.
Arab, Rumah and Eshan,
Janum, Beth-tappuah and Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath-arba — that is Hebron — and Zior: nine cities, with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph and Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam and Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah: ten cities, with their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur and Gedor,
Maarath, Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six cities, with their villages.
Kiriath-baal — that is Kiriath-jearim — and Rabbah: two cities, with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin and Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt and En-gedi: six cities, with their villages.
But the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the Judahites were not able to dispossess, and the Jebusites have dwelt with the Judahites in Jerusalem to this day.

joshua_16.t: The lot for the descendants of Joseph went out from the Jordan of Jericho, to the waters of Jericho on the east, the wilderness going up from Jericho into the hill country to Bethel.
It goes out from Bethel to Luz and passes on to the border of the Archites, to Ataroth,
and goes down westward to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, ending at the sea.
And the descendants of Joseph — Manasseh and Ephraim — received their inheritance.
The territory of the Ephraimites by their clans was this: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon;
the border goes out westward — Micmethath is on the north — turns eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passes by it on the east to Janoah,
goes down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touches Jericho and goes out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border goes westward to the Wadi Kanah and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites by their clans;
and the cities set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all the cities with their villages.
But they didn't dispossess the Canaanites living in Gezer; the Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day, and they've become a slave gang doing forced labour.

joshua_17.t: The lot fell to the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn — to Machir, Manasseh's firstborn, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war; and Gilead and Bashan belonged to him.

And it belonged to the rest of the Manassites by their clans: to the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh had no sons, only daughters; and these were his daughters' names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

They came forward before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun and before the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So he gave them, according to the mouth of the LORD, an inheritance among their father's brothers.
So ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan;
because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons; and the land of Gilead went to the rest of the Manassites.
The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Micmethath, which faces Shechem, and the border goes south, to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.
The border goes down to the Wadi Kanah, south of the wadi. These cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh, and the border of Manasseh was on the north of the wadi, ending at the sea.
Southward it belonged to Ephraim and northward to Manasseh, and the sea was its border. On the north they touch Asher, and on the east Issachar.

In Issachar and in Asher there belonged to Manasseh: Beth-shean and its daughter-towns, Ibleam and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of En-dor and its daughter-towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its daughter-towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughter-towns — the three of Napheth.
But the Manassites couldn't take possession of these cities; the Canaanites were determined to stay in this land.
Once the Israelites grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labour, but they never did utterly dispossess them.
The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given me just one lot, one portion, as an inheritance, when I'm a numerous people — seeing how the LORD has blessed me up to now?"

Joshua said to them, "If you're a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear ground for yourself there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

The descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country won't be enough for us, and the Canaanites who live down in the valley country all have iron chariots — the ones in Beth-shean and its daughter-towns and the ones in the Valley of Jezreel."
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and you have great strength. You won't have just the one lot —
"the hill country will be yours. It is forest, but you'll clear it, and its farthest parts will be yours; you will dispossess the Canaanites, iron chariots and all, strong as they are."

joshua_18.t: The whole congregation of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there; the land was subdued before them.
But seven tribes were left among the Israelites who had not received their inheritance by division.
So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long are you going to hold back from going in and taking possession of the land the LORD the God of your ancestors has given you?
"Provide three men for each tribe, and I'll send them out. They're to go and walk through the land and describe it in writing according to their inheritance, and come back to me.
"They're to divide it among themselves into seven portions. Judah stays on its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph stays on their territory in the north.
"You describe the land in writing in seven portions and bring it back to me here, and I'll cast the lot for you here before the LORD our God.

"The Levites have no portion among you — the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan eastward, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."

So the men set out and went. And Joshua's orders to those going out to describe the land in writing were: "Go and walk through the land, describe it in writing and come back to me, and here in Shiloh I'll cast the lot for you before the LORD."
The men went and passed through the land, described it in writing on a scroll, city by city, in seven portions, and came back to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
So Joshua cast the lot for them in Shiloh before the LORD, and there he apportioned the land to the Israelites according to their divisions.
The lot of the tribe of the Benjaminites came up by their clans, and the territory of their lot lay between the Judahites and the descendants of Joseph.
Their northern border was from the Jordan; the border goes up to the northern slope of Jericho, goes up in the hill country westward, and ends at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the border passes on to Luz, to the southern slope of Luz — that is Bethel — and goes down to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

The border bends and turns on the western side southward, from the mountain facing Beth-horon on the south, and ends at Kiriath-baal — that is Kiriath-jearim, a city of the Judahites. This is the western side.
The southern side is from the end of Kiriath-jearim; the border goes out westward and goes out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The border goes down to the end of the mountain facing the Valley of Ben-hinnom, in the Valley of Rephaim to the north, then down the Valley of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusites, and down to En-rogel.
It bends from the north, goes out to En-shemesh and to Geliloth, opposite the Ascent of Adummim, and goes down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben,
passes on to the slope opposite the Arabah northward, and goes down to the Arabah;
and the border passes on to the northern slope of Beth-hoglah, ending at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This is the southern border.
The Jordan borders it on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the Benjaminites, by its borders round about, by their clans.
The cities of the tribe of the Benjaminites by their clans were Jericho, Beth-hoglah and Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim and Bethel,
Avvim, Parah and Ophrah,
Kephar-ammoni, Ophni and Geba: twelve cities, with their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah and Beeroth,
Mizpeh, Kephirah and Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel and Taralah,
and Zela, Haeleph and the Jebusite city — that is Jerusalem — Gibeah and Kiriath: fourteen cities, with their villages. This is the inheritance of the Benjaminites by their clans.

joshua_19.t: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans; and their inheritance lay within the inheritance of the Judahites.
They had as their inheritance: Beersheba, Sheba and Moladah,
Hazar-shual, Balah and Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul and Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah,
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen cities, with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four cities, with their villages;
and all the villages around these cities as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites by their clans.
The inheritance of the Simeonites came out of the portion of the Judahites, because the portion of the Judahites was too great for them; and the Simeonites received their inheritance within theirs.
The third lot came up for the Zebulunites by their clans, and the border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
Their border goes up westward to Maralah, touches Dabbesheth, and touches the wadi facing Jokneam;
it turns back from Sarid eastward, toward the rising of the sun, to the border of Kisloth-tabor, goes out to Daberath and goes up to Japhia;
from there it passes on eastward, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, and goes out to Rimmon, which bends round to Neah;
the border turns about it on the north to Hannathon and ends at the Valley of Iphtah-el;
and Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the Zebulunites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
For Issachar the fourth lot came out, for the Issacharites by their clans;
their border was to Jezreel, Kesulloth and Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion and Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion and Ebez,
Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah and Beth-pazzez.
The border touches Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-shemesh, and their border ends at the Jordan: sixteen cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Issacharites by their clans: the cities, with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the Asherites by their clans;
their border was Helkath, Hali, Beten and Acshaph,
and Allammelech, Amad and Mishal; and it touches Carmel on the west and Shihor-libnath,
it turns back toward the rising of the sun to Beth-dagon, touches Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el northward, Beth-emek and Neiel, and goes out to Cabul on the north,
and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
The border turns back to Ramah and to the fortified city of Tyre, then turns back to Hosah and ends at the sea, in the region of Aczib;
and Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Asherites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
For the Naphtalites the sixth lot came out, for the Naphtalites by their clans;
their border ran from Heleph, from the great tree at Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, ending at the Jordan.
The border turns back westward to Aznoth-tabor and goes out from there to Hukkok; it touches Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath and Kinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah and Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei and En-hazor,
and Yiron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities, with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Naphtalites by their clans: the cities, with their villages.
For the tribe of the Danites by their clans the seventh lot came out.
The territory of their inheritance was Zorah, Eshtaol and Ir-shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon and Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah and Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon and Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-berak and Gath-rimmon,
and the waters of the Jarkon and the Rakkon, with the territory opposite Joppa.

The territory of the Danites went out from them, so the Danites went up and fought against Leshem, captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, took possession of it and settled in it; and they called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their ancestor.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Danites by their clans: these cities, with their villages.
When they had finished dividing the land for possession by its borders, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
According to the mouth of the LORD they gave him the city he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and lived in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites apportioned by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And so they finished dividing the land.

joshua_20.t: "Say to the Israelites: 'Assign yourselves the cities of refuge that I spoke to you about by the hand of Moses,
'so that a killer who strikes a person down inadvertently, without knowing, can flee there; they'll be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

'He is to flee to one of these cities, stand at the entrance of the city gate and state his case in the hearing of the elders of that city; and they are to take him into the city with them, give him a place, and he lives with them.
'And if the avenger of blood comes after him, they are not to hand the killer over to him, because he struck his neighbour without knowledge and hadn't hated him beforehand.

'He lives in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgement, until the death of the high priest in office in those days. Then the killer can go back to his own city and his own house, the city he fled from.'"
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba — that is, Hebron — in the hill country of Judah.

And beyond the Jordan of Jericho, eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness, out on the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the appointed cities for all the Israelites and for the resident alien living among them, so that anyone who strikes a person down inadvertently could flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood before he had stood before the congregation.

joshua_21.t: The heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the Israelites;
and they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan: "The LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock."
So the Israelites gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the mouth of the LORD, these cities with their pasture lands.
The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites, and the descendants of Aaron the priest, from among the Levites, received by lot thirteen cities from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.
The rest of the descendants of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received by lot thirteen cities from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, by their clans, received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.
And the Israelites gave these cities with their pasture lands to the Levites by lot, just as the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses.
They gave from the tribe of the Judahites and from the tribe of the Simeonites these cities, which are named here.
It went to the descendants of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathites, of the descendants of Levi, for the first lot was theirs.
They gave them Kiriath-arba — Arba was the father of Anak — that is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with its pasture lands around it.
But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his holding.
To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave the city of refuge for the killer, Hebron, with its pasture lands; and Libnah with its pasture lands,
Jattir with its pasture lands, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
Holon with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
Ain with its pasture lands, Juttah with its pasture lands and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands: nine cities from these two tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasture lands, Geba with its pasture lands,
Anathoth with its pasture lands and Almon with its pasture lands: four cities.
All the cities of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
To the clans of the descendants of Kohath, the Levites who remained of the descendants of Kohath — the cities of their lot were from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them the city of refuge for the killer, Shechem, with its pasture lands, in the hill country of Ephraim; and Gezer with its pasture lands,
Kibzaim with its pasture lands and Beth-horon with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasture lands, Gibbethon with its pasture lands,
Aijalon with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands: two cities.
All the cities were ten, with their pasture lands, for the clans of the descendants of Kohath who remained.

And to the descendants of Gershon, of the clans of the Levites: from the half-tribe of Manasseh, the city of refuge for the killer, Golan in Bashan, with its pasture lands; and Beeshterah with its pasture lands: two cities.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
Jarmuth with its pasture lands and En-gannim with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,
Helkath with its pasture lands and Rehob with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Naphtali: the city of refuge for the killer, Kedesh in Galilee, with its pasture lands; Hammoth-dor with its pasture lands and Kartan with its pasture lands: three cities.
All the cities of the Gershonites, by their clans, were thirteen cities with their pasture lands.
And to the clans of the descendants of Merari, the Levites who remained: from the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its pasture lands, Kartah with its pasture lands,
Dimnah with its pasture lands and Nahalal with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasture lands, Jahaz with its pasture lands,
Kedemoth with its pasture lands and Mephaath with its pasture lands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge for the killer, Ramoth in Gilead, with its pasture lands; and Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
Heshbon with its pasture lands and Jazer with its pasture lands: four cities in all.
All the cities of the descendants of Merari, by their clans, who remained of the clans of the Levites — their lot was twelve cities.
All the cities of the Levites within the holding of the Israelites were forty-eight cities with their pasture lands.
Each of these cities had its pasture lands around it; so it was for all these cities.
So the LORD gave Israel the whole land he had sworn to give to their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled in it.
And the LORD gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors; not one of all their enemies stood before them. The LORD gave all their enemies into their hand.
Not one word failed of all the good word the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel; every bit of it came to pass.

joshua_22.t: Then Joshua called in the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
and said to them, "You've kept everything Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you've listened to my voice in everything I commanded you.
"All this long time, right up to today, you haven't forsaken your brothers; you've kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God.

"And now the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, just as he said he would. So turn round and go to your tents, to the land of your holding, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.

"Only take great care to do the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cling to him, and to serve him with your whole heart and your whole soul."
So Joshua blessed them and sent them off, and they went to their tents.

Now Moses had given the half-tribe of Manasseh a portion in Bashan, and Joshua gave the other half a portion with their brothers beyond the Jordan westward. And when Joshua sent them off to their tents, he blessed them

and said to them, "Go back to your tents with great riches, with a great deal of livestock, with silver, gold, bronze and iron, and with a great many garments. Share the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."

So the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their holding, where they had taken possession according to the mouth of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
When they came to Geliloth of the Jordan, in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan — a great altar to look at.

And the Israelites heard it said, "The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built that altar opposite the land of Canaan, at Geliloth of the Jordan, on the side that belongs to the Israelites."
When the Israelites heard it, the whole congregation of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go up against them for war.
And the Israelites sent to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest —
and ten leaders with him, one for each ancestral house, for all the tribes of Israel; every one of them was head of his ancestral house among the thousands of Israel.
They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, and spoke with them:

"Thus says the whole congregation of the LORD: What is this unfaithfulness you've committed against the God of Israel — turning back today from following the LORD, building yourselves an altar, rebelling today against the LORD?
"Wasn't the iniquity of Peor enough for us? We haven't cleansed ourselves of it to this day, and the plague came on the congregation of the LORD because of it —
"and now you turn away today from following the LORD? Here is what will happen: you rebel today against the LORD, and tomorrow he'll be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

"Look, if the land of your holding is unclean, then cross over to the land of the LORD's holding, where the tabernacle of the LORD dwells, and take a holding among us. But don't rebel against the LORD, and don't rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of the LORD our God.
"Didn't Achan son of Zerah break faith over what was devoted to destruction, and wrath came on the whole congregation of Israel? And he was one man — didn't he perish for his iniquity?"
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the thousands of Israel:
"God, God, the LORD! God, God, the LORD! He knows — and let Israel know it too: if this was rebellion, if this was unfaithfulness against the LORD, then don't save us today!

"If we built ourselves an altar to turn back from following the LORD, or to offer up on it a burnt offering and a grain offering, or to make on it sacrifices of peace offerings — may the LORD himself require it!
"No — we did this because we were anxious about something. We said, 'One day your children will say to our children: What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
"'The LORD has put a border between us and you, Reubenites and Gadites — the Jordan. You have no portion in the LORD.' That way your children would stop our children fearing the LORD.
"So we said, 'Let's act for ourselves and build the altar — not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,

"'but so that it will be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we do perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices and our peace offerings; so that your children won't say to our children one day: You have no portion in the LORD.'

"And we said, 'When they say this to us, or to our generations to come, we'll answer: Look at the copy of the altar of the LORD that our ancestors made — not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but as a witness between us and you.'

"Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD, to turn back today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering or for sacrifice, besides the altar of the LORD our God that stands before his tabernacle."

When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites and the Manassites said, it seemed good to them.

And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you haven't committed this unfaithfulness against the LORD. You've delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD."
So Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the Reubenites and the Gadites and went back from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought them word.
The word seemed good to the Israelites, and the Israelites blessed God. They said no more about going up against them for war, to destroy the land where the Reubenites and the Gadites were living.
And the Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar a name — for it is a witness between us that the LORD is God.

joshua_23.t: A long time afterwards, when the LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies round about, and Joshua was old, well on in years,
Joshua called all Israel together — its elders, its heads, its judges and its officers — and said to them, "I'm old, well on in years.
"You have seen for yourselves everything the LORD your God has done to all these nations before you; the LORD your God — he is the one fighting for you.
"Look, I've allotted you these nations that are left as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan on; and all the nations I cut off, and the Great Sea, toward the setting of the sun.
"The LORD your God — he will thrust them out before you and dispossess them before you, and you will take possession of their land, just as the LORD your God told you.
"So be very strong: take care to do everything written in the book of the law of Moses, and don't turn aside from it to the right or the left,
"and don't go in among these nations, the ones left with you. Don't invoke the name of their gods, don't make anyone swear by them, don't serve them and don't bow down to them.
"Cling to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
"The LORD has dispossessed great and mighty nations before you; and as for you — no one has stood before you to this day.
"One man of you puts a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God is the one fighting for you, just as he told you.
"So watch yourselves closely: love the LORD your God.
"Because if you ever do turn back and cling to what is left of these nations, the ones left with you, and intermarry with them and go in among them and they among you,

"then know for certain that the LORD your God will not go on dispossessing these nations before you. They'll become a trap for you and a snare, a scourge in your sides and pricks in your eyes, until you perish from this good ground that the LORD your God has given you.

"And here I am, going today in the way of all the earth. You know with your whole heart and your whole soul that not one word has fallen of all the good words the LORD your God spoke about you. Every one of them has come to you; not one word of them has fallen.

"And just as every good word came upon you that the LORD your God spoke to you, so the LORD will bring on you every bad word, until he has destroyed you off this good ground that the LORD your God has given you,

"when you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God that he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you'll perish quickly off the good land he has given you."

joshua_24.t: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and called for the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges and its officers; and they presented themselves before God.

And Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the River — Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor — and they served other gods.
'I took your ancestor Abraham from beyond the River and led him through the whole land of Canaan. I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac.
'To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau; and to Esau I gave Mount Seir to take possession of, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
'I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt according to what I did there in its midst; and afterwards I brought you out.
'I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea; and Egypt came after your ancestors with chariotry and horsemen, right to the Sea of Reeds.

'They cried out to the LORD, and he put gloom between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you lived in the wilderness a long time.
'I brought you to the land of the Amorite who lived beyond the Jordan, and they fought you; and I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
'Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel, and he sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
'But I wasn't willing to listen to Balaam, and he blessed you again and again; and I delivered you from his hand.

'You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho, and the lords of Jericho fought against you — the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite and the Jebusite — and I gave them into your hand.
'I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out before you — the two kings of the Amorite — not by your sword and not by your bow.
'I gave you a land you never laboured for, and cities you never built, and you live in them; vineyards and olive trees you never planted, and you're eating them.'"
"So now — fear the LORD and serve him in blamelessness and in faithfulness. Get rid of the gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

"And if serving the LORD seems bad to you, choose today whom you will serve — the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorite in whose land you're living. But as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD."
The people answered, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD and serve other gods!

"It is the LORD our God who brought us and our ancestors up from the land of Egypt, from a house of slaves, and who did those great signs before our eyes and kept us all along the way we went, among all the peoples we passed through.
"And the LORD drove out all the peoples before us, and the Amorite who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD — he is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You aren't able to serve the LORD. He is a holy God; he is a jealous God. He won't forgive your transgression and your sins.
"If you forsake the LORD and serve gods of foreignness, he'll turn and do you harm and make an end of you, after he has done you good."
But the people said to Joshua, "No — we will serve the LORD."
And Joshua said to the people, "You're witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD for yourselves, to serve him." "Witnesses," they said.
"So now — get rid of the gods of foreignness that are among you, and turn your heart to the LORD, the God of Israel."
And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God, and we will listen to his voice."
So that day Joshua cut a covenant for the people, and set them a statute and an ordinance at Shechem.
And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. Then he took a great stone and set it up there under the oak that stood at the sanctuary of the LORD.

And Joshua said to all the people, "Look — this stone will be a witness against us, because it has heard all the sayings of the LORD that he spoke with us. It will be a witness against you, so that you don't deny your God."
Then Joshua let the people go, each to his own inheritance.
Some time after this, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, at a hundred and ten years old.
They buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who had known the whole work of the LORD that he did for Israel.

And the bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the piece of field that Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money; and they became an inheritance for the descendants of Joseph.
And Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, the place that had been given him in the hill country of Ephraim.

lamentations_1.t: How she sits alone, the city once crowded with people! She has become like a widow — great among the nations, a princess among the provinces, and now put to forced labour.
Bitterly she weeps in the night; her tears are on her cheek. Among all her lovers there's no one to comfort her; all her friends have dealt treacherously with her and become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile out of affliction and hard servitude. She lives among the nations and finds no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the narrows.
The roads of Zion mourn, because nobody comes to the appointed feast. All her gates lie desolate; her priests groan; her virgins grieve, and she herself is in bitterness.
