Her adversaries have come out on top; her enemies are at ease; the LORD has brought her grief for her many transgressions. Her children have gone into captivity ahead of the adversary.
All her splendour has gone from the daughter of Zion. Her princes are like deer that find no pasture, going on without strength ahead of the pursuer.

In the days of her affliction and homelessness, Jerusalem remembers all the precious things that were hers in days gone by, when her people fell into an adversary's hand with no one to help her. The adversaries looked on and laughed at her downfall.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously, and so she has become an impurity. All who honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness; she groans and turns her face away.

Her uncleanness is on her skirts; she never thought of how it would end. Her fall has been astonishing; there's no one to comfort her. "Look, LORD, at my affliction — the enemy has made himself great."
The adversary has laid his hand on all her precious things; she has watched nations enter her sanctuary — the very ones you commanded should not come into your assembly.
All her people are groaning, looking for bread. They have traded their precious things for food, just to stay alive. "Look, LORD, and see — I have become despised."
Is it nothing to you, all you who pass along the road? Look and see whether there is any pain like the pain dealt out to me, the pain the LORD brought on me on the day of his burning anger.
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overcame them. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back; he left me desolate, faint the whole day long.

The yoke of my transgressions has been bound on by his hand; they are woven together and have come up on my neck; he has made my strength fail. The Lord has handed me over to those I cannot withstand.
The Lord has swept aside all my mighty men from my midst. He has summoned an assembly against me to break my young men. The Lord has trodden the winepress of the virgin daughter of Judah.
This is why I weep; my eye, my eye runs with water, because any comforter is far from me, anyone who might restore my life. My children are desolate; the enemy has prevailed.
Zion spreads out her hands; there's no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded that Jacob's neighbours should be his adversaries. Jerusalem has become an impure thing among them.
The LORD is righteous — it is I who rebelled against his word. Listen, all you peoples, and look at my pain: my virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers, and they deceived me. My priests and my elders died in the city while they were looking for food to keep themselves alive.

Look, LORD — I am in distress; everything inside me is churning. My heart is overturned within me, because I have been utterly rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside the house, it is like death.

They have heard me groaning; there's no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my distress and they rejoice, because you have done it. Bring on the day you proclaimed, and let them become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before you, and deal with them as severely as you dealt with me for all my transgressions; for my groaning is endless and my heart is faint.

lamentations_2.t: How the Lord has covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has thrown the splendour of Israel down from heaven to earth, and has not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.

The Lord has swallowed up all the settlements of Jacob and spared nothing. In his wrath he has torn down the fortifications of the daughter of Judah, brought them to the ground, profaned the kingdom and its princes.
In burning anger he has cut off every horn of Israel; he has drawn back his right hand before the enemy; he has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire, consuming everything around.

He has bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand set like an adversary's; he has killed everything that was a delight to the eye. In the tent of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his rage like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed Israel up. He has swallowed up all her palaces and ruined his fortifications; he has multiplied mourning and lamentation in the daughter of Judah.

He has broken down his booth as if it were a garden; he has ruined his appointed place. The LORD has made appointed feast and sabbath be forgotten in Zion, and in the indignation of his anger has spurned king and priest.
The Lord has rejected his own altar and repudiated his sanctuary. He has handed the walls of her palaces over to an enemy. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a feast day.

The LORD planned to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion. He stretched out the measuring-line and did not draw his hand back from swallowing up; he made rampart and wall mourn, and together they languished.
Her gates have sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no law; and her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.

My eyes are worn out with tears; everything inside me churns. My liver is poured out on the ground over the brokenness of the daughter of my people, because children and infants faint in the open squares of the town.
They say to their mothers, "Where's the grain and wine?" as they faint away like the fatally wounded in the city squares, as their life pours out into their mothers' arms.

What can I say for you? What can I liken you to, daughter of Jerusalem? What can I compare you to, so I might comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? Your brokenness is as vast as the sea; who can heal you?
Your prophets saw worthlessness and sham for you; they never laid bare your iniquity, which might have restored your fortunes; they saw for you oracles of worthlessness, and enticements.
All who pass along the road clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city they called 'perfect in beauty, a joy to all the earth'?"
All your enemies open their mouths wide at you; they hiss and gnash their teeth and say, "We've swallowed her up! This is the day we waited for — we've found it, we've seen it."

The LORD has done what he purposed; he has fulfilled the speech he commanded long ago. He has torn down and spared nothing; he has made the enemy rejoice over you and lifted up the horn of your adversaries.
Their heart cries out to the Lord. Wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river, day and night! Give yourself no rest; let your eyes not stop.

Get up, cry out in the night, at the start of every watch! Pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord. Lift your hands to him for the life of your children, who faint with hunger at the head of every street.
Look, LORD, and see! Whom have you ever dealt with so severely? Are women to eat their own offspring, the children they have reared? Are priest and prophet to be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You killed on the day of your anger; you slaughtered; you didn't spare.
You summoned my terrors from every side, as if to a feast day, and on the day of the LORD's anger no one escaped, no one survived. The children I bore and reared, my enemy has finished them.

lamentations_3.t: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his fury.
He has driven me and made me walk in darkness and not in light.
Again and again he turns his hand against me, all day long.
He has worn away my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones.
He has thrown up works against me and hemmed me in with poison and hardship.
He has made me live in dark places, like those long dead.
He has walled me in so I can't get out; he has weighed me down with bronze fetters.
Even when I cry out and call for help, he shuts my prayer out.
He has blocked my ways with hewn stone; he has made my paths crooked.
To me he is a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding.
He has turned me off my ways and torn me to pieces; he has left me desolate.
He has bent his bow and set me up as a target for the arrow.
He has driven into my kidneys the sons of his quiver.
I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their mocking song all day long.
He has filled me full of bitterness; he has made me drink wormwood.
He has broken my teeth on gravel and pressed me down into the ashes.
My life is shut out from peace; I have forgotten what good is.
And I said, "My endurance has perished, and so has what I expected from the LORD."
Remember my affliction and my homelessness, the wormwood and the poison.
I remember it well, and I am bowed down inside.
This is what I call to mind; and so I will wait.
The steadfast love of the LORD — surely we are not consumed; his compassion does not come to an end.
They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
"The LORD is my portion," I have said; "so I will wait for him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to anyone who seeks him.
It is good to wait quietly for the deliverance of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear a yoke while he is young.
Let him sit alone and be silent, since he has laid it on him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust — perhaps there's hope.
Let him give his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him take his fill of reproach.
For the Lord won't reject for ever.
Though he has brought grief, he will have compassion in the greatness of his steadfast love.
He doesn't afflict from the heart, or grieve the children of a man.
To crush under foot all the prisoners of the land,
to deny a man justice before the presence of the Most High,
to twist a person's case at law — does the Lord not see it?
Who ever spoke and it came to be, unless the Lord commanded it?
Don't both troubles and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should a living person complain — a man — about his own sins?
Let us examine our ways and search them out, and return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.
We ourselves have transgressed and rebelled; you haven't forgiven.
You wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you killed, and you didn't spare.
You wrapped yourself in a cloud so that no prayer could get through.
You have made us scourings and refuse among the peoples.
All our enemies open their mouths wide at us.
Terror and a pit have come on us, devastation and brokenness.
My eye runs with streams of water over the brokenness of the daughter of my people.
My eye pours itself out and will not stop, with no let-up,
until the LORD looks down and sees from heaven.
What my eye sees brings me grief, because of all the daughters of my city.
My enemies hunted me down like a bird, for no reason at all.
They cut off my life in the pit and threw a stone down on me.
The waters closed over my head; I said, "I'm cut off."
I called on your name, LORD, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice: "Don't close your ear to my plea for relief, to my cry for help."
You drew near on the day I called on you; you said, "Don't be afraid."
You took up my cause, Lord; you redeemed my life.
You have seen the wrong done to me, LORD; now judge my case.
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plans against me.
You have heard their reproach, LORD, all their plans against me —
the lips of those who rise against me, their muttering against me all day long.
Look at them sitting and rising: I am their mocking song.
Repay them what they deserve, LORD, according to the work of their hands.
Give them hardness of heart; let your curse be on them.
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the LORD's heavens.

lamentations_4.t: How the gold is dimmed, the fine gold changed! The holy stones lie scattered at the head of every street.
The precious children of Zion, once worth their weight in pure gold — how they are reckoned as earthenware jars, the work of a potter's hands!
Even jackals give the breast and suckle their young; but the daughter of my people has turned cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
The infant's tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst; children ask for bread, and no one breaks it for them.
Those who ate delicacies now lie desolate in the streets; those brought up in crimson embrace ash heaps.
The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and no hands were wrung over her.
Her nobles were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies more ruddy than corals; their form like sapphire.
Their faces are darker than soot; nobody recognises them in the streets. Their skin has shrivelled on their bones; it has gone dry as wood.
Better were those slain by the sword than those slain by hunger, who wasted away, pierced through, for lack of the produce of the field.
The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food in the brokenness of the daughter of my people.
The LORD has spent his rage; he has poured out his burning anger; he has kindled a fire in Zion that has consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth didn't believe it, nor did anyone living in the world, that opponent and enemy would enter the gates of Jerusalem.
It came from the sins of her prophets, the iniquities of her priests, who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
They wandered blind through the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could so much as touch their garments.
"Away! Unclean!" people shouted at them; "Away, away, don't touch!" So they fled and wandered; and among the nations they said, "They can't stay here."
The presence of the LORD has scattered them; he will look on them no more. They showed no regard for the priests, no favour to the elders.
Our eyes failed, still looking for a help that was vapour. From our watchtower we watched for a nation that could not save.
They hunted our steps so we couldn't walk in our own squares. Our end drew near; our days were finished; our end had come.
Our pursuers were swifter than eagles in the sky; they chased us down on the mountains; in the wilderness they lay in wait for us.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was caught in their pits — the one of whom we said, "In his shadow we shall live among the nations."
Exult and rejoice, daughter of Edom, living in the land of Uz! The cup will pass to you as well; you will get drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your iniquity is finished, daughter of Zion; he will not exile you again. He will punish your iniquity, daughter of Edom; he will lay bare your sins.

lamentations_5.t: Remember, LORD, what has happened to us; look, and see our disgrace.
Our inheritance has passed to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We've become orphans, with no father; our mothers are like widows.
We pay money for our own water; our own wood comes at a price.
They are on our necks, driving us; we are worn out, and we are given no rest.
We have given a hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, just to have enough bread.
Our ancestors sinned, and they're gone; and we have carried their iniquities.
Slaves rule over us; there's no one to pull us free from their hand.
We bring in our bread at the risk of our lives, because of the sword of the wilderness.
Our skin is hot as an oven, from the scorching heat of hunger.
Women in Zion they have violated, virgins in the cities of Judah.
Princes were strung up by their hands; the faces of elders were shown no honour.
Young men carry the millstone; boys stagger under loads of wood.
The elders are gone from the gate, the young men from their music.
The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head! Woe to us now, for we've sinned.
Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes have grown dim.
For Mount Zion lies desolate; foxes prowl over it.
You, LORD, are enthroned for ever; your throne stands from generation to generation.
Why do you forget us for ever, abandon us for so long?
Turn us back to yourself, LORD, and we will return; make our days new again as they were long ago.
Unless you've rejected us for good, and are angry with us beyond all measure.

leviticus_1.t: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting.
Tell the people of Israel: when one of you brings an offering to the LORD, bring it from the livestock — from the herd or from the flock.
If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, it has to be an unblemished male. He brings it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, for acceptance before the LORD.
He presses his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it's accepted for him, to make atonement for him.
He slaughters the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests bring the blood and dash it against the altar on every side, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He skins the burnt offering and cuts it into pieces.
Aaron's sons, the priest, put fire on the altar and lay the wood out on the fire.
Aaron's sons the priests lay out the pieces, the head and the suet, on the wood that's on the fire on the altar.
He washes its entrails and its legs with water, and the priest turns all of it to smoke on the altar: a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If the offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, it has to be an unblemished male.
He slaughters it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests dash its blood against the altar on every side.
He cuts it into pieces, with its head and its suet, and the priest lays them out on the wood that's on the fire on the altar.
He washes the entrails and the legs with water, and the priest brings all of it and turns it to smoke on the altar. It's a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If the burnt offering for the LORD is from birds, he brings turtle-doves or young pigeons.
The priest brings it to the altar, pinches off its head and turns it to smoke on the altar, and its blood is drained out against the altar wall.
He takes out its craw with its feathers and throws it down beside the altar on the east side, where the fatty ashes go.

He tears it apart by its wings without pulling it in two, and the priest turns it to smoke on the altar, on the wood that's on the fire. It's a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.

leviticus_2.t: When someone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering is fine flour. He pours oil on it and puts frankincense on it.

He brings it to Aaron's sons the priests. The priest scoops out a full handful of the fine flour and the oil, with all the frankincense, and turns that memorial portion to smoke on the altar: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
What's left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It's most holy, from the LORD's food offerings.
When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it's fine flour — unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers brushed with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked on a griddle, it's fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Crumble it up and pour oil on it. It's a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering made in a pan, it's made of fine flour with oil.
You bring the grain offering made from these to the LORD. It's handed to the priest, and he brings it to the altar.
The priest lifts out the memorial portion from the grain offering and turns it to smoke on the altar: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
What's left of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It's most holy, from the LORD's food offerings.
No grain offering you bring to the LORD is made with leaven, because you're not to turn any leaven or any honey to smoke as a food offering to the LORD.
You bring them to the LORD as an offering of first produce, but they don't go up on the altar as a soothing odour.
Salt every grain offering of yours with salt. Don't let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering — bring salt with all your offerings.
If you bring a grain offering of first fruits to the LORD, bring fresh ears roasted in fire — groats of fresh grain — as your first-fruits grain offering.
You put oil on it and place frankincense on it. It's a grain offering.
The priest turns its memorial portion to smoke — some of the groats and some of the oil, with all the frankincense: a food offering to the LORD.

leviticus_3.t: If the offering is a sacrifice of peace offering and he's bringing it from the herd, male or female, he brings it unblemished before the LORD.
He presses his hand on the head of his offering and slaughters it at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons the priests dash the blood against the altar on every side.
From the sacrifice of peace offering he brings a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he takes off along with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons turn it to smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that's on the wood on the fire: a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, he brings it unblemished, male or female.
If he's bringing a sheep as his offering, he brings it before the LORD.
He presses his hand on the head of his offering and slaughters it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons dash its blood against the altar on every side.

From the sacrifice of peace offering he brings a food offering to the LORD: its fat — the whole fat tail, cut off close to the backbone — and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he takes off along with the kidneys.
The priest turns it to smoke on the altar: food of a food offering to the LORD.
If his offering is a goat, he brings it before the LORD.
He presses his hand on its head and slaughters it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons dash its blood against the altar on every side.
From it he brings his offering, a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he takes off along with the kidneys.
The priest turns them to smoke on the altar: food of a food offering, a soothing odour. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a perpetual statute for all your generations, wherever you live: you're to eat no fat and no blood.

leviticus_4.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Tell the people of Israel: when someone sins inadvertently against any of the LORD's commandments about things that aren't to be done, and does any one of them —
If it's the anointed priest who sins, bringing guilt on the people, then for the sin he's committed he brings the LORD an unblemished young bull as a sin offering.
He brings the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, presses his hand on its head, and slaughters it before the LORD.
The anointed priest takes some of the bull's blood and brings it into the tent of meeting.
The priest dips his finger in the blood and sprinkles some of it seven times before the LORD, towards the face of the veil of the holy place.

The priest puts some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and pours out all the rest of the bull's blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He lifts out all the fat of the bull of the sin offering: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he takes off along with the kidneys,
just as it's lifted out from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offering. Then the priest turns them to smoke on the altar of burnt offering.
But the bull's hide and all its flesh, with its head and legs, its entrails and its dung —
he carries all the rest of the bull outside the camp to a clean place, where the fatty ashes are poured out, and burns it on wood in a fire. It's burned where the fatty ashes are poured out.
If the whole congregation of Israel goes astray and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do one of the things the LORD commanded not to be done, and so become guilty —
and the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly brings a young bull as a sin offering and sets it in front of the tent of meeting.
The elders of the congregation press their hands on the head of the bull before the LORD, and the bull is slaughtered before the LORD.
The anointed priest brings some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
The priest dips his finger in the blood and sprinkles it seven times before the LORD, towards the face of the veil.

He puts some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and pours out all the rest at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He lifts out all its fat and turns it to smoke on the altar.
He does with this bull just what he did with the bull of the sin offering. The priest makes atonement for them, and they're forgiven.
He carries the bull outside the camp and burns it the way he burned the first bull. It's the sin offering of the assembly.
When a leader sins and inadvertently does one of the things the LORD his God commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty —
or the sin he committed is made known to him, he brings an unblemished male goat as his offering.
He presses his hand on the goat's head and slaughters it where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It's a sin offering.
The priest takes some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger and puts it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, then pours out the rest at the base of that altar.
He turns all its fat to smoke on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offering. The priest makes atonement for him from his sin, and he's forgiven.
If one of the ordinary people sins inadvertently by doing one of the things the LORD commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty —
or the sin he committed is made known to him, he brings an unblemished female goat as his offering, for the sin he committed.
He presses his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughters it where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest takes some of its blood on his finger and puts it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, then pours out all the rest at the base of the altar.

He removes all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of peace offering, and the priest turns it to smoke on the altar as a soothing odour to the LORD. The priest makes atonement for him, and he's forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, it has to be an unblemished female.
He presses his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughters it as a sin offering where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest takes some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger and puts it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, then pours out all the rest at the base of the altar.

He removes all its fat, just as the fat of the sheep is removed from the sacrifice of peace offering, and the priest turns it to smoke on the altar, on the LORD's food offerings. The priest makes atonement for him for the sin he committed, and he's forgiven.

leviticus_5.t: When someone sins this way — he hears a public adjuration and he was a witness, whether he saw it or knew about it, and he doesn't report it — he has to bear his iniquity.
Or if someone touches anything unclean — the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or unclean livestock, or an unclean swarming creature — and doesn't realise it, he's unclean and becomes guilty.
Or if he touches a human uncleanness — any uncleanness that makes a person unclean — without realising it, and then finds out, he becomes guilty.

Or if someone swears, blurting out with his lips that he'll do harm or do good — whatever people blurt out in an oath — without realising it, and then finds out, he becomes guilty in one of these ways.
When he becomes guilty in one of these ways, he confesses the sin he's committed.
He brings his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he's committed: a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering. The priest makes atonement for him from his sin.
If he can't afford a sheep, he brings the LORD two turtle-doves or two young pigeons as his guilt offering for the sin he's committed — one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He brings them to the priest, who offers the one for the sin offering first. He pinches off its head at the front of its neck but doesn't sever it.
He sprinkles some of the blood of the sin offering against the altar wall, and the rest is drained out at the base of the altar. It's a sin offering.
The second one he offers as a burnt offering, according to the ordinance. The priest makes atonement for him from the sin he committed, and he's forgiven.

If he can't afford two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, he brings a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as his offering for the sin he's committed, as a sin offering. He doesn't put oil on it or frankincense, because it's a sin offering.
He brings it to the priest, and the priest scoops out a full handful as its memorial portion and turns it to smoke on the altar, on the LORD's food offerings. It's a sin offering.
The priest makes atonement for him for the sin he committed in any of these ways, and he's forgiven. What's left belongs to the priest, like the grain offering.

When someone acts unfaithfully and sins inadvertently against the holy things of the LORD, he brings the LORD an unblemished ram from the flock as his guilt offering, at the valuation in silver shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
He repays what he took wrongly from the holy thing, adds a fifth to it, and gives it to the priest. The priest makes atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he's forgiven.
If someone sins by doing one of the things the LORD commanded not to be done, and didn't know it, he becomes guilty and has to bear his iniquity.

He brings the priest an unblemished ram from the flock at the valuation, as a guilt offering. The priest makes atonement for him for the inadvertence he strayed into without knowing, and he's forgiven.
It's a guilt offering. He is certainly guilty before the LORD.

leviticus_6.t: The LORD said to Moses:

When someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by cheating a fellow Israelite over a deposit, or a pledge left in his hands, or something taken by robbery, or by extorting from a fellow Israelite,
or if he's found lost property and lied about it and sworn falsely — any of the things people do and so sin —
then, once he sins and becomes guilty, he gives back what he took by robbery, or what he got by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
or anything he swore falsely about. He repays it in full, adds a fifth, and gives it to its owner on the day he's found guilty.
He brings the LORD his guilt offering: an unblemished ram from the flock, at the valuation, as a guilt offering, to the priest.
The priest makes atonement for him before the LORD, and he's forgiven for any of the things a person may do and so become guilty.
The LORD said to Moses:
Command Aaron and his sons: this is the law for the burnt offering. The burnt offering stays on the hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire is kept burning on it.
The priest puts on his linen garment and linen undergarments next to his body, lifts up the fatty ashes the fire has reduced the burnt offering to on the altar, and sets them beside the altar.
Then he takes off his garments, puts on others, and carries the fatty ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar is kept burning; it doesn't go out. Morning by morning the priest kindles wood on it, lays the burnt offering out on it, and turns the fats of the peace offerings to smoke on it.
A fire is kept burning continually on the altar; it doesn't go out.
This is the law for the grain offering. Aaron's sons present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

He lifts out a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and some of its oil, with all the frankincense on the grain offering, and turns it to smoke on the altar: a soothing odour, its memorial portion, to the LORD.
Aaron and his sons eat what's left of it. It's eaten unleavened, in a holy place — in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It isn't to be baked with leaven. I've given it as their share from my food offerings. It's most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.
Every male among Aaron's sons eats it — a perpetual due for all your generations from the LORD's food offerings. Whatever touches them becomes holy.
The LORD said to Moses:
This is the offering Aaron and his sons bring the LORD on the day he's anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It's made on a griddle with oil, and you bring it well mixed. You present it baked in pieces, a grain offering of crumbs, a soothing odour to the LORD.
The anointed priest who takes his place from among his sons makes it. It's a perpetual due to the LORD, turned entirely to smoke as a whole offering.
Every grain offering of a priest is a whole offering; it isn't eaten.
The LORD said to Moses:
Tell Aaron and his sons: this is the law for the sin offering. The sin offering is slaughtered before the LORD where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It's most holy.
The priest who offers it as a sin offering eats it. It's eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh becomes holy, and if any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, you wash the sprinkled part in a holy place.
An earthenware vessel it was boiled in has to be broken; a bronze vessel it was boiled in is scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests eats it. It's most holy.
But any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place isn't eaten. It's burned in the fire.

leviticus_7.t: This is the law for the guilt offering. It's most holy.
The guilt offering is slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood is dashed against the altar on every side.
He brings all its fat: the fat tail and the fat covering the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them, at the loins, and the lobe on the liver, which he takes off along with the kidneys.
The priest turns them to smoke on the altar as a food offering to the LORD. It's a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests eats it. It's eaten in a holy place. It's most holy.
The guilt offering works like the sin offering — one law covers both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who presents anyone's burnt offering keeps the hide of that burnt offering; it belongs to him.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything made in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who presents it.
Every grain offering, mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all Aaron's sons alike, each like his brother.
This is the law for the sacrifice of peace offering that a person brings to the LORD.

If he brings it for thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he brings unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers brushed with oil, and loaves of well-mixed fine flour mixed with oil.
He brings his offering with loaves of leavened bread, along with his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offering.
From each kind he brings one as a contribution to the LORD, and it belongs to the priest who dashes the blood of the peace offerings.
The meat of his thanksgiving sacrifice of peace offering is eaten the same day it's offered. He leaves none of it till morning.
If his sacrifice is a vow or a freewill offering, it's eaten on the day he brings it, and what's left may be eaten the next day.
Whatever's left of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day is burned in the fire.

If any of the meat of his sacrifice of peace offering is eaten at all on the third day, it isn't accepted. It isn't credited to the one who presented it; it's tainted, and whoever eats it has to bear his iniquity.
Meat that touches anything unclean isn't eaten; it's burned in the fire. Otherwise, anyone who's clean may eat the meat.
But anyone who eats meat from the sacrifice of peace offering that belongs to the LORD while his uncleanness is on him is cut off from his kin.

If someone touches anything unclean — a human uncleanness, unclean livestock, or any unclean detestable creature — and then eats meat from the sacrifice of peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person is cut off from his kin.
The LORD said to Moses:
Tell the people of Israel: you're to eat no fat of ox, sheep or goat.
The fat of a carcass or of an animal torn by beasts can be put to any use, but you're certainly not to eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering is presented to the LORD is cut off from his kin.
You're to eat no blood anywhere you live, whether of bird or of livestock.
Anyone who eats blood of any kind is cut off from his kin.
The LORD said to Moses:
Tell the people of Israel: whoever brings his sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD brings his offering to the LORD from that sacrifice.
He brings the LORD's food offerings with his own hands: the fat along with the breast, the breast to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest turns the fat to smoke on the altar, and the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your sacrifices of peace offerings.
Whichever of Aaron's sons presents the blood of the peace offerings and the fat gets the right thigh as his portion.

For I've taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the people of Israel, out of their sacrifices of peace offerings, and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual due from the people of Israel.
This is the anointing portion of Aaron and his sons from the LORD's food offerings, from the day they were presented to serve as priests to the LORD,
which the LORD commanded to be given them by the people of Israel on the day he anointed them — a perpetual statute for all their generations.
This is the law for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering and the sacrifice of peace offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the people of Israel to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.

leviticus_8.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams and the basket of unleavened bread,
and gather the whole congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses did just what the LORD commanded him, and the congregation assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the congregation: this is what the LORD commanded to be done.
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on him, tied the sash round him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, tied the waistband of the ephod round him and fastened it on him with it.
He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim into it.
He placed the turban on his head and set the gold plate, the holy crown, on the front of the turban, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil, anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and set them apart as holy.
He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its articles, and the washbasin and its stand, to set them apart as holy.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him, to set him apart as holy.
Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes round them and bound headdresses on them, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.

It was slaughtered, and Moses took the blood and with his finger put it on the horns of the altar all round, purifying the altar from sin. He poured the blood out at the base of the altar and set it apart as holy, to make atonement for it.
He took all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and their fat, and Moses turned them to smoke on the altar.
The bull, with its hide, flesh and dung, he burned in the fire outside the camp, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.
It was slaughtered, and Moses dashed the blood against the altar on every side.
He cut the ram into pieces, and Moses turned the head, the pieces and the suet to smoke.

He washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses turned the whole ram to smoke on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
He brought forward the second ram, the ram of the ordination offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.
It was slaughtered, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, the thumb of his right hand and the big toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron's sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, the thumbs of their right hands and the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses dashed the blood against the altar on every side.
He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD he took one unleavened loaf, one loaf of oiled bread and one wafer, and placed them on the fat portions and the right thigh.
He put all of it on the palms of Aaron and his sons, and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then Moses took them from their palms and turned them to smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. From the ram of the ordination offering it was Moses' portion, just as the LORD commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments with him. So he set apart as holy Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons: boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting and eat it there, along with the bread in the basket of the ordination offering, as I commanded — Aaron and his sons are to eat it.
Whatever's left of the meat and the bread you burn in the fire.
You aren't to leave the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until your days of ordination are completed — for seven days he ordains you.
What's been done today is what the LORD commanded to be done, to make atonement for you.
You're to stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and keep the charge of the LORD, so you don't die — that's what I've been commanded.
Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD commanded through Moses.

leviticus_9.t: On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron: take a young bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both unblemished, and bring them before the LORD.
And say to the people of Israel: take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and unblemished, for a burnt offering,
and an ox and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil — because today the LORD is appearing to you.
They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said: this is what the LORD commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.

Moses said to Aaron: come up to the altar, offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then offer the people's offering and make atonement for them, just as the LORD commanded.
Aaron came up to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.
Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he dipped his finger in it and put it on the horns of the altar, then poured out the rest at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering he turned to smoke on the altar, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
The flesh and the hide he burned in the fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he dashed it against the altar on every side.
They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, along with the head, and he turned them to smoke on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs and turned them to smoke on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat of the sin offering that was for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it as a sin offering like the first.
He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.
He presented the grain offering, filled his palm from it, and turned it to smoke on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram, the people's sacrifice of peace offering, and Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he dashed it against the altar on every side.
As for the fat portions from the ox and the ram — the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys and the lobe of the liver —
they placed the fat portions on the breasts, and he turned them to smoke on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, just as Moses commanded.
Aaron lifted his hands towards the people and blessed them, then came down from making the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting. When they came out they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire went out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. All the people saw it, shouted, and fell on their faces.

leviticus_10.t: Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, each took his censer, put fire in it, placed incense on it, and brought unauthorised fire before the LORD — fire he hadn't commanded them.
Fire went out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Moses said to Aaron: this is what the LORD said — 'Among those near me I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be honoured.' And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said: come forward, carry your kinsmen away from the front of the holy place, outside the camp.
They came forward and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, just as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar: don't let your heads go loose and don't tear your garments, so you don't die and he doesn't become angry with the whole congregation. But your kinsmen, all the house of Israel, may weep for the burning the LORD has burned.
Don't leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you'll die, because the LORD's anointing oil is on you. And they did as Moses said.
The LORD said to Aaron:
You and your sons with you aren't to drink wine or strong drink when you come into the tent of meeting, so you don't die. This is a perpetual statute for all your generations,
so you can separate the holy from the common, and the unclean from the clean,
and teach the people of Israel all the statutes the LORD has spoken to them through Moses.
Moses spoke to Aaron and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: take the grain offering left from the LORD's food offerings and eat it unleavened beside the altar — it's most holy.
You're to eat it in a holy place, because it's your due and your sons' due from the LORD's food offerings — that's what I've been commanded.

The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you're to eat in a clean place — you, your sons and your daughters with you — because they're given as your due and your sons' due from the sacrifices of peace offerings of the people of Israel.

They bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering along with the food offerings of the fat portions, to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD. It belongs to you and your sons with you as a perpetual due, just as the LORD commanded.
Moses searched and searched for the goat of the sin offering, and there it was — burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said:
Why didn't you eat the sin offering in the holy place? It's most holy, and he gave it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Look, its blood wasn't brought inside the holy place. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.

Aaron said to Moses: look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and then this happened to me. If I'd eaten a sin offering today, would that have been good in the eyes of the LORD?
Moses heard this, and it was good in his eyes.

leviticus_11.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Tell the people of Israel: these are the creatures you may eat from among all the animals on the land.
Any animal with a divided hoof, cleft right through, that chews the cud, you may eat.
But of those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you're not to eat these: the camel, because it chews the cud but doesn't have a divided hoof — it's unclean for you;
and the rock hyrax, because it chews the cud but doesn't have a divided hoof — it's unclean for you;
and the hare, because it chews the cud but doesn't have a divided hoof — it's unclean for you;
and the pig, because it has a divided hoof, cleft right through, but doesn't chew the cud — it's unclean for you.
You're not to eat their meat, and you're not to touch their carcasses. They're unclean for you.
Of everything in the waters you may eat these: anything with fins and scales, in the seas and in the wadis.
But anything in the seas and wadis without fins and scales — any swarming creature of the waters, any living creature in the waters — is detestable to you.
They're to be detestable to you: don't eat their flesh, and treat their carcasses as detestable.
Anything in the waters without fins and scales is detestable to you.
And these you're to treat as detestable among the birds; they aren't eaten, they're detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, every kind of falcon,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every winged swarming creature that goes on four legs is detestable to you.
But of all the winged swarming creatures that go on four legs, you may eat these: the ones with jointed legs above their feet, for hopping on the ground.
Of these you may eat: every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket, every kind of grasshopper.
But every other winged swarming creature with four feet is detestable to you.
These make you unclean: whoever touches their carcasses is unclean until evening,
and whoever carries any of their carcasses washes his garments and is unclean until evening.
Every animal with a divided hoof that isn't cleft right through, or that doesn't chew the cud, is unclean for you. Whoever touches them is unclean.
Anything that goes on its paws, among all the creatures that go on four feet, is unclean for you. Whoever touches their carcasses is unclean until evening,
and whoever carries their carcasses washes his garments and is unclean until evening. They're unclean for you.
These are unclean for you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the choled, the mouse, every kind of tsav,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are unclean for you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they're dead is unclean until evening.

Anything one of them falls on when dead becomes unclean: any wooden vessel, garment, hide or sacking, any vessel used for work. It's put into water and stays unclean until evening, and then it's clean.
If one of them falls into an earthenware vessel, everything in it is unclean, and you break the vessel.
Any food that may be eaten which such water has touched is unclean, and any drink that may be drunk from any such vessel is unclean.
Anything part of their carcass falls on is unclean. An oven or a stove is broken down; they're unclean, and they stay unclean for you.
But a spring or a cistern, a gathering of water, stays clean; still, whoever touches their carcass in it is unclean.
If part of their carcass falls on seed that's to be sown, the seed stays clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and part of their carcass falls on it, it's unclean for you.
If an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass is unclean until evening.
Whoever eats of its carcass washes his garments and is unclean until evening, and whoever carries its carcass washes his garments and is unclean until evening.
Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it isn't eaten.
Anything that goes on its belly, anything on four feet, anything with many feet, among all the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground — don't eat them; they're detestable.
Don't make yourselves detestable by any swarming creature that swarms, and don't make yourselves unclean by them, and so become unclean through them.
For I am the LORD your God. Set yourselves apart as holy and be holy, because I am holy. Don't make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that creeps on the ground.
For I am the LORD who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You are to be holy, because I am holy.
This is the law about livestock and birds and every living creature that moves in the waters and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to separate the unclean from the clean, and the creature that may be eaten from the creature that may not.

leviticus_12.t: Tell the people of Israel: when a woman conceives and bears a boy, she's unclean for seven days, as in the days of her menstrual impurity.
On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin is circumcised.
Then for thirty-three days she stays in the blood of her cleansing. She isn't to touch any holy thing or enter the sanctuary until the days of her cleansing are completed.
If she bears a girl, she's unclean for two weeks, as in her menstrual impurity, and for sixty-six days she stays upon the blood of her cleansing.

When the days of her cleansing are completed, for a son or a daughter, she brings a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtle-dove for a sin offering, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest.
The priest presents it before the LORD and makes atonement for her, and she's clean from the flow of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth, whether to a boy or a girl.
If she can't afford a sheep, she takes two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering. The priest makes atonement for her, and she's clean.

leviticus_13.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:

When someone has a swelling, a rash or a bright spot on the skin of his body, and it becomes an affliction of leprosy on the skin of his body, he's brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.

The priest examines the affliction on the skin of the body. If the hair in it has turned white and it looks deeper than the skin, it's an affliction of leprosy; the priest examines him and pronounces him unclean.
But if it's a white bright spot on the skin of his body, not deeper than the skin, and the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest shuts the afflicted person away for seven days.
The priest examines him on the seventh day. If the affliction has stayed as it was and hasn't spread in the skin, the priest shuts him away for a second seven days.
The priest examines him again on the seventh day. If the affliction has faded and hasn't spread in the skin, the priest pronounces him clean. It's a rash; he washes his garments and is clean.
But if the rash spreads further in the skin after he's shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shows himself to the priest a second time.
The priest examines him, and if the rash has spread in the skin, he pronounces him unclean. It's leprosy.
When an affliction of leprosy is on a person, he's brought to the priest.
The priest examines him. If there's a white swelling in the skin that's turned the hair white, and a raw spot of living flesh in the swelling,
it's a long-standing leprosy in the skin of his body, and the priest pronounces him unclean. He doesn't shut him away, because he's unclean.
But if the leprosy breaks out all over the skin and covers the afflicted person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
then the priest examines him, and if the leprosy has covered his whole body, he pronounces the afflicted person clean. All of it has turned white; he's clean.
But on the day living flesh appears on him he's unclean.
The priest examines the living flesh and pronounces him unclean. The living flesh is unclean; it's leprosy.
Or if the living flesh changes back and turns white, he comes to the priest.
The priest examines him, and if the affliction has turned white, he pronounces the afflicted person clean. He's clean.
When there's a boil on someone's skin and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there's a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, he shows himself to the priest.
The priest examines it, and if it looks lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, he pronounces him unclean. It's an affliction of leprosy that's broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there's no white hair in it, it isn't lower than the skin, and it's faded, he shuts him away for seven days.
If it spreads further in the skin, the priest pronounces him unclean. It's an affliction.
But if the bright spot stays where it is and hasn't spread, it's the scar of the boil, and the priest pronounces him clean.
Or when someone has a burn from fire on the skin, and the raw spot of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white bright spot,

then the priest examines it. If the hair has turned white in the bright spot and it looks deeper than the skin, it's leprosy that's broken out in the burn. The priest pronounces him unclean. It's an affliction of leprosy.
But if the priest examines it and there's no white hair in the bright spot, it isn't lower than the skin, and it's faded, he shuts him away for seven days.
The priest examines him on the seventh day. If it's spread further in the skin, he pronounces him unclean. It's an affliction of leprosy.
But if the bright spot stays where it is and hasn't spread in the skin, and it's faded, it's the swelling of the burn, and the priest pronounces him clean — it's the scar of the burn.
When a man or a woman has an affliction on the head or in the beard,
then the priest examines the affliction. If it looks deeper than the skin and there's thin yellow hair in it, he pronounces him unclean. It's a scall; it's leprosy of the head or the beard.
But when the priest examines the affliction of the scall and it doesn't look deeper than the skin, and there's no black hair in it, he shuts the person with the scall away for seven days.
The priest examines the affliction on the seventh day. If the scall hasn't spread, there's no yellow hair in it, and it doesn't look deeper than the skin,
he shaves himself, but doesn't shave the scall; and the priest shuts the scall away for a second seven days.
The priest examines the scall on the seventh day. If it hasn't spread in the skin and doesn't look deeper than the skin, he pronounces him clean; he washes his garments and is clean.
But if the scall spreads further in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest examines him, and if the scall has spread in the skin, he doesn't need to look for the yellow hair. He's unclean.
But if in his sight the scall has stayed as it was and black hair has grown in it, the scall has healed. He's clean, and the priest pronounces him clean.
When a man or a woman has bright spots on the skin — white bright spots —
then the priest examines them. If the bright spots on the skin are a faded white, it's a harmless rash that's broken out on the skin. The person is clean.
When a man's head loses its hair, he's bald; he's clean.
If his head loses its hair at the front, towards his face, he's bald at the forehead; he's clean.
But if there's a reddish-white affliction on the bald patch or the bald forehead, it's leprosy breaking out there.
The priest examines him. If the swelling of the affliction on his bald patch or bald forehead is reddish-white, like the look of leprosy on the skin of the body,
he's a man with leprosy; he's unclean. The priest is certainly to pronounce him unclean; his affliction is on his head.
The person with leprosy, the one with the affliction, has his garments torn and his head let loose; he covers his upper lip and calls out, Unclean! Unclean!
As long as the affliction is on him he's unclean. He's unclean. He lives alone; his dwelling is outside the camp.
When there's an affliction of leprosy on a garment, whether wool or linen,
or in the warp or weft of linen or wool, or in a hide or anything made of hide,
and the affliction is greenish or reddish in the garment, the hide, the warp, the weft or anything made of hide, it's an affliction of leprosy and is shown to the priest.
The priest examines the affliction and shuts it away for seven days.
He examines the affliction on the seventh day. If it's spread in the garment, the warp, the weft or the hide, in whatever the hide is made into, the affliction is a persistent leprosy. It's unclean.
He burns the garment, or the warp or weft of wool or linen, or any article of hide with the affliction in it, because it's a persistent leprosy. It's burned in the fire.
But if the priest examines it and the affliction hasn't spread in the garment, the warp, the weft or anything made of hide,
then the priest gives orders, and they wash the thing with the affliction in it, and he shuts it away for a second seven days.

The priest examines it after the affliction has been washed, and if the affliction hasn't changed its appearance and hasn't spread, it's unclean. You burn it in the fire. It's a pitting, on the back or the front of it.
But if the priest examines it and the affliction has faded after washing, he tears it out of the garment, the hide, the warp or the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, the warp, the weft or anything made of hide, it's breaking out. You burn the thing with the affliction in it.
Any garment, warp, weft or article of hide you wash, that the affliction leaves, is washed a second time and is clean.
This is the law for an affliction of leprosy in a woollen or linen garment, in the warp or weft, or in any article of hide, to pronounce it clean or unclean.

leviticus_14.t: The LORD said to Moses:
This is the law for the person with leprosy on the day of his cleansing: he's brought to the priest,
and the priest goes outside the camp and examines him. If the affliction of leprosy has healed in the person who had it,
then the priest gives orders, and two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet and hyssop are taken for the person being cleansed.
The priest gives orders, and one of the birds is slaughtered into an earthenware vessel over living water.
He takes the live bird, with the cedar wood, the scarlet and the hyssop, and dips them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the living water.
He sprinkles it seven times on the person being cleansed from the leprosy, pronounces him clean, and lets the live bird go over the open field.
The person being cleansed washes his garments, shaves off all his hair and bathes in water, and he's clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he stays outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he shaves off all his hair — his head, his beard, his eyebrows; all his hair he shaves off. He washes his garments and bathes his body in water, and he's clean.
On the eighth day he takes two unblemished male lambs, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb, three tenths of fine flour as a grain offering mixed with oil, and one log of oil.
The priest who pronounces him clean stations the person being cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest takes one of the lambs and presents it as a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and waves them as a wave offering before the LORD.
He slaughters the lamb in the holy place, where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered; like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest. It's most holy.
The priest takes some of the blood of the guilt offering and puts it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and the big toe of his right foot.
The priest takes some of the log of oil and pours it into his own left palm.
The priest dips his right finger in the oil on his left palm and sprinkles some of it with his finger seven times before the LORD.

From the rest of the oil on his palm the priest puts some on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and the big toe of his right foot, over the blood of the guilt offering.
What's left of the oil on the priest's palm he puts on the head of the person being cleansed. So the priest makes atonement for him before the LORD.
The priest offers the sin offering and makes atonement for the person being cleansed from his uncleanness. After that he slaughters the burnt offering.
The priest offers up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. The priest makes atonement for him, and he's clean.
But if he's poor and can't afford that, he takes one lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and a log of oil,
and two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford; one is a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
He brings them on the eighth day for his cleansing to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
The priest takes the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil and waves them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He slaughters the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest takes some of the blood and puts it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and the big toe of his right foot.
The priest pours some of the oil into his own left palm.
The priest sprinkles with his right finger some of the oil on his left palm, seven times before the LORD.

The priest puts some of the oil on his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
What's left of the oil on the priest's palm he puts on the head of the person being cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
He offers one of the turtle-doves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford,
whatever he can afford: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. So the priest makes atonement for the person being cleansed before the LORD.
This is the law for someone with an affliction of leprosy who can't afford the usual offerings for his cleansing.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
When you come into the land of Canaan, which I'm giving you as a possession, and I put an affliction of leprosy in a house in the land you possess,
then the owner of the house comes and tells the priest: something like an affliction has appeared to me in the house.
The priest gives orders that the house be cleared before he comes to examine the affliction, so that everything in it doesn't become unclean. After that the priest comes to examine the house.
He examines the affliction. If the affliction in the walls of the house is greenish or reddish hollows that look lower than the wall,
then the priest goes out of the house to its entrance and shuts the house up for seven days.
The priest returns on the seventh day and examines it. If the affliction has spread in the walls of the house,
then the priest gives orders, and they tear out the stones with the affliction in them and throw them outside the city, to an unclean place.
He has the house scraped inside all round, and they pour out the plaster dust they've scraped off outside the city, to an unclean place.
They take other stones and put them in place of the first ones, and he takes fresh plaster and plasters the house.
But if the affliction comes back and breaks out in the house after the stones have been torn out, the house scraped and plastered,
then the priest comes and examines it, and if the affliction has spread in the house, it's a persistent leprosy in the house. It's unclean.
He pulls the house down — its stones, its timbers and all its plaster — and carries them outside the city, to an unclean place.
Whoever goes into the house during the days it's shut up is unclean until evening.
Whoever lies down in the house washes his garments, and whoever eats in the house washes his garments.
But if the priest comes and examines it and the affliction hasn't spread in the house after the plastering, he pronounces the house clean — the affliction has healed.
To purify the house from sin he takes two birds, cedar wood, scarlet and hyssop.
He slaughters one of the birds into an earthenware vessel over living water.
He takes the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet and the live bird, dips them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the living water, and sprinkles the house seven times.
So he purifies the house from sin with the blood of the bird, the living water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet.
He lets the live bird go outside the city, over the open field, and makes atonement for the house, and it's clean.
This is the law for every affliction of leprosy, for the scall,
for the leprosy of a garment and of a house,
for the swelling, the rash and the bright spot,
to give a ruling on the day something is unclean and on the day it's clean. This is the law for leprosy.

leviticus_15.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Tell the people of Israel: when a man has a discharge from his body, that discharge is unclean.
His uncleanness works this way: whether the discharge is running or blocked, he's unclean either way.
Any bed he lies on becomes unclean, and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits where he sat has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches him has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
If he spits on someone who's clean, that person has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
Any saddle he rides on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches anything he's been on top of will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries those things has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
If he touches someone without rinsing his hands first, that person has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
A clay pot he touches has to be smashed; a wooden one just gets rinsed.
Once the discharge stops and he's clean of it, he counts seven days for his cleansing, washes his clothes, and bathes in running water. Then he's clean.
On the eighth day he takes two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, comes before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and hands them to the priest.
The priest offers them — one as a sin offering, one as a burnt offering — and makes atonement for him before the LORD because of his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he bathes his whole body, and he's unclean until evening.
Any clothing or leather with semen on it gets washed, and it's unclean until evening.
When a man and a woman have sex, both of them bathe, and both are unclean until evening.
When a woman is bleeding — her monthly period — she's in menstrual impurity for seven days, and anyone who touches her is unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during that time becomes unclean, and anything she sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she's sat on has to wash their clothes and bathe, and they'll be unclean until evening.
If it's on the bed or on the seat she used, whoever touches it is unclean until evening.
If a man does sleep with her and her impurity passes to him, he's unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on becomes unclean.
If a woman bleeds for many days outside her period, or her period keeps going, then for as long as the discharge lasts she's in the same state as during her period. She's unclean.
Any bed she lies on while the discharge lasts counts like the bed of her period, and anything she sits on is unclean the same way.
Anyone who touches them is unclean; they wash their clothes and bathe, and they're unclean until evening.
Once the discharge stops and she's clean of it, she counts seven days, and after that she's clean.
On the eighth day she takes two turtle-doves or two young pigeons and brings them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest offers one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and makes atonement for her before the LORD because of her unclean discharge.
Keep the people of Israel clear of their uncleanness, so they don't die in it by defiling my tabernacle, which stands among them.
That's the law about a man with a discharge, and about a man who has an emission of semen and is made unclean by it —
and about a woman ailing in her period, and anyone with a discharge, male or female, and a man who sleeps with an unclean woman.

leviticus_16.t: The LORD spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died — after they drew near before the LORD and died.

The LORD said to Moses: Tell your brother Aaron he can't come into the holy place inside the veil whenever he likes — in front of the mercy seat on the ark — or he'll die. I appear in the cloud over the mercy seat.
Here's how Aaron is to come into the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He wears a holy linen tunic with linen undergarments underneath, a linen sash tied round him and a linen turban wound on his head. These are holy garments. He bathes his body in water first, then puts them on.
From the congregation of the people of Israel he takes two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron presents the bull of the sin offering that's his own, and makes atonement for himself and his household.
He takes the two goats and stands them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron casts lots over the two goats — one lot for the LORD, one lot for Azazel.
Aaron presents the goat the LORD's lot came up for, and offers it as a sin offering.
But the goat that Azazel's lot came up for is set alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it, and then sent away to Azazel into the wilderness.
Aaron presents the bull of the sin offering that's his own and makes atonement for himself and his household, and he slaughters that bull.
He takes a censer full of coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and brings them inside the veil.
He puts the incense on the fire before the LORD, so the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat over the testimony, and he won't die.
He takes some of the bull's blood and sprinkles it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat, and in front of the mercy seat he sprinkles blood seven times with his finger.

Then he slaughters the goat of the sin offering that's for the people, brings its blood inside the veil, and does with it what he did with the bull's blood — sprinkles it on the mercy seat and in front of it.

So he makes atonement for the holy place because of the people of Israel' uncleannesses and transgressions — all their sins — and does the same for the tent of meeting, which stands among them right in the middle of their uncleannesses.

No one else is to be in the tent of meeting from the moment he goes in to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out. He makes atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.
Then he goes out to the altar that's before the LORD and makes atonement on it. He takes some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's, and puts it on the horns of the altar all around.
He sprinkles blood on it seven times with his finger, cleansing it and setting it apart as holy from the uncleannesses of the people of Israel.
When he's finished making atonement for the holy place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he presents the living goat.

Aaron presses both hands on the living goat's head and confesses over it all the iniquities of the people of Israel and all their transgressions — all their sins — putting them on the goat's head. Then he sends it into the wilderness by a man standing ready.
The goat carries all their iniquities away on itself into a solitary place, and the man lets it go in the wilderness.
Then Aaron goes into the tent of meeting, takes off the linen garments he wore going into the holy place, and leaves them there.
He bathes his body in water in a holy place and puts on his own garments. Then he comes out and offers his burnt offering and the people's, making atonement for himself and for the people.
He turns the fat of the sin offering to smoke on the altar.
The man who lets the goat go to Azazel washes his clothes and bathes, and after that he can come back into the camp.
The bull and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, are taken outside the camp, and their hides, flesh, and offal are burned with fire.
The man who burns them washes his clothes and bathes, and after that he can come back into the camp.
