This is a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you afflict yourselves and do no work at all — the native-born and the foreigner living among you.
On this day atonement is made for you, to cleanse you; you'll be clean before the LORD from all your sins.
It's a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you afflict yourselves. This is a perpetual statute.
The priest who's anointed and ordained to serve in his father's place makes the atonement, wearing the linen garments, the holy garments.
He makes atonement for the holy sanctuary, for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.
This is a perpetual statute for you: atonement is made for the people of Israel once a year, for all their sins. And he did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

leviticus_17.t: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel: this is what the LORD has commanded.
Any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or a sheep or a goat, inside the camp or outside it,

and doesn't bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the tabernacle of the LORD — that man is charged with blood. He has shed blood, and he is to be cut off from among his people.

The point is that the people of Israel should bring the sacrifices they're now making out in the open field — bring them to the LORD, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD.
The priest dashes the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and turns the fat to smoke as a soothing odour to the LORD.
They're not to sacrifice any more to the goat-demons they prostitute themselves after. This is a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.
Say to them: any man of the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, who offers up a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
and doesn't bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD — that man is to be cut off from his kin.
If anyone of the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, eats any blood, I'll set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people.
The life of the flesh is in the blood, and I myself have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; it's the blood that makes atonement, by the life.
That's why I've said to the people of Israel: none of you is to eat blood, and no foreigner living among you is to eat blood.
Anyone of the people of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, who hunts and catches an animal or bird that may be eaten has to pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

The life of all flesh is its blood; its blood is its life. So I've said to the people of Israel: don't eat the blood of any flesh. The life of all flesh is its blood, and anyone who eats it is to be cut off.
Anyone who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, native-born or foreigner, has to wash their clothes and bathe. They'll be unclean until evening, and then they're clean.
But if he doesn't wash them and doesn't bathe, he'll bear his iniquity.

leviticus_18.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: I am the LORD your God.
Don't do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and don't do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I'm bringing you. Don't walk by their statutes.
Do my judgements and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and my judgements. Anyone who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
None of you is to draw near to a close relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the LORD.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your father, which is the nakedness of your mother. She's your mother — don't uncover her nakedness.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. It's your father's nakedness.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your sister — your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born elsewhere.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter. They're your own nakedness.
Don't uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She's your sister.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your father's sister. She's your father's close relative.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister. She's your mother's close relative.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your father's brother — don't draw near to his wife. She's your aunt.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law. She's your son's wife — don't uncover her nakedness.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife. It's your brother's nakedness.
Don't uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, and don't take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness. They're close relatives. It's depravity.
Don't take a woman as a rival to her sister, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is still alive.
Don't draw near to a woman in her menstrual impurity to uncover her nakedness.
Don't have intercourse with your neighbour's wife and be made unclean by her.
Don't give any of your offspring to be offered to Molech, and don't profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You are not to lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is an abomination.
Don't have intercourse with any animal and be made unclean by it. And a woman is not to present herself to an animal to mate with it. It's a perversion.
Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these things. By all of these the nations I'm driving out before you have made themselves unclean.
The land became unclean, and I brought its iniquity down on it, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
But you are to keep my statutes and my judgements and do none of these abominations — not the native-born and not the foreigner living among you.
The people of the land who were there before you did all these abominations, and the land became unclean.
Then the land won't vomit you out when you make it unclean, the way it vomited out the nation before you.
Anyone who does any of these abominations — those who do them are to be cut off from among their people.
Keep my charge. Don't follow any of the abominable customs that were practised before you, and don't make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.

leviticus_19.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the whole congregation of the people of Israel: you are to be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you is to revere your mother and your father, and to keep my sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Don't turn to worthless idols, and don't make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you sacrifice a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, sacrifice it so it will be accepted for you.
Eat it on the day you sacrifice it and the next day. Whatever's left until the third day has to be burned with fire.
If it's eaten at all on the third day, it's tainted, and it won't be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person is to be cut off from his kin.
When you reap the harvest of your land, don't reap right to the edge of your field, and don't gather up the gleanings.
Don't strip your vineyard bare or gather up the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
Don't steal. Don't deceive. Don't deal falsely with one another.
Don't swear falsely by my name and profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Don't oppress your neighbour or rob him. A hired worker's wages aren't to stay with you overnight until morning.
Don't curse a deaf person or put a stumbling block in front of a blind person. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
Don't do injustice in judgement. Don't show partiality to the poor, and don't defer to the great. Judge your neighbour with righteousness.
Don't go about as a slanderer among your kin. Don't stand on the blood of your neighbour. I am the LORD.
Don't hate your brother in your heart. Reprove your neighbour openly, so you don't incur sin because of him.
Don't take vengeance, and don't hold a grudge against your own people. Love your neighbour as yourself. I am the LORD.
Keep my statutes. Don't breed your livestock with another kind, don't sow your field with two kinds of seed, and don't wear a garment made of two kinds of material.

If a man has intercourse with a woman who is a slave designated for another man, and she hasn't been redeemed and hasn't been given her freedom, there is to be punishment. They aren't to be put to death, because she wasn't free.
He brings his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting — a ram as a guilt offering.
The priest makes atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the LORD, for the sin he committed, and he'll be forgiven the sin he committed.
When you come into the land and plant any tree for food, treat its fruit as forbidden. For three years it's forbidden to you and not to be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit is holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
In the fifth year you can eat its fruit, so its yield will increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
Don't eat over the blood. Don't practise divination or soothsaying.
Don't round off the hair at the sides of your head, and don't spoil the edge of your beard.
Don't make gashes in your flesh for the dead, and don't put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Don't profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will prostitute itself and be filled with depravity.
Keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Don't turn to mediums or seek out spiritists, and be made unclean by them. I am the LORD your God.
Rise in the presence of the grey-headed, and honour an old person. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, don't wrong him.
The foreigner living with you is to count as one of your own native-born, and you're to love him as yourself — you were foreigners in the land of Egypt yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
Don't do injustice in judgement — in measures of length, weight, or volume.
Keep honest balances, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my statutes and all my judgements, and do them. I am the LORD.

leviticus_20.t: The LORD said to Moses:

Say to the people of Israel: any man of the people of Israel, or any foreigner living in Israel, who gives any of his offspring to Molech is to be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given his offspring to Molech, to make my sanctuary unclean and to profane my holy name.
And if the people of the land do close their eyes to that man when he gives his offspring to Molech, and don't put him to death,

then I myself will set my face against that man and against his clan, and I'll cut him off from among their people, along with everyone who prostitutes themselves after him by prostituting themselves after Molech.
As for anyone who turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting themselves after them — I'll set my face against that person and cut them off from among their people.
Set yourselves apart as holy and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD, who sets you apart as holy.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother is to be put to death. He has cursed his father and his mother; his blood is on him.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife — with the wife of his neighbour — both the adulterer and the adulteress are to be put to death.
A man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them are to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them are to be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is on them.
If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done an abomination. They are to be put to death; their blood is on them.
If a man takes a woman and her mother, it's depravity. He and they are to be burned with fire, so there is no depravity among you.
A man who has intercourse with an animal is to be put to death, and you are to kill the animal.
If a woman draws near to any animal to mate with it, you are to kill both the woman and the animal. They are to be put to death; their blood is on them.

If a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his, it's a disgrace. They are to be cut off before the eyes of their own people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he'll bear his iniquity.

If a man lies with a woman while she is ailing and uncovers her nakedness, he has laid bare her spring and she has uncovered the spring of her blood. Both of them are to be cut off from among their people.
Don't uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister. That lays bare your own close relative; they will bear their iniquity.
A man who lies with his aunt has uncovered his uncle's nakedness. They'll bear their sin and die childless.
If a man takes his brother's wife, it's impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they'll be childless.
Keep all my statutes and all my judgements and do them, so the land I'm bringing you into to live doesn't vomit you out.
Don't walk by the statutes of the nation I'm driving out before you. They did all these things, and I came to loathe them.

And I said to you: you'll take possession of their soil, and I myself will give it to you to possess — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.

Separate the clean animal from the unclean and the unclean bird from the clean. Don't make yourselves detestable by any animal or bird or anything that crawls on the ground, which I've set apart for you as unclean.
You are to be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy, and I've separated you from the peoples to be mine.
A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist is to be put to death. They are to be stoned; their blood is on them.

leviticus_21.t: The LORD said to Moses: tell the priests, the sons of Aaron — a priest is not to make himself unclean for a dead person among his kin,
except for his closest relatives — his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
and for his virgin sister, close to him, who has never belonged to a husband — for her he may make himself unclean.
He is not to make himself unclean as a husband among his kin, profaning himself.
They're not to shave a bald patch on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their flesh.
They're to be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, because they're the ones who present the food offerings of the LORD, the food of their God. They are to be holy.
They're not to take a woman profaned by prostitution, or a woman divorced from her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
Set him apart as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He's to be holy to you, because I, the LORD who sets you apart as holy, am holy.
If a priest's daughter profanes herself by prostituting herself, she's profaning her father. She is to be burned with fire.
The priest who is greatest among his brothers — the one on whose head the anointing oil was poured, ordained to wear the garments — is not to let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
He's not to go near any dead body — not even to make himself unclean for his father or his mother.
He's not to leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, because the consecration of his God's anointing oil is on him. I am the LORD.
He is to take a wife who is a virgin.
He's not to take a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been profaned, or a prostitute. He's to take a virgin from his own kin as his wife.
He's not to profane his offspring among his kin, because I am the LORD, who sets him apart as holy.
The LORD said to Moses:
Tell Aaron: none of your offspring, in any generation, who has a blemish is to draw near to present the food of his God.
No man with a blemish is to draw near — not the blind or the lame, not a man with a disfigured face or a limb too long,
no one with a broken foot or a broken hand,
no hunchback or dwarf, no one with a defect in the eye, an itching disease or scabs, or crushed testicles.
No one of Aaron's offspring who has a blemish is to come near to present the food offerings of the LORD. He has a blemish; he isn't to come near to present the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, from the holiest of the holy things and from the holy things.
But he's not to come to the veil or approach the altar, because he has a blemish. He's not to profane my sanctuaries, because I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel.

leviticus_22.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Tell Aaron and his sons to keep themselves separate from the holy things the people of Israel set apart as holy to me, so they don't profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them: in every generation, if any of your offspring draws near to the holy things the people of Israel set apart as holy to the LORD while his uncleanness is on him, that person is to be cut off from before me. I am the LORD.

No one of Aaron's offspring who has leprosy or has a discharge may eat of the holy things until he's clean. The same goes for anyone who touches something made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has an emission of semen,
or anyone who touches a swarming creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean — whatever the uncleanness is:
Anyone who touches such a thing is unclean until evening, and can't eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun goes down he's clean, and after that he may eat of the holy things — they're his food.
He's not to eat an animal that died of itself or was torn by beasts, and become unclean by it. I am the LORD.
They're to keep my charge, so they don't bear sin on account of it and die by it, having profaned it. I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
No outsider is to eat a holy thing. Neither a priest's resident nor a hired worker may eat a holy thing.
But if a priest buys a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and those born in his household may eat of his food.
If a priest's daughter is married to an outsider, she isn't to eat of the contribution of the holy things.
But if a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and has no children, and comes back to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food. No outsider is to eat of it.
If anyone eats a holy thing by mistake, he adds a fifth to it and gives the holy thing to the priest.
They aren't to profane the holy things the people of Israel set aside for the LORD,
and so make them bear the iniquity of guilt by eating their holy things. I am the LORD, who sets them apart as holy.
The LORD said to Moses:

Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the people of Israel: when any man of the house of Israel, or any foreigner in Israel, presents his offering — for any vow or freewill offering they present to the LORD as a burnt offering —
it has to be, for your acceptance, an unblemished male from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
Don't present anything with a blemish in it — it won't be accepted for you.

When anyone presents a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD — to fulfil a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock — it has to be unblemished to be accepted. There's to be no blemish in it at all.
Don't present to the LORD an animal that's blind, injured, mutilated, or has a running sore, an itch, or scabs. Don't put any food offering from such animals on the altar to the LORD.
You may offer an ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short as a freewill offering, but it won't be accepted for a vow.
Don't present to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut, and don't do this in your land.
Don't present the food of your God from any such animals got from a foreigner. They're corrupted and blemished; they won't be accepted for you.
The LORD said to Moses:
When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it stays seven days with its mother. From the eighth day on it's accepted as an offering, a food offering to the LORD.
Don't slaughter an ox or a sheep and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving sacrifice to the LORD, sacrifice it so it will be accepted for you.
It's to be eaten that same day; don't leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
Keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
Don't profane my holy name. I will be set apart as holy among the people of Israel. I am the LORD, who sets you apart as holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be God for you. I am the LORD.

leviticus_23.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: these are the appointed times of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as holy convocations. These are my appointed times.
Work is done for six days, but the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. Do no work at all. It is a sabbath to the LORD wherever you live.
These are the appointed times of the LORD, holy convocations, which you are to proclaim at their appointed time.
In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, at twilight, is a passover to the LORD.
On the fifteenth day of that month is the festival of unleavened bread to the LORD. For seven days you eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you hold a holy convocation. Do no occupational work.
For seven days you present a food offering to the LORD. On the seventh day there's a holy convocation; do no occupational work.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: when you come into the land I'm giving you and reap its harvest, bring the sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest.
He waves the sheaf before the LORD so it will be accepted for you. The priest waves it on the day after the sabbath.
On the day you wave the sheaf you offer an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering to the LORD,
with its grain offering — two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a food offering to the LORD, a soothing odour — and its drink offering of wine, a quarter of a hin.
Don't eat bread, roasted grain, or fresh grain until that very day, until you've brought the offering of your God. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Count off from the day after the sabbath, from the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering: seven complete weeks.
Count fifty days, up to the day after the seventh week, and then present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From your homes you bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering, made of two tenths of fine flour and baked with leaven, as first-fruits to the LORD.

With the bread you present seven unblemished year-old lambs, one young bull, and two rams. They'll be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and drink offerings — a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
You offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of peace offering.
The priest waves them, with the bread of the first-fruits and the two lambs, as a wave offering before the LORD. They are holy to the LORD, for the priest.
On that very day you make a proclamation: hold a holy convocation and do no occupational work. This is a perpetual statute wherever you live, throughout your generations.
When you reap the harvest of your land, don't reap right to the edge of your field, and don't gather up the gleanings. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: in the seventh month, on the first of the month, you have a day of rest, a memorial of the blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.
Do no occupational work, and present a food offering to the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
The tenth of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It's to be a holy convocation for you. Afflict yourselves and present a food offering to the LORD.
Do no work at all on that day, because it's a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
Anyone who isn't afflicted on that day is to be cut off from his kin.
And anyone who does any work at all on that day — I'll destroy that person from among his people.
Do no work at all. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, wherever you live.
It's a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you afflict yourselves. From the evening of the ninth of the month, evening to evening, you keep your sabbath.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: on the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the festival of booths, seven days to the LORD.
On the first day there's a holy convocation; do no occupational work.
For seven days you present a food offering to the LORD. On the eighth day you hold a holy convocation and present a food offering to the LORD. It's a solemn assembly; do no occupational work.

These are the appointed times of the LORD, which you proclaim as holy convocations, for presenting to the LORD a food offering — burnt offering and grain offering, sacrifice and drink offerings, each on its own day —
these are on top of the sabbaths of the LORD, and on top of your gifts, all your vows, and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

On the fifteenth of the seventh month, when you've gathered in the produce of the land, you celebrate the festival of the LORD for seven days. The first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day is a day of rest.
On the first day you take the fruit of a splendid tree, palm fronds, a branch of a leafy tree, and willows of the wadi, and you rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You celebrate it as a festival to the LORD for seven days in the year. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations; celebrate it in the seventh month.
You're to live in booths for seven days. Every native-born Israelite lives in booths,
so your generations will know that I made the people of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
So Moses declared the appointed times of the LORD to the people of Israel.

leviticus_24.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, so a lamp can be kept burning continually.
Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron tends it from evening until morning before the LORD continually. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
He arranges the lamps on the pure lampstand before the LORD continually.
Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, two tenths for each loaf.
Set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD.
Put pure frankincense on each row. It serves for the bread as a memorial portion, a food offering to the LORD.
Sabbath after sabbath he arranges it before the LORD continually, on behalf of the people of Israel, as a covenant of perpetuity.
It belongs to Aaron and his sons, and they eat it in a holy place. It's a holy thing of holy things for him, from the food offerings of the LORD — a perpetual prescribed portion.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the people of Israel, and he and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until the decision should be made clear to them by the mouth of the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him press their hands on his head, and the whole congregation stones him.
And say to the people of Israel: anyone who curses his God will bear his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD is to be put to death; the whole congregation stones him. Foreigner and native-born alike — when he blasphemes the Name, he is to be put to death.
Anyone who strikes down a human life is to be put to death.
Whoever strikes down an animal makes it good, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbour, what he has done is to be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has injured a person, so he is to be injured.
Whoever strikes down an animal makes it good; whoever strikes down a person is to be put to death.
You're to have one law: the same for the foreigner as for the native-born. I am the LORD your God.
Moses spoke to the people of Israel, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. So the people of Israel did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

leviticus_25.t: The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai,
Speak to the people of Israel: when you come into the land I'm giving you, the land is to keep a sabbath to the LORD.
For six years you sow your field, and for six years you prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
But in the seventh year the land has a sabbath of complete rest, a sabbath to the LORD. Don't sow your field or prune your vineyard.
Don't reap the grain that grows of itself or gather the grapes of your untrimmed vines. It's a year of rest for the land.
The sabbath of the land will provide food for you — for yourself, your male and female slaves, your hired worker, and the resident living with you,
and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce is for food.
Count off seven weeks of years — seven times seven — so that the seven weeks of years come to forty-nine years.
Then in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month — the day of atonement — you sound a ram's horn loudly, throughout all your land.
Set the fiftieth year apart as holy and proclaim a release throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It's a jubilee for you: each of you returns to his holding, each to his clan.
The fiftieth year is a jubilee for you. Don't sow, don't reap what grows of itself, don't gather from the untrimmed vines.
It's a jubilee; it's holy for you. Eat its produce straight from the field.
In this year of jubilee each of you returns to his holding.
When you sell something to your neighbour or buy from him, don't wrong one another.
Buy from your neighbour by the number of years since the jubilee, and he sells to you by the number of harvest years left.
The more years there are, the higher the price; the fewer the years, the lower it is. What he's selling you is a number of harvests.
Don't wrong one another. Fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
Carry out my statutes, keep my judgements and do them, and you'll live on the land in security.
The land will yield its fruit, you'll eat your fill and live on it in security.
And if you ask, What are we going to eat in the seventh year, since we can't sow or gather in our produce? —
then I'll command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will produce a crop for three years.
You'll sow in the eighth year and still be eating the old crop; until the ninth year, until its harvest comes in, you'll be eating the old.
The land is not to be sold beyond reclaim. The land is mine, and you are sojourners and residents with me.
Throughout the land of your holding you must allow a right of redemption for the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his holding, his nearest kinsman-redeemer comes and redeems what his brother sold.
If a man has no kinsman-redeemer, but he comes by the means and finds enough for its redemption,
he reckons the years since the sale, repays the balance to the man he sold it to, and returns to his holding.
But if he can't find enough to repay him, what he sold stays with the buyer until the year of jubilee. In the jubilee it's released, and he returns to his holding.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, his right of redemption lasts until the end of the year of the sale — a full year.
If it isn't redeemed before a full year is out, the house in the walled city passes to the buyer and his generations in perpetuity. It isn't released in the jubilee.
But houses in villages with no wall around them count as open farmland: they carry a right of redemption, and they're released in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites — the houses in the cities of their holding — the Levites have a perpetual right of redemption.
Whatever one of the Levites redeems — a house sold, and the city of his holding — is released in the jubilee, because the houses in the Levites' cities are their holding among the people of Israel.
But the pasture land belonging to their cities isn't to be sold; it's their perpetual holding.
If your brother becomes poor and can't support himself among you, hold him up as you would a sojourner or a resident, so he can live with you.
Don't take interest or increase from him. Fear your God, so your brother can live with you.
Don't lend him your silver at interest or give him your food for increase.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be God for you.
If your brother becomes poor among you and sells himself to you, don't make him do the labour of a slave.
He's to be with you as a hired worker or a resident, serving with you until the year of jubilee.
Then he goes out from you, he and his children with him, and returns to his clan and to the holding of his fathers.
They're my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They aren't to be sold as slaves are sold.
Don't rule over him harshly. Fear your God.
As for your male and female slaves, you may buy them from the nations around you.
You may also buy from the children of the residents living among you, and from their families born in your land. They'll be your holding.

You may pass them on as an inheritance to your children after you, as a possession to hold, and keep them in service for ever. But over your brothers, the people of Israel, no one is to rule harshly over his brother.
If a sojourner or resident among you prospers and your brother becomes poor beside him and sells himself to that sojourner or resident, or to a member of a sojourner's family,
he keeps a right of redemption after selling himself. One of his brothers may redeem him.
His uncle or his cousin may redeem him, or any close relative from his clan; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
He reckons with his buyer from the year he sold himself until the year of jubilee. The price of his sale is set by the number of years, reckoned as a hired worker's days with him.
If many years remain, he repays a proportionate part of the purchase price for his redemption.
If few years remain until the year of jubilee, he reckons accordingly and repays for his redemption in proportion to those years.
He's to be with him as a worker hired year by year, and his employer isn't to rule over him harshly where you can see it.
If he isn't redeemed by any of these means, he's released in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.
The people of Israel are servants to me. They are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

leviticus_26.t: Don't make worthless idols for yourselves, or raise up a carved image or a standing pillar, or set a figured stone in your land to bow down on it. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
If you walk by my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
then I'll give you your rains in their season, the land will give its yield, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.
Your threshing will run right up to the grape harvest, and the grape harvest to the sowing. You'll eat your fill and live in security in your land.
I'll give peace in the land, and you'll lie down with no one to make you afraid. I'll rid the land of wild beasts, and no sword will pass through your land.
You'll pursue your enemies, and they'll fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I'll turn towards you, make you fruitful and multiply you, and establish my covenant with you.
You'll still be eating last year's stored grain, and you'll have to clear out the old to make room for the new.
I'll set my tabernacle among you, and I will not abhor you.
I'll walk among you. I'll be God for you, and you'll be a people for me.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so you wouldn't be slaves to them any more. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
But if you don't listen to me and don't carry out all these commandments,
if you reject my statutes and abhor my judgements, so that you don't carry out all my commandments and you break my covenant —

then I in turn will do this to you: I'll bring on you sudden terror, wasting disease and fever that consume the eyes and drain the life away. You'll sow your seed for nothing — your enemies will eat it.
I'll set my face against you, and you'll be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you'll run with no one chasing you.
And if after all this you still don't listen to me, I'll go on disciplining you sevenfold for your sins.
I'll break the pride of your strength. I'll make your heavens like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be spent for nothing. Your land won't give its yield, and the trees of the land won't give their fruit.
If you walk contrary to me and won't listen, I'll add blows sevenfold, in proportion to your sins.
I'll send wild beasts among you. They'll bereave you of your children, cut off your livestock and make you few, and your roads will lie desolate.
If even these things don't discipline you, and you walk contrary to me,
then I in turn will walk contrary to you, and I in turn will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I'll bring a sword on you that avenges the vengeance of the covenant. You'll gather into your cities, I'll send pestilence among you, and you'll be given into the hand of an enemy.
When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and dole it back to you by weight. You'll eat and not be satisfied.
If in spite of this you don't listen to me, and you walk contrary to me,
then I'll walk contrary to you in fury, and I in turn will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
I'll destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and pile your corpses on the corpses of your idols. And I will abhor you.
I'll make your cities a waste and lay your sanctuaries desolate, and I won't smell your soothing odours.
I myself will lay the land desolate, and your enemies who come to live in it will be appalled at it.
I'll scatter you among the nations and draw a sword after you. Your land will become a desolation, your cities a waste.
Then the land will make up for its sabbaths, all the days it lies desolate while you're in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and make up for its sabbaths.
All the days it lies desolate it will rest, because it didn't rest during your sabbaths while you lived on it.

As for those of you who are left, I'll bring faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will chase them; they'll run as if from a sword and fall with no one after them.
They'll stumble over one another as though a sword were behind them, with no one pursuing, and you'll have no power to stand before your enemies.
You'll perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
Those of you who are left will rot away in their iniquity in the lands of their enemies — and in the iniquities of their fathers along with them they'll rot away.
But they'll confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers — the unfaithfulness by which they were unfaithful to me, and that they walked contrary to me —
— I too walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies — if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make up for their iniquity,
then I'll remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I'll remember. And I'll remember the land.

The land will be left by them and will make up for its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they'll make up for their iniquity — because, and again because, they rejected my judgements and abhorred my statutes.
And yet even so, while they're in the land of their enemies, I won't reject them or abhor them so as to make an end of them and break my covenant with them. I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I'll remember the covenant of the ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be God for them. I am the LORD.
These are the statutes, judgements, and laws that the LORD established between himself and the people of Israel on Mount Sinai, through Moses.

leviticus_27.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the people of Israel: when anyone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the valuation of persons, here is the scale.
The valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old is fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the holy place.
If it's a female, the valuation is thirty shekels.
For ages five to twenty, it's twenty shekels for a male and ten for a female.
From one month to five years, it's five shekels of silver for a male and three for a female.
From sixty and up, it's fifteen shekels for a male and ten for a female.
If he's too poor for the valuation, he's presented before the priest, and the priest values him according to what the one making the vow can afford.
If the vow concerns an animal of a kind that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, anything of it given to the LORD becomes holy.
He isn't to replace it or exchange it — a good one for a bad or a bad one for a good. If he does exchange one animal for another, both it and its substitute become holy.
If it's an unclean animal, of a kind that can't be presented as an offering to the LORD, he presents the animal before the priest,
and the priest values it, whether good or bad. As the priest values it, so it stands.
If he does redeem it, he adds a fifth to the valuation.
When anyone sets apart his house as holy to the LORD, the priest values it, whether good or bad. As the priest values it, so it stands.
If the one who set it apart wants to redeem his house, he adds a fifth of the silver of the valuation, and it's his.
If anyone sets apart to the LORD part of the field of his holding, the valuation goes by the seed it takes — a homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver.
If he sets apart his field from the year of jubilee, it stands at the full valuation.
If he sets apart his field after the jubilee, the priest reckons the price by the years remaining until the year of jubilee, and that much is deducted from the valuation.
If the one who set the field apart does redeem it, he adds a fifth of the silver of the valuation, and it stands as his.
But if he doesn't redeem the field, or has sold it to another man, it can't be redeemed any more.
When the field is released in the jubilee, it becomes holy to the LORD, like a field that's been devoted. It becomes the priest's holding.
If he sets apart to the LORD a field he has bought, which isn't part of the field of his holding,
the priest reckons for him the amount of the valuation up to the year of jubilee, and he pays it that same day as a holy thing to the LORD.
In the year of jubilee the field returns to the one it was bought from, the one whose holding of the land it is.
Every valuation goes by the shekel of the holy place: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
But no one is to set apart a firstborn animal — as a firstling it already belongs to the LORD. Ox or sheep, it's the LORD's.
If it's among the unclean livestock, he ransoms it at the valuation and adds a fifth. If it isn't redeemed, it's sold at the valuation.
But nothing a man devotes to the LORD out of all he has — a person, livestock, or a field of his holding — may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is a holy thing of holy things to the LORD.
No person who has been devoted may be ransomed. He is to be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the tree, belongs to the LORD. It's holy to the LORD.
If anyone does redeem part of his tithe, he adds a fifth to it.
Every tithe of the herd and the flock — all that passes under the shepherd's rod — the tenth is holy to the LORD.
He isn't to inspect whether it's good or bad, and he isn't to exchange it. If he does exchange it, both it and its substitute become holy and can't be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the LORD commanded Moses for the people of Israel on Mount Sinai.

malachi_1.t: An oracle. The word of the LORD to Israel, through Malachi.
'I have loved you,' says the LORD. And you say, 'How have you loved us?' 'Wasn't Esau Jacob's brother' — declares the LORD — 'and I loved Jacob,
but Esau I hated. I made his hills a wasteland and left his inheritance to the jackals of the wilderness.'

Edom may say, 'We've been shattered, but we'll come back and rebuild the ruins.' Here is what the LORD of hosts says: let them build — I will tear it down. People will call them the territory of wickedness, the people the LORD is indignant with, for ever.
You'll see it with your own eyes, and you'll say, 'The LORD is great — beyond Israel's border.'

A son honours his father; a servant honours his master. So if I'm a father, where's my honour? If I'm a master, where's the fear owed me? — says the LORD of hosts to you priests, who despise my name. And you say, 'How have we despised your name?'
You bring defiled food up to my altar. And you say, 'How have we defiled you?' By saying the LORD's table is despicable.

When you bring a blind animal to sacrifice — isn't that evil? A lame one, a sick one — isn't that evil? Try presenting it to your governor. Will he be pleased with you? Will he show you any favour? — says the LORD of hosts.
So now, go and entreat God's face, that he may show us favour. This came from your own hand — will he show any of you favour? — says the LORD of hosts.
If only someone among you would shut the doors, so you'd stop lighting my altar for nothing. I have no delight in you, says the LORD of hosts, and I won't accept an offering from your hand.

From the rising of the sun to its setting my name will be great among the nations. Everywhere, incense will be brought near to my name, and a pure offering. My name will be great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
But you profane it when you say the Lord's table is defiled, and the food on it is despicable.

And you say, 'What a weariness!' — and you sniff at it, says the LORD of hosts. You bring what has been stolen, and the lame and the sick; and that's what you bring as the offering. Am I to accept it from your hand? says the LORD.

A curse on the deceiver who has a male in his flock, makes his vow, and then sacrifices a corrupted animal to the Lord. For I am a great king, says the LORD of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.

malachi_2.t: And now this command is for you, priests.

If you won't listen, and won't take it to heart to give honour to my name, says the LORD of hosts, I will send the curse on you. I'll curse your blessings — in fact I've already cursed them, because you're not taking it to heart.
I'm going to rebuke your offspring, and I'll scatter dung on your faces — the dung of your own festivals — and you'll be carried off with it.
Then you'll know that I sent you this command, so that my covenant with Levi would stand, says the LORD of hosts.
My covenant with him was life and peace. I gave him those, as fear — and he feared me, and stood in awe before my name.
True law was in his mouth; nothing unrighteous was on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many back from iniquity.
A priest's lips are to keep knowledge, and people are to seek law from his mouth, because he's the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
But you've turned off the way. You've made many people stumble by your law. You've corrupted the covenant of Levi, says the LORD of hosts.
So I in turn have made you despised, brought low in front of all the people — because you don't keep my ways, and you lift up faces when you teach.
Don't we all have one Father? Didn't one God create us? Then why do we deal treacherously with one another, and profane the covenant of our ancestors?
Judah has dealt treacherously. An abomination has been done in Israel and in Jerusalem: Judah has profaned the holy place of the LORD, which he loves, and married the daughter of a foreign god.
May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this — whoever he may be — and the one who brings an offering to the LORD of hosts.
And here's a second thing you do: you cover the LORD's altar with tears, weeping and groaning — because he no longer turns towards the offering, or takes it from your hand with pleasure.
And you say, 'Why?' Because the LORD has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth. You dealt treacherously against her — and she's your companion, the wife of your covenant.

And did he not make one, with a remnant of spirit belonging to him? And what was that one seeking? Godly offspring. So take heed in your spirit, and let no one deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.
For the one who hates and divorces, says the LORD, the God of Israel, covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. So take heed in your spirit, and do not deal treacherously.

You've wearied the LORD with your words. And you say, 'How have we wearied him?' By saying, 'Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of the LORD, and he delights in them' — or, 'Where is the God of judgement?'

malachi_3.t: I'm sending my messenger, and he'll clear a way before me. Then suddenly the Lord you are seeking will come to his temple — and the messenger of the covenant, the one you delight in. He is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
But who can endure the day he comes? Who can stand when he appears? He's like a refiner's fire, like the soap of those who wash.
He'll sit refining and purifying silver. He'll purify the sons of Levi and purge them like gold and silver, and they'll belong to the LORD, bringing an offering in righteousness.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD, as in the days of old, as in years gone by.

Then I'll draw near to you for judgement. I'll be a swift witness against the sorcerers, the adulterers, those who swear falsely, those who cheat a hired labourer of his wages, those who wrong the widow and the fatherless, those who push the sojourner aside — the ones who don't fear me, says the LORD of hosts.
For I, the LORD, haven't changed — and you, sons of Jacob, haven't come to an end.
Ever since your ancestors' time you've turned aside from my statutes and not kept them. Return to me, and I'll return to you, says the LORD of hosts. And you say, 'How are we to return?'
Would a human being rob God? Yet you're robbing me. And you say, 'How have we robbed you?' In the tithe and the contribution.
You're cursed with the curse, and still you're robbing me — the whole nation of you.

Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so there's food in my house. Test me on this, says the LORD of hosts: see whether I don't open the floodgates of the heavens for you and pour out blessing until there is no sufficiency.
I'll rebuke the devourer for you, so it won't destroy the fruit of your ground, and the vine in the field won't fail to bear, says the LORD of hosts.
All the nations will call you blessed, because you'll be a land of delight, says the LORD of hosts.
Your words have been strong against me, says the LORD. And you say, 'What have we spoken among ourselves against you?'
You've said, 'Serving God is emptiness. What's the profit in our keeping his charge, or in our walking about in mourning before the LORD of hosts?'
And now we call the arrogant blessed. People who do wickedness are built up; they test God and get away with it.
Then those who fear the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD paid attention and heard. A book of remembrance was written before him, for those who fear the LORD and hold his name in esteem.
They'll be mine, says the LORD of hosts, for the day on which I make a treasured possession. I'll have compassion on them, as a man has compassion on the son who serves him.
Then you'll return and see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who doesn't serve him.

malachi_4.t: The day is coming, burning like a furnace. All the arrogant, everyone who does wickedness, will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the LORD of hosts — it will leave them neither root nor branch.
But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings, and you'll go out skipping like calves from the stall.
And you'll tread the wicked down — they'll be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day I act, says the LORD of hosts.
Remember the law of Moses my servant — what I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel: statutes and judgements.
I'm going to send you Elijah the prophet, before the day of the LORD comes — the great and fearsome day.
And he'll turn the hearts of parents back to their children, and the hearts of children back to their parents — so that I don't come and strike the land, devoting it to destruction.

micah_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah — what he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, all you peoples; pay attention, earth, and everything in you — let Lord GOD be a witness against you, my Lord from his holy temple.
Look — the LORD is coming out from his place. He'll come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath him and the valleys will be split open — like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.
All this is for the transgression of Jacob, for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Isn't it Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Isn't it Jerusalem?
I'll make Samaria a heap of ruins in the open field, a place for planting a vineyard. I'll pour her stones down into the valley and lay her foundations bare.

All her carved images will be shattered, all her hire burned in the fire, all her idols I'll make a waste — because she gathered them from a prostitute's hire, and to a prostitute's hire they'll go back.
For this I'll lament and wail. I'll go barefoot and naked. I'll howl like the jackals and mourn like the daughters of the ostrich.
Her wounds can't be healed. It has come as far as Judah; it has reached the gate of my people — Jerusalem itself.
Don't tell it in Gath; weeping, don't weep. In Beth Leaphrah, roll yourself in the dust.
Pass on your way, you who live in Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. Those who live in Zaanan haven't come out. Beth Ezel's lament will take its standing place from you.
Those who live in Maroth writhe, waiting for good, because calamity has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the chariot to the steed, you who live in Lachish. She was the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, because in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
So you'll give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath. The houses of Achzib will prove a deceit to the kings of Israel.
Again I'll bring the dispossessor upon you, you who live in Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come as far as Adullam.
Shave your head, cut off your hair for the children you delighted in. Make yourself as bald as the eagle, because they've gone from you into exile.

micah_2.t: Woe to those who plan wickedness, who work out evil on their beds — and at first light they do it, because it's in the power of their hand.
They want fields, and they seize them; houses, and they carry them off. They crush a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
So this is what the LORD says: Look — I'm planning a calamity against this clan, and you won't get your necks out from under it. You won't walk with your heads high, because it will be an evil time.

On that day someone will take up a saying against you and wail a bitter wailing. He'll say: We're completely devastated! He trades away my people's portion. How he takes it from me! He hands out our fields to an apostate.
So you'll have no one to cast a measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
Don't preach! — so they preach — they shouldn't preach about these things; the reproaches won't be turned back.
Is this what's said, house of Jacob — is the LORD's spirit short? Are these his doings? Don't my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
And lately my own people have risen up like an enemy. You strip the splendid robe right off people passing by in safety, coming home from war.
You drive the women of my people out from the house she delighted in; from her children you take away my glory for ever.
Get up and go — this is not the resting place. Because of uncleanness it destroys, and the destruction will be bitter.
If a man who walks after wind and lies came saying, 'I'll preach to you of wine and strong drink' — he'd be just the preacher for this people.
I will surely gather all of you, Jacob. I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel. I'll put them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the middle of its pasture — noisy with people.
The one who breaks through has gone up ahead of them. They've broken through, passed the gate and gone out by it. Their king has passed on ahead of them, the LORD at their head.

micah_3.t: And I said: Listen, heads of Jacob, rulers of the house of Israel — isn't it for you to know justice? —
you who hate good and love evil, who tear the skin off them and the flesh off their bones —
who eat the flesh of my people, strip the skin off them, break their bones in pieces, chop them up as for the pot, like meat in a cauldron.
Then they'll cry out to the LORD, and he won't answer them. He'll hide his face from them at that time, because of the evil they've made of their deeds.

This is what the LORD says about the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and call out 'Peace', and against anyone who doesn't put something in their mouth they declare a holy war.
So it will be night for you, with no vision; darkness for you, with no divining. The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will go dark over them.
The seers will be ashamed, the diviners abashed. Every one of them will cover his upper lip, because there's no answer from God.
But I — I am filled with power, with the spirit of the LORD, with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
Listen to this, heads of the house of Jacob, rulers of the house of Israel — you who loathe justice and twist everything straight into something crooked;
who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
Her heads judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, her prophets divine for money — and they lean on the LORD, saying, 'Isn't the LORD among us? Calamity won't come on us.'
So because of you, Zion will be ploughed like a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded high place.

micah_4.t: And in the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established at the head of the mountains, lifted high above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will come and say, 'Come, let's go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so he can teach us from his ways and we can walk in his paths.' Because from Zion law goes out, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He'll judge between many peoples and decide for mighty nations far away. They'll beat their swords into ploughshares and their spears into pruning knives. Nation won't lift sword against nation, and they won't learn war any more.
Each will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to make him afraid, because the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
All the peoples walk, each in the name of his god; but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.
On that day, declares the LORD, I'll gather the lame, assemble the outcast, and those I have harmed.
I'll make the lame into a remnant and the one driven far off into a mighty nation. And the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and for ever.
And you, tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion — to you it will come. The former dominion will come, the kingship, to the daughter of Jerusalem.
Now, why do you cry out? Is there no king among you? Has your counsellor perished, that anguish grips you like a woman in labour?

Writhe and burst forth, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labour. Now you'll go out of the town and camp in the open country; you'll go as far as Babylon. There you'll be delivered; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
And now many nations have gathered against you — the ones who say, 'Let her be defiled; let our eyes gloat over Zion.'
But they don't know the LORD's thoughts; they don't understand his counsel. He has gathered them like cut grain to the threshing floor.

Get up and thresh, daughter of Zion. I'll make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you'll crush many peoples. I'll devote their unjust gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

micah_5.t: Now you'll gash yourself, daughter of a troop. He's set a siege against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the clans of Judah — out of you will come one for me to be ruler over Israel, whose goings forth are from of old, from ancient days.
So he'll give them up until the time when the one in labour has given birth, and the rest of his brothers return to the people of Israel.
He'll stand and shepherd by the strength of the LORD, by the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they'll remain, because now he'll be great to the ends of the earth.
And this one will be peace. When Assyria comes into our land and tramples our fortresses, we'll raise up against it seven shepherds and eight princes of men.
They'll shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, the land of Nimrod at its gateways. And he'll deliver us from Assyria when it comes into our land and tramples our territory.
The remnant of Jacob will be in the middle of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass — which waits for no one and hopes for no human being.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the middle of many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep — which passes through, tramples and tears, and there's no one to deliver.
May your hand be lifted over your adversaries; may all your enemies be cut off.
And on that day, declares the LORD, I'll cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots;
I'll cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses;
I'll cut off sorceries from your hand, and you'll have no soothsayers;
I'll cut off your carved images and your pillars from among you, and you'll no longer bow down to the work of your hands;
I'll uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
And in anger and rage I'll take vengeance on the nations that haven't listened.

micah_6.t: Listen to what the LORD is saying: Get up, bring your case before the mountains; let the hills hear your voice.
Hear the LORD's case, you mountains, and you enduring ones, foundations of the earth. The LORD has a case with his people; with Israel he'll argue it out.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Testify against me.
I brought you up from the land of Egypt; from a house of slaves I ransomed you. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam ahead of you.
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him; from Shittim to Gilgal — so you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.
With what shall I come before the LORD and bow down to the God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my being?
He has told you, mortal, what is good, and what the LORD is asking of you: only this — to do justice, to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God.
The voice of the LORD calls out to the city — and it is sound wisdom to fear your name — Hear, O rod, and whoever appointed it.
Are there still, in the house of the wicked, treasures of wickedness and a short ephah that's accursed?
Am I to be held innocent with dishonest balances and a bag of false weights?
Her rich are full of violence, her people speak lies, and their tongue is deceit in their mouth.
And I too have made myself sick striking you, leaving you desolate for your sins.
You'll eat and not be satisfied; your emptiness will stay inside you. You'll carry things off and not get them to safety, and what you do get to safety I'll give to the sword.
You'll sow and not reap. You'll tread the olive and not anoint yourself with oil, and tread new wine and not drink wine.
The statutes of Omri are kept, every deed of the house of Ahab, and you've walked in their schemes — so that I make you a horror and her people a hissing, and you bear the reproach of my people.

micah_7.t: Woe is me! I've become like the last of the summer fruit, like the gleanings after the grape harvest — not a cluster to eat, not an early fig that I crave.
The loyal have perished from the land; there's not one upright person left. All of them lie in wait for blood; each hunts his own brother with a net.
Both hands are on the evil, to do it well. The official asks; the judge goes for a bribe; the great man speaks the craving of his being — he himself — and they weave it together.
The best of them is like a briar; the most upright, worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen — your punishment — has come. Now comes their confusion.
Don't believe a neighbour; don't trust a close friend. From the woman who lies in your arms guard the openings of your mouth.
A son treats his father with contempt, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies are the people of his own house.
But as for me, I'll watch for the LORD; I'll wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
Don't gloat over me, my enemy. Though I've fallen, I'll rise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.
I'll bear the LORD's indignation, because I've sinned against him, until he conducts my case and executes my judgement. He'll bring me out into the light, and I'll look on his righteousness.
My enemy will see it, and shame will cover her — the one who says to me, 'Where is the LORD your God?' My eyes will look on her. Now she'll be trampled underfoot like mud in the streets.
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will stretch far out.
That day — and they'll come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
And the earth will become a desolation because of the people living in it, from the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your rod, the flock of your inheritance, living alone, a forest in the middle of a garden land. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of long ago.
As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.
Nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They'll put a hand over the mouth; their ears will go deaf.
They'll lick dust like the serpent, like things that crawl on the ground. They'll come trembling out of their strongholds, in dread of the LORD our God, afraid of you.
Who is a God like you, lifting away iniquity, passing over transgression for the remnant of his inheritance? He doesn't hold on to his anger for ever, because he delights in steadfast love.
He'll come back and have compassion on us; he'll subdue our iniquities. And you'll cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You'll give faithfulness to Jacob, steadfast love to Abraham, as you swore to our ancestors from the days of long ago.

nahum_1.t: An oracle about Nineveh. This is the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The LORD is a jealous God, and he takes vengeance. The LORD takes vengeance, and rage is his to hold. The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he keeps his anger for his enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, but he won't let the guilty go. His way runs through the whirlwind and the storm; the cloud is the dust of his feet.
He shouts down the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers dry. Bashan withers, and Carmel with it, and the blossom of Lebanon withers.
Mountains shake because of him; the hills melt away. The earth heaves up in front of him — the world, and everyone living in it.
Who can stand up to his fury? Who can hold his ground when his anger burns? His rage pours out like fire, and the rocks are torn down by him.
The LORD is good — a stronghold when trouble comes, and he knows the ones who take refuge in him.
With a flood sweeping through he'll make a complete end of her place, and he'll chase his enemies into darkness.
What are you scheming against the LORD? He is making a complete end. Trouble won't rise a second time.
For while they are tangled up like thorns and soaked through with their own drink, they are eaten up like stubble fully dry.
Out of you came someone who plots evil against the LORD — a counsellor who's worth nothing.
This is what the LORD says: Even if they are at full strength and that many, they'll still be cut down and be gone. I did afflict you; I won't afflict you again.
And now I'll break his yoke-bar off you and rip your fetters apart.

And the LORD has given an order about you: your name will be sown no more. From the house of your gods I'll cut off carved image and cast-metal image. I'll make your grave, because you count for nothing.

Look — up on the mountains, the feet of someone bringing news, announcing peace! Keep your festivals, Judah. Pay your vows. Never again will a worthless one pass through you. He is cut off — all of him.

nahum_2.t: A scatterer has come up against you. Guard the fortification. Watch the road. Brace yourself. Make your strength very firm.
For the LORD is restoring Jacob's majesty the way Israel's majesty was, because the ones who lay waste have laid them waste and destroyed their branches.
His warriors' shields are dyed red; the fighting men are dressed in scarlet. The chariotry blazes like metal in fire on the day he readies it, and the cypress spears quiver.
The chariots race through the streets and rush about in the open squares. They look like torches; they run like lightning.
He calls his nobles to mind; they stumble as they go. They hurry to her wall, and the covering is set up.
The river gates have been thrown open, and the palace has melted away.
And it is settled: she was stripped bare, she was carried off, and her serving women moan like doves, beating on their hearts.
Nineveh is like a pool of water, and always has been — and now they are in flight. "Stop! Stop!" — and nobody turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There's no end to the store — an abundance of every precious thing.
Emptiness, emptiness, devastation! The heart melts, the knees give way, anguish grips every body, and every face has gone pale.
Where is the lions' den now, the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion walked, and the lioness, and the lion's cub, and nothing disturbed them?
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his holes with the kill and his dens with torn flesh.

Look, I am against you — declares the LORD of hosts. I'll burn her chariotry in smoke, and the sword will eat up your young lions. I'll cut off your prey from the earth, and no one will hear your messengers' voices again.

nahum_3.t: Woe to the city of bloodshed! All of it is lies, packed with plunder; the prey never leaves.
The crack of a whip, the rattle of a wheel, a galloping horse, a jolting chariot!
A horseman charging, a sword blade, a spear flashing, heaps of the slain, a weight of corpses, no end to the bodies — they stumble over their bodies.
Because of the prostitute's endless whoring — lovely, full of charm, a mistress of sorceries, who sells nations with her whoring and clans with her sorceries —
Look, I am against you — declares the LORD of hosts. I'll lift your hem up over your face, and I'll show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
I'll throw filth on you, I'll treat you with contempt, and I'll make you a spectacle.
And everyone who sees you will run from you and say, "Nineveh is destroyed! Who will grieve for her?" Where am I to find comforters for you?
Are you any better than No Amon, that sat among the canals with water all around her, whose rampart was the sea, her wall out of the sea?
Cush was her strength, and Egypt too, without end. Put and the Libyans were there to help you.
She too went into exile, into captivity. Her children too were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots over her honoured ones, and all her great ones were bound in fetters.
You too will get drunk; you will go into hiding. You too will look for a stronghold to keep the enemy off.
All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs: shake them and they drop straight into the eater's mouth.
Look — your troops inside the city are women. The gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies; fire has eaten through your bars.
Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Get into the clay, trample the mortar, take hold of the brick mould!
There fire will eat you up, the sword will cut you off, it will eat you like the young locust. Make yourselves as many as the young locust! Make yourselves as many as the swarming locust!
You have made your traders more numerous than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips everything bare and flies away.
Your courtiers are like the swarming locust, your officials like a locust of locusts, settling on the walls on a cold day. The sun comes up and they are gone, and nobody knows where — where are they?
Your shepherds are asleep, king of Assyria; your nobles have lain down. Your people are scattered over the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
There's no easing your fracture; your wound is a bad one. Everyone who hears the news of you claps their hands over you — for who has not felt your evil, again and again?

nehemiah_1.t: The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in Susa the citadel,
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah, and I asked them about the Jews — the escaped remnant who had survived the captivity — and about Jerusalem.
They told me, 'The survivors who came through the captivity, there in the province, are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.'
When I heard this, I sat down and wept. I mourned for days, fasting and praying before the God of the heavens.
And I said: 'I beg you, LORD, God of the heavens — the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments —

let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant that I'm praying before you today, day and night, for the people of Israel your servants — confessing the sins of the people of Israel that we have sinned against you. And I and my father's house have sinned.
We have acted utterly corruptly against you. We haven't kept the commandments, the statutes and the ordinances that you commanded Moses your servant.
Remember the word you commanded Moses your servant: 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples.'

'But if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, then even if your banished are at the end of the heavens, from there I'll gather them and bring them to the place I have chosen to make my name dwell.'
And they are your servants and your people, the ones you redeemed by your great strength and your strong hand.

I beg you, Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name. Grant your servant success today, and give him compassion before this man.' Now I was cupbearer to the king.

nehemiah_2.t: In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, wine was set before him. I took up the wine and gave it to the king. Now I'd never been sad in his presence before.
And the king said to me, 'Why is your face sad? You're not sick. This is nothing but sadness of heart.' And I was very, very afraid.
And I said to the king, 'May the king live for ever! Why shouldn't my face be sad, when the city — the place of my ancestors' tombs — lies desolate and its gates have been consumed by fire?'
And the king said to me, 'What is it you're asking for?' So I prayed to the God of the heavens,
and I said to the king, 'If it seems good to the king, and if your servant has your favour, send me to Judah, to the city of my ancestors' tombs, so I can build it.'
And the king said to me — the queen consort was sitting beside him — 'How long will your journey take, and when will you get back?' It seemed good to the king, and he sent me; and I gave him a date.
And I said to the king, 'If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of Beyond the River, so they'll let me pass through until I reach Judah;

and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so he'll give me wood for the beams of the gates of the citadel by the house, for the city wall, and for the house I'll be living in.' And the king gave them to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
So I came to the governors of Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army commanders and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard about it, it displeased them greatly that a man had come to seek good for the people of Israel.
So I came to Jerusalem, and I was there three days.
I got up at night, I and a few men with me. I'd told no one what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem. And there was no animal with me except the one I was riding.
I went out at night by the Valley Gate, past the Dragon's Spring and on to the Dung Gate, examining the walls of Jerusalem where they were broken down, and its gates consumed by fire.
I went on to the Spring Gate and the King's Pool, and there was no room for the animal to get through under me.
So I went up the wadi at night, examining the wall. Then I turned back, came in by the Valley Gate, and returned.
The officials didn't know where I'd gone or what I was doing, and so far I'd told nothing to the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest of those doing the work.
