Then I said to them, 'You can see the trouble we're in: Jerusalem lies desolate, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let's build the wall of Jerusalem, and be a reproach no longer.'

I told them about the hand of my God, that it had been good upon me, and about the words the king had spoken to me. And they said, 'Let's get up and build.' And they strengthened their hands for the good work.

When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked us and despised us and said, 'What is this you're doing? Are you rebelling against the king?'
I answered them, 'The God of the heavens will grant us success. We, his servants, will get up and build. But you have no share, no right and no memorial in Jerusalem.'

nehemiah_3.t: Then Eliashib the high priest and his brothers the priests set to work and built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and consecrated the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri built.
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz did the repairs; next to them Meshullam son of Berekiah son of Meshezabel; next to them Zadok son of Baana.
Next to them the Tekoites did the repairs — but their nobles wouldn't put their necks to the work of their lords.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Jeshanah Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.
Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite did the repairs — the men of Gibeon and Mizpah — up to the seat of the governor of Beyond the River.
Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, did the repairs; and next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers. And they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, official of half the district of Jerusalem, did the repairs.
Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph did the repairs, opposite his own house; and next to him Hattush son of Hashabneiah.
Malkijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired a second section, and the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, official of half the district of Jerusalem, did the repairs — he and his daughters.
Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Malkijah son of Rechab, official of the district of Beth-hakkerem, repaired the Dung Gate. He built it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars.

Shallun son of Col-hozeh, official of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Spring Gate. He built it, roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars — and the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, official of half the district of Beth-zur, did the repairs, as far as opposite the tombs of David, the artificial pool, and the house of the mighty men.
After him the Levites did the repairs: Rehum son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, official of half the district of Keilah, repaired for his own district.
After him their brothers did the repairs: Bavvai son of Henadad, official of half the district of Keilah.
And Ezer son of Jeshua, official of Mizpah, repaired a second section next to him, opposite the ascent to the armoury, at the buttress.
After him Baruch son of Zaccai zealously repaired a second section, from the buttress to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired a second section, from the entrance of the house of Eliashib to the end of the house of Eliashib.
After him the priests did the repairs — the men of the surrounding region.
After him Benjamin and Hasshub did the repairs, opposite their own house. After him Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah, beside his own house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired a second section, from the house of Azariah to the buttress and to the corner.
Palal son of Uzai, opposite the buttress and the tower that projects from the king's upper house, by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh.
The temple servants were living on the Ophel, as far as opposite the Water Gate to the east, and the projecting tower.
After him the Tekoites repaired a second section, from opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of the Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests did the repairs, each one opposite his own house.
After him Zadok son of Immer did the repairs, opposite his own house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berekiah, opposite his own chamber.
After him Malkijah, one of the goldsmiths, did the repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the traders, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber at the corner.
And between the upper chamber at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the traders did the repairs.

nehemiah_4.t: When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he burned with anger. He was furious, and he mocked the Jews.

He said in front of his brothers and the army of Samaria, 'What are these feeble Jews doing? Are they going to restore it for themselves? Are they going to sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring the stones back to life out of the heaps of debris — burned as they are?'
And Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, 'Even what they're building — let a fox go up on it and it'll break down their wall of stones.'
Hear us, our God — we've become an object of contempt. Turn their reproach back on their own head; give them up as plunder in a land of captivity.
Don't cover over their iniquity; don't let their sin be wiped out from before you. They've provoked you to anger in front of the builders.
So we built the wall, and the whole of it was joined together to half its height, because the people had a heart to work.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem had gone forward and the broken places had begun to be closed, they were furious.
They all conspired together to come and make war on Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
So we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.
And Judah said, 'The strength of the burden-bearers has given out, and there's too much debris. We can't build on the wall.'
And our adversaries said, 'They won't know and they won't see, until we're right among them — and we'll kill them and put an end to the work.'
And when the Jews who lived near them came, they told us ten times over, 'From every place you turn, they'll come at us.'
So I stationed the people at the lowest points of the site, behind the wall, in the exposed places — I stationed them by clans, with their swords, their spears and their bows.

I looked, and I got up and said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, 'Don't be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, the great and awesome one, and fight for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives and your homes.'
And when our enemies heard that we'd found out, and that God had frustrated their plan, we all went back to the wall, each to his own work.
From that day on, half my young men did the work and half held the spears, the shields, the bows and the body armour, with the commanders behind the whole house of Judah,
the ones who were building on the wall. And those carrying loads carried them like this: with one hand each did the work, and with the other held a weapon.
And every builder had his sword strapped at his side as he built; and the man who sounded the ram's horn stayed beside me.
And I said to the nobles, the officials and the rest of the people, 'The work is great and spread wide, and we're separated along the wall, far from one another.'
Wherever you hear the sound of the ram's horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us.
So we did the work, with half of them holding the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also said to the people, 'Let every man and his young man stay the night inside Jerusalem, so they can be a guard for us at night and a workforce by day.'
And neither I nor my brothers nor my young men nor the men of the guard who followed me — none of us took off our clothes. Each took his weapon even to the water.

nehemiah_5.t: Now there was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.
There were those who said, 'Our sons and our daughters — there are so many of us. Let us get grain, so we can eat and stay alive.'
There were those who said, 'We're mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain during the famine.'
There were those who said, 'We've borrowed money for the king's tribute against our fields and our vineyards.'

And now our flesh is the same flesh as our brothers', our children the same as their children — and here we are, subduing our own sons and daughters as slaves. Some of our daughters are already subdued. And there is no power in our hand: our fields and our vineyards belong to others.
And I was furious when I heard their outcry and these words.

My heart took counsel within me, and I contended with the nobles and the officials. I said to them, 'You are exacting a loan, each man against his brother.' And I called a great assembly against them.

And I said to them, 'We ourselves have bought back our brothers the Jews who'd been sold to the nations, as far as we were able. And now will you sell your own brothers — so they have to be sold back to us?' They were silent; they found not a word to say.
And I said, 'What you're doing is not good. Shouldn't you walk in the fear of our God, because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?'
And I too — I and my brothers and my young men — have been lending them money and grain. Let's abandon this loan.
Give them back this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses — and the hundredth of the money, the grain, the new wine and the oil that you're lending them.
And they said, 'We'll give it back, and we'll require nothing from them. We'll do just as you say.' So I summoned the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.

I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, 'So may God shake out every man who doesn't carry out this word, from his house and from his property. So may he be shaken out and left empty.' And the whole assembly said, 'Amen,' and praised the LORD. And the people acted according to this word.

Also, from the day I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah — from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, twelve years — neither I nor my brothers ate the governor's food allowance.

The former governors before me laid a heavy burden on the people, taking food and wine from them, besides forty shekels of silver; and their young men domineered over the people too. But I didn't do that, because of the fear of God.
I also kept my hand to the work of this wall, and we acquired no field; and all my young men were gathered there for the work.
And the Jews and the officials — a hundred and fifty men — and those who came to us from the nations around us were at my table.

What was prepared for a single day was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me; and every ten days, all kinds of wine in abundance. And even so I never asked for the governor's food allowance, because the service lay heavy on this people.
Remember for my good, my God, all that I have done for this people.

nehemiah_6.t: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies heard that I'd built the wall and no breach was left in it — though up to that time I hadn't set up the doors in the gates —
Sanballat and Geshem sent me word: 'Come, let's meet together at Hakkephirim, in the plain of Ono.' But they were planning to do me harm.
So I sent messengers to them with this: 'I'm doing a great work and I can't come down. Why should the work stop while I let it drop and come down to you?'
They sent me the same message four times, and I sent them back the same answer.
Then Sanballat sent his young man to me the same way a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.

Written in it: 'It's being said among the nations — and Gashmu says it too — that you and the Jews are planning to rebel. That's why you're building the wall. And you're to become their king, according to these reports.'
'And you've also appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem: "There's a king in Judah!" And now this will get back to the king. So come — let's take counsel together.'
And I sent back to him, 'None of this has happened, none of these words you're saying. You're inventing them out of your own heart.'
They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, 'Their hands will drop from the work, and it won't get done.' And now — strengthen my hands.

Then I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel, who was shut in; and he said, 'Let's meet at the house of God, inside the temple, and close the temple doors — because they're coming to kill you. By night they're coming to kill you.'
And I said, 'Should a man like me run? And who is there like me who could go into the temple and live? I won't go.'
And I recognised that God hadn't sent him — he'd spoken the prophecy against me, and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He was hired for this: so that I'd be afraid, act on it and sin — and so it would give them a bad name to use, and they could reproach me.
Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these works of theirs — and Noadiah the prophetess too, and the rest of the prophets who were trying to frighten me.
And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
And when all our enemies heard of it, and all the nations around us saw it, they were afraid and fell greatly in their own eyes; and they knew that this work had been done by our God.
In those days, too, the nobles of Judah were sending letter after letter to Tobiah, and Tobiah's letters kept coming back to them.
Many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was son-in-law to Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.
They kept reporting his good deeds in front of me and carrying my words out to him. And Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.

nehemiah_7.t: When the wall had been built and I'd set up the doors, the gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites were appointed.
I put Hanani my brother and Hananiah the commander of the citadel in charge of Jerusalem, because he was a faithful man and feared God more than most.

And I said to them, 'The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot; and while the gatekeepers are still on duty, let them shut the doors and bolt them. Appoint guards from the people living in Jerusalem — each at his post, and each opposite his own house.'
The city was wide on both sides and large, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been built.

My God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the officials and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. And I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found written in it:

These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, the ones Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile. They returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his own city,
those who came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh, 2,172;
the sons of Shephatiah, 372;
the sons of Arah, 652;
the sons of Pahath-moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, 2,818;
the sons of Elam, 1,254;
the sons of Zattu, 845;
the sons of Zaccai, 760;
the sons of Binnui, 648;
the sons of Bebai, 628;
the sons of Azgad, 2,322;
the sons of Adonikam, 667;
the sons of Bigvai, 2,067;
the sons of Adin, 655;
the sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, 98;
the sons of Hashum, 328;
the sons of Bezai, 324;
the sons of Hariph, 112;
the sons of Gibeon, 95;
the men of Bethlehem and Netophah, 188;
the men of Anathoth, 128;
the men of Beth-azmaveth, 42;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Kephirah and Beeroth, 743;
the men of Ramah and Geba, 621;
the men of Michmas, 122;
the men of Bethel and Ai, 123;
the men of the other Nebo, 52;
the sons of the other Elam, 1,254;
the sons of Harim, 320;
the sons of Jericho, 345;
the sons of Lod, Hadid and Ono, 721;
the sons of Senaah, 3,930.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, 973;
the sons of Immer, 1,052;
the sons of Pashhur, 1,247;
the sons of Harim, 1,017.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah, 74.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, 148.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, 138.
The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon,
the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Shalmai,
the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar,
the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda,
the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah,
the sons of Besai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephushesim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida,
the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Amon.
All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants: 392.
And these came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon and Immer, but they couldn't declare their ancestral house or their offspring, whether they were of Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, 642.
And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai — who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These searched for their record among those enrolled by genealogy, and it wasn't found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
And the Tirshatha told them they were not to eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand for Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together: 42,360,
besides their male and female servants, of whom there were 7,337; and they had 200 male and female singers.
Their horses, 736; their mules, 245;
camels, 435; donkeys, 6,720.
Some of the heads of the ancestral houses gave to the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, 50 basins and 530 priests' garments.
Some of the heads of the ancestral houses gave to the treasury of the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 silver minas.
And what the rest of the people gave was 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 silver minas and 67 priests' garments.

So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants and all Israel settled in their own cities. And when the seventh month came, the people of Israel were in their cities.

nehemiah_8.t: And all the people gathered as one in the open space before the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the scroll of the law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
And Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly — men and women and all who could understand what they heard — on the first day of the seventh month.

He read aloud from it, in the open space before the Water Gate, from daybreak until midday, in front of the men and the women and those who could understand. And the ears of all the people were toward the scroll of the law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a high wooden platform that had been made for the purpose. Beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah and Maaseiah on his right, and on his left Pedaiah, Mishael, Malkijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the scroll where all the people could see it, because he was above them all; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, 'Amen, Amen,' lifting up their hands. And they bowed low and bowed down to the LORD with their faces to the ground.

And Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan and Pelaiah — the Levites — were making the people understand the law, while the people stayed in their place.
They read aloud from the scroll, from the law of God, explaining it; they gave the sense, and the people understood the reading.

And Nehemiah — he was the Tirshatha — and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were making the people understand, said to all the people, 'This day is holy to the LORD your God. Don't mourn and don't weep.' For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the law.

And he said to them, 'Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drink, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared. This day is holy to our Lord. Don't be grieved — the joy of the LORD is your stronghold.'
And the Levites quieted all the people, saying, 'Hush — this day is holy. Don't be grieved.'
So all the people went off to eat and drink, to send portions and to make great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
On the second day the heads of the ancestral houses of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe, to gain insight into the words of the law.
And they found it written in the law that the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the people of Israel should dwell in booths during the festival in the seventh month,

and that they should make proclamation and send it through all their cities and in Jerusalem: 'Go out to the hill country and bring olive leaves, oil-tree leaves, myrtle, palm and leafy branches, to make booths, as it is written.'

So the people went out and brought them and made themselves booths — each on his own roof, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of the house of God, in the open space of the Water Gate and in the open space of the Gate of Ephraim.

And the whole assembly that had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in them, because the people of Israel hadn't done so since the days of Jeshua son of Nun until that day. And there was very great joy.

And he read aloud from the scroll of the law of God day by day, from the first day to the last; and they kept the festival seven days, and on the eighth day a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.

nehemiah_9.t: On the twenty-fourth day of this month the people of Israel gathered with fasting, in sackcloth, with earth on them.
And the offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their ancestors.

They stood up in their place and read aloud from the scroll of the law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day; and for another quarter they were confessing and bowing down to the LORD their God.
And Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani and Kenani stood up on the platform of the Levites and cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.

And the Levites — Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah and Pethahiah — said, 'Arise, bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. Let them bless your glorious name; may it be exalted above all blessing and praise.'

You are he, the LORD, you alone. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You preserve them all alive, and the host of the heavens bow down to you.
You are he, the LORD God, who chose Abram, brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans and made his name Abraham;

and you found his heart faithful before you, and made the covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite and the Girgashite — to give it to his offspring. And you fulfilled your words, because you are righteous.
You saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt, and you heard their outcry at the Sea of Reeds.

You gave signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants and against all the people of his land, because you knew they had acted presumptuously against them. And you made a name for yourself, as it is to this day.
You split the sea before them, and they passed through the middle of the sea on dry ground; and their pursuers you threw into the depths like a stone into mighty waters.
In a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, to light the way they should walk.
On Mount Sinai you came down and spoke with them from heaven, and you gave them upright ordinances and laws of faithfulness, good statutes and commandments.
You made known to them your holy sabbath, and commanded them commandments, statutes and law through Moses your servant.

You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought them water out of a rock for their thirst, and you told them to go in and take possession of the land you had lifted your hand to give them.
But they and our ancestors acted presumptuously. They stiffened their neck and didn't listen to your commandments.

They refused to listen, and didn't remember the wonders you had done among them. They stiffened their neck and appointed a head to go back to their servitude, in their rebellion. But you are a God of forgivenesses — gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love — and you didn't abandon them.
Even when they had made themselves a calf of cast metal and said, 'This is your god who brought you up from Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies —

you in your great compassion didn't abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud didn't depart from over them by day, to lead them on the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to light up for them the way they should walk.
You gave your good spirit to instruct them; you didn't withhold your manna from their mouth; you gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing. Their clothes didn't wear out and their feet didn't swell.
You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and allotted to them every corner; and they took possession of the land of Sihon king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You multiplied their children like the stars of the heavens, and brought them into the land you had told their ancestors to go in and take possession of.

The children went in and took possession of the land, and you brought low before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand — them, their kings and the peoples of the land — to do with them as they pleased.

They captured fortified cities and fertile ground, and took possession of houses full of every good thing — hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive trees and fruit trees in abundance. They ate and were satisfied and grew fat, and luxuriated in your great goodness.
They were disobedient and rebelled against you. They threw your law behind their back and killed your prophets who had warned them to bring them back to you, and they committed great blasphemies.

You gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who caused them distress; and in the time of their distress they cried out to you, and you heard from heaven. In your great compassion you gave them deliverers, and they delivered them from the hand of their adversaries.

And as soon as they had rest they went back to doing evil before you, and you abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, and they ruled over them. Then they turned back and cried out to you, and you heard from heaven and rescued them according to your compassion, many times over.

You warned them, to bring them back to your law; but they acted presumptuously and didn't listen to your commandments. Against your ordinances they sinned — the ordinances a person lives by, if he does them — and they turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their neck and didn't listen.
You were patient with them for many years, warning them by your spirit through your prophets; and they wouldn't give ear, so you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
But in your great compassion you didn't make an end of them and didn't abandon them, because you are a gracious and compassionate God.

And now, our God — the great, the mighty and the awesome God, who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love — don't let all the hardship seem small before you that has come upon us: on our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
And you are righteous in all that has come upon us, because you have acted in faithfulness and we have acted wickedly.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests and our ancestors did not do your law, and paid no attention to your commandments or your testimonies with which you admonished them.
And they — in their own kingdom, in your great goodness which you gave them, in the broad and fertile land which you set before them — did not serve you and did not turn back from their evil deeds.
Here we are, slaves today. And the land you gave our ancestors to eat its fruit and its good things — here we are, slaves on it.
Its produce increases for the kings you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and over our cattle as they please. And we are in great distress.
And in view of all this we are making a firm agreement and putting it in writing; and on the sealed document are our leaders, our Levites and our priests.

nehemiah_10.t: And on the sealed documents were Nehemiah the Tirshatha son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah. These were the priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

And the rest of the people — the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and everyone who had separated himself from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, along with their wives, their sons and their daughters, everyone who knew and understood —

they held fast to their brothers, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given through Moses the servant of God, and to keep and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and his ordinances and his statutes;
that we won't give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and won't take their daughters for our sons;

that if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain to sell on the sabbath day, we won't take it from them on the sabbath or on a holy day; and that we'll let go the seventh year and the loan of every hand;
and we established commandments for ourselves: to lay on ourselves a third of a shekel a year for the service of the house of our God —

for the bread of the row, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the sabbaths, the new moons, the appointed times, the holy things and the sin offerings, to make atonement for Israel — and all the work of the house of our God.

We cast lots concerning the offering of the wood — the priests, the Levites and the people — to bring it to the house of our God by our ancestral houses, at appointed times, year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the law.
And to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all the fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of the LORD;

and the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle, as it is written in the law; and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who serve in the house of our God;

and the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, new wine and fresh oil, we'll bring to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God; and the tithe of our ground to the Levites — and it's the Levites who collect the tithes in all the cities where we labour.

And the priest, the son of Aaron, is to be with the Levites when the Levites collect the tithes; and the Levites are to bring up a tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.

For the people of Israel and the sons of Levi are to bring the contribution of grain, new wine and fresh oil to the storerooms, where the articles of the sanctuary are, and the priests who serve, and the gatekeepers and the singers. And we will not neglect the house of our God.

nehemiah_11.t: The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine parts stayed in the other cities.
And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

These are the heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem; and in the cities of Judah each lived on his own property, in their own cities — Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants.

In Jerusalem lived some of the people of Judah and some of the people of Benjamin. Of the people of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah son of Zechariah son of Amariah son of Shephatiah son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;
and Maaseiah son of Baruch son of Col-hozeh son of Hazaiah son of Adaiah son of Joiarib son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.
All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem: 468 men of strength.
And these are the people of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam son of Joed son of Pedaiah son of Kolaiah son of Maaseiah son of Ithiel son of Jeshaiah;
and after him Gabbai and Sallai: 928.
Joel son of Zikri was officer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command over the city.
Of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin;
Seraiah son of Hilkiah son of Meshullam son of Zadok son of Meraioth son of Ahitub, supervisor of the house of God;
and their brothers who did the work of the house, 822; and Adaiah son of Jeroham son of Pelaliah son of Amzi son of Zechariah son of Pashhur son of Malkijah,
and his brothers, heads of ancestral houses, 242; and Amashsai son of Azarel son of Ahzai son of Meshillemoth son of Immer,
and their brothers, mighty men of strength, 128; and Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was officer over them.
And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah son of Bunni;
and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the heads of the Levites, in charge of the outside work of the house of God;

and Mattaniah son of Micah son of Zabdi son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving at the prayer; and Bakbukiah, second among his brothers; and Abda son of Shammua son of Galal son of Jeduthun.
All the Levites in the holy city: 284.
And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates: 172.
And the rest of Israel — the priests and the Levites — were in all the cities of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
The temple servants were living on the Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were over them.
The officer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani son of Hashabiah son of Mattaniah son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, for the work of the house of God.
For the king's commandment was upon them, and a firm ordinance was upon the singers — the matter of each day in its day.
And Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah son of Judah, was at the king's side for every matter concerning the people.
As for the villages with their fields: some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its daughter-towns, in Dibon and its daughter-towns, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
and in Jeshua, Moladah and Beth-pelet,
and in Hazar-shual, and in Beersheba and its daughter-towns,
and in Ziklag, and in Meconah and its daughter-towns,
and in En-rimmon, Zorah and Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its daughter-towns. And they encamped from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
And the people of Benjamin were from Geba: Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its daughter-towns,
Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod and Ono, the Valley of the Craftsmen.
And of the Levites, divisions of Judah belonged to Benjamin.

nehemiah_12.t: These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
And the Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah — he and his brothers were in charge of the songs of thanksgiving.
And Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood opposite them in the duties.
Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, Eliashib, Joiada,
Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim the priests, heads of the ancestral houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
of Abijah, Zikri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan and Jaddua were recorded as heads of ancestral houses; and so were the priests, until the reign of Darius the Persian.
The sons of Levi, the heads of the ancestral houses, were recorded on the scroll of the annals, up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah and Jeshua son of Kadmiel; and their brothers stood opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, by the commandment of David the man of God, division answering division.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon and Akkub kept guard as gatekeepers at the storerooms of the gates.
These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to hold the dedication with joy — with thanksgivings and song, cymbals, harps and lyres.
And the sons of the singers gathered from the district around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites,
and from Beth-gilgal and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
And the priests and the Levites cleansed themselves, and they cleansed the people, the gates and the wall.
I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great thanksgiving choirs and processions. One went to the right along the wall, toward the Dung Gate.
After them went Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah,
and Azariah, Ezra and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah and Jeremiah,
and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Micaiah son of Zaccur son of Asaph,
and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah and Hanani, with the instruments of song of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe went ahead of them.
At the Spring Gate, straight ahead of them, they went up the steps of the City of David, by the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, and on to the Water Gate to the east.
The second thanksgiving choir went the opposite way, and I was behind it with half the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens and as far as the Broad Wall,
and above the Gate of Ephraim, over the Jeshanah Gate and the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
And the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God, and so did I, with half the officials,
and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah and Hananiah, with trumpets;
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malkijah, Elam and Ezer. And the singers made themselves heard, with Izrahiah as officer.
They offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, because God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and the children rejoiced too. And the rejoicing of Jerusalem was heard from far off.

On that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the first fruits and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions of the law for the priests and the Levites — because the joy of Judah was over the priests and the Levites who stood there.
And they kept the service of their God and the service of the cleansing — as did the singers and the gatekeepers — according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.
For in the days of David and Asaph, long ago, there were heads of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgivings to God.

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, the matter of each day in its day. They set apart for the Levites, and the Levites set apart for the sons of Aaron.

nehemiah_13.t: On that day the scroll of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should enter the assembly of God, ever,
because they didn't meet the people of Israel with food and water, and he hired Balaam against them to curse them — and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
And when they heard the law, they separated all those of mixed descent from Israel.
Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the storeroom of the house of our God, being closely allied to Tobiah,

had made him a large room where they used to put the grain offering, the frankincense and the articles, and the tithe of grain, new wine and oil — the portion commanded for the Levites, the singers and the gatekeepers — and the contribution of the priests.
During all this I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. And at the end of some time I asked leave of the king,
and I came to Jerusalem, and I saw the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah in making him a room in the courtyards of the house of God.
It displeased me greatly, and I threw all the goods of Tobiah's household outside, out of the room.
I gave the order, and they cleansed the storerooms; and I brought back there the articles of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
And I learned that the portions of the Levites hadn't been given, and that the Levites and the singers who did the work had fled, each to his own field.
So I contended with the officials and said, 'Why has the house of God been neglected?' And I gathered them and set them back at their place.
And all Judah brought the tithe of grain, new wine and oil to the storerooms.

I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah of the Levites, and next to them Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, because they were reckoned reliable. It was their charge to distribute to their brothers.
Remember this for me, my God; and don't wipe out my acts of loyalty, which I have done for the house of my God and for its services.

In those days I saw men in Judah treading winepresses on the sabbath, bringing in the heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys — and wine, grapes, figs and every kind of load — and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day. And I protested on the day they sold provisions.
And the Tyrians living there were bringing in fish and every kind of merchandise and selling on the sabbath to the people of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
So I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, 'What is this evil thing you're doing, profaning the sabbath day?'
Didn't your ancestors do the same, so that our God brought all this trouble on us and on this city? And you are adding to the wrath on Israel by profaning the sabbath.

And when the gates of Jerusalem grew dark before the sabbath, I gave the order and the doors were shut, and I said they weren't to open them until after the sabbath. I stationed some of my young men at the gates, so that no load should come in on the sabbath day.
And the traders and the sellers of every kind of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem, once and twice.
So I warned them and said, 'Why are you spending the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I'll lay a hand on you.' From that time they didn't come on the sabbath.

And I told the Levites to cleanse themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the sabbath day holy. Remember this too for me, my God, and have pity on me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.
Also in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab.
Half their children spoke Ashdodite and didn't know how to speak Judean, but spoke the language of one people or another.

So I contended with them, cursed them, struck some of the men among them and pulled out their hair; and I made them swear by God: 'You are not to give your daughters to their sons, and you are not to take any of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.'

Didn't Solomon king of Israel sin over these? Among the many nations there was no king like him; he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel — and yet even him the foreign women caused to sin.
And are we to hear of you doing all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?
And one of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite — and I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, for the defilements of the priesthood, and of the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
So I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I assigned duties to the priests and the Levites, each in his own work;
and for the offering of the wood at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember this for me, my God, for good.

numbers_1.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, at the tent of meeting. It was the first day of the second month in the second year after they came out of Egypt. He said:
Take a census of the whole Israelite congregation, clan by clan and ancestral house by ancestral house, listing every male by name, one by one,
everyone twenty years old and up who goes out with Israel's army. You and Aaron are to enrol them by their divisions.
One man from each tribe is to be with you — each of them the head of his ancestral house.
These are the names of the men who are to stand with you. From Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from Joseph's sons: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan;
These were the men called from the congregation — the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of Israel's clans.
So Moses and Aaron took these men, who had been designated by name,
and they assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. They registered their descent by clan and ancestral house, by name, from twenty years old and up, one by one.
This was just what the LORD had commanded Moses, and so he enrolled them in the wilderness of Sinai.
Reuben's descendants — Israel's firstborn — their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, one by one, every male from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Reuben: 46,500.

Simeon's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, those of them enrolled, listed by name, one by one, every male from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Simeon: 59,300.
Gad's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Gad: 45,650.
Judah's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Judah: 74,600.
Issachar's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Issachar: 54,400.
Zebulun's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Zebulun: 57,400.
Joseph's descendants — Ephraim's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Ephraim: 40,500.
Manasseh's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Manasseh: 32,200.
Benjamin's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Benjamin: 35,400.
Dan's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Dan: 62,700.
Asher's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Asher: 41,500.
Naphtali's descendants: their family records by clan and ancestral house, listed by name, from twenty years old and up, everyone who goes out with the army:
The tribe of Naphtali: 53,400.
These are the men enrolled, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled along with Israel's leaders — twelve men, one for each ancestral house.
So all the Israelites who were enrolled, by ancestral house, from twenty years old and up, everyone in Israel who goes out with the army —
came to 603,550.
The Levites, though, were not enrolled with the rest.
The LORD had told Moses:
'Just don't enrol the tribe of Levi — don't take their census along with the Israelites.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its articles and everything that goes with it. They're to carry the tabernacle and all its articles, they're to serve it, and they're to camp around it.
When the tabernacle sets out, the Levites take it down; when it camps, the Levites set it up. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to camp each in his own camp, each by his own standard, division by division.
But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that no wrath falls on the Israelite congregation. The Levites are to keep guard over the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites did it all exactly as the LORD had commanded Moses. That is what they did.

numbers_2.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
The Israelites are to camp each by his own standard, under the emblems of their ancestral houses — facing the tent of meeting, all around it.
Camping on the east side, toward the sunrise: the standard of Judah's camp, division by division. The leader of Judah's descendants is Nahshon son of Amminadab;
His division, those enrolled: 74,600.
Camping next to them, the tribe of Issachar. The leader of Issachar's descendants is Nethanel son of Zuar;
His division, those enrolled: 54,400.
Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of Zebulun's descendants is Eliab son of Helon;
His division, those enrolled: 57,400.
All those enrolled in Judah's camp, division by division: 186,400. They set out first.
On the south side, the standard of Reuben's camp, division by division. The leader of Reuben's descendants is Elizur son of Shedeur;
His division, those enrolled: 46,500.
Camping next to them, the tribe of Simeon. The leader of Simeon's descendants is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
His division, those enrolled: 59,300.
Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of Gad's descendants is Eliasaph son of Reuel;
His division, those enrolled: 45,650.
All those enrolled in Reuben's camp, division by division: 151,450. They set out second.
Then the tent of meeting sets out, with the Levites' camp in the middle of the camps. They set out in the same order they camp in, each in his own position, by their standards.
On the west side, the standard of Ephraim's camp, division by division. The leader of Ephraim's descendants is Elishama son of Ammihud;
His division, those enrolled: 40,500.
Next to them, the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of Manasseh's descendants is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
His division, those enrolled: 32,200.
Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of Benjamin's descendants is Abidan son of Gideoni;
His division, those enrolled: 35,400.
All those enrolled in Ephraim's camp, division by division: 108,100. They set out third.
On the north side, the standard of Dan's camp, division by division. The leader of Dan's descendants is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
His division, those enrolled: 62,700.
Camping next to them, the tribe of Asher. The leader of Asher's descendants is Pagiel son of Ocran;
His division, those enrolled: 41,500.
Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of Naphtali's descendants is Ahira son of Enan;
His division, those enrolled: 53,400.
All those enrolled in Dan's camp: 157,600. They set out last, by their standards.
These are the Israelites who were enrolled by ancestral house. All those enrolled in the camps, division by division: 603,550.
The Levites, though, weren't enrolled along with the Israelites — just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Israelites did it all exactly as the LORD had commanded Moses. That is how they camped, by their standards, and how they set out — each with his clan, by his ancestral house.

numbers_3.t: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses, from the day the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they presented unauthorised fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while Aaron their father was still alive.
The LORD said to Moses:
Bring the tribe of Levi forward and station it before Aaron the priest, and they're to serve him.
They're to keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
They're to look after all the articles of the tent of meeting and keep the charge of the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.
You're to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given over to him outright, from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons, and they're to keep their priesthood. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The LORD said to Moses:
As for me — I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn, every one that opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are to be mine.
Every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in Egypt I set apart as holy for myself every firstborn in Israel, human and animal alike. They're to be mine. I am the LORD.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said:
Enrol Levi's descendants by ancestral house and clan. Enrol every male from a month old and up.
So Moses enrolled them at the LORD's command, just as he'd been commanded.
These were Levi's sons by name: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
These are the names of Gershon's sons by clan: Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons by clan: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
Merari's sons by clan: Mahli and Mushi. These are the Levite clans by ancestral house.
To Gershon belonged the Libnite clan and the Shimeite clan. These are the Gershonite clans.
Those enrolled, counting every male from a month old and up: 7,500.
The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
The leader of the Gershonites' ancestral house was Eliasaph son of Lael.
The charge of Gershon's sons at the tent of meeting was the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the courtyard hangings, the screen for the courtyard entrance that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its ropes — all the work they require.
To Kohath belonged the Amramite, Izharite, Hebronite and Uzzielite clans. These are the Kohathite clans.
Counting every male from a month old and up: 8,600, who kept the charge of the holy place.
The clans of Kohath's sons were to camp on the tabernacle's south side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
Their charge was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the holy place's articles used in its service, the screen, and all the work it required.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He oversaw those who kept the charge of the holy place.
To Merari belonged the Mahlite clan and the Mushite clan. These are the Merarite clans.
Those enrolled, counting every male from a month old and up: 6,200.
The leader of the ancestral house of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the tabernacle's north side.
The appointed charge of Merari's sons was the tabernacle frames, its bars, pillars and bases, all its articles and all its work,
and the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and ropes.

Camping in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses, Aaron and his sons. They kept the charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
All the Levites enrolled — whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the LORD's command, by clan, every male from a month old and up: 22,000.
The LORD said to Moses: Enrol every firstborn male among the Israelites from a month old and up, and take a count of their names.
Take the Levites for me — I am the LORD — in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the Levites' livestock in place of every firstborn among the Israelites' livestock.
So Moses enrolled every firstborn among the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded him.
All the firstborn males, listed by name from a month old and up, came to 22,273.
The LORD said to Moses:
Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the Levites' livestock in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD.
And to redeem the 273 firstborn Israelites who outnumber the Levites —
you're to take five shekels each, by the sanctuary shekel — a shekel is twenty gerahs.
Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the ones over the number.
So Moses took the redemption money from the ones over the number the Levites redeemed.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he took the money: 1,365 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the LORD's command, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_4.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Take a census of Kohath's sons from among the Levites, by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who comes to the service to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of Kohath's sons at the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons come and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
They put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth of solid violet over that, and set its poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they spread a violet cloth and set on it the dishes, pans, bowls and jars for the drink offering, with the regular bread on it.
They spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and set its poles in place.
They take a violet cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, tongs, firepans and all the oil articles used with it.
They put it and all its articles into a covering of fine leather and set it on the carrying frame.
Over the golden altar they spread a violet cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and set its poles in place.
They take all the service articles used in the holy place, put them into a violet cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and set them on the carrying frame.
They clear the ashes off the altar and spread a purple cloth over it,
and put on it all the articles used with it: the firepans, forks, shovels and basins — all the altar's articles. They spread a covering of fine leather over it and set its poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy place and all its articles, as the camp sets out, then Kohath's sons come and carry them. But they mustn't touch the holy things, or they'll die. This is Kohath's sons' load at the tent of meeting.

Eleazar son of Aaron the priest oversees the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil — oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, the holy place and its articles.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Don't let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them so they'll live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons go in and assign each man to his own service and his own load.
They aren't to come in and look at the holy things even for a moment, or they'll die.
The LORD said to Moses:
Take a census of Gershon's sons too, by ancestral house and clan.
Enrol them from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who comes to perform service, to do the service in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans — what they do and what they carry:
They carry the tabernacle curtains, the tent of meeting with its covering and the fine leather covering over it, and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

the courtyard hangings, the screen for the entrance at the courtyard gate that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes and all the articles for their service. They do everything that has to be done with them.
All the service of the Gershonites is to be at Aaron's and his sons' direction, for all their loads and all their service. You're to assign them, as their charge, everything they carry.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their charge is under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Merari's sons: enrol them by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty. Enrol everyone who comes to the service, to do the service of the tent of meeting.
This is the charge of what they carry, for all their service at the tent of meeting: the tabernacle frames, its bars, pillars and bases,
the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and ropes, with all their equipment and all their service. Assign by name the articles they're charged to carry.
This is the service of the Merarite clans, all their service at the tent of meeting, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the congregation enrolled the Kohathites by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
Those enrolled, by clan: 2,750.
These are the enrolled of the Kohathite clans, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the LORD's command, through Moses.
The enrolled of Gershon's sons, by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
those enrolled, by clan and ancestral house: 2,630.
These are the enrolled of the Gershonite clans, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the LORD's command.
The enrolled of the Merarite clans, by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who comes to the service, for service in the tent of meeting.
those enrolled, by clan: 3,200.
These are the enrolled of the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron enrolled at the LORD's command, through Moses.
All those enrolled, whom Moses, Aaron and Israel's leaders enrolled — the Levites, by clan and ancestral house,
from thirty years old up to fifty, everyone who came to do the work of serving and the work of carrying at the tent of meeting —
those enrolled: 8,580.
At the LORD's command they were enrolled through Moses, each to his own service and his own load. Those enrolled were just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_5.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Command the Israelites to send out of the camp anyone with leprosy, anyone with a discharge, and anyone made unclean by a corpse.
Send them out, male and female alike — outside the camp — so they don't make their camps unclean, since I dwell among them.
The Israelites did it. They sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had told Moses, that's what the Israelites did.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites: When a man or a woman does any of the sins people commit, acting unfaithfully against the LORD, and that person becomes guilty —
then they're to confess the sin they've committed. He repays in full what his guilt amounts to, adds a fifth, and gives it to the person he wronged.
But if the man has no kinsman to receive the repayment, what is repaid belongs to the LORD, for the priest — apart from the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for him.
Every contribution from the holy things the Israelites present to the priest is his.
Each person's holy things are his own, but whatever anyone gives to the priest becomes the priest's.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If any man's wife turns aside and acts unfaithfully against him,

and a man lies with her and there's an emission of semen, and it's hidden from her husband and she isn't found out, and she has been made unclean, and there's no witness against her, and she wasn't caught —

and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he's jealous of his wife, and she has been made unclean; or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he's jealous of his wife, and she has not been made unclean —

then the man brings his wife to the priest and brings her offering with her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He isn't to pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it's a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, which brings iniquity to remembrance.
The priest brings her forward and stands her before the LORD.
The priest takes holy water in an earthenware vessel, takes some dust from the tabernacle floor, and puts it into the water.

The priest sets the woman before the LORD, unbinds her hair, and puts the grain offering of remembrance in her hands — the grain offering of jealousy — while the priest holds the water of bitterness that brings a curse.

The priest puts her under oath and says to her: If no man has lain with you, and you haven't turned aside to uncleanness while married to your husband, then be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have turned aside while married to your husband, and you have been made unclean, and a man other than your husband has lain with you —
then the priest puts the woman under the oath of the curse and says to her: May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell;
and this water that brings a curse will enter your body, making your belly swell and your thigh fall away. And the woman says: Amen, amen.
The priest writes these curses on a scroll and washes them off into the water of bitterness.
He makes the woman drink the water of bitterness that brings a curse, and the water that brings a curse enters her, causing bitterness.
The priest takes the grain offering of jealousy from the woman's hand, waves the grain offering before the LORD, and presents it at the altar.
The priest scoops out the memorial portion from the grain offering and turns it to smoke on the altar, and after that he makes the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then if she has been made unclean and acted unfaithfully against her husband, the water that brings a curse enters her, causing bitterness: her belly swells and her thigh falls away, and she becomes a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not been made unclean and she is clean, then she's free, and she will conceive children.
This is the law concerning jealousy, when a wife turns aside while married to her husband and is made unclean,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he's jealous of his wife. He sets the woman before the LORD, and the priest carries out for her all this law.
The man will be free from iniquity, and that woman will bear her iniquity.

numbers_6.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow — the vow of a nazirite, to live as a nazirite to the LORD —
he's to keep away from wine and strong drink. No wine vinegar, no vinegar from strong drink, no grape infusion of any kind, and no grapes, fresh or dried.
The whole time of his consecration he isn't to eat anything the grapevine produces, from the seeds to the skins.
The whole time of his vow of consecration, no razor is to touch his head. Until the time is up for which he lives as a nazirite to the LORD, he's to be holy, letting his hair grow long.
The whole time of his consecration to the LORD he isn't to go near a dead body.
He isn't to make himself unclean for his father or mother, his brother or sister when they die, because the consecration of his God is on his head.
The whole time of his consecration he's holy to the LORD.
If someone dies beside him suddenly, without warning, and so makes his consecrated head unclean, he shaves his head on the day of his cleansing — the seventh day.
On the eighth day he brings two turtle-doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest offers one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering, and makes atonement for him because he sinned in the matter of the corpse. And he consecrates his head that day.
He starts his consecration to the LORD over again and brings a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days don't count, because his consecration became unclean.
This is the law for the nazirite: on the day his time of consecration is up, he's brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He presents his offering to the LORD: an unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, an unblemished year-old ewe lamb as a sin offering, and an unblemished ram as a peace offering;
and a basket of unleavened bread — fine flour loaves mixed with oil and unleavened wafers smeared with oil — with their grain offering and drink offerings.
The priest presents them before the LORD and offers his sin offering and his burnt offering.
The ram he offers as a sacrifice of peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of unleavened bread, and the priest offers its grain offering and its drink offering.
The nazirite shaves his consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting, takes the hair from his consecrated head, and puts it on the fire under the sacrifice of peace offering.
The priest takes the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and puts them into the nazirite's hands after he has shaved off his consecration.

The priest waves them as a wave offering before the LORD. It's holy, and it belongs to the priest, along with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution. After that the nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law for the nazirite who makes a vow: his offering to the LORD for his consecration, apart from whatever else he can afford. He does exactly what he vowed, following the law for his consecration.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and his sons and say: This is how you're to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
May the LORD bless you and keep you.
May the LORD's face shine on you, and may he show you favour.
May the LORD turn his face towards you and give you peace.
That is how they put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.

numbers_7.t: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it, along with all its articles, and the altar with all its articles. He anointed them and consecrated them.
Then Israel's leaders, the heads of their ancestral houses, presented offerings. These were the tribal leaders, the men who had presided over the enrolment.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen — a cart for every two leaders, an ox for each — and presented them in front of the tabernacle.
The LORD said to Moses:
Accept these from them. They're for the service of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his service.
So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
Two carts and four oxen went to Gershon's sons, according to their service.
Four carts and eight oxen went to Merari's sons, according to their service, under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Kohath's sons got none, because the service of the holy things fell to them — they carried on the shoulder.
The leaders presented the dedication offerings for the altar on the day it was anointed. They presented their offering before the altar.
The LORD said to Moses: One leader a day, one leader a day — that is how they're to present their offering for the dedication of the altar.
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, presented his offering.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day: the leader of Zebulun's descendants, Eliab son of Helon.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day: the leader of Reuben's descendants, Elizur son of Shedeur.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day: the leader of Simeon's descendants, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day: the leader of Gad's descendants, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day: the leader of Ephraim's descendants, Elishama son of Ammihud.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day: the leader of Manasseh's descendants, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day: the leader of Benjamin's descendants, Abidan son of Gideoni.
