His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day: the leader of Dan's descendants, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day: the leader of Asher's descendants, Pagiel son of Ocran.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.
On the twelfth day: the leader of Naphtali's descendants, Ahira son of Enan.
His offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin of 70 shekels by the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold pan of 10 shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the sacrifice of peace offering: two oxen, five rams, five he-goats and five year-old male lambs. That was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar, on the day it was anointed, from Israel's leaders: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver basins, twelve gold pans.
Each dish weighed 130 shekels and each basin 70; all the silver of the articles came to 2,400 shekels by the sanctuary shekel.
Twelve gold pans full of incense, 10 shekels each by the sanctuary shekel; all the gold of the pans came to 120 shekels.
All the livestock for the burnt offering: twelve bulls, twelve rams, twelve year-old male lambs with their grain offering, and twelve male goats for a sin offering.
All the livestock for the sacrifice of peace offering: 24 bulls, 60 rams, 60 he-goats and 60 year-old male lambs. That was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And he spoke to him.

numbers_8.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light towards the front of the lampstand.
Aaron did so. He set up its lamps towards the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
This is how the lampstand was made: hammered work of gold, from its base to its blossom all of one piece, made according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
The LORD said to Moses:
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.
This is what you do to cleanse them: sprinkle water of purification from sin on them, have them shave their whole body, wash their clothes, and so cleanse themselves.
Then they take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you take a second young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites forward before the tent of meeting and assemble the whole Israelite congregation.
Bring the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites are to press their hands on the Levites.
Aaron waves the Levites as a wave offering before the LORD, from among the Israelites, and they're to do the service of the LORD.
The Levites press their hands on the heads of the bulls; then offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
Set the Levites before Aaron and his sons and wave them as a wave offering to the LORD.
Separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
After that the Levites come and do the service of the tent of meeting. You cleanse them and wave them as a wave offering.
They're given over to me outright from among the Israelites. In place of every firstborn that opens the womb — the firstborn of all the Israelites — I've taken them for myself.
Every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, human and animal alike. On the day I struck down every firstborn in Egypt I set them apart as holy for myself.
And I've taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.

And I've given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to do the service of the Israelites at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague falls on the Israelites when the Israelites come near the holy place.
So Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite congregation did to the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses about them. That's what the Israelites did to them.
The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron waved them as a wave offering before the LORD. Aaron made atonement for them to cleanse them.
After that the Levites came to do their service at the tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons — just as the LORD had commanded Moses about them, so they did to them.
The LORD said to Moses:
This is the rule for the Levites: from twenty-five years old and up a Levite comes and takes part in the work of serving at the tent of meeting;
and from fifty years old he retires from the service of the work and serves no longer.
He may assist his brothers at the tent of meeting in keeping the charge, but he isn't to do the service. That's how you're to deal with the Levites in their charges.

numbers_9.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out of Egypt. He said:
The Israelites are to keep the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you keep it at its appointed time, according to all its statutes and all its ordinances.
So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.
They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, that's what the Israelites did.
But some men were unclean because of a human corpse and couldn't keep the Passover that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that day.
Those men said to him: We're unclean because of a human corpse. Why should we be kept back from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time along with the Israelites?
Moses said to them: Wait here, and let me hear what the LORD commands about you.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say: If any of you or your descendants is unclean because of a corpse or away on a distant journey, he may still keep a Passover to the LORD.
They keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight, and eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They aren't to leave any of it till morning, and they aren't to break a bone of it. They keep it according to every statute of the Passover.

But anyone who is clean and isn't away on a journey, and who fails to keep the Passover — that person is to be cut off from his kin, because he didn't present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man will bear his sin.

When a sojourner is staying with you and wants to keep a Passover to the LORD, he does it according to the statute of the Passover and its ordinance. There's one statute for you, for the sojourner and for the native of the land alike.
On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it — the tent of the testimony — and in the evening it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire, until morning.
That's how it always was: the cloud covered it, and by night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, the Israelites would set out; and wherever the cloud settled, that's where they camped.
At the LORD's command the Israelites would set out, and at the LORD's command they would camp. As long as the cloud settled over the tabernacle they stayed put.
When the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for a long time, the Israelites kept the LORD's charge and didn't set out.
Sometimes the cloud was over the tabernacle only a few days. At the LORD's command they camped, at the LORD's command they set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening till morning, and when it lifted in the morning they set out; or it stayed a day and a night, and when it lifted they set out.
Or two days, or a month, or longer — whenever the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, settling on it, the Israelites stayed in camp and didn't set out; and when it lifted they set out.
At the LORD's command they camped, at the LORD's command they set out. They kept the LORD's charge, at the LORD's command given through Moses.

numbers_10.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Make yourself two silver trumpets, of hammered work. They're for summoning the congregation and for setting the camps in motion.
When both are blown, the whole congregation gathers to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders — the heads of Israel's thousands — gather to you.
When you sound an alarm, the camps on the east side set out.
When you sound an alarm a second time, the camps on the south side set out. An alarm is sounded for each departure.
When the assembly is to be summoned, you blow a blast but don't sound an alarm.
Aaron's sons, the priests, are the ones to blow the trumpets. This is a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.
When you go to war in your own land against a foe pressing you, sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you'll be remembered before the LORD your God and delivered from your enemies.

On your day of rejoicing, at your appointed times and at each new month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your sacrifices of peace offerings. They'll be a memorial for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the LORD's command, given through Moses.
The standard of Judah's camp set out first, division by division, with Nahshon son of Amminadab over its division.
over the division of the tribe of Issachar's descendants, Nethanel son of Zuar;
over the division of the tribe of Zebulun's descendants, Eliab son of Helon;
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and Gershon's sons and Merari's sons, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
The standard of Reuben's camp set out, division by division, with Elizur son of Shedeur over its division;
over the division of the tribe of Simeon's descendants, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
over the division of the tribe of Gad's descendants, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived.
The standard of Ephraim's camp set out, division by division, with Elishama son of Ammihud over its division;
over the division of the tribe of Manasseh's descendants, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
over the division of the tribe of Benjamin's descendants, Abidan son of Gideoni;
The standard of Dan's camp set out last, the rearguard for all the camps, division by division, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai over its division;
over the division of the tribe of Asher's descendants, Pagiel son of Ocran;
over the division of the tribe of Naphtali's descendants, Ahira son of Enan;
That was the marching order of the Israelites, division by division. And so they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law: We're setting out for the place the LORD said he'd give us. Come with us and we'll do good to you, because the LORD has promised good for Israel.
He said to him: I'm not going. I'll go back to my own land and my own people.
Moses said: Please don't leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness — you can be our eyes.
And if you do come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we'll do the same good for you.
They set out from the mountain of the LORD on a three days' journey, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went ahead of them for those three days, to find them a resting place.
And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day whenever they set out from camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say: Rise up, LORD, let your enemies scatter, let those who hate you flee before you.
And when it came to rest, he would say: Come back, LORD, to the ten thousands of Israel's thousands.

numbers_11.t: The people took to complaining of misfortune, and the LORD heard it. His anger burned, and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
That place was named Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
The rabble among them had a craving, and the Israelites started weeping again too, saying: Who'll give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt for nothing — the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, the garlic.
But now our appetite is dried up. There's nothing at all — nothing but this manna in front of us.
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.
People would go about gathering it, grind it in hand-mills or pound it in a mortar, boil it in a pot and make it into cakes. It tasted like a rich cake made with oil.
When the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each at the entrance of his tent. The LORD's anger burned fiercely, and to Moses it seemed wrong.
Moses said to the LORD: Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why haven't I found favour in your eyes, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should tell me, 'Carry them in your bosom, like a nurse carrying a nursing child,' to the land you swore to their fathers?
Where am I supposed to get meat for all this people? They weep at me and say, 'Give us meat to eat.'
I can't carry all this people by myself. It's too heavy for me.
If this is how you're going to deal with me, then kill me outright, I beg you — if I've found favour in your eyes — and don't let me look on my misery.

The LORD said to Moses: Gather seventy men to me from Israel's elders — men you know to be elders of the people and its officials. Bring them to the tent of meeting and have them take their place there with you.
I'll come down and speak with you there, and I'll take some of the spirit that's on you and put it on them. They'll share the burden of the people with you, so you don't carry it alone.

And tell the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you'll eat meat — because you wept in the LORD's hearing, saying, 'Who'll give us meat to eat? We had it good in Egypt.' Now the LORD will give you meat, and you'll eat.
You won't eat it for one day, or two, or five, or ten, or twenty,
but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and you can't stand it — because you've rejected the LORD who is among you and wept before him, saying, 'Why did we ever come out of Egypt?'
But Moses said: The people I'm among number six hundred thousand on foot, and you say, 'I'll give them meat, and they'll eat for a whole month.'
Are flocks and herds to be slaughtered for them — would that be enough? Or all the fish of the sea gathered for them — would that be enough?
The LORD said to Moses: Is the LORD's hand too short? Now you'll see whether my word comes about for you or not.
So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He gathered seventy of the people's elders and stationed them around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them they prophesied — and never did so again.

But two men had stayed in the camp — one named Eldad, the other Medad. The spirit rested on them (they were among those registered, though they hadn't gone out to the tent), and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses: Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!
Joshua son of Nun, Moses' attendant since his youth, spoke up: My lord Moses, stop them!
But Moses said to him: Are you jealous on my account? If only all the LORD's people were prophets, and the LORD would put his spirit on them!
Then Moses withdrew into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

Then a wind went out from the LORD, drove quails in from the sea, and dropped them by the camp — about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on that, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the ground.
The people were up all that day, all that night and all the next day gathering the quail. The one who gathered least gathered ten homers. They spread them out all around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, not yet chewed, when the LORD's anger burned against the people and he struck them with a very severe blow.
That place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and there they stayed.

numbers_12.t: Miriam spoke against Moses, and Aaron with her, because of the Cushite woman he had married — he had married a Cushite woman.
They said: Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't he spoken through us too? And the LORD heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble — more than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam: The three of you, come out to the tent of meeting. So the three of them went out.
The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance of the tent and summoned Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
And he said: Listen to my words: If there's a prophet among you, I the LORD make myself known to him in a vision, I speak with him in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.
Mouth to mouth I speak with him, plainly and not in riddles; he beholds the form of the LORD. Why then weren't you afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?
The LORD's anger burned against them, and he left.
When the cloud lifted from over the tent, there was Miriam, struck with leprosy, white as snow. Aaron turned towards her — and there she was, struck with leprosy.
Aaron said to Moses: Please, my lord, don't hold against us the sin we committed so foolishly.
Don't let her be like a stillborn child, whose flesh is half eaten away when it comes from its mother's womb.
Moses cried out to the LORD: God, please — heal her!
The LORD said to Moses: If her father had spat in her face, wouldn't she bear the shame for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp for seven days; after that she can be brought back.
So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people didn't set out until she was brought back.
After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

numbers_13.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I'm giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a leader among them.
So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the LORD's command, all of them heads of the Israelites.
These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph — that is, from the tribe of Manasseh — Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Maki;
These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land. And Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan and told them: Go up here into the Negev, then up into the hill country.
See what the land is like, and whether the people living in it are strong or weak, few or many;
and what the land they live in is like, good or bad; and what their cities are like, open camps or fortresses;
and what the land is like, fertile or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be resolute, and bring back some of the fruit of the land. It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and scouted out the land, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, at Lebo-hamath.
They went up into the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Wadi Eshcol, cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and carried it on a pole between two of them, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was named the Wadi Eshcol, because of the cluster the Israelites cut down there.
They came back from scouting out the land at the end of forty days.

They came to Moses and Aaron and the whole Israelite congregation in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh, brought back word to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They gave him this report: We went to the land you sent us to, and it really does flow with milk and honey. This is its fruit.
But the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large — and we saw the descendants of Anak there too.
Amalek lives in the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.
Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said: Let's go straight up and take possession of it. We can certainly prevail over it.
But the men who had gone up with him said: We can't go up against those people. They're stronger than we are.

So they spread a bad report among the Israelites about the land they had scouted out: The land we went through to scout it out is a land that devours its inhabitants, and everyone we saw there is a giant of a man.
And there we saw the Nephilim — the sons of Anak come from the Nephilim — and we felt like grasshoppers, and that's how we looked to them.

numbers_14.t: Then the whole congregation raised their voice and cried out, and the people wept that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them: If only we'd died in Egypt! Or in this wilderness — if only we'd died!
Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will be taken as plunder. Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?
And they said to one another: Let's appoint a leader and go back to Egypt.
Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembled congregation of the Israelites.
And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of those who had scouted out the land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole Israelite congregation: The land we went through to scout it out is an exceedingly good land.
If the LORD delights in us, he'll bring us into this land and give it to us — a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only don't rebel against the LORD, and don't be afraid of the people of the land — they're our bread. Their shade has departed from over them, and the LORD is with us. Don't be afraid of them.
But the whole congregation talked of stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses: How long will this people spurn me? How long will they refuse to believe in me, after all the signs I've done among them?
I'll strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and make of you a nation greater and mightier than they are.
But Moses said to the LORD: Then the Egyptians will hear of it — you brought this people up by your strength from among them —

and they'll tell the inhabitants of this land. They've heard that you, LORD, are among this people; that you, LORD, are seen face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
If you put this people to death as one man, then the nations that have heard the report of you will say:
It's because the LORD wasn't able to bring this people into the land he swore to give them — so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.
And now let the Lord's power be great, as you said:

The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, bearing iniquity and transgression, yet by no means clearing the guilty — visiting the iniquity of fathers on sons, to the third and fourth generation.
Forgive the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now.
The LORD said: I have forgiven, just as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD —
none of the men who saw my glory and my signs — which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness — and who have tested me ten times over and haven't listened to my voice,
will see the land I swore to give their fathers. None of those who spurned me will see it.
But my servant Caleb — because a different spirit was with him and he followed me fully — I'll bring him into the land he went to, and his offspring will take possession of it.
Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn back and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
How long must I put up with this evil congregation grumbling against me? I've heard the grumblings of the Israelites, the way they grumble against me.
Say to them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what you said in my hearing.
In this wilderness your corpses will fall — all of you who were enrolled, your whole number, from twenty years old and up, who grumbled against me.
None of you will come into the land I swore with uplifted hand to settle you in — except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your little ones, the ones you said would be taken as plunder — I'll bring them in, and they'll know the land you rejected.
As for you — your corpses will fall in this wilderness.
Your sons will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the consequence of your faithlessness until the last of your corpses lies in the wilderness.
For forty years — a year for each of the forty days you spent scouting out the land — you'll bear your iniquities, and you'll know my opposition.
I the LORD have spoken: I will do exactly this to the whole of this evil congregation that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they'll meet their end; there they'll die.
As for the men Moses sent to scout out the land, who came back and set the whole congregation grumbling against him by spreading a bad report of the land —
those men, who spread the bad report of the land, died in the plague before the LORD.
But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh stayed alive out of the men who went to scout out the land.
Moses told all the Israelites these words, and the people mourned bitterly.
They got up early in the morning and went up to the top of the hill country, saying: Here we are. We'll go up to the place the LORD spoke of — we have sinned.
But Moses said: Why are you going against the LORD's command? It won't succeed.
Don't go up. The LORD isn't among you — you'll be defeated in front of your enemies.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there in front of you, and you'll fall by the sword. Because you've turned back from following the LORD, the LORD won't be with you.
But they presumed to go up to the top of the hill country — though neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah.

numbers_15.t: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land where you're to settle, which I'm giving you,

and you make a food offering to the LORD — a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfil a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed times — to make a soothing odour to the LORD, from the herd or the flock,
then whoever presents his offering presents to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
And you offer a quarter of a hin of wine as the drink offering with the burnt offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.
Or for a ram, a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil;
and you present a third of a hin of wine as the drink offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
And when you offer a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfil a vow, or as a peace offering to the LORD,
then with the young bull he presents a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil;
and you present half a hin of wine as the drink offering — a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
That's what's done for each bull, each ram, or each of the flock, whether a lamb or a goat.
Whatever number you offer, do this for each one, according to their number.
Every native does these things this way, presenting a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
And when a sojourner is staying with you, or anyone else among you throughout your generations, and offers a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD, he does just as you do.
As for the assembly: one statute for you and for the sojourner who stays with you, a perpetual statute throughout your generations. You and the sojourner are alike before the LORD.
One law and one ordinance apply to you and to the sojourner who stays with you.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land I'm bringing you to,
then, when you eat the food of the land, you present a contribution to the LORD.
From the first of your dough you present a loaf as a contribution — present it the way you present the contribution from the threshing floor.
From the first of your dough you give a contribution to the LORD throughout your generations.
When you go astray and fail to do all these commandments the LORD has spoken to Moses —
everything the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and onward through your generations —

then, if it was done inadvertently, without the congregation's knowledge, the whole congregation offers one young bull as a burnt offering, a soothing odour to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest makes atonement for the whole Israelite congregation, and they're forgiven, because it was inadvertent and they've brought their offering — a food offering to the LORD — and their sin offering before the LORD for their inadvertence.
The whole Israelite congregation will be forgiven, and the sojourner staying among them, because it happened to all the people inadvertently.
If one person sins inadvertently, that person presents a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest makes atonement before the LORD for the person who has gone astray by sinning inadvertently, to make atonement for that person; and he's forgiven.
For the native among the Israelites and for the sojourner staying among them, there's one law, for anyone who acts inadvertently.
But anyone who acts with a high hand, whether native or sojourner, is reviling the LORD. That person is to be cut off from among his kin.
He has despised the word of the LORD and broken his commandment. That person is surely to be cut off — his iniquity is on him.
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the sabbath day.
The men who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation.
They put him in custody, because it hadn't been made clear what should be done to him.
The LORD said to Moses: The man is surely to be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.
So the whole congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him, and he died, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels for themselves on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a violet cord on the tassel at each corner.

It will serve you as a tassel: you'll look at it and remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, instead of going off after your own heart and your own eyes, the way you go whoring after them;
so that you'll remember and do all my commandments and be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.

numbers_16.t: Now Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi took men — along with Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, of the sons of Reuben —
and they rose up before Moses, together with 250 Israelites — leaders of the congregation, called to the appointed meeting, men of renown.

They assembled against Moses and Aaron and said to them: You've gone too far! The whole congregation, every one of them, is holy, and the LORD is among them. So why do you exalt yourselves over the assembly of the LORD?
When Moses heard it, he fell on his face.

Then he said to Korah and all his company: In the morning the LORD will make known who is his and who is holy, and will bring that person near to himself. The one he chooses he'll bring near to himself.
Do this: take censers for yourselves — Korah and his whole company —
put fire in them and set incense on them before the LORD tomorrow. The man the LORD chooses is the one who is holy. You've gone too far, sons of Levi!
Moses said to Korah: Now listen, sons of Levi!

Is it too little for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, bringing you near to himself to do the service of the tabernacle of the LORD and to stand before the congregation and minister to them?
He's brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you — and now you want the priesthood too?
So it's against the LORD that you and your whole company have banded together. And Aaron — what is he, that you grumble against him?
Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said: We won't come up.
Is it too little that you brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness — and now you'd set yourself up as a ruler over us as well?
What's more, you haven't brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Are you going to gouge these men's eyes out? We won't come up.
Moses was very angry and said to the LORD: Don't turn towards their offering. I haven't taken one donkey from them, and I've done harm to none of them.
Moses said to Korah: You and your whole company are to present yourselves before the LORD tomorrow — you and they and Aaron.
Each man takes his censer and puts incense on it, and each presents his censer before the LORD — 250 censers — and you and Aaron, each with his censer.
So each man took his censer, put fire in it and set incense on it, and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron.
Korah assembled the whole congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Separate yourselves from this congregation, and I'll consume them in a moment.
They fell on their faces and said: God, God of the spirits of all flesh — one man sins, and will you be angry with the whole congregation?
The LORD said to Moses:
Say to the congregation: Get away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, with the elders of Israel following him.
He said to the congregation: Move away from the tents of these wicked men, and don't touch anything of theirs, or you'll be swept away in all their sins.
So they moved away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents, with their wives, their sons and their little ones.
Moses said: This is how you'll know that the LORD sent me to do all these works, and that it wasn't of my own devising:
If these men die a natural death, the fate of everyone, and what happens to all people happens to them, then the LORD hasn't sent me.
But if the LORD creates something new — the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and everything of theirs, and they go down alive to Sheol — then you'll know these men have spurned the LORD.
As he finished speaking all these words, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, everyone belonging to Korah, and all their property.
They went down alive to Sheol, they and everything of theirs. The earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
All the Israelites around them fled at their cry, saying: The earth may swallow us too!
And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were presenting the incense.
The LORD said to Moses:
Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers from among the burning and scatter the fire far away, for they've become holy —

the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives. They're to be hammered into plates as an overlay for the altar, since they were presented before the LORD and became holy. They'll be a sign to the Israelites.
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers the burned men had presented, and they were hammered out as an overlay for the altar,

a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who isn't of Aaron's offspring should come near to burn incense before the LORD, and so end up like Korah and his company — just as the LORD had said to him through Moses.
But the next day the whole Israelite congregation grumbled against Moses and Aaron: You have killed the people of the LORD.
When the congregation assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned towards the tent of meeting — and there the cloud had covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
The LORD said to Moses:
Get away from this congregation, and I'll make an end of them in a moment. And they fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron: Take the censer, put fire on it from the altar, set incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them. Wrath has gone out from before the LORD — the plague has begun.
So Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the middle of the assembly, where the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was checked.
Those who died in the plague came to 14,700, besides those who died over the matter of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the plague had been checked.

numbers_17.t: Speak to the Israelites and take from them a staff for each ancestral house, from all their leaders by ancestral house — twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his own staff.
Write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, since there's one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
Put them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will bud, and so I'll put an end to the grumblings of the Israelites against me — the grumblings they direct at you.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader, by ancestral house — twelve staffs. Aaron's staff was among theirs.
Moses put the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
The next day Moses came into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron's staff, of the house of Levi — it had budded, put forth buds, produced blossoms and ripened almonds.
Moses brought out all the staffs from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses: Put Aaron's staff back before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels. That will put an end to their grumblings against me, and they won't die.
Moses did exactly as the LORD had commanded him. That is what he did.
The Israelites said to Moses: Look, we're perishing! We're lost — all of us lost!
Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD dies. Are we all going to perish?

numbers_18.t: The LORD said to Aaron: You and your sons and your father's house with you are to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; you and your sons with you are to bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
Bring your brothers too — the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe — near with you. Let them join themselves to you and minister to you, while you and your sons are before the tent of the testimony.
They're to keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, but they mustn't come near the articles of the holy place or the altar, or they'll die — and you with them.
They're to join themselves to you and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent. No outsider is to come near you.
You're to keep the charge of the holy place and the charge of the altar, so that wrath doesn't fall on the Israelites again.
And I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. They're a gift to you, given over to the LORD, to do the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you are to keep your priesthood in everything to do with the altar and within the veil — that is how you serve. I give you your priesthood as a service of gift. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.
The LORD spoke to Aaron: I myself have put you in charge of my contributions. Of all the holy gifts of the Israelites, I've given them to you as a portion, and to your sons, as a perpetual due.

This is what's yours from the most holy things, kept back from the fire: every offering of theirs — every grain offering, sin offering and guilt offering they render to me. It's most holy for you and your sons.
You're to eat it in a most holy place; every male may eat it. It's to be holy to you.

This is yours too: the contribution from their gift, from all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I've given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual due. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the fresh oil, and all the best of the new wine and grain — the firstfruits of these, which they give to the LORD — I've given to you.
The firstfruits of everything in their land, which they bring to the LORD, are yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
Every devoted thing in Israel is yours.

Every firstborn of the womb, of all flesh, presented to the LORD, whether human or animal, is yours — but you must certainly redeem the firstborn of human beings, and you're to redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
You redeem them from a month old, at your valuation: five shekels of silver by the sanctuary shekel — twenty gerahs to the shekel.
But the firstborn of a cow, sheep or goat you aren't to redeem — they're holy. Dash their blood against the altar and turn their fat to smoke as a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
Their meat is yours, like the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh.

All the contributions of the holy gifts the Israelites present to the LORD I've given to you, and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual due. It's a covenant of salt for ever before the LORD, for you and your offspring with you.
The LORD said to Aaron: You're to have no inheritance in their land and no share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
To the sons of Levi I've given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.
The Israelites are no longer to come near the tent of meeting, or they'll bear sin and die.

The Levites are to perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they'll bear their iniquity. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations. Among the Israelites they're to inherit no inheritance.

For the tithe of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD as a contribution, I've given to the Levites as an inheritance. That's why I said of them: Among the Israelites they're to inherit no inheritance.
The LORD said to Moses:

Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you take from the Israelites the tithe I've given you from them as your inheritance, you're to present from it a contribution to the LORD — a tithe of the tithe.
Your contribution will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as the full yield from the winepress.
That's how you too are to present a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from it give the LORD's contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive, present every contribution of the LORD from the best of it — its sacred portion out of it.
Say to them: When you present the best of it, it will be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and of the winepress.
You and your households may eat it anywhere. It's your wages in return for your service at the tent of meeting.
You'll bear no sin in the matter when you present the best of it — but you're not to profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, or you'll die.

numbers_19.t: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
This is the statute of the law the LORD commanded. Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer — unblemished, with no defect in it, one that has never worn a yoke.
Give her to Eleazar the priest. He takes her outside the camp, and someone slaughters her there in front of him.
Eleazar the priest takes some of her blood on his finger and sprinkles it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
The heifer is burned while he watches — hide, flesh, blood, dung, all of it.
The priest takes cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and throws them into the middle of the fire where the heifer is burning.
The priest washes his clothes and bathes his body in water. After that he can come into the camp, but he stays unclean until evening.
The man who burns her washes his clothes in water and bathes his body in water, and he stays unclean until evening.

A clean man gathers the ashes of the heifer and puts them outside the camp in a clean place. They are kept there for the congregation of the Israelites, for the water to remove impurity. It is a sin offering.
The man who gathers the heifer's ashes washes his clothes and stays unclean until evening. This is a perpetual statute for the Israelites and for the sojourner living among them.
Anyone who touches a dead body — any human corpse — is unclean for seven days.
He purifies himself with the water on the third day, and on the seventh day he is clean. If he does not purify himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead body — the corpse of someone who has died — and does not purify himself, defiles the LORD's tabernacle. That person is to be cut off from Israel. The water to remove impurity was not dashed on him, so he stays unclean; his uncleanness is still on him.
Here is the law: when someone dies in a tent, everyone who goes into the tent and everyone already in it is unclean for seven days.
Any open container with no lid tied down on it is unclean.
Anyone out in the open field who touches someone killed by a sword, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, is unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person they take some of the dust from the burning of the sin offering, and someone pours running water over it into a vessel.

A clean person takes hyssop, dips it in the water, and sprinkles it on the tent, on all the articles, on the people who were there, and on whoever touched the bone, or the body of someone killed, or the corpse, or the grave.

The clean person sprinkles the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh. On the seventh day he purifies him from sin. Then the man washes his clothes and bathes in water, and by evening he is clean.

Anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself is to be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the LORD's sanctuary. The water to remove impurity has not been dashed on him; he is unclean.
This is a perpetual statute for them. Whoever sprinkles the water to remove impurity washes his clothes, and whoever touches the water to remove impurity is unclean until evening.
Anything the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and whoever touches that is unclean until evening.

numbers_20.t: The Israelites, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people settled at Kadesh. Miriam died there, and she was buried there.
There was no water for the congregation, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarrelled with Moses. "If only we had died when our brothers died in front of the LORD!"
"Why did you bring the LORD's assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?"
"Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this terrible place? Nothing grows here — no grain, no figs, no vines, no pomegranates — and there is no water to drink."
Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and they fell on their faces. The glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD said to Moses:

"Take the staff, and gather the congregation, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock in front of them, and it will give its water. You will bring water out of the rock for them, and give the congregation and their livestock a drink."
Moses took the staff from before the LORD, just as he had been commanded.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock. "Listen, you rebels," he said. "Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water came pouring out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me, to treat me as holy in front of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land I have given them."
These are the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarrelled with the LORD, and he showed himself holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says. You know all the hardship that has come on us.
"Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt a long time, and the Egyptians treated us badly, and our ancestors before us.
"We cried out to the LORD, and he heard us and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are at Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

"Please let us pass through your land. We will not go through any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well. We will keep to the King's Highway, and we will not turn aside right or left until we have passed through your territory."
But Edom said to him, "You will not pass through my land, or I will come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will keep to the highway, and if we drink your water — I or my livestock — I will pay for it. Just let me pass through on foot, nothing more."
But he said, "You will not pass through." And Edom came out against him with a large force and a strong hand.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory, and Israel turned away.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
"Aaron will be gathered to his kin. He will not enter the land I have given the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
"Take Aaron and his son Eleazar, and bring them up Mount Hor.
"Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered, and he will die there."
Moses did as the LORD commanded, and they went up Mount Hor while the whole congregation watched.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar, and Aaron died there at the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down.
When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, the whole house of Israel wept for Aaron for thirty days.

numbers_21.t: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim. He attacked Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the LORD: "If you really do give this people into my hand, I will devote their cities to destruction."
The LORD listened to Israel and gave the Canaanites up. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction, and the place was named Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom, and on the way the people lost patience.
The people spoke against God and against Moses. "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread, there is no water, and we are sick of this worthless bread."
The LORD sent the fiery serpents among the people. They bit the people, and many of the people of Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned. We spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the serpent away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make yourself a fiery serpent and put it on a standard. Anyone who is bitten will look at it and live."
So Moses made a bronze serpent and put it on the standard. Whenever the serpent bit someone, he would look at the bronze serpent and live.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness facing Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Wadi Zered.
From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness that stretches out from Amorite territory; the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: Waheb in Suphah, and the wadis, the Arnon,
and the slope of the wadis that runs down toward Ar and leans on the border of Moab.
From there they went on to Beer. That is the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, well! Sing to it!
A well — princes dug it, the nobles of the people hollowed it out, with the ruler's staff, with their own staffs. And from the wilderness to Mattanah,
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley in Moabite country, at the top of Pisgah, looking down over the wasteland.
Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites:

"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from a well. We will keep to the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. He gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel in the wilderness. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the edge of the sword and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites; the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these cities and settled in all the Amorite cities — in Heshbon and all its outlying villages.
Heshbon was Sihon's city, the king of the Amorites. He had gone to war against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him, as far as the Arnon.
That is why the ballad-makers say: Come to Heshbon! Let it be built, let the city of Sihon be established.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's town; it consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are finished, people of Chemosh! He has made his sons fugitives and his daughters captives, to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
And we overthrew them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon; we laid it waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. They captured its outlying villages, and he drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against them with all his people, for battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him. I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So they struck him down, and his sons, and all his people, until he had no survivor left, and they took possession of his land.

numbers_22.t: The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many of them. Moab dreaded the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "Now this company will lick up everything around us, the way an ox licks up the grass of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor by the River, in the land of his own people, to summon him: "A people has come out of Egypt. They have covered the face of the land, and they are settling right across from me.

"So come, please, and curse this people for me. They are too strong for me. Perhaps then I can strike them and drive them out of the land. I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian set out with the fees for divination in their hand. They came to Balaam and told him what Balak had said.
He said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back whatever the LORD tells me." So the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:
"'A people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land. Come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I can fight them and drive them out.'"
God said to Balaam, "You are not to go with them. You are not to curse the people, because they are blessed."
In the morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's leaders, "Go back to your own land. The LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the leaders of Moab went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
So Balak sent again — more leaders this time, and more honoured than the first.
They came to Balaam and said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Please do not let anything hold you back from coming to me.
"I will honour you richly, and whatever you tell me, I will do it. Just come and put a curse on this people for me."
Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go against the command of the LORD my God, in anything small or great."
"So stay here tonight, you as well, and I will find out what more the LORD has to say to me."
God came to Balaam that night and said, "If the men have come to summon you, get up and go with them. But only the word I speak to you — that is what you are to do."
In the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the leaders of Moab.
But God's anger burned because he was going, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road as an opponent to him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn, and she turned off the road into the field. So Balaam struck her to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD, and she squeezed against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot against it. So he struck her again.
The angel of the LORD went on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn aside, right or left.
The donkey saw the angel of the LORD, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger burned, and he beat the donkey with his stick.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me three times now?"
Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you on the spot."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your own donkey, the one you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever been in the habit of doing this to you?" "No," he said.
Then the LORD uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn. He bowed low and put his face to the ground.
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey three times? I came out as an opponent, because the way is perverse before me.
"The donkey saw me and turned aside from me three times. If she had not turned aside, by now I would have killed you and let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know you were standing in the road to meet me. If this displeases you, I will turn back."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men. But only the word I speak to you — that is what you are to speak." So Balaam went with Balak's leaders.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send for you? Why did you not come? Am I really not able to honour you?"
Balaam said to Balak, "Here I am. I have come. But am I really able to say anything at all? Whatever word God puts in my mouth — that is what I will speak."
Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and the leaders with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal, and from there he could see the outer edge of the people.

numbers_23.t: Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and get me seven bulls and seven rams ready."
Balak did what Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stand by your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come and meet me, and whatever word he shows me, I will tell you." And he went off to a bare height.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have set out the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on each one."
The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
He went back to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering with all the leaders of Moab.
Then he lifted up his oracle: From Aram Balak led me, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me, come, denounce Israel.
How can I put a curse on someone God has not cursed? How can I denounce someone the LORD has not denounced?
For from the top of the rocks I see him, from the hills I watch him. Here is a people that dwells alone and does not count itself among the nations.
Who has counted the dust of Jacob, or numbered even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright; let my end be like his.
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to put a curse on my enemies, and instead you have blessed them outright!"
He answered, "Must I not take care to say what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Balak said to him, "Come with me, please, to another place where you can see them — only the edge of them, not the whole — and put a curse on them for me from there."
So he took him to the field of Zophim, at the top of Pisgah, built seven altars, and offered up a bull and a ram on each one.
He said to Balak, "Stand here by your burnt offering, while I go to meet him over there."
The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
He came to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering with the leaders of Moab. Balak asked him, "What has the LORD said?"
Then he lifted up his oracle: Get up, Balak, and listen; hear me, son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a human being, that he should change his mind. Has he spoken, and will he not do it? Has he said it, and will he not carry it out?
I have been given a charge to bless. He has blessed, and I cannot take it back.
He has not looked on misfortune in Jacob, or seen trouble in Israel. The LORD his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.
God is bringing them out of Egypt. He has what are like the horns of a wild ox.
There is no enchantment against Jacob, no divination against Israel. In due time it will be said of Jacob and of Israel: See what God has done!
Here is a people that rises like a lioness, that lifts itself up like a lion. It will not lie down until it has devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain.
Balak said to Balaam, "Then do not put a curse on them at all — and do not bless them either!"
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you? Whatever the LORD says, that is what I will do."
Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will seem right to God, and you can put a curse on them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, looking down over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and get me seven bulls and seven rams ready."
Balak did what Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.

numbers_24.t: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go looking for omens as he had done each time before. He set his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the spirit of God came on him.
Then he lifted up his declaration: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, with his eyes uncovered:
How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwelling places, Israel!
Like wadis stretched out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the water.
Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will be in abundant water. His king will be higher than Agag, and his kingdom will be lifted high.
God is bringing him out of Egypt; he has what are like the horns of a wild ox. He will devour the nations, his adversaries, break their bones, and shatter his arrows.
He crouched, he lay down like a lion, like a lioness — who will rouse him? Blessed be those who bless you, and cursed be those who curse you.
Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. "I summoned you to put a curse on my enemies," he said, "and instead you have blessed them outright — three times now!"
"Now get away to your own place. I said I would honour you richly, but the LORD has kept you from your honour."
Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not tell the very messengers you sent to me:
"'Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go against the command of the LORD, to do good or evil out of my own heart. What the LORD says, that is what I will say.'"
"Now I am going back to my own people. Come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in the days to come."
Then he lifted up his declaration: The declaration of Balaam son of Beor, the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,
the declaration of one who hears the sayings of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, with his eyes uncovered:

I see him, but not now; I watch him, but not close at hand. A star has marched forth from Jacob, a sceptre has risen from Israel. It will shatter the corners of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will become a possession, and Seir, his enemies, will become a possession, while Israel does valiantly.
One from Jacob will rule, and will destroy whoever survives from the city.
Then he saw Amalek, and he lifted up his oracle: Amalek was first among the nations, but his end will be destruction.
Then he saw the Kenites, and he lifted up his oracle: Your dwelling is secure; your nest is set in the rock.
Yet Kain will be burned away. How long before Asshur takes you captive?
Then he lifted up his oracle: Woe! Who will live when God does this?
And ships from the coast of Kittim — they will afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too will come to destruction.
Then Balaam got up and went back to his own place, and Balak went his way too.

numbers_25.t: Israel settled at Shittim, and the people began to whore with the daughters of Moab.
They invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel joined itself to Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the heads of the people and impale them before the LORD in the sun, so that the LORD's burning anger may turn away from Israel."
Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you, kill your own men who have joined themselves to Baal of Peor."

Then one of the Israelites came and brought the Midianite woman to his brothers, right in front of Moses and the whole congregation of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he got up from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He went in after the Israelite man, into the chamber, and ran them both through — the Israelite man and the woman, into her belly. And the plague was held back from the Israelites.
Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.

"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath back from the Israelites by being zealous with my own zeal among them, so that I did not make an end of the Israelites in my zeal."
"So say this: I am giving him my covenant of peace.
"It will be for him and for his descendants after him a covenant of perpetual priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites."
The name of the Israelite who was struck down with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of an ancestral house among the Simeonites.
The name of the Midianite woman who was struck down was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He was head of the tribes of an ancestral house in Midian.
"Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them down,

"for they are hostile to you with the deceits they used against you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor."

numbers_26.t: After the plague, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
"Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, by their ancestral houses — everyone in Israel who goes out with the army."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"From twenty years old and upward" — as the LORD had commanded Moses and the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben, Israel's firstborn. The descendants of Reuben: through Hanoch, the Hanochite clan; through Pallu, the Palluite clan;
through Hezron, the Hezronite clan; through Carmi, the Carmite clan.
These are the Reubenite clans; those enrolled came to forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
The descendants of Pallu: Eliab.

The descendants of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, called from the congregation, who contended against Moses and Aaron in Korah's company, when they contended against the LORD,
and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men. They became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon by their clans: through Nemuel, the Nemuelite clan; through Jamin, the Jaminite clan; through Jachin, the Jachinite clan;
through Zerah, the Zerahite clan; through Shaul, the Shaulite clan.
These are the Simeonite clans: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Gad by their clans: through Zephon, the Zephonite clan; through Haggi, the Haggite clan; through Shuni, the Shunite clan;
through Ozni, the Oznite clan; through Eri, the Erite clan;
through Arod, the Arodite clan; through Areli, the Arelite clan.
These are the clans of Gad's descendants, according to those enrolled: forty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah by their clans were: through Shelah, the Shelanite clan; through Perez, the Perezite clan; through Zerah, the Zerahite clan.
The descendants of Perez were: through Hezron, the Hezronite clan; through Hamul, the Hamulite clan.
These are the clans of Judah, according to those enrolled: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Issachar by their clans: through Tola, the Tolaite clan; through Puvah, the Punite clan;
through Jashub, the Jashubite clan; through Shimron, the Shimronite clan.
These are the clans of Issachar, according to those enrolled: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: through Sered, the Seredite clan; through Elon, the Elonite clan; through Jahleel, the Jahleelite clan.
These are the Zebulunite clans, according to those enrolled: sixty thousand five hundred.
The descendants of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The descendants of Manasseh: through Machir, the Machirite clan; and Machir fathered Gilead; through Gilead, the Gileadite clan.
These are the descendants of Gilead: through Iezer, the Iezerite clan; through Helek, the Helekite clan;
and Asriel, the Asrielite clan; and Shechem, the Shechemite clan;
and Shemida, the Shemidaite clan; and Hepher, the Hepherite clan.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad's daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh; those enrolled came to fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
These are the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: through Shuthelah, the Shuthelahite clan; through Becher, the Becherite clan; through Tahan, the Tahanite clan.
And these are the descendants of Shuthelah: through Eran, the Eranite clan.
These are the clans of Ephraim's descendants, according to those enrolled: thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: through Bela, the Belaite clan; through Ashbel, the Ashbelite clan; through Ahiram, the Ahiramite clan;
through Shephupham, the Shuphamite clan; through Hupham, the Huphamite clan.
The descendants of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the Ardite clan; through Naaman, the Naamanite clan.
These are the descendants of Benjamin by their clans; those enrolled came to forty-five thousand six hundred.
These are the descendants of Dan by their clans: through Shuham, the Shuhamite clan. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the Shuhamite clans, according to those enrolled: sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Asher by their clans: through Imnah, the Imnite clan; through Ishvi, the Ishvite clan; through Beriah, the Beriite clan.
Of the descendants of Beriah: through Heber, the Heberite clan; through Malchiel, the Malchielite clan.
And the name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
These are the clans of Asher's descendants, according to those enrolled: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: through Jahzeel, the Jahzeelite clan; through Guni, the Gunite clan;
through Jezer, the Jezerite clan; through Shillem, the Shillemite clan.
These are the clans of Naphtali by their clans; those enrolled came to forty-five thousand four hundred.
These are those enrolled of the Israelites: six hundred and one thousand, seven hundred and thirty.
The LORD said to Moses:
"The land is to be divided among these as an inheritance, by the number of names.
"To the large tribe give a large inheritance, and to the small a small one. Each is to be given its inheritance according to the number enrolled.
"But the land is to be divided by lot; they will inherit according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
"Each inheritance is to be divided according to the lot, between the large and the small."
And these are those enrolled of the Levites by their clans: through Gershon, the Gershonite clan; through Kohath, the Kohathite clan; through Merari, the Merarite clan.
These are the clans of Levi: the Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, the Korahite clan. And Kohath fathered Amram.
Amram's wife was named Jochebed, daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron and Moses to Amram, and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they presented unauthorised fire before the LORD.
Those enrolled of them came to twenty-three thousand, every male a month old and upward; they were not enrolled among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These are those enrolled by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who enrolled the Israelites in the plains of Moab at the Jordan across from Jericho.
Among these there was not one man from those enrolled by Moses and Aaron the priest, who enrolled the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, "They will surely die in the wilderness." Not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

numbers_27.t: Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward — Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders and the whole congregation, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said:
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not part of the company that gathered against the LORD with Korah; he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
