"Why should our father's name be taken away from his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father's brothers."
So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
The LORD said to Moses:
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You are to give them a possession as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and transfer their father's inheritance to them.
"And say to the Israelites: If a man dies and has no son, transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
"If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
"If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

"And if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and he will take possession of it. This is to be a statute of judgement for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim and see the land I have given the Israelites."
"When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your kin, as your brother Aaron was gathered,

"since you rebelled against my command in the wilderness of Zin, during the strife of the congregation, to treat me as holy at the waters before their eyes. Those are the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin."
Moses said to the LORD:
"Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
"one who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the LORD's congregation will not be like sheep with no shepherd."
The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
"Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him where they can see it.
"Put some of your majesty on him, so that the whole congregation of the Israelites will obey him.

"He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will enquire for him by the judgement of the Urim before the LORD. At his word they will go out and at his word they will come in — he and all the Israelites with him, the whole congregation."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,
and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had spoken through Moses.

numbers_28.t: The LORD said to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and tell them: Take care to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food, for my food offerings, my soothing odour."
"And say to them: This is the food offering you are to present to the LORD: two unblemished year-old male lambs a day, as a continual burnt offering.
"Offer the one lamb in the morning and the second lamb at twilight,
"and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil.
"It is a continual burnt offering, the one instituted at Mount Sinai, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place pour out a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD.
"Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD.
"On the sabbath day: two unblemished year-old male lambs, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
"This is the burnt offering for each sabbath, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"At the beginnings of your months, present a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for the one bull; and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for the one ram;
"and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil, for each lamb. It is a burnt offering, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"Their drink offerings: half a hin of wine for the bull, a third of a hin for the ram, a quarter of a hin for the lamb. This is the burnt offering for each month, through the months of the year.
"And one male goat as a sin offering to the LORD, offered in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is a Passover to the LORD.
"On the fifteenth day of this month is a festival; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
"On the first day there is to be a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.
"Present a food offering, a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs — they are to be unblemished for you;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull and two tenths for the ram.
"A tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
"And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
"Offer these in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is the continual burnt offering.
"Offer these in the same way each day for seven days — the food of a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD — in addition to the continual burnt offering and its drink offering.
"On the seventh day you are to have a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.
"On the day of the firstfruits, when you present a new grain offering to the LORD at your Weeks, you are to have a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work.
"Present a burnt offering as a soothing odour to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old male lambs;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the one bull, two tenths for the one ram,
"a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for all seven lambs;
"one male goat, to make atonement for you.
"Offer them in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering — they are to be unblemished — with their drink offerings."

numbers_29.t: "In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you are to have a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work. It is to be for you a day of a loud blast.
"Offer a burnt offering as a soothing odour to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
"and one tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for all seven lambs;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you;

"in addition to the new-moon burnt offering and its grain offering, and the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, with their drink offerings as prescribed, a soothing odour, a food offering to the LORD.
"On the tenth day of this seventh month you are to have a holy convocation, and you are to afflict yourselves; you are to do no work at all.
"Present a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing odour: one young bull, one ram, seven year-old male lambs — they are to be unblemished for you;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
"a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for all seven lambs;
"one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the continual burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you are to have a holy convocation; you are to do no occupational work. You are to celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days.
"Present a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, fourteen year-old male lambs — they are to be unblemished;
"and their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams;
"and a tenth of an ephah for each lamb, for all fourteen lambs;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
"On the third day: eleven young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the fourth day: ten young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the fifth day: nine young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the sixth day: eight young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offerings.
"On the seventh day: seven young bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed for them;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"On the eighth day you are to have a solemn assembly; you are to do no occupational work.
"Present a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing odour to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, seven unblemished year-old male lambs;
"with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, the ram and the lambs, by their number, as prescribed;
"and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"These you are to offer to the LORD at your appointed times, apart from your vows and freewill offerings — your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings and your peace offerings."
So Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded Moses.

numbers_30.t: Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites: "This is the word the LORD has commanded.
"When a man vows a vow to the LORD or swears an oath binding an obligation on himself, he is not to break his word. He is to do everything that comes out of his mouth.
"When a woman vows a vow to the LORD and binds an obligation on herself in her father's house while she is young,
"and her father hears of her vow and the obligation she has bound on herself, and says nothing to her — then all her vows stand, and every obligation she has bound on herself stands.
"But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or the obligations she has bound on herself stand; and the LORD will forgive her, because her father forbade her.
"If she marries while her vows are on her, or the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself,
"and her husband hears of it on the day he hears and says nothing to her — then her vows stand, and the obligations by which she has bound herself stand.
"But if on the day her husband hears of it he forbids her and annuls the vow that is on her and the rash utterance of her lips by which she has bound herself, then the LORD will forgive her.
"But the vow of a widow or a divorced woman — everything by which she has bound herself stands against her.
"If she made a vow in her husband's house, or bound an obligation on herself by an oath,
"and her husband heard of it, said nothing to her and did not forbid her — then all her vows stand, and every obligation she bound on herself stands.

"But if her husband annuls them on the day he hears of it, nothing that has gone out of her lips — her vows or the obligation on herself — stands. Her husband has annulled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
"Every vow and every binding oath to afflict herself, her husband may confirm or annul.
"But if her husband says nothing to her at all, from day to day, then he has confirmed all her vows or all the obligations on her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing on the day he heard.
"But if he annuls them after he has heard, then he bears her iniquity.
These are the statutes the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father's house.

numbers_31.t: The LORD said to Moses:
"Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midianites. After that you will be gathered to your kin."
So Moses spoke to the people: "Equip men from among you for the army, and send them against Midian, to carry out the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
"Send out a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to the army."
So a thousand from each tribe were handed over from the thousands of Israel: twelve thousand armed for the army.
Moses sent them out, a thousand from each tribe — them and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, with the articles of the holy place and the trumpets for the blast in his hand.
They waged war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian along with the rest of their slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. And they killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian captive along with their little ones, and plundered all their cattle, all their livestock, and all their wealth.
They burned with fire all the cities where they lived and all their encampments.
They took all the spoil and all the booty, both people and livestock.
They brought the captives, the booty and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the Israelites, at the camp in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
But Moses was angry with the officers of the force, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, as they came in from the campaign.
Moses said to them, "Have you let every female live?"
"These were the ones who, on Balaam's word, led the Israelites to act unfaithfully against the LORD in the matter of Peor, and the plague came on the congregation of the LORD.
"Now then, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by lying with a male.
"But all the young among the women who have not known lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.

"And you, camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed a person and everyone who has touched a slain one is to purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day — you and your captives.
"And purify every garment, every article of hide, everything made of goats' hair, and every article of wood.
Eleazar the priest said to the men of the army who had gone into battle, "This is the statute of the law the LORD commanded Moses.
"Only the gold and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin and the lead —

"anything that can go into the fire, pass through the fire, and it will be clean; even so, it must be purified with the water to remove impurity. Anything that cannot go into the fire, pass through the water.
"Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean; after that you can come into the camp."
The LORD said to Moses:
"Take the sum of the booty that was taken, both people and livestock — you, Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the congregation.
"Divide the booty in half between the fighting men who went out with the army and the whole congregation.
"Raise a levy for the LORD from the men of war who went out with the army: one out of every five hundred — from the people, the cattle, the donkeys and the sheep.
"Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution to the LORD.

"From the Israelites' half take one drawn out of every fifty — from the people, the cattle, the donkeys, the sheep, from all the livestock — and give them to the Levites who keep the charge of the LORD's tabernacle."
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The booty, beyond the plunder the men of the army had taken for themselves, came to: 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 people — the women who had not known lying with a male.
The half that was the portion of those who went out with the army came to: 337,500 sheep,
and the levy for the LORD from the sheep was 675;
the cattle were 36,000, and their levy for the LORD was 72;
the donkeys were 30,500, and their levy for the LORD was 61;
and the people were 16,000, and their levy for the LORD was 32 persons.
Moses gave the levy, the LORD's contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
As for the Israelites' half, which Moses had divided off from the men who went to war —
the congregation's half was 337,500 sheep,
36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.

Moses took from the Israelites' half the one drawn out of every fifty, from the people and from the livestock, and gave them to the Levites who keep the charge of the LORD's tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the officers over the thousands of the army came to Moses — the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds —
and said to Moses, "Your servants have taken the sum of the men of war under our charge, and not one of us is missing.
"So we have presented the LORD's offering — each of us what he found, articles of gold: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and necklaces — to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them, all of it worked articles.
All the gold of the contribution that they raised for the LORD came to 16,750 shekels, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds.
The men of the army had each taken plunder for himself.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.

numbers_32.t: The descendants of Reuben and Gad had a great deal of livestock, a very large amount. When they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, the place turned out to be good country for livestock.
So the descendants of Gad and Reuben came and said to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation:
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon —
"the land the LORD struck down before the congregation of Israel — it is livestock country, and your servants have livestock."
They said, "If we have found favour in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
But Moses said to the descendants of Gad and Reuben, "Are your brothers to go to battle while you sit here?"
"Why would you turn the Israelites' hearts away from crossing into the land the LORD has given them?
"This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
"They went up as far as the Wadi Eshcol and saw the land, and they turned the Israelites' hearts away, so that they would not go into the land the LORD had given them.
"The LORD's anger burned that day, and he swore an oath:
"'Surely the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, will not see the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob — because they have not followed me fully.'"
"except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the LORD fully.
"So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the eyes of the LORD was gone.
"And here you are, risen up in place of your fathers, a brood of sinful men, adding still more to the LORD's burning anger against Israel.
"If you turn back from following him, he will leave them in the wilderness once more, and you will have destroyed this whole people."
Then they came up to him and said, "We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones,

"and we ourselves will arm and go in haste ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones will live in the fortified cities, because of the people living in the land.
"We will not go back to our houses until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
"We will not inherit with them across the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan, to the east."
Moses said to them, "If you do this — if you arm yourselves before the LORD for battle,
"and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies before him,

"and the land is subdued before the LORD, and after that you return — then you will be clear of obligation before the LORD and before Israel, and this land will be yours as a possession before the LORD.
"But if you do not, then you have sinned against the LORD; and know that your sin will find you out.
"Build cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do what you have said."
The descendants of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "Your servants will do just as my lord commands.
"Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our cattle will stay there, in the cities of Gilead.
"But your servants will cross over, every man armed for the army, before the LORD to the battle, just as my lord says."
So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel.

Moses said to them, "If the descendants of Gad and Reuben cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
"But if they do not cross over armed with you, then they will receive their possession among you in the land of Canaan."
The descendants of Gad and Reuben answered, "What the LORD has spoken to your servants — that is what we will do.
"We ourselves will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance will stay ours on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave them — the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph — the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its cities within their borders, the cities of the surrounding country.
The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth and Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer and Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran — fortified cities and sheepfolds.
The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
and Nebo and Baal-meon — their names being changed — and Sibmah; and they gave names to the cities they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their tent-villages, and named them Havvoth-jair.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its outlying villages, and named it Nobah, after himself.

numbers_33.t: These are the stages of the Israelites, who came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, under Moses and Aaron.
Moses wrote down their points of departure stage by stage, at the command of the LORD; and these are their stages, by their points of departure.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out with a high hand, in full view of all Egypt,
while the Egyptians were burying those the LORD had struck down among them, every firstborn; and on their gods the LORD had carried out judgements.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
They set out from before Hahiroth, passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness, went three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Sea of Reeds.
They set out from the Sea of Reeds and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom.

Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of the LORD and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of the Abarim, in front of Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of the Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.
They camped along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
"you are to dispossess all the inhabitants of the land before you, destroy all their figured stones and all their cast-metal images, and demolish all their high places.
"You are to take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

"You are to apportion the land by lot according to your clans: to the large, a large inheritance; to the small, a small one. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that is his. You will inherit by your ancestral tribes.

"But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land before you, then those you leave will be thorns in your eyes and pricks in your sides, and they will be hostile to you in the land where you live.
"And it will be that what I intended to do to them, I will do to you."

numbers_34.t: The LORD said to Moses:
"Command the Israelites and say to them: When you come into the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance — the land of Canaan with its borders:
"Your southern side will run from the wilderness of Zin along the edge of Edom; your southern border will begin at the end of the Salt Sea, on the east.
"The border will turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, pass on toward Zin, and end south of Kadesh-barnea; then it goes out to Hazar-addar and on toward Azmon.
"The border turns from Azmon toward the Wadi of Egypt, and ends at the sea.
"For the western border, the Great Sea will be your border; that is your western border.
"This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea, mark out a line to Mount Hor.
"From Mount Hor, mark out a line to Lebo-hamath, and the border ends at Zedad.
"The border goes out to Ziphron and ends at Hazar-enan. That is your northern border.
"For your eastern border, mark out a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
"The border goes down from Shepham to Riblah, east of Ain; then it goes down and reaches the slope of the Sea of Kinnereth on the east.
"The border goes down to the Jordan and ends at the Salt Sea. That is your land, with its borders all round."
Moses commanded the Israelites: "This is the land you are to inherit by lot, which the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral house and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral house have taken theirs, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has taken its inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have taken their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise.
The LORD said to Moses:
"These are the names of the men who will apportion the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
"And take one leader from each tribe to apportion the land as an inheritance.
"These are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
"of the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
"of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
"of the tribe of Dan, a leader: Bukki son of Jogli;
"of the descendants of Joseph: of the tribe of Manasseh, a leader: Hanniel son of Ephod;
"of the tribe of Ephraim, a leader: Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
"of the tribe of Zebulun, a leader: Elizaphan son of Parnach;
"of the tribe of Issachar, a leader: Paltiel son of Azzan;
"of the tribe of Asher, a leader: Ahihud son of Shelomi;
"of the tribe of Naphtali, a leader: Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the ones the LORD commanded to apportion the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.

numbers_35.t: The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho:
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites, out of the inheritance they possess, cities to live in; and give the Levites pasture land around those cities.
"The cities will be theirs to live in, and the pasture lands will be for their cattle, their property and all their animals.
"The pasture lands of the cities you give the Levites are to extend a thousand cubits out from the city wall, all round.

"Measure outside the city: the east side two thousand cubits, the south side two thousand, the west side two thousand, the north side two thousand, with the city in the middle. That is theirs, the pasture lands of the cities.
"The cities you give the Levites are to be the six cities of refuge, for the killer to flee to, and in addition to them forty-two cities.
"All the cities you give the Levites are to be forty-eight, with their pasture lands.

"The cities you take from the possession of the Israelites are to be in proportion: more from the large, fewer from the small. Each tribe gives some of its cities to the Levites according to the inheritance it receives."
The LORD said to Moses:
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
"you are to provide yourselves cities to serve as cities of refuge, and a killer who has struck someone down unintentionally can flee there.
"The cities will be a refuge for you from the avenger, so that the killer will not die until he has stood before the congregation for judgement.
"The cities you give are to be six cities of refuge for you.
"Give three cities on the far side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan; they are to be cities of refuge.
"These six cities will be a refuge for the Israelites, for the sojourner and the resident alien among them, so that anyone who strikes someone down unintentionally can flee there.
"But if he struck him with an iron instrument and he died, he is a killer; the killer is certainly to be put to death.
"If he struck him with a stone in his hand of a kind that can kill, and he died, he is a killer; the killer is certainly to be put to death.
"Or if he struck him with a wooden instrument in his hand of a kind that can kill, and he died, he is a killer; the killer is certainly to be put to death.
"The avenger of blood is the one to put the killer to death; when he meets him, he is to put him to death.
"If he pushed him out of hatred, or threw something at him from ambush, so that he died,

"or struck him with his hand out of enmity so that he died, the one who struck him is certainly to be put to death; he is a killer. The avenger of blood is to put the killer to death when he meets him.
"But if he pushed him suddenly, without enmity, or threw something at him without lying in wait,
"or with any stone that can kill, without seeing him, and dropped it on him so that he died — and he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him —
"then the congregation is to judge between the one who struck and the avenger of blood, according to these rules.

"The congregation is to deliver the killer from the hand of the avenger of blood and return him to the city of refuge he fled to, and he is to live in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
"But if the killer ever goes beyond the border of the city of refuge he fled to,
"and the avenger of blood finds him outside the border of his city of refuge and kills him, there is no blood-guilt on him.
"He must stay in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; after the death of the high priest the killer may return to the land of his possession.
"These are to be a statute of judgement for you throughout your generations, wherever you live.
"Anyone who strikes someone down is to be killed on the testimony of witnesses; but no one is to be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
"You are not to take a ransom for the life of a killer who is guilty and deserves to die; he is certainly to be put to death.
"And you are not to take a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, letting him return and live in the land before the death of the priest.
"You are not to pollute the land where you are, because blood pollutes the land; and no atonement can be made for the land, for the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
"You are not to make unclean the land where you live, in the midst of which I dwell; for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites."

numbers_36.t: The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of Gilead's descendants — Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of Joseph's descendants — came forward and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel.

They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

"But if they marry into any of the other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken from our fathers' inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into; it will be taken out of our allotted inheritance.
"And when the jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the tribe they married into, and taken from the inheritance of our fathers' tribe."
So Moses commanded the Israelites at the command of the LORD: "The tribe of Joseph's descendants is right.
"This is what the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whoever seems good to them — only, they must marry within the clan of their father's tribe.
"An Israelite inheritance is not to pass round from tribe to tribe; each Israelite is to cling to the inheritance of his fathers' tribe.

"Every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the Israelites is to marry within the clan of her father's tribe, so that each Israelite keeps possession of the inheritance of his fathers.
"An inheritance is not to pass round from one tribe to another; each of the tribes of Israel is to cling to its own inheritance."
The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married their cousins on their father's side.
They married within the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance stayed with the tribe of their father's clan.
These are the commandments and the judgements that the LORD commanded through Moses to the Israelites in the plains of Moab, at the Jordan across from Jericho.

obadiah_1.t: The vision of Obadiah. This is what Lord GOD says about Edom: We've heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Get up! Let's rise against her for battle!"
Look — I've made you small among the nations. You're despised, utterly.
Your heart's presumption has fooled you — you who live in the clefts of the rock, whose home is set high up, who say to yourself, "Who's going to bring me down to the ground?"
Even if you set yourself as high as the eagle, even if your nest is placed among the stars — from there I'll bring you down. So declares the LORD.
If thieves came for you, if night raiders came — and how ruined you are! — wouldn't they steal only as much as they wanted? If grape-pickers came for you, wouldn't they leave a few gleanings?
How thoroughly Esau has been searched! His hidden treasures — hunted out!

They've driven you to the border, every one of the men who had a covenant with you; they deceived you, they overpowered you, the men who were at peace with you. Your bread — they set a trap under you. There's no understanding in him.
On that day — declares the LORD — won't I destroy the wise out of Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
Your warriors will be dismayed, Teman — so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
Because of the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you'll be cut off for ever.
On the day you stood there and did nothing, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners came through his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem — you were just like one of them.
Don't stand and watch your brother's day, the day disaster came on him; don't gloat over the people of Judah on the day they perish; don't talk big on the day of distress.
Don't come through the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; don't look, you too, at his ruin on the day of his disaster; don't reach out for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
Don't stand at the fork in the road to cut down the ones escaping; don't hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
The day of the LORD is near — for all the nations. What you have done will be done to you; your recompense will come back on your own head.
For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, all the nations will drink, and keep drinking; they'll drink and swallow it down, and they'll be as though they had never been.
But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be a holy place, and the house of Jacob will take back what belongs to them.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble; they'll burn through them and consume them, and not one survivor will be left to the house of Esau — because the LORD has spoken.

The people of the Negev will take possession of the mountain of Esau, and the people of the Shephelah, of the Philistines; they'll take possession of the region of Ephraim and the region of Samaria, and Benjamin, of the Gilead.

And the exiles of this rampart, the people of Israel, the ones among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem, the ones in Sepharad — they will take possession of the cities of the Negev.
And deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingship will belong to the LORD.

proverbs_1.t: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:
To learn what wisdom is, and discipline; to take in sayings that give understanding;
to take in the discipline that gives insight — righteousness, justice, fair dealing;
to give the naive some shrewdness, to give the young knowledge and discretion —
Let the wise listen and learn more; let the discerning pick up some guidance —
to make sense of a proverb, a figure of speech, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The fear of the LORD is where knowledge starts. Fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Listen to your father's discipline, my son, and don't push aside what your mother teaches you.
They'll be a wreath of favour on your head, a necklace at your throat.
My son, if sinners try to talk you into it, don't go along with them.
If they say, "Come along with us — let's lie in wait for blood, let's lurk for someone innocent, for no reason at all;
let's swallow them alive, the way Sheol does, whole, like people going down into the pit;
we'll find every kind of valuable thing, we'll fill our houses with loot;
throw your lot in with us — we'll all share one purse" —
My son, don't walk that road with them. Keep your foot off their path.
Their feet run straight to evil; they're in a hurry to shed blood.
No point spreading the net where the bird can see you do it.
But it's their own blood they're lying in wait for; it's their own lives they're lurking after.
That's how it goes for anyone out for dishonest gain: it takes the life of whoever holds it.
Wisdom is out in the street, calling; in the open squares she raises her voice.
She calls out where the crowds are loudest; at the city gates she speaks her sayings:
"How long, you naive ones, are you going to love being naive? Mockers delight in their mockery; dullards hate knowledge.
If you turn back when I correct you, look — I'll pour out my spirit on you; I'll let you know what I have to say.
Because I called and you refused; because I reached out my hand and nobody was listening;
because you let all my counsel go and wanted nothing to do with my correction —
Then I'll laugh at your disaster; I'll mock when the thing you dread arrives —
when what you dread comes like a wreck, when your disaster arrives like a storm, when trouble and distress come down on you.
Then they'll call me and I won't answer; they'll search hard for me and won't find me —
because they hated knowledge and would not choose the fear of the LORD.
They wanted none of my counsel; they spurned every correction I gave.
So they'll eat the fruit of their own road and get their fill of their own schemes.
The naive are killed by their own turning away; the dullards are destroyed by their own complacency.
But whoever listens to me will live secure, at ease, with nothing to dread."

proverbs_2.t: My son, if you take in my sayings and keep my commandments by you,
turning your ear towards wisdom, bending your heart towards discernment;
if you actually call out for understanding and raise your voice for discernment;
if you go after her the way you'd go after silver, hunt for her like buried treasure,
then you'll understand what the fear of the LORD is, and you'll find the knowledge of God.
It's the LORD who gives wisdom; knowledge and discernment come out of his mouth.
He has sound sense stored up for the upright, a shield for those who walk with integrity,
keeping watch over the paths of justice, guarding the way of his godly ones.
Then you'll understand righteousness, justice and equity — every good course there is.
Wisdom will get into your heart, and knowledge will be a pleasure to you;
discretion will keep watch over you; discernment will guard you,
to get you clear of the way of evil, of anyone who talks perversity,
the ones who leave the paths of uprightness to walk the ways of darkness —
the ones who take pleasure in doing evil, who exult in evil's perversity —
people whose paths are twisted, who go crooked on their own tracks —
to get you clear of the forbidden woman, the adulteress with her smooth sayings,
the one who walks out on the companion of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of her God —
Her house sinks down towards death; her tracks run to the shades.
Nobody who goes in to her comes back; they never reach the paths of life.
So you'll walk the way of good people and keep to the paths of the righteous.
The upright will live in the land; the blameless will stay in it.
But the wicked will be cut off from the land; the treacherous will be torn out of it.

proverbs_3.t: My son, don't forget my law; let your heart hold on to my commandments —
They'll add length of days to you, years of life, and peace.
Don't let steadfast love and faithfulness leave you. Tie them round your neck; write them on the tablet of your heart.
You'll find favour and a good name with God and with people.
Trust the LORD with all your heart; don't lean on your own understanding.
Know him in everything you do, and he'll make your paths straight.
Don't be wise in your own eyes. Fear the LORD, and turn away from evil.
It'll be healing for your body, refreshment for your bones.
Honour the LORD with your wealth, with the first of everything you bring in,
and your storehouses will be filled to the top, your vats bursting with new wine.
My son, don't reject the LORD's discipline; don't come to loathe his correction —
The LORD corrects the one he loves, the way a father does with a son he delights in.
How blessed the person who finds wisdom, who comes into discernment!
What she yields beats what silver yields; what she brings in beats fine gold.
She's more precious than corals; nothing you want compares with her.
Length of days is in her right hand; wealth and honour in her left.
Her ways are pleasant ways; all her pathways are peace.
She's a tree of life to anyone who takes hold of her; anyone who keeps hold of her is called blessed.
The LORD founded the earth by wisdom; he set the heavens in place by discernment;
By his knowledge the deeps were split open, and the clouds drip down dew.
My son, don't let them out of your sight. Hold on to sound sense and discretion —
and they'll be life to you, something graceful at your throat.
Then you'll go your way secure, and your foot won't strike anything.
When you lie down, you won't be afraid; you'll lie down and sleep sweetly.
Don't be afraid of sudden terror, or the ruin that comes on the wicked when it comes —
The LORD will be what you rely on; he'll keep your foot from getting caught.
Don't hold good back from the people it belongs to when you have it in your power to act.
Don't say to your neighbour, "Go away and come back — I'll give it to you tomorrow" — when you have it right there.
Don't plot harm against your neighbour when he's living beside you, trusting you.
Don't pick a fight with anyone for no reason, if he hasn't done you any harm.
Don't envy a violent person; don't choose any of his ways.
The crooked person is an abomination to the LORD, but he takes the upright into his confidence.
The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses where the righteous live.
He mocks the mockers, but to the humble he gives favour.
The wise inherit honour; what dullards come away with is disgrace.

proverbs_4.t: Listen, children, to a father's discipline; pay attention, and you'll come to know understanding.
What I'm giving you is good learning. Don't walk away from my law.
I was a son to my father too — young and tender, my mother's only one.
He taught me. He said to me: "Let your heart hold on to my words. Keep my commandments and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. Don't forget; don't turn away from the sayings of my mouth.
Don't abandon her, and she'll keep you. Love her, and she'll guard you.
Here's where wisdom starts: get wisdom. Whatever else you get, get understanding.
Prize her, and she'll lift you up; she'll honour you when you hold her close.
She'll set a wreath of favour on your head, hand you a crown of beauty."
Listen, my son. Take in my sayings, and the years of your life will be many.
I've taught you the way of wisdom; I've led you along tracks of uprightness.
When you walk, nothing will cramp your step; if you run, you won't stumble.
Take hold of discipline and don't let go. Guard her — she is your life.
Don't set foot on the path of the wicked; don't walk the way of evil people.
Steer clear of it. Don't travel it. Turn off it and keep going.
They can't sleep unless they've done harm; their sleep is taken from them unless they've tripped someone up.
The bread they eat is wickedness; the wine they drink is violence.
The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, growing brighter and brighter till the day is full.
The way of the wicked is deep darkness; they've no idea what they're tripping over.
My son, pay attention to my words; turn your ear towards my sayings.
Don't let them out of your sight; keep them deep in your heart.
They're life to whoever finds them, health to the whole body.
Guard your heart above everything else you guard — everything that life comes from is in there.
Get rid of a crooked mouth; put devious lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight ahead; keep your gaze fixed right in front of you.
Make the track under your foot level, and all your ways will hold firm.
Don't turn aside to the right or the left. Turn your foot away from evil.

proverbs_5.t: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; turn your ear towards my discernment,
so you'll hold on to discretion and your lips will keep hold of knowledge.
The lips of the strange woman drip honey; her mouth is smoother than oil.
But in the end she's bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet are going down to death; her steps have hold of Sheol.
She doesn't level the path of life; her tracks wander and she doesn't know where.
So now, children, listen to me; don't turn away from the sayings of my mouth.
Keep your road well away from her; don't go near the door of her house —
or you'll hand your vigour over to others, your years to somebody cruel —
or strangers will get their fill of your strength and what you worked for will end up in a foreigner's house —
and at the end of it you'll groan, when your flesh and your body are wasting away,
and you'll say, "How I hated discipline! How my heart spurned reproof!
I didn't listen to my instructors; I never turned my ear towards my teachers.
I came to the brink of every kind of ruin, right there among the assembly and the congregation."
Drink water from your own cistern, running water from your own well.
Should your springs be running out into the street, your channels of water into the open squares?
Let them be yours — yours alone — not shared with strangers.
Let your spring be blessed; find your joy in the wife of your youth —
a loving doe, a graceful mountain goat. Let her breasts satisfy you always; let her love keep you intoxicated.
So why go astray, my son, with a strange woman? Why hold a foreign woman close?
A man's ways are right in front of the LORD's eyes; he measures out every track he takes.
The wicked man's own iniquities will catch him; the cords of his own sin will hold him fast.
He'll die for lack of discipline, lost in the sheer size of his own folly.

proverbs_6.t: My son, if you've gone surety for your neighbour, if you've shaken on it for a stranger —
you've been snared by the sayings of your own mouth; you've been caught by the sayings of your own mouth.
So do this, my son, and get yourself free, since you've fallen into your neighbour's hands: go, humble yourself, and press him hard.
Don't give your eyes any sleep, your eyelids any slumber.
Get yourself free like a gazelle from the hand, like a bird out of the fowler's hand.
Go to the ant, sluggard. Have a look at her ways and get wise.
She has no commander, no officer, no ruler —
yet she gets her bread ready in the summer, gathers her food at harvest.
How long are you going to lie there, sluggard? When are you going to get up?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest —
and poverty will show up like a traveller, your want like an armed man.
A worthless person, a man of wickedness, goes about with a crooked mouth —
winking his eyes, scuffing his feet, pointing with his fingers —
perversity in his heart, always plotting evil, sowing quarrels wherever he goes.
So his disaster will come on him suddenly; in an instant he'll be broken, past healing.
There are six things the LORD hates — seven that are an abomination to him:
haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
a heart that plots wickedness, feet in a hurry to run to evil,
a false witness breathing out lies, and anyone who stirs up quarrels between brothers.
Keep your father's commandment, my son; don't forsake what your mother teaches you.
Bind them on your heart, always; tie them round your neck.
When you walk, it'll guide you; when you lie down, it'll watch over you; and when you wake, it'll speak with you.
The commandment is a lamp; the law is a light; the reproofs of discipline are a way of life —
to keep you clear of the evil woman, of the foreign woman's smooth tongue.
Don't let your heart desire her beauty; don't let her capture you with a glance.
A prostitute will cost you a loaf of bread; but another man's wife hunts down a life worth having.
Can a man scoop fire into his lap and not burn his clothes?
Can a man walk on burning coals and not scorch his feet?
That's how it is with the man who goes in to his neighbour's wife: no one who touches her gets off.
People don't despise a thief who steals just to fill his stomach when he's hungry;
but if he's caught he pays back sevenfold — he hands over everything his house is worth.
The man who commits adultery with a woman has no sense; whoever does it destroys himself.
What he'll find is a wound and disgrace, and his reproach won't be wiped away.
Jealousy rouses a man's rage, and he'll show no mercy on the day of vengeance.
He won't take any ransom; he won't agree, however big the bribe.

proverbs_7.t: My son, keep my sayings; store my commandments up inside you.
Keep my commandments and live; guard my law like the pupil of your eye.
Bind them on your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom, "You're my sister," and call understanding your kin —
to keep you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman and her smooth sayings.
I was at the window of my house, looking down through the lattice,
and I saw, among the naive — I picked out among the young men a youth with no sense —
going along the street by her corner, striding down the road towards her house,
at twilight, at the close of day, in the deep of night and darkness.
And there she was, a woman coming to meet him, dressed like a prostitute, her heart under guard.
She's loud and rebellious; her feet won't stay at home.
One moment in the street, the next in the open squares, lurking beside every corner.
She grabs hold of him and kisses him; brazen-faced, she says to him:
"I had peace offerings to make; today I paid my vows.
That's why I came out to meet you, to look for you — and here you are.
I've spread coverings on my couch, coloured fabrics, Egyptian linen.
I've sprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
Come on — let's drink our fill of love till morning; let's take our delight in love.
My husband isn't at home; he's gone away on a long journey.
He took the money bag with him; he won't be home till the full moon."
She wins him over with all her persuading; with her smooth lips she drives him on.
He goes after her, just like that — an ox walking to the slaughter, a stag caught fast in a fetter —
till an arrow goes through its liver — like a bird rushing into a trap, not knowing it will cost him his life.
So now, children, listen to me; pay attention to the sayings of my mouth.
Don't let your heart turn aside to her ways; don't wander off into her pathways.
She has brought many down; the ones she has killed are past counting.
Her house is the road to Sheol, going down to the chambers of death.

proverbs_8.t: Doesn't wisdom call out? Doesn't discernment raise her voice?
At the top of the heights, beside the road, where the paths meet, she takes her stand.
By the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the entrance to the doorways, she cries out:
"It's you I'm calling, all of you; my voice goes out to everyone alive.
You naive ones, get some shrewdness; you dullards, get some sense.
Listen — what I speak is noble; what my lips open with is equity.
My mouth speaks truth; wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness; there's nothing twisted or crooked in it.
They're all plain to anyone who discerns, straight to anyone who finds knowledge.
Take my discipline instead of silver, knowledge rather than choice gold.
Wisdom is better than corals; nothing you could want compares with her.
I, wisdom, live with shrewdness; I have knowledge and discretion at hand.
The fear of the LORD is hating evil. Pride, arrogance, the way of evil, a mouth full of perversity — I hate them all.
Counsel is mine, and sound sense; I am understanding; strength is mine.
It's by me that kings reign and rulers decree righteousness;
by me princes rule, and nobles — everyone who judges righteously.
I love the ones who love me; those who search hard for me find me.
Wealth and honour are with me, lasting wealth, and righteousness.
What I bear is better than fine gold, better than pure gold; what I yield beats choice silver.
I walk the path of righteousness, right down the middle of the pathways of justice,
handing on real substance to those who love me, filling their treasuries.
The LORD brought me forth at the beginning of his way, before his works, from of old.
From long ago I was set in place, from the beginning, before the earth ever was.
When there were no deeps, I was brought forth; when there were no springs heavy with water.
Before the mountains were sunk into place, before the hills, I was brought forth —
while he still hadn't made the earth and its open spaces, nor the first grains of the world's dust.
When he set the heavens in place, I was there; when he marked out a circle on the face of the deep,
when he made the clouds firm above, when the springs of the deep grew strong,
when he set the sea its limit, so the waters wouldn't overstep what he said, when he marked out the foundations of the earth —
then I was beside him, a master craftsman, his delight day after day, playing in front of him always,
playing in the world he made, taking my delight in the people who live in it.
So now, children, listen to me: how blessed are the ones who keep my ways!
Listen to discipline and be wise; don't let it go.
How blessed is the person who listens to me, watching at my doors day after day, keeping watch at my doorposts!
Whoever finds me finds life and wins favour from the LORD;
but whoever misses me does himself violence; everyone who hates me is in love with death."

proverbs_9.t: Wisdom has built her house; she has cut out her seven pillars.
She's butchered her meat, mixed her wine, and set her table.
She's sent out her young women; she calls from the high points of the town:
"Anyone who's naive, turn in here!" To anyone with no sense she says:
"Come and eat my bread; drink the wine I've mixed.
Leave being naive behind and live; walk straight on in the way of understanding."
Correct a mocker and you take disgrace on yourself; reprove a wicked person and you pick up a blemish.
Don't reprove a mocker — he'll hate you for it. Reprove a wise person, and he'll love you.
Give to a wise person and he gets wiser still; teach a righteous one and he learns more.
Wisdom starts with the fear of the LORD; knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
By me your days will be many; years of life will be added to you.
If you're wise, you're wise for your own sake; if you mock, you'll bear it on your own.
The woman Dullness is loud — nothing but naivety, and she knows nothing at all.
She sits at the doorway of her own house, on a seat at the high points of the town,
calling out to people going by on the road, people going straight on their way:
"Anyone who's naive, turn in here!" And to anyone with no sense she says:
"Stolen water is sweet; bread eaten in secret is a pleasure."
And he doesn't know the shades are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.

proverbs_10.t: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes his father glad; a dull son is his mother's grief.
Treasures got by wickedness are no use; righteousness delivers from death.
The LORD won't let the righteous go hungry, but he pushes aside what the wicked crave.
A slack hand leaves you poor; the hand of the diligent makes you rich.
A son who gathers in summer has insight; a son who sleeps through harvest brings shame.
Blessings rest on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing; the name of the wicked rots.
Someone wise at heart takes in commandments; a babbling fool comes to ruin.
Walk in integrity and you walk secure; make your ways crooked and you'll be found out.
Winking an eye causes pain; a babbling fool comes to ruin.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life; the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
Hatred stirs up quarrels; love covers over every transgression.
Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning; a rod is for the back of someone with no sense.
The wise store knowledge up; a fool's mouth is ruin waiting to happen.
The wealth of the rich is their fortified town; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
What the righteous earn leads to life; what the wicked bring in leads to sin.
Keep discipline and you're a path to life; abandon reproof and you lead others astray.
Cover up hatred and your lips are lying; spread slander and you're a dullard.
Where there are many words, transgression doesn't stop; restrain your lips and you act with insight.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth next to nothing.
The lips of the righteous feed many; fools die for want of sense.
It's the LORD's blessing that makes rich, and he adds no sorrow to it.
A dullard treats depravity as sport; a person of discernment treats wisdom that way.
What the wicked dreads will come to him; what the righteous desire will be granted.
When the storm passes, the wicked is gone; the righteous is a foundation that lasts.
Like vinegar on the teeth, like smoke in the eyes — that's what the sluggard is to whoever sends him.
The fear of the LORD adds days; the years of the wicked are cut short.
What the righteous expect is joy; what the wicked hope for comes to nothing.
The way of the LORD is a stronghold for the blameless, but ruin for those who do wickedness.
The righteous will never be shaken; the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous bears wisdom like fruit; a perverse tongue gets cut off.
The lips of the righteous know what will be received; the mouth of the wicked is perversity.

proverbs_11.t: Crooked scales are an abomination to the LORD; an accurate weight is his delight.
Insolence arrives and disgrace arrives with it; but wisdom is with the modest.
The integrity of the upright guides them; the distortion of the treacherous destroys them.
Wealth is no use on the day of fury; righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless makes his way straight; the wicked falls by his own wickedness.
The righteousness of the upright delivers them; the treacherous are caught by what they crave.
When a wicked person dies, hope is lost; whatever he expected from his own strength perishes.
The righteous is pulled out of distress, and the wicked takes his place.
The godless ruins his neighbour with his mouth; the righteous are delivered by knowledge.
When things go well for the righteous, the town rejoices; when the wicked perish, there's a shout of joy.
The blessing of the upright lifts a town up; the mouth of the wicked tears it down.
Despise your neighbour and you lack sense; a person of discernment keeps quiet.
A talebearer goes about revealing confidences; someone faithful in spirit keeps a matter quiet.
With no guidance a people falls; with many counsellors there's deliverance.
Go surety for a stranger and you'll suffer for it; hate striking hands on a deal and you're secure.
A gracious woman gets hold of honour; the ruthless get hold of wealth.
A loyal person does himself good; a cruel one brings trouble on his own body.
The wicked earns wages that are a lie; sow righteousness and the wage is real.
Righteousness leads to life; chase after evil and you go to your own death.
The perverse of heart are an abomination to the LORD; those blameless in their way are his delight.
Depend on it — the evil won't go unpunished; the offspring of the righteous will be delivered.
A gold ring in a pig's snout — that's a beautiful woman who has turned from discretion.
What the righteous desire is only good; what the wicked hope for is fury.
One person scatters and gains still more; another holds back what is due and ends in want.
A generous person will be enriched; whoever gives water will be given water himself.
People curse the one who holds grain back; a blessing rests on the head of the one who sells.
Seek good in earnest and you seek favour; search out evil and it will come to you.
Trust in your wealth and you'll fall; the righteous flourish like green leaves.
Trouble your own household and you'll inherit wind; a fool ends up servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; the wise wins people over.
Look — the righteous gets what's due on this earth; how much more the wicked and the sinner!

proverbs_12.t: Love discipline and you love knowledge; hate reproof and you're a brute.
A good person wins favour from the LORD; a man of schemes he condemns.
Nobody is established by wickedness; the root of the righteous won't be moved.
A capable wife is her husband's crown; one who acts shamefully is rot in his bones.
What the righteous plan is justice; what the wicked counsel is deceit.
The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood; the mouth of the upright delivers people.
Overthrow the wicked and they're gone; the house of the righteous stands.
A person is praised for the insight he has; the perverted of heart is held in contempt.
Better to be thought little of and have a servant than to give yourself airs and go hungry.
The righteous knows what his animal needs; the compassion of the wicked is cruel.
Work your ground and you'll have plenty of food; chase worthless things and you lack sense.
The wicked covets what evil men have taken; the root of the righteous yields.
A person's own lip-transgression is an evil snare; the righteous comes out of trouble.
The fruit of your own mouth fills you with good; what your hands have dealt out comes back to you.
A fool's way is right in his own eyes; listen to counsel and you're wise.
A fool's annoyance is known the same day; the shrewd person covers an insult over.
Breathe out faithfulness and you declare what's right; a false witness declares deceit.
Some people's rash talk is like sword thrusts; the tongue of the wise heals.
Truthful lips last for ever; a lying tongue only for a moment.
Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil; those who counsel peace have joy.
No trouble befalls the righteous; the wicked are full of distress.
Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD; those who act in faithfulness are his delight.
A shrewd person keeps knowledge to himself; the heart of dullards shouts out folly.
The hand of the diligent rules; slackness ends in forced labour.
Anxiety in the heart weighs it down; a good word makes it glad.
The righteous shows his neighbour the way; the way of the wicked leads them astray.
The slack man never roasts what he catches; the diligent person's wealth is precious.
Life is in the path of righteousness; along that pathway there is no death.

proverbs_13.t: A wise son takes a father's discipline; a mocker won't listen to a rebuke.
You eat good from the fruit of your own mouth; what the treacherous have an appetite for is violence.
Guard your mouth and you keep your life; fling your lips open and ruin is yours.
The sluggard craves and gets nothing; the appetite of the diligent is well fed.
The righteous hates a lying word; the wicked makes himself stink and comes to shame.
Righteousness guards the one whose way is blameless; wickedness overthrows the sinner.
One person plays rich and has nothing; another plays poor and has great wealth.
Wealth is the ransom for a person's life; a poor person never even hears the threat.
The light of the righteous burns bright; the lamp of the wicked is put out.
Insolence brings nothing but quarrels; wisdom is with those who take counsel.
Wealth that comes out of nowhere dwindles; gather it a handful at a time and it grows.
Hope drawn out makes the heart sick; a desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
Despise a word and it holds you in pledge; fear a commandment and you'll be rewarded.
The law of the wise is a fountain of life, turning you aside from the snares of death.
Good insight wins favour; the way of the treacherous is their undoing.
Every shrewd person acts with knowledge; a dullard spreads his folly out for display.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble; a faithful envoy brings healing.
Let discipline go and you get poverty and disgrace; keep reproof and you'll be honoured.
A desire fulfilled is a pleasure; turning away from evil is an abomination to dullards.
Walk with the wise and you become wise; keep company with dullards and you'll be harmed.
Calamity chases sinners down; the righteous are repaid with good.
A good person leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren; a sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.
There's plenty of food in the fallow ground of the poor, but some of it is swept away because there's no justice.
Hold back your rod and you hate your son; love him and you're diligent to discipline him.
The righteous eats his fill; the belly of the wicked goes empty.

proverbs_14.t: The wisest of women builds her house; folly pulls it down with her own hands.
Walk in uprightness and you fear the LORD; be crooked in your ways and you despise him.
In a fool's mouth is a rod of pride; the lips of the wise keep them safe.
With no cattle the manger stays clean; but it's the ox's strength that brings in the crop.
A faithful witness doesn't lie; a false witness breathes out lies.
A mocker looks for wisdom and finds none; knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Get away from a dull person — you'll find no lips of knowledge there.
The wisdom of the shrewd is understanding his own way; the folly of dullards is deceit.
Fools make a mockery of the guilt offering; among the upright there is favour.
The heart knows its own bitterness; no stranger shares its joy.
The house of the wicked is destroyed; the tent of the upright flourishes.
There's a way that looks right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
Even in laughter the heart can ache, and that joy ends in grief.
Whoever's heart has turned back gets his fill of his own ways; a good man gets his fill of what is his.
A naive person believes anything; a shrewd one watches where he puts his foot.
A wise person is afraid and turns away from evil; a dullard storms ahead, sure of himself.
Quick to anger, quick to folly; a man of schemes is hated.
The naive inherit folly; the shrewd are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow down before the good, the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Even his neighbour hates the poor man; the rich have friends by the dozen.
Despise your neighbour and you sin; how blessed is the one who shows favour to the humble!
Don't those who plot evil go astray? Loyalty and faithfulness belong to those who plot good.
There's profit in every kind of hard labour; mere talk leads only to want.
The crown of the wise is their wealth; the folly of dullards is just folly.
A truthful witness saves lives; someone breathing out lies deals in deceit.
In the fear of the LORD there's strong confidence, and his children have a refuge.
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning you aside from the snares of death.
A king's glory is in a multitude of people; without people, a ruler is ruined.
Slow to anger, deep in discernment; short of temper, and folly is what you raise up.
A tranquil heart gives the body life; jealousy is rot in the bones.
Oppress the poor and you reproach his Maker; show favour to the needy and you honour him.
The wicked is thrust down by his own evil; the righteous finds refuge even in his death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, and even among dullards it makes itself known.
Righteousness lifts a nation up; sin is a disgrace to any people.
A king's favour goes to a servant with insight; his fury goes to one who brings shame.

proverbs_15.t: A soft answer turns rage away; a hurtful word stirs anger up.
The tongue of the wise makes knowledge attractive; the mouth of dullards pours out folly.
The eyes of the LORD are in every place, watching the evil and the good.
A healing tongue is a tree of life; twisted words break the spirit.
A fool spurns his father's discipline; keep reproof and you're shrewd.
There's great store in the house of the righteous; the income of the wicked brings trouble.
The lips of the wise scatter knowledge; the heart of dullards does no such thing.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD; the prayer of the upright is his delight.
The way of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD; he loves the one who pursues righteousness.
Forsake the path and harsh discipline awaits you; hate reproof and you die.
Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD — how much more the hearts of human beings.
A mocker doesn't like being reproved; he won't go near the wise.
A joyful heart brightens the face; sorrow of heart leaves the spirit stricken.
A discerning heart looks for knowledge; the mouth of dullards grazes on folly.
Every day of the afflicted is wretched; a cheerful heart keeps a feast all the time.
Better a little with the fear of the LORD than a great treasure with turmoil along with it.
Better a dish of greens where there's love than a fattened ox with hatred alongside.
A hot-tempered man stirs up strife; someone slow to anger quiets a dispute.
The sluggard's way is a thorn hedge; the path of the upright is a raised road.
A wise son makes his father glad; a dullard despises his mother.
Folly delights someone with no sense; a person of discernment walks straight ahead.
Plans fall apart where there's no counsel; with many counsellors they stand.
There's joy in giving the right answer, and a word at the right time — how good that is!
The path of life runs upward for the one with insight, turning him away from Sheol beneath.
The LORD pulls down the house of the proud, but he sets a widow's boundary firm.
The plans of an evil person are an abomination to the LORD; sayings of kindness are pure.
Take unjust gain and you trouble your own house; hate bribes and you'll live.
The heart of the righteous weighs its answer; the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked; he hears the prayer of the righteous.
Light in the eyes makes the heart glad; good news puts fat on the bones.
An ear that listens to life-giving reproof will lodge among the wise.
Let discipline go and you reject yourself; heed reproof and you gain sense.
The fear of the LORD is the discipline of wisdom; humility comes before honour.

proverbs_16.t: A person arranges things in his heart; but the answer on the tongue comes from the LORD.
Every one of a person's ways is pure in his own eyes; the LORD weighs the spirits.
Roll what you do onto the LORD, and your plans will stand.
The LORD made everything for its own purpose — even the wicked, for a day of calamity.
Everyone haughty of heart is an abomination to the LORD; depend on it — he won't go unpunished.
Loyalty and faithfulness atone for iniquity; the fear of the LORD turns you away from evil.
When the LORD is pleased with someone's ways, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him.
Better a little with righteousness than great gains got without justice.
A person's heart plans his way; the LORD directs his steps.
There's an oracle on a king's lips; in judgement his mouth doesn't break faith.
Honest balance and scales belong to the LORD; every weight in the bag is his work.
Doing wickedness is an abomination to kings; a throne is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are a king's delight; he loves whoever speaks what's upright.
A king's rage is a death sentence; a wise person appeases it.
There's life in the light of a king's face; his favour is like a cloud bringing spring rain.
Getting wisdom — how much better than fine gold! Getting understanding beats silver.
The highway of the upright turns away from evil; guard your way and you keep your life.
Pride comes before a fall; haughtiness of spirit before a stumble.
Better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide plunder with the proud.
Pay attention to a word and you'll find good; how blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD!
The wise of heart get called discerning; sweet speech makes learning grow.
Insight is a fountain of life to whoever has it; the discipline fools give is folly.
The heart of the wise puts insight in his mouth and adds learning to his lips.
Sayings of kindness are a honeycomb — sweet to the taste, healing to the bones.
There's a way that looks right to a person, but its end is the ways of death.
A labourer's own appetite works for him; his mouth drives him on.
A worthless person digs evil up; there's a scorching fire on his lips.
A perverse person sets quarrels loose; a slanderer separates close friends.
A violent man talks his neighbour round and leads him down a way that is not good.
The man who shuts his eyes is plotting perversity; the man who purses his lips has already done the evil.
Grey hair is a crown of splendour, found in the way of righteousness.
Better slow to anger than a warrior; better to rule your own spirit than to take a city.
The lot is thrown into the lap, but every decision it gives comes from the LORD.

proverbs_17.t: Better a dry crust with quiet than a house full of feasting and strife.
A servant with insight will rule over a son who brings shame, and share the inheritance with the brothers.
