A crucible for silver, a furnace for gold — but the LORD tests hearts.
An evildoer listens to wicked lips; a liar gives ear to a destroying tongue.
Mock the poor and you reproach his Maker; be glad at calamity and you won't go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the old; parents are the splendour of their children.
Fine talk doesn't suit a boor — and lying talk suits a noble even less.
A bribe looks like a lucky stone to the one who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.
Cover over a transgression and you're seeking love; repeat a matter and you separate close friends.
A rebuke sinks deeper into a person who understands than a hundred blows into a dullard.
An evil person is out for nothing but rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Better to run into a bear robbed of her cubs than a dullard in his folly.
Return evil for good, and evil won't leave your house.
Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam; walk away from the dispute before it breaks out.
Justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous — the LORD abominates both alike.
What's the use of money in a dullard's hand to buy wisdom, when he has no sense for it?
A friend loves at all times; a brother is born for adversity.
Someone with no sense shakes on it, standing surety in front of his neighbour.
Love transgression and you love contention; build your gateway high and you're asking for a fall.
The twisted of heart finds no good; the perverted of tongue falls into trouble.
Have a dullard for a son and you have grief; the father of a boor gets no joy from him.
A joyful heart does you good like medicine; a stricken spirit dries the bones up.
A wicked person takes a bribe out of the fold of a garment to bend the paths of judgement.
Wisdom is right in front of the person who understands; a dullard's eyes are off at the ends of the earth.
A dull son is a vexation to his father, bitterness to the woman who bore him.
Fining the righteous is not good, and neither is striking nobles for being upright.
Restrain your sayings and you know knowledge; someone of a rare spirit is a person of discernment.
Even a fool is reckoned wise if he keeps quiet; shut your lips and you pass for discerning.

proverbs_18.t: The person who cuts himself off is after his own desire; he rages against all sound sense.
A dullard takes no pleasure in discernment — only in airing what's in his own heart.
When the wicked arrive, so does contempt, and with disgrace comes reproach.
The words of a person's mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a running stream.
Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, and neither is pushing the righteous aside in judgement.
A dullard's lips walk him into strife; his mouth calls out for a beating.
A dullard's mouth is his ruin; his lips are a snare on his own life.
A slanderer's words go down like delicacies, right into the inner chambers of the belly.
Someone slack in his work is brother to a destroyer.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous runs into it and is set safe on high.
The wealth of the rich is their fortified town, a high wall — in their own imagination.
Before a fall a person's heart grows haughty; humility comes before honour.
Answer before you've listened, and it's folly on your part, and ignominy.
A person's spirit will carry him through sickness; but a stricken spirit — who can bear that?
A discerning heart takes knowledge in; the ear of the wise goes looking for it.
A gift makes room for the one who brings it and gets him in front of the great.
The first to state his case sounds right — until the other party comes and cross-examines him.
The lot puts an end to quarrels and parts powerful opponents.
A wronged brother is harder to win over than a fortified town; quarrels are like the bar across a fortress gate.
The fruit of your own mouth fills your belly; the produce of your lips fills you up.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
Find a wife and you've found a good thing; you win favour from the LORD.
A poor person pleads; a rich one answers roughly.
Having many companions can break a person; but there's a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

proverbs_19.t: Better a poor person walking in integrity than someone with perverse speech who is a dullard.
Being without knowledge is not good, and hurrying your feet makes you miss the way.
A person's own folly wrecks his way, and then his heart rages against the LORD.
Wealth brings friends in numbers; a poor person is cut off even from the friend he has.
A false witness won't go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies won't escape.
Many court a noble's favour; everyone is friend to a man with gifts to give.
All a poor man's brothers hate him — how much further off his friends keep! He goes chasing sayings; they are his.
Get sense and you love yourself; keep discernment and you'll find good.
A false witness won't go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will perish.
Luxury doesn't suit a dullard — and a servant ruling over princes suits even less.
Insight makes a person slow to anger; it's his splendour to let a transgression pass.
A king's rage is a lion's roar; his favour is dew on the grass.
A dull son is his father's ruin; a wife's quarrelling is a roof that never stops dripping.
House and wealth you inherit from your parents; a prudent wife comes from the LORD.
Laziness drops you into deep sleep; a slack person goes hungry.
Keep a commandment and you keep your life; despise your ways and you die.
Show favour to the poor and you lend to the LORD; he'll repay you what's due.
Discipline your son while there's hope, but don't set your heart on killing him.
A man of great rage pays the penalty; rescue him once and you'll be doing it again.
Listen to counsel; take discipline, so you'll be wise at the end of it.
There are many plans in a person's heart, but it's the counsel of the LORD that stands.
What people want in a person is steadfast love; better to be poor than a liar.
The fear of the LORD leads to life; you rest satisfied, and harm doesn't come near.
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish and won't even bring it back to his mouth.
Strike a mocker and the naive get shrewder; reprove a discerning person and he understands knowledge.
Assault your father, drive out your mother, and you're a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Stop listening to discipline, my son, and you'll stray from the sayings of knowledge.
A worthless witness makes a mockery of justice; the mouth of the wicked swallows wickedness down.
Judgements are ready for mockers, and blows for the backs of dullards.

proverbs_20.t: Wine is a mocker; strong drink is a brawler. Nobody who staggers under it is wise.
A king's terror is a lion's roar; enrage him and you forfeit your life.
It's an honour to keep clear of strife; every fool bursts out into it.
When winter's on, the sluggard won't plough; at harvest he asks, and there's nothing.
Counsel in a person's heart is deep water; someone with discernment draws it up.
Plenty of people proclaim their own loyalty; but a faithful person — who can find one?
The righteous walks about in his integrity — how blessed his children are after him!
A king on the throne of judgement winnows out all evil with his eyes.
Who can say, "I've kept my heart pure; I'm pure from my sin"?
One weight for buying and another for selling, one measure and another — the LORD abominates both alike.
Even a child shows what he is by what he does — whether his conduct is pure and upright.
An ear that hears and an eye that sees — the LORD made them both.
Don't love sleep, or you'll end up poor; open your eyes and you'll have plenty of food.
"Bad, bad," says the buyer — and once he's off, then he boasts.
Gold there is, and corals in plenty; but lips of knowledge are the precious thing.
Take the coat of anyone who's gone surety for a stranger; hold it in pledge on a foreign woman's account.
Bread got by lying tastes sweet; afterwards your mouth is full of gravel.
Plans are established by counsel; wage war with good guidance.
A talebearer goes about uncovering confidences; so don't get involved with anyone whose lips are always open.
Curse your father or your mother and your lamp goes out in deep darkness.
An inheritance grabbed at the start won't be blessed at the end.
Don't say, "I'll pay back the evil." Wait for the LORD, and he'll deliver you.
Two kinds of weight are an abomination to the LORD; deceitful scales are not good.
A man's steps come from the LORD; so how can anyone understand his own way?
It's a snare to blurt out "It's holy!" and only start weighing the vows afterwards.
A wise king winnows out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
A human being's breath is the LORD's lamp, searching every chamber of the belly.
Loyalty and faithfulness keep a king safe; he holds his throne up by loyalty.
The splendour of young men is their strength; the honour of the old is grey hair.
Bruising wounds scour evil away; blows reach the innermost chambers.

proverbs_21.t: A king's heart is a channel of water in the LORD's hand; he turns it wherever he wants.
Every way a person takes is upright in his own eyes; the LORD weighs hearts.
Doing righteousness and justice is what the LORD chooses over sacrifice.
Haughty eyes, an arrogant heart — what the wicked cultivate is sin.
The plans of the diligent lead only to gain; haste leads only to want.
Getting treasures by a lying tongue is vapour blown away — and a hunt for death.
The violence of the wicked will drag them off, because they refuse to do justice.
A guilty person's way is crooked; the pure — his work is upright.
Better to live up on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
A wicked person's appetite craves evil; his neighbour gets no mercy from him.
Punish a mocker and the naive get wiser; instruct a wise person and he takes in knowledge.
The Righteous One takes note of the wicked man's house and brings the wicked down to calamity.
Shut your ear to the cry of the poor, and you'll call out yourself and get no answer.
A gift given in secret subdues anger; a bribe slipped into the fold of a garment, strong rage.
Doing justice is a joy to the righteous; it's ruin to those who do wickedness.
Wander off the way of insight and you'll come to rest among the shades.
Love pleasure and you'll end in want; love wine and oil and you won't grow rich.
The wicked ends up a ransom for the righteous; the treacherous take the place of the upright.
Better to live out in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome, vexing wife.
Treasure worth having, and oil, are in the dwelling of the wise; a dullard swallows it all up.
Pursue righteousness and loyalty and you find life, righteousness and honour.
A wise person storms a city full of warriors and brings down the stronghold it trusted in.
Guard your mouth and your tongue and you keep yourself out of trouble.
Proud, arrogant — "Mocker" is what he's called, someone who acts in an overflow of insolence.
A sluggard's own desire kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
All day long he's craving; the righteous gives and doesn't hold back.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination — how much more when he brings it with depravity!
A lying witness will perish; someone who has listened will speak on and be heard.
A wicked person brazens it out; an upright one gives thought to his way.
No wisdom, no discernment, no counsel can stand against the LORD.
The horse is got ready for the day of battle, but deliverance belongs to the LORD.

proverbs_22.t: A good name is worth more than great wealth, favour more than silver and gold.
Rich and poor meet together; the LORD made them all.
A shrewd person sees trouble coming and takes cover; the naive walk on and pay for it.
What comes of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth and honour and life.
Thorns and snares lie on the way of the perverse; guard yourself and you keep well clear.
Train a youth in the way he should go, and even when he's old he won't turn from it.
The rich rule over the poor; the borrower is servant to the lender.
Sow unrighteousness and you reap trouble; the rod of your fury comes to an end.
The generous will be blessed, because he shares his bread with the poor.
Drive the mocker out and strife goes with him; dispute and disgrace stop.
Love purity of heart, have grace on your lips, and the king will be your friend.
The eyes of the LORD keep watch over knowledge; he overturns the words of the treacherous.
The sluggard says, "There's a lion out there! I'll be murdered in the open squares!"
The mouth of the strange woman is a deep pit; anyone the LORD has cursed falls into it.
Folly is bound up in a young heart; the rod of discipline drives it far away.
Oppress the poor to get more for yourself, give to the rich — and you come only to want.
The Words of the Wise Turn your ear and hear the words of the wise; set your heart on what I know;
It's a pleasure to keep them inside you, to have them ready together on your lips.
so your trust will be in the LORD, I've made it known to you today — to you.
Haven't I written you thirty of them, full of counsel and knowledge,
to let you know the truth of faithful sayings, so you can bring back faithful sayings to whoever sends you?
Don't rob the poor just because he's poor; don't crush the afflicted at the gate.
The LORD will take up their case and rob the life of those who rob them.
Don't make friends with a hot-tempered man; don't go about with a man of rages —
or you'll learn his ways and take a snare on yourself.
Don't be one of those who shake on it, one of those who go surety for debts.
If you've nothing to pay with, why should your bed be taken out from under you?
Don't move an ancient boundary marker that your ancestors set up.
See someone skilled at his work? He'll stand before kings; he won't be standing before nobodies.

proverbs_23.t: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, look hard at what's in front of you,
and put a knife to your own throat if you have a big appetite.
Don't crave his dainties; that food is a deception.
Don't wear yourself out getting rich; have the sense to stop.
Set your eyes on it and it's gone — it makes itself wings and flies off to the sky like an eagle.
Don't eat the food of a stingy man; don't crave his dainties,
He's working it out inside all the while. "Eat and drink," he says to you, but his heart isn't with you.
The morsel you ate you'll bring back up, and your pleasant words will have gone for nothing.
Don't speak in a dullard's ears; he'll only despise the insight in what you say.
Don't move an ancient boundary; don't go into the fields of the fatherless,
Their Redeemer is strong; he'll take up their case against you.
Bring your heart to discipline, your ears to sayings of knowledge.
Don't withhold discipline from a young person; strike him with the rod and he won't die.
You strike him with the rod and you deliver his life from Sheol.
My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will be glad —
and everything in me will exult when your lips speak what's upright.
Don't let your heart envy sinners; stay in the fear of the LORD all day long —
there is a future, for certain, and your hope won't be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise; keep your heart going straight on the way.
Don't be one of those who drink wine deep, one of those who gorge on meat —
the deep drinker and the glutton end up poor, and drowsiness dresses you in rags.
Listen to the father who begot you, and don't despise your mother when she's old.
Buy truth; don't sell it — wisdom, discipline and understanding.
The father of a righteous son rejoices greatly; whoever begets a wise son rejoices in him.
Let your father and mother rejoice; let the woman who bore you be glad.
Give me your heart, my son; let your eyes hold to my ways.
A prostitute is a deep pit; a foreign woman is a narrow well.
She lies in wait like a robber and multiplies the treacherous among people.
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for nothing? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Those who sit late over wine, who go looking for the mixed bowl.
Don't look at wine when it's red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a snake, stings like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange things; your heart will speak perversity.
You'll be like someone lying out in the middle of the sea, like someone lying at the top of a mast.
"They hit me — I felt nothing. They beat me — I never knew. When do I wake up? I'll go looking for another."

proverbs_24.t: Don't envy evil people; don't want to be with them —
their hearts plot violence, and their lips talk trouble.
A house is built by wisdom and established by discernment;
and by knowledge its rooms fill up with every precious and pleasant thing.
A wise man is strong; a person of knowledge makes his strength greater.
You wage war by good guidance, and deliverance lies in many counsellors.
Wisdom is out of a fool's reach; at the gate he has nothing to say.
Anyone who plans to do evil gets called a master of schemes.
Folly's scheming is sin; a mocker is an abomination to people.
Go slack on the day of trouble and your strength is small indeed.
Deliver those being led off to death; hold back those staggering to the slaughter.
If you say, "But we didn't know" — doesn't the one who weighs hearts see it? Doesn't the one who guards your life know? He repays each person according to what they have done.
Eat honey, my son — it's good; honey from the comb is sweet on the tongue.
So know wisdom for yourself: find it, and there's a future; your hope won't be cut off.
Don't lie in wait, wicked one, at the home of the righteous; don't wreck the place where he rests —
The righteous falls seven times and gets up; the wicked stumble into calamity.
When your enemy falls, don't rejoice; when he stumbles, don't let your heart be glad —
or the LORD will see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
Don't work yourself up over evildoers; don't envy the wicked —
The evil person has no future; the lamp of the wicked is put out.
Fear the LORD, my son, and the king; don't get mixed up with people who change sides —
Their calamity comes up suddenly — and who knows what ruin the two of them can bring?
These too are from the wise. Showing partiality in judgement is not good.
Say to the wicked, "You're in the right," and peoples will curse you, nations denounce you.
But it goes well for those who reprove, and a rich blessing comes on them.
A straight answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Get your work ready outside, have it ready for yourself in the field; after that, build your house.
Don't be a witness against your neighbour for no reason; don't use your lips to deceive.
Don't say, "I'll do to him what he did to me; I'll repay him for what he's done."
I went past a lazy man's field, past the vineyard of someone with no sense,
and there it was, all grown over with thorns, the ground covered with nettles, the stone wall broken down.
I looked, and I took it to heart; I saw, and I accepted the instruction.
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest —
and poverty will come walking in, your want like an armed man.

proverbs_25.t: These too are proverbs of Solomon, copied out by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah.
It's the glory of God to conceal a matter, the glory of kings to search one out.
The heavens for height, the earth for depth, and the heart of kings — past searching out.
Take the dross out of silver and the smith gets a vessel out of it.
Take the wicked out of a king's presence and his throne is established in righteousness.
Don't put yourself forward in front of a king; don't stand where the great stand —
Better that he says to you, "Come up here," than that you're put lower in front of a noble you'd seen with your own eyes.
Don't rush into a lawsuit, because what will you do at the end of it when your neighbour shames you?
Take your case up with your neighbour himself; don't give away someone else's confidence —
or whoever hears will shame you, and what's said about you will never be undone.
Apples of gold in settings of silver — that's a word spoken at the right time.
A gold ring, an ornament of fine gold — that's a wise reprover to an ear that listens.
Like the cold of snow at harvest time is a faithful envoy to those who send him: he restores the life of his masters.
Clouds and wind and no rain — that's someone boasting about a gift he never gives.
Patience wins a ruler over; a soft tongue breaks a bone.
Found honey? Eat just your fill, or you'll have too much and bring it back up.
Don't wear out your welcome at your neighbour's house, or he'll have too much of you and hate you.
A war-club, a sword, a sharpened arrow — that's someone who bears false witness against his neighbour.
A broken tooth, a foot that gives way — that's what trusting a treacherous person is, on the day of trouble.
Taking someone's coat off on a cold day, pouring vinegar on soda — that's singing songs to a heavy heart.
If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; if he's thirsty, give him water to drink.
for you'll be heaping burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings rain; a tongue that works in secret brings angry faces.
Better to live up on a corner of the roof than share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
Cool water to someone worn out — that's good news from a far country.
A muddied spring, a ruined fountain — that's a righteous person giving way before the wicked.
Eating too much honey isn't good — and neither is hunting after your own glory.
A city broken open, its wall gone — that's someone with no control over his own spirit.

proverbs_26.t: Like snow in summer, like rain at harvest — that's how honour suits a dullard.
Like a bird flitting past, a swallow in flight — a curse without cause never lands.
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, a rod for the back of dullards.
Don't answer a dullard according to his folly, or you'll end up like him yourself.
Answer a dullard according to his folly, or he'll be wise in his own eyes.
Cutting off your own feet, drinking down violence — that's sending a message by a dullard's hand.
A lame man's legs hang useless — so does a proverb in a dullard's mouth.
Like tying a stone into a sling — that's giving honour to a dullard.
A thorn stuck in a drunkard's hand — so is a proverb in a dullard's mouth.
Like an archer shooting at random and hitting everyone — that's hiring a dullard, or hiring any passer-by.
Like a dog going back to its own vomit — that's a dullard repeating his folly.
See someone wise in his own eyes? There's more hope for a dullard than for him.
The sluggard says, "There's a lion in the road! A lion out in the open squares!"
A door turns on its hinge; a sluggard turns on his bed.
A sluggard buries his hand in the dish; he's too tired to bring it back to his mouth.
A sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who can give a discerning answer.
Grabbing a passing dog by the ears — that's meddling in a quarrel that isn't yours.
Like a madman shooting firebrands, arrows, death —
so is someone who deceives his neighbour and then says, "I was only joking!"
With no wood a fire goes out; with no slanderer, strife dies down.
Charcoal to embers, wood to a fire — that's a quarrelsome person kindling strife.
A slanderer's words go down like delicacies, right into the inner chambers of the belly.
A glaze of silver dross over a clay pot — that's warm words with an evil heart behind them.
A hater disguises himself with his lips and stores deceit up inside.
When his voice turns gracious, don't trust him; there are seven abominations in his heart.
Hatred can hide itself behind deception, but his wickedness comes out in the assembly.
Dig a pit and you fall into it; roll a stone and it comes back on you.
A lying tongue hates the ones it crushes; a flattering mouth brings people down.

proverbs_27.t: Don't boast about tomorrow; you don't know what a day will bring.
Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth; a stranger, not your own lips.
A stone is heavy, sand is a burden — but a fool's provocation outweighs them both.
Rage is cruel, anger a flood — but who can stand up to jealousy?
Better a reproof out in the open than love that stays hidden.
A friend's wounds can be trusted; an enemy's kisses come thick and fast.
When you're full you'll tread on honeycomb; when you're hungry every bitter thing tastes sweet.
Like a bird strayed from its nest — that's a person strayed from his place.
Oil and perfume gladden the heart; so does the sweetness of a friend's counsel.
Don't forsake your own friend or your father's friend; don't go to your brother's house on the day disaster hits you. Better a neighbour close by than a brother far off.
Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, so I can answer whoever taunts me.
A shrewd person sees trouble coming and takes cover; the naive walk on and pay for it.
Take the coat of anyone who's gone surety for a stranger; hold it in pledge on a foreign woman's account.
Bless your neighbour in a loud voice first thing in the morning, and it'll be reckoned to you as a curse.
A roof that never stops dripping in steady rain and a quarrelsome wife are the same thing.
Holding her back is like holding back the wind, like trying to grip oil in your right hand.
Iron sharpens iron; one person sharpens the face of another.
Tend a fig tree and you'll eat its fruit; guard your master and you'll be honoured.
As water gives face back to face, so one person's heart answers another.
Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; nor are a person's eyes.
A crucible for silver, a furnace for gold — and a person is tested by the praise he gets.
Pound a fool in a mortar, among the grain, with a pestle — his folly still won't leave him.
Know your flock well, by sight; set your heart on your herds.
Wealth doesn't last for ever, nor does a crown, generation after generation.
The old grass goes, new growth appears, and the mountain vegetation is gathered in.
The lambs are for your clothing; the goats will buy you a field.
and enough goats' milk for your food, for your household's food, and a living for your servant girls.

proverbs_28.t: The wicked run with nobody chasing them; the righteous are as confident as a young lion.
When a land transgresses, it gets one ruler after another; under someone with understanding and knowledge it lasts.
A poor man oppressing the poor is a driving rain that leaves no food behind.
Those who forsake law praise the wicked; those who keep law take them on.
Evil people don't understand justice; those who seek the LORD understand it fully.
Better a poor person walking in integrity than someone with crooked ways who happens to be rich.
Keep law and you're a son of understanding; keep company with gluttons and you shame your father.
Build your wealth on interest and usury and you're gathering it for someone who's generous to the poor.
Turn your ear away from hearing law and even your prayer is an abomination.
Lead the upright astray down an evil road and you'll fall into your own pit; the blameless will inherit good.
A rich person is wise in his own eyes; a poor one with understanding sees right through him.
When the righteous triumph, there's great glory; when the wicked rise, people go into hiding.
Conceal your transgressions and you won't prosper; confess and forsake them and you'll be shown mercy.
How blessed is the person who keeps a proper fear; harden your heart and you fall into calamity.
A roaring lion, a charging bear — that's a wicked ruler over a poor people.
A ruler with no discernment is a great extortioner; hate unjust gain and you'll prolong your days.
A person weighed down by another's blood will run to the pit — let nobody hold him back.
Walk blameless and you'll be delivered; be crooked in your ways and you'll fall all at once.
Till your ground and you'll have plenty of food; chase empty things and you'll get your fill of poverty.
A faithful person will have blessings in plenty; rush to get rich and you won't go unpunished.
Showing partiality is not good — and a man will transgress for a piece of bread.
The stingy hurry after wealth and never realise that poverty is coming for them.
Reprove someone and in the end you'll find more favour than the person who flatters with a smooth tongue.
Rob your father or mother and say, "That's no transgression," and you're a companion to a destroyer.
The greedy stir up strife; rely on the LORD and you'll prosper.
Trust your own heart and you're a dullard; walk in wisdom and you'll escape.
Give to the poor and you'll lack nothing; hide your eyes and you'll get curse after curse.
When the wicked rise, people go into hiding; when they perish, the righteous multiply.

proverbs_29.t: Harden your neck after being reproved again and again and you'll be broken suddenly, past healing.
When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, a people groans.
Love wisdom and you make your father glad; keep company with prostitutes and you destroy your wealth.
A king establishes a land by justice; one who exacts levies tears it down.
Flatter your neighbour and you're spreading a net for your own feet.
An evil person's transgression is a snare to him; the righteous sings out and rejoices.
The righteous knows the poor person's case; the wicked understands nothing of it.
Men of mockery set a town alight; the wise turn anger away.
Take a fool to law and, wise as you are, he rages, he laughs, and there's no quiet.
Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless; the upright seek to save his life.
A dullard lets his whole temper out; a wise person keeps it back.
Let a ruler listen to lies and all his officials turn wicked.
The poor and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
A king who judges the poor truthfully — his throne is established for ever.
The rod and reproof give wisdom; a youth left to himself shames his mother.
When the wicked increase, so does transgression; the righteous will look on their downfall.
Discipline your son and he'll give you rest; he'll be a delight to you.
With no vision, a people runs wild; how blessed is the one who keeps law!
Words alone won't discipline a servant; he understands and still gives no answer.
See someone hasty with his words? There's more hope for a dullard than for him.
Pamper a servant from his youth and in the end he'll turn out to be your heir.
An angry person stirs up strife; a hot-tempered one is full of transgression.
Pride brings a person low; the lowly in spirit attain honour.
Go shares with a thief and you hate your own life: you hear the adjuration and say nothing.
Fear of other people lays a snare; trust in the LORD and you'll be set safe on high.
Many court a ruler's favour, but a person's justice comes from the LORD.
An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous; someone whose way is upright is an abomination to the wicked.

proverbs_30.t: The words of Agur son of Jakeh. The oracle. The declaration of the man to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ukal.
I'm more of a brute than anyone; I haven't the understanding of a human being.
I've not learned wisdom, and I don't know the knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has gone up to the heavens and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has wrapped the waters in a cloak? Who has set up all the ends of the earth? What is his name — and his son's name — if you know?
All the speech of God is refined; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
Don't add to his words, or he'll reprove you and you'll be shown up as a liar.
Two things I'm asking of you; don't withhold them from me before I die:
Keep falseness and lying words far from me; give me neither poverty nor wealth; feed me the food that is my portion —
or I'll have my fill and deny you and say, "Who is the LORD?" — or I'll be poor and steal, and lay hold of the name of my God.
Don't slander a servant to his master, or he'll curse you and you'll bear the guilt.
There's a generation that curses its father and doesn't bless its mother;
a generation that's pure in its own eyes and not washed clean of its filth;
a generation with eyes raised high, eyelids lifted;
a generation with swords for teeth, knives for jaws, devouring the afflicted off the earth, the needy from among the living.
The leech has two daughters: "Give! Give!" There are three things never satisfied, four that never say "Enough":
Sheol; a barren womb; land that never has enough water; and fire, which never says "Enough".
The eye that mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother — the ravens of the valley will peck it out; the young eagles will eat it.
Three things are too wonderful for me, four that I don't understand:
the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship out in the open sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
That's the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, "I've done nothing wrong."
Under three things the earth quakes, four it cannot bear:
a servant who becomes king; a boor with his belly full;
a hated woman who gets married; a servant girl who supplants her mistress.
Four things on earth are small, yet they are wise beyond measure:
ants — a people with no strength, yet they get their food ready in the summer;
rock badgers — a people with no power, yet they make their home in the rock;
locusts have no king, yet out they all go in ranks;
a lizard you can catch in your hands, yet there it is in a king's palace.
Three things step out well, four of them walk in style:
the lion, mightiest of animals, which turns back for nothing;
a strutting cock, a he-goat, and a king with his troops around him.
If you've been a fool and exalted yourself, or if you've been plotting — hand over your mouth!
Squeeze milk and you get butter; squeeze the nose and you get blood; squeeze anger and you get strife.

proverbs_31.t: The words of Lemuel the king. An oracle, with which his mother instructed him.
What, my son? What, son of my own womb? What, son of my vows?
Don't give your strength to women, or your ways to those who destroy kings.
It's not for kings, Lemuel — not for kings to drink wine, not for rulers to crave strong drink —
or he'll drink and forget what's been decreed, and twist the case of all the afflicted.
Give strong drink to someone who's perishing, wine to those who are bitter in spirit;
let him drink and forget how poor he is, and remember his trouble no more.
Open your mouth for those who have no voice, for the cause of all who are passing away.
Open your mouth; judge with righteousness; plead the cause of the afflicted and the needy.
A capable wife — who can find one? She is worth far more than corals.
Her husband's heart trusts her, and he goes short of nothing.
She does him good and not evil all the days of her life.
She looks out wool and flax and works with willing hands.
She's like a merchant's ships, bringing her food from far away.
She's up while it's still night, giving food to her household, a portion to her servant girls.
She sizes up a field and buys it; out of what her hands have earned she plants a vineyard.
She girds her loins with strength; she makes her arms strong.
She can tell her trading is good; her lamp doesn't go out at night.
She puts her hands to the distaff; her palms take hold of the spindle.
She opens her hand to the afflicted and stretches out her hands to the needy.
She has no fear of snow for her household; they're all clothed in scarlet.
She makes her own coverings; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Her husband is known at the gates, sitting there with the elders of the land.
She makes linen garments and sells them, supplies belts to the merchants.
Strength and honour are what she wears, and she laughs at the days to come.
She opens her mouth with wisdom; the law of kindness is on her tongue.
She keeps watch over the ways of her household; she doesn't eat the bread of idleness.
Her children stand up and call her blessed; her husband too, and he praises her:
"Many daughters have done capably, but you have surpassed them all."
Favour is deceptive; beauty is vapour; a woman who fears the LORD — she is the one to be praised.
Give her a share of the fruit of her hands; let her works praise her at the gates.

psalms_1.t: How blessed is the person who hasn't walked in the counsel of the wicked, hasn't stood in the way of sinners, hasn't sat in the seat of mockers;
but his delight is in the LORD's law, and he murmurs over it day and night.
He's like a tree planted by streams of water, that gives its fruit in its time, and its leaves don't wither; and everything he does prospers.
Not so the wicked — they're like chaff the wind drives away.
So the wicked won't stand in the judgement, and sinners won't stand in the congregation of the righteous.
For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked perishes.

psalms_2.t: Why are the nations in an uproar, and the peoples murmuring a vain thing?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and rulers take counsel together against the LORD and against his anointed:
'Let's tear off their bonds, and throw their cords off us.'
The one who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord mocks them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger, and terrifies them in his fury:
'But I myself have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain.'
Let me tell the LORD's decree. He said to me: 'You are my son; today I have fathered you.
Ask me, and I'll make the nations your inheritance, and the ends of the earth your possession.
You'll break them with a rod of iron; you'll shatter them like a potter's vessel.'
So now, kings, act prudently; take the discipline, judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the son, or he'll be angry and you'll perish on the way, because his anger burns in a little while. How blessed are all who take refuge in him.

psalms_3.t: A psalm of David, from when he fled from his son Absalom.
LORD, how many my foes are! Many are rising up against me.
Many are saying about my being, 'There's no salvation for him in God.' Selah
But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, the one who lifts my head.
I call out to the LORD, and he answered me from his holy mountain. Selah
I lay down and slept; I woke up, for the LORD sustains me.
I won't be afraid of ten thousands of people who've set themselves against me on every side.
Get up, LORD! Save me, my God! You've struck all my enemies on the jaw; you've broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; your blessing be on your people. Selah

psalms_4.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
When I call, answer me, God of my righteousness! When I was hemmed in you made room for me; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
You sons of man, how long will my glory be turned to disgrace? How long will you love a vain thing and go after falsehood? Selah
Know that the LORD has set apart the loyal one for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.
Tremble, and don't sin. Say it in your heart on your bed, and be silent. Selah
Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, 'Who will show us anything good?' Lift up the light of your face on us, LORD!
You've put more gladness in my heart than they have when their grain and new wine come in.
In peace I'll both lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me dwell in security.

psalms_5.t: For the choir director, to nehiloth. A psalm of David.
Listen to my sayings, LORD; give thought to my murmuring.
Pay attention to the sound of my cry for help, my King and my God, because you are the one I pray to.
LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I lay out my case before you, and I watch.
You're not a God who delights in wickedness; evil doesn't stay with you.
The boastful can't take their stand before your eyes; you hate everyone who does wrong.
You destroy those who speak falsehood; the LORD abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I will come into your house through the abundance of your steadfast love; I'll bow down toward your holy temple in fear of you.
LORD, lead me in your righteousness because of those watching me; make your way straight in front of me.
There's nothing reliable in his mouth; inside them is destruction; their throat is an open grave; with their tongue they speak smooth words.
Hold them guilty, God! Let them fall by their own schemes. Banish them for all their transgressions, because they've rebelled against you.
But let everyone who takes refuge in you be glad; let them shout for joy forever; and may you shelter them, and let those who love your name exult in you.
For you bless the righteous, LORD; you surround him with good pleasure like a body-shield.

psalms_6.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments, upon the sheminith. A psalm of David.
LORD, don't reprove me in your anger, and don't discipline me in your wrath.
Be gracious to me, LORD — I'm withered away; heal me, LORD — my bones are dismayed.
And my being is dismayed to the depths; and you, LORD — how long?
Come back, LORD! Rescue my being! Save me for the sake of your steadfast love.
In death there's no remembrance of you; in Sheol, who gives you thanks?
I'm worn out with groaning; every night I make my bed swim; with my tears I dissolve my couch.
My eye has wasted away from vexation; it's grown weak because of all my adversaries.
Get away from me, all of you who do wrong — the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my supplication; the LORD accepts my prayer.
Let all my enemies be ashamed and dismayed to the depths; let them turn back and be ashamed in a moment.

psalms_7.t: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD about the words of Cush, a Benjaminite.
LORD my God, I've taken refuge in you. Save me from all my pursuers and deliver me,
or he'll tear my being apart like a lion, ripping away with no one to deliver.
LORD my God, if I've done this, if there's injustice on my hands,
if I've repaid evil to the one at peace with me, or plundered my adversary for nothing —
then let an enemy pursue my being and overtake it, let him trample my life into the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah
Get up, LORD, in your anger! Raise yourself against the rages of my adversaries, and wake for me — you have commanded judgement.
Let the congregation of peoples gather round you, and take your place on high above it.
The LORD gives judgement to the peoples. Judge me, LORD, by my righteousness and by the integrity that is in me.
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and establish the righteous — you test hearts and kidneys, righteous God.
My shield is with God, the saviour of the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge — a God who is indignant every day.
If a man doesn't turn back, he sharpens his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready.
And he has prepared instruments of death for him; he makes his arrows into flaming shafts.
Look — he's in labour with wrongdoing; he has conceived trouble and given birth to a lie.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and he's fallen into the ditch he was making.
His trouble comes back on his own head, and his violence comes down on his own skull.
I'll give thanks to the LORD for his righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

psalms_8.t: For the choir director, upon the gittith. A psalm of David.
LORD our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth — you who have set your splendour above the heavens!
Out of the mouth of children and infants you have established strength, because of your adversaries, to put an end to enemy and avenger.
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you set in place —
what is a human being that you remember him, a son of humankind that you attend to him?
You've made him just a little lower than the heavenly beings, and you crown him with glory and majesty.
You make him rule over the works of your hands; you've put everything under his feet:
flocks and cattle, all of them, and the animals of the field too,
the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
LORD our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth!

psalms_9.t: For the choir director, upon muth-labben. A psalm of David.
I'll give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I'll recount all your wonders.
I'll be glad and exult in you; I'll make music to your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.
You've upheld my judgement and my cause; you've taken your seat on a throne, judging righteously.
You've rebuked nations, you've destroyed the wicked; you've wiped out their name forever and ever.
The enemy is finished, in ruins for good; you've uprooted cities — their very memory has perished.
But the LORD sits forever; he has established his throne for judgement.
And he himself will judge the world in righteousness; he'll give judgement to the peoples in uprightness.
Let the LORD be a high refuge for the oppressed, a high refuge in times of distress.
Those who know your name will trust in you — you have not forsaken those who seek you, LORD.
Make music to the LORD who dwells in Zion; tell his deeds among the peoples.
The one who seeks out bloodshed has remembered them; he hasn't forgotten the cry of distress of the humble.
Be gracious to me, LORD! See my affliction at the hands of those who hate me — you who lift me up from the gates of death,
so I can recount all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion, and rejoice in your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the ditch they made; their own foot is caught in the net they hid.
The LORD has made himself known; he has done judgement. The wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah
The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
The needy won't be forgotten in perpetuity; the hope of the afflicted won't perish forever.
Rise up, LORD! Let no human being prevail; let the nations be judged before your face.
Put terror in them, LORD; let the nations know they're only human beings. Selah

psalms_10.t: Why do you stand at a distance, LORD? Why do you hide in times of distress?
In his pride the wicked hotly pursues the afflicted; let them be caught in the schemes they've devised.
The wicked boasts about what his being craves, and the greedy one renounces and scorns the LORD.
The wicked, in all his haughtiness, does not seek; 'There is no God' — that's all he ever thinks.
His ways endure at all times. Your judgements are on high, far out of his sight; as for all his adversaries, he snorts at them.
He says to himself, 'I'll never be shaken; from generation to generation I'll never be in trouble.'
His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression; under his tongue are trouble and wrongdoing.
He sits in ambush near the villages; from his hiding places he kills the innocent; his eyes lie in wait for the hapless.
He lies in wait in his hiding place like a lion in its lair; he lies in wait to seize the afflicted; he seizes the afflicted and drags him off in his net.
He crouches, he sinks down, and the hapless fall into his powerful grip.
He says to himself, 'God has forgotten; he has hidden his face; he'll never see.'
Rise up, LORD! God, lift up your hand! Don't forget the humble.
Why has the wicked spurned God? He tells himself, 'You won't call it to account.'
You have seen it — you do observe trouble and vexation, to take it into your hand. The hapless commits himself to you; you have been a helper to the fatherless.
Break the arm of the wicked and the evil one; seek out his wickedness until you find none.
The LORD is king forever and ever; the nations have perished out of his land.
You've heard the desire of the humble, LORD; you steady their heart, you make your ear attend,
to give judgement for the fatherless and the oppressed, so that a mere human being from the earth will terrify no more.

psalms_11.t: For the choir director. Of David.
I've taken refuge in the LORD. How can you say to my being, 'Flee to your mountain, bird!'?
Look — the wicked bend a bow; they've set their arrow on the string, to shoot from the dark at the upright in heart.
If the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?
The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD's throne is in the heavens. His eyes see; his eyelids test the children of humankind.
The LORD tests the righteous; but the wicked and the one who loves violence — his being hates them.
He'll rain snares on the wicked; fire and sulphur and a scorching wind are the portion of their cup.
The LORD is righteous; he loves righteous deeds. The upright will see his face.

psalms_12.t: For the choir director, upon the sheminith. A psalm of David.
Save us, LORD — the loyal one has come to an end; the faithful have vanished from among the children of humankind.
They speak emptiness, each to his neighbour; with flattering lips and a double heart they speak.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaks great things —
those who say, 'With our tongue we'll prevail; our lips are our own — who is master over us?'
'Because of the devastation of the afflicted, because of the groaning of the needy, now I will arise,' says the LORD; 'I will set in safety the one who pants for it.'
The LORD's speech is pure speech — silver refined in a crucible on the ground, purged seven times over.
You, LORD, will keep them; you'll guard him from this generation forever.
The wicked walk about on every side, when vileness is exalted among the children of humankind.

psalms_13.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
How long, LORD? Will you forget me in perpetuity? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I hold counsel within my being, with sorrow in my heart all day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
Look at me, answer me, LORD my God! Give light to my eyes, or I'll sleep the sleep of death,
or my enemy will say, 'I've prevailed over him,' and my foes will rejoice when I'm shaken.
But I have trusted in your steadfast love; let my heart rejoice in your salvation.
I'll sing to the LORD, because he has dealt bountifully with me.

psalms_14.t: For the choir director. Of David.
The fool has said to himself, 'There is no God.' They act corruptly, they make their deeds abominable; there's no one who does good.
The LORD looked down from the heavens on the children of humankind, to see if there's anyone acting prudently, anyone seeking God.
They've all turned aside; together they've gone bad; there's no one who does good — not even one.
Do they not know, all these workers of wrongdoing, who devour my people the way they eat bread? They don't call on the LORD.
There they were seized with dread, for God is with the righteous generation.
You would shame the counsel of the afflicted, but the LORD is his refuge.
Who will grant from Zion the salvation of Israel? When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.

psalms_15.t: LORD, who may stay as a guest in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy mountain?
The one who walks blameless and does righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart;
he doesn't go about slandering with his tongue, he doesn't do evil to his neighbour, and he doesn't take up a reproach against his kinsman;
in his eyes a rejected man is despised, but he honours those who fear the LORD; he has sworn to his own hurt and doesn't go back on it;
he doesn't lend his money at interest, and he doesn't take a bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.

psalms_16.t: Keep me, God — I've taken refuge in you.
I said to the LORD, 'You are Lord; I have no good apart from you.'
As for the holy ones who are in the land — they are the magnificent ones, and all my delight is in them.
Their sorrows increase — they've hurried after another god; I won't pour out their drink offerings of blood, and I won't take their names on my lips.
The LORD is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; you hold my lot.
The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; my inheritance is beautiful to me.
I'll bless the LORD, who has counselled me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.
I keep the LORD before me continually; because he's at my right hand, I won't be shaken.
So my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh too dwells in security.
You won't forsake my being to Sheol; you won't let your loyal one see decay.
You'll make known to me the path of life; fullness of gladness is in your presence, pleasant things at your right hand in perpetuity.

psalms_17.t: Hear a righteous cause, LORD! Attend to my cry of entreaty! Give ear to my prayer — it comes from lips without deceit.
Let my vindication come from your presence; let your eyes see what is upright.
You've tested my heart, you've visited by night, you've refined me — you'll find nothing. I've resolved that my mouth won't transgress.
As for what people do — by the word of your lips I've kept clear of the paths of the violent man.
My steps have held to your tracks; my footsteps haven't slipped.
I call on you, because you answer me, God; turn your ear to me, hear my speech.
Show the wonder of your acts of steadfast love — saviour of those who take refuge at your right hand from those who rise against them.
Keep me like the pupil of the eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings,
from the wicked who have assailed me, from my deadly enemies who surround me.
They've closed up their fat hearts; with their mouth they speak in pride.
They've surrounded us at every step; they fix their eyes to bring us down to the ground.
He's like a lion longing to tear, like a young lion crouching in hiding places.
Rise up, LORD! Confront him, bring him down! Bring my being to safety from the wicked by your sword,

from men by your hand, LORD, from men of this world whose portion is in this life, whose belly you fill with what you have stored up; they have sons enough, and they leave their abundance to their children.
As for me, in righteousness I'll see your face; I'll be satisfied, when I awake, with your form.

psalms_18.t: For the choir director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David, who spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
And he said: I love you, LORD, my strength.
The LORD is my rock and my fortress and the one who brings me to safety; my God is my Rock, the one I take refuge in, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my high refuge.
I call on the LORD, who is to be praised, and I'm saved from my enemies.
The cords of death wrapped round me, and the torrents of worthlessness overwhelmed me.
The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the traps of death came at me.
In my distress I called on the LORD, and cried to my God for help; he heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help came before him, into his ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled; they shook back and forth, because he was angry.
Smoke went up from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth consumed; coals burned out from him.
He stretched out the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his secret place, his shelter around him — a darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
Out of the brightness before him his thick clouds swept past, hail and coals of fire.
The LORD thundered in the heavens, and the Most High gave forth his voice: hail and coals of fire.
He sent out his arrows and scattered them; he shot many lightning flashes and routed them.
Then the channels of water appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare, at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils.
He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from those who hate me — they were too strong for me.
They came at me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD became my support.
He brought me out into open ground; he rescued me, because he delighted in me.
The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; he repaid me according to the purity of my hands.
For I've kept the ways of the LORD; I haven't wickedly turned from my God.
All his judgements have been before me; I haven't put his statutes away from me.
I've been blameless with him, and I've kept myself from my iniquity.
And the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the purity of my hands before his eyes.
With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless man you show yourself blameless;
with the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself twisted.
You save an afflicted people, and you bring lofty eyes low.
You light my lamp; the LORD my God brightens my darkness.
With you I can charge a raiding band; with my God I can leap a wall.
As for God — his way is blameless; the speech of the LORD is refined; he is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
Who is God apart from the LORD? Who is a Rock except our God?
The God who girds me with might and makes my way blameless;
who makes my feet like a deer's and makes me stand firm on my high places;
who trains my hands for battle, so my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You've given me the shield of your salvation; your right hand has supported me, and your gentleness has made me great.
You widened my stride beneath me, and my ankles didn't slip.
I pursued my enemies and overtook them, and I didn't turn back until they were finished.
I shattered them, and they couldn't rise; they fell under my feet.
You girded me with might for the battle; you brought those who rose against me down beneath me.
As for my enemies, you gave me their necks; and those who hate me, I destroyed them.
They cried for help, and there was no saviour — to the LORD, and he didn't answer them.
I crushed them like dust before the wind; I poured them out like mud in the streets.
You brought me to safety from a people's quarrels; you set me at the head of nations; a people I never knew serve me.
The moment they hear of me they obey; foreigners come cringing to me.
Foreigners wither, and come trembling out of their strongholds.
The LORD lives! Blessed be my Rock, and let the God of my salvation be exalted —
the God who gives me vengeance and subdues peoples beneath me,
who brings me to safety from my enemies — you lift me above those who rise against me; you deliver me from a man of violence.
So I'll give thanks to you among the nations, LORD, and make music to your name.
He gives great salvation to his king and shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and to his offspring, to perpetuity.

psalms_19.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
The heavens are recounting the glory of God, and the vault is telling the work of his hands.
Day pours out utterance to day, and night shows knowledge to night.
There's no utterance and there are no words; their voice isn't heard.
Their line has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. For the sun he has set a tent in them;
and it comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, delighting like a mighty man to run its course.
Its rising is from one end of the heavens, its circuit to the other, and nothing is hidden from its heat.
The LORD's law is perfect, restoring the being; the LORD's testimony is reliable, making the simple wise.
The LORD's precepts are upright, making the heart glad; the LORD's commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; the LORD's judgements are truth — all of them righteous.
They're more desirable than gold, than heaps of refined gold, and sweeter than honey, than the drippings of the comb.
Your servant too is warned by them; in keeping them there is great reward.
Who can discern his own errors? Acquit me of what's hidden.
Hold your servant back from presumptuous sins as well; don't let them rule over me. Then I'll be blameless, and I'll be acquitted of great transgression.
Let the sayings of my mouth and the murmuring of my heart be acceptable before you, LORD, my Rock and my redeemer.

psalms_20.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
May the LORD answer you in the day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high.
May he send your help from the sanctuary, and support you from Zion.
May he remember all your grain offerings, and receive your burnt offering as fat. Selah
May he give you what your heart wants, and fulfil all your counsel.
Let us shout for joy at your salvation, and raise a banner in the name of our God. May the LORD fulfil all your requests.
Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed; he answers him from his holy heavens with the mighty deeds of his saving right hand.
Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They've bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stood upright.
LORD, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.

psalms_21.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
LORD, in your strength the king is glad, and how greatly he rejoices in your salvation!
You've given him the desire of his heart, and you haven't withheld the request of his lips. Selah
You meet him with blessings of good; you set a crown of refined gold on his head.
He asked you for life; you gave it to him — length of days forever and ever.
Great is his glory through your salvation; you place splendour and majesty on him.
You make him a blessing forever; you make him rejoice with gladness in your presence.
The king trusts in the LORD, and through the steadfast love of the Most High he won't be shaken.
Your hand will find out all your enemies; your right hand will find out those who hate you.
You'll make them like a furnace of fire when you appear; the LORD in his anger will swallow them, and fire will consume them.
You'll destroy their fruit from the earth, and their offspring from among the children of humankind.
They stretched out evil against you; they devised a scheme, but they won't succeed.
You'll make them turn and run; with your bowstrings you'll aim at their faces.
Be exalted, LORD, in your strength! We'll sing and make music of your might.

psalms_22.t: For the choir director, upon 'The Doe of the Dawn'. A psalm of David.
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my roaring.
My God, I call by day and you don't answer; by night too, and I find no rest.
And you are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel.
Our ancestors trusted in you; they trusted, and you brought them to safety.
They cried out to you and they escaped; they trusted in you and they weren't put to shame.
But I'm a worm and not a man, scorned by humankind and despised by the people.
Everyone who sees me mocks me; they curl the lip, they shake the head:
'Commit it to the LORD — let him bring him to safety! Let him deliver him, since he delights in him!'
You're the one who drew me out from the belly, who made me trust at my mother's breasts.
I was cast on you from the womb; from my mother's belly you've been my God.
Don't be far from me — distress is near, and there's no helper.
Many bulls have surrounded me; the strong bulls of Bashan have encircled me.
They open their mouths wide at me, a lion tearing and roaring.
I'm poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart has turned to wax, melted away inside me.
My strength is dried up like a potsherd, my tongue sticks to my jaws, and you lay me in the dust of death.
Dogs have surrounded me; a gang of evildoers has encircled me; they pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones; they look, they stare at me.
They divide my garments among themselves, and cast lots for my clothing.
But you, LORD — don't be distant; my strength, hurry to help me!
Deliver my being from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog.
Save me from the mouth of the lion — and from the horns of the wild oxen you have answered me!
I'll recount your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I'll praise you.
You who fear the LORD, praise him! All the offspring of Jacob, honour him! And stand in awe of him, all the offspring of Israel!
He hasn't despised or detested the affliction of the afflicted; he hasn't hidden his face from him; and when he cried to him for help, he heard.
My praise comes from you in the great assembly; I'll pay my vows before those who fear him.
The humble will eat and be satisfied; those who seek him will praise the LORD. May your heart live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the clans of the nations will bow down before you.
The kingship belongs to the LORD; he rules over the nations.
All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and bowed down; before him will bow all who go down to the dust — even the one who could not keep his own being alive.
Offspring will serve him; it will be told of the Lord to the coming generation.
They'll come and declare his righteousness to a people yet to be born — that he has done it.

psalms_23.t: The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; he leads me by waters of rest.
He restores my being; he guides me along tracks of righteousness for the sake of his name.
Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death I won't fear evil, because you are with me; your rod and your staff — they comfort me.
You spread a table for me right in front of my adversaries; you have enriched my head with oil; my cup is abundance.
Surely goodness and steadfast love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I'll return to the house of the LORD for length of days.

psalms_24.t: The earth belongs to the LORD, and everything in it, the world and those who dwell in it.
He founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.
Who may go up the mountain of the LORD? And who may stand in his holy place?
The one with innocent hands and a pure heart, who hasn't lifted up his being to what is empty and hasn't sworn deceitfully.
He will receive a blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
This is the generation of those who seek him, those who seek your face — Jacob. Selah
Lift up your heads, gates! Be lifted up, ancient doors — let the King of glory come in!
Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, gates! Lift up, ancient doors — let the King of glory come in!
Who is he, this King of glory? The LORD of hosts — he is the King of glory. Selah

psalms_25.t: Of David.
To you, LORD, I lift up my being.
My God, I trust in you; don't let me be put to shame; don't let my enemies exult over me.
No one who waits for you will be put to shame; those who act treacherously without cause will be put to shame.
Make your ways known to me, LORD; teach me your paths.
Lead me in your truth and teach me, because you are the God of my salvation; I've waited for you all day long.
Remember your compassion, LORD, and your acts of steadfast love — they are from of old.
Don't remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions; remember me according to your steadfast love — you, for the sake of your goodness, LORD.
Good and upright is the LORD; so he teaches sinners in the way.
He leads the humble in what is just, and he teaches the humble his way.
All the LORD's paths are steadfast love and faithfulness to those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.
For the sake of your name, LORD, forgive my iniquity — it is great.
Who is the man who fears the LORD? He'll teach him the way he should choose.
His being will rest in good, and his offspring will possess the land.
The counsel of the LORD is for those who fear him, and his covenant, to make it known to them.
My eyes are always toward the LORD; he brings my feet out of the net.
Turn to me and be gracious to me — I'm solitary and afflicted.
The distresses of my heart have grown wide; bring me out of my straits.
Consider my affliction and my trouble, and take away all my sins.
Consider my enemies — they've become many, and they hate me with a violent hatred.
Keep my being and deliver me; don't let me be put to shame — I've taken refuge in you.
Let integrity and uprightness preserve me — I have waited for you.
Redeem Israel, God, from all its distresses.

psalms_26.t: Judge me, LORD — I have walked in my integrity, and I have trusted in the LORD; I won't slip.
Test me, LORD, and put me to the proof; refine my kidneys and my heart.
Your steadfast love is before my eyes, and I've walked in your faithfulness.
I don't sit with men of emptiness, and I won't go with dissemblers.
I hate the assembly of evildoers, and I won't sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, LORD,
to make the sound of thanksgiving heard, and to recount all your wonders.
LORD, I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells.
Don't gather my being with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed,
in whose hands is depravity, whose right hand is full of bribes.
But I will walk in my integrity; redeem me and be gracious to me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I'll bless the LORD.

psalms_27.t: The LORD is my light and my salvation — who should I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life — who should I dread?
When evildoers came at me to devour my flesh — my foes and my enemies — they stumbled and fell.
If an army encamps against me, my heart won't fear; if war rises against me, even then I'm trusting.
One thing I've asked from the LORD — this I will seek: that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the pleasantness of the LORD and to inquire in his temple.
He'll conceal me in his shelter in the day of evil; he'll hide me in the secret place of his tent; he'll raise me high on a rock.
And now my head will rise above my enemies around me, and I'll offer in his tent sacrifices with shouts; I'll sing and make music to the LORD.
Hear my voice, LORD, when I call; be gracious to me and answer me.
My heart has said of you, 'Seek my face.' Your face, LORD, I will seek.
Don't hide your face from me; don't turn your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Don't abandon me, don't forsake me, God of my salvation.
My father and my mother have forsaken me, but the LORD will gather me.
Teach me your way, LORD, and lead me on a level path because of those who watch me.
Don't give me over to the will of my foes; false witnesses have risen against me, and one breathing out violence.
If I hadn't believed that I would look on the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living —
Wait for the LORD! Be strong, and let your heart show strength. And wait for the LORD!

psalms_28.t: To you, LORD, I call — my Rock, don't be deaf to me; if you are silent toward me I'll become like those who go down to the pit.
Hear the sound of my supplications when I cry to you for help, when I lift up my hands toward your holy innermost room.
Don't drag me away with the wicked or with the workers of wrongdoing, who speak peace with their neighbours while evil is in their heart.
Give them what their work deserves, and the wickedness of their deeds; give them according to the work of their hands; turn back on them what they've earned.
They don't consider the deeds of the LORD or the work of his hands; he will tear them down and not build them up.
Blessed be the LORD — he has heard the sound of my supplications.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him and I was helped; my heart is jubilant, and with my song I give thanks to him.
The LORD is strength for them; he is the stronghold of salvation for his anointed.
Save your people and bless your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them for ever.

psalms_29.t: Ascribe to the LORD, you heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; bow down to the LORD in the majesty of holiness.
The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders — the LORD is over many waters.
The voice of the LORD is in strength; the voice of the LORD is in majesty.
The voice of the LORD breaks cedars; the LORD shattered the cedars of Lebanon.
He made them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of the LORD strikes out flames of fire.
The voice of the LORD makes the wilderness tremble; the LORD makes the wilderness of Kadesh tremble.
The voice of the LORD makes the does writhe in labour and strips the forests bare; and in his temple, everything says: Glory!
The LORD sat at the flood, and the LORD sits as king forever.
The LORD will give strength to his people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.

psalms_30.t: A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. Of David.
I'll exalt you, LORD — you have drawn me up, and you haven't let my enemies rejoice over me.
LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you healed me.
LORD, you brought my being up from Sheol; you kept me alive from among those going down to the pit.
Make music to the LORD, you his loyal ones, and give thanks to his holy remembrance.
His anger lasts a moment, his good pleasure a lifetime; weeping stays the night, and at morning, a shout of joy.
And I said, when I was at ease: 'I'll never be shaken.'
LORD, in your good pleasure you made my mountain stand strong; you hid your face — and I was dismayed.
To you, LORD, I call; to the Lord I make supplication:
'What profit is there in my blood, in my going down to destruction? Will the dust give you thanks? Will it declare your faithfulness?
Hear, LORD, and be gracious to me; LORD, be my helper.'
You turned my wailing into dancing; you loosened my sackcloth and girded me with gladness,
so that my glory may make music to you and not be silent. LORD my God, I'll give thanks to you forever.

psalms_31.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
In you, LORD, I've taken refuge; never let me be put to shame; in your righteousness bring me to safety.
Turn your ear to me, deliver me quickly; be a Rock of refuge for me, a fortified house, to save me.
You are my rock and my fortress; and for the sake of your name you'll guide me and lead me.
You'll bring me out of the net they hid for me — you are my stronghold.
Into your hand I entrust my spirit; you have redeemed me, LORD, God of faithfulness.
I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but I trust in the LORD.
I'll rejoice and be glad in your steadfast love, because you have seen my affliction; you've known the distresses of my being,
and you haven't shut me up in an enemy's hand; you've set my feet in open ground.
Be gracious to me, LORD — I'm in distress; my eye has wasted away with vexation, and my being and my belly too.
My life is spent in sorrow, my years in groaning; my strength has failed through my iniquity, and my bones have wasted away.
Because of all my adversaries I've become a reproach — to my neighbours especially, and a dread to my acquaintances; those who see me in the street flee from me.
I'm forgotten like a dead man, out of mind; I've become like a broken vessel.
I've heard the slander of many — terror all around — when they set themselves together against me; they plotted to take my being.
But I have trusted in you, LORD; I said, 'You are my God.'
My times are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from my pursuers.
Make your face shine on your servant; save me in your steadfast love.
LORD, don't let me be put to shame — I have called on you; let the wicked be put to shame, let them be silenced into Sheol.
Let lying lips be struck dumb, those who speak arrogantly against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How great is your goodness, stored up for those who fear you, done for those who take refuge in you, in front of the children of humankind!
You hide them in the secret place of your presence from human conspiracies; you conceal them in a shelter from the strife of tongues.
Blessed be the LORD — he has made his steadfast love wonderful to me in a besieged city.
And I said in my alarm, 'I've been cut off from before your eyes.' But you heard the sound of my supplications when I cried to you for help.
Love the LORD, all you his loyal ones! The LORD preserves the faithful, and repays in full the one who acts in pride.
Be strong, and let your heart show strength, all you who wait for the LORD.

psalms_32.t: How blessed is the one whose transgression is lifted away, whose sin is covered!
How blessed is the man the LORD does not reckon iniquity against, and in whose spirit there's no treachery!
When I kept silent, my bones wore away with my roaring all day long.
Day and night your hand was heavy on me; my sap dried up as in the heat of summer. Selah
I made my sin known to you; I didn't cover my iniquity. I said, 'I'll confess my transgressions to the LORD' — and you lifted away the iniquity of my sin. Selah
So let every loyal one pray to you while you may be found; surely when the flood of many waters comes, it won't reach him.
You are a secret place for me; you preserve me from distress; you surround me with shouts of safety. Selah
I'll make you prudent and teach you the way you should go; I'll counsel you with my eye on you.
Don't be like a horse or a mule, without understanding, whose trappings are bridle and halter to restrain it, or it won't come near you.
Many are the pains of the wicked, but steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.
Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart!

psalms_33.t: Shout for joy in the LORD, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.
Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre; make music to him with the ten-stringed harp.
Sing him a new song; play skilfully, with a shout.
The word of the LORD is upright, and all his work is done in constancy.
He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the LORD's steadfast love.
By the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and by the breath of his mouth all their host.
He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap; he puts the deeps in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the LORD; let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him.
He spoke and it was; he commanded and it stood firm.
The LORD has broken the counsel of the nations; he has frustrated the plans of the peoples.
The counsel of the LORD stands forever, the plans of his heart from generation to generation.
How blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people he has chosen as his own inheritance!
From the heavens the LORD looks; he sees all the children of humankind.
From his dwelling place he gazes on all the inhabitants of the earth —
he who forms their hearts together, who attends to all their deeds.
No king is saved by great might; no mighty man is delivered by great strength.
The horse is a false hope for salvation; for all its great might it lets no one escape.
Look — the eye of the LORD is on those who fear him, on those who wait for his steadfast love,
to deliver their being from death and keep them alive in famine.
Our being waits for the LORD; he is our help and our shield.
Our heart is glad in him; we have trusted in his holy name.
Let your steadfast love be on us, LORD, just as we have waited for you.

psalms_34.t: Of David, when he feigned madness before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he went.
I'll bless the LORD at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth.
My being makes its boast in the LORD; let the humble hear and be glad.
Magnify the LORD with me, and let's exalt his name together.
I sought the LORD and he answered me, and delivered me from all my terrors.
They looked to him and were radiant; their faces are not abashed.
