This poor man called and the LORD heard, and saved him from all his distresses.
The angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, and he rescues them.
Taste and see that the LORD is good; how blessed is the one who takes refuge in him!
Fear the LORD, you his holy ones — there's no lack for those who fear him.
Young lions are in want and go hungry, but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
Come, children, listen to me; I'll teach you the fear of the LORD.
Who is the one who desires life, who loves days in which to see good?
Guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and his ears open to their cry for help.
The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth.
They cry out and the LORD hears, and delivers them from all their distresses.
The LORD is near to the broken-hearted; he saves the crushed in spirit.
Many are the evils that come on the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken.
Evil will kill the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.
The LORD redeems the being of his servants; no one who takes refuge in him will be held guilty.

psalms_35.t: Of David.
Contend, LORD, with those who contend with me; fight against those who fight against me.
Take hold of shield and body-shield, and rise up to help me.
Draw out spear and javelin to meet my pursuers; say to my being, 'I am your salvation.'
Let them be put to shame and humiliated, those who seek my being; let them be turned back and abashed, those who plot harm against me.
Let them be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them.
Let their way be darkness and slippery places, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.
For no reason they hid the ditch of their net for me; for no reason they dug a pit for my being.
Let destruction come on him unawares, and let his own net that he hid catch him; let him fall into it, into destruction.
And my being will rejoice in the LORD; it will delight in his salvation.
All my bones will say, 'LORD, who is like you, delivering the afflicted from one too strong for him, the afflicted and the needy from the one who robs him?'
Malicious witnesses rise up; they question me about things I don't know.
They repay me evil in place of good — bereavement for my being.
But when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I humbled my being with fasting, and I prayed with my head sunk to my chest.
I went about as if for a neighbour, as if for a brother; like someone mourning a mother, I bowed down in mourning.
But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered; attackers I didn't know gathered against me; they tore at me and didn't stop.
Like the godless, mocking for a morsel, they gnashed their teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you look on? Bring back my being from their ravages, my only one from the young lions.
I'll give thanks to you in the great assembly; among a numerous people I'll praise you.
Don't let my lying enemies rejoice over me; don't let those who hate me for no reason wink the eye.
They don't speak peace; against the quiet of the land they devise words of deceit.
They open their mouths wide at me; they say, 'Aha! Aha! We've seen it with our own eyes.'
You have seen it, LORD — don't be silent; Lord, don't be far from me.
Rouse yourself and wake up for my vindication, my God and Lord, for my cause.
Judge me according to your righteousness, LORD my God, and don't let them rejoice over me.
Don't let them say to themselves, 'Aha, just what we wanted!' Don't let them say, 'We've swallowed him.'
Let them be put to shame and abashed together, those who are joyful at my harm; let them be clothed with shame and disgrace, those who magnify themselves against me.
Let them shout for joy and be glad, those who desire my vindication, and let them say continually, 'Let the LORD be great, who desires the welfare of his servant.'
And my tongue will murmur your righteousness, your praise all day long.

psalms_36.t: For the choir director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David.
Transgression speaks to the wicked deep in my heart: there is no dread of God before his eyes.
He flatters himself in his own eyes, too much to find out his iniquity and hate it.
The words of his mouth are wrongdoing and deceit; he has stopped acting prudently, stopped doing good.
He plans wrongdoing on his bed; he takes his stand on a way that isn't good; he doesn't reject evil.
LORD, your steadfast love is in the heavens, your constancy reaches to the skies.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgements are a great deep; you save both humankind and animals, LORD.
How precious is your steadfast love, God! The children of humankind take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
They take their fill from the fatness of your house, and you give them drink from the river of your delights.
With you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
Keep drawing out your steadfast love to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Don't let the foot of pride come on me, and don't let the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the workers of wrongdoing have fallen; they were thrust down and couldn't rise.

psalms_37.t: Of David.
Don't fret over evildoers; don't be jealous of those who do injustice.
They'll wither quickly like grass, and fade like the green herb.
Trust in the LORD and do good; dwell in the land and feed on constancy.
Take delight in the LORD, and he'll give you the requests of your heart.
Commit your way to the LORD; trust in him, and he will act.
He'll bring out your righteousness like the light, and your justice like the noonday.
Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for him; don't fret over someone who prospers in his way, over a man who carries out schemes.
Refrain from anger and forsake wrath; don't fret — it leads only to doing evil.
Evildoers will be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD will possess the land.
In a little while the wicked will be no more; you'll look carefully at his place, and he won't be there.
But the humble will possess the land, and take delight in abundance of peace.
The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him.
The Lord laughs at him; he sees that his day is coming.
The wicked have drawn a sword and bent their bow, to bring down the afflicted and the needy, to slaughter those upright in the way.
Their sword will enter their own heart, and their bows will be broken.
Better the little the righteous has than the wealth of many wicked.
The arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD sustains the righteous.
The LORD knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever.
They won't be put to shame in a time of evil; in days of famine they'll be satisfied.
The wicked will perish, and the enemies of the LORD are like the glory of the pastures: they come to an end; they vanish in smoke.
The wicked borrows and doesn't repay, but the righteous is gracious and gives.
Those he blesses will possess the land, and those he curses will be cut off.
A man's steps are established by the LORD, and he delights in his way.
Even if he falls, he won't be thrown down; the LORD holds his hand.
I've been young, and now I'm old, and I haven't seen the righteous forsaken, or his offspring begging bread.
All day long he is gracious and lends, and his offspring become a blessing.
Turn away from evil and do good, and dwell forever.
The LORD loves justice, and he won't forsake his loyal ones; they are preserved forever, but the offspring of the wicked is cut off.
The righteous will possess the land, and dwell on it forever.
The mouth of the righteous murmurs wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
The law of his God is in his heart; his steps don't slip.
The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him.
The LORD won't leave him in his hand, and won't condemn him as guilty when he is judged.
Wait for the LORD and keep his way, and he will exalt you to possess the land; when the wicked are cut off, you'll see it.
I've seen a wicked man, ruthless, spreading himself like a luxuriant native tree.
Then he passed away, and look — he was gone; I looked for him, and he wasn't found.
Watch the blameless and see the upright: there is a future for the man of peace.
But transgressors will be destroyed together; the future of the wicked will be cut off.
The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD, their stronghold in a time of distress.
The LORD helps them and brings them to safety; he brings them to safety from the wicked and saves them, because they've taken refuge in him.

psalms_38.t: A psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.
LORD, don't reprove me in your displeasure, and don't discipline me in your wrath.
Your arrows have sunk into me, and your hand has come down on me.
There's no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there's no health in my bones because of my sin.
My iniquities have gone over my head; like a heavy burden they're too heavy for me.
My wounds stink and fester because of my folly.
I'm bent down, bowed very low; all day long I've gone about mourning.
My loins are full of burning, and there's no soundness in my flesh.
I'm numb and crushed very low; I roar from the groaning of my heart.
Lord, all my desire is before you, and my sighing isn't hidden from you.
My heart pounds, my strength has left me; and the light of my eyes — even that is gone.
My friends and my neighbours stand back from my affliction; my kinsmen stand far off.
Those who seek my being set traps; those who seek my harm speak of destruction, and all day long they murmur deceits.
But I'm like a deaf man — I don't hear; like a mute who doesn't open his mouth.
I've become like a man who doesn't hear, with no reproofs in his mouth.
It's you, LORD, I have waited for; you will answer, Lord my God.
For I said, 'Don't let them rejoice over me; when my foot slips, they magnify themselves against me.'
I'm ready to stumble, and my pain is before me continually.
I declare my iniquity; I'm anxious because of my sin.
My enemies are alive and vigorous, and those who hate me falsely are many.
Those who repay evil in place of good accuse me, because I pursue good.
Don't forsake me, LORD; my God, don't be far from me.
Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation.

psalms_39.t: For the choir director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
I said, 'I'll guard my ways from sinning with my tongue; I'll keep a muzzle on my mouth while the wicked is in front of me.'
I was dumb and silent; I held back even from good, and my pain was stirred up.
My heart grew hot inside me; as I murmured, a fire burned; I spoke with my tongue:
Make known to me my end, LORD, and the measure of my days — what it is; let me know how fleeting I am.
Look — you've made my days handbreadths, and my lifespan is as nothing before you. Surely every human being who stands is nothing but a breath. Selah
Surely a man goes about as a shadow; surely they're in turmoil for a breath. He heaps up and doesn't know who will gather it.
And now, what am I waiting for, Lord? My hope is in you.
Deliver me from all my transgressions; don't make me the reproach of the fool.
I'm dumb, I don't open my mouth — you have done it.
Take your plague off me; by the hostility of your hand I'm finished.
With reproofs for iniquity you discipline a man, and you melt away what he treasures, like a moth. Surely every human being is a breath. Selah
Hear my prayer, LORD, and give ear to my cry for help; don't be silent at my tears — I'm a sojourner with you, a resident alien like all my ancestors.
Look away from me, and let me be cheerful, before I go and am no more.

psalms_40.t: For the choir director. Of David, a psalm.
I waited and waited for the LORD, and he bent down to me and heard my cry for help.
He brought me up from a pit of tumult, from the mud of the mire, and he set my feet on a rock; he steadied my steps.
He put a new song in my mouth, a praise to our God. Many will see and fear, and they'll trust in the LORD.
How blessed is the one who has made the LORD his trust, and hasn't turned to the proud or to those who fall away to falsehood.
You've done many things, LORD my God — your wonders, and your plans toward us; there's none to compare with you. I would declare and speak of them, but they're too many to recount.
Sacrifice and grain offering you didn't desire; ears you have dug open for me; burnt offering and sin offering you didn't ask for.
Then I said, 'Look — I have come; in the scroll of the book it's written concerning me.
Doing your will, my God, is my desire, and your law is deep inside me.'
I've brought the news of righteousness in the great assembly; look — I don't restrain my lips. LORD, you know it.
I haven't covered your righteousness within my heart; I've spoken of your faithfulness and your salvation; I haven't concealed your steadfast love and your faithfulness from the great assembly.
You, LORD, won't withhold your compassion from me; your steadfast love and your faithfulness will always preserve me.
Evils have encompassed me beyond number; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I can't see; they're more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has forsaken me.
Be pleased, LORD, to deliver me; LORD, hurry to help me.
Let them be put to shame and abashed together, those who seek my being to snatch it away; let them be turned back and humiliated, those who desire my harm.
Let them be appalled at their own shameful reward, those who say to me, 'Aha! Aha!'
Let all who seek you delight and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation say continually, 'The LORD is great!'
But I'm afflicted and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my help and the one who brings me to safety; my God, don't delay.

psalms_41.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
How blessed is the one who considers the poor; in a day of evil the LORD will bring him off safe.
The LORD will keep him and preserve him alive; he'll be called blessed in the land; and don't give him over to the will of his enemies.
The LORD will support him on his sickbed; all his bed you have changed in his sickness.
I said, 'LORD, be gracious to me; heal my being — I have sinned against you.'
My enemies speak evil of me: 'When will he die and his name perish?'
And if someone comes to see me, he speaks emptiness; his heart gathers up wrongdoing; he goes outside and speaks of it.
All who hate me whisper together against me; they devise evil against me:
'Some deadly thing has been poured into him; he has lain down and won't get up again.'
Even the man at peace with me, whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
But you, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, and let me repay them.
By this I know that you delight in me: my enemy doesn't shout aloud over me.
As for me, you have held me in my integrity, and set me before you forever.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and amen.

psalms_42.t: For the choir director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.
As a deer pants for streams of water, so my being pants for you, God.
My being thirsts for God, for the living God: when will I come and appear before God?
My tears have been my food day and night, while they say to me all day long, 'Where is your God?'

These are the things I remember, and I pour out my being within me: how I used to pass on with the throng, leading them in procession to the house of God, with the sound of a shout of joy and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.
Why are you bowed down, my being, and in turmoil within me? Wait for God — I will yet give thanks to him, the salvation of his presence.
My God, my being is bowed down within me; so I remember you from the land of the Jordan, and the Hermons, from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep at the sound of your waterfalls; all your breakers and your waves have passed over me.
By day the LORD commands his steadfast love, and at night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I'll say to God my rock, 'Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go about mourning under an enemy's oppression?'
With a shattering in my bones my adversaries have taunted me, while they say to me all day long, 'Where is your God?'
Why are you bowed down, my being, and why in turmoil within me? Wait for God — I will yet give thanks to him, the salvation of my face, and my God.

psalms_43.t: Judge me, God, and conduct my case against a nation that is not loyal; bring me to safety from a man of deceit and injustice.
You are the God of my stronghold. Why have you rejected me? Why do I go about mourning under an enemy's oppression?
Send your light and your truth — let them lead me; let them bring me to your holy mountain and to your dwelling places.
And I'll come to the altar of God, to God, the gladness of my rejoicing, and give thanks to you with the lyre, God, my God.
Why are you bowed down, my being, and why in turmoil within me? Wait for God — I will yet give thanks to him, the salvation of my face, and my God.

psalms_44.t: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.
God, we've heard it with our own ears; our ancestors have recounted to us the deed you did in their days, in the days of old.
You — with your own hand you dispossessed nations and planted them; you did harm to peoples and drove them out.
It wasn't by their sword that they took possession of the land, and their own arm didn't save them, but your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, because you took pleasure in them.
You are the one, my King, God; ordain the salvation of Jacob.
By you we gore our foes; in your name we tread down those who rise against us.
I don't trust in my bow, and my sword doesn't save me.
You have saved us from our foes, and put to shame those who hate us.
In God we have boasted all day long, and we'll give thanks to your name forever. Selah
Yet you've rejected and humiliated us, and you don't go out with our armies.
You make us turn back from the foe, and those who hate us have plundered us at will.
You give us over like sheep for food, and you've scattered us among the nations.
You sell your people for nothing; you've gained nothing by their price.
You make us a reproach to our neighbours, a mockery and derision to those around us.
You make us a byword among the nations, something the peoples shake their heads at.
All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me,
at the sound of the one who taunts and reviles, because of the enemy and the avenger.
All this has come on us, and we hadn't forgotten you; we hadn't dealt falsely with your covenant.
Our heart hadn't turned back, and our steps hadn't turned aside from your path.
You've crushed us in a place of jackals, and covered us over with deep darkness.
If we'd forgotten the name of our God, and spread out our hands to a strange god,
wouldn't God search this out? He knows the secrets of the heart.
On your account we're killed all day long; we're reckoned as sheep for slaughter.
Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Rouse yourself! Don't reject us in perpetuity.
Why do you hide your face? Do you forget our affliction and our oppression?
Our being has sunk down to the dust; our belly clings to the earth.
Rise up to help us, and redeem us for the sake of your steadfast love.

psalms_45.t: For the choir director, upon 'Lilies'. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.
My heart is stirred with a good word; I speak my work to a king; my tongue is the stylus of a skilled scribe.
You're more handsome than the sons of humankind; grace has been poured on your lips; so God has blessed you forever.
Gird your sword on your thigh, mighty one — your splendour and your majesty.
And in your majesty ride out in triumph for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness, and let your right hand teach you awesome deeds.
Your arrows are sharpened — peoples fall under you — in the heart of the king's enemies.
Your throne, God, is forever and ever; a sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; so God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy beyond your companions.
Myrrh and aloes and cassia are all your garments; from palaces of ivory stringed instruments have made you glad.
Daughters of kings are among your noble women; the queen stands at your right hand in the gold of Ophir.
Listen, daughter, and look, and turn your ear; forget your people and your father's house,
and let the king desire your beauty; he is your lord — bow down to him.
And the daughter of Tyre will come with a gift; the richest of the people will seek your favour.
All glorious is the king's daughter within; her clothing is of gold settings.
In embroidered robes she's led to the king; the virgins behind her, her companions, are brought to you.
They're brought with gladness and rejoicing; they enter the palace of the king.
In place of your ancestors will be your sons; you'll make them princes in all the land.
I'll cause your name to be remembered in every generation; so peoples will give you thanks forever and ever.

psalms_46.t: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah, upon alamoth. A song.
God is a refuge and strength for us, a help in distresses, very readily found.
So we won't fear when the earth changes, when the mountains shake in the heart of the seas.
Its waters roar and foam; the mountains shake at its swelling. Selah
There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy place of the dwellings of the Most High.
God is in her midst; she won't be shaken; God will help her at daybreak.
Nations were in a tumult, kingdoms shook; he gave forth his voice, and the earth melted.
The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is a high refuge for us. Selah
Come and see the works of the LORD, who has set desolations on the earth.
He makes wars cease to the end of the earth; he breaks the bow and cuts the spear in two; he burns the carts in the fire.
'Stop, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.'
The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is a high refuge for us. Selah

psalms_47.t: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
Clap your hands, all you peoples! Shout aloud to God with the sound of a shout of joy!
The LORD Most High is to be feared, a great king over all the earth.
He subdues peoples under us, and nations under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob whom he loves. Selah
God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a ram's horn.
Make music to God, make music; make music to our King, make music.
For God is the king of all the earth; make music with a maskil.
God reigns over the nations; God sits on his holy throne.
The nobles of the peoples have gathered as the people of the God of Abraham; the shields of the earth belong to God; he is greatly exalted.

psalms_48.t: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, his holy mountain.
Beautiful in elevation, the delight of all the earth, is Mount Zion, the far reaches of the north, the town of the great king.
God in her fortresses has made himself known as a high refuge.
Look — the kings assembled; they passed on together.
They saw, and were astonished; they were terrified, they hurried away.
Trembling seized them there, anguish like a woman in labour.
With an east wind you shatter the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God; God will establish her forever. Selah
We have reflected on your steadfast love, God, in the midst of your temple.
Like your name, God, so is your praise, to the ends of the earth; your right hand is full of righteousness.
Let Mount Zion be glad; let the daughters of Judah rejoice, because of your judgements.
Walk around Zion and encircle her; count her towers.
Set your heart on her rampart; walk through her fortresses, so you can recount it to a later generation.
For this is God, our God, forever and ever; he will guide us beyond death.

psalms_49.t: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you inhabitants of the world,
both children of humankind and children of man, rich and needy alike.
My mouth will speak wisdom, and the murmuring of my heart will be understanding.
I'll turn my ear to a proverb; I'll open my riddle with the lyre.
Why should I fear in days of evil, when the iniquity of those who cheat me surrounds me —
those who trust in their wealth and boast in the abundance of their riches?
No one can ever redeem a brother; he can't give God his ransom.
for the redemption price of their life is costly, and he must cease forever —
that he should live on in perpetuity and not see destruction.
He sees that wise men die; the stupid and the brutish perish alike, and they leave their wealth to others.
They think their houses last forever, their dwelling places from generation to generation; they've called lands by their own names.
A human being in honour doesn't remain; he's like the animals that are destroyed.
This is their way — folly is theirs; and those who come after them approve their sayings. Selah
Like sheep they're appointed for Sheol; death shepherds them; and the upright rule over them in the morning; their form is for Sheol to consume, far from its lofty dwelling.
Surely God will redeem my being from the hand of Sheol, for he will take me. Selah
Don't fear when a man becomes rich, when the glory of his house increases,
at his death he'll take nothing; his glory won't go down after him.
Though while he lives he blesses himself — and people praise you when you do well for yourself —
he will go to the generation of his ancestors, who will never see light.
A human being in honour, and without understanding — he's like the animals that are destroyed.

psalms_50.t: A psalm of Asaph.
God, God, the LORD has spoken and summoned the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting.
From Zion, the perfection of beauty, God has shone forth.
Our God comes and does not keep silent; fire consumes before him, and around him it is a raging tempest.
He summons the heavens above, and the earth, to judge his people:
'Gather to me my loyal ones, those who made my covenant over a sacrifice.'
And the heavens declare his righteousness — God himself is judge. Selah
'Hear, my people, and let me speak; Israel, and I will warn you — I am God, your God.
It's not for your sacrifices that I reprove you; your burnt offerings are before me continually.
I won't take a young bull from your household, or goats from your folds.
Every living creature of the forest is mine, the animals on a thousand hills.
I know every bird of the mountains, and the moving creatures of the field are with me.
If I were hungry I wouldn't tell you — the world and everything in it are mine.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer God a thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High,
and call on me in the day of distress; I'll rescue you, and you'll honour me.'
But to the wicked God says: 'What right have you to recount my statutes, or take my covenant on your lips?
And you hate discipline; you've thrown my words behind you.
If you saw a thief, you were pleased with him, and your portion was with adulterers.
You let your mouth loose in evil, and your tongue is harnessed to deceit.
You sit and speak against your brother; against your own mother's son you put out slander.
These things you've done and I kept silent; you imagined I was altogether like you. I will reprove you and lay it out before your eyes.
Consider this, you who forget God, or I'll tear you apart, and there'll be no deliverer.
Whoever offers a thanksgiving honours me, and to the one who orders his way I'll show the salvation of God.'

psalms_51.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.
Be gracious to me, God, according to your steadfast love; according to the abundance of your compassion wipe out my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
I myself know my transgressions, and my sin is before me continually.
Against you, you alone, I have sinned, and I've done the evil in your eyes, so that you may be just when you speak, and blameless when you judge.
Look — in iniquity I was brought forth, and in sin my mother conceived me.
Look — you desire truth in the inward places, and in a hidden place you make me know wisdom.
Purify me from sin with hyssop, and I'll be clean; wash me, and I'll become whiter than snow.
Make me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you've crushed rejoice.
Hide your face from my sins, and wipe out all my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Don't cast me away from your presence, and don't take your holy spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and let a willing spirit sustain me.
I'll teach transgressors your ways, and sinners will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, God, God of my salvation; let my tongue shout for joy of your righteousness.
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
You don't desire sacrifice, or I would give it; you're not pleased with a burnt offering.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, God, you won't despise.
Do good to Zion in your good pleasure; build the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you'll delight in sacrifices of righteousness, burnt offering and whole offering; then they'll offer up young bulls on your altar.

psalms_52.t: For the choir director. A maskil of David. When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said to him, 'David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.'
Why do you boast in evil, mighty man? The steadfast love of God lasts all day long.
Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharpened razor, you worker of treachery.
You love evil more than good, lying more than speaking righteousness. Selah
You love all devouring words, a tongue of deceit.
God will tear you down forever too; he'll snatch you up and tear you away from your tent, and root you out of the land of the living. Selah
The righteous will see and fear, and they'll laugh at him:
'Look at the man who didn't make God his stronghold, but trusted in the abundance of his riches and grew strong in his own destruction.'
But I'm like a luxuriant olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
I'll give thanks to you forever, because you have acted; and I'll wait for your name, for it is good, in the presence of your loyal ones.

psalms_53.t: For the choir director, upon mahalath. A maskil of David.
The fool has said to himself, 'There is no God.' They act corruptly and they make injustice abominable; there's no one who does good.
God looked down from the heavens on the children of humankind, to see if there's anyone acting prudently, anyone seeking God.
Every one of them has turned back; together they've gone bad; there's no one who does good — not even one.
Do they not know, these workers of wrongdoing, who devour my people the way they eat bread? They don't call on God.
There they were seized with dread where there was no dread, for God has scattered the bones of the one who encamped against you; you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
Who will grant from Zion the salvation of Israel? When God turns back the captivity of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.

psalms_54.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A maskil of David. When the Ziphites came and said to Saul, 'Isn't David hiding among us?'
God, save me by your name, and by your might give judgement for me.
God, hear my prayer; give ear to the sayings of my mouth.
Strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men have sought my being; they haven't set God before themselves. Selah
Look — God is my helper; the Lord is among those who sustain my being.
May he turn the evil back on those who watch me; in your faithfulness destroy them.
With a freewill offering I'll sacrifice to you; I'll give thanks to your name, LORD, for it is good.
He has delivered me from every distress, and my eye has looked on my enemies.

psalms_55.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A maskil of David.
Give ear to my prayer, God, and don't hide yourself from my supplication.
Attend to me and answer me; I'm restless in my complaint and I moan,
because of the voice of an enemy, because of the pressure of the wicked; they drop wrongdoing on me, and in anger they are hostile to me.
My heart trembles inside me, and the terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fear and trembling come over me, and shuddering has covered me.
And I said, 'Who will give me wings like a dove? I'd fly away and settle down.'
Look — I'd flee far away; I'd lodge in the wilderness. Selah
I'd hurry to a place of escape from the rushing wind, from the storm.
Confuse them, Lord; divide their tongue — I've seen violence and strife in the city.
Day and night they go round it on its walls, and wrongdoing and trouble are inside it.
Destruction is inside it, and oppression and deceit never leave its public square.
It isn't an enemy who taunts me — then I could endure it; it isn't someone who hates me who has magnified himself against me — then I could hide from him.
But it's you, a man of my own rank, my close friend and my acquaintance,
with whom I once made counsel sweet; in the house of God we walked about in the throng.
Let death come on them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive — evils are where they dwell, right inside them.
As for me, I'll call to God, and the LORD will save me.
Evening and morning and noon I complain and murmur, and he has heard my voice.
He has redeemed my being in peace from the battle against me — there were many against me.
God will hear and humble them — he who has sat from of old, Selah — those who have no changes and do not fear God.
He has stretched out his hands against those at peace with him; he has violated his covenant.
His mouth's smooth talk was creamy, but war was in his heart; his words were softer than oil, and they were drawn swords.
Cast your burden on the LORD, and he'll provide for you; he'll never let the righteous be shaken.
And you, God, will bring them down to the well of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit won't live out half their days. But I will trust in you.

psalms_56.t: For the choir director, upon 'The Dove among Terebinths Far Away'. Of David, a miktam. When the Philistines seized him in Gath.
Be gracious to me, God — a human being has crushed me; all day long a fighter oppresses me.
My watchers have crushed me all day long — many are fighting against me proudly.
On a day when I'm afraid, I will trust in you.
In God I praise his word; in God I have trusted, I'm not afraid. What can flesh do to me?
All day long they twist my words; all their plans against me are for evil.
They stir up trouble, they lie hidden; they watch my heels, just as they've waited for my being.
Because of wrongdoing — deliverance for them? In anger bring down peoples, God.
You've taken account of my wandering; put my tears in your skin-bottle — aren't they in your record?
Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call. This I know: God is for me.
In God I praise a word; in the LORD I praise a word.
In God I have trusted, I'm not afraid. What can a human being do to me?
Your vows are on me, God; I'll pay thanksgivings to you.
You have delivered my being from death — haven't you kept my feet from stumbling? — to walk about before God in the light of the living.

psalms_57.t: For the choir director, upon 'Do Not Destroy'. Of David, a miktam. When he fled from Saul, in the cave.
Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me — in you my being takes refuge; and in the shadow of your wings I take refuge until the destruction passes by.
I call to God Most High, to the God who carries things through for me.
He'll send from the heavens and save me; he reproaches the one who crushes me. Selah God will send his steadfast love and his faithfulness.
My being is among lions; I lie among those who devour the children of humankind. Their teeth are spear and arrows, their tongue a sharp sword.
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
They prepared a net for my steps; my being was bowed down. They dug a pit before me, and they have fallen into the middle of it. Selah
My heart is steadfast, God, my heart is steadfast; I'll sing and make music.
Awake, my glory! Awake, harp and lyre! I will waken the dawn.
I'll give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord; I'll make music to you among the nations.
Your steadfast love is great, reaching to the heavens, your faithfulness to the skies.
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.

psalms_58.t: For the choir director, upon 'Do Not Destroy'. Of David, a miktam.
Do you rulers really speak righteousness? Do you judge the children of humankind with uprightness?
Indeed, in your heart you do injustices; in the land you weigh out the violence of your hands.
The wicked are estranged from the womb; those who speak falsehood go astray from birth.
Their venom is like the venom of a serpent, like a deaf cobra that stops its ear,
which doesn't listen to the voice of charmers, however skilful the caster of spells.
God, break away their teeth in their mouth; break off the fangs of the young lions, LORD.
Let them melt away like water that runs off; when he bends his arrows, let them be blunted.
Like a snail that melts away as it goes, like a woman's miscarriage that has never seen the sun.
Before your pots feel the thorn bush, green or burning, he will sweep it away.
The righteous will be glad when he sees vengeance; he'll bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.
And people will say, 'Surely there is fruit for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges in the earth.'

psalms_59.t: For the choir director, upon 'Do Not Destroy'. Of David, a miktam. When Saul sent men, and they watched the house to kill him.
Deliver me from my enemies, my God; set me on high, away from those who rise up against me.
Deliver me from the workers of wrongdoing, and save me from men of bloodshed.
Look — they lie in wait for my being; fierce men attack me, not for my transgression and not for my sin, LORD.
Through no iniquity of mine they run and take their positions. Awake to meet me, and see!
And you, LORD God of hosts, God of Israel, rouse yourself to punish all the nations; don't be gracious to any treacherous workers of wrongdoing. Selah
They return at evening; they growl like a dog and prowl round the city.
Look — they pour out words with their mouth; swords are on their lips — 'Who's listening?' they say.
But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.
His strength — I'll watch for you, because God is my high refuge.
The God of my steadfast love will meet me; God will let me look on my watchers.
Don't kill them, or my people will forget; make them wander by your might and bring them down, our shield, Lord.
The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips; let them be caught in their pride, for the cursing and lying that they speak.
Make an end of them in wrath, make an end, and let them be no more; and let them know that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah
And they return at evening; they growl like a dog and prowl round the city.
They wander about for food; if they aren't satisfied, they stay out all night.
But I'll sing of your strength, and in the morning I'll sing for joy of your steadfast love; you have been a high refuge for me, and a place of flight in the day of my distress.
My strength, to you I'll make music — God is my high refuge, the God of my steadfast love.

psalms_60.t: For the choir director, upon 'The Lily of the Testimony'. A miktam of David, to teach. When he struggled with Aram Naharaim and with Aram Zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
God, you've rejected us, you've broken out against us; you have been angry — restore us!
You've made the land quake, you've split it open; repair its fractures — it is shaking.
You've made your people see hard things; you've made us drink wine that makes us stagger.
You have given a standard to those who fear you, to be raised because of the bow. Selah
so that your beloved ones may be rescued. Save with your right hand, and answer me.
God has spoken in his sanctuary: 'I will exult; I'll divide up Shechem and measure off the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the stronghold of my head, Judah my commander's staff.
Moab is my washing-pot; over Edom I throw my sandal; shout aloud over me, Philistia!'
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who has led me as far as Edom?
Haven't you rejected us, God? And you don't go out, God, with our armies.
Give us help against the foe — human salvation is vain.
In God we'll act with might, and he will tread down our foes.

psalms_61.t: For the choir director, upon a stringed instrument. Of David.
Hear my cry of entreaty, God; attend to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart grows faint; lead me to a rock that's higher than I am.
You have been a refuge for me, a tower of strength against the enemy.
Let me stay as a guest in your tent forever; let me take refuge in the secret place of your wings. Selah
You, God, have listened to my vows; you have given the heritage of those who fear your name.
You'll add days to the days of the king; let his years be like many generations.
May he be enthroned forever before God; appoint steadfast love and faithfulness to preserve him.
So I'll make music to your name forever, paying my vows day after day.

psalms_62.t: For the choir director, upon Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
My being is silent toward God alone; from him comes my salvation.
He alone is my Rock and my salvation, my high refuge — I won't be greatly shaken.
How long will you all attack a man? You'll be murdered, every one of you, like a leaning wall, a fence pushed down.
Surely they plot to thrust him down from his height; they take pleasure in falsehood. With their mouth they bless, and inwardly they curse. Selah
Be silent toward God alone, my being — from him comes my hope.
He alone is my Rock and my salvation, my high refuge — I won't be shaken.
My salvation and my glory rest on God; the Rock of my strength, my refuge, is in God.
Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah
Surely the children of humankind are a breath, the children of man a falsehood; put in the balances, they rise — together they're lighter than a breath.
Don't trust in extortion, and don't put vain hope in robbery; if wealth increases, don't set your heart on it.
One thing God has spoken, two things I have heard: that strength belongs to God,
and that to you, Lord, belongs steadfast love; for you repay each man according to his work.

psalms_63.t: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.
God, you are my God; I seek you earnestly. My being thirsts for you; my flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land without water.
So in the sanctuary I have looked upon you, to see your strength and your glory.
Your steadfast love is better than life; my lips will extol you.
So I'll bless you as long as I live; in your name I'll lift up my hands.
My being will be satisfied as with the richest food, and with joyful lips my mouth will praise you.
When I remember you on my bed, in the night-watches I murmur about you.
You have been my help, and in the shadow of your wings I shout for joy.
My being clings to you; your right hand holds me.
But those who seek my being, to ruin it, will go into the lower parts of the earth.
They'll hand him over to the power of the sword; they'll be the portion of foxes.
And the king will be glad in God; everyone who swears by him will boast, for the mouth of those who speak lies will be shut.

psalms_64.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
Hear my voice, God, in my complaint; preserve my life from dread of an enemy.
Hide me from the secret counsel of evildoers, from the tumult of the workers of wrongdoing,
who sharpen their tongue like a sword, who have bent their bow to shoot a bitter word,
to shoot at the blameless from the hiding places; suddenly they shoot at him and aren't afraid.
They encourage each other in an evil matter; they talk of hiding traps; they say, 'Who will see them?'
They search out injustices: 'We've perfected a well-plotted plot!' And a man's inner being, and the heart, runs deep.
But God shot an arrow at them; suddenly their wounds came.
And they're made to stumble; their own tongue is against them; all who look on them shake their heads.
And all humankind will fear; they'll declare the work of God and consider what he has done.
Let the righteous be glad in the LORD and take refuge in him, and let all the upright in heart boast.

psalms_65.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David. A song.
To you silence is praise, God, in Zion; and to you a vow will be paid.
You who hear prayer — to you all flesh will come.
Matters of iniquity are too strong for me; our transgressions — you atone for them.
How blessed is the one you choose and bring near to dwell in your courts! Let us be satisfied by the goodness of your house, the holy place of your temple.
With awesome deeds in righteousness you answer us, God of our salvation, the trust of all the ends of the earth and of the distant sea,
who establishes the mountains by his strength, girded with might;
who calms the uproar of the seas, the uproar of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
And those who live at the farthest ends are in awe of your signs; you make the going out of morning and evening shout for joy.
You've visited the earth and made it overflow; you greatly enrich it — the stream of God is full of water. You prepare their grain, for so you prepare the earth.
Watering its furrows, settling its ridges; with copious showers you soften it; you bless its growth.
You crown the year with your goodness, and your tracks drip fatness.
The pastures of the wilderness drip, and the hills gird themselves with rejoicing.
The meadows are clothed with flocks, and the valleys cover themselves with grain; they shout aloud, they even sing.

psalms_66.t: For the choir director. A song. A psalm.
Shout aloud to God, all the earth!
Make music to the glory of his name; make his praise glorious.
Say to God, 'How awesome are your works! Through the greatness of your strength your enemies cringe before you.'
All the earth will bow down to you and make music to you; they'll make music to your name. Selah
Come and see the works of God — awesome in his deeds toward the children of humankind.
He turned the sea into dry ground; they crossed the river on foot. There let us be glad in him,
who rules by his might forever; his eyes keep watch on the nations. Let the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah
Bless our God, you peoples, and let the sound of his praise be heard,
who has kept our being among the living, and hasn't let our foot slip.
You have tested us, God; you've refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into the net; you laid a crushing weight on our hips.
You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, and you brought us out to abundance.
I'll come into your house with burnt offerings; I'll pay you my vows,
which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in distress.
I'll offer up to you burnt offerings of fatlings, with the smoke of rams; I'll offer cattle with goats. Selah
Come and listen, all you who fear God, and let me recount what he has done for my being.
I called to him with my mouth, and high praise was under my tongue.
If I had cherished wrongdoing in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But God has heard; he has attended to the sound of my prayer.
Blessed be God, who hasn't turned aside my prayer, or his steadfast love from me.

psalms_67.t: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.
May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine on us. Selah
so that your way may be known on the earth, your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God; let all the peoples give thanks to you.
Let the nations be glad and shout for joy, for you judge the peoples with uprightness, and guide the nations on the earth. Selah
Let the peoples give thanks to you, God; let all the peoples give thanks to you.
The earth has given its produce; God, our God, will bless us.
God will bless us, and all the ends of the earth will fear him.

psalms_68.t: For the choir director. Of David. A psalm. A song.
Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from before him.
As smoke is driven away, drive them away; as wax melts before a fire, let the wicked perish before God.
But the righteous will be glad; they'll exult before God, and be jubilant with gladness.
Sing to God, make music to his name; build up a highway for the one who rides through the deserts — the LORD is his name — and exult before him.
A father of the fatherless and a judge of widows is God in his holy dwelling.
God settles the solitary in a household; he brings out prisoners into prosperity. Only the rebellious dwell in a parched land.
God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wasteland, Selah
the earth quaked, the heavens also poured down before God — the One of Sinai — before God, the God of Israel.
You spread abroad a generous rain, God; your inheritance was weary, and you established it.
Your community settled in it; in your goodness you provided for the afflicted, God.
The Lord gives the utterance; the women who bear the news are a great host.
'Kings of armies flee, they flee!' And the woman who stays at home divides the plunder.
Though you lie down among the sheepfolds — the wings of a dove covered with silver, her pinions with the green sheen of gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
A mountain of God is Mount Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan.
Why do you look with envy, mountains of many peaks, at the mountain God desired for his dwelling? Indeed, the LORD will dwell there forever.
The chariotry of God is twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them — Sinai is in the sanctuary.
You went up on high, you took captives captive; you received gifts among humankind, and even from the rebellious — that the LORD God might dwell there.
Blessed be the Lord day by day; he bears our burden — the God of our salvation. Selah
Our God is a God of saving acts, and to GOD the Lord belong the escapes from death.
Surely God will shatter the head of his enemies, the hairy scalp of the one who goes on in his guilt.
The Lord said, 'From Bashan I'll bring them back; I'll bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so that you may bathe your foot in blood, and the tongue of your dogs have its portion from the enemies.'
They have seen your processions, God, the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
The singers went in front, the musicians behind, among young women playing tambourines.
In the assemblies bless God, the LORD, you who are from the fountain of Israel.
There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
Your God has ordained your strength. Show your strength, God — you who have acted for us!
Because of your temple above Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, trampling down those who delight in pieces of silver. He has scattered the peoples who delight in wars.
Envoys will come from Egypt; Cush will hurry to stretch out its hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; make music to the Lord. Selah
to him who rides in the ancient heaven of heavens. Look — he gives forth his voice, a mighty voice.
Ascribe strength to God! His majesty is over Israel, and his strength is in the skies.
Awesome is God from your sanctuary; the God of Israel — he gives strength and might to the people. Blessed be God!

psalms_69.t: For the choir director, upon 'Lilies'. Of David.
Save me, God — the waters have come up to my neck.
I've sunk in deep mire, and there's no foothold; I've come into deep waters, and a flood has swept over me.
I'm weary with calling; my throat is parched; my eyes have failed while I wait for my God.
Those who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head; those who would destroy me, my lying enemies, are many. What I didn't steal I must then restore.
God, you know my folly, and my guilt isn't hidden from you.
Don't let those who wait for you be put to shame through me, Lord GOD of hosts; don't let those who seek you be humiliated through me, God of Israel.
On your account I have borne reproach; dishonour has covered my face.
I've become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's children.
Zeal for your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.
When I wept for my being with fasting, it became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sit in the gate talk about me; I'm the taunt-song of drinkers of strong drink.
But as for me, my prayer is to you, LORD, at an acceptable time; God, in the abundance of your steadfast love answer me, in the faithfulness of your salvation.
Deliver me from the mud, and don't let me sink; let me be delivered from those who hate me and from the deep waters.
Don't let the flood of waters sweep over me, or the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, LORD — your steadfast love is good; according to the abundance of your compassion turn to me.
And don't hide your face from your servant; I'm in distress — hurry, answer me.
Draw near to my being, act as its kinsman-redeemer; on account of my enemies redeem me.
You know my reproach and my shame and my disgrace; all my adversaries are before you.
Reproach has broken my heart, and I'm sick; I waited for sympathy, and there was none, for comforters, and I found none.
They put poison in my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table before them become a snare, and a trap for their allies.
Let their eyes grow too dim to see, and make their loins shake continually.
Pour out your indignation on them; let your burning anger overtake them.
Let their encampment be made desolate; let no one dwell in their tents.
They've harassed the one you struck, and they tell of the pain of those you have wounded.
Add iniquity to their iniquity, and don't let them enter into your righteousness.
Let them be wiped out from the scroll of the living, and not be written down with the righteous.
But I'm afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, God, set me on high.
I'll praise the name of God with a song, and magnify him with thanksgiving.
And this will please the LORD more than an ox, a young bull with horns and hooves.
The humble have seen it — let them be glad; you who seek God, let your heart live!
The LORD listens to the needy, and he doesn't despise his prisoners.
Let the heavens and the earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah; they'll dwell there and take possession of it.
And the offspring of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell in it.

psalms_70.t: For the choir director. Of David, to bring to remembrance.
God, come and deliver me! LORD, hurry to help me!
Let them be put to shame and abashed, those who seek my being; let them be turned back and humiliated, those who desire my harm.
Let them turn back because of their own shame, those who say, 'Aha! Aha!'
Let all who seek you delight and be glad in you, and let those who love your salvation say continually, 'God is great!'
But I'm afflicted and needy — God, hurry to me! You are my help and the one who brings me to safety; LORD, don't delay.

psalms_71.t: In you, LORD, I've taken refuge; never let me be put to shame.
In your righteousness rescue me and bring me to safety; turn your ear to me and save me.
Be for me a Rock of refuge, one I can always come to; you have given command to save me — you are my rock and my fortress.
My God, bring me to safety from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the wrongdoer and the ruthless.
You are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
I have leaned on you from the womb; you were the one who brought me out of my mother's body; my praise is continually of you.
I've become like a portent to many, but you are my strong refuge.
My mouth is filled with your praise, all day long with your splendour.
Don't cast me away in the time of old age; when my strength fails, don't forsake me.
My enemies speak about me, and those who watch for my being take counsel together,
saying, 'God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him — there's no one to deliver.'
God, don't be far from me; my God, hurry to help me.
Let the accusers of my being be put to shame and come to an end; let those who seek my harm be covered with reproach and disgrace.
But I'll wait continually, and I'll add to all your praise.
My mouth will recount your righteousness, all day long your salvation, though I don't know their number.
I'll come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; I'll bring to remembrance your righteousness, yours alone.
God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I declare your wonders.
And even to old age and grey hair, God, don't forsake me, until I declare your arm to a generation, your might to all who are to come.
And your righteousness, God, reaches to the height — you who have done great things. God, who is like you?
You who have made us see many distresses and calamities will return and preserve us alive, and from the depths of the earth you will return and bring me up.
Increase my greatness, and turn and comfort me.
I too will praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God; I'll make music to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy when I make music to you, and so will my being, which you have redeemed.
My tongue too will murmur your righteousness all day long, because they are put to shame, they are abashed, those who seek my harm.

psalms_72.t: Of Solomon.
God, give your judgements to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son.
May he judge your people with righteousness, and your afflicted ones with justice.
Let the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills, in righteousness.
May he judge the afflicted of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
May they fear you as long as the sun endures, and before the moon, through all generations.
May he come down like rain on mown grass, like copious showers that water the earth.
In his days let the righteous flourish, and abundance of peace till the moon is no more.
And may he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
Before him let the desert-dwellers bow down, and let his enemies lick the dust.
May the kings of Tarshish and the islands bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba bring a gift.
And let all kings bow down to him; let all nations serve him.
He will deliver the needy who cries for help, and the afflicted who has no helper.
He'll have compassion on the poor and the needy, and save the lives of the needy.
From oppression and from violence he'll redeem their being, and their blood will be precious in his eyes.
And may he live, and may gold of Sheba be given to him; may prayer be made for him continually; all day long may he be blessed.
Let there be an abundance of grain in the land, on the tops of the mountains; let its fruit wave like Lebanon, and let people blossom from the city like the vegetation of the earth.
May his name endure forever; before the sun may his name increase, and may they bless themselves by him; may all nations call him blessed.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed be his glorious name forever; let his glory fill all the earth. Amen and amen.
The prayers of David, the son of Jesse, are ended.

psalms_73.t: A psalm of Asaph.
God really is good to Israel — to the ones whose hearts are pure.
But me — my feet had nearly gone out from under me; my steps had all but poured away.
I was jealous of the arrogant — I kept looking at how well the wicked were doing.
There's no pain in their dying; their belly is fat.
They're not in the trouble everyone else is in; they don't get hit the way people do.
So pride is the chain around their neck; violence is the robe that covers them.
Their eyes bulge out of the fat; their heart's imaginings run right over.
They mock, and their talk is malicious; from up on high they speak oppression.
They set their mouth in the heavens; their tongue walks the earth.
So his people come back around here, and they drain the full waters dry.
And they say, 'How would God know? Does the Most High even have knowledge?'
Look at them: these are the wicked — always comfortable, always getting richer.
So it was all for nothing — keeping my heart pure, washing my hands in innocence.
I've been stricken all day long, and rebuked every morning.
If I'd said, 'I'll talk that way,' I'd have been false to a whole generation of your children.
When I tried to understand it, it was nothing but trouble to me.
until I went into the sanctuaries of God — then I understood how they end.
You've put them on slick ground; you bring them down into ruin.
In a moment they're a desolation — done, finished off by terrors.
Like a dream when someone wakes up — Lord, when you rouse yourself you'll despise their image.
When my heart turned sour and I was stabbed through the kidneys,
then I was stupid and knew nothing; I was an animal with you.
But I'm always with you; you've taken hold of my right hand.
You guide me by your counsel, and afterwards you'll receive me to glory.
Who else do I have in the heavens? And next to you there's nothing on earth I want.
My flesh and my heart give out; God is the Rock of my heart, my share, for ever.
Look — everyone far from you will perish; you finish off everyone who whores away from you.
But me — being near God is good for me. I've made the Lord GOD my refuge, so I can tell everything you've done.

psalms_74.t: A maskil of Asaph.
Why have you cast us off for good, God? Why is your anger smoking against the sheep of your own pasture?
Remember the congregation you acquired long ago, the tribe you redeemed as your own inheritance — Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
Lift your steps toward the ruins that never end — all the harm the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
Your foes roared right inside your meeting place; they planted their signs there as signs.
It looked like men bringing axes up into a stand of trees.
And now they're smashing all its carved work with axe and hatchets.
They've put your sanctuary to the fire; they've profaned the dwelling place of your name, right down to the ground.
They said to themselves, 'Let's crush them all at once.' They burned every meeting place of God in the land.
We don't see our own signs any more; there's no prophet left, and nobody with us knows how long.
How long, God, is the foe going to taunt? Is the enemy going to spurn your name for ever?
Why do you pull your hand back, your right hand? Out of your bosom — destroy!
But God has been my king from long ago, working salvation right in the middle of the earth.
You split the sea open with your strength; you smashed the heads of the sea creatures on the water.
You crushed Leviathan's heads; you gave him as food to a people, to desert-dwellers.
You broke open spring and torrent; you dried up rivers that never run dry.
The day is yours, the night is yours too; you set the light and the sun in place.
You set every boundary of the earth; summer and winter — you formed them.
Remember this: an enemy has taunted, LORD; a foolish people have spurned your name.
Don't hand the being of your turtledove over to the beast; don't forget the life of your poor, ever.
Look to the covenant — the dark places of the land are full of the dwellings of violence.
Don't let the crushed go back humiliated; let the poor and the needy praise your name.
Get up, God, argue your own case; remember the reproach you take from a fool all day long.
Don't forget the voice of your foes, the uproar of those who rise against you, going up all the time.

psalms_75.t: For the choir director. 'Do Not Destroy'. A psalm of Asaph. A song.
We give you thanks, God, we give you thanks; your name is near, and people tell of your wonders.
'When I take the appointed time, I'm the one who will judge, and judge fairly.'
'The earth and everyone in it are melting away; I'm the one who set its pillars firm. Selah.'
I said to the boastful, 'Don't boast,' and to the wicked, 'Don't lift up your horn —
don't lift your horn up high; don't talk with your neck stuck out.'
Because it isn't from the east or the west, and not from the wilderness, that lifting up comes.
God is the judge: he brings one down and lifts another up.
There's a cup in the LORD's hand, the wine foaming, full of spices, and he pours from it; and all the wicked of the earth will drain the dregs and drink them down.
But I'll declare it for ever; I'll make music to the God of Jacob.
'I'll cut off every horn of the wicked; the horns of the righteous will be lifted up.'

psalms_76.t: For the choir director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.
God is known in Judah; in Israel his name is great.
His lair is in Salem, his den in Zion.
There he shattered the bow's flames, shield and sword and battle. Selah.
You shine out, more majestic than the mountains of prey.
The stout-hearted were stripped bare; they slept their sleep, and not one of the warriors could find his hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, chariot and horse both lay stunned in sleep.
You — you're the one to be feared. Who can stand in front of you once your anger comes?
From the heavens you made your verdict heard; the earth was afraid and went quiet.
when God rose up to judge, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah.
Even the wrath of humankind gives you thanks; the wrath that's left, you put on like a belt.
Make your vows and pay them to the LORD your God; let everyone around him bring tribute to the one to be feared.
He cuts off the spirit of rulers; the kings of the earth have to fear him.

psalms_77.t: For the choir director. According to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.
My voice goes up to God, and I cry out; my voice goes up to God, and he listens to me.
On the day of my distress I went looking for the Lord; all night my hand was stretched out and never went numb; my being refused to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan; I complain, and my spirit faints away. Selah.
You held my eyelids open; I was too troubled to speak.
I thought about the days of old, the years long past.
At night I remember my song; I complain to my own heart, and my spirit goes searching.
Is the Lord going to reject us for ever, and never show favour again?
Has his steadfast love run out for good? Has his utterance ceased for all generations?
Has God forgotten how to be gracious? Has he shut his compassion off in anger? Selah.
And I said, 'This is my grief — that the right hand of the Most High has changed.'
I'll remember what the LORD has done; I'll remember your wonder from long ago.
I'll go over everything you've done; I'll dwell on your deeds.
God, your way is in holiness. What god is great the way God is?
You're the God who does wonder; you've made your strength known among the peoples.
You redeemed your people with your arm, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God; the waters saw you and writhed; the deeps trembled too.
The clouds poured out water; the skies gave out their sound; your arrows went flying about.
The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
Your way went through the sea, your path through many waters, and nobody knew your footprints.
You led your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

psalms_78.t: A maskil of Asaph.
Listen, my people, to my law; turn your ear to the sayings of my mouth.
I'll open my mouth in a parable; I'll pour out riddles from long ago.
things we've heard and known, that our fathers told us.
We won't hide them from their children; we'll tell a later generation the praises of the LORD and his might, and the wonders he has done.
He set up a testimony in Jacob, appointed a law in Israel, and commanded our fathers to make it known to their children,
so a later generation would know — children not yet born — and would get up and tell their own children,
so they'd put their confidence in God, not forget what God has done, and keep his commandments;
and wouldn't be like their fathers — a stubborn, rebellious generation, a generation that never set its heart firm, whose spirit was never faithful to God.
The sons of Ephraim, armed and shooting the bow, turned back on the day of battle.
They didn't keep God's covenant; they refused to walk in his law.
They forgot what he had done, the wonders he had shown them.
In front of their fathers he did wonder in the land of Egypt, the region of Zoan.
He split the sea open and brought them through; he made the waters stand up like a heap.
He guided them with the cloud by day, and all night by the light of a fire.
He split open rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink in abundance, as from the deeps.
He brought streams out of a rock and made the water run down like rivers.
But they kept on sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High in the parched land.
They tested God in their heart, asking for food to satisfy themselves.
They spoke against God. They said, 'Can God set a table in the wilderness?'
'Look — he struck a rock and water came pouring out, torrents overflowing. But can he give bread too? Can he provide meat for his people?'
So the LORD heard and was furious; fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel —
because they didn't believe in God and didn't trust his salvation.
Yet he gave orders to the skies above and opened the doors of the heavens,
and rained manna down on them to eat, and gave them the grain of the heavens.
Everyone ate the bread of the mighty; he sent them provision till they had enough.
He set an east wind loose in the heavens and drove out a south wind by his strength.
He rained meat down on them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas.
He made them fall right in the middle of the camp, all around his dwelling places.
They ate and had more than enough — he brought them exactly what they craved.
They hadn't turned away from what they craved; their food was still in their mouths
when God's anger rose against them. He killed their strongest, and brought the young men of Israel down.
In spite of all this they kept on sinning and didn't believe in his wonders.
So he ended their days in futility, their years in sudden terror.
Every time he killed them they sought him; they turned back and went looking hard for God.
They remembered that God was their Rock, God Most High their redeemer.
But they deceived him with their mouth and lied to him with their tongue.
Their heart wasn't steadfast with him; they weren't faithful to his covenant.
But he was compassionate. He made atonement for iniquity and didn't destroy them. Time after time he turned his anger back and didn't stir up all his rage.
He remembered they were flesh — a wind that goes and doesn't come back.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, how often they grieved him in the wasteland!
Again and again they tested God and pained the Holy One of Israel.
They didn't remember his hand, the day he ransomed them from the foe,
when he performed his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the region of Zoan,
He turned their canals to blood, so they couldn't drink from their streams.
He sent the swarm among them, and it devoured them; frogs, and they ruined them.
He gave their produce to the shearer-locust, and everything their labour won to the swarming locust.
He killed their vines with hail, their sycamore-figs with frost.
He handed their cattle over to the hail, their livestock to the flames.
He sent his burning anger against them, fury and indignation and trouble, a deputation of angels of calamity.
He levelled a path for his anger; he didn't hold them back from death — he handed their life over to the pestilence.
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the first of their vigour in the tents of Ham.
He led his people out like sheep and drove them like a flock in the wilderness.
He guided them safely, and they weren't afraid; and the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to the territory of his holiness, to this mountain his right hand had acquired.
He drove out nations ahead of them, allotted their inheritance by measuring-line, and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
But they tested and rebelled against God Most High, and didn't keep his testimonies.
They turned back and acted treacherously, just like their fathers; they twisted like a treacherous bow.
They provoked him to anger with their high places and made him jealous with their carved images.
God heard and was furious; he rejected Israel completely.
He abandoned the dwelling place at Shiloh, the tent he had pitched among humankind.
He gave his strength over to captivity, his splendour into the hand of the foe.
He handed his people over to the sword and was furious with his own inheritance.
Fire consumed their young men, and their virgins went unpraised.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows didn't weep.
Then the Lord woke like a sleeper, like a warrior overcome by wine.
He drove his foes back with a blow and gave them a reproach that never ends.
He rejected the tent of Joseph and didn't choose the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth he founded for ever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds.
He brought him in from following the nursing ewes to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with an honest heart and guided them with the skill of his hands.

psalms_79.t: God, the nations have come into your inheritance; they've made the temple of your holiness unclean; they've left Jerusalem in heaps of ruins.
They've given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the heavens, the flesh of your loyal ones to the beasts of the earth.
They've poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there was nobody to bury them.
We've become a reproach to our neighbours, mockery and derision to everyone around us.
How long, LORD? Are you going to be angry for ever? Is your jealousy going to burn like fire?
Pour out your rage on the nations that don't know you, on the kingdoms that don't call on your name.
For they've consumed Jacob and devastated his habitation.
Don't hold the iniquities of earlier generations against us; let your compassion come to meet us quickly — we've been brought very low.
Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us, make atonement for our sins, for your name's sake.
Why should the nations say, 'Where is their God?' Let it be known among the nations, right before our eyes, that you avenge the poured-out blood of your servants.
Let the prisoner's groaning come before you; by the greatness of your arm, leave alive those under sentence of death.
Pay our neighbours back sevenfold into their bosom for the reproach they reproached you with, Lord.
And we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will give you thanks for ever; generation after generation we'll recount your praise.

psalms_80.t: For the choir director. To 'Lilies, Testimony'. Of Asaph. A psalm.
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a flock; you who sit enthroned on the cherubim, shine out.
In front of Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might; come and save us.
God, restore us; make your face shine, and let us be saved.
LORD, God of hosts, how long will you smoke at your people's prayer?
You've fed them the bread of tears and made them drink tears by the measureful.
You make us something our neighbours fight over, and our enemies mock us among themselves.
God of hosts, restore us; make your face shine, and let us be saved.
You uprooted a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground ahead of it; it took root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered with its shade; its boughs were the cedars of God.
It sent its branches out to the sea, its shoots to the River.
Why have you broken down its walls, so everyone passing along the road plucks at it?
A boar out of the forest gnaws at it; whatever moves in the field grazes on it.
God of hosts, please turn back; look down from the heavens and see; attend to this vine —
and the stock your right hand planted, and the son you made strong for yourself.
It's burned with fire, cut down; at the rebuke of your face they perish.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, on the son of humankind you made strong for yourself.
Then we won't turn back from you; give us life, and we'll call on your name.
LORD, God of hosts, restore us; make your face shine, and let us be saved.

psalms_81.t: For the choir director. According to the Gittith. Of Asaph.
Shout for joy to God our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob.
Raise a song and strike up the tambourine, the sweet lyre along with the harp.
Blow the ram's horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on the day of our festival.
It's a statute for Israel, a judgement of the God of Jacob.
He set it up as a testimony in Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt. I heard a language I didn't know:
'I took the load off his shoulder; his hands were freed from the basket.
You called in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the secret place of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
'Listen, my people, and let me warn you. Israel — if only you'd listen to me!
'You shall have no strange god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.
'I am the LORD your God, the one who brought you up out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I'll fill it.
'But my people didn't listen to my voice; Israel wouldn't have me.
'So I handed them over to their stubborn heart; they walked in their own schemes.
'If only my people would listen to me, if Israel would walk in my ways!
'It would take me no time to subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.
'Those who hate the LORD would cringe before him, and their fate would last for ever.
'He would feed them the finest of the wheat, and from a rock I'd satisfy you with honey.'

psalms_82.t: God takes his stand in the divine congregation; in the middle of the gods he gives judgement.
How long are you going to judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah.
Give judgement for the poor and the fatherless; vindicate the afflicted and the destitute.
Rescue the poor and the needy; get them out of the hand of the wicked.
They don't know and they don't understand; they walk about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I said myself, 'You are gods, sons of the Most High, every one of you.'
