Let my tongue cleave to my palate if I don't remember you, if I don't set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
Remember, LORD, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem — the ones who said, 'Lay it bare, lay it bare, down to its foundation!'
Daughter of Babylon, you who are to be destroyed — how blessed is the one who pays you back what you dealt out to us!
How blessed is the one who grabs your infants and smashes them against the rock!

psalms_138.t: I'll give you thanks with all my heart; before the gods I'll make music to you.
I'll bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness; you've made your speech great above all your name.
The day I called, you answered me; you made me bold, with strength in my being.
All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, LORD, once they hear the sayings of your mouth,
and they'll sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
The LORD is exalted, yet he sees the lowly; the proud he knows from afar.
Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you give me life; you stretch out your hand against my enemies' anger, and your right hand saves me.
The LORD will accomplish what concerns me; LORD, your steadfast love is for ever — don't abandon the works of your hands.

psalms_139.t: For the choir director. Of David. A psalm.
LORD, you've examined me and known me.
You know when I sit down and when I get up; you understand my thought from far off.
My travelling and my lying down you sift out; you know all my ways intimately.
Before a word is even on my tongue, look — LORD, you know all of it.
Behind and before you have enclosed me; you've laid your hand on me.
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it's set too high — I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from your spirit? Where can I flee from your presence?
If I go up to the heavens, you're there; if I make my bed in Sheol, there you are.
If I take the wings of the dawn and settle at the far end of the sea,
even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will keep hold of me.
So I said, 'Surely darkness will crush me, and the light around me will be night' —
even the darkness isn't dark to you; night shines like the day — darkness and light are the same.
You created my kidneys; you wove me together in my mother's womb.
I'll give you thanks, because I am fearsomely and wonderfully made; your works are wonders, and my being knows it well.
My frame wasn't hidden from you when I was made in the secret place, embroidered in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in your scroll they were all written down — the days that were formed, and one of them was for it.
And to me — how precious are your thoughts, God! How vast their sum!
If I tried to count them, they'd outnumber the sand; I awake, and I am still with you.
If only you would kill the wicked, God! You men of blood, get away from me —
the ones who speak of you with wicked intent, your enemies take your name in vain.
Don't I hate those who hate you, LORD, and loathe those who rise up against you?
With perfect hatred I hate them; they've become my enemies.
Examine me, God, and know my heart; put me to the test and know my disquieting thoughts.
And see whether there's any hurtful way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.

psalms_140.t: For the choir director. A psalm of David.
Rescue me, LORD, from the evil man; preserve me from the violent man —
those who plan evil in their heart, who stir up wars all day long.
They sharpen their tongue like a serpent; viper's venom is under their lips. Selah.
Keep me, LORD, out of the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man — those who plan to trip up my footsteps.
The proud have hidden a trap for me, and cords; they've spread a net beside the path; they've set snares for me. Selah.
I said to the LORD, 'You're my God'; give ear, LORD, to the sound of my supplications.
GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you covered my head on the day of battle.
Don't grant the desires of the wicked, LORD; don't promote his plot, or they'll be exalted. Selah.
As for the head of those who surround me — let the mischief of their own lips cover them.
Let burning coals fall on them; let them be thrown into the fire, into pits, never to rise.
Let the slanderer not be established in the land; let evil hunt down the man of violence, blow after blow.
I know the LORD will maintain the cause of the poor, the justice of the needy.
Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will live in your presence.

psalms_141.t: LORD, I'm calling on you — hurry to me; give ear to my voice when I call to you.
Let my prayer be set before you like incense, the lifting of my hands like the evening offering.
Set a guard over my mouth, LORD; keep watch at the door of my lips.
Don't turn my heart to anything evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds alongside men who do wickedness; and don't let me eat their delicacies.
Let a righteous man strike me — it is steadfast love; let him rebuke me — it is oil for the head; let my head not refuse it. My prayer is still against their evil deeds.
Their judges have been thrown down from the sides of a rock, and they'll hear my sayings — they are pleasant.
As when someone plows and breaks open the earth, our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
My eyes are toward you, GOD the Lord; in you I take refuge — don't pour out my life.
Keep me from the jaws of the trap they've laid for me, from the snares of those who do wickedness.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets, all together, while I go past.

psalms_142.t: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.
With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I beg the LORD for favour.
I pour out my complaint before him; I tell him my trouble.
When my spirit faints away within me, you know my pathway. On the path where I walk they've hidden a trap for me.
Look to the right and see — there's no one who recognises me; every place of escape is lost to me; no one cares for my life.
I cry out to you, LORD; I say, 'You're my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.'
Attend to my cry of entreaty — I've been brought very low. Deliver me from those who harass me; they're stronger than I am.
Bring me out of prison, so I can give thanks to your name. The righteous will surround me, because you will deal bountifully with me.

psalms_143.t: LORD, hear my prayer; give ear to my supplications; answer me in your constancy, in your righteousness.
And don't enter into judgement with your servant; no one living is righteous before you.
An enemy has pursued my life; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead.
My spirit faints away within me; inside me my heart is appalled.
I've remembered the days of old; I've meditated on all your deeds; I muse on the work of your hands.
I've spread out my hands to you; my throat thirsts for you like a parched land. Selah.
Hurry, answer me, LORD — my spirit is spent. Don't hide your face from me, or I'll be like those who go down to the pit.
Let me hear your steadfast love in the morning; in you I have trusted. Make known to me the way I should go; to you I lift up my being.
Deliver me from my enemies, LORD; to you I've fled for cover.
Teach me to do your will — you are my God. May your good spirit lead me on level ground.
For your name's sake, LORD, give me life; in your righteousness bring me out of trouble.
And in your steadfast love cut off my enemies and destroy all who oppress my life — I am your servant.

psalms_144.t: Blessed be the LORD my Rock — the one who trains my hands for war, my fingers for battle;
my steadfast love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer, my shield, the one I take refuge in, who subdues my people under me.
LORD, what is humankind, that you take knowledge of them, a child of humanity, that you should regard them?
Humankind is just like a breath; their days are like a shadow passing by.
LORD, bend your heavens down and come down; touch the mountains, and they'll smoke.
Flash out lightning and scatter them; send your arrows and rout them.
Stretch your hands out from on high; set me free and deliver me from the great waters, from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouth speaks falsehood, whose right hand is a right hand of deception.
God, I'll sing a new song to you; on a ten-stringed harp I'll make music to you,
the one who gives deliverance to kings, who sets David his servant free from the evil sword.
Set me free and deliver me from the hand of foreigners — whose mouth speaks falsehood, whose right hand is a right hand of deception —
so our sons may be like plants full-grown in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars, carved for the structure of a palace;
our granaries full, providing every kind of store; our flocks bringing forth thousands, ten thousands out in our fields;
our cattle heavy with young; no loss, no miscarrying, no outcry in our streets.
How blessed are the people for whom it is so! How blessed are the people whose God is the LORD!

psalms_145.t: A praise. Of David.
I'll exalt you, my God the King, and bless your name for ever and ever.
Every day I'll bless you, and praise your name for ever and ever.
Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; his greatness is unsearchable.
One generation to another will extol your works and declare your mighty deeds.
I'll meditate on the majesty of the glory of your splendour, and on the story of your wonders.
They'll tell of the might of your fearsome deeds, and I'll recount your greatness.
They'll pour out the remembrance of your abundant goodness and shout for joy at your righteousness.
The LORD is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in steadfast love.
The LORD is good to everyone, and his compassion is over all his works.
Every one of your works will give you thanks, LORD, and your loyal ones will bless you.
They'll tell of the glory of your kingdom and speak of your might,
to make his mighty deeds known to the children of humankind, and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages; your dominion endures through all generations.
The LORD holds up everyone who falls and raises up everyone bent down.
The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food at the right time.
You open your hand and satisfy the desire of everything living.
The LORD is righteous in all his ways, loyal in all his works.
The LORD is near to everyone who calls on him, to everyone who calls on him in truth.
He brings about what those who fear him desire; he hears their cry for help and saves them.
The LORD guards everyone who loves him, but all the wicked he will destroy.
My mouth will speak the LORD's praise, and all flesh will bless his holy name for ever and ever.

psalms_146.t: Hallelujah. Praise the LORD, my being!
I'll praise the LORD as long as I live; I'll make music to my God while I still am.
Don't trust in nobles, in a mortal, in whom there is no deliverance.
His breath goes out, he returns to his ground; that very day his plans perish.
How blessed is the one who has the God of Jacob for help, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
who made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them, who keeps faithfulness for ever,
the one who does justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free;
The LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD raises up those bent down; the LORD loves the righteous.
The LORD watches over sojourners; he upholds the fatherless and the widow, but he makes the way of the wicked crooked.
The LORD will reign for ever, your God, Zion, through every generation. Hallelujah.

psalms_147.t: Hallelujah. It's good to make music to our God; it's pleasant, and praise is fitting.
The LORD is the one building Jerusalem; he gathers the banished of Israel.
the one who heals the broken-hearted and binds up their wounds,
he counts the number of the stars and calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord, abundant in power; his understanding is beyond number.
The LORD lifts up the humble; he brings the wicked low to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the lyre,
the one who covers the heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains.
who gives the beast its food, and the young ravens when they cry out.
He doesn't delight in the horse's strength; he takes no pleasure in a man's legs.
The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those hoping for his steadfast love.
Extol the LORD, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion!
He has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you.
the one who makes peace in your territory; he satisfies you with the finest of wheat.
he sends his speech to the earth; his word runs very swiftly.
he gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes.
he throws his ice down like crumbs — who can stand before his cold?
He sends out his word and melts them; he makes his wind blow, and the waters flow.
He declares his words to Jacob, his statutes and judgements to Israel.
He hasn't done that for any nation; as for his judgements, they don't know them. Hallelujah.

psalms_148.t: Hallelujah. Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts.
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you stars of light.
Praise him, highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens.
Let them praise the name of the LORD — he commanded, and they were created.
He established them for ever and ever; he gave a statute that will not pass away.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea creatures and all the deeps,
fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind that does his word,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all livestock, creeping things and winged birds,
kings of the earth and all peoples, officials and all judges of the earth,
young men and virgins alike, old and young together.
Let them praise the name of the LORD — his name alone is exalted; his splendour is above earth and heavens.
And he has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his loyal ones, for the Israelites, a people near to him. Hallelujah.

psalms_149.t: Hallelujah. Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the loyal.
Let Israel rejoice in its maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their king.
Let them praise his name with dancing; with tambourine and lyre let them make music to him.
For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation.
Let the loyal exult in honour; let them shout for joy on their beds.
The high praises of God in their throat, and a two-edged sword in their hand,
to execute vengeance on the nations, punishments on the peoples,
to bind their kings with fetters and their nobles with shackles of iron,
to execute on them the judgement that is written — that is honour for all his loyal ones. Hallelujah.

psalms_150.t: Hallelujah. Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in the vault of his strength.
Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his abundant greatness.
Praise him with the blast of the ram's horn; praise him with harp and lyre.
Praise him with tambourine and dancing; praise him with strings and pipe.
Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with shouting cymbals.
Let everything that breathes praise the LORD. Hallelujah.

ruth_1.t: Back when the judges were judging, a famine hit the land. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live for a while in Moab — he and his wife and his two sons.
The man's name was Elimelech, his wife was Naomi, and his two sons were Mahlon and Kilion — Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They reached Moab and settled in.
Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
They married Moabite women — one named Orpah, the other Ruth — and they lived there about ten years.
Then both of them died too — Mahlon and Kilion — and the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
So she got up, she and her daughters-in-law, to head back from Moab — she'd heard there that the LORD had come to his people and given them bread.
She left the place where she'd been, her two daughters-in-law with her, and they started down the road back to Judah.
But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go on — each of you go back to your mother's house. May the LORD treat you with steadfast love, the way you've treated the dead and me.
May the LORD grant you each a place of rest in a husband's house." Then she kissed them, and they broke down and wept.
And they said, "No — we're going back with you, to your people."
But Naomi said, "Go back, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons inside me who could become your husbands?
Go back, my daughters, go. I'm too old to have a husband. Even if I said, 'There's hope for me' — even if I had a husband tonight and even bore sons —

— would you wait, then, until they were grown? Would you, then, refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters. It's far more bitter for me than for you, because the LORD's own hand has gone out against me."
So they broke down and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye — but Ruth clung to her.
And she said, "Look — your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods. Go back after her."

But Ruth said, "Don't press me to leave you, to turn back from following you. Where you go, I'll go; where you spend the night, I'll spend the night. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Where you die, I'll die, and there I'll be buried. May the LORD do so to me, and worse, if anything but death separates us."
When Naomi saw she was set on going with her, she stopped arguing.
So the two of them travelled on until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was stirred up over them, and the women said, "Is this Naomi?"
But she said, "Don't call me Naomi. Call me Mara — the Almighty has made it very bitter for me.
I went out full, and the LORD brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought harm on me?"
So Naomi came back, and with her was Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who had come back from Moab. They arrived in Bethlehem just as the barley harvest was starting.

ruth_2.t: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side — a man of real standing, from Elimelech's clan. His name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the field and glean among the ears of grain behind whoever will show me favour." And she said, "Go ahead, my daughter."
So she went out and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came upon the piece of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was from Elimelech's clan.
And there was Boaz, coming out from Bethlehem. He said to the harvesters, "The LORD be with you," and they answered, "May the LORD bless you."
Then Boaz asked the young man in charge of the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"
The young man in charge of the harvesters answered, "She's a Moabite young woman — the one who came back with Naomi from Moab.
She said, 'Let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came, and she's been at it from morning until now — she's barely rested at all."
Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Don't go glean in another field, and don't move on from this one — stay close by with my young women.

Keep your eyes on the field they're harvesting and go along behind them. Haven't I told the young men not to touch you? And when you're thirsty, go over to the jars and drink what the young men have drawn."
She fell on her face and bowed to the ground, and said to him, "Why have I found favour in your eyes — why take notice of me, when I'm a foreigner?"

Boaz answered her, "I've been told everything you've done for your mother-in-law since your husband died — how you left your father and mother and your native land and went to a people you'd never known.
May the LORD repay what you've done, and may your wages be full from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you've come to take refuge."
And she said, "May I find favour in your eyes, my lord — you've comforted me, you've spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I'm not even the equal of one of your maidservants."

At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here, have some bread, and dip your piece in the sour wine." So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he held out roasted grain to her, and she ate her fill and had some left over.
When she got up to glean, Boaz gave his young men orders: "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don't humiliate her.
And pull some out for her from the bundles and leave it there for her to glean — and don't rebuke her."
So she gleaned in the field until evening, then beat out what she'd gleaned — about an ephah of barley.
She picked it up and carried it into town, and her mother-in-law saw what she'd gleaned. She also brought out and gave her what was left over after she'd eaten her fill.

Her mother-in-law asked, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you." So she told her mother-in-law whom she'd worked with: "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz."

And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed be he by the LORD, who hasn't abandoned his steadfast love toward the living or the dead." And Naomi added, "The man is a close relative of ours — he's one of our kinsman-redeemers."
And Ruth the Moabite said, "He even said to me, 'Stay close by my young men until they've finished all my harvest.'"
And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It's good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women — that way no one sets upon you in another field."
So she stayed close by Boaz's young women, gleaning until the barley and wheat harvests were done — and she went on living with her mother-in-law.

ruth_3.t: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, shouldn't I look for a place of rest for you, so that things go well for you?
And now — isn't Boaz our kinsman, the one whose young women you've been with? Look, tonight he's winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
So wash, anoint yourself, put on your clothes, and go down to the threshing floor. Don't let him know you're there until he's finished eating and drinking.
And when he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down — and he'll tell you what to do."
And she said, "Everything you tell me, I'll do."
So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.
Boaz ate and drank, and he was in good spirits, and he went to lie down at the end of the grain heap. Then she came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
In the middle of the night the man gave a start and turned over — and there was a woman lying at his feet.
He said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I'm Ruth, your slave woman. Spread your wing over your slave woman — you are a kinsman-redeemer."
And he said, "Blessed be you by the LORD, my daughter. This last act of steadfast love of yours is better than the first — you haven't gone after the young men, poor or rich.
And now, my daughter, don't be afraid. Everything you ask I'll do for you, because the whole gate of my people knows you're a woman of ability.
And now — it's true that I'm a kinsman-redeemer, but there's another one nearer of kin than I am.
Stay the night. In the morning, if he'll redeem you, good — let him redeem. But if he isn't willing to, then I'll redeem you myself, as the LORD lives. Lie down until morning."
So she lay at his feet until morning and got up before anyone could recognise anyone else. And he said, "Don't let it be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
And he said, "Hold out the shawl you're wearing." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and lifted it onto her; and he went into town.
When she came to her mother-in-law, Naomi said, "Who are you, my daughter?" And she told her all that the man had done for her.
And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley — he told me, 'Don't go back empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
And she said, "Sit still, my daughter, until you know how this falls out — the man won't rest until he's settled it today."

ruth_4.t: Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there. And there was the kinsman-redeemer he'd spoken about, passing by. He said, "Turn aside, sit down here, So-and-so." So he turned aside and sat down.
Then he took ten of the town's elders and said, "Sit down here." And they sat down.
Then he said to the kinsman-redeemer, "Naomi, who's come back from Moab, is selling the piece of field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

So I thought I'd bring it into the open and say: acquire it here in front of those sitting by and the elders of my people. If you'll redeem it, redeem it; and if you won't, tell me, so I know — there's no one but you to redeem, and I come after you." And he said, "I'll redeem it."
Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from Naomi's hand, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the dead man's wife, to raise up the dead man's name over his inheritance."
And the kinsman-redeemer said, "I can't redeem it for myself — I'd ruin my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself. I can't redeem."

Now this was the practice in Israel in earlier times, for redemption and for exchange, to confirm any matter: a man would take off his sandal and hand it to the other party. That was how a thing was attested in Israel.
So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire it for yourself" — and he drew off his sandal.

Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "You are witnesses today that I've acquired everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Kilion and Mahlon, from Naomi's hand.

And Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's wife, I've also acquired as my wife, to raise up the dead man's name over his inheritance, so that his name won't be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today."

And all the people at the gate, and the elders, said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman coming into your house like Rachel and like Leah, the two who built the house of Israel. Act with ability in Ephrathah, and make a name in Bethlehem.
And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman."
So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went in to her, and the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son.
Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who hasn't left you today without a kinsman-redeemer. May his name be proclaimed in Israel.
He'll be one who restores your life and sustains you in your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loves you has borne him — and she's better to you than seven sons."
Then Naomi took the child and laid him in her lap, and she became his nurse.
And the women of the neighbourhood gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." They called his name Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
Now these are the generations of Perez. Perez fathered Hezron,
Hezron fathered Ram, Ram fathered Amminadab,
Amminadab fathered Nahshon, Nahshon fathered Salmon,
Salmon fathered Boaz, Boaz fathered Obed,
Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

song of songs_1.t: Let him kiss me — kiss me with his mouth! Your lovemaking is better than wine.
Your oils smell good; your name is oil poured out. That's why the young women love you.
Pull me after you — let's run. The king has brought me into his rooms. Let's rejoice, let's be glad in you; let's remember your lovemaking more than wine. They're right to love you.
I'm black and lovely, daughters of Jerusalem — like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
Don't stare at me because I'm dark, because the sun has looked at me. My mother's sons were angry with me; they made me keep the vineyards — and my own vineyard I haven't kept.
Tell me, you whom my being loves — where do you graze? Where do you bed your flock down at noon? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside your friends' flocks?
If you don't know, most beautiful of women, go out and follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats beside where the shepherds stay.
You, my companion — you're like a mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are lovely with their strings of ornament, your neck with its beads.
We'll make you strings of gold, with studs of silver.
While the king was at his table, my nard gave off its scent.
My beloved is a bag of myrrh to me, spending the night between my breasts.
My beloved is a cluster of henna to me, in the vineyards of En Gedi.
Look at you — beautiful, my companion; look at you, beautiful. Your eyes are doves.
Look at you — beautiful, my beloved, and pleasant. And our bed is green.
Our houses are beamed with cedar, our rafters are cypress.

song of songs_2.t: I'm a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
A lily among thorns — that's my companion among the daughters.
An apple tree among the trees of the forest — that's my beloved among the sons. I loved to sit in his shade, and his fruit was sweet in my mouth.
He's brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
Hold me up with raisin cakes, revive me with apples — I'm weak with love.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand holds me close.
Promise me, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, by the does of the field: don't wake love, don't rouse it, until it wants to.
That's his voice — my beloved! Here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer. There he is, standing behind our wall, looking in at the windows, peering through the lattices.
My beloved spoke up and said to me: Get up, my companion, my beautiful one, come away.
Look, winter's over; the rain has passed and gone.
The blossoms are out in the land; the time of singing has come, and the turtle-dove's voice has been heard in our land.
The fig tree's early figs are ripe, and the vines in blossom are giving off their scent. Get up, my companion, my beautiful one, come away.
My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in your hiding place on the cliff, let me see the look of you, let me hear your voice — your voice is sweet and the look of you is lovely.
Catch us the foxes, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards — and our vineyards are in blossom.
My beloved is mine and I'm his — he grazes among the lilies.
Until the day breathes and the shadows run, turn, my beloved — be like a gazelle, like a young deer on the mountains of Bether.

song of songs_3.t: Night after night on my bed I looked for the one my being loves; I looked for him and didn't find him.
I'll get up now and go round the city, through the streets and the open places; I'll look for the one my being loves. I looked for him and didn't find him.
The watchmen making their rounds of the city found me. Have you seen him — the one my being loves?
I'd barely got past them when I found the one my being loves. I held on to him and wouldn't let him go until I'd brought him to my mother's house, to the room of the one who conceived me.
Promise me, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles, by the does of the field: don't wake love, don't rouse it, until it wants to.
Who's this coming up out of the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the trader's scented powders?
There it is — Solomon's own couch, with sixty warriors around it, warriors of Israel,
every one of them holding a sword, trained for war, each with his sword at his thigh against terror in the night.
King Solomon made himself a litter out of the wood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; inside, it was fitted out with love, by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out and look, daughters of Zion, at King Solomon, at the crown his mother crowned him with on his wedding day, the day his heart was glad.

song of songs_4.t: Look at you — beautiful, my companion; look at you, beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down off Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes just up from the washing — every one of them bearing twins, not one of them bereaved.
Your lips are a thread of scarlet, and your mouth is lovely. Your temple is a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
Your neck is like the tower of David, built course on course; a thousand shields hang on it, all of them warriors' bucklers.
Your two breasts are two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among the lilies.
Until the day breathes and the shadows run, I'll go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
You're beautiful, all of you, my companion — there's not a blemish on you.
With me from Lebanon, bride — with me from Lebanon you'll come. You'll look down from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the leopards' mountains.
You've taken my heart, my sister, bride; you've taken it with one glance of your eyes, with one bead of your necklace.
How beautiful your lovemaking is, my sister, bride! Your lovemaking is so much better than wine, and the scent of your oils better than any spice!
Your lips drip honey from the comb, bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the scent of your clothes is the scent of Lebanon.
My sister, bride, is a locked garden, a locked spring, a sealed fountain.
Your shoots make an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest fruit — henna and nard,
nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon, with all the frankincense trees, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices —
a garden spring, a well of living water, streams running down from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind; come, south wind. Breathe over my garden, let its spices flow. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choicest fruit.

song of songs_5.t: I've come into my garden, my sister, bride; I've gathered my myrrh with my spice, I've eaten my honeycomb with my honey, I've drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, companions; drink till you're drunk, lovers.
I was asleep, but my heart was awake. That's my beloved — knocking: Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one — my head is wet with dew, my curls with the drops of the night.
I've taken off my tunic — am I to put it back on? I've washed my feet — am I to get them dirty?
My beloved reached his hand in through the opening, and everything inside me stirred for him.
I got up to open to my beloved, and my hands were dripping myrrh, my fingers running with myrrh, all over the handles of the bolt.
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had turned away — he was gone. My being went out of me when he spoke. I looked for him and didn't find him; I called him and he didn't answer.
The watchmen making their rounds of the city found me; they beat me, they bruised me. They took my shawl right off me — those watchmen of the walls.
Promise me, daughters of Jerusalem: if you find my beloved — what will you tell him? That I'm weak with love.
What makes your beloved better than any other, most beautiful of women? What makes your beloved better than any other, that you put us under oath like this?
My beloved is dazzling and ruddy — you'd pick him out among ten thousand.
His head is gold, pure gold; his hair is in curls, black as a raven.
His eyes are doves by the channels of water, washing in milk, mounted like jewels.
His cheeks are a bed of spice, towers of scented herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
His hands are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is a panel of ivory overlaid with sapphires.
His legs are pillars of marble standing on bases of pure gold. He looks like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself, and all of him is desirable. That's my beloved, that's my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.

song of songs_6.t: Where's your beloved gone, most beautiful of women? Which way did your beloved turn, so we can look for him with you?
My beloved's gone down to his garden, to the spice beds, to graze in the gardens and gather lilies.
I'm my beloved's and my beloved is mine — he grazes among the lilies.
You're as beautiful as Tirzah, my companion, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as the bannered hosts.
Turn your eyes away from me — they've overwhelmed me. Your hair is like a flock of goats coming down off Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes just up from the washing — every one of them bearing twins, not one of them bereaved.
Your temple is a slice of pomegranate behind your veil.
Sixty queens there are, eighty concubines, young women beyond counting —
but she is the one, my dove, my perfect one; her mother's only one, pure to the one who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her.
Who's this looking down like the dawn, beautiful as the full moon, pure as the sun, majestic as the bannered hosts?
I went down to the nut garden to look at the new growth in the wadi, to see if the vine had budded, if the pomegranates were in bloom.
I didn't know it — my being had set me among the chariots of my princely people.
Turn, turn, Shulammite; turn, turn, so we can look at you. And why would you look at the Shulammite, as though at the dance of the two camps?

song of songs_7.t: How beautiful your feet are in their sandals, you nobleman's daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewellery, made by a master craftsman's hands.
Your navel is a rounded bowl — may it never run short of mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat with lilies set round it.
Your two breasts are two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is the tower of ivory. Your eyes are the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is the tower of Lebanon that faces Damascus.
Your head on you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head is like purple. A king is held fast in the tresses.
How beautiful you are, how lovely — my love, among all the delights!
You stand like a palm tree, and your breasts are the clusters.
I said: I'll climb that palm tree, I'll take hold of its fruit-stalks. Let your breasts be like clusters on the vine, and the scent of your nose like apples,
and your mouth like the best wine — going down smooth for my beloved, gliding over the lips of sleepers.
I'm my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved, let's go out to the field; let's spend the night in the villages.
Let's be up early to the vineyards; let's see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom. There I'll give you my lovemaking.
The mandrakes are giving off their scent, and over our doorways is every choice thing, new as well as old, that I've stored up for you, my beloved.

song of songs_8.t: If only you were a brother to me, one who nursed at my mother's breasts! Then I'd find you outside and kiss you, and no one would despise me.
I'd take you, I'd bring you to my mother's house — she'd teach me. I'd give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand holds me close.
Promise me, daughters of Jerusalem: why wake love, why rouse it, until it wants to?

Who's this coming up out of the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? It was under the apple tree that I woke you. That's where your mother was in labour with you; that's where she was in labour and bore you.
Set me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm — love is as strong as death, jealousy as hard as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of the LORD.
Many waters can't put love out; rivers can't wash it away. If a man gave everything his house is worth for love, he'd be utterly despised.
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What are we going to do for our sister on the day she's spoken for?
If she's a wall, we'll build a silver battlement on her; and if she's a door, we'll close her in with a cedar plank.
I am a wall, and my breasts are the towers. So in his eyes I've become like one who finds peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He handed the vineyard over to keepers; each of them would bring in a thousand of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is right here in front of me. You can have your thousand, Solomon, and two hundred for the ones who keep its fruit.
You there, in the gardens — friends are listening for your voice. Let me hear it.
Hurry, my beloved — be like a gazelle, like a young deer on the mountains of spices.

zechariah_1.t: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berekiah son of Iddo the prophet:
The LORD was very angry with your fathers.
So say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Come back to me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I'll come back to you, says the LORD of hosts.

Don't be like your fathers. The former prophets called out to them, "This is what the LORD of hosts says: Turn back, please, from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they wouldn't listen, and they paid me no attention, declares the LORD.
Your fathers — where are they? And the prophets — do they live for ever?

But my words and my statutes, the ones I commanded my servants the prophets — didn't they catch up with your fathers? Then they turned back and said, "Just what the LORD of hosts planned to do to us, according to our ways and our deeds — that's what he's done to us."
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month — the month of Shebat — in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berekiah son of Iddo the prophet:
I was looking in the night, and there was a man riding a red horse. He was standing among the myrtles down in the hollow, and behind him were horses — red, sorrel and white.
And I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who was speaking with me said, "I'll show you what they are."
And the man standing among the myrtles answered, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to go about on the earth."
And they answered the angel of the LORD standing among the myrtles, "We've been about on the earth, and all the earth is at rest, undisturbed."
And the angel of the LORD answered, "LORD of hosts, how long will you have no compassion on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, the ones you've been indignant with these seventy years?"
And the LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me — good words, comforting words.
And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Proclaim this — "This is what the LORD of hosts says: I'm jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy,
and I'm angry, very angry, with the nations that are at ease; because I was only a little angry, and they made it worse.
So this is what the LORD says: I've come back to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring-line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.
Proclaim again: This is what the LORD of hosts says: My cities will overflow with good again; the LORD will comfort Zion again, and choose Jerusalem again.
And I looked up, and there were four horns.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" And he said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
And the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

And I said, "What have these come to do?" And he said, "Those are the horns that scattered Judah, so that nobody lifted his head. And these have come to terrify them — to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted a horn against the land of Judah, to scatter it."

zechariah_2.t: And I looked up, and there was a man with a measuring cord in his hand.
And I said, "Where are you going?" And he said, "To measure Jerusalem — to see how wide it is and how long."
And there was the angel who was speaking with me, going out — and another angel coming out to meet him.
And he said to him, "Run and tell that young man: Jerusalem will stay open country, because of all the people and livestock inside her."
"And I myself will be a wall of fire all round her, declares the LORD, and I'll be the glory inside her."
Alas, alas! Run from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I've spread you out like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.
Alas, Zion! Get away, you who live with the daughter of Babylon.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says — after glory he sent me to the nations who plundered you — because whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
For look, I'm brandishing my hand over them, and they'll become plunder for their own slaves; and you'll know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
Shout for joy, daughter of Zion, be glad — for look, I'm coming, and I'll dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
And many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they'll become a people for me. And I'll dwell in your midst, and you'll know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
And the LORD will take Judah as his portion, his own inheritance, on the holy ground, and he'll choose Jerusalem again.
Hush, all flesh, before the LORD, for he's roused himself from his holy dwelling.

zechariah_3.t: And he showed me Joshua the high priest, standing before the angel of the LORD, with the accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
And the LORD said to the accuser, "May the LORD rebuke you, accuser! May the LORD rebuke you — he who has chosen Jerusalem! Isn't this a brand pulled out of the fire?"
Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments as he stood there in front of the angel.

And he spoke up and said to those standing in front of him, "Take the filthy garments off him." And he said to him, "Look — I've taken your iniquity away from you, and I'm going to clothe you in robes."
And I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they put the clean turban on his head and clothed him in garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
And the angel of the LORD gave Joshua this charge:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, then you'll govern my house and guard my courts too, and I'll give you access among these who are standing here.
Listen, please, Joshua the high priest — you and your companions sitting in front of you, because they're men who are a sign — look, I'm bringing my servant, the Branch.

For here's the stone I've set in front of Joshua — one stone, with seven eyes on it. Look, I'm engraving its engraving, declares the LORD of hosts, and I'll remove the iniquity of that land in a single day.
On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbour to sit under a vine and under a fig tree.

zechariah_4.t: And the angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, like someone woken out of sleep.
And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a lampstand, all of it gold, with a bowl on top of it and its seven lamps on it — and seven and seven pipes for the lamps on top of it."
And there are two olive trees by it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left.
And I spoke up and said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
And the angel who was speaking with me answered, "Don't you know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
And he answered me: This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by strength and not by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
Who are you, great mountain? In front of Zerubbabel you'll be flattened! And he'll bring out the top stone with shouts of "Favour, favour to it!"
And the word of the LORD came to me:
Zerubbabel's hands laid this house's foundation, and his hands will finish it. Then you'll know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of small things? They'll rejoice and see the tin stone in Zerubbabel's hand. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, roving about through all the earth.
And I spoke up and said to him, "What are these two olive trees, on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
And I spoke up a second time and said to him, "What are these two clusters of the olive trees beside the two golden pipes, the ones pouring the gold out of them?"
And he said to me, "Don't you know what these are?" And I said, "No, my lord."
And he said, "These are the two sons of the fresh oil, who stand by the Lord of all the earth."

zechariah_5.t: And I turned and looked up, and there was a flying scroll.
And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying scroll — twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

And he said to me: "This is the curse that's going out over the face of the whole land. Everyone who steals has been purged away on this side, according to it; and everyone who swears has been purged away on this side, according to it."

"I've sent it out, declares the LORD of hosts, and it will go into the house of the thief and into the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will settle inside his house and destroy it — timbers and stones alike."
And the angel who was speaking with me came out and said to me, "Look up, please, and see what this is that's going out."
And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the ephah going out." And he said, "This is what they look like in all the land."
And there was a round cover of lead being lifted, and there was one woman sitting inside the ephah.
And he said, "This is Wickedness." And he threw her into the ephah and threw the weight of lead over its mouth.
And I looked up, and there were two women coming out, with wind in their wings — and they had wings like a stork's. And they lifted the ephah up between the earth and the heavens.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"
And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. And when it's ready, it'll be set down there on its own stand."

zechariah_6.t: And I turned and looked up, and there were four chariots coming out from between the two mountains — and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses, the second chariot black horses,
the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot dappled, strong horses.
And I spoke up and said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
And the angel answered, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out from presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth."
The chariot with the black horses is going out to the land of the north; the white have gone out after them, and the dappled have gone out to the land of the south.
And the strong ones have gone out and asked to go, to go about on the earth. And he said, "Go, go about on the earth." And they went about on the earth.
And he called out to me and said, "Look — the ones going out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."
And the word of the LORD came to me:
Take from the exiles — from Heldai, from Tobiah and from Jedaiah — and go yourself, that same day, to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, the ones who've come from Babylon.
And take silver and gold and make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest.
And say to him: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and from where he is he'll sprout, and he'll build the temple of the LORD.

He himself will build the temple of the LORD, and he himself will bear majesty, and he'll sit and rule on his throne. And there'll be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.
And the crown will be for Helem, Tobiah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.

And those far off will come and build in the temple of the LORD, and you'll know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. And this will happen, if you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God —

zechariah_7.t: In the fourth year of Darius the king, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.
Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to entreat the face of the LORD,
to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts, and the prophets, "Should I weep in the fifth month, consecrating myself, the way I have these many years?"
And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and the seventh, these seventy years — was it really for me that you fasted?
And when you eat and when you drink — isn't it you doing the eating, and you doing the drinking?
Aren't these the very words the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets, back when Jerusalem was lived in and at ease, with her cities round her, and the Negev and the Shephelah were lived in?
And the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Judge with a judgement of faithfulness, and show loyalty and compassion, each to his brother.
And don't oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor; and don't plan harm against one another in your heart.
But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and made their ears too heavy to hear.
They made their heart flint, so they wouldn't hear the law and the words the LORD of hosts had sent by his spirit through the former prophets. And great anger came from the LORD of hosts.
And so it was: just as he called and they wouldn't listen, so they called and I wouldn't listen, says the LORD of hosts.

And I stormed them away among all the nations they hadn't known, and the land was left desolate behind them, with nobody passing through and nobody coming back. They turned a land of desire into a waste.

zechariah_8.t: And the word of the LORD of hosts came:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: I'm jealous for Zion with a great jealousy, and with great rage I'm jealous for her.

This is what the LORD says: I've come back to Zion, and I'll dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts, the Holy Mountain.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Old men and old women will sit again in the open squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand, for the abundance of their days.
And the open squares of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in her squares.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: If it seems too hard to the remnant of this people in those days, will it be too hard in my eyes as well? declares the LORD of hosts.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Look, I'm saving my people from the land of the east and from the land where the sun sets.
And I'll bring them, and they'll dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They'll become a people for me, and I myself will become God for them, in faithfulness and in righteousness.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: Let your hands be strong, you who are hearing these words in these days from the mouth of the prophets — the ones who spoke from the day the house of the LORD of hosts was founded, the temple, to be rebuilt.

For before those days there was no wage for a person and no wage for the animal; and for anyone going out or coming in there was no peace from the adversary — I set every person against his neighbour.
But now I'm not as I was in the former days towards the remnant of this people, declares the LORD of hosts.

For there'll be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the land will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew; and I'll give the remnant of this people all these things as an inheritance.
And just as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I'll save you, and you'll be a blessing. Don't be afraid. Let your hands be strong.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Just as I planned to do you harm when your fathers provoked me to anger, says the LORD of hosts, and I didn't relent —
so I've turned back and planned in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Don't be afraid.
These are the things you're to do: Speak truth, each to his neighbour; judge with faithfulness and a judgement of peace in your gates.
And don't plan harm against one another in your heart, and don't love a false oath — because all these are things I hate, declares the LORD.
And the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:

This is what the LORD of hosts says: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, the fast of the tenth — they'll turn into joy and gladness for the house of Judah, and good appointed times. So love faithfulness and peace.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Peoples will yet come, and the inhabitants of many cities;
and the inhabitants of one city will go to another and say, "Let's go at once to entreat the face of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts." "I'll go too."
And many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the face of the LORD.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: In those days, ten men from all the tongues of the nations will take hold — they'll take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man and say, "Let's go with you, because we've heard that God is with you."

zechariah_9.t: An oracle. The word of the LORD: It's against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place; for the eye of humankind belongs to the LORD, and all the tribes of Israel.
and Hamath too, which borders on it; Tyre and Sidon — for she's very wise.
And Tyre built herself a fortification, heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud in the streets.
Look, the Lord will dispossess her, strike her wealth into the sea, and she'll be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid, and Gaza, and she'll writhe in anguish, and Ekron, because what she trusted in has been shamed. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon won't be inhabited.
And a mixed people will live in Ashdod, and I'll cut off the pride of the Philistines.
And I'll take his blood out of his mouth and his detestable things from between his teeth; and he too will be left for our God. He'll be like a chief in Judah, and Ekron like a Jebusite.
And I'll camp at my house as a guard against anyone passing through or coming back, and no oppressor will pass over them again, because now I've seen it with my own eyes.

Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you: righteous, and one who has salvation; poor, and riding on a donkey — on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

And I'll cut off chariotry from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow will be cut off. He'll speak peace to the nations, and his dominion will run from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.
And you too — by the blood of your covenant I've set your prisoners free from the pit that has no water in it.
Come back to the stronghold, you prisoners of the hope! Today I'm telling you again: I'll restore you double.
For I've bent Judah for myself as a bow; I've filled it with Ephraim. And I'll rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior's sword.
And the LORD will appear over them, and his arrow will go out like the lightning; and Lord GOD will blow the horn and go in the storm winds of the south.
The LORD of hosts will shield them, and they'll devour and subdue the sling-stones; and they'll drink and roar as with wine, and be full like the basin, like the corners of the altar.
And the LORD their God will save them on that day as the flock of his people; for they're stones of a crown, glittering over his ground.
For how great his goodness is, and how great his beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the virgins.

zechariah_10.t: Ask the LORD for rain at the time of the spring rain — the LORD who makes the thunder-clouds. And he gives them showers of rain, vegetation in the field to each one.

For the teraphim speak wickedness and the diviners see falsehood; they speak dreams of emptiness and comfort with futility. That's why the people have set out like a flock; they're afflicted, because there's no shepherd.

My anger has burned against the shepherds, and I'll visit punishment on the leaders; for the LORD of hosts has visited his flock, the house of Judah, and he'll make them like his horse of majesty in the battle.
From him a cornerstone, from him a tent peg, from him the bow of war, from him every ruler will come forth together.
And they'll be like warriors, treading down in the mud of the streets in the battle. They'll fight, because the LORD is with them, and they'll put the riders of horses to shame.

And I'll make the house of Judah strong, and the house of Joseph I'll save. I'll restore them, because I've had compassion on them, and they'll be as though I'd never rejected them, for I am the LORD their God and I'll answer them.
And Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their heart will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and be glad; their heart will rejoice in the LORD.
I'll whistle for them and gather them in, because I've redeemed them, and they'll multiply the way they once multiplied.
And I'll sow them among the peoples, and in far-off places they'll remember me. They'll live with their children, and they'll come back.
And I'll bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I'll bring them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon, and there won't be room enough for them.
And he'll pass through the sea of trouble and strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt will depart.
And I'll make them strong in the LORD, and in his name they'll go about, declares the LORD.

zechariah_11.t: Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire consume your cedars!
Wail, cypress, because the cedar has fallen, because the majestic ones have been devastated! Wail, oaks of Bashan, because the impenetrable forest has come down!
The sound of the shepherds wailing, because their splendour has been devastated! The sound of young lions roaring, because the thicket of the Jordan has been devastated!
This is what the LORD my God says: Shepherd the flock of slaughter,
whose buyers kill them and aren't held guilty, and whose sellers say, "Blessed be the LORD — I've grown rich!" — and their own shepherds have no compassion on them.

For I won't have compassion on the inhabitants of the land any longer, declares the LORD. Look, I'm handing over each person into the hand of his neighbour and into the hand of his king; and they'll crush the land, and I won't rescue it from their hand.
So I shepherded the flock of slaughter — the afflicted of the flock, that is. I took two staffs for myself: one I called Pleasantness, and one I called Bonds. And I shepherded the flock.
And I annihilated the three shepherds in one month. My being grew short with them, and their being loathed me too.
And I said: I won't shepherd you. Let the dying one die; let the one being destroyed be destroyed; and let those that survive devour each the flesh of her neighbour.
And I took my staff Pleasantness and cut it up, to break my covenant that I'd made with all the peoples.
And it was broken that day. And so the afflicted of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
And I said to them, "If it seems good to you, give me my wages; and if not, don't." And they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter — that magnificent price they valued me at!" And I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
And I cut up my second staff, Bonds, to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
And the LORD said to me, "Take up the equipment of a foolish shepherd again."

For look, I'm raising up a shepherd in the land: the ones being destroyed he won't visit, the young he won't seek out, the maimed he won't heal, the one still standing he won't sustain — and he'll eat the flesh of the fat one and tear off their hooves.
Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! A sword against his arm and against his right eye! Let his arm wither away entirely, and let his right eye go completely dim.

zechariah_12.t: An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel — declares the LORD, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth and formed the spirit of a human inside him:
Look, I'm making Jerusalem a bowl of reeling for all the peoples round about; and it'll be against Judah too, in the siege against Jerusalem.
And on that day I'll make Jerusalem a stone of burden for all the peoples; everyone who lifts it will injure himself, for certain, and all the nations of the earth will gather against her.

On that day, declares the LORD, I'll strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness; but over the house of Judah I'll keep my eyes open, and every horse of the peoples I'll strike with blindness.
And the chiefs of Judah will say in their heart, "The inhabitants of Jerusalem are strength for me, by the LORD of hosts their God."

On that day I'll make the chiefs of Judah like a pot of fire among wood and like a torch of fire among cut grain, and they'll consume all the peoples around them, right and left; and Jerusalem will remain again in her place, in Jerusalem.
And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the splendour of the house of David and the splendour of the inhabitants of Jerusalem won't be exalted above Judah.

On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the one among them who stumbles will be like David on that day, and the house of David like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.
And on that day I'll seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

And I'll pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of favour and supplications; and they'll look to me, the one whom they pierced through, and they'll mourn over him as one mourns over an only son, and grieve bitterly over him as one grieves over a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.

And the land will mourn, clan by clan, each on its own: the clan of the house of David on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of the house of Nathan on its own, and their wives on their own;
the clan of the house of Levi on its own, and their wives on their own; the clan of the Shimeites on its own, and their wives on their own;
all the clans that are left, clan by clan, each on its own, and their wives on their own.

zechariah_13.t: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

And on that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I'll cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they won't be remembered again; and I'll make the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness pass out of the land as well.

And when anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother who begot him will say to him, "You shall not live, because you've spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD." And his father and his mother who begot him will pierce him through when he prophesies.
And on that day the prophets will be ashamed, each of his vision when he prophesies; and they won't put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
And he'll say, "I'm no prophet. I'm a man who works the ground — somebody sold me when I was young."
And someone will say to him, "What are these wounds on your chest?" And he'll say, "The ones I got in the house of my friends."
Sword, awake against my shepherd, against the man who is my companion, declares the LORD of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and let the flock be scattered; and I'll turn my hand against the little ones.
And in all the land, declares the LORD, two parts of it will be cut off and perish, and a third will be left in it.

And I'll bring the third into the fire and refine them the way silver is refined, and test them the way gold is tested. They'll call on my name, and I'll answer them. I'll say, "They are my people"; and they'll say, "The LORD is my God."

zechariah_14.t: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, and your plunder will be divided in your midst.

And I'll gather all the nations to Jerusalem for the battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women raped; half the city will go out into exile, but the rest of the people won't be cut off from the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as on the day he fights, on a day of battle.

And on that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will split in half, from east to west, making a very great valley; and half the mountain will move northward and half southward.

And you'll flee by the valley of my mountains, because the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal; and you'll flee the way you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
And on that day there'll be no light; the splendid ones will congeal.
And there'll be one day — known to the LORD — neither day nor night; and at evening time there'll be light.
And on that day living waters will flow out from Jerusalem, half of them to the eastern sea and half to the western sea; in summer and in winter it'll be so.
And the LORD will become king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.

The whole land will be changed like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she'll rise up and stay in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
And people will live in her, and there'll be no more devoting to destruction; and Jerusalem will remain in security.

And this is the plague the LORD will strike all the peoples with, the ones that waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they're standing on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongue will rot in their mouth.
And on that day a great panic from the LORD will be among them. Each will take hold of the hand of his neighbour, and his hand will go up against the hand of his neighbour.
And Judah will fight at Jerusalem too; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered in — gold and silver and garments in very great abundance.
And the same will be the plague of the horse, the mule, the camel and the donkey, and of all the livestock in those camps — a plague like this one.
And everyone left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the festival of booths.
And whoever doesn't go up, from the clans of the earth, to Jerusalem to bow down to the King, the LORD of hosts — on them there'll be no rain.

And if the clan of Egypt doesn't go up and doesn't come, then there'll be no rain on them; there'll be the plague the LORD strikes the nations with, the ones that don't go up to keep the festival of booths.
This will be the punishment for the sin of Egypt, and the punishment for the sin of all the nations that don't go up to keep the festival of booths.
On that day there'll be on the bells of the horses: "Holy to the LORD." And the pots in the house of the LORD will be like the basins in front of the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts; and everyone who sacrifices will come and take some of them and boil in them; and there'll no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts on that day.

zephaniah_1.t: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
I'll sweep it all away, everything, from the face of the ground — declares the LORD.

I will make an end of human and animal; I will make an end of the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling-blocks along with the wicked; and I will cut humankind off from the face of the ground — declares the LORD.
I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against everyone living in Jerusalem; and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idol-priests along with the priests —
and those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens; and those who bow down and swear to the LORD and swear by Milcom as well;
and those who turn back from following the LORD, who have not sought the LORD or enquired of him.
Hush before Lord GOD! The day of the LORD is near; the LORD has prepared a sacrifice, he has consecrated his guests.
And on the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the princes and the king's sons and everyone who dresses in foreign clothing.
And on that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, those who fill their masters' house with violence and deceit.
And on that day — declares the LORD — there will be a cry from the Fish Gate, and wailing from the Second District, and a great crash from the hills.
Wail, you who live in the Mortar, for all the trading people are destroyed; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
And at that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and punish the men settling like wine on its dregs, who say to themselves, "The LORD won't do any good, and he won't do any harm."
Their wealth will become plunder, their houses a ruin; they'll build houses and never live in them, plant vineyards and never drink the wine.
The great day of the LORD is near — near, and coming fast. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; there the warrior cries out.
That day is a day of fury, a day of trouble and distress, a day of devastation and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,
a day of trumpet and war-cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner-towers.
And I will bring distress on humankind, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, their bowels like dung.

Their silver and their gold won't be able to save them on the day of the LORD's fury. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed; he will make a complete destruction, a terrible one, of all who live on the earth.

zephaniah_2.t: Gather yourselves, gather together, you nation without shame —
before the decree gives birth — the day passes like chaff — before the burning anger of the LORD comes on you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes on you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, you who have kept his ordinance. Seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD's anger.
For Gaza will be abandoned, Ashkelon a desolation; Ashdod — at midday they will drive her out, and Ekron will be uprooted.
Woe to those who live on the sea-coast, the nation of the Kerethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I'll destroy you, until no one is left living there."
And the sea-coast will become pasture, meadows for shepherds and folds for sheep.

And the coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will graze on it; in the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down at evening; for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard how Moab reproached them and how the Ammonites reviled them — how they reproached my people and made themselves great against their territory.

Therefore, as I live — declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel — Moab will become like Sodom, the Ammonites like Gomorrah: a patch of nettles and a salt-pit, a waste for ever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, the rest of my nation will take possession of them.
This is what they get for their pride, because they reproached and made themselves great against the people of the LORD of hosts.
The LORD will be terrible to them, for he will shrivel all the gods of the earth; and they will bow down to him, each from their own place — all the coastlands of the nations.
You also, Cushites — they are the slain of my sword.
And he will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria; he will make Nineveh a waste, a dry place like the desert.

Herds will lie down inside her, every kind of animal; owl and hedgehog will roost on her column-tops; a voice will sing in the window, desolation on the threshold, for the cedar-work has been stripped away.

This is the jubilant city that lived secure, that said to herself, "I am, and there's no one besides me." How she has become a waste, a lair for animals! Everyone who passes by hisses and shakes a fist.

zephaniah_3.t: Woe to the filthy and defiled one, the city that oppresses!
She hasn't listened to any voice, she hasn't accepted discipline; she hasn't trusted the LORD, she hasn't drawn near to her God.
Her princes are roaring lions inside her; her judges are evening wolves that leave nothing to gnaw by morning.
Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men; her priests have profaned what is holy, they've done violence to law.
The LORD is righteous in her midst; he does no injustice. Morning after morning he brings his justice to light; it never fails. But the unjust one knows no shame.
I have cut off nations; their corner-towers lie desolate. I have laid waste their streets, so no one passes through. Their cities are destroyed, with no one in them, nobody living there.
I said, "Surely you'll fear me, you'll accept discipline, and her dwelling won't be cut off — all that I appointed for her." But they were up early, corrupting everything they did.

"So wait for me — declares the LORD — for the day I rise up as prey; for my judgement is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out my indignation on them, all my burning anger. For in the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed."
For then I will give the peoples clean speech, so that all of them call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.
From beyond the rivers of Cush my suppliants, the daughter of my scattered ones, will bring my offering.

On that day you won't be ashamed of all the things you did when you transgressed against me; for then I will remove from among you those who exult in your pride, and you will never again be haughty on my holy mountain.
And I will leave among you an afflicted and poor people, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will do no injustice, will not speak falsehood, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouth; for they will graze and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.
Shout for joy, daughter of Zion; shout aloud, Israel; rejoice and exult with your whole heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
The LORD has removed the judgements against you; he has cleared away your enemy. The king of Israel, the LORD, is with you; you will never again fear evil.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Don't be afraid, Zion; don't let your hands go slack."
The LORD your God is with you, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with joy; he will be silent in his love; he will be glad over you with a shout of joy.
Those grieved at being kept from the appointed feast I will gather; they were from among you — a burden upon her, a reproach.
Here I am, dealing with all who afflicted you at that time. I will save the lame and gather the outcast; and I will make them a praise and a name in every land where they were put to shame.
