At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you; for I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.

1 corinthians_1.t: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Sosthenes our brother,
to God's community in Corinth — people made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be holy — together with everyone everywhere who calls on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God about you, for the grace of God that was given you in Christ Jesus,
because in him you were made rich in everything — in all speech and all knowledge,
just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,
so you're not lacking any gift while you wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed —
He'll keep you firm to the end too, beyond accusation on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful — the one through whom you were called into partnership with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: all of you say the same thing. Let there be no splits among you; be knit together in the same mind and the same judgment.
Chloe's people have made it clear to me about you, my brothers and sisters, that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is this: each of you is saying, 'I belong to Paul,' or 'I to Apollos,' or 'I to Cephas,' or 'I to Christ.'
Has Christ been carved up? Paul wasn't crucified for you, was he? Or were you baptised into Paul's name?
I thank God that I didn't baptise any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so no one can say you were baptised into my name.
I did baptise Stephanas' household too. Beyond that, I don't know whether I baptised anyone else.
Christ didn't send me to baptise but to announce the good news — and not with clever speech, so the cross of Christ isn't emptied out.
For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is God's power.
For it is written: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the intelligence of the intelligent I will set aside.'
Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Hasn't God made the world's wisdom foolish?
Since, in God's wisdom, the world didn't come to know God through its wisdom, God was pleased to save those who trust through the foolishness of what's preached.
Jews ask for signs and Greeks look for wisdom,
but we proclaim a crucified Christ — an offence to Jews, foolishness to the nations,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ — God's power and God's wisdom.
Because God's foolish thing is wiser than human beings, and God's weak thing is stronger than human beings.
Look at your calling, brothers and sisters: not many of you were wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many well-born.
But God chose the world's foolish things to shame the wise, and God chose the world's weak things to shame the strong,
and God chose the world's low-born and despised things — things that are not — to nullify the things that are,
so that no flesh may boast in God's presence.
It's from him that you are in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom for us from God — and rightness and holiness and release,
so that, as it is written, 'Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.'

1 corinthians_2.t: And when I came to you, brothers and sisters, I didn't come announcing God's mystery to you with any superiority of speech or wisdom.
For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ — and him crucified.
And I came to you in weakness, in fear, and in a great deal of trembling,
and my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom but in a demonstration of Spirit and power,
so that your trust wouldn't rest in human wisdom but in God's power.
Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature — but not the wisdom of this age, nor of this age's rulers, who are being brought to nothing.
No — we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, wisdom that's been hidden, which God marked out beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.
None of the rulers of this age has known it — if they had, they wouldn't have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written: 'What eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and what has not come up into a human heart — what God has prepared for those who love him.'
But God has revealed them to us through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For who knows a person's own matters except that person's spirit within them? It's the same with God's matters — no one has known them except the Spirit of God.
And we didn't receive the spirit of the world, but the Spirit that is from God, so we can know the things God has freely given us.
And we speak these things not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things to spiritual people.
A merely natural person doesn't accept the things of God's Spirit, because they're foolishness to him and he can't know them — they're examined spiritually.
But the spiritual person examines everything, while he himself is examined by no one.
'For who has known the Lord's mind, who will instruct him?' But we have the mind of Christ.

1 corinthians_3.t: And I, brothers and sisters, couldn't speak to you as spiritual people but as people of flesh — as infants in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink, not solid food — you weren't ready yet. In fact you still aren't ready,
because you're still fleshly. When there's jealousy and quarrelling among you, aren't you fleshly? Aren't you walking the way people ordinarily do?
For when one says, 'I belong to Paul,' and another, 'I to Apollos,' aren't you merely human?
So what is Apollos? What is Paul? Ones who serve, the ones you came to trust through — and to each of them as the Lord gave.
I planted, Apollos watered — but God kept making it grow.
So neither the one who plants is anything, nor the one who waters — but God, the one who makes it grow.
The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive his own wage according to his own labour.
For we are God's co-workers; you are God's field, God's building.
By the grace God gave me, I laid a foundation like a skilled master builder, and someone else is building on it. But let each one watch how he builds.
For no one can lay another foundation than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw —
each one's work will become visible. The Day will show it, because it's revealed in fire — and the fire itself will test what sort of work each has done.
If the work someone built survives, he'll receive a wage.
If someone's work burns up, he'll suffer loss; he himself will be saved, but like someone coming through fire.
Don't you know that you are God's temple, and that God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person — because God's temple is holy, and that's what you are.
Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks he's wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he can become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written: 'He is the one who catches the wise in their own craftiness' —
and again: 'The Lord knows that the reasonings of the wise are empty.'
So let no one boast in people. For everything is yours —
whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, whether the world or life or death, whether things present or things to come — all of it is yours,
and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

1 corinthians_4.t: This is how a person should regard us: as Christ's assistants and stewards of God's mysteries.
Now what's looked for in stewards is that a person be found faithful.
For me it counts for very little to be examined by you, or by any human court. In fact I don't even examine myself.
I'm aware of nothing against myself — but that's not what acquits me. The one who examines me is the Lord.

So don't judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes — the one who'll bring to light what's hidden in darkness and make visible the intentions of hearts. And then each will get his praise from God.

Brothers and sisters, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that through us you may learn 'nothing beyond what is written', and so that none of you will be puffed up in favour of one against another.
For who makes you different? What do you have that you didn't receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you hadn't?
Already you're full! Already you've grown rich! You've begun to reign without us — and I wish you really did reign, so we could reign with you!
For I think God has put us apostles on display at the end of the line, like people condemned to death — because we've become a spectacle to the world, to angels and to people.
We're fools for Christ's sake, but you're sensible in Christ; we're weak, but you're strong; you're honoured, but we're dishonoured.
Right up to this hour we go hungry and thirsty, we're poorly clothed, beaten, homeless,
and we work hard with our own hands. When we're abused, we bless; when we're persecuted, we endure;
when we're slandered, we speak kindly. We've become like the scourings of the world, the scrapings of everything, right up to now.
I'm not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.
Even if you had ten thousand guardians in Christ, you don't have many fathers — because in Christ Jesus I fathered you through the good news.
So I appeal to you: become imitators of me.
That's why I sent Timothy to you — he's my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He'll remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every community.
Some have become puffed up, as though I weren't coming to you.
But I'll come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I'll find out not the talk of these puffed-up people but their power.
For the kingdom of God is not in talk but in power.
What do you want? Am I to come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

1 corinthians_5.t: It's actually being reported that there's sexual immorality among you — and immorality of a kind not even found among the nations: someone has his father's wife.
And you're puffed up! Shouldn't you have gone into mourning instead, so the man who did this would be removed from among you?
For my part — absent in body but present in spirit — I've already passed judgment, as if I were there, on the man who did this,
in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: when you're gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
Your boasting isn't good. Don't you know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
Clean out the old yeast so you can be a new batch, since you are unleavened. For our Passover lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
So let's keep the festival — not with old yeast, not with the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to mix with sexually immoral people —
I didn't mean the immoral of this world generally, or the greedy and the swindlers or idolaters — in that case you'd have to leave the world.

But now I'm writing to you not to mix with anyone who's called a brother if he's sexually immoral, or greedy, or an idolater, or abusive, or a drunkard, or a swindler — with a person like that, don't even eat.
What business is it of mine to judge outsiders? Isn't it the ones inside that you're to judge —
while God judges those outside? 'Remove the evil one from among yourselves.'

1 corinthians_6.t: When one of you has a matter against another, does he really dare go to law before the unjust and not before God's people?
Or don't you know that God's people will judge the world? And if the world is judged among you, are you unworthy of the smallest cases?
Don't you know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, everyday matters!
So when you have cases about everyday matters, do you seat as judges those the community counts as nothing?
I say this to shame you. Is there really no one wise among you who will be able to decide between one brother and another?
Instead, brother goes to law against brother — and that before unbelievers!
Actually, it's already a total defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not be wronged instead? Why not be defrauded instead?
But you yourselves wrong and defraud — and you do it to brothers and sisters.
Or don't you know that wrongdoers won't inherit God's kingdom? Don't be misled: not the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who lie with men —
nor thieves, nor the greedy; no drunkards, no abusers, no swindlers will inherit God's kingdom.
And some of you were these things. But you were washed; you were made holy; you were justified — in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
'Everything is permitted me' — but not everything is good for me. 'Everything is permitted me' — but I won't be brought under anything's authority.
'Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food' — and God will bring both to nothing. But the body isn't for sexual immorality; it's for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
And God both raised the Lord and will raise us up through his power.
Don't you know that your bodies are parts of Christ? So shall I take Christ's parts and make them a prostitute's parts? Absolutely not.
Or don't you know that whoever is joined to a prostitute is one body with her? For it says, 'The two will become one flesh.'
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.
Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the one who's sexually immoral sins against his own body.
Or don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God — and that you aren't your own?
You were bought at a price. So glorify God in your body — and in your spirit, which are God's.

1 corinthians_7.t: Now, about the things you wrote to me: 'It is good for a man not to touch a woman.'
But because of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife and each woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give his wife what he owes her, and likewise the wife her husband.
The wife doesn't have authority over her own body; her husband does. And likewise the husband doesn't have authority over his own body; his wife does.

Don't defraud one another — except maybe by agreement, for a set time, so you can be free for fasting and prayer — and then be together again, so Satan doesn't test you through your lack of self-control.
I say this as a concession, not as a command.
I wish all people were as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one of this kind, another of that.
To the unmarried and to the widows I say: it is good for them if they remain as I am.
But if they don't have self-control, let them marry — it's better to marry than to burn.
To the married I give this instruction — not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband.
But if she does separate, she is to remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband is not to divorce his wife.
To the rest I say — I, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she is content to live with him, he is not to divorce her.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is content to live with her, she is not to divorce her husband.

For the unbelieving husband has been made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been made holy through the brother. Otherwise your children would be unclean — but as it is, they are holy.
But if the unbelieving partner separates, let them separate. The brother or the sister is not enslaved in such cases; God has called you in peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
Only, let each person walk as the Lord has assigned, as God has called each one. This is what I lay down in all the communities.
Was anyone called already circumcised? He shouldn't undo it. Was anyone called uncircumcised? He shouldn't be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; keeping God's commands is what matters.
Let each remain in the calling he was called in.
Were you called as a slave? Don't let it trouble you — but if you're able to gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
For the one called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord's freed person; likewise the one called as a free person is Christ's slave.
You were bought at a price; don't become slaves of people.
Brothers and sisters, let each remain with God in whatever condition he was called.
Now about virgins: I have no command from the Lord, but I give an opinion as one who has been shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
So I think this is good, because of the present pressure — that it's good for a person to stay as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? Don't seek release. Are you free of a wife? Don't go looking for one.
But if you do marry, you haven't sinned; and if a virgin marries, she hasn't sinned. But people like that will have distress in the flesh, and I'm trying to spare you.
This I say, brothers and sisters: the time has been shortened. From now on, let even those who have wives be as though they had none,
and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,
and those who use the world as though not using it up. For the present shape of this world is passing away.
I want you to be free from anxieties. The unmarried man is anxious about the Lord's matters, how to please the Lord;
but the married man is anxious about the world's matters, how to please his wife,

and he is divided. And the unmarried woman, or the virgin, is anxious about the Lord's matters, so that she may be holy in body and in spirit; but the married woman is anxious about the world's matters, how to please her husband.
I say this for your own benefit — not to throw a noose over you, but for what is fitting and for undistracted devotion to the Lord.
If anyone thinks he's behaving improperly toward his betrothed — if she's past her prime, and it has to be so — let him do what he wants; he isn't sinning: let them marry.
But whoever stands firm in his heart, under no compulsion, having authority over his own will, and has decided this in his own heart — to keep his own virgin — he will do well.
So the one who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and the one who doesn't will do better.
A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives. But if her husband falls asleep, she's free to marry whoever she wants — only in the Lord.
But in my opinion she's happier if she stays as she is — and I think I have God's Spirit too.

1 corinthians_8.t: Now about food sacrificed to idols. We know that 'we all have knowledge'. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
If anyone thinks he knows something, he doesn't yet know as he ought to know.
But if anyone loves God, this person is known by him.
So, about eating food sacrificed to idols: we know that 'an idol is nothing in the world' and that 'there is no God but one'.
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth — as indeed there are many gods and many lords —
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom all things are and for whom we exist; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things are and through whom we exist.
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some are still accustomed to the idol, and they eat the food as though it really were sacrificed to an idol — and their conscience, weak as it is, is stained.
Food won't present us to God: we're no worse off if we don't eat, and no better off if we do.
But watch that this right of yours doesn't somehow become a stumbling-block to the weak.
For if someone sees you — you who have knowledge — reclining at table in an idol's temple, won't his conscience, weak as it is, be built up to eat food sacrificed to idols?
So the weak person is destroyed by your knowledge — the brother for whom Christ died.
And when you sin like this against brothers and sisters, striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
So if food trips up my brother, I'll never eat meat again, so that I don't trip up my brother.

1 corinthians_9.t: Aren't I free? Aren't I an apostle? Haven't I seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Aren't you my work in the Lord?
If I'm not an apostle to others, at least I am to you — you're the seal on my apostleship in the Lord.
Here is my defence to those who put me on trial:
Don't we have the right to eat and drink?
Don't we have the right to take a believing wife along with us, the way the other apostles do — and the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones with no right to stop working for a living?
Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and doesn't eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and doesn't drink from the flock's milk?
Am I saying this only on human authority? Doesn't the law say the same?
In the law of Moses it is written: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. Is it oxen God is concerned about?
Isn't he saying it entirely for our sake? Yes, it was written for us, because the one who ploughs ought to plough in hope, and the one who threshes should thresh in hope of a share.
If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?
If others share this right over you, don't we all the more? But we didn't use this right. We put up with everything rather than put any obstacle in the way of the good news of Christ.
Don't you know that those who work in the temple eat what comes from the temple, and those who attend at the altar share in what is on the altar?
In the same way the Lord commanded that those who announce the good news should live from the good news.
But I've used none of these rights. And I'm not writing this so it'll be done for me. I'd rather die than — no one is going to empty out my boast.
If I announce the good news, that's no boast of mine — I'm under compulsion. It would go badly for me if I didn't announce it.
If I do this willingly, I've got a wage coming. If unwillingly, I've simply been entrusted with a job to manage.
So what's my wage? Just this: that when I announce the good news I can offer it free of charge, and so not make full use of my right in the good news.
Free as I am from everyone, I made myself a slave to everyone, to win over as many as possible.
To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law — though I'm not myself under the law — to win those under the law.
To those outside the law I became like one outside the law — not being outside God's law, but inside the law of Christ — to win those outside the law.
To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I've become all things to all people, so that by every means I might save some.
I do all of this because of the good news, so that I may share in it.
Don't you know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to take it.
Every competitor goes into strict training. They do it for a wreath that withers; we do it for one that doesn't.
So I don't run aimlessly, and I don't box like a man punching the air.
I bruise my own body and lead it as a slave, so that after preaching to others I'm not myself found to fail the test.

1 corinthians_10.t: I don't want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptised into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
But God wasn't pleased with most of them; their bodies were scattered across the desert.
These things happened as patterns for us, so that we wouldn't crave what's evil, the way they craved.
Don't become idol-worshippers, as some of them were. As it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to play.
And let's not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did — and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day.
And let's not put Christ to the test, as some of them did — and they were destroyed by snakes.
And don't grumble, as some of them grumbled — and they were destroyed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as patterns, and they were written down as a warning for us, on whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
So then, whoever thinks he's standing had better watch out that he doesn't fall.

No trial has taken hold of you except what's common to human beings. God is trustworthy: he won't let you be tried beyond what you can bear, but with the trial he'll make the way out too, so you're able to endure it.
So then, my dear friends, run from idol-worship.
I'm speaking to you as sensible people; judge for yourselves what I'm saying.
The cup of blessing that we bless — isn't it a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break — isn't it a sharing in the body of Christ?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body — for we all share in the one loaf.
Look at Israel according to the flesh: aren't those who eat the sacrifices partners with the altar?
So what am I saying? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No — what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don't want you to become partners with demons.
You can't drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons. You can't share the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Or are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?
Everything is permitted for me — but not everything is good for anyone. Everything is permitted for me — but not everything builds up.
No one should look for his own good, but for the good of the other person.
Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
for the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.
If an unbeliever invites you over and you want to go, eat whatever is set in front of you without raising questions of conscience.
But if someone says to you, This has been offered in sacrifice, then don't eat it — for the sake of the one who told you, and for conscience; for the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.
By conscience I mean the other person's, not your own. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I take part with thanks, why am I slandered over something I give thanks for?
So whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do it all for God's glory.
Give no offence to Jews or Greeks or to God's community,
just as I try to please everyone in everything, not looking for my own advantage but for that of the many, so that they may be saved.

1 corinthians_11.t: Follow my example, as I follow Christ's.
I praise you for remembering me in everything and for holding on to the traditions just as I passed them to you.
But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
Any man who prays or prophesies with something down over his head shames his head.
And any woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered shames her head — it's one and the same thing as having it shaved.
If a woman won't cover her head, she may as well have her hair cut off. And if it's a disgrace for a woman to have her hair cut off or shaved, then let her cover her head.
A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; the woman is the glory of the man.
For the man didn't come from the woman, but the woman from the man;
and the man was not created for the woman's sake, but the woman for the man's.
This is why the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head — because of the angels.
Even so, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man of woman.
For just as the woman came from the man, so also the man comes through the woman — and everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Doesn't nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it's a dishonour to him,
but if a woman has long hair it's her glory? Her hair has been given to her in place of a covering.
If anyone wants to argue about this — we have no such practice, and neither do God's communities.
In giving this instruction I have no praise for you, because your meetings do more harm than good.
First of all, I hear that when you meet as a community there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
There have to be factions among you, I suppose, so that those who are genuine become obvious.
So when you gather in one place, it isn't the Lord's supper that you eat.
Each of you goes ahead with your own supper, so one is hungry and another is drunk.
Don't you have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise God's community and humiliate those who have nothing? What am I to say to you? Am I to praise you? In this I do not.
For what I received from the Lord I also passed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night he was handed over, took bread,
and when he had given thanks he broke it and said, Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.
In the same way he took the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, whenever you drink it, in memory of me.
For every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you announce the Lord's death until he comes.
So whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy manner will be answerable for the body and blood of the Lord.
Let each person examine himself, and then eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
For whoever eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgement on himself.
That's why many among you are weak and ill, and quite a number have died.
If we discerned ourselves, we wouldn't be judged.
But when we're judged by the Lord, we're being trained, so we won't be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so your meetings don't bring judgement on you. I'll give directions about the rest when I come.

1 corinthians_12.t: Now about spiritual matters, brothers and sisters: I don't want you to be uninformed.
You know that when you were pagans you were somehow drawn away to idols that couldn't speak.
So I want you to understand that no one speaking by God's Spirit says, Jesus is cursed, and no one can say, Jesus is Lord, except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord.
There are different kinds of activity, but the same God, who activates all of them in everyone.
To each person the Spirit's showing is given for the common good.
To one, a word of wisdom is given through the Spirit; to another, a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
to another, faith by the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing by the one Spirit;
to another, workings of power; to another, prophecy; to another, distinguishing between spirits; to another, kinds of tongues; to another, interpretation of tongues.
All of these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who distributes them to each person individually, as he chooses.
For just as the body is one and has many parts, and all the parts of the body, many as they are, are one body — so it is with Christ.
For we were all baptised by one Spirit into one body — Jews or Greeks, slaves or free — and we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
For the body isn't a single part but many.
If the foot were to say, Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body — that wouldn't make it any less part of the body.
And if the ear were to say, Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body — that wouldn't make it any less part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
But in fact God arranged the parts, each one of them, in the body just as he wanted.
If they were all one part, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts but one body.
The eye can't say to the hand, I do not need you — nor again the head to the feet, I do not need you.
On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
and the parts of the body we think less honourable we surround with greater honour, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty,
while our presentable parts need none of this. But God combined the body, giving greater honour to the part that lacked it,
so that there would be no division in the body, but the parts would have the same care for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honoured, every part rejoices with it.
You are Christ's body, and individually parts of it.
And God has placed in the community first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powerful deeds, then gifts of healing, acts of help, acts of guidance, kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work powerful deeds?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But be eager for the greater gifts. And now I'll show you a way beyond all comparison.

1 corinthians_13.t: If I speak in the tongues of human beings and of angels but do not have love, I have become a booming gong or a clashing cymbal.
If I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all the faith needed to move mountains but do not have love, I am nothing.
If I give away everything I own, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
Love waits without anger; love is kind. Love is not jealous, does not brag, is not inflated with itself,
does not behave disgracefully, does not look for its own interests, is not provoked, keeps no account of wrong,
does not rejoice at wrongdoing but rejoices along with the truth,
puts up with everything, trusts in everything, hopes for everything, endures everything.
Love never falls. But prophecies will be brought to an end; tongues will stop; knowledge will be brought to an end.
For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
but when the complete comes, the partial will be brought to an end.
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put an end to childish things.
For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle; then, face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, just as I have been fully known.
So now these three remain: faith, hope, love. And the greatest of these is love.

1 corinthians_14.t: Pursue love. Be eager for the things of the Spirit, and above all that you may prophesy.
Anyone who speaks in a tongue isn't speaking to people but to God, since no one understands; he's speaking mysteries by the Spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people, building them up, urging them on and consoling them.
The one who speaks in a tongue builds himself up; the one who prophesies builds up the community.

I'd like all of you to speak in tongues, but even more that you'd prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues — unless he interprets, so the community can be built up.
As it is, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what good will I do you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
Even lifeless instruments that make a sound — a flute, say, or a lyre — if they don't give distinct notes, how will anyone know what's being played?
And if the trumpet gives an uncertain call, who will get ready for battle?
It's the same with you: unless you produce speech that's clear, how will anyone know what's being said? You'll be talking into the air.
There are, no doubt, any number of kinds of language in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
So if I don't know what a language means, I'll be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.
So with you: since you're eager for spirits, seek to overflow with what builds up the community.
So the one who speaks in a tongue should pray for the power to interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit is praying but my mind is unproductive.
So what am I to do? I'll pray with my spirit, and I'll pray with my mind as well. I'll sing with my spirit, and I'll sing with my mind as well.
Otherwise, if you're blessing God with your spirit, how will the person who's in the position of an outsider say the Amen to your thanksgiving, when he doesn't know what you're saying?
You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person isn't built up.
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the assembly I'd rather speak five words with my mind, to instruct others as well, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Brothers and sisters, don't be children in your thinking. Be infants when it comes to evil, but in your thinking be grown up.
In the law it is written: By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me, says the Lord.
So then, tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers; prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
So if the whole community comes together in one place and everyone's speaking in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, won't they say you're out of your minds?
But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or an outsider comes in, he is convicted by all, examined by all,
and the secrets of his heart become plain, and so he falls on his face and worships God, declaring that God is really among you.
So what should happen, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each of you has a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Let everything be for building up.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be two, or at most three, and one at a time — and someone must interpret.
If there's no interpreter, he should keep silent in the assembly and speak to himself and to God.
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said.
And if a revelation comes to someone else sitting there, the first speaker should stop.
For you can all prophesy one by one, so that everyone may learn and everyone be encouraged.
And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
For God isn't a God of disorder but of peace. As in all the assemblies of God's people,
women should keep silent in the assemblies. They are not permitted to speak; they are to be in submission, as the law also says.
If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in the assembly.
Or did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
If anyone thinks he's a prophet or a spiritual person, he should recognise that what I'm writing to you is the Lord's command.
If anyone doesn't recognise this, he isn't recognised.
So, my brothers and sisters, be eager to prophesy, and don't stop anyone speaking in tongues.
But let everything be done properly and in order.

1 corinthians_15.t: Now I want to remind you, brothers and sisters, of the good news I announced to you, which you received, in which you stand,
and through which you're being saved — if you hold on to the message I announced to you. Otherwise you came to trust for nothing.
For I passed on to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures,
and that he was buried, and that he has been raised on the third day according to the scriptures,
and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at once, most of whom are still alive, though some have died.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
And last of all he appeared to me too, as to one born at the wrong time.
For I'm the least of the apostles, not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's community.
But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace toward me wasn't wasted. On the contrary, I worked harder than all of them — not I, though, but God's grace with me.
So whether it was I or they, this is what we announce, and this is what you came to trust.
Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say there's no resurrection of the dead?
If there's no resurrection of the dead, then Christ hasn't been raised either.
And if Christ hasn't been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your trust is empty too.
What's more, we're found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ — whom he didn't raise, if in fact the dead aren't raised.
For if the dead aren't raised, then Christ hasn't been raised either.
And if Christ hasn't been raised, your trust is futile; you're still in your sins.
It would follow, too, that those who have died in Christ are lost.
If our hope in Christ is for this life only, we're the most pitiable of all people.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have died.
For since death came through a human being, the resurrection of the dead comes through a human being as well.
For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then, at his coming, those who belong to Christ.
Then comes the end, when he hands the kingdom over to God the Father, after he has brought every ruler and every authority and power to an end.
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be brought to an end is death.
For he has put everything under his feet. But when it says that everything has been put under him, it's obvious that this doesn't include the one who put everything under him.
And when everything has been put under him, then the Son himself will also be put under the one who put everything under him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those people do who are baptised for the dead? If the dead aren't raised at all, why are they baptised for them?
And why do we put ourselves in danger every hour?
I die every day — as surely as I boast about you, brothers and sisters, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If I fought wild animals at Ephesus on merely human terms, what did I gain? If the dead aren't raised, then let's eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Don't be deceived: bad company ruins good character.
Sober up, as you should, and stop sinning. Some of you are ignorant of God — I say this to your shame.
But someone will ask: How are the dead raised? What kind of body do they come with?
You fool! What you sow doesn't come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow isn't the body that's going to be — it's a bare seed, of wheat perhaps, or something else.
But God gives it a body as he chose, and to each kind of seed its own body.
Not all flesh is the same flesh: there's one kind for human beings, another for animals, another for birds, another for fish.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the splendour of the heavenly is one thing and the splendour of the earthly is another.
The sun has one kind of splendour, the moon another, the stars another — and star differs from star in splendour.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable; what is raised is imperishable.
It is sown in dishonour, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power.
It is sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body. If there's a natural body, there's also a spiritual one.
So it is written: The first human, Adam, became a living soul; the last Adam became a life-giving Spirit.
But the spiritual didn't come first; the natural did, and then the spiritual.
The first human was from the earth, made of dust; the second human is the Lord from heaven.
As the man of dust was, so are those made of dust; and as the heavenly man is, so are those who are heavenly.
And just as we have borne the image of the man of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly one.
I tell you this, brothers and sisters: flesh and blood can't inherit God's kingdom, and what decays doesn't inherit what doesn't decay.
Look — I'm telling you a mystery: we won't all sleep, but we will all be changed,
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
For this perishable thing must put on imperishability, and this mortal thing must put on immortality.
And when this perishable thing has put on imperishability and this mortal thing has put on immortality, then the saying that is written will come true: Death has been swallowed up in victory.
Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm, immovable, always overflowing in the Lord's work, since you know that your labour in the Lord isn't empty.

1 corinthians_16.t: Now about the collection for God's people: do what I directed the communities in Galatia to do.
On the first day of every week, each of you should set something aside at home, saving up whatever you can afford, so that no collections have to be made when I come.
When I arrive, I'll send those you approve, with letters, to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
And if it seems worth my going too, they'll travel with me.
I'll come to you after I pass through Macedonia — I'm going through Macedonia —
and I may well stay with you, perhaps even spend the winter, so that you can send me on my way wherever I go.
I don't want to see you just in passing this time; I hope to stay with you for a while, if the Lord permits.
I'll stay on in Ephesus until Pentecost,
because a wide door has opened for me, one with real work in it — and there are many opponents.
If Timothy comes, see that he has nothing to fear among you, because he's doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
So no one should look down on him. Send him on his way in peace, so he can come back to me — I'm waiting for him with the brothers.
About our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to visit you with the brothers, but he was quite unwilling to come now. He'll come when he has the opportunity.
Keep alert. Stand firm in the faith. Show yourselves men. Be strong.
Let everything you do be done in love.
I urge you, brothers and sisters — you know the household of Stephanas, that they were the firstfruits of Achaia and set themselves to serve God's people —
— that you in turn put yourselves under people like this, and under everyone who works and labours with them.
I'm glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus have arrived, because they've made up for your absence.
They refreshed my spirit, and yours. So give recognition to people like this.
The communities in Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the community that meets in their house.
All the brothers and sisters greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
This greeting is in my own hand — Paul.
If anyone has no love for the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Marana tha.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1 john_1.t: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our own eyes, what we looked at and our own hands handled — concerning the word of life —
and the life was made visible — we have seen it, and we testify, and we announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was made visible to us —
what we have seen and heard, we announce to you too — so that you can have a share with us as well. And our share is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
And we are writing these things so that our joy may be complete.
And this is the message we have heard from him and announce to you: God is light, and there is no darkness in him at all.
If we say we have a share with him and we are walking in the dark, we are lying — and we are not doing the truth.
But if we walk in the light, the way he himself is in the light, we have a share with one another — and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from every sin.
If we say we have no sin, we're leading ourselves astray, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just — so he forgives us the sins and cleanses us from all wrongdoing.
If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

1 john_2.t: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you won't sin. And if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father — Jesus Christ, the Just One.
and he himself is the propitiation for our sins — and not just for ours, but for the whole world's.
And this is how we know that we have come to know him: if we keep his commands.
Anyone who says 'I have come to know him' and doesn't keep his commands is a liar, and the truth is not in this one.
But whoever keeps his word — in this one the love of God has truly been brought to completion. This is how we know that we are in him.
Anyone who says he remains in him ought to walk himself just as that one walked.
Beloved, I am not writing you a new command but an old one, which you have had from the beginning. The old command is the word you heard from the beginning.
Again, a new command I am writing to you — which is true in him and in you — because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
Anyone who says he is in the light and hates his brother or sister is in the darkness still — right up to now.
Anyone who loves his brother or sister remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
But the one who hates his brother or sister is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn't know where he's going, because the darkness blinded his eyes.
I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven you on account of his name.
I am writing to you, fathers, because you have come to know the one who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have conquered the evil one.

I wrote to you, children, because you have come to know the Father. I wrote to you, fathers, because you have come to know the one who is from the beginning. I wrote to you, young men, because you are strong and the word of God remains in you and you have conquered the evil one.
Don't love the world, or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
because everything in the world — the craving of the flesh, the craving of the eyes, the boasting about one's living — is not from the Father but from the world.
And the world is passing away, and its craving with it — but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
Children, it is the last hour — and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have come. That is how we know it is the last hour.
They went out from us, but they were not of us. If they had been of us, they would have remained with us — but so that it might be shown that none of them are of us.
And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all know.
I didn't write to you because you don't know the truth, but because you do know it — and because no lie comes out of the truth.
Who is the liar, if not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This one is the antichrist — the one who denies the Father and the Son.
Anyone who denies the Son doesn't have the Father either. The one who confesses the Son has the Father too.
As for you — let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. And if what you heard from the beginning remains in you, then you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
And this is the promise he himself promised us: the eternal life.
I have written these things to you about the ones who are leading you astray.

And as for you — the anointing you received from him remains in you, and you don't need anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about everything, and is true and is no lie — and just as it taught you — remain in him.
And now, little children, remain in him — so that if he is made visible, we may have boldness and not be shamed away from him at his coming.
If you know that he is just, then you know too that everyone who does what is right has been born from him.

1 john_3.t: Look what kind of love the Father has given us — that we should be called children of God. And we are. This is why the world does not know us: because it did not know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God, and what we will be has not yet been made visible. But we know that if he is made visible, we will be like him, because we will see him just as he is.
And everyone who has this hope resting on him purifies himself, just as that one is pure.
Everyone who does sin does lawlessness too — and sin is lawlessness.
And you know that that one was made visible to take our sins away — and there is no sin in him.
Everyone who remains in him does not sin. Everyone who sins has not seen him and has not come to know him.
Little children, don't let anyone lead you astray. The one who does what is right is righteous, just as that one is righteous.
The one who does sin is from the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. This is why the Son of God was made visible: to undo the works of the devil.
Everyone who has been born from God does not do sin, because his seed remains in him — and he cannot sin, because he has been born from God.
This is how the children of God and the children of the devil are visible: everyone who does not do what is right is not from God — nor is the one who does not love his brother or sister.
because this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another —
not like Cain, who was from the evil one and butchered his brother. And why did he butcher him? Because his own works were evil and his brother's were right.
And don't be surprised, my brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
We know that we have crossed over out of death into life, because we love the brothers and sisters. Anyone who does not love remains in death.
Everyone who hates his brother or sister is a murderer — and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
This is how we have come to know love: that one laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers and sisters.
But whoever has the world's livelihood and sees his brother or sister in need and shuts his guts against him — how does the love of God remain in him?
My little children, let's not love with word or with the tongue, but in deed and truth.
And this is how we will know that we are from the truth — and we will persuade our heart before him —
for if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows everything.
Beloved, if our heart doesn't condemn us, we have boldness toward God,
and whatever we ask, we receive from him — because we keep his commands and do what pleases him.
And this is his command: that we trust the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us command.
And the one who keeps his commands remains in him, and he in him. And this is how we know that he remains in us: from the Spirit he gave us.

1 john_4.t: Beloved, don't trust every spirit — test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
This is how you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ having come in flesh is from God.

And every spirit that does not confess Jesus Christ having come in flesh is not from God. And this is the spirit of the antichrist, the one you have heard is coming — and it is already in the world now.
You are from God, little children, and you have conquered them — because the one in you is greater than the one in the world.
They are from the world. That is why they speak out of the world, and the world listens to them.
We are from God. Anyone who knows God listens to us; anyone who is not from God does not listen to us. That is how we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of deception.
Beloved, let's love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born from God and knows God.
The one who does not love did not know God, because God is love.
This is how the love of God was made visible among us: God has sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him.
This is what love is: not that we have loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the atonement for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us like this, then we ought to love one another too.
No one has ever yet gazed on God. If we love one another, God remains in us and his love has been brought to completion in us.
This is how we know that we remain in him and he in us: he has given us of his Spirit.
And we have gazed, and we testify, that the Father has sent the Son as Saviour of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus Christ is the Son of God — God remains in him, and he in God.
And we have come to know and have trusted the love that God has among us. God is love — and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
This is how love has been brought to completion with us: so that we may have boldness on the day of judgement — because just as that one is, so are we in this world.
There is no fear in love — complete love throws fear outside, because fear has punishment in it, and the one who fears has not been brought to completion in love.
We love him because he first loved us.
If anyone says 'I love God' and hates his brother or sister, he is a liar. Because the one who does not love his brother or sister, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen.
And this is the command we have from him: that the one who loves God is to love his brother or sister too.

1 john_5.t: Everyone who trusts that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God — and everyone who loves the one who fathered loves the one fathered from him.
This is how we know that we love the children of God: whenever we love God and do his commands.
This is what the love of God is: that we keep his commands. And his commands are not heavy.
because everything born from God conquers the world. And this is the conquest that conquered the world: our trust.
And who is it that conquers the world, except the one who trusts that Jesus is the Son of God?
This is the one who came through water and blood: Jesus Christ — not in the water only, but in the water and in the blood. And the Spirit is the one testifying, because the Spirit is the truth.
For there are three that testify:
the Spirit and the water and the blood — and the three converge on the one.
If we accept the testimony of people, the testimony of God is greater — because this is God's testimony: he has testified about his Son.
The one who trusts into the Son of God has the testimony in himself. The one who does not trust God has made him a liar, because he has not trusted the testimony God has testified about his Son.
And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
Whoever has the Son has the life. Whoever does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
These things I have written to you who trust into the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.
And this is the boldness we have toward him: if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.
And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, then we know that we have the requests we have asked him for.

If anyone sees his brother or sister sinning a sin not toward death, he will ask, and he will give him life — to those sinning not toward death. There is a sin toward death; I do not say he should make request about that one.
All wrongdoing is sin — and there is sin that is not toward death.
We know that everyone who has been born from God does not sin — rather, the one born from God keeps him, and the evil one does not touch him.
We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the evil one.

And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know the True One. And we are in the True One, in his Son Jesus Christ. This one is the true God and eternal life.
Little children, guard yourselves from the idols. Amen.

1 peter_1.t: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to those chosen and living as resident foreigners in the dispersion — Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia —
chosen in keeping with the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the Spirit's setting-apart, for obedience and for the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: may grace and peace be multiplied to you.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that can't decay, can't be defiled and can't fade, kept in the heavens for you,
you who are being garrisoned by God's power through trust, for a rescue that's ready to be revealed at the last moment.
In this you rejoice — though for a little while now, if it has to be, you've been grieved by trials of every kind,

so that the tested genuineness of your trust — worth far more than gold, which perishes even though it's assayed by fire — may be found to result in praise and glory and honour at the revealing of Jesus Christ.
You love him without having seen him; and though you don't see him now, you trust him, and you rejoice with a joy beyond words and full of glory,
as you receive the outcome of your trust — the rescue of your lives.
It was this rescue the prophets searched and searched about — the ones who prophesied about the grace meant for you —
searching to find out what person or what time the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing to, when it testified in advance to the sufferings meant for Christ and the glories after them.

It was revealed to them that they weren't serving themselves but you, in the things now announced to you through those who brought you the good news by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven — things angels long to stoop and look into.
So then: with the belt of your mind fastened, sober, set your hope completely on the grace being brought to you at the revealing of Jesus Christ.
As children of obedience, don't let yourselves be shaped by the cravings you had before, in your ignorance,
but just as the one who called you is holy, you yourselves become holy in your whole way of life,
since it is written: 'You are to be holy, because I am holy.'
And if you call on him as Father — the one who judges impartially according to each person's work — then live out your time here as foreigners in fear.
You know it wasn't with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were ransomed out of the futile way of life handed down from your fathers,
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot — the blood of Christ,
foreknown before the world was founded, but revealed at the end of the times for your sake —
you who through him trust in God — the God who raised him from the dead and gave him glory — so that your trust and hope are in God.
Now that you've purified your lives by obedience to the truth, for sincere brotherly love, love one another intensely from a clean heart —
born again, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the word of God, living and remaining.
For 'all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of the grass. The grass withered and the flower fell off,
but the word of the Lord remains for ever.' And that is the word that was announced to you as good news.

1 peter_2.t: So strip off all malice and all deceit, hypocrisies, envies and every kind of slander,
and like newborn babies long for the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow up into rescue,
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.
As you come to him — a living stone, rejected by people but chosen and precious in God's sight —
you yourselves, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it stands in Scripture: 'Look, I am laying in Zion a chosen and precious cornerstone, and the one who trusts on him will never be put to shame.'
So the honour is yours, who trust; but for those who don't trust, 'the stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner',
and 'a stone to strike against and a rock to trip over'. They strike against it because they disobey the word — which is also what they were appointed to.

But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his possession, so that you may announce the excellences of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light —
you who once were not a people, but now are God's people; who had not received mercy, but now have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you as foreigners and resident aliens to keep away from the cravings of the flesh, which are on campaign against your life.
Keep your way of life among the nations good, so that where they speak against you as wrongdoers, they may see your good works and glorify God on the day he visits.
Submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake: whether to a king as the one holding power,
or to governors as those he sends to punish wrongdoers and to praise those who do good.
Because this is God's will: that by doing good you should muzzle the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people — not using your freedom as a cover for malice, but as God's servants.
Honour everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the emperor.
Household slaves, submit to your masters with all fear — not only to the good and reasonable ones, but also to the crooked.
Because this is a gracious thing: if, because of an awareness of God, someone bears up under griefs while suffering unjustly.
What credit is it if you take a beating for doing wrong and put up with it? But if you endure while doing good and suffering for it, this is a gracious thing before God.
This is what you were called to, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you a copy to trace, so that you would follow in his footsteps.
'He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.'
When he was insulted he didn't insult back; suffering, he didn't threaten, but handed himself over to the one who judges justly.
He himself carried up our sins in his body onto the tree, so that we might be done with sins and live for rightness. By his welt you were healed.
You were straying like sheep, but now you've turned back to the shepherd and overseer of your lives.

1 peter_3.t: In the same way, wives, submit to your own husbands, so that even if some of them disobey the word they may be won over without a word, through their wives' way of life,
when they see how pure your way of life is, lived in fear.
Don't let your adornment be the outward kind — braided hair, gold jewellery, fine clothes —
but the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable quality of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is of great value before God.
This is how the holy women who hoped in God used to adorn themselves long ago, submitting to their own husbands —
as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You became her children when you do good and are not frightened by any terror.

Husbands, in the same way, live with your wives with understanding, as with a weaker vessel — the female one — assigning her honour as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers aren't cut off.
Finally, all of you: be of one mind, sympathetic, loving as brothers and sisters, tender-hearted, humble-minded.
Don't pay back evil for evil, or insult for insult; on the contrary, bless — because this is what you were called to, so that you may inherit a blessing.
For 'whoever wants to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit;
he must turn away from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it.
Because the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are turned to their plea, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.'
And who is going to harm you if you become zealots for what is good?
But even if you should suffer for the sake of rightness, you are blessed. Don't be afraid of what they fear, and don't be shaken.
but set apart Christ as Lord in your hearts, always ready to make a defence to anyone who asks you for an account of the hope in you —
but with gentleness and reverence, keeping a good conscience, so that when you're spoken against, the people who abuse your good way of life in Christ will be put to shame.
Because it's better to suffer for doing good, if that should be God's will, than for doing evil.
Because Christ also suffered for sins once for all, a righteous one for unrighteous ones, to bring you to God — put to death in the flesh, made alive in the spirit.
In which he also went and made proclamation to the spirits in prison,
those who disobeyed long ago, when God's patience was waiting in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In it a few — that is, eight lives — were brought safely through water.
And baptism, which corresponds to that, now saves you too — not a removal of dirt from the flesh, but a pledge to God from a good conscience — through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at God's right hand, having gone into heaven, with angels and authorities and powers made subject to him.

1 peter_4.t: So then — since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves with the same intention, because whoever has suffered in the flesh has finished with sin —
so as to live out the rest of your time in the flesh no longer by human cravings but by God's will.
The time that's gone by is long enough for doing what the nations want — walking in debauchery, cravings, drunkenness, revels, drinking parties and lawless idolatries.
They're taken aback that you don't run with them into the same flood of dissipation, and they abuse you for it —
and they'll give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
This is why the good news was announced even to the dead: so that, though they're judged in the flesh the way people are, they might live in the spirit the way God does.
The end of all things has come close. So keep a clear head, and be sober for prayer.
Above all, keep your love for one another at full stretch, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each of you has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good managers of God's varied grace:

if anyone speaks, let it be as God's oracles; if anyone serves, let it be out of the strength God supplies — so that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, don't find the burning among you strange — it's happening to test you — as though something strange were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice to the extent that you share in Christ's sufferings, so that at the revealing of his glory you may rejoice and be overjoyed as well.
If you're insulted for the name of Christ, you're blessed, because the Spirit of glory — the Spirit of God — rests on you: on their side he is blasphemed, but on your side he is glorified.
None of you should suffer as a murderer or a thief or a wrongdoer — or as a meddler in other people's business.
But if anyone suffers as a Christian, he shouldn't be ashamed; he should glorify God in this name.
Because it's time for the judgement to begin at God's own household — and if it begins with us, how will it end for those who disobey God's good news?
And 'if the righteous person is only just rescued, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?'
So then, those who suffer according to God's will should hand their lives over to a faithful Creator while they go on doing good.

1 peter_5.t: So I urge the elders among you — I'm a fellow elder myself, a witness of Christ's sufferings, and a sharer in the glory about to be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God that's among you, overseeing it — not because you have to but because you want to, as God would have it; not for shameful gain but eagerly;
not lording it over those in your charge, but becoming patterns for the flock.
And when the chief shepherd is revealed, you'll receive the unfading crown of glory.

In the same way, you who are younger, submit to the elders. And all of you, tie humility round yourselves toward one another, because 'God sets himself against the arrogant, but to the lowly he gives grace.'
So be brought low under God's mighty hand, so that he can lift you up at the right time,
throwing all your anxiety onto him, because he cares about you.
Be sober. Stay awake. Your opponent in court, the slanderer, prowls about like a roaring lion, looking for someone to swallow.
Stand against him, firm in your trust, knowing that the same kinds of suffering are being completed in your brotherhood all over the world.
And the God of all grace, who called you into his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore you, steady you, strengthen you and settle you, after you've suffered a little while.
To him belong the glory and the power for ever and ever. Amen.
I've written to you briefly through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother — urging you, and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand in it.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1 thessalonians_1.t: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers without stopping
remembering before our God and Father the work that comes out of your trust, the labour that comes out of your love, and the endurance that comes out of your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
We know, brothers and sisters loved by God, that he has chosen you;

because our good news didn't come to you in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with much full assurance — and you know what kind of people we turned out to be among you, for your sake.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction, with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
so you became a pattern for every believer in Macedonia and Achaia.
The word of the Lord has rung out from you — and not just in Macedonia and Achaia; your trust toward God has gone out everywhere, so we don't need to say anything.
They themselves report about us what kind of welcome we had among you, and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God
and to wait for his Son from the heavens, the one he raised from the dead — Jesus, who rescues us from the anger that's coming.

1 thessalonians_2.t: You know yourselves, brothers and sisters, that our coming to you wasn't empty.
Instead — even after we'd already suffered and been outrageously treated in Philippi, as you know — we found boldness in our God to speak God's good news to you in the face of great opposition.
Our appeal didn't come out of error or impurity, and there was no deceit in it;
Instead, since God has approved us and trusted us with the good news, that's how we speak — not to please people, but to please God, who tests our hearts.
We never came with flattering talk, as you know, and never with a pretext for greed — God is witness —
and we weren't looking for glory from people — not from you, not from anyone else.
though as Christ's apostles we could have made our weight felt. Instead we were gentle among you — like a nurse cherishing her own children.
That's how much we longed for you: we were glad to give you not just God's good news but our own selves, because you had become dear to us.
You remember our labour and hardship, brothers and sisters: we worked night and day so as not to burden any of you, and we proclaimed God's good news to you.
You are witnesses — and so is God — of how devoutly and justly and blamelessly we behaved toward you believers,
and you know how we treated each one of you, the way a father treats his own children —
appealing to you, encouraging you, urging you — so you would walk worthily of the God who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.

And this is why we thank God constantly too: when you received the word of God's message from us, you took it not as a human word but as what it really is — the word of God, which is also at work in you who trust.
For you, brothers and sisters, became imitators of God's assemblies in Judea that are in Christ Jesus — because you suffered the same things from your own countrymen that they suffered from the Jews
who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out, and do not please God, and are hostile to all people —
stopping us from speaking to the nations so they can be saved, and so always filling up the measure of their sins. But God's anger has come upon them at last.
But we, brothers and sisters, orphaned from you for a short time — in person, not in heart — tried all the harder to see you face to face, longing for it.
We wanted to come to you — I, Paul, more than once — and Satan blocked our way.
After all, what is our hope, our joy, our crown to boast in? Isn't it you, before our Lord Jesus at his coming?
Yes — you are our glory and our joy.

1 thessalonians_3.t: So when we couldn't stand it any longer, we were content to be left behind in Athens alone,
and we sent Timothy — our brother, God's servant, our co-worker in the good news of Christ — to strengthen you and encourage you about your faith,
so no one would be shaken by these afflictions. You know yourselves that this is what we are appointed for.
In fact, while we were with you we kept telling you ahead of time that we were going to be afflicted — and that's how it turned out, as you know.
That's why, when I couldn't stand it any longer, I sent to find out about your faith — in case the tempter had tempted you and our labour had come to nothing.
But now Timothy has come to us from you, and he has brought us the good news of your faith and love — and that you always remember us kindly, and long to see us just as we long to see you —
so, brothers and sisters, in all our distress and affliction we were encouraged about you, through your faith —
because now we live — if you are standing firm in the Lord.
What thanks can we pay back to God for you — for all the joy we rejoice with because of you before our God,
praying night and day, beyond all measure, to see your face and to make up what is lacking in your faith?
Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus, make our way straight to you.
And may the Lord make you increase and overflow in love — for one another, and for everyone — just as we do for you,
