so that he may strengthen your hearts to be blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints.

1 thessalonians_4.t: Finally then, brothers and sisters, we ask and urge you in the Lord Jesus — you received from us how you ought to walk and please God, and that is how you are walking — to do it all the more.
You know what instructions we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
This is God's will: that you be holy — that you keep away from sexual immorality;
that each of you know how to control his own body in holiness and honour,
not in the passion of lust, the way the nations do who don't know God;
that no one overstep and take advantage of his brother in this matter — because the Lord is the avenger in all these things, just as we told you before and testified solemnly.
God did not call us to impurity but in holiness.
So whoever rejects this is rejecting not a human being but God — the God who also gives you his Holy Spirit.
Now about brotherly love — you don't need anyone to write to you, because you yourselves are taught by God to love one another;
and in fact you are doing it for all the brothers and sisters throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers and sisters, to do it all the more,
and to make it your ambition to live quietly, mind your own business and work with your own hands, just as we instructed you,
so that you may walk decently toward those outside, and depend on no one.
We don't want you to be uninformed, brothers and sisters, about those who are sleeping, so that you won't grieve the way the rest do, who have no hope.
If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, then in the same way, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep.
This is what we tell you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who are left until the Lord's coming, will certainly not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.
The Lord himself will come down from heaven — with a shouted command, with an archangel's voice, with God's trumpet — and the dead in Christ will rise first.
Then we who are alive, who are left, will be snatched up along with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air — and that is how we will always be with the Lord.
So encourage one another with these words.

1 thessalonians_5.t: Now about the times and the seasons, brothers and sisters — you don't need anything written to you,
because you know perfectly well yourselves that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
Just when people are saying 'Peace and security,' sudden destruction comes on them — like labour pains on a pregnant woman — and they will certainly not escape.
But you, brothers and sisters, are not in darkness, so that day should overtake you like a thief.
You are all sons of light and sons of the day. We do not belong to the night or to the darkness.
So then, let's not sleep like the rest, but stay awake and keep sober.
People who sleep sleep at night, and people who get drunk are drunk at night.
But we belong to the day, so let's keep sober — putting on the breastplate of trust and love, and for a helmet the hope of deliverance.
God did not appoint us for anger, but for obtaining deliverance through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with him.
So encourage one another and build each other up — which is what you are doing.
We ask you, brothers and sisters, to recognise the ones who labour among you, who lead you in the Lord and warn you,
and to hold them in the highest regard, in love, because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
And we urge you, brothers and sisters: warn the ones who are out of line, comfort the discouraged, hold on to the weak, be patient with everyone.
See that no one pays anyone back evil for evil, but always pursue what is good — for one another, and for everyone.
Rejoice always.
Pray without stopping.
Give thanks in everything — this is God's will in Christ Jesus for you.
Don't put out the Spirit's fire.
Don't treat prophecies as worth nothing.
Test everything; hold on to what is good.
Keep away from every form of evil.
May the God of peace himself make you holy through and through, and may your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The one who calls you is faithful — and he will do it, too.
Brothers and sisters, pray for us too.
Greet all the brothers and sisters with a holy kiss.
I put you under oath by the Lord: this letter is to be read to all God's people, the brothers and sisters.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. [To the Thessalonians, first letter, written from Athens.]

1 timothy_1.t: Paul, an apostle of the Lord Christ Jesus by the command of God our Saviour and of the Lord Christ Jesus our hope,
To Timothy, my true child in faith: grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
Just as I urged you to stay on in Ephesus when I was setting out for Macedonia, so that you could charge certain people not to teach a different doctrine,
or to give their attention to myths and endless genealogies. Those things produce speculations rather than God's stewardship, which is in faith.
What this charge is aiming at is love — out of a clean heart, a good conscience, and unhypocritical trust.
Some have missed the mark on these and turned off into empty talk,
wanting to be teachers of the law — though they don't understand what they're saying, or the things they insist on so confidently.
Now we know the law is good, if a person uses it lawfully —
knowing this: law isn't laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and unruly, the ungodly and sinful, the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers,
the sexually immoral, men who lie with men, slave-traders, liars, perjurers — and whatever else stands opposed to the healthy teaching,
in accord with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God — the one I myself was entrusted with.
I'm grateful to the one who gave me strength, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he considered me trustworthy and appointed me to service —
even though I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, a violent man. But I was shown mercy, because I acted in ignorance, in unbelief.
and the grace of our Lord overflowed beyond measure, with the trust and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Trustworthy is the saying, and worthy of full acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners — and I'm the first of them.
But this is why I was shown mercy: so that in me, as the first, Christ Jesus could display the whole of his patience — as a sketch for those about to trust in him for eternal life.
Now to the King of the ages — imperishable, invisible, the only wise God — be honour and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This is the charge I'm entrusting to you, my child Timothy, in accord with the prophecies once made over you — so that by them you can fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have thrown these away and made shipwreck of the faith —
Hymenaeus and Alexander are among them — I handed them over to Satan so they'd be taught not to blaspheme.

1 timothy_2.t: So first of all, I urge that requests, prayers, appeals and thanksgivings be made for all people,
for kings and everyone in high position — so that we can lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and dignity.
This is good, and acceptable before God our Saviour,
who wants all people to be saved and to come to a full knowledge of truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and people — a human being, Christ Jesus,
who gave himself as a ransom for all — the testimony given at its own proper times.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle — I'm telling the truth in Christ, I'm not lying — a teacher of the nations, in trust and truth.
So I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or argument;
and likewise the women, to adorn themselves in orderly dress, with modesty and self-control — not with braided hair and gold or pearls or expensive clothing,
but with good works — which is what suits women who profess reverence for God.
A woman is to learn in quietness, in all submission.
I do not permit a woman to teach, or to have authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived; but the woman, thoroughly deceived, came into transgression.
But she will be saved through childbearing — if they remain in trust and love and holiness, with self-control.

1 timothy_3.t: Trustworthy is the saying: if anyone aspires to oversight, he desires a good work.
So the overseer must be beyond reproach: the husband of one wife, clear-headed, self-controlled, orderly, hospitable, able to teach,
not a drunkard, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,
managing his own household well, keeping his children in submission with all dignity —
for if someone doesn't know how to manage his own household, how will he care for God's community?
not newly planted, so he doesn't become puffed up and fall into the devil's judgement.
He also has to have a good reputation with those outside, so he doesn't fall into disgrace and the devil's trap.
Those who serve, likewise, are to be dignified: not two-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for shameful gain,
holding the mystery of the faith with a clean conscience.
And these too must first be tested; then let them serve, being beyond accusation.
Their wives likewise are to be dignified: not slanderers, clear-headed, trustworthy in everything.
Those who serve are to be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.
For those who have served well gain a good standing for themselves, and great boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
I'm writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon —
but if I'm delayed, so that you'll know how one must behave in God's household, which is the community of the living God, a pillar and buttress of the truth.
And by common confession, great is the mystery of godliness: who was revealed in flesh, vindicated in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, trusted in the world, taken up in glory.

1 timothy_4.t: But the Spirit says plainly that in later times some will stand away from the faith, giving their attention to deceiving spirits and to teachings of demons,
through the hypocrisy of liars whose own conscience has been branded,
forbidding marriage and requiring abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who trust and have come to know the truth.
because everything God created is good, and nothing is to be thrown away if it's received with thanksgiving —
since it's made holy through God's word and prayer.
If you set these things before the brothers and sisters, you'll be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching you've followed.
Have nothing to do with profane, old-wives' myths. Train yourself for godliness instead.
Bodily training is of limited use, but godliness is useful for everything — it holds a promise of life, both now and to come.
Trustworthy is the saying, and worthy of full acceptance.
This is what we labour and struggle for: we've set our hope on the living God, who is the Saviour of all people — especially of those who trust.
Charge these things, and teach them.
Let no one look down on your youth. Instead become a pattern for those who trust — in speech, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in trust, in purity.
Until I come, attend to the public reading, to the exhortation, to the teaching.
Don't neglect the gift in you — the one given you through prophecy, with the laying on of the elders' hands.
Practise these things; be immersed in them, so that everyone can see your progress.
Watch yourself, and watch the teaching. Stay with them — because by doing that you'll save both yourself and those who hear you.

1 timothy_5.t: Don't come down hard on an older man; appeal to him as a father — younger men as brothers,
older women as mothers, younger women as sisters — in all purity.
Honour widows who are really widows.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to show godliness toward their own household and to pay their parents back — because this is good and acceptable before God.
The one who is really a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and stays at her requests and prayers night and day;
but the one who lives for pleasure is dead while she lives.
Charge these things too, so that they may be beyond reproach.
If anyone doesn't provide for their own — especially their own household — they've denied the faith and are worse than someone who doesn't trust.
Let a widow be enrolled only if she is not less than sixty years old, the wife of one husband,

attested by good works: if she raised children, if she showed hospitality to strangers, if she washed the feet of God's people, if she came to the aid of the afflicted, if she pursued every good work.
But refuse younger widows. For when their desires pull them away from Christ, they want to marry,
and so they incur judgement, because they've set aside their first pledge.
And at the same time they learn to be idle, going round from house to house — and not just idle, but gossips and busybodies, saying what they shouldn't.
So I want younger women to marry, to bear children, to manage a household, to give the adversary no occasion for abuse;
for some have already turned aside after Satan.
If any believing man or woman has widows, that person should help them, so the community isn't burdened and can help those who are really widows.
Elders who preside well are to be considered worthy of double honour — especially those who labour in speaking and teaching.
For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain," and, "The worker is worthy of his wages."
Don't accept an accusation against an elder except on the word of two or three witnesses.
Those who go on sinning — reprove them in front of everyone, so the rest will have fear as well.
I solemnly charge you before God and the Lord Christ Jesus and the chosen angels: keep these things without prejudging, and do nothing out of favouritism.
Don't lay hands on anyone hastily, and don't share in other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Stop drinking only water; use a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
The sins of some people are obvious, going ahead of them to judgement; the sins of others follow after.
In the same way, good works are obvious too — and the ones that aren't can't stay hidden.

1 timothy_6.t: All who are under the yoke as slaves are to consider their own masters worthy of all honour, so that the name of God and the teaching are not blasphemed.

And those who have believing masters mustn't look down on them because they're brothers; they should serve them all the more, because the ones who benefit from their good service are trusting and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches a different doctrine and doesn't come over to healthy words — the words of our Lord Jesus Christ — and to the teaching that accords with godliness,
he's puffed up, understanding nothing, just sick over controversies and word-battles. Out of these come envy, strife, slanders, evil suspicions,
constant frictions among people whose minds are ruined and who have been robbed of the truth, supposing that godliness is a means of gain. Keep away from such people.
But godliness with contentment is a great means of gain.
We brought nothing into the world, and it's clear we can't carry anything out.
But if we have food and covering, we'll be content with those.
Those who want to be rich fall into temptation and a trap and many senseless and harmful desires, which plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some, reaching for it, have been led away from the faith and have pierced themselves through with many pains.
But you, person of God, flee these things. Pursue rightness, godliness, trust, love, endurance, gentleness.
Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and about which you made the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who under Pontius Pilate testified to the good confession,
to keep the command spotless and beyond reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which he will display at his own proper times — the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
who alone has immortality, living in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or is able to see. To him be honour and eternal power. Amen.

Charge those who are rich in the present age not to be arrogant, and not to set their hope on how uncertain wealth is, but on God, the living one, who richly supplies us with everything for our enjoyment.
to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous, ready to share,
storing up for themselves a good foundation for what's coming, so they can take hold of the life that's really life.
Timothy, guard the deposit. Turn away from the profane empty talk and the contradictions of what's falsely called knowledge —
which some have professed, and so have missed the mark concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen. [To Timothy, the first, written from Laodicea, which is the chief city of Phrygia Pacatiana.]

2 corinthians_1.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God's will, and Timothy our brother — to God's community in Corinth, and to all God's holy people right across Achaia:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,
who comforts us in all our pressure, so that we can comfort people in any kind of pressure — with the comfort God comforts us with.
Because just as the sufferings of Christ overflow into us, so through Christ our comfort overflows too.
If we are under pressure, it is for your comfort and rescue; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort — and that comfort does its work as you endure the same sufferings we suffer.
And our hope for you doesn't waver, because we know that as you share in the sufferings, you share in the comfort too.

Brothers and sisters, we don't want you left in the dark about the pressure that came on us in Asia. We were weighed down beyond all measure, past our strength — so much so that we despaired of life itself.
In fact, we had the death sentence inside us — so that we would put our confidence not in ourselves but in the God who raises the dead.
He rescued us from a danger that deadly, and he will rescue us. On him we have set our hope — that he will rescue us again,
as you join in and help us with your prayer — so that many people will give thanks for us, for the gift given to us through many.

This is our boast — what our conscience testifies: that we behaved in the world, and above all toward you, with God's own singleness of heart and sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom but with God's grace.
We aren't writing you anything but what you read and actually understand — and I hope you'll go on understanding to the end,
just as you have understood us in part — that we are your boast, as you will be ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
It was with this confidence that I meant to come to you first, so that you would get a second gift of grace —
to go by way of you into Macedonia, then come back to you from Macedonia and be sent on by you to Judea.
So when I meant to do that, was I just being casual about it? Or do I make my plans the way the flesh makes plans, so that with me it's 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no' in the same breath?
But God is faithful — our word to you is not Yes and No.
Because God's Son, Jesus Christ, the one we proclaimed among you — I and Silvanus and Timothy — was not Yes and No. In him it has become Yes.
However many promises God has made, in him they are Yes. And so it is through him that we say the Amen, to God's glory.
It is God who makes us stand firm with you in Christ, and who anointed us,
who also put his seal on us and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as the down payment.
I call God as witness against my own life: it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
Not that we lord it over your faith — we are fellow workers for your joy, because it's by faith that you stand.

2 corinthians_2.t: So I decided this for myself — that I wouldn't come to you again in grief.
Because if I'm the one who grieves you, who's left to cheer me up — except the very person I grieved?
And that is exactly what I wrote, so that when I came I wouldn't be grieved by the very people who ought to make me glad — trusting you all, that my joy is the joy of all of you.
I wrote to you out of great pressure and anguish of heart, through many tears — not to grieve you, but so you would know how much love I have for you.
And if someone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but — not to overstate it — all of you, in part.
For a person like that, this rebuke by the majority is enough.
So now you should do the opposite — forgive him and comfort him, or he'll be swallowed up by too much grief.
So I urge you to confirm your love for him in public.
That is in fact why I wrote — to find out whether you would stand the test, whether you are obedient in everything.
Anyone you forgive, I forgive too. And whatever I have forgiven — if I have forgiven anything — I forgave for your sake, in the presence of Christ,
so that Satan would not outmanoeuvre us — we are not ignorant of his designs.
When I came to Troas for the good news of Christ, and a door was opened for me in the Lord,
I still had no relief in my spirit, because I didn't find Titus my brother there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always leads us in his triumphal procession in Christ, and through us spreads the aroma of knowing him everywhere.
Because we are the fragrance of Christ to God — among those being rescued and among those perishing:
to the one, a stench from death leading to death; to the other, a fragrance from life leading to life. And who is adequate for that?
We are not like so many, hawking God's word for profit. No — we speak in Christ, out of sincerity, out of God, and in God's sight.

2 corinthians_3.t: Are we starting to recommend ourselves again? Or do we need letters of recommendation to you, or from you — the way some people do?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
It is plain that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us — written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.
This is the kind of confidence we have toward God through Christ.
Not that we're adequate in ourselves to count anything as coming from us — our adequacy comes from God,
who made us adequate as servants of a new covenant — not of letter but of Spirit. Because the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

Now if the ministry that brought death — carved in letters on stones — came with such glory that the sons of Israel couldn't look straight at Moses' face, because of the glory of his face, a glory being brought to nothing,
how will the ministry of the Spirit not come with far more glory?
Because if the ministry of condemnation had glory, the ministry of rightness overflows with far more.
In fact, what was glorified has not been glorified at all in this respect, because of the glory that goes beyond it.
Because if what is being brought to nothing came through glory, how much more is what remains in glory.
So, with hope like this, we speak with great openness —
and not like Moses, who used to put a veil over his face so the sons of Israel would not gaze at the end of what was being brought to nothing.
But their minds were hardened. To this very day the same veil remains over the reading of the old covenant — it is not lifted, because it is in Christ that it is brought to nothing.
But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with unveiled face, looking at the Lord's glory as in a mirror, are being transformed into that same image, from glory to glory — just as from the Lord who is the Spirit.

2 corinthians_4.t: That is why, since we have this ministry — since we were shown mercy — we don't lose heart.

Instead we have renounced the hidden things people are ashamed of. We don't work by cunning, and we don't water down God's word; we commend ourselves to every human conscience, in God's sight, by putting the truth on open display.
And even if our good news is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing —
among whom the god of this age blinded the minds of those who do not trust, so the light of the good news of the glory of Christ — who is the image of God — would not dawn on them.
We do not proclaim ourselves — we proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants, for Jesus' sake.
Because the God who said 'Light will shine out of darkness' is the one who has shone in our hearts — to give the light of the knowledge of God's glory, in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we hold this treasure in clay pots, so that the extraordinary power is God's and doesn't come from us.
Pressed on every side but not crushed; at a loss but not at a dead loss;
pursued but not abandoned; knocked down but not destroyed;
always carrying around in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our body.
Because we who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake — so that the life of Jesus may be made visible in our mortal flesh too.
So death is at work in us, but life in you.
But we have the same spirit of trust as in what is written — 'I trusted, so I spoke' — and we trust too, and so we speak,
knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you.
It is all for your sake, so that grace, as it reaches more and more people, may make thanksgiving overflow to God's glory.
That is why we don't lose heart. Even if our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day after day.
Because this light, momentary pressure of ours is producing for us an eternal weight of glory, beyond all measure and beyond all comparison —
as we keep our eyes not on what is seen but on what is not seen — because what is seen is temporary, but what is not seen is eternal.

2 corinthians_5.t: We know that if our earthly house — this tent — is torn down, we have a building from God: a house not made by hands, eternal, in the heavens.
In fact we groan in this one, longing to put our dwelling from heaven on over it —
if in fact, once we have put it on, we will not be found naked.
We who are in this tent groan under the weight — not that we want to be stripped, but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
And the one who prepared us for this very thing is God, who gave us the Spirit as the down payment.
So we are always confident — and we know that while we are at home in the body we are away from home, away from the Lord —
because we walk by trust, not by sight —
and we are confident, and would much rather leave home from the body and be at home with the Lord.
So whether at home or away from home, we make it our ambition to please him.
All of us must be made visible before the judgement seat of Christ, so that each of us is paid back for what was done through the body, according to what he practised — whether good or worthless.
So, knowing the fear of the Lord, we try to persuade people. To God we are already visible — and I hope we are visible to your consciences too.
We are not recommending ourselves to you again — we are giving you an occasion to boast about us, so you have something to say to people who boast in appearances and not in the heart.
If we were out of our minds, it was for God; if we're in our right mind, it is for you.
The love of Christ holds us together, once we have reached this judgement: one died on behalf of all, and so all died.
And he died on behalf of all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves but for the one who died and was raised on their behalf.
So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, we know him that way no longer.
So if anyone is in Christ — new creation. The old things have passed; look, they have become new.
And all of it is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and placing in us the word of reconciliation.
So we are ambassadors on Christ's behalf, as though God were making his appeal through us. We beg you on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
The one who did not know sin, he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become God's rightness.

2 corinthians_6.t: Working together with him, then, we urge you not to receive God's grace for nothing.
Because he says: 'At an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of rescue I helped you.' Look — now is the well-accepted time; look — now is the day of rescue.
We give no one any cause to stumble, so that no fault can be found with the ministry.
Instead, in everything we commend ourselves as God's servants: in great endurance, in pressures, in hardships, in tight places,
in beatings, in prisons, in riots, in labours, in sleepless nights, in times without food,
in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love without pretence,
in the word of truth, in God's power; through the weapons of rightness for the right hand and the left,
through glory and dishonour, through slander and praise; treated as deceivers, and true;
as unknown, and well known; as dying — and look, we live; as disciplined, and not put to death;
as grieved but always rejoicing; as poor but making many rich; as having nothing and possessing everything.
Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians — our heart is wide open.
You are not cramped by us — you are cramped in your own affections.
In fair exchange — I am speaking as to children — open wide yourselves too.
Do not become unevenly yoked with those who do not trust. What partnership do rightness and lawlessness have? What fellowship has light with darkness?
What agreement does Christ have with Beliar? What share has one who trusts with one who does not?

What agreement has God's temple with idols? Because we are the temple of the living God, just as God said: 'I will live among them and walk among them; I will be their God and they will be my people.'
'So come out from among them and be separated,' says the Lord, 'and touch nothing unclean; and I will welcome you,'
'and I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me,' says the Lord Almighty.

2 corinthians_7.t: So, dear friends, since we have these promises, let's cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, and complete holiness in the fear of God.
Make room for us. We wronged no one, we ruined no one, we took advantage of no one.
I am not saying this to condemn you — I said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
I speak to you with great openness; I boast about you a great deal. I am filled with comfort — I am overflowing with joy in all our pressure.
In fact, when we came into Macedonia our flesh had no relief at all. We were under pressure from every side — fights outside, fears inside.
But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus —
and not only by his arrival, but by the comfort he had received from you, as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me — so that I rejoiced all the more.
Because even if I grieved you with the letter, I do not regret it. Even if I did regret it — I see that that letter grieved you, if only for an hour —
now I rejoice — not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved into a change of mind. You were grieved in a way that answers to God, so that you suffered no loss from us in anything.
Grief that answers to God produces a change of mind that leads to rescue and leaves no regret. The world's grief produces death.

Look at what this very thing — being grieved in a way that answers to God — produced in you: what earnestness, what defence, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what punishment! In every way you proved yourselves clean in the matter.
So even though I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor for the sake of the one wronged, but so that your earnestness for us might be made plain to you before God.
That is why we have been comforted. And beyond our own comfort, we rejoiced even more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
If I had boasted to him at all about you, I was not put to shame. On the contrary — just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus turned out true as well.
And his affection for you is all the greater as he remembers the obedience of you all — how you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.

2 corinthians_8.t: Brothers and sisters, we want you to know the grace of God that has been given among the communities of Macedonia:
that in a severe test of pressure, the overflow of their joy and their rock-bottom poverty overflowed into the wealth of their single-hearted generosity.
Because it was according to their means — I testify to it — and beyond their means, of their own accord,
they begged us urgently for the favour of sharing in this service to God's people —
and not as we had hoped: they gave themselves first to the Lord, and then to us, through God's will.
So we urged Titus that, just as he had made a start, he should complete this act of grace among you too.

But just as you overflow in everything — in trust, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love that comes from us and is among you — see that you overflow in this act of grace as well.
I am not saying this as a command — I am testing the genuineness of your love against the earnestness of others.
You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ — that for your sake he became poor, being rich, so that you by his poverty might become rich.
And I give my opinion in this, because it is to your advantage: you were the ones who last year made a start not only on the doing but on the wanting.
So now finish the doing as well, so that just as there was readiness in the wanting, there is a completing out of what you have.
If the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what someone has, not according to what he doesn't have.
This is not so that others get relief and you get pressure, but a matter of equality:
at the present time your surplus goes to their lack, so that their surplus may in turn go to your lack — so that there may be equality,
as it is written: 'The one with much had nothing over, and the one with little had no lack.'
But thanks be to God, who put the same earnestness for you into Titus' heart,
because he welcomed our appeal — and being all the more earnest, he is going out to you of his own accord.
And we are sending with him the brother whose praise in the good news runs through all the communities —

and not only that: he was also appointed by the communities as our travelling companion in this act of grace that we are administering, for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our own readiness.
We are avoiding this — that anyone should find fault with us over this generous sum we are administering.
We are taking thought for what is good — not only in the Lord's sight but in the sight of people.
And we are sending with them our brother, whom we have often tested in many things and found earnest — and now much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.
As for Titus — he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers — they are emissaries of the communities, the glory of Christ.
So give them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you — in full view of the communities.

2 corinthians_9.t: Now about the service to God's people — there is no need for me to write to you,
because I know your readiness, which I boast about on your behalf to the Macedonians — that Achaia has been ready since last year — and your zeal has stirred up most of them.
But I have sent the brothers so that our boasting about you would not prove hollow in this matter — so that, as I kept saying, you would be ready;
in case some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, and we — not to say you — would be humiliated in this confident undertaking.

So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to go on ahead to you and arrange in advance your previously promised blessing, so that it would be ready as a blessing and not as something squeezed out of you.
This is the point: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows on blessings will also reap on blessings.
Each should give as he has decided in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion — because God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is able to make every grace overflow to you, so that having enough of everything at all times, you may overflow into every good work —
as it is written: 'He scattered, he gave to the poor; his rightness stands forever.'
And the one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed, and will increase the harvest of your rightness.
You will be made rich in every way for every kind of single-hearted generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us;
because the administration of this service is not only filling up what God's people lack — it is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God.

Through the proof this service gives, they glorify God for your obedience to the confession of the good news of Christ, and for the single-hearted generosity of your sharing with them and with everyone,
while they also pray for you and long for you, because of the surpassing grace of God on you.
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.

2 corinthians_10.t: I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ — I who am humble when I am with you face to face, and bold toward you when I am away.
I beg you not to make me bold when I am present, with the confidence I reckon I will dare to use against certain people who reckon that we walk according to the flesh.
Though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
The weapons of our campaign are not fleshly but powerful — by God — for the demolition of strongholds, demolishing arguments
We demolish arguments and every height raised up against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive into obedience to Christ,
and we are ready to punish every disobedience, once your obedience is complete.
You are looking at what is in front of your faces. If anyone is convinced he belongs to Christ, let him reckon this again about himself — that just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
Even if I boast a bit too much about our authority — which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down — I will not be put to shame.
— so that I may not seem to be frightening you off with my letters.
Because, someone says, 'His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is contemptible.'
Let a person like that reckon this: what we are in word through letters when absent, that is what we will be in action when present.

We would not dare to class or compare ourselves with certain people who commend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they do not understand.
We will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the field God assigned us as our measure — to reach even as far as you.
We are not overextending ourselves, as if we had not reached you — we did in fact get all the way to you with the good news of Christ.
We do not boast beyond measure in other people's labours; but we hope that as your trust grows, we will be enlarged among you, according to our own field, and abundantly so —
so as to bring the good news to the regions beyond you — not to boast in another's field about work already done.
'Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.'
It is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one the Lord commends.

2 corinthians_11.t: I wish you'd put up with a little foolishness from me. Do bear with me!
I am jealous over you with God's own jealousy. I betrothed you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure virgin.
But I am afraid that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted away from the singleness and purity that belong to Christ.

If someone comes and proclaims another Jesus — one we did not proclaim — or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different good news which you did not accept, you put up with it well enough.
I reckon I am in no way inferior to the super-apostles.
Even if I am untrained in speech, I am not in knowledge — in fact we have made this plain to you in every way, in all things.
Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted — by announcing God's good news to you free of charge?
I robbed other communities, taking their pay, to serve you.

And when I was with you and in need, I was a dead weight on no one — the brothers who came from Macedonia filled up my lack. I kept myself from being a burden to you in every way, and I'll keep on doing it.
The truth of Christ is in me: this boast of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I don't love you? God knows.
And what I am doing I will keep on doing, so as to cut away the pretext of those who want a pretext — so that in the thing they boast about, they may be found to be just like us.
People like that are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
And no wonder — Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of rightness. Their end will match their works.
I'll say it again: let no one think me a fool. But if you do, then take me as a fool, so that I can boast a little too.
What I am saying, I am not saying according to the Lord — I am speaking as in foolishness, in this confident boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I'll boast too.
You gladly put up with fools — being so wise yourselves.
You put up with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes you in, if someone puts on airs, if someone slaps you in the face.
I say this to my shame — as though we had been too weak for that! But whatever anyone else dares — I am speaking in foolishness — I dare too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's seed? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? — I am talking like a madman — I am more: in far greater labours, in far more imprisonments, in beatings beyond measure, in death after death.
Five times I received from Jews the forty minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked; I spent a night and a day in the open sea.

On journeys often: dangers from rivers, dangers from bandits, dangers from my own people, dangers from the nations, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers;
in labour and hardship, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and without clothing.
And apart from everything else, there is the daily pressure on me: my anxiety for all the communities.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
and I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall, and escaped his hands.

2 corinthians_12.t: Boasting is necessary. It does no good — but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a person in Christ who fourteen years ago — whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know, God knows — was caught up to the third heaven.
And I know that this person — whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows —
was caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words, which no human being is permitted to utter.
On behalf of a person like that I will boast; but on my own behalf I will not boast — except in my weaknesses.
If I did want to boast, I would not be a fool — I would be speaking the truth. But I hold back, so no one will credit me with more than what he sees in me or hears from me,

and because of the extraordinary character of the revelations. So, to keep me from being lifted up, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to beat me — to keep me from being lifted up.
Three times I appealed to the Lord about this, that it would leave me.

And he has said to me, 'My grace is enough for you, because power is brought to completion in weakness.' So I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may pitch its tent over me.
That is why I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions and tight places, for Christ's sake — because whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
I have become a fool. You forced me to it — I ought to have been commended by you. I fell short of the super-apostles in nothing, even if I am nothing.
The signs of an apostle were performed among you with all endurance — signs and wonders and acts of power.
In what way were you worse off than the rest of the communities — except that I myself was not a dead weight on you? Forgive me this wrong!

Look — this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a dead weight, because I am not looking for what is yours but for you. Children ought not to store up for their parents, but parents for their children.
And I will most gladly spend, and be spent out, for your lives. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
Let it stand: I did not burden you. But — being the crafty one — I took you in by deceit!
Did I take advantage of you through anyone I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Titus didn't take advantage of you, did he? Didn't we walk in the same spirit? In the same footsteps?
You have been thinking all along that we are defending ourselves to you. We speak in God's sight, in Christ — and all of it, dear friends, is for building you up.

I am afraid that when I come I may not find you as I want, and you may not find me as you want — that there may be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, slander, whispering, arrogance, disorder;

and that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many who sinned before and have not changed their minds about the uncleanness and sexual immorality and unrestraint they practised.

2 corinthians_13.t: This is the third time I am coming to you. 'Every matter shall be established on the word of two witnesses, or three.'
I said it before, and I say it in advance now — as when I was present the second time, and now absent — to those who sinned before and to all the rest: if I come again, I will not spare anyone.
— since you are looking for proof that Christ speaks in me. He is not weak toward you; he is powerful among you.
He was indeed crucified out of weakness, but he lives by God's power. And we too are weak in him, but we will live with him by God's power toward you.
Test yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not recognise about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless you fail the test.
And I hope you will realise that we do not fail the test.
And we pray to God that you do nothing wrong — not so that we may appear to have passed the test, but so that you may do what is good, even if we should look like failures.
We can do nothing against the truth — only for the truth.
We rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong. And this is what we pray for: that you be put back in order.
This is why I am writing these things while absent — so that when I am present I will not have to be severe, using the authority the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
Finally, brothers and sisters: rejoice; be put back in order; be comforted; think the same thing; live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the holy ones send you their greetings.

The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you. Amen. [Second to the Corinthians, written from Philippi in Macedonia by Titus and Luke.]

2 john_1.t: The elder — to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth; and not only me, but everyone who has come to know the truth,
because of the truth that remains in us — and it will be with us forever.
Grace, mercy and peace will be with us from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I was very glad to find some of your children walking in truth, just as the Father commanded us.
And now, lady, I'm asking you — not that I'm writing you a new command, but the one we've had from the beginning — that we love one another.
And this is what love is: that we walk by his commands. And this is the command, just as you heard from the beginning — that you walk in it.
because many deceivers have gone out into the world — the ones who don't confess Jesus Christ coming in flesh. This one is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Watch yourselves, so you don't lose what we worked for, but get a full wage.
Anyone who runs ahead and doesn't remain in the teaching of Christ doesn't have God. The one who remains in the teaching — that's the one who has both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you and doesn't bring this teaching, don't take him into a house, and don't say 'welcome' to him.
Because whoever says 'welcome' to him shares in his evil works.
I have a lot to write to you, but I didn't want to use paper and ink — I'm hoping to come to you and talk mouth to mouth, so that your joy may be complete.
The children of your chosen sister send you their greetings.

2 peter_1.t: Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have been allotted a trust worth just as much as ours, in the rightness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:
May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the full knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness, through the full knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and excellence.

Through these he has given us the precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become sharers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through craving.
For this very reason, put every effort into it: supply excellence alongside your trust; and knowledge alongside the excellence;
and self-control alongside the knowledge; and endurance alongside the self-control; and godliness alongside the endurance;
and brotherly love alongside the godliness; and love alongside the brotherly love.
Because if these things are yours and keep increasing, they'll keep you from being idle or unfruitful in the full knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Anyone who doesn't have these things is blind, short-sighted, having taken on forgetfulness of the cleansing from his old sins.
So all the more, brothers and sisters, make every effort to make your calling and choosing secure; because if you do these things, you'll never stumble.
That's how the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you.
So I'll always be ready to remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
And I think it's right, as long as I'm in this tent, to stir you up with a reminder,
since I know that the laying aside of my tent is coming soon, just as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.
And I'll make every effort to see that after my departure you'll be able to call these things to mind at any time.
We didn't follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and arrival of our Lord Jesus Christ — we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty.
He received honour and glory from God the Father when a voice like this was carried to him by the Majestic Glory: 'This is my Son, my beloved, the one I have taken delight in.'
And we heard that voice ourselves, carried from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain — and you do well to pay attention to it, like a lamp shining in a murky place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts —
knowing this above all — that no prophecy of Scripture comes about from anyone's own untying of it.
Because prophecy was never carried along by any human being's will; it was people carried along by the Holy Spirit who spoke from God.

2 peter_2.t: But there were false prophets among the people too, just as there will be false teachers among you — people who will smuggle in destructive divisions and even deny the Master who bought them, and bring swift destruction on themselves.
And many will follow their debaucheries, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed;
and in their greed they'll exploit you with fabricated words. Their judgement, pronounced long ago, isn't idle, and their destruction isn't asleep.
For if God didn't spare angels when they sinned, but threw them into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of deep gloom, kept for judgement;
and if he didn't spare the ancient world but preserved Noah, a herald of rightness, along with seven others, when he brought a flood on a world of the ungodly;
and if he condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, reducing them to ashes in an overturning, setting them as an example of what is coming for the ungodly;
and if he rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the lawless people's way of life in their debauchery —
for that righteous man, living among them, tormented his righteous soul day after day with what he saw and heard of their lawless deeds —
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly out of a trial, and how to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgement —
and above all those who go after the flesh in a craving that defiles, and who look down on authority. Bold, self-willed, they don't tremble when they blaspheme glorious ones,
whereas angels, who are greater in strength and power, don't bring a blasphemous judgement against them before the Lord.
But these people — like irrational animals, creatures of instinct born to be caught and destroyed, blaspheming what they don't understand — will also be destroyed in their own destruction,
wronged as the wage for wrongdoing. They count it a pleasure to revel in broad daylight; stains and blemishes, they revel in their deceptions while they feast with you.
Their eyes are full of an adulteress and never stop sinning. They bait unsteady souls. Their heart is trained in greed. Children of a curse!
They left the straight road and were led astray. They followed the road of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wage of wrongdoing
but was rebuked for his own lawbreaking: a mute beast of burden spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet's madness.
These people are springs with no water, mists driven by a squall; the gloom of darkness has been kept for them.
They utter swollen, empty words, and they use the cravings of the flesh and debaucheries to bait people who are only just escaping from those who live in error.
They promise them freedom, and they're slaves of corruption themselves — because whatever overpowers a person is what he's been enslaved to.

Because if they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the full knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, and then get entangled in them again and overpowered, the last state has become worse for them than the first.
It would have been better for them never to have known the way of rightness than to know it and then turn back from the holy command handed on to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: 'A dog goes back to its own vomit,' and 'a washed sow goes back to wallow in the mud.'

2 peter_3.t: This is the second letter I'm writing to you now, beloved. In both of them I'm stirring up your sincere mind with a reminder,
so that you'll remember what the holy prophets said beforehand, and the command of the Lord and Saviour given through your apostles.
Know this above all: in the last days mockers will come with their mocking, following their own cravings
and saying, 'Where is the promise of his arrival? Ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything goes on just the way it has from the beginning of creation.'
In holding this they overlook the fact that heavens existed long ago, and an earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
and by these the world of that time was flooded with water and destroyed.
But by that same word the present heavens and earth have been stored up for fire, kept for the day of judgement and destruction of ungodly people.
But don't let this one thing escape you, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord isn't slow about his promise, the way some people reckon slowness; he's patient toward you, not wanting anyone to be destroyed but wanting all to make room for a change of mind.
The day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements will be dissolved as they burn, and the earth and the works in it will be exposed.
Since all these things are being dissolved this way, what sort of people ought you to be, in holy ways of living and godliness,
expecting and hurrying on the arrival of the day of God — and because of it the heavens will be dissolved in flames and the elements melt as they burn?
But according to his promise we're expecting new heavens and a new earth, where rightness lives.
So then, beloved, since you're expecting these things, make every effort to be found by him without spot or blemish, at peace.
And count the patience of our Lord as rescue — just as our beloved brother Paul wrote to you too, according to the wisdom given to him,

as he does in all his letters when he speaks about these matters in them. There are some things in them that are hard to understand, and the untaught and unsteady twist them — as they twist the rest of the Scriptures — to their own destruction.
So you, beloved — you know this in advance, so be on your guard: don't get carried off by the error of lawless people and fall from your own steadiness.
Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be the glory, both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

2 thessalonians_1.t: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We owe God thanks for you always, brothers and sisters — and it is fitting that we do — because your trust is growing beyond measure and the love every one of you has for each other keeps increasing.
So we boast about you ourselves, among God's assemblies — about your endurance and trust in all your persecutions, in the afflictions you're bearing.
This is evidence of God's just judgement — so that you may be counted worthy of God's kingdom, which you are also suffering for.
since it's just, in God's sight, to pay affliction back to those who afflict you —
and relief to you who are afflicted, along with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with the angels of his power,
in flaming fire, dealing out justice to those who don't know God and those who don't obey the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They'll pay the penalty: eternal ruin, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his strength,
when he comes on that day to be glorified in his holy ones and marvelled at among all who believed — because our testimony to you was believed.
That's what we're always praying for you: that our God may count you worthy of his call and fulfil every good desire and work of trust with power,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

2 thessalonians_2.t: Now about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered to him — we're asking you, brothers and sisters,
don't let yourselves be shaken out of your mind so fast, or alarmed — not by a spirit, or a word, or a letter supposedly from us — as though the day of the Lord had already come.
Don't let anyone deceive you, in any way at all. For that day won't come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed — the son of destruction,
the one who opposes and lifts himself above everything called god or object of worship — so that he takes his seat in God's temple, displaying himself as being God.
Don't you remember? When I was still with you, I kept telling you these things.
And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed at his own time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work — only until the one now restraining is out of the way.
And then the lawless one will be revealed — and the Lord Jesus will do away with him by the breath of his mouth and abolish him by the appearing of his coming.
The coming of the lawless one is by Satan's working, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
and with every deception of wrongdoing, for those who are perishing — because they did not receive the love of the truth, so as to be saved.
And that is why God sends them a strong delusion, so that they believe the lie,
so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wrongdoing instead.
But we owe God thanks for you always, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for deliverance — in the holiness the Spirit gives, and in trust in the truth,
That's what he called you to, through our good news — so that you may obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers and sisters — stand firm, and hold on to the traditions you were taught, whether by word or by our letter.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father — the one who loved us and gave us eternal encouragement and good hope in grace —
encourage your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.

2 thessalonians_3.t: Finally, brothers and sisters, pray for us — that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, just as it is with you,
and that we may be rescued from perverse and evil people — for not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He'll strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
And we're confident in the Lord about you: that you're doing what we instruct, and will do it.
May the Lord direct your hearts into God's love and into the endurance of Christ.

We instruct you, brothers and sisters, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: keep away from every brother or sister who walks in a disorderly way, not according to the tradition they received from us.
For you know yourselves how you must imitate us: we were not disorderly among you,
and we didn't eat anyone's bread as a gift — instead we worked night and day, at labour and hardship, so as not to burden any of you.
Not that we don't have the right, but so that we could give you ourselves as a pattern to imitate.
For even when we were with you, this is what we kept instructing you: if anyone is not willing to work, he is not to eat either.
For we hear that some among you are walking in a disorderly way — doing no work, just being busybodies.
Such people we instruct and urge, in the Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and eat their own bread.
And you, brothers and sisters — don't grow weary in doing good.
If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of that person and don't associate with him, so that he may be put to shame.
Yet don't regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times, in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
This greeting is in my own hand — Paul's. That's the sign in every letter. That's how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen. [To the Thessalonians, second letter, written from Athens.]

2 timothy_1.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, in keeping with the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
To Timothy, my dear child: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I'm grateful to God — the God I serve as my forebears did, with a clean conscience — as I remember you constantly in my requests, night and day,
longing to see you — remembering your tears — so that I can be filled with joy.
I've been reminded of the unhypocritical trust in you — the trust that lived first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice — and I'm persuaded it lives in you too.
That's why I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands —
for God didn't give us a spirit of cowardice, but of power and love and sound judgement.
So don't be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, or of me, his prisoner. Instead, take your share of suffering for the gospel, according to God's power —
the God who saved us and called us with a holy calling — not because of our works but because of his own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times,
and now made visible through the appearing of our Saviour Christ Jesus, who put an end to death and brought life and incorruptibility to light through the gospel.
It's for this that I was appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher of the nations.
That's why I'm suffering all this. But I'm not ashamed, because I know the one I have trusted, and I'm persuaded that he is able to guard what has been entrusted to me until that day.
Hold on to the pattern of healthy words you heard from me, in the trust and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know this: everyone in Asia turned away from me — Phygelus and Hermogenes among them.
May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and wasn't ashamed of my chain.
On the contrary — when he got to Rome he looked hard for me, and he found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know better than I do how much he served in Ephesus.

2 timothy_2.t: So you, my child — be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And what you heard from me through many witnesses — hand that on to trustworthy people who will be competent to teach others too.
Take your share of suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one serving as a soldier gets tangled up in the affairs of ordinary life, so that he can please the one who enlisted him.
And if someone competes as an athlete, he doesn't get the crown unless he competes by the rules.
The farmer who works hard must be the first to get a share of the crops.
Think about what I'm saying — the Lord will give you insight in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, from David's seed — according to my gospel,
and it's for that gospel that I suffer hardship, right down to chains, like a criminal. But God's word is not chained.
So I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may get the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
Trustworthy is the saying: If we died with him, we'll also live with him;
if we endure, we'll also reign with him; if we deny him, he will also deny us;
if we are unfaithful, he stays faithful — he cannot deny himself.
Keep reminding them of these things, charging them solemnly before God not to fight over words — it does no good, and it ruins the people listening.
Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved — a worker with nothing to be ashamed of, cutting the word of truth straight.
Keep away from profane empty talk — they'll only advance further into ungodliness,
and their word will spread like gangrene. Hymenaeus and Philetus are among them —
they've missed the mark about the truth, saying the resurrection has already happened, and they're overturning the faith of some.
All the same, God's firm foundation stands, and it carries this seal: "The Lord knew those who are his," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord stand away from unrighteousness."
In a large house there are vessels not just of gold and silver but of wood and clay too — some for honour, some for dishonour.
So if anyone cleans himself out from these things, he'll be a vessel for honour — made holy, useful to the master, ready for every good work.
Run from the desires of youth. Chase after rightness, trust, love and peace, along with those who call on the Lord out of a clean heart.
Have nothing to do with foolish, uninstructed debates — you know they breed fights.
And the Lord's servant must not fight, but be gentle with everyone, able to teach, patient when wronged,
correcting opponents gently. Maybe God will grant them a change of mind leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
and they'll come back to their senses, out of the devil's trap, having been captured alive by him to do his will.

2 timothy_3.t: Know this: in the last days hard times are going to set in.
For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, savage, hating what is good,
treacherous, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
holding on to a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from people like that.
Some of them are the ones who slip into households and take captive weak women loaded down with sins, driven along by all kinds of desires,
always learning and never able to arrive at a full knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, these people oppose the truth too — their minds ruined, and failing the test when it comes to the faith.
But they won't get much further, because their folly will be obvious to everyone — just as theirs was.
You, though — you have followed my teaching closely: my way of life, my purpose, my trust, my patience, my love, my endurance,
my persecutions, my sufferings — the kind of thing that happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra. What persecutions I endured! And the Lord rescued me out of them all.
And in fact everyone who wants to live in a godly way in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
while evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
You, though — stay in what you learned and were convinced of. You know who you learned it from,
and that since you were a baby you have known the sacred writings, the ones that can make you wise for salvation through trust in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for reproof, for setting straight, for training in rightness,
so that the person of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.

2 timothy_4.t: So I charge you solemnly, before God and the Lord Christ Jesus — the one who is about to judge the living and the dead — and by his appearing and his kingdom:
proclaim the word. Be ready in season and out of season. Reprove, rebuke, urge — with all patience, and with teaching.
For a time is coming when they won't put up with healthy teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they'll pile up teachers for themselves, with itching ears,
and they'll turn their hearing away from the truth and be turned aside to myths.
But you — keep a clear head in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, carry out your service in full.
As for me, I'm already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is here.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on there's a crown of rightness laid up for me, which the Lord — the righteous judge — will give me on that day; and not only to me but to everyone who has loved his appearing.
Do your best to come to me soon.
Demas has deserted me — he loved the present age — and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens went to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Pick up Mark and bring him with you — he's useful to me for service.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas — and the scrolls, especially the parchments.
Alexander the coppersmith did me a lot of harm. The Lord will repay him according to his works.
Watch out for him yourself — he strongly opposed what we said.
At my first defence nobody stood with me; they all deserted me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the proclamation might be carried out in full and all the nations might hear — and I was rescued out of the lion's mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth. I left Trophimus ill at Miletus.
Do your best to get here before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers and sisters.
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

3 john_1.t: From the elder — to Gaius the beloved, the one I love in truth.
Beloved, I pray that everything goes well with you and that you're in good health, just as it goes well with your soul.
I was so glad when brothers came and testified to your truth — that you're walking in truth, just as you do.
There's no greater joy for me than these — hearing that my children are walking in the truth.
Beloved, you're doing a faithful thing in whatever you do for the brothers — and for strangers at that —
They testified to your love in front of an assembly. You'll do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
They set out for the sake of the Name, and they took nothing from the gentiles.
So we ought to take people like that in, so we can become co-workers with the truth.
I wrote something to the community, but Diotrephes — who loves to be first among them — won't receive us.

So if I come, I'll bring up the things he's doing — babbling against us with evil words. And not satisfied with those, he won't receive the brothers himself, and he stops the ones who want to, and throws them out of the community.
Beloved, don't imitate the bad but the good. Whoever does good is from God; whoever does bad hasn't seen God.
Everyone has testified to Demetrius — and so has the truth itself. And we testify too, and you know our testimony is true.
I had a lot to write to you, but I don't want to write to you with ink and pen.
But I hope to see you soon, and we'll talk face to face.
Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

acts_1.t: The first account I put together, Theophilus, was about everything Jesus began to do and to teach,
up to the day he was taken up, after he'd given orders through the Holy Spirit to the apostles he had chosen.
After he suffered, he showed himself alive to them with many proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
While he was with them he ordered them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised — "which you heard from me;
because John baptised with water, but you will be baptised in the Holy Spirit — and not many days from now."
So when they were together they asked him, "Lord, is this the time you're restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
He said to them, "It's not for you to know times or seasons — the Father has set those by his own authority,
but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you, and you'll be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."
When he had said this, as they watched, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight.
They were still staring into the sky as he went when suddenly two men in white clothes were standing beside them,
and they said, "Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way you watched him go into heaven."
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called Olive Grove — it's near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's walk.

When they came in, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
They were all devoted to prayer, of one mind, together with women and Mary the mother of Jesus and his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and sisters — there were about a hundred and twenty people gathered — and said,
"Brothers, the scripture had to be fulfilled that the Holy Spirit spoke long beforehand through David's mouth about Judas, who became the guide for the men who arrested Jesus.
He was counted as one of us, and he drew a share in this service."
(This man bought a field with the payment for his wrongdoing, and he fell headlong, burst open in the middle, and all his insides spilled out.
It became known to everyone living in Jerusalem, so they called that field, in their own language, Hakeldama — that is, Field of Blood.)
"For it is written in the book of Psalms: 'Let his home be deserted, and let there be no one living in it,' and, 'Let someone else take his position of oversight.'
So one of the men who were with us the whole time the Lord Jesus came and went among us —
from John's baptism right up to the day he was taken up from us — has to become a witness with us of his resurrection."
So they put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, also known as Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, "Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show which of these two you have chosen
to take the place in this service and mission that Judas left to go to his own place."
They cast lots for them, the lot fell to Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

acts_2.t: When the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all together in one place.
Suddenly there was a sound from the sky like a violent wind rushing through, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw tongues like fire, dividing apart, and one settled on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them to speak out.
Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
