Look — I, Paul, am telling you: if you get circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
And I testify again, to every person who gets circumcised: he's under obligation to do the whole law.
You who are being justified by law — you've been cut off from Christ. You've fallen out of grace.
For by the Spirit, out of trust, we eagerly await the hope of rightness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything — only trust working through love.
You were running well. Who cut in on you and stopped you being persuaded by the truth?
That persuasion doesn't come from the one who calls you.
A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
I'm confident about you in the Lord — that you'll think nothing otherwise. But the one who is unsettling you will bear the judgement, whoever he is.
But brothers and sisters — if I'm still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the scandal of the cross has been abolished.
I wish the people stirring you up would go the whole way and castrate themselves.
You were called to freedom, brothers and sisters — only don't turn that freedom into a base of operations for the flesh. Instead, through love, serve one another as slaves.
For the whole law has been fulfilled in one word: 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.'
But if you bite and devour one another — watch out you aren't consumed by one another.
Here's what I mean: walk by the Spirit, and you will certainly not carry out the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do the things you want.
But if you're led by the Spirit, you're not under law.
The works of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, indecency,
idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of rage, selfish rivalries, dissensions, factions,
envy, murders, drunkenness, wild parties, and things like these. I'm warning you about these, as I warned you before: those who practise such things will not inherit God's kingdom.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let's keep in line with the Spirit too.
Let's not become conceited — provoking one another, envying one another.

galatians_6.t: Brothers and sisters, if a person is caught out in some misstep, you who are spiritual should restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness — watching yourself, in case you too are tested.
Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfil the law of Christ.
For if someone thinks he's something when he's nothing, he's deceiving himself.
Let each person test his own work. Then he'll have grounds to boast in himself alone, and not by comparison with someone else.
For each one will carry his own load.
The one being taught the word should share all good things with the one teaching.
Don't be deceived: God is not mocked. Whatever a person sows, that's what he will also reap.
The one who sows into his own flesh will reap decay from the flesh; the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Let's not grow weary in doing good; for in its own season we will reap, if we don't give out.
So then, as we have opportunity, let's work what is good toward everyone — and especially toward those of the household of the faith.
Look at the size of the letters I'm writing to you with my own hand.
It's the ones who want to make a good showing in the flesh who are compelling you to be circumcised — and only so they won't be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For not even the circumcised keep the law themselves — but they want you circumcised, so they can boast in your flesh.
But may I never boast — except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything — what counts is new creation.
And as many as keep in line with this rule — peace be on them, and mercy, and on the Israel of God.
From now on, let no one cause me trouble — for I carry the brand-marks of Jesus on my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers and sisters. Amen.

hebrews_1.t: Long ago, in many pieces and in many ways, God spoke to the ancestors through the prophets.
and at the end of these days he has spoken to us in a Son — the one he appointed heir of everything, the one through whom he also made the ages —

He is the shining-out of God's glory and the exact stamp of his very being, and he carries everything along by the word of his power. When he had made cleansing for sins through himself, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
having become as much better than the angels as the name he has inherited is finer than theirs.
For to which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are my Son; today I have fathered you'? Or again, 'I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me'?
And again, when he brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says, 'And let all God's angels bow down before him.'
About the angels he says, 'He makes his angels winds, and his ministers a flame of fire.'
but to the Son he says, 'Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of what is right.'
'You loved rightness and hated lawlessness; that is why God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy above your companions.'
And, 'You, Lord, laid the earth's foundation in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands.'
'They will perish, but you remain. They will all wear out like a piece of clothing;'
'you will roll them up like a coat, like clothing, and they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will never run out.'
And to which of the angels has he ever said, 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet'?
Aren't they all spirits in service, sent out to help those who are going to inherit rescue?

hebrews_2.t: So we have to pay much closer attention to what we have heard, or we'll drift past it.
For if the message spoken through angels proved firm, and every violation and act of disobedience received a just repayment,
how will we escape if we neglect a rescue as great as this? It began by being spoken through the Lord, and it was confirmed to us by those who heard him,
while God testified alongside them with signs and wonders and all kinds of acts of power, and with distributions of holy spirit given as he willed.
For it was not to angels that God subjected the world that is coming, the one we are talking about.
Somewhere someone has testified: 'What is a human being, that you keep him in mind, or a son of man, that you look after him?
'You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honour, and set him over the works of your hands;
'you put everything in subjection under his feet.' In subjecting everything to him, God left nothing outside that subjection. But as things are, we don't yet see everything subjected to him.
But we do see Jesus — made a little lower than the angels because of the suffering of death, and now crowned with glory and honour — so that by God's grace he might taste death for everyone.
It was fitting that God — the one for whom and through whom everything exists — in bringing many sons to glory, should bring the one who leads them to rescue to completion through sufferings.
For the one who makes holy and those being made holy all come from one source; that is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters,
saying, 'I will announce your name to my brothers and sisters; in the middle of the assembly I will sing your praise.'
And again, 'I will put my trust in him.' And again, 'Here I am, and the children God gave me.'
Since the children share blood and flesh, he too shared the same things in the same way, so that through death he might break the power of the one who holds the power of death — that is, the devil —
and set free all those who through fear of death were held in slavery their whole life long.
For it is surely not angels he takes hold of, but Abraham's offspring.
So he had to be made like his brothers and sisters in every way, so that he could become a merciful and faithful high priest in what concerns God, to make propitiation for the people's sins.
Because he himself suffered when he was tested, he is able to help those who are being tested.

hebrews_3.t: So then, holy brothers and sisters, sharers in a heavenly calling — think hard about the one God sent, the high priest of what we confess: Jesus,
who was faithful to the one who appointed him, as Moses also was in all God's house.
For this one has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, in the same way that the builder of a house has more honour than the house itself.
Every house is built by someone, and the one who built everything is God.
Moses was faithful in all God's house as an attendant, as a testimony to what would be spoken later,
but the Christ was faithful as a son over God's house. And we are that house, if we hold on to our freedom to speak and the hope we boast in, firm to the end.
So, as the Holy Spirit says: 'Today, if you hear his voice,
'don't harden your hearts as they did in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the desert,
'where your ancestors put me to the test, tried me out, and saw what I did
forty years. That is why I was angry with that generation, and said, 'Their hearts are always wandering, and they have never known my ways.'
'So I swore in my anger: They will never enter my rest.'
Watch out, brothers and sisters, that none of you has an evil, untrusting heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, keep encouraging one another every day, as long as it is still called 'Today,' so that none of you is hardened by the trickery of sin.
For we have come to share in the Christ — if we hold the ground we first stood on firm to the end.
as it is said: 'Today, if you hear his voice, don't harden your hearts as they did in the rebellion.'
Who was it that heard and rebelled? Wasn't it all those who came out of Egypt under Moses?
And who was he angry with for forty years? Wasn't it with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the desert?
And who did he swear to that they would never enter his rest, if not to the ones who refused to be persuaded?
So we see that they could not enter, because they would not trust.

hebrews_4.t: So let us be careful: while the promise of entering his rest still stands open, none of you should turn out to have fallen short of it.
For we have had the good news announced to us just as they did; but the message they heard did no good, because they were not joined by faith to those who heard it.
We who have trusted are entering that rest, just as he has said, 'So I swore in my anger: They will never enter my rest' — and this even though his works were finished from the founding of the world.
For somewhere he says this about the seventh day: 'And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.'
And again in this place: 'They will never enter my rest.'
So since it remains for some to enter it, and those who were given the good news before did not enter because they refused to be persuaded,
God again marks out a certain day — 'Today' — speaking through David so long afterwards, in the words already quoted: 'Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.'
For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
So there is still a sabbath rest waiting for God's people.
For whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his own work, just as God did from his.
So let us make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one falls by following the same pattern of refusal.
For God's word is alive and at work, sharper than any double-edged sword. It cuts through to where soul and spirit divide, joints and marrow, and it can judge the heart's thoughts and intentions.
No creature is hidden from him; everything lies naked and exposed before the eyes of the one we must answer to.
So, since we have a great high priest who has gone right through the heavens — Jesus, the Son of God — let us hold on to what we confess.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to feel our weaknesses with us; he was tested in every way as we are, apart from sin.
So let us come to the throne of grace with freedom to speak, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.

hebrews_5.t: Every high priest is taken from among people and appointed to act on their behalf in what concerns God, to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, since he himself is wrapped in weakness.
And because of that weakness he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for the people's.
And no one takes this honour on himself; he is called by God, as Aaron was.
So too the Christ did not give himself the glory of becoming high priest. It was given by the one who said to him, 'You are my Son; today I have fathered you.'
As he also says in another place, 'You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.'
In the days of his flesh he offered up prayers and pleas, with loud crying and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death; and he was heard because of his reverence.
Though he was a son, he learned obedience from what he suffered,
and once brought to completion he became the source of eternal rescue for all who obey him,
and was named by God a high priest in the line of Melchizedek.
We have a great deal to say about this, and it is hard to explain, because you have grown dull of hearing.
By now you ought to be teachers, but you need someone to teach you the basic elements of God's words all over again. You have come to need milk, not solid food.
For anyone living on milk has no experience of the word of rightness; he is still an infant.
Solid food is for the mature — those who through practice have trained their senses to tell good from bad.

hebrews_6.t: So let us leave behind the first teaching about the Christ and be carried on toward completeness. We are not laying the foundation again — a change of mind that turns from dead works, and trust toward God,
teaching about washings, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
And this we will do, if God permits.
For it is impossible, in the case of people who were once given light, who tasted the heavenly gift and came to share in holy spirit,
who tasted the goodness of God's word and the powers of the age that is coming,
and who have then fallen away — it is impossible to renew them again to a change of mind, since they are crucifying the Son of God for themselves all over again and holding him up to public disgrace.
Land that drinks in the rain that often falls on it, and produces a crop useful to those it is farmed for, receives a share of blessing from God.
But if it produces thorns and thistles, it is worthless and close to being cursed, and it ends up burned off.
But in your case, dear friends, we are convinced of better things — things that belong to rescue — even though we speak like this.
God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you showed for his name in serving his holy people, as you still do.
We want each of you to show the same eagerness right to the end, so that your hope may be fully realised,
so that you will not grow dull, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
When God made his promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater to swear by, he swore by himself,
saying, 'I will surely bless you and surely multiply you.'
And so, after waiting patiently, Abraham obtained the promise.
People swear by someone greater than themselves, and the oath settles every dispute and confirms what is said.
So God, wanting to show the heirs of the promise even more clearly that his purpose does not change, guaranteed it with an oath.
So by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have run for refuge have strong encouragement to take hold of the hope set before us.
We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, safe and firm, and it goes right inside, behind the curtain,
where Jesus has entered ahead of us on our behalf, having become a high priest forever in the line of Melchizedek.

hebrews_7.t: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham as he came back from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
and Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name means first 'king of rightness', and then he is also king of Salem, that is, 'king of peace'.
He has no father, no mother, no family record, no beginning of days and no end of life; made like the Son of God, he remains a priest without a break.
See how great he was: even Abraham the patriarch gave him a tenth of the best of the spoils.

The descendants of Levi who take up the priesthood have a command in the law to collect a tenth from the people — that is, from their own brothers and sisters — even though they too are descended from Abraham.
But this man, who does not trace his descent from them, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who held the promises.
And beyond dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
In the one case, mortal men receive the tenth; in the other, someone of whom it is testified that he lives.
One might even say that Levi, who receives the tenth, paid it himself through Abraham,
since he was still in his ancestor's body when Melchizedek met him.

Now if completeness could have come through the Levitical priesthood — and it was on that basis that the people received the law — why was there still need for another kind of priest to arise in the line of Melchizedek, rather than one named in the line of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed too.
The one these things are said about belonged to a different tribe, and no one from that tribe has ever served at the altar.
It is obvious that our Lord came from Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests in connection with that tribe.
This is even clearer if another priest arises who is like Melchizedek,
one who has become a priest not by a rule about physical descent but by the power of a life that cannot be destroyed.
For it is testified of him, 'You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.'
The earlier command is set aside because it was weak and useless —
for the law brought nothing to completion — and a better hope is brought in alongside it, and through that hope we draw near to God.
And it did not happen without an oath. For those became priests without an oath-taking,
but he became a priest with an oath, through the one who said to him, 'The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek' —
That is how much better the covenant is that Jesus has become the guarantee of.
There have been many of those priests, because death kept them from staying in office.
But because he remains forever, he holds a priesthood that does not pass to anyone else.
So he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, since he always lives to plead for them.
Such a high priest is exactly what we needed: devoted, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and raised above the heavens.
He has no need, as those high priests did, to offer sacrifices day after day — first for his own sins and then for the people's. He did this once for all when he offered himself.
The law appoints as high priests men who have weakness; but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been brought to completion forever.

hebrews_8.t: The main point of what we are saying is this: we do have such a high priest, and he has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
and he serves in the holy place, the true tent that the Lord set up, not a human being.
Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, so this one too must have something to offer.
If he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already those who offer the gifts prescribed by the law.
They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was warned when he was about to build the tent: 'See that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.'
But as it is, the ministry he has obtained is that much better, since he is also the mediator of a better covenant, one enacted on better promises.
For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need to look for a place for a second.
For God does find fault with them when he says: 'Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will bring to completion a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
'not like the covenant I made with their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. They did not stay in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.'

'This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws into their mind and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they will be my people.'
'No longer will each one teach his fellow citizen, or each one his brother, saying, "Know the Lord", because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.'
'For I will be merciful toward their wrongs, and I will remember their sins no more.'
By calling this covenant 'new', he has made the first one old; and what is growing old and ageing is close to disappearing.

hebrews_9.t: Now the first tent did have regulations for worship, and its holy place belonged to this world.
A tent was set up. In its first section were the lampstand, the table, and the setting out of the loaves; this is called the Holy Place.
Behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies.
It had the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant, covered all over with gold. In it were a gold jar holding the manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the place of mercy. We cannot speak about these things in detail now.
With everything arranged like this, the priests go regularly into the first section to carry out their duties.
But only the high priest goes into the second section, once a year, and never without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins the people committed in ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit shows that the way into the holy place had not yet been revealed while the first tent still had its standing.
This is a picture for the present time: gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot bring the worshipper to completion in conscience.
They deal only with food and drink and various washings — regulations for the flesh, imposed until the time of setting things right.
But the Christ came as high priest of the good things that have now come, through the greater and more complete tent, not made by hands — that is, not part of this creation.
He entered the holy place once for all, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own blood, and so obtained an eternal setting-free.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who have been defiled, makes them holy so that their flesh is clean,
how much more will the blood of the Christ — who through eternal spirit offered himself to God without blemish — cleanse our conscience from dead works, so that we can serve the living God?

This is why he is the mediator of a new covenant: a death has taken place that sets people free from the violations committed under the first covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.
For where there is a covenant, the death of the one who made the covenant has to be brought forward;
for a covenant is confirmed over the dead, since it never takes effect while the one who made it is alive.
That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.

When Moses had spoken every command of the law to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
saying, 'This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you.'
In the same way he sprinkled with blood both the tent and all the vessels used in worship.
In fact, under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without blood being shed there is no forgiveness.
So the copies of the heavenly things had to be cleansed this way, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
For the Christ did not enter a holy place made by hands, a copy of the true one, but heaven itself, to appear now before God's face on our behalf.
And he did not enter in order to offer himself again and again, as the high priest enters the holy place year after year with blood that is not his own.
Otherwise he would have had to suffer many times since the founding of the world. But as it is, he has appeared once, at the completion of the ages, to set sin aside through his sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so the Christ, offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time — not to deal with sin, but to bring rescue to those who are eagerly waiting for him.

hebrews_10.t: The law has only a shadow of the good things that are coming, not the actual form of those things. So it can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year without a break, bring to completion those who come to worship.
Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered? The worshippers, once cleansed, would no longer have had any consciousness of sins.
But in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins,
because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take sins away.
That is why, when he comes into the world, he says: 'Sacrifice and offering you did not want, but you prepared a body for me.
'You took no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sin offerings.'
'Then I said, "Here I am — it is written about me in the scroll of the book — I have come to do your will, God."'
First he says, 'Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not want, and took no pleasure in them' — and these are the ones offered according to the law.
Then he says, 'Here I am, I have come to do your will.' He takes away the first in order to set up the second.
And by that will we have been made holy, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Every priest stands day after day at his service, offering the same sacrifices again and again — sacrifices that can never take sins away.
But this one offered a single sacrifice for sins for all time, and then sat down at God's right hand,
and since then he waits until his enemies are made a footstool under his feet.
For by one offering he has brought to completion for all time those who are being made holy.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. After saying,
'This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws on their hearts, and write them on their mind' —
then he adds, 'And I will remember their sins and their lawless acts no more.'
And where these have been forgiven, there is no longer any offering for sin.
So then, brothers and sisters, we have freedom to enter the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
by the fresh and living way he opened for us through the curtain — that is, through his flesh —
and since we have a great priest over God's house,
let us come near with a true heart, in the full assurance that faith brings, our hearts sprinkled clean from a bad conscience and our bodies washed with clean water.
Let us hold on to the hope we confess, without swerving, for the one who promised is faithful.
And let us think hard about how to provoke one another to love and good deeds,
not staying away from our own gatherings, as some have made a habit of doing, but encouraging one another — and all the more as you see the Day coming closer.
If we go on sinning deliberately after we have received the full knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left,
only a terrifying expectation of judgment, and a fury of fire about to consume those who set themselves against God.
Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much worse a punishment do you think someone deserves who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, treated as ordinary the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know the one who said, 'Vengeance is mine; I will repay,' and again, 'The Lord will judge his people.'
It is a terrifying thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But remember the earlier days, when you had just been given light and endured a hard contest of suffering.
Sometimes you were publicly exposed to insult and persecution; at other times you stood alongside those who were treated that way.
You suffered along with the prisoners, and you accepted with joy the seizure of your property, because you knew that you have for yourselves a better and lasting possession in the heavens.
So do not throw away your freedom to speak; it carries a great reward.
You need endurance, so that after you have done God's will you may receive what was promised.
For in just a very little while, 'the one who is coming will come and will not delay.'
'But the one who is right with me will live by faith; and if he shrinks back, I take no pleasure in him.'
But we are not people who shrink back and are destroyed; we are people who trust, and so keep our lives.

hebrews_11.t: Faith is the assurance of what we hope for, the conviction of things we do not see.
It was for this that the people of old were spoken well of.
By faith we understand that the ages were put in order by God's word, so that what is seen has not come from things that appear.
By faith Abel offered God a greater sacrifice than Cain did. Through it he was attested as right with God, since God testified about his gifts; and through it he still speaks, though he died.
By faith Enoch was taken away so that he did not see death; he was not found, because God took him. Before he was taken he was attested as one who had pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please him. Anyone who comes to God must trust that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him out.
By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen, took God seriously and built an ark to rescue his household. Through it he condemned the world and became heir of the rightness that comes by faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he was going to receive as an inheritance; and he went out without knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a stranger in the land he was promised, as though it belonged to someone else, staying in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.
For he was looking for the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive even past the season of her age, since she counted faithful the one who had promised.
And so from one man — and one as good as dead — there came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
All these died in faith. They did not receive what was promised; they saw it from a distance and greeted it, and confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.
People who say such things make it clear that they are looking for a homeland of their own.
If they had been thinking of the country they left, they would have had a chance to go back.
But as it is, they long for a better country — a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when he was tested, has offered up Isaac. The man who had received the promises was offering up his only son,
even though he had been told, 'It is through Isaac that your offspring will be named.'
He reasoned that God is able even to raise the dead; and figuratively speaking, he did receive him back from there.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things still to come.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons, and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, spoke of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw he was a beautiful child; and they were not afraid of the king's order.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing rather to be mistreated along with God's people than to have the short-lived enjoyment of sin,
He considered the reproach borne for the Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, because he was looking ahead to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt, not afraid of the king's anger; he kept going as though he could see the one who is invisible.
By faith he has kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as though it were dry land; when the Egyptians tried it, they were swallowed up.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after being encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not die along with those who refused to obey, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.
What more should I say? I do not have time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, did what was right, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
put out the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became powerful in war, and turned back foreign armies.
Women received back their dead, raised to life. Others were beaten to death on the wheel, refusing the release offered them, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
Others faced mocking and flogging, and even chains and prison.
They were stoned, sawn in two, put to the test, killed by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, in need, oppressed, mistreated —
the world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
All of these were attested for their faith, yet none of them received what was promised,
since God had foreseen something better for us, so that they would not be brought to completion apart from us.

hebrews_12.t: So then, since we have such a great cloud of witnesses all around us, let us throw off every weight and the sin that so easily entangles us, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,

fixing our eyes on Jesus, who leads the way in our faith and brings it to completion. For the joy set before him he endured a cross, thinking nothing of its shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of God's throne.
Think carefully about the one who endured such hostility from sinners against himself, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of blood.
And you have forgotten the encouragement that speaks to you as sons: 'My son, do not think lightly of the Lord's training, and do not lose heart when he corrects you.
'For the Lord trains the one he loves, and flogs every son he receives.'
Endure what you suffer as training; God is dealing with you as sons. For what son is there whom a father does not train?
If you are without the training that everyone has shared in, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
Besides, we had fathers of our flesh who trained us, and we respected them. How much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live!
They trained us for a few days as they thought best; he does it for our benefit, so that we may share his holiness.
No training seems pleasant at the time, but painful. Later, though, it yields a peaceful harvest of rightness to those who have been trained by it.
So strengthen your drooping hands and your weakened knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame is not put out of joint but healed instead.
Make every effort to be at peace with everyone, and to be holy; without holiness no one will see the Lord.
See to it that no one falls short of God's grace, and that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile many;
and that no one is sexually immoral or without reverence, like Esau, who sold his rights as firstborn for a single meal.
For you know that afterwards, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He found no place for a change of mind, though he sought it with tears.
You have not come to something that can be touched: a mountain blazing with fire, and darkness and gloom and storm,
to a trumpet blast and a voice speaking words — a voice whose hearers begged that no further word be spoken to them.
For they could not bear the command: 'If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned, or shot through with an arrow.'
The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, 'I am terrified and trembling.'
Instead you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to countless angels in festal gathering,
to the assembly of the firstborn whose names are enrolled in heaven, to God the judge of all, to the spirits of righteous people brought to completion,
and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel.

See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. If they did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, how much less will we, if we turn away from the one who warns from heaven.
At that time his voice shook the earth; but now he has promised, 'Once more I will shake not only the earth but heaven too.'
The words 'once more' show the removal of what is shaken — that is, of created things — so that what cannot be shaken may remain.
So then, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us hold on to grace, and through it serve God acceptably, with reverence and awe.
For our God is a consuming fire.

hebrews_13.t: Let love for one another as brothers and sisters remain.
Do not forget to welcome strangers; by doing this some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
Remember those in prison as though you were in prison with them, and those who are mistreated as though it were your own body.
Marriage is to be held in honour by all, and the marriage bed kept undefiled; God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Keep your way of life free from the love of money, and be content with what you have; for he himself has said, 'I will never leave you, and I will never abandon you.'
So we can say with confidence, 'The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can a person do to me?'
Remember your leaders, the ones who spoke God's word to you. Look closely at how their way of life turned out, and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Do not be swept along by all kinds of strange teachings. It is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by food rules, which have never benefited those who followed them.
We have an altar, and those who serve at the tent have no right to eat from it.
The bodies of the animals whose blood the high priest carries into the holy place as a sin offering are burned outside the camp.
That is why Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to make the people holy through his own blood.
So let us go out to him, outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore.
For here we have no lasting city; we are looking for the city that is to come.
So through him let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise — that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.
And do not forget to do good and to share what you have; God is pleased with sacrifices like these.

Let your leaders persuade you, and defer to them; they keep watch over your lives as people who will have to give an account. Let them do it with joy and not with groaning, since that would be no benefit to you.
Pray for us. We are confident that we have a clear conscience, since we want to conduct ourselves honourably in every way.
I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you sooner.
Now may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of an eternal covenant,
equip you with every good thing so that you may do his will, working in us what pleases him, through Jesus Christ. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
I urge you, brothers and sisters, put up with this word of encouragement; I have written to you only briefly.
You should know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will see you when he does.
Greet all your leaders and all God's holy people. Those from Italy send you greetings.
Grace be with all of you. Amen. [Written to the Hebrews from Italy, through Timothy.]

james_1.t: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: greetings.
Count it nothing but joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you fall into trials of every kind,
because you know that the testing of your trust produces endurance.
And let endurance finish its work, so that you'll be complete and whole, lacking nothing.
If any of you is short of wisdom, he should ask God — who gives to everyone without holding back, and without a reproach — and it will be given to him.
But he has to ask in trust, without a moment's doubt — because the one who doubts is like the swell of the sea, wind-driven and blown about.
That person shouldn't suppose he'll receive anything from the Lord —
a two-souled man, unsteady in everything he does.
Let the brother who is low boast in his height,
and let the rich one boast in being brought low, because he'll pass away like a wildflower.
For the sun came up with its scorching heat and dried out the grass; its flower dropped, and the beauty of its face was gone. That's how the rich man will wither, right in the middle of his business.
Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because once he's proved genuine he'll receive the crown of life — the one he promised to those who love him.
No one under trial should say, 'I'm being tried by God.' God can't be tried by evils, and he himself tries no one.
Each person is tried when his own craving drags him off and baits him.
Then the craving conceives and gives birth to sin; and sin, once it's full-grown, delivers death.
Don't be led astray, my beloved brothers and sisters.
Every good gift and every complete present is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, and with him there's no variation, no shadow cast by turning.
He chose to give us birth by a word of truth, so that we'd be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
Know this, my beloved brothers and sisters: everyone should be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
because a man's anger doesn't produce God's rightness.
So strip off everything filthy and every overflow of malice, and take in the implanted word with meekness — it's able to save your lives.
Become doers of the word, not just hearers, reasoning yourselves out of it.
Because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he's like a man studying the face he was born with in a mirror:
he studied himself, and off he's gone, and right away he forgot what he was like.
But whoever stoops to look into the complete law, the law of freedom, and stays there — not a hearer who forgets but a doer of work — that man will be blessed in what he does.
If anyone thinks he's observant and doesn't bridle his tongue but deceives his own heart, his observance is worthless.
Observance that's clean and undefiled before God the Father is this: looking in on orphans and widows in their affliction, and keeping yourself unstained by the world.

james_2.t: My brothers and sisters, don't hold the faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, the Glory, together with acts of favouritism.
Say a man comes into your gathering wearing gold rings and bright clothes, and a poor man comes in too, in filthy clothes,
and you turn to the one in the bright clothes and say, 'You sit here, in the good seat,' and to the poor man, 'You stand over there,' or, 'Sit under my footstool' —
haven't you made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil reasoning?
Listen, my beloved brothers and sisters: didn't God choose the world's poor to be rich in trust, and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
But you dishonoured the poor man. Isn't it the rich who tyrannise you? Aren't they the ones who drag you into court?
Aren't they the ones who blaspheme the good name that was called over you?
Now if you do carry out the royal law according to the Scripture — 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself' — you're doing well.
But if you show favouritism, you're committing sin, convicted by the law as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at one point has become liable for all of it.
Because the one who said 'Do not commit adultery' also said 'Do not murder.' So if you don't commit adultery but you do murder, you've become a transgressor of law.
Speak and act as people about to be judged by a law of freedom.
For judgement is without mercy to the one who showed no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgement.
What's the use, my brothers and sisters, if someone says he has trust but doesn't have works? That trust can't save him, can it?
If a brother or a sister is without clothes and short of the day's food,
and one of you says to them, 'Go in peace, keep warm and eat well,' and doesn't give them what the body needs — what's the use?
So too trust: if it doesn't have works, it's dead by itself.
But someone will say, 'You have trust and I have works.' Show me your trust apart from the works, and I'll show you my trust out of my works.
You trust that God is one — you do well. The demons trust that too, and they shudder.
Do you want proof, you empty man, that trust apart from works is workless?
Wasn't Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that trust was working together with his works, and out of the works the trust was brought to completion —
and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, 'Abraham trusted God, and it was reckoned to him as rightness' — and he was called God's friend.
You see that a person is justified by works and not by trust alone.
And in the same way, wasn't Rahab the prostitute justified by works too, when she took in the messengers and sent them out by another road?
For just as the body without breath is dead, so too trust without works is dead.

james_3.t: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers and sisters, since you know we'll receive a heavier judgement.
We all stumble in a lot of ways. If anyone doesn't stumble in what he says, he's a complete man, able to bridle his whole body as well.
If we put bits in horses' mouths to make them obey us, we steer their whole bodies as well.
Look at ships too — as big as they are, driven by hard winds, they're steered by a tiny rudder, wherever the impulse of the helmsman wants.
So too the tongue is a small part of the body, and it makes huge claims. Look how big a forest so small a fire sets alight —
And the tongue is a fire. The world of injustice, the tongue, is set among our members, staining the whole body, setting the wheel of our existence ablaze, and set ablaze itself by Gehenna.
Every kind of animal and bird, reptile and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed, by humankind —
but no human being can tame the tongue: an unsteady evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse the people who have been made in God's likeness.
Out of the same mouth come blessing and curse. My brothers and sisters, these things shouldn't be happening this way.
A spring doesn't pour fresh water and bitter out of the same opening, does it?
My brothers and sisters, a fig tree can't produce olives, can it? Or a vine, figs? And salt water can't produce fresh either.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show his works out of a good way of life, in the meekness that wisdom brings.
But if you've got bitter zeal and rivalry in your heart, don't boast and lie against the truth.
That's not the wisdom that comes down from above — it's earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
Because where there's zeal and rivalry, there's disorder and every worthless practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, undivided, without pretence.
And the fruit of rightness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

james_4.t: Where do the wars among you come from? Where do the fights come from? Isn't it from right here — from your pleasures, on campaign in your members?
You crave and you don't have. You murder and you envy, and you can't get what you want. You fight and you wage war. You don't have because you don't ask.
You ask and you don't receive, because you ask wrongly — so you can spend it on your pleasures.
Adulterers and adulteresses! Don't you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? So anyone who decides to be a friend of the world is made an enemy of God.
Or do you think Scripture speaks for nothing? 'He yearns jealously over the spirit he has made to live in us' —
But he gives greater grace. That's why it says: 'God sets himself against the arrogant, but to the lowly he gives grace.'
So submit to God. Stand up to the devil, and he'll run from you.
Come near to God and he'll come near to you. Clean your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you two-souled people.
Be wretched, mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into gloom.
Be brought low before the Lord, and he'll lift you up.

Don't speak against one another, brothers and sisters. Whoever speaks against a brother or judges his brother speaks against law and judges law — and if you judge law, you're not a doer of law but a judge.
There's one lawgiver and judge, the one able to save and to destroy. So who are you to judge your neighbour?
Now then, you who say, 'Today or tomorrow we'll go to this or that city, spend a year there, do business and turn a profit' —
and you don't even know what tomorrow holds. What is your life? You're a mist, showing up for a little while and then gone.
Instead you should say, 'If the Lord wills, we'll both live and do this or that.'
But as it is, you boast in your pretensions. All boasting like that is evil.
So then, anyone who knows the good thing to do and doesn't do it — for him it's sin.

james_5.t: Now then, you who are rich: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted and your clothes have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and the corrosion will be evidence against you — it will eat your flesh like fire. You stored up treasure in the last days.
Look — the wages of the workers who mowed your fields, the wages you kept back, are crying out; and the shouts of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
You lived in luxury on the earth and gave yourselves to pleasure. You fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.
You condemned, you murdered the righteous person. He does not oppose you.
So be patient, brothers and sisters, until the Lord's arrival. Look at the farmer — he waits for the precious fruit of the earth, patient over it until it gets the early and the late rain.
You be patient too. Steady your hearts, because the Lord's arrival has drawn near.
Don't groan against one another, brothers and sisters, so you aren't judged. Look — the judge is standing at the doors.
For an example of suffering and patience, brothers and sisters, take the prophets who spoke in the Lord's name.
Look — we call those who endured blessed. You've heard of Job's endurance, and you saw what the Lord did in the end, because the Lord is deeply compassionate and merciful.
Above all, my brothers and sisters, don't swear — not by heaven, not by earth, not by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so you don't fall under judgement.
Is anyone among you suffering hardship? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing.
Is anyone among you weak? He should call for the elders of the community, and they should pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord's name.
And the prayer of trust will save the one who's failing, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he's committed sins, it will be forgiven him.
So confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you can be healed. The prayer of a righteous person has great power in its working.
Elijah was a human being with the same nature as ours, and he prayed a prayer that it wouldn't rain — and it didn't rain on the land for three years and six months.
And he prayed again, and the sky gave rain and the earth produced its fruit.
My brothers and sisters, if anyone among you is led astray from the truth and someone turns him back,
let him know that whoever turns a sinner back from the wandering of his way will save that person's life from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

john_1.t: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
Everything came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being that has come into being.
In him was life, and that life was the light of humanity.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
There came a man sent from God. His name was John.
He came as a witness, to testify about the light, so that everyone might believe through him.
He was not the light; he came to testify about the light.
The true light, which gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, and the world did not know him.
He came to what was his own, and his own people didn't receive him.
But to all who did receive him, the ones who trusted in his name, he gave the right to become children of God —
children born not of blood, not of the flesh's will, not of a husband's will, but of God.
And the Word became flesh and made his home among us. We saw his glory — glory as of the Father's only Son — full of grace and truth.
John testified about him. He cried out, "This is the one I was talking about when I said, 'The one coming after me has surpassed me, because he was before me.'"
From his fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
The law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God. The only Son, himself God, who is at the Father's side — he has made him known.
This is John's testimony, when the Jews in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, "Who are you?"
He confessed and did not deny it; he confessed, "I am not the Christ."
So they asked him, "Then what? Are you Elijah?" "I'm not," he said. "Are you the Prophet?" "No," he answered.
So they said to him, "Who are you? Give us an answer for the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
He said, "I am a voice crying out in the wilderness: 'Make the Lord's road straight' — as the prophet Isaiah said."
Now the ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
They asked him, "Why are you baptising, then, if you're not the Christ, or Elijah, or the Prophet?"
John answered, "I baptise with water. There is someone standing among you that you don't know,
the one coming after me. I'm not worthy to untie his sandal strap."
This took place in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptising.
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and said, "Look — the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!"
"This is the one I meant when I said, 'A man is coming after me who has surpassed me, because he was before me.'"
"I didn't know him myself, but I came baptising with water so that he might be revealed to Israel."
And John testified, "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him.
I didn't know him, but the one who sent me to baptise with water told me, 'The one you see the Spirit come down on and remain on — he's the one who baptises with the Holy Spirit.'
And I have seen it and testified that this is the Chosen One of God."
The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples.
Looking at Jesus as he walked by, he said, "Look — the Lamb of God!"
The two disciples heard him say this and followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following, and said, "What are you looking for?" They said, "Rabbi" (which means Teacher), "where are you staying?"
"Come and see," he said. So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about four in the afternoon.
Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who heard John and followed Jesus.
The first thing he did was find his own brother Simon and tell him, "We've found the Messiah" (which means Christ).
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, "You are Simon son of John. You will be called Cephas" (which is translated Peter).
The next day Jesus decided to leave for Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, "Follow me."
Philip was from Bethsaida, Andrew and Peter's town.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We've found the one Moses wrote about in the law — and the prophets too — Jesus son of Joseph, from Nazareth."
"Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" Nathanael said. "Come and see," said Philip.
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him, "Here is a true Israelite, in whom there is no deceit."
"How do you know me?" Nathanael said. Jesus answered, "Before Philip called you, while you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
Nathanael answered, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!"
Jesus answered, "You believe because I told you I saw you under the fig tree? You'll see greater things than these."
And he said to him, "I tell you the truth: you'll see heaven opened, and God's angels going up and coming down on the Son of Man."

john_2.t: On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and Jesus' mother was there.
Jesus and his disciples had been invited to the wedding too.
When the wine ran out, Jesus' mother said to him, "They don't have any wine."
Jesus said to her, "What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour hasn't come yet."
His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
Six stone water jars were standing there, used for the purification rites of the Jews, each holding twenty or thirty gallons.
"Fill the jars with water," Jesus said to them. So they filled them to the brim.
Then he said, "Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast." So they took it.
When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine — he didn't know where it came from, though the servants who'd drawn the water knew — he called the bridegroom
and said to him, "Everyone serves the good wine first, and the cheaper wine after people have drunk freely. You've kept the good wine until now."
This was the first of his signs, and Jesus did it at Cana in Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money-changers sitting at their tables.
So he made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple courts, sheep and cattle and all. He scattered the money-changers' coins and overturned their tables.
To the ones selling doves he said, "Get these out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a market."
His disciples remembered that it is written, "Zeal for your house will consume me."
So the Jews said to him, "What sign can you show us to justify doing this?"
Jesus answered, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
"It's taken forty-six years to build this temple," the Jews said, "and you're going to raise it in three days?"
But he was speaking about the temple of his body.
After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the scripture and the word Jesus had spoken.
While he was in Jerusalem at the Passover festival, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was doing.
But Jesus wouldn't entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
He didn't need anyone to tell him about people; he knew himself what was in a person.

john_3.t: There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews.
He came to Jesus at night and said, "Rabbi, we know you're a teacher who's come from God, because no one can do the signs you do unless God is with him."
Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: no one can see the kingdom of God unless they're born from above."
Nicodemus said, "How can someone be born when they're old? They can't enter their mother's womb a second time and be born, can they?"
Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they're born of water and Spirit."
Flesh gives birth to flesh, and the Spirit gives birth to spirit.
Don't be astonished that I said to you, 'You must be born from above.'
The wind blows where it wants. You hear its sound, but you don't know where it's coming from or where it's going. That's how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.
Nicodemus said, "How can this happen?"
Jesus answered, "You're Israel's teacher, and you don't understand this?"
"I tell you the truth: we speak about what we know and testify to what we've seen, and you people don't accept our testimony.
If I've told you earthly things and you don't believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven — the Son of Man[, who is in heaven].
And just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life.
God didn't send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him isn't condemned; whoever doesn't believe stands condemned already, because they haven't believed in the name of God's only Son.
And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, because what they did was evil.
Everyone who does wrong hates the light and won't come to the light, so their deeds won't be exposed.
But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that it's clear their deeds have been done in God."
After this, Jesus and his disciples went into the Judean countryside, where he spent some time with them and baptised.
John was baptising too, at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there, and people kept coming to be baptised.
(John hadn't been put in prison yet.)
A dispute arose between some of John's disciples and a Jewish man about purification.
They came to John and said, "Rabbi, the one who was with you across the Jordan, the one you testified about — look, he's baptising, and everyone's going to him."
John answered, "No one can receive anything unless it's been given them from heaven.
You can testify for me yourselves that I said, 'I am not the Christ, but I have been sent ahead of him.'
The bride belongs to the bridegroom. The bridegroom's friend, who stands and listens for him, is overjoyed at the bridegroom's voice. That joy is mine, and now it's complete.
He must become greater; I must become less.
The one who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
He testifies to what he has seen and heard, and no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever does accept it has certified that God is truthful.
For the one God sent speaks God's words, since God gives the Spirit without measure.
The Father loves the Son and has placed everything in his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever refuses to obey the Son won't see life, and God's wrath remains on them.

john_4.t: When Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard he was making and baptising more disciples than John —
(though in fact it wasn't Jesus who baptised, but his disciples) —
he left Judea and went back to Galilee.
He had to go through Samaria.
So he came to a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given his son Joseph.
Jacob's spring was there. Jesus, worn out from the journey, sat down just as he was beside the spring. It was about noon.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and Jesus said to her, "Give me a drink."
(His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)
The Samaritan woman said to him, "How is it that you, a Jew, are asking me for a drink — and me a Samaritan woman?" (Jews have nothing to do with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered her, "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that's saying to you, 'Give me a drink,' you'd have asked him, and he'd have given you living water."
The woman said, "Sir, you don't have a bucket and the well is deep. Where do you get this living water?
You're not greater than our father Jacob, are you? He gave us the well and drank from it himself, with his sons and his livestock."
Jesus answered, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again,
but whoever drinks the water I'll give them will never be thirsty again. The water I give will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life."
The woman said, "Sir, give me this water, so I won't get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw."
He said to her, "Go, call your husband and come back here."
"I have no husband," the woman answered. Jesus said to her, "You're right in saying you have no husband.
You've had five husbands, and the man you have now isn't your husband. What you've said is true."
"Sir," the woman said, "I see you're a prophet.
Our ancestors worshipped on this mountain, but you people say the place where people must worship is in Jerusalem."
Jesus said, "Believe me, woman: a time is coming when you'll worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you don't know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
But a time is coming — it's here now — when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. These are the worshippers the Father is looking for.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."
The woman said, "I know that Messiah is coming" (the one called Christ). "When he comes, he'll tell us everything."
Jesus said to her, "I am he — the one speaking to you."
Just then his disciples came back. They were astonished that he was speaking with a woman, but no one said, "What do you want?" or "Why are you speaking with her?"
So the woman left her water jar, went off into the town and said to the people,
"Come and see a man who told me everything I've ever done. Could this be the Christ?"
They left the town and came toward him.
Meanwhile the disciples were urging him, "Rabbi, eat something."
But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you know nothing about."
So the disciples said to one another, "Has someone brought him food?"
Jesus said to them, "My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to finish his work.
Don't you say, 'Four more months and then the harvest'? Look, I'm telling you: lift up your eyes and see the fields — they're already white for harvesting.
The reaper is already receiving wages and gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
For here the saying holds true: one sows and another reaps.
I sent you to reap what you didn't work for. Others have done the hard work, and you've entered into their labour."
Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the woman's testimony: "He told me everything I've ever done."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.
And many more believed because of his own word.
They said to the woman, "We no longer believe because of what you said; we've heard for ourselves, and we know that this really is the Saviour of the world."
After the two days he left for Galilee.
(Jesus himself had testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country.)
When he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, because they'd seen everything he did in Jerusalem at the festival — they'd been to the festival themselves.
So he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And there was a royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.
Jesus said to him, "Unless you people see signs and wonders, you'll never believe."
The official said, "Sir, come down before my little boy dies."
Jesus said to him, "Go. Your son lives." The man believed the word Jesus spoke to him, and he went.
While he was still on his way down, his slaves met him with the news that his boy was alive.
So he asked them what time it was when the boy began to get better, and they told him, "Yesterday at one in the afternoon the fever left him."
Then the father realised that this was the very hour Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives." And he believed, and his whole household with him.
This was the second sign Jesus did, after coming from Judea into Galilee.

john_5.t: Some time later there was a festival of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there is a pool called in Hebrew Bethzatha, with five covered colonnades.
In these lay a great many people who were ill — blind, lame, paralysed — waiting for the stirring of the water.
[For an angel would go down into the pool at certain times and stir the water, and the first one in after the water was stirred was made well of whatever disease held them.]
One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and knew he'd been like that a long time, so he said to him, "Do you want to get well?"
The sick man answered, "Sir, I don't have anyone to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I'm on my way, someone else goes down ahead of me."
Jesus said to him, "Get up, pick up your mat and walk."
At once the man was made well; he picked up his mat and walked. Now that day was a sabbath.
So the Jews said to the man who'd been healed, "It's the sabbath. You're not allowed to carry your mat."
He answered, "The man who made me well told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
They asked him, "Who is the man who told you to pick it up and walk?"
But the man who'd been healed didn't know who it was, because Jesus had slipped away into the crowd that was there.
Later Jesus found him in the temple and said, "Look, you're well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you."
The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
So the Jews began persecuting Jesus, because he was doing these things on the sabbath.
But Jesus answered them, "My Father is still working, and I'm working too."
That made the Jews try all the harder to kill him: not only was he breaking the sabbath, he was calling God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
So Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: the Son can't do anything on his own, only what he sees the Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does the same.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does; and he'll show him greater works than these, so that you'll be amazed.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wishes.
The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
so that everyone may honour the Son just as they honour the Father. Whoever doesn't honour the Son doesn't honour the Father who sent him.
I tell you the truth: whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life. They don't come under judgment; they've crossed over from death into life.
I tell you the truth: a time is coming — it's here now — when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
For as the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son to have life in himself,
and he's given him authority to pass judgment, because he is a son of man.
Don't be amazed at this, because a time is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice
and will come out — those who've done good to a resurrection of life, and those who've done evil to a resurrection of judgment.
I can't do anything on my own. I judge as I hear, and my judgment is just, because I don't seek my own will but the will of the one who sent me.
If I testify about myself, my testimony isn't valid.
There is another who testifies about me, and I know his testimony about me is valid.
You sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
Not that I accept human testimony — I say these things so that you may be saved.
He was a lamp, burning and shining, and you were willing to rejoice in his light for a while.
But I have testimony greater than John's: the works the Father has given me to complete — the very works I'm doing — testify that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me has testified about me himself. You've never heard his voice or seen his form,
and you don't have his word remaining in you, because you don't believe the one he sent.
You search the scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life — and they're the very ones that testify about me,
and yet you refuse to come to me so that you may have life.
I don't accept glory from people,
but I know you: you don't have the love of God in you.
I have come in my Father's name and you don't receive me; if someone else comes in his own name, you'll receive him.
How can you believe, when you accept glory from one another and don't seek the glory that comes from the only God?
Don't think I'll accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses — the one you've put your hope in.
If you believed Moses you would believe me, because he wrote about me.
But if you don't believe his writings, how will you believe my words?"

john_6.t: After this Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee (that is, of Tiberias).
A large crowd followed him, because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick.
Jesus went up the mountainside and sat down there with his disciples.
The Passover, the festival of the Jews, was near.
Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward him, and said to Philip, "Where are we going to buy bread for these people to eat?"
He said this to test him, for he already knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered, "Two hundred denarii wouldn't buy enough bread for each of them to get a little."
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said to him,
"There's a boy here with five barley loaves and two small fish — but what's that among so many?"
Jesus said, "Have the people sit down." There was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks and distributed them to those seated, and the same with the fish, as much as they wanted.
When they'd had enough he said to his disciples, "Gather up the leftover pieces, so nothing is lost."
So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
When the people saw the sign he had done, they said, "This really is the Prophet who is to come into the world."
Jesus, knowing they intended to come and seize him to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea,
got into a boat and set off across the sea for Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus hadn't come to them yet.
A strong wind was blowing and the sea grew rough.
When they'd rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.
But he said to them, "It is I. Don't be afraid."
Then they were willing to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the land they were heading for.
The next day the crowd standing on the other side of the sea realised that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus hadn't got into it with his disciples — they'd gone off alone.
Then some boats from Tiberias came near the place where they'd eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks.
So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum looking for him.
When they found him on the other side of the sea they said, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"
Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: you're looking for me not because you saw signs, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
Don't work for food that perishes, but for food that lasts into eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for on him God the Father has set his seal."
So they said to him, "What must we do to be doing the works of God?"
Jesus answered, "This is the work of God: that you believe in the one he sent."
So they said to him, "What sign will you do, then, so we can see it and believe you? What are you going to perform?
Our ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: it wasn't Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; it's my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world."
Then they said, "Sir, give us this bread always."
Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
But as I told you, you've seen me and still you don't believe.
Everyone the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I'll never drive away.
For I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of the one who sent me.
And this is the will of the one who sent me: that I should lose none of all he's given me, but raise them up on the last day.
For this is my Father's will: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I'll raise them up on the last day."
At this the Jews began grumbling about him, because he'd said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
They said, "Isn't this Jesus, Joseph's son? We know his father and mother. How can he say now, 'I have come down from heaven'?"
Jesus answered, "Stop grumbling among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them, and I'll raise them up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: 'And they will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from him comes to me.
