Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.
I tell you the truth: whoever believes has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live for ever. And the bread I'll give for the life of the world is my flesh."
Then the Jews argued sharply among themselves, saying, "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?"
So Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I'll raise them up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.
Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them.
As the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so whoever feeds on me will live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven — not like the bread your ancestors ate and died. Whoever feeds on this bread will live for ever."
He said these things while teaching in a synagogue in Capernaum.
On hearing this, many of his disciples said, "This teaching is hard. Who can listen to it?"
Aware that his disciples were grumbling about this, Jesus said to them, "Does this offend you?
Then what if you see the Son of Man going up to where he was before?
The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I've spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
Yet there are some of you who don't believe." For Jesus had known from the beginning who didn't believe and who would betray him.
He went on, "This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it's granted them by the Father."
From that time many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him.
So Jesus said to the Twelve, "You don't want to go away too, do you?"
Simon Peter answered him, "Lord, who would we go to? You have the words of eternal life,
and we've come to believe and to know that you are the Holy One of God."
Jesus answered them, "Didn't I choose you, the Twelve? And one of you is a devil."
He meant Judas son of Simon Iscariot, who was going to betray him, one of the Twelve though he was.

john_7.t: After this Jesus moved about in Galilee. He wouldn't go about in Judea, because the Jews were looking to kill him.
The festival of the Jews, Shelters, was near.
So his brothers said to him, "Leave here and go to Judea, so your disciples can see the works you're doing.
No one who wants to be publicly known acts in secret. If you're doing these things, show yourself to the world."
(For not even his brothers believed in him.)
So Jesus said to them, "My time hasn't come yet, but your time is always here.
The world can't hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
You go up to the festival. I'm not going up to this festival, because my time hasn't been fulfilled yet.
Having said this, he stayed in Galilee.
But after his brothers had gone up to the festival, he went up too — not openly, but in secret.
So the Jews were looking for him at the festival, asking, "Where is that man?"
There was a lot of muttering about him among the crowds. Some said, "He's a good man." Others said, "No — he leads the crowd astray."
Still, no one would speak openly about him, for fear of the Jews.
About halfway through the festival, Jesus went up into the temple courts and began to teach.
The Jews were astonished. "How does this man know letters," they said, "when he's never been taught?"
So Jesus answered them, "My teaching isn't mine; it's from the one who sent me.
Anyone who's willing to do his will shall know about the teaching — whether it's from God or whether I'm speaking on my own.
Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there's no injustice in him.
Didn't Moses give you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill me?"
The crowd answered, "You have a demon. Who's trying to kill you?"
Jesus answered them, "I did one work, and you're all astonished.
Moses gave you circumcision — not that it comes from Moses, but from the fathers — and you circumcise a man on the sabbath.
Now if a man can be circumcised on the sabbath so that the law of Moses isn't broken, why are you angry with me for making a man's whole body well on the sabbath?
Don't judge by appearances; judge with right judgment."
Then some of the people of Jerusalem said, "Isn't this the man they're trying to kill?
And here he is, speaking openly, and they don't say a thing to him. Can it be that the authorities really have concluded he's the Christ?
But we know where this man is from; when the Christ comes, no one will know where he's from."
Then Jesus, teaching in the temple courts, cried out, "You know me, and you know where I'm from. And I haven't come on my own; the one who sent me is true, and you don't know him.
I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me."
So they tried to seize him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour hadn't come yet.
But many in the crowd believed in him and said, "When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than this man has done?"
The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
So Jesus said, "I'm with you a little while longer, and then I'm going to the one who sent me.
You'll look for me and you won't find me; and where I am, you can't come."
So the Jews said to one another, "Where does this man intend to go that we won't find him? He doesn't intend to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks, does he?
What does he mean by saying, 'You'll look for me and you won't find me,' and, 'Where I am, you can't come'?"
On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood up and cried out, "If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink.
Whoever believes in me — as the scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from within them."
He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were going to receive; for the Spirit hadn't been given yet, because Jesus hadn't yet been glorified.
On hearing these words, some of the crowd said, "This really is the Prophet."
Others said, "This is the Christ." But others said, "Surely the Christ doesn't come from Galilee?
Doesn't the scripture say that the Christ comes from David's offspring, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?"
So the crowd was divided because of him.
Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.
Then the officers went back to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them, "Why didn't you bring him in?"
The officers answered, "No one ever spoke like this man."
The Pharisees answered them, "You haven't been led astray too, have you?
Has any of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?
But this crowd, that doesn't know the law — they're cursed."
Nicodemus — the one who'd come to him earlier, and who was one of them — said to them,
"Our law doesn't judge a person without first hearing from them and finding out what they're doing, does it?"
They answered him, "You're not from Galilee too, are you? Look into it and you'll see that no prophet arises from Galilee."
[[And each of them went to his own house,

john_8.t: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
At dawn he came again into the temple courts. All the people came, and he sat down and taught them.
The scribes and the Pharisees brought in a woman caught in adultery. They stood her in the middle
and said to him, to test him, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of adultery.
In the law Moses commanded us to stone women like this. So what do you say?"
They said this to test him, so they'd have grounds to accuse him. But Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, "Whichever of you is without sin — let him be the first to throw a stone at her."
And he bent down again and wrote on the ground.
When they heard this they began to go away one by one, beginning with the elders, until only Jesus was left, with the woman there in the middle.
Jesus straightened up and, seeing no one but the woman, said to her, "Where are they? Has no one condemned you?"
"No one, sir," she said. And Jesus said, "Neither do I condemn you. Go, and don't sin again."]]
Then Jesus spoke to them again: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness but will have the light of life."
So the Pharisees said to him, "You're testifying about yourself. Your testimony isn't valid."
Jesus answered, "Even if I do testify about myself, my testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I'm going. But you don't know where I come from or where I'm going.
You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
And even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I'm not alone: I and the Father who sent me judge together.
In your own law it is written that the testimony of two people is valid.
I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me."
So they said to him, "Where's your father?" Jesus answered, "You don't know me or my Father. If you knew me, you'd know my Father too."
He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple courts, and no one seized him, because his hour hadn't come yet.
Again he said to them, "I'm going away, and you'll look for me, and you'll die in your sin. Where I'm going, you can't come."
So the Jews said, "Is he going to kill himself? Is that why he says, 'Where I'm going, you can't come'?"
He said to them, "You're from below; I am from above. You're of this world; I am not of this world.
That's why I told you that you'd die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am he, you'll die in your sins."
So they said to him, "Who are you?" Jesus said to them, "What I have been telling you from the beginning."
"I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the one who sent me is true, and what I've heard from him is what I tell the world."
They didn't understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.
So Jesus said, "When you've lifted up the Son of Man, then you'll know that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own but speak just as the Father taught me.
And the one who sent me is with me. He hasn't left me alone, because I always do what pleases him."
As he was saying these things, many believed in him.
So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him, "If you remain in my word, you're truly my disciples,
and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They answered him, "We're Abraham's offspring and have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, 'You will become free'?"
Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
A slave doesn't remain in the household for ever; a son remains for ever.
So if the Son sets you free, you'll be free indeed.
"I know you're Abraham's offspring. Yet you're trying to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.
I speak of what I've seen in the Father's presence; and you do what you've heard from your father."
They answered him, "Abraham is our father." Jesus said to them, "If you were Abraham's children you'd be doing the works of Abraham.
But now you're trying to kill me — a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham didn't do this.
You're doing the works of your own father." They said to him, "We weren't born of sexual immorality. We have one Father — God himself."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father you'd love me, for I came from God and am here. I haven't come on my own; he sent me.
Why don't you understand what I'm saying? Because you can't bear to hear my word.

You're from your father the devil, and you want to do what your father desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and has not stood in the truth, because there's no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks from what is his own, because he's a liar and the father of lies.
But because I tell the truth, you don't believe me.
Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why don't you believe me?
Whoever is from God hears the words of God. You don't hear, because you aren't from God."
The Jews answered him, "Aren't we right in saying that you're a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered, "I don't have a demon. I honour my Father, and you dishonour me.
I don't seek my own glory. There is one who seeks it, and he is the judge.
I tell you the truth: whoever keeps my word will never see death."
The Jews said to him, "Now we know you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, and you say that whoever keeps your word will never taste death.
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?"
Jesus answered, "If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It's my Father who glorifies me — the one you say is your God,
though you haven't known him. But I know him. If I said I didn't know him I'd be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.
Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day; and he saw it and was glad."
So the Jews said to him, "You aren't fifty years old yet, and you've seen Abraham?"
Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: before Abraham was, I am."
At that they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple courts.

john_9.t: As he was going along he saw a man who'd been blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?"
Jesus answered, "Neither this man sinned nor his parents — but so that God's works might be made visible in him."
"We must work the works of the one who sent me while it's day. Night is coming, when no one can work."
"As long as I'm in the world, I am the world's light."
When he had said this he spat on the ground and made mud from the saliva and smeared the mud on the man's eyes.
and said to him, "Go, wash in the pool of Siloam" (which is translated "Sent"). So he went off and washed, and came back seeing.
So the neighbours, and those who'd seen him before as a beggar, kept saying, "Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?"
Some said, "It's him." Others said, "No, but he looks like him." He himself kept saying, "I am the man."
So they said to him, "Then how were your eyes opened?"
He answered, "The man called Jesus made mud and smeared my eyes and told me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' So I went and washed, and I could see."
They said to him, "Where is he?" "I don't know," he said.
They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
It was a Sabbath on the day Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
So the Pharisees also asked him again how he'd come to see. He told them, "He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
Some of the Pharisees said, "This man isn't from God, because he doesn't keep the Sabbath." But others said, "How can a sinful man do signs like these?" And there was a split among them.
So they said to the blind man again, "What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?" "He is a prophet," he said.
The Jews didn't believe about him that he'd been blind and had come to see, until they called the parents of the man who'd received his sight.
and they asked them, "Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? How is it, then, that he sees now?"
His parents answered, "We know that this is our son and that he was born blind."
"But how he sees now we don't know, and who opened his eyes we don't know. Ask him. He's of age; he'll speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews; the Jews had already agreed that anyone who confessed him as Christ should be put out of the synagogue.
That's why his parents said, "He's of age; ask him."
So a second time they called the man who had been blind and said to him, "Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner."
He answered, "Whether he's a sinner I don't know. One thing I know: I was blind, and now I see."
So they said to him again, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He answered them, "I already told you and you didn't listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don't want to become his disciples too, do you?"
They abused him and said, "You're that man's disciple; we're Moses' disciples."
"We know that God has spoken to Moses; but as for this man, we don't know where he's from."
The man answered them, "That's the astonishing thing: that you don't know where he's from — and he opened my eyes."
"We know that God doesn't listen to sinners, but if anyone is God-fearing and does his will, God listens to them."
"Never in all time has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind."
"If this man weren't from God, he couldn't do anything."
They answered him, "You were born entirely in sins, and you're teaching us?" And they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they'd thrown him out, and when he found him he said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
He answered, "And who is he, sir, so that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him, "You have seen him — and the one speaking with you is he."
[He said, "I believe, Lord," and he knelt before him.]
And Jesus said, "I came into this world for judgement, so that those who don't see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him, "Surely we aren't blind too?"
Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you'd have no sin. But now you say, 'We see' — so your sin remains."

john_10.t: "I tell you the truth: whoever doesn't come into the sheepfold through the gate but climbs in some other way is a thief and a bandit.
But the one who comes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens for him, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he's brought out all his own, he goes ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
They'll never follow a stranger; they'll run away from him, because they don't know the voice of strangers.
Jesus told them this figure of speech, but they didn't understand what it was he was saying to them.
So Jesus said again, "I tell you the truth: I am the gate for the sheep.
All who came before me are thieves and bandits, but the sheep didn't listen to them.
I am the gate. Whoever comes in through me will be kept safe, and will go in and out and find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal and slaughter and destroy. I came so that they may have life, and have it in abundance.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
The hired man, who isn't a shepherd and doesn't own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and abandons the sheep and runs; and the wolf snatches them and scatters the sheep.
He runs because he's a hired man and the sheep don't matter to him.
I am the good shepherd; I know my own, and my own know me,
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father — and I lay down my life for the sheep.
I have other sheep that aren't from this fold; I must bring them too, and they'll hear my voice, and they'll become one flock, one shepherd.
This is why the Father loves me: because I lay down my life, so that I may take it up again.
No one takes it from me; I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down and I have authority to take it up again. This is the command I received from my Father."
There was a split again among the Jews because of these words.
Many of them said, "He has a demon and he's out of his mind. Why do you listen to him?"
Others said, "These aren't the words of a man with a demon. A demon can't open the eyes of the blind, can it?"
Then came the Festival of Dedication in Jerusalem. It was winter,
and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's Portico.
So the Jews surrounded him and said to him, "How long are you going to keep us in suspense? If you're the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered them, "I told you and you don't believe. The works I do in my Father's name — these testify about me.
But you don't believe, because you aren't among my sheep, as I told you.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me,
and I give them eternal life, and they'll never be destroyed, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than anyone, and no one can snatch them out of my Father's hand.
I and the Father are one."
The Jews picked up stones again to stone him.
Jesus answered them, "I've shown you many good works from the Father. For which of them are you stoning me?"
The Jews answered him, "We're not stoning you for a good work but for blasphemy — because you, a man, make yourself God."
Jesus answered them, "Isn't it written in your law, 'I said: you are gods'?
If he called them gods, those to whom the word of God came — and the scripture can't be broken —
do you say of the one the Father consecrated and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming,' because I said, 'I am God's Son'?
If I'm not doing my Father's works, don't believe me.
But if I am, then even if you don't believe me, believe the works, so that you may come to know and go on knowing that the Father is in me and I am in the Father."
So they tried again to seize him, but he went out of their hand.
He went away again across the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptising, and he stayed there.
Many came to him and said, "John did no sign, but everything John said about this man was true."
And many believed in him there.

john_11.t: There was a man who was ill: Lazarus of Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
This Mary was the one who anointed the Lord with perfume and wiped his feet with her hair; it was her brother Lazarus who was ill.
So the sisters sent word to him: "Lord, look — the one you love is ill."
When Jesus heard it he said, "This illness won't end in death. It's for God's glory, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
So when he heard that Lazarus was ill, he stayed where he was for two more days.
Then, after that, he said to the disciples, "Let's go back to Judea."
The disciples said to him, "Rabbi, the Jews there were just trying to stone you, and you're going back?"
Jesus answered, "Aren't there twelve hours of daylight? Anyone who walks during the day doesn't trip, because he sees by the light of this world.
But anyone who walks at night trips, because the light isn't in him."
He said this, and then told them, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I'm going to wake him up."
The disciples said, "Lord, if he's fallen asleep, he'll recover."
Jesus had been speaking about his death, but they thought he meant natural sleep.
So then Jesus told them plainly, "Lazarus died."
"And for your sake I'm glad I wasn't there — so that you may believe. But let's go to him."
Then Thomas, the one called the Twin, said to his fellow disciples, "Let's go too, so that we may die with him."
When Jesus arrived he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days.
Bethany was near Jerusalem, less than two miles away.
Many of the Jews had come out to Martha and Mary to console them about their brother.
So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming she went to meet him, while Mary stayed sitting in the house.
Martha said to Jesus, "Lord, if you'd been here my brother wouldn't have died."
"Even now I know that whatever you ask God for, God will give you."
Jesus said to her, "Your brother will rise."
Martha said, "I know he'll rise in the resurrection on the last day."
Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even if they die,
and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die at all. Do you believe this?"
She said to him, "Yes, Lord. I've come to believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world."
When she'd said this she went and called her sister Mary, telling her quietly, "The Teacher is here and is asking for you."
As soon as she heard it she got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus hadn't come into the village yet; he was still at the place where Martha had met him.
The Jews who were with her in the house consoling her saw Mary get up quickly and go out, and they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to weep there.
When Mary reached the place where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, "Lord, if you'd been here my brother wouldn't have died."
When Jesus saw her wailing, and the Jews who'd come with her wailing too, anger surged through his spirit and he shook himself,
and he said, "Where have you laid him?" "Lord, come and see," they said.
Jesus wept.
So the Jews said, "Look how he loved him."
But some of them said, "This man opened the blind man's eyes. Couldn't he have kept this man from dying?"
Jesus, angry again within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, with a stone lying against it.
Jesus said, "Take away the stone." Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, "Lord, by now there's a stench. It's the fourth day."
Jesus said to her, "Didn't I tell you that if you believed you'd see the glory of God?"
So they took away the stone. Jesus looked upward and said, "Father, I thank you that you heard me.
I knew that you always hear me, but I said it for the sake of the crowd standing around, so that they may believe that you sent me."
When he'd said this he shouted at the top of his voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
The dead man came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth and his face wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them, "Untie him and let him go."
So many of the Jews, those who'd come to Mary and had seen what he did, believed in him.
But some of them went off to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
So the chief priests and the Pharisees called the council together and said, "What are we doing? This man is performing many signs.
If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation."
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, "You know nothing at all.
You aren't taking into account that it's better for you that one man should die for the people than that the whole nation be destroyed."
He didn't say this on his own. As high priest that year he was prophesying that Jesus was going to die for the nation —
and not for the nation only, but so that he might also gather into one the scattered children of God.
So from that day on they planned to kill him.
So Jesus no longer moved about openly among the Jews, but went from there to the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and he stayed there with his disciples.
The Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.
They were looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they kept saying to one another, "What do you think? That he won't come to the festival at all?"
The chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where he was should report it, so they could arrest him.

john_12.t: Six days before the Passover Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was — the man he had raised from the dead.
They gave a dinner for him there. Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at the table with him.
Then Mary took nearly a pint of very costly perfume, pure nard, anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
But Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, one of his disciples — the one who was going to hand him over — said,
"Why wasn't this perfume sold for a year's wages and the money given to the poor?"
He said this — so the narrator tells us — not because he cared about the poor but because he was a thief: he kept the money box and used to take what was put in it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She was to keep it for the day of my burial."
"You always have the poor with you, but you don't always have me."
The large crowd of the Jews found out that he was there, and they came not only because of Jesus but to see Lazarus, whom he'd raised from the dead.
So the chief priests planned to kill Lazarus too,
because on his account many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.
The next day the large crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord — the King of Israel!"
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as it is written:
"Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look, your king is coming, seated on a donkey's colt."
His disciples didn't understand this at first. But when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that this had been written about him and that they had done this to him.
The crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept testifying to it.
That was also why the crowd went out to meet him: they'd heard that he had done this sign.
So the Pharisees said to one another, "You see, you're getting nowhere. Look — the whole world has gone off after him."
There were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the festival.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, "Sir, we want to see Jesus."
Philip went and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
I tell you the truth: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it stays a single grain. But if it dies it bears much fruit.
Whoever loves their life loses it, and whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, they must follow me; and where I am, my servant will be there too. If anyone serves me, the Father will honour them.
Now my soul is in turmoil. And what am I to say — Father, save me from this hour? No: it was for this that I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your name." Then a voice came from heaven: "I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
The crowd standing there heard it and said it had thundered. Others said, "An angel has spoken to him."
Jesus answered, "This voice came not for my sake but for yours.
Now is the judgement of this world. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
He said this to signal what kind of death he was going to die.
So the crowd answered him, "We've heard from the law that the Christ remains for ever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"
Jesus said to them, "The light is among you a little longer. Walk while you have the light, so the darkness doesn't overtake you. Whoever walks in the darkness doesn't know where they're going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light." Jesus said this, then went away and was hidden from them.
Though he'd done so many signs in front of them, they were not believing in him,
so that the word of Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled, the word he spoke: "Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
This was why they couldn't believe: because Isaiah also said,
"He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn — and I would heal them."
Isaiah said this because he saw his glory and spoke about him.
All the same, even many of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they wouldn't confess it, so as not to be put out of the synagogue.
For they loved human approval more than the glory of God.
Jesus cried out, "Whoever believes in me doesn't believe in me but in the one who sent me;
and whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.
I have come as light into the world, so that no one who believes in me stays in the darkness.
If anyone hears my words and doesn't keep them, I don't judge them; for I didn't come to judge the world but to save the world.
Whoever rejects me and doesn't accept my words has a judge: the word I spoke will judge them on the last day.
For I haven't spoken on my own; the Father who sent me has himself commanded me what to say and how to speak it.
And I know that his command is eternal life. So what I say, I say just as the Father has told me."

john_13.t: Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that his hour had come to move out of this world and go to the Father. He had loved his own who were in the world, and he loved them to the very end.
It was during supper. The devil had already put it into the heart that Judas son of Simon Iscariot should hand him over.
Jesus knew that the Father had given everything into his hands, and that he'd come from God and was going to God.
He got up from the meal, took off his outer clothes, and picked up a towel and tied it round himself.
Then he poured water into the basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and to dry them with the towel he'd tied round himself.
He came to Simon Peter, and Peter said to him, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus answered him, "You don't know now what I'm doing, but you'll know after this."
Peter said to him, "You'll never wash my feet — never." Jesus answered him, "If I don't wash you, you have no share with me."
Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, then not my feet only, but my hands and my head as well."
Jesus said to him, "Someone who's bathed doesn't need washing, except for the feet — he's clean all over. And you are clean, though not all of you."
He knew who was going to hand him over; that's why he said, "Not all of you are clean."
When he'd washed their feet and put his clothes back on and taken his place again, he said to them, "Do you know what I've done for you?
You call me Teacher and Lord, and you're right to, because that's what I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, then you also ought to wash one another's feet.
I've given you a pattern, so that you should do just as I have done for you.
I tell you the truth: a slave is not greater than his master, and one who is sent is not greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things — and you do — you are blessed if you act on them.
I'm not speaking about all of you. I know the ones I chose. But this is so that the scripture may be fulfilled: "The one who feeds on my bread has lifted his heel against me."
I'm telling you now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you'll believe that I am he.
I tell you the truth: whoever receives anyone I send receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
After saying this, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and he testified: "I tell you the truth, one of you will hand me over."
The disciples looked at one another, at a loss about which of them he meant.
One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining close against him.
So Simon Peter motioned to him and told him to ask which one he meant.
He leaned back against Jesus' chest and said to him, "Lord, who is it?"
Jesus answered, "It's the one I give this piece of bread to, when I've dipped it." So he dipped the piece of bread and took it and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
As soon as he took the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, "What you're doing, do quickly."
No one at the table knew why he said this to him.
Some thought that, because Judas kept the money box, Jesus was telling him, "Buy what we need for the festival," or telling him to give something to the poor.
So he took the piece of bread and went straight out. And it was night.
When he'd gone out, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
[If God has been glorified in him,] God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him at once.
My children, I'm with you only a little longer. You'll look for me, and what I said to the Jews I now say to you as well: where I'm going, you can't come.
I'm giving you a new command: love one another. As I have loved you, so you also are to love one another.
This is how everyone will know that you're my disciples: if you have love among one another.
Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, where are you going?" Jesus answered, "Where I'm going you can't follow me now, but you will follow later."
Peter said to him, "Lord, why can't I follow you now? I'll lay down my life for you."
Jesus answered, "You'll lay down your life for me? I tell you the truth: the cock won't crow before you've denied me three times."

john_14.t: "Don't let your heart be troubled. Believe in God; believe in me too."
"In my Father's house there are many places to stay. If it weren't so, would I have told you that I'm going to prepare a place for you?
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I'm coming back and will take you to myself, so that you may be where I am.
And you know where I'm going, and you know the way."
Thomas said to him, "Lord, we don't know where you're going. How can we know the way?"
Jesus said to him, "I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you've come to know me, you will know my Father as well. From now on you do know him, and you've seen him."
Philip said to him, "Lord, show us the Father, and that's enough for us."
Jesus said to him, "Have I been with you all this time, Philip, and you don't know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
Don't you believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words I say to you I don't speak on my own; the Father, who remains in me, is doing his works.
Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or else believe because of the works themselves.
I tell you the truth: whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater ones than these, because I'm going to the Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, you will keep my commands.
And I will ask the Father, and he'll give you another Advocate to be with you for ever —
the Spirit of truth, whom the world can't receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. You know him, because he remains with you and will be in you.
I won't leave you orphaned; I'm coming to you.
In a little while the world will see me no more, but you will see me. Because I live, you also will live.
On that day you'll know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
Whoever has my commands and keeps them is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love them and will show myself to them.
Judas — not Iscariot — said to him, "Lord, what's happened, that you're going to show yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered him, "Anyone who loves me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we'll come to them and make a place to stay with them.
Whoever doesn't love me doesn't keep my words. And the word you hear isn't mine; it belongs to the Father who sent me.
I've told you all this while I'm still staying with you.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and will remind you of everything I said to you.
Peace I leave with you; my own peace I give you. I don't give as the world gives. Don't let your heart be troubled, and don't let it be afraid.
You heard me say to you, 'I'm going away, and I'm coming to you.' If you loved me you'd have been glad that I'm going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.
I've told you now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you'll believe.
I won't talk with you much longer, because the ruler of this world is coming. He has no hold on me,
but the world must know that I love the Father, and that I do exactly as the Father commanded me. Get up; let's go from here."

john_15.t: "I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
Every branch in me that doesn't bear fruit he takes away, and every branch that does bear fruit he cleans, so that it may bear more fruit.
You are already clean because of the word I've spoken to you.
Stay in me, and I in you. Just as the branch can't bear fruit by itself unless it stays in the vine, neither can you unless you stay in me.
I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever stays in me, and I in them, bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
If anyone doesn't stay in me, he's thrown out like a branch and withers; and they gather such branches and throw them into the fire, and they burn.
If you stay in me and my words stay in you, ask whatever you want, and it will happen for you.
This is how my Father was glorified: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
As the Father loved me, I also loved you. Stay in my love.
If you keep my commands, you'll stay in my love, just as I've kept my Father's commands and stay in his love.
I've told you this so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be made complete.
This is my command: that you love one another as I loved you.
No one has greater love than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you slaves, because a slave doesn't know what his master is doing. I've called you friends, because everything I heard from my Father I've made known to you.
You didn't choose me; I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit — fruit that will stay — so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you.
This is my command to you: love one another.
If the world hates you, bear in mind that it has hated me before it hated you.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love you as its own. But you don't belong to the world; I chose you out of the world, and that's why the world hates you.
Remember the word I said to you: a slave is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they'll persecute you too; if they kept my word, they'll keep yours too.
But they'll do all this to you because of my name, since they don't know the one who sent me.
If I hadn't come and spoken to them, they wouldn't have sin. As it is, they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me hates my Father too.
If I hadn't done among them the works that no one else did, they wouldn't have sin. But now they have seen, and they have hated both me and my Father.
But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: "They hated me for nothing."
When the Advocate comes, whom I'll send to you from the Father — the Spirit of truth who goes out from the Father — he will testify about me.
And you also testify, because you've been with me from the beginning.

john_16.t: "I've told you all this so that you won't be tripped up.
They'll put you out of the synagogues. In fact, an hour is coming when anyone who kills you will think they're offering worship to God.
And they'll do these things because they haven't known the Father or me.
But I've told you these things so that when their hour comes you'll remember that I told you about them. I didn't tell you this at the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I'm going to the one who sent me, and not one of you asks me, 'Where are you going?'
Instead, because I've told you these things, grief has filled your heart.
But I'm telling you the truth: it's better for you that I go away. If I don't go away, the Advocate won't come to you; but if I go, I'll send him to you.
And when he comes, he will put the world in the wrong about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment.
About sin, because they don't believe in me.
About righteousness, because I'm going to the Father and you see me no longer.
And about judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have much to say to you, but you can't carry it now.
But when he comes — the Spirit of truth — he'll guide you in the whole truth. He won't speak on his own; he'll speak whatever he hears, and he'll announce to you the things that are coming.
He'll glorify me, because he'll take from what is mine and announce it to you.
Everything the Father has is mine. That's why I said he takes from what is mine and will announce it to you.
A little while, and you no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me — because I'm going to the Father."

So some of his disciples said to one another, "What is this he's telling us — 'a little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me,' and 'because I am going to the Father'?"
They kept saying, "What is this 'a little while' he speaks of? We don't know what he's talking about."

Jesus knew they wanted to ask him about it, and he said to them, "Are you discussing with one another what I meant by 'a little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me'?
I tell you the truth: you'll weep and mourn, and the world will be glad. You'll grieve, but your grief will turn into joy.

When a woman is giving birth she has pain, because her hour has come. But when she has delivered the child, she no longer remembers the distress, because of the joy that a person has been born into the world.
So you too have grief now; but I'll see you again, and your heart will be glad, and no one takes your joy away from you.
On that day you won't ask me anything. I tell you the truth: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
Until now you haven't asked for anything in my name. Ask, and you'll receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I've said all this to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I'll no longer speak to you in figures, but will tell you about the Father plainly.
On that day you'll ask in my name. And I'm not saying that I'll ask the Father on your behalf,
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and have come into the world; again, I'm leaving the world and going to the Father.
His disciples said, "Look, now you're speaking plainly and not using any figure of speech.
Now we know that you know everything and don't need anyone to question you. This is why we believe that you came from God."
Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?
Look — an hour is coming, and has now come, when you'll be scattered, each to his own place, and you'll leave me alone. And I'm not alone, because the Father is with me.
I've told you these things so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble — but take courage, I have conquered the world."

john_17.t: Jesus said these things, and then he lifted his eyes to heaven and said: "Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may glorify you,
since you gave him authority over all flesh, so that he might give eternal life to everyone you have given him.
And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent.
I glorified you on the earth, having completed the work you gave me to do.
and now, Father, glorify me at your own side with the glory I had at your side before the world existed.
I have made your name known to the people you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now they know that everything you have given me is from you,
because the words you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and truly knew that I came from you, and they believed that you sent me.
I am asking on their behalf. I am not asking on behalf of the world, but for those you have given me, because they are yours;
and everything that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine; and I have been glorified in them.
and I am no longer in the world, and they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given me, so that they may be one as we are.

While I was with them I kept them in your name, which you have given me. I guarded them, and not one of them was lost except the one who belonged to destruction — so that the scripture would be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say these things while I am in the world, so that they may have my joy made complete in themselves.
I have given them your word, and the world hated them, because they are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but to keep them from the evil one.
They are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
Set them apart in the truth. Your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, I also sent them into the world.
And for their sake I set myself apart, so that they too may be set apart in truth.
I am not asking on behalf of these only, but also for those who believe in me through their word,
so that they may all be one — as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so that they too may be in us — so that the world may believe that you sent me.
And I have given them the glory you have given me, so that they may be one as we are one —
I in them and you in me, so that they may be brought to completion as one, and so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.
Father, as for those you have given me, I want them to be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me because you loved me before the world was founded.
Righteous Father, the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these have known that you sent me.
And I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.

john_18.t: When Jesus had said all this, he went out with his disciples across the Kidron valley stream. There was a garden there, and he and his disciples went into it.
Judas, the one handing him over, knew the place too, because Jesus had often met there with his disciples.
So Judas took the cohort of soldiers, and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, "Who is it you're looking for?"
They answered him, "Jesus the Nazorean." Jesus said to them, "I am he." Judas, the one handing him over, was standing there with them.
So when he said to them, "I am he," they drew back and fell to the ground.
So he asked them again, "Who is it you're looking for?" They said, "Jesus the Nazorean."
Jesus answered, "I told you that I am he. So if it's me you're looking for, let these men go."
This was so that the word he had spoken would be fulfilled: "Of those you have given me, I lost none."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's slave, cutting off his right ear. The slave's name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, "Put your sword back in its sheath. The cup the Father has given me — am I not to drink it?"
So the cohort, its commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews arrested Jesus and bound him,
and they led him first to Annas, since he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who'd advised the Jews that it was better for one person to die on behalf of the people.
Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went in with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard.
Peter was standing outside at the door. So the other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the woman keeping the door, and brought Peter in.
So the servant girl at the door said to Peter, "You aren't one of this man's disciples too, are you?" "I am not," he said.
The slaves and the officers had made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and were standing there warming themselves. Peter was standing with them too, warming himself.
The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered him, "I've spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I said nothing in secret."
"Why are you questioning me? Question the people who heard what I said to them. Look — they know what I said."
When he said this, one of the officers standing nearby struck Jesus in the face and said, "Is that how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus answered him, "If I spoke wrongly, testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you hit me?"
Then Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was standing there warming himself. So they said to him, "You aren't one of his disciples too, are you?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
One of the high priest's slaves, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Didn't I see you in the garden with him?"
Peter denied it again, and at once a rooster crowed.

Then they took Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor's headquarters. It was early morning. They themselves didn't go into the headquarters, so that they wouldn't be defiled but could eat the Passover meal.
So Pilate came outside to them and said, "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
They answered him, "If this man weren't doing something criminal, we wouldn't have handed him over to you."
So Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law." The Jews said to him, "We aren't permitted to put anyone to death."
This was so that what Jesus had said would be fulfilled, when he indicated the kind of death he was going to die.
So Pilate went back into the headquarters, summoned Jesus, and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus answered him, "Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about me?"
Pilate answered, "I'm not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?"

Jesus answered, "My kingship doesn't originate in this world. If it did originate in this world, my own officers would be fighting to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingship doesn't come from here."

So Pilate said to him, "So you're a king, then?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. This is why I was born, and this is why I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth hears my voice."
Pilate said to him, "What is truth?" And having said this, he went back out to the Jews and said to them, "I find no case against him.
But you have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at the Passover. So do you want me to release the king of the Jews to you?"
So they shouted back, all of them, "Not this man — Barabbas!" Barabbas was a bandit.

john_19.t: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
The soldiers wove a wreath out of thorns and put it on his head, and they threw a purple robe around him,
and they kept coming up to him and saying, "Greetings, king of the Jews!" And they kept striking him in the face.
Pilate came outside again and said to them, "Look, I'm bringing him out to you so that you'll know I find no case against him."
So Jesus came outside, wearing the thorn wreath and the purple robe. And Pilate said to them, "Here is the man."
So when the chief priests and their officers saw him, they shouted, "Crucify! Crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and crucify him. I find no case against him."
The Jews answered him, "We have a law, and by that law he ought to die, because he made himself out to be God's Son."
When Pilate heard that, he became still more afraid,
and he went back into the headquarters and said to Jesus, "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
So Pilate said to him, "You won't speak to me? Don't you know that I have the authority to release you and the authority to crucify you?"
Jesus answered him, "You'd have no authority over me at all if it hadn't been given to you from above. That's why the one who handed me over to you bears the greater guilt."
From then on Pilate kept trying to release him. But the Jews shouted, "If you release this man you're no Friend of Caesar. Anyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and took his seat on the judge's bench at the place called the Stone Pavement — in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about noon. And Pilate said to the Jews, "Here is your king."
They shouted, "Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king but Caesar."
Then Pilate handed him over to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away.
Carrying the cross himself, he went out to what is called the Place of the Skull — in Hebrew, Golgotha —
and there they crucified him, and two others with him, one on either side, with Jesus in the middle.
Pilate also wrote a notice and had it fastened to the cross. It read: Jesus the Nazorean, the King of the Jews.
Many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek.
So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, "Don't write 'The King of the Jews,' but that this man said, 'I am king of the Jews.'"
Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."

When the soldiers had crucified Jesus they took his outer clothes and divided them into four shares, one for each soldier, and they took the tunic as well. The tunic was seamless, woven in one piece from the top down.

So they said to one another, "Let's not tear it. Let's cast lots for it, to see whose it will be." This was so that the scripture would be fulfilled which says: They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots. So that is what the soldiers did.
Standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple he loved standing beside her, he said to his mother, "Woman, here is your son."
Then he said to the disciple, "Here is your mother." And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
After this, knowing that everything had now been completed, and so that the scripture would be brought to its end, Jesus said, "I am thirsty."
A jar of sour wine was standing there. So they put a sponge soaked in the sour wine on a hyssop stalk and held it up to his mouth.
When Jesus had taken the sour wine he said, "It is completed." Then he bowed his head and handed over his spirit.

Since it was the day of Preparation, the Jews didn't want the bodies left on the crosses on the sabbath — for that sabbath was a high day — so they asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies taken away.
So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man and of the other who'd been crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they didn't break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
The one who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he's telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
For these things happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled: "Not one of his bones will be broken."
And another passage of scripture says, "They will look at the one they pierced through."

After this, Joseph of Arimathea — a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one, because he was afraid of the Jews — asked Pilate to let him take away the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and took the body away.
Nicodemus came too — the one who'd first come to him at night — bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds of it.
So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, following the burial custom of the Jews.
There was a garden at the place where he was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
So because it was the Jews' day of Preparation, and because the tomb was near, they laid Jesus there.

john_20.t: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away from it.
So she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, the one Jesus loved, and said to them, "They've taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we don't know where they've put him."
So Peter and the other disciple set out and went toward the tomb.
The two were running together, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
He bent down and saw the linen cloths lying there, but he didn't go in.
Then Simon Peter came, following him, and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there,
and the cloth that had been on his head — not lying with the linen cloths but rolled up in a place by itself.
Then the other disciple, who'd reached the tomb first, went in too. He saw, and he believed.
For they still didn't understand the scripture, that he had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back to where they were staying.
But Mary stood outside near the tomb, weeping. As she wept she bent down to look into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain — one at the head and one at the feet.
They said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" "They've taken away my Lord," she said, "and I don't know where they've put him."
Saying this, she turned round and saw Jesus standing there — and she didn't know it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?" Thinking he was the gardener, she said, "Sir, if you've carried him off, tell me where you've put him, and I'll take him away."
Jesus said to her, "Mary." She turned and said to him in Hebrew, "Rabbouni!" — which means Teacher.
Jesus said to her, "Don't hold on to me, for I haven't gone up to the Father yet. But go to my brothers and tell them, 'I'm going up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.'"
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord" — and that he had said these things to her.
On the evening of that first day of the week, with the doors locked where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."
When he'd said this he showed them his hands and his side. Then the disciples were overjoyed to see the Lord.
Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I'm sending you."
And with that he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit."
"If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven them; if you retain them, they are retained."
Now Thomas, one of the Twelve, called the Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.

So the other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord." But he said, "Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I won't believe."
Eight days later his disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you."
Then he said to Thomas, "Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting and believe."
Thomas answered him, "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him, "Because you've seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed."
Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples that aren't written in this book.
But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.

john_21.t: After this Jesus showed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. This is how he showed himself.
Simon Peter, Thomas called the Twin, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee and two other disciples were together.
Simon Peter said, "I'm going fishing." "We're coming with you," they said. They went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing.
Just as day was breaking Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples didn't know it was Jesus.
So Jesus said to them, "Children, you haven't caught anything, have you?" "No," they answered.
He said to them, "Throw the net on the right side of the boat and you'll find some." So they threw it, and they couldn't haul it in because of the number of fish.

Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It's the Lord!" When Simon Peter heard it was the Lord, he wrapped his outer garment round himself — for he'd stripped for work — and threw himself into the sea.
The other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net full of fish. They weren't far from land, only about a hundred yards.
When they came ashore they saw a charcoal fire there, with fish on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish you've just caught."
So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish — a hundred and fifty-three of them. And even with so many, the net wasn't torn.
Jesus said to them, "Come and have breakfast." None of the disciples dared ask him, "Who are you?" — they knew it was the Lord.
Jesus came, took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish as well.
This was now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he was raised from the dead.
When they'd finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Feed my lambs."
He said to him again, a second time, "Simon son of John, do you love me?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Shepherd my sheep."

He said to him the third time, "Simon son of John, do you love me?" Peter was grieved that he asked him a third time, "Do you love me?" and he said, "Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Feed my sheep."

"I tell you the truth: when you were younger you dressed yourself and went where you wanted. But when you grow old you'll stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and carry you where you don't want to go."
He said this to show by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. Then he said to him, "Follow me."
Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them — the one who'd leaned back against him at the supper and said, "Lord, who's going to betray you?"
When Peter saw him he said to Jesus, "Lord, what about him?"
Jesus said to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me."
So the saying spread among the brothers that this disciple wouldn't die. But Jesus didn't say to him that he wouldn't die — only, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?"
This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who wrote them down, and we know that his testimony is true.
There are many other things that Jesus did. If every one of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself could hold the books that would be written.

jude_1.t: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James — to those who are called, who are loved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ:
May mercy and peace and love be multiplied to you.
Beloved, while I was making every effort to write to you about the salvation we share, I had to write and urge you to contend for the faith that was handed over once for all to the holy ones.

Some people have slipped in alongside — the ones written about long ago for this judgement — irreverent people, trading the grace of our God for licence and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
But I want to remind you — you who know all things once for all — that Jesus saved a people out of the land of Egypt, and the second time destroyed those who did not trust.
And the angels who did not keep their own domain but left the dwelling that was theirs — he has kept them in everlasting chains under gloom for the judgement of the great day.

So too Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them: they committed sexual immorality in the same way as these and went after other flesh, and they lie exposed as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire.
And yet these dreamers do the very same: they defile flesh, they set lordship aside, they blaspheme glories.
But when Michael the archangel was disputing with the devil, arguing about the body of Moses, he didn't dare bring a judgement of blasphemy; he said, 'May the Lord rebuke you.'
But these blaspheme whatever they don't know; and whatever they do understand by instinct, like the unreasoning animals — by those very things they're being destroyed.
Woe to them! They went the way of Cain; for pay they poured themselves out into the error of Balaam; in the contradiction of Korah they were destroyed.

These are the reefs in your love-feasts — feasting right alongside you without fear, shepherding themselves. Waterless clouds, carried past by the winds. Autumn trees with no fruit, dead twice over, torn up by the roots.
Wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shameful things. Wandering stars — and for them the gloom of darkness has been kept forever.
Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about these too. He said: 'Look — the Lord came with his holy myriads,

to bring judgement against everyone and to convict all the irreverent for all the works of irreverence they committed irreverently, and for all the harsh things irreverent sinners have spoken against him.'
These are grumblers, discontented with their lot, going according to their own cravings — and their mouth speaks swollen things, flattering faces for what they can get out of it.
But you, beloved — remember what the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ said beforehand,
how they kept telling you, 'In the last time there will be mockers, going according to their own cravings for irreverent things.'
These are the ones who make separations — soulish, without spirit.
But you, beloved — as you build yourselves up on your most holy faith and pray in the Holy Spirit,
keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, to eternal life.
Have mercy on some — the ones who are wavering;
save others, snatching them out of the fire; have mercy on others with fear, hating even the tunic stained by the flesh.
Now to the one who can guard you from stumbling and set you before his glory without blemish, in exultation —
to the only God, our Saviour, through Jesus Christ our Lord — glory, majesty, power and authority, before all the age and now and to all the ages. Amen.

luke_1.t: Since many have set out to draw up an account of the things that have come to fulfilment among us,
just as they were handed on to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and became servants of the word,
I too decided — having followed everything closely from the start — to write it out for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know how firm the ground is under what you were taught.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, from the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both of them were upright before God, and they lived blamelessly by all the Lord's commandments and requirements.
But they had no child, because Elizabeth couldn't bear one, and both of them were well on in years.
While he was serving as priest before God in his division's turn,
the lot fell to him, by the custom of the priesthood, to go into the sanctuary of the Lord and burn incense.
And outside, at the hour of incense, the whole gathered people were praying.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
When Zechariah saw him he was shaken, and fear fell on him.
But the angel said to him: "Don't be afraid, Zechariah — your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to name him John."
He will be your joy and your delight, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great in the Lord's sight. He is never to drink wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit while he is still in his mother's womb.
He will turn many of Israel's people back to the Lord their God,

and he will go on ahead of him in the spirit and power of Elijah — turning the hearts of parents to their children, and the disobedient to the good sense of the upright — to make ready for the Lord a people prepared.
And Zechariah said to the angel: "How am I to know this? I'm an old man, and my wife is well on in years."
The angel answered him: "I am Gabriel. I stand in God's presence, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.
And look — you'll be silent, unable to speak, until the day these things happen, because you didn't believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time."
Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah, wondering at how long he was staying in the sanctuary.
When he came out he couldn't speak to them, and they realised he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them, and he stayed unable to speak.
When his days of service were over, he went home.
After that his wife Elizabeth conceived, and for five months she kept herself out of sight. She said,
"So this is what the Lord has done for me — in the days when he looked on me, to take away my disgrace among people."
In the sixth month God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,
to a young woman promised in marriage to a man named Joseph, of the house of David. Her name was Mary.
The angel came in to her and said: "Greetings, favoured one — the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."
What he said troubled her deeply, and she kept turning over what kind of greeting this could be.
The angel said to her: "Don't be afraid, Mary — you have found favour with God.
And look — you'll conceive and bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus.
He will be great, and he will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
and he will reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and his kingdom will never end."
Mary said to the angel: "How will this happen? I have no relations with a man."
The angel answered her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And so the one to be born will be called holy — Son of God.
And look — Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son herself, in her old age; this is the sixth month for her, the one who was called barren,
because no word from God will ever be powerless."
Mary said: "Here I am, the Lord's servant. Let it happen to me just as you've said." And the angel left her.
In those days Mary set out and hurried into the hill country, to a town in Judah,
and she went into Zechariah's house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leapt in her womb, and she was filled with the Holy Spirit
and she cried out at the top of her voice: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And why is this given to me — that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
Look — the moment the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the child leapt for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who trusted that what the Lord spoke to her would be brought to completion."
And Mary said: "My soul makes the Lord great,
and my spirit has exulted in God my Saviour,
because he looked on the low estate of his servant. Look — from now on every generation will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me — and his name is holy —
and his mercy is on those who fear him, from generation to generation.
He has done a mighty deed with his arm; he has scattered the arrogant in the thoughts of their hearts;
he has pulled rulers down from their thrones and lifted up the lowly;
he has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty;
he has taken hold of Israel his servant, remembering mercy,
just as he said to our ancestors — to Abraham and his offspring for ever."
Mary stayed with her about three months, and then went home.
When Elizabeth's time came to give birth, she bore a son.
Her neighbours and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were about to name him Zechariah, after his father.
But his mother spoke up: "No — he's to be called John."
They said to her: "There's no one in your family called by that name."
So they made signs to his father, to find out what he wanted the child called.
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John." And they were all astonished.
At once his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, blessing God.
Fear came over all their neighbours, and all these things were talked about through the whole hill country of Judea.
and everyone who heard it laid it up in their hearts and said, "What will this child be, then?" For the Lord's hand was with him.
And his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied:
"Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because he has visited and made a redemption for his people,
and has raised up a horn of rescue for us in the house of David his servant —
just as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old —
rescue from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our ancestors and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath he swore to Abraham our ancestor — to grant us
to grant that we, rescued from our enemies' hand, might serve him without fear
in holiness and rightness before him, all our days.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go on before the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people knowledge of rescue through the release of their sins,
through the deep mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine on those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace."
The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the wilderness until the day he appeared publicly to Israel.

luke_2.t: In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole inhabited world was to be registered.
This was the first registration, made while Quirinius was governing Syria.
So everyone went to be registered, each to his own town.
Joseph too went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, into Judea, to David's town, Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family line of David,
to be registered along with Mary, who was promised to him in marriage and was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth,
and she gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in cloths and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no space for them in the guest room.
There were shepherds in that same region, out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock through the night.
An angel of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord blazed all round them, and they were terrified.
But the angel said to them: "Don't be afraid — look, I'm bringing you good news of a great joy, and it will be for all the people.
Today, in David's town, a Saviour has been born to you — he is Christ, Lord.
And this will be the sign for you: you'll find a baby wrapped in cloths and lying in a feeding trough."
