And all at once there was with the angel a great company of the heavenly army, praising God and saying:
"Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among people on whom his favour rests."
When the angels had gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let's go over to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, the thing the Lord has made known to us."
They hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the feeding trough.
Once they had seen it, they told what had been said to them about this child.
And everyone who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these things, turning them over in her heart.
The shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
When the eight days were up and it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus — the name the angel had given before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification under the law of Moses were over, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord —
as it is written in the law of the Lord: "Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord" —
and to offer a sacrifice according to what the law of the Lord says: "a pair of turtle-doves or two young pigeons".
There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was upright and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
He came in the Spirit into the temple, and when the parents brought the child Jesus in, to do for him what the law required,
he took him up in his arms, blessed God, and said:
"Now, Master, you are letting your servant go in peace, according to your word,
because my eyes have seen your rescue,
which you have prepared in the sight of all peoples —
a light for revelation to the nations, and glory for your people Israel."
His father and mother were amazed at what was being said about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother: "Look — this child is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that is spoken against,
and a sword will pass through your own soul too — so that the thoughts of many hearts may be laid bare."
There was a prophet there too, Anna, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was well on in years; she had lived with her husband seven years after her marriage,
and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, serving night and day with fasting and prayer.
She came up at that very hour and began to give thanks to God and to speak about him to everyone who was waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
When they had finished everything the law of the Lord required, they went back to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and God's favour was on him.
Every year his parents used to go to Jerusalem for the festival of Passover.
When he was twelve, they went up as usual for the festival,
and when the days were over and they were heading home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and his parents didn't know it.
Thinking he was in the travelling party, they went a day's journey, and then started looking for him among their relatives and the people they knew.
When they didn't find him, they went back to Jerusalem, searching for him.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was astounded at his understanding and his answers.
When they saw him they were overwhelmed, and his mother said to him, "Child, why have you done this to us? Look — your father and I have been searching for you in anguish."
He said to them, "Why were you searching for me? Didn't you know that I must be in my Father's house?"
But they didn't understand what he said to them.
He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother held on to all these things in her heart.
And Jesus went on advancing in wisdom and in stature, and in favour with God and with people.

luke_3.t: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod ruler over Galilee, his brother Philip ruler over the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruler over Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas — the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
He went all through the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a washing that goes with a change of mind, for the release of sins,
as it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: "A voice of one calling out in the wilderness: prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Every ravine will be filled and every mountain and hill made low; the crooked will become straight, and the rough roads smooth,
and all flesh will see the rescue that comes from God."
So he said to the crowds coming out to be baptised by him, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to run from the wrath that's coming?
So produce fruit that fits a change of mind, and don't start saying among yourselves, 'We've got Abraham for our father.' I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.
The axe is already at the root of the trees; so every tree that doesn't produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "So what should we do?"
He answered them, "Anyone who has two tunics should share with the one who has none, and anyone who has food should do the same."
Tax collectors came to be baptised too, and they said to him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
He said to them, "Don't collect any more than you've been ordered to."
Soldiers asked him too: "And what about us — what should we do?" He said to them, "Don't shake anyone down, don't bring false charges, and be content with your pay."
The people were full of expectation, and they were all turning over in their hearts whether John might be the Christ,

so John answered them all: "I baptise you with water. But someone stronger than me is coming, and I'm not fit to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptise you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, to clear his threshing floor right through and gather the wheat into his barn; but the chaff he will burn with fire that can't be put out."
And so, with many other appeals, he announced the good news to the people.
But Herod the ruler, who had been rebuked by him over Herodias, his brother's wife, and over all the evil things Herod had done,
added one more thing to it all: he shut John up in prison.
When all the people had been baptised, and Jesus too had been baptised and was praying, heaven was opened
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: "You are my Son, the beloved; in you I have taken delight."
Jesus himself was about thirty when he began. He was the son — as people supposed — of Joseph, son of Heli,
son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Jannai, son of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semein, son of Josech, son of Joda,
son of Joanan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri,
son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmadam, son of Er,
son of Joshua, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonam, son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menna, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Sala, son of Nahshon,
son of Amminadab, son of Admin, son of Arni, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor,
son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah,
son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan,
son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

luke_4.t: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, came back from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness
for forty days, tested by the devil. He ate nothing in those days, and when they were over he was hungry.
The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to turn into bread."
Jesus answered him, "It is written: 'A person shall not live on bread alone, but on every word of God.'"
The devil led him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in one instant,
and said to him, "I'll give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to anyone I want.
So if you'll bow down before me, it will all be yours."
Jesus answered him, "Get behind me, Satan. It is written: 'You shall bow down before the Lord your God, and serve him only.'"
Then he led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written: 'He will give his angels orders about you, to guard you carefully,'
and, 'On their hands they will lift you up, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered him, "It has been said: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
When the devil had finished every test, he left him — until an opportune time.
Jesus went back to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread through all the surrounding country.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and on the sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as he always did, and stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him; he unrolled it and found the place where it was written:

"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to prisoners and recovery of sight to the blind, to send the crushed away in release,
to proclaim the year of the Lord's favour."
He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant and sat down; and every eye in the synagogue was fixed on him.
He began to say to them, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
And they all spoke well of him, and they were amazed at the gracious words coming out of his mouth. And they said, "Isn't this Joseph's son?"
He said to them, "No doubt you'll quote me this proverb: 'Doctor, heal yourself. Do here in your home town the things we've heard you did at Capernaum.'"
And he said, "I tell you the truth, no prophet is accepted in his own home town.
In truth I tell you, there were plenty of widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land;
and Elijah wasn't sent to any of them — only to a widow at Zarephath in Sidon.
And there were many people with skin disease in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and not one of them was cleansed — only Naaman the Syrian."
Everyone in the synagogue was filled with fury when they heard that.
They got up, drove him out of the town and took him to the brow of the hill their town was built on, to throw him off the cliff.
But he passed through the middle of them and went on his way.
He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and he was teaching them on the sabbath.
They were astounded at his teaching, because his word carried authority.
In the synagogue there was a man with the spirit of an unclean demon, and he shouted out at the top of his voice:
"Ha! What have you got to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are — the Holy One of God!"
Jesus rebuked it: "Be quiet, and come out of him." The demon threw the man down in front of them all and came out, without doing him any harm.
Amazement came over them all, and they said to one another, "What is this word? He gives orders to the unclean spirits with authority and power, and out they come!"
And the sound of him went out into every place in the surrounding country.
He got up and left the synagogue and went into Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was in the grip of a high fever, and they asked him about her.
He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. She got up straight away and began to serve them.
As the sun was going down, everyone who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him, and he laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.
Demons came out of many people too, shouting, "You are the Son of God!" But he rebuked them and wouldn't let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
When day came he went out to a deserted place. The crowds went looking for him, and when they reached him they tried to hold him back from leaving them.
But he said to them, "I must announce the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns too, because that's what I was sent for."
And he went on proclaiming in the synagogues of Judea.

luke_5.t: One day, while the crowd was pressing in on him to hear the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
and he saw two boats at the shore, and the fishermen had got out of them and were washing their nets.
He got into one of the boats — Simon's — and asked him to put out a little from the land; then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into the deep water, and let your nets down for a catch."
Simon answered, "Master, we worked all night and took nothing — but at your word I'll let the nets down."
When they did this they enclosed a huge shoal of fish, and their nets were starting to tear.
So they signalled to their partners in the other boat to come and give them a hand. They came, and filled both boats so full that they were starting to sink.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord — I'm a sinful man."
For amazement had taken hold of him and everyone with him at the catch of fish they had taken,
and so it had James and John too, sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. And Jesus said to Simon, "Don't be afraid. From now on you'll be catching people alive."
And when they had brought the boats in to shore, they left everything and followed him.
While he was in one of the towns, there was a man covered with a skin disease. When he saw Jesus he fell on his face and begged him, "Lord, if you're willing, you can make me clean."
He reached out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing. Be clean." And at once the disease left him.
And he ordered him to tell no one — "but go and show yourself to the priest, and make the offering for your cleansing, just as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
But the word about him spread all the more, and great crowds kept gathering to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses.
But he would go off to deserted places and pray.

One day he was teaching, and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting there who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem; and the power of the Lord was there for him to heal.
And some men came carrying a paralysed man on a bed, and they were trying to bring him in and lay him down in front of Jesus.
When they couldn't find a way in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down through the tiles, bed and all, into the middle of the room in front of Jesus.
When he saw their trust, he said, "Friend, your sins are forgiven you."
The scribes and the Pharisees started reasoning, "Who is this, speaking blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
Jesus knew what they were thinking and answered them, "Why are you reasoning like this in your hearts?
Which is easier — to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man — "I'm telling you: get up, pick up your bed and go home."
On the spot he stood up in front of them, picked up what he'd been lying on and went home, glorifying God.
Astonishment took hold of them all, and they glorified God and were filled with fear, saying, "We've seen incredible things today."
After this he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, "Follow me."
And he left everything behind, got up and followed him.
Levi put on a great banquet for him at his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others reclining at table with them.
The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to his disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered them, "It's not the healthy who need a doctor, but the ones who are ill.
I haven't come to call the upright, but sinners, to a change of mind."
They said to him, "John's disciples fast often and say prayers, and so do the Pharisees' disciples; but yours go on eating and drinking."
Jesus said to them, "Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?
But days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast — in those days."
He told them a parable too: "Nobody tears a patch off a new garment and puts it on an old one. If he does, he's torn the new, and the patch from the new won't match the old.
And nobody puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, and it'll spill out, and the skins will be ruined.
New wine has to go into fresh skins.
And nobody who's been drinking old wine wants new; he says, 'The old is good.'"

luke_6.t: One [second-first] sabbath he was going through the grainfields, and his disciples were picking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands and eating them.
Some of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what isn't permitted on the sabbath?"
Jesus answered them, "Haven't you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry —
how he went into the house of God, took the bread of the Presence and ate it, and gave some to his companions — bread nobody is permitted to eat except the priests alone?"
And he said to them, "The Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath."
On another sabbath he went into the synagogue and was teaching, and there was a man there with a withered right hand.
The scribes and the Pharisees were watching him closely, to see if he'd heal on the sabbath, so they could find a charge against him.
But he knew what they were thinking, and he said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand here in the middle." And he got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, "Let me ask you: is it permitted on the sabbath to do good or to do harm — to save a life or to destroy it?"
He looked round at them all and said to him, "Stretch out your hand." He did, and his hand was restored.
But they were filled with fury and started discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.
In those days he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night in prayer to God.
When day came he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, and he named them apostles:
Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon called the Zealot,
Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
He came down with them and stood on a level place, with a great crowd of his disciples and a large gathering of people from all over Judea and Jerusalem and the coast of Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases; and those tormented by unclean spirits were cured.
And the whole crowd kept trying to touch him, because power was going out from him and healing them all.
Then he looked up at his disciples and said: "Blessed are you who are poor, because the kingdom of God is yours.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, because you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, because you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they shut you out and insult you and throw out your name as evil, because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day — leap for joy — because look, your reward is great in heaven. That's exactly what their ancestors did to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich — you've had your comfort already.
Woe to you who are full now, because you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you. That's exactly what their ancestors did to the false prophets.
But I tell you who are listening: love your enemies; do good to those who hate you;
bless those who curse you; pray for those who mistreat you.
If someone strikes you on the cheek, offer the other as well; and if someone takes your cloak, don't hold back your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if someone takes what is yours, don't demand it back.
And treat people the way you want them to treat you.
If you love the people who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love the people who love them.
And if you do good to the people who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that.
And if you lend to people you expect to be paid back by, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to get back the same amount.
Instead, love your enemies, do good, and lend expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you'll be children of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Don't judge, and you won't be judged. Don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Release, and you will be released.
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure — pressed down, shaken together, running over — will be poured into your lap. For the measure you use is the one that will be measured back to you.
He told them a parable too: "Can one blind person guide another? Won't they both fall into a pit?
A disciple isn't above his teacher; but everyone fully trained will be like his teacher.
And why do you look at the splinter in your brother's eye, and not notice the plank in your own?

Or how can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me get that splinter out of your eye,' when you don't see the plank in your own? You hypocrite! Take the plank out of your own eye first, and then you'll see clearly enough to take the splinter out of your brother's eye.
No good tree produces rotten fruit, and no rotten tree produces good fruit;
each tree is known by its own fruit. You don't gather figs from thorns, or pick grapes from a bramble.
A good person brings good out of the good treasure of the heart, and an evil person brings evil out of evil; for the mouth speaks out of what overflows in the heart.
Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord', and not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to me and hears my words and acts on them — I'll show you what he's like.
He's like someone building a house, who dug down deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood came, the river burst against that house and couldn't shake it, because it had been well built.
But the one who hears and doesn't act is like someone who built a house on the ground with no foundation. The river burst against it, and down it came at once, and the ruin of that house was great.

luke_7.t: When he had finished everything he had to say in the hearing of the people, he went into Capernaum.
There was a centurion whose slave was ill and about to die — a slave he valued highly.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent some elders of the Jews to him, to ask him to come and save his slave.
When they came to Jesus they pleaded with him hard: "He's worthy for you to do this for him,
he loves our nation, and he's the one who built us our synagogue."
So Jesus went with them. When he wasn't far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say to him, "Sir, don't trouble yourself — I'm not worthy to have you come under my roof.
That's why I didn't think myself fit to come to you. Just say the word, and let my boy be healed.
I'm a man under authority myself, with soldiers under me. I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes; to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this he was amazed at him, and he turned to the crowd following him and said, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found trust like this."
And when those who had been sent got back to the house, they found the slave well.
Soon after that he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went along with him.
As he came near the town gate, a dead man was being carried out — his mother's only son, and she was a widow; and a large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her, "Don't weep."
He went up and touched the bier, and the bearers stopped. And he said, "Young man, I'm telling you, get up."
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.
Fear took hold of them all, and they glorified God, saying, "A great prophet has been raised up among us," and, "God has visited his people."
And this word about him went out through the whole of Judea and all the surrounding country.
John's disciples reported all this to him. So John called two of his disciples to him
and sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we be expecting someone else?"
When the men came to him they said, "John the Baptist sent us to you to ask: Are you the one who is to come, or should we be expecting someone else?"
Right then he cured many people of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and gave sight to many who were blind.

And he answered them, "Go and tell John what you've seen and heard: the blind see again, the lame walk, those with skin disease are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news announced to them.
And blessed is anyone who isn't tripped up by me."
When John's messengers had gone, he began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? Look — the people who wear splendid clothing and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you — and more than a prophet.
This is the one it's written about: 'Look — I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.'
I tell you, of everyone born of women no one is greater than John; and yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."
All the people who heard this — the tax collectors included — acknowledged God's justice, having been baptised with John's baptism;
but the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected God's purpose for themselves; they had not been baptised by him.
"So what shall I compare the people of this generation to? What are they like?
They're like children sitting in the marketplace, calling out to one another: 'We played the flute for you and you didn't dance; we sang a lament and you didn't weep.'
For John the Baptist has come, eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look — a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.'
And wisdom is vindicated by all her children."
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, so he went into the Pharisee's house and reclined at table.
And there was a woman in the town who was a sinner, and when she learned he was reclining at table in the Pharisee's house she brought an alabaster jar of perfumed oil,
and stood behind him at his feet, weeping. She began to wet his feet with her tears and wipe them with the hair of her head, and she kept kissing his feet and anointing them with the oil.

When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, "If this man were the prophet, he'd know who this woman is who's touching him, and what kind of woman she is — that she's a sinner."
Jesus answered him, "Simon, I have something to say to you." "Teacher, say it," he says.
"Two men were in debt to a moneylender. One owed five hundred denarii, the other fifty.
When they couldn't repay, he let them both off. Now which of them will love him more?"
Simon answered, "I suppose the one he let off more." And he said to him, "You've judged rightly."
Then he turned to the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the moment I came in she hasn't stopped kissing my feet.
You didn't anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfumed oil.
So I tell you: her many sins have been forgiven — that's why she has loved much. But the one who is forgiven little, loves little."
And he said to her, "Your sins are forgiven."
Those reclining at table with him started saying among themselves, "Who is this, who even forgives sins?"
But he said to the woman, "Your trust has saved you. Go in peace."

luke_8.t: Soon after that he travelled town by town and village by village, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him,
and some women too who had been cured of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others — they were providing for them out of their own means.
When a large crowd was gathering, and people were coming to him from one town after another, he spoke in a parable:
"A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the path and got trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
Some fell on the rock, and when it came up it withered, because it had no moisture.
Some fell in among the thorns, and the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
And some fell into the good soil, and it grew and produced fruit a hundredfold." As he said this he called out, "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
His disciples asked him what this parable meant.
He said, "To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of God; but to the rest it comes in parables, so that 'seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.'
"This is what the parable means: the seed is the word of God.
Those along the path are the ones who hear; then the devil comes and takes the word out of their hearts, so that they may not trust and be saved.
Those on the rock are the ones who hear and welcome the word with joy; but they have no root — they trust for a while, and when the testing comes they fall away.
What fell among the thorns is those who hear, and as they go on their way they get choked by the worries and riches and pleasures of life, and they don't bring anything to maturity.
But the seed in the good soil is those who hear the word with a good and upright heart, hold on to it, and bear fruit with endurance.
Nobody lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. You put it on a lampstand, so that people coming in can see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not become visible, and nothing concealed that will not be known and come out into the open.
So take care how you listen; because whoever has will be given more, and whoever doesn't have — even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him."
His mother and his brothers came to him, and they couldn't get to him because of the crowd.
He was told, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you."
But he answered them, "My mother and my brothers are these — the ones who hear the word of God and do it."
One day he got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, "Let's cross over to the other side of the lake." So they set out,
and as they sailed he dropped off to sleep. A squall of wind came down on the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.
They went to him and woke him: "Master, Master, we're perishing!" He woke up and rebuked the wind and the raging water, and they stopped, and there was a calm.
He said to them, "Where is your trust?" And they were afraid and amazed, and said to one another, "Who is this, then, that he gives orders even to the winds and the water, and they obey him?"
They sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
As he stepped out onto the land, a man from the town met him, a man who had demons. For a long time he'd worn no clothes, and he didn't live in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus he cried out, fell down in front of him and shouted at the top of his voice, "What have you got to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don't torment me."

For Jesus had ordered the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was kept under guard, bound with chains and shackles, he'd break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" He said, "Legion" — because many demons had gone into him.
And they kept begging him not to order them off into the abyss.
There was a large herd of pigs feeding there on the hillside, and the demons begged him to let them go into the pigs. He gave them permission,
and the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
When those tending them saw what had happened, they ran off and reported it in the town and out in the countryside.
People came out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man the demons had gone out of sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind — and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the man who'd been possessed by demons was saved.
Then the whole population of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to go away from them, because they were gripped by a great fear. So he got into the boat and went back.
The man the demons had gone out of begged to be with him. But Jesus sent him away, saying,
"Go back home and tell everything God has done for you." And off he went, proclaiming through the whole town everything Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus got back, the crowd welcomed him, because they'd all been waiting for him.
And a man named Jairus came — he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to his house,
because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As he went, the crowds were crushing in on him.
And a woman who'd had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent everything she had on doctors and couldn't be healed by anyone,
came up behind him and touched the edge of his cloak, and on the spot her flow of blood stopped.
Jesus said, "Who touched me?" When they all denied it, Peter said, "Master, the crowds are all round you, pressing in on you!"
But Jesus said, "Someone touched me. I know power has gone out from me."
When the woman saw that she hadn't gone unnoticed, she came trembling, fell down before him, and told him in front of all the people why she had touched him, and how she had been healed on the spot.
He said to her, "Daughter, your trust has saved you. Go in peace."
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue ruler's house and said, "Your daughter has died. Don't trouble the teacher any further."
But Jesus heard it and answered him, "Don't be afraid. Only trust, and she will be saved."
When he came to the house he didn't let anyone go in with him except Peter and John and James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and beating their breasts for her. But he said, "Don't weep. She hasn't died — she's asleep."
And they laughed at him — they knew she had died.
But he took her by the hand and called out, "Child, get up."
Her spirit returned, and she got up on the spot; and he told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were astounded, but he ordered them to tell nobody what had happened.

luke_9.t: He called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to cure diseases,
and he sent them out to announce the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them: Take nothing for the road — no staff, no bag, no bread, no silver — and don't have two shirts each.
Whatever house you go into, stay there, and leave from there.
And wherever they don't welcome you, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that town, as evidence against them.
So they set out and went from village to village, announcing the good news and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about everything that was going on, and he didn't know what to make of it, because some were saying that John had been raised from the dead,
and others that Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the prophets of long ago had risen.
But Herod said: John — I beheaded him. So who is this I'm hearing such things about? And he kept trying to see him.
When the apostles got back they told him everything they had done. And he took them with him and went off privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. He made them welcome, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed the ones who needed curing.

The day began to wear away. The Twelve came up and said to him: Send the crowd off, so they can go into the villages and farms round about and find lodging and provisions — we're in a deserted place out here.
But he said to them: You give them something to eat. They said: We've got no more than five loaves and two fish — unless we go and buy food for all these people.
There were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples: Get them to sit down in groups of about fifty.
They did so, and got them all seated.
Then he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to the sky, blessed them, broke them into pieces and kept handing them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
They all ate and had their fill, and what was left over was picked up — twelve baskets of pieces.
One time when he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he asked them: Who do the crowds say I am?
They answered: John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and others, that one of the prophets of long ago has risen.
He said to them: And you — who do you say I am? Peter answered: The Christ of God.
But he warned them sharply and ordered them to tell nobody this,
saying: The Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
And he said to them all: If anyone wants to come after me, he must say no to himself and pick up his cross day after day and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
What good is it to anyone to gain the whole world and lose or forfeit himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
I tell you truly, there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.
About eight days after he said this, he took Peter and John and James and went up the mountain to pray.
And as he prayed, the look of his face changed, and his clothing turned a dazzling white.
And two men were talking with him. They were Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and were speaking of his exodus, which he was about to complete in Jerusalem.
Peter and the others with him were heavy with sleep, but they stayed awake and saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And as the men were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus: Master, it's good for us to be here. Let's make three shelters — one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah. He didn't know what he was saying.
While he was still saying it, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they went into the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud, saying: This is my Son, the Chosen One. Listen to him.
When the voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they kept quiet, and in those days they told nobody anything of what they had seen.
The next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
And a man from the crowd shouted out: Teacher, I beg you, take a look at my son — he's my only child.
A spirit takes hold of him and all of a sudden he screams, and it convulses him till he foams at the mouth, and it'll hardly leave him, and it wears him down.
I begged your disciples to drive it out, and they couldn't.
Jesus answered: You unbelieving and twisted generation, how long will I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.
While the boy was still on his way, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the child and gave him back to his father.
And they were all astounded at the greatness of God. While everyone was marvelling at everything he was doing, he said to his disciples:
You, put these words into your ears: the Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands.
But they didn't understand what he said. It was concealed from them so that they wouldn't grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
An argument started among them about which of them was the greatest.
But Jesus knew the reasoning of their heart, and he took a child and stood the child beside him,
and said to them: Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. For the one who is least among you all — that's the one who is great.
John said: Master, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we kept trying to stop him, because he doesn't follow along with us.
But Jesus said to him: Don't stop him. Whoever is not against you is for you.
As the days drew to their full for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers on ahead of him. They went into a Samaritan village to get things ready for him.
But they didn't welcome him, because his face was set for going to Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said: Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from the sky and burn them up, the way Elijah did?
But he turned and rebuked them, and said: [You don't know what kind of spirit you are of.]
[For the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives but to save them.] And they went on to another village.
As they were going along the road, someone said to him: I'll follow you wherever you go.
And Jesus said to him: The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
He said to another: Follow me. But he said: Lord, let me go and bury my father first.
But Jesus said to him: Leave the dead to bury their own dead. You go and proclaim the kingdom of God.
Someone else said: I'll follow you, Lord, but let me first say goodbye to the people at home.
But Jesus said to him: Nobody who puts his hand to the plough and looks at what's behind him is fit for the kingdom of God.

luke_10.t: After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them on ahead of him, two by two, into every town and place he was going to go himself.
And he said to them: The harvest is big, but the workers are few. So beg the lord of the harvest to throw workers out into his harvest.
Go. Look, I'm sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Don't carry a purse or a bag or sandals, and don't greet anyone on the road.
Whatever house you go into, say first: Peace to this house.
And if there's a person of peace there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it'll come back to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking whatever they give you, because the worker deserves his pay. Don't go moving from house to house.
And whatever town you go into, if they welcome you, eat what's put in front of you
and heal the sick there and say to them: The kingdom of God has come near to you.
But whatever town you go into where they don't welcome you, go out into its streets and say:
Even the dust from your town that's clinging to our feet — we wipe it off against you. But know this: the kingdom of God has come near.
I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.

How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! Because if the acts of power done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they'd have changed their minds long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum: will you be lifted up to heaven? You will go down to Hades.
Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. And whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
The seventy-two came back full of joy, saying: Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.
He said to them: I saw Satan fall like lightning from the sky.
Look, I've given you the authority to walk on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing at all will harm you.
But don't be glad about this, that the spirits submit to you. Be glad instead that your names have been written in the heavens.

Right then he was overjoyed in the Holy Spirit and said: I acknowledge you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from the wise and the clever and revealed them to infants. Yes, Father — this is how it was pleasing before you.

And turning to the disciples he said: Everything has been handed over to me by my Father, and nobody knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son — and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.
And turning to the disciples privately he said: Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
For I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you're seeing and didn't see it, and to hear what you're hearing and didn't hear it.
And a lawyer got up to test him and said: Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?
He said to him: What is written in the law? How do you read it?
He answered: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind, and your neighbour as yourself.
He said to him: You've answered right. Do this and you will live.
But he wanted to justify himself, so he said to Jesus: And who is my neighbour?
Jesus took this up and said: A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among bandits. They stripped him and beat him and went off, leaving him half dead.
As it happened, a priest was going down that road, and when he saw him he passed by on the other side.
And the same with a Levite: he came to the place, saw him, and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan travelling that way came to where he was, and when he saw him he was moved with compassion,
and he went over to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, took him to an inn and looked after him.
And the next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper and said: Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I'll repay you when I come back.
Which of these three do you think became a neighbour to the man who fell among the bandits?
He said: The one who showed him mercy. And Jesus said to him: Go — and you do the same.
As they went on their way, he came into a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her house.
She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to what he was saying.
But Martha was being pulled in every direction by all the serving, and she came up and said: Lord, don't you care that my sister has left me to do the serving on my own? Tell her to give me a hand.
The Lord answered her: Martha, Martha, you're anxious and worked up about many things,
but only one thing is needed. For Mary chose the good portion, and it won't be taken away from her.

luke_11.t: One day he was praying in a certain place, and when he stopped, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, the way John taught his disciples.
He said to them: When you pray, say: Father [ours who is in the heavens], let your name be treated as holy. Let your kingdom come. [Let your will happen, as in heaven, so also on earth.]
Give us each day the bread we need for the day ahead.
And forgive us our sins, since we ourselves also forgive everyone in debt to us. And do not bring us into testing. [But rescue us from the evil one.]
And he said to them: Suppose one of you has a friend and goes to him in the middle of the night and says: Friend, lend me three loaves,
because a friend of mine has turned up from a journey, and I've got nothing to set in front of him.
And the man inside answers: Don't bother me. The door's already locked, and my children are in bed with me. I can't get up and give you anything.
I tell you, even if he won't get up and give him anything because he's his friend, still because of his shamelessness he'll get up and give him whatever he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given you; look, and you'll find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever looks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which of you fathers, if his son asks for [bread, will hand him a stone; or if he asks for] a fish, will hand him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he hand him a scorpion?
So if you, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
He was driving out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said: He drives out the demons by Beelzeboul, the ruler of the demons.
Others were testing him, looking to him for a sign from heaven.
But he knew what they were thinking and said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and a house falls on a house.
And if Satan is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul.
And if I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul, who do your own sons drive them out by? So they'll be your judges.
But if I drive out the demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are safe.
But when someone stronger than he is comes at him and beats him, he takes away the armour he'd been trusting in and hands out the spoils.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever doesn't gather with me scatters.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it goes through waterless places looking for rest, and when it finds none it says: I'll go back to my house, the one I came out of.
And when it gets there, it finds the house empty, swept and put in order.
Then off it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there. And that person ends up worse off than before.
As he was saying this, a woman in the crowd called out to him: Blessed is the womb that carried you and the breasts you nursed at.
But he said: Rather, blessed are the ones who hear the word of God and keep it.
As the crowds were packing in around him he began to say: This generation is an evil generation. It looks for a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also the Son of Man will be to this generation.

The queen of the south will be raised at the judgement with the men of this generation and will condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up at the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because they changed their minds at Jonah's proclamation, and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
Nobody lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket — you put it on a lampstand, so that people coming in can see the light.
Your eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is single, your whole body is full of light too; but when it is evil, your body is dark as well.
So watch out that the light in you isn't darkness.
So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp lights you with its flash.
While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him in for a meal. So he went in and reclined at table.
The Pharisee saw it and was surprised he hadn't washed first, before the meal.
But the Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of greed and evil.
You fools! Didn't the one who made the outside make the inside too?
But give what is inside as charity, and look, everything is clean for you.
But how terrible for you Pharisees! You tithe the mint and the rue and every herb, and you pass right by justice and the love of God. These you should have done, without leaving those aside.
How terrible for you Pharisees! You love the front seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
How terrible for you! You're like unmarked graves, and people walk over them without knowing.
One of the lawyers answered him: Teacher, when you say these things you insult us too.
But he said: How terrible for you lawyers too! You load people up with loads that are hard to carry, and you yourselves don't touch the loads with one of your fingers.
How terrible for you! You build the tombs of the prophets, and it was your fathers who killed them.
So you are witnesses, and you approve of your fathers' works: they killed them, and you build.
That's why the wisdom of God said: I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,
so that the blood of all the prophets poured out since the foundation of the world may be required from this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the house. Yes, I tell you, it will be required from this generation.
How terrible for you lawyers! You took away the key of knowledge. You didn't go in yourselves, and you stopped the ones who were going in.
When he had gone out from there, the scribes and the Pharisees started pressing him hard and firing questions at him about many things,
lying in wait for him, trying to catch something out of his mouth so that they could accuse him.

luke_12.t: Meanwhile the crowd had gathered in their tens of thousands, so that they were trampling one another, and he began to say to his disciples first: Watch yourselves against the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
There is nothing covered up that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be known.
So whatever you've said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you whispered in someone's ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the rooftops.
And I tell you, my friends: don't be afraid of the people who kill the body and after that have nothing more they can do.
But I'll show you who to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you — fear that one.
Aren't five sparrows sold for two small coins? And not one of them is forgotten before God.
But even the hairs on your head have all been counted. Don't be afraid. You're worth more than many sparrows.
And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me in front of people — the Son of Man will acknowledge him too, in front of the angels of God.
But whoever denies me in front of people will be denied in front of the angels of God.
And everyone who says a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever slanders the Holy Spirit won't be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, don't worry about how to defend yourself, or what to say in your defence, or what to say,
for the Holy Spirit will teach you right then what you must say.
Someone in the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
But he said to him: Man, who appointed me a judge or an arbitrator over you?
And he said to them: Watch out — guard yourselves against every kind of greed, because a person's life doesn't consist in how much he owns.
And he told them a parable: There was a rich man whose land produced well.
And he reasoned to himself: What am I going to do? I've got nowhere to gather my crops.
And he said: This is what I'll do. I'll pull down my barns and build bigger ones, and I'll gather all my grain and my goods in there,
and I'll say to my soul: Soul, you've got plenty of good things stored up for many years. Take it easy, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.
But God said to him: Fool! Tonight they're demanding your soul back from you. And the things you've got ready — whose will they be?
That's how it is for the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.
And he said to his disciples: That's why I tell you, don't worry about your life, what you'll eat, or about your body, what you'll wear.
For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Think about the ravens: they don't sow or reap, they've no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more you are worth than the birds!
And which of you can add a single hour to his span of life by worrying?
So if you can't do even the smallest thing, why worry about the rest?
Think about the lilies, how they grow: they don't labour or spin. But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of them.
And if that's how God clothes the grass — in the field today and thrown into the oven tomorrow — how much more you, you of little trust.
And you — don't go looking for what you'll eat and what you'll drink, and don't be unsettled.
For all the nations of the world chase after these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
Rather, look for his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Don't be afraid, little flock — your Father was pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to charity. Make yourselves purses that don't wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
Keep your waists belted and your lamps lit,
and be like people waiting for their master to come home from the wedding feast, so that the moment he comes and knocks they can open up for him.
Blessed are those slaves the master finds awake when he comes. I tell you the truth, he'll belt himself up and have them recline, and he'll come and serve them.
Even if he comes in the second watch, or comes in the third and finds them like that, those slaves are blessed.
But know this: if the householder had known what time the thief was coming, he wouldn't have let his house be broken into.
You be ready too, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you don't expect.
Peter said: Lord, are you telling this parable for us, or for everyone?
And the lord said: So who is the trustworthy manager, the sensible one, whom the master will put in charge of his household of attendants to give them their ration at the right time?
Blessed is that slave his master finds doing just that when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his property.
But if that slave says in his heart: My master's taking his time coming — and starts to beat the slave boys and slave girls, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that slave will come on a day he isn't expecting and at an hour he doesn't know, and will cut him in two and put his portion with the unfaithful.
That slave who knew his master's will and didn't get ready or act on it will be beaten with many blows.

But the one who didn't know, and did things deserving a beating, will be beaten with few. From everyone who's been given much, much will be required; and from the one they've entrusted much to, they'll ask all the more.
I came to throw fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled.
But I have a baptism to be baptised with, and how constrained I am until it's completed.
Do you think I came to give peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
And he said to the crowds as well: When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say straight away that a downpour's coming — and it does.
And when a south wind is blowing, you say it's going to be scorching — and it is.
Hypocrites! You know how to read the face of the earth and the sky — so how is it you don't know how to read this present time?
And why don't you judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you're going with your opponent before a magistrate, do your best on the way to be rid of him — or he'll drag you off to the judge, and the judge will hand you over to the officer, and the officer will throw you into prison.
I tell you, you certainly won't get out of there until you've paid back even the last lepton.

luke_13.t: Just then some people were there telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
And he answered them: Do you think those Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this?
No, I tell you. But unless you change your minds, you'll all be destroyed the same way.
Or those eighteen the tower in Siloam fell on and killed — do you think they were in greater debt than everyone else living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you change your minds, you'll all be destroyed the same way.
And he told this parable: Someone had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and didn't find any.
So he said to the vine-worker: Look, for three years now I've been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and I don't find any. Cut it down. Why should it use up the ground as well?
But he answered him: Sir, leave it this year as well, till I dig round it and put manure on it.
And if it bears fruit next year, well and good. If not, you can cut it down.
He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
And there was a woman there who'd had a spirit of weakness for eighteen years. She was bent double and couldn't straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her he called her over and said to her: Woman, you've been released from your weakness.
And he put his hands on her, and at once she was straightened up and began praising God.

But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the sabbath, and he said to the crowd: There are six days when work is to be done. So come and be healed on those, and not on the sabbath day.
But the Lord answered him: Hypocrites! Doesn't every one of you untie his ox or his donkey from the manger on the sabbath and lead it off for a drink?
And this woman — a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan bound for eighteen years — wasn't it necessary for her to be untied from this bond on the sabbath day?
As he said this, all his opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd was rejoicing at all the splendid things that were happening through him.
So he said: What is the kingdom of God like, and what shall I compare it to?
It's like a mustard seed that a man took and threw into his own garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.
And again he said: What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
It's like yeast that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until the whole batch was leavened.
And he went on through towns and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem.
Someone said to him: Lord, are only a few being saved? And he said to them:
Struggle to get in through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will try to get in and won't be able to.
Once the householder has got up and shut the door, you'll start standing outside, knocking at the door and saying: Lord, open up for us. And he'll answer you: I don't know where you're from.
Then you'll start saying: We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.
And he'll say: I tell you, I don't know where you're from. Get away from me, all you workers of injustice.
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves thrown outside.
And people will come from east and west and from north and south and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
Just then some Pharisees came and said to him: Get out and go away from here — Herod wants to kill you.
And he said to them: Go and tell that fox: Look, I am driving out demons and completing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I complete my mission.
But I must go on today and tomorrow and the next day, because it isn't acceptable for a prophet to be destroyed outside Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you — how often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a bird gathers her brood under her wings, and you wouldn't have it.
Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you the truth, you won't see me until the time comes when you say: Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord.

luke_14.t: One sabbath he went into the house of one of the leading Pharisees to eat bread, and they were watching him closely.
And right there in front of him was a man with dropsy.
And Jesus said to the lawyers and Pharisees: Is it permitted to heal on the sabbath, or not?
But they said nothing. So he took hold of him, healed him and sent him away.
And he said to them: Which of you, if a son or an ox falls into a well, won't pull him straight out on the sabbath day?
And they couldn't give any answer to that.
And he told the guests a parable, when he noticed how they were picking out the places of honour. He said to them:
When someone invites you to a wedding, don't recline in the place of honour, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him,
and the man who invited you both comes and says to you: Give this man your place. And then you'll start, in shame, to take the last place.

But when you're invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the man who invited you comes he'll say to you: Friend, move up higher. Then you'll have honour in front of everyone reclining with you.
For everyone who lifts himself up will be brought low, and the one who lowers himself will be lifted up.

And he said to the man who had invited him as well: When you put on a lunch or a dinner, don't call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbours, in case they invite you back in return and you get repaid.
But when you put on a reception, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.
And you'll be blessed, because they've nothing to repay you with. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just.
One of those reclining with him heard this and said to him: Blessed is whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
But he said to him: There was a man giving a great dinner, and he invited a lot of people.
And at dinner time he sent his slave to say to the ones who had been invited: Come — it's ready now.
And every one of them started making excuses. The first said to him: I've bought a field and I have to go out and look at it. Please accept my excuses.
And another said: I've bought five pairs of oxen and I'm on my way to test them. Please accept my excuses.
And another said: I've married a woman, and that's why I can't come.

And the slave came back and reported this to his master. Then the householder was angry and said to his slave: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town and bring the poor and crippled and blind and lame in here.
And the slave said: Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there's still room.
And the master said to the slave: Go out to the roads and the hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my dinner. [For many are called, but few are chosen.]
Large crowds were travelling with him, and he turned and said to them:
If anyone comes to me and doesn't hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters — and his own life as well — he can't be my disciple.
And whoever doesn't carry his own cross and come after me can't be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, doesn't sit down first and work out the cost, to see whether he's got enough to finish it?
Otherwise, once he's laid a foundation and can't finish, everyone watching will start making fun of him,
saying: This man started building and couldn't finish.
Or what king, going out to take on another king in war, won't sit down first and think out whether he's able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
And if not, while the other is still far off he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
So then, not one of you who doesn't say goodbye to all his own possessions can be my disciple.
So salt is good; but if even the salt goes flat, what will it be seasoned with?
It's no use for the soil or for the manure heap. They throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

luke_15.t: All the tax collectors and the sinners kept coming near him to listen to him.
And the Pharisees and the scribes kept grumbling among themselves: This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.
So he told them this parable:
Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn't he leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that's lost till he finds it?
And when he's found it he puts it on his shoulders, rejoicing,
and he comes home and calls his friends and neighbours together and says to them: Celebrate with me — I've found my lost sheep.
I tell you, in the same way there'll be more joy in heaven over one sinner who changes his mind than over ninety-nine just people who have no need to change their minds.
Or suppose a woman has ten drachmas and loses one drachma. Doesn't she light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully till she finds it?
And when she's found it she calls her women friends and neighbours together and says: Celebrate with me — I've found the drachma I lost.
In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who changes his mind.
And he said: There was a man who had two sons.
And the younger one said to his father: Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me. So he divided his living between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went off to a distant country, and there he scattered his property, living without restraint.
When he'd spent everything, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and the man sent him out into his fields to feed pigs.
And he was longing to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, and nobody was giving him anything.
But he came to himself and said: How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread — and here am I, dying of hunger.
I'll get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I've sinned against heaven and in front of you.
I'm no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.
So he got up and went to his own father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and he ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him: Father, I've sinned against heaven and in front of you. I'm no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers.
But the father said to his slaves: Quick — bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
And bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let's eat and celebrate,
because this son of mine was dead and he's come back to life; he was lost and he's been found. And they began to celebrate.
But his elder son was out in the field. And as he came near the house he heard music and dancing,
and he called one of the young slaves over and asked what all this was about.
He said to him: Your brother's come home, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he's got him back safe and sound.
But he was angry and wouldn't go in. So his father came out and kept pleading with him.
But he answered his father: Look, all these years I've been slaving for you and I never disobeyed an order of yours, and you never gave me a young goat to celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came home — the one who ate up your living with prostitutes — you killed the fattened calf for him.
But he said to him: Child, you're always with me, and everything that's mine is yours.
But we had to celebrate and be glad — this brother of yours was dead and he's come alive, he was lost and he's been found.

luke_16.t: He said to his disciples as well: There was a rich man who had a manager, and this man was accused to him of squandering his property.
So he called him in and said to him: What's this I hear about you? Hand over the account of your management — you can't be manager any longer.
And the manager said to himself: What am I going to do? My master's taking the management away from me. I'm not strong enough to dig, and I'm ashamed to beg.
I know what I'll do, so that when I'm removed from the management, people will welcome me into their houses.
So he called in each one of his master's debtors, and he said to the first: How much do you owe my master?
He said: A hundred baths of olive oil. And he said to him: Take your bill, sit down, quick, and write fifty.
Then he said to another: And you — how much do you owe? He said: A hundred kors of wheat. He said to him: Take your bill and write eighty.
And the master commended the manager of injustice, because he'd acted shrewdly. For the children of this age are shrewder toward their own generation than the children of light.
And I tell you, make friends for yourselves out of the mammon of injustice, so that when it gives out they may welcome you into the eternal tents.
Whoever is trustworthy in the smallest thing is trustworthy in much too, and whoever is unjust in the smallest thing is unjust in much too.
So if you haven't proved trustworthy with the unjust mammon, who will entrust you with the true wealth?
And if you haven't proved trustworthy with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what's your own?
No household slave can serve two masters. Either he'll hate the one and love the other, or he'll hold to one and think nothing of the other. You can't serve God and mammon.
The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all this and they were sneering at him.
And he said to them: You're the ones who justify yourselves in front of people, but God knows your hearts. What is exalted among people is a disgusting thing before God.
The law and the prophets were until John. From then on the kingdom of God is announced as good news, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
But it's easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
There was a rich man who used to dress in purple and fine linen, enjoying himself in splendour every day.
And a poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gateway, covered in sores,
and longing to be filled with what fell from the rich man's table. And the dogs even came and licked his sores.
And it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels to Abraham's side. And the rich man died too, and was buried.
And in Hades he looked up, in torment, and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus at his side.
And he called out: Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue — I'm in agony in this flame.
But Abraham said: Child, remember that you received your good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise the bad. But now he's comforted here, and you're in agony.
And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you can't, and nobody crosses from there to us.
And he said: Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father's house,
because I have five brothers — so that he can warn them, so they don't come to this place of torment as well.
But Abraham said: They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.
But he said: No, father Abraham — but if someone goes to them from the dead, they'll change their minds.
But he said to him: If they don't listen to Moses and the prophets, they won't be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.

luke_17.t: He said to his disciples, "It's impossible for the traps not to come — but misery to the one they come through.
It'd pay him better to have a millstone hung round his neck and be thrown into the sea, than to trip up one of these little ones.
Watch yourselves. If your brother sins against you, confront him — and if he changes his mind, release him.
And if he sins against you seven times in one day, and seven times turns back to you saying, 'I'm changing my mind' — you will release him."
And the apostles said to the Lord, "Give us more faith."
And the Lord said, "If you have faith like a mustard seed, you'd say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea' — and it would obey you."
"Which of you, with a slave ploughing or shepherding, will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come straight in and take your place at table'?
Won't he rather say to him, 'Get my dinner ready, and tie up your clothes and serve me while I eat and drink — and after that you can eat and drink'?
Does he thank the slave for doing what he was told? I think not.
So with you: when you've done everything you were told, say, 'We're useless slaves. We've done what we owed.'"
And as he was travelling to Jerusalem, he was passing through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he was entering a village, ten men with a skin disease met him. They stood at a distance,
and they called out, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us."
And when he saw them he said, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as they went, they were made clean.
One of them, when he saw he'd been healed, turned back, glorifying God at the top of his voice.
And he fell on his face at his feet, thanking him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, "Weren't the ten made clean? Where are the nine?
Was no one found to turn back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
And he said to him, "Get up and go. Your faith has saved you."
When the Pharisees asked him when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them, "The kingdom of God isn't coming with things to watch for,
nor will they say, 'Look, here!' or 'Look, there!' For look — the kingdom of God is among you."
And he said to the disciples, "Days will come when you'll long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you won't see it.
