And they'll say to you, 'Look, there!' 'Look, here!' Don't go off; don't chase after them.
For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, that's how the Son of Man will be in his day.
But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
And just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
They were eating, drinking, marrying, being given in marriage — right up to the day Noah went into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building.
But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulphur rained down from the sky and destroyed them all.
That's how it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever's up on the roof, with his belongings in the house, mustn't go down to get them; and the one out in the field, likewise, mustn't turn back for what's behind.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever tries to hold on to his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
I tell you, on that night there'll be two on one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
There'll be two women grinding together: one will be taken and the other left."
[Two will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.]
And they answered him, "Where, Lord?" And he said to them, "Where the body is, that's where the vultures will gather."

luke_18.t: He told them a parable about the need to pray always and not lose heart.
He said, "In a certain city there was a judge who didn't fear God and had no regard for anyone.
And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against my opponent.'
And for a while he wouldn't. But then he said to himself, 'Even if I don't fear God or have regard for anyone,
still, because this widow keeps bothering me, I'll give her justice, so she doesn't wear me out by coming for ever.'"
And the Lord said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says.
And won't God give justice to his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he be slow with them?
I tell you, he'll give them justice, and quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He told this parable too, to some who were confident that they themselves were righteous and looked down on everyone else.
"Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed this, to himself: 'God, I thank you that I'm not like the rest of humanity — greedy, unjust, adulterers — or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I tithe on everything I acquire.'
But the tax collector, standing far off, wouldn't even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest and said, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner.'
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified, rather than the other. For everyone who lifts himself up will be brought low, and the one who brings himself low will be lifted up."
They were bringing him even their babies, so that he might touch them; but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them to him and said, "Let the children come to me, and don't stop them; the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
I tell you the truth: whoever doesn't receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it."
And a certain ruler questioned him: "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God.
You know the commandments: do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honour your father and your mother."
And he said, "I've kept all these since I was young."
When Jesus heard this he said to him, "There's still one thing you lack. Sell everything you have and give it out to the poor, and you'll have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow me."
But when he heard this he became deeply grieved, for he was extremely rich.
Jesus looked at him, deeply grieved as he was, and said, "How hard it is for people with money to go into the kingdom of God!
It's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who heard it said, "Then who can be saved?"
And he said, "What is impossible for people is possible for God."
And Peter said, "Look, we've left what was ours and followed you."
And he said to them, "I tell you the truth: there's no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive back many times as much in this present time, and in the age to come, eternal life."
He took the twelve aside and said to them, "Look, we're going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be completed.
For he will be handed over to the nations, and mocked and insulted and spat on;
and after they've flogged him they'll kill him, and on the third day he will rise."
And they understood none of it. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn't grasp what was being said.
And as he came near Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road begging.
When he heard a crowd going past, he asked what it might be.
And they told him that Jesus the Nazorean was going by.
And he shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Those going ahead rebuked him and told him to be quiet; but he shouted all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered him to be brought to him. When he came near, he asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" And he said, "Lord, let me see again."
And Jesus said to him, "See again. Your faith has saved you."
And on the spot he saw again, and he kept following him, glorifying God. And all the people, seeing it, gave praise to God.

luke_19.t: He came into Jericho and was making his way through.
And there was a man called by the name Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
And he was trying to see who Jesus was, and he couldn't, because of the crowd — he was short.
So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see him, because he was about to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place he looked up and saw him and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry up and come down — today I must stay at your house."
And he hurried down and welcomed him, rejoicing.
And when they all saw it they grumbled, saying, "He's gone in to stay with a sinful man."
But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord — half of what I own I give to the poor; and if I've extorted anything from anyone, I pay back four times over."
And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, since he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."
While they were listening to this, he went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God was about to appear at once.
So he said, "A man of noble birth travelled off to a distant country to get himself a kingdom and then come back.
He called ten of his slaves and gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Do business with these until I come.'
But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him to say, 'We don't want this man to reign over us.'
And when he came back, having received the kingdom, he sent for the slaves he'd given the money to, so that he might know what business each had done.
The first came forward and said, 'Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.'
And he said to him, 'Well done, good slave! Because you were trustworthy in a very small thing, take authority over ten cities.'
And the second came, saying, 'Your mina, lord, has made five minas.'
And he said to this one too, 'And you — be over five cities.'
And the other came and said, 'Lord, here's your mina. I kept it put away in a cloth.'
For I was afraid of you, because you're a harsh man: you take up what you didn't put down, and you reap what you didn't sow.'
He said to him, 'Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked slave. You knew I'm a harsh man, taking up what I didn't put down and reaping what I didn't sow.
So why didn't you put my money in the bank? Then when I came I'd have collected it with interest.'
And he said to those standing by, 'Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas.'
And they said to him, 'Lord, he's got ten minas!'
'I tell you, to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for these enemies of mine, who didn't want me to reign over them — bring them here and slaughter them in front of me.'"
And when he had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
And when he came near Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
saying, "Go into the village opposite, and as you go in you'll find a colt tied up, which nobody has ever sat on. Untie it and bring it.
And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' say this: 'Its Lord has need of it.'"
So those who were sent went off and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
And they said, "Its Lord has need of it."
And they brought it to Jesus, and they threw their cloaks over the colt and set Jesus on it.
And as he went along, they kept spreading their cloaks on the road.
And as he came near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God at the top of their voices for all the powerful acts they'd seen,
saying, "Blessed is the one who comes, the king, in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
And some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to him, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples."
And he answered, "I tell you, if these keep quiet, the stones will cry out."
And as he came near and saw the city, he wept over it,
saying, "If only you'd known, on this day of yours, the things that make for peace! But now they're hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you and encircle you and press you in on every side,
and they'll level you to the ground, you and your children inside you, and they won't leave one stone on another in you — because you didn't recognise the time of your visitation."
And he went into the temple and began to drive out those who were selling,
saying to them, "It is written: 'And my house shall be a house of prayer' — but you've made it a bandits' cave."
And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the leading men of the people were seeking to destroy him,
and they couldn't find what to do, for all the people hung on his words.

luke_20.t: One of those days, while he was teaching the people in the temple and announcing the good news, the chief priests and the scribes came up on him with the elders
and said to him, "Tell us — by what authority are you doing these things? Or who is it who gave you this authority?"
He answered them, "I'll ask you a question too. Tell me:
was John's baptism from heaven or from people?"
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "If we say 'From heaven,' he'll say, 'Why didn't you believe him, then?'
But if we say 'From people,' all the people will stone us — they're convinced John was a prophet."
And they answered that they didn't know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
And he began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard and leased it out to farmers, and went abroad for a long time.
And when the season came he sent a slave to the farmers, so that they'd give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And he sent yet another slave; and that one too they beat and dishonoured and sent away empty-handed.
And he sent yet a third; and this one too they wounded and threw out.
And the lord of the vineyard said, 'What am I to do? I'll send my beloved son. Perhaps they'll respect him.'
But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned with one another and said, 'This is the heir. Let's kill him, so the inheritance becomes ours.'
And they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. So what will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others." When they heard it they said, "May it never be!"
But he looked straight at them and said, "Then what does this mean, the thing that is written: 'The stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be shattered; and the one it falls on, it will crush to dust."
And the scribes and chief priests tried to lay hands on him then and there, but they were afraid of the people — they knew he'd told this parable against them.
So they watched him and sent in spies who pretended to be righteous, so as to catch him in a word and hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
And they questioned him: "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and show no partiality, but teach the way of God in truth.
Is it permitted for us to pay tribute to Caesar or not?"
But he saw through their trickery and said to them, "Why are you testing me?
"Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" And they said, "Caesar's."
And he said to them, "Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And they couldn't catch him in a word in front of the people, and, amazed at his answer, they fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees came up — those who say there is no resurrection — and questioned him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died childless.
And the second took the wife, and he died childless.
And the third took her, and it was the same with all seven: they left no children and died.
Last of all, the woman died too.
So the woman — in the resurrection, whose wife does she end up being? For the seven had her as wife."
And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage;
but those counted worthy to attain that age, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry nor are given in marriage.
For they can't die any more, since they are like angels, and they are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
And that the dead are raised — even Moses disclosed that, at the bush, where he calls the Lord 'the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.'
He is not God of the dead but of the living; for to him all are alive."
Some of the scribes answered, "Teacher, you've spoken well."
For they no longer dared to ask him anything.
And he said to them, "How is it that they say the Christ is David's son?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."'
So David calls him Lord — then how is he his son?"
While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
"Watch out for the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes and love greetings in the marketplaces and the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honour at dinners,
who eat up widows' houses and pray at length for show. These will receive a heavier judgement."

luke_21.t: He looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
And he saw a needy widow put in two small coins there.
And he said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
For all these put in gifts to God out of what they had spare, but she out of her lack put in all the living she had."
And while some were talking about the temple — how it was adorned with fine stones and votive offerings — he said,
"These things you're looking at — days will come when not one stone will be left on another here that won't be thrown down."
And they questioned him: "Teacher, when will these things be, then? And what will the sign be when these things are about to happen?"
And he said, "Watch that you're not led astray. For many will come in my name, saying 'I am he' and 'The time has drawn near.' Don't go after them.
And when you hear of wars and uprisings, don't be terrified. These things must happen first, but the end won't come at once."
Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There'll be great earthquakes, and in place after place famines and plagues; and there'll be terrors and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, they'll lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, dragging you before kings and governors for the sake of my name.
It'll turn out for you as an opportunity to testify.
So settle it in your hearts not to work out your defence in advance,
for I'll give you a mouth and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to stand up to or contradict.
You'll be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
And you'll be hated by everyone because of my name.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance you will gain your lives.
"But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, and those inside the city must get out, and those in the countryside must not go into it.
For these are days of vengeance, for all that is written to be fulfilled.
Misery for those who are pregnant and those nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the land and wrath against this people,
and they'll fall by the mouth of the sword and be taken captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations, until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
"And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in bewilderment at the roaring of the sea and the surge,
people fainting from fear and from expectation of what is coming on the inhabited world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
But when these things begin to happen, straighten up and lift your heads — your redemption is drawing near."
And he told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
Once they've budded, you see it for yourselves and you know that summer is already near.
So with you: when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all this has happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
"Watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the worries of daily life, and that day will come upon you suddenly
like a trap. For it will come upon all who sit on the face of the whole earth.
But stay awake all the time, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
By day he was teaching in the temple, and at night he'd go out and spend the night on the mount called Olivet.
And all the people would come to him first thing in the morning in the temple to hear him.

luke_22.t: The festival of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was drawing near,
and the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to do away with him — they were afraid of the people.
And Satan entered into Judas, called Iscariot, who was one of the twelve.
And he went off and talked with the chief priests and the temple officers about how he might hand him over to them.
And they were glad, and agreed to give him money.
And he consented, and began looking for a good moment to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
And the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
And he sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover for us, so we may eat it."
And they said to him, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
And he said to them, "Look — as you go into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he goes into,
and say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
And he'll show you a large upstairs room, furnished. Get it ready there."
And they went off and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when the hour came, he took his place at table, and the apostles with him.
And he said to them, "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I won't eat it again until it's fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and said, "Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I won't drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
And he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, [given for you. Do this in remembrance of me."
And the cup likewise, after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.]
"But look — the hand of the one handing me over is with me on the table.
For the Son of Man goes as it has been determined; but misery to that man through whom he is handed over."
And they started arguing among themselves about which of them it might be who was going to do this.
And there was a quarrel among them too, about which of them seemed to be the greatest.
And he said to them, "The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called 'Benefactors'.
But not so with you. Rather, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one at table or the one who serves? Isn't it the one at table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me through my trials.
And I confer on you a kingdom, just as my Father conferred one on me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
"Simon, Simon — look, Satan asked to have you all, to sift you like wheat.
But I've prayed for you, that your faith may not fail. And you, when you've turned back, strengthen your brothers."
And he said to him, "Lord, I'm ready to go with you both to prison and to death."
And he said, "I tell you, Peter, the cock won't crow today until you've three times denied knowing me."
And he said to them, "When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?" And they said, "Nothing."
And he said to them, "But now, whoever has a purse must take it, and a bag likewise; and whoever has none must sell his cloak and buy a sword.
For I tell you, this that is written must be completed in me: 'And he was counted with the lawless.' For what concerns me has its end."
And they said, "Lord, look — here are two swords." And he said to them, "It is enough."
And he went out and made his way, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed him.
And when he came to the place he said to them, "Pray that you don't come into testing."
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and knelt down and prayed,
saying, "Father, if you're willing, take this cup away from me. But let not my will be done, but yours."
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And being in anguish he prayed more intently; and his sweat became like clots of blood falling to the ground.
And he got up from prayer and came to the disciples and found them sleeping from grief,
and he said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you don't come into testing."
While he was still speaking, a crowd came — and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. And he came up to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said to him, "Judas — with a kiss you're handing over the Son of Man?"
When those around him saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?"
And one of them struck the slave of the high priest and took off his right ear.
But Jesus answered, "Let it go this far." And he touched the ear and healed him.
And Jesus said to the chief priests and temple officers and elders who had come out against him, "Have you come out with swords and clubs, as against a bandit?
Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you didn't stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour — and the authority of darkness."
They seized him and led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest. And Peter was following at a distance.
When they had lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them.
And a slave girl saw him sitting in the firelight and stared at him and said, "This man was with him too."
But he denied it, saying, "I don't know him, woman."
And a little later someone else saw him and said, "You're one of them too." But Peter said, "Man, I am not."
And about an hour later, someone else kept insisting, "In truth this man was with him too — he's a Galilean."
But Peter said, "Man, I don't know what you're talking about." And on the spot, while he was still speaking, a cock crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him, "Before a cock crows today, you will deny me three times."
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
And the men who were holding him kept mocking him and beating him.
And they blindfolded him and kept asking him, "Prophesy! Who was it that hit you?"
And they said many other insulting things against him.
And when day came, the council of elders of the people gathered — both chief priests and scribes — and they led him away into their council chamber,
saying, "If you are the Christ, tell us." And he said to them, "If I tell you, you won't believe;
and if I ask you, you won't answer.
But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
And they all said, "Are you then the Son of God?" And he said to them, "You say that I am."
And they said, "Why do we still need testimony? We've heard it ourselves, from his own mouth."

luke_23.t: And the whole assembly of them got up and led him to Pilate.
And they began to accuse him: "We found this man subverting our nation and forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king."
And Pilate questioned him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" And he answered him, "You say so."
And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no ground for a charge in this man."
But they kept insisting: "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout the whole of Judea — he started in Galilee and he's come as far as here."
When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean;
and when he learned that he was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him up to Herod, who was himself in Jerusalem in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus he was very glad — he'd been wanting to see him for a long time, because he'd heard a great deal about him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
And he questioned him at some length, but he gave him no answer.
And the chief priests and the scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him.
And Herod, with his soldiers, treated him with contempt and mocked him; and he put a splendid robe on him and sent him back to Pilate.
And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day — before that they'd been enemies.
And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
said to them, "You brought me this man as one who turns the people away. And look — I've examined him in front of you, and I've found no grounds in this man for the charges you bring against him.
Nor did Herod — for he sent him back to us. And look, he has done nothing deserving death.
So I'll have him flogged and let him go."
[Now he was obliged to release one man to them at the festival.]
But they all cried out together, "Take this man away! Release Barabbas to us!"
He was a man who'd been thrown into prison for an uprising that had happened in the city, and for murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus.
But they kept shouting back, "Crucify him! Crucify him!"
And a third time he said to them, "Why? What evil has this man done? I've found no ground for death in him. So I'll have him flogged and let him go."
But they pressed him with loud shouts, demanding that he be crucified; and their shouts prevailed.
And Pilate ruled that their demand should be granted.
He released the man who'd been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, the one they asked for; but Jesus he handed over to their will.
And as they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the country, and put the cross on him, to carry it behind Jesus.
And a great crowd of the people followed him, and women who were beating their breasts and lamenting for him.
But Jesus turned to them and said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, don't weep for me; weep for yourselves instead, and for your children.
For look, days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.'
Then they'll begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us.'
For if they do these things when the wood is green, what's going to happen when it's dry?"
And two others, criminals, were being led away with him to be executed.
And when they came to the place called The Skull, that's where they crucified him, and the criminals — one on the right and one on the left.
And Jesus was saying, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And they cast lots, dividing up his clothes.
And the people stood watching. But the rulers kept sneering, saying, "He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, the chosen one."
And the soldiers mocked him too, coming up and offering him sour wine,
and saying, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself."
And there was also an inscription over him, written in Greek and Latin and Hebrew letters: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And one of the criminals hanging there kept blaspheming him: "Aren't you the Christ? Save yourself — and us!"
But the other rebuked him and said, "Don't you even fear God, since you're under the same sentence?
And we're here justly — we're getting back what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing out of place."
And he said, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
And Jesus said to him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."
And it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
as the sun failed. And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, "Father, into your hands I entrust my spirit." And having said this, he breathed his last.
And when the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God and said, "Truly this man was righteous."
And all the crowds who'd gathered for this spectacle, when they saw what had happened, went home beating their breasts.
And all those who knew him stood at a distance, and so did the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching all this.
And there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council — a good and righteous man —
he hadn't agreed with their decision and action — from Arimathea, a city of the Jews — and he was waiting for the kingdom of God.
This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb cut in rock, where no one had yet been laid.
And it was the day of Preparation, and the sabbath was beginning to dawn.
And the women who had come with him from Galilee followed after, and they saw the tomb, and how his body was laid.
And they went back and got spices and perfumed oils ready. And on the sabbath they rested, according to the commandment.

luke_24.t: But on the first day of the week, at deep dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they'd prepared; and some others were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
And when they went in they didn't find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And while they were at a loss about this — look, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.
And as they became terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, the men said to them, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead?
He isn't here — he has been raised. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,
saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and on the third day rise."
And they remembered his words.
And they went back from the tomb and reported all this to the eleven and to all the rest.
It was Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James, and the rest of the women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles,
and these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they didn't believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb, and stooping down he sees only the linen wrappings; and he went away home, wondering at what had happened.
And look — two of them were going, that same day, to a village sixty stadia from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus.
and they were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
And while they were talking and debating, Jesus himself came near and went along with them —
but their eyes were held from recognising him.
And he said to them, "What are these words you're exchanging with each other as you walk?" And they stopped, looking gloomy.
And one of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who doesn't know the things that have happened there in these days?"
And he said to them, "What things?" And they said to him, "The things about Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to a sentence of death and crucified him.
But we were hoping he was the one about to redeem Israel. And besides all this, it's now the third day since these things happened.
But some women of our group have astonished us too: they were at the tomb early,
and when they didn't find his body they came back saying they'd even seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive.
And some of those with us went off to the tomb and found it just as the women had said; but him they didn't see."
And he said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Wasn't it necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and enter into his glory?"
And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
And they came near the village where they were going, and he made as if to go further on.
And they pressed him hard: "Stay with us — it's toward evening and the day has already declined." And he went in to stay with them.
And when he had taken his place at table with them, he took the bread and blessed it, and having broken it he was giving it to them.
And their eyes were opened, and they recognised him — and he became invisible to them.
And they said to each other, "Weren't our hearts burning within us as he spoke to us on the road, as he opened the scriptures to us?"
And they got up that very hour and went back to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and those with them gathered together,
who were saying, "The Lord has really been raised, and he has appeared to Simon!"
And they were describing what had happened on the road, and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
And while they were saying these things, he himself stood in their midst, and says to them, "Peace to you."
But they were terrified and frightened, and thought they were seeing a spirit.
And he said to them, "Why are you troubled? And why do doubts rise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet — that it's I myself. Handle me and see: a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones, as you see I have."
And having said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still couldn't believe it, for joy, and were wondering, he said to them, "Have you got anything here to eat?"
And they gave him a piece of grilled fish [and some honeycomb];
and he took it and ate it in front of them.
And he said to them, "These are my words which I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled."
Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
and said to them, "Thus it is written: that the Christ is to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and that a change of mind, for the release of sins, is to be proclaimed in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are witnesses of these things.
And look — I'm sending out the promise of my Father upon you. But you, stay in the city until you're clothed with power from on high."
And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them.
And while he was blessing them, he was parted from them and carried up into heaven.
And they worshipped him and went back to Jerusalem with great joy,
and they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. [Amen]

matthew_1.t: The book of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham had Isaac, Isaac had Jacob, Jacob had Judah and his brothers,
Judah had Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez had Hezron, Hezron had Ram,
Ram had Amminadab, Amminadab had Nahshon, Nahshon had Salmon,
Salmon had Boaz by Rahab, Boaz had Obed by Ruth, Obed had Jesse,
Jesse had David the king, and David had Solomon by Uriah's wife,
Solomon had Rehoboam, Rehoboam had Abijah, Abijah had Asaph,
Asaph had Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat had Joram, Joram had Uzziah,
Uzziah had Jotham, Jotham had Ahaz, Ahaz had Hezekiah,
Hezekiah had Manasseh, Manasseh had Amos, Amos had Josiah,
and Josiah had Jechoniah and his brothers, at the deportation to Babylon.
After the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah had Shealtiel, Shealtiel had Zerubbabel,
Zerubbabel had Abiud, Abiud had Eliakim, Eliakim had Azor,
Azor had Zadok, Zadok had Achim, Achim had Eliud,
Eliud had Eleazar, Eleazar had Matthan, Matthan had Jacob,
and Jacob had Joseph, the husband of Mary — and it was from her that Jesus was born, the one called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
Here is how the origin of Jesus Christ came about. His mother Mary was pledged in marriage to Joseph, and before they came together she was found to be pregnant — from the Holy Spirit.
Joseph her husband was a man who did what was right, and he didn't want to make a public example of her, so he decided to divorce her quietly.

But while he was turning this over, look — a messenger of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, don't be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because what's been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She'll give birth to a son, and you're to name him Jesus, because he'll save his people from their sins."
All this happened so that what the Lord said through the prophet would be fulfilled:
"Look, the virgin will be pregnant and will give birth to a son, and they will call his name Immanuel" — which translated is "God with us".
Joseph woke from sleep and did what the messenger of the Lord had told him: he took his wife,
and he did not have relations with her until she gave birth to a son; and he named him Jesus.

matthew_2.t: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod — look, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
saying, "Where's the one born king of the Jews? We saw his star at its rising, and we've come to bow down to him."
When King Herod heard it he was shaken, and all Jerusalem with him,
and he gathered all the chief priests and the people's teachers of the law, and kept asking them where the Christ was to be born.
They told him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, because this is how it stands written through the prophet:
'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"
Then Herod called the magi in secretly and got out of them exactly when the star had appeared,
and he sent them off to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child; and when you find him, report back to me, so I can come and bow down to him too."
They listened to the king and went. And look — the star they'd seen at its rising went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star they were overjoyed — enormously.
They went into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and bowed to him. Then they opened their treasure-boxes and offered him gifts — gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And after they were warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they withdrew to their own country by another road.

When they had withdrawn — look, a messenger of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream and says, "Get up, take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; because Herod's about to look for the child, to destroy him."
So he got up, took the child and his mother in the night, and withdrew to Egypt,
and stayed there until Herod died — so that what the Lord said through the prophet would be fulfilled: "Out of Egypt I called my son."

Then Herod, seeing he'd been outwitted by the magi, was enraged, and he sent and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and all its districts, from two years old and under, going by the time he'd got from the magi.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
"A voice was heard in Ramah, wailing and loud lamentation — Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more."
When Herod had died — look, a messenger of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
and says, "Get up, take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel; because the ones who were after the child's life have died."
So he got up, took the child and his mother, and went into the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and after being warned in a dream he withdrew to the region of Galilee,
and he came and settled in a town called Nazareth — so that what was spoken through the prophets would be fulfilled: that he will be called a Nazorean.

matthew_3.t: In those days John the Baptist arrives, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea
and saying, "Change your minds, because the kingdom of heaven has come near."
This is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, who said: "A voice of one crying in the wilderness — 'Prepare the road of the Lord, make his paths straight.'"
John's own clothing was made of camel hair, and he wore a leather belt around his waist; his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan kept going out to him,
and they were baptised by him in the river Jordan, openly confessing their sins.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "You offspring of vipers! Who warned you to run from the anger that's coming?
So produce fruit worthy of the change of mind.
And don't presume to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' Because I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham out of these stones.
The axe is already laid at the root of the trees; so every tree that isn't producing good fruit gets cut down and thrown into fire.
"I baptise you in water, into a change of mind; but the one coming after me is stronger than I am, and I'm not fit to carry his sandals. He'll baptise you in the Holy Spirit — and fire.
His winnowing-fork is in his hand, and he'll clear his threshing-floor right through and gather his wheat into the barn — but the chaff he'll burn up with fire that can't be put out."
Then Jesus arrives from Galilee at the Jordan, to John, to be baptised by him.
But John kept trying to stop him: "I'm the one who needs to be baptised by you, and you come to me?"
Jesus answered him, "Let it be for now; this is how it's fitting for us to fulfil all rightness." Then he lets him.
And when Jesus had been baptised he came up from the water at once. And look — the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and coming on him.
And look — a voice out of the heavens, saying, "This is my son, the beloved; in him I was well pleased."

matthew_4.t: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tested by the slanderer.
And after forty days and forty nights of fasting, he was hungry.
And the tester came and said to him, "If you're the son of God, tell these stones to become loaves."
But he answered, "It stands written: 'A person will not live on bread alone, but on every word coming out through the mouth of God.'"
Then the slanderer takes him into the holy city and stood him on the parapet of the temple

and says to him, "If you're the son of God, throw yourself down; because it stands written: 'He will give his messengers orders about you, and they will lift you on their hands, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus said to him, "Again, it stands written: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
Again the slanderer takes him to a very high mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and said to him, "All these I'll give you, if you fall down and bow to me."
Then Jesus says to him, "Get away behind me, Satan! Because it stands written: 'You shall bow to the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.'"
Then the slanderer leaves him; and look — messengers came and were serving him.
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.
And he left Nazara and came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the districts of Zebulun and Naphtali —
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the road of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations —
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light; and on those sitting in the country and shadow of death, a light rose on them."
From then on Jesus began to proclaim and to say, "Change your minds, because the kingdom of heaven has come near."
Walking beside the sea of Galilee he saw two brothers — Simon, the one called Peter, and Andrew his brother — casting a net into the sea; they were fishermen.
And he says to them, "Come after me, and I'll make you fishers of people."
And they left the nets at once and followed him.
And going on from there he saw two other brothers — James the son of Zebedee and John his brother — in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And they left the boat and their father at once and followed him.
And he went round the whole of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every weakness among the people.

And the report of him went out into all of Syria; and they brought him everyone who was ill — gripped by all kinds of diseases and torments, demon-possessed and moonstruck and paralysed — and he healed them.
And large crowds followed him from Galilee and the Ten Towns and Jerusalem and Judea and beyond the Jordan.

matthew_5.t: Seeing the crowds he went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down his learners came to him.
And he opened his mouth and began to teach them, saying:
How fortunate are the poor in spirit — because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
How fortunate are those who mourn — because they will be comforted.
How fortunate are the gentle — because they will inherit the earth.
How fortunate are those hungering and thirsting for rightness — because they will be filled.
How fortunate are the merciful — because they will be shown mercy.
How fortunate are the pure in heart — because they will see God.
How fortunate are the peacemakers — because they will be called sons of God.
How fortunate are those who have been persecuted for the sake of rightness — because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
You're fortunate when they insult you and persecute you and say every kind of evil thing against you, lying, because of me.
Rejoice and be glad, because your reward is great in the heavens; that's how they persecuted the prophets before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt is made foolish, what will it be salted with? It's no good for anything any more except to be thrown outside and trampled by people.
You are the light of the world. A city can't be hidden when it sits on a hill;
and people don't light a lamp and put it under the basket; they put it on the lampstand, and it shines for everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine in front of people, so they can see your good works and give glory to your Father in the heavens.
Don't think I came to tear down the law or the prophets. I didn't come to tear down but to fill full.
I tell you the truth: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota, not one stroke, will pass from the law until everything has happened.

So whoever breaks one of the least of these commands and teaches people to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Because I tell you that unless your rightness goes beyond that of the teachers of the law and the Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You've heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not murder"; and whoever murders will be liable to judgement.

But I tell you that everyone who's angry with his brother or sister [without cause] will be liable to judgement; and whoever says to his brother or sister, "Empty-head!" will be liable to the council; and whoever says, "Idiot!" will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
So if you're bringing your gift to the altar and there you remember that your brother or sister has something against you,
leave your gift there in front of the altar and go — first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and bring your gift.

Come to terms with the one bringing a case against you, quickly, while you're with him on the road — or the accuser may hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you'll be thrown into prison.
I tell you the truth: you will certainly not come out of there until you've paid back the last penny.
You've heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not commit adultery."
But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to want her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
And if your right eye trips you up, tear it out and throw it away from you; it's better for you that one of your parts be destroyed than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand trips you up, cut it off and throw it away from you; it's better for you that one of your parts be destroyed than that your whole body go off into Gehenna.
And it was said: "Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of separation."
But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife — apart from a matter of sexual immorality — makes her commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again, you've heard that it was said to the ancients: "You shall not break an oath, but you shall pay to the Lord what you have sworn."
But I tell you: don't swear at all — not by heaven, because it's God's throne,
nor by the earth, because it's the footstool of his feet; nor towards Jerusalem, because it's the city of the great king;
and don't swear by your head, because you can't make one hair white or black.
Let your word be "Yes, yes" — "No, no"; anything beyond these is from the evil one.
You've heard that it was said: "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth."
But I tell you: don't stand against the one who is evil. Instead, whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn the other to him as well;
and to the one wanting to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
and whoever presses you into service for one mile, go with him two.
Give to the one who asks you, and don't turn away from the one wanting to borrow from you.
You've heard that it was said: "You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy."
But I tell you: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who abuse you and persecute you —
so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens; because he raises his sun on the evil and the good, and rains on the right and the wrong.
Because if you love those who love you, what wage do you have? Don't the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers and sisters, what more are you doing? Don't the gentiles do the same?
So you are to be complete, as your heavenly Father is complete.

matthew_6.t: Take care not to do your rightness in front of people, to be seen by them; otherwise you have no wage with your Father in the heavens.

So when you give to the poor, don't sound a trumpet in front of you, the way the play-actors do in the synagogues and in the streets so that people will praise them. I tell you the truth: they've got their wage in full.
But when you give to the poor, don't let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will pay you back.

And when you pray, you're not to be like the play-actors; because they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so people can see them. I tell you the truth: they've got their wage in full.
But you, when you pray, go into your storeroom and shut your door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will pay you back.
And when you pray, don't babble on like the gentiles, because they think they'll be heard for their many words.
So don't be like them; because God your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
So this is how you are to pray: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name;
let your kingdom come; let your will happen, as in heaven, so also on earth;
Give us today our daily bread;
and let go of our debts for us, as we ourselves have let go of our debtors;
and do not bring us into testing, but rescue us from evil. [Because yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory, into the ages. Amen.]
Because if you let go of people's missteps for them, your heavenly Father will also let go of yours;
but if you don't let go of people's missteps for them, neither will your Father let go of your missteps.
And when you fast, don't become gloomy-faced like the play-actors; because they disfigure their faces so that people will see them fasting. I tell you the truth: they've got their wage in full.
But you, when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
so that you don't appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will pay you back.
Don't store up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and eating destroy and where thieves dig through and steal;
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor eating destroys and where thieves don't dig through or steal.
Because where your treasure is, that's where your heart will be too.
The lamp of the body is the eye. So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light;
but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. So if the light in you is darkness — how great that darkness is.
Nobody can serve two masters as a slave; either he'll hate the one and love the other, or he'll hold to one and think nothing of the other. You can't serve God and mammon as slaves.
That's why I tell you: don't be anxious about your life — what you'll eat or what you'll drink — or about your body, what you'll wear. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they don't sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren't you worth more than they are?
And which of you by being anxious can add one forearm's length to his span?
And why are you anxious about clothing? Learn from the lilies of the field, how they grow: they don't labour or spin;
but I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
And if that's how God clothes the grass of the field — here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow — won't he much more clothe you, you of little trust?
So don't be anxious, saying, "What will we eat?" or "What will we drink?" or "What will we wear?"
Because the gentiles chase after all these things; and your heavenly Father knows you need all of them.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his rightness, and all these things will be added for you.
So don't be anxious about tomorrow, because tomorrow will be anxious about itself. Enough for the day is its own trouble.

matthew_7.t: Do not judge, so that you are not judged;
because with the judgement you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you measure out, it will be measured to you.
And why do you look at the splinter in your brother's eye, but don't notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, "Let me get the splinter out of your eye" — and look, the beam is in your own eye?
Play-actor! First get the beam out of your own eye, and then you'll see clearly enough to get the splinter out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to the dogs, and do not throw your pearls in front of the pigs — or they will trample them with their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
Because everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Or which of you is the sort of person who, when his son asks him for bread, will hand him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he hand him a snake?
So if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him!
So everything you want people to do for you, do the same for them; because this is the law and the prophets.
Go in through the narrow gate; because wide is the gate and broad is the road leading away into destruction, and many are the ones going in through it.
How narrow is the gate and how pressed the road leading away into life — and few are the ones finding it.
Watch out for the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inside are ravenous wolves.
You'll recognise them by their fruits. People don't gather grapes from thorn bushes, or figs from thistles, do they?
In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, but the rotten tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree can't produce bad fruit, and a rotten tree can't produce good fruit.
Every tree that isn't producing good fruit gets cut down and thrown into fire.
So then, you'll recognise them by their fruits.
Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," will go into the kingdom of heaven, but the one doing the will of my Father in the heavens.
Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord — didn't we prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many acts of power in your name?"
And then I'll declare to them: "I never knew you. Go away from me, you who work lawlessness."
So everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a sensible man who built his house on the rock.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and fell against that house, and it didn't fall — because it had been founded on the rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn't do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and struck against that house, and it fell — and its fall was great.
And when Jesus had finished these words, the crowds were astounded at his teaching;
because he was teaching them like someone who has authority — and not like their teachers of the law.

matthew_8.t: When he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
And look — a man with a skin disease came and bowed to him, and said, "Sir, if you're willing, you can make me clean."
And he stretched out his hand and touched him, and said, "I am willing — be clean." And at once his skin disease was cleansed.
And Jesus says to him, "See that you tell nobody; but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded — as a testimony to them."
When he had entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, appealing to him
and saying, "Sir, my boy is laid up at home, paralysed, in terrible torment."
And he says to him, "Am I to come and heal him?"
And the centurion answered, "Sir, I'm not fit for you to come in under my roof; but just say the word, and my boy will be healed.
Because I'm a man under authority myself, with soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes; and to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does it."
Hearing this Jesus was amazed, and said to those following, "I tell you the truth: I haven't found trust like this from anyone in Israel.
And I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness; there there will be weeping and grinding of teeth."
And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go; let it happen for you as you trusted." And the boy was healed in that hour.
And Jesus came into Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law laid up with a fever;
and he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she got up and began to serve him.
When evening came they brought him many who were possessed by demons; and he drove out the spirits with a word, and healed everyone who was ill —
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled: "He himself took our weaknesses and carried our diseases."
Seeing a crowd around him, Jesus gave orders to go off to the other side.
And one scribe came and said to him, "Teacher, I'll follow you wherever you go."
And Jesus says to him, "The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
And another of the disciples said to him, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."
But Jesus says to him, "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
And when he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And look — a great shaking happened in the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but he was sleeping.
And the disciples came and woke him, saying, "Lord, save us — we're perishing!"
And he says to them, "Why are you cowards, you of little trust?" Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
And the people were amazed, saying, "What sort of being is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
And when he came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tombs — so violent that nobody was strong enough to pass by along that road.
And look — they screamed, "What have we to do with you, son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?"
Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding, some distance from them.
And the demons appealed to him, saying, "If you drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs."
And he said to them, "Go." And they came out and went off into the pigs; and look — the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the waters.
And the herdsmen ran, and went off into the city and reported everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
And look — the whole city came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him they appealed to him to move on from their district.

matthew_9.t: And he got into a boat and crossed over and came to his own town.
And look — they were bringing him a paralysed man laid on a bed. And seeing their trust, Jesus said to the paralysed man, "Take heart, child; your sins are released."
And look — some of the scribes said among themselves, "This man is speaking blasphemy."
And seeing their thoughts, Jesus said, "Why are you thinking evil things in your hearts?
Because which is easier — to say, 'Your sins are released,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to release sins" — then he says to the paralysed man, "Get up, pick up your bed and go to your house."
And he got up and went off to his house.
Seeing it, the crowds were afraid, and they gave glory to God, who had given such authority to people.
And as Jesus was passing on from there he saw a man sitting at the tax booth, called Matthew, and he says to him, "Follow me." And he stood up and followed him.
And it happened, as he was reclining at table in the house — look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.
And seeing it, the Pharisees said to his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
But hearing it he said to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a doctor — but those who are ill do.
But go and learn what this means: 'I want mercy and not sacrifice.' Because I didn't come to call the right but sinners — to a change of mind."
Then John's disciples come to him and say, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast a great deal, but your disciples don't fast?"
And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn while the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they'll fast.
Nobody puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; because the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear happens.

And they don't put new wine into old skins; otherwise the skins burst, and the wine is spilled and the skins are destroyed. Instead they put new wine into fresh skins, and both are preserved together.
While he was saying these things to them — look, a ruler came and bowed to him and said, "My daughter has just died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
And Jesus got up and followed him — and so did his disciples.
And look — a woman who'd been bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the tassel of his cloak;
because she was saying to herself, "If I only touch his cloak, I'll be saved."
But Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, "Take heart, daughter; your trust has saved you." And the woman was saved from that hour.
And Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the flute-players and the crowd making a commotion,
and he said, "Get out — because the girl didn't die, she's sleeping." And they laughed at him.
But when the crowd had been put out, he went in and took hold of her hand, and the girl was raised.
And this report went out into that whole region.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting, "Have mercy on us, son of David!"
And when he came into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus says to them, "Do you trust that I can do this?" They say to him, "Yes, Lord."
Then he touched their eyes, saying, "According to your trust let it happen to you."
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus warned them sternly, "See that nobody knows."
But they went out and spread the news about him through that whole region.
As they were going out — look, they brought him a man who couldn't speak, possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had been driven out, the man who hadn't been able to speak spoke. And the crowds were amazed, saying, "Nothing like this has ever appeared in Israel."
But the Pharisees were saying, "He drives out the demons by the ruler of the demons."
And Jesus went round all the towns and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every weakness.
Seeing the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and thrown down like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then he says to his disciples, "The harvest is large, but the workers are few;
so beg the Lord of the harvest to throw out workers into his harvest."

matthew_10.t: He called his twelve disciples to him and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon (the one called Peter) and Andrew his brother; James son of Zebedee and John his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus who was surnamed Thaddaeus;
Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot — the one who also handed him over.
These twelve Jesus sent out, with these instructions: "Don't go off on a road of the nations, and don't enter a town of Samaritans.
Go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
As you go, proclaim: "The kingdom of heaven has come near."
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin disease, drive out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
Don't acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,
no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, no staff — because the worker deserves his food.
Whatever town or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
As you enter the house, greet it.
If the house is worthy, let your peace come on it; if it isn't worthy, let your peace return to you.
And if anyone won't welcome you or listen to your words, as you leave that house or town, shake the dust off your feet.
I tell you the truth: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that town.
Look — I'm sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be shrewd as snakes and unmixed as doves.
Be on guard against people: they'll hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues,
and you'll be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the nations.
When they hand you over, don't worry about how or what you're to say; it'll be given to you in that hour what to say.
Because it isn't you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against parents and put them to death.
You'll be hated by everyone because of my name; but the one who endures to the end — this one will be saved.
When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. I tell you the truth: you won't have gone through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple isn't above the teacher, and a slave isn't above his master.
It's enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they called the head of the house Beelzeboul, how much more the members of his household!
So don't be afraid of them. Nothing is covered that won't be uncovered, and nothing hidden that won't be known.
What I tell you in the dark, say in the light; and what you hear in your ear, proclaim from the rooftops.
Don't fear those who kill the body but can't kill the soul. Fear instead the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Aren't two sparrows sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
As for you — even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
So don't be afraid; you're worth more than many sparrows.
So everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge before my Father in the heavens;
but whoever disowns me before people, I too will disown before my Father in the heavens.
Don't think I came to bring peace on the earth. I didn't come to bring peace, but a sword.
For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a bride against her mother-in-law;
and a person's enemies will be the members of his own household.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me isn't worthy of me; and whoever loves son or daughter more than me isn't worthy of me;
and whoever doesn't take up his cross and follow behind me isn't worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Whoever welcomes a prophet because he's a prophet will receive a prophet's wage, and whoever welcomes an upright person because he's upright will receive an upright person's wage.
And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he's a disciple — I tell you the truth, he will certainly not lose his wage."

matthew_11.t: And when Jesus had finished instructing his twelve disciples, he moved on from there to teach and proclaim in their towns.
When John heard in prison what the Christ was doing, he sent word through his disciples
and asked him, "Are you the one who's coming, or should we expect someone else?"
Jesus answered them, "Go and report to John what you hear and see:
the blind see again, the lame walk, those with skin disease are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news announced to them.
And blessed is anyone who isn't tripped up by me.
As they were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? Look — those who wear soft clothes are in kings' houses.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it's written: "Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you."
I tell you the truth: among those born of women no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen; and yet the lesser one in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.
From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent people are taking it by force.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
And if you're willing to accept it, he is Elijah, the one who is to come.
Whoever has ears, let them hear.
What shall I compare this generation to? It's like children sitting in the marketplaces who call out to the others,
"We played the flute for you and you didn't dance; we sang a lament and you didn't beat your breasts."
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, "He has a demon."
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, "Look — a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners." And wisdom was vindicated by her works.
Then he began to reproach the towns where most of his acts of power had happened, because they didn't change their minds:
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the acts of power that happened in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they'd have changed their minds long ago, in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell you: it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgement than for you.
And you, Capernaum — will you be lifted up to heaven? You'll go down to Hades. Because if the acts of power that happened in you had happened in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
But I tell you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgement than for you."
At that time Jesus responded, "I acknowledge you publicly, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from the wise and the clever and revealed them to infants.
Yes, Father, because this is how it pleased you.
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father; and nobody fully knows the Son except the Father, and nobody fully knows the Father except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.
Come to me, all of you who are labouring and loaded down, and I'll give you rest.
Take my yoke on you and learn from me, because I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is kind and my load is light."

matthew_12.t: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat them.
When the Pharisees saw it they said to him, "Look — your disciples are doing what isn't permitted on a sabbath."
He said to them, "Haven't you read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
How he entered the house of God and they ate the bread of the Presence, which wasn't permitted for him to eat, or for those with him, but only for the priests?
Or haven't you read in the law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are not guilty?
But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
If you'd known what this means — "I want mercy and not sacrifice" — you wouldn't have condemned the guiltless.
For the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath."
He moved on from there and went into their synagogue.
And there was a man there with a withered hand. They questioned him: "Is it permitted to heal on the sabbaths?" — so that they could bring a charge against him.
He said to them, "Which one of you who has a single sheep, if it falls into a pit on the sabbath, won't take hold of it and lift it out?
How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the sabbaths."
Then he says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy as the other.
The Pharisees went out and took counsel against him — how they might destroy him.
Knowing this, Jesus withdrew from there. Large crowds followed him, and he healed them all,
and he warned them sharply not to make him known,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled:
"Look — my servant, whom I chose; my beloved, in whom my soul was well pleased. I will put my Spirit on him, and he will announce judgement to the nations.
He will not quarrel or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
A bruised reed he will not break, and a smouldering wick he will not put out, until he brings judgement through to victory.
And in his name the nations will hope."
Then a man possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the mute man could both speak and see.
All the crowds were beside themselves and said, "This isn't the Son of David, is it?"
But when the Pharisees heard it they said, "This man doesn't drive out the demons except by Beelzeboul, the ruler of the demons."
Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand.
And if the Adversary drives out the Adversary, he's divided against himself; so how will his kingdom stand?
And if I drive out the demons by Beelzeboul, who do your sons drive them out by? That's why they'll be your judges.
But if I drive out the demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has arrived upon you.
