Or how can anyone get into the strong man's house and seize his goods unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he'll plunder his house.
Whoever isn't with me is against me, and whoever doesn't gather with me scatters.
So I tell you: every sin and slander will be released for people, but the slander of the Spirit will not be released.

And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be released for him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be released for him — not in this present age, nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; because the tree is known by its fruit.
You offspring of vipers! How can you speak good things when you're evil? Because the mouth speaks out of the overflow of the heart.
The good person brings good things out of the good treasure of the heart, and the evil person brings evil things out of the evil treasure.
And I tell you that people will give an account on the day of judgement for every idle word they speak.
Because by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned."
Then some of the teachers of the law and Pharisees answered him, "Teacher, we want to see a sign from you."
He answered them, "An evil and adulterous generation hunts for a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Ninevite men will rise at the judgement with this generation and condemn it, because they changed their minds at Jonah's proclamation — and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

A queen of the south will be raised at the judgement with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom — and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it passes through waterless places looking for rest and doesn't find it.
Then it says, "I'll go back to my house, the one I left." And when it comes it finds it standing idle, swept and put in order.

Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and settle there; and that person's last state becomes worse than the first. So it'll be for this evil generation too.
While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, wanting to speak with him.
Someone said to him, "Look — your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you."
He answered the one who told him, "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?"
And stretching out his hand towards his disciples he said, "Look — my mother and my brothers.
Because whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens — this one is my brother and sister and mother."

matthew_13.t: That day Jesus went out of the house and sat down beside the sea.
Large crowds gathered to him, so he got into a boat and sat there, and the whole crowd stood on the shore.
And he spoke to them at length in parables: "Look — the sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
Other seed fell on rocky ground where it didn't have much soil, and it sprang up at once because the soil wasn't deep.
But when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.
Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it.
And other seed fell on the good soil and produced fruit — one a hundred, another sixty, another thirty.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
The disciples came and said to him, "Why do you speak to them in parables?"
He answered them, "Because it's been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it hasn't been given.
Because whoever has, more will be given to him and he'll have plenty; but whoever doesn't have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
This is why I speak to them in parables: because seeing they don't see, and hearing they don't hear and don't understand.
And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: "You will hear and hear, and never understand; and you will look and look, and never see.

For this people's heart has grown fat; they've heard heavily with their ears, and they've shut their eyes — so that they might not see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them."
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
I tell you the truth: many prophets and upright people longed to see what you see and didn't see it, and to hear what you hear and didn't hear it.
So listen to the parable of the sower:
When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and doesn't understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown along the path.
The one sown on rocky ground is the person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
but he has no root in himself and lasts only a season; when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he's immediately tripped up.
The one sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word, but the worry of this age and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
But the one sown on the good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it, who then bears fruit and produces — one a hundred, another sixty, another thirty."
He put another parable before them: "The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat, and went away.
When the blade sprouted and produced fruit, then the darnel appeared as well.
The householder's slaves came and said to him, "Master, didn't you sow good seed in your field? Where did the darnel come from, then?"
He said to them, "An enemy — a person — did this." The slaves say to him, "Do you want us to go and gather them?"
He says, "No — if you gather the darnel you might pull up the wheat along with it.
Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I'll tell the reapers: gather the darnel first and tie it in bundles to burn it, but bring the wheat into my barn."
He put another parable before them: "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed which a man took and sowed in his field.
It's the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it's the largest of the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches."
He told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole batch was leavened."
Jesus said all these things to the crowds in parables, and he said nothing to them without a parable,
so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: "I will open my mouth in parables; I will pour out things hidden from the foundation of the world."
Then he left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, "Explain to us the parable of the darnel in the field."
He answered them, "The one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; the darnel are the children of the evil one;
the enemy who sowed them is the accuser; the harvest is the completion of the age; and the reapers are angels.
So just as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the completion of this age.
The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they'll gather out of his kingdom everything that trips people up, and those who do lawlessness,
and will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping there, and grinding of teeth.
Then the upright will shine out like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and in his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
When he found one very valuable pearl, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet thrown into the sea, gathering from every kind;
when it was full they hauled it up on the shore, and they sat down and collected the good into containers, but the rotten they threw outside.
So it will be at the completion of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from among the upright,
and will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping there, and grinding of teeth."
Jesus says to them, "Have you understood all these things?" They say to him, "Yes."
He said to them, "So every teacher of the law who's been trained as a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old."
And when Jesus had finished these parables, he moved on from there,
and coming to his home town he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astounded and said, "Where did this man get this wisdom and these acts of power?
Isn't this the carpenter's son? Isn't his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And aren't his sisters all here with us? So where did this man get all this?"
And they were tripped up by him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honour except in his home town and in his own household."
And he didn't do many acts of power there, because of their lack of trust.

matthew_14.t: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus
and said to his attendants, "This is John the Baptist. He's been raised from the dead, and that's why these powers are at work in him."
For Herod had seized John, tied him up and put him away in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
Because John kept telling him, "It isn't permitted for you to have her."
And though he wanted to kill him, he was afraid of the crowd, because they held him to be a prophet.
But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in front of them and pleased Herod,
so he promised on oath to give her whatever she asked.
Prompted by her mother, she says, "Give me the head of John the Baptist here, on a platter."
The king was grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining at table with him, he ordered it to be given,
and he sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
His head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
His disciples came and took the corpse and buried him; then they went and reported it to Jesus.
When Jesus heard it he withdrew from there by boat to a deserted place by himself. But when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.
When he came out he saw a large crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them and healed their sick.
When evening came the disciples came to him and said, "The place is deserted and the hour's already passed. Send the crowds away so they can go into the villages and buy food for themselves."
But Jesus said to them, "They don't need to go away. You give them something to eat."
They say to him, "We've got nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
He said, "Bring them here to me."

He ordered the crowds to recline on the grass, and taking the five loaves and the two fish he looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing, and broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces — twelve baskets full.
Those eating were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
At once he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he released the crowds.
After releasing the crowds he went up the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came he was there alone,
but the boat was already many stadia away from the land, battered by the waves, because the wind was against them.
In the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea they were terrified and said, "It's a phantom!" — and they cried out in fear.
But at once Jesus spoke to them: "Take courage — I am. Do not be afraid."
Peter answered him, "Lord, if it is you, order me to come to you on the waters."
He said, "Come." And Peter got down from the boat and walked on the waters and came towards Jesus.
But seeing the strong wind he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, "Lord, save me!"
At once Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and says to him, "You of little trust — why did you doubt?"
And when they got into the boat the wind dropped.
Those in the boat bowed down before him and said, "Truly you are God's Son."
And crossing over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
When the men of that place recognised him, they sent word into all the surrounding region and brought him everyone who was ill,
and they begged him to let them just touch the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were brought safely through.

matthew_15.t: Then Pharisees and teachers of the law from Jerusalem come to Jesus and say,
"Why do your disciples step over the tradition of the elders? Because they don't wash their hands when they eat bread."
He answered them, "And why do you step over the command of God because of your tradition?
Because God said: "Honour your father and your mother", and "Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must certainly die."
But you say: whoever tells his father or mother, "Whatever help you might have had from me is a gift to God" —
then he needn't honour his father or his mother. And so you've made the word of God void because of your tradition.
Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you when he said:
"This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me;
and they revere me in vain, teaching as teachings the commands of people."
He called the crowd to him and said to them, "Listen and understand.
It isn't what goes into the mouth that makes a person common; it's what comes out of the mouth that makes a person common."
Then the disciples came and say to him, "Do you know that the Pharisees were tripped up when they heard that saying?"
He answered, "Every plant that my heavenly Father didn't plant will be pulled up by the roots.
Leave them. They're blind guides of the blind. And if a blind person guides a blind person, both will fall into a pit."
Peter answered him, "Explain this parable to us."
He said, "Are you still without understanding too?
Don't you grasp that everything going into the mouth passes into the belly and is thrown out into the latrine?
But what comes out of the mouth comes out of the heart, and those things make a person common.
Because out of the heart come evil thoughts — murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false testimonies, slanders.
These are the things that make a person common; but eating with unwashed hands doesn't make a person common."
Jesus left there and withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that territory came out and kept crying to him, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is badly possessed by a demon."
But he didn't answer her a word. And his disciples came and asked him, "Send her away, because she keeps crying out behind us."
He answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
But she came and bowed down before him, saying, "Lord, help me."
He answered, "It isn't right to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
She said, "Yes, Lord — and yet the little dogs do eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, your trust is great. Let it happen for you as you want." And her daughter was healed from that hour.
Jesus moved on from there and went along the Sea of Galilee, and he went up the mountain and sat there.
Large crowds came to him bringing with them the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and they put them down at his feet; and he healed them,
so that the crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples to him and said, "I'm moved with compassion for the crowd, because they've already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat. And I don't want to send them away hungry, in case they collapse on the way."
The disciples say to him, "Where in a deserted place could we get enough loaves to fill such a crowd?"
Jesus says to them, "How many loaves do you have?" They said, "Seven — and a few small fish."
And he instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground,
and he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them and kept giving them to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces — seven hampers full.
Those eating were four thousand men, besides women and children.
And after releasing the crowds he got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.

matthew_16.t: The Pharisees and Sadducees came and, to test him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
He answered them, "When evening comes you say, 'Fair weather — the sky is red.'
And in the morning, "Storm today — the sky is red and lowering." You know how to judge the face of the sky, but you can't judge the signs of the times.
An evil and adulterous generation hunts for a sign, and no sign will be given it except the sign of Jonah." And he left them and went away.
When the disciples came to the other side, they'd forgotten to take bread.
Jesus said to them, "Watch out, and be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
They were reasoning among themselves and saying, "It's because we took no bread."
Knowing this, Jesus said to them, "Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little trust, that you have no bread?
Don't you grasp it yet, or remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Or the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many hampers you took up?
How is it you don't grasp that I wasn't speaking to you about bread? But be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
Then they understood that he hadn't told them to be on guard against the yeast of bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi he asked his disciples, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"
They said, "Some say John the Baptist; others Elijah; others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
He says to them, "But you — who do you say that I am?"
Simon Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus answered him, "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, because flesh and blood didn't reveal this to you, but my Father in the heavens.
And I tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I'll build my church, and the gates of Hades won't overpower it.
I'll give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in the heavens."
Then he ordered the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.

From that time Jesus Christ began to show his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and teachers of the law, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him: "Mercy on you, Lord! This will never happen to you."
But he turned and said to Peter, "Get behind me, Adversary. You're a trap to me, because you're not minding the things of God but the things of people."
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and take up his cross and follow me.
Because whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
Because what will it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
Because the Son of Man is about to come in his Father's glory with his angels, and then he'll repay each one according to what he has done.
I tell you the truth: there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom."

matthew_17.t: Six days later Jesus takes Peter and James and John his brother and leads them up a high mountain by themselves.
And he was transformed in front of them: his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as the light.
And Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
Peter answered and said to Jesus, "Lord, it's good for us to be here. If you want, I'll make three shelters here — one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice out of the cloud said: "This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I was well pleased. Listen to him."
When the disciples heard it they fell on their faces and were terrified.
Jesus came and touched them and said, "Get up, and don't be afraid."
And lifting their eyes they saw no one except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, "Tell no one the vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."
And the disciples asked him, "Why then do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"
He answered them, "Elijah does come first, and he will restore all things.
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they didn't recognise him but did to him whatever they wanted. So too the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands."
Then the disciples understood that he'd spoken to them about John the Baptist.
When they came to the crowd, a man came to him, kneeling before him
and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he's moonstruck and suffers badly: he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, and they couldn't heal him."
Jesus answered, "You untrusting and twisted generation — how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him here to me."
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, "Why couldn't we drive it out?"

He says to them, "Because of your little trust. For I tell you the truth: if you have trust like a mustard seed, you'll say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there', and it will move — and nothing will be impossible for you."
[But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.]
As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands,
and they'll kill him, and on the third day he'll be raised." And they were deeply grieved.
When they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and said, "Doesn't your teacher pay the two drachmas?"
He says, "Yes." And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke first: "What do you think, Simon? Who do the kings of the earth take duties or poll-tax from — from their own sons, or from others?"
When he said, "From others", Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free.
But so that we don't trip them up, go to the sea, throw in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. Open its mouth and you'll find a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and you."

matthew_18.t: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus and said, "Who then is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
He called a child to him and stood it in the middle of them
and said, "I tell you the truth: unless you turn and become like children, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.
So whoever lowers himself like this child — this one is the greater in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me.
But whoever trips up one of these little ones who trust in me — it'd be better for him to have a donkey's millstone hung round his neck and to be drowned in the open sea.
Woe to the world because of the things that trip people up. It's necessary that the trip-ups come, but woe to that person through whom the trip-up comes.
If your hand or your foot trips you up, cut it off and throw it away from you. It's better for you to enter life maimed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye trips you up, take it out and throw it away from you. It's better for you to enter life one-eyed than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
See that you don't look down on one of these little ones. Because I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of my Father in the heavens.
[For the Son of Man came to save what was lost.]
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them is led astray, won't he leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go looking for the one that has gone astray?
And if he happens to find it, I tell you the truth: he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that weren't led astray.
In the same way, it isn't the will before your Father in the heavens that one of these little ones should be lost.
If your brother sins against you, go and put it to him between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you've gained your brother.
But if he doesn't listen, take one or two others with you, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every matter may be established.
If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the community. And if he refuses to listen even to the community, let him be to you as the outsider and the tax collector.
I tell you the truth: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
Again I tell you the truth: if two of you agree on earth about any matter they ask for, it will come about for them from my Father in the heavens.
For where two or three have been gathered in my name, there I am in the middle of them."
Then Peter came and said to him, "Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? As many as seven times?"
Jesus says to him, "I don't say to you as many as seven times, but as many as seventy-seven times."
For this reason the kingdom of heaven has become like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.
When he'd begun the settlement, one debtor of ten thousand talents was brought to him.
Since he didn't have the means to repay, the master ordered him to be sold, and his wife and his children and everything he had, and repayment to be made.
So the slave fell down and was bowing before him, saying, "Be patient with me, and I'll repay you everything."
The master of that slave was moved with compassion, released him, and cancelled the loan for him.
But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and he seized him and was throttling him, saying, "Pay back whatever you owe."
So his fellow slave fell at his feet and begged him, "Be patient with me, and I'll repay you."
But he was unwilling; instead he went off and threw him into prison until he should repay what was owed.
When his fellow slaves saw what had happened they were deeply grieved, and they went and reported to their master everything that had happened.
Then his master called him in and says to him, "Evil slave! I cancelled that whole debt for you because you begged me.
Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I had mercy on you?"
And his master was angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should repay everything that was owed him.
So my heavenly Father will do to you too, unless each of you releases his brother from your hearts."

matthew_19.t: And when Jesus had finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went into the territory of Judea across the Jordan.
Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
Some Pharisees came up to test him. They asked, "Is a man allowed to divorce his wife for any reason at all?"
He answered, "Haven't you read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female,
and said, "This is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh"?
so they're no longer two but one flesh. What God has yoked together, then, let no one separate."
They said to him, "Then why did Moses command a man to give her a certificate of divorce and send her away?"
He said to them, "Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts are hard. It wasn't like that from the beginning.
And I tell you: whoever divorces his wife — except on the ground of sexual immorality — and marries another commits adultery. And the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
His disciples said to him, "If that's how it stands between a man and his wife, it's better not to marry."
He said to them, "Not everyone can make room for this saying, only those to whom it's been given.

Because there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb; there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by others; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let the one who can make room for this make room for it."
Then children were brought to him so that he could lay his hands on them and pray, and the disciples scolded them.
But Jesus said, "Let the children be, and don't stop them coming to me — the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."
And he laid his hands on them and went on from there.
And look — a man came up to him and said, "Good teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?"
He said to him, "Why do you ask me about what is good? There is one who is good. But if you want to enter life, keep the commandments."
"Which ones?" he asked. Jesus said, "You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not give false testimony,
honour your father and mother, and you shall love your neighbour as yourself."
The young man said to him, "I've kept all these. What am I still missing?"
Jesus said to him, "If you want to be complete, go, sell what belongs to you and give to the poor, and you'll have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
When the young man heard this he went away grieving, because he had many possessions.
Jesus said to his disciples, "I tell you the truth: it'll be hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you: it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
When the disciples heard it they were astounded, and said, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked straight at them and said, "With people this is impossible, but with God everything is possible."
Then Peter answered him, "Look — we've left everything and followed you. So what will there be for us?"

Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of my name will receive a hundred times as much, and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

matthew_20.t: For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out at daybreak to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed with the workers on a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
About nine in the morning he went out and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
and he said to them, "You go into the vineyard too, and I'll give you whatever is right."
And they went. He went out again about noon and about three in the afternoon and did the same.
About five he went out and found others standing there, and he said to them, "Why have you been standing here idle all day?"
They said to him, "Because no one hired us." He said to them, "You go into the vineyard too, and you'll get whatever is right."
When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, "Call the workers and pay them their wage, beginning with the last and going to the first."
Those hired about five came and each received a denarius.
When the first came, they assumed they'd get more; and they too each received a denarius.
When they got it, they began to grumble against the landowner,
saying, "These last ones worked one hour, and you've made them equal to us — and we bore the day's burden and the scorching heat!"
But he answered one of them, "Friend, I'm doing you no wrong. Didn't you agree with me on a denarius?
Take what is yours and go. I choose to give this last man the same as you.
Am I not allowed to do what I want with what's mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?"
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside on the road and said to them,
"Look, we're going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They'll condemn him to death,
and they'll hand him over to the nations to be mocked and flogged and crucified — and on the third day he'll be raised."
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to him with her sons, kneeling down and asking something of him.
He said to her, "What do you want?" She said to him, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom."
Jesus answered, "You don't know what you're asking. Can you drink the cup I'm about to drink, and be baptised with the baptism I'm baptised with?" They said to him, "We can."

He said to them, "You'll drink my cup and be baptised with the baptism I'm baptised with. But to sit at my right and at my left isn't mine to give; it's for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father."
When the ten heard it, they were indignant at the two brothers.
Jesus called them to him and said, "You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones throw their weight about over them.
It won't be like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you must be the one who serves you,
and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave —
just as the Son of Man didn't come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
And look — two blind men were sitting by the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, "Have mercy on us, Lord Jesus, Son of David!"
The crowd told them off and ordered them to be quiet, but they shouted all the louder, "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"
Jesus stopped, called them and said, "What do you want me to do for you?"
They said to him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they could see again, and they followed him.

matthew_21.t: When they came near Jerusalem and reached Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
telling them, "Go into the village ahead of you. You'll find a donkey tied up there straight away, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, say, "The Lord needs them" — and he'll send them at once."
This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:
"Say to the daughter of Zion: Look, your king comes to you, gentle, and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden."
The disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, put their cloaks on them, and he sat on them.
Most of the crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds going ahead of him and those following kept shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, and said, "Who is this?"
And the crowds said, "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee."
Jesus went into the temple of God and drove out everyone selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves,
and he said to them, "It's written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer' — but you're making it a bandits' cave."
The blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
But when the chief priests and the teachers of the law saw the wonderful things he did, and the children shouting in the temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David!", they were indignant
and said to him, "Do you hear what they're saying?" Jesus said to them, "Yes. Haven't you ever read, 'Out of the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise'?"
And he left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and spent the night there.
Early in the morning, as he was returning to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree by the road and went to it, and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, "May no fruit ever come from you again." And the fig tree withered on the spot.
When the disciples saw it they were amazed. "How did the fig tree wither so quickly?" they said.

Jesus answered them, "I tell you the truth: if you have trust and aren't divided in yourselves, you'll not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea', it will happen.
And whatever you ask for in prayer, trusting, you'll receive."

When he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him while he was teaching, and said, "By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered them, "I'll ask you one question too. If you answer me, I'll also tell you by what authority I do these things.
Where did John's baptism come from? From heaven or from human beings?" They talked it over among themselves: "If we say 'From heaven', he'll say to us, 'Then why didn't you trust him?'
But if we say "From human beings", we're afraid of the crowd — they all hold John to be a prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We don't know." And he said to them, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
What do you think? A man had two children. He went to the first and said, "Child, go and work in the vineyard today."
He answered, "I don't want to" — but later he changed his mind and went.
The father went to the other son and said the same thing. He answered, "I will, sir" — and did not go.

Which of the two did the father's will?" They said to him, "The first." Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

For John came to you in the way of rightness, and you didn't trust him — but the tax collectors and the prostitutes trusted him. And even when you saw it, you didn't change your minds afterwards and trust him.
Listen to another parable. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard, put a fence round it, dug a winepress in it and built a tower. Then he leased it to tenant farmers and went abroad.
When the time for the fruit came near, he sent his slaves to the tenants to collect his fruit.
The tenants seized his slaves: one they beat, one they killed, one they stoned.
Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
Finally he sent his son to them, saying, "They'll respect my son."
But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, "This is the heir. Come on — let's kill him and have his inheritance."
So they took him, threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
They said to him, "He'll bring those wretches to a wretched end, and lease the vineyard to other tenants who will give him the fruit at the proper times."
Jesus said to them, "Haven't you ever read in the scriptures: 'The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes'?
This is why I tell you: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation that produces its fruit.
And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and anyone it falls on it will crush to dust.
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew he was speaking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowds, because the crowds held him to be a prophet.

matthew_22.t: Jesus answered them again in parables:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his slaves to call those who'd been invited to the wedding, and they refused to come.
Again he sent other slaves, saying, "Tell those who've been invited: Look, I've prepared my dinner, my oxen and fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything's ready. Come to the wedding."
But they took no notice and went off, one to his own field, another to his business.
And the rest seized his slaves, outraged them and killed them.
The king was enraged. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he said to his slaves, "The wedding is ready, but those invited weren't worthy.
So go out to where the roads leave the city, and invite everyone you find to the wedding."
Those slaves went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, bad and good alike — and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
But when the king came in to look at the guests, he saw a man there who wasn't wearing wedding clothes,
and he said to him, "Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?" The man was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, "Tie him hand and foot and throw him out into the darkness outside. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there."
For many are called, but few are chosen."
Then the Pharisees went and made a plan to trap him in what he said.

They sent their disciples to him along with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that you're truthful, that you teach the way of God in truth, and that no one sways you, because you don't look at people's faces.
So tell us what you think: is it lawful to pay the poll tax to Caesar, or not?"
But Jesus knew their malice and said, "Why are you testing me, you play-actors?
Show me the coin used for the tax." They brought him a denarius.
He said to them, "Whose image is this, and whose inscription?"
They said to him, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Then give back to Caesar what's Caesar's, and to God what's God's."
When they heard this they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
That same day some Sadducees — who say there is no resurrection — came to him and questioned him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If a man dies without children, his brother is to marry the widow as next of kin and raise up offspring for his brother.'
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother.
The same with the second and the third, down to the seventh.
Last of all the woman died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be, out of the seven? All of them had her."
Jesus answered them, "You're being led astray, because you don't know the scriptures or the power of God.
Because in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage; they're like the angels of God in heaven.
And about the resurrection of the dead — haven't you read what was said to you by God:
"I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob"? He is not God of the dead but of the living."
When the crowds heard it, they were astounded at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that he'd silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together in one place.
And one of them, an expert in the law, put him to the test with a question:
"Teacher, which commandment in the law is the great one?"
Jesus said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And a second is like it: "You shall love your neighbour as yourself."
On these two commandments the whole law hangs, and the prophets."
While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them:
"What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?" They said to him, "David's."
He said to them, "Then how is it that David, in the Spirit, calls him Lord, saying:
"The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet"?
So if David calls him Lord, how is he his son?"
No one could answer him a word, and from that day on no one dared to question him any more.

matthew_23.t: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples:
"The teachers of the law and the Pharisees sit in the seat of Moses.
So do and keep everything they tell you — but don't do what they do, because they say and don't do.
They tie up heavy loads, hard to carry, and lay them on people's shoulders — and they themselves aren't willing to lift a finger to move them.
They do everything they do to be seen by others. They make their phylacteries broad and their tassels long.
They love the place of honour at dinners and the front seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and being called "Rabbi" by people.
But you aren't to be called "Rabbi", because you have one teacher, and you're all brothers and sisters.
And don't call anyone on earth your father, because you have one Father, the heavenly one.
And don't be called instructors, because you have one instructor, the Christ.
The greatest among you will be the one who serves you.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces. You don't go in yourselves, and you don't let those who are going in enter.
[Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You devour widows' houses and for a show you pray at length. For this you will receive a heavier judgement.]
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You cross sea and dry land to make a single convert, and when he becomes one you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides, who say, "If anyone swears by the sanctuary, it's nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the sanctuary, he's bound by it."
You fools and blind! Which is greater, the gold, or the sanctuary that makes the gold holy?
And, "If anyone swears by the altar, it's nothing; but if anyone swears by the offering on it, he's bound by it."
You blind! Which is greater, the offering, or the altar that makes the offering holy?
So the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it,
and the one who swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one who dwells in it,
and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.

Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You tithe mint and dill and cumin, and you've left aside the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you should have done, without leaving the others aside.
Blind guides! You strain out the gnat and swallow the camel.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they're full of what you've seized and of self-indulgence.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may become clean too.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You're like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of dead men's bones and every kind of uncleanness.
So you too look right to people on the outside, but inside you're full of play-acting and lawlessness.
Woe to you, teachers of the law and Pharisees, play-actors! You build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, "If we'd lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn't have shared with them in the blood of the prophets."
So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
Go on, then — fill up the measure of your fathers.
Snakes! Brood of vipers! How are you going to escape the judgement of Gehenna?
This is why I'm sending you prophets and wise men and teachers of the law. Some of them you'll kill and crucify, and some of them you'll flog in your synagogues and hound from town to town,
so that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
I tell you the truth: all these things will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her — how often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.
Look — your house is left to you deserted.
For I tell you: you will not see me from now on until you say, "Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.""

matthew_24.t: Jesus left the temple and was going away when his disciples came up to show him the temple buildings.
He answered them, "You see all these, don't you? I tell you the truth: not one stone will be left here on another that won't be thrown down."

As he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and said, "Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the completion of the age?"
Jesus answered them, "Watch out that no one leads you astray.
Because many will come using my name and saying, "I am the Christ", and will lead many astray.
You'll hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that you aren't alarmed — this must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and plagues and earthquakes in place after place.
All these are the beginning of the birth pains.
Then they'll hand you over to be afflicted and will kill you, and you'll be hated by all the nations because of my name.
And then many will be tripped up, and will hand one another over and hate one another.
And many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
And because lawlessness will be multiplied, the love of most people will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end — that person will be saved.
And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations — and then the end will come.
So when you see the desolating abomination, spoken of through the prophet Daniel, standing in a holy place — let the reader understand —
then those in Judea must flee to the mountains.
The one on the roof mustn't go down to take anything out of his house,
and the one in the field mustn't turn back to get his cloak.
Woe to those who are pregnant and those nursing babies in those days!
Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a sabbath.
For there will be great distress then, such as hasn't happened from the beginning of the world until now, and never will.
And if those days hadn't been cut short, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones those days will be cut short.
Then if anyone says to you, "Look, here is the Christ", or "Here!" — don't trust it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
Look — I've told you beforehand.
So if they say to you, "Look, he's in the wilderness", don't go out; "Look, he's in the inner rooms", don't trust it.
For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.
Immediately after the distress of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and then all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
And he'll send his angels with a great trumpet blast, and they'll gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the parable from the fig tree: as soon as its branch becomes tender and it puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you: when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors.
I tell you the truth: this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But about that day and hour no one knows — not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son — only my Father.
For as the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For as in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, right up to the day Noah went into the ark,
and they didn't know until the flood came and took them all away — so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left.
Two women will be grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.
So keep awake, because you don't know on what day your Lord is coming.
But know this: if the householder had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he'd have stayed awake and wouldn't have let his house be broken into.
So you too must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you don't expect.
Who then is the faithful and sensible slave, whom his master put in charge of his household to give them their food at the right time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing so when he comes.
I tell you the truth: he'll put him in charge of all he owns.
But if that wicked slave says in his heart, "My master's taking his time",
and starts beating his fellow slaves, and eating and drinking with drunkards,
the master of that slave will come on a day he doesn't expect and at an hour he doesn't know,
and will cut him in two and put his portion with the play-actors. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.

matthew_25.t: Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish and five were sensible.
For the foolish ones took their lamps and didn't take oil with them,
but the sensible ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.
While the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
In the middle of the night there was a shout: "Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!"
Then all those young women got up and trimmed their lamps.
And the foolish ones said to the sensible ones, "Give us some of your oil — our lamps are going out."
But the sensible ones answered, "There may not be enough for us and for you. Go instead to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves."
While they were away buying it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding — and the door was shut.
Later the other young women came too, saying, "Lord, lord, open to us!"
But he answered, "I tell you the truth: I do not know you."
So keep awake, because you don't know the day or the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
For it's like a man going abroad, who called his own slaves and handed his property over to them.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one — to each according to his own ability. Then he went away. At once
the man who'd received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five.
In the same way the one with the two made another two.
But the one who'd received the one talent went off, dug in the ground and hid his master's silver.
After a long time the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.
The one who'd received five talents came and brought another five, saying, "Master, you handed over five talents to me. Look — I've made another five on top of them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a little; I'll put you in charge of much. Come into your master's joy."
The one with the two talents came and said, "Master, you handed over two talents to me. Look — I've made another two on top of them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful slave. You were faithful over a little; I'll put you in charge of much. Come into your master's joy."
Then the one who'd received the one talent came and said, "Master, I knew you're a hard man, reaping where you didn't sow and gathering where you didn't scatter,
and I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here — you have what's yours."
His master answered him, "You wicked and shrinking slave! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?
Then you should have put my silver with the bankers, and when I came I'd have got back what was mine with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
Because to everyone who has, more will be given, and he'll have plenty; but from the one who doesn't have, even what he has will be taken away.
And throw the useless slave out into the darkness outside. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there."
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
and he will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
Then the king will say to those on his right, "Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me a drink; I was a stranger and you took me in;
naked and you clothed me; I was ill and you looked after me; I was in prison and you came to me."
Then the righteous will answer him, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
And when did we see you ill or in prison and come to you?"
And the king will answer them, "I tell you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these my brothers, you did for me."
Then he will say to those on his left, "Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink;
I was a stranger and you didn't take me in; naked and you didn't clothe me; ill and in prison and you didn't look after me."
Then they too will answer, "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or ill or in prison, and didn't serve you?"
Then he will answer them, "I tell you the truth: whatever you did not do for one of these least ones, you did not do for me."
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

matthew_26.t: And when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
"You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified."
Then the chief priests and the teachers of the law and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, the one called Caiaphas,
and they made a plan to seize Jesus by trickery and kill him.
But they said, "Not during the festival, or there'll be a riot among the people."
While Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume, and poured it on his head as he reclined at table.
When the disciples saw it they were indignant. "Why this waste?" they said.
"This could've been sold for a great deal and given to the poor."
But Jesus knew, and said to them, "Why are you making trouble for the woman? She's done a beautiful thing for me.
For you always have the poor with you, but you don't always have me.
When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
I tell you the truth: wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she's done will also be told, in memory of her."
Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, "What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?" And they weighed out thirty pieces of silver for him.
And from then on he was looking for a good opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said to him, "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?"
He said, "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, 'The teacher says: My time is near. I'm keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples.'"
The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them and prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he reclined at table with the twelve disciples.
And while they were eating he said, "I tell you the truth: one of you will hand me over."
They were deeply distressed, and each one began to say to him, "Surely it isn't me, Lord?"
He answered, "The one who dipped his hand in the bowl with me — he'll hand me over.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about him — but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been better for that man if he hadn't been born."
Judas, the one handing him over, answered, "Surely it isn't me, Rabbi?" He said to him, "You said it."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it and broke it, and gave it to the disciples and said, "Take, eat. This is my body."
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you,
for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the release of sins.
And I tell you, I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now on, until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom."
And when they'd sung the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, "All of you will be tripped up because of me tonight. For it's written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But after I'm raised, I'll go ahead of you to Galilee."
Peter answered him, "Even if everyone is tripped up because of you, I never will be."
Jesus said to him, "I tell you the truth: tonight, before the cock crows, you'll disown me three times."
Peter said to him, "Even if I have to die with you, I'll never disown you." And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, and he began to be grieved and in anguish.
Then he said to them, "My soul is overwhelmed with grief, to the point of death. Stay here and keep awake with me."
He went on a little further, fell on his face and prayed, "My Father, if it's possible, let this cup pass from me. But not as I want — as you want."
He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter, "So you couldn't keep awake with me for one hour?
Keep awake and pray that you don't come into testing. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak.
Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, "My Father, if this cup can't pass unless I drink it, let your will be done."
He came again and found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy.
So he left them and went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words again.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, "Go on sleeping now and take your rest. Look — the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let's go. Look — the one handing me over has come near."
While he was still speaking — look — Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
The one handing him over had given them a signal: "The one I kiss — that is him. Seize him."
He went straight up to Jesus and said, "Greetings, Rabbi" — and kissed him.
Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you came for." Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus and seized him.
And look — one of those with Jesus reached out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest's slave and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, "Put your sword back in its place. For all who take up the sword will die by the sword.
Or do you think I can't call on my Father, and he'd put more than twelve legions of angels at my side this minute?
How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that say it must happen this way?"
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me, as though I were a bandit? Day after day I sat teaching in the temple, and you didn't seize me.
But all this has happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples left him and fled.
Those who had seized Jesus took him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the teachers of the law and the elders had gathered.
Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the high priest's courtyard. He went inside and sat with the attendants, to see how it would end.
The chief priests and the elders and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus, so that they could put him to death,
but they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward
and said, "This man said, 'I can destroy the sanctuary of God and build it in three days.'"
The high priest stood up and said to him, "Have you no answer? What is it these men are testifying against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent. And the high priest said to him, "I put you on oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus said to him, "You said it. But I tell you: from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of the sky."
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, "He has blasphemed! Why do we still need witnesses? Look, you've now heard the blasphemy.
What do you think?" They answered, "He deserves death."
Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists; and others struck him with open hands,
saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ! Who was it that hit you?"
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, "You were with Jesus the Galilean too."
But he denied it in front of them all: "I don't know what you're talking about."
When he went out to the gateway, another girl saw him and said to those there, "This man was with Jesus the Nazorean."
And again he denied it, with an oath: "I do not know the man."
A little later the bystanders came up and said to Peter, "You really are one of them — your accent gives you away."
Then he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know the man!" And at once the cock crowed.
And Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: "Before the cock crows you'll disown me three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.

matthew_27.t: When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people made their plan against Jesus, to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, the one who'd handed him over, saw that Jesus had been condemned. He changed his mind and brought the thirty pieces of silver back to the chief priests and the elders,
saying, "I've sinned — I handed over innocent blood." They said, "What's that to us? You see to it."
He threw the silver into the sanctuary, left, and went off and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver and said, "It isn't lawful to put this into the treasury, since it's blood money."
So they made a plan, and with the money they bought the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners.
That's why that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one whose price had been set, on whom a price was set by the sons of Israel,
and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord instructed me."
Jesus was made to stand before the governor, and the governor questioned him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus said to him, "You say so."
And when he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, "Don't you hear how much they're testifying against you?"
And he didn't answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At the festival the governor was in the habit of releasing to the crowd one prisoner, whichever one they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
So when they'd gathered, Pilate said to them, "Which one do you want me to release to you? Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
For he knew they'd handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgement seat, his wife sent word to him: "Have nothing to do with that righteous man. I've suffered a great deal today in a dream because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus destroyed.
The governor answered them, "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?" They said, "Barabbas."
Pilate said to them, "Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?" They all said, "Let him be crucified."
The governor said, "Why — what evil has he done?" But they shouted all the more, "Let him be crucified."

When Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that a riot was starting instead, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, "I'm innocent of this righteous man's blood. You see to it."
And all the people answered, "His blood be on us and on our children."
Then he released Barabbas to them; and he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort round him.
They stripped him and put a scarlet military cloak on him,
and they twisted together a crown out of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. They knelt in front of him and mocked him: "Hail, king of the Jews!"
And they spat on him, took the reed and struck him on the head.
When they'd finished mocking him, they took the cloak off him, put his own clothes back on him and led him away to be crucified.
As they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon, and they pressed him into service to carry his cross.
And when they came to a place called Golgotha (which means Place of a Skull),
they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall; and when he tasted it, he wouldn't drink it.

When they had crucified him, they divided his clothes among them by casting lots, so that what was spoken by the prophet would be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots."
And they sat down and kept watch over him there.
And above his head they put the written charge against him: "This is Jesus, the king of the Jews."
Then two bandits were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.
Those who passed by insulted him, shaking their heads
and saying, "You who destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days, save yourself! If you're the Son of God, come down from the cross."
In the same way the chief priests, with the teachers of the law and the elders and the Pharisees, mocked him and said,
"He saved others; he can't save himself. He's the king of Israel — let him come down now from the cross, and we'll trust him.
He trusted in God — let God rescue him now, if he wants him. For he said, "I am God's son."
The bandits crucified with him taunted him in the same way.
From about noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over the whole land.
About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" — that is, "My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?"
Some of those standing there heard it and said, "This man is calling Elijah."
At once one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave it to him to drink.
But the rest said, "Leave him. Let's see whether Elijah comes to save him."
And Jesus cried out again in a loud voice and let go of his spirit.
And look — the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook and the rocks were split,
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised.
And coming out of the tombs after his rising, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were terrified and said, "Truly this was God's son."
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived, who had himself been made a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given to him.
Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
and put it in his own new tomb, which he'd cut in the rock. He rolled a great stone across the doorway of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the grave.
The next day — the day after the Preparation — the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate
and said, "Sir, we remember that while he was still alive that deceiver said, 'After three days I am raised.'

So give the order for the grave to be made secure until the third day, in case his disciples come and steal him and tell the people, "He's been raised from the dead." Then the last deception would be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them, "You have a guard. Go and make it as secure as you know how."
So they went and made the grave secure, sealing the stone and posting the guard.

matthew_28.t: After the sabbath, as the first day of the week was growing light, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the grave.
And look — there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, came and rolled the stone away, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning and his clothing white as snow.
The guards shook with fear of him and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, "You — do not be afraid. For I know that you're looking for Jesus, the crucified one.
He isn't here — he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
And go quickly and tell his disciples that he's been raised from the dead. And look — he's going ahead of you to Galilee; there you'll see him. Look, I've told you."
So they left the tomb quickly, with fear and great joy, and ran to tell his disciples.
And as they were going to tell his disciples — look — Jesus met them and said, "Greetings." They came up, took hold of his feet and knelt before him.
Then Jesus said to them, "Don't be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they'll see me."
While they were going, some of the guard went into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
They met with the elders, made a plan, and gave a large sum of silver to the soldiers,
telling them, "Say, 'His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.'
And if this reaches the governor, we'll persuade him and keep you out of trouble."
So they took the silver and did as they were instructed. And this story has been spread among Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had arranged to meet them.
And when they saw him they knelt before him — but they doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
So go and make disciples of all the nations, baptising them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep everything I have commanded you. And look — I am with you all the days, to the completion of the age." Amen

mark_1.t: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: 'Look, I'm sending my messenger ahead of you, and he'll prepare your road' —
a voice shouting in the wilderness: 'Get the Lord's road ready, make his paths straight.'
John came, baptising in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of a change of mind for the forgiveness of sins.
And the whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem kept going out to him, and they were baptised by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
And John wore camel hair with a leather belt round his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
And he proclaimed, 'The one stronger than me is coming after me, and I'm not fit to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.'
'I baptised you with water, but he'll baptise you with the Holy Spirit.'
And it happened in those days: Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptised by John in the Jordan.
And at once, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit coming down into him like a dove.
And a voice came from the heavens: 'You are my Son, the beloved; in you I am well pleased.'
And at once the Spirit drives him out into the wilderness.
And he was there in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan; and he was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God,
and saying, 'The time has been filled up and the kingdom of God is at hand. Change your minds, and trust in the good news.'
And passing alongside the Sea of Galilee he saw Simon and Simon's brother Andrew casting a net in the sea — for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them, 'Come after me, and I'll make you become fishers of people.'
And at once they left their nets and followed him.
And going on a little from there he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, and they were in the boat mending the nets.
And at once he called them. And they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and went off after him.
And they go into Capernaum. And at once, on the sabbath, he went into the synagogue and was teaching.
And they were astonished at his teaching, because he taught them as one who has authority, not like the teachers of the law.
And at once there was a man in their synagogue in an unclean spirit, and he screamed out,
saying, 'What do you want with us, Jesus the Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know who you are — the holy one of God!'
And Jesus rebuked it: 'Be silent! Come out of him.'
And the unclean spirit convulsed him and shouted with a loud voice and came out of him.
And they were all amazed, so that they argued with each other: 'What is this? A new teaching — with authority! He even gives orders to the unclean spirits, and they obey him.'
