And the report about him went out at once everywhere, into the whole region around Galilee.
And at once they came out of the synagogue and went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and at once they tell him about her.
And he came and took her by the hand and raised her up; and the fever left her at once, and she was serving them.
When evening came, once the sun had set, they were bringing him everyone who was ill and everyone possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
And he healed many who were ill with various diseases, and he drove out many demons, and he would not let the demons speak, because they knew him.
And very early, while it was still night, he got up and went out and went off to a deserted place, and there he was praying.
And Simon and those with him hunted him down,
and they found him, and they say to him, 'Everyone's looking for you.'
And he says to them, 'Let's go somewhere else, to the neighbouring towns, so I can proclaim there too — that's what I came out for.'
And he went proclaiming in their synagogues throughout the whole of Galilee, and driving out the demons.
And a man with a skin disease comes to him, begging him and kneeling to him and saying to him, 'If you want to, you can make me clean.'
And moved with compassion, he reached out his hand and touched him, and says to him, 'I want to. Be clean.'
And at once, as soon as he'd said it, the skin disease left him, and he was made clean.
And he snorted at him and at once threw him out,
and he says to him, 'See that you don't say anything to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest and offer what Moses commanded for your cleansing, as evidence to them.'

But he went out and began to proclaim it freely and spread the word, so that Jesus couldn't go openly into a town any more, but was outside in deserted places. And they kept coming to him from everywhere.

mark_2.t: And he went into Capernaum again after some days, and word got round that he was at home.
And at once so many gathered that there was no room left, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
And they come, bringing him a paralysed man, carried by four.
And when they couldn't get him to Jesus because of the crowd, they took the roof off where he was, dug through it, and lower the mat the paralysed man was lying on.
And when Jesus saw their trust, he says to the paralysed man, 'Child, your sins are forgiven.'
Now some of the teachers of the law were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts:
'Why does this man talk like that? He's blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except one — God?'
And at once Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were reasoning like this among themselves, says to them, 'Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier — to say to the paralysed man, "Your sins are forgiven," or to say, "Get up and pick up your mat and walk"?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins on the earth' — he says to the paralysed man,
'I'm telling you: get up, pick up your mat, and go home.'
And he got up and at once picked up the mat and went out in front of everyone, so that they were all beside themselves and glorified God, saying, 'We've never seen anything like this!'
And he went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.
And passing by he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he says to him, 'Follow me.' And he got up and followed him.
And it happens that he's reclining at table in his house, and a lot of tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples — there were many of them, and they were following him.
And the teachers of the law of the Pharisees, when they saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors, kept saying to his disciples, 'Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?'
And Jesus heard it and says to them, 'It's not the strong who need a doctor, but the ill. I didn't come to call the righteous, but sinners.'
Now John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they come and say to him, 'Why is it that John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don't?'
And Jesus said to them, 'The wedding guests can't fast while the bridegroom is with them, can they? As long as they've got the bridegroom with them, they can't fast.
But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they'll fast, on that day.
Nobody sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. If he does, the new patch pulls away from the old, and you get a worse tear.
And nobody puts new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost and so are the skins. No — new wine into new wineskins.
And it happened that he was going through the grainfields on the sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way, picking the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees kept saying to him, 'Look, why are they doing on the sabbath what isn't permitted?'
And he says to them, 'Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him —

how he went into the house of God, in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the presence, which no one is permitted to eat except the priests, and gave it also to those with him?'
And he was saying to them, 'The sabbath came into being for the sake of people, and not people for the sake of the sabbath.
So the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.'

mark_3.t: And he went into the synagogue again, and there was a man there with a withered hand.
And they were watching him closely, to see whether he would heal him on the sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
And he says to the man with the withered hand, 'Get up — into the middle.'
And he says to them, 'Is it permitted on the sabbath to do good or to do harm — to save a life or to kill?' But they said nothing.
And he looked round at them with anger, deeply grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and he says to the man, 'Stretch out your hand.' And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
And the Pharisees went out and at once began plotting with the Herodians against him, how they could destroy him.
And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great crowd from Galilee followed, and from Judea
and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and from beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon — a great crowd, when they heard all he was doing, came to him.
And he told his disciples to keep a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so they wouldn't crush him.
For he healed many, so that all who had diseases were falling on him to touch him.
And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, would fall down before him and scream, 'You are the Son of God!'
And he rebuked them sharply, so that they would not make him known.
And he goes up onto the mountain and calls to himself the ones he himself wanted, and they went off to him.
And he made twelve, whom he also named apostles, so that they would be with him and so that he could send them out to proclaim,
and to have authority to heal diseases and to drive out the demons.
And he made the twelve, and he gave Simon the name Peter,
and James son of Zebedee and John the brother of James — he gave them the name Boanerges, which means 'sons of thunder';
and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.
And he comes home, and the crowd gathers again, so that they couldn't even eat bread.
And when his family heard, they went out to seize him; they were saying, 'He's out of his mind.'
And the teachers of the law who had come down from Jerusalem kept saying, 'He has Beelzebul,' and, 'It's by the ruler of the demons that he drives out the demons.'
And he called them to him and was speaking to them in parables: 'How can Satan drive out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household won't be able to stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he can't stand — he's finished.
But nobody can go into the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he ties the strong man up first; and then he'll plunder his house.
I tell you the truth: everything will be forgiven the children of men — the sins and the blasphemies, whatever they blaspheme.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin' —
because they were saying, 'He has an unclean spirit.'
And his mother and his brothers come, and they stood outside and sent to him, calling him.
And a crowd was sitting around him, and they say to him, 'Look, your mother and your brothers and your sisters are outside asking for you.'
And he answered them and says, 'Who is my mother — and my brothers?'
And he looked round at the ones sitting in a circle around him, and he says, 'Look — my mother and my brothers.
Whoever does the will of God — this person is my brother and sister and mother.'

mark_4.t: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And such a great crowd gathers to him that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, and the whole crowd was on the land facing the sea.
And he was teaching them many things in parables, and he was saying to them in his teaching:
'Listen! Look — the sower went out to sow.
And it happened, as he sowed, that some fell along the road, and the birds came and ate it up.
And other seed fell on the rocky ground, where it didn't have much soil, and at once it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
And when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it was withered.
And other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
And other seeds fell into the good soil, and they were giving fruit, coming up and growing, and it bore thirty and sixty and a hundred.
And he was saying, 'Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.'
And when he was alone, those around him with the twelve were asking him about the parables.
And he was saying to them, 'To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that "seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, in case they turn back and it be forgiven them."'
And he says to them, 'Don't you understand this parable? Then how will you know all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones along the road, where the word is sown: and when they hear, at once Satan comes and takes away the word that has been sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on the rocky ground in the same way: when they hear the word, at once they receive it with joy,
and they have no root in themselves but last only a short time. Then, when pressure or persecution comes because of the word, at once they are tripped up.
And others are the ones sown among the thorns. These are the ones who heard the word,
and the worries of this age and the deceit of wealth and the desires for everything else come in and choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.
And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and take it in and bear fruit — thirty and sixty and a hundred.'
And he was saying to them, 'Does the lamp come in to be put under the basket or under the bed? Isn't it to be put on the lampstand?
For nothing is hidden except to be made visible, and nothing was concealed except to come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.'
And he was saying to them, 'Watch what you hear. By the measure you measure it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
For whoever has, it'll be given to him; and whoever doesn't have, even what he has will be taken from him.'
And he was saying, 'The kingdom of God is like this: as if a person throws the seed on the ground,
and sleeps and gets up, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows long — and how, he doesn't know.
By itself the earth bears fruit: first a blade, then a head, then full grain in the head.
But when the crop allows, at once he sends the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.'
And he was saying, 'What shall we compare the kingdom of God to? Or what parable shall we put it in?
It is like a mustard seed, which when it is sown on the ground is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.
And when it is sown it comes up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.'
And with many parables like these he was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
And he was not speaking to them without a parable; but privately he was explaining everything to his own disciples.
And he says to them on that day, when evening had come, 'Let's go across to the other side.'
And they left the crowd and take him along, just as he was, in the boat; and other boats were with him.
And a great windstorm comes, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already being swamped.
And he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they wake him and say to him, 'Teacher, don't you care that we are being destroyed?'
And he woke up and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, 'Be quiet! Be muzzled!' And the wind dropped, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, 'Why are you cowardly? Do you still have no trust?'
And they were terrified with a great fear and were saying to one another, 'Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?'

mark_5.t: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.
And when he had come out of the boat, at once a man in an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs —
a man who lived among the graves. And nobody could bind him any more, not even with a chain,
because he'd often been bound with shackles and chains, and he'd torn the chains apart and smashed the shackles, and nobody was strong enough to subdue him.
And all the time, night and day, he was in the tombs and in the hills, screaming and cutting himself with stones.
And when he saw Jesus from a distance he ran and bowed down before him,
and screaming at the top of his voice he says, 'What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I put you under oath by God — don't torture me!'
For he was saying to him, 'Come out of the man, unclean spirit!'
And he was asking him, 'What's your name?' And he says to him, 'My name is Legion — because there are many of us.'
And he was begging him urgently not to send them out of the region.
Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding there, near the hillside.
And they begged him, saying, 'Send us into the pigs, so that we can go into them.'

And at once Jesus permitted them. And the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea — about two thousand — and they were drowning in the sea.
And those feeding them fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside. And they came to see what it was that had happened.
And they come to Jesus and see the man who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed and in his right mind — the one who had had the legion — and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it described to them what had happened to the man possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to go away from their district.
And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by demons was begging him to be with him.
And he wouldn't let him, but says to him, 'Go home, to your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and that he had mercy on you.'
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered to him, and he was beside the sea.
And look — one of the synagogue rulers comes, named Jairus; and when he saw him he falls at his feet
and begs him urgently, saying, 'My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.'
And he went off with him. And a large crowd was following him and pressing in on him.
And there was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered a great deal under many doctors and had spent everything she had and had got nothing out of it — she'd only got worse.
She heard about Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his cloak;
because she kept saying, 'If I touch even his clothes, I'll be saved.'
And at once the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And at once Jesus, recognising in himself that power had gone out of him, turned around in the crowd and was saying, 'Who touched my clothes?'
And his disciples were saying to him, 'You can see the crowd crushing you, and you say, "Who touched me?"'
And he was looking around to see the woman who had done it.
And the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And he said to her, 'Daughter, your trust has saved you. Go in peace, and be well from your affliction.'
While he was still speaking, they come from the synagogue ruler's house, saying, 'Your daughter has died. Why bother the teacher any more?'
But Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, at once says to the synagogue ruler, 'Don't be afraid; only trust.'
And he wouldn't let anyone follow along with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
And they come to the house of the synagogue ruler, and he sees a commotion and people weeping and wailing loudly,
and he went in and says to them, 'Why all this commotion and weeping? The child hasn't died — she's sleeping.'
And they were laughing at him. But he threw them all out and takes the child's father and mother and those with him and goes in where the child was.
And he took hold of the child's hand and says to her, 'Talitha koum' — which means, 'Little girl, I'm telling you, get up.'
And at once the girl got up and was walking around — for she was twelve years old. And at once they were beside themselves with great amazement.
And he ordered them strictly that no one should know this, and he said to give her something to eat.

mark_6.t: And he went out from there and comes to his home town, and his disciples follow him.

And when the sabbath came he began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard him were astonished, saying, 'Where did this man get these things? And what is this wisdom given to him, that such deeds of power happen through his hands?
Isn't this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And aren't his sisters here with us?' And they were tripped up over him.
And Jesus was saying to them, 'A prophet isn't without honour except in his home town and among his relatives and in his own household.'
And he wasn't able to do any deed of power there — except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he was amazed at their lack of trust. And he was going around the villages in a circuit, teaching.
And he calls the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he was giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
And he ordered them to take nothing for the road except a staff only — no bread, no bag, no copper in the belt —
but to wear sandals, and 'do not put on two tunics.'
And he was saying to them, 'Wherever you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place.

And any place that will not receive you or listen to you — as you leave there, shake off the dust under your feet as evidence to them.' [I tell you the truth: it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgement than for that town.]
And they went out and proclaimed that people should change their minds,
and they were driving out many demons and anointing many sick people with oil and healing them.
And King Herod heard, because his name had become known, and they were saying, 'John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and that's why these powers are at work in him.'
But others were saying, 'He is Elijah'; and others were saying, 'He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.'
But when Herod heard he was saying, 'John, whom I beheaded — this man has been raised.'
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison, because of Herodias his brother Philip's wife, since he had married her.
For John kept saying to Herod, 'It isn't permitted for you to have your brother's wife.'
And Herodias had it in for him and was wanting to kill him — and could not,
because Herod was afraid of John — he knew he was a righteous and holy man — and he was protecting him. And when he heard him he was thoroughly perplexed, and he liked listening to him.
And an opportune day came, when Herod on his birthday made a banquet for his officials and the commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
And when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining with him. And the king said to the girl, 'Ask me for whatever you want, and I'll give it to you.'
And he swore to her over and over, 'Whatever you ask me I'll give you — up to half my kingdom.'
And she went out and said to her mother, 'What should I ask for?' And she said, 'The head of John the Baptist.'
And she came in at once, with haste, to the king and asked, saying, 'I want you to give me right now, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.'
And the king became deeply grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him he didn't want to refuse her.
And at once the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring his head. And he went off and beheaded him in the prison
and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard, they came and took his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gather to Jesus and reported to him everything — all they had done and all they had taught.
And he says to them, 'Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.' For there were many coming and going, and they had no time even to eat.
And they went off in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And people saw them going, and many recognised them, and they ran together there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
And he came out and saw a large crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
And when it was already late, his disciples came to him and were saying, 'This is a deserted place, and it's already late.
Send them away, so that they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.'
But he answered them, 'You give them something to eat.' And they say to him, 'Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?'
And he says to them, 'How many loaves have you got? Go and see.' And when they knew, they say, 'Five — and two fish.'
And he ordered them to make everyone recline, group by group, on the green grass.
And they reclined in rows, in groups of a hundred and of fifty.
And he took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves and was giving them to his disciples to set before them; and he divided the two fish among them all.
And they all ate and were filled,
and they took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and of the fish.
And those who ate the loaves were about five thousand men.
And at once he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself dismisses the crowd.
And after saying goodbye to them he went off to the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea and he was alone on the land.
And he saw them being tormented as they rowed, because the wind was against them; and about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them, walking on the sea. And he was meaning to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost, and they screamed out;
for they all saw him and were shaken. But at once he spoke with them and says to them, 'Take heart — it is I. Do not be afraid.'
And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind dropped. And they were completely and utterly beside themselves,
because they hadn't understood about the loaves — their heart was hardened.
And when they had crossed over to the land, they came to Gennesaret and moored there.
And when they came out of the boat, people recognised him at once,
and they ran around that whole region and began to carry the sick about on their mats to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went — into villages or towns or the countryside — they were putting the sick in the marketplaces and begging him that they might touch even the edge of his cloak; and as many as touched him were made well.

mark_7.t: And the Pharisees gather to him, and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem.
And they saw some of his disciples eating their bread with defiled — that is, unwashed — hands.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with a fist, holding to the tradition of the elders;

and when they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things they have received to hold to — washings of cups and jugs and copper vessels and dining couches.
And the Pharisees and the teachers of the law question him: 'Why don't your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?'
And he answered and said to them, 'Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: "This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me.
And they worship me in vain, teaching as teachings the commandments of people."
You leave behind the commandment of God and hold to the tradition of people — washings of jugs and cups, and you do many other things like this.
And he was saying to them, 'How nicely you set aside the commandment of God, so that you can establish your tradition!
For Moses said, "Honour your father and your mother," and, "Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must certainly die."
But you say, "If a person says to his father or his mother, 'Whatever you would have gained from me is Korban'" — that is, a gift —
then you no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother,
cancelling the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. And you do many things like this.'
And he called the crowd to him again and was saying to them, 'Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that can defile them by going into them; but the things that come out of a person — those are what defile a person.'
[If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.]
And when he had gone into a house away from the crowd, his disciples were questioning him about the parable.
And he says to them, 'Are you also without understanding? Don't you see that nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile them,
because it does not go into their heart but into the stomach, and goes out into the latrine?' (By saying this he made all foods clean.)
And he was saying, 'What comes out of a person, that is what defiles a person.
For from inside, out of people's hearts, come the evil reasonings: sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, greed, wickednesses, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
All these evil things come out from inside and defile a person.'
And he got up from there and went off into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And he went into a house and didn't want anyone to know — and he couldn't escape notice.
But at once a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, and she came and fell at his feet.
The woman was a Greek, Syrophoenician by race, and she was asking him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
And he was saying to her, 'Let the children be fed full first; it isn't good to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs.'
But she answered and says to him, 'Yes, sir — and the little dogs under the table eat from the children's crumbs.'
And he said to her, 'Because of this word, go — the demon has gone out of your daughter.'
And she went away to her house and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.
And he went out again from the region of Tyre and came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of the Decapolis.
And they bring him a man who was deaf and could hardly speak, and they beg him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside from the crowd privately, put his fingers into his ears, and spat and touched his tongue,
and he looked up to heaven and groaned and says to him, 'Ephphatha' — which means, 'Be opened.'
And at once his hearing was opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he was speaking properly.
And he ordered them to tell no one; but the more he ordered them, the more abundantly they proclaimed it.
And they were utterly astonished, saying, 'He has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.'

mark_8.t: In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called the disciples to him and says to them,
'I'm moved with compassion for the crowd, because they've already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away to their homes hungry, they'll collapse on the road — and some of them have come from a long way.'
And his disciples answered him, 'Where's anyone going to get enough bread to feed these people here in a deserted place?'
And he was asking them, 'How many loaves have you got?' And they said, 'Seven.'

And he orders the crowd to recline on the ground, and taking the seven loaves and giving thanks he broke them and was giving them to his disciples to set before them, and they set them before the crowd.
And they had a few small fish; and blessing them he said that these too should be set before them.
And they ate and were filled, and they took up seven large baskets of leftover pieces.
And there were about four thousand. And he sent them away.
And at once he got into the boat with his disciples and came into the district of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, looking for a sign from heaven from him — testing him.
And groaning deeply in his spirit he says, 'Why does this generation look for a sign? I tell you the truth: no sign will be given to this generation.'
And he left them, got into the boat again, and went off to the other side.
And they forgot to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he was warning them, saying, 'Watch out — look out for the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.'
And they were reasoning with one another, saying, 'It's because we've got no bread.'
And he knew it, and he says to them, 'Why are you reasoning that you've got no bread? Do you still not perceive or understand? Is your heart hardened?
You have eyes — don't you see? You have ears — don't you hear? Don't you remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you take up?' They say to him, 'Twelve.'
'And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of pieces did you take up?' And they say to him, 'Seven.'
And he was saying to them, 'Do you still not understand?'
And they come to Bethsaida. And they bring him a blind man and beg him to touch him.
And he took the blind man by the hand and brought him outside the village, and he spat into his eyes and laid his hands on him and was asking him, 'Do you see anything?'
And he looked up and was saying, 'I see people — because I see them like trees, walking.'
Then he laid his hands on his eyes again, and he saw clearly and was restored, and he was seeing everything sharply.
And he sent him home, saying, 'Don't even go into the village.'
And Jesus went out, and his disciples, to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the road he was asking his disciples, saying to them, 'Who do people say that I am?'
And they told him, saying, 'John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, that you are one of the prophets.'
And he was asking them, 'But you — who do you say that I am?' Peter answered and says to him, 'You are the Christ.'
And he rebuked them, that they should tell no one about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and be killed, and after three days rise.
And he was speaking the word openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned round and, seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter and says, 'Get behind me, Satan — because you're not minding the things of God but the things of people.'
And he called the crowd to him with his disciples and said to them, 'If anyone wants to follow after me, let him say no to himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and the good news will save it.
For what good does it do a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
For what could a person give in exchange for his life?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.'

mark_9.t: And he was saying to them, 'I tell you the truth: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come in power.'
And six days later Jesus took Peter and James and John along and brought them up a high mountain by themselves, alone. And he was transformed in front of them,
and his clothes became dazzling, intensely white, like snow — the way no cloth-bleacher on earth could whiten them.
And Elijah appeared to them along with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
And Peter responds and says to Jesus, 'Rabbi, it's good that we're here — let's make three shelters, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.'
— he didn't know what to say, because they'd become terrified.
And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: 'This is my son, the beloved. Listen to him.'
And all at once they looked round and no longer saw anyone — only Jesus with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain he gave them strict orders to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
And they held on to that saying among themselves, arguing about what rising from the dead means.
And they were asking him, 'Why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?'
And he said to them, 'Elijah does come first and restores everything. And how is it written of the Son of Man that he should suffer much and be treated as nothing?'
'But I tell you, Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written of him.'
And when they came to the disciples they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
And at once the whole crowd, when they saw him, were completely astonished, and they ran up and greeted him.
And he asked them, 'What are you arguing about with them?'
And one of the crowd answered him, 'Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that cannot speak.'
'And wherever it takes hold of him it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and goes stiff. And I told your disciples to drive it out, and they weren't strong enough.'
And he answered them, 'You generation without trust — how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.'
And they brought him to him. And when the spirit saw him it at once convulsed him, and he fell on the ground and rolled about, foaming.
And he asked his father, 'How long has this been happening to him?' And he said, 'From childhood.'
'And it has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.'
And Jesus said to him, "'If you can' — everything is possible for the one who trusts."
At once the child's father cried out, in tears: 'I trust — help my lack of trust!'
When Jesus saw that a crowd was rushing together he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, 'Spirit that cannot speak and cannot hear, I command you: come out of him, and never enter him again.'
And it cried out and convulsed him violently and came out, and the boy became like a corpse, so that most of them said he had died.
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he got up.
And when he had gone into a house his disciples asked him privately, 'Why weren't we able to drive it out?'
And he said to them, 'This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer [and fasting].'
And they left there and were passing through Galilee, and he didn't want anyone to know,

because he was teaching his disciples. And he was telling them, 'The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill him, and once he has been killed, after three days he will rise.'
But they didn't understand what he said, and they were afraid to ask him.
And they came to Capernaum. And once he was in the house he asked them, 'What were you discussing on the road?'
But they kept quiet, because on the road they had argued with one another about who was greatest.
And he sat down and called the twelve and says to them, 'If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and the one who serves all.'
And he took a child and stood it in the middle of them, and he put his arms around it and said to them,
'Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me is not welcoming me but the one who sent me.'
John said to him, 'Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and he doesn't follow us, and we tried to stop him, because he wasn't following us.'
But Jesus said, 'Don't stop him. No one who does an act of power in my name will be able to speak evil of me straight afterwards.'
'For whoever is not against us is for us.'
'For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to the Christ — I tell you the truth, he will certainly not lose his reward.'
'And whoever trips up one of these little ones who trust in me — it would be better for him if a millstone the size a donkey turns were hung round his neck and he had been thrown into the sea.'
'And if your hand trips you up, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have your two hands and go off into Gehenna, into the fire that is never put out —'
['where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out.']
'And if your foot trips you up, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have your two feet and be thrown into Gehenna —'
['where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out.']
'And if your eye trips you up, throw it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out.'
'For everyone will be salted with fire.'
'Salt is good. But if the salt loses its saltiness, what will you season it with? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.'

mark_10.t: And he got up and left there and comes into the territory of Judea and across the Jordan, and crowds gather to him again, and as he was used to doing he was teaching them again.
And Pharisees came up and were asking him whether it is permitted for a man to divorce a wife — testing him.
And he answered them, 'What did Moses command you?'
And they said, 'Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of separation and send her away.'
And Jesus said to them, 'He wrote you this command because of your hard-heartedness.'
'But from the beginning of creation, "God made them male and female."'
"For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,"
"and the two will become one flesh." So they are no longer two, but one flesh.'
'So what God has yoked together, let no person separate.'
And in the house the disciples were asking him about this again.
And he says to them, 'Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.'
'And if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.'
And they were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, and the disciples rebuked them.
But when Jesus saw it he was angry and said to them, 'Let the children come to me. Don't stop them. The kingdom of God belongs to people like these.'
'I tell you the truth: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.'
And he took them in his arms and kept blessing them warmly, laying his hands on them.
And as he was setting out on the road, one man ran up and knelt in front of him and was asking him, 'Good teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?'
And Jesus said to him, 'Why do you call me good? No one is good except one — God.'
'You know the commandments: do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not defraud, honour your father and mother.'
And he said to him, 'Teacher, I've kept all these from my youth.'
And Jesus looked straight at him and loved him and said to him, 'One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come, follow me.'
But his face fell at the word and he went away grieving, because he had many possessions.
And Jesus looked around and says to his disciples, 'How hard it will be for those who have money to enter the kingdom of God!'
And the disciples were astounded at his words. But Jesus responds again and says to them, 'Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!'
'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.'
And they were completely amazed, saying to one another, 'Then who can be saved?'
Jesus looked straight at them and says, 'With people it's impossible, but not with God. Everything is possible with God.'
Peter began to say to him, 'Look, we've left everything and we've followed you.'
Jesus said, 'I tell you the truth: there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the gospel's sake

who will not receive a hundred times as much now, in this present time — houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions — and in the age that is coming, eternal life.'
'But many who are first will be last, and the last first.'

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them, and they were astounded, and those following were afraid. And he took the twelve aside again and began to tell them what was about to happen to him:
'Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the nations,
and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise.'
And James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, come up to him, saying to him, 'Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you.'
And he said to them, 'What do you want me to do for you?'
And they said to him, 'Give us this — to sit one at your right and one at your left in your glory.'
But Jesus said to them, 'You don't know what you're asking. Can you drink the cup I drink, or be baptised with the baptism I'm baptised with?'
And they said to him, 'We can.' And Jesus said to them, 'The cup I drink you'll drink, and the baptism I'm baptised with you'll be baptised with.
But to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give — it is for those for whom it has been prepared.'
And when the ten heard, they began to be angry at James and John.
And Jesus called them to himself and says to them, 'You know that those who are supposed to rule the nations lord it over them, and their great ones throw their weight around on them.
It isn't like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you shall be the one who serves you,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man didn't come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.'
And they come to Jericho. And as he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a sizeable crowd, the son of Timaeus — Bartimaeus, the blind beggar — was sitting beside the road.
And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene he began to cry out and say, 'Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!'
And many were telling him off, that he should be quiet. But he was crying out all the more, 'Son of David, have mercy on me!'
And Jesus stopped and said, 'Call him.' And they call the blind man, saying to him, 'Take heart — get up, he's calling you.'
And he threw off his cloak, jumped up, and came to Jesus.
And Jesus answered him, 'What do you want me to do for you?' And the blind man said to him, 'Rabbouni, that I might see again.'
And Jesus said to him, 'Go. Your trust has saved you.' And at once he saw again, and he was following him on the road.

mark_11.t: And when they come near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples
and says to them, 'Go into the village opposite you, and as soon as you go in you'll find a colt tied up — one nobody has ever sat on. Untie it and bring it.'
'And if anyone says to you, "Why are you doing this?" say, "The Lord needs it, and he's sending it back here at once."'
And they went off and found a colt tied at a door, outside on the street, and they untie it.
And some of the people standing there were saying to them, 'What are you doing, untying the colt?'
And they said to them what Jesus had said, and they let them go.
And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw their cloaks over it, and he sat on it.
And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others cut leafy branches out of the fields and spread them on the road.
And those going ahead and those following were shouting, 'Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!'
And he went into Jerusalem, into the temple, and looked round at everything; and since it was already late he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And the next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.
And he saw a fig tree in the distance that had leaves, and he went to see whether he'd find anything on it. And when he came to it he found nothing but leaves — because it wasn't the season for figs.
And he responded and said to it, 'May no one ever eat fruit from you again.' And his disciples were listening.

And they come to Jerusalem. And he went into the temple and began to throw out those selling and those buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves,
and he would not let anyone carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching them and saying, 'Isn't it written, "My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations"? But you've made it a bandits' cave.'
And the chief priests and the scribes heard, and they were looking for a way to destroy him — because they were afraid of him, since the whole crowd was astounded at his teaching.
And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
And passing by early in the morning they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter remembered and says to him, 'Rabbi, look — the fig tree you cursed has withered.'
And Jesus answered and says to them, 'Have trust in God.'
'I tell you the truth: whoever says to this mountain, "Be lifted up and thrown into the sea," and does not waver in his heart but trusts that what he says is happening — it will be his.
'For this reason I tell you: whatever you pray for and ask for, trust that you received it, and it will be yours.
'And whenever you stand praying, release whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in the heavens may also release you your trespasses.'
['But if you do not release, neither will your Father in the heavens release your trespasses.']
And they come to Jerusalem again. And as he was walking in the temple the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him
and were saying to him, 'By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do them?'
And Jesus said to them, 'I'll ask you one question. Answer me, and I'll tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John — was it from heaven or from people? Answer me.'
And they were arguing with one another, saying, 'If we say "From heaven", he'll say, "Then why didn't you trust him?"'
But if we say "From people" — ' They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone held that John really had been a prophet.
And they answered Jesus, 'We don't know.' And Jesus says to them, 'Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.'

mark_12.t: And he began to speak to them in parables. 'A man planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug out a wine-vat and built a tower, and he leased it to farmers and went away abroad.
And at the season he sent a slave to the farmers, to receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
And they took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And again he sent another slave to them; and that one they hit on the head and dishonoured.
And he sent another; and that one they killed — and many others, beating some and killing others.
He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him to them last of all, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
But those farmers said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come on, let's kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
And they took him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
'What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Haven't you read this scripture: "The stone the builders rejected — this one became the head of the corner;
this came from the Lord, and it is marvellous in our eyes"?'
And they were looking to seize him — and they were afraid of the crowd, because they knew he had told the parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they send some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, to trap him in a word.

And they came and say to him, 'Teacher, we know you're truthful and that no one's opinion concerns you — you don't look at people's faces, you teach the way of God in accordance with truth. Is it permitted to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not?'
Should we pay, or should we not?' But he saw through their pretence and said to them, 'Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so I can look at it.'
And they brought one. And he says to them, 'Whose image is this, and whose inscription?' And they said to him, 'Caesar's.'
And Jesus said to them, 'Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.' And they were amazed at him.
And Sadducees come to him — the ones who say there is no resurrection — and they were asking him,
'Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone's brother dies and leaves a wife behind and does not leave a child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. And the first took a wife, and when he died he left no offspring.
And the second took her and died, leaving no offspring behind. And the third likewise.
And the seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.'
Jesus said to them, 'Isn't this why you're going astray — because you don't know the scriptures or the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in the heavens.
But about the dead being raised — haven't you read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, "I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob"?
He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are going far astray.'
And one of the scribes came up, having heard them arguing and seeing that he had answered them well, and asked him, 'Which commandment is first of all?'
Jesus answered, 'The first is: "Hear, Israel — the Lord our God is one Lord;
and you shall love the Lord your God out of your whole heart and out of your whole soul and out of your whole mind and out of your whole strength."
The second is this: "You shall love your neighbour as yourself." There is no other commandment greater than these.'
And the scribe said to him, 'Well said, teacher. You have spoken the truth, that he is one and there is no other besides him,

and to love him out of the whole heart and out of the whole understanding and out of the whole strength, and to love the neighbour as oneself, is far more than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.'
And Jesus, seeing that he had answered with intelligence, said to him, 'You are not far from the kingdom of God.' And no one dared to question him any more.
And Jesus responded, teaching in the temple, 'How do the scribes say that the Christ is son of David?
David himself said, in the Holy Spirit, "The Lord said to my lord: Sit at my right until I put your enemies under your feet."
David himself calls him lord — so how is he his son?' And the large crowd was listening to him with pleasure.
And in his teaching he was saying, 'Watch out for the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces
and to have the front seats in the synagogues and the top places at dinners —
the ones who devour widows' houses and pray at length for show. These will receive a heavier judgement.'
And he sat down opposite the treasury and was watching how the crowd throws copper into the treasury. And many rich people were throwing in a lot.
And one poor widow came and threw in two small coins, which make a quadrans.
And he called his disciples and said to them, 'I tell you the truth: this poor widow has thrown in more than all those throwing into the treasury.
For they all threw in out of their surplus, but she out of her lack threw in everything she had — her whole life.'

mark_13.t: And as he was going out of the temple one of his disciples says to him, 'Teacher, look — what stones and what buildings!'
And Jesus said to him, 'Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left here on another that will not be thrown down.'
And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking him privately,
'Tell us, when will these things be, and what is the sign when all these things are about to be brought to completion?'
And Jesus began to say to them, 'Watch out that no one leads you astray.
Many will come on my name, saying, "I am," and they will lead many astray.
And when you hear of wars and reports of wars, don't be alarmed. It has to happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in place after place; there will be famines. These things are the beginning of birth-pangs.
But watch out for yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them.
And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
And when they lead you away and hand you over, don't worry beforehand about what you'll say; but whatever is given you in that hour, say that. For you are not the ones speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But the one who endures to the end — this one will be saved.
But when you see the desolating abomination standing where it shouldn't — let the reader understand — then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the roof not come down or go inside to take anything out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to get his cloak.
And how terrible for those who are pregnant and those nursing in those days.
Pray that it does not happen in winter.
For those days will be a tribulation such as has not happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will.
And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he chose, he cut short the days.
And then, if anyone says to you, "Look, here's the Christ," or "Look, there," don't trust it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
But you, watch out. I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give its light,
and the stars will be falling out of the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send out the angels and gather his chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Learn the parable from the fig tree. Whenever its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, whenever you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
I tell you the truth: this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
But about that day or the hour no one knows — not the angels in heaven, nor the Son — except the Father.
Watch out. Stay awake. You do not know when the time is.
It is like a man away from home who left his house and gave his slaves the authority, each with his own work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake — for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether late, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or early —
so that he does not come suddenly and find you sleeping.
And what I say to you I say to everyone: stay awake.

mark_14.t: It was two days before the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by trickery and kill him.
For they were saying, 'Not during the festival — there might be a riot of the people.'

And while he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he was reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of ointment — pure nard, very costly. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
And some were indignant, saying to one another, 'Why this waste of the ointment?
This ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.' And they were furious with her.
But Jesus said, 'Leave her alone. Why are you making trouble for her? She has done a good work for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good for them; but you don't always have me.
She did what she had. She anointed my body beforehand for burial.
I tell you the truth: wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken of, in memory of her.'
And Judas Iscariot, the one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests to hand him over to them.
And when they heard they were glad, and they promised to give him silver. And he was looking for a good opportunity to hand him over.
And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover lamb, his disciples say to him, 'Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?'
And he sends two of his disciples and says to them, 'Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
And wherever he goes in, say to the householder, "The teacher says: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?"'
And he will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.'
And the disciples went out and came into the city and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when evening came he comes with the twelve.
And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, 'I tell you the truth: one of you will hand me over — one eating with me.'
They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, 'Surely not me?'
And he said to them, 'One of the twelve — the one dipping into the one bowl with me.
For the Son of Man goes as it is written of him, but how terrible for that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over. It would have been good for him if that man had not been born.'
And as they were eating he took bread, blessed it, broke it and gave it to them, and said, 'Take[, eat]. This is my body.'
And he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, 'This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
I tell you the truth: I will certainly not drink again from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.'
And when they had sung the hymn they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus says to them, 'You will all be tripped up, because it is written: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered."
But after I am raised I will go ahead of you into Galilee.'
But Peter said to him, 'Even if they're all tripped up, I won't be.'
And Jesus says to him, 'I tell you the truth: today, this very night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times.'
But he kept saying all the more insistently, 'If I have to die with you, I'll never deny you.' And they were all saying the same.
And they come to a place whose name was Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, 'Sit here while I pray.'
And he takes Peter and James and John along with him, and he began to be utterly shaken and distressed.
And he says to them, 'My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Stay here and stay awake.'
And he went forward a little and was falling on the ground and praying that if it were possible the hour might pass from him.
And he was saying, 'Abba, Father — everything is possible for you. Take this cup away from me. But not what I want, but what you want.'
And he comes and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter, 'Simon, are you sleeping? Weren't you strong enough to stay awake one hour?'
Stay awake and pray that you don't come into testing. The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak.'
And he went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he comes the third time and says to them, 'Sleep on now and take your rest. Enough. The hour has come. Look — the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let's go. Look — the one handing me over has come near.'
And at once, while he was still speaking, Judas arrives — one of the twelve — and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
The one handing him over had given them a signal, saying, 'The one I kiss is him. Seize him and lead him away under guard.'
And he came and at once went up to him and says, 'Rabbi,' and kissed him warmly.
And they laid hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the high priest's slave and cut off his ear.
And Jesus responded and said to them, 'Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a bandit?
Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me. But — so that the scriptures may be fulfilled.'
And they all left him and fled.
And a certain young man was following him, with a linen cloth thrown over his bare body, and they seize him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
And Peter followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the attendants and warming himself at the fire.
And the chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, and they were not finding any.
For many were giving false testimony against him, and the testimonies did not agree.
And some stood up and were giving false testimony against him, saying,
'We heard him saying, "I will destroy this sanctuary made with hands, and in three days I will build another, not made with hands."'
And not even so did their testimony agree.
And the high priest stood up in the middle and questioned Jesus, 'Do you answer nothing? What is it these men are testifying against you?'
But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest questioned him and says to him, 'Are you the Christ, the son of the Blessed One?'
And Jesus said, 'I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.'
And the high priest tore his clothes and says, 'Why do we still need witnesses?
You heard the blasphemy. What do you think?' And they all condemned him as deserving death.
And some began to spit at him and to cover his face and to hit him with their fists and to say to him, 'Prophesy!' And the attendants took him with slaps.
And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls comes,
and seeing Peter warming himself she looked straight at him and says, 'You too were with the Nazarene, Jesus.'
But he denied it: 'I don't know and I don't understand what you're saying.' And he went outside into the forecourt. And a cock crowed.
And the servant girl saw him and began again to say to those standing there, 'This man is one of them.'
But he denied it again. And after a little while those standing there were saying to Peter again, 'You really are one of them — you are a Galilean too[, and your speech matches].'
But he began to curse and to swear, 'I don't know this man you're talking about.'
And at once a cock crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word Jesus had said to him: 'Before a cock crows twice, you will deny me three times.' And he broke down and wept.

mark_15.t: And at once, early in the morning, the chief priests held a council with the elders and scribes — the whole council — and they bound Jesus and led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned him, 'Are you the king of the Jews?' And he answered him, 'You say so.'
And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
And Pilate questioned him again, 'Do you answer nothing? Look how many things they are accusing you of.'
But Jesus answered nothing more, so that Pilate was amazed.
At the festival he used to release for them one prisoner, whomever they asked for.
And there was a man called Barabbas, imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.
And the crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.
And Pilate answered them, 'Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?'
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd, so that he should release Barabbas for them instead.
And Pilate answered them again, 'What then do you want me to do with the one you call the king of the Jews?'
And they shouted again, 'Crucify him!'
And Pilate said to them, 'Why? What evil has he done?' But they shouted all the more, 'Crucify him!'
And Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them, and he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
And the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard — that is, the praetorium — and they call together the whole cohort.
And they dress him in purple, and they twist together a crown of thorns and put it on him.
And they began to salute him: 'Hail, king of the Jews!'
And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting at him, and they were kneeling down and bowing before him.
And when they had mocked him they stripped the purple off him and put his own clothes on him. And they lead him out to crucify him.
And they conscript a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, coming in from the countryside — the father of Alexander and Rufus — to carry his cross.
And they bring him to the place Golgotha — which means Place of a Skull.
And they were giving him wine drugged with myrrh, but he did not take it.
And they crucify him, and they divide his clothes among themselves, casting lots for them to see who should take what.
It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And the inscription of the charge against him was written up: The King of the Jews.
And with him they crucify two bandits, one at his right and one at his left.
[And the scripture was fulfilled that says, 'And he was counted with the lawless.']
And those passing by were insulting him, shaking their heads and saying, 'Aha! You who would destroy the sanctuary and build it in three days —
save yourself and come down from the cross!'
In the same way the chief priests, along with the scribes, were mocking him among themselves and saying, 'He saved others; he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and trust.' And those crucified with him were reviling him.
And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out at the top of his voice, 'Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?' — which means, 'My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?'
And some of those standing by heard it and were saying, 'Look — he's calling Elijah.'
And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave him a drink, saying, 'Leave him. Let's see whether Elijah comes to take him down.'
But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed out his life.
And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom.
And when the centurion standing opposite him saw that he breathed out his life like this, he said, 'Truly this man was the Son of God.'
And there were also women watching from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome —
women who used to follow him and serve him when he was in Galilee, and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And when evening had already come, since it was the day of preparation — that is, the day before the sabbath —
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected member of the council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God, and he dared to go in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And Pilate was surprised that he had already died, and he called the centurion and asked him whether he had been dead for some time.
And when he learned it from the centurion he granted the corpse to Joseph.
And he bought a linen cloth, took him down, wrapped him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.

mark_16.t: And when the sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices, so that they could come and anoint him.
And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb, just after the sun had risen.
And they were saying to one another, 'Who's going to roll the stone away from the door of the tomb for us?'
And they looked up and see that the stone has been rolled back — for it was extremely large.
And they went into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were utterly shaken.
And he says to them, 'Don't be shaken. You're looking for Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified one. He was raised. He isn't here. Look — the place where they laid him.
But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.'

And they went out and fled from the tomb — trembling and bewilderment had hold of them. And they said nothing to anyone. They were afraid, for — [[And they briefly reported all they had been told to those around Peter. And after this Jesus himself sent out through them, from east to west, the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.]]
[[And when he had risen, early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went and reported to those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe it.
After this he appeared in a different form to two of them as they were walking, on their way into the country.
And they went and reported to the rest; they did not believe them either.
Later he appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and he rebuked their unbelief and hard-heartedness, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
And he said to them, 'Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to the whole creation.
The one who believes and is baptised will be saved; the one who does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons, they will speak in new tongues,
and they will pick up snakes; and if they drink anything deadly it will certainly not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick and they will be well.'
So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right of God.
And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the accompanying signs.]]

philippians_1.t: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all God's people in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, along with the overseers and deacons:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God every time I remember you,
always, in every prayer of mine for all of you, making that prayer with joy
because of your partnership in the good news, from the first day right up to now.
And I'm confident of this very thing: that the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion by the day of Christ Jesus.
It's right for me to think this way about all of you, because I hold you in my heart — all of you sharing with me in the grace, both in my chains and in the defence and confirmation of the good news.
God is my witness how I long for all of you with the deep affection of Christ Jesus.
And this is what I pray: that your love may overflow more and more, in knowledge and every kind of discernment,
so you can test what really matters, and be sincere and blameless for the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of rightness that comes through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that what's happened to me has actually helped the good news along,
so it's become clear right through the praetorium, and to everyone else, that my chains are for Christ.
and most of the brothers and sisters, made confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare all the more to speak God's word without fear.
Some, it's true, proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry; others out of goodwill.
The one group does it out of love, knowing I've been put here for the defence of the good news.
The other group proclaims Christ out of rivalry — not sincerely — thinking they can stir up trouble for me in my chains.
So what? Only this: in every way, whether from pretence or from truth, Christ is announced — and in that I rejoice. Yes, and I'll go on rejoicing.
for I know that this will turn out for my deliverance, through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

in keeping with my eager expectation and hope — that I'll be put to shame in nothing, but that with full boldness, now as always, Christ will be made great in my body, whether through life or through death.
For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
But if I go on living in the flesh, that means fruitful labour for me — and I don't know which I will choose.
I'm hemmed in between the two. I want to cast off and be with Christ — which is far better by much;
but staying on in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
Convinced of this, I know I'll remain — remain right alongside all of you — for your advance and joy in the faith,
so that your boast may overflow in Christ Jesus on account of me, through my coming to you again.

Only — live in a way worthy of the good news of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, what I hear about you is this: that you're standing firm in one spirit, with one soul, contending side by side for the faith of the good news,
and not frightened in anything by those who oppose you. This is a sign to them of destruction, but of your deliverance — and this from God.
For this is what you've been given as a gift, on Christ's behalf: not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him,
having the same struggle you saw in me and now hear that I have.

philippians_2.t: So if there's any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any sharing in the Spirit, any deep affection and mercy —
then complete my joy: think the same way, have the same love, be joined in soul, set your minds on the one thing.
Do nothing out of rivalry or empty conceit, but in humility count one another as surpassing yourselves,
each of you looking not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Think this way among yourselves — the way that was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped,
but emptied himself by taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of human beings, and being found in appearance as a human
He humbled himself, becoming obedient as far as death — and death on a cross.
Therefore God also raised him to the highest place and gave him as a gift the name that is above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend — in heaven and on earth and under the earth —
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my beloved — just as you have always obeyed, not only when I was present but now much more while I'm away — work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
for God is the one at work among you, producing both the willing and the working, for the sake of his good pleasure.
Do everything without grumbling and arguing,
so that you may be blameless and unmixed, children of God without fault in the middle of a crooked and twisted generation — and among them you shine like lights in the world,
holding out the word of life — so that on the day of Christ I'll have something to boast about: that I didn't run for nothing, or labour for nothing.
But even if I'm being poured out as a drink offering on the sacrifice and priestly service of your faith — I rejoice, and I rejoice together with all of you.
And you — in the same way, rejoice, and rejoice together with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I'll be encouraged too, when I learn how you are.
I have no one else of like soul who will genuinely care about your situation.
